Friendly service, cute decor, fresh food, very long wait time. My rating: nothing special.

The table service here is phenomenal. All of the servers help each other out. Drinks stay full. Empty plates are cleared. I don't think the kitchen is set up for large parties. We had about 20 and half the people had finished their food before the others had even received it. 3 people were still waiting on food when everyone else was finishing dessert. For smaller tables I think they are very efficient. Had the Mac N Cheese croquettes. They were decent. $12 for 5 seemed a little pricey. In fact, the entire menu is priced higher than the menu online. Also had the Seitan 'not chos'. The nachos were good, guac is fresh and mild, with some fresh spicy jalapenos. The seitan, not so much. I am a meat eater, I went to this restaurant at the behest of my friend who is vegan. I tried the Seitan. Personally, I found it disgusting. My vegan friend thought it was amazing. So, I guess it's a matter of opinion. The other meat eaters at the table weren't impressed with it either. Personally, cannibalism seemed like a better option than ever eating that again. That's how disgusting I found it. If you ate vomit, threw it up, and then ate it again, that would be how seitan tastes to me. My son got the tofu 'rich girl' sandwich and thought it was great. If you are vegan/vegetarian, this place will probably be awesome for you. For the rest of us, maybe not so much... They do have beer and good coffee though.

So I had seen a Groupon and such for this place a few times and finally got one because I had been wondering what it was all about for quite some time. It was ok. Not what I was expecting. It is a great place if you live downtown for sure. They have a small grocery as well as a cafe inside as well. They have a lot of 'organic-esque' items; things that you would typically find at whole foods in here. They have anything from hot sauce, to gluten free pasta, breakfast items, baking items, sweet treats, well just a little bit of everything. They also have a decent selection of wine and craft beers. They also have a cold section with some to-go food and local items. One thing I did get was local made feta dip and it was AMAZING! It was so good!! We went early so we were able to find street parking right in front of the market which helped. I for sure want to come back and try breakfast!

(If you're whining about "too rich" or "too sweet" or "too eggy," you are doing it wrong. Get real, son.) Here's another late-night review by yours truly. So, not being from the St. Louis metropolitan area, my husband and I never fully understood the hype surrounding this place, or frozen custard in general. Kind of like provel cheese or the Cardinals. Having lived in Southern IL for awhile, our options were limited, and we typically were only able to get our hands on custard. Now that we've moved into the city of St. Louis, we have access to delicious ice creams and gelatos. I thought we'd never go back to custard again, especially not to a custard-serving establishment that was some traditional Cardinal fan haven. But for some reason last night, I thought it would be nice to go to Ted Drewes. The weather was only a little chilly and we thought it might be nice to take our dog out for a joy ride. And I was kind of feeling like a nostalgic St. Louisan. The St. Louis feels are overtaking my body and that scares me. I don't know why I even wanted to go. The last (and really only) time I remember going, I ordered the cookie sandwich, which was -- in a word -- disgusting. I think I have to chalk that up to the fact that Dad's Cookies (oatmeal) taste like hell. In fact, they all taste like hell. But that's another review for another time. I ordered another simple pleasure this time, a.k.a. not a sundae or concrete with gobs of hot fudge, peanut butter cups, etc. Which, don't get me wrong, I love. I just wasn't feeling it last night. So I ordered three scoops of custard dipped in chocolate in a cake cone. Simple AND inexpensive, this treat will run you about $2.50. In the overpriced world of frozen confections, this is considered a steal. Best dipped cone I have ever eaten, as far as dipped cones go. Mostly because I'm used to the dipped cones at Dairy Queen where the "ice cream" runs like diarrhea. And even though Ted Drewes only has one flavor of custard (vanilla...boring), it was still the best custard I've tried. Would it kill them to serve chocolate as a flavor, though? I ended up feeding the bottom part of the cone to our dog (no signs of chocolate anywhere...back off, PETA). It was probably the best thing that has happened to him, short of getting adopted. Then again, he eats his own vomit, so I'm not sure it was an indication of anything. I don't know whether to rate this a 3 or a 5. It's a 5, in terms of custard and a 3, in terms of frozen confections. Might even be a 2, as the place was packed and rife with Cardinals fans. Since I'm feeling generous, I'll give it 3 stars. Next time, we'll probably just bite the bullet and muster up enough energy to drive to the Clayton Rd. Schnucks, park, walk in, and order some delicious Benitos gelato. Now THAT is good eats.

Great food! The burger and fries were some of the best I've ever had. If I eat beef these days, I try to restrict it to grass fed, so was delighted to find this gem while on the road. Wonderful slow fast food. My travel companion is sensitive to gluten and always has to order burgers without the bun. At Elevation Burger they will wrap your gluten free burger in lettuce and prepare the whole meal in a separate area to prevent gluten contamination.

I ordered the build your own scramble to go, with Russet Potatoes, Spinach, House cured Salmon, Pepper Jack Cheese, poached eggs, and hollandaise sauce. It sounds delicious, but what I received left quite a bit to be desired. The potatoes were well cooked but lack any sort of seasoning, the spinach was non-existent (like, there was no spinach), the eggs over-poached to the point of having hard yolks (may have been because of the 5 minute trip from the restaurant to my work, but they would have had to have been overcooked in the first place to end up this hard), less cheese than you would find on a steak sandwich at a kosher deli, and, wait for it, a bland and flavorless country gravy in place of my hollandaise. It's not that the food is inedible, but for the (lack of) quantity and flavor, $12.50 is a steep price to pay for something that will leave you disappointed through-out the morning. I will say that my coworkers enjoyed the gluten free pancakes, buttermilk pancakes, and sides of bacon they ordered, and the service was friendly and excellent, but I will leave it to them to write their own reviews should they feel so inclined. At the end of the day, there are many breakfast places nearby that offer comparable pricing with a much more generous dose of flavor. If you have to eat breakfast on State and Gutierrez, I would walk a block or two somewhere else first.

I was in from out of town and so excited to try the gluten free donuts. My whole family came. We drove 45 minutes just to try them. They are literally the worst donuts we have ever tried. Dry and cakey, not very tasty and I only took two bites of the gluten free donut before throwing it away. My son tried a bite of 6 different donuts and wasn't impressed. They only had one flavor of the gluten free as well. Very disappointed. Waste of my valuable time money.

Cupcakes were okay. I got red velvet and a gluten free chocolate cupcake. The service however was poor. I walked in and the young girl who was working didn't acknowledge me. There was nobody in there so it was a little awkward. Finally I asked what type of chocolate ones they had. She said they were out. No other suggestions were made and the I pointed at the cupcakes that were sitting on the side of the wall and asked if they were chocolate flavored. And she said "yes they're gluten free." Uhhm okay... Then I mentioned that it was my birthday month and that I saw their website displayed a free cupcake during your birthday month. And she did confirm the special but added that she did not know how to process that. She didn't try get any help or even offer to have the owner call me. I ended up paying for both cupcakes. I'm not sure I'll be coming back here.

The service was not so great but the pizza was amazing!!! The waitress took forever getting to us, there were only two other tables in the place. She also forgot my salad, I had to ask for it and then the pizza was almost out. However, the pizza was so fantastic which is saying a lot because I got the gluten free crust. I have celiac and can have a reaction easily just from cross contamination so any new restaurant is a gamble but this pizza was no only the most delicious gluten free pizza, I didn't have even the slight reaction. Even writing this I'm thinking about my next trip there!

We live in the neighborhood and were excited to be able to walk over for Sunday breakfast. The restaurant was not busy, yet the tables were not bussed and were dirty. We ordered and sat outside, and even the manager walked by without thinking to clean our dirty table, until we asked him over to do so (and to clean the one next to us so we didn't have to look at it too). We ordered Spinach Eggs Benedict, yet were told that they were out of spinach. They offered to substitute zucchini, which we accepted - yet had to look hard for when it came. The hollandaise was more like a mayonnaise without any true flavor. And while it was good that they didn't overcook the egg so the yolk would still be runny - they way undercooked it, with parts of the white still uncooked. Yuck. We were thinking to point that out to them, but there was a definite sense that no one who worked there would have even cared enough. We also ordered huevos rancheros which was quite under-seasoned and bland. We bought a loaf of gluten-free bread to take home, and were seriously unimpressed - threw it away after eating less than half. The inside atmosphere was fun, with the bright metal and orange colors, yet outdoor seating begs for more plants to hide and soften the boring and busy street corner the restaurant is on. Come on Our Daily Bread! Step it up and care!

It was nice that they offered a veggie benedict and that they offered it on top of gluten free toast. However, when I think of benedict I think smothered in hollandaise and perfectly poached eggs. This place did neither. The eggs were overcooked so that the yolk was hard, the pesto hollandaise sauce was not impressive and they put only a small amount on top of each egg (it wasn't even enough to cover the egg). Maybe I just ordered that wrong thing, but I am not really inclined to go back.

This is the 2nd time I've been and I'm still left unimpressed. The menu items sound amazing and our waitress was very friendly and helpful, although a bit clueless regarding dietary needs. They were out of the only naturally gluten-free entree on the menu so I was left with salads as my only choice. Also very frustrating to hear "we can make the sandwiches gluten free" and then hearing "we just won't give you the bread". Hm...not exactly the meal experience most people are looking for. I can't say I'll be jumping at the chance to go back unless they offer more options.

The pizza has a good flavor but everything else presents a problem. The squirrel answering the phone always messes up my order and the last time I visited, will be my last time visiting. Squirrelly wasn't there but food poison certainly was. I was down for 48 hours after I ate 2 slices of my large pizza. I have my 1 year old a few bites and he has diarrhea as well. Disgusting!

So my girlfriend & I came in during the Manayunk "Stroll the Street" event. Cactus Only had 1 appetizer available for the $5 special & it was a cheese dish. What if I was lactose intolerant? Why isn't there a cheese free option for the special? Or why wasn't that clearly explained on the door, sign or via rude ass doorman. But fine we order & our food was less than ideal (how do you mess up your signature wings??). All waitresses seemed very scattered. They didn't take our order right away. Another waitress was cutting oranges on the bar counter with NO CUTTING BOARD & didn't wipe it off after she was finished. Then proceeded to dig in her ear; YUCK especially from a lady!!! I WONT be back. EVER. #MrProTip

On two separate occasions I asked for no dairy, and twice they got it wrong. It's especially irritating since she repeated it back to me correctly and it's correct on my receipt, and then I bite into it and need to throw it away because I'm lactose intolerant. So don't expect them to get your order right.

I have been to Bareburgers all throughout New York and have always loved them. Tonight my experience in Philadelphia was less than happy. I ordered a burger to go with fries on a gluten free bun and a side of Brussels sprout slaw. 1: the gluten free bun is not what they used to offer. The mouth feel is gross. It gets soggy and is much bigger than the burger. 2: The fries were exceptionally cold and soggy. I know fried foods doesn't stay great for long, but I ate my meal almost immediately after ordering and they tasted raw. 3: The slaw, I don't even know how it can be called that. It was completely dry, had no flavor. It literally tasted like Brussels sprouts were shredded with red onion or shallots and that's it. I took two bites and throw it away. For $20.52 to eat a burger with fries and coleslaw, I expect to thoroughly enjoy my meal. I did not at all, and actually am still hungry. Very disappointing.
The worst gluten free menu on the planet $24 for a medium pizza. I'll stick to rons school house which has a awesome gluten free menu

Yolk is a national chain and judging by the menu it is probably very good, sometimes or in other places. Everyone we interacted with was courteous and pleasant. The decor was modern, clean, and cheery. The food and coffee were terrible, only the toast and sliced avocado garnish were well prepared. The salsa verde was very good but I would assume that wasn't prepared fresh onsite. The two dishes we ordered both involved a form of scrambled egg.. all forms of scrambled egg demonstrated either a deep animosity for scrambled eggs or a complete ignorance of what they are supposed to look or taste like.. they were also cold. The dish that featured the house made tortilla chips appeared as a plate of limp sad tortilla chips, fried at the wrong temperature, left to languish too long, and then possibly microwaved at some point to ensure a consistent greasy mess of reimagined polenta. My scrambler contained a mix of avocado, chorizo, and other delicious sounding things.. placed into a blender until a chunky consistency, then poured onto a grill into a sort of fried vomit patty. It was gross and horrible. I mostly blame whomever was the cook but the dish with tortilla chips looked wrong at a glance.. maybe that's how those things are treated there so the servers didn't see anything amiss.. maybe we ordered the worst two things on the menu.. lots of other people seemed very happy. Based on other reviews.. yes, the strawberry orange juice is way good.. AND we also got one of the nasty greasy menus.. what up with getting that feedback previously and not training staff to pay attention? I gave two stars because, while the food was very bad, everyone and everything else was delightful.

I went here for Mother's Day last year because it had many options for gluten free diners. My family came with me. We came in the middle of a shift change, so the service was slow and the food was just okay. I am thinking of trying it again because the menu sounds so delicious and because many of the menu items (like the calamari) I can't find without gluten.

I finally found this place... literally after driving around for about 5 minutes! The place is a little difficult to get in and out of, especially if you happen to be driving a larger vehicle. If there is a line, well then you might just be blocking for a minute seeing how the traffic lights in S. Tampa are sooooo quick! Needless to say, I was a little concerned with going to a photo hut for raw fish... you know, a shack on the corner selling raw meats... Not sure which gives a bigger impression of food poisoning, sushi photo hut or a hot dog cart vendor on the street in August?? Anywho, the food got piled on as I watched the dude make it... it "looked" ok from a distance but I was still a whee bit skeptical. Needless to say, by the time I got home, sat down, and stuffed this entire bowl of happy into my pie hole, I was rather impressed!! My only complaint, that dropped a star, is that I wish they would use slightly less base and more veggies & fish. I've been back to this place 3 times.. second was just as good as the first, but the 3rd, well.. whole different story... I pulled up at 8:10pm, they were closed, and I was upset! Oh well Big Island Poke, I'll see you next time!
Gluten Free Goodies and Barista was even careful to ask me about cross contamination! I felt confident I could eat here! The atmosphere is totally cool to!!!

Not sure if it's worth throwing my two cents in here, since so many have reviewed it! But I will anyway. This place is a bit hit or miss. Sure, they've got an extensive beer list--but they're also out of stuff a lot. And to tell you the truth, their beer is often on the lighter side of craft beer. That said, they do have some cool bottle finds--including a decent gluten-free brew. As for food: I'd recommend the beer cheese. But this pub, like many, has the unfortunate distinction of offering hummus that's unrecognizable in its overly salted, chalky character. You're probably best off with the (quite good) pizzas. But how could I rate it lower than three? It's such a crowdpleaser, and I do always enjoy myself here.

As a Cuban-American, I was excited to hear that St. Louis once again had a place to go for Cuban food. I have had the food at Mi Caribe on three occasions (twice in the restaurant, and once as a to-go order)--overall, the quality is hit and miss. I understand that this is more of a Dominican restaurant instead of a Cuban or Puerto Rican restaurant, but there is some cross-over in cuisine with distinguishing features for each country. The mofongo is good here, and a sure thing. The Cuban sandwich is quite good and I have had it twice. The tostones and maduros are also great. Ropa vieja--fair at best. We were asked by the manager how we liked our meal, my husband (who--like I--is one of those people who cannot stand cilantro--even the smallest sprig makes an entire dish taste like dish soap) expressed that he did not enjoy his rope vieja because he did not expect to find cilantro in it. The snarky reply from the manager was "we're Dominican" and he walked away. Fine...but don't call it rope vieja. Call it Dominican carne ripiada or Dominican Ropa Vieja, but don't tell a Cuban that it is OK to contaminate our national dish with the offensive herb. Rude. Needless to say, I did not ask if they made Cuban coffee, and we asked for our check. I guess Mi Caribe is not my cup of Caribe and we will probably not return.

If I could give them no stars I would. I ordered an ice cream without nuts because of allergies. To my horror it was mixed into a ball on a steel board where ice cream with nuts are also being rolled. When I told the man serving me he scraped the area with a dirty scraper with all sorts of ice cream on it. I think he missed the point that an action with sort of carelessness could make someone very ill.

Sizzler back in the day was so much better. Do not know what I was expecting. Went for a late lunch. Always get the salad bar . Today I decide to deviate and try some of the hot items they offer on the bar. The so called chicken nuggets were chicken pellets. Dry and yea dry. Here is where it gets real gross. Sprinkled some of the taco meat onto my salad. As I was eating my salad with the pile of taco meat I pull our of my mouth a rough piece of plastic the size of a dime. It really grossed me out. Also the thought of me maybe choking on the piece. Waited for our server to make her way back to our table to inform her of this. Sensed an attitude. And when asked to speak with the manger we were waiting for quite awhile. We waited quite some time. We were given my portion of the bill returned. I would've comp'd the whole meal. Finally after what seemed like fifteen minutes the Manager pops over to say " hear you didn't like the salad bar.?" Replied no! your salad bar bit back today in the form of a piece of plastic in the hot food. He shook my hand and said we apologize, Seriously! My advice to you all steer clear.... If your food is contaminated they won't give a rats ash. They'll just pay you back. No Coupon. No free lunch. Just deal with it lady

Dear lord what an awful milkshake, and fries and a burger to match. The shake was like drinking chocolate milk, thin and watery. Fries were lukewarm and soggy. And the burger is TINY. This isn't any better than any fast food chain, and three or four times the price. Portions here are VERY meager for the price, and they are WAY overstaffed and STILL slow. My friend and I were the only people in there and it still took forever for them to get around to talking to us. And they had no idea what kind of oil the fries are cooked in. Be careful if you have allergies! Only plus here is that it's open late, but we'll see if that lasts. But during normal hours go to Five Guys if you want a sizeable, reliable burger and fries at a reasonable price. It's further from my house, but worth the extra block of walking.

Totally dig this place. Happened upon it while traveling and looking for gluten free options and we were really happy with the result. The waiters were informative and careful about my boyfriend's allergy but also very laid back which I always appreciate. They are very careful about cross contamination and took extra precautions. We started with the drink menu. I ordered the only thing that didn't have ingredients listed. Well, Trust was an ingredient. Turned out to be a good option, and a good laugh at the menu. Still don't know what's in it though. Next came some tasty BBQ chicken wings as an appetizer. My bf hasn't had chicken wings in years! Very tasty but a bit spicy so be warned. Entree wise, almost all burgers come with the option for a gluten free bun, lettuce wrap, or no bun (the gf bun is upcharged fyi) and my bf got the Woodstock. I asked him what he thought, but he, being a man of few words occasionally, said he was just happy to have a burger again. He did devour it though, and quite a few of the house fries which come unlimited. I had the bison burger which was super juicy and well seasoned with a nice jalapeño kick, and sweet potato fries. Honestly? I've had better sweet potato fries but they were still good. I knew I had to try the Krispie Kreme donut bread pudding. It was not what I expected but tasty without the overwhelming sweetness that usually comes with a Krispie Kreme label. The consistency was weird to be honest but I think that's a personal thing. The one downfall? It's kind of pricey. With everything we got, it was over $50 which can be considered insane for a burger joint, but all in all, I'd say it was worth it. I'm always supportive of places that make sure people with celiac can eat safely and it always helps when it's tasty too. We will definitely be back when we swing through town again.

i met a client here for lunch the other day and was underwhelmed. While they have have a lot of gluten free and veggie friendly options, which is great, they epitomize why people think this kind of food tastes like cardboard. To make matters worse the service seemed determined to make me feel unwanted. I know I lack tattoos or sarcastic facial hair, but I could do without the attitude. And did I mention that its pretty pricey considering the food you get? So lets sum it up - Poor food and poor service with high prices. Whats not to love?

With the opening of Elevate in Edmonton​ City Centre in October 2016, this is a new addition to the roster. It's in an attractive heavy traffic area of the court. I enjoy the refresh of this food court with it's posh wooden tables and metal stools in combination with white clean tables and chairs. Shanghai 360 fits in well with this upgrade. Reading the menu is simple if you don't have any food allergies or dietary preferences. Dishes are displayed with their description and cost. The display counter shows off the hot and savoury ingredients. There were three staff available at 11:40am and the line up was four in the queue. I reviewed my options to see if they had anything vegan friendly. It seemed the rice, broccoli and spicy tofu would work. The staff were polite, quick and worked excellent as a team. It was everything you would hope for in a quick food establishment. The food was standard fare. Again, nothing to brag about it's what I expect in Westernized Chinese food. The broccoli was my favorite part. It was still crisp while being cooked. The rice was a nice amount of starch and salt. While the tofu was soft but not spicy. After 20 minutes of eating my meal I felt weighed down, fatigued and lathaegic. It was a calorie dense meal with all the oil used. If your looking for tasty, cheap and quick Chinese food this place will do. I most likely won't have another meal here due to the calories density. But overall the staff are excellent, food is safe and tasty.

The live piano entertainment was great during our light supper stopover. This small restaurant and bar served clean, gluten free and vegan share plates for okayish price. Nothing else to really write home about though.

veggie burger was house made (kudos!), yet fries soggy. overpriced. cute location during the fair weather days when you can sit outside. nothing was spectacular, everything was expensive. brunch is inordinately packed and impractical for sub par omelettes, do not recommend for this occasion. if you're gluten free, this spot has very limited and tasteless options. nope.

After getting food poisoning once, I have this place another shot and have to say I was pleasantly surprised. My bison burger was delicious and so we're my husband wings. The waitress was very attentive and friendly. I'm still not sure I'd eat the shellfish, but overall I am happy we returned.

Cute and wide menu of elaborate breakfasts (waffles bananas foster, etc). Service was good and I was happy to have gluten free options. I ordered the berry pancakes, gluten free and was disappointed. Pancake had a weird GF aftertaste. I actually forgot that they were berry because I didn't run into one until I was about a third of the way in. My husband loved the bananas foster and my preteen was psyched that they had chocolate chip pancakes (not on the menu). All in all, meh for me but I can imagine folks really liking it.

Horrible, waited 5 min for the servers to seat us after their personal conversation and the place was empty. Chips were cold and stale and salsa had no taste, I ordered fajitas and the wife ordered cheese enchiladas, she got her food drowned in red sauce and little tiny enchiladas and I sent my fajitas back immediately as they looked and tasted horrible,, did not resemble shrimp fajitas at all looked like a pile of vomit. paid the bill and stopped by taco bell on the way home,, it was OK lol.. will never go back again.

I went into trying this place for my fathers birthday thinking great another melting pot restaurant (I'm not too fond of cooking my own food) lol. Anyways my family and I ordered a ton of food from mussels , steak, shrimp, gizzards, pork, clams, quail eggs, octopus and a few others and I will say it's delicious. We all got the hot pot & bbq , you can choose between either or/ both. The waiters and waitresses were so friendly and helpful, they never let our glasses empty and promptly changed the grilling pad when it was time. The only reason why this place is getting 4 stars is because of all the smoke and for people with allergies. I'm unfortunately allergic to pork, peanuts, clams, and a lot of other things so I had to be very careful with cross contamination, my entire family though enjoyed it and I would come back again!

This store is old and dirty. It is in major need of a complete tear-down and reconstruction. I have often purchased food from here which only turned out to be spoiled or contaminated with chemical-like odors and tastes. This town really needs to build a modern grocery store. Oh how I would love to see a Whole Foods, Trader Joe's or Wegman's... I would definitely not recommend going to this store.

I went in with high hopes. Now, it had snowed over 8" the night before we went here. It was a bit treacherous for me (slightly disabled) to get into. There was ice on the sidewalk. When we got in i was shocked at how few gluten free cupcakes there were to choose from. There was 2. A maple pecan and a vanilla. I opted to try both. The frosting on both was terribly hard, like it had been sitting out for a few days. I ended up not eating the frosting. The cake was equally as dry. Now I know gluten free cupcakes can be moist and delicious, I have had other places. I was sadly disappointed in the cupcakes and the lack of variety. We read on your website about all these different flavors and your cookies (there were none and my son was disappointed). The girl behind the counter seemed irritated to be there and didn't like the flow of customers. Maybe we just picked a bad day? I don't know but for close to $9 for cupcakes with hard icing and dry cake made me very disappointed.

Shop was clean and people at the front were friendly. Prices were pretty big for how small and standard the cookies are. Friends in my party enjoyed their cookie but said they weren't something they would pay that much for. I wasn't able to eat because they don't carry any gluten free options. Was hoping they would since they're such a big chain. Please add this to your menu! We would really appreciate it :)

This place opened a week ago, and we've tried it twice since then. Both were very mediocre experiences. On both visits the food was not great, and on the second the service was downright awful. I will say that they did a great job renovating the place from the former Max & Erma's. It's bright and vibrant, and if you're looking for sports on TV, the walls are lined with them. The first visit had some major issues. I ordered a salad without the chicken and bacon that were supposed to come with it. We were sitting in a corner that was very dark, where we needed our phone flashlights to see the menu. It also meant we could not see the food that came out. My salad was served with bacon in it, which I didn't find till eating it. Now some people ask for bacon to be left out because of allergies, some due to religious reasons, and others because they don't eat meat. I happen to hate bacon. Any way it goes, it's a major mistake to put it in when asked to leave it out. My friend had ordered French fries with his meal, and these were so salty they were impossible to eat. The unsalted ones they brought out to replace them were hot, freshly cooked and delicious, we just don't know why nobody had tasted the other fries before they left the kitchen. Even the server didn't want to try them as she could see all the salt. The manager was nice and gave us a $20 gift card to compensate. And that's why we tried the place again a few days later. This time we tried the bison burgers. Service was completely horrendous. . .close to an hour to get the burgers. And the bottom of my basket was dripping in grease. . .so much so that I had to question the server as to whether it was truly bison that was served. Bison is extremely lean, so where was all the grease from? The server was never around to get drink refills and it took so long to get out of there. Don't you just hate it when you really want to leave a place and you can't get anyone to give you the check or pick up the payment? The good thing is that they are open late. We work nearby, and at times late hours, so any time we find somewhere serving food late it's a plus. But we likely won't be going back to this place any time soon, unless they work out the many kinks.

On our way in to Sparks we looked up independent pizza joints and found not only good reviews but also a $30 for $15 deal for Boulevard Pizza. For our $30 we had a 2 topping medium pizza, 2 beverages, an all you can eat salad bar and a 3 piece order of fried chicken with rojo potatoes. Lots of food for 2 adults and 2 growing boys and we did great with our order coming up to $29.49! Salad bar: great selection including spring greens and even full pieces of pepperoni vinaigrette was nice with the veggies and greens my kids were thrilled to have baby corn off the salad bar Pizza: (as reported by my family) crust was good toppings not as plentiful as previous Yelpers have reported but what was there lots of good, stringy cheese gluten free dough was available - unfortunately if you suffer with multiple allergies they do not have the ingredient list for the GF dough and their regular dough does have whey/milk in it Fried chicken & rojo potatoes: chicken was fresh made and cooked well rojo potatoes were interesting - kids liked them a lot while tasty, the dish was pretty greasy and heavy 3 piece chicken & rojo potatoes was the smallest chicken dish offered - Joint: The restaurant was large, booths lined the wall with lots of long tables and benches in the middle. The small arcade area was popular with my husband and sons. Our family loves air hockey and we were thrilled to see a huge air hockey table but disappointed that the air flow was weak and made it tough to play. Ample parking in the adjacent lot. Service: The young man who took our order was very helpful and polite. I have food allergies and he went out of his way to make sure that the food I would be eating was not contaminated.

I really wish I could give this place negative stars based on both service AND food. We arrived at 7:30 pm on Saturday before a nearby concert. We walked in and the place looked pretty cool compared to what it had been. We found two seats at a half crowded bar. The bartender seemed nice enough at first. She was pleasant and offered us a menu. We ordered a large bottle of hard cider to share and I asked about gluten-free items. The bartender said she would ask the chef and get back to us. Roughly 10 minutes later, she came back to us and asked if we were ready to order. We reminded her that we were waiting to hear about gluten-free items. She remembered and went back into the kitchen. About 10 minutes later she came back, and full misinformed about gluten intolerance (told me to stay away from anything with potatoes), started guiding me through the menu. I corrected her, she went back into the kitchen, came back out, and gave me an updated version of her recommendations. We ordered the wings (for the BF), fries, crab cakes (no filler, coated in potato chips), and a salad. Ten minutes later, she checked back in on us and I ordered a black cherry gimlet, which looked really tasty. Twenty minutes later (still no food), she stopped by to ask how we were doing. We reminded her of the drink order and she made it without charging us. It was actually quite good. Our wings, fries, and crab cakes were solid, but uneventful (until later - you'll see). Still no salad. We asked about the salad and were told it was on its way. Close to 10 minutes later, no salad. It was 9 pm. We had been there for 1.5 hours. So we asked for our check, hoping to catch the headliner at the concert. As we received it, the salad arrived. We had to pass. We headed to the concert about 2.5 blocks away. As soon as we entered, the BF felt terrible. He left the venue and headed to my place (another 2 blocks). Before he could even make it there, he puked in the alley. The chicken wings had become eventful. The worst part of the whole thing was that the bartender kept telling us the place was new and "still working out the kinks." It's pretty clear they have more than a few "kinks" to work out.

This had been one of the worst dining experiences I have had! Their menu states that things are gluten free, such as gluten free biscuits and gravy. However, only the gravy is gluten free but it's served on regular biscuits. WTH? Doesn't that defeat the purpose of being gluten free? The floors are black and disgusting. There are flies everywhere, landing on us, the table our glasses, you name it. The service is terrible. While trying to ask our server something he walked away to go talk to a table of people he knows. Another waitress walked by and knocked my brand new $400 purse on their disgusting floors. The food isn't cooked all the way, what is cooked is burned. I will NEVER come back here. This has been terrible.

We got Mahi tacos all around. Most were grillef, one order was fried and one was on corn tortilla with no soy. Everyone thought they were great. We would come again just for them. The nachos with spicy tuna was also a hit. Fresh tortillas with a small bowl of tuna. Capers jalapeño. Not too spicy. Bewared: if anyone in your group is gluten free you could have a problem. For those of us that were gluten sensitive asking for corn tortillas instead and no soy for our celiac the choices were limited. They use soy on a lot of the proteins and cook everything in the same fryer and on the same grill so there is a lot of cross contamination (we thought Mexican would make the GF issue easy) we will be back but sans-serif the celiac among us.

Pretty ok food. Gluten free options available however I always end up getting the same thing, the gluten free Pei Wei spicy chicken, which is always overly sweet and never spicy. I once ordered the edamame as gluten free and ended up with a glutenous noodle in the box, so I'm not sure how well their cooks are trained on allergen. Not a good option for vegans or vegetarians either. I will probably return but it's not my first choice.

Service was really bad. Salad ordered without sprouts. It came out with sprouts on it. Sent it back. The waiter brought the same salad back from the kitchen after trying to pick all the sprouts off. Which is both gross and dangerous because of food allergies. The noise level was so loud you couldn't have a conversation with the people you were dining with. Overall just not a good experience

They touch the fries with their hands when they pick up the containers. I've witnessed countless times employees scratching their heads and making te fries without washing their hands! I've seen the scooper laying in the middle of the fries after an employee has touched other things and handled money than touched the fry scooper- dropping scooper back into the fries! Cross contaminated to the max! McDonald's doesn't require them to wear gloves to make the fries. That needs to change! Fries should be handled like any other food ( with gloves) Manager said they wash their hands each time- I witnessed them NOT washing their hands at all!

Cute restaurant/market. Disappointing food. I tried the poutine with duck confit and the bouillabaisse and both were just way too greasy. Like, yeah, I get the fries in the poutine were double-blanched and that it was all centered around the duck, the greasiest and oiliest of birds... but it was not appealing. Except for the cheese curds, which were DELICIOUS. But I don't know--I've had poutine from like, an outdoor food cart (yes, a cart, not a truck) in Canada, and that was much better and not as greasy as what I had at Maynard's. And probably was not $10? The bouillabaisse was so oily I was kind of surprised it didn't congeal by the time I left the restaurant. I also wasn't too big a fan of the flavor. The toast & rouille... the toast tasted kinda burnt, the rouille kinda bland (full disclosure: I was kinda congested. It's March. I have allergies.). Nicely cooked scallops and mussels within it, though. My friend had a steak. She liked it. Our server was super nice. Parking was pretty bad and I'm still not quite sure if I was allowed to park where I did. Legit made my friend run outside halfway through the meal to make sure we hadn't gotten towed or ticketed.

This place was...ok. We were a group of seven there on a weekday right after the Fourth of July. We were celebrating two birthdays. The drinks were great, and while the service was sweet and attentive, it took forever to get our food. I have allergies, and when I called to make the reservation, I was told they could cook anything on the menu plain. Six of the seven in our party ordered steaks, and they were happy with them, but no one was blown away. My husband didn't finish his, and that never happens. The sides were the hidden gem in this meal, as the risotto ( which could have been a meal in itself) was the table's favorite. I ordered salmon, no sauce, and the asparagus, also plain. Some of the best asparagus I've ever eaten, but the salmon was some of the worst. It had that fishy smell that fish isn't supposed to have (if you cook, you know what I mean by this). It then was undercooked in the middle. It was just an altogether bad dish. I left it alone, didn't bother our waitress, as it had taken so long for our food to begin with, and ate my asparagus. The birthday folk were pleased, but we won't be returning.

I never would've found this place if not for a friend taking me there. Best pizza I've had here in Nashville so far. I have had some issues with pricing inconsistency- one person didn't charge me for extra cheese but the next person I ordered from wanted to charge me almost $3 more for extra cheese even though their large pizza special ($7.99) was for a 1-topping pizza. I like the fact that they have gluten free pizza crusts, too. Those crusts are super thin and sweet. The gluten free pizzas are not included with any of their specials.

I discovered this place through a coupon in the Entertainment Book. We were greeted immediately and the wait service was good for the entire visit. We both ordered burgers and they were pretty good cooked to order. I do have some questions about their food preparation and handling. I observed an employee standing behind the bar and drinking directly from a blender that is used to mix drinks on several occasions, and continuing to use it after it was contaminated. I was also overcharged for my burger, a dollar over menu price.

This is an interesting place. The décor looks like a knickknack shop threw up all over the dining room. Literally it is like the Red Robin décor on steroids. Still, it is fun to look at and adds a bit of fun to the experience. Service is friendly if a bit disjointed at times. Our salads arrived before the wine but everything came at a pretty good pace otherwise. I must say that the server recommended what turned out to be a great wine (Klinker Brick Zin) and when we ordered two glasses asked us if we would rather get a bottle, which we did. When I got the check I was pleasantly surprised at the bottle price, which I found very reasonable and competitive with other wine lists in the area. A bump from three to four stars for that. For some reason I expected this to be more of an Italian restaurant. There are some pastas and pizzas on the menu but there are equally as many sandwiches and other items. If you are expecting pasta Bolognese or linguini with clam sauce it will not be here. The wife had a pasta primavera which she judged to be good and I had the ravioli of the day, which was chicken and mushroom. I also had a Cesar salad which came cold and crisp. The pasta portions were very large and we ended up taking a lot home. Maybe I am getting old but I am not a fan of large portions and would rather have a reasonable size portion of really good food than a giant plate of food that is just OK. That being said, the pasta was OK. A good preparation and presentation. It did not knock my socks off or send me into a foodie frenzy, but they were solid dishes and enjoyable. This is a good place if you are looking for family friendly an unpretentious dining option.

I stopped in this morning to grab a cup of coffee on my way into work. I recently was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease that dictates that I am not allowed to consumer gluten in any capacity, and it's been quite a struggle. I haven't had coffee in a few weeks since I have started this journey, but keeping with my routine now, I had to ask if the coffee contained any gluten. (Sometimes it's hidden in preservatives, or used for flavoring, and it's harmful in any form.) The response I received, "Yeah, there's no bread in our coffee", was rude, inconsiderate, and made me feel about 3 inches tall. Clearly I am aware that there is no bread in your coffee, and perhaps you are not educated enough to understand that sometimes gluten is toxic to certain people and not all people are gluten free due to a diet fad; however, the response was neither warranted, nor what I would expect when paying 2.50 for a normal sized light roast coffee. I apologize if my question, which was regarding my health, was an inconvenience in the morning rush, but because of this statement, I will never return again. Service can make or break a business, and I sincerely hope that a statement like this one is an isolated incident, and that arrogant and inconsiderate statements are not frequently made to paying customers. However, I must say I usually I enjoy their coffee and selection. I used to get the hot chocolate frequently because it comes unsweetened and you can add sugar, or whatever your preference, to your liking, which for me was awesome! They have a decent selection of beverages, and their pastries always look delicious, but of course I am unable to try any.

Saint Louis National, or "Natty's" as they call it, now offers gluten-free pizza... and it's REALLY good! Best gluten-free pizza I've had since moving to Saint Louis!. Talked to the owner, he has the gluten-free crust shipped in from a place in California. It is made in a gluten-free certified location so the only chance for cross-contamination is in his kitchen...and he really understands what to watch out for! Thank you, thank you!! The crust was very soft and chewy, the sauce excellent and the toppings fresh and good. A fantastic gluten-free dining experience!!! I will be back again and again. :-)
How can you not offer gluten free bread..? But, the omelet was good.. Fruit was overpriced, we shared one omelet and fruit and it was $23 Good luck...its Largo, FL not New York City.

A great starter, but a poor finisher. That sums up my few experiences at Stella Rossa. We visit because they have gluten free options for my wife, but we have been disappointed in our main entrees. The salads, soups, apps, and sides are great. During our last visit we dined with others and they had a similar impression. In fact, one of our guests commented - "I can't see this place lasting". Its a shame because the building is very unique and there aren't a lot of Italian places in the area that offer "finer" dining. I will check back with this place in a few months to see if things have improved. For now, I just think they are below average at best.

This is a nice location with decent ambiance and generally good service. I've usually gotten good seafood here (with one big exception below) and they even have a very respectable large burger here. They kind of flip flop between 2 and 3 stars and the main three things that make them flop to two stars are: 1. (minor) that on my last visit there was a bad smell around the bar area; 2. (major) lack of consistency; 3. (major) every time I've been here they are serving escolar (AKA butterfish, snake mackerel, and white tuna). Escolar TASTES great BUT... Even the Japanese have outlawed people being served this poison known as escolar as it can cause your body to expel yellowish-orange drops of oil instead of liquid bowel movements and there are also reports of "other digestive issues, including stomach cramps, diarrhea, headaches, nausea, vomiting, and anal leakage; onset may occur between 30 minutes and 36 hours following consumption" (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escolar). Let's just say the one and only time I ever ate this fish at Grand Isle was my last! Other than the issues above I've usually enjoyed my food here except for some inconsistencies and they do some very interesting things with oysters (in fact during my last visit with a friend and his young son, who has never liked oysters, resulted in the kid devouring the cold smoked fried ones!).

I do enjoy going to this place. I probably eat here once a week, but I can't say that the food is great. It's all just okay. I feel that it's a decent "clean-eating" kind of eatery. I also agree with other reviewers that this place isn't strictly vegetarian. It's never given me that feel. I've been around long enough to see the staff changes. Everyone has always been nice and I like that I'm accommodated when they are out of an ingredient. Like when they were out of avocado I was allowed to opt for a slightly different salsa mix. The vegetacos are my favorite. I did like eating the flatbread before, but unfortunately my lactose tolerance has finally caught up to me. Be warned! If you have digestive trouble with dairy, you shouldn't order the flatbreads. I have now tried eating them twice with the same result. The smoothies are a good fair price. You can have any mix of the ingredients that you want and then add other items at a small cost. It usually ends up being about $5 for me. This is a decent lunch/brunch place. It won't wow you, but I don't think you'd be severely disappointed either.

I was really excited to go here for brunch one day after looking over the menu online. I am a vegan due to food allergies and I saw they had vegan pancakes and sausage on the menu. When I showed up it was a different menu altogether and there wasn't anything vegan on it. They were very accommodating and ended up having the ingredients to make vegan pancakes, but it would have been easier if hey updates their menu or stated somewhere that it was seasonal. Parking can be a pain I that area. We had reservations but even though it was a large group for brunch at nooning a Sunday, we could probably have done without reservations. I would go back here if I knew for sure there would be someone thing I could eat. The service was really good and their Bloody Mary was really good too.

I'm REALLY into baked goods. I grew up in a family of bakers and I bake a lot, so my standards are pretty high. I find that a lot of bakeries overbake nearly everything, and that problem is compounded by the fact that most places let their baked goods sit for way too long before discarding or discounting them. Although I can't speak for how long things stay on the shelves at Swiss Haus, I can say that they do a good job of baking things properly. Their traditionally dry cookies and pastries are a bit on the dry side (though not in a bad way), and the things that should be moist (like brownies or cupcakes) are moist. This alone puts them ahead of 90% of the bakeries I've been to. I also really liked that Swiss Haus has a good variety of baked goods. My personal favorite is the devil's food cupcake, and there are a lot of great cakes, cookies, and brownies. I took some stuff home to my parents in Illinois on a recent visit, and my dad went nuts over the chocolate peanut butter brownie. This would be the moist stuff, and nearly everything I've sampled has been pretty good. On the dry end of the spectrum (and oddly enough, the baked goods almost seem to be arranged in order of moistness to dryness, from left to right), there are a number of cookies and pastries to choose from. If you don't like dry cookies, you probably won't like most of what this place has to offer. The only cookie I've eaten here that was moist was the black and white cookie, and it was pretty delicious - especially the white side. The rest are harder, like the kind of cookies someone might eat with their tea or coffee. You can get them individually, or by the pound. I'm guessing the larger cookies might be a bit softer, but I've yet to sample them all. If you're looking for traditionally Jewish/Eastern European baked goods, you'll find a reasonable selection here. I'm not sure if it varies by when you come in, but I've seen a variety of apple pastries, hamantaschen, and rugelach in their cases. If you're vegan or gluten-free, you'll find a FEW options, but not a ton. It's a bakery, what do you expect? I'm also not sure what their procedures are in terms of avoiding cross-contamination for gluten-free items, so if you have a serious medical need to avoid gluten, you might want to call ahead. The only things I don't like about this place are the fact that there aren't more "fancy" cookies, especially very moist and soft ones, along with the fact that the staff is very hit or miss in terms of friendliness. Most of my experiences have been great, but there were a couple times I felt like they seriously wanted to shove all the customers out the front door. It's not that they did anything specifically unfriendly, they just seemed rushed and impatient as people were telling them what they wanted from the cases.

This place completly and totally blows bathrooms are disgusting and full of shit and vomit the walls are covered in God knows what. I've been to nicer Porta potties. Then they expect us to pay a mandatory gratuity when the service was shitty fuck this place never going back again don't go if you don't have a tetanus shot

We went with friends to this Chili's on a Saturday night. Waiting time was acceptable but that was the only fun we had all night. Not being a fan of restaurant chains, we went to enjoy our friends' company and conversation, not the food. Faint hope. The canned music is so loud that private conversations are quite impossible. That leaves the food as the focus for the evening. The menu looks appetizing but the results are hit-or-miss. I had the chorizo sausage soup that was a sausage-free zone. Great for people with sausage allergies. My wife had chicken enchilada soup that not only lacked chicken but tasted awful. Three of us had chicken fajitas that arrived charred with a small container of tiny tortillas to share. We were assured that the tortillas were bottomless but we felt like Oliver Twist when we asked for more. The hamburger was delivered looked good and it was BIG. Be prepared. The Santa Fe chicken salad also elicited no complaints. I can't comment on the desserts because we had baked a cake that afternoon and we all had coffee and cake in the peace and quiet of our home. The service is slow, which may be why the fajitas came out charred. The servers guard their territory like junkyard dogs so you can only deal with problems with your particular server. Perhaps service is better on a weekday but I wouldn't bet on it. Chili's is run by a generic corporation called Brinker International that seems more interested in selling Franchises and cellphone apps than in improving the food or service. Unlike Arnold, I won't be back

***UPDATE*** IT'S BEEN TWO HOURS SINCE EATING HERE AND I AM VOMITING LIKE CRAZY! MY STOMACH IS CRAMPED AND I AM LAYING IN MY BED FEELING HORRID. NO WAY WILL I BE COME BLACK TO THIS PLACE. Great service but the food was lacking flavor. My ribs were a little dry and the brisket in the porky pie was dry as well. The sauces were interesting, however you shouldn't have to drown your food in bbq sauce to make it satisfying. Maybe we had an off night because all the rave reviews just didn't add up tonight. I'd classify this place as a coin toss, give it a go if you want.

We came here for breakfast bc we did not want to pay for overpriced hotel breakfast food. The place was small and relatively charming - most of the places in the French Quarter have that quality, but it felt a little bit dingy (like the FQ as well) We ordered Greek omelettes (one with feta and one without)... they got both without. They redid my order, but it too awhile and ..well, i really wanted my food ASAP. The coffee creamer (half and half) was already on the table with 1/2 veg oil butter and some jams. I needed non-dairy alternative that was also gluten-free... no luck. my friend wanted alternative sweeteners, but they didn't seem to have much. The orders for toast went to the wrong people.. and everything was just kind of like.. a carefree environment more than.. business. I get Southern hospitality and some more of a laid-back experience, but this might have been too much so. The potatoes were good, the eggs were good... just needed more service.

I waited a few weeks after this place opened to allow it to get its act together. Seeing that their menu still has "french quarter" location printed on it, this immediately threw up a red flag that this restaurant is not ready for local business, (this restaurant is located uptown). As I walked in the place, I did feel welcomed, and the decor does match the theme of the restaurant: New Orleans jazz and seafood restaurant (even though most of the this remains unchanged from C'est La vie, the former hard-luck restaurant to fail due to its own demise.) i ordered a Stella Artois, which the menu says is on draft, but came in a bottle, (so did every other beer, so don't be fooled). Our waitress was kind and polite, slightly brash and presumptuous. Once seated, we were served raw oysters, which were perfectly sized, shucked properly, and exploding with salty deliciousness. We were given one additional oyster over what the order had called for. Butter crackers were provided with the oysters, instead of saltines. These crackers were smaller than saltines, and lacked the complimentary saltiness that a saltine offers. It was difficult to eat an oyster together with the butter cracker (and hold the oyster on the cracker), due to its lack of durability and shape. Freshly made cocktail sauce was provided with the oysters, that was spot-on. The Cowan snapping turtle was cooked nicely, tender all the way through, credit to slow cooking. This dish is advertised as stewed, and comes with a "red gravy." However, this sauce resembles more of a liquid poured over white rice. Although the turtle was marinated with complimentary spices, the sauce tasted more like a crab boil gone completely wrong. The sauce was under seasoned, runny and over-powered with lemon. The delicacy of the turtle was completely subdued by the sauce. Two slices of garlic bread were served with the dish, sliced too thinly, and soaked with butter. By the time the plate reached the table, the bread was soggy. I would not order this dish again. The red beans and rice are vegetarian. The beans were soaked properly and cooked nicely, but lacked freshness, and therefore, lacked flavor. A red beans dish does not require ham to have flavor, but it does require fresh red beans. i found myself adding hot sauce as an enhancement, not a complement. I would not order this dish again. Upon ordering the baked cornish hen, the waitress notified us after about 10 minutes of waiting that this dish was not available. The cajun half rotisserie chicken was ordered in its place. The chicken was mildly over seasoned, but being called a "cajun" dish, the saltiness was acceptable. The chicken itself was tender and juicy, but it was easy to tell that the meat was not fresh, (maybe it sat in the refrigerator over night?). I would consider ordering this dish again. The W.F. N'awlin's cajun pasta was served 10 - 15 minutes after every other dish was served. The pasta was difficult to taste due to the disproportionate amount of Alfredo sauce served with the dish. It was more like eating cheese and noodle soup than an Alfredo pasta dish. The taste of the sauce was fair, but overpowered all aspects of the dish, including the chicken and andouille. The dish lacked appeal, and it's presentation grew more distasteful as it sat on the table. Our waitress, although polite, gave us no warning of the bottled beers, the delay in preparation of the pasta, nor any apology for bringing a dish out after everyone else had eaten their meals. One meal was also served without its advertised side, which had to be addressed by the table. Some veggie sides contained frozen, packaged vegetables. Ratings: Service: 2 starts Presentation: 2 stars Food: 2 stars Experience and ambience: 2-1/2 stars

I would NEVER go back here EVER again...... Their sushi was really DRY and that just didn't make sense since they are sushi buffet restaurant... I can spend half of what I spent there and eat twice as much at so many different buffets that are so much fresh in quality. I just feel sorry for the owner because for whatever reason, I couldn't find a SINGLE HAPPY FACE at the restaurant(i am talking about STAFF). Besides the food, I really didn't like the fact that they were vaccuming while we were eating. When I mentioned it to the staff, a young kid that isn't even 18 yet, smirks. When I asked for a manager, really old and short guy comes out and tells me that he is sorry and tells us to leave after paying for the bill... We paid our bill and kindly told the manager that we are not coming back. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO ANYONE ESPECIALLY PEOPLE WITH ALLERGIES...

My daughter loves Fazoli's so I brought her here. She is 15 and she happened to pick kids eat free night. (Do not go on Tuesdays if you don't have younger kids). I could tell by the sad faces when we walked in people had been waiting a long time. We ordered and got our drinks. I felt $19 for 2 pieces of pizza and a little pasta meal was a bit prices but my daughters happiness is priceless. Our food came out pretty quick. My daughters pizza did not look good but she enjoyed it. My pasta was alright. I just ordered something quick and it was a pesto chicken thing but was over the top w cheese and Alfredo. And I am lactose intolerant but I ate it anyway. (I did regret that later) The staff was nice, brought us the extra breadsticks I asked for. My only issues is they want to clean the dishes off the table but they were insanely busy so it just seemed messy. I feel it is expensive for what you get and drinks are still separate. Plus sorry I am not a fan of kids eat free nights anywhere. So I will eat here again to make my teen smile but I will order something minus cheese.

Bra placering på restaurangen och supergod mat! Vi provade bla lobstersandwich och fiskrätter vilka samtliga var toppen - när man väl fick det man beställt vill säga... Behövde pga allergier göra specialbeställning vilket vår servitris uppenbarligen tykte var jättejobbigt och kom dessutom efter lång väntan ut med fel saker!!! Efter mycket om och men kom kollegor och "ordnade upp" det hela med ett helt annat tillmötesgående och med en "no problem" mentalitet... Rekommenderar varmt men hoppas då ni blir uppassade av någon med gott humör ;)

I wish there were in between ratings or you could split them by category, but alas, only whole star ratings. The food here is good for sure and the menu is really good as it specifies what is vegan, vegetarian and gluten free. Though the staff here is hit or miss. The manager, or who I assume to be the manager, was polite and courteous, but the second we got in I got a bad vibe from the initial person to greet us. The waiter, who wound up being alright, started out upset that we changed the number of guests (albeit something I'm not happy about myself, but things happen). There was some initial complaining, a bunch of it, which we could easily hear. Eventually he warmed up and wasn't bad, but not a particularly enthusiastic waiter. The other staff was way too comfortable chatting and hanging out. I started having flashbacks to kitchen impossible and whatever show that is where they install cameras to observe the staff. Definitely could use some work in that regard. The fact it was a Wednesday night in Wilmington DE and we had a sizable party, despite losing some guests, and we were spending a fair amount of money there, just seemed to be lost on the staff. We could have easily gone somewhere else and spent our evening, and money, elsewhere. Be thankful for our patronage and we'll be thankful for your service. Serve good food while doing so and we'll even come back, plus maybe even recommend the place.

Place was empty at 2 on Friday. Staff were friendly and helpful. Had a small mushroom, shrimp and Pepperoni pizza and asked for a thin crust. (They have gluten free crust too but no gluten free pasta). 8" pizza with good flavour, lots of topping and probably more cheese than it really needs. Tasted good both hot, and day later cold. The only complaint is the price!!! Really, $18 for a small three topping pizza is pretty out there. Doubt I would go back very often as there are other places just as good at literally half the price. I can get an XL at Tony's with one more topping, which is literally 4 times as much food, for $27. They do deliver but small area and there is a substantial up charge.

This was my first (and last) time ordering from this place. I bought a family platter with fried whiting, crab sticks, "scallops", shrimp (the width of my ring finger, and fries. It came with cole slaw in a condiment container (remember this is a family platter) and ONE container of cocktail sauce. The "scallops" were made of imitation crab meat...gross! There was no indication on the menu that the scallops were "imitation". The food was not seasoned and I was underwhelmed with all of it. The fries were good but they seemed to be from the seasoned bag you buy from the market. After tasting a small sample of each thing, I now feel the strong urge to vomit.

This particular Marathon only gets two stars, but I do not dislike Marathon as a general rule. In fact, I like Marathon as a general rule. But this location... I want to like it. I work less than a block from here. My only frame of reference with this restaurant comes from the first time I tried to order take out and I was placed on hold. For about 7 minutes. Why I stayed on hold so long? I was desperate for a salad. I called back two weeks later for this same salad: spring greens, artichoke hearts, goat & cheddar cheese, and white balsamic. I successfully ordered this salad. When I picked it up, service was decent. It was ready when they said it would. Then I got back to work, ready to EAT! I opened the bag and found a soggy, wet, nasty soup that barely lined the bottom of the plastic container it came in. The veggies were completely swimming in white balsamic. I ate three bites and wanted to vomit. Perhaps I should have ordered the dressing on the side, but I thought that was common practice with to-go salads. The size of the salad was unacceptable - I've had their salads before and this was maybe half the size. Perhaps I should have complained at the time and taken it back, but I was so sickened and disappointed I didn't. All of that being said, I'm giving this place two stars because it's not all that bad. Just that one time, it was really, really bad. Marathon on the Square is better. But Marathon in University City is worse (FYI).

So greasy....Had the steak burrito which was okish but so greasy. Woke up in the middle of the night with the runs and vomiting. Husband had the beef taco and ended up destroying the bathroom at his job. No Bueno. Soda was good though.
Cosi is a great option for Gluten Free diners! The GF items are clearly marked on the menu boards. There were several GF salad and soup options to choose from.

Went for the Feast of the Seven Fishes. Food is mediocre. There was one dish out of a plethora that was remarkable. The seafood salad. Other than that, dishes and dishes of mediocrity. I'm assuming the palate of your average Franklin diner is pretty bland. In which case, they'll be incredibly successful. A Nashville city resident need not waste the gas money to head out to copville USA. Stay closer to home and save yourself the stomach/headache. Yes, my dining partner got a terrible migraine halfway through the 3 hour dinner, and I later vomited up my seafood salad. I'd like to say it was something else, perhaps it was, but not likely. They said "gluten-free upon request", i requested at the time of the reservation. 4 out of the 10 dishes I could not eat because there was no substitution provided. So that's 40% of a meal I paid for, that I could not eat. 2 appetizers, and 2 desserts. I would have never gone to this event, knowing the menu, if they didn't advertise that they would make accommodations for people like me. I'm not even going to go into the pelligrino debacle, you can read that in another review. Suffice it to say, that waitress is on my list. I would only recommend this to a friend who preferred salt as the one flavor in a dish and loved wheat products. Oh yes, and there was a conga line.

Should have turned around as soon as I got to the door. I was immediately greeted by a strong smell of garbage, but giving it the benefit of the doubt, (thinking it was from the street), I went in. The server was less than knowledgeable. If the poor wine selection and over-priced shrimp cocktail wasn't bad enough, the bathroom situation topped it off. The ladies room was occupied by at least 1 coed couple and they weren't coming out any time soon. The men's bathroom door came off its hinges. And upon exiting the restaurant I witnessed several rancid bags of garbage being dragged out of the basement to be placed out front. The smell was enough to make you vomit. Never going back, although I doubt this place will stay open for long.

It does not matter how good your food is if your customer service is deplorable. I was really excited to pick up pizza because my coworkers had been bragging about this place. I showed up and the hostess/cashier was completely rude. For a restaurant, the hostess is the first person you see when you come into a restaurant and represents your company . I didn't get a greeting or any sort of an acknowledgement for over five minutes even though I was standing two feet away from her. She was on the phone with a customer, visibly and verbally getting upset with the customer for asking about gluten free options. She was waving her arms around in frustration and put the customer on hold (still ignoring me afterwards ). So I go to the next nearest employee and inform him that I still haven't been helped and how told him how rude the girl was being. No apologies or anything, he proceeds to get my order. Good thing I checked it because something I ordered was missing and it was a very simple order. I go towards the food window, upset and about fed up and the hostess sees this and rushes over. I told her that I needed the rest of my order and then she scoffed at me! She replied.. "uh.. OK!" Unacceptable, hire yourselves a pleasant person to represent your company because it has potential.

To preface this: We have gone to the University City one and Willow Grove, which we love. We did also go the day after Christmas and it was quite busy. First...Food. To be honest, I want my money back. We ordered guacamole and then quickly sent it back because it was overloaded on lime concentrate and unripened avocados. The busgirl who I had to stare down to get any service told us that they were having a huge problem and ran out of ripe avocados. If you ran out of avocados...don't serve any. You can get people ill if they have too much of it. Just stupid. Then we had the Tofu tacos and Mahi Mahi Salad. The tofu was not marinated and basically tasted like someone just decided to flash fry it and then just sprinkle sauce on it. The fish was like rubber and I specifically said that I wanted to change out the dressing to an non-dairy one since I am lactose intolerant. After the mayhem of having to pay 9 dollars for chips and salsa (they swapped it out), it was just too annoying to send another dish back. So we quickly paid (seriously way too much money for food we did not eat) and rushed out. Service...it was so bad. We waited at least 15 minutes at the table to get any waitress to give us any mind and that was my basically eye-stalking the busgirl. She was fairly nice though but really slow service and unable to fix all the bad food that was coming out of that kitchen. If you want a good Mad Mex experience, just don't go here. it's a sad shell of the other locations.

From the moment I arrived at Casa Blanca I felt unsafe and displeased with service. We paid for our entry, hookah, and food which he said we must buy because my friend who was with us did not have his ID. We waited roughly 15 min just to be seated, or even acknowledged by staff. When the server finally seated us at a table, I sat down trusting that our server knew the table was OK for a customer. When I sat down I smelled a foul oder, only to realize I had stepped and slid my foot across a pile of vomit. My boyfriend returned from the restroom and after I told him what happened, he politely brought up the situation with management. Which they proceeded to tell him "well we didn't know" & "where are you from? Oh, well in Tucson it's not like that" ..... There is absolutely no excuse for this. First of all, IF YOU SERVE FOOD THERE SHOULD BE NO VOMIT ON THE FLOOR. BOTTOM LINE. WE WILL BE CONTACTING THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT FOR THE SAFETY OF ALL OF OUR HEALTH. DO NOT GO HERE! !!

Generally enjoyed eating at the restaurant but when I ordered take out I was soooooo disappointed! I ordered a noodle bowl that gave the option for vegan and gluten free (which I am both) and when it arrived it was literally a bowl of noodles in broth, nothing else! Why give the option for vegan and gluten free when everything would be removed leaving me with the most bland meal I've ever had! So misleading and honestly felt a bit cruel!

FIVE STARS! I have become addicted to this place for so many reasons. The most important part to disclose IS THAT THE GLUTEN FREE PIZZA AND PASTA ARE AMAZING!!!! The wife of the chef has celiac disease and the attention to the gluten free safety is outstanding. All pasta and pizza can be made gluten free. The wait staff mention over and over of how was no contamination with gluten containing areas of the kitchen. The wings are gluten free and baked to boot! So the menu-the Fun Guy pizza is a prize. If you order one pizza, this is it. The CiCi salad - which is the former Milan salad with shrimp, bacon and egg over crisp iceberg is also a must. Fav of the salads although the goat cheese salad is also great. Katie behind the bar makes a dirty martini I had never had before - she mottles the olives to create the "dirty" part and instead of salty from jarred olive juice it's smooth and delicious. Ask for this! Shelby at reception is always smiling and accommodating. Two thumbs up! Parlor is both a great date place and also extremely kid friendly. Rob Wasserman (the owner) - you have a winner here and I hope you become a Main Line institution as you have done with Rouge on Rittenhouse Square!

Fine dining prices with terrible service does not make a great meal. Our waiter took forever to greet us and seemed completely disinterested once he finally did. He got both of my parent's orders wrong and they had thoroughly discussed their food allergies and sensitivities with him while ordering. The pacing of the meal was totally off; entrees were brought as appetizers and appetizers as entrees. Once it was set right, the food was all very good but the service left us all with a bad taste. I don't think I'll be returning.

I have a love-hate relationship with Pancake Pantry. Someone once told me it was as if Jesus was making pancakes and working in the kitchen. This is not true. While their sides and pancakes are good, they have absolutely no gluten free pancakes or options. At a special place in their menu it even states: we have no gluten free items for the safety of our OTHER customers. I'm sorry what? Your other customers? That just doesn't make sense. Anyway, this restaurant has failed many health inspections and has almost been closed down, but they push that under the table. The floor is always dirty, but the staff is very very nice. So overall, great side items and staff, but the restaurant itself is gross.

The "totchos" appetizer was a 10! But. . I ordered the taco truck burger on a gluten free bun. The bun was dry as can be and fell apart before my second bite. Didn't exactly work out. Had to finish it with my fork. The chicken wasn't really that good either. Most people probably just get beef on a regular bun so you may not have my experience, but mine wasn't good regarding the main course. Minus 2 stars for this. Vibe of the restaurant was modern and cool with outside seating. Update: My stomach has been hurting me all night. This was the only meal I had today so there is nothing else I could blame for this. I wouldn't eat here again.

The pizza, even the gluten free (gf) is decent. The service is not. They can't seem to get you your pizza anywhere near the estimated time. This was not the first time, but it was the worst and will be the last. I ordered one gf pizza, and one regular. When I got there they had over looked the 2nd pizza and had to make it while we waited. Total time from phone order to receiving pizzas was 65 minutes! I ordered 6 extras on my gf pizza, and the adds aren't cheap at $1.49 each on a medium. It looked like they put about 25 cents worth on the pizza and I mean a few dabs of sausage, a teaspoon of feta, etc., and left off one of the ingredients entirely. I saw the guy show the pizzas to other folks when they picked up and they looked great - were totally loaded. I never thought to look at ours because I was dealing with kids. I probably would have cancelled the whole order if it wasn't a late night and my kids were hungry and still awaiting dinner. When other food places get you order wrong or mess something up, they use customer service to make it right, so that you might want to comeback again. Not these guys though, nothing at all. The above review was on 9/12 or so. The folks at Pizza Guys contacted me on Yelp today, 9/25 and offered compensation to give them another try (see below) Being that the pizza is really good, if they can get their service up to par, then it's good by me. I have increased the star level for this reason. Sent to me on 9/25: Hi George My name is Simran I am the new owner Pizza Guys Reno. First I want apologize for the inconvenience and secondly, I want to thank you for bringing this up to my attention by this review. I now know that I need to better train my staff both in the kitchen and in customer service. A 65 minute wait time is unacceptable and personally, I would not have waited that long. The gluten free pizza has to be done properly, if it's gluten free that does not mean it's gonna have less topping. I extremely apologize what happen that day. To make it up here is 50.00$ gift you can use towards whatever you like on the menu. I would kindly ask you to give us another chance!

It's been quite a while since I was last at Brio, and not a lot has changed since the last time. Brio's always had a nice location at the corner of the Plaza Frontenac parking lot overlooking Manchester Road, with a large outdoor patio for diners. The other week, the weather turned nice enough that we decided to try dining outside for a change and Brio sounded good.
