What I always forget about Brio is that even at lunch time nothing is under $10 on the menu. At least they've started adding some healthier options to the menu in addition to the pastas, flatbreads, soups and entrees. And although the menu seems large, it's actually a bit sparse in options (and my mom asked for the gluten free menu and was given a list as small as the little special card - not very accommodating, in my opinion). I ended up ordering a quinoa chicken salad, my mom had the strawberry fields salad with chicken and my dad got the lobster bisque and salad. Everything was fine, but I wasn't overly impressed, especially since everything was $12 or more. It just seems expensive for what it is. Luckily, we went on a weekday, but on the weekend, trying to get in for lunch is nearly impossible without a reservation. Brio's is very popular even though it's just average as far as food goes. But I guess if you want to see and be seen in Frontenac, it's a safe bet.

We weren't really intending to have a date night but we saw the sign on our way for groceries and decided to check it out. Once we heard there were squid ink noodles we were very interested. They are really great with allergies, the chef actually came and talked to me. He says everything possible is made fresh, surprisingly even the pizza sauce, and I didn't get hives so I am currently inclined to believe it. We ended up ordering a vegetarian pizza and sat at the bar and got a drink each. The entire staff is very friendly and the ambiance is really nice! It seems to be a great date place. The bartender recommended I try a taste of Hendricks gin after I insisted I strongly disliked that type of alcohol and I was surprised to discover I liked it! The pizza was amazing (my only complaint was it was extremely soft and bendy and I usually prefer a thin and crunchy pizza crust). We are definitely going to be back!

The ambience is pleasant. Am here for a conference and found myself desperately seeking fresh air outside after my first 24 hours inside of this massive resort. Stopped at The Conservatory Cafe for a salad and gluten free treat since I cannot eat wheat, and upon returning to my room to eat my Greek Salad, I discovered that all of the lettuce had turned brown! Pretty disappointing to say the least. For a $7 salad, I'd expect that the lettuce would be relatively fresh. I did return the next morning to inform them of what happened, and they refunded my purchase. The resort is huge. Expect to trek your luggage for a very long distance to get to your room with no offer of assistance. Overall, it's a pleasant environment, but if you do have a bit of clausterphobia, be forewarned that you will need to get out of the building occasionally for fresh air. The conference food was average at best. Not many options for those with food allergies, and the coffee usually disappeared by 9 a.m.! They also had Starbucks machines which you had to use a debit/credit card in order to get any coffee once the conference co

I was at a conference nearby and was craving something other than hotel food. So I 'yelped' [can't believe that's a verb now] Cal Taco. To be honest, I had low expectations so I wasn't expecting anything stellar. There are seats inside and out. The woman who helped me was extremely nice - we had a conversation about allergies. I ordered a steak burrito with everything aside from lettuce and beans. **I know it's against the burrito religion to avoid beans but I am not a fan. They simply fill space and don't add flavor for me. I excluded lettuce because it tends to add too much moisture to the burrito, thus leaving a pool of liquid at the end of the burrito. Trust me, I've thought about these things a lot. I also got fries and a large drink. My total was around $12. The burrito itself was pretty good. The steak was decently season and the melted cheese in its core brought out the flavor. The salsa that they provide was actually decently good as well and mixed well with my meal. Being that there aren't many choices in the area, I'd recommend Cal Taco for some decent burritos.

It's just ok! Nothing to rave about! I ordered the Nom Nom Pork bowl during the week around 1p on a Thursday. The service was fast, but the food, well it's just ok. It's crammed into a small rectangular plastic to-go container and not mixed so it's hard to mix it up in that shallow bowl. The kale included the stems which were too crunchy to eat. The pork had great flavor but almost each piece was inedible to completion; it has grizzly fat that cannot be chewed. Other than this, the flavor of the dish was great so they got that right, and without taste testing :( It seems like it's run by a bunch of college-aged students. Some are friendly, but others clearly lack the desire to even smile - it's a "forced smile Id rather be doing something else" kind of feeling. The greeter closer to the door was very friendly, but the two cashiers not so much. They'd rather hang together and talk Not sure this place is going to make it. I also see no tasting of the food - it's just cooked and put together in a container. I question the gluten free items and whether they are cooked on clean surfaces in between other types of meals - same for vegetarian!

Wish the bottom of the pizza crust was not so charred. Previous comment about staff not cleaning oven seems correct, even though they were not busy around 4pm. Servers were nice. Fresh looking toppings can be generous if you ask for it, but moist toppings challenge a fully cooked crust. Enough left over to take home. Meats are at the end of the line instead of right after sauce, so plan ahead. Several of the sauces are hidden below the deck if you want alternatives. Just a note: Gluten free crust has more calories than the regular crust.

This is the spot for gluten free pizza!!! I paid $12.75 for a 12-inch gluten free white with spinach pizza and it was perfect. Truly one of the best gluten free pies I've found, and a great price! For celiacs: they cook the pizza on its own disposable tin tray and give you a disposable pizza cutter to avoid cross contamination!

I like the Remedy Cafe because they can accommodate vegetarians, vegans, gluten free, and meat eaters! Not many restaurants lay claim to this kind of consideration. However, I just feel like all their food tastes the same-- maybe I'm just not appreciative enough of East Indian dishes... Their chai tea latte is amazing though! And I love how they give you the option of soy, almond milk, or dairy milk! All in all, a nice little place! The music was a little loud though!

Warning - I actually know what I'm talking about when it comes to Thai food. This review may offend those who don't. My parents are from Laos, whose cuisine is very similar to Thai food. We have cooked, eaten and continue to eat a lot of traditional Thai cuisine. We like to eat around town at different Thai restaurants because for us it's like going to our friend's mom's house for dinner. There is a lot of hype about the Smiling Elephant and we had an afternoon to kill so we made our trek across town to check it out. The area is an up-and-coming part of Nashville close to downtown. Trendy little shops, restaurants, and condos are popping up all over this part of town. The restaurant was small and quaint, very homely and comfortable. The employees greeted us with warm smiles as soon as we stepped in, and made sure service was exceptional throughout our lunch. Thumbs up. We ordered the fresh rolls, tofu Pad Thai with green bean noodles, and Pad Kra Pao. The fresh rolls were fresh, but we prefer ours with either shrimp or pork or both like a lot of other places give you - especially for that price. The Pad Thai was interesting. The menu says it's not like the "Americanized" Pad Thai you get at other restaurants, but maybe it should be. People read that from the menu and put it in their review like they actually know the difference between traditional and Americanized Thai food. Some might have an idea, but most - no. The low-carb green bean noodles were actually pretty good, but the dish as a whole was not satisfactory - again, especially for the price. Our other lunch entree was the Pad Kra Pao with jumbo lump crab, served with a fried egg and white Jasmine rice. Meh. This restaurant has been voted in the Nashville Scene as Best Thai, but the only ones who vote on these surveys are the same group of people every year who live in their bubble they perceive as Nashville. There is so much more to Nashville than what the Nashville Scene chooses to display. Best Thai in Nashville? Far from it. Location - Good. Service - Great. Parking - Good. Quality - Great. Food - Fair. Authenticity - Questionable. Pricing - Fair. So our overall first impression of the Smiling Elephant is this: Although the owners may be Thai or Lao, they cater to the area and its market. Their menu says "not Americanized" but to us it is just that. They have altered some of their items to meet the needs of a gluten-free or low-carb diets. This may be good for people on those diets, but not for people who want a simple, authentic meal. Don't get me wrong - the food was not horrible, it just wasn't what we expected. I will say it again - the food is way overpriced. Maybe we should give it another chance and try more of their menu items, but I highly doubt that will happen anytime soon.

No doubt food is good....But, client service is poor! Too many rules that makes it hard to enjoy group dinning! For example: no reservations, no separate checks for groups, and not allowed to serve cake brought in for birthday party! In addition, there are very few gluten free options!! And No complementary exchange for bread for GF customers ( their yuca fries would do)! Server was nice, but restaurant has too many rules that only benefit the restaurant owners, not the customer!

Living close to here and loving sweets, I tried it out right away. Definitely a great selection of donuts. The coffee is alright. Be careful if you have an allergy- a plain donut I had was cross contaminated somehow and I had a pretty bad allergic reaction to whatever nuts it was by. Cool atmosphere when it's not a Saturday morning & stupidly busy. (Go to cherry coffee inside of Steins deli for your coffee- you'll thank me)

On 2/20/16, I encountered this place that my friends raved about. Once we were seated the waitress brought water to the table OMG the PLASTIC cup was cloudy, Grease was floating on top of my water made me want to VOMIT. I asked for a to go cup of water she said those cups are not allowed on The tables in the dining room but she did give me a straw to drink my GREASY CLOUDY WATER. I have no idea how the food taste. All 8 of us left went around the corner to Jerry Bobs, the food was great got my water with my meal in a to go cup. Everyone does not drink from plastic ware. For me the impression I got from Brawleys made me VOMIT

Love, Love, Love. It was one sunny day after I'd been sick for a couple days prior. I was desperately searching for a drink that could soothe my sore/swollen throat. Then I saw the signs for Tbar. I had passed by Tbar so many times but had never given a chance. Why? Because I figured it would be just like Starbucks...and I really am not a fan of Starbucks. However, since I was running out of time/options on that day when I had nasty throat situation going on... I walked right into the Tbar. Boy was I ever so wrong to make assumptions about this wonderful place. The barista(or...teamaker?!) was so nice and she fixed me sweet ginger tea with honey and lemon that wasn't scorching hot so I can actually drink it pronto. I couldn't sit and enjoy as I had to go to work but that tea was SO delish until the very last drop. Since I was so impressed by the first visit, I decided to visit once again a week later (which was yesterday). This time, I got the black milk bubble tea(blended style) with soy milk. YUM YUM it was sooooo lovely and perfect for a miserable hot day in the city. Once again, the girl who made it for me was such a sweetheart and was very helpful. I actually sat on one of the comfy couches and enjoyed the bubbletea. The whole experience was so awesome. I am totally hooked to this place. Will definitely go back.. perhaps today? p.s. 1 star is off because though everything was wonderful, the price was the only thing that reminded me of Starbucks(which once again, I despise). BUT I'd totally skip a meal and have a cup of tea instead. I could stand to lose a few pounds anyway. xoxo

Pretty bad gluten-free pizza. But OK, that's not so easy. Ordered 2 pizzas. They got one pizza wrong. When i called to talk to the owner, he said no problem, he would have a new pizza delivered to my door in 15 minutes. Sounded great but when the delivery person got to my house, he wanted to charge me! Said that's what the owner wanted. They screwed up. And they're charging me for a third pizza? I don't think so! Will never go back and will tell my friends to boot.

I went there last night and it was amazing. Our waiter Mike was great. The wine was great and we set outside in July and it was hot but they had enough fans so that it was comfortable. We sat by this brick oven and we saw them making the pizza and it looked amazing. I can't wait to go back and actually order some of it. Their chocolate cake was amazingly sweet but just make sure to read the fine print. I don't think it said that there were almonds....and there'll were almonds in the cake and I'm allergic to almonds..but thankfully no allergic reaction.

Batch......yeeeeeuuuckkkk! Have been there twice. First time I had the paleo pumpkin/ coconut cupcake. It was moist, I will give them that. The taste was weird and unnatural . It left a horrible after taste. I went late in that day, so I figured maybe I'd go in the morning to see if it might be better. First thing that almost knocks me to the floor is a funky smell in the place. What is that smell? I chose a chocolate paleo cupcake. It was extremely dry and literally crumbled whilst trying to eat it. The real topper was the long black human hair that was the focal point in the gluten free case. Disgusting! And $3? Really? I'm certain that I was paying for the box, not the cupcake. Over all a rotten experience. I am amazed that anyone would post a positive review on this place. Sad for a local owned business.

Not a buffet person to begin with, but this place is really bad. Ambience: 0 noisy. Kids running back and forth to the chocolate fountain unsupervised. One kid stuck his hands in it. Ugh. I told the guy cutting the pies and he just shrugged. Cleanliness: 2..and that was for my server who had thoroughly cleaned our table and kept it bussed. Carpet was gross and I never dared to use the bathroom. Food: 2. The salad bar was pretty good and appeared fresh. The fried shrimp was all breading and the steak, although 'cooked to order,' was shoe leather (ordered medium rare). Service: 3 our server was very good and attentive which is why I'm giving a 3. The grill person was rude and the dessert guy ignored the contaminated chocolate. Value: 1. Over priced, even with the addition of seafood (it wasn't good). I basically paid for salad - nothing else was edible. If you are not particular about what you eat and want to gorge on plate after plate, then this place is for you. If you prefer a more pleasant dining experience, go elsewhere. And if you like buffets, hit Sweet Tomatoes in Palm Harbor

*Celiac friendly* Very good gluten free crust! ($2 extra though ) They will change gloves and make the pizza "off-line" meaning they will gather the ingredients from original containers to avoid cross contamination. Always very nice staff behind the pizza bar as well

Do not stay at this resort if you have allergies to dust, dirt or mold. The spa facilities are extremely dated and in need of a serious overhaul. I suffered a burn in their whirlpool. My bedsheets were only changed twice in six days (I know because I have a frequent traveler trick that I use) and the conference room that I spent a day in had no running water in the washroom just a bottle of hand soap. The decor is more modern in my 90-year old mother's nursing facility but she doesn't care as she is blind. Maybe she would enjoy a vacation there. I doubt it because she still has some taste. Absolutely deplorable. And, if you are thinking of attending the smoking cessation program, forget about it; save your money, buy the patches and go to a luxury hotel instead!

I met my love at Oakleys in our quest to try more new restaurants to find more options for gluten free goodness. Oakleys was listed as being gluten friendly, so we decided to meet one day for lunch. Upon arrival, the place was clean and contemporary and not too busy. I asked the waiter if there was a gf menu and he said no. I asked if there were manu gf options and he said not really and left me standing at the door with a menu. I had to wait a few minutes for my love to arrive to decide where to go and a manager came over to me. I asked if there was ANYTHING i could have and she said that most items were gluten free, including the soups. I was skeptical since the waiter had told me there was nothing, but we decided to stay. We sat at a nice table and sat...and sat...and sat. Turned out the waiter who said that there wasn't anything there for me was our waiter. We eventually got a drink and were thinking about leaving when the manager came over and took our order. I got a soup and salad and both were very tasty. It was a little pricey, but it was nice to be able to have a fancy soup. I had a mild reaction to something, but it wasn't severe and i don't know for certain it was oakley's. I won't go back though. Between not feeling safe to not feeling welcome, well, no.

I would have given it a 2.5 but did not like it enough to give it a 3. Don't get me wrong, we had a fairly serviceable meal here. But only because we ordered something that is not on the menu...and we really only enjoyed part of that. We stopped in on a Saturday after being wallet molested at the nursery behind it. It's a simple layout with plastic covered tables set up in really odd directions. The staff seem nice enough and our waitress was quick to bring us a menu. There is where my first problem was. The menu was disgusting and the prices were the same as French Quarter prices. Clean yo menus! We looked and looked and finally decided to risk just doing a couple of appetizers. As we waited for our waitress to come back, we saw someone get the apps we were going to order. Both guys tried them and both guys made gross-out faces. One mentioned that it was 7.50 for something the size and flavor of a freezer section taquito. So we needed to find something else to order. As we waited some more, the waitress brought a giant platter of boiled seafood to the table in front of us. I saw crab legs! We asked the waitress about that. It's not on the menu but it was about 40 bucks. We ordered one to share. This platter came with 3lbs of crawfish, a cluster of snowcrab legs, a cluster of dungeness crab and a pound of shrimp. We dug into the crab. Both sets of legs were tasty and the butter dipping sauce was spot on. Once we demolished those we moved onto the crawfish and shrimp. That's where things went back down hill. She shrimp were over-cooked and tough to peel. Not much flavor to them. The crawfish were some of the most bland, boring crawfish I'd ever eaten. Just horrible. I asked the waitress about this and she said they had a lot of older folks in who didn't like the spice. Ok..But why NO flavor at all? I swear they tasted like they had been boiled in unsalted water. Needless to say, we didn't get to finish the platter but the crab-legs were delicious. I just wish they knew how to boil the other seafood. It ended up costing us 50 bucks for 2 sets of crab legs, 4 shrimp and 3 crawfish, before tip. Not a great bargain, really. I would recommend this place to people with spice allergies and extreme crab leg lovers.

The restaurant upon entering has a strong stench of mold. Similar to what I have experienced in locations down at the shore after the effects of Sandy. The food was fair and so the service. Their strong suit is items ordered off the Mediterranean menu. But if you have allergies toward mold there are plenty of locations in the area.

I've been wanting to try Egg and I for sometime now. When I was meeting friends in Carmel I suggested Egg and I since it was only 10 minutes from their home. The restaurant was easy to find and location would not deter me from returning. The restaurant can handle a large number of customers with fairly comfortable booths in the dining area. There is a large meeting room in the back of the restaurant perfect for business meetings or large family gatherings. A gorgeous, shaded patio is available weather permitting. When I arrived, I joked I hope we could get a seat, especially since my friends were already seated. We were one of only 3 booths in this very large restaurant at 9:30 am. I guess everyone was working. My friends ordered the 2 eggs, meat (sausage) and toast and was very satisfied. My other friend ordered the Make Your Own Omelette due to food allergies and it came out perfect and was filling and tasty. Because I was visting with my friends and not focusing on the menu, I was off my game. I usually would have ask the server if the Corn Beef Hash was made from scratch in-house but I didn't seeing they add in their own potatoes. Well, it was exactly what I strive to avoid at all cost. Obviously canned corn beef hash, mushy texture, nasty smelling and what I detest. I always joke it taste just like cat food smells. Yolk has spoiled me which I appreciate more and more everyday. Again, not the businesses fault since I know I Hate Canned Corn Beef hash. Apparently it sells or they'd remove from the menu but for those like me, just know what your getting. Service was fine, she handled the basics well but void of personality or offering a friendly, welcoming smile. I will be back to try a few of the omlettes that sounded delicious. My friends enjoyed breakfast and would return with me but they really wanted to go to First Watch.

Just visited here on Thursday and was so excited to try it out. The waitress acted as if she didn't know what she was doing and even mixed up our drinks. My mom didn't get her salad. The onion rings still had not come, so she told them to please cancel the order; they brought them anyway! My nachos were disgusting. The meat looked weird and the tortillas that they used had a horrible taste. After starting her salad, my sister could not finish and almost vomited. I've been to Cheddars in other cities and was totally delighted. If this is what this restaurant will be, you need to go ahead and close now.

Good food all organic and stuff for gluten free vegan hipsters but smaller portions and about 4 dollars more per dish than other places and expect to order extra rice if you get a curry dish. They have a limited simple menu which is smart for white ppl but as a thai person the dishes lack full flavor.

Not good! Normally not the type of guy to complain but dinner was simply not a pleasurable experience. My girlfriend ordered gluten free pasta that came hard so we sent it back expecting a fresh cooked dish to come back and it comes back microwaved... I ordered the veal parm and while not terrible it could have been much better. Way too much sauce and the serving sizes were TINY. I expected so much more for $20 a plate. Sadly will not come back

I forgive you for your bad service and occasionally bad food. I forgive you, manager, who made a rude jest regarding my gluten intolerance you have no idea about. Your life must be really awful to go out of your way to attempt to humiliate a guest. Luckily I eat humble pie every day without your assistance. Thanks for letting me know your cheese is not gluten free. I won't be partaking of that any longer along with your nasty attitude. Hopefully you find peace and a new outlet for your hateful regard other than your patrons. Unfortunately your actions have cost your employer my business.

I am a complete Trader Joes fan. In fact I used to live in Chicago, where we had 2 or 3 within an hr drive. Spoiled, I know. Now I need to drive an hr and a half. And I did. And I still love TJs. They are unbeatable for gluten free stuff, frozen stuff, everything. and their soy ice cream is the Yum. However. If you want something specific, and you call first to make sure they have it, get the name of the person that you talked to that assured you it would be there, just in case it isn't there. We did not get a name, and had to leave without our Case Of Chocolate Soymilk. I hope to revise this up to a normal 4 or 5 stars, as they are my fave, on the next visit.

The website said "open 7am to 3pm everyday" so silly me, I believed it. On Sunday morning my mom and I decided to get an early start to the day and left our hotel at 7:00am. Our walk through the French Quarters consisted of: 1) watching the vomit from the night before being cleaned off the street with high powered hoses 2) having my behind grabbed rather forcefully by a very drunk man outside of a bar who proclaimed "juicy." After this, I wasn't really ready to stomach much of anything when I arrived at Cafe Fleur De Lis. Then I realized it didn't open till 8am on Sundays...Luckily the wonderful lady behind the counter let us in early after seeing how pathetic we looked staring in the window. She told us that if we weren't in a rush, we could wait. So we did. By 8am the place was crowded and we were enjoying some coffee and some amazing pancakes. We also split what had to be the unhealthiest (but quite delicious) breakfast ever. It consisted of a large plate of hash browns covered in bacon, sausage, sausage gravy and cheese. I figured if I could stomach that I could brave the walk back down Bourbon Street. Cafe Fleur De Lis is definitely a great breakfast spot, whether you are hung over or not. And if you are extra lucky, you might get some unsolicited action on the way there.

Do you long for poor quality drinks served in plastic cups all the while the smell of vomit and urine assault you? Then you'll love the quarter! If you want great wine, thoughtfully handcrafted cocktails, great food, live music, and amazing service, then consider coming here instead.

We typically go to Macaroni Grill to celebrate special occasions, due to my moms terminal illness, we have not had opportunity in over a year to dine out together but decided to go for my daughters 24th birthday - so on 4-2-12 we picked Macaroni Grill as it had always been good in the past. This turned out to a huge disappointment on several levels - We went for lunch the restaurant was basically empty at 1:45 when we arrived - the service was terrible - We were presented with the dinner menu and when we asked for the lunch menu were told this was all there was... Once the order was placed, the waiter parked himself by the cooking line & never came back, so we had to ask the bus boy for the Focaccia bread. The waiter then brought everything directly after the bread arrived, therefore we didn't have time to enjoy the bread, which we normally devour as soon as it is put in front of us. Then had to again wait for someone to come back so we could ask for balsamic vinegar to add to the dipping olive oil. My mom ordered: Calamari Fritti crisp-fried, pepperoncini, arrabbiata 10 & house salad The birthday girl ordered: Bellini Cipriani - la marca prosecco, white peach purée 7 and we shared Italian for Two @ $25.00 Tappas - Zucchini Fritti Eggplant Quadratini roasted eggplant, basil, tomato, ricotta salata, red chile 13.5 Chicken Milanese (add $3.00) arugula Parmesan salad, roasted potatoes, lemon butter ok the - Bellini in a tulip glass - lovely but $7.00?? The Calamari was a disappointment - pale & - not crispy as advertised- the house salad was good. Zucchini Fritti - my daughter & I each ordered one, which for a change was a mistake because one would have been enough for 3, it was good but... not as good as it looked on the menu or I had hoped - the " ribbons" were not long ribbons instead they were small pieces and a little greasy - should have ordered only one of these and a different 2nd tappas... The Chicken Milanese was pounded so thin that it was dried out & had no flavor - the coating was thicker than the chicken& the sauce over top was almost non existent - the arugula salad had absolutely no taste what so ever, the potatoes were plentiful, cooked correctly & had loads of roasted garlic which I did love - The eggplant quadratini was good going down, not so much later that evening when my daughter became ill and eventually threw up after being miserable for several hours ... therefore she never touched the leftovers... The ambiance we had always loved in the dining room was gone - the music was no longer classic Italian music, the beautiful white gladiolas were gone and the happy birthday song which the waiters sing in Italian never even happened - The hostess never looked up from the stand to say goodbye - Total for lunch for 3 guests including tip almost $70.00 I don't think we will be using Macaroni Grill for our special occasions anymore...

I really enjoy their food which is definitely a lot more flavorful compared to your regular Chinese restaurant. On the other hand, from my experience, the staff is extremely unknowledgeable about the dishes they serve and what's in them. People with any allergies should be cautious. The service is very slow as well.

We went there today and I was excited to try a new place. We will never return to this location for a few reasons. Keep in mind it was the same employee every time but we are too skeeved out to ever go back. 1) The employee didn't know the menu and when I asked about a topping instead of finding out the answer he lied about it. Had it been an allergen I was asking about the outcome could have been tragic. 2) He was rude and not friendly at all. He acted as if we were bothering him. 3) All the tables were dirty and sticky. 4) We watched the same employee clean the bathroom then without washing his hands (I had my eyes on him the whole time) went to the front counter and brought us our food. Gross!!! 5) While the manager was refunding our money I saw the bucket filled with cleaner and water that they use to wipe the tables down with and it had stuff floating in it and filmy layer that was thick and gross looking. I would avoid this location because it is a public health nightmare! The manager did give us coupons which I will use but I'll be visiting the Centerton Rd. location in Moorestown.

I'm taking J.B. Dawson's up a star and 1/2, for a few good reasons. First of all they make an awesome lemon drop or dirty martini and they are huge and powerful, yes and only $7.00, but do plan on hitting the sack after you've had one of these babies. J.B. Dawson's mailed us a $15.00 gift card for no good reason, to be used when you spent $25.00 or more in food, so hey, why not? I'm glad we did, even though we spent a good $80.00, we were really quite pleased. The baked potato soup was awesome this time, creamy and loaded with crispy bacon and cheddar cheese and I had seen the lump crab cakes scattered all over the menu and after inquiring and Shannon telling us they were pretty well pure lump and backfin, I opted to do the four mini crab cakes appetizer. They had a bit more filler in than I like, but they were still loaded with crab meat, peppers and spices, very good indeed and the bonus was a dill sauce served on the side which really complimented them. These were not little balls either they were larger than I had anticipated. We also ordered the cajun shrimp appetizer because I am an appetizer whore and it was enough to be a meal with eight large shrimp, cajun coated and grilled and served on top of two thick slices of grilled garlic bread with a side garlic butter dipping sauce, something you could make at home easily, but it was still very good and gave me a new idea for a quick fix. For my entree, yes, I have to have it all, I ordered the jumbo lump crab linguine alfredo! Hello, loaded with lump crab meat and the portion was huge, the linguine was cooked to perfection and the sauce was delightful, it's been a long time since I've had alfredo and it was a nice change of pace. Listen to what hubby had! Monday's only, all you can eat baby back ribs with a salad of your choice and unlimited house or premium sides, $24.95! He choose the caesar and they do have anchovy filet's and extra shaved parmesan cheese, he added red onion and I ate half of it, shhh, no sharing is allowed on the all you can eat deals and no take home bags, even though we did... We had a very long and tiring weekend with a wedding and a birthday party and we were both hungry, yet exhausted, so he did not even finish one rack and I had scarfed two of those bones. The ribs were outstanding, seriously perfectly seasoned, the sauce was very tasty, the ribs were beyond tender and meaty! He could have had twelve or more different sides be he only asked for the cole slaw, which was fresh and a large portion, garlic mashed for me and their fries rock, delightful little shoestrings of potato fried to a golden brown. We ended up taking most of the food home and have another good meal out of it, I would not hesitate after this last experience to pay J.B. Dawson's another visit, especially with all of the new restaurants opening up and so many others closing down and what constitutes a chain to the other reviewers? There are four J.B. Dawson's well scattered, it's not like they are a factory or something and the food and service is good and their martinis kick butt!. Oh and hey gluten free friends, they have an extensive menu just for you, including pastas!

Never eat at Sofra on Friday the 13th! (and certainly don't send anything back to the chef!) Normally a devout and 3-4X a year Sofra fan, I've always ordered the Sultan's Sofrasi, as mentioned in other reviews: a 4 course platter of appetizers, main course of meats and the almighty baklava finish. When eating the lamb portion of our dinner, the lamb was raw of both pieces of meat. Normally, I enjoy a medium or well done cutlet (and the chef/owner ALWAYS cooks it in this fashion without special request to the amazing and professional wait staff). Considering the potential for bacteria and food poison, my bff and I request that the meat be cooked thoroughly. It's returned in only slightly better condition. This game of ping pong is done 3 more times over 2 different selections of lamb (the owner refuses to swap out for other kind of meat such as hamburger patties, chicken or beef that is also served with the dish), before I'm vehemently told that "this is the way that it is always prepared" and that "You're stupid for not telling the wait staff how you want it done". Upon consultation with our two servers, this is apparently typical behaviour for the owner whenever food is deemed unsafe or undesirable by patrons. The owner smugly repeats his aforementionned comments when I pay for my meal with one of our servers for the evening. After 4 years of dining at Sofra, I think it's time to find a new Turkish place.

This hotel is too aesthetically pleasing to be located on a the corner of a street that smells of vomit, bad hot dogs, and people the size of polar bears in midriffs, unless, of course, you're into that. The hotel itself was clean, and well maintained. The pool area was adorable, but the actual pool was questionable. It needed a good scrub down, for sure. Also, if you're a pillow snob like I am, you're going to want to request extra pillows. They're mediocre, at best. Personally, I found Bourbon Street repulsive, but other than that, I LOVED the city. If you're interested in staying on Bourbon Street for a party trip, I would definitely recommend Royal Sonesta. The staff members were professional, and friendly. If you're more interested in checking out the city for its famous Cajun/Creole cuisine, intriguing history, and unique culture, I would suggest checking into accommodations elsewhere in the French Quarter.

I got over the tacky decor reminiscent of a 1980s garage sale once I took a bite of my delicious omelette and home fried potatoes. The egg to cheddar to spinach ratio was the perfect balance most restaurant-made omelettes lack. My side of ranch was so delicious and enhanced my potatoes. Our large party was handled well by waitstaff and only a couple plates were missed or mixed up. Service was relatively fast. Everyone seemed to enjoy their breakfast, which was served until 11:30 am. I would give four stars if they offered anything gluten free besides the eggs and potatoes. Menu is limited for folks with allergies. I would stop by again during my next Indian Rocks beach vacation.

el husbando works in jersey and often returns home each night with tales of New and Exciting things he has eaten whilst toiling. pei wei was the latest and greatest star of his tales, so i thought....well, it's time for the fam to try this wonderment, no?? i've heard this is a semi-fast/diner take on asian fusion from the folks behind p.f. chang's. okay, fair enough, but i have no real field of comparison. i believe i might be one of the only people in the tri-state area who have never been there, frankly. anyhoodle! we went there, smack dab in the middle of the xmas season, just beating the dinner rush. we started off with an order of their version of the crab rangoon, simply called crab wontons. heh. hard to decipher, right? they were at the table almost as soon as we were, fresh, hot and quite lovely. they're served with a ridiculously tasty sweet chili sauce, that i kind of wanted to lick off of the plate. i'm sure they frown upon that sort of thing, though, so i refrained. el sproggo got the kids' wei lo mein, as, for him, it's a known quantity. sometimes you just don't want to push the whole TRY SOMETHING NEW agenda, and lo mein works for those times. i'd say he ate more than half of the plate, which was quite something. they seem to have large portions, which struck me as awesome. i went with the shrimp pad thai. all in all?? not too bad, actually. i haven't had pad thai since i moved to the philly area back in 2001, so it was high time i got some. while tasty enough, the pad thai wasn't as good as what i'd had regularly back home. again, HUGE portion. yum, and also...ouch. the dude got what is, apparently, his regular--the pei wei spicy. i tasted a couple of bites of it, and damn!! it is spicy, but it's that kind of spicy that creeps. they have plenty for folks are vegetarian, have gluten-free needs, and those of us who have kidlets. these all seem to be good things.... what prevents any extra stars?? i'll be frank--poor management. pei wei features an open kitchen, which is wonderful for the customer. you see that your food is fresh, you see what your chefs are up to, you see the cleanliness factor. however, when there is a rush, and the kitchen isn't performing up to snuff (or so it seemed, by who seemed to be the manager at the time), well, you end up in a pickle. we spent over half of our dinner being witness to a man in a tie yelling, top volume, at the kitchen staff. WHAT IS THIS??! WHY AREN'T YOU FINISHED?? THE CHICKEN NEEDS TO BE CRISPY!! THIS LOOKS TERRIBLE!! uh....i've worked several jobs over the years in the food industry, be it bars, restaurants, fast food, whatever. there is absolutely no need to upbraid an employee like that within earshot of the guest. we'll be back to pei wei, but most likely not that location.

you know how sometimes your reallh excited for pizza and just cant wait to get it? then you pick it up all hot, get It home, open it up and it looks amazing... it looks so good you just have to take a bite before you get the table set? then you bite into it and it tastes even better then it looks? this is not one of those pizzas. more like dominos on a good day. but now I feel like im insulting dominos. apparently they are the only gluten free pizza place. if u dont need gluten free go somewhere else.

So i had a really bad experience there the first time i ever went there a really bad bad time I still have nightmares about fish bones stuck in my throat , When you think of really bad sushi and what can happen to you if you eat bad fish. oooohhhhwwwww was not fun. So i had to meet the inlaws for dinner there the other night . Let me tell you i started crying but sucked it up and went . To cut the story short we all left ,my food was okay , father in law his food sucked , mother in law well lets say food poison . Husband well he got the honey walnut shrimp wow that was pretty good yummy let me say. But i love the words i told you so ..... HAHAHAHA ... So i thank you jazmine for your most gross out sushi . For letting me tell the woman who got a kick out of my tears , I TOLD YOU SO ... So for that i give you one star.

I have kind of a love-hate relationship with this place. It's nice to be able to buy local produce, eggs, and other product. The competitiveness of the prices fluctuates, but they aren't terrible, and can be pretty good for products on sale. They carry a lot of things that you won't find in other stores, like locally produced gluten free bread, tofu, and other items. Sometimes the local items are prohibitively expensive ($12 bread?) and sometimes they're very competitive with nonlocal items at other stores. I really like the espresso that they sell, too, and the cheese selection is great and the prices are totally reasonable for the quality. However, the selection of many other items isn't good, even for specialty-ish products. You will find a much larger selection of dairy-free milks at Acme, for example. I think the only greek yogurt they sell is Fage, and it's much pricier than you'll find elsewhere. The prices also fluctuate more than is typical for chain stores (not sales, but the regular prices of eggs and produce and such). But those are issues that I'm going to guess are pretty typical for coops, and worth dealing with for access to the local produce and cheese. My main issue is, it is a MISERABLE shopping experience. I was skeptical of the reviews about the crowds and rude customers, thinking many of the reviewers are just used to shopping in roomy suburban locations. I don't know if I've ever seen a review for a smaller store in the city without complaints about narrow aisles and crowds and rushed, rude patrons, and usually I find that these stores are perfectly pleasant in reality. But in this case, the reviews are spot-on. The layout is such that you cannot stand still at any location in the store without blocking the circulation of the store. Even when the store is nearly empty, I feel rushed, because I am always in someone's way, just by virtue of the store layout. People will literally drive their shopping carts into you and look at you expectantly, as though fully expecting you to just go limp and allow yourself to be shoved out of the way. I would recommend you not even bother trying to shop here your first few times if you can't shop well outside peak hours (before 3:30 PM), because you can't just stand there and look over the shelf trying to find the items that you need or easily move amongst the shelves. If you do have to shop during peak hours, I would recommend that you just accept that you are going to be in everyone's way and everyone is going to be in yours, dispense with any rules of politesse, and try to get your items and get out of there as quickly as possible. This store does have a larger selection of some things than the Chestnut Hill one, especially the value-oriented items, like the bulk bins and some types of conventional produce. (I could not find non-organic berries at CH, for example.) But for more basic things that are in stock at both stores, I would highly recommend Chestnut Hill over this location. It's compact too, but the layout doesn't leave people trying to bulldoze each other out of the way of the kale.

I was really looking forward to eating here, but unfortunately the food was so bad I will never be going back. My thoughts: Pros: * Very friendly girl working. * Place was nice inside. Cons: * I got their daily special...not sure the name but it was thick slabs of dry cheap tasting chicken on gluten free bread with what tasted like hot sauce. The bread was crumbly in texture, very dry, and not very good at all. The slabs of chicken should have been cut up smaller. I couldn't eat more than 2 bites of this sandwich...and I'm not that picky. * The broccoli soup was watered down badly and completely flavorless. Why not make it creamy? How about some flavor, even a bit of salt and pepper or cheese? I understand that there may be culinary limitations when cooking gluten free, but the food needs to be good, right? Especially for $14 a meal. I wasn't a fan of the food here, though I suppose it's "A Matter Of Taste".

I usually go to the 30th and Market location, but I have been to the University City location as well. 30th and Market usually gives me a larger portion but I got a generous sample of fried fish (really tasty!) at the University City location, so each location has won me over in their own way. I am a huge fan of jerk chicken, and this place comes pretty close to Negril. In a small platter, you get three large chicken drumsticks, cooked until it's falling off the bone. I don't mind that it's not grilled fresh, because the chicken sits in a hot dish of delicious peppery and spicy jerk gravy, so the flavors really penetrate the meat. If you choose rice and beans as one of the two sides in a platter, they'll ladle some extra gravy over the rice and beans. When you reheat the leftovers, the rice and beans will have soaked up that sauce, making it even better than the first time. I also love the collard greens at these trucks, which they drain after piling into the styrofoam container. This prevents the juices from contaminating the other foods, especially if you choose to get other distinct sides like sweet potato. I get the mac and cheese if I'm in the mood for a pick me up, because Gigi and Big R's mac has that thick, starchy, sticks together, made in a huge batch quality, that is so (wonderfully) different from the box variety. Freshness is not my top priority when eating comfort food. As other posters mentioned, the portions are big enough for 2 meals. At University City, a large platter ($9) more than does the trick, at the 30th and Market location, the small ($7) is sufficient. I can't imagine having a better home-cooked meal for less than $5. It's a Philly staple I will definitely miss.

This food is phenomenal, the cook was awesome, and the waitress was nice, but I have to knock off stars. Let me explain. I am a vegetarian. My waitress knew I was a vegetarian. My waitress then served me a chicken based soup and did not tell me. I tried it. I nearly vomited. When I asked if there was chicken in it, she very casually said yes. She did not seem concerned that she'd just served a vegetarian a meat product. Friends at my table mentioned that they do have a vegetarian soup, but she never offered it to me. Disappointing... however, the cooks are good enough to prepare the vegetable hibachi meals on the grill top before the meat goes on it, so someone there gets it. If you're a vegetarian, please be aware- even if you tell them you are, you will still need to ask for meat free dishes. Do not assume that they will warn you.

So I just started coming here a couple months ago because it was quite close to my house and I noticed they had a gluten free menu. Every time I have gone there I enjoy there gluten free menu so much. The fact that they have gluten free buns available is awesome because not many places have them for you. I got the pulled pork sandwich and that was to die for. I have never had a problem with there food it has always come out how I wanted it. As for why I only gave this place an okay is because almost everytime I have been there I have had the slowest service. I mean given I come in most of the time when it isn't that busy but you would think that if it's slow you would get better service instead it takes 5 -10 mins to get the bartenders attention to grab a drink and then when you do, they give you a drink menu and disappear again for 10 minutes. It's quite annoying because they have maybe two others customers at the bar and I just can't understand why it takes the bartenders so long to get my drink. I will never go there at night though because I've had to wait almost 15 20 minutes for a drink when the bartenders walked and stood right in front of us and didn't see my friend and I sitting there with no drink or menu in front of us, but instead they kept walking... I will keep coming back because of the food but I hope the service can improve.

I'm a pretty big fan of this place! Whenever I'm looking for any vegan alternatives, I always head straight to this store. I love the selection of gluten free options and I feel like anyone with diet restrictions could find whatever they needed at this store. A bit pricey, but none the less a great place. I love their raw carbo squares too, YUM!

We received our second holiday gift from a corporate partner who sends out pies from Sugar Pie in 2014; the prior year we received the apple pie. We were thrilled to receive it as the prior year's apple pie was fantastic. We saved the pie for Christmas Eve when we had family and friends over. We opened the container after our guests arrived and much to our surprise, the "sugar cream pie" looked awful. (One comment was that it looked liked vomit.) No takers and the pie went in the trash. I emailed the owner to let her know and sent her photos of the pie. She responded with many questions (including an agreement that the pie did not look edible in the photos) but after I followed up, I never heard from her again. We had considered using this for our client holiday gifts in 2014 and after the total lack of care for a substandard product, I am so glad that we did not use them. The only reason that this is not a one star review (which the customer service merits) is because the prior year's apple pie was truly delicious.

Not bad for a dive bar, but I don't think I'll be back. The food we had was good, but the menu is limited if you want to consume anything healthy. This is all carbs and fat in monster portions -- good luck even getting a salad that isn't the maximum number of calories possible to dump on lettuce. If you're gluten-free or vegetarian, you can't eat here. All that said, my souvlaki was delicious and everyone at my table enjoyed their plates as well. Service was kind of short and curt with us, even though we had made a reservation and warned them we'd be a big group. The restaurant wasn't busy when we were there, so there was no reason to rush us through our orders. Regardless, decent food. If you want a steak sandwich & fries, definitely come here, but if you want anything else, stay away.
The lamb and rice were delicious and the fries were fabulous. Delicious gluten free pita bread. But the tatkoutki and the roasted eggplant need work. I will be back to try other dishes.

Stopped in for dinner after a matinee theater show at the Walnut Street Theater. I liked the decor of the place and it makes you feel like you stepped back in time a bit, but the meal itself was just Ok for us. My wife is gluten free and it was a bit hard to find stuff on the menu that she could eat. We started with nachos for an appetizer. I thought they were pretty good, but she was just OK with it. Her $10 margarita wasn't very strong. Lots of toppings on each chip which I liked! For her entree, she went a chicken sandwich minus the bread and a side salad while I went with the meatloaf. The meals were OK but nothing special. You certainly got plenty of it and I didn't hungry by any means. Not many GF choices for her, so she had to go with the mixed berry sorbet while I went with the Banana Cream Pie. The pie was delicious. All in all, an OK meal, but she doesn't want to go back.

Biggest mistake this morning... awful food. Eggs Benedict came with some nasty brown sauce that looked like leftover chicken gravy. I had to send them back, and had the urge to flee the place but my son was eating before I got a chance to say anything... they took the eggs back, and I got a dried out Western (Denver?) omelet, with stringy onions (NOT CHOPPED, tasted like the were probably sliced yesterday from their salad bar!?!?) and burnt tater tots that they re-dipped into grease to reheat them from my previous plate. Tater tots for home fries - seriously? At least serve Ore Ida... Nasty!! Bacon was over-cooked and very greasy. My toast was limp. My son's pancakes just went right through him... time to leave and never come back. We'll be lucky if we last the day without stomach issues... I had to laugh as the server said to another couple "sorry your omelette has cheese in it, but consider it a bonus.' Not real smart if the woman didn't want cheese, and could've been lactose intolerant??? I had a funny feeling when I saw an empty parking lot... $25 for our breakfast and we couldn't eat it! But I will have to say I told the server, and she took the tater tots off, and gave us a 10% discount and offer me a piece of pie. I declined the pie as I couldn't bear to think I would eat another piece of food from there. Over 30 years of being in business, I can't understand how this establishment has declined so badly! Safe to say, You won't see us again!

I've been to the Loews on multiple occasions. I've had a wonderful time each time i've gone there. The most recent time I went there I brought my two springer spaniel pups. I was so excited that Loews allows pets. Most of the other pet friendly hotels in philly are not nice. They had no restrictions on the weight or breed of dog so that was nice. Upon arrival they greeted us and handed us two bags (one for each dog). Each bag contained two metal dog dishes, a mat for under the dog bowls, biscuits, a loews chain for their collars, and poop bags. My one dog threw up in the lobby and a hotel employee came right away and cleaned it up for us. Every time a hotel employee saw my dogs they enthusiastically greeted them and pet them. One of the men who worked there sincerely said, "Make sure you bring the dogs back, we love having them!" Their motto is Loews Loves Pets and they truly do! The only downside is that it was a bit of a walk to take them somewhere with grass to go do their business. I live in the country so i'm not used to that. There is a nice dog park called Seger Dog Park somewhat close by that I took the girls to one day and they loved it. Loews is a pretty nice contemporary hotel. Some of the furniture has little nicks in it but overall it is very nice. The hotel seems very clean which is the most important thing to me. One night the room service girl came to the room to deliver a dessert that a family member ordered for us. She saw that my girlfriend was sick in bed and sincerely asked if she was okay. My girlfriend responded that she was not feeling well. The girl offered her tea and I declined saying that I could make it on the in room Keurig machine (because I didn't want go spend 10 bucks on tea). The girl insisted that she get my girlfriend tea and left. She returned with a tray full of get well goodies. She brought chicken noodle soup, a big bottle of water, tea, lemons, cream, and crackers free of charge!! You could tell that she really honestly cared about the customers at the hotel. I would highly recommend the Loews to anyone going to philly! I will definitely be staying there again and again.

No wonder WFM stock prices are down. So is their inventory. If the can't be a one stop grocery store for everything I need, who wants to go to a second store for the one, two or three items they are out of. Graham crackers?!!!!! Not one in the store. But they have many boxes of chocolate and strawberry flavored ones that are Gluten free . How frustrating. I'm done with WFM.

The frozen yogurt here tends to be on the sweeter side, but is a nice balance between creamy and stiff (so it isn't grainy, but it isn't as quick to melt as soft serve). They have some great flavors that they rotate every so often, including some great soy based flavors for those who are lactose intolerant or prefer soy. Last time I went, they had a Nutella flavor that was quite delicious. Unfortunately, they do not carry the flavor 'tart' for some reason. This is probably the only reason I will not be returning to this location. They also serve a delicious hot chocolate (comes in different flavors). It's made with frozen yogurt, so it quite thick and creamy and sweet. I would definitely recommend. The toppings bars is usually decent. Some of the fruits could be fresher, but all in all, nothing to complain about. This is a small location, so there are only a few seats inside. The parking right next to the shop is extremely small, but there is a larger parking area behind the shop, near Dewey's. Unfortunately, every time I've been there, service has been quite poor. Either the workers failed to include relevant information when answering a question, or they seemed extremely irritated at the customers or uninterested in helping us. On previous trips, a worker (possibly a manager) reacted quite rudely to a woman trying to use a gift card (they weren't taking gift cards at that moment, for technical issues), and in my last trip, the worker treated a pregnant woman before me in general disdain. All in all, I would give the frozen yogurt 4 stars, but the service 2 stats.

I was very excited when somoene told me about a Bareburger opening where the 5 Guys used to be for 2 reasons: I love burgers and I love bears. I was very disappointed to find out there were almost no bears involved of any kind and certainly not a single panda. If you made the same mistake I did, I feel your pain. It is actually "bare," and that is aptly named as the burger I had there was lacking of any redeeming qualities. Food: The burgers/sandwiches we had were just horrible, and even more so for the price. If you make such a huge deal about using bison and goats and penguins for your burger, your burger better be the shiznit. You ever had "cherry" flavored robitussin? That nonsense doesn't taste like cherries at all, son! Similarly, my bison burger looked like a burger, but that's about it. Go to your pantry, roll up a paper towel, and put it inside a brioche bun with a "green leaf," wtf-ever that means (it seriously says "green leaf" on that burger on the menu). Close your eyes and take a big bite. You will have replicated the taste and texture of the El Matador burger, and I just saved you $12.65 (minus the cost of your paper towel and green leaf). If your paper towel accidentally gets moist, however, then this comparison no longer applies as your paper towel must truly be bone dry to get a sense of what this burger was like. We also had the "Duck Duck Gouda," which was essentially a less pleasing form of a bacon and egg breakfast sandwich. To be fair, the fries and onion rings were pretty good. If you eat a full meal of fries and onion rings I could see you being happy here. Remember that these potatoes and onions were all free range potatoes and onions, mind you, and each one of them had names like "Atticus" or "Lincoln." Service: We had a friendly but busy waiter who was pretty enthusiastic about the food and the brand in general. Service was a bit slow, which makes sense as everyone there spends 5 minutes informing you their food is 100% organic, free range, antibiotic free, gluten free, hormone free, coddled livestock. After hearing the pitch, it would lead you to believe that someone is reading fairy tales to these goats at night and braiding their hair while they fingerpaint and write haikus. In summary: People who would like Bareburger: - you care very strongly about eating a meal that is free of any hormones, antibiotics, or gluten - you don't care very strongly about eating a juicy burger with any taste - you don't care that a burger and fries costs you about $20 People who would not like Bareburger: - you like your burgers to be good - you don't like getting ripped off - you went in wanting to pet a bear

I must recommend the toast with avocado, olive oil, lime juice and chili flakes. And for those of you like me they offer gluten free toast! It was so tasty and left me wanting another slice, but for $5 a slice I passed on seconds. I also had a green tea which was flavored wonderfully. The staff puts great attention into the drinks they make (my friend had a coffee) but the amount of time it took to prepare the tea and coffee left something to be desired. This isn't a stop in quick for a drink and leave kind of place. The worst part of my experience here was the a horrible noise coming from the coffee grinding machines (I think). We had to move from the cozy couch by the window (furthest from the machine) to the bar in the other room. The noise was seriously irritating and the shop could use more comfortable seating throughout.

Where to begin. I have come here a lot since it is my neighborhood bar but weekend before last changed all of that. I will not come back. I was greeted by an attractive new bartender and there was a manager standing behind her all of the evening. A few customers bought the new bartender shots. Before long things got very strange. She started pouring her own shots, consuming them alone and later was in the bathroom vomiting. I know this because I tried to go to the bathroom and after waiting and hearing her vomit went back to my seat. Then she came back out and did some more shots, gagging the whole time. Manager in tow pretty much starring at her behind all night. She started getting really confused. I asked for a shot of Patron and she took a glass and proceeded to pour sprite off the soda gun into it. Then she took my money off the bar to pay for it. When she brought my change back I informed her that she had poured me sprite, when she explained that their patron was on the gun, while I'm starring at the bottle on the shelf that I have ordered several times in the past. I was in the restaurant industry for over 20yrs. there is no such thing as Patron on the gun. Finally I asked the manager who had been watching her terrible behavior all night to please make me a shot of Patron which I had already paid for and that I just wanted to leave after that. He gave me a dirty look and poured a giant shot of "real" Patron in a shot glass that he slammed in front of me spilling part of it. I did the shot and proceeded to leave halfway to the door he had a bouncer follow me the rest of the way as if I was going to come back in or something. Weird. I wish the owner of this establishment knew more about what goes on there. I think they would be appalled. He should have at the very least sent her home via a cab, and finished out her shift. He seemed to have no concern for her well being or anyone else at the bar. It was a disgusting display. I have hundreds of industry friends which I've shared this story with not to mention my neighbors at the lofts I live in.

This place is great! The food was really yummy, our waitress was super nice + caring, and the atmosphere is fun. Make sure you ask for Bailey. I told her about my avocado allergy + she made sure there was no cross contamination in my food. She checked on us a good amount + was just a great waitress.

The employees are so nice, the atmosphere clean and relaxed, and they offer a gluten free sub role which is awesome. It's $2.50 extra and not great tasting but the ability to eat a sandwich makes it worth it. BUT my sandwich sucked!! I ordered the cuban. They gave me one slice of cheese and one slice of each meat. I know because I opened the sandwich to look. It had no flavor and overall it sucked

Went there (Tako) tonight. I'm Gluten intolerant so I called ahead to see if they had a GF menu. All she said was "they have GF soy sauce". When the waitress 'finally' came to our table (there were only a few booths with diners and 2 single diners.) I told her I was gluten intolerant and the only thing she said was "we will give you gluten free soy sauce for dipping"... when she came back I asked what was on the menu that was gluten free, answer "Sushi"... (However, I knew not all the sushi was gf.) She brings an 'unmarked bottle" of what appeared to be soy sauce, I did not use it. :-( I carefully chose 2 sushi rolls that I hoped would be ok. She didn't seem to care if we were happy or not. never asked if we needed anything. just took away dirty dishes, didn't fill empty water glasses either. It was not a very comfortable mealier me . She seemed to be the only wait person. But there weren't many diners in the restaurant. The restaurant was basically empty so she sits us right outside of a booth with 8 people who where not what you would call quite. and right under the speaker from which music was playing. Won't go back.

As an avid foodie, I consult most of the review sites for restaurants and write a lot of reviews as we travel the country. I can honestly say, and my partner agrees, i have never been as disappointed as I am today. We had the chocolate chip pancakes, which my partner gave a 3/10. We got a donut, which was also not that great (bland and overcooked) and the Hudson cake that was maybe a 6/10. My cocktail (airmail) also tasted to me like the lime juice was squeezed with a few bad limes in the batch. Although, I give credit for anything that uses fresh juice, it tasted off enough that I had to send it back. The manager offered to make another drink and squeeze it In front of me, which I appreciated but honestly, it just felt like she wanted to try to show me that I was wrong. I certainly would've offered for her to taste it, but as a manager who is getting a complaint from a customer about the quality of their food, she should think to taste it on her own. Maybe my taste buds were off, but my partner had the same opinion and we can't both be wrong. I also threw up about an hour later and my boyfriend had diarrhea so something wasn't right. Maybe they were just having an off day.

If I could give this ZERO STARS, I would. We ordered 3 orders of French Toast, and ALL of them had MOLD on the bread. It was absolutely disgusting. Now we're all sitting here feeling like we need to vomit. Don't order breakfast from here. I personally won't be ordering anything else either.

I got a 12 inch gluten free pizza with daiya cheese, free range chicken (tasted like frozen subway chicken) jalapeños, tomatoes, spinach, and basil. It was mediocre at best but that wasn't the real issue. This 12 inch thin crust pizza cost $28. We were quite hungry when we sat down and after the waitress told us pizzas take 30-45 minutes we hurried up and ordered not entirely realizing just how much this little pizza would cost. Absolutely ridiculous and not worth the money one bit. My husband got the Italian sandwich and he said it was "basic" but that is okay because the price matched the product. Not the case for my insanely expensive little pizza. Never coming back again. Ever.

I have ordered takeout from here a number of times. From the chicken parm pasta platter to a burger with fries they have a nice array of options... The food is not that memorable but I'm just grateful I didn't get food poisoning as I have had happen to me in the past with these sorts of venues. Overall I give them 4 stars for the convenience of being able to get a hoagie with fries and a slice of cheesecake all under one roof. Additionally they offer online ordering through seamless and delivery was faster than I was originally told. Combine that with the fact that they are open later than a lot of other venues in UC and all in all a win!

Wow, just wow! We have lived near Gray Brothers for 5 years and have never dined there. We have food sensitivities and eat most of our meals at home or at restaurants that we know can accommodate our gluten and MSG sensitivity. Tonight we were in the mood for something new so I called to ask if they can work with us to identify anything on their menu that we can have. The woman who answered the phone immediately told me that they are not gluten free. I was a bit surprised at the tone and abrupt reply. No one who has had food sensitivities for very long would expect a restaurant to be fully gluten free. I always call in advance before we try a new place to forego the hassle for both the restaurant staff and our family and consider it a courtesy. After giving her abrupt and somewhat abrasive answer, she did backpedal to say well maybe the whatever might be gluten free. In this day and age with so many people finding out that they are sensitive to a variety of foods it is very sad to find what I understand to be a local institution so lacking in understanding and empathy for possible customers who simply want to know if they can enjoy your food. I won't make the mistake of calling again.

I've been to Hendricks three times now so I feel prepared to give an appropriate review. Service - Twice the service we received was pretty bad and once it was fantastic. Our first experience was a quiet Monday night and the server seemed to forget that we were there. We waited over 10 minutes for a hello and a water once we were seated. The entire meal continued as such. Our second experience was with a group of 9 and we were seated at a table that was made for 8 maximum. We made accurate reservations so I felt this was unacceptable. The service during the meal was just ok. A lot of waiting...for food, refills, and bills. On the third visit, the service we received was fantastic but it was a quiet night in the restaurant and we were seated directly next to someone who was obviously a professional restaurant reviewer. I'm pretty sure the service was directly affected by our proximity to the reviewer. Food - Most of the food is just ok. We enjoyed the pork cracklin as an appetizer but the first time we went it was priced at $2 and then the second time it was priced at $5. Yikes! A $3 price hike for twelve little pieces of cracklin. You've got to be joking. The pulled pork is the best meat but I feel like the portion is a crock. Maybe 3-4 ounces of pork with 3 ribs and 2 sides for $18? Um...I'll be at Pappy's, thanks. The pulled pork is moist and has decent flavor. The ribs are not tender. I've tried them three times, both the St. Louis style and the baby back and neither has been tender. The flavor is good but when you have trouble cutting the ribs apart with a butter knife, that's not a good sign. My sister got turkey and again it had good flavor but she said it was really dry. I laughed when she kept it to give to the dog when we got home. The sides, again, are ok. The highlight is the sweet potato casserole which is more like a dessert. It's very good. The bacon braised greens are ok. The server told us the green are soaked in Dr. Pepper for a length of time before they are cooked. I picked up a sweetness but I just didn't think they were that flavorful. The corn casserole was a bit mushy and unexciting. The green beans were not great. Just boring. The potato salad is potatoes and eggs with onions and mayo. Zero spice. Cover it in pepper and it's a lot better. Gluten free - All of the meats except the sausage are gluten free. The 4 BBQ sauces on the table are gluten free. As for sides, you're limited to bacon braised greens, cole slaw, potato salad, and green beans. The first time we went, my husband was told the baked beans were gf and the second time he was told they are not. Bottom line - Mediocre food at high prices and spotty service. I've had better.

It's a shame because I really like Buffalo Wild Wings, buy on my visit last night I was disgusted by a fully feathered wing. Luckily it was at the bottom of the bowl cause I was hungry. On the flip side, it does kind of nauseate me that the wings I ate were contaminated. The manager heard and came to apologize, and just said "oh well, it's chicken anatomy". He was lucky I was there with my nephew or I would have caused a scene. Chicken anatomy? Really? How about you make sure food is edible before you serve it!

We stopped here casually on a Sunday to get some food before a movie. The appearance of the bar/restaurant to start was great- i loved the environment/decor/vibe. We sat in a corner "booth" space, which was actually just the two booth type seats that fit together- which was a super comfy spot in the bar. I would say- if me or my Fiance had been asked to sit at another table, we probably would have opted for the bar. THe bar stools looked super comfy, where as the other side tables in the bar area had these weird tiny stools that I don't think anyone would want to sit on while eating- especially if you are normal height. Anyway- Beer selection is OK- just ok though. Nothing too grand, nothing too bad- just average. Cocktail selection seems to be the same, nothing too interesting or captivating. Menu was great for brunch, and i love that they had all gluten free options noted. I got the mushroom Omelet. It was sub par. Honestly, the best thing about it was the side of sweet potato fries that came with it (which were delicious). Absolutely use the rosemary aioli as a dipping sauce- its heaven! I loved the fries, hated the omelet. My fiance got the Chicken and Sweet Potato waffle, and he loved it. He devoured it, actually! Service was ok- out waiter was generally knowledgable and nice, but insincere. I can't say that i would really come back here to eat, considering the prices don't really match the food quality- but i will probably go back for drinks after I eat dinner in the area.

I have honestly never been a fan of this place, but recently visited again with a co-worker. I do have to say that I was pleasantly surprised with my meal (lunch). My co-worker has several severe food allergies, so I always leave the restaurant choice up to her. They seem to have plenty of options to meet her restrictions, and are willing to prepare the food properly for her to enjoy. While I don't require the same restrictions I can appreciate their attention to the situation. The lunch menu was decent, and relatively new from what I heard. I ordered the Asian Grilled Salmon with fried rice and a cup of Egg Drop Soup. The salmon was absolutely delicious - I loved it. Like I said, I was pleasantly surprised at how delicious it was. The service was okay.. I felt bombarded by the numerous servers coming to the table (one brought drinks, one took the order, one brought food, another cleared the food, etc). I appreciate their work ethic, but it almost felt rushed. The food also took a while to come out, but that may be due in part to the dietary restrictions/prep of my coworkers meal. All in all it was okay. I probably won't go back (unless dining with her again) but it was a good lunch.

My friend recommended to come here. Staff was kind of rude. Menu is on chalk board with small and blurry handwriting. No paper menus offered. Guy at the Counter did not want to explain anything or tell us options knowing that it was our first experience. Neat place though, very clean. Burrito was bland at best. I had countless better burritos for a cheaper price in New York and north jersey. Two burritos and 2 bottles drinks came up to 30 dollars. Beans were not well seasoned or cooked well. Guac was okay. Whole grain rice was over cooked.The bank street burrito was better but still bland. The lime sauce made it burrito better. Ingredients still tasted fresh but not probably utilized and cooked. Straight out the bag chips that was probably gluten free and organic but very small portion of it. Honestly do not see what the hype is about. The store's staple is probably just smoothies. Wouldn't recommend the burrito but maybe their salads are better. Would maybe come back if they had better customer service.

I went with a large group (15 people)- they easily accommodated us. It is BOYB and service was polite. Only about half of the people at our table enjoyed their meal. I got the salad, Yum Nau Yang, and almost broke my tooth on several bites. I ended eating only a few bites and just going hungry. However- the prices were good! Not the best place if you're gluten free either.

Disappointing meal. Quality of food on same level as taco bell. Queso dip was like water consistency. Asked for no sour cream on burrito, waitress said ticket was right but remade burrito without it. Then added jalapeños I also did not want. Good thing I didn't have any allergies, the communication between waitstaff and cook was a joke. Staff was overly friendly, borderline cheerleader annoying. Probably do better to focus on their service and not their hair. Go next door to Greek City, they are the best!

I wanted to give this cute cafe with a lot of character and good food more stars; however, the portion sizes are seriously lacking. The basic breakfast $7 has two eggs, home fries (mostly carrots) and slightly underdone potatoes, and toast. The portion of the mostly carrots home fries is the size of your palm and one slice of bread. The options for gluten free bread and vegan options earn them another star. Adding bacon is 2.50 and I added an extra egg (I didn't want to be hungry in an hour) (1.50 for the egg but not actually an itemized bill) and had a hot ginger Lemmon honey drink (2.50) (yummy) for 2.50. My friend had the exact same thing all around an we got a 29.09 bill that was not itemized at all. I appreciate the local/organic food sourcing when possible (that doesn't mean I was served local/organic btw). But the price of the ticket, their "moderate" food portions on tiny plates mean come here but not if your actually hungry.

When it comes to fresh sushi and authentic Asian cuisine dining in the suburbs. I definitely recommend this place. Staff are very friendly and accommodating to our requests. Their special rolls are delicious! With one bite of the lobster roll, my mouth was bursting with exciting flavors. This place is very clean and that's very important when you're dealing with raw fish. We wouldn't want any cross contamination.

So before I came to this place I came on yelp to review it, and while the reviews were basically 50/50 I decided to give them a chance. First, it took us 45 minutes to finally get our appetizers. A guest in our party didn't get the correct order. She specifically asked for no tomatoes because of her allergies- she received tomatoes. When the waiter tried to bring the right order the chef still got it wrong. They brought out literally pita bread and lettuce- the meat was missing. Pissed, she wound up leaving the restaurant only to pick something up on the way home. On another note, me and my cousin ordered the jerk wings and each meal came out differently. My wings were coated in the jerk sauce while his wings were dry and the jerk sauce was in a puddle underneath them. I ordered the peach double margarita. Although it didn't taste like peach (more like grapefruit), it poured 4 glasses and had a good amount of liquor. While, on the other hand, my cousin had a single strawberry margarita and said it tasted like syrup and didn't really have any liquor at all. We had a cool waiter I guess....there were more things that went wrong, but I really don't feel like typing anymore. I'm thinking the 2 stars says it all.
