I found weeks Luke's by checking out a gluten free restaurant option google search for New Orleans. I'm so happy I decided to make reservations! The food was incredible! The staff listened to my food restriction requests and delivered with tasty food. Not just leaving off ingredients but making adjustments to the dish which enhances the flavors. It was our favorite meal of the trip

I never actually ate the food because I was so turned off after talking to the personnel. I called and spoke to two different people on the phone, 1st said yes, they make paleo pizza and only need 15-20 minutes notice. I told him it was for a party but he neglected to mention it was a dine-in only option. After seeing that detail on their online "secret" menu I called again to confirm it was dine-in only. The person I spoke to told me it doesn't travel well but that I should definitely come in to try it. So we lugged the whole family (grandparents, aunts, cousins, kids...) to go try this pizza and when we get there the guy at the counter said he doesn't really recommend it, it's just kind of a pile of stuff on mashed pepperoni and it's hard to make... then tried to push the gluten free pizza instead. Total mixed messages from 3 different people. We just left and found somewhere else to eat... Buenos Grill was delicious.

Good selection, good prices, but they don't bother to list allergens on their labels (beware coconut in the granola). When I politely called and asked them to label it (as they are required by law, coconut is a tree nut and as such is a priority allergen according to our government) I was met with confrontation and was told "it behooves you to beware of you own allergens"... a little tough to do when there is no indication on the label... I get that they just opened and I am sympathetic to that but the appropriate response by management is "sorry, we will make that change right away" not that its my own fault. *update* went again today and salads with walnuts labelled cashews, management clearly doesnt take your life threatening food allergies seriously. If you have them, just stay away

I just had a baby and this was my husband and I's first night out! We were so excited! First we get there and sat at the bar and had a drink, my old fashion was great, it took a couple of minutes to be acknowledged but overall good drink and service. When we were sat at our table, our waiter was awful. And not in the didn't fill our drinks promptly kind of way, he had a terrible personality, he talked about how crappy his life was, never made eye contact then once he knew my husband and I had both worked in the service industry he started to pay closer attention. He word vomited all over us about how he needs a new job and he has been a server for over 20/40 some-odd years. He talked about himself and had a washed up used car salesman personality and it just wasn't the service we expected, but I could have dealt with that. What was the worst part was that my husband and I both ordered the aged ribeye medium Rare with a crab cake on the side. My Ribeye was over cooked and the WORST CUT OF MEAT I've ever had. It took me what felt like 30 minutes to chew one bite. It was terrible. Manager never stopped by. My husbands was cooked rare and not as bad as mine but still did not meet our expectations. After dropping well over $100 we should have had a better experience, we should have had a better waiter and certainly a better steak. Yes I mentioned to the server that the steak was incredibly hard to chew he showed zero concern. The ambiance is nice and drinks are good, but that's the only positive thing I have to say.
Threw up after eating here. Absolutely disgusting Not good at all I was excited to try, not authentic, too much food coloring . Everything tastes fake

I don't know what all the hype is about. We sampled every beer on the property and only 4 of the 16 were drinkable -- two actually reminded me of vomit and nearly made me do the same. Didn't have the food, so I can't speak to it. Service was friendly and prompt. The only beer worth ordering was either the Porter, Red Ale, Stout, or Scottish Ale -- avoid everything else, esp. the Hefewizen and various beers made with fruit (i.e. Raspberry-whatever).

First off, there was a minor problem because I seated myself at an outdoor table instead of waiting to be seated. This could be avoided with simple signs: "Please Wait to be Seated." I stopped by here after a movie while I was killing time waiting for my car to get repaired. I ordered a bowl of wild mushroom soup and a beer, a red ale I believe. The beer was okay. Better than Budweiser but nothing fantastic. The soup was terrible. It didn't really have any flavor and was overwhelmed by the grated dry cheese they put in it. And the aftertaste was a like mild vomit. I couldn't eat it. The waiter was nice enough to offer to let me try their other soup, but I'm not a big leek fan. I got charged for the bowl. I'd like it if someone else tried a cup of the wild mushroom soup some time to see if they get that vomit aftertaste with it.

My husband ordered Hawaiian pizza with extra cheese and garlic wings for dinner, and it was good but after an hour me and my husband starting to have a stomach ache. Husband used the bathroom so many times and had told me that he couldn't go, so am i. We got a food poison bad. I cant believe that we had to experience this. I love pizza hut! The only pizza that i like since before but today this makes me feel disgusted. Never had this experience before, today looks like food is not cook properly and maybe its dirty, who knows maybe they're so busy and they drop some toppings. So DISGUSTING.... fuck pizza hut!!!! Dont waste your money on this dirty place...

this might've been one of the few times my trusted fellow yelpers have let me down: it was raining (pouring), and on a Saturday, it was near dinner time. this place came up, and it featured high reviews. ok i said, let's go! mind you, i had to hail and uber to go here as i'm visiting the area, and it was a bit of a way to walk. before i forget, first off, the service was so great. i didnt catch the name, but he was a nice chap, very patient with our party deciding what to get, which leads me to: the menu is a bit confusing -- no explanations so it's hard to discern the difference between your chicken tikka chaat (which i had) or the lahori tikka. FYI make sure to mention gluten free if need be when ordering as they were able to accommodate my party (yay!) also there's like 10000 different types of lassis, which is both good and bad as it might've been a tad too many choices. (but the PLUS IS THAT THEY HAVE VEGAN ALMOND MILK LASSIS YAY ) OK so the chicken tikka chaat: first glance looks good? first bites ok? then it hits me: where's the chicken even???? oh it's mashed? ok (?) also it was super spicy. the thing that drops this down is that the cilantro chutney was a green that no cilantro is -- it looked like it was dyed :( and so was this other tamarind chutney that was dyed red :( why tho??? also, the lassi? glad i had an option as it's not always i find almond milk lassis, but as i drank more of the mango lassi it was way too sweet. :( all in all, for this west coaster and from this region of the world, could be better.
Convenient but I wish there was a larger gluten free selection.

a reasonably planned out whole foods, but ya know, its whole foods, aka whole paycheck. you get overblown granolas-seeking-sustanability prices. would rather shop at trader joes prices, but sometimes they don't have enough selection and that much whole foods does have, plus the gluten free options if you're willing to sacrifice a limb.

Driving through St. Louis and stopped at Pi. It was a very enjoyable dinner for my wife and I and our 3 boys (under 8). Great salads choices and very accommodating on the pizza selection. The toppings are delicious and fresh, not locally grown but fresh. With 3 separate seating areas one could enjoy the bar, the restaurant or a table in the 'carry-out' room, good for the kids. Crowd and staff were lively and the upbeat music was nice. Great to have vegan and gluten-free options. 5 stars!

Highway robbery... They raised the price of their gluten free pies by over 30%. No warning about a price increase when I placed my order over the phone. My $12 pie turned into $17. I can understand the gf crusts aren't the cheapest, but for the size of the pies and what you're getting, they already were at a premium over standard pies. Now it's just way out of line, and I'll not buy again from them. Much cheaper to make my own at home.

***This is more of a 3.5 place but I rounded up*** Okay, so I was in Nashville last weekend for a friend's bachelorette party. For our first night in town, we came here for dinner. I'll start by saying that the building itself is super swanky. It looked small from the outside but once inside, it grew into a really lovely dining area. It looked as though there were some fireplace features that could have been really pretty but those were turned off. It was FREEZING in the restaurant. It was in the 80s outside but dreadfully cold inside which always puts a damper on any dining experience for me but I powered through. Okay, drinks: pass on the cocktails. They sound good but they're small and feel watered down. They have a great wine selection so I'd recommend going that route unless you're inclined to have a glutenous beer. For food, the maid of honor ordered a charcuterie board. She specified that she needed to have the crackers on a separate plate because she has celiac's disease and any cross-contamination of gluten could cause her to be sick. They brought everything out together on one plate anyway which was disappointing but our waiter made it right by bringing out a whole new charcuterie board sans crackers. The cheese and meats were loved by all in my group. It was a perfect appetizer. They also bring out a really good bread that has great seasoning and is perfectly baked. For my meal, I ordered the swordfish which is one of their daily specials. It was very good except super salty. I wish they had toned down the seasonings a little. Otherwise I really enjoyed it and I believe my friends also really enjoyed their meals. We were disappointed a bit with our server who seemed to disappear for long periods of time. We ordered 2nd drinks before our meals came out and didn't receive them until after our plates were cleared away :( Not cool. So then we had to stay there longer than we wanted in order to drink the drinks we wanted to have with our meals. Overall, I'd say this place was a roller coaster ride for our group. Some things were fantastic and other things were pretty bad. I come to Nashville fairly regularly since I have a lot of family and friends in the area so I may come back and see if things have shaped up to make good on my four stars!

I've had pizza here before and it was good. I got a chicken cheese steak with fries. The steak was good but the sandwich feel apart. The fries were still cold and undercooked. The person I was with got the supreme nachos. Lets just say elementary school threw up on the plate. Cheap nachos, cheese sauce from a can, the chili was so sweet it was gross.

As a whole, we shop at Winn Dixie for the meat specials and the BOGO's. Geographically we switch between this store and the location up on Hwy 19 in Hudson. On 1/6/2014 my spouse purchased some dried Beans from this store. Unfortunately, the beans (Hurst's Cajun 15 bean soup mix) were contaminated with bugs. I sent an email to Winn Dixie Customer Service and never got a response. I sent a second email and called, now very upset with both the product manufacturer and WD's lack of response to a potentially dangerous situation. Today a very competent, and knowledgeable Assistant Manager named Bill Dowling called me. We discussed the problem and I've got to say, this guy has pride in his company, knows how to handle irate customers, and works hard to make sure any dissatisfied customers will stay shoppers at Winn Dixie... We weren't looking for any free stuff, we just wanted to make sure the defective product was removed and addressed with WD Corporate. I feel good about continuing to shop here, and commend Bill Dowling for his character and great attitude in the face of a bad situation... Complacency is common these days, most people in restaurants and stores just go through the motions. I hope Winn Dixie recognizes, for their own benefit, that they have a winner in their midst!

Placed an online order last night while visiting SB for work. Called and asked Veronica the differences in the sauces. She was less than friendly. We still placed an order online. FYI they don't give an ETA when placing your order online. We placed the order at 4:15pm. After an hour I called and spoke with Veronica again. She assured me the order was on its way. A half hour after that our food arrived (around 5:45pm). The delivery guy was super friendly. We liked him. Husband had a gluten free pepperoni and mushroom pizza. He said it was pretty good. I ordered a personal thin crust pizza with kalamata olives, onion, feta cheese and sun dried tomatoes. I was impressed at the generous heap of toppings on both pizzas. Overall, we liked the food and our delivery guy but were unimpressed with the "service" we received over the phone and the very long wait for the food.

We went to this restaurant tonight with a group to celebrate a special occasion. After ordering our drinks, it took 45 minutes for them to arrive at our table; appetizers took an hour; and the two sushi rolls that I ordered, along with everyone else's food took an hour and a half. The food was fairly good; however, the service was mediocre at best. The server was not able to make good recommendations to guests that had allergies and specific food restrictions. I was never asked if I wanted a second drink. And although the menu stated that an 18% gratuity would be charged to large groups, when we received our checks a 20% gratuity was added. After addressing this with our server she tried to justify it saying that they charged extra gratuity for groups our size. I spent many years working in the service industry, & I could not believe that a server that delivered service the caliber that she did would even consider increasing the auto gratuity amount on a large group without saying something about it. I reduced my tip amount to the 18 percent stated on the menu, but really it probably should have only been between 12 or 15 (and that is being courteous and from a service industry alumna). My personal opinion is that there is much better Japanese food and service in the st. Louis area and I will not be going back to this restaurant.

The place has a wow factor once you walk in. The dimmed lighting and wall to wall fish tanks are captivating. We ordered appetizers and a main course. We skipped lunch and were starving so would have been happy with anything served. My first dish was a ceviche and it was not good. It was missing that right amount of sour flavor and tasted like defrosted fish. It did not have the right amount of spices that a good ceviche should have. My entree was the gluten free mahi mahi dish with risotto. It was good, but nothing to write home about. It was a good hearty meal with decent presentation without any wow factors to it in flavor. Finally - we ended the meal on a high note. They make this gluten free lava cake out of corn starch that was great. It was nice and soft inside and paired with salted caramel ice cream. I would defiantly recommend it even to those who do not follow a gluten free diet. Overall - great decor, ok food and a bit pricey for what it is.

Overall, this was a disappointment. The menu online indicated some items were gluten free which the menu on site did not. There were very few choices left which were gluten free and those I chose were very salty or underdone. I like Puerto Rican food but this was not somewhere I would go again.

One challenge with being gluten-free is finding restaurants that have adapted menu selections to suit our needs. Brio has done so. Tonight I enjoyed a petit filet, mashed potatoes, and tasty roasted vegetables. The meal was very good. Our servers were attentive and well mannered. The atmosphere was a little loud...mostly due to the TV volume in the adjacent bar (Golden Globes and NFL Playoffs). But, overall a satisfactory experience once again.

Just moved here went for sandwich take out pricey for the food two girls in the front poor customer service when I asked to make sure the sandwich had no cheese as my friend is lactose intolerant. One girl responded with something flippant with her back to us and the other one facing us said of course we will make sure. Got the food home and everything had cheese. Normally wouldn't care cut it was grilled in. Send a note to the owner won't go back. Poor customer service for the high price they charge. Spend some of that money on more training of the staff to make sure food is cooked As ordered and on customer service.

Yuk! I ordered a gluten free White Special Ricotta and after 1 1/3 hours ended up with a pepperoni tomato based Luke warm pizza. Had to throw it away and felt stupid for paying for it before looking to see what it was.

I am giving them one star for their over priced, straight from a big old vat-o-frozen new England clam chowder soup. The calamari was burnt, my kid picks off the breading so she didn't mind, but my meal was so tainted I literally pulled over to the side of the road to vomit on my drive home...where I proceeded to throw up some more. I had the plain old fish and chips. The manager came by to tell me it was good fish...that he "broke it open and smelled it." I told him...I'm a Certified Chef....ur fish is bad...I'm feeling ill...u should check your stock. Not sure if it was on our tab. I had to leave before my husband and kid...still ill.... the manager seemed incredulous instead of contrite and apologetic...as I would be...if I had just fed someone tainted fish. I plan on calling someone in the county health department tomorrow. He offered me more food as I sat there going three shades of green....thanks but no. I will never eat here again. First and last time all in one....rare and disgusting

I have been to this place in the past and they were okay, but this morning the rudest workers were there. The first one was acting like she had about 5 too many coffees this morning, and she was talking so fast we couldn't even order the way we wanted. Then, she ended the order with "pull forward" before we could even finish. When she threw our food at us, she forgot one of our sandwiches and as we were asking her for it she threw up her hand in a way to say "hush" so she could order for the next person. Then, another employee waddled in still half asleep and asked us to pull forward and wait. So we did, and realized we needed a stir stick for our coffee to mix in the bunched up mixed handful of sugars we were given when we asked for "two yellows." So I went inside to get one, and the lady who first took our order was on her way out the door to bring our sandwich...in such a hurry to not even look up and proceeded to almost run into me and push me out the door until I grabbed the sandwich bag as a way to show her I existed and she said "oh is this yours," handed it to me, walked away, and I tried asking for a stir stick- to which I got another raised hand to tell me to hush. So I asked the employee who just came in for a stir stick, and she picked one up on one end, and before handing it to me, grabbed it with the other end with her very obviously still dirty fingers/fingernails (I don't understand how people can have such dirty hands even if they wash their hands once a day). Very disappointed and very rude service, along with the poor hygiene.

I went here my first night in New Orleans, after a wretched two days of travel and a bout of food poisoning. I really needed a nice comforting place to get a bowl of chicken soup. A bit of searching on Yelp led us to Lüke, and I'm so glad we went there. All the staff were tremendously kind, especially our server, Kyle, a total charmer. We asked for a quiet(er) table and were seated upstairs where we could watch the kitchen staff, who were impressively efficient and clearly enjoying their work. Though everyone was busy, all the people who helped us--the two hosts, Kyle, and another server--took time to laugh and joke with us and help us feel welcome. The food was top-notch. My mother is a) a professional chef and b) a Jewish mother, and the matzo ball soup was almost the equal of hers: fluffy, peppery matzo balls, a superb rich broth, and delicious bits of roast chicken. When Kyle came by to check on us and I jokingly asked for a refill on the broth because I'd slurped it all up and had a giant matzo ball left to go through, he whisked away and came back a few minutes later with more broth--for which we weren't charged, even though it was practically the equivalent of another whole bowl of soup! My partner, who isn't usually much of a foodie, was rhapsodic over the poulet grand-mère. And by our New York standards the prices were staggeringly low, especially for such good food. With that soup in my belly I feel better than I have in days. Thanks, Lüke. I'll be back for sure.

Got the sandwich with turkey, brie, apples, and honey mustard on gluten-free bread. Bread was okay, but a little dry. The turkey slices were huge, which made the whole sandwich hard to eat. But tasted good. Cute place. Would come here again.

Pretty cool place. Smoking is allowed. So if your not a smoker this place might not be for you. The place had an interesting menu. They serve, typical bar food, hamburgers, club sandwiches and heavy poured drinks from the bar. The cool thing is, is that every sandwich/burger/sub you order has cole slaw and french fries on it. Reminded me of some food network show. Also they have the 10 lb cheesesteak challenge. I looked at the leader board. Noone has ever won. 1 hour, no bathroom breaks, no help, no vomiting. 50$if you lose. $100 if you win, which i doubt you can win. Overall great service, bar atmosphere, decent food!

I was really excited to try this place out after I had read so many great reviews. I went with a group of friends and we all had something different and the overall thought was that it was good. I ordered the Buffalo Chicken sandwich. I was excited to see that they had gluten free bread (and it tasted pretty good, but was very crumbly.) The sandwich was pretty dry though, it was supposed to have ranch...it didn't and I never got it after asking for it. Their homemade ketchup is really good though. I would say the food was good, the service not so great. I was never asked if I wanted a refill on my drink and as stated did not receive the ranch. I feel like the prices were a little high for what you actually get as well. Overall just an ok place for me. I would probably give it a second chance though.

We visited after a Nashville Sounds game. It was a super cute walk over to the restaurant, but apparently everyone else has the same idea because the wait was long and the bar was packed. The pizzas take a long, long time to bake, so my husband got a thin crust instead of a deep dish. He said it was really good! (And we took one home because thin crusts we're buy one get one half off on Sundays.) I had one of the best margaritas I've ever had, I would definitely go back just for that. There weren't many gluten free options, however. I had a Caesar salad with chicken that was definitely nothing special. I might go back to try the wings, as they aren't breaded but they were out when we were there.

this Deli is either hit or miss.......The last time I ate here I ordered the once famous Mushroom barley soup. Boy was I in shock when I found a clothing button floating in ,my soup.......I almost vomited....The owner came over and didn't offer any explanation. How gross is that ????? Also the corned beef was horrible, chewy and not fresh, The meat tasted like it was sitting in the fridge from yesterday and heated up in a microwave. The worst sandwich I ever ate......This Diner/deli deserves a minus O.... and I would highly suggest avoiding this dump. and go to a Real Deli, "Kibbitz Room,,,,,!!! You'll be glad you did,

I have called a dozen times over the last 5 months trying to order a yummy gluten free pizza. I have been told every time that they were out of the GF dough. So, fed up, the last time I called I asked if they planned on carrying it again. The woman on the phone gave me a very odd response; said they might start carrying it again when it was warmer out??!? I asked what the weather had to do with it and her response also made no sense. Sadly I think SLN is no longer a resource for the gluten free individual. Sad, it was really good :-(

Corporate atmosphere, corporate generic food with typical creative selling points that just don't hold up. For instance, beer cheese...just Meh. And, Way way over priced. Would probably be better as a group outing. But I paid $37 for a 10" pep and 12" gluten free special pizza. Pep was good. Gluten free crust was sad and flat and burnt and plain nasty. They should lose it all together. Especially for the outrageous charge! Find a nice mom and pop pizza place that doesn't try so hard and you'll be much more satisfied :)

I went in there for a early morning coffee. When I took the last sip of my coffee there something weird in my mouth along with the coffee. To my shock and horror I pulled out a short and curly pubic hair, complete with the follicle. I started to vomit in my mouth in my booth and I had to sprint to the bathroom where my coffee and breakfast tacos forcefully and uncontrollably projectile vomited out of my mouth, splattering the toilet. I confronted the manager who seemed ambivalent and I called the number on the back of my receipt and did nothing. So in exchange for their inaction I would like everyone to know what happened to me at this location.

Terribly smug attitudes by the cashiers, always. One creamer available, which is usually whole milk in a never clean station. Yucky doesn't stop at the milk stand. Their gimmicky coffee is of a fine chalky rust with a splash of cross-contaminated feces. Harsh but it must be warned. Sad it's most convenient stop when my personal coffee supply is up, but the place proves you can prefer to starve than to ever eat.

This place sucks. Food is horrible, I almost threw up. I was so hungry and we waited for almost and hour and a half for it to come out. For an appetizer we ordered the loaded tator tots.. can't mess that one up right? Wrong! The cheese wasn't even melted when it came out! We also ordered firecracker shrimp which never made it to the table. And then finally our food came out. I ordered the chicken curry, they gave me shrimp. It was disgusting. Along with their chicken piccata which they made into a disgusting lemon soup and their chicken Mediterranean pasta/spinach salad, whatever it was. Our server, tall, younger Caucasian man wasn't any help. We asked to take it back but he didn't bother listening to us when we were telling him our food was gross. I work in the food and bev industry in Las Vegas and this place had very bad service. If a customer doesn't like the food, you take it back, always. He only took one back. Music is too loud, food is expensive for how it tastes. Next time I'll just go to mcDonalds down the street to get a fish sandwich.

I love this place, don't get me wrong. But for gluten free or dairy free options, this is not your place. It was great when I used to eat wheat (their biscuits are amazing with honey butter and jam) but since I went gluten free, I haven't found anything I can have that actually fills me up. I got the omelette without the egg and asked for sausage instead of ham (as I don't eat ham) and I basically got a small portion of sautéed spinach, onions, and tomatoes with 3 small pieces of ham. It was good, but it would be awesome if they had slightly larger portions when substituting. Otherwise, their gluten free peanut butter cookies are the bomb.

Good food. I stopped eating here since a couple of years ago because I got food poisoned and had some major stomach issues afterward. I don't feel like taking the risk to go back.. Just be aware that fast-food restaurants aren't very reliable, and you should be fine!

This is probably the worst Thai meal I've had in Santa Barbara. Stopped by with a friend to branch out for our regular Thai spots. I ordered the yellow curry with beef. If you want to mix veggies or tofo with beef is an extra $1.50. The curry had long pieces of beef with a few carrots floating around with little to no flavor. My friend ordered gluten free spicy noodles with chicken and tofu. Warning it's extremely bland. They remove all the sauces. Which is fine but definitely let the customer know beforehand. Thai ice tea was delicious with a good ratio of tea and condense milk.

Been coming here since they opened and I loved it, until tonight. Tonight, I was having dessert with dogs... This is a restaurant and these were NOT service dogs, and they were eating out of the same dishes people eat out of. I'm pretty sure this is a health code violation, and I have allergies. I will not be back. Maybe that's why the place always smells of disinfectant... It's a shame cause the food is great.

I've tried this place before and was very excited to come back. I placed my order asking for no dairy because I'm sensitive and confirmed multiple times that I didn't want cheese. The order was messed up and there was tons of cheese in my burrito. Truly disappointed, a restaurant needs to pay attention to a customers specifications especially when it comes to intolerances and allergies!

Ok last night I bought a pizza here for take out, even though I usually grab one from sal's pizza box a few minutes away. It was AWFUL. First of all, it wasn't cut. What the hell. I guess you have to specify that?? So, after I cut it, I started eating. The moment I lifted up a slice, all the sauce, cheese, and topping slid right off. This happened to about half of the slices. So, I had to scrape up all the cheese and sauce and toppings from the box and try to spread it onto the pizza. When, I finally started to eat, I almost threw up. The dough wasn't cooked all the way! I guess that's why the toppings fell off. There was literally a layer of raw dough on my pizza. GROSS!! Also, the entire thing was soggy for some reason. But the worst part? I found a hair baked right into the crust. I had to pull it it of my mouth. They don't make the pizza in front of you, so I can only speculate as to the horrible sanitary conditions in the kitchen. The hair was over a foot long, and I will never forget the disgusting feeling of pulling it out of my mouth. Nor will I forget the looks of horror on my family's faces as they watched me pull the hair out of my throat. Definitely the worst pizza place in the area, by far. STAY AWAY.

This is like a larger Chuck E Cheese's. Thank God I had two Groupons, because it would have been super expensive. The good: 1. My nieces loved the go karts-the older one (7) got to drive her own. They have two speeds-slow or fast. The younger one (4) and I also rode double (I drove) in a slow one. I think you have to be 48" tall to drive your own. Not sure of how tall for the fast ones. 2. Good game selection. Also had bumper cars and a few other small "ride" type things and laser tag. 3. Lots of seating. 4. It was a good 2.5 hours of entertainment. The bad: 1. The food. Not of the best quality. The buffet is mostly pizza and pasta. There was a separate salad bar and dessert bar. 2. Expensive. I had two groupons that equaled $50. This paid for our food and plenty of time for playing games (but this was only for two kids). HOWEVER, the bumper cars and go karts, etc, cost more money. HOWEVER, I accidently didn't pay for the go-karts. Seriously accidental. I didn't see the thing to swipe your card-no staff member was standing there. I honestly thought we would swipe it just before we got on. Nope. I got a $15 freeby. Oopsie. 3. The people sitting outside smoking. The benches were lined with older people, who obviously were not there with children(Mostly elderly), who had apparently partaken (is that a word?) of the $9.99 "All You Can Eat" buffet. It was wonderful to think that all the kids entering were walking through their cloud of smoke. 4. The type of clientele. I found many people to be rude. Mostly in the dining room. The dining room is set up with rooms in themes, and lots of people have birthday parties there. At one point, some people saw me standing there trying to get through-they were between tables standing up and talking, and I had to walk around to get to my nieces. Like go out, walk around the whole room and come in another entrance. Also lots of kids running. In the medium category: 1. Lots of staff people. I saw multiple people going by with mop buckets. I kept wondering if there were that many kids vomitting or what. Also, I instructed the elder niece to sit at the table while I took her sister to the restroom. Of course, she is 7 and can't follow those types of instructions. I come out of the bathroom and she is getting another plate of food. We go back to the table, and it is all bussed away. Everything. I was a bit bitter about my salad, but I guess with it being mostly kid clientele, there are used to lots of food getting wasted, and probably thought we were done. We had literally just sat down. In conclusion, go if you have a groupon. I don't think I could afford to go if I did not. And yes, I realize that it is expected that lots of kids will be there, but I also expect manners out of kids, regardless of where they are. Oh, and out of adults too.

The decor of this restaurant is great. Alas, it was a disappointing meal. With two of our party gluten free, this menu had very few options. The salad that was an entree version had the smallest piece of grilled chicken possible on it. It was terribly overpriced for what was basically mostly romaine lettuce. Upon being seated, we were offered a 10 discount if we checked in on Facebook. We did so and received a discount on the food portion only -- not on our cocktails or wine -- which would have been fine, if they had disclosed it. The cocktails served were not as on the menu, and the server, while pleasant, was not very knowledgeable about the menu.

Meh. It's just okay. Came in around 5pm to a completely empty deli with the cashier (owner?) playing on his laptop. I was greeted with a grunt and nod of a head, nothing else the entire duration of our transaction, but its Jersey so whatever. I ordered a basic cheesesteak, fairly hard to mess up. Front clerk picked up a set of gloves that were sitting on the counter and began making my sandwich. Um, excuse me, would you please stop touching every counter, door knob, laptop and cabinet with the same glove that you are touching my food with? Better yet, wash your hands and be done with it, or at least change your glove when it becomes cross contaminated, for god sake, an entire box of gloves is like $4. I'll give you an extra $5 if you don't cause me to vomit after eating from your establishment. Also, the last thing I want to see as I bite into my sandwich are your feet, so could you also put on a pair of socks and shoes or is that honestly asking too much? The sandwich (after I got all the images out of my head and prayed real hard) was not terrible, definitely not great, but not terrible. I probably wouldn't go back unless I was somehow stranded outside, unable to get anywhere else. Sorry guy, you were THE fail of this experience.

Had high hopes for Dawn Patrol based on the photo of their gluten-free pancakes. Well, they're just OK. The gluten-free pumpkin pancakes at Trader Joe's from a mix are 100 times better than these. Trust me. We also had the coffee cake which was dry as a bone and had hardly any crumble. Based on these two menu items, I wouldn't come back. It's a friendly, bright, open space, though.

I've been eating at Szechuan Hill for well over 15 years and my family absolutely loves this restaurant. My wife and I married in early September and we selected Szechuan Hill to be the location of a very tiny wedding reception for only immediate family members. We reserved the large table in front of the kitchen area and brought my flat-panel TV with built-in DVD so we could play the wedding DVD as we ate our meal. The staff was very accommodating, even allowing us to use their extension chord. Nobody minded that we were having a blast at the table, watching a wedding DVD, and enjoying our food. For $100, a group of 8 people had a wonderful meal and a night to remember. But getting back to the food... This place has terrific Chinese food. It's rated 4 stars for a reason; It's delicious! Let me just say one thing though about the last review someone left regarding this restaurant... The last reviewer claims he's eaten here 4 times and recently got some sort of food poisoning and it was so bad it caused toxic shock and he couldn't walk or talk. Uhhh...Do you think your sickness could have been due to something ELSE, bro?! I had the same exact meal he had (the General Tso's chicken combo platter with wonton soup) and didn't have a toxic event happen to me.

Mostly gluten-free ("paleo") and most of that seemed to be vegan as well. I've had decent gluten-free and vegan baked goods before (it is difficult, but possible) and this was not it. I got a vegan/paleo goji berry muffin and it took me literally 2 minutes to extract the muffin wrapper from it. I knew it would be extremely dry, but it was also disgusting; I tried, but failed to eat even half of it. I made a beeline for their water dispenser, but it was horribly undrinkable. It said "infused" but it tasted like mouthwash, as they must have dumped in mint essential oil instead of muddled mint leaves. Their labeling was inconsistent and it was difficult to determine which items were vegan. They did not seem to have any vegan wheat-based cupcakes, but later my sister said they had one kind, which none of us got. My sister disliked her paleo/vegan chocolate cupcake, but it looked better than my muffin. My cousin liked her raw vegan/paleo pumpkin pie, however. The 3 non-vegans with us didn't try anything, so I can't say if their "normal" (wheat & non-vegan) cupcakes are any good. For vegans who are not GF, nearby Laughing Planet and Great Full Gardens both have better vegan baked goods (cookies).

Eaten here several times and it's always delicious. I normally get the drunken chicken and chicken maque choux. Get extra bread. It's one of my favorite things to eat. The food will look like vomit in rice, but trust me you'll love it.

Sbraga has been reviewed on Yelp pretty extensively for a newer establishment. The reviews have been very thorough. Good job kids. I am at a loss to find a new or poignant aspect of this restaurant. All I am left with is to write what an excellent time I had dinning here. I really appreciated the amount of choices you were given for each course. Often, a fixed price multi course meal can be limiting. You run the risk of having one course where you don't care for any option. This is not an issue at Sbraga,each course has 4 to 5 options. In complete juxtaposition to many reviews, our service was stellar. We were taken care of by multiple staff members. Each one seemed genuinely interested in our dining experience. It is a slower pace then most places, but if you are trying to enjoy each of four courses it is necessary. We were never rushed, even when the back up at the door was swelling. One of the floor managers checked in with us at the end of the meal. He not only asked "did we enjoy our meal" but also "which was your favorite dish" He presented a certain pride in the food which was not forced. I was also pleased to see the owner; a celebrity chef, working in the open kitchen. if you go to a place on the reputation of the chef, you want to know they are more than a general manager. I loved every one of my dishes. The foi gras soup lives up to the hype. The portions were perfect size and the wine pairing made sense to my armature palette. $45 is a steal for the quality of the meal. $30 for the wine pairing was worth it. The combo at Sbraga is more than dinner, its a perfect night out.

If your read pretty much ANY of the other reviews from my fellow Yelpers, they will all tell you the food is delish, so I am going to review something some of you might think nothing about but is oh-so-important -- sanitary conditions! I was one of the grillers at their annual Eggfest, and I was so impressed with how clean they kept everything. I am a total germaphobe and get food poisoning so easily, so it is always wonderful to see a really clean culture with a place. First, they let me use their "employee only" restroom, and it was as clean as the one in my own house. Woo! Second, they made EVERY griller follow Dept. of Health safety protocols when cooking, including wearing gloves, a hat or hairnet, and close toed shoes. Also, they only brought out meat in half-hour portions so it never set out in the heat. Finally, our hand washing stations had actual hot water. I probably sound so lame for pointing all this out, but if you read some of my reviews of other places, you will see that food served to me is a magnet for hair, bugs, and undercooked poultry. It is so nice to know that if you come here, the food will be delicious and prepared in an environment even cleaner than your own house (yes, I skip the hairnet at home).
Good fries. Loved the Rooster mayo. The whisky BBQ burger was okay. The gluten free bun was not good- but they seldom are.

This was the third time I've gave this place a shot.. Each time is worse that the first. 186 Tiara A was horrible. Never smiles once, forgot my toast and by the time she came to check up one me I was mostly finished eating. Then the toast came out and it was dreadful. How to you mess up toast? The butter they used was horrible! And this coming from a guy who likes I CANT BELieVE ITS NOT BUTTER fake butter..lol I asked for American cheese and they used dyes yellow American in which I am allergenic too. Luckily a little bit won't bother me much. There was only LITTLE tiny bits of bacon bits in the omelette I got. Barely noticeable. This place might have good pancakes but they really blow at everything else. Never going back

I want to post an update here. Thank you 312 for your quick response to my review. We were unable to order another 312 pie last night since our company arrived and we don't live close to the restaurant, but I appreciate you responding and offering us a credit to use at a later date. I'm giving an extra star because I should've looked at this gluten-free pizza before we left the restaurant to see that it was completely charred. We have house guests on their way and we need to order another pizza because this one isn't edible. So much for that $23.

Popped in for a quick lunch during my first visit ever to Indianapolis. We are staying at the Hyatt Regency so it was close by. Had been curious about the gluten free pizza for about six months so here was the perfect opportunity to try it. Half way through my first slice out on the patio I hit a snag. I am absolutely revolted to see a 12" black hair baked into cheese topping. That was what was between my teeth? Really? One of the staff sees my plate pushed off to the side......I explain, and she is clearly astounded. My waitress comes over and suggests they will make another pizza. I was ready to bolt but she convinces me to stay. A while later a fellow comes over to my table, does not introduce himself or apologize. Just stares at me and then says he will take 20% off the tab. Like I care about the money. He has a problem in that kitchen that he blamed on ambiant conditions on the patio. Honestly, where is the professionalism? I guess California Pizza Kitchen should be considered mall fare and nothing more.

This place is horrible! We had 2 gluten free members in our party, and found a menu with gluten free options, designated with stars. One was the tilapia, which was advertise to be baked. Our meals arrived, and the tilapia came out obviously fried. We asked the waitress and she stated that the tilapia was breaded in flour and flash fried. Seriously?! Flour is gluten, idiot! Do you realize that you could be sued for this false advertising, since it could potentially really harm someone! Management better figure this out! When we said we weren't happy, they stated that they would take off the 2 tilapia entrees. Thanks! But really, management, the meal needs to be completely comped. Hey steak out learn how to run a restaurant before you get sued!

Used to be one of my favorite spots in the Northeast. But has not been good the last two times. I had a Caesar salad today. Shrimp smelled bad and didn't taste good either. Dressing was heavy and lacked flavor. Before that I had a slice of Sicilian pizza. I almost threw up.

Can't get through dinner fast enough to try this cake!!! I did have Mini red velvet while I was waiting for them to write on top of a great looking cake that was walk in ready :-) made it very convenient! Staff was all great. There were a few tables~but I was on the run to meet the family. Large gluten FREE menu....grabbed a cupcake for one on my kidos friends :-) ****dropped down to 3from 5...got said cake to dinner~was told it was stored in fridge as it had whipped icing. It was in my possession about 2.5 hours~NOT in a fridge...but when trying to cut it, the cake was FROZEN. REALLY wish they had told me it'd be frozen~chances are I would not have bought a cake to be eaten soon after that was frozen. It was around $35 for the cake and the mini cupcake...I mentioned on the phone and in store that it was for after dinner :-(

Bayou Burger had some great selections & the bartender helped us to decide on the cowboy burger but we had the pretzel bun instead of the brioche which was a good choice. Due to that being a double, my wife & I split that along with the Zydeco bites (mini corn dogs dipped in home made zydeco batter which had a little sweetness & a little zing) they came with two dipping sauces, a creole mustard & a spicy ketchup, both of which were very good. The burgers here are all cooked above medium, closer to medium well, probably due to them not wanting to be sued for food poisoning by some drunk partiers is my guess, but they were not overdone. Overall we enjoyed our meal & the service was very good!

So the wife and I decided we needed to go out and grab food. However we did not want our usual choices, so we opted finally check out Brewsters. I wasn't sure what to expect and upon arrival, it almost seemed like a "fancy dining" type place. Yet when we moved closer inside we noticed it was casual yet elegant, if that even makes sense? To the right is a lounge/bar style and to the left was dinner seating. We were almost immediately greeted by a server and placed in a booth. We were made aware of the specials and not rushed with our orders. When we were ready to order my wife got the fish and chips while I got the aussie lamb burger. We also opted to go with the beer special of the day and picked up a scooner of Bigfoot Blueberry Wheat Ale. The ale was amazingly delicious. I am immensely impressed with Brewsters attention to detail and quality in regards to their beers. So many restaurants/bars do not clean the lines and if they do they rarely clean them. This means the alcohol is not contaminated and gives a hood clean crisp taste. It also was a nice touch that they put actual blueberries into the beer. When the food arrived we noticed the portions were large and equaled the price we paid. In fact my wife couldn't even finish her fries. I on the otherhand devoured my burger in record time. It tased amazing and the mint mayo really aided in the flavor. The only negative about my burger was that it had far too much lettuce on it. It was overflowing and spilling out all sides of the burger, almost an inch. I had to eat too much leafy greens before I got to the actual burger. The server was very nice and polite and attentive to our needs. This is definitely a 4-5 star place to eat. Loved it and will be back to try some more food and drink some more beer... Thinking the Czech Vampire Pilsner next time.

Alright- let's just call this place what it is: its a $30 flat bread, and it's ridiculous. Yes the ingredients are organic and yes you can get gluten free (which is stupid for a pizza anyway), but you will also get a pizza that is a disappointment. Period. I knew better- we had these in Miami, and when I lived there we ordered a few times, but alway felt like we were getting ripped off. I guess I had a laps in judgement and decided to give them a go, which I quickly regretted. The pizza ($37 with tax, delivery and tip) arrives with miniscule toppings- I ordered with prosciutto and I would have needed a magnifying glass to see the chopped prosciutto!! I decided to call and speak with the manager the next day- honestly I thought he should have given me a refund for half the pizza- I'm serious when I say I could have counted the topping on this xlarge on two hands- but instead he reacted the way I would have expected a Dominos pizza manager to react: unaccomodating and huffy. he offer a small discount off my next pizza which I will never order. not the type of reaction you would expect from a specialty (supposedly) pizza place. Crappy experience, flatbread rip off pizza: that is what you will get at Pizza Fusion- unfortunately....

This place has great pizza! I eat gluten-free crust because I don't like to feel so bloated and stuffed after eating pizza and their gluten-free crust is amazing! They have an amazing list of toppings, any of which you can mix and match! They have a wonderful spinach salad with a warm olive oil, pine nut dressing! This place has any sort of pizza you could want! Quite a few times no one has been at the front of the restaurant to seat me and I've had to seat myself. On only one occasion did they make me move from where I had sat down. I would just be patient to be seated and the wait will be worth the great food! :)

Sitting at the bar with my wife and it smells like vomit. It smells so terrible we will no eat here and will not ever come back, For t not being busy and for it so smell like this and have terrible service is beyond disgusting.

Dude. It's Dairy Queen. Need I say more? If you haven't been to a dairy queen in your life, you must have been living in a remote island cave or something. Or you're lactose intolerant. Either one seems plausible. This one is the same as all the rest. Blizzards are delicious until you get home and poop your brains out. I do have one minor beef with this particular spot. The lines are unorganized and a lot of people cut. I guess I can't totally fault my beloved DQ for that, but more-so the delco trash that frequent places like Dairy Queen and are so much in need of their blizzard fix that they need to cut in line. (But wait, aren't I one of those trashy delco people that loves Dairy Queen? Whatevs! I'm talking about rude people!) Aaaaaaaany hooooo. Sometimes you just need some DQ. Nameen?

I hate to say what a disappointment, but I just did. I was really excited to try this place with some friends b/c I am dying for a restaurant in Doylestown that I cannot wait to go back to, but I guess I will keep waiting. I thought the service was decent and the ambiance was very cool and trendy, although I must complain about the lighting in the basement. It was so dark that I could barely see what I ordered and if my steak was done correctly. I don't think they need fluorescent lighting or anything but they have beautiful chandeliers upstairs and then hardly any lights downstairs. Anyway, onto the most important thing here, the food and this is where the disappointment really sets in. First I would like to say I am pregnant so that ruled out some of the menu options and my one friend is a strict vegetarian, possibly vegan, maybe gluten free picky eater, so the chef actually had to make her something off menu, which he did and she really liked it. I ended up with the $33 strip steak b/c I did not want a burger or chicken. The steak was good, but it did not have any seasoning, it lacked flavor. I could have gone to anyone's house for dinner and gotten the same steak and I could have gone to Costco and gotten a whole package of steaks for the same price. I was excited to try the potato o's that came with the steak, but that also had no taste, it was like battered mashed potatoes, but tasteless mashed potatoes? My other friend had the bipimbap, it tasted good, but like normal Chinese food. My husband had the tuna burger, which he said was flavorless too. I also got a Caesar salad since I knew my husband would have some of my steak, it was $9 for a relatively small salad and I made my friend taste it b/c I swore it tasted like lemons. It desperately needed some more dressing. We ended up spending $85 (my husband got 2 beers) and I would have been way happier eating burrito bowls at Chipotle for $20. I don't mind spending the money, but give me something with flavor and that I want to come back for.

Cute cafe with vintage signs on the walls. The waitress asked if we wanted to try the apple pie, and then charged us for it. She clearly has tricked tourists before. Food was decent, gluten free options were $1 more on top of high prices.

I usually avoid Mexican in any place but southern Cali, because let's be honest...we're too close to the border to have anything but THE BEST Mexican food. However, after checking out the menu in passing and spotting more than one vegetarian option, my sister and I decided to give this place a try. Now I knew when I arrived in New Orleans for a work conference that the veggie options were going to be slim, but I didn't realize how slim. One night, we literally ate carrots and bread at a fancy reception because there was NOTHING else. We got complimentary chips and salsa which was nice. The salsa wasn't Cali fab, but it wasn't bad. I ordered the vegetarian quesadilla and it came out in four triangle shaped pieces. The cheese was good at the first 2 bites, but quickly became overwhelming. I decided not to test my lactose intolerant luck, and swapped entrees with my sister. She ordered the vegetarian fajita and it was really good. The had more veggies that just the standard peppers and onions which was nice. We both had sangrias and I was more impressed that they teamed up with the wine bar across the street to make them than anything else, but I thought it was a decent drink. Above all else, the customer service was AMAZING! Our waiter was FAB and the owner(?)/manager(?) came over to thank us for dining with them. Just superb.

Loved the service and cozy interior, but the food wasn't anything special. Fried green tomatoes lacked flavor. My shrimp angel hair pasta dish was tasty, though a bit overly garlicky. My husband said his catfish po'boy and fried payers were so so. Mom liked her salad with a burger, and they were super accommodating of her food allergies and substitutions.

On a recent trip to the French Quarter for a friends wedding my boyfriend and I stopped in here for a quick breakfast before skipping town. We had picked this place after reading all the reviews about their hash browns and pancakes. Since I am gluten free the pancake were out and the hash browns were in. We LOVE hash browns and living in Miami we don't get them too often because Miami seems to favor home fries (don't know why...). Anywho, They did not live up to the reviews. Not even close. Ours came in pools of butter, which don't get me wrong can be a very good thing but it wasn't working for there hash browns. I ordered a 2 egg breakfast with bacon and hash browns and my eggs came in a similar pool. If I had been hungover or still drunk from the night before I probably would have been in heaven but for a sober meal I would skip this place. Oh! The coffee....AWFUL. Couldn't drink it. Threw out both of them after the first sip.

I would classify this as a Yelp FAIL. Honestly, I don't understand how this restaurant was rated so high. Perhaps tourists who were overly happy about being in Santa Barbara? We stopped on morning for breakfast. Food was marginal at best. Generous portions, organic and gluten free offers, fresh bacon, but the highlights stopped there. Ambiance was ok. Pancakes were not great. Wait time was not worth it, and like most tourist traps certainly overpriced. I would suggest traveling down State St. for something else.

I'm fairly sure, based on the menu, what we saw at other tables, and the general design and crowdedness of the place, that Milk & Honey Nashville is probably a great restaurant. Out experience wasn't so great, but it was probably because of what we ordered...we think. Milk & Honey is a large, crowded but comfortable restaurant which serves food comprised of ingredients sourced from local farmers. That's cool. They have an extensive menu of items which are suitable for vegetarians and healthy-eaters, including toasts, porridge, oatmeal, sandwiches and other dishes, cold press juices, loose leaf teas etc. My wife was initially disappointed that a tea she saw on the website menu wasn't available in the restaurant. I had the Black China Tea which I thought was good and strong, served in a loose leaf pouch for steeping at the table. I ordered the Apple Cinnamon Porridge which didn't like at all. It had weird aftertaste and I had to ask for maple syrup to doctor it up and make it edible for my palette. I also ordered a Super Famous Biscuit (though I declined to ask for its autograph) - This was definitely a legit southern biscuit. It was LARGE and served with butter, strawberry preserves and honey. It was larger than your average biscuit (thus the "super"...and I couldn't finish it. They had 1 gluten free baked good available. Our waitress had to leave to ask about ingredients for a number of items to see if they were suitable for my wife's gluten and dairy free preference. She seemed like she was in an awful hurry. We understand that it was super busy and it takes extra time to deal with us folks with crazy diets, but there's no excuse for making customers feel like you're inconveniencing them for asking questions about food. The bread service we saw "walk by" looked amazing. (okay it was actually carried by a waiter and not walking under its own power.) We sat at the silver bar (one of 2 first come first serve seating bars) to avoid the long wait and had a view of the super busy kitchen and baker working with lots of dough, which was cool. As I said my experience wasn't great, but the food part of it may have came down to my choices. I was feeling a little under the weather and wanted a healthier choice (thus the porridge) If I was feeling better, I would have had a biscuit sandwich or something else and probably would have loved it. That having been said we were only in Nashville for a few nights on vacation so this was our only opportunity to come here.

If I could give this restaurant zero stars, I definitely would. We had family in town during Mother's Day so we took them all to Watermark since it had such great reviews (which I find highly suspect now). Our waiter was incredibly rude and told us there would be no substitutions even though I'd discussed my daughter's food allergies with the manager when I made reservations for a table of 12. We had to insist that they make something gluten free for her or we'd have to leave. He acted as though the restaurant was packed when there was only two other tables of people seated. When her food finally came, it was inedible. It only got worse from there. The portions are the equivalent of an amuse bouche rather than that of an appetizer or entree. My 21 year old nephews ordered eggs and grits which were sand dry and due to the portion being so small, they had to order two more entrees to make one meal, which was extremely expensive. There are many wonderful new restaurants coming into Nashville. PLEASE do not waste your time or your money here.

Vomit, is the most accurate description to the veal parmigiana this place serves. Upon arrival, three depressed and bothered waiters looked over and walked away without acknowledging their paying customers. The ambiance reeks of 1980's worst restaurants in Tucson; with outdated lighting fixtures, plain and boring decor with goodwill furniture. I don't believe any of the other customers are aware of what Italian cuisine is. I fell ill to my stomach after two bites of the gamy scented garbage. I do not recommend this to anyone who is looking to pay a pretty penny for a worthwhile meal.

A one star bagel served with a frown. Seriously, dunkin' makes a higher quality bagel, and tops the customer service at this place. Unpleasant service - niceties like please, thank you, of course, are forced or nonexistent. It can take 5-10 minutes to receive a one-bagel order. Signs plastered on every surface prohibit touching, sitting, etc. I had to borrow a chair from a family while I waited as several tables were marked off limits (?). The bagel taste gluten free, crumbly with no chew, not a real bagel. I remembered a similar experience from my last visit in 2011, and as of today (2014) nothing has changed. Sorry I gave them another chance. The only positive thing to say about this place is their specialty cream cheeses are artfully displayed and contain real chunks of fruit, capers or whatever .

Recently, my wife and I spent a great weekend at Benihana in Plymouth Meeting for my sister-in-law's birthday. I have been to hibachi restaurants all over the world, but never the famous Benihana so I was quite interested how it compared to the previous ones. The most striking difference, right off the bat, was that our chef was Italian! I can honestly say that I have never had an Italian hibachi chef at one of these restaurants. This immediately threw up red flags and I started fearing the worst. Luckily, he used many of the same tricks and techniques that I've seen done before and of the same caliber. It was also nice because he could joke around with us while he was preparing our meal. I chose the spicy hibachi chicken at level 8 on the spicy scale. How he knew he prepared it at level 8 and not 7 or 9 the world may never know, but it was delicious nonetheless. I also had a Sapporo and Stella Artois on tap, as well as a Kirin Ichiban in a 22oz bomber. All of the beers were very light and bubbly with the Japanese beers containing rice as one of the main ingredients. Ever since I was a little kid, I always loved going to hibachi restaurants, so this was a real treat. Although the restaurant did have a chain feel to it, the food was great and the beer was flowing. If you have never eaten at this style of restaurant before, you owe it to yourself to try it at least once.

Wawa get worse by the second. Their sandwiches are way down hill, lines are always too long, there's always vomit in the parking lot, and definitely over priced. Wawa gets a star for being convenient late at night and a star for letting me poop in their bathrooms (which you now need a key for by the way).

It wasn't a good experience. It was my first time going there and I went there because I heard so many good things about it. But the experience started pretty bad. The guy at the counter who was taking the order, was not letting us even talk. We ordered "prime time donair" and we asked for mix. As I mentioned he was not even letting us finish what we were saying like he was in a hurry and had to go somewhere! Then when we got the donairs, it was just beef! Not mix! I didn't really have energy to go argue with the guys that already showed what customer service means! As soon as we sat down, before we even start, the guy left and showed why he wasn't even listening. The beef, didn't taste good and it didn't even have the texture that usual meat has! After I left, about half an hour, I started feeling bad in my stomach and feeling like vomiting. The taste in my mouth was very bad even 4 hours after that! I don't think I like to experience that again and I don't think I will ever go back there again.

Often times I have come here over the years as they have a great selection of organic and gluten free options. I love the wide array of pre-prepared foods/freezer items and even micro brew beer selections. The staff has always been wonderful and I have had no problem checking out. Here is the thing that has now been bothering me for some time and this weekend will be my last time going. I have complained directly with the store manager about this twice several months ago, very nice but I have seen no strides made to improve this. Please...anyone who buys things here, check your expiration dates. Almost every whole chicken I looked at was expired that day, many of the prepacked goods in clear containers near the cheese area also expired same day. I'm angry now b/c as diligent as I was looking at this, I just went to open up a container of tabbelouh, expired. It is too much hassle to travel back to the store and complain about this again. I did mention to the staff while there that the whole chickens in the cold area were expiring that day, the associate just so happened to have a new one he was carting out and I took that one. Great...but then when I circled back 15 mins later, I noticed he just arranged them back into order and never took the same day expired ones out. Sure, someone may come and buy the six chickens up...but more than likely, I bet they are sitting there still today and someone has purchased expired meat. I've had this issue in almost every area of the store where things are kept cold, the food they make on the premise, I've never had an issue with. It is the items in the fridge areas. Pickled items, cheese, meat products, hummus, tabbouleh, meat substitutes, salsa, etc. The list is too numerous. RO...please be diligent in checking expiration dates so that customers like me have the confidence to want to come back. I have much love for you and you can be a great store, but for now, I need to shop at a place that has fresh items.

My sister and dad kept raving about this place, and even though it's a chain, I thought I'd give it a shot. I'm sorry I did. The atmosphere is nice and cozy, and I liked the little "windows" at the end of the table that butted up to the kitchen area where the waitress took our order and delivered our food. But that's about where it stopped. The hashbrowns were greasy and tasteless and the eggs a little runnier than the over medium I ordered, but still hot and yolk flowing. For four triangles of toast, you are given one small package of jelly. No jam, no preserves. Many other restaurants (every locally owned breakfast place I've been to, anyway) have those nice little holders with a fun selection of jams, jellies, and fruit butters to spread on your toast but here I felt like I was being provisioned and given the benefit of getting one container of grape jelly. Okay. I'm sure I could have asked, but I shouldn't have to. The coffee was okay. No dairy free creamer which was a disappointment for my lactose intolerance but I ended up using the cream and was no worse for wear in the end, so that was good. I don't plan to return and I'm sorry to my family that I didn't enjoy it! I don't often rate places poorly, but we can't all have winners.

I went in to see if this restaurant had gluten free options. The hostess said they had some on the menu. I asked if they had a good amount or just a few. The hostess then said she would ask a staff member. She took a look around the room and told me to come back tomorrow, they were too busy.

I went to Essene on Sunday and spent $170 mostly on bulk goods to stock up and got jars from ikea to keep it in. On closer inspection that night a shitload of it is conveniently premoldy. Kidney beans, chickpeas, figs, golden flax seeds, and that's just what I could tell from looking at it. I'm returning all the bulk I got from there and never buying from them again, they obviously top off the old stuff with the new and everything is thus contaminated. I called and talked to a manager to alert them that things were moldy and she sounded very unimpressed and just told me to bring it back with my receipt to return. Believe me, i will be returning everything i bought there that wasnt presealed. I am super paranoid now at any of their stuff. And all this at prices that aren't much better than Whole Foods. God knows if they ever clean anything there, sooo disgusting. Decent selection, but I certainly will never, ever shop there again.

I was not impressed. Prices are high and why have a lobster tank if it's empty? Too many gimmick rolls on the menu. If there are no live lobsters in the lobster tank, where are they getting lobsters for their fancy raw lobster roll? I'm guessing way dead frozen ones in the back. And if that's true, I certainly wouldn't want to eat it. I ordered some fried oysters and received fried chicken instead. It was actually kind of funny because the waitress insisted that despite it not looking like the picture in the menu, they were indeed oysters. I had each of my friends sample it before deciding conclusively that it was instead chicken. I ordered the sweet shrimp and received the standard raw shrimp on rice and fried shrimp heads. I ate one piece and nearly threw up. It tasted like an old aquarium, which is not a good place for raw shrimp to be. When I asked the waitress about striking it from the bill, she did. However, if that was my sushi restaurant and I was confident in the freshness of the food, I would have explained all that before striking it from the bill. The fact that they did not come over to speak to me speaks volumes about the freshness of their food. That is to say, it probably isn't very fresh. The hot food was a joke. My friend ordered bul golgi (Korean dish). It was absolutely pathetic. And it was 16 bucks. Unforgivable. The uni was good. For 7 bucks, I should hope that it is. Otherwise, I do not plan on going back.

Not a huge fan of dunkin stores- every time I go the coffee tastes like poison or like bad coffee beans or burnt. My mom wanted to go somewhere quick to grab coffee and I was against it but went since she wanted it so badly and it was on the way to where we were going that day. So went through the drive thru. The man was hurrying us up to order and I thought that was a bit rude cause we needed some time to look at the menu. We ordered our things and moved on to the window to pay. Once we got our food- that's where this weird smell hit us both in the face. We ordered the poppy bagel with egg bacon and cheese. And something about the bagel smelled very badly. To me it smelled like a grill cleaner but to my mom she thought maybe the poppy was burnt- either way I ended up spitting it out after one bite and almost vomiting on myself since it stunk so badly. The iced coffee I ordered was good though so I was happy about that- since I've had some of the worse tasting iced coffee at other locations on and near bustleton avenue. For the best iced coffee I drive a bit further and Go to the park wood location- just a tip if you want to taste flavor and not something that tastes like poison in your mouth. Anyway so I end up telling my mom I have to go in in not eating the food when it tastes like that- I went inside told the guy the sandwiches tasted weird- the man at the counter was a lot friendlier then the one in the drive thru- go figure. I say I want just plain bagels toasted with cream cheese instead- he doesn't give me any money in return since the meals were different in price or anything- but I just honestly wanted to get out of there and hopefully enjoy a bagel that didn't taste like a grill cleaner- which I knew if eaten I would end up in the bathroom within minutes- expelling it all out. So I said thanks to the guy and left with bagels that tasted better and had no smell. Would not go to this location again-

You know, it's really too bad that I have to give the Hookah House a three-start review. The place is beautiful, and I've often said that it seems like a place that James Bond would have visited. If Bond were to have visited the Hookah House, he'd have enjoyed a seat in one of the establishment's dark corners--quietly discussing espionage while sipping Turkish tea and enjoying water-cooled hookah smoke. He'd also enjoy the excellent Middle-Eastern fare, although I'm sure that in his travels (even in the Indianapolis area), he'd had better. However, James Bond is a character of fiction. I'm a real customer, and I have to admit that I was a mite dissatisfied with many aspects of the Hookah House. My biggest complaints are with the staff. During my last visit, I had a wonderful server. She was quick with our orders, was friendly, and if it wasn't for her, I would have left. On my first trip to the Hookah House, a friend of mine, not used to high levels of nicotine, vomited on the floor. Of course, no one was happy about this. To make matters worse, a young man, who I later learned was the owner's son, began screaming, "FML! FML!!" (although he didn't speak in abbreviations). He then told us that we would have to pay for his cushions to be laundered in the event that they were soiled (which they were not). Come on, man. You sell a stimulant drug (nicotine)--accidents are bound to happen. On my second trip to the Hookah House, the establishment's owner would just not leave us alone. When we asked for a few moments to look over the menu, he huffed away. When we finally ordered, he did not seem to like our selections. For the next 30 minutes, he swore that he was eavesdropping on our conversation. Was it espionage? I couldn't tell. He also did not mention that he charged us for refills on our Diet Coke. I believe that I spent $16 just on diet soda (out of a fountain). Ripoff. Get your act together, Hookah House.

I'm going to start on a good note and compliment them on including Vegetarian options on their menu as well as Gluten Free (that is corn) tacos as an option. You can also enjoy Vegetarian BBQ Wings that are made out of Seitan. Pretty cool. The food is presented well and arrives at the table relatively fast. Taste is good, no complaints. You get what you pay for, and the prices aren't high. My confusion is with the look and ambiance of this place: it looks rather like a bar with food than a proper restaurant. That is due to its cleanliness. And if it is a restaurant then it needs some maintenance. The bathrooms especially: scary bad! Just AWEFUL!

Tortugas is, hands down, our favorite Collegeville restaurant ! Not only is the food top notch, but find the employees and owner to be very welcoming and friendly. I don't know if there has ever been a time where we've walked in and NOT been greated with a geniune smile and immediate seating or an apology for our 5 or 10 minute wait and an immaculate table with chips and salsa waiting. I would say on average, we eat here once a week. I tend to order the same thing time after time while the Warden has tried many different things and short of an allergic reaction to fish that the Warden didn't realize that she had, our meals have ALWAYS been delicious. Also...an 1800 Margarita tends to go well with anything on the menu and has become my ground zero for my impending alcoholism and possible rehab.

I am grateful that Jeni's was very careful when it came to food allergies, as they went as far as to open up new ice cream containers for me to make sure there was no cross contamination. I felt a lot safer here than I usually do at other ice cream places. There was a large variety of flavors and they were pretty good too.

This is the spot for gluten free and health conscious type peeps. They do bagels, slinach pies, cookies and some pastries. Their goodies are also sold at Rollin' Oats. Tasty stuff. Various sliced bread offerings. Also some nutra bar and wrap type entities. Date coconut rolls. A cool slot to check out and pretty tasty offerings altboigh not as crusty (in a good way) as my fav.bakeries that serve up golden brown baked goods with plenty of gluten.

TRASH Food is straight garbage. If you like this place, you obviously have bad taste buds, & when you walk in it smells like straight up SH!T. Like the food isn't clean, I damn near threw up my food. Stay away from this dump. Waste of money, time, & effort. On a scale trash-fresh it's trash. Majority of the lobster in the tanks were dead, then on top of that they don't clean the shrimp it still has dirt in the food after they steamed them... grossssssssss!!!!!!!!!

Newtown needed this restaurant. The food is fantastic. They cater to gluten free and are aware of avoiding cross contamination. Try the gluten free naan with just about anything on the menu and you'll be happy. I frequent this place more than I should, and am never disappointed. If what you're looking for is simply great Indian cuisine, without any of the fluff, you can't go wrong here.

First Impressions: The entry looks quite upscale, prompting my partner to feel underdressed (he wasn't). Inside, the tall ceilings and wood panelling continued the impression with comfortable, inviting booths. There were a few ubiquitous pop culture posters on the walls; not enough to detract from the setting, but enough that I found them amusing. Can't find a casual restaurant nowadays that doesn't sport Marilyn's image. Atmosphere: While the decor was pleasant enough, the TV screens everywhere ruined the general effect. I don't mind them in a casual bar, but I don't understand their purpose in a dining room. The background music was decidedly Muzak, but it was quiet, so I didn't mind. Even as the place filled up, the sound level remained reasonable and we couldn't hear the conversations of other patrons. Menu: Reasonable selection for omnis and vegs alike with gluten-free pasta available for a surcharge (of course...). Veg items are not marked, but the server assured me that they could work with most of the dishes. Prices were comparable to other casual restaurants. Wine list: Not particularly varied, but enough for the average person to find accompaniment for their meal. Food: We started with the Arancini, deep-fried risotto balls. The menu didn't mention that they contained mushrooms; I wouldn't have ordered them had it said so. They came on a bed of wilted lettuce with a dollop of a delicious sauce on each. They weren't bad at all, if a little boring. And I hate mushrooms. My partner had this to say about his Penne Polo Alfredo ($17.95): "It was thin - milky rather than creamy. The pasta was cooked appropriately, but there wasn't much flavour and I had to work to coat each piece with sauce. I coulda got better at Boston Pizza." For my part, the Cannelloni ($15.95) was certainly palatable, if a little bland. I appreciated the sparing use of cheese in the filling, but the shells were over-cooked and the sauce lacked interest. For the price, I'd've been much happier at Sicilian Kitchen. Service: Our server was quite gracious, but she was also very busy. Perhaps they hadn't expected the rush? I'm not sure, but, well... We were prepared to order dessert, but it took so long for her to return to our table that we gave up and paid our bill instead.
