She also ignored my request for the 5oz glass of wine, neglected to clarify the size required by my partner, and brought us 8oz each. I didn't quibble with the bill, as we did drink the wine, but I do prefer a smaller glass with my meal. All in all, my partner and I agreed that, while we left full, we certainly weren't satisfied. I do appreciate the coupon with which we paid for my meal. I wouldn't've cared to pay full price for what we got. We likely won't return.

Gourmet Pizza Company offers hearty portions of gourmet toppings on their pizzas. There are tons of options on the menu for vegans or people with gluten allergies. Personally, I'm not a big fan of the pizza. Something is off about the pizza combinations. A lot of the flavors don't mesh well for me. I think the pizza at Gourmet Pizza is just a little too healthy.... I don't want a ton of gourmet veggies or fancy sauce on my pizza! I just want some good, thin crust NY style cheese pizza. My husband loves the Chicken and Spinach White Pizza, but in my opinion it seems undercooked and I don't love big hunks of chicken on my pizza. On a positive note, the location is great and the service is friendly. If you are looking for a healthier and fancier pizza this is your spot!

This is by far the worst burrito I have ever had in my entire life. While waiting in line, I had second thoughts because of how messy it was behind the counter. I should have stepped away and started running had I known what was next. This was not an ordinary burrito. This burrito was made not fresh but with cigarettes. I took one bite and instantly wanted to vomit. It tasted like I was eating a cigarette combined with soggy disgusting mystery ingredients. Baja "Fresh" more like Baja poop. Don't ever ever eat here.

My brother sold me at best pad thai in Nashville (or so they advertise). Super cute interior - very bright and fun. Our server was perfectly charming and attentive. For an app we ordered the fresh roll. Amazingly tasty, but small portion - there were three of us and definitely not big enough for us to share. For our entrees, I had to order pad thai. They clearly advertise the fact that their pad thai is likely not what you would eat (meaning more traditional than the usual Americanized pad thai) - not served with rice noodles (although it is an option). I liked it, but didn't love it, and would likely not go with best pad thai in Nashville.... but then again I don't live in Nashville soooo... Biggest mistake though was ordering the homemade gelato. I think gelato, I think creamy. They think gelato, you get two scoops of flavored ice (think snow cone). Very disappointing. Overall, we agreed that it wasn't bad, but that we probably wouldn't make it our first choice of places to go. note - very gluten-free friendly!

Unfortunately Big Apple Pizza & Subs has closed down. They have moved to Sacramento to pursue the start up of their gluten free line of frozen pizza as well as move their pizza and sub shop. Big Apple Pizza & Subs will be sorely missed in the Reno/Sparks area. Where will we all go now for such fantastic pizza and fantastic people?

I used to frequent this place with my friends late at night, but not anymore. I ordered some cheese fries with bacon, when it came out, the cheese was cold and congealed. For whatever reason, I decided to taste one of the fries, and found a string used to tie meat together COOKED INTO THE CHEESE. I was entirely disgusted...literally almost threw up. The cook came out and offered 3 times to cook me something else, and seemed offended when I said no. Do not go here. It's too expensive, and not to mention, who knows what might have touched your food before it came to you.

Herbies is a great place for both a semi-casual or a fancy meal. They have a fairly extensive gluten free menu, and they seem to know how to avoid cross-contamination. If you are looking for cheap(er) options, then the flatbread is fantastic (and much cheaper than Pi across the street). The Balaburger, house salad, and french onion soup are also excellent. I love onions, and I never knew how good french onion soup can be. I would come here just for the soup. If you are able to spend more money, the filet and scallops do not disappoint. I do wish they had a gluten free complimentary bread or appetizer, as well as some dessert options.

Cupcakes. One word that could make almost anyone smile. Dropped by this cupcakery after eating at a joint next door. We were intrigued by the gluten free and paleo items. When we walked in, it felt a little odd as the lady who worked there had a stare that made me think I must've had something on my nose. Quite uncomfortable but we went with it. She did get through the basic service questions and we got our cupcakes. We picked up a vanilla cupcake and an apple cinnamon one. So far, we have tried the apple cinnamon. It was soft and moist, great texture. My only complaint was the frosting. Holy cow there was a ton of sugar. It made me actually cringe a bit and I proceeded to remove it. The vanilla is still sitting in the box but I'm sure we'll give that one a try later on. $3/cupcake. Although I think cupcakes are way overpriced nowadays, I get it. The display was a little odd. I'd rather see cupcakes in a glass case rather than those funky racks. It was still easy to navigate though to find which flavors we wanted. If you look to the left, there are the gluten free cupcakes. To the right, you'll find the paleo options. Not bad. 3 stars...with a stare.

There are two Boston Pizza's in Sherwood Park. One on Broadmoor Blvd off of Baseline (just before the Costco) and the other off of Wye Road. This restaurant was the second to open after the Wye Road branch being open for many years. I would like to say it is second to none, but that wouldn't be accurate - I would say it is second to the Wye Road location. This branch has been riddled with service issues ever since it opened a few years ago. I'm not sure why, but I have heard a lot of complaints about inconsistent service. My experience has confirmed that as well. Sometimes the service is just fine and other times you are left hungry and annoyed. In contrast, the one off Wye almost always has great service. That is not to say the service is atrocious, not by a long shot. We keep going back for the pizza - especially the gluten free pizza. It is not on the menu but just specify that you want and which toppings. There have been occasions when it has arrived a bit overdone (black around the edges) so I might consider asking a head of time to make sure it isn't too overdone or crispy. While the hubs is gnawing on his GF pizza, I was enjoying a regular Mediterranean pizza. This is a great pizza choice and one I wish I had ordered earlier. Artichokes, spinach, pesto sauce and sun-dried tomatoes make for a very nummy combination. The crust was perfect for this type of pizza, nice and thin and crispy, without being crumbly or flakey. Overall, I would go back because it is Boston Pizza.

I do not get the hype of this place. The whole feel just seemed dirty to me. I think the reasoning for me was the cook. She came out and was talking, I saw her wipe her nose once, and then had one of those mouths with spit in the corners when she talked. Not very appetizing. For me, that is what made me a bit put off with the whole place. I will say though, my gluten-free friends really enjoy it, and I guess it is good there is a place in Nashville which caters to those needs. Not my cup of tea, however!
I personally do not see a difference between this place and Chipotle however I do enjoy both! My go to is the chicken bowl with black beans, they are courteous about food allergies.

Good food; bad service! This place was recommended for brunch, and EVERYONE must know about it, because the place was packed! They told us it'd be an hour, to an hour and 15 minutes for a table. Luckily, they take your name and cell phone number, and they text you when your table is ready. So, we left and came back. We were in town, on vacation, so we went and visited the Grand Ole Opry, in the meantime. We got back, after just over an hour, and our table still wasn't ready. We waited about an hour and a half, total, before we were seated. By now, we're starving! The menu is small and on the pricey side, providing upscale cuisine. I ordered the Pepper & Squashes omelette. It's an omelette with bell peppers and a mix of zucchini & squash, topped with a mushroom relish. It's served with a side of their signature White Trash Hash. I inquired what exactly this White Trash Hash is. Described as a hashbrown casserole with onions & cheese, then it's baked and topped with scallions. I asked if I could get it without cheese. I was told 'No.' The waitress said it's pre-made and that's how it comes. I told the waitress that I am lactose intolerant, and I can't have cheese. She reiterated, 'That's how it comes.' I asked if they serve regular hashbrowns, or some other kind of potatoes that I could have instead. She said, 'No. We don't have any other potatoes.' Ridiculous! Is this really how you treat people with food allergies? Because it seemed like I was being told, "too bad". They were not accomodating, whatsoever. I asked what my options are, for a side. She said I could have toast or a biscuit. Then she said, 'You could have french fries.' I thought to myself.. Didn't you just say that you don't have any other potatoes? Are french fries not potatoes? Well, not that I really wanted french fries with my omelette, I still opted to go with the french fries. We watched, eagerly, as servers delivered food to other tables. After all, we're still starving! Then a server comes to us with 2 entrees. We are a table of four. Two people just got their food, while two sit and wait. Then, a second server brings the third person their food, while I'm left to wait. One of my friends shared a few bites of her brunch with me, while I waited. She had ordered the Singapore Stir Fry, and it was good; I enjoyed it. Finally, a third server brings my food. It was good; just weird to eat french fries with an omelette.

I'm Greek and was also born in Ohio, so Skyline and I are basically twinsies! That being said, I had to give it a try. While I'm really more of a sweet/spicy chili kind of person, I respected that this chili was more savory and cinnamon-y on account of its origins (my mom ALWAYS puts it in her red sauces and it's delish.) We both tried it over spaghetti (mine with a mountain of cheese!) and it was a filling lunch. I thought it was A-Okay, but my boyfriend loved it; he even said so with his face covered in sauce. The service at this location was impeccable and they were very careful with our allergies. We ordered to go and they separated every little thing (without us even asking) to make sure we would have the best experience! Can't beat that. I'll be back to check out the chili dogs!

Twice! Two times too many I bought a large bag of new dry dog food at this store, only to have insects crawling around the kibble and the moths flying out and latching on to the walls of my house. It was gross. I've bought bags at the grocery store and other Pet stores, and this has never happened. I believe a grain insect came into contact with the product, which can occur in any food product in the marketplace. Grain insects can infiltrate almost any container, except glass or metal with a tight fitting lid. During production at the dog food factory, all ingredients are subjected to high temperatures and pressures, which renders them free of pathogens and insects when the product leaves our facility. So, even though this store is conveniently in my neighborhood I will not return! Interestingly, I find it odd that Concord Pet will take back the insect infested bag, leaving the opened bag by the cash register to contaminate all the other products in the store.

My boyfriend and I came here on whim, as our first choice lunch restaurant was booked and it was too cold to aimlessly wander. We came here as Yelp recommended, with high reviews. If I had only ordered the burgers, I would have given Bareburger a higher rating, as my county fair burger (with bison meat) was really delicious! I was excited to try something new, and didn't know what to choose as the menu had bison, elk, and a bunch of other different types of fascinating burgers. My boyfriend "built his own burger" with a great beef patty and delicious gluten-free bun. I love how the entire store is organic/natural, GMO-free, and had many vegan and GF options! However, after scarfing down my burger (which was really small for its price--but I guess it's expected for an "all natural" burger"), I ordered a cocktail and sweet fries. The Rachel Carson looked delicious--with homemade lemonade, rosemary, blackberry, and rum--but came out full of ice and really weak. The sweet fries were underwhelming as well, with really soggy interiors and mediocre sauces. The service was a bit uncomfortable as well, as our waiter didn't seem to know what to do and was pretty awkward....

when I told the waitress I'm vegan, she came back with a manager who presented me a full list of allergens. Ordering online is easy for take out. most of the dishes are VERY salty, might want to request extra rice.

Food was good. The waitress seemed hesitant to ask the cook to make a meal gluten-free because he sometimes gets mad when that ask that. That was kind of weird, right? Overall, the wait staff was attentive and friendly. I got the eggs Benedict breakfast (I am not sure what the name of the meal is on the menu). The poached eggs were amazing, two of the best I have ever had. And, the cucumber basil lemonade was perfect. One negative: The veggie eggs Benedict was a little vinegary. I would give it another try though.

I want to like Luke. I want to LOVE Luke. But, every time I dine here, I am beyond disappointed. My first experience, way back when, was for happy hour, and the oysters were pretty good. Now that I often stay in the area when I'm in town, Luke is one of the few restaurants within walking distance with my hopes and dreams for a decent experience still dangling on a string. I'm so determined to make it work that whenever I'm in town, I usually eat here at least once hopping that it's me, but alas, it's most definitely them... On my most recent trip, I actually stayed at the Hilton St. Charles, and on my last night in town I was looking to not have to change into real people clothes, and instead get some food to go so I could eat in my room. I got a menu at the bar, and asked a bunch of questions. The waitress didn't know a lot of the answers, but she graciously said she'd check with the kitchen. Awesome. I wound up ordered an appetizer with shrimp and then a side of rosemary potatoes. For some reason I was really in the mood for potatoes... A little while after I paid, someone from the kitchen came up to the bar and said that they could not make the shrimp dish I ordered gluten free (even though the waitress said that the kitchen staff said they could). I was instead given the option to switch to a crab dish. Without a menu in front of me, the kitchen worker explained what the dish was. I agreed. Shrimp. Crab. I love both. The kitchen guy went back, and then the waitress told me it would be a slight up charge. Ok... I wasn't all that happy with this, but I understood. I handed over my credit card, and she redid the order. I waited a while for the order to come out (ordered to go), and just when I was about to leave, someone from the kitchen came out and said, "You forgot your fries." I didn't order fries. Apparently, they all forgot to mention that the crab dish came with fries. While this is not a terrible thing, it is pretty obnoxious that they clearly saw that I ordered potatoes, and didn't think to mention that the dish came with fries. Couldn't they have said something so I could then cancel the potato order? Or maybe they could have eliminated the fries and not up-charged me for the changed dish? The whole thing left a bad taste in my mouth, and that was before I even tried the food! I had way too many starchy dishes (one of which was thrown away...) The food: -The fries were over salted and wilted, not crisp -The potatoes were ok -The crab was tasteless. There was no seasoning whatsoever. It's like they just through the thing in the fryer. They get points for convenience, a nice location downtown, and pretty interior.

Jones is cozy. I think that's what they're going for, and they've succeeded. So well, in fact, that even watching a dude dressed like Santa Claus vomit into a trashcan outside the window seemed somehow quaint and homey. I generally don't go for the uber-girly drinks, but the pb&j martini is The Yum. I felt like a little kid lapping at the peanut butter and sipping down the purple stuff. The food is tasty, too. It's like Cracker Barrel, except less bigoted and way more delicious and better prepared.

How can I describe how fucking disgusting this place is. I ordered the Shoyu Ramen with chicken Katsu on the side and shrimp fried rice. It was the nastiest shit I've ever tasted. First of all the ramen broth was like warm and smelled like some type of rotten pig meat and dirty Tripe. It smelled so bad it made me want to vomit. I tried to taste it but when I did I almost threw up. It was the worst ramen dish I've ever had in my life. Possibly the nastiest meal I ever tasted because of the disgusting pungent smell of pig shit. It smelled like shit... and the broth was cloudy as if it they just threw in a Bouillon to give the porky broth a taste. The should inform people that the broth is cooked with pork for those who can't eat it. I love pork but this wasn't fresh at all. The fried rice was dry and flavorless. The rice tastes like it was precooked so they threw it back in the pan and reheated it because it had that hard texture like it was leftover fried rice. I didn't bother eating that either because the pork they used for the soup broth was used for the rice and I was at the point of puking. That taste was stuck in my Mouth for hours. I wasted 15 bucks on the food and should have waited in line to go to Terakawa Ramen which I did right after. If you want real Ramen that's fresh and delicious please go there it's right around the corner.

This place is gross bartenders suck,walk around half naked and believe me it's nothing no one wants to see,can't get a drink ,place smells like urine and vomit.Cockroaches crawling across the bar disgusting

The gluten free organic beef burger is a frozen patty and had the texture of rubber. I took one bite and knew right away even though the waitress denied that it was. The manager who came and spoke with us later confirmed that it was a frozen patty. The waitress left the gross burger on the table while the kitchen was cooking another one. She assured us she would bring out the new beef patty when it was cooked....huh..? Lol she expected us to transfer the new burger onto the bun on our tiny table. I told her we didnt have enough room to complete that job. Lol. So she took the plate back and they put the new burger onto the now soggy bun which was caked in BBQ sauce & i specifically asked for the BBQ sauce to be put on the burger when it was cooking and not on the bun. The manager spoke to us, took the gross burger off our bill & said he'd cook the burger himself next time. There won't be a next time. I ate here a few years ago & the blue cheese infused Delux burger was delicious. Why the heck would they change their signature burger? Restaurants seem to build a name bc theyre initially high quality and then start cutting corners and cheaping out. Their "efficiency" & cost cuts make their business suffer. The quality at this place is not what it started out as. However thr chicken burger and fries were good. But its a burger joint..? They should have the best burgers in town. The Burger Joint (BJ Joint) near 91st is waaay better and its locally owned & everything is handmade.

Yall the place has so much potential. But the vomit (yes vomit ) rags that were left in our *check in* clean room were enough to gross me out, until our daughter noticed diarrhea splatter on the not so cleaned toilet. Literally 5 hours later, after notifying management. And we are still waiting on housekeeping to rectify.. opryland you could be amazing but you never are, and at 400$ a night this is unacceptable.

Five guys is always a solid choice in my opinion. This location is no dofferent. I have celiac disease and they are wonderful about cross contamination. I have never been glutened in the many times I've eaten at this location. I so appreciate being able to go to a normal fast food restaurant with my friends and being able to eat gluten free. It really makes a difference for me. Employees here are always friendly. Service is always reasonably fast.

This is probably the all around worst dining experience I've ever had. Poor service, long wait for food (almost 1 1/2 hours) cold food and a chicken breast that was pink and raw in the middle. My daughter-in-law cannot eat gluten and our server was clearly annoyed when asked for a gluten free menu or gluten free options on the regular menu. She was unable to find any options that were GF and finally suggested a salad and eventually a grilled chicken breast from the kids menu. The "salad" was just arugula-no dressing-and it was accompanied by a small amount of cold, undercooked grilled chicken. We waited for an unreasonable amount of time (1 hour, 20 minutes) without the waitress even checking on us). I think a certain amount of grace needs to be granted to a new restaurant (new staff, new menu, new processes), but this restaurant will not survive without a dramatic turnaround. Really disappointing: we won't be going back.

Usually not one to review food places but I couldn't help it with this particular place. Their advertised photos are not even close to what they make. The shakes are so poorly made. The girl who made my drink used the blender she previously used to make another customers drink, which was not the same flavour as mine. She was scratching her nose with her hands and shirt while she was making our drinks and said her nose allergies were acting up today. She didn't wash her hands. The place was not close to being clean. There was trash and banana peels all over the place. She didn't use measurements to make our drinks, she examined with her eyes and decided on her own wether or not she should keep adding one ingredient or the other. This is the worst place I have ever been to, hands down. It's a complete waste of money. Not satisfied at all. Never again!

Thank God my inner hipster scoffed at the idea of brunch at a chain this morning. This is a family owned and operated joint. The love and devotion put in to every item I've tried is plainly apparent. The walls are covered in art made by family members. Every customer is smiling and happy. The atmosphere is genuine and welcoming. I was lucky enough to skip the 15 minute because I am flying solo today. I had the West Gemantown Eggs Benedict. I cannot emphasize how perfectly they prepared this dish. I'm actually considering going to the bathroom and vomiting so I can have another helping. I wasn't going to get a Bloody Mary, but they make it with sake so I basically had no choice. If every non-choice was so good as this Bloody Mary, nobody would give a shit about free will. The coffee is good. Not like Dunkin Donuts good... because that's not good, that's garbage dishwater with a bunch of sugary toppings. This is coffee made for people who love the delicate, slightly bitter joy that is an unadulterated cup of pure black java. I've ordered a side of the bananas foster pancake as a desert for my brunch because I'm a special kind of glutton. It is heaven in my mouth. It's like angels stayed up all night making me breakfast and they finished right before this was brought to my table.

Arrived for an early bird dinner, restaurant almost empty. Took over 8 minutes to get a waitress to our table. All staff standing around talking with each other, manager included. Special order, due to food allergies made our server "roll her eyes" at us twice. Been 12 minutes and we are still eaiting for drinks. Blech.

A lively atmosphere and a sweet time! A bunch of frozen yogurt flavors to choose from, and a wholllleee lot of toppings. All the yogurt flavors are gluten free, you just have to be careful with the toppings for cross contamination, and have a good knowledge of what candies/sprinkles/syrups are gluten free. ALL the flavors are delicious, and a great summer treat!

Moving to a new community gives opportunity to explore new places. Being gluten free can make new places to eat a challenge. So pleased to give New Day 5 stars. I had grilled cheese and tomato soup and was able to enjoy without the fear of the dreaded cross contamination. Food was tasty and even my non gluten free husband enjoyed his gluten free meatball sandwich. He said it tastes like real bread. I finished off my visit with a carrot cake muffin. Very very good. I would highly recommend New Day and will make regular visits here.

To put it simply, I wasn't impressed. I could tell none of our group was, but no one wanted to outright say it. And it's a shame too because I think the place has potential -- the menu items sound good in theory. The place has a neat vibe to it and the outdoor seating works well. The service is very good and the server was friendly and helpful. We all enjoyed our shakes, although the boozy ones for $10 to $11 seem overpriced for what you get. Which really seems like a theme at this place. The burger experience was similar. There are quite a few on the menu and overall the presentation of them is good. I like that you can choose the meat (beef, pork, chicken, bison, veggie). I ordered one of their two face-off burgers (smokey, jalapenos, some other spicy things). The burgers themselves are about $10 and then sides are extra. We ordered fries to split for another $4. They come with various fancy sauces and ketchups. When the burger came I was pretty disappointed. They're fairly small, particularly given the price (which is funny, because some of the Yelper uploaded photos show much larger burgers than I got). Mine at least held together, though. Another in our group dared to get the gluten-free bun, which was already in 4 pieces when the plate was first set down. It only got worse from there, the burger pretty much fell apart too. We've seen enough gluten-free bread to know this could be done better. I guess beyond that the biggest travesty was out BLAND the burger was. I can't even stress how little flavor it had. I had some of my wife's too, it wasn't just mine. I've had flavorful beef before, this wasn't it. And oddly, despite all of the fancy supposedly spicy toppings it had... none of them helped. I would have been happy with the prices if food actually was flavorful and worth the effort they clearly put into the actual recipes (many of which sounded very interesting)... But the end result in our cases was bland, boring and over priced. There's better burger places out there, some charging half of what you'll spend at Range. I might go back if I feel like a shake and am nearby, but otherwise? Nah.

Ever been to Portland? Tired Hands Fermentaria, the expanded version of the original brewery just 2 blocks away, is a full on testament to the IPA centric west coast hipster vibe. A little too much for my taste- but the friendly service and clientele both wear well. They taken the IPA recipe to new heights with their beer "milkshakes" - created using lactose sugar to give these crazy varietals that never repeat themselves a milk Stoudt mouthfeel. They also produce an IPA In which the bitterness aspect has been removed but the formal and citrus notes remain. Very interesting. I have to say I prefer the original brewery's wider range of styles, but if your a hophead, this is a good choice.

I Eek! at writing one star reviews. But this quick trip away deserves it. Checked in late on a Thursday, no problems. Strangely, though, front desk had zero recommendations on a solid sports bar. Interesting for such a sports-crazy town. The worst of it came the next morning when getting ready for the day. The inside shower curtain liner had black smudges/specks that have to be either mold/mildew, dirt or a Sharpie. Gross. Mental note made to not get near the curtain or touch any walls. Easy enough. Then came the drying portion. Pull off a hand towel from the rack and *fortunately* open before touching/using only to see vomit all over the towel. Beeline to the phone. Informed them of the Vomit Towel and the Questionable Curtain, which received a few "I'm so sorry"'s and "We'll be right up"'s. When we got back later that day, the offending Vomit Towel was replaced, but with two towels that weren't freshly folded, and thus were not used. Unfortunately the curtain remained. Pillows were a bust. No free WiFi/Internet Connection. *Generally* functional TV. Not what I expect in a "Luxury" King room. I'll stick with the old reliable brands and known chains. The pluses: Keurig machine and good coffee; location.

Ok so came back and got the pizza sub on gluten free bread, 12" sub. The sub was awesome but it's $FOURTEEN dollars. For a sub that has marinara, cheese and pepperoni. I get that G-free is more expensive but common.

I looked forward to the opening of this new local bakery. I had spotted them at Wiregrass at the market a couple times, but hadn't tried them until their recent opening. Their shop is quaint and nice. Although, truthfully my first impression was it was as loud as a daycare with kids running rampantly and screaming to the top of their lungs. I really wanted to leave, but I did want to check them out! They have cupcakes, coffee, cookies, cakes, cannolis! I picked out the tres leches cake and the rainbow cake bars. The rainbow cake bars are in layers of an almond cake, raspberry filling and chocolate cake. I have never tasted anything like it, and I loved it! I think next time I will order the gluten free version and try that. The tres leches cake was okay. No biggie to me. I think I'm hooked on the rainbow cakes.

Tried a gluten free pizza. It was really good but I was nervous to eat it because the red sauce was spread onto my crust with the same spoon and from the same container as regular pizza - major cross contamination issue. I was also concerned about the pizza slicer being reused and therefore contaminated also. So far no problems. Normally I wouldn't have taken this chance but with traveling I had no other options.

Ehhhhh there are a few things in life that should not be messed with. Ketchup is one of them. The homemade tomato ketchup was less then desirable. The gluten free bun was more of a biscuit not a bun. The decor was nice but cold inside. Nashville your music is awesome ...... Food ..... Not so much

Found a place that makes me feel like I'm back in Seattle: world weary, edging on annoyed service (no extra charge for the eye-roll) but fair trade, free range, gluten free beans! So feel good about yourself. Drip coffee was fine (didn't have any espresso drinks) if unremarkable. The space is really cute: nice outdoor seating, big sturdy tables, and seems like a genuine neighborhood third place. People saying hi to each other; students studying. Also great bike parking out front. WiFi was dial-up slow so not a good place (for me) to work, but we'll probably give it a few more tries. No music playing when I was there. Neither a good or bad thing, but kinda unusual.

We asked for 3 pies. Got them an hr and a half later... They were not the way we ordered them. Then we needed more so we asked for 3 more and 3 sodas and they send they would send ranch free bc of the discrepancy. Another 1.5 hrs later and we got pizza, no ranch, and the guy drove off without giving us the darn sodas. He simply forgot them. So then 45 minutes later we get the sodas and still no ranch. And we asked for one gluten free pizza but they don't carry it at this location!

I'm sorry, St. Louis, I just can't get into Ted Drewes. I don't know what frozen custard is, but it ain't ice cream. It's some sort of melted ice cream stew mixed with overwhelmingly rich and sweet toppings. This was my second visit, and instead of the concrete with which I was unsatisfied last time, I got a sundae. I could not distinguish a difference. This visit I got a sundae that had a "brownie" (it seemed to be raw?) and a ton of chocolate syrup. After two bites I was done. It was sickeningly sweet and filled my stomach in a queasy way. I don't know how anyone can eat an entire sundae or concrete without vomiting. I don't get the appeal. I just want a cup of hard ice cream!

I have not been to this particular Wendy's in years before last night. It was in a handy location on a night that we needed dinner quick and cheap as well as having something gluten free for me. When we arrived, there was a guy already eating and no one else other than several workers were in the restaurant. For some reason, we still had to wait for several minutes for them to stop chatting (even though two of them made definite eye-contact with me). Finally, one of the workers stepped over to take our order. I thought that they must all be working on something for the drive-through, since they looked a little like they were actually doing something since they were messing with equipment and such as they chatted, but when they stopped chatting and one came over to take my order, it became clear that their delay had nothing to do with the drive through. They just were taking their time getting to me apparently. I was sorry that I could not understand what they were saying so I had no way of knowing if it was work related or not. It was a good thing that your order shows up on a screen in front of you as you are ordering so I was able to make significant corrections on my relatively small order three times. My order was done correctly after my corrections, so that was nice. It most definitely was not anywhere near my best Wendy's experiences, but unfortunately wasn't my worse either. They were nice and the place was clean, but somethings could definitely improve.

My quest for Indy's best tacos takes me to the place that's all the rage, Indy Tacos. With a name like Indy Tacos, I suppose you know what you are getting yourself into. The location certainly takes me out of my Carmel comfort zone. My partner and I ordered 4 tacos (together, not each. That would be considered obesity to many). I got the fish and the carne asada (steak). The fish was a REEL CATCH. No, really. It was super tasty. I don't know what the fish is and I sure know it's not fresh. But the mixture of the lightly breaded shrimp with the slaw on top was super flavorful. This isn't a San Diego fish taco - this is a street fish taco. The steak taco was fine and the salsa was a helpful addition. I went with the green as red generally scares me. As a read head, you've got to know when there is too much of a good thing so I steer clear of red food. He got the mango chicken and while I don't recall his specific sentiment, but I don't remember medically induced vomit or an impromptu quinceanera so we will assume it was average. The staff are awesome, plenty of parking, and Jarritos for all (assuming you pay, which they most certainly encourage). Best so far in Indy if you count legit, real-deal Mexican taqueria (which rules out Bakersfield).

We were in a mood for burgers and got a recommendation to go here from a Lyft driver that apparently worked there. My fiancé can't eat wheat and they had gluten free buns so it sounded perfect. Everything seemed good going in. The menu has a lot of options for different patties and buns. The selection of house burger recipes was pretty good. I ended up getting one that was on a pretzel roll with bacon, cheese, dijon and an onion ring. So we waited and waited. The bartender tells us that it should be any minute, realizing that things were taking a while. Finally after about 30 minutes the bartender informed us that there had been a screw up with the printer in the kitchen but they were now cooking our food. About 5-10 minutes later the food showed up and it was pretty disappointing. The bun I had was so dry that I actually double checked to make sure i didn't get the gluten-free bun. The bun was small to lend the appearance of having been served a large amount of food and it made the burger a giant mess to eat. The bisson patties were way overcooked and dry. I recognize that bison is a drier meat but if you put it on the menu you should cook it right. In the end they gave us 10% off of the bill for the delay without asking for it. Overall though if I'm going to a burger place I expect the burgers to be pretty good. Not so much.

Its subway. This establishment is really a hit or miss depending on who is making the subs. I have had two completely different situations here. One was terrible toppings. It looked like someone just vomited on a sandwich and charged me $8 for it. The other time everything was in good portions and the sandwich was great but they charged me for the wrong one. I would say just go to IV deli mart and get a sandwich there.

UPDATE*** Received a call from the manager and was given a gift card for the amount spent on the soup and calamari. I went back with my boyfriend and we had a completely different experience! We both had pasta dishes that were to die for. The service was great, as usual. ***** Went to London about a month ago with my boyfriend. We sat outside, and had a really nice waiter, food was okay, beer was good. Went home and threw up all night long. Had the watermelon soup and the calamari, and I am 100% sure I got sick from one of those things. My boyfriend didn't try any of mine, so he was just up all night listening to me get sick. NOT FUN. I called and was told I would get refunded, but I never got a call back from the manager. Disappointing.

I am torn on this post. I will give you the low down on Kelp S Tampa. I have eaten here twice for lunch, great service each time, good food, and great prices. My sister also enjoyed both visits. Gonna get negative so skip the next paragraph if you want the nuts and bolts. Tonight the staff/customer ratio was 11/16 and they could not keep up read below. We waited over 5 min for greeting, over 10 for our drinks, and had a roll made with the wrong ingredients then told they were correct (you can see the difference between shrimp and fish especially cooked solid vs flakey). Normally I would not post all of this but we sent it back only to have the chef say it was shrimp then we opened it up and it was clearly not shrimp and they remade the roll (unsat for allergies). Charged us for edamame we never received and forgot our last roll. I chalk this up to bad service or bad training. Either way I am docking 2 's for service because food and environment were great. 1) Most competitive sushi prices outside if Publix 2) Small/Tasty lunch menu 3)Outdoor neighborhood feel and saw tons of people getting takeout. Thats how to do Kelp!

Good food. HORRIFIC customer service! Owner Jon Smee launchd into a loud, belligerent tirade when I politely questioned the sauce that was added to my daughter's fish in error, after ordering it plain due to her severe food allergies. My little girl was devastated and in tears at the horrible things he said right in front of her. His employees were obviously mortified at his behavior and apologized profusely. I can only imagine how he treats them.

I can see why a lot of people like this place. It's small, the ambience is very "hole-in-the-wall", and it makes you feel like you've discovered a nice little gem in the restaurant world in Nashville. In my opinion, it's a bit overrated. Now this is coming from a Laotian girl, (for those who don't know, Laos is next to Thailand) and the cuisine is very similar. So my entire body is constructed of food from Southeast Asia, and this place just doesn't do it for me. It SEEMS hole-in-the-wall, but there seems to be a lot of trendiness that makes it feel inauthentic to me. And from what I've been told, The Smiling Elephant is supposed to have the "most authentic" Thai food in Nashville. When I arrived at the restaurant, there was already a wait, which was no surprise because the place is quite small, and it made me excited to see that so many people were waiting to eat there. I was seated fairly quickly, and as I flipped through the menu, I noticed the lower-carb, gluten-free, and vegetarian options--which is good for people with those dietary restrictions because it's not common for many Thai places--and I was familiar with most of the dishes. So my date and I ordered the Fresh Rolls as an appetizer and the Pad-kee-mao and BBQ Curry Chicken for entrees. When the Fresh Rolls came out, I was super disappointed just looking at them. The rolls I was looking at were filled 60% with carrots, and I was confused. Usually the fresh spring rolls are filled with shrimp or some kind of pork, and I knew that their version was vegetarian, but I've had vegetarian spring rolls before, and they usually have more herbs, lettuce, and vermicelli noodles. They came pre sliced which looked nice, but made it very hard to pull the cut sections apart. The sauce it came with was kind of bland, and the chunk of shredded carrots in the center made it very hard to chew and swallow. It was just dry, and the caramelized radish made it way too sweet. I ordered my Pad-kee-mao extra spicy, like native Thai spicy, and it definitely was not so. When I asked the waiter for some chili sauce or Sriracha sauce, he brought me sweet chili sauce and chili flakes and told me it was all they had. What kind of Thai restaurant doesn't give you Sriracha?! I mean, usually they have that stuff already on the table. Also, I didn't enjoy the bits of kaffir lime leaves all throughout my noodles. Usually those things are taken out after the flavor is infused, like a bay leaf. And those hard little bits of leaves were not pleasant to chew. The green bean noodles were...interesting. A different texture I'm just not used to. I prefer the fresh rice noodles. The BBQ curry, according to my date, was just okay. It was fine to eat, but it lacked vegetables or something else to add to the dish. It was just shredded chicken on some rice. It sounded better on the menu than it tasted, and he said he probably wouldn't order it again. I wanted this place to be good so badly. I really did. It's close to my house, so I thought I'd be able to come often, but I know of better Thai places in Nashville. If you're looking for a cute little Thai place and don't care about the authenticity too much, then this is the place. Unfortunately, it just didn't meet my expectations for good Thai food, but then again, my expectations are pretty high.

What a joke. Here's our story of one of the worst experiences I have had lately. We decided to try out something new. I'm the first to arrive as parking is a nightmare on Whyte so I enter the establishment and stand awkwardly waiting for the man behind the counter to acknowledge my presence. I've never been here before so after 5 minutes I ask if it's self seating or what the process. He tells me grab a menu and seat myself and then come and order. That's fine by me, next time at least acknowledge me maybe? Grab a seat. We decide to order The Veggievore ($12), The Dirtiest ($10) and The Completo ($8). With a large order of Asiago Fries ($9) to share as a group. Along with a How Bah Dah ($9) and Ski Apline ($9) milkshake and one of the Minttobe ($9) . We walk to the counter as a group to place our order. They only have one hot dog left and no veggivore so we can't get two of our three choices. One of the people I was with was a vegetarian so she now only had one option to choose from, a generic veggie burger. My partner ends up with the Recession Buster burgers and I get The Dirtiest. Then when my veggie friend goes to order, he says he isn't sure he has a veggie burger either. That is a huge issue as we can't eat there if they don't. We tell him to check right away and considered cancelling our order and going across the street to the Next Act, which we should've. Then fellow returns and tells us that he does so we return to our table and wait...and wait...and wait. Then my partner and my friends food come out....and I wait...and wait, and watch my food sit in the window, not being delivered. What comes out is literally inedible and cold. My friend didn't eat her veggie burger, it was one of the worst she's ever had. My hot dog, which by description would be messy came out looking like someone had vomited Bacon Potato Chowder over it. It was literally almost an entire bowl of chowder and an order of fries on a hot dog, which made the bun a soggy moist mess. I was expecting something more like a chili dog but what I got was a disgusting disgrace. The chowder was bland and I literally had to dig through it to get to the only edible bit which was the sausage. Then the drinks came out, the milkshake was standard, about as good as you'd get at a fast food joint, but for $9. The hot chocolate came out wrong, with the wrong toppings and was disgusting. Much too bitter and my partner ended up not drinking it. All total we maybe finished half of one drink as a group. In addition to this, despite having repeatedly asked for water, it didn't come until we were almost ready to leave. Add of this to the unkempt cooks, beards with no hair nets. Looking unwashed and unclean and the wildly inappropriate music filled with expletives and we will not be back.

This place has the best tacos I have ever had! In fact all the food was delicious. Having celiac disease it's hard to find places to eat but the staff at this restaurant was very knowledgeable as well as very helpful in making sure nothing was cross contaminated. I highly recommend going here!

5 Star service from our amazing waitress! The place was packed after the wine walk downtown, drunken girls in the bathroom vomiting and crying... That was a side note... I took Mike T's advice and stuck with the Brewer's burger (medium rare, of course!) It was awesome! And the usual XXX Blonde and tried a seasonal Pumpkin Ale, you have to try before it's gone, easy to drink and great! The hubby was a little disappointed with his Vietnamese BBQ beef but only because it was lacking on the amount of beef although he loved his IPA as usual (Anchor Steam lover that he is!)

We had 3 ! -------- Chicken Fajita, Steak Fajita, and fish taco made to order. They were served hot in a flour tortilla. I should have checked to see if corn tortilla was a sub for the flour tortilla for those who need gluten free. I wasn't thinking about that issue the day I was there / so sorry gluten free friends. As you enter you will find a bank of ordering pads and pencils set up for you to mark your order before you reach the cashier. Get in line, fill out your order, hand it to the cashier. Receive your drink cup, listen for your name to be called out by the cooks "Sam I am?" , and take your order to the salsa / fixings bar. Fill the tiny cups with your choice of toppings and find a table to sit and enjoy your tacos. You may eat inside or out , have a coke or a beer, dash in for a quick lunch or linger for a few laughs with friends. It is a great place for a taco!

I Read the reviews and I was so curious to see how it was. Well, I HAD the WORSE CHEESESTEAK I'VE EVER HAD,EVEN THE FRIES WERE TERRIBLE! !! I WENT HOME AND THREW UP! NEVER AGAIN ! The only thing I liked was the roll. So not worth it. And I went with a friend who treated and I picked this terrible place. I felt terrible ,she hated her sandwich too!

Heard rave reviews walk 3 miles to eat there ....AND was NOT impressed at all what so ever....I did not eat the buffet but my friends did, they had fried chicken...bland, gumbo OK, and bread pudding ...not the best, and I ordered off the menu cheesy grits, over easy egg, and grilled chicken....let me tell you about this "grilled chicken" omg I almost threw up, it was the nastiest piece of chicken I've ever put in my mouth, I nearly threw up! It was WAY OVER COOKED, and smothered in onions and bell peppers, it was so bad I can't explain it....but I DID EAT A BULISCUT AND IT WAS THE BEST DAMN BISCUIT I EVER ATE....

My husband and I have eaten here twice since it's been open. Our first experience was a few months ago, we came in for Wing Wednesdays. We both felt the experience was very mediocre, but perhaps we are simply partial to the wings at other specific places. Our second experience was last night. Service was great as usual. We ordered pretzels and beer cheese to start, and both felt that the pretzels could have been softer and salted more. However they weren't unbearable. I ordered a buffalo chicken sandwich which was good, but I had to get an extra side of wing sauce because there was barely any on the sandwich. My husband a burger (western?) Which came with bacon, cheese, topped with onion rings. While he was satisfied with the food, on our way home he mentioned feeling a little dizzy. We get home, he goes to sit in the shower to try to feel better, and just started throwing up everywhere. He threw up all of his dinner including the appetizer. He complained that he just kept tasting the bacon afterward. I suppose that's what we get for trying to give the place a second chance when we weren't entirely satisfied the first time. If I had to guess, the bacon was undercooked or old, or perhaps had been left sitting out.

My job used but these all the time but since I'm vegan I would just stare. Recently I came in to try their vegetarian burger with no cheese. It's a bean based burger which was good but they were really heavy on the sauces which took away from the overall burger. They have gluten free doughnut holes which I tried and loved. They have a wonderful atmosphere and the staff is amazing!
This place sucks. The sioft serve is nasty as hell and the ppl working there are rude. seriosly i took one lick of the soft serve adn wanted to vomit

O HWK... how you have disappointed me. I had been to HWK's No Menu Monday once before and was pleasantly surprised. It had an inventive, delicious menu. Thus, when a group of 6 of us were deciding where to eat, we exciting chose this place. We weren't surprised that the only available slot for a party of our size was at 8:30p, but we waited anxiously in anticipation. We were seated promptly and eventually we were asked for our allergies, dislikes, preferences, etc. Several of asked for the wine pairing. Strangely, when one of us reported a preference for red wine over white, we were told "it's whatever matches the food." The proceded to get 2/3 wines white, not red. Hm.. since this is "no menu monday" if a preference is for the wine, can't you just give that person food that matches red wine? Then we waited. and waited. and waited. At 9:35, the food finally started to come out. Appetizer dishes included: scallops over tomato puree (everyone was jealous of the scallops), fried grits (grits???), bone marrow and toast, pork belly, "potted beef," and duck egg salad over toast with truffles. The best of these were the scallops and duck egg salad, but none of these were amazing. The pork belly was so tough that as my friend sawed away at it, he had to use so much force that the fat just squirted out the sides leaving dry, tough meat. The potted beef was basically salted baby food. Literally the consistency and taste of those meat baby foods but much much saltier. Main courses: Cornish game hen over wild rice, trout with brown butter, pork chop with cooked cherries, filet mignon, red snapper, and ground pork with red sauce over polenta. Out of this the filet was the best - you can't really go that wrong as long as you don't overcook the darn thing. The red snapper was pretty boring. The pork chop was dry. The polenta/red sauce dish looked amazing, but was sadly pretty tasteless. Supposedly there was gnocchi in there, but there was never one sighted or detected. The polenta was watery which further diluted the taste. Dessert: Overall fine. The best parts were the chocolate dishes. One was a flourless chocolate torte with sea salt and the other was chocolate ganache. Again, you can't go wrong with ganache. There were donut holes which were pretty plain. A caramel butter cake was too sweet for it being so dry. The banana bread pudding looking promising, but also too dry and surprisingly not very sweet. Then there was the goat cheese ice cream. It was.. interesting. My taste buds still don't know how to react. But I don't want to try it again. Maybe it was just a really off night. Like I said the first time we were so impressed. Our most recent visit wasn't horrible. It just wasn't that good. And it sucked to wait an hour for the food to come out. We ate the three courses, paid the bill, and were out of there in less that time.

I don't know why I end up dating girls who can't eat wheat. I love hearty Italian loaves, pizza, and toothsome pasta, but I find myself seeking the oat, sorghum, and rice alternatives so I can enjoy meals with my sweetheart. This limitation has been most frustrating in my quest for decent pizza because gluten's resilient proteins are essential for a firm, supple pizza crust. 'Gourmet' as an adjective doesn't mean too much any more, though I suppose they could fit in under the sister term 'artisanal.' It's not stellar pizza, but for Gluten Free options in the bay area, they practically hold a monopoly. It's not as good (it'll never be as good), but it's an acceptable compromise. We had a mushroom gorgonzola pie and a hawaiian pie. Both were worthwhile attempts at their established genres, though neither was revolutionary or exemplary of the craft. Of course, if I hadn't been eating pizza regularly for the past few years (like the celiacs I went to dinner with), my opinion would probably have been much higher (theirs was). Final Verdict: It's not the best, but if you can't eat wheat then it's better than nothing.

A welcome respite from the sea of French quarter revelers, cheap liquor, cafeteria grade imitations of creole/Cajun/southern cooking, and vomit smell. The scene is crowded for sure, but finally for a good reason. The music was spot on. A four piece jazz band set up shop for hours . The wine selection was solid, beer selection better than I've seen elsewhere, but still pretty limited. The food wasn't trying to be "New Orleans". It was just good. There was a line to get in, and while lines usually immediately disqualify a place, I'm glad I waited.

Stopped in for a gluten free brunch on a Sunday. Cute café space with plenty of gluten free offerings - which can be hard to find in New Orleans. I ordered the chilaquiles and got a little greedy and ordered the chunky monkey gluten free muffin too - although disappointed this was the only gluten free pastry option they had available. Muffin was most and chewy - probably due to the coconut - really good & probably my fave thing I ordered. Had an iced latte with almond milk that was solid and served in a cute mason jar. Husband ordered a french press coffee and was disappointed that it was served in a paper cup with plastic plunger despite us dining in. Chilaquiles were OK - sauce was pretty bland but edible. One annoying thing was the amount of pesky flies in the place that seemed to hover around the dining area! We would have stayed a bit longer had we not had to swat flies off our heads the entire time. Overall: good gluten free pastry, OK coffee/food, a bit pricey and ambiance left a lot to be desired.
A group of us tried the gluten free waffles, which were dry and mediocre. regular coffee was $5 and a glass of orange juice was $5. Not worth the price - pass on this place

This got a 2 stars instead of 1 because the staff is awesome and are always ready to help you out and customize your meal. This place is not good and is ridiculously overpriced. Most ppl on campus hate this place and avoid it like the plague. Their food isn'tthat bad, it's just very very expensive. Their flatbreads used to be the bomb and used to be 2x as large. Now they're so small they don't touch the sides of the box provided and they're 6.75$ . If I'm paying that much for a meal, I want to be full at the end of it. What a ridiculous place. There are a few gluten free options but it's made in a kitchen with gluten so only a small amount work for those with severe allergies. A friend of mine who can't eat gluten only gets two dishes here. I will say that they have really good sweets, esp their new maple syrup cupcake. It's fantastic. Their coffee is incredibly cheap and way better than Starbucks. And of course their smoothies are also very good which is probably what the entire campus drinks. You can pour whatever you want in then with extra charge for some certain additions. It's so damn close to campus, to be honest I'll probably pop in there again

Harry & Izzy's is the place to go when your looking for a good steak at a reasonable price if you find yourself in downtown Indy. To those unfamiliar with H&I, it can be described as St. Elmo's more casual little brother. What makes H&I great: - You can still get St. Elmo's classic shrimp cocktail. If you have some sinus issues, the sauce will clear that up for you - Reasonable prices in a more relaxed environment. Lunch time is the way to go if you have a smaller budget, but want to enjoy the food. - The servers are very friendly and knowledgeable about the different menus and offerings - Decent Bloody Mary's - They do a good job of cooking your steak to order and the cuts of meat are of good quality - Lower level bar with tv's to watch the games while enjoying your meal - Separate gluten free menu with a nice selection of items, including fries! They have a small separate dedicated fryer for fries only. They also do a really good job of handling gf orders and try to reduce possible cross contamination. A manager usually comes out to make sure of your order and verify any questions and gf procedures. - Online reservations accepted via OpenTable. If you want a specific meal time, make sure to schedule, especially prior to Pacers and Colts' home games - Paid parking is right across the street. It is one of the Circle City garages, or you can just valet.

We went to Vetri for our second wedding anniversary. I wish I could give this place an extra star, because this is as good as it gets. I should go lower every other review I made by one star so this place stands out. I made my reservation two months in advance on Open Table. I originally tried calling the restaurant, months in advance, but they told me they only book through open table. I had to put my credit card number in and I would be booked $155 a person if we were a no-show. The next day I was contacted by Vetri staff to describe the style of the meal and to inquire about food allergies. When we arrived, we were promptly seated and a complimentary glass of champagne was brought out for our anniversary. The wait staff was incredibly friendly and so professional. Again, they asked about food allergies and presented us with menus. We were asked if there was anything we definitely wanted or anything we wanted to avoid. I said I was in for the adventure and I was warned that there was goat and snails on the menu. My wife really wanted to try the sweet onion crepe and the spinach gnocchi. I secretly wanted the ribeye, because that is my favorite cut of meat, but I thought I would be cheating myself if I got that. The food started coming out and we were presented with three plates. My wife and I both were given the sweet onion crepes with truffle fondue and another plate of fish for the both of us. Throughout the night more and more plates kept on coming, even the spinach gnocchi. We kept looking over at the other tables and chatting with those people as they looked at our food too. We were all getting different foods and we would compare notes with each other. By the time our entree came, my wife had a sad look on her face. Our awesome waitress asked what was wrong and we mentioned that we are sad the final entree is here and we were hoping we would have gotten snails. She apologized immediately and told us she would get some for us. Not only did she get us the braised snails, but she brought us a complimentary glass of wine that she thought paired really well with that dish. While awaiting dessert, we heard some screaming from the table behind us and all of this liquid splatter onto the floor. Staff were scrambling and I thought someone bumped into this guy and spilled something on him. After a few minutes staff came to us and apologized. Apparently this man was pretty drunk and vomited on the floor. The table behind us were asking for the check, trying to get their drunkard out of this nice place. Our waitress brought us a Vetri cookbook with a lot of the recipes from that evening to make up for the "horrible" experience, but it wasn't even that much of a diversion. By the time dessert came, pretty much nothing could have ruined that evening.

I don't know what all the low stars are, I think this is a cool little spot even though it does look a little like an indian pinata threw up but it's got it's own thang and you gotta love that no matter what. Food is good and service is good. I'd do it again!

Love this place! Best sausage cart in philly.. mike is always friendly. Service is always fast and professional.. he deals with money, and makes food but always remembers to change gloves when he touches money so your food isn't contaminated.

Giving 3 stars. I was so excited to take my sister here for her birthday. She got the gluten free cupcake. I got a chocolate. The cake was dry. The icing was ok. Definitely a let down though. The kicker was there were about 4 younger employees workings all behind the counter. The place was a mess! We took our cupcakes to go for that reason. This could be a great place! They need to get it together and hire staff that care about where they work.

If I could I would give Poke Bowl a 2 1/2 solely based on the food and value. I was ecstatic when a poke restaurant opened up especially so close to where I live. I have to say after being anxious to try, I was extremely underwhelmed. The bowls were a lot smaller than I thought- even the large. I ordered Kale for my base which took up more than half of the small bowl. As for protein I had 2 scoops of salmon, 2 scoops of octopus, and 1 scoop of tuna. The scoops are very small especially because the pieces of fish are so big. The salmon and octopus tasted fresh but the tuna (i think) was too fishy for me and I eat sashimi regularly. There is a good variety of toppings and sauces which accommodate for gluten free etc. However, I didn't want to top off the bowl too much because I already knew it would be impossible to mix. In the end it was a pretty unsatisfying meal for dinner after a long day and for a price tag of about $13. I had to try it but I have to say I won't be returning any time soon. The staff was friendly and helpful.

Went to this pizza restaurant based on reviews for gluten free pizza. While the service was good, I cannot recommend their GF pizza. The crust was very thin and burnt. It was basically a burnt cracker with toppings on it.

If I were to come back again, I would make my dinner composed of entirely appetizers. I had the phyllo pastry stuffed with feta cheese and drizzled with honey. It was hot, crispy, and ooh so yummy. I'm a sucker for dolmas and hummus, so I wished I could have tried those too. My rosemary lamb stew was good. It had a lot of vegetables and a pretty complex flavor, but it occassionally tasted of fish. I wasn't sure if that's the way it was supposed to be prepared or if there was some cross-contamination in the kitchen. But the 5 stars is really for the service. I came on a Friday night as a single diner, visiting Phillie, basically -- the lowest denominator a customer can be for a restaurant because I don't fill a table nor will I be a repeat customer. My hostess was really apologetic that the place was full (you might need reservations for Friday or Saturday night, the place is small), and she tried her best to accommodate me. She was extremely gracious and well-meaning, and I could tell she values the customers, and it's why I gave this place 5 stars.

I purchased a Groupon and received notification I no longer needed to bring the Groupon to the restaurant. Simply give them my name and they'll know I purchased one. That was not true. Luckily we brought the Groupon with us to dinner. What I didn't know is in the fine print of that Groupon Pita Jungle specified I needed to buy to "regular drinks" to redeem this. I generally drink water and perhaps a cocktail or a glass of wine but I never buy a regular drink of soda, tea, lemonade, etc. So we complied - the herbal berry tea was awful as it tasted of grape juice watered down. There was a happy hour special going on when we arrived so we had the $1.50 hummus trio. Seemed simple enough on the face of it. There were four tiny pieces of bread that were too small for the portion of hummus which was small enough in its own right. We sat on the patio which has awful acoustics. The sound of all the neighboring groups/families were so loud and we were right under the music speaker as well. Uggh. Pita Jungle still refuses to mark their menu like other restaurants are doing for items that are already gluten-free and/or vegan. There is a false disclaimer that almost everything on the menu could be vegan with one modification. In trying to determine what to order we had to get a special book and chart out our own meals. What a pain and how low class of them for making their guests feel like second rate citizens. Now onto the servers, bussers and food delivery people. I couldn't tell anyone who worked there other than the servers because of their black aprons. The food delivery people came scurrying over and dropped our food off and ran away quickly. I couldn't tell if it was someone off the street or an employee. How weird and rude. The busser I saw that night was wearing a ball-cap. He looked more like a patron than an employee. I will not be going back.

The casino is laid out in a winding loop. You will walk through the gaming floor and follow signs to the various restaurants. It looks pretty much like all casinos. Beware the heavily saturated smoky air if you have asthma, allergies or other breathing concerns. This is also typical of every casino, but somehow the air seemed more trapped here that in Vegas. I understand there may be non-smoking blackjack tables near the pool. There is an attached parking garage that is free. the food is pretty high but that is normal as well. Otherwise, its a casino. If you are there to gamble, you will like it. If not, probably not so much.
One place I can always count on to have a decent pizza and being that my daughter has celiacs they always do a good job of avoiding cross contamination from the gluten.
The service was good. Nice view! Warning if you have fish allergies they fry everything together.. Husband had bad seafood reaction after ordering burger

Quick summary: 312 is a "just decent" pizza place in a city with great pizza places within a five mile radius of its location. We arrived on a Friday shortly after 9pm. The place seemed like it was nearing the tail end of their Friday night busy period. We were greeted & seated within a minute or two of arriving. After placing drink orders, we placed our pizza orders - one gluten-free and one deep dish. And then we waited...and waited...and waited. It took more than an hour for our food to arrive, and this was after the bulk of the restaurant was empty. I know, I know - deep dish pizzas take longer to cook. I get that. Still, what made matters worse was this - the smaller and thinner crust pizza we ordered took an extra 10 minutes to arrive! Needless to say, we were frustrated, but we wanted to give the food a try. After all, a phenomenal meal can make up for lackluster or disappointing service (to some degree). The results? The deep dish pizza was more tomato saucy than anything else. The sauce overpowered the other ingredients. As for the gluten-free option, it turned out fine. Some unrelated but rather annoying aspects of the gluten-free pizza, however, were that it was barely sliced and it was served in a thin aluminum pan with a large serving spatula, making the plating of the pizza quite difficult. Bottom line: we could have taken a cab to Desano, ordered a couple of their amazing pizzas paired with our own bottles of wine, consumed the pizzas, and taken a cab ride home all in the time it took to order and receive our pizzas at 312. I would encourage you to learn from my experience.

This restaurant was highly recommended and very crowded. The staff was friendly and the atmosphere was nice. The menu looked pretty tasty. My friend had a scone which she said was good while we waited for our table. After sitting, she had the waffles which were a bit soggy. Unfortunately, for me, they were unable to make alterations to accommodate my food allergies. The waiter said some days there are options on the menu that can be adjusted for dairy and grain allergies, but not today. They did end up making me a couple eggs and some sorghum bacon, but they were not worth the wait. I'd say try this place, unless you have dietary restrictions.

Good gluten free pizza option. My friend's sandwich was amazing. The fries are great. You can tell it's all made fresh! Horrible music selections on a Saturday morning. Very little parking. While I was there, 8 cars were booted across the street in the Cumberland Machining lot. My server sweetly notified us but it was too late. Who boots cars on a weekend morning?!?! (Cumberland Machining does!) Especially in a neighborhood where parking is becoming close to impossible. I wasn't paying attention to the signs bc it was Saturday. Lesson learned. The gluten free pizza was good, but not $50 booted car good.

At least they don't waste good whiskey... We didn't have dinner, but whiskey and appetizers. We found this place on Yelp because we were looking for a place to sit down and sip some scotches. We walked in, I took one look at the menu and my wallet started to bleed. And I don't mean the food prices. Yeah, they have a lot of whiskeys. A LOT. But every single whiskey that I've had elsewhere, they were charging about double what I would expect to pay. I can get excited about trying new scotch, but not when I'm paying double what every other bar I know charges. OK, so they have a 2oz pour, slight larger than average. Still, I'm not quite sold. Anyway, the girl liked the place, so I agreed to give it a try. We decided to do a flight of tastes, which we built to our own interests. Oban, The Macallan, and Lagavulin. Of course the scotches were good. BUT, the bartender mis-poured and accidentally poured out a measure of Laphroaig, which was another we had considered. Now that one was $30 for a taste, so I was thinking that's an expensive mistake. But, no, I couldn't believe my eyes, he poured it back into the bottle. Wow. That's class right there. In addition, they use a common measuring cup to measure all of your drinks, so each one is actually contaminated with a little of the scotch before it. Wait... I ordered a single-malt, not a blend. The only food we got were the cheese balls. They were tasty ...and tiny. I'm sure the food is good and all, but I'll pass, thanks.

I don't know why people are so hard on Pho Bistro. I have eaten here probably 10 times and never gotten food poisoning or diarrhea (which is more than I can say for Caje). I alway get the raw beef and meatballs (which admittedly look a little grey but they are delicious). If you are recalling craving hot beef soup, look no further than Pho Bistro.

There are hardly any food choices at the airport in Nola and I was so hungry! Our flight was first delayed before we boarded then after we boarded. There were a few fast food options and one local food stand where everything was fried in the same oil as shell fish not at all keeping in mind people who have shell fish allergies like me which can be deadly. So out of the very few options available I got something at Smoothie King. There was a yogurt parfait with canned peaches and frozen strawberries in it. At least that's what it seemed like. And I got a bag of mixed nuts. The yogurt was not super healthy but I was grateful to have something to eat after waiting so long in the airport! The employee was friendly. cant ask for much more at an airport with hardly any food.

The 3 star review is more about the service than the food. Customer service needed to warm up a little. We had 2 kids with us. They tried to seat us at a round table with nothing for kids. We asked for the booth next to the table and we got a "no" followed by a "let me check". It wasn't busy. When we asked for a menu that reflected food for peanut allergies, the server seemed put off. Food was decent for Americanized Chinese good. Not authentic but you don't or shouldn't go to PF Change for authentic Chinese.

While the ingredients tasted fresh, the pizza as a whole (veggie + italian sausage) was extremely bland. The flavors didn't meld or melt together. The pizza tasted like the 6 individual toppings. Not to mention that one of the worst things about bad thin-crust pizza occurred: the layer of toppings just slid of the slice. Unfortunate pizza and bad experience. This review is for the non-gluten free pizza. We didn't try that. After this experience, we won't. Another Tampa pizzeria bites the dust in our book!

Paul Walker ate here shortly before he passed away. His picture hangs on the wall near the door; a tribute to the blond hunk with piercing baby blues who mesmerized me at age 14 when I snuck into Varsity Blues in the theatre because my mom wouldn't let me see it. I guarantee, somewhere up in the heavenly beyond, Paul Walker has found a way to re-create Lilly's pho and is enjoying it by the vat-ful. My mother forgave me for being a dishonest little teenage heathen. I took her to Lilly's on one of her recent trips to New Orleans. She has traveled extensively through Asia and Vietnam, and she stated that this is the best pho she's ever had in her life. Have I convinced you yet? Lilly's tofu bánh mì may have very well saved my sister's life when she was ill with food poisoning. The bun dishes may very well have saved MY life when I am over-stressed, over-worked, and over-studied. Lilly's is my favorite comfort food and the top place I will frequent and recommend to others for absolutely delicious, "knock-your-socks-off" Vietnamese food. To top it off, Lilly herself is the nicest woman. Every time I walk in, I want to give her a hug.

Not sure if the pizza, it did look amazing. I had a pasta dish with shrimp and saffron which I loved, the arugula salad with mushrooms was just okay- lacking something. The grilled squired was very flavorful and tender. The artichoke appetizer had too much vinegar. We didn't care for it at all. We also tried the three cannoli they offer were not good. Four of us couldn't finish them because they tasted so bad. Not sweet and very tart. Not like a typical cannoli at all. The shell was crunchy but overall not worth it. The chocolate gelato was very strong and I understand was good. I am not a chocolate fan due to an allergie but my friend said it was good but not life changing or anything. The place has a lot of character but that's it. Like I said maybe the pizza is good.

Great Gluten Free options, and the waitress was very knowledgeable on what sauces were gluten free. The Gluten Free bread was very dry and crumbly, and the burger was fair, nothing that was exciting. The pickles were absolutely disgusting!!! They were so sour and tasted like someone poured vinegar all over, then sprinkled dill on them that I couldn't eat them, which was very disappointing, as I love pickles on my burger. The fries were awesome though, but be prepared as the portion sizes are small. Our waitress was training another girl and both were very friendly. This place definitely didn't live up to all the hype, but the building concept was really cool as well as the decor. Not a place that I would go out of the way to return to.

Searching for a restaurant that has offerings for vegans and people with dairy issues can be tough. Not only does Gourmet Pizza company accommodate both, but they also have a lot of gluten free offerings - something very rare for a pizza joint. And I guess if you're vegan or have gluten allergies, just about any pizza that you're actually able to eat without dying (physically or just emotionally) is probably a great treat. Our vegan friends had tried their pizza at a vegetarian festival, liked it and suggested we go there since we were nearby. The problem is that if you're not limited to vegan/GF options, the pizza really isn't that great. It's not bad, but it's pretty mediocre. If you're adventurous, you can try crawfish tails or escargot on your pizza. Interesting, but I just wasn't in the mood for snails on my pizza - just some pepperoni, thanks. Had it just been a matter of the pizzas, I would have gone 2.5 stars, rounded to 3. But we also got an order of the pizza breadsticks and my wife ordered the Mayan salad. The breadsticks are covered in melted mozzarella and then an entire block of parmesan is grated and dumped on top. The result is a very dry taste that is somewhat ameliorated by the tomato dipping sauce. Unfortunately, the cup of it is so small that you only get about 2-3 breadsticks dipped in there before you're out. The biggest complaint, though, was the Mayan salad. To call this salad "crappy" would be a compliment. Made up entirely of romaine hearts and a handful of tasteless beans, corn, tomatoes and cheese - not even the mango dressing could help it. The only thing gourmet about this place is the toppings list.

Horrible and expensive for being a hole in the wall. Waitress was terrible TV was way too loud. If I wanted to hear novelas I would go to my moms and eat. I literally threw up on our way home. My husbands beans where overly dry looked like they were sitting since the morning. Rice, was nothing special I could've made it at home for free. We definitely won't be going back. I would love to rate it no stars! I recommend mi nidito.

The food was very good and I love that they have gluten free items on the menu. I was less than impressed with the waitress. She made a point to tell us that she was the only one on Tuesday's and also that if we wanted to sit in the dining room "at the other end of the restaurant" she hoped we didn't mind that everything would take a while....and it did. We went DQ

I have ordered from them several times. The food is not bad, but the employees really ruin this place. They are obnoxious and waaaay too snooty for their own good. In addition to their crappy attitude, the pizza is hit or miss. Sometimes it is really good, sometimes just ok. I will echo a previous reviewers comment that the salad leaves MUCH to be desired, a complete waste. Really, the only reason I ever went there was the gluten free options, but I can make it myself and do without the attitude.

This place blows. They told me on the phone they had a gluten-free menu...... it's 5 items and everything is 20 dollars.
