They don't even have gluten free beer, which is ridiculous since it's a bar.... I wouldn't send my worst enemy here. I wouldn't spend another dollar if it was the last restaurant in tampa. The steak and shrooms meal I ordered was subpar at most. Not to mention the food took way too long. The steak was literally smaller than the palm of my hand for 20 dollars. The manager didn't even come over and ask why I sent it back. Point is the staff even knows they're spine - less dicks. I'm done.

Due to food allergies and constant dangerous mix ups with my order I finally gave up. Be careful if you order food here they don't care about the customer and was also refused information to file a complaint with the franchise owner. I guess you can't expect much else from a McDonald's huh? Go to the one continental and avoid this place like the plague!

Pricey yogurt and ice cream. Its def.not worth all that! The ice cream really has no flavor no matter what you chose or your tried, no flavor at all! I was not crazy about it at all and would of chose a TASTI D LITE or YOGURTBERRY over this spot any day and time. Not my place regardless how good and diet gluten free it is, not worth it and you def.can find better and cheaper and prob. the same ingredients somewhere else.

Love this place! A top BYOB brunch spot. I was a little hesitant at first because of the name, but then I realized it is because the place had Australian roots. It is good for someone with a nut allergy too! Even though the kitchen is small only 2 items on the menu had nuts and as soon as I asked if I could be accommodated they immediately assured me cross contamination would not be an issue. I ordered the hot and sweet breakfast sandwich and it was to die for! Light roll, crispy bacon, delicious! Can't wait to go back.

Always great food and service here. Then six of us come in today for lunch and two have severe food allergies so they prepare their own meals and still purchased alcohol, just not a entree. The manager then approaches us and poorly explains that in the future they cannot come in with their meals because God knows why? 4 of us purchased meals and drinks and 2 of us just drinks. After being loyal customers, for this to even happen was very annoying and I can assure you that our business will not be back at that establishment.
Middle of the road pizza joint. Gluten Free pizza takes 40 minutes and only comes in one size (medium). Waitstaff was friendly.

When I first called Bertucci's to place a reservation my hopes were high, boy was I wrong. The hostess that I talked to was very nice and polite. That is where the good service ended. When my girlfriend, her friend, and I arrived we waited a few minutes until we were seated. We sat at a booth and waited for our waiter. We waited and waited and then a hostess walks up to our waiter as he "is about to greet us" (after 10 minutes and a direct quote from him). He tells us his name and we order our drinks.We get our drinks and he asks if we are ready, my girlfriend has a hard time choosing meals, so we ask for more time. We wait for another 10 minutes to order. He comes back and takes our order, he doesn't act like he wants to be working and it is obvious. I ordered a Roasted Artichoke Fonduta as an appetizer, it sounded very good and when we got it I almost vomited. The whole thing was sour and tasted of fish. I love cheeses that are aromatic like Brie, but this was a spoiled taste. We decided to just eat the bread with the olive oil dip, which is always good. Our waiter walks by us and looks at the table and walks right away not giving me a chance to even say something about the fonduta. He doesn't appear until our dinners are ready and then I tell him the fonduta tastes spoiled. He says "Uhhh ok" and then have to say "We don't like it". He has his manager take it off the bill which was nice. The girls and I start eating and time passes by and our waiter isn't anywhere to be found. Normally this is the time where we get asked how the meal is. We don't get that question till we are done and wanting to leave. The waiter is lucky that we have some heart and still tipped him for his remarkably bad service. The food was on par with any chain Italian restaurant, but the service ruined the entire night. I would not go here again unless I am feeling particularly sadistic.

I give this place 3 stars because the food there was fairly good, but after my mom started getting red bumps and allergies while others where having stomachaches. If this had not happened then this place would be getting a five star. The price for all of my family was very unreasonably high.

Disgusting!!! The pizza smelled like a moldy old rag.. threw the entire thing in the trash. Never in my life did I smell such a thing from a pizza!! The cheesesteak was also inedible. The roll was saturated with water (I assume from steam to melt the cheese). It was a soggy sloppy disgusting mess that also went directly into the trash can. Unless you want to vomit, I wouldn't ever order from this poor excuse for a pizza place.

The salads are fresh and the menu is generally healthy. The service for people with food allergies is inconsistent. Our first visit was very positive....the manager knew his ingredients and he worked with me to make sure the food they served was safe. The second visit was much less positive...the manager was unsure and we left. The third visit was so-so....I was not confident eating the food delivered. Since 3% of the population has serious food allergies, and since they offer such a fresh menu, they're missing an opportunity.

food really good, cute outdoor and indoor setting, husband god food poisoning from the carne asada, probably marinating too long without a fridge or something, but that could happen at any restaurant, I gave him some phenergan anti nausea and he was fine after a while, he has a sensitive stomach though

What blew me away about Kermits is the place itself. Absolutely stunning! A beautiful display case of baked goods AND pizza! Everything looked and smelled heavenly and the decor was over the top with a huge rolling pin hanging from the ceiling! Now, I wouldn't say they have the best anything. Good, but not the best. I had a few things. First I tried the red velvet crumb cake which was ok. The crumb was a bit salty and the edges where crispy. I had to get to the middle for that light fluffy cake texture. Then I had a mini pineapple upside down cake. It was actually more like a bread pudding. The "cake" was really dense and super moist. Not cake like at all, but still good. Sugar cookies where standard and last but not least, the pizza. I had a plain slice which was tasty. The gluten free crust was good, fluffy and crispy at the same time with a sweet sauce and nice amount of cheese. I was disappointed that their cakes where not sold by the slice as I came specifically to try the confetti cake. I highly recommend adding that as an option. I will be returning to sample more sweets. The homemade pop tarts are next on my list. Welcome to the neighborhood Kermits and please sell slices of cakes. I can't go buying a whole cake on a Tuesday for no reason.

Of the 3 Chipotles in town, this is my favorite. The staff is fast, attentive, and friendly. I have tons of food allergies and they are getting better at avoiding cross contamination, but once in a while some sofritas will sneak into my chicken and I end up having to take Benadryl. But this hasn't happened in several months. So good job guys.

Used to be our go to pizza place when I was little - 20 years ago. We've tried the gluten free pizza twice and it was worse the second time. There's no reason the crust should be that bad - there's a ton of awesome gf crusts out there that are actually proper for a pizza. But the sauce was bland and cheese not even to the edges. Won't be ordering from here again.
You can do better. Nice enough place with average coffee. Good morning pastry options. Gluten free options. Playing bad techno at 7AM - ugh.
Waitress was slow and we had to asked for refills , soda was flat , food was good but not many gluten free options , won't go back

We're standing inside our 6th floor condo that practically hovers over the beach as the light drains from the day and pools onto the horizon. The vast expanse of the Gulf of Mexico slices through the distant sky as the remaining embers of the day burn away; people lined up and down the long sand disperse for the evening hand-in-hand. These are slow, long days in my gravy adventure, perhaps caused by the natural relaxation a beach destination brings, but more likely due to the fact that everything here in America is very much more spread out and it takes a while to get anywhere. Walking to places isn't really an option in 90-degree weather, but I'm always amazed at the size and scope of these united states that seem to act as mini-nations within a greater nation of drawling accents and huge restaurant portions. We're here in Florida with my family so I left it up to my sister to decide where we should test the gravy-waters, so on a lazy Sunday found ourselves just up the coast at Maggie Mae's Sunrise Café - an unassuming little nugget along the shoreline overlooking mega-mansions, fishing boats, and run-down tin-roofed shacks left neglected for decades against the salty ocean air. Maggie Mae is a restaurant nestled in a strip mall filled with nail salons and tattoo parlours - and I swear I looked into that ink place and saw a 9-year-old furrowing his brow with indecision about what his next tat should be - it's great to be back in Florida. I wasn't interested in fries as accompaniment this time out, because I had come here for dat southern gravy - and everyone knows what you pair with that particular sauce - the most buttery of biscuits. We don't have biscuits like this back in Glasgow, since biscuits are cookies over there and anything that even resembles a proper biscuit ends up being a proper disappointment. My mouth watered as they brought out the dish of one biscuit cut in half and slathered with so much country-white gravy that it looked like they ladled it out of a giant bucket onto the plate. The presentation was somewhat expected, but I didn't really think it would appear as if they made way too many buckets of gravy and really had to get rid of it before it went bad. Unfortunately, it tasted a little like it already had. Labeled a 'sausage' gravy, the bits of meat visible in the sauce felt a little unnecessary, as the sausage flavor had no problem shining through on it's own. The way I would describe the gravy's actual taste was as if I was eating thick cream that had fell into pieces of gravel. It didn't taste BAD really, just confusing, like eating a gravy flavoured-cloud. The biscuit itself was magnificent; a buttery delight that I really do miss now that we're in Glasgow - but I digress. An opacity of 99% only served to amplify the bland white sauce, and in the end I had unknowingly slathered so much of the stuff up I started to feel like I was becoming lactose intolerant. Being in Florida for me is like travelling back in time; we used to come here almost every year in our youth, the scent of saltwater taffy being pulled down at the boardwalk; the leathery brown figures adorning beach chairs below us; it always amazes me how so little actually changes. The restaurants with the charming names, the friendliness of the people, and the spectacularly warm weather are reasons to come back to the state best known for it's lack of motorcycle-helmet laws - so it's unfortunate that I can't say Maggie Mae's gravy will be one of those reasons. The southern states are a huge place though, and maybe one day I'll have some luck adding 'best gravy' to that list above in the state often referred to as 'America's Wang'. For more gravy reviews, visit https://gluttonforgravy.wordpress.com/

Quiet little Cafe with lots of character and charm! We had breakfast here while visiting Old Town Philadelphia and were pleasantly surprised!! I eat a Gluten Free, Vegan diet and avoid Oats as well. The staff were knowledgeable and very accommodating to my dietary needs and the breakfast was delicious!! I ordered Breakfast Tacos with a couple adjustments, no egg add tofu sauce, with no toasting to prevent cross contamination (their suggestion). This was a great start to our day and affordable! Oh by the way, they are a Cash Only establishment with an ATM on site.

Gluten free menu is okay, though I would call ahead or look it up online to be sure you're in the mood for what's on the gf menu - I say this because only part of our party was. Maybe we had a tough crowd? We had a party of six, everyone enjoyed their meals - I think the steak was the most enjoyed by all of us. Desserts were great- vanilla gelato and creme brûlée. The service was outstanding as was the atmosphere.

I walked in and realize they were a lot smaller that the original building Frm back in the day. The spanish waitress wasnt that friendIy. They didnt have a lactose option....ok...this is 2016....how dont you have lactose free milk or soy....unbelieveable. ..... I ordered chicken friend steak eggs over easy with american cheese. First it took about 20 mins for me to get my food. My eggs were cold and the cheese wasn't melted and my hashbrowns were cold. So I have to now wait until my eggs and hashbrowns come back. About 8 mins my food comes back out and my hashbrowns are hot but again my eggs are cold and the cheese wasn't melted....I immediately asked for the manager ...she apologize and no.....I don't want anything else except my juice ...Good day..

Ordered the buffalo chicken sandwich. The chicken was spoiled. The manager said she threw away 12 pieces of chicken this morning and may have missed one. I felt like vomiting on the table. This place has earned a lifetime ban. My co-worker got a burger and said it tasted like "old" beef. After he smelled my chicken sandwich he couldn't finish the burger. We were there after 11am and the place virtually empty, one or two other tables with a couple of people eating lunch. I wanted to warn a couple who just sat down not to eat the chicken or maybe even find a different restaurant.

I've read a lot of positive reviews about this place but I was just not impressed. The only exciting aspect of my dining experience was drinking a very cheaply priced margarita, and hey I love margaritas, and also running into my friend while drinking said margarita. Mmm good combination. The food though was lackluster. If you are looking for inexpensive and cheap quality Mexican food (if authentic concerns you not) this is your place but honestly I'd prefer the Fresh Mex variety of Chipotle or Qdoba, which lack the same restaurant atmosphere but you choose your battle... I got excited to see a chicken mole dish on the menu, I love a rich coffee, chocolate spicy mole sauce so I figured I'd give it a go...horrible mistake. The sauce was a light brown, almost reddish and had the taste of vomit. The chicken was shredded and combined with the sauce seemed like it had been regurgitated onto my plate. The "Mexican" rice was dry and non-descript and the limp iceburg and tomato garnish didn't do much to freshen the plate. Needless to say i couldn't finish the food, and not because i was full. I didn't bother to bring home leftovers and for me that is rare. My friend ordered chicken enchiladas and didn't finish them. I didn't get too much feedback from her except that they were ok, decent. The chips and salsa were tasty however, I'll give it that but thats not usually too hard to mess up unless the chips are cold or soggy or the salsa too spicy. Perhaps other menu items were better or perhpas I'm too picky but i will not be back.

3.5 stars If you happen to find yourself in the SoBro area and you are looking for some Gluten Free fare, Delicia is a great option. While there is no dedicated GF menu, a majority of the items are either GF as is or might need a small modification to be GF. Sadly, the sweet plantains contain flour and are oddly a no go. One thing to keep in mind about Delicia is that they are a scratch kitchen, so the food does take a little bit longer to make. Service The servers are generally friendly and helpful when walking through the menu. They do a good job of answering my questions/concerns and verified with the kitchen if they were unsure. Food The food isn't bad and the menu consists of a nice selection of items.I feel like some of the items are hit and miss, case in point the short ribs. The description and my expectations didn't seem to match, but hey, there are plenty of other options to chose from. Bebidas The prices are in line with what other restaurants are charging for cocktails. While this may seem high, trust me, it could be worse. In some cities it is almost impossible to find a cocktail under $15. The options are pretty decent. While everyone raves about the Fire 'N' Ice, I wasn't exactly a fan. It might have been the hibiscus, but the after taste seemed a little off. If nothing else, it is a really strong drink. The margarita's and mojitos are really good if your looking for something sweet and strong. Bar I love the bar seating. If you are looking to have drinks and appetizer, this is the way to go. Parking This can be a hassle. While there is a small lot in the front, as well as a few spots in the back, it isn't enough for the number diners. Plus, it is shared with La Mulita. Your best option is finding a spot along College. Noise Delicia's industrial design plays a huge factor in this. The high ceilings tends to amplify the noise and it can get extremely loud. I find the best time to go is either later in the evenings, ~8:30 pm, or when they first open. Reservations Love it or hate it, they don't accept reservations

The food here is hot, fresh, and not that expensive but it's different from authentic Indian food. Perhaps because of all the gluten-free stuff. Tastes are different than what I'm used to but that happens at almost any Indian restaurant. Or it may have something do with them not using butter or ghee. The naan is also not their own I'm pretty sure. It looks like the frozen kind. I'll still come back every now and then, but only in a group. If it's up to me I'll always pick something else. Not a lot of seats here so the place can fill up fast during lunch. I did like that the samosas were big but they only had 1 type of chutney and I'm a spicy-mint chutney kind of guy, otherwise I can never really enjoy my samosa experience. If you absolutely must have Indian food and don't want to venture out to University city or even a little farther into Center City, then this is an okay spot. When I go out for Indian food, taste is what I am looking for above all else. Other people may really like this place since they are gluten/butter/ghee free. I'm just not one of them. I can't really comment on the service because you serve yourself here. The best thing about this place is that it's consistent and managed well, but other than that, I can't say that this place really impresses me. When it comes to Indian food there are a huge number of recipes for any one dish. It might be a good idea for them to try a few different ones for each and see if they fare any better.

They are very knowledgeable about and accommodating of gluten allergies. I got the Standard Burger in a lettuce wrap instead of a bun, with pickled onions instead of stout (beer) ones. The lettuce wrap was expertly executed and delicious! I also got sweet potato fries, which come in a dedicated fryer - so no cross-contamination with battered products. Nom. Also, delivery was quick and easy. I'll definitely order from them again. Thank you for making the world a happier place for gluten-free people like me!

Stayed here for 4 nights for the Florida bar exam. The location is nice, that's the biggest advantage. There is also a fairly decent breakfast buffet and happy hour, and the staff has been nice. There were a few con's though for those of you considering staying here (especially for the cost). 1. Cleanliness: Our first room was dirty, and one of the beds was completely wet. Soaked through to the mattress. The bed was completely made up though, so we only noticed it after sitting on the bed for a few minutes and then finding our clothes were soaked. It was bizarre/freaky and super gross. We did get transferred to another room immediately, so the staff was helpful with that. In our second room there were definitely some cleanliness issues as well---shower curtains were dirty, walls were dirty, a lot of dust so allergies were bad. 2. Air conditioning: It's a weird set up. It's either freezing/humid or really hot. It doesn't circulate well in the room so the suite area ends up being freezing and the bedroom is hot/muggy. 3. Sound: The walls are extremely thin. You can hear all conversations in the hall, people dropping things upstairs, everything that goes on in the bathroom, and people slamming doors. More so than any other hotel I've stayed at. 4. Room service: The delivery was prompt, and the food was pretty good. Unfortunately they add a 24% gratuity as well as a $3.00 delivery fee. It would be nicer if there was a wider selection on the menu though--it's a lot of bar food/burgers/fries and not many vegetarian/vegan options. 5. Ice/vending machines: Unfortunately there are only ice machines on every other floor, same with vending machines. Vending machines only means soda machines essentially. It would be nice to have both on each floor, or to at least have stairs more centrally located so it's not a trek to the ice machine. 6. Hotel coffee was good. 7. The shampoo/conditioner is NOT good. Leaves your hair feeling like straw. 8. Wifi is very slow and annoying to login honestly since it always logs you out. 9. Pillows are very flat and uncomfortable. They should provide you with more/fluffier or more supportive pillows. 10. There are not enough plugs near the nightstand. There's only one (especially for multiple people trying to charge their phones) 11. Check out is at 11am (not noon)

We ordered "zhajiang mian" "Lurou Fan", the dishes were so greasy, after taken lunch I felt like almost vomit all the afternoon, the egg was not fresh at all and had some smell, the waiting time was so long since only one chef in there. Will never go to this place.

If you're looking for a good burger, this is NOT the place. Over cooked and hard. Not at all a double party. I've had better fast food versions. It's nice they offer a gluten free bun but what's inside gotta count!

As someone who works in the restaurant industry I can be very cynical when I go out for a meal. I tend to overanalyze every aspect of a restaurant and think how it could be done better. This was the case last Saturday when I was in Limoncello's for my sister's engagement party and I could find no flaw. The servers did a great job not only efficiently managing a room full of people that were socializing with each other, bouncing from one side of the room to the other but also of balancing personalized service in a professional manner. At one point I tried to tip one of the servers and he declined, saying "That's not necessary, Sir." I was in awe, I have never seen anyone decline a tip before! The food also left nothing to be desired. We had a round of family style appetizers, everything was prepared nicely and the calamari was cooked perfectly. My steak was prepared exactly as I had ordered, which is no easy task when cooking 20+ different steaks all to be served at the same time, and everyone else at the table seemed to share my enthusiasm for Limoncello. I have dined at every restaurant in West Chester, got food poisoning at Nonna's on my one and only visit (so did a friend of mine on a separate evening), recently had a very underwhelming and overpriced meal at Pietro's Prime, so I can say with the utmost confidence that Limoncello is the best restaurant in downtown West Chester and want to applaud them on a perfect execution of my sister's engagement party.

The store is always clean and the staff is always helpful. My girlfriend has a dairy allergy and so she has to get toppings that hasn't been cross contaminated and the staff is always willing to go out of their way to fulfill her request. Love the variety they have, but I always go with the steak bowl. I do need to try some of their signature tacos one of these days.

Finally got around to trying Cheu! Love the small, cozy, Christmaslight-y vibe here, although it's usually pretty packed I guess since it's so small. The waitstaff were super chill, willing to answer any questions, and were very proactive about things like bringing extra bowls for sharing, refilling water, etc. Came with two ladyfriends and shared the: Pork & pickle dumplings Crispy corn rangoon Yakisoba (no broth) Coconut curry noodles (brothy) Everything was fantastic, although my personal faves were the crispy corn rangoons and the coconut curry noodles. Left feeling perfectly full but not over-the-top i'm gonna vomit type full. Will definitely be back!

This place is good but nothing spectacular. We tried the gluten free pizza and it was subpar but maybe the regular crust is better. The burger and fries however were phenomenal. The staff is super friendly and welcoming.

While in the Poker Room it can take an hour for service to respond after floor contacts them and their supervisor several times. After they arrive they bring the wrong food and any request you have for how the food should be served is not correct. No one smiles on the service team. They show how unhappy they are to serve us. This is due to not knowing who they are hiring and poor training. The other night I tried to order once again after three years of watching the failure. Still happening. I ordered shrimp they brought me chicken. I also ordered a few drinks for the guys. My total bill was under $27.00 at that time. I tipped $10.00. I then looked into the bag. Just awful. The wrong food. The coleslaw was with the hot food. I had to beg to get my money back on the food. Very bad service. Poor management skills. Manager no smile. And after I questioned a manager they say maybe you always come at the late hours. What's the difference. Service is service. I've posted this before in other locations . Sometimes someone reply's back. Oh yes we will fix this. Not in the last three years you haven't. The owners should watch over what goes on in their casino and maybe ask around to see if their customers are happy with the service. I'm not the only one with this issue. You are the ones taking a loss on food and beverage. Now I walk over to a restaurant and bar to bring back to the poker room. I want to add. I always thought your buffet was the best in town. Always ate there. But on Thanks giving the price was high, but exceptable for what I'm used to. NOT THIS DAY. After they sat us I smelled the Ocean . I went closer to where the water was that cooked the crab legs. Just awful. The seafood was bad. We seen someone throw up over by the cheese section. The staff took a long time to clean up. The one that did clean up almost threw up. I made sure we did not eat the seafood. I made sure I did not eat there at Christmas and will skip New Years . I can't believe your staff does not know bad food is cooking in front of them. I watched a lady sweat and go to the restroom. He family was eating the seafood. You are not the only ones with bad reviews. Tucson does not have good quality casinos. When you go to a casino you should feel like your in Vegas for that moment.
This place was great! I would recommend it to anyone with Celiac. They have a warm and friendly staff. And you can 100%trust them to not have any cross contamination!

I have been to another Sabrina's location before and left severely underwhelmed, so I figured why not try the Collingswood location? I had heard nothing but great things... And we had the same exact experience as the first, it was just mehhh. The location is wonderful, but I am not a fan of the interior of the restaurant. Yes I know the building has history, but the utilization of space is just too open and has a loud cafeteria feel.. Nothing about this place is cozy or inviting. Now onto the food. The menu choices are great, the food items and pairings sound absolutely delightful, but the actual execution is definitely lacking. For example, I was so excited to try the Apple and Wisconsin cheddar omelette, can't go wrong with cheese and apples right? The taste was ok, but the texture of the apples were as if they were microwaved. Just chewy and semi hard, not crunchy nor cooked? Was not a fan. The presentation of food is nice as well, but if your food is bland, it doesn't really matter how pretty it looks. The portions are pretty big though. But I would take quality over quantity any day. The breakfast potatoes were just plain crispy potatoes topped with a few bland grilled onions? How can onions taste so... tasteless? Doesn't make sense. My side of Turkey bacon again seemed microwaved, it was ice cold and so rubbery textured I couldn't even eat it. I took only 2 bites because I've never had turkey bacon be so unappealing before. And to top it off, I upgraded my toast to gluten free sour dough bread, sounded yummy. It was literally cold bread, that was wet. Yuck. Didn't look toasted or anything. You couldn't have grilled the obviously frozen bread just a little? Even the strawberry jam seemed like cheap store bought stuff. My girlfriend ordered pancakes and they too were not that good. They tasted very yeasty and had almost no flavor at all. She also got a side of veggies sausage, which literally was plain ol' Morning Star frozen patties.. Not impressed. The server was really nice but she only walked passed us one time holding a coffee pot, not once during our meal did she ask how we liked everything, even after clearing our half eaten plates. And the place was near empty at the time. We did however really enjoy the coffee, but not enough to return.

It was my first time trying out this place. I like that there are vegan/vegetarian/gluten free options on their menu. Overall, the food was just average; felt like the menu was slightly overpriced for the quantity and quality received. I had ordered the curry and grilled avocado bowl with tofu added; quality was so-so. The tofu was overcooked and dry and they forgot the quinoa. I also ordered the 'real fries' which were tasty and had decent flavor. I may try this place again but I wouldn't recommend as a must try to my family and friends. I feel like this place needs to bump up the flavor and quality of their food. Didn't feel impressed overall.

Tried this restaurant for the first, because i had read that they will use gluten free bread with sandwiches and they did! I had a turkey sandwich with lettuce, tomato & cheese on gluten free bread and it was excellent. Everything tasted fresh. My only concern was the length of time it took for our meal to be served. The restaurant was busy, but it appears the kitchen couldn't handle a full house. I'm willing to give the place another try, hoping this was not the norm.
If you enjoy a few bugs floating in your Pho broth, then this is the place to go. I just vomitted a little in my mouth writing this as I go back on the experience. It will haunt me for life....

I hate it! Food is disgusting! Not worth the price! Escargot was SUPER salty! And they only give like 4 pierces with bread for $11! The crab cakes gave a lot of crab but it's not your typical crab cake! Beyond creamy where it would make you want to vomit! The cauliflower Au gratin,wasn't even "Au gratin" it was 1/4 chop cauliflower on a plate! Not even COOK! The salad was even a disgrace! It's was so BITTER! The steak, was a thin slick like a piece of paper! So thin that Waffle House steak is thicker! The desserts? The "profiteroles" is basically cream puffs! The pastries sucks! Only the ice cream was good! SAMs cream puffs are even better and cheaper! The lemon crème brûlée is ok. The custard is good but the sugar on top they over burn it so it make the whole dessert very bitter at the end of each bit. Horrible! I will NEVER return!

I miss the lakeside location, but the flavor and service hasn't changed a bit. The atmosphere is ok...when I go out for pizza I'm not out for the ambiance. Pizzas are thin crust. Fresh ingredients. Tasty salads. This is the best pizza in Reno and has been for years. It would be better if they offered a gluten free option for pizza, boo.

Tomo spelled backwards is Omot....I kinda like that. So in honor of Omot let's do a little reverse engineering. The end of another satisfying meal is met with the pleasant,simple presentation of after dinner orange slices. Sharing four rolls was the way to go. Could I have eaten more...yeah I probably could have eaten 14 more rolls. But after four I feel good and guilt free. I keep finding these crunchy rice crispy bits in my sushi. I've never had anything like this...airy and delightful taking the food to another level. The Volcano roll is one of my favorites and is often key to how I judge my sushi bar. Tomo does it like no other. It looks like someone just dumped 2 quarts of this orange crab concoction onto some circularly arranged rolls. Hell yes! Our sushi is presented on a simple white plate except for the Volcano roll which comes on its own flame engulfed plate with Japanese curse words written on the plate with saracha. The miso is great here. It's so salty I can feel my fingers swelling as finish the last bits of tofu. The salad that comes with meal is iceberg lettuce with a ginger dressing. And Im okay with that......every meal doesn't have to be micro-greens. Iceberg lettuce has a time and place. Plus with the polar ice caps melting its gonna get harder and harder to find. So eat up. Our waitress is super bummed out. She got dumped. Or just got her first Morrisey CD. Or hates her job. I don't really care. I'm not here for fake smiles. Just bring the food and the check in a timely manner and you will get 20% guaranteed. As we enter the restaurant, I'm always pleasantly surprised by lounge like atmosphere. It is a black, low lit environment with touches of modern interior design....not exactly a reflection of exterior. Let's go to TOMO!!!!!

Being vegan, those days where you want a treat and are too lazy to cook, you're limited on where you can go in this town. That being said, That's probably Why I gave this place as many chances as I did, hoping the bad times were a fluke. The service is fine, I'm not a demanding consumer by any means, but it varies from clerk to clerk, usually young college kids and they're friendly enough. However, it's all about the product, and with the price I'd expect at least a decent product. When they win, they win good. Some of their vegan cupcakes are absolutely fantastic, (with the exception of that coconut German cake that looks like vomit and that chocolate lemon monstrosity ). Unfortunately it's not necessarily the cupcakes that are the problem here, it's the business practice the place employs. I was in a bulk phase and stopped by grateful gardens 4 times over the course of two weeks. I stopped by batch every time. The first day they only had one vegan cupcake on the shelf and it was that abhorrent German coconut shaved vomit unappealing one. I passed. I went back to the restaurant two days later... sure enough I walked into batch and I was appalled to see it was the same...the SAME cupcake on the shelf still and no new options. Three days later I went back...you wouldn't believe it. That is almost a week that cupcake sat on the shelf for sale. And I left each time disappointed. The last time I went in the day after they'd finally baked another batch and I bought 4. That's one of few instances I've gotten cupcakes that were actually worth the price. Then There's days like today. Lemon...chocolate disgusting. It sounded disgusting, but I hadnt been to batch, or had a cupcake in months so I decided...hey I have a free cupcake so I bought one and grabbed another with my reward. When I picked them out of the container they were rock hard. They crumbled to pieces when I tried to separate the cap from the bottom part of the cake. I took one skeptical bite and spit it out. Way too stale, horrible flavor combination, just bad. I'll never be back. Hopefully they change their business practice to include...Oh I don't know, not selling stale cupcakes to customers and charging them pretty high for said stale cupcake.

This is a review mainly for the food, service, and environment as I did not actually try out any of their beers. Food: So I tried the Sockeye Cedar Plank salmon (since this place IS Sockeye Grill and Brewery) and it was pretty decent. It came out to my table only warm, but even so, it was enjoyed. Unfortunately for the sides, you're only limited to whatever frozen "mixed vegetable" melange is available or fries or salad. Husband had a burger sans bun, and side salad. According to him, nothing particularly exciting. Food: BASIC. Service: Our server was very friendly and helpful in helping us to find items that did not contain allergens. Lots of gluten at this place (but not surprised as - hello! - it's a brewery. I did NOT factor the levels of gluten into this review just FYI, I'm an adult, I walked in knowing what to expect). The service was especially friendly, but the food took a long time to come out. In the end my salmon ended up only warmish and my husband's order was incorrect. Environment: Noice! I'm as far from sports-loving bar bro as you can imagine, but I can appreciate the thought and expense that was put into tricking out this restaurant into full on modern lodge mode. Complete with naked tree beams and private TVs in booths - it's very bromantic. Clean and well appointed, with just enough lodginess that I can feel a little naturey without expecting Ron Swanson to actually show up. Would I come back? Sure, probably with family, but not really for the food.

I have a mixed review on this place. We went with a party of 7 and only had a 15 minute wait on a Friday night for a bachelorette party dinner group, so the wait wasn't bad. Service was pretty snappy, but our waitress was kind of a snooty b-word. The girl next to me ordered pinot noir just like I did, and when it arrived, we noticed the coloring was off, like it had been watered down tremendously. After each taking a sip, we looked at each other and knew something was off with it. It tasted weird, like it had been corked a week ago. We weren't trying to pay $8 for a glass of spoiled kool-aid, so we VERY kindly and apologetically asked our waitress if she would mind bringing us a different glass, to which she responded, "Well, do you want something different then or....? Cause if I bring you another glass of pinot, it's just going to be the exact same thing, so..." ...Uh...okay, durh. Obviously we want something different. Moving past that, the food was pretty good. Amongst the table we tried the BBQ pork rinds which were bomb, the bacon jam which was also great, a beet salad and a kale salad, all of which were delicious. Our main entrees were good, but overly salty. Like, SUPER salty. My fries burned my tongue with all the salt, and the girl next to me had a pulled pork sandwich and only ate half because she said she could already feel her ankles swelling from all the salt, haha! I had the special which was lobster mac and cheese with shrimp. It was good, but very very heavy and rich. The portion was WAY too big for such a dense entree. I wish they had served it half or third the size in a small boat or something. Haha. Anyway, it was okay. Our waitress did split our bill without much of a fuss which was nice. I'll probably be back another time to sample some other things.

Pizza was ok but the server was awful . I can only have gf pizza so we ask the server what would be a good combination because of the gf crusts she made it so awkward and said we are known for deep corn crust. We we told her I have allergies to gluten then she looked at us funny . No help at all us. She made us feel super uncomfortable. Pizza took forever and when she came to check on us we told her we barely have any cheese she told us that how we make it here . No respect dietary needs and after paying $52 for two 12in pizza and dirty looks from server we will never go back .

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would. Some of the best Italian food the city has to offer. I have a fish allergy and the fantastic chef always offers to use fresh grease for anything I order that is fried so there is no chance of cross contamination. I typically order the same things and they are always spot on. The fried zucchini appetizer is delicious and the fried onion rings are the best I have ever had. The eggplant parmesan is incredible! Do yourself a favor and please check this place out as soon as you can!

Should restaurants allow felons to dine at their joints? That's the question of the century. I would like to say no; however, while dining at this cafe I saw a man. A man with a filled in tear drop under his eye indicating that he has murdered someone. While driving home I saw a wanted sign with a familiar face and I am convinced that he was the same man I saw eating next to me. During my overly rich meal this man mouthed at me that my purse was open. How did he notice that??? I appreciate my waitresses overbearing personality and enthusiasm about the food upon which I was munching; however, the food was composed of fancy ingredients that should never mingle together. For example, mustard and vinaigrette. My stomach is swelling just thinking about it. Now after this meal I wanted to reflect on how I was feeling. I feel as if there is an unborn child in my intestines clawing to be realized. I haven't had a baby in me long since menopause! I shouldn't have to experience this again, especially from food. I've been expelling gas all day like an automobile trying to relieve myself. This is all for now lovely murielbugs! Cya on the flip side.

Finally checked out ABC after driving by quite a bit. The parking lot was packed on a Friday night. I was surprised by how much seating they have, and liked that most of the options are booths. Many families were inside chowing down on the inexpensive food. We started with a pepperoni pizza as an appetizer (yeah, we're fat) just so everyone could get a slice and experience the restaurant's namesake offering. The pizza is good, although have others have commented it's not your typical New York style but rather "Greek style" which from what I can tell means a puffy crust and tons of cheese. For dinner, everyone in my group went with an entree. I was tickled when reading the menu because it says all entrees come with MELTED CHEESE, salad (which never arrived), and garlic bread. We anxiously waited to see if we'd each be presented with a side dish of melted cheese. When our food came out, we quickly realized what they meant -- each dish was cloaked in a thick blanket of cheese, making one dish indistinguishable from the next. I'm not complaining since cheese is like oxygen to me, but if you're lactose intolerant you best not be ordering one of these dishes. My chicken parm was served over spaghetti. It was satisfying and I ended up taking about 3/4 of it home. I tried my friend's eggplant rollatini which was also quite tasty. The garlic bread was not worth eating (but I did anyway, because... carbs.) The decor in this place is incredibly random and unintentionally kitschy. Table placemats are covered in ads, which included ads for a bail bondsman, pawn shop and critter removal (which really gets your appetite working). There are framed posters throughout the restaurant which range from a knock off of the Last Supper (seriously, it wasn't even a print of the real thing just a completely different rendition with JC sitting on his own side of the table -- most likely eating Greek pizza but I didn't look close enough), a 300 movie poster, a map of the world, St Pete sunset, and many more. My motivation for coming back will most likely be to better inspect the entire poster collection. It was totally bizarre and wonderful. Also weird is that you're given a "check" which is really just a take out menu with everything you ordered circled on it, and you're not given the total. I guess since it's so cheap no one minds this oversight. But, alas, ABC gets 3 stars since I left full and with leftovers, I had a good laugh, and I didn't spend much money.
Went in yesterday and looked at gluten-free items and some were LEANING ON YES TOUCHING gluten items!!! I mean, why bother then?

I'm trying really hard to not let one bad apple ruin the bunch, but let me tell you about that apple: I came in one Saturday morning, having strolled around the neighborhood and saw this place. Grabbed a menu and brought it home. It looked like they had a lot of vegan and gluten free options and even encourages you to customize the menu, so my roommate and I decided to order dinner from here! We called 1 hour to close (we live a few blocks away) and while I can't remember what she ordered, I know that I got the BLT + A. Everything was fine and dandy until we got there and realized it's cash only (I know, I'm one of those people but it's 2017! Come on!) So my roommate goes to take out cash and I noticed the bill was incredibly high. I asked to look at the receipt and see we were charged an EXTRA $2 for EACH sandwich for the avocado. I asked the woman at the front what that was for, and she pointed to a sign on the counter that said that avocado would be a $2 upcharge because of demand or something like that. So, let me tell you that both sandwiches are ALREADY made with avocado, with mine having "avocado" in the name. How are you going to charge $2 for a few slices of avocado on a $6 sandwich? That makes no sense. I would understand if I added avocado to an existing sandwich that didn't already have one, but the $6 price already reflects the cost of the avocado. My second qualm here is that when we called, WE WERE NEVER TOLD OF THE UPCHARGE! I would have gotten something else with no issue. When both of these points were raised to the extremely rude worker at the front, she scowled and gave myself and my roommate and attitude. I asked for the manager and she said that they were not there and "even if they were here, they would say the same thing." Words cannot describe how incredibly rude this woman/girl...I'll call her a girl...was to us. No "I'm sorry for the misunderstanding. Unfortunately this is our current policy. I'd be happy to remove the avocado for you if you wouldn't like to pay" or anything pleasant of the sort! We left without the food. So that was the one bad apple. However, I decided to give it another try yesterday morning because I really do love gluten free and vegan foods. This experience was significantly better. I essentially took like 5 things off of the menu in other items and created my own "concoction" and they were very accommodating and helpful! They even made the thing look pretty, too! Overall, I think I will be back...just not at night when that awful person is there. Remember it's CASH ONLY, though!

Food good, service unfriendly. Arriving around 10pm, we found a short line that we were pleased to find moved quickly. While waiting in line, I looked through the window into the kitchen to admire the rack-upon-rack of fresh donuts. That must have offended the sensibilities of one of the employees, because a moment later, he taped a piece of wax paper over the window. Nice. Subsequently, the guy behind the counter was unfriendly and unsmiling, and of little help other than placing our selections in the box. He seemed rather annoyed that we were so inconsiderate as to ask a question about the paleo/gluten free offering. The donuts are somewhere between good and very good. We picked up a box with a nice selection of different varieties to share and compare. The maple bacon donut surprised me with how good it was. I ordered it as a novelty, but genuinely liked it. The Gooey Butter donut was also tasty, but not as gooey or moist as I'd hoped. The Chocolate Haze was very good, as you would expect a chocolate donut to be. High marks for the Blueberry Cheesecake donut. My favorite of the flavors we tried.

No signs of food poisoning yet. Will update if need be. So far this is a positive experience. Came on a Sunday just before midnight, very convenient they are open till midnight every night. Gotta say though, key lime pie was no bueno. Dark night is definitely got the win on this one. This place is much better than Dough Cone next to Carrabbas. Very negative experience there. The little chocolate bear is a nice touch, we were very satisfied with that one.

Well I seem to have poor luck in the fast food world and it continued tonight a Chic-fil-a. I have tried to take away food for my family on two occasions from this location. In both instances food was missing from the order. The last time was 4/4/19 at 4:58. My cashier was Ryan and he rang up an order for my entire family to go. I had forgotten about my previous experience with the store so I didn't not check the order when it came out. $38 for what turned out to be French fries x3 a gluten free chicken sandwich and chicken nuggets as well as 4 drinks. They forgot an order of nuggets and a chicken sandwich all together. No matter how many "my pleasures", the service failed and in all honesty I feel cheated. I gave the food I did receive to my wife and children and I write this having gotten nothing but a drink. As a note to the store manager whom I left a message for ( we shall see if I receive a reply)kind words from a cashier will never replace actual food in my bag. I will not return.

I have loved this placed since it opened. They've always had such great food and I'm glad to say that has never changed. The last few times I've been with both friends and family, the service has seemed to lag. With two other girl friends (visited in January 2014) we were seated and then forgotten. No one came by for about 10-15 minutes to take our drink orders so we eventually flagged down a waitress who was incredibly busy already and she took care of us and apologized profusely. Things happen, we understood that. And the food was delcious when we finally got it. The next time I went I was with my parents and grandma (March 2014). We were seated right away and our drink orders were taken promptly. Then we waited. We eventually ordered about 15 minutes later and the food took another 20-30 minutes to receive. Again, it was absolutely delicious and worth the wait, but man, it was a wait. I order their Gluten Free Tomato Sunrise to-go all the time, and I can honestly say it's the best Gluten Free pizza at a reasonable price that I've found in Reno/Sparks so far. My to-go orders are always ready on time and the ordering process is very easy. If they improve their customer service then this place will absolutely receive 5 stars from me. I'll be back to visit as soon as I'm craving GF pizza again!

Wow. It appears that I'm the only one that has had multiple 'meh' expeirences here. I came here once, when it first opened- and almost threw up into my plate. No joke. But I digress... After sitting myself, I had to hunt down a waitress- who did not speak english- and I had to keep repeating 'water please' until she understood me. I actually had to gesture with my hands that I wanted a drink. She returned with a glass of tepid water that was only half full, with literally 3 little peices of ice and no straw. UGH. I ordered a Crystal Shrimp long roll (no avocado) with cream cheese. It's my 'test' order, if you will. Yea, they failed in my opinion. Big time. The rice was notably dry and unimpressive. The breading on the shrimp was not good. It tasted like it had been either overcooked or fried in old oil. Bleh. I'd eaten only a couple pieces of the roll when I looked at the roll and noticed that the shrimp wasn't deveined! EW! In every piece of the roll you could see little black lines of shrimp shit. I almost hurled in my plate. I waved the waitress over, but of course she couldn't understand a word I was saying. I tried explaining it to the sushi chef behind the counter but again, no clue what I was saying. Needless to say, I paid & left. I would have refused to pay for my shit filled shrimp roll, but they had no clue what I was trying to tell them. I swore to myself I'd never go back. Buuuut, it's near my house and I wanted to be SURE that they sucked before I ruled them out - they are so much closer than Ijji. I went back, and yea...still not impressed. I very specifically asked the waitress to make sure the shrimp was deveined. She seemed to understand what I was asking so that was a plus. The woman who took my order, was also the woman that made my food. I hope she washed her hands. She informed me that she cut the veins out of my shrimp. However, the shrimp was not merely overcooked- it was burnt. It had that lovely scorched taste to it and even though I asked for NO sesame seeds- there they were, in all their glory. IN ABUNDANCE. Like last time, I didn't eat more than a few pieces of the roll. It wasn't good. Too much rice and burnt shrimp-bleh. I also didn't appreciate all the sesame seeds that were in my teeth! One positive that I will say, is that even though my food was not good, the ladies were nice (even though most of them had no clue what I was saying) they were still smiling that I-have-no-idea-wtf-you-just-said smile. Will I go back? Meh. They've already got two strikes in my book- so it'll have to be pretty good next time for me to change my mind.

A lonely beacon of hope in the dreary, fluorescence of Suburban Station. Coffee quality is superb. Iced and Expresso drinks are molto bene. Service is friendly, and quick.. think of the opposite of Dunkin Donuts They offer Gluten free this and that.. fine selection of Croissants, 4th street cookies, biscottis, bagels, fruit. Only negatives.. coffee prices a tad up there..and need to add real/fresh cream cheese and toaster for the bagels.. cmon, DD can do it.

My honest review: Average pasta joint. Went there Monday night for back to school dinner. Super clean and beautiful inside. I would say on par with Olive Garden. Service was average and friendly. The meals are all served with Salad, bread, entree, Spinoni or ice cream. The salad is an iceberg blend but their dressing was tasty. The bread it served warm but it is so crusty and hard on the outside it left a mound of crumbs everywhere. My hubby tried 3 loaves asking for a fresh one each time and just all hard outside and airy no substance inside. The pasta was average. We had the three meat with spaghetti. The shrimp Alfredo (7 pieces of shrimp). 3 kids spaghetti-they loved it just fine and only cost about $6 each includes a drink. And my parents had the gluten free pasta and added a chicken breast. Funny enough their gluten free pasta was the biggest serving. The portions were more than enough. The most redeeming thing if the chilled metal cup of single scoop vanilla ice cream or Spumoni (think Italian neopolitan pistachio/cherry/chocolate) I don't know if we will be back soon but not saying we will never go back.

We came here after wedding dress shopping, I was super hungry and it seemed like a good place. I'm a vegan and I am also gluten free, they did not have any gluten free options besides a salad which was sad because their burgers looked amazing. Five of us ordered food and it took 35min to get our to-go order. Only once we got to where we were going did we realize they messed up three of our orders and gave us nothing to eat our salads with. What a mess!

Worst dining experience of my life. Bartender could not serve me a drink while we were waiting for our table because he only made drinks for the dining room. There is another bartender for the bar who was not there. Our reservation was for 7:30. We were not seated until after 8. Appetizers were good but uninspired. My "Pittsburgh" steak was warm in the middle, cooked medium at best. How do you call yourself a steak house and can't even properly cook a steak? Service was horrible from the hostess to the stoner manager that had no management skills. Not one visit to any table the 2 hours we were there. Best part of that meal was projectile vomiting it up when we got back to our hotel. Gross.

I won't be going back. The service was alright. Food was lackluster. The menu does not properly state ingredients, which is critical for me because I have food allergies. One dish a friend and myself shared was the tuna poke. The menu mentions nothing of avocado but I know it is usually in it at other places. I requested this to be on the side just in case it was in it. Of course the dish came out saturated in avocado and it was almost as if it was our fault it came out wrong. They poured the wrong champagne for my friend and instead of it being lagniappe they tossed it down the drain. I mean it could've been lagniappe considering our food was wrong. The lobster taco shells were stale as hell. No redo on that. The Brussels sprout salad was meh. Nothing about this experience has me running back. In fact I'll keep running past it.
Ordered the baked potato from gluten free menu, it was so dry I had to ask for sour cream. Other than that, everything was fine and service was good.

I came here with my parents, because my mother needs gluten-free and never gets good pasta when you're gluten-free. She was impressed how delicious the bread and pasta were compared to other gluten-free bread she's had in the past. So, A+ for the gluten free choices. The PESTO sauce (my weakness) was very good. I love a rich pesto, not weakened with heavy cream. This pesto, even though light in color, was very strong with the basil and seasonings that it tasted delicious to me. The RAVIOLI was the winning dish of the night. The square puffs were so delicate and fell apart in my mouth. It tasted like grandma was hand-making them for hours in her home kitchen. Very impressed, I used all the bread to wipe up the leftover sauce after all my raviolis were gone. Our server was a tad over-elaborate, or over-excited? But I actually loved it because he was cracking me up. My parents loved him because he carefully explained which dishes my mom could not eat due to cross-contamination of possible gluten in different sauces or oils. How honest! I love the BYOB. I love the gluten-free options. I love the casual, friendly atmosphere. And I love the reasonable prices. My only downfalls are; the tables are on top of each other. We were crammed in there, in heat from the oven, and on top of our neighbors conversations. Other downfall, is not all pastas are offered gluten free. I thought the entire menu was, but I was wrong. For example, my mom couldn't get the raviolis in gluten free, it was specific pasta noodles only. But, still, a much larger variety than majority of places in the city! 4 stars.

Eeeesh...so, this place has disappointed me one too many times. Ever since the so-called renovation it seems worse. First off, the menu hanging when you walk in has the tiniest print that you need binoculars to read. SECOND AND MOST IMPORTANT: They warm up and heat all the bread in a microwave WRAPPED IN PLASTIC. It is entirely toxic to do so and pretty idiotic to it on their part without knowing the repercussions that has on your health and ALSO in plain site's view. It's disgusting. The gyro was disgusting with way too much sauce and enough meat to fill up three sandwiches. it was not even edible. If the fact that they heat their bread over and over again with the loaf in the plastic in the microwave all day long doesn't make you want to vomit and get a cancer screening, maybe the terrible food will. Steer clear from this place, specifically all of them but this experience was in green hills.

My friend is was served tainted meat and threw up. It would be nice if they served untainted meat. This place should change its name to Inferior Grill. They also served me a margarita when I was 16, 12 years ago. They lack sufficient controls all around.

3 Stars overall: Our waiter last night was great (he was 5 stars) due to his desire to be of assistance. 4 stars for the pool tables and shuffle boards, and overall environment. We were a party of 6 on a Tuesday night and had the place to ourselves (mostly, that is). The deduct in points comes from the food. The menu is limited, especially for people who are gluten free and/or paleo. I think this place excels at bar food, but not healthier options. It is pricey and not everyone in our group loved their selections. My $16.95 salad left me completely under-whelmed. I left hungry!

I used my Yelp app to find a restaurant open at midnight that was not a bar. Brixx was an intriguing option because of the wood fire, and I like to support places that work to meet dietary needs like vegan or gluten free. The woman who answered was very welcoming to us when I called to make sure they'd be open and serving by the time we got there. We didn't have a host or anyone greet us so we made a lap through to the rear and back to the front. What I assume was the same friendly gal from the phone did then seat us, but it was right next to another table which for late night when all the other tables are open is not my favorite thing. I ordered a starter of Brixx Stixx, which at four for $6 is excessive. This comes with three dishes of sauce, one marinara and two that didn't look so good so we did not delve in. I think it was a cheesy honey sauce. Anyway, breadsticks were amazingly flavorful, hot, and balanced with the crunchy/soft aspects that make a perfect breadstick. More stixx, less sauce please Brixx! Kids pepperoni pizza and a margherita pizza were next. Bland on both counts. These are the basic two pizzas I get at first visit to a pizza place and these missed the mark. They didn't look so good and the cheese did not seem entirely melted. It did not look like the one pictured. $11 for a six slice pie seems overpriced. The feeling of paying for location and not so much for what went into the food was pervasive. In summary, I would give Brixx one more shot for pizza, and would return for Brixx Stixx and cocktails. +fairly reasonable distance to accessible parking -water on the floor the entire time we were there, that my partner slipped on, and staff were using as some sort of late night slip n slide. I see lawsuit city but none of the half dozen staff that were there seemed too concerned. It looked kinda low class in what is a very trendy and visually appealing restaurant. +attractive outdoor seating area -you can hear the convo of the table next to you if you get sat right by another party

They have really let this place go. Went on a Monday, restaurant was destroyed. We soon discovered why; one poor women was the hostess, waitress, bartender, and bus person. Food took forever to get. The tamale was acceptable. The shrimp enchiladas were a nightmare. These were not baked as one would expect. Think bad shrimp taco covered with a mushroom sauce. The sauce did not have one mushroom in it and had the consistency and appearance of baby vomit. Fried ice cream was acceptable.

The Affton diner is probably the worst place I've ever been to for lunch. While I was eating lunch, I noticed that the owner and waitress were bickering. I looked away for a moment, but when I turned around, I was stunned to see that the waitress had threw up her middle finger towards the owner. My friend had been served a soda with no carbonation because they were too lazy to fix the machine. I haven't even gotten to the food yet. My cheeseburger tasted like it was re-heated in an easy bake oven. My fries were cold and could easily tell they were microwaved. The restaurant looked like it had been coated in grease and spilled soda, despite the soda, the worst part was sitting in a cheap add on section to the restaurant that still had its grand opening sign from February -Its April 9..-. Happy 5th grand opening.

Love Korean BBQ, but our experience at Stacey's was a total train wreck. We were a party of six. And arrive 5 minutes early for our 1:00 reservation. We were seated and did not see a server until 1:22. Finally we were offered water, we had to request menus. When we asked if they had any gluten free items we were told - No. we ask to speak to a manager but we're told that they were not available. When we insisted they said they would get the manager. We saw manager come up and the server speakers g with him. The server told us that the manager said" if we don't like the menu we can leave". Really? So giving us a handful of un marinated shrimp was so out of the question that we were asked to leave? We could see in the servers eyes that he was terrified of the chef he told us the chef does not take to changes in the menu. So, we got up, paid for our appetizers and left. HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE, SERVICE, AND ATTITUDE. I WOULD GIVE IT 0zero0 Stars if I could!

This place is advertised as a gluten free place, but when you get there the owner will tell you that she sprinkles the cooking surface with wheat flour before cooking the injera bread, this might work for some folks but for the more sensitive among us it is a guaranteed "glutening", and definitely not "gluten free". I was charged full price for a small pile of spiced meat and had to go home and fill up on leftovers.

I've been looking for a good chinese food place in south Edmonton for a while now, This popped up on Yelp, thought I'd try it since it's close to my residence. I ordered: Crispy Ginger beef Chicken fried rice spring rolls Beef, broccoli and mushroom. What I got was perhaps the worst chinese food I've ever had, which is really saying something since I eat chinese food at least 1-2 times a week. Crispy ginger beef was a lie. In fact is was a big pile of mush with a terrible flavor. No real spice, tasted like breaded meat mush. chicken fried rice was bland, but acceptable. spring rolls. One bite, chew chew, spit out. what the hell did I just eat? almost threw up. beef broccoli and mushroom. - mediocre, tasted like it had been sitting in a pot for a couple days. I think I got 1 entire mushroom in the whole dish. I will never return to this place and I suggest you find another spot to try out.

The outside porch is fun, but the rest is mediocre at best. First the drinks...happy hour margaritas were too sweet and syrupy. Then we got the wrong beers. To Ballyhoo's credit, they replaced with the right ones and left the pumpkin beer for us to sip. We ordered a salad. It was fine. Mostly iceberg lettuce and unspectacular. The meal and sides were equally unspectacular. Edible yes. Not vomit inducing. Adequate. They came with overcooked sweet potato fries but the side of steamed broccoli was spot on. Overall, this place is overpriced for the value. Keep driving and find something better

Being gluten free and hearing all the rave about this place made me more than excited to try it I would like to compliment the waitress for being extremely aware of gluten allergies. They supplied gluten free bread for myself and regular bread for my fiancé. They served it with an oil. His came with garlic which would have been nice to try but due to the chance of cross contamination I was given my own oil. We ordered chicken perm pasta WHICH I WOULD RECOMMEND!!! The gluten free pasta was delicious!!! We also got the special of the night. The pesto sausage pizza. Which would have been good but we weren't aware of the stinky French cheese that topped it. The sausage and cheese and pesto was a weird combination. But once again it was a special. If you have never been here before read the menu and ask questions and do not settle for a special until you know everything about it! P.S. THEY HAVE A GLUTEN FREE FRYER!!!

This place is the case for Yelp to add a half star rating. The place had four star service (we sat at the bar because it was very busy but the bartender was great). I also liked how the place was set up as a restaurant/bar grocery store look it hives it a unique feel. Where it falls short is in the price and quality. My omelette was a two egg architect which had bacon, spinach and mushrooms. It was around $12/13 dollars. When I received it, it had a nice presentation and was nice and light, but the tomato wasn't flavorful (didn't have that garden fresh taste), a moderate amount of filling, and the bacon was burnt. So, due to the price and food quality I'm going with a three star rating but would be willing to try it again the next time I'm in Franklin.

Whoever made the Mac and cheese today, it was disgusting. I almost threw up. There were 3 noodles and way too much thick, slimy, cheese. Waste of $6.00. If you want to eat a pound of cheese for lunch, this is the place to be. Vomit

ZERO STARS. I just want to start out by saying we've been a long, long, long time customer of Olympia. Food is always good and hot when it gets delivered and we always make sure to tip well on top of the two dollar delivery charge. My issue today is not with the quality of the food but is in fact with the delivery. The other night we ordered take out like we do every week from Olympia and when I received my order upon opening my delivery I discovered that my mozzarella fries were half eaten. I don't know about you but I find that pretty disgusting when someone sticks their hands in my food. As crazy as I found that possibility I contacted the restaurant, asked for the manager or owner and began to explain the situation. He assured me he himself had packed my order and that it was fine and possibly got squished along the way to my house. I insisted this was not the case as I've ordered these several times before and they have never ever looked the way they looked when they arrived. After much convincing he gave me his cell phone number and I sent him a picture of my delivery and then he told me that it in fact did not look like that when he packaged it to send to my house - just confirming that the delivery guy had in fact helped himself to my families dinner on the way. Again DISGUSTING. Who does that ??? So I'm writing this review because the owner chose not to make it right. Not only he did not send new food ( we ate nothing who knows what else he contaminated or touched) he also did not offer any compensation for my $29 order and 4.50 tip. Thanks for nothing Olympia! So long story short DO NOT GO HERE and definitely do NOT order delivery. Needless to say we will not be going back. EVER.

Start prepping your gastronomic vocabulary sheets, it's time to head to Essene! Loaded with more organic, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, free range, hormone-free, unmolested, natural foods than you can shake your slightly funky poncho at, this local food market and cafe is a safe haven for the health-conscious inhabitants of Queen's Village and beyond. Walk in and feast your eyes on their small, yet high-end selection of vegetables, fruits and cheeses, followed by coolers stocked with everything from roasted garlic hummus to coconut water. The tiny aisles wrap their way around the store, containing a fairly expansive selection of all-natural, wholesome food tastiness. The hot bar and cafe are nestled towards the back end, allowing patrons to self-serve cafeteria style and take a seat to grub out. Expect an all vegetarian (or vegan) smorgasbord with plenty of gluten-free options. Buffalo tofu, pickled vegetables, roasted eggplant, seitan-inspired dishes...you get the point. ::Puts on copywriter hat:: - "Whether you want a freshly prepared vegan meal, local produce, vitamins, or fair trade chocolate, you'll find it all at Essene!" Phew, well that was fun, but the mitigating factor and deciding point on whether or not you shop here is the borderline oppressive pricing in this store. Yes, I understand the higher costs for organic, vegan (and on and on) foods, but I can't ever walk in here without getting tagged for $20-30, and sometimes I'm literally leaving with a couple items. The hot bar is a tasty veg option for a quick meal and there's plenty of specialty food items you won't find elsewhere, but I can't really understand some of the pricing in here at all.

I cannot express my love of Backspace enough. Being a writer, I instantly fell in love with the atmosphere of Backspace, it's a dive with a sentiment of corner bar in any neighborhood in America. Books and typewriters? You're speaking my native tongue. Strong Jameson shots? Cold beers? All there. We stumbled in late night and we're met with a safe haven of fantastic rock and roll instead of the vomit-inducing thug rap that litters every other bar in the quarter. Any bartender who'll put on some Social Distortion and pour me a whiskey just found a friend in me. We spent a damn few fine hours with the late night dude, Swede and it was amazing. I didn't bother with the food, I had all the bottles of hooch a man needed. Swede hooked us up anytime we needed a refill and kept all of the strippers who just got off work on their toes. You wanna talk about knowing the clientele? Dude had smokes, lit people's for them and never let my glass go empty. Next time I'm in Nola, count on my ass in a seat in Backspace. Best hidden gem in the Quarter.

Mediocre meal, mediocre music -- not terrible by any means, but nothing special either. Waitress was spunky and fun, but the service overall was a little casual, the food was pretty bland, and the space was an odd one too. They did have gluten-free options though, which is why we picked it. We probably won't be back.

My wife and I have lived close by the Parkallen Restaurant for years, but this was the first time we went for dinner. Overall it was quite enjoyable, but probably not on my top list of restaurants. We ordered one the their mezza's to share (a selection of various lebanese foods). We also added on some stuffed grape leaves. All the food was quite good, with the falafel, grape leaves, lebanese salad, and hummus being the hits. Probably the weak points were the two varieties of lebanese sausage. They were tasty, but cold and a little dry. Overall I really enjoyed the food though and, as someone with a gluten intolerance, I also really appreciated that they offered gluten-free pita (my wife said it was almost as good as the regular pita). The service did seem a little swamped though, and it took quite a while for our food to come out / then later to get the bill. Our server later told us they were missing one of the servers, so I'll cut them some slack. And although we were seated within a couple minutes, I saw some people waiting to be seated for quite a while, despite there being open tables. Finally is the price. It's definitely not cheap. And while I'll say that some of the food was worth it, some was definitely not. Overall we'll probably be going back, but not all that often because of the price. I would like to try one of their pizzas, as I also saw it is offered on a gluten-free crust.

they're service was terrible. when we asked how much longer, all of the staff got aggressive with myself and acted like i had no right to ask how much longer after 20 minutes. It felt like I was being rude just asking when my food would be ready! The staff was beyond rude and the lines were unreal. Never going back. we also got a gluten free pizza and they didn't follow any of topping requested. they gave me whenever food was ready, regardless if it was what we actually preferred. This was the rudest service ever.

Meh - this is how I left after having dinner at Burger Study. It was ok, not as good as other burger places but not terrible by any means. I do appreciate gluten free buns being available. I had the turkey burger and it was ok; again not the best turkey burger I've ever experienced but not the worst. Keep in mind, everything on the menu is a la carte so aides are different price points. If you have children with you, their menu is very affordable. $5.00 for an kids' entree, side and beverage.

I went for the first time tonight and I had one of the worst experiences I've ever had dining in Philly. I ordered a few rolls and took a seat. Then a mouse walks not runs but walks from behind the counter to the soda fridge. The cashier didn't see it but the cook did see it. He looked at me and then turned away. On top of all that, the sushi was warm and disgusting. I vomited. It was my first and needless to say last time. I will be reporting them to the city. They don't maintain a clean kitchen.

This was the last meal I had in NOLA and I'm hitting myself on the head for not trying Desire earlier. The raw oysters are HUGE they look like mutants. They have the same fresh, raw taste so nothing much to say about it except you get more bangs out of your buck. However, the spicy broiled shrimp is God-sent delicious, and had I known this place earlier I would have come by every single day to have shrimps (and possibly get food poisoning).

They burnt my first pizza, put dairy on the second (I'm lactose intolerant) then when they made a new one it was completely trash and fell apart. All of this took atleast an hour and a half or more of waiting. Then wasted more of my time with very bad and inattentive service. Completely wasted most of my night out with my girlfriend. I don't usually review restaurants because I'm usually carefree but I downloaded yelp just to trash this mellow mushroom, place was simply run by people who were incapable of doing things correctly. I love mellow mushroom but do NOT go to this one. Terrible food and terrible service.

Cute little breakfast place, with a few good gluten-free options. I chose this place because online the menu stated that they had gluten-free waffles. However when we got there we learned that the kitchen has cross contamination issues. I ordered an omelette which was fantastic and my father ordered a unique dish of mole tamales. I appreciated the honesty that the servers had with my gluten allergy.

i'm going to tell you that i absolutely loved my burger. now i'm going to tell you that i've been eating green beans and all things vegan for the past few weeks, so anything not gluten free/healthy is gonna get an A+ in my book. all that aside, i have to say that the objective side of me expected more from this place. while i loved the guys behind the counter and the star wars/jurassic park soundtrack music playing in the background, i wanted more from my $10 meal. we also tried the truffle fries --- i wasn't really feeling those. apparently, philadelphia is big on truffle oil --- news to me. come to nyc, try a shack burger. walk away happy.

We had lunch there yesterday as in a previous occasion we had been there, ordered the seafood pasta and it was great. This time the food and service were below average. I ordered a burger and it was dry and the sangria was watery with no flavor. We ordered extra napkins and straws and never got them. This time we sat inside and it was full of flies, they said it was normal because of the weather (personally unacceptable). Later that day I got food poisoned from eating the burger and today I was unable to go to work. I will not return or recommend this place.

Cannuli's is GREAT and very reasonably priced. Chicken, meats, turkey is all fresh and good there. Recently, I've been ordering their cooked food too...chicken parm and oddly chicken meatloaf. Yeah, that sounds weird but, throw a little hot sauce on this stuff along with cannuli's tomato sauce and its like crack. Incredibly good.
