I've been privileged to go behind the scenes at cannuli's and these guys are CLEAN. Don't have to worry about contamination of meats here. Great service is a huge plus.

Horrible food! Fair drinks! I saw some disgusting behavior at the bar. One chick used her bare hands with no gloves to refill olives! They use their nasty contaminated hands at the bar to garnish drinks! DISGUSTING!! The food at this location is the absolute worst I've ever experienced at a Bar Louie! I had to send my food back it was so bad! My friend picked through his food and it was equally as bad!! To top it off when we ordered "to go" for later that evening at the hotel... they brought it out with our dine in meal Ugh and when we were ready to eat it later that evening..... we would touch it!!!!! It was terribly prepared and horrible tasting! Don't go to this place for dinner! You'll be HIGHLY disappointed with their food! MANAGEMENT Hire some new cooks people!!!!! AND TEACH YOU TEAM ABOUT SANITATION! Yuck I didn't want to give this place any stars! Worse Bar Louie on the map! Good luck

My family has complicated food allergies, so it is always comforting to come here. The staff is always incredibly accommodating and friendly about making sure no one has to use their epi pen (ha). The food is always delicious, but so filling so maybe don't eat before you come.

I saw a show on the food network that spoke about Texas Roadhouse ribs. Supposedly they take 3 days to make. So I was really excited when my sister let me talk her into coming despite the fact that we were really busy in the middle of moving her out of her apartment. (Thanks, sis!) The place was very noisy with about 3 birthdays. I really admire the stamina of the wait staff, there was a lot of loud singing and even dancing. The wait staff generally seemed very nice and the manager even came out to ask us to do a survey. I thought the food came out a bit on the slow side, but then it is a steakhouse, and we were so exhausted from the moving that I can not 100% vouch for my sense of time. Needless to say I ordered the ribs (with a side house salad and mashed potatoes). Prior to ordering, there is a good sized pail of peanuts on the table and homemade rolls with cinnamon and honey butter is served. The peanuts are nice, and I mention them for those with peanut allergies planning on visiting this place. But the true star were those soft and warm rolls. As one can imagine, the cinnamon and honey butter really helped matters too. My salad came out first, and I was really impressed, for a small side salad, it was a pretty good size with lots of great ingredients. It had a good amount of eggs, tomatoes, cheese and crouton. The croutons were supposedly homemade and tasted like it. When the rest of my food came out., I was really excited. Unfortunately, then came the crash. The ribs, although falling off the bone, were on the dry side. There really was not much BBQ sauce on it, and a lot of smokiness. I know some people like as much smokiness as they can get, but I prefer just a hint. I should mention that the mashed potatoes were good, but the portion was on the small side.

First time to visit Bandit. Love the decor and relaxed atmosphere though it is a loud room. The tables are high top and there is a wall of smaller gathering spaces. I wouldn't say that the coffee house is conducive to discussing business as the music is a bit on the loud side. Now to the coffee. I ordered a regular cup of coffee and added a bit of cream and sugar. I enjoy a robust cup of coffee. The coffee is thin and acidic and really does not suit my palate. Jet City and Urban Bungalow in Tampa are still my faves with Jet City brewing Seattle's Best it is my top favorite- a robust full bodied coffee. I also had a pumpkin muffin which I believe is gluten free- what isn't anymore in these hipster places? That said it was very tasty, dense but pleasantly spongy and naturally good tasting! Bandit is a nice place, but doesn't hit the mark with me for a cup of coffee. I left with an aftertaste of bitterness sitting on my tongue, odd and not pleasant.

I was soo excited to try eats American Grill. The reviews were great. Unfortunaty my experience there wasn't very good. Our server was excellent... Amd upon being seated they bring out some tasty homemade potatoe chips. They offer a good 2for 1 happy hour on beers and well liquirs as well... But that is where the good ends for me. I ordered the Sandiego burger medium rare on a gluten free bun and my friend order his medium well. When the food came out my burger was on toast it looked like so I asked if it was gluten free. The server took it right back into the kitchen. My friend went to eat his burger and it was rare. Not even edible rare just rare. We flagged down the server and sent the burger back. A while later my burger came out on a gluten free bun... I cut into it to check how it was cooked... And it was rare even more so than my friends burger. We told the server... She offered to have them remade but we had lost our appetite by then. The server kindly said they would comp our drinks and appologized and we left.

I decided to make a reservation here for my girlfriend and I for this years valentines day. I'm not a snob at all, but this place was a horrible horrible disappointment. Beer was warm, they didn't have one of the apps that I ordered and the waiter gave me something else without asking me first. Food wasn't good at all. When I got the bill I saw that 20% gratuity was already added! for a table of two. I've never seen that before ever for a two top. I felt almost as if the waiter wants to scam the customers into overlooked the added gratuity in hope they'll tip on top of bill. If the place couldn't get worse I threw up 2 hours after leaving the restaurant. I would never recommend this place to anyone ever. Do not go here. I'm also writing the owner with my complaint.

I'm upset. I've been ordering from here for years which is why I'm giving two stars. Side Bar: a common trend on Yelp is for people to comment on an establishment when they mess up. Sorry Szechuan but I am doing just that. This was a huge mistake. The first mistake was when I noticed brown rice even though I requested white rice. I let it slide because brown is healthier and this was the first time they made this mistake BUT THE BIG mess up is coming up next. Another Side Bar: I'm a vegetarian. So as I was chowing down on my food, I tasted something funny and chewy. I immediately knew it was meat! I don't know if it was pork or chicken but I was disgusted! I had to spit it out and examine and YES it was meat! When you haven't eaten meat in a while, the taste and texture of meat is equivalent to vomit (for me). I'm really upset because this was my go-to chinese spot.

After quite a bit of chatter, Mumbai bistro finally opened last week as a welcome addition to the buzzing neighborhood. The whole concept is to deliver fresh meals on a budget, and I believe delivering on a wholesome food promise without putting a dent on my wallet is a healthy proposition. The is no décor per se, a small dining area if u want to eat in, and a fridge loaded wid goodies and ofcourse the buffet line complete the place. One of owners, Kyle manned the register and he patiently explained about the 4.95$ per pound of food, the daily rotating food menu, the vegan and the lactose free menu items. The service is absolutely fantabulous and very welcoming. It is funny that I couldn't picture how much a single pound of food would look like, and I was pleasantly surprised to fill most of the plastic container with about a scoop of most things and a couple scoops each of my favs, all in 1.5 pounds. I am not a big fan of the buffet line, just cos I generally hog tooo much and am rendered useless for most of the afternoon but this blows that theory out of the pond. The menu changes daily, and includes fan favorites like chicken tikka and paneer masala, but there are also some of the more homely dishes like saag paneer (spinach / mustard leaf gravy) and aloo gobi ( potatoes and cauliflower ) which hold more appeal to me. I felt some of the curries were a bit bland, but nothing too bad. Only the entrees are lined on the buffet, but not the rice, breads and the appetizers, so that's an extra as u complete the meal. U can pick one of the lassi or mango drinks from the cooler to fight the heat and a dessert to seal the deal. So if it is gluttony on the cheap u are looking for, this might not be the best bet. But if u want curries , kormas and vegetables to taste the way they intend to and not like overused baking soda u have chosen wisely my friends. Very Wisely. Cheers

Not impressed. I've never visited The Flying Cupcake but decided to the other day since I was in the neighborhood. I got the "Happy Birthday to Me" and DH got the gluten free chocolate. The cake tasted like box mix. Duncan Hines, Betty Crocker, whatever--there's no way these were made from scratch. To top this off, after tax, we paid nearly $7. Now, I don't mind spending money on quality, but, again, this was not quality. At least boxed cake mix is not quality in my world.

This little brewery ain't so bad! This brewery is located in a pretty industrial area and seems rather huge. My husband and I sat at the bar and was greeted by a very friendly bartender. I ordered the Tucson Blonde which was nothing to write home about. In fact, it was a little flat. My husband and I ordered the artichoke dip and that was FANTASTIC. For our main dishes, he had the western burger which he describes as, "good". I had the veggie burger which was less than MEH. I had literally, 4-5 bites and was over it. I used the top bun to dip into the artichoke dip. Lol For our second round of drinks he had the IMPERIAL RED and I had a Bloody Mary. He loved his beer (which had a high alcohol content). The Bloody Mary, however, had the consistency of drinking vomit from a straw. It was NOT awesome. The atmosphere was nice, which I really appreciate.

This place was not great. The margaritas tasted like yellow gatorade and only maybe had tequila in them. The guacamole had no flavor. We tried to leave as quickly as possible. Also, no gluten free options, so that was kind of disappointing. I would not recommend anyone go here.

ETA: I spoke with Angie, the manager, and she was wonderful. Although the customer service we experienced during our dinner was not great, I feel like Angie heard and validated my frustrations. She offered me a gift card to return to the restaurant and I look forward to a more positive experience next time. I have food allergies and came to Timpano thinking they would not have an issue accommodating. Unfortunately, I found that the majority of their items could not be made without dairy, soy, and nuts. Our server took our order and returned a LONG while later to tell me they couldn't make the dishes he had told me would be OK. He suggested I just order a protein and steamed vegetables (which is super boring and not what I want when I go out to eat). We were able to enjoy the mussels, thankfully. We decided to share scallops and broccolini. Our server explained that it typically comes with 3 scallops so he added 1 scallop on so we could each have 2. Imagine my SHOCK to receive a bill for $45 for 4 scallops and 4 sprigs of broccolini - a $15 charge for 1 scallop (when the only side they could give me was a vegetable). We were there for over 2 hours (not because we were having a leisurely meal, but because it took them WAY too long...) and didn't want to get into a battle over the bill then. I have tried to reach out to the restaurant to give them an opportunity to listen to my concerns, but have not received a response. There are too many good restaurants that care about customer service to return here.

Went there for lunch without researching the place beforehand, huge mistake. Ordered a $10 chicken salad only to find out when I took a bite that it's fake chicken. I am unsure what the chicken was actually made of but I feel like I have been deceived. It's fine to have a restaurant that only serves vegetarian food, but HipCityVeg did an unbelievably poor job of making it clear to customers that the meat isn't actually meat. Besides the fake meat, the salad was an extremely small portion for $10. I know a lot of food is pricier in Center City, but I can guarantee that within one block, I could find a restaurant that had a salad twice as filling for the same price. On top of that, I paid an extra $1 for added avocado. There ended up being a single slice of avocado in the salad. Although I can't fault HipCityVeg for being crowded, I can say that the lines were unorganized and there was no order for where to go to be handed your (lack of) meal. The few positives included a nice, friendly staff and a delicious salad dressing. This is a restaurant for vegan, gluten-free hipsters who pay a pricey premium to get food that they can Instagram. Will not go back.
Dirty and poor atmosphere, in a sketchy neighborhood. Food was mediocre, but unique. Had many gluten free options. Fast service.

What a waste! Was excited about going here as they showed up in a list of gluten free restaurants however NONE of their meat patties are marked gluten free!!! Not even the grilled chicken! What's the point of carrying GF buns and marking gluten free on the menu when there is clearly no intention of truly catering to gluten free diners? The only GF burger is also vegan. What's the point of going to a burger joint and not being able to get a burger??? This whole gluten free "effort" is FRAUDULENT! Edits....I was mistaken, they do have GF buns, and the burgers are GF. Given the design of the menu it's easy to miss these but there are in fact GF options available. I enjoyed my burger but wasn't overwhelmed. I haven't been back since the one time, shortly after my initial review. Also, I had asked for the bun to be toasted (or grilled), something you must do with GF bread or else it breaks apart when you eat it. It didn't look grilled when it came to the table so I mentioned that to the waiter who assured me it had been grilled. But then it crumbled in my hands like all other GF breads that aren't toasted or grilled. I ended up eating the burger with a knife and fork.

Averaged three star rating based on four stars for taste and two stars for execution. The user friendly website featuring generous coupon offers and simplistic online ordering platform also displays the current status of your pie. Once it has been cooked and inspected it should be on its way out the door. Unfortunately several minutes go by while your pizza cools down and is delivered lukewarm or cold. As for the gluten free pizzas, wow! They nailed it. The crust and toppings are surprisingly tasty. The premium chicken is pretty tender. I'm a fan of the creamy garlic sauce and prefer it over the tomato sauce. Overall a satisfying pie that would be so much better if it arrived piping hot like pizza should. Something changed over the past year. Delivery service isn't slow but they may need to turn the AC down or upgrade their insulation. Pizza should burn the roof of your mouth and the cheese should string from mouth to slice!

I had heard great things about M.L. Rose and it has been on my list of places to try for several months. We go to church in Sylvan Park and it was a good excuse to give it a try today...with our 2 young children (mistake). If I were just rating the food, I'd give it 4.5 stars. My husband and I both ordered the burger of the month, which was the Cowabunga Burger with pineapple and teriyaki, served with waffle fries. The burgers were very juicy and flavorful and the fries were slightly above average. As for the service, I'd give it a 2. As I mentioned, we had our boys- ages 4 and 9 months. We were told to sit anywhere we'd like, and we chose the patio. Nothing was offered as far as seating for the kids so when I went to the front to ask about high chairs, the young woman I spoke to said less than cordially, "We have booster seats." After a pause I said I would take one, and she seemed a little annoyed to have to walk to the back to get one for me. I immediately felt like we were an inconvenience to the staff, and then when there seemed to be no kids' menu, I was convinced that this wasn't a family place, but we still wanted to try it so we hung in there. It was a challenge to figure out how to comfortably feed my 9 month old when I was nervous that the booster seat wouldn't support him enough. It barely worked sitting in a chair with me having one hand on him while I ate. Our server (maybe the same woman who got the booster seat, not sure) was also less than friendly when my husband asked if the sauce was gluten free. She did say that she would ask the chef, but again, we felt like an inconvenience and my husband perceived some rudeness. We paid $8 for my 4 year old to get a full plate of quesadillas, which he could barely eat a quarter of. They were good too, but having kid-sized options would have been nice. All this to be said, even if your restaurant doesn't really draw families with young children, a little accommodation and a smile can go a long way. We might be willing to give it a try again on date night and I'd sample the beer, which actually might have helped take the edge off my frustration today!

Don't get me wrong, the food here is creative and delicious. The flavor combinations are unique and the ingredients of the best quality. The service is another matter. I've been here three different times and the service is consistent, meaning consistently disappointing. I would define it as hipsters trying-too-hard-to-be-arrogant-hipsters. They got the uniform down pat: drab (seems unwashed) tees, piercings and tats galore, greasy hair colored with tints not seen in nature, etc. This is all fine but we found the staff doesn't understand customer service. When I ordered a cappuccino and kindly requested a bit of steam milk, I was given a mini-lecture on "a cappuccino is supposed to be all foam" (not so or at least not in Italy) When we asked a question about gluten-free items, the waitress was visibly put off, sighed and rolled her eyes. On two separate visits, we had to get our server's attention multiple times. And don't ask questions about a dish...you'll get "the look". As they say in Shark Tank, because of all of the above, I'm out.

Breakfast food is my favorite. And this place is delicious! Way more unique than a waffle house or IHOP with it's semi - organic menu and some things are even gluten free ( however, I'm not sure how much I would trust the cross contamination...). I had the lemon poppyseed waffle. It was so good. Light and fresh. I also ordered the homemade country sausage, which wasn't bad. But my friend got the ham and I wish I had ordered that instead. I also had a bite of their french toast, which was amazing. But don't even try their biscuits and gravy. They were bland and dissapointing. The resturant is small and gets pretty warm. It's also in a fairly hidden and questionable outlet mall. But try it! The food is so worth it!

Le Booze is your typical Bourbon St ultra clean but still extremely non sober for the middle aged crowd. Its absolutely spotless and does not smell of spring break vomit. The gentleman tending bar was incredibly nice, diligent, and professional. Gotta say though I didn't return. A lite beer was $5 for a 12oz bottle. They may have a hard time keeping that up when Big Ass Beer is $3 across the street.

Went to the mall today (7/1/20 around 5:30pm) with my mother to grab a pretzel and a drink from Cinnabon and then we were going to leave. My mom has severe asthma. She's been isolated for months cause she can't wear a mask without literally passing out. We walked up and a worker (who said his name was Steve, but he had no name tag on and I'm sure he lied) and he started SCREAMING at my mother for not wearing a mask. He called her a Karen over and over completely cussing her out and telling her how selfish she was. He then picked up his phone (with the same gloves he uses to grab peoples food with) and began to record her on his phone. My mom tried to explain we just came to grab food and leave and she can't wear a mask for medical reasons. He wasn't willing to hear anything. He kept recording my mom and cussing her out. Not only was this guy on the clock being paid to act like this and touch his dirty phone with the gloves he uses to touch everyone pretzels with, but he completely humiliated a customer. He has no idea of her health issues, so he had no right to say anything to her!! Much less record her and cuss her out WHILE ON THE CLOCK. He was screaming across the mall as we were trying to leave. This is honestly not acceptable behavior, especially during these times. My mom has been locked away in her home to be safe, unable to go anywhere and do anything due to her health and gets treated like this by an employee. I'm not sure how Auntie Anne's is okay with employing someone like this and putting peoples health at risk by cross contaminating his gloves by touching his phone to record someone and cuss them out while on the clock. These times have been hard on everyone, but this is beyond unacceptable.

I was invited to join friends for Dim Sum on a Saturday. We wanted to make reservations for 11 am but were told they do nit take reservations for 11 or later. We had to make them for 10:45. The food was your typical Dim Sum fare with a few different offerings such as the "Chinese donut" fried dough inside a moist rice wrap and fried taro root stuffed with bbq pork. The service was slow. Not surprising as the restaurant is huge. We had to try and get the attention of some servers as they pushed their trolleys of food anywhere but near us. I recommended that you go with someone who either had eaten there before or speaks Chinese ad several of the servers do not speak English well and dining was an adventure as we didn't know what we were eating. It was hard for the two children with us who had nut allergies. Their parents basically had to see if I reacted before the girls could eat some of the things (yes, I have nut allergies too). The food was very good. Ask to try the Oolong tea, it is a delicious alternative to their tasty jasmine tea. The price is not too high in comparison to other Dim Sum locations. I did use the washrooms and the owners must have read the other Yelp reviews. The women's washroom was spotless! I highly recommend you make reservations. It is a popular restaurant!

Consistently the most amazing pho I've ever had. As someone who eats a lot of pho and normally dumps roasted chile paste into it, I say.... Don't do it. Do not contaminate this profoundly delicate exquisite broth with spice. It is perfection just the way it comes. I always order the rare beef pho, and it is so far above any other place I've been, there's no comoparison. The beef is so thinly sliced it's almost translucent, and is essentially placed raw in an elegant pile above the broth, so when you submerge it into the hot liquid with fresh thai basil it cooks just the perfect amount, turning color before your eyes. The Lilly spring rolls are amazing too. Seriously, strawberries and shrimp with peanut sauce? Yes.

Let me preference with saying, I didn't know this was a gluten free, all natural etc ice cream shop when I walked in. And it's not something i would think makes a big difference in ice cream. It does. It took a lot of bites but I've decided I do like it for what it is which is a more natural, perhaps healthier (no preservatives) approach to ice cream. However, lacking that information, on its own, it's not as tasty as its comparable counter parts in the city. It's pricy, but you're paying for quality, albeit very sparing ingredients. The flavors are very subtle and the consistancy is a little icy. But it's not as heavy as others and I feel good about consuming it. I tried the peanut butter honey banana and the almond something. Both were subtle and light. Overall, maybe not my first choice in a treat, but interesting.

Tasty! The owner was SO nice. And what's better is she was actually from Hawaii, born and raised. Gotta love that. I got the homemade veggie burger and it was nom nom nom! Loved it. I will totally go back and recommend this place. I did not get to stay for the hula show (Fridays at 7pm I think--people reserve their seats days in advance just FYI), but I love that they have it and I have heard that it is great. Lots of healthy options, which I love and they cater to gluten free and sugar free diets for those of us who are conscious about what we eat. Very nice atmosphere with down to earth staff and owner. Great place overall.

What a gem! I recently had a family member with celiac disease visiting and we stopped in for lunch. The Clayton location is convenient with parking on the side and a fair amount of seating available both inside and outside. None of us had ever tasted gluten free sandwich break or breadsticks that were so amazing. Many gluten free bread products have a texture that is dry and crumbly. Not the bread at New Day! Being able to order anything off of the menu without fear or cross contamination, not feeling "different" for asking for a gluten free menu, and not quizzing waitstaff on ingredients was such a treat. I wish there were more cafes and bakeries like New Day. If you have celiac disease this is a must visit!

This is a fun place to go to. We had to wait about 20 minutes for a table, Saturday evening 6:30 pm. Fun décor. Staff very friendly and competent. Quick, efficient service. What a menu! Very exotic selections of burgers. Also gluten free friendly which is great. I had the elk with blue cheese, bacon, tomato relish on and on. Good. Well prepared. The fries and rings are tasty but not crisp. Guess that's not their style. We sat in a booth. The crowd was thinning so there were empty table. Even so, the bus person came by at least 7 or 8 times to take our plates. Little by little he succeeded in removing things from the table. He kept asking. even tho I had a piece of burger in one hand and the other hand was holding on to my plate. Later on our waiter dropped off our bill. No one asked if we wanted desert or coffee. By that time a loud group was in the next booth and our ears were ringing. My rating would have been 4 stars except for the fact we received the bum's rush. Maybe we didn't fit their demographic or perhaps there was a plate shortage in the kitchen. Who knows.

I appreciate that they offer gluten free crepes, but in general I was disappointed with the prices. Dear GOD, some of the crepes are $14, $15, even $16!!! I would never spend that kind of money on one crepe, that's highway robbery! Also a cup of soup was $9.

I was really taken in by the amazing service the first time I came and the interesting and appetizing menu options. But the next and final visit were great disappointments. The gluten-free bowls (the Moroccan Mac and cheese) were soupy both times and the smoothies were watered down. I love the concept and idea but that's not enough to keep me coming back and spending my money to still feeling hungry and dissatisfied.

VERY small facility, VERY understaffed. After being told 3 times by 2 servers someone would be witth us in a minute, a waitress took our order 15 minutes later. Don't misunderstand. The employees were working and moving but they couldn't keep up. The caprese salad had very little olive oil and no balsamic. It was really difficult to get an extra glass of wine, a beer, or water because they were so busy. However, they are so busy because the pizza was fabulous! Three different kinds: one with pesto, one with white sauce, and one with traditional red sauce. All were delish! The fennel sausage was wow! The wine was a really lovely Italian red that would have complemented the pizza bite I had finished it before the pizza came. We had both a gluten free and traditional crust. The gluten free wasn't overly sweet like so many are; the crusts were thin and charred perfectly. And the price is reasonable. SO! Excellent food!!!! Mediocre service, although everyone was charming. I hate giving a 3+++ but we arrived at 5:30 and didn't leave until 7. FOOD a 5. SERVICE a 2. Ana I was shortchanged $5 in change. :-(

I used to order SoFresh a lot, however, I had to stop because of the increase in price. Everything on their menu has gone up in price, which is upsetting because I used to love ordering from this restaurant. That being said, the food is really good, and so are the gluten free cookies.

Wow what poor food quality and service.. Every time we come here the lids meals are the last meals to come out. Everyone at the table ate all their food before a simple kids meal crepe came. The same thing happened last visit, but with a grilled cheese.. The excuse.. A new chef... In addition the steamed broccoli tasted like dishwasher water.. When the food finally came, the so called manager who had just came is from smoking and didn't even wash her hands prior to getting the crepe off the food line, brought it to the table and reached across my face,which almost made me want to vomit.. Who else has had this poor service and poor quality or experience. $70 dinner that we couldn't even enjoy as a family. I vow to never eat here again P.S. I yelp would not allow me to put less than 1 star Definitely Not KID FRIENDLY since the kids meals always come last to the table.
Wtf is this crap. Seriously bad service. Bad food. Too much grease. I'd rather eat my own vomit.

The owners are so lovable & just geniuses with healthy affordable gourmet foods.Tons of Gluten free!!!! I'm sad that their desserts are not gluten-free & that the desserts & most of the beverages contain refined white sugar. My take-out box meal is literally heavy; enough food for 2 meals. The creative combination of flavors is indescribable in what might normally be described as "a mountain of quinoa" "a pile of tomatoes & onions". Eases my sadness that Cajun Kitchen just closed. It's Near my house, I'm in heaven. They are careful with cross-contamination Vegan options, too

Miucha aesthetic is top notch, if you want a cute place for an insta story or snap story, they really took time to decorate for millennials and under. I ordered the mixed boba tea as per recommendation of the cashier. She recommended to add cheese to it. So I did. --- As I drank my sweet boba tea I would get a chunk of cheese that would surprise my taste buds from time to time and I honestly was about to vomit. Personally, I think that cheese does not belong in boba. My gf got the peach oolong tea which expressed tasted okay. Long story short if you want an aesthetic for the social media, this place is a must. But if you want a good boba tea try the other bubble tea shops near Miucha.

Disgusting. Terrible smells like vomit and poop throughout the whole place. Absolutely terrible. And the whole pie was burnt. Do not recommend this place to anyone and definitely don't waste your time going here. I would give it 0 stars if that was an option.

I ended up having an allergic reaction because they put onions in my food, when i asked for none. In their defense they were sooooo busy!! So Stuff happen I called the manager, they were very nice and rectified the situation Staff is always nice, you always get greeted by at least 3 people Food is always amazing Good work honeygrow

Felt compelled to write this even though I hate giving bad reviews. I work in customer service and I am VERY lenient when it comes to those in the service industry but could not let this experience go. First off, it took a long time for a waiter to even come to our table. Minus one. Then when we gave the waiter our order he had another tables order and thought it was ours. We clearly explained that wasn't ours and then he argued saying we gave that to him as well. We didn't. Minus two. My order was special because I had allergies so I had a separate sheet to order my rolls. That's the one plus I will give. However one roll of mine was wrong but I didn't complain. Minus three. Our other orders of appetizers came out and were pretty good. The mussels were my favorite. The sushi rolls that were brought out next were all wrong but we were starving at this point and didn't care. At least one of the rolls was one we ordered. Minus four. We constantly had to ask for more refills and the right drinks. Minus five. Then a next plate came out with five rolls that, again, we didn't order. Minus six. Something was wrong. We asked if they were ours and the waiter told us they were and showed us the menu with orders. It was the original one that we clearly told him was NOT ours with about ten rolls of which we didn't order. Minus seven. Clearly for the big table around the corner. When we said again that it was the wrong table and wrong paper, the waiter actually RAISED his voice and was very very angry and told us it was our fault. Minus eight. BIG NO IN MY BOOK. No matter if you despise a customer you never raise your voice. Then we asked to talk to a manager. The waiter stood next to him to listen. The polite thing and proper thing is to excuse yourself so the guest feels comfortable voicing their opinion without having them to interrupt. Minus nine. Then AS I was talking and explaining everything that happened the manager actually cut me off and said "no miss listen" another HUGE red flag in my book. Minus ten. Way in the negatives here people. I was calm, polite, and tried to be patient and just make sure they knew what went wrong and to fix it. By far the worst service experience and management/employee service skills I've personally encountered. Yes I acknowledge that instead of paying for 3 AYCE we all split paying for two but would much rather paid full price for good service that we didn't get. To top that off, the sushi was mediocre and I never got the nigiri or dessert that I ordered. This was my first experience at Sushi Rose and I do not think I will come back.

Dear lord. I will never return to this place. I've been wanting to stop in, as it looks like a nice spot The atmosphere inside was very nice - very low key and airy. However, that's about where this love affair ends. We walked in and they said pick a seat. We sat down in the middle. Within a couple minutes, a party of about 8 walked in. There were a lot of empty tables, but since we were in the middle there would be no room for them. They were about to turn them away so we offered to move. Totally not a big deal, but they were pretty disorganized and flustered about it. We ordered drinks - I ordered the Pomegranate martini which was drinkable but not good by any means. It looked slightly like dirty water - couldn't tell there was any pomegranate in it. We only wanted a light afternoon snack. I asked if they did the roasted apple and cheese plate in the daytime (which was on their happy hour menu), and the waitress informed me that she was unsure if they had cheese. I mentioned it was on their happy hour menu and she informed me that she doesn't work the night shift. So, since that was apparently a giant question mark, I asked about the hummus plate. My girlfriend is gluten free, so she inquired about what accompanied the hummus. The waitress said there were crostini with it, and she asked if we could do veggies instead. "What type of vegetables?" the waitress asked. My GF said, "Whatever you have - carrots, celery, etc" The waitress rudely let her know that she didn't think there was anything on the menu that required carrots or celery. "I can't eat bread, which is why I'm asking. So whatever you have, " my GF said. She said let's do the cheese plate if you are able to, and if not, the hummus with veggies. Time goes by, but she did not return to let us know what was possible. In the meantime, we decided we'd had enough of the awkward service and decided to abort mission, so we asked for our order to-go. The waitress was almost accusatory and asked us why we were leaving. A painful $40 dollars later, we get our order to go. Hop in the car and to see the saddest $10 roasted apples and cheese plate you've ever seen. No roasted apples, 5 stale apricots, horribly terrible brie (which I normally love), approximately 8 walnuts and a little blue cheese and goat cheese. The turkey sandwich we got also had the brie on it...RIP. I do have one more nice thing to say about this: the goat cheese was good. We cut up our own apples when we got home and went to town.

So excited to try this place because they have Gluten-free options. It was our bad luck there was a party of 22 ahead of us. Ugh. Thankfully we had some of the homemade ice cream while we were waiting to be seated. Once we were seated however our luck continued to be poor cause they were obviously short staffed. No water, and we waited longer and had to flag someone down to get water, and a table that was seated after us got service first...double ugh...24 min after being seated I went to the front to ask what was going on. The manager came up to see and ended up taking our order. OVER an HOUR after being seated we Finally got our food...no apologies from staff or anything...no Discount or comp on our bill.

I've been in here a couple of times and was not impressed at all. This place might be able to fool some Reno peeps, but it ain't gonna fool people from the Bay Area or other cities with some food experience. The service is slightly above terrible. I came in to get Ramen but I'm gluten free so I thought of a few different options but they were not having it. Apparently there are a million rules to what you can and cannot order. I asked them if they could just substitute my Ramen with Soba noodles and they replied with ... "Oh we can't do that because the Soba noodles go with different dishes." Ummm, ok... So then I asked them to deliver more meat and vegetables into my Ramen Bowl but just leave out the noodles. When I was served, i found no difference in extra vegetables or meat compared to my friend who ordered a normal Ramen Bowl. I asked them what they thought extra ingredients were, because my bowl was basically filled with broth and barely any food. This time the manager came over and said that he took his cook's word over mine and that there was in fact extra food put in my bowl. I asked him if he was arguing with his customer about the food. He then told me that he could give me extra food if that's what I "really needed to be satisfied." I told him that at this point I felt like I was begging for food, I wasn't satisfied, and wondered why they were 10 million rules about what I could order. He said that they don't like to mess with the Integrity of the dishes because that is not what the head chef has in mind for his creations. He also said that when customers mess with the food that they leave unsatisfied. I actually couldn't believe he said something like that but anyway I told him that everyday I have to mess with some sort of substitute because I am gluten free. Taking out noodles and just leaving more vegetables and meat doesn't mess with the Integrity of the food. I then asked for extra rice because it just dawned on me that that could be a substitute starch for my soup. The waitress said that they don't have extra rice and I would have to order a different dish with rice made into balls with sauce and add that instead. A $7 dish, because apparently they don't have extra rice in a Japanese restaurant. The manager also explained that he didn't make the food he just made sure that everything went well in the restaurant. I had to tell him that I didn't care what type of position he was in, but that I was dissatisfied with the argument of their word versus mine, the attitude problem, and the myriad of food rules that come at any cost. I'm sorry but Reno just isn't hip enough yet for your attitude problem, and your food is actually pretty lackluster. Byyyeeeeee!

Giving Soda Fountain Square three stars is being generous from my first visit. I will give the owner some credit in creating an adorable atmosphere. However, service could improve (it was slow) especially since I was the only table in the place. I asked a few simple questions about food b/c of food allergies and the waiter blew it off, then brought the wrong thing out. Again, the only table in the joint. Not sure if was an off night or not. The menu is decent, offering items catering to everyone's food taste, even vegetarians :) And I will note that the homemade gooey butter cake is sinfully delicious.

First let me say, I love this place! Every time I come home to visit I eat here and it's always amazing. My last visit was yesterday and we ordered the queens 8 sampler. The food was good but we were given gluten free injera and told they don't have the regular injera anymore. Would have been nice to know before as I am not a fan of the gluten free injera. They also changed the tomato salad and it's more of just a bowl of vinegar and tomatoes. For what it's worth, hopefully this was just a mishap. I will come back

Party of 8, including one infant, for dinner Friday night. Not impressed. We have had great experiences at other locations, but this time was not very good. We were only offered one bowl, which was not even full, of rice to share. One of us was served a gluten free meal, even after we specified it was not to be gf, which was only luke-warm. Another in our party was served a cold meal, and another received his meal about 5 minutes after everyone else. At least his was hot. The waitress offered no explanation, and we had to ask for refills on our drinks more than once. After we were finished eating, we didn't receive the check for at least another 10 minutes or so. The restaurant wasn't busy, as we arrived around 9pm, so I would have expected better service and hot food.

I stopped in for a quick and snack-type late lunch during a visit to St Pete. With a name promising tapas, you know it will be a bright spot to fill the gap before dinner. We were among a few patrons on a Saturday afternoon, and chose to sit semi-outside on their covered porch along Corey Ave., which I highly recommend. Our waitress was friendly, but there were a few areas which tarnished our experience. While we really enjoyed the Arnold Palmer (homemade iced tea/lemonade) and "Leaded" Iced Toddy (purportedly very caffeinated iced coffee), we were a little dismayed that our lunch item wasn't delivered as promised or described. We opted for the Fish Tacos, and I asked if the fish was grilled or fried, and if the corn tortillas were crispy or soft. I was told the fish was grilled and the tortillas soft, however the tacos arrived with fried fish displayed over double-stacked deep-friend corn tortilla in more of a "tostada" arrangement than the tacos we had been promised (as a PS - I'm not sure how these tacos can be listed as a "gluten free" item on the menu as the fish is breaded and fried). One item we did enjoy a bit more was the Goat Cheese Tapanade Terrine, which was layer upon decadent layer of goat cheese, olive tapanade, and roasted tomatoes/bell pepper, served with toasted baguette chips for dipping. Definitely a very shareable dish and totally delicious. While I was put off by the inaccuracy of the "tacos," we still ate them, as they weren't cheap for two "tostada" tacos, and we were hungry. The tapanade helped to fill in the blanks, and the nice semi-outdoor atmosphere was nice as well.
Saturday 2/6/16 2:30 pm host needs to go. Not helpful at all about allergy question / concern. Either Darryl or Darren was his name. Move him the hell out of the front of the store!

So Collingswood is full of good restaurants and Sabrina's is no exception. I ended up here unexpectedly for brunch on a Saturday morning with a friend who suggested it. The floor plan of the restaurant is completely open. There is some loungy type seating in the front by the windows, and the rest of the floor is high tops and regular tables. The ceiling is high and the floor is wood and the place was packed for brunch. First impression: loud. We were seated at a high top that we shared with three teenagers. Very quickly, we were greeted by our server who commented that I looked completely overwhelmed, and for sure I was. I don't want to make too many judgements on the noise level in the building because really a packed house means they're doing something right. I'll just say it caught me off guard and took me a while to adjust to. Anyway, the food. Every time I go out for brunch, I tell myself I'm going to get something sweet like pancakes or French toast, and then I end up ordering something savory. My visit to Sabrina's was no exception. I ordered a breakfast burrito that was served with amazing crispy potatoes. I felt like the brunch offerings on the menu were pretty regular - except for the specials. My only issue with that was the specials were all priced close to $15 which I guess isn't unheard of for brunch but still. Coffee is a brunch essential for me - I ordered a cafe latte with almond milk. They get some points for being friendly to the lactose intolerant crowd. I had hoped to find some flavored coffee on the menu but I didn't look too hard for it, as I said, I was pretty overwhelmed. The service was very fast and friendly. Our food came out maybe 10-15 minutes after we ordered it, and our server was attentive. They didn't rush us along but we didn't wait very long for anything either, which I'm grateful for because I had plans that afternoon. It's also impressive to note how well we were taken care of given how crowded they were. And finally, the parking situation. If you're not familiar with Collingswood, it's one of the few places in South Jersey where it's impossible to find a place to park, and when you do, you have to pay for it. We parked a few blocks away across from the Collings at the Lumber Yard or some similar name. You will definitely want to factor in some extra time to park. Overall: not my first choice for brunch, I definitely wouldn't return during peak hours, but I won't say I'll never come back. Atmosphere: 2 out of 5 Service: 5 out of 5 Food: 4 out of 5 Parking: annoying but available

3 stars was very generous considering the service we received. Had to ask twice for tea, twice for boxes and three times for water. To be fair, it was New Year's Eve and we had not had bad service on previous visits, but there was a whole restaurant full of tables waiting for food. Seemed like they were more concerned with their take out business than the eat in customers. Several people were taking what they were waiting for off empty tables, going to the hostess and asking for what they needed. Seriously considered calling the restaurant from our table and asking for what our waitress never brought. The prices are very reasonable and the food is excellent quality even if they are not overly willing to accommodate special requests or alterations for allergies. Would go again, just not on a holiday or if the waitress we had is working.

I really wanted to like Tuna Bar and was looking forward to our Valentine's Day dinner reservation. After making the reservation and realizing we weren't able to preview the prix fixe menu, I decided to contact the restaurant since my boyfriend has a shellfish allergy and this can often be a problem with sushi. I called, no answer. So I messaged them via Facebook. I explained his allergy and asked if this would be issue with the menu and their exact response was "...confirmed with management and there will be no shellfish on tonight's menu..." (See pic) Great, so we went. As soon as we sat down and looked at the menu we realized almost half of it included shrimp aka SHELLFISH (see V-day menu pic). Now maybe they were unaware that shrimp is shellfish? Or maybe they were just too lazy to actually check when I inquired, but either way, it's pretty inexcusable to ignore someone's food allergies and risk a health scare. What if we had asked if a dish included shellfish and my boyfriend had eaten it due to their ignorance? We would have ended up at the hospital. I'm giving three stars because our waiter did his best to accommodate us once we were already seated and expecting a decent meal. The sushi roll that he subbed for the 6th course (didn't have a name, his creation) was pretty quality and we did really enjoy it. I just can't get past the staff's ignorance regarding food allergies and a $210 dinner with drinks that we didn't really get to enjoy.

Horrible management and staff knowledge! I have celiac disease- this means that I cannot eat anything that contains wheat, barley or rye. We took a friend out for his birthday and he wanted to eat at Sushi Rose. We sat at at the bar and I talked with the sushi cook explaining my allergy and that I could order nigiri but that I would need him to use a separate cutting board (clean and sanitized) and separate knife (also cleaned and sanitized). The cook looked at me like I was an alien. Then wanted to know if my allergy was severe... to which I answered yes. He then confirred with management and other cooks and finally told me that they simply did not have another cutting board or knife to use! The cook made no attempt to accommodate me. He did not apologize or even try to figure out another way to help me so that I could eat at the establishment. Are you freaking serious!?! The rest in my party were already eating and so I sat there... Everyone was so angry that they wanted to leave and I insisted that if we were already paying for it we should stay I'd just eat later. A bit of information about myself... I am a food service manager and have worked in the food service industry for 20 years. I have never had any issues at any other sushi restaurant I have eaten at! I will never go here again and will discourage others as well, considering that their staff knows nothing about basic food safety and the ingredients they serve.

I thought this place would be great off the reviews, however I ended up getting food poisoning from here. It was unfortunate because it was our first stop of the day and it ruined the rest of the day for me. My friends food was fine and delicious. Our drinks were great, the waiter was amazing and the atmosphere was cool as well, which is why I am giving it a 3.

Food was splendid & tasty. Service was decent. We had to ask for more water (if you follow me, you know I value this). They also do not allow modifications to their meals... allergies are apparently the only exceptions. We were appreciative of the coffee/pastry bar since it took about an hour to get seated. If you're a traditional American breakfast eater, this is not a greasy spoon dinner with your typical eggs, bacon, or pancakes. Everything about Milktooth is modern eclectic, and the plates are very healthy. We loved the ambiance! Music was great and the bathroom artwork was quite entertaining!

Disability Accomodations at the Royal Senesta Hotel, New Orleans. June 2011 Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes. Most people think in terms of the well known and visible conditions, such as mobility issues, deafness, blindness... But there are many more little known conditions that are just as devastating for a normal life. Getting accommodations for these is often a tough and frustrating battle. The Royal Senesta Hotel of New Orleans, and in particular, the Director of Guest Relations, Katherine Jolivette, took the opposite tack. Before we even arrived, they went above and beyond my expectations in trying to create a safe place for me. Upon our arrival Katherine personally met us in the lobby and took us up to a room that had been specially prepared, went over the steps they had taken and asked if there was anything MORE they could do. I travel quite a lot, and have never seen a hospitality staff this hands on and attentive to detail. She acted like I was the only person she needed to be concerned about, taking as much time as needed, and never made me feel rushed or like an inconvenience. I found out later in the evening that she was also coordinating three weddings that day! Because my condition is relatively rare, I explained what I could about it and gave her a website where she could find out more, if she wanted. Usually when I do this, I imagine the person just tosses it as soon as I'm out of sight, however Katherine went to the site and actually read it through, asking me more questions about it next time she saw me. I have a very severe allergy to a very common substance, Latex. This is so severe that the amount needed to cause an anaphylactic reaction is measured in micrograms. A microgram is 1,000th of a milligram, in case you were wondering. And anaphylaxis means, essentially, death measured in minutes without intervention. In my first twenty four hours in NOLA, I had already suffered three anaphylactic events. Fortunately, I carry a pharmacy of intervention medicines with me at all times or I wouldn't be writing this. Trying to find a hotel willing to accommodate this is a nightmare. At the Royal Senesta, the reservation desk took the time to check all the possible sources of contamination and reported back that the hotel food service and restaurants were clear, and that although the housekeeping staff normally uses latex gloves, they had appropriate alternatives for our room. They did this all before we actually made the reservation. Reservation made, Katherine arranged for us to be in an upgraded room for the same price because it was isolated from the other hotel rooms where latex might be used. To my surprise, we were moved a couple days later to a newly available room with easy access to fresh air when needed to help relieve the asthma attacks I was having from multiple surprise encounters with latex in New Orleans. I never asked for the room change, she simply saw that I was having difficulty and made the necessary arrangements. She continued to check in with me, by phone and every time we passed in the hotel, to make sure things were going well. I really can't think of enough words to commend this kind of superlative service. In addition to my severe allergy issues, my husband is blind. He also had a wonderful customer experience. All the staff, from housekeeping, to the restaurant and food service, to the front desk and porters were friendly, cheerful, and always ready to help if needed. Of note, none of them over compensated in that annoying let-me-do-everything-for-you caretaking way that drives us who are disabled nuts. I would recommend this hotel to anyone with special needs without hesitation. If you are clear about what you need, I have no doubt that Katherine and her staff will find a way to make things work for you.

This is the closest Chinese restaurant to my house, and I really wanted to like it. Sadly, the first time I ate here, I got very sick. Like vomiting and diarrhea sick. Once I looked up the health inspections, and saw that it was not so good, I knew why. Against my better judgment, I have gotten food here since, and their lo mein is very good, but the General Tso's chicken is tough with watery sauce (and a few weird broccoli pieces). Pass on this place, and Doordash from somewhere else.

Switching to three stars because I've been here four times, two of which someone has ended up waking up sick in the middle of the night. I don't know that it's food poisoning, I'm told that if you have food poisoning you'll know it. Maybe the food is just extremely heavy and doesn't digest quickly enough? Either way, from other yelpers' reviews it seems like this is an all too common occurrence. I'm afraid to go back anytime soon.

Got food poisoning here, twice, from most likely the dairy. The 2nd time it happened, I complained by calling and the staff/management had absolutely NO idea how to proceed with or fix the situation. Plus, the staff have to be told multiple times the same requests, yet they still manage to get your order wrong right in front of you. And the interior of this location looks more bland/depressing than a prison cafeteria. It seems not even corporate cares about this location, seeing how everything's been on the decline since opening.

I always say that you can judge the quality of a restaurant by its bread pudding. When I'm right, I'm right. I asked about the bread pudding and the otherwise cheerful waitress whispered something inaudible with a viscerally winced face. Needless to say, red flags were raised. Unfortunately, I was with my besties who really wanted to eat there and I already felt like a douche bag saying a very disapproving "oh nooooo" following with the display of disgust by the waitress. I felt like the only person who realized that the food would be crap. Then again, let's save that c-word for later. I ordered the red beans and rice with a glass of pineapple juice and another of water. The vegetarian in our group had only one choice--the grilled cheese sandwich. The round of water arrived shortly after ordering. (Let me preface the following remarks by saying that I have a VERY sensitive stomach in that if I am to have any gastrointestinal issues with my food, I know shortly after the first bite. In this case, it was the first sip that did it.) I began drinking my water. The beverage had not yet been noticeably consumed before my body began urging me toward the bathroom in it's own special way. I began to bloat and had to fight to keep my gag reflex under control. My Best friend, who hates vomit, had to quickly run out of the way for fear of the worst. I drowned my stomach in pineapple juice which subdued the urge to vomit and some of the discomfort, but I didn't want to ruin anyone else's meal. For some of us, it was the last few hours in town. I trudged through my meal which was average at best. The side sausage was flavorless and almost blanched. The po boy my other buddy ordered was not made to order even though he ordered it dressed with cheese--quite standard for the average guy. The food left a lot to be desired for several of us, especially our vegetarian who supplemented her meal at Ihop a short walk away. Sad to say, the best part of my meal was the pineapple juice. Further, because of the temporary nausea and diarrhea, I had to rush back to my hotel room and could barely say goodbye to my buddies who were leaving town. The moral of the story is that you should trust your instincts. If you can't make good bread pudding, your restaurant should just give up. Stick with Mother's instead. Their food is at least consistent, not to mention their bread pudding is delightful.

Don't even bother coming to this location. The Jasper Ave one is better and more consistent. The south location shouldn't even deserve any stars. I went there for a Christmas party; the waitress had horrible attitude, who also spilled wine while serving -- in the process, I got soaked! Also, a person from our table has specific allergies, but the waitress did not take any care of it and it still ended up being on her plate. If that wasn't bad enough, she did not respect the fact that I was the designated driver, so I could not drink -- the portion of my bar tab goes to another person. (This was properly communicated to her when food was ordered, but she did not bother remembering) I ended up having to pay -- a bit frustrated, I talked to the manager and explained my situation. Right in front of her manager, she dropped the printed receipt rudely on the floor, then briskly walked away. He picked it up and apologized, but bad attitude always leaves a very bad taste, no matter how decent the food is.

I will go on the record and state that there are very few chain restaurants that I really love. Perhaps that's why they are a chain. Perhaps not, but I digress. My 1st visit to Carabba's was mid August 2015. Since we had our little one with us, we decided to go early and beat the crowd and found the restaurant nearly empty at 5:30 PM on a weekday. I was immediately pleased with how clean the restaurant was and was equally impressed with the trendy décor. Our hostess seated us immediately and our less than enthusiastic server came shortly thereafter and took our drink order. Our drinks arrived shortly along with some hot bread and dipping sauce; and we placed our son's "kid's grilled chicken" dinner order and also ordered a Tomatoes Caprese appetizer while we looked over the menu at the entrees. The bread was perfectly baked and piping hot, and the dipping sauce was their own twist of olive oil with a bit of pesto in the middle. Very good. The appetizer was also good as the thick sliced mozzarella was the perfect texture, as nothing is more unsatisfying than some "rubbery" mozzarella. Not the case here. My little one's "kid's grilled chicken dinner" was the probably the best tasting chicken we've ever gotten as part of a kid's meal. It was grilled and seasoned perfectly and the fresh green beans were also a big hit. My wife's Taglierini with chicken (extra charge), asparagus, tomato and basil was a solid dish, and quite filling. Kudos for the shaved parmesan on top. Trying to eat light, I got the Johnny Rocco Salad, which featured grilled shrimp and scallops on a bed of greens; also with shaved parmesan on top. Also very good. Kudos to Carrabba's for offering a gluten free options as well as entrees and appetizers with 600 calories or less. And although we didn't sit at the bar since we had our little one, the bar is worth mentioning as it is very inviting and I could see myself eating here while I enjoyed a game on one of the big screen televisions. So with all the good things I have to say, you may be wondering why I didn't give them a 4-star rating. The reason I gave a 3-star rating (A-Ok), is because of my server. Although she was not impolite, she was far from friendly. She went through all the motions but could have been a little more attentive, especially since she only had 1 other table. And to me, it looked as if her other table was getting pretty good / courteous service from her. Perhaps she was having a bad day, a bad vibe, or didn't like kids. I just know that if she had been really friendly, I may have delved out my 1st 4-star rating to a chain restaurant. There is no need to mention her by name, but I hope that management sees this and emphasizes that a positive attitude goes a long way in the service industry. However, the food was pretty decent and I can see myself going back here; just not with the same server.

May be overrated? Both of my kids are allergic to peanuts and the fries are Cooked in 100% peanut oil. In addition, they really should stop making the veggie sandwich, it's gross without any flavor. Pretty pointless to have on the menu. Instead they should actually make a veggie burger with some seasoning. So I don't recommend this spot for people with peanut allergies or vegetarians.

I have to admit that I was a little bit of a "negative nancy" going in, because I already have my favorite Thai place .. which also has my favorite server. I heard that they have rice noodles and are semi-knowledgeable when it comes to Gluten Free .. it's also one of my boyfriends fave places .. so I gave it a shot. We first went one afternoon .. but they were closed. They have a split shift type schedule. Lunch - close - Dinner. Went last night. From first observation it's very small and had it not been recommended I would never have gone based on experience. Service was a tad slow at first. Then I was given hot tea when I asked if they had any degaf-unsweet ice team. That's okay, it was good and it was a tad chilly inside. I was starving so I ordered spring rolls as an app. YUCK. They were horrible! All three people in my part ordered some and each of us hated them. For my meal I got the Curry of the day. She forgot to ask me how hot I wanted it .. so I had to request some extra spices .. but overall it was great. I love that they let you substitute brown rice (for extra)! Bottom line. It's not the best Thai food in Nashville by a long shot. I probably won't go back ... but I didn't leave unsatisfied!

I never write reviews but I have to for this restaurant as I am so disappointed/angry.I had Sunday brunch here with 5 other friends and we all got food poisoning from this place. It was a terrible way to end the week.

This place is truly disappointing. I ordered a salad which I know does not have any pork product. Half way through my meal, I discovered a once of bacon. After I told my waitress that the bacon is in the salad, her response is "it's probably got thrown in there by accident". Really?! After I told her I don't eat pork, all she said is "ok!" And walked away. Wow! Didn't care at all. What if I was allergic?! I didn't even going to ask for a replacement. Yet, if she would have cared a bit to offer me for a replacement, it would have been better. She didn't even take it out of my bill! I've been in a less classy places to eat yet their service was top notched compared to this place. Don't waste your money people. Go someplace else.

I still stand by the shrimp and gratis and green chili corn waffle as PHENOMENAL. However, today I had the Corkscrew Gravy and it was like being served someone else's vomit on a plate. It said it came with biscuits but it was served over bread and it texture, taste, looks of the gravy was appauling. The gravy was broken (grease separated from milk) and whatever the ground up pink meat and unharmonious mix of spices just... ewww. Also, the Cajun house sausage almost tasted medicinal or like a spice in it tasted like when you chew a tylenol. Disappointed this time but not saying I won't go back for the shrimp/grits and corn waffle in the future.

Experience was bad from the first minute. I tried to give the benefit of the doubt. But it just sucked. From the rude attitude of the person who served the food, to my charred black and burnt fajitas. One person at my table ordered no onions and sure enough it came with onions. We said that we specifically asked for no onions due to an allergy, the Guy goes "that's the way it comes". Right, because you can't not add onions right? Taco Bell is literally better than this. Do yourself a favor and go to Chueys or VIP Mexican in st Pete. Vallarta's even. This place was just awful. Oh and the 9 dollar queso dip is the consistency of water.

On Friday night, I went with 5 friends to Xochitl for dinner to celebrate a friend's birthday, and 4 of the 6 of us ended up with the worst case of food poisoning ever! The nausea, vomiting, chills, & fever were nasty... And we were all out of comission for about 3 days. All of us had the "special" entree of the night -- the bronzino fish. It tasted great going down, but boy did we all regret it by Saturday night. I'm sorry to say we won't be back to Xochitl again...

Haven't even received our food yet and I'm super disappointed. This was the only sushi place open between 3-5 as most in the area close in the later afternoon. We thought we'd try a it out. They were not able to tell us anything gluten free. Typically rice flour is used when frying things in a Japanese restaurant. Not even gluten free soy sauce!!!! So, here we sit hoping the food we could find will be edible. Super bummer

Don't eat here. This place is fowl. The service is fine, and there is some okay sushi rolls. But last time I will ever eat sushi, this place gave me food poisoning. I have not been able to leave my house for the past 24 hours because of constant puking and dirreah. I will never have sushi again because of the pain I have went through with the food poisoning. Thanks jazmine.
Ok... I had to update again because it's now 4 days later, and I'm still sick!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! This is crazy... a serious case of food poisoning.
We all got food poisoning last time we were here. It was dirty, food cold, and service wss horrible. Probably good reason it's gone now.

We walked in at 11:30 am on a Sunday and the place was filthy. One employee was sweeping, but it literally looked like no one cleaned anything from the night before. All of the veggies in the cold bar looked like they had been sitting since the night before as well. My husband and I got a philly and a chicken philly plain, which is the only reason we stayed. No way I would have eaten any of those veggies. They get two stars (which is generous): 1 for friendliness of staff and one because we managed not to get food poisoning. Will not be returning to this location. I have never experienced this at any other Jersey Mike's.

I drove out to the east side to take my nephew out to celebrate his honor roll. We ordered orange chicken ( so tough could not be cut and no flavor. We order the volcano appetizer and actually could not eat half as it was inedible. The only thing truly edible was the lo neon and even then I specified no shrimp as I am highly allergic and they brought it out with shrimp and then laughed. They then said they made a new one which came out in less than three minutes. I took a bite in about three minutes later my tongue was tingling and I started coughing. I believe they only took the shrimp off but said they made new one. When I told them it was wrong. I told them that as a business owner I would not be back as they made no consolation just excuses about how the woman must have overlooked it. My nephew could not even eat his food. So much for a celebration.. if I could have given them a 1/2 star I would have. I actually took the remaining lo me on home and had my friend test it and if fact it has remnants of shrimp within them. I had to take my epi pen as I began having issues with breathing.

Pros: Good size city A lot of sun if you enjoy the sunshine Desert mountains and nature around the city are very nice. Great hiking, trail running, etc. Downtown Tucson and U of A seemed very progressive, up-and-coming. These are great for Tucson. People overall seemed friendly and extremely easy going Inexpensive to live...because of cons Cons: About 80% of Tucson is very grungy and run-down Most of the city is very far behind on infrastructure. The roads are very bad No easy way to commute in a car. Interstate 10 services the west side of the city. You will experience a lot of bumpy roads with 45 mph stop-and-go traffic. Road construction no matter where you drive (at least they're trying to do something about the roads) Extremely hot about 4 months of the year Crime rate is very high in Tucson Mostly retirees and college students, not a lot in the middle. Can be very difficult to find a nice and quiet place to rent in Tucson if you are in the rental market. Houses and buildings are very dark, old and not well taken care of Very windy in the spring, most people have allergies due to the dust

I really want to love this place and give it more stars - and I keep coming back because I love the food - but the customer service is just absolutely awful. Every.Single.Time we have been here they have messed up our order. My boyfriend has a gluten allergy and we always specify CORN tortillas, multiple times, yet every time we have paid $30+ and received flour - with nothing he can eat. Sitting in the drive thru now and was just handed a card tray for my receipt covered in syrup. There have been so many issues with this place - from small to big. In all fairness, we have only gone through the drive thru - but we have yet to dine here without an issue. I keep convincing him to come back, and every time he says this will be the last.

I tried this donut shop after I read about it in the local paper. The donuts are very sweet. I got a hazelnut donut that I could not eat because the put walnuts on top. They should list ingredients so folks with nut allergies aren't surprised. The place has a hipster vibe. I may try it again but they need more variety.

Just ordered DoorDash of the Turkey Manhattan and Mac and cheese. I thought the Mac and cheese tasted funny but it also tasted very sweet so I thought maybe that was just the recipe. I wasn't a fan of it but hey, sometimes you don't like a dish at a restaurant that others love. Added a bunch of spices at home and it was okay. Next I went to eat my manhattan. The flavor wasn't there for me once again but I was hungry so I ate it after adding much needed spices to the gravy and potatoes. This alone did not warrant a negative review. Now about a quarter of the way through I felt started to be disgusted by the smell and then ended up having to run to the bathroom to vomit. I vomited up the portion of the meal that I ate and have felt queasy since. I don't have a sensitive stomach at all. Not sure if something had spoiled in the gravy or Mac and cheese or what happened here but had to throw out the rest of my food and now feel ill. If I hadn't gotten sick I'd have given it another two stars because portions were decent but the flavor just isn't there for me (not enough seasoning). But after getting sick from the meal I can't give it anything more that what it ended up being.

Is there any good way to wait for your food at Remedy? They just shout it out when the order is ready, but you don't know if it's actually your food or someone else's who for the same thing. Plus if you're sitting upstairs it's almost impossible to hear anything that's going on downstairs, so it's difficult to know when your food is ready. But no one wants to stand by the till and wait there 10-15 minutes for their food to come out... I just really do not understand Remedy's service system. That being said their food is wonderful. I particularly like the butter chicken and curry chicken. They are to die for and are ridiculously filling. They've got tons of options for all you vegans, vegetarians and celiacs! All you lactose intolerants and but allergists should probably do a quick check with the staff before you order though. The store is kind of... Grungy feeling? Not in the cool and hip kind of way, but in the dirty and questionable one. I feel like the way that some of the stuff near the till is arranged in a way that would easily accumulate dust and I have a feeling dusting isn't priority number 1 here. Table tops and whatnot are usually clean but don't look too hard at the floor. I'd say just get your food to go. There isn't really any reason to stay in store. The music is loud. It's often super crowded. And you leave smelling like spices and curry if you eat in.

I was served a disgusting, half-eaten quarter pounder sandwich from this McDonald's drive through at around 11PM on 28 May 2016. I only found out after I got home and opened the box. I immediately sent an email (with a picture of the food, and the receipt) to the area supervisor's email address on the receipt. I later submitted a complaint on the McDonald's feedback website as well: http://www.mcdonalds.com/content/us/en/contact_us/restaurant_feedback.html I then drove back to the restaurant, expecting a refund and an apology. It was after hours so I had to go through the drive-through again. The manager denied that they served the sandwich that way, and said she would not be issuing a refund. I had no choice but to leave. I called the restaurant again when I got home, to try and get the manager's name. I got her on the phone, but she hung up the phone on me as soon as she realized that I was the one calling. The manager did not ask for my information or for when exactly it happened to try to look into it, which to me means that this could very well happen again. This is food that has been touched and eaten by another person, and then served again to a customer. Very disturbing. I have also submitted a complaint with the Florida Department of Health: http://www.floridahealth.gov/diseases-and-conditions/food-and-waterborne-disease/how-to-report-a-problem-with-food-in-florida.html Inspection records for this restaurant show that they have had repeat violations related to failure to protect food from cross-contamination in the past, from as far back as 2010 to as recently as 2016. The most recent inspection on 27 Jan 2016 included a note saying: "Employee personal food not properly identified and segregated from food to be served to the public". You can see the details of the inspection results and violations online: http://data.tallahassee.com/restaurant-inspections/hillsborough/mcdonalds-1155/sea3900989/2183631/ I've gotten bad orders from McDonald's before: wrong drink, stale fries, no fries, etc. and I usually just let it go. But I've never seen anything quite like this.

Not a bad diner. I ordered the turkey club. The price was reasonable. The service was sub par. 2 waitresses in the place. I noticed a lot of people waiting several minutes at the register to pay. As for cleanliness.... I always take issue with people handling filthy money then touching the bread for toast.. Seems to me they could have someone work the register so waitresses aren't contaminating food. I will not be returning.

Update 7/26/19: I am more than happy to update from 3 stars to 5 stars They have added stickers with dates on them. Thank you for taking this seriously. I'm torn. I usually love stopping here but today was the first day I started asking questions about the "freshness" of their ingredients and supplies. Ordered some pretzels with cheese and got home, saw the cheese cups had mold in them, so I got back in the car and took them both down there and asked for "fresh" cheese. Girl goes to the back and gets two more cups of cheese, returns with them, and I start walking out the door and really started looking at the "new cheese" and there's mold in these as well. This does not sit with me well because I've had food poisoning from cheese; so I turn around and hand the two cups back to her and say, "look, these have mold in it as well. You probably just need to throw out your batch and get a fresh supply". She says, "yeah, probably. These are the last two cheeses we have so there's nothing else I can do." So you're literally telling me at 6pm (they close at nine) that you can't open a can of nacho cheese? I read a older review that says almost the same thing about fresh juice. Can employees not make anything FRESH appear? Had I known that all you had was moldy cheese, I wouldn't have spent my money here today. Teach your employees to MARK everything with a date and throw out when it's expired. LOOK over everything and make sure it's good!

BE AWARE if you have allergies! I ordered a salad and told them I had a serious shellfish allergy and the assholes didn't alert me that they use clam sauce in their dressing. If you're this much of an idiot, don't work at a restaurant where you're preparing food for tons of people. I even complained to the manager and he was like "Oops sorry! Come back again." Disgusting.

I've been to Upland's taproom a few times and haven't really been impressed. They certainly know how to do beer well, but I feel the kitchen is lacking in consistency. My most recent visit was with a bridal party. We had issues with getting a table for our group because they don't do reservations. Several of us were waiting around for more tables to free up because of the no-reservation policy. It was rather frustrating. They have decent options on their menu to satisfy most taste-buds. But, I don't feel they do anything particularly well. My walnut-crusted salmon was burnt and I'm surprised that they would let that leave the kitchen as it was. I did ask them to hold the risotto, which they kindly obliged, but you would think that if a customer asks to remove a part of the dish they would offer something in its place. Not so much.
