Furthermore, the kale and sweet potatoes that came on the side were super oily and there wasn't much of them. So, I essentially had burnt salmon and oily greens. Not very appetizing. I can't drink beer due to an allergy, and when I asked our server about wine options, he was rather rude about it and seemed put out that I asked to see a wine list. I don't think I want to visit this place again based on this last experience. The front of house staff has some coaching to do and the kitchen needs to work on their consistency.

We have been going to Jazmines for over 5 years. We work right down the street from them and go at least 2x a week. This last visit was unexceptable. We ordered 4 rolls with spicy crab on top... the most sloppy rolls i have ever seen. They through crab on it with gobs of siracha sauce. We also ordered rainbow rolls with a couple of exceptions because the person has a gluten allergy and an allergy to sesame seeds. The roll came with no exceptions made and tons of sesame seeds. The Owner would do nothing about it. Wouldn't even make her a new roll. Horrible service. The server who helped me argued with me when I called and explained what had happened. So disappointing.

My husband and I live a few blocks from Franklins. Yesterday was the first time we were really disappointed. We usually save Franklins for nice days when we can go outside and have a beer, but my husband really wanted a burger. We were the only ones in the dining room and were served immediately. However, the dining room still smelled like stale beer. It reminded me of college and the day after a party. It wasn't the most pleasant smell. I brought over a high chair and had to wipe it down because it was pretty disgusting. I realize children get them dirty, but they really should be wiped down. The bartender/server did offer to wipe it down for us. Now, I used to be both a server and a bartender, so I realize I am about to get picky here. When we ordered our food, our server chose to sit down with us like we were all buddies. I can't stand that more than anything. Like I said, I am being picky, but we aren't buddies. I am not sure why he felt comfortable enough to sit down with my family. The thing that put me over the edge and made me write this review was the fact that I am pretty sure I got food poisoning or at least sick from eating there. I had a burger that was slightly undercooked. I asked for a medium burger. It is partly my fault because I did not mention to them that there was still some pink, but I have eaten a medium rare burger and been fine. I was not fine last night. I spent it in the bathroom. I don't have a sensitive stomach, so this was a very rare occasion. I will most likely still go back, but I will stick to the outdoor deck and beers from now on. I really hope they clean the restaurant a little better so they don't keep on attracting just college kids. There are plenty of young families in this neighborhood from whom they could receive plenty of business.

If I could give NO star I would! Where to start, The meat to all the tacos variations are unseasoned and over cooked. So the meat is very dry. Next, I order the kids meal that comes with two tacos and the side of beans and rice. The beans were spoiled and you can smell it. I paid for my food, explained to the young lady that the beans went bad. She tells me "Well no one else has complained ". I stated "I can bring you my child's plate so you can smell them". She didn't want to, or at least consider the formal complaint. She then ignores me and moves onto the next customer, mind you I'm standing in front of her! I'm not one to complain or pay for my food, but total ignorance is on the next level! Food is cheap but be ready for spoiled or over cooked food! I don't recommend at all! Only good thing about the place is homemade tortillas. That's all! Very disappointing. An hour later, I threw up everything I ate from this place.

We ate here on the second day of our New Orleans vacation. I thought my dish was pretty terrible, but my husband got food poisoning from the shrimp in his omelet. Our trip has been ruined. Needless to say, we will never eat here again.

Food took about 45 minutes. Also the order was not correct. Worst part was i got food poisoning. Do not get the seafood Benedict! Worst way to spend your jazz fest. Avoid this place, or do not order anything with seafood.

Went for dinner and ordered the hog fish. They served it to me completely raw and when I told the waiter, they brought it back and gave me the same fish on the same plate that my raw fish was on. So therefore the plate was contaminated. The table I was sitting at was very wobbly and moved every time I went to cut anything. My meal itself was 30.00 and for that price I would think I would get better service. The service needs work for sure and giving me the raw fish is unacceptable. My husband ordered a chicken hoagie and that was good. I won't be coming back though.

I came into Casia Taqueria with high hopes. The taquito selection was excellent. I ordered chips with salsa and guacamole as a starter, and 2 tacos: chorizo & carne asada. The chips were good and clearly fresh. The salsa was ok, but nothing special. It was clearly homemade, but did not taste particularly fresh. This was a bigger problem with the guacamole. Fresh guac is usually bright green, and this had started to turn the darker shade of guac a few days old. The flavor was ok, but definitely not same-day fresh. Since adding guacamole to your starter doubles the price, it really needs to be super fresh. Local avocados are just finishing out their season here, so there's really no excuse. The main dish was ok. The tortillas are fantastic. Truly some of the best and freshest handmade corn tortillas. I did not find the chorizo or carne as flavorful as they could have been. The carne asada actually just needed a little more salt. My biggest issue was that they had a slightly fishy air about them. Honestly, this could be an allergy issue as the biggest possible problem. Further, if the dish does not contain fish, it certainly should smell like it. Because this place is new, I'll give it another shot in a few weeks/month. There are clearly some kinks that need to be worked out. I think they have potential based on the quality of the tortillas and the quick & friendly service, so I am hoping it was just a single bad day for them.

Terrible experience! We were literally the only ones in the restaurant. We were given paper menus and they did not have enough menus for everyone at the table. I ordered the chicken quesadilla. When I got it, there was no chicken in it. The cheese was so thick and gooey, I was scared to eat it all. It was hard to chew and a lactose intolerant person's nightmare. They didn't have ginger ale to make a drink that I wanted, which was a huge disappointment. The $1 tacos were extremely small and the margarita specials didn't taste like any tequila was in them. They looked like kool-aid. As far as pros, the place was clean and the waitress was super nice. Unfortunately, that's not enough, so I won't be returning.

While I rarely eat from fast food chains, I was shopping nearby and had a coupon. I ordered a beef and cheddar sandwich meal, just like I enjoyed when I was a kid. The sandwich itself was alright, but very sloppily made. It took nearly 10 minutes to receive my order, which seemed ridiculous considering all they need to do is slap some meat and squeeze some cheese between two buns. But the worst part was that it made me sick for 2 days. Beginning the next morning, I could barely eat anything and always felt like I wanted to vomit. I already knew that Arby's didn't have quality food, but I was craving a sandwich and took a risk anyway. Now I will be avoiding them at all costs.

Ok, this place has earned their bad review like you wouldn't believe. First time around, they closed at 9:30 when their hours state that they close at 10. Ok, so I'm not going to write this place off because they are lazy and don't want to work. I will, however, write them off and never, ever return because the one time I ordered a tuna salad and began to mix it, prepared to take a huge bite when I see that something beige and weirdly textured was hidden underneath my salad. Guess what I pulled out? A PAPER TOWEL. Yes, you read that correctly. A freakin wet paper towel. How's that for a horror story? Vomit.

For a restaurant in the heart of the tourist district, this isn't a bad option. The fact that it offered a gluten-free menu, and GF prix fixe, was a draw. The bar may have been the best part of the restaurant, with skilled, friendly bartenders whipping up a range of classics. The food itself was, as my companion described it, "like a really good cruise ship dinner." Not chef-driven and clearly catering to a wide range of diners, the menu offered fairly standard dishes executed well but without any particular inspiration. I had the house salad (standard), double pork chops (tasty and HUGE) and the flourless chocolate cake (essentially dark chocolate fudge). Not amazing, but the atmosphere boosted the experience.

Cannot believe I'm the only one to not rave about this place. Staff: honestly the only good thing here, all pleasant and nice, nothing bad to say. Flow of traffic/efficiency: terrible, who set this up, does not function well. The line for putting your name in is ridiculous and yeah I didn't have to wait in it but hey I can be patient. I just won't ever wait in the line again. Food: come eat here before going to dinner because you'll still be hungry. I got a 12 dollar potato salad that tasted okay (I could probably make myself something better) and was not filling. This main dish was the size of a side salad. I'm a small girl, I like small portions, but this was too small and I'm on my way home to go eat again. The waffles and pancakes look like the only thing they really excel at but I'm gluten free and they really don't have options for that. Don't even have gluten free bread on hand... Nice atmosphere here and I get what they are going for, Im into the healthy, organic, small portions, rare and interesting flavors but I can name better places in Indy to eat at.

The pharmacy department at this store has gone above and beyond to help when my mother was visiting and ended up in the hospital. Getting her prescriptions from the mail order to be transferred was not a simple task yet the pharmacist went out of her way to make a few calls and get some answers and in the end it was her actions that solved all the problems that we encountered. I am so grateful and they are always pleasant and helpful. THANK YOU to all. Two small words that mean so much.

Good evening. I want to write about my awful experience yesterday. Me and my partner called ahead and there was absolutely no wait so we drove to Cherry Hill. Once we got there, there was a 10-15 minute wait, Okay, that's tolerable. Over 35 minutes before we get called. We get stuck in a very small table. I ordered the cream of chicken soup. How can you call this chicken soup when it was predominately mushrooms, which I am allergic to? I wish the waitress would have said something - not many people like mushrooms like that. It was not warm. Because of the amount of people she was waiting on and the busy nature of the place, I decided not to say something. I took maybe 2 spoonfuls of the soup and the waitress takes it away, doesn't ask why the bowl is full. My partner ordered the chicken pasta carbonara, the noodles were barely al dente, looks like the pasta wasn't even drained and thrown into a bowl with a watery alfredo sauce, it really didn't look appealing at all. If you're going to charge $18.50 for a lackluster dish, at least make sure the sauce is thick. I ordered the grand lux deluxe, while the meat was okay, the bread was OLD and I ordered a side of mashed potatoes - they were also old tasting as well. Our waitress was okay, but didn't really care. For $63.00 I could have had a hell of a better experience somewhere else. Doubt I'll be back anytime soon. Thanks for reading.

I've been here 3 times before and always loved it, especially the coconut soup and mango sticky rice, but this time I'm pretty sure my boyfriend and I got food poisoning, either from the pad thai or pork dumplings.

So, interesting little spot in a great and easily accessible location in Westchase. Really friendly, helpful staff, a little cluttered but easy to get to toppings and so forth, and great tasting gluten-free/sugar-free/fat-free (?) Froyo... I loved it. Lot of comments about "clean" here, not sure I completely agree with that but it is a cozy, charming little store and I recommend that you give it a try.

No no no! Let me make this short and, well, not so sweet. I ordered an apple coffee cake and was handed an aluminum tray containing a frozen pastry-looking object, smothered in icing. I appealed for an exchange on second thought. A few non-frozen fritters were placed into a paper bag and I was out the door with serious doubts, based on what I observed. The first fritter was removed and the icing-like coating (on a fritter?) was so aromatically overpowering, it triggered a spasm that tends to be a precursoer to vomiting, in most cases. The "icing" was a sweetness that could have been a cross between cotton-candy and the sweetest of sickly sweet cheap perfumes. It was very unnatural. I do a lot of baking with many types of sugar, honey and agave. I have also been to high-end and mid-level bakeries all over the country and a few in Europe. Over the years, I have either purchased or been offered baked goods from grocery-store bakeries. On that basis, let me say this: Sweet-N-Sassy should not be compared to any serious bakeries; it should only be compared to grocery-store bakeries. On that scale, Whole Foods' bakeries absolutely destroy all other grocery-store bakeries. However, even Kroger bakeries churn out products far superior to that of Sweet-N-Sassy. I suppose that Sweet-N-Sassy is more on-par with Wal-Mart bakeries. In other words: If you just need some everyday pastries, try Whole Foods or even Kroger. If you want to go to a real bakery and enjoy baked goods on a whole new level, do your homework - and be wary of all casual recommendations.

This review is based on Sam's Brick Oven Pizza and caviar. I ordered via caviar and put a modification on a pizza and it arrived with mushrooms which my fiancé is allergic too! The oversight could have caused a bad reaction! You have to be more vigilant if people are making modifications. I know that the pizzas can be modified too, because they pizzas are made to order. I contacted caviar about the mistake and they blamed it on the restaurant manager, very classy. Caviar offers the worst customer service ever. No refund was offered to me either, especially since the pizza was inedible.

I don't normally post reviews but we came in for brunch this morning and received some of the worst customer service I've ever had anywhere. I asked the girl at the counter what "beef sloppy" was, what's in it and asked "is like a sloppy joe?" Her response was "I'm assuming, yeah." I then asked her if she could find out what's in it she threw the pen that was in her mouth on the counter and stomped off to the kitchen. When she returned she said "yeah. It's like a sloppy joe." Which still did not answer my question. I then asked a woman who was preparing food and she told us the ingredients which included chipotle sauce/peppers. Thank you! That's some handy information for those of us who have food allergies or sensitivities. My boyfriend then asked if he could get a beer and, rather than answering his question or addressing him directly, the girl bellowed over her shoulder towards the kitchen "STONER!" My boyfriend then took a guess that she was calling for someone over 21 who could get a beer for him. At that point we were just so confused and put-off by her nasty attitude that we just decided to leave. That girl acted like she couldn't care less about serving us, what was in their food or taking our money and actually made us feel like we were inconveniencing her! Sorry for the inconvenience... we won't be back. By the way, I should point out they were not busy or rushed... we were the only people there. There are new places popping up all over Donelson and the area with better service and who will take our money with a smile.

The staff is the worst that I've dealt with in my entire life. You could probably get better service from a closed McDonald's. They have messed up my order every single time that I've come here, and the manager proceeded to tell me what I should do differently (order each item separately) in order for THEM to do their job correctly. The manager also told me that I should just accept bad service since the people in the kitchen were "hungover students". They made my food incorrectly and then just scraped off what shouldn't be on there and claimed that they remade my food, and I have many food allergies. I would NEVER recommend this place to someone. I personally know that they aren't even a kosher kitchen!!!

I've almost recovered from passing out from discovering that this place has almost a 4 star average. Are you KIDDING me Florida? Has the sun burned the tastebuds off your tongue and fried your brain? I knew when we went in that I was in for ultra casual dining, but I wasn't in for this. I've had better 'homemade" meals at the Publix kitchen station. People - I set off my smoke alarm every time I cook and I STILL cook BETTER than this place. Are you understanding the words that are coming out of my mouth?!? They don't even cut the lettuce fresh here - they straight up pour it from a publix bag. I ordered the buffalo shrimp. It came out with so little sauce I had to ask to make sure they remembered to buffalo my buffalo shrimp or to get more sauce. The waitress told me to just add the Chula sauce b/c that's all it was. WHAT?!? You can't even make your own buffalo sauce?!? My boyfriend got the ribs and chicken combo and the only good thing about that was it was a lot of food for the price. If you are a family on a budget, you can have an affordable meal that won't land you in the hospital from food poisoning, but if you like good food and want to actually enjoy your meal, then SKIP this joint and go to another chain or, better yet, do yourself a big favor and don't go to any chain.

Half our group got the runs. The one star is for the dope michelada. Most of the salsas at the salsa bar tasted like bland tomato sauce, and I'm guessing the tepid sour cream one may have been the source of our food poisoning. This place needs a visit from the health department, there's no excuse for this shit, literally.

I drove out to the east side to take my nephew out to celebrate his honor roll. We ordered orange chicken ( so tough could not be cut and no flavor. We order the volcano appetizer and actually could not eat half as it was inedible. The only thing truly edible was the lo neon and even then I specified no shrimp as I am highly allergic and they brought it out with shrimp and then laughed. They then said they made a new one which came out in less than three minutes. I took a bite in about three minutes later my tongue was tingling and I started coughing. I believe they only took the shrimp off but said they made new one. When I told them it was wrong. I told them that as a business owner I would not be back as they made no consolation just excuses about how the woman must have overlooked it. My nephew could not even eat his food. So much for a celebration.. if I could have given them a 1/2 star I would have. I actually took the remaining lo me on home and had my friend test it and if fact it has remnants of shrimp within them. I had to take my epi pen as I began having issues with breathing.

So the cakes here are very fresh and delicious-- there is no doubt about that. But today I bought one of the mini cakes that was labeled marble and when I bit into it turned out to be the pecan praline flavor. I was disappointed. However, this could have been a real problem for someone allergic to nuts. So... maybe label your cakes correctly.

I was having a hard time deciding whether to give Kermit's 2 or 3 stars. I settled on three because I got my sister a salted caramel chocolate tart and she raved about it. The items I got for myself, however, were seriously underwhelming, hence the 2 star consideration. On one occasion I got a flourless salted chocolate brownie, which had very little chocolate flavor. I mean, how is that a brownie??? Even so, I went ahead and tried the gluten free pizza. Now, I've been gluten free for over three years, and have eaten dozens of gf pies, some of them pretty terrible, and this was without a doubt the WORST! It was too thick for starters, gf pizza has got to be thin because it just gets crumbly when it's thicker. Which is exactly what happened to my pizza. It was disintegrating and utterly unpalatable. I ended up pulling the cheese and toppings off and eating that alone. And by "toppings" I mean the fifteen (I counted) mushrooms on the entire pie. Which cost me $2 extra. Boo to you Kermit's. I'd rather eat the gf pizza from Slice. Which, until now, held the gold on my Worst GF Pizza list. Congratulations.

Ugh. This place was gross. We came here on a weekday afternoon hoping it would help to fill the hole in our hearts for delicious mexican food. Let me tell you, it does and will not. So we got in line and even though there were a bunch of employees working the line it went so slow. Finally we get someone to take our order. We got a large order of steak nachos. The counter and the food containers were so messy and had drippings of other foods in them so if you have an allergy I would not even try the food here. Once again, even though it was just a matter of putting toppings on nachos the person working took forever and the "queso" they put on everything was cold by the time we even got to sit down. Once again, it is not even busy and the tables and floor are messy with food scraps and napkins. I also noticed not one employee changing gloves or washing their hands throughout our visit here. Ew. The food was just a sad mixture of cold and lukewarm bland toppings. The chips were soaked in the cold queso gloopy crap and totally floppy. I dumped a ton of salsa and got extra jalapeños which was the only saving grace to this meal since everything else on the nachos tasted bland and had the texture of glue. Finally, this place is way overpriced for the crappy nasty food. Just make the drive out to chipotle or go to taco bell even or you know, anywhere else.

Amazing nut free selection! My son has a severe peanut and tree nut allergy so we usually have to avoid sweets due to cross contamination. I was so happy when I saw Skip's entire nut free wall! My little one was so happy that he could pick anything he wanted. Wonderful job to ownership for being so inclusive!

I went to a happy hour at Landmark and sat in the bar area. Appetizers were fine, but nothing special (wings, quesadillas, egg rolls). They did have a large beer selection. However, the service was non existent. For such a large group, spending lots of $$ you kind of expect more. We all had to go to the bar and order drinks, no table service. One nice thing was there is a gluten free menu - with lots of choices!

Slowest service ever. Restaurant completely empty and it took over an hour to get a bowl of soup and a waffle. Waitresses sit around and chat while food sits waiting to get delivered. The food is good but it is not worth the wait. Half the time they bring my kids waffle with pecans when we stress her allergy when ordering. Then it's another 20 minutes for a new waffle. Overall good food and awful service.

As you'll see by my profile, I rarely review, and it takes an exceptional performance (either good or bad) to inspire me to take the time to write a review... Some buddies and me traveled to Nashville for the weekend and decided to have a lazy night in and ordered from Castrillo's. We placed an online order for an extra large thin crust "kitchen sink" with a couple slices of cheesecake. Confirmation email told us it would be 80 minutes! Now on a Friday... I get it's going to be busy... but that's a bit ridiculous. They need to get that down to an hour. The Pie arrived at just over 100 minutes. But we were hungry and let it slide. The pizza was sparsely populated with toppings. Assuming the "kitchen sink" is the pizza pictured on their take out pamplet... this looked like a poorly topped frozen pizza. It was cold, cheeze was solidified, and the crust... our beloved thin crust was flimsy and devoid of any crunch whatsoever. To top it all off the pizza didn't agree with two of us... one spending the entire night with raging heartburn, the other we spent convincing it wasn't food poisoning as they prayed to the porcelain god all night. The highlight was the cheescake. Boxed frozen cheesecake complete with the paper separators still attached. Needless to say, we'll be ordering Dominos the next time.

This was formerly my favorite restaurant in Nashville. Unfortunately, I got severe food poisoning from a burger here and also have a friend who had a similar experience. I would not trust the meat here.

Hands down the worst Peruvian food we've ever had. The ceviche took 30 min, was warm and the fish tasted bad, but they still made us pay for it. The chicken looked and tasted like fried pigeon. The Lomos Saltado was the only decent plate we tried, but even then the meat was over cooked. I wish I had my $40 back, hoping the bad fish doesn't give us food poisoning.

Three of us had breakfast. I had the Mexican Ole eggs. Scrambled eggs were overcooked and there was so much salsa that it drowned the multitude of potatoes underneath. I couldn't find the chorizo in the salsa...too little! So I ordered crispy bacon after I was finished with the eggs. It came well cooked but cold. My husband had the egg white vegetable omelet and the eggs were overcooked as well. We are allergic to gluten and disappointed that they didn't offer gluten free toast. They need to work on their culinary arts.

Poor service all around! Used the app for reservation claiming 5 minutes, when we checked in we were told they had to clean the table. 15 minutes later still waiting for the table to be cleaned. They acted annoyed when I asked but I repeated what they told me about cleaning the table and they acted confused. My kid threw up on the table (seriously) and we didn't even get extra napkins. The waitress was complaining about more table since she wanted to get off work. Better food at other Cracker Barrel's so keep driving!

Stopped in to pick up dessert for our weekly dinner and TV night. I chose Sprinkles because I read online they carry gluten free cupcakes and my friend can't have gluten and I didn't want to leave her out of dessert... No option today; luckily they had a gluten free cookie! The cookie was good. Also got carrot cake and red velvet cupcakes for those of us without restrictions. The frosting was good, the cake was good, but nothing mouth-melting, run home and tell your mama good. I didn't enjoy the signature dot and sizes didn't seem consistent (some larger than others ). Maybe my expectations were high from everything is heard, but could just be rage over the ATM and convenience. They have a good program you can sign up for a free cupcake which was nice. Awkwardly long, number of required questions could use some truncating- took too long to complete on their iPad but was happy to get free cake.

Today was my second visit to The Cake Bake Shop, and I my experience was very different from my first visit. I am glad i did not leave my review the first time, because my second visit changed my opinion entirely. So I take my sister who is in town visiting. My sister bakes and looooves cake, so i was dying to get her in there. She ordered a slice of pie and i ordered a gluten free cupcake. After our orders were taken, the family next to us paid their bill and another family was sat, ordered, and had FINISHED their deserts before our server came back EMPTY HANDED to tell us ours would be out soon. How long does it take to place a slice of pie on a plate?! When they did come out after an hour of waiting, my sister's pie was beautiful and awesome, as expected at this business, but my cupcake was dry and very obviously purchased from somewhere else. It was so-so, even for a gluten free cupcake and tasted like it may have been frozen. I came there expecting great service and delicious fresh made baked goods. I would have much preferred to order a bowl of chili instead of a stale sub par lie of a cupcake. You didn't fool me, Cake Bake, and I am still shocked that the server thought her service was perfectly normal. Try spending less time and effort on fancy facade, and more on great service and you will go further. D+

How do I even start. Sooooo... we're in the city for Mardi Gras right, it's understood that there's delays in every restaurant, especially close to parade routes. But that's the thing, if the delay was the issue I probably wouldn't be writing this. From the beginning I had a bad vibe, after being seated at two separate tables by the manage of all people, the hostess came to us and said "he should had never seated y'all". Funny thing, I thought she was manager until the end of the story, but I'm getting ahead of myself. So anyway back to the beginning. She frantically explained that she didn't have a number in the register so we would have to wait so she can assign a server to us, aight I don't even know what that means let's keep going. I asked well can we at least go to the bar and order drinks, her reply, no because then that would tie up a server that I could send to your table, really -_-. Finally we get a server, the reason for the 1 star, he was friendly funny but you can tell, over worked. Either way, he takes the drink order, mad slow but we eventually got the drinks. Once again expected. I forgot we ordered food too when we ordered the drinks trying to speed up the service. While waiting on our ordered food our server gave us some salad and gumbo to kinda apologize for the wait, don't order the gumbo. We also ordered some crawfish while we waited because it would come out quickly, don't order the crawfish. They were small under seasoned and somehow dry. Over an hour later and after seeing plate after plate arrive at tables of customers that were seated after us arrive at there destination, the food started arriving. The hot sausage po-boy.. not bad, the bread could use some work. Anyway I bet your like that sounds like they should at least get 3 stars, just wait. So let's talk about the shrimp and grits. How do you even get uncooked rice in grits. Y'all gotta help me on this one. Back to the kitchen it goes, and gonna offer jambalaya. That's not the same bruh. So one of the people in our group ordered the fried chicken, big mistake. Stomach growling, because he has a shellfish allergy, he puts his fork in the chicken... pause for a moment.... BLOOD, yes, BLOOD came oozing out of the chicken. You mean in over an hour you couldn't fully fry chicken. You're a whole restaurant, this isn't something to play with. So we ask for the manager, and the guy that seated us was the manager, I know I spoiled that reveal earlier but we were shocked. He's like, we'll take the dish of the check because you didn't eat it.... lol. This guy is starving and we had to deal with a rude hostess, a long wait, dry crawfish and bad gumbo. That's all you gotta say. Anyway, I was still willing to give this place 2 stars cause the hot sausage po-boy, once again, not bad. But then the waiter that I thought was doing his best had the nerve to be like, y'all owe me $45 in gratuity. Ya know what we are great tippers. But after paying for what we did eat you should be happy we didn't post pics of the food. Anyway good luck at this place E.A.O.R. Eat At Own Risk

I wish I could give this place either negative or zero stars. This past week, an acquaintance I used to work with invited me to come on down and have some lunch there. I ran out of time, as I was on my lunch hour and needed to get back to the office. I brought back some eggrolls for my co-workers and a shrimp and noodle dish for myself. I promptly put the food in the fridge for later. My co-workers heated up and ate the eggrolls and commented on how yummy they were. When I got home, I nuked up my shrimp and noodle dish, thought it tasted just okay. About seven hours later, I woke up in the middle of the night hugging the porcelain bowl. Despite the lack of sleep, I attempted to go to work the next day. I ended up having to leave early, and one of my co-workers started feeling sick around 1 pm. Among communications on Saturday, I found out that my other co-worker is sick, too, with the same symptoms. Since we all ate food from the same place and got sick around the same time and have the same symptoms, obviously it was food poisoning. I contacted my acquaintance and she stated that she informed the kitchen and they basically stated that I need to nuke the food prior to eating, which kind of annoyed me, as it sounded like they were placing the blame on us. None of us will EVER go back! I don't know when the last time was that I felt so miserable. :-(

3 people recommended this place to me and based on the reviews, I was really excited to try it. So I was surprised when the food was totally average. We tried their pasta, chicken parm, roasted peoper (no flavor) and beef tips. What I was partially surprised by, was when we ordered the creme brûlée no one mentioned (and it wasn't listed on the menu) that they change the flavors weekly. We had no idea it was a black cherry until after we had a bite- glad we weren't allergic!

I had read all of the good reviews and swung by to check it out. I love a good cookie, which is what I was after... I had read about the Walnut chocolate chip cookies here, and it was time to try one. I ordered one "Gluten-Free" Walnut Chocolate Chip cookie, one "Gluten-Free" Oatmeal Raisin cookie... and a Cherry Turnover (just because!) ;) Ate the cookies on the way home... or maybe I should say I "tried" the cookies on the way home. The Walnut Chocolate Chip? Very dry, crispy, not very chocolaty, not very walnutty either. This was like eating a "GHOST" of a Chocolate Chip cookie... it was ok, but I will stick to Chewy, evil, MOIST Yummy chocolate chip cookies! The Oatmeal Raisin! A bit more moist, and the raisins were tasty.. but again, just not a hearty, chewy, rich yummy cookie. Both cookies tasted like diet food... which is fine if that is what you want... but I like EVIL cookies! The Cherry Turnover... pretty damn good! I heated it slightly after getting home, and had a big glass of cold WHOLE milk (yes... I hate 2% and skim... I work out, stay in shape, and occasionally have a small splurge!) The cherry turnover almost made the trip worthwhile. But I doubt if I will go back! The whole Gluten-free thing is a nonsense fad too, per some studies (unless you have Celiac disease! Which is a very small percentage of the population!) http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/most-people-shouldnt-eat-gluten-free/ but some people ignore science and medicine... fads and nonsense are more fun, right?

I ordered a chicken spinach floritine for delivery and was so hungry and hadn't are all day because I was in class. It came around 930pm and I take a bite and there was a walnut.. I am allergic to walnuts and realized they gave me the chicken and Carmelized walnuts instead. I called then immediately and a guy answered saying they were closed. I explained to him what happened and all he could do was give me credit for the pizza. They are lucky I'm not deathly allergic to walnuts. I'll never eat here and definitely will not recommend it.

The biggest dump in town everything is filthy I'd rather sit on the ground outside and eat then sit on those tables I couldn't even enjoy my half warmed burger and every bite felt as if I was gonna get food poisoning. This place needs to be shut down. This is a -5 stars from me.
Got hot wings on Sunday and still have food poisoning one week later. HORRIBLE! Never again

Wowza. Someone doesn't often expect any South Philly establishment off the beaten path (aka Passyunk) to serve non-food-poisoning-containing raw fish (SPTR aside). But Hibachi2Go breaks the mold and serves decently fresh sashimi, delicious rolls and a slew of tasty salads/teriyaki, and at penny pincher prices. Not to mention they deliver. What a score! Don't be frightened of this place - it's legit. Not "OMG YOU'LL DIE WHEN YOU EAT THIS" sushi, but "YUM YUM THIS HITS THE SPOT" sushi. And for more than fair prices. Serious South Philly score. Note: I am not a roll fan, but try the Special Boston.

This was our second trip in a week. We asked each time a out what was safe for but allergies. Both times we were told the same things that were safe. He tried cookies and cream first time and wanted to try Christmas tree this time. They gave him a sample (deemed safe) and as he was putting in my mouth I saw that it had m&ms (not safe for nut allergies). Need to better educate as to what is in the ingredients. That was scary (he spit it out quickly and was fine but....)

In New Orleans, the legendary Bourbon Street is full of sin. And by sin, I mean vomit, discarded thongs, booze, beads, and boobs. If you need an escape from the debauchery on Bourbon Street, you should consider stepping into LeBooze. Most of the clientele here is fully clothed, chatting in their deep voices, sipping on scotch, smoking cigars, and showing off a little chest hair. And these are just the women that I am talking about. Kidding. Kidding aside, the place has a classy feel with dark brown wood furnishings, some big screens, and a very professional and polite staff. My bartender looked like Jon Bon Jovi. Yes, that Jon Bon Jovi. The guy that your wife thinks about whenever she needs to get herself in the mood. You know, in the mood to clean the kitchen. Anyway, after every round I would buy for my clients, I would say things like... "Oh! Oh! Drinkin' on a prayer!" "Your drink is like bad medicine. Bad medicine is what I need!" "It's my life! It's now or never!" The bartender was not pleased, but he was a good sport about it. He fueled up my clients, so I could take him to other less than desirable joints on Bourbon Street. I heart NOLA.

Today "Mama's Vegetarian" is closed for the Jewish holidays. I was always thinking to try the Falafel Truck since I heard alot about it on Yelp. Despite the raining day I went there and to my surprise there is a line under the rain! I think the line is another way to distinguish this truck because it has no name, kinda a truck on the road similar to a hole in the wall type bars. If it is your 1st time here please listen carefully to what I will say:- 1. Location NE Corner 20th and Market St, you have to walk a bit on the 20th st towards JFK to find it. No Signs just a truck and always people in long line infront of it so be prepared to wait. 2. No Menu either, you will never know the price or what to order unless you reach the truck, no need to order either the chef will just give you the only one dish he has on the day. 3. If you are allergic to garlic this place is not for you, he is using alot of garlic! 4. The platter contains (Garlic well grilled Chicken, Flalafel balls and other things/sauces depend on the mode of the chef on that day) I got some green hummus I think and other veggie thing I couldn't identify but it taste delicious and even some fruits all covered with tomato sauce and above it Chicken and Falafel. some white peta and bread. 5. DO NOT ASK what is on your platter, this is considered a very rude behavior by the Chef and he will go defensive about his food, how expensive it cost him to make it, how cheap is it sold to you, and how much efforts he made to make it, and you will not be hungry the rest of your day because this is "more than enough" food. I am allergic to spices and I asked him innocently if the sauce is spicy, the chef went nuts on me gave me a lecture under the rain about his food, I tried to explain to him this is my 1st time to his truck but he get more mad every time I reply to him, looking at the people behind me waiting on the rain I decided to cut it short smiled thanked him and decided to move but he kept urging me to carry his food very carefully and with more passion! telling me again this is Expansive food I will never find it with $10 price on any restaurant on Philly! I giggled trying to move away from this crazy chef to avoid more arguments. 6. The truth is the food is delicious. Falafel is very tasty and grilled chicken is fresh and awesome, $10 is OK price for that but the behavior of the chef is ridiculous.

I've been here before and it's been fine. Tonight I noticed the girl making salads was using her hands to pick up ingredients rather than using the tongs. This causes cross contamination that can make me very ill. I don't think I'll be back.

I love barbecue. I did not love this. Ribs were overdone and so salty I could not eat more than one. My tongue feels like it weighs ten 10 lbs and tastes like I licked a beach! The sauce is thin and underwhelming to say the least. I'm giving it one star since I didn't get food poisoning. Don't waste your time. If you want really good BBQ, take the ride to Schaffer's in Ethridge.

Not sanotary they use alot of the salad ingredients from the pizza line which is touched without gloves.management is horrible. No refunds just empty credits. I feel bad for staff that gets yelled at infront of custoners for things they didnt do especially when ive come in and seen it first hand . soda is always out. Never stocked. Floors r filthy. Dough is not fresh at all. Its mostly almost frozen then quickly defrosted. Cross contamination. 100% food safety precautions are not takrn what so ever. Ceo of marcos needs to look deeply into this store and see hpw the stores owner treats employees and ex employees. Ignorong them refusing to serve them or communicate without a ban notice. Its sad.

We were so excited to hear about Organico Pizza. Its concept -- organic, locally-sourced ingredients -- really appealed to us. We recently ordered a gluten-free Margherita pizza and arancini. Although the gluten-free pizza shell wasn't bad, both the pizza and the arancini were bland and close to flavorless. I was very disappointed, given the concept of the restaurant, and the rich flavors typically provided by organic, locally-sourced, well-seasoned foods.

Very disappointing experience... Happened across this restaurant as my mom has Celiac, and it offers gluten-free pizza. My mom called and ordered take-out for herself and my brother because we were traveling and the other members of our family had already eaten at other places in Philly. My mom ordered their Verde pizza, and my brother ordered their Margherita. When we arrived at the restaurant, we were hot and tired from being out in the sun all day and had asked if we could eat instead in their (very empty restaurant) instead of taking the pizza outside. They told us that the tables in the whole restaurant were being saved for people walking in for dinner. Even though we had in essence paid for dinner and would of course have left a tip if we were going to be waited on. They ended up eating on a curb. My brother asked for water, and they treated him like he had leprosy and gave him an EXTREMELY difficult time for one glass of water. This experience was just picking up our pizza! The pizza itself was dry, tasteless, and the toppings were extremely large. My mom had ordered arugula to go on top, which they forgot to put on. She had also wanted olives on her pizza but was told they didn't have any. Not sure how an Italian restaurant doesn't have olives, but there you go. My brother and mother both agreed that it was the worst gluten-free pizza they've tasted, so I would recommend to the restaurant not only working on customer service, but also buying/making a different recipe for their gluten-free pizza. Upsetting as there are few Italian restaurants that offer gluten-free pizza safe for Celiacs. Will not be back.

I know the people making the food are swamped but they need to be more careful with cross contamination. I made them aware but they clearly didn't take what I said into consideration since I just threw my guts up! I'm sure it's hard when you're busy but if a customer is telling u of their food sensitivity should listen and not roll your eyes & suck your teeth. I can't imagine I'm the first & I won't be the last if they continue to ignore & throw food together so haphazardly.

I have given this restaurant two separate tries and both time have gotten sick. This last time was my honeymoon and we decided to give them one more try since they didn't seem buys. The food was gross and I couldn't hardly eat it. My husband ate half of his meal and couldn't eat the rest. By the time we paid and went back to our hotel room I was super sick and throwing up. Mind you this is the first night of our honeymoon! The next morning my husband eats some of his cheesecake (we had refrigerated it) which he didn't eat the night prior and ended up getting sick the entire second day. We ended up cutting our honeymoon short due to both of us being sick and decided we would try going on another one later. We persisted to have the runs and stomach aches the rest of the week as if we had food poisoning. Thankfully mine was just the runs, my poor husband would throw up on and off. Will never go tot his location again!

You definitely come here for the beer selection, not the food, so as a celiac, this place doesn't do much for me. Iron Hill has a gluten free menu (if you ask) with a decent amount of choices. I ordered a lamb burger on a gluten free bun. It came topped with a few strands of red onion, a couple pieces of feta, and a spoonful of a green spiced sauce. The flavors were pretty good, but overall, the portion was small and didn't seem thoughtfully prepared. Others at my table enjoyed the variety of beers, but agreed that their sandwiches were just OK, nothing special. With decently expensive prices for standard American food, Iron Hill just isn't the kind of place I'd ever choose to check out again.

45 minutes to get 10 wings, 2 burgers, nachos and a buffalo chicken wrap. First off, the place was dead. 9:30 PM on a Sunday night, so our orders should have come out quickly. I don't know what the freaking hold up in the kitchen was, but I think the wait time was a little extreme. The food was decent, but as is the case with most Wing House restaurants, everything was edible, yet underwhelming. My Belt-Bustin' Nachos were piled high, but it was all bark, no bite. So they took 700 pounds of tortilla chips and tossed them on a plate, and only put the cheese and chili on the top layer, so there was absolutely NO topping penetration on the lower levels of chips. So after eating the top layer, the rest was just dry-ass chips. The wings were alright, nothing spectacular, and the two burgers my buddies ordered came out well done, even though they ordered medium. Our waitress was friendly and kept the cold beer flowin'. In my opinion should have given us one of the three pitchers for free due to the aforementioned issues. However, other than an apology, she offered us nothing. The bathroom was a hot mess. Looked like someone vomited all over the sink in the stall, and there was poop all over the toilet. There was also toilet paper shreds all over the floor. Went to wash my hands--no soap in the dispenser. Not sure what the staff was doing that caused a 45 minute wait for our food, but one thing is certain, they weren't cleaning the restrooms! Needless to say, I won't be back.

Just left chili's on McCarran my girlfriend got food poisoningBecause I gave her old Southwest eggrolls that was probably under the warmer she didn't want to say anything She threw up three times as soon as we were all the eggrolls She's a server's ash well she's knows it feels Thats that's why We didn't complain but

We ate here in the middle of a road trip and were excited to try the unique burgers and ice cream. Our waitress was AMAZING and she made our experience much better, but the food wasn't great. They advertised having gluten free options, but the gluten free bun was undercooked -still cold in the middle- and difficult to eat. Our fries were over cooked, thicker fries but so crispy that they weren't good, and SO greasy. I squeeze one of the crispy fries and drips of grease came off just that one fry. I loved the concept of all the burgers and the sauces were delicious, but more needed to be done to make the food something worth the price we paid.

The service is mediocre we are gluten free. I asked for pad thai with chicken. Japanese rice noodles are gluten free. But unstead if giving me those, they substituted the dumb fusilli noodles, and forgot the chicken. I took it back. They have me the same thing again, still no chicken. My wife ordered the Japanese Pan noodles with tofu. The tofu was cold she took it back. They came back with it 5 mins later was luke warm. And everything else tasted burnt and very salty. Not recomended.

Tried Katie's off my help book mark. It was pretty good. I tried the platter and the crab cakes . I ate my platter first which was fish shrimp oysters onion rings and fries. It was amazing. Last I begin to eat my crab cakes and had to run out and vomit. I'm not sure it was me or the cakes . I didn't complain because everything else was amazing and the staff is super friendly. The chef came by to our table as well.

The pizza is ok. I like the Domino's gluten free pizza crust. It's better than most other places but needs to be cooked extra to be good (there's an option in the app for well-done). I have had a number of issues with my pizzas but keep ordering from this location because they get it right most of the time. I have had pizzas that were ordered with extra or double of something and come with just a couple pieces. My last order came cold, I saw on the Tracker that the pizza was out of the oven and checked for quality 22 minutes before it left the store. I understand that it takes time for delivery drivers to get back and make their rounds but there is no good excuse for a cold pizza. All of the employees I have dealt with were very friendly and I enjoy my pizza when it gets delivered without problems.

We ordered takeout curbside. Ordering online was quick and easy. I specified on everything to be gluten free. The order was simple enough because nothing we ordered contained gluten and I requested no bread. A steak dinner (2 rib eyes bone in with 2 sides) for under 75$ after tip is not bad if you aren't being picky. I probably would have given a 3 star review but the main issue was that I ordered 2 medium rare steaks and basically got 2 rare steaks. The second steak was so rare we had to put it in the oven to get it to medium rare which obviously is not ideal. If it werent for the incorrect temperature on the steaks it would have been a better experience. Nonetheless, I still appreciate that they had curbside pickup and I know their steaks are usually cooked correctly at other locations I have been to (from past experience). Nothing I had contained gluten or was cross contaminated also which is always important when you have food allergies. I do wish I had looked at the reviews though because quite a few people have reported undercooked and overcooked steaks.

My gf threw up the pork chops she had not one hour later. Unfortunately the chicken pot pie and great beer selection isn't enough to hold this place down. Also rednecks everywhere, and they over serve them, people bringing beers into bathroom and trying to start fights.

I got really bad food poisoning at this place. The front looks ok, but the kitchen must be disgusting. I have a strong stomache but I was vomiting just an hour after eating there. Definitely not a fluke. Anyone raving about this place is probably just a friend of theirs trying to get business. This place is basically just a very expensive way to get salmonella poisoning. Do yourself a favor and just eat out of a trash can.

gianna's raises a some questions in me. like, why do i think "dogfood" when i am eating their vegan cheesesteaks? and, why do i get sudden and powerful cravings for them every few weeks? i don't really like eating here (they lied to vegans/lactose intolerant people for years about their "dairy free" cheese) but sometimes i just really need a huge gross vegan cheesesteak and nothing else will do.

This place is seriously the bee's knees. Service is amazing. Our server was so cool, cracking jokes left and right. Also very serious though. Super knowledgeable of the menu as well as the whole gluten free issue below. First of all, my little brother has celiac so HAS to eat gluten free (like legit gluten free, no cross contamination, no "im just on a diet" nonsense). They offer EVERYTHING on their menu as gluten free. I personally loveeeeee rice noodles so I was all about sharing with him. My favorite apps: dan dan noodles, spicy crispy cucumbers, dumplings in chili oil. I certainly eat more than most people but dining with three people, this is PLENTY. Everything on their menu is sharing style so don't come with your picky friends (we all have some). All of the hot pots are exceptional. To date, my favorite was one we ordered off of the special menu..................................... Sorry I was just wiping the drool off of my face. Half kidding. We ordered pork shoulder in a spicy brown sauce filled with bok choy, eggplant, green beans, and other veggies. The pork was crispy on the outer layer and just the right amount of juicy fat. It was so succulent and literally fell off the bone Between three of us, we no where near finished. But I had an awesome lunch the next day! They offer some decent craft beers and have a few TVs which can be great if you're dragging someone to dinner and they can't miss "their" game (I still don't understand how the game belongs to them). PS. The prices are insanely cheap and I am still unsure why but I will not be complaining anytime soon.

I dream of Primo Hoagies all the way in Sunny South FL. I'm not supposed to eat Gluten, but a Celiac Attack is so worth it. Primo Hoagies oozes South Philly. They're family owned, everyone is nice and the Hoagies are extremely delicious. It's a sandwich shop, you can't eat in here. I also think they close early, like before dinner.

The service was decent. I ordered a rice bowl that came with flank steak and kimchi and spinach. There was maybe 3 spinach leaves. The flank steak was a little greasy. My friend got the Italian Mac n cheese which was good. Not that flavorful but good. She had an allergic reaction and I'm assuming there may have been pesto in it. Don't recall seeing it on the menu, but she didn't ask (dumb). The live music was nice and set a pleasant mood.

My wife has a number of dietary issues (allergic to dairy, soy, gluten). The West Ave Grille used to be one of the few places we could go out to eat where we could both have nice meals. Before my last two experiences, I always thought the food was way overpriced. But, I didn't mind paying a little bit more if it meant we could eat out. My daughter was in a play. We wanted to go out to dinner to celebrate in between the afternoon and evening performance . We walked in this past Saturday and there was no one in the restaurant. Wow! What good luck, right? Nope. It took forever to get drinks, our order taken, and then the food. We were seated at 4:00 and didn't start eating until 4:40. Here was our meal: 3 kids meals (1 chicken nuggets with fries, 1 grilled cheese with fries, 1 pancake), a salad with plain chicken for my wife, and a portabella "burger" for myself. The meal was over $50 bucks. So, the verdict. The food is ok but the prices are way too much. West Ave Grille is the kind of place that will charge you $9 for a burger + 1 dollar for cheese and additional dollars for every other topping. On top of which, all of their sandwiches come with chips. For the price, you could at least give fries. My wife's salad was inedible. The kids were at least happy. Oh, my portabella burger wasn't a burger at all (even though I asked the waitress and she assured me it was--had there been more time between the shows, I would have sent it back), was two small mushrooms, some onions and a few peppers on a roll. That's it. I ate in about 3 bites then went home and ate something else. We won't be back.

Don't eat here. This place is fowl. The service is fine, and there is some okay sushi rolls. But last time I will ever eat sushi, this place gave me food poisoning. I have not been able to leave my house for the past 24 hours because of constant puking and dirreah. I will never have sushi again because of the pain I have went through with the food poisoning. Thanks jazmine.
Ate there yesterday with my fiancé. Great service, but the food was terrible. My fiancé got food poisoning which led to her needing to go to the ER. I highly recommend never eating here.

Granted, we had the latest reservation on a Monday night (10:45 pm) but we weren't the only ones in the place. We knew we had to be quick in ordering but the food was a little underwhelming. The Famous Shrimp Cocktail was everything we could have asked for and as amazing experience as you'd think, but the ribeye was chewy - like, really chewy - and the Brussels sprouts that we asked for with bacon - and were sort of laughed at like "of course, they come with bacon" even though the gluten free menu we were ordering from said we had to add it to the dish - did not come with bacon. Our server asked after we'd finished if we'd like anything else and when we ordered a draft beer he said, "we're not serving anything else tonight." Just a bit off...maybe expecting too similar of care that you'd get at St. Elmo's. I think we'll try there next time instead.

If I was writing a review about dinner at Herbie's it would be 4 stars edging towards 5. This review, though, it just for brunch. We went to brunch with a group of 6 and while there wasn't anything glaringly wrong...there wasn't anything fantastic either. I had the three cheese omelette with sausage and veggies added. It came with roasted potatoes and choice of bread. The omelette tasted great and the filling was delicious but it was seriously the tiniest omelette I've ever seen at a restaurant. The roasted potatoes were actually just french fries. I was literally hungry within an hour of finishing brunch. They were able to accomodate a gluten free diet but not with very many choices. Herbie's caters so well to gluten free for dinner that we were very disappointed with what felt like neglect on the brunch menu. While Ryan did enjoy his food (eggs benedict with salmon and capers), it was nothing spectacular. Our group had a coupon that included cocktails but without that, I would call Herbie's brunch unnecessarily pricey. I enjoy spending money on good food but for the portions, this was just flatout overpriced. I'll be back to Herbie's but it will definitely be during dinner hours.

So, my feelings on this place are mixed. I can't complain about the prices for this store directly, because it's a corporation. I saw other complaining about the prices, but the store itself is not setting the prices. What I can complain about is the set up of the products at the front of the store. When you are waiting in line there's a section of homemade bath products lingering there with you. I don't know about you, but myself and a lot of people I know, have bad allergies. When I'm stuck waiting in line, I can hardly breathe and have actually left because it was so bad. I can't stand perfume scented ANYTHING and this makes it very difficult to have to wait in their lines. Their lines. There's another issue. Why do they have one person ringing you up and another cashier standing next to them, literally being handed your groceries, just to put them into a bag that's in front of them both? It seems counter productive if anything. Also, why is the register set up the way it is? The screen is like, 50 feet away from the actual scanner. Dumb. The bakery items are AMAZING, and love the pastries. I recently had the double fudge brownies, to, die, for.

Cappy's Pizza located just south of N. Florida Ave and Hillsborough Ave is something unique to the landscape of pizzerias. The setup is something unique, as if Chunk from The Goonies opened a restaurant to preserve his childhood and favorite food, but granted atmosphere is nice, but food has to hold up and this is where I feel Cappy's didn't do justice. Now my review is solely based on their rendition of the Chicago Style Pizza. Seems that they use a corn meal crust, with very little cheese and the standard tomato topping. As a trooper for Giordano's (*sniff* Please come back), I must say that even understanding that people have different Chi-town Styles, this wasn't one that held me over, What was good about the pizza, was the tomato sauce. Has a nice subtle kick to it. The Negtives about the pizza was the lack of cheese (c'mon Chi-town makes lactose intolerants fear the toilet). I'm not a fan of corn meal crust (I did like Lou Malnati's in Chicago though), but this just seemed to hard. So now that Tampa is bare without Giordano's Cappy's seems to be able to wear the crown by default. Though the value is there (very nice size large for $13), the flavor is not.

I'm sure that this place is lovely for the average person whose body doesn't believe ordinary substances are poison, but I have Celiac Disease so unfortunately that is my life. I started off disappointed because, unlike most Thai restaurants that tend to handle my Celiac Disease easily, I was limited to curry as an entree. But ok, at least I talked to the cook to determine what I could eat, and she was clear on the problem of oyster sauce and soy sauce. Unfortunately they weren't as consciencious about the non-sauce part of the meal. I was in for the lunch special, which is a great deal and comes with an appetizer. I asked about the spring roll, was told its contents were good for me, and ordered it. I'm expecting one of those cabbage-wrapped or rice paper rolls, naturally, because Celiac. That is unfortunately not what I was served, and I only didn't end up horribly horribly sick because I have learned to identify potential problems and be pushy about second checks when I'm suspicious about an ingredient. The spring rolls used egg roll wraps, which are pure wheat. So yeah, that could have been REAL bad. The curry itself was fresh and tasty and all kinds of wonderful. They brought me replacement edamame which I took to go and which was the same. But...they served me gluten even when I was offered the very limited safe menu. And let's be honest, I was coming for noodles, so I just don't think I can come back. I really wanted to love this cute Thai hole-in-the-wall, and I probably would have if I didn't need strict gluten free.

Clean Juice is a franchise that is a 100% certified organic juice bar, that offers a variety of juices, smoothies, toast, and acai bowls. Highlights: * Location: It's tucked into the strip mall between a Five Guys and Happy Dragon, so it is not easy to spot from the main road *Parking: This strip mall parking lot can get pack midday, especially during lunch, so spots can be somewhat a hard to find * They do list items that they use that aren't certified organic, including the gluten free bread and pink Himalayan salt * For sweetness in their juices and smoothies, honey or maple syrup seem to be their go to - Prices are a bit high + Fresh and high quality produce is used * They do have gluten free bread, though not sure of their handling of cross contamination processes - Small seating area with a handful of lower table tops and higher chaired seating - Orders are made fresh, so there can be a bit of a wait if there is a line ahead of you. If you are in a hurry, they do offer their juices in bottles to go Overall, a decent refreshing pick me up if you are in the area.

The restaurant was inconsistent at best. I went for the lunch buffet. The food was actually pretty good. The food was tasty and fish was fresh. The sashimi was actually normal thickness. There were also a hot food selection. The problem was there isn't that many people that go for lunch so the food wasn't too fresh. Another problem is with how they served the sushi. They had four tongs for around 12 types of sushi. About half of them had sauce on them(spicy mayo , etc.) So all the tongs had sauce on them. When I grab a non sauce sushi, it got contaminated with the tongs. The selection was small. They only had the basics. They didn't have any mackerel or yellowtail. they should do made to order. The service was very warm and welcoming. They were very attentive. The atmosphere was very average. It needs some renovating in my perspective. The restaurant had very cheap laminate that was bubbling. The bathroom was clean but the decor and appearance seem dirty. The people that go there are just low. Some lady asked me about whether some dish was included in the buffet and then asked if I spoke English after I ignored her question. Apparently she assumed I worked at the restaurant despite the fact I was not in uniform and had a plate of food. They then exclaimed how "cosmopolitan" they are for using chopsticks. I guess that is just Land O' Lakes. Overall conclusion. Food is good but need improvement. I think it is a overpriced. $15 is pretty expensive for a weekday lunch buffet. If you live in the area, I would suggest trying it out. I imagine ordering a-la-carte would be decent. I would only suggest the lunch buffet if you are not too familiar with sushi or are a budget. I would recommend Kozi over this place for sushi buffet.

My family members keep picking this place for big outings since they usually have seating for everyone. However, after recently visiting, I have noticed that every time we go, someone gets food poisoning. First it was me, then an aunt, now my son. Another time I went with co-workers and my boss got food poisoning.

Horrible Pharmacy! DO NOT FILL or REFILL any scripts here. Service rep (gentleman) was not helpful at all. Must be this specific location. Asked him to contact my daughters physician to request a new refill on a script for allergy medication. He was uncooperative as well as VERY unknowledgeable of how certain things work. Instead of paying for a "Brand Named" over the counter Med. at a much higher cost per pill. This adds up and from a non Medicare/Medicaid non food stamp recipient- this is my personal route for a more cost effective out of pocket route that I mus take. It is purely common sense for a person to obtain a script for certain "OVER THE COUNTER" meds to take advantage of "Walmart's" low cost "AFFORDABLE" generic drugs list program. If it's not possible and can't be done or so he was implying...then again why is that specific generic drug listed on Walmart's drug list? Maybe there's no one at the pharmacy department who has much common sense. Great prices but definitely not worth the time and aggravation. Will transfer my other medications elsewhere or perhaps to TARGET!

Go here for an indulgent meal. Pretty unhealthy all around. Sandwiches are nice and buttery. Honestly, I'd opt for an alcoholic milkshake only and eat somewhere else. Or go for fries and food and skip the shake. You can't do it all in one sitting - too much! It's a cute atmosphere and I like this strip of Locust, there are some awesome old buildings from the STL glory days when auto mechanics and show rooms owns the street. Dill pickle soup extremely pickley, no other real flavors, like creamy pickle juice. I got the Cuban and it was so greasy almost couldn't eat it. Felt pretty weighed down for the rest of the day. They do have a decent number of gluten free options though!!

We made a reservation. We took seat was pretty smooth. My son and husband both has allergies. They have a list for break down ingredients that was very nice. But I think the restaurant was under staffed , they took forever to bring drinks and appetizers. And they didn't have edamame and white rice. The food were already cold and not so good. I had Mongolian beef (one of my favorite). It was overcooked. So disappointed overall, we were paying pretty good money for meal. But we can't get what we want and decent food. I haven't been PF Chang years. I always had a great experience in Orange County, CA. I hope only this location is not good.

I had to take back a star. When I got back to my hotel room, I felt queasy and just assumed I had gotten some gluten cross contamination. When I rejoined my dinner companions today, the three of them each reported that they felt like they had eaten something "off". My conclusion is that this place needs a visit from Kitchen Nightmares.

I have some food allergies. I tried to ask the waiter questions. He was snobby and supercilious and told me they catered to the general public. The food portions were small - the bread was white bread out of a plastic bag, and it was pricey. It might be ? a good bar, but certainly not a decent eatery!

I love this concept. I am a healthy eater for the most part and love finding places that have healthy but tasty options. I feel like Nook really has potential to be really, really good but our experience last weekend was just average. I do like the menu options. They have tacos, pizza, and more that are gluten free, low carb, Paleo, etc. The only problem is the food is lacking flavor. We ordered the sweet potato wedges and the texture was mushy and they needed salt badly. At least there was salt on the table. The Brussel sprouts were the highlight of our meal and I would highly recommend those. We also had a wood fire pizza, Paleo style. While the toppings were tasty and the presentation beautiful the texture of the crust was weird- not bad- but weird. The crust was thin- which we love- but not crispy. It was sort of soggy. The two cocktails we tried were quite good- Kombucha mule and Kombucha Rita. I would order both of those again. Overall- I think Nook gets 5 stars for concept but 3 stars for execution. The prices were a tad steep but fresh, healthier ingredients are usually more expensive.

The most incredible breakfast spot in Nashville. This experience was definitely one that my boyfriend and I will never forget. It just happened to be close to the airport and we came in for a late breakfast on Sunday afternoon. Ella helped us ordering and recommended their omelette and waffle bar - their weekend special. After we had paid my boyfriend realized he had forgotten to order coffee and Ella was more than happy to accommodate this mistake. We originally ordered two waffles but after watching Julie whip up some omelettes my boyfriend decided to switch to an omelette which was the best decision he could have made. It was the best omelette either of us have ever had in our lives. Julie was very nice about switching the order and was excited to cook his omelette to his liking. I have a deadly allergy to strawberries and was worried about cross contamination at the waffle topping bar. I raised this concern and Sunflower went to the back and cut up an entire banana just for me which I was incredibly appreciative for. Julie even tossed the banana slices in the cinnamon mixture that was on the bananas on the topping table. It was the most incredible food we could have ever asked for. My boyfriend said the coffee was delicious. While we would have been extremely satisfied with just the food, the environment made it a true Nashville experience. They had live music with two guys playing the banjo and guitar and singing. The restaurant is located in garages with cool graffiti artwork and decorations all over the walls. This was truly a special and authentic Nashville experience. We highly recommend Phat Bites and we will be returning every time we find ourselves in Nashville.

Worst experience ever!! Cedric my waiter was horrible! Especially told him I was allergic to avocado and to not put it on my food. 55 minutes later avocado on my lettuce wrap! Stay away from this place. Poor service and poor management!!

We tried Ledo pizza for the first time just recently. My bf tried a calzone and I got a gluten free pizza. He reported back that he simply felt his wasn't good. I was not a big fan of the gluten free pizza. It was doughy with a thick layer of cheese that was filling but relatively tasteless. Although I am grateful that they offer a gluten free option, this one out of many I have tried else where was far from being my favorite. I do like that they offered rectangler pizzas. That's unique for our area.

You know...spiritually speaking, I'm going with 3 stars for now. My soul wasn't stirred. Here I am on a Saturday, looking for God in all the wrong places. All I had were the gluten free chocolate chip cookie and the Rose matcha green tea, and well...My thoughts? 1.) I like the pools of chocolate in the cookie, but I wish it were chewier. Gluten free anything always feels like it's missing something... (gluten? Lol) Gluten is the glue that holds everything together, and without it, everything falls apart. I mean this on a spiritual level. 2.) And the rose matcha fell flat somewhere. It was neither pronounced in rose or matcha flavor. You need to pick a side. You need to make a choice. You need to commit. You need to be STRONG with one flavor and have a HINT of the other, but you kinda did neither. You were half-assed polyamorous. You didn't pick a winner and run with it. You shied away from both. It was colored green iced water. At the end of the day, I feel some potential here. I suggest going back to the drawing board.

Yes, this place is surprisingly inexpensive (all food, including desserts, for three at $67) and the range of food is wonderful. Many dishes include cheese so it would be a difficult place for strictly paleo or lactose intolerant foodies to enjoy. Those cheese-stuffed and bacon-wrapped dates just wouldn't be the same without the cheese! I like the sangrita (margarita topped with a little sangria) but the hibiscus-infused margarita was too tart for my taste and the sangria was less fruity than I like. I'd visit again for the food but our server appeared to be running the server marathon which I found antithetical to relaxing and enjoying an evening out.

This was one of the worst dining experiences EVER! I'd rather sit at the DMV for 4 hours than spend another minute at this restaurant. Came here for a bachelorette dinner. The food was mediocre but the service was absolutely terrible. Sat down and was told "let's hurry up to expedite your meal", not to mention the drinks were terrible, server walked away while taking orders, unwilling to accommodate a dairy allergy, and simply did not listen to the order. We're told we could split the bill for 10 and it took 1.5 hours to deal with the bill. Worst decision to have a special meal at this restaurant. Will never recommend to anyone in Santa Barbara or traveling there. In addition, this should NOT be a 100 restaurant on opentable.

I really like the burgers , They also claim better ingredients then your typical burger chain and they'll do a dairy free grill for people who have allergies which is really fantastic however for some reason they refuse to answer the phone they lose out on so many orders not just people ordering on the phone but people who think the restaurant will be too crowded even to show up. Just called them three times went to the restaurant and there was nobody there. I refuse to do their online ordering because they shut down the restaurant sometimes early on holidays they just don't open but they don't shut down online ordering. Was charged and never refunded for my purchase. The place used to be managed better now they've gotten too big. management needs to come back because the product is there and the concept is there. Hurry before you lose a good business.

I'm shocked at the reviewer who gave this place 5 stars. Were they eating at the same restaurant I was??? The service was absolutely deplorable...unless, of course, you like being insulted and treated rudely while dining out. The food was NOT authentic German food, and 2 people in our party experienced a not-very-lovely take-home gift of food poisoning. Do yourself a favor and go eat at the German Bistro instead at 5232 S MacDill. Outstanding customer service, great food, and free beer. Can't be beat.

I got the choucroute garnie maison, which was a mix of ham leg, pork belly, and bratwurst. I started with the crawfish bisque. All was fantastic, until I got an allergic reaction to the bisque a couple of hours after dinner. I am not allergic to crawfish but I am allergic to crab. So warning, other seafood makes its way into the crawfish bisque. My friend got shrimp and grits and reported that it was great.

If your in Nashville this is a great place to stay. My wife and I wanted to take a small vacation to get away and this place seemed like a unique option compared to downtown hotels with much less to do for a similar price. Tips: - Get an atrium view, you will love it - Be on at least the fourth floor of you don't want people looking in your window - It's a resort, so if you forget a toothbrush just expect to pay 3xs the normal price. Come prepared - The hotel can be packed, so plan accordingly for dinner if you don't want an hour wait for Mexican food. Pros: - The rooms are finished really well with great materials. Still a hotel, but one with a bit more premium feel. - The hotel is massive with many places to spend time. - The garden areas are amazing, full of real plants. This makes it a great place to visit in the colder months. - Boat ride tour is great for leaning more about the building and this history of the resort. - Solario Cantina has gluten free options for most meals - Netflix & Hulu can be signed into to watch on the nice TV's - Guest services are super helpful - WiFi is included Cons: - Gluten Free dinner options are scarce outside of one place - You pay a lot for food, and it's not always impressive - Bathrooms are really small (regular room) ** UPDATE ** I am updating this review because the last night we stayed here we think we stayed in a room that had bedbugs present. My wife woke up with bites all over her arms and legs. Her bag was next to the door that divides two rooms and our guess is that our neighbors had them and they came in through that door. We left with all of our stuff in trash bags...

I think the key here is "Vietnamese-*inspired*". Not actually Vietnamese. Its okay but don't go in with the hope of getting something authentic. The servers were really great, though. Very careful about allergies and very friendly. Probably won't return - it was pricey and the quality of the food just wasn't proportionate to the cost. Not that the food was bad. Just seems like you pay for the ambience more than anything.

Had high hopes since it was recommended by lady from Vietnam. Pho broth was good. "Fresh" Basil leaves were spotted black with slim on them, when we pointed it out, they said it was okay, and did not offer fresh, or any other option. I guess We are use to basil without slim.
