My wife threw up after seeing it. Go to egg roll # 1 for great pho, and numerous other things.

Our server, Dawt, was the only one who seemed to have work ethic. She has a pleasant demeanor and cleaned tables, organized what she could when she wasn't helping customers. Other staff sat on their cell phones in the dining area. One of the kitchen staff came out and also joined on the cell phone action with sanitary gloves on. I hope his phone was clean. There was also a stench. Almost like the sour smell of vomit. Food was decent. Higher expectation for staff by the manager and a thorough cleaning and this place would receive a better review from me!

While I love supporting local businesses I have to warn everyone of my recent experience. I went in on a Saturday evening to get their seafood gumbo which is pretty good to serve during the saints game. I did not feel like cooking that night so I grabbed some spaghetti which was the worst decision I could have made. I became extremely ill and had to go to urgent care the next morning for treatment due to food poisoning, thank God my one year old wanted nothing to do with it. I ended up throwing away the rest of the spaghetti and gave away the almost $100 worth of potatoe salad, gumbo etc. I purchased for fear of becoming even more sick. My family did end up eating the potatoe salad and gumbo without falling ill but beware of the spaghetti. I will never purchase anything from here prepared by them again!

All the meat looked like it had been sitting out for days. Everything was dried out and stringy. The only appetizing meat I found were chicken sticks and they were so dry they hurt my teeth. My stomach has been hurting all night to the point that I'm getting a bit worried about food poisoning. None of the food is even labeled properly so you dont even know what you're eating; my girlfriend thought she was getting chicken but it turned out to be fried bananas. The place looks like it was beautiful at one point but now it is completely disgusting. The backs of the booths are stained and filthy and were pretty sure we saw bugs crawling around on one. There is a dirty glass case on the floor by the register that is full of laughably filthy bottles of juice. Some of the poles holding up the awnings of the buffet are covered in flaky rust that is likely falling into the food. There is no hand soap in the absolutely disgusting bathroom. The woman who works there is very rude and wouldn't even look at us. The whole time we were there she was yelling at her poor husband. We couldn't help but feel bad for the guy. She wouldn't even sit us at first, she just totally ignored us until we realized that she was suddenly calling for us from across the room. I have no idea how this place is still open. It's dangerous to eat there. It actually made me sick. Stay away.

I still love the food but the quality of staff is getting ridiculous. We all knew about the poor bar service situation, but a counter worker not properly checking for a food allergy question, just guessing and passing that off as the truth, AND THEN GUESSING WRONG is completely unacceptable. And then acting totally annoyed when the food arrives and it was pointed out to her. Any respectable establishment should educate it's employees about the danger that food allergies can present. Completely turned me off to going there and even hoping that someone knows anything about the food served. Still the tuck special is delicious.

Food: 5/5 Service: 2.5-3/5 Overall Score: 4/5 A date and I came here the Friday before Thanksgiving around 7pm for dinner. The place was not full, however the restaurant seemed short-staffed to accommodate the amount of guests. There were long waits to be seated (despite only half the tables in the dining room being used), and once seated, we experienced a somewhat long wait for a waiter to greet us (at least 15 minutes went by). Throughout our time there, our waiter was slammed and rarely checked on us with refills, requested items, etc. We had to remind him for things we asked for before receiving them (ie forks, refills, etc) The forks that we received upon request were plastic mind you, so they were practically worthless against the crab legs that we needed them for. Now, that Negative Nancy has made her appearance, let's invite Positive Polly to the review. The food was great! I ordered off the a la carte menu as my date didn't want to share meal-for-two smh. I had a pound of crab legs, a pound of shrimp, one corn on the cob, and one order of potatoes (a pack of three). I got these with the "whole shebang" seasoning and mild temperature. It was all delicious! I especially loved the corn! It was great and well prepared.The mild temperature still had a kick to it. For my drink I had the peach tea, which was really tasty! My date had the "middle" pre-fixe meal. I don't remember the name of it, but it came with crab legs, shrimp, crawfish, potatoes, sausages, and corn. He got this with the "whole shebang" seasoning, and medium temperature. He really enjoyed everything! I had some sausage from his meal and it was delicious! The medium was definitely hotter than the mild, which again was still spicy. This was no cheap feast, but it was about what you'd expect for a seafood boil in St. Louis (expect around $30-$40 a person depending on what you plan on adding to it). Now, I'd be remiss if I didn't add that my date was sick the next day with a stomach bug. He told me that he woke up at 5am the next day vomiting and it continued all day. I did not get sick at all. I repeat, I DID NOT GET SICK AT ALL! So I can't say that it was from something that he ate or not. Granted, we ate out of two different boil bags, although I still had a couple crawfish and sausages from his bag and wasn't sick at all. I just thought I'd share that because it was the last meal he ate prior to getting sick.

So, the food and ambience and service is sublime. Let's start there, but we are approaching this from a food-sensitivity perspective that makes every meal out a potential minefield. I want to say that Hearthside really did put in a solid effort to accommodate my allergies and my partner's Celiac, but at the end of the night, my partner was sick as hell and showed clear signs of gluten exposure. We believe that it was the "Special", the fried potato small plate, since he started feeling sick after eating that but before dessert. They were kind enough to comp out dessert, but our server was slightly dismissive at the end of the night - I get it, it was late, she tried, they may have thought we were free-food seeking - but I want the chef/management to be aware that this exposure occurred for the future. This was our special night out; we usually cannot afford such fine food. But, are all safety precautions truly being taken? It could have been as simple as grabbing the potatoes from the wrong fryer.

Meh. The woman working at the counter and bringing out pizzas while we were there was pleasant, courteous, checked in on us at the table once the food was out, and brought boxes so we could leave with our leftover slices. She made the rounds to the other diners during lunch as people filtered in and out, too. Welcoming. Props on staff hiring decisions there. There are so many options for pizza and fast-casual in Tucson that this one feels superfluous. The pizza was crust-heavy for handtossed style. The combinations are run of the mill: pesto, with some pinon nuts, neopolitan, white pizza, a veggie combination... You have different diameter choices, the smallest at 10'', and you can build your own if you don't fancy the menu options, but the price starts at eight dollars for a 10'' and each topping is a dollar. I was underwhelmed. If I'm going to be doing the standard pizza thing, I would prefer one of the big delivery chains; you'll spend a lot less money on pie, it'll come to your door, and you haven't missed any unique or intriguing features from Fresco. Plus, the price to substitute gluten free crust is a pretty hefty upcharge for a 12'' pizza. No trash cans out for guests. It's not something that bothers you until you go looking for one to dispose of your drink cup. There's a big concrete one outside. Not that this is related to much, but there's a picture of a sailor (I think) in the women's bathroom that's hung on the wall/looking at the camera in such a way that you've got a spectator for your visit to the restroom. It's an individual bathroom, too. Very... personal.

Food was so bad, my friends and I work at the gem show and was in desperate need of food. Our boss told us they have a decent variety so we decided to check it out. Instead, we were stuck paying $17 each for endless about of chewy zucchini, and nasty ass food. All I can say is that my friend had diarrhea , exploded all over the bathroom, my other friend felt nauseas. And I threw up all over the quality inn restroom, anyways Love this place

Y' know that feeling you get when you are supposed to meet friends at a bar. There are so many people in the room and you scan the crowd for a familiar face, careful not to make direct eye contact with anyone. You dont want to seem like a lost puppy, so you walk with purpose but the bigger the place, the bigger you are screwed. Im now calling this " Chickie and Pete's Syndrome" or CPS. I came here to meet friends , there was no major sporting event but it was pretty packed. i cant imagine what its like for a playoff game from any philly sport. Months earlier, I had made an aborted attempt to come before a regular season Flyers game and couldnt find parking. I like me some sports, I like me some wings, and I like me some fries, so this place is a winner in that respect. i may be allergic to the fries though as I enjoy eating them but they make me blotchy and ill afterwards. I eventually did find my friends. But not before walking the wrong way to a dead end,and being jostled by patrons. I advise you all to stick to pitchers as opposed to the "cool" beer towers. Think about it. Can they really clean those things out effectively on a regular basis? Things that make ya go HMMMMMM.

We had an amazing dinner last Friday, in part and thanks to our amazing server in the bar, Brittney. Can't say we expected much despite the 20minute wait and thought it would be like every other "chain" but it was anything but. I have a severe Paprika allergy and eating out can be scary. Their staff was attentive to this, discussed cross contamination and foods that were off limits. I had the bison burger which was good, but a little dry. Their mashed potatoes was AMAZING. My husband had their sirloin and it was cooked to perfection with the most amazing flavors. We then had their trio dessert which was even more amazing! brownie, cookie and cheesecake. To die for! My husband enjoyed his beer, northern (I think) so much so that we bought a growler, which was a phenomenal deal and you can't beat the refill price. We can't wait to go back and we'll ask to be seated in Brittneys section each time. Don't forget to get their rewards card too!!!! Amazing way to have savings at every visit!

This establishment is tucked away and right away the building felt forced into the space. It was small and awkward. There was extra space across street for parking but I didn't notice it until I left. We entered through two large doors and we're greeted by the hostess. She was polite and quick to get us a table. The restaurant was small with about 13 booths and tables. The lounge was overcrowded with high tables and chairs. The washrooms are located through the lounge and even with no one in the lounge it was difficult to move through the space. I would not recommend this place to anyone that needs accessibility. The atmosphere was warm and dark. The seating was all dark brown leather and tables were a beautiful dark brown wood. The server was excellent, he was easy to work with and had no problem making substitutions for me. The menu looked amazing, so many creative and decadent dishes. It was extremely difficult for me to find a decent filling vegan option. But they do cater to vegetarian and gluten free. Prior to visiting I looked up nutrition information and all items as they are on the menu are extremely calorie and fat dense. Even the salads. I had the Forager Burger with no cheese or mayo and subbed the brioche buns for the sour dough bread and a side of fries. It was delicious. The other dishes were chicken tacos, clam chowder and dynamite roll. Everyone ate without comment so I assume it was good. It did look amazing. They had a decent selection of wine. The washrooms were elegant with complete closed stalls with granite tile and wooden doors. The sink was automatic and had a nice trough granite sink. Overall the staff were the best part. They were pleasant and helpful. The food from a vegan and health perspective was very disappointing. But from my company's point of view was adequate. The space is awkward and tight. I would not go again unless it was a group choice.

Food is ok but there are other better meat and threes. Eaten there several times- fried chicken and chicken tenders are the best. Pork chops are good but tastes like mainly seasoned with Lowery's salt. Best side is corn. Mac and cheese below average. Vegetables taste like out of a can. One thing that bothered me was the smell. The back room smells like mildew! I actually started having an allergic reaction the last time there!

I ordered a chicken spinach floritine for delivery and was so hungry and hadn't are all day because I was in class. It came around 930pm and I take a bite and there was a walnut.. I am allergic to walnuts and realized they gave me the chicken and Carmelized walnuts instead. I called then immediately and a guy answered saying they were closed. I explained to him what happened and all he could do was give me credit for the pizza. They are lucky I'm not deathly allergic to walnuts. The manager Sean called me the next morning and explained what he was going to do for me. He was so sincere and because of him I am changing my one star to three. We need more people like him in the restaurant industry!

Waited 50 minutes for spaghetti and meatballs and a gluten free pizza. 40 minutes in we had to ask for the salad that came with the spaghetti. Spaghetti was served without meatballs. Pizza was cold. No one came back to check. We had to ask for the meatballs they arrived when the meal was nearly over. GF pizza was awful. Spaghetti heavily spiced. If you are looking for a good meal, keep looking.

Ordered 6 cookies, cause I have low blood sugar, was told they would be delivered by 11:20 pm by grub hub and I have not received my cookies and the grub hub app tells me to call you directly, but your number goes directly to voicemail. This is bad business and very hurtful for someone in desperate need of cookies. Also, I am lactose, but I ordered 2 milks to wash down what I thought would be amazing cookies, but to my surprise, no cookies, no milks, my my credit card was charged. If I could click no stars for this misery you have caused me, I would. Also, let me tell you a little about myself. I am overweight. It is hard for me to talk about, so I eat my feelings, but it appears that tonight grub and Tucson cookie company don't care about, my weight, my blood sugar, or my feelings. It is hard enough having people call me names like fatty, or saddle bags, but to not be able to have a moment of happiness holding a cookie hurts. I hope that no one at grub hub or Tucson cookie company ever has to experience the pain or hurt I am going through Also, where is my $18.95 I paid via PayPal to grub hub for cookies that I never got?

Came to Bernie's on a random Sunday for some dinner. The food was great but I was not impressed with the service. We showed up an hour before closing time for a quick bite and I could definitely sense some irritation, like they all just wanted to go home. It was a pretty slow night too. I have a gluten allergy and when I asked what was gluten free on the menu the server responded by saying "water". Hmm.... rude. We ordered some apps, I got a salad and Brussels sprouts. All of which were very tasty. The staff kept coming up to us asking if we were done, it was clear they were in a hurry and even reminded us that the kitchen closes in a half hour. I work in the restaurant industry and a half hour is a lot of time to enjoy a quick bite without feeling that much pressure. Overall, the food was good but I don't know if I'll go back.

For years, I've always liked the taste of the food. The hummus is decent, the meat is good, and the rice and broth are really good. However, it has given me awful food poisoning more than once. Both times, their lettuce was wilted and old, and left me sick for days. I will no longer take the chance.

Oh man. I really hate writing these kind of reviews - especially for smaller businesses trying to make it in this world - but I also believe if you are going to make it, you have to do what you do and do it well. We called at 7:45 and asked if we made it by 8:30, could they serve us. They said yes, they do not close until 9. We arrived at 8:20 and they refused to seat us. Said they were closing. The place had one other table and I am guessing they just wanted to leave - but we made a special trip after working all day and were starving. They finally relented and sat us. We tried to be really nice and be good customers and order quickly, etc. They continued to be unfriendly. The food was mediocre and being a vegetarian, I ordered the chile paneer dish - which I will admit was good, but I ended up really sick later on that night. I really do have this feeling that it was cross contaminated with the lamb and chicken dishes my friends ordered - which I know can happen, but it would be great if kitchens, especially ethnic ones that tout vegetarian dishes, would be more aware of this issue. The Naan basket, which is my favorite part of eating Indian, was soggy and not very flavorful. All and all, we didn't have a good time and will not be going back when we are in town for work next.

worst food ive had in awhile i ordered the cheese platter and they literally put sandwich meat/cheese on the platter, the strawberries were mushy and gross it was disgusting to be honest the best thing i had was the grapes. I tried everyones food it was horrible i had this app with brie and i almost vomited when i tried it, if i could give this place 0 stars i would, never coming here again.

Today I was at this location for the first time in years. And I completely remember why this location is the worst in Edmonton possibly all of Alberta. I ordered a mozza burger lettuce wrapped as I am Celiac. I am sure that a buddy burger party was used also just because it's a lettuce wrap you wrap it not just take a bunch of lettuce and shove a little burgar in. Your head office should be evaluating this location. I'm sure training and standards are not up to pare. The only thing good about this burgar was the tomato. If I could give 1/2 a star I would

I really wanted to give this place a good review. It was busy and noisy and so that did not help. My angel har pasta with meat balls was hot ewhen it came to the table but the meatballs were a problem. One of them was just over cooked the other was a rock from the pavement outside. The pretzell appetizer was warm and soft but the cheese sauce was too thick and would have been nice to have small plates. Our waitress was nice and helpful but she was so busy it was hard tos get her attention. Just a few words of advice. Your servers and bussers are using the same small door and have to go down 3 stairs. You are asking for contaminating dishes and it is clearly a hazzard. The bar needs to speed up their work. It is holding up the wait staff. I am in lebanon once a year and am glad this is a restaurant instead of just a bar. I will be back next year and will try this restaurant next time.

I have to preface this review by saying the first time my bf and I went to Red Pony, we were both blown away. The service was amazing, we got complimentary dishes from the chef, and the food was prepared extremely well. We were extremely excited to return to Red Pony again, so what happened next was very disappointing. Service was OK. Our waiter seemed more interested in talking to the chefs in the kitchen than taking our order. The food was merely OK. I got the ahi tuna which tasted like it was smeared with A1 sauce. OK, I could have made this myself at home. My boyfriend got the grouper which was heavy on the tomato/salsa. Later that night, he started vomiting and he thinks it was because the fish wasn't thoroughly cooked. Our experience was further tarnished by a couple sitting next to us who had many complaints about their food. The lady's steak was too cold, then when it came back, burnt. I believe one of the managers came out to talk to them and ended up compensating her meal, which was very nice. However, our waiter seemed to be in a bad mood after this incident. I was already thinking silently to myself that I was never going to come back to this restaurant. What made up my mind NOT to come back was this: When our waiter came and asked us whether we wanted dessert, he had a palate cleanser (apples and caramel) in his hand, which I think is delicious. When we explained politely that we did not want dessert, he said OK then and left the check, but get this: HE TOOK THE PALATE CLEANSER AWAY AS WELL! My bf and I were both shocked by the bad manners. Yeah, there's not much to say after this, except that our awful dinner turned into a truly awful night b/c my bf was up vomiting for most of it. Bottomline is, I thought there was something special about Red Pony that made it immune to bad food or bad service. Turns out there isn't.

The tacos are very good. I especially enjoyed the grilled mahi mahi. I like the limited menu, and the price point is fair. The carne quesadilla was tasty, but it was all cheese on one side and beef on the other. It would have been better if it was more evenly dispersed and much less greasy. The guacamole needs some tomato. I was very uneasy about the containers the sauces were in at the tables. It seems unsanitary and likely to suffer cross contamination for people who suffer allergies and all kinds of possible germs. The ceramic containers also had chips on the top edge... Hope the broken bits didn't land in the sauce. They should be in squeeze bottles. Period. Also, there should be napkin dispensers next to each caddy, as the majority of these dishes are eaten with your hands. Garces has a bad habit of choosing form over function...

Service is a little slow during dinner because it gets so packed. Overall fair prices and they were able to accommodate and serve me a gluten-free plate. Make sure you double plates listed under the vegetarian menu really don't have any meet though because my friend found meat in her "vegetarian" dish

I would say that each visit here is a bit worse than the last...the shame is their vegan gluten free crust is the best! For that I give them 1 star. The problem here is that when it gets busy their team tend to get super overwhelmed and I sit and watch them snap at customer after customer. My last visit consisted of one customer ranting to me the entire time I waited for just that reason. I waited in the store 40 minutes past the time I was supposed to pick up my online order and was yelled at (he unfortunately was not wearing a name tag) when I asked if they had started my order. Finally after watching them serve five people who walked in after me I asked for a refund and was told by the manager to give her five more minutes...so I waited ten...at that point I had to insist that I get my refund. It's not often I find myself in situations so frustrating and it is unfortunate that I will have to find another spot for awesome gluten free pizza as I won't be back again.
This place gave me food poisoning. Had me throwing up all afternoon, with stomach cramps. Never get the Royale with Cheese. You're better off getting a quarter pounder at McDonald's.

NOT WORTH THE RUDE SERVICE. SHE PUT TABASCO IN OUR KETCHUP!!! Our waitress was literally so rude I was shocked and all I literally could do is laugh. So her service to start with was below average she was not friendly she didn't say please thank you or your welcome. She seemed very much bothered with the fact that she had to do her job and take our order. To top it off when we asked for extra ketchup because the meal only came with one little thing of it you could taste that she put Tabasco sauce in the ketchup!! First of all this lady Cionne Is what the receipt says her name was didn't even know if we had allergies or sensitivities to Tabasco sauce and when my husband asked her what it was she smugly giggled and said it's good right he said no it's spicy what is it she said again while smiling it's ketchup it's good right knowing what she did. She made up some name for the ketchup. We don't tip her. Food was ok. But she made the experience so bad that we don't even finish our food.

I care about what I eat. I buy fresh foods, rarely items packaged in plastic. I don't use plastic to store my food, even if the container says"BPA free"--it just means it the manufacturer likely used some other hormone-mimicking compound. I mention my concern for what I eat because EVERYTHING here has GLITTER in it. If your food is good, it shouldn't need bedazzling. And this isn't about price-I've paid 20€ for slice of cake and coffee in Vienna, I'm perfectly happy paying the money for food that is worth it. I asked what their glitter was once, and you'd think I'd asked for some trade secret. Someone said they were "natural", another said "I think they are made from fish scales. If that's the case, where is your allergen disclaimer for "contains fish"? Being the skeptic I am, I took some of the glitter buttercream put it in a coffee filter and poured boiling water over it. It was still there in the filter. I rubbed it between my fingers. Still there. If you buy edible glitter from a well known cake baking supply company at a craft store, or luster, it dissolves. At best, Cake Bake is probably taking the word of some product manufacturers who says the glitter they buy is edible. At best, Cake Bake is naive to what common sense would say. People make claims about products (like "flushable" wipes that are clogging our sewers) all the time that are too good to be true. At the worst, these glitter products with who knows what chemical or colorants, represent a health risk to customers, many of which are little children, who parents want up treat to the beauty and whimsy. Are these colon cancer cases in 30 years? Just for a sparkly piece of cake. Let's grow up and get the glitter out of your product Gwendolyn. For now, I'll be around the corner at a better bakery that doesn't need glitter or glam to sell their products.

Was there last night ask for no tomato on my sandwich. Sandwich came out with tomatoes. Ask for sandwich to be taken back . It was they pulled tomato's off the sandwich and gave it back to me . Not thinking ate a piece realized there was tomatoes still on it . Ended up in the hospital. I have a food allergy to raw tomatoes!

Found this place while looking for a new pizza place to check out. The pizza menu offers toppings that are different from most pizza places, with a lot of pesto sauce options, which I prefer. They offer gluten free and cauliflower crust options which is great (despite being a little pricey). And there's a "secret menu" which isn't really secret because they publish it on their website. We ordered a medium of The Tour and The Eclipse Combination and 6 buffalo wings. Total was $55. Overall everything was good. Not spectacular, but good. And a little pricey. There were zero complaints on the quality, flavor, ingredients, or blend of flavors. The Tour could have used more sun-dried tomatoes; I think I got one bite in each slice of pizza. The location is pretty convenient to the 'burbs. The restaurant itself is pretty small inside, but there is a lot of patio seating for the warmer months. During the week we could've easily eaten at the restaurant, but the ambiance was sort of lacking (no music, no energy, no people), so I'm glad we ordered to go.

Meh. The folks at the register aren't the most friendly. Food was good but if I ask/pay for cheese, I expect that. I was clear on no tomatoes and guess what? Tomatoes. Thankfully I am not allergic. They also forgot a part of my order. It's like they weren't paying attention. My daughter was pleased with her order.

Siam Elephant was pretty good. Went here on a whim with my dad and ordered the asparagus and mushroom stir-fry and he ordered some basil scallops. Nothing was too stand-out but the service. It's a fairly average Thai place compared to what I've had before, but if I lived in Carp I'd eat here again. I may have got food poisoning from my dinner, but I'm not going to hold it against them -- can't confirm it was due to this and it happens.

Allergy folks beware! I used to shop at Essene often due to my gluten allergy. While shopping this past weekend I was offered a free sample of a gluten free cookie, from a table advertising a variety of gluten free cookies. I took and ate one, after which I went to ask the sales person where I could buy some. It turns out that the cookie was NOT gluten free and was confined to my house for the rest of the day due to my allergic reaction. I would have been mollified if I had received any sort of appropriate response/apology from the company. I alerted the manager who just acknowledged my complaint and walked away, and received NO response from alerting the company online via their online contact form. I was appalled at the ineptitude of the staff to handle this issue and strongly caution anyone with an allergy against shopping there. In my personal experience my allergy was not taken seriously and my complaints were ignored.

Where else can you get unlimited sushi & Hibachi at a legit asian restaurant that is not a typical rundown buffet that might kill you due to grease and food poisoning?????? Nit Koizi!!! Oh and yeah.... of you're a Floridian/tampa bay resident...... DEF APPRECIATE!!!!! The fact we are the lucky ones to have this type of establishment in the Bay Area bc theres no other place or restaurant that offers this type of service and the selections of food across the state of country! Here's what i mean.... if you ever decided to go for a endless meal aka buffet style but not having to standup and pick your food then this is the place to GO. Yes, your traditional would be the cheap/nasty taste of rundown china buffet table with the same exact crap you would fine at a buffet style restaurant. Not with Koizi!! Not only do you have the luxury to order off the menu for your food but they cook it from the back and bring it to you. Now, the tradeoff is.. if you don't finish your order... they will charge you unless if its not a protein item. Oh btw, if you want to get fancy and step up the quality of their food... you can get a teppanyaki/hibachi grill table too! And no reservations needed unless you're celebrating with a large group. Comprendai?!?! Your typical hibachi grill has a set menu to pay and its pretty expensive plus no option to get certain food endless(Sushi/meal.. well with Koizi.. the same exact menu where you can get endless food (sushi & meat) endlessly!!! Yrs and they freakin grill it with your rice/veggie... which btw everything taste better on the hibachi grill. Not its a onetime grill from the hibachi grill.. but thats all you need for your meat. And yess.. even the traditional apps and entree of chinese foods are unlimited. Not from a buffet table you typically walk to get from. So yeah, tampa, clearwater, NPR... appreciate and love the ideal of having this unique kind of restaurant where you can get better quality food that is endless and able to get hibachi table grill too with the endless meal menu. Don't hate! Just own it fool!!!! Cuz no hibachi restaurant will offer or come close to what koizi offer...unless you like the cheap/trashy style buffet. Oh yeah, sushi is great! But the steak & shrimp on the tableside grill...... wowwww weeee Yummy!! Its the best taste wuality shrimp you'll ever find for a low cost endless meal. Under $20 dinner price baaaaay baaaay!!

STAY AWAY... I'm only giving this Taco Bell a one start because I can't give a negative star. We went at 10:30pm lobby close drive through only. Order was wrong. We ordered 3 #10 and 1 #11. I'm still trying to figure out what we got. The food was cold like it was cooked hours ago. If you had lettuce it was wilted. The taco shells were suppose to be hard shell but they was busted up and so soft like the food was prepared hours ago. Definitely was not freshly cooked. Absolutely the worse Taco Bell I have ever been to. Absolutely Disgusting and disgraceful to serve food like that to the general public. I hope my family don't end up with food poisoning.

I've been here before and it's been fine. Tonight I noticed the girl making salads was using her hands to pick up ingredients rather than using the tongs. This causes cross contamination that can make me very ill. I don't think I'll be back. A few months later ... ordered a Bentley salad tonight. It was delicious ... until I was about 3/4 done with my big salad and I found a big piece of pasta. Thankfully, I caught it and it being in and mixed around with my salad didn't seem to hurt me ... but I won't take the chance again. Cross contamination is a huge deal for people with Celiac and I was nonchalant.

We were so looking forward to our dinner at Muriel's and initially, we were impressed. My daughter had the Bayoubaisse, my son the turtle soup and the entrees included the Shrimp & Grits, Double-cut pork chop. All were well cooked and tasted great....then came the food poisoning. My daughter shared some of her Bayoubaisse with my son and both ended up with food poisoning. Now, to be clear, my son is 18 and did not drink any alcohol, my daughter is 25 and had one glass of wine. The only food they had in common the entire day was the Bayoubaisse soup. When Muriel's was called, we were told it couldn't possibly be their food. I don't mind paying $200 for an excellent meal, but I do mind my kids getting sick.

Good food but overpriced. Owner was very hospitable but short staffed. They offered a 15% discount due to the delayed service and wrong orders. (One order came out with seafood, which the person who ordered it is deathly allergic to seafood.) The food was good so we'll likely visit again but with the lower expectations in regards to service. Sorry no pictures available. We were so hungry that when the food came out we immediately scarfed it down.

Absolute waste of time. Poorly managed. Was doing our normal bounce around & eat apps at restaurants we haven't been to in a while & stepped in for a drink at midnight. . We wanted to sit in one of the 6 vacant hi-top booths in the bar area. The young hostess told us it was only available if we had dinner only. Im sorry, but dinner at midnight!!!? GFY. Between 2 Our tab would have been 6-7 drinks, 3 apps & prob a dessert. In lieu of seating us, she tells me i need to order two burgers or i couldn't be seated. Ehhhh?? Absolute Stupid on the rocks. So instead of adding $150 to their ring & a $30 tip for the server, we threw up deuces & will never go back. Resurrection Ale House came threw like they alway do. Don't waste your time here. So many better run spots who are willing to accommodate folks willing to part with their coin.

We chose this place because someone in our group needs gluten free options and the menu had some. We had 6:30pm reservations. We arrived first and were greeted by a server who told us someone would be with us shortly. The hostess (we later found out she is the owner) very brusquely told us we couldn't be seated until our whole party was there and that they'd only hold our table for 15 minutes. She told us we'd have to wait in the bar. This really did not start the evening well for me because her tone was very negative. As the others arrived, they were told by that woman that each table is scheduled for 1 hour 45 minutes before it turns over. I really found this to be rude and not a positive way to greet paying customers. Our party of 6 was seated at a back round table that was part booth. Ann took care of us. We had cheesesteak egg rolls as an appetizer that were good and not greasy. The other dishes were chicken pot pie (which was huge and I saw many others being delivered to other tables during the evening), tuna steak, ravioli, grilled octopus, and prosciutto burratta flatbread. Everyone agreed their meals were good. Ann brought a dessert tray to show us and we picked warm toll house cake, carrot cake and Oreo mousse cake. Those were all good, too. It did seem to take a really long time to get our entrees especially when we were told in the beginning the time frame for flipping the table. It was 7:50pm when we received our dinners. As we were waiting for dessert, the hostess/owner stopped by to let us know that she didn't need to flip our table and we could stay longer- again this really seemed inappropriate. They do not have Coke products. The parking is not great. I won't be rushing back anytime soon.

Pizza was absolutely disgusting, almost inedible. Pizza was cold because the guy didn't even bother to heat it up! I was lured in by the smell but they didn't even have oregano or garlic powder!! I feel the world has gone to shit just a little bit more after tasting this vomit. Shoulda known better but fml for people fcking up pizza on such a bad level

I came here for breakfast with my extended family for brunch one weekend. They have an expansive menu with many, many breakfast selections and a few (I mean few lunch options). If your in the mood for breakfast and love pancakes and waffles this is the place for you! Pancakes is in the name so that's what your gonna get! I ordered scrambled eggs, and turkey sausage. And guess what it came with a side of pancakes. I opted for the gluten free pancakes and they were great! This place is super busy and the food is similar to a diner. Quick, hot, and good!

For those who, like my mom, follow a gluten free diet, this place is really a ray of sunshine (a "New Day," if you will). It's so empowering for them to be able to order ANYTHING off the menu, no questions asked, no worries about cross-contamination (New Day is strict, you can't bring outside food in). It has favorite American comfort food classics like turkey club sandwiches, meatball subs, pizza, and lasagna. You can also order breakfast all day! New Day even sells gooey butter cake cookies, which are the #1 thing I will miss when I move away from St. Louis (in case you're wondering, it's as good as the original!). I enjoyed how crispy the pizza was, and how I could customize it with different toppings. The baked goods assortment is vast and includes everything from cake pops and apple tarts to cinnamon rolls. New Day also sells regrigerated to-go items such as prepared pizzas (with or without toppings) and preformed French baguette and cheesy garlic bread. It's a relaxed, coffee shop style vibe inside with big bright windows and great service. Give them a try, especially if a loved one is gluten free!

The servers are just terrible at what they do... You are seen by them in which they don't ask if you've been helped or not yet. Having to ask for your order to be taken after 20-30 minutes of sitting down is ridiculous! The next morning my family & I had an upset stomach with diarrhea in which it was food poisoning smh. Never are we coming back especially with the service given & food quality.

Terrible service. Waited 20 minutes to be greeted by a server and another 20 for drinks. There were 4 tables there. We ordered a charcuterie board and I requested no peanuts or nuts be on the board since I have an allergy. The server asked me how bad it was? And asked if I carried an epi pen? How is that your business? just don't put the nuts on there ridiculous. will not be back.

I truly don't understand the high ratings of this place. For my entree, I had the sea bass/sablefish duo. The sablefish was encrusted with cilantro and/or lemon grass, which was a strange pairing with parmesan orzo/risotto. It was edible, but weird. Parmesan and cilantro just does not go. The sea bass though, had a funky smell, and after taking a few bites, my entire mouth was fishy all throughout dinner. It was old fish, but the question is, how old? My breath could not get rid of the fishiness until I drove to a convenience store to buy gum afterwards. The appetizer, a shrimp/crab/lobster combo was served chopped up, smothered in a vinegar yellow sauce and served in a glass which really made and tasted like vomit. It made me wonder if the kitchen tasting what they're serving out? The "palette cleanser" was an uninspiring lump of old mascrapone with cut fruit. The sweetness and old dairy left a weird film in my mouth. It was really a palette buster. The restaurant felt gimmicky. It tried to be high end, and that's what we thought we were paying for. All these "fine dining" buzzwords, but the most important thing that fine dining should be, which is delicious food, this restaurant did not have.

I had been to Surrey's a few times when we lived in New Orleans. It was OK. We were back for vacation a couple of weeks ago and I decided to meet a friend there who I haven't seen in 3 years. We were both disappointed, especially with the service. We did go on a Sunday morning so it was a busy time. Within the first 5 minutes of sitting down, our server came over 4 times to ask if we were ready to order. I was a waitress for years. If you know people are catching up and haven't looked at the menu, LEAVE THEM ALONE. (At least for a few minutes!). She was a bit rude when we politely said we would like to start with coffee and take a minute to look at the menu. My friend and I are extremely health conscious. I have Celiac Disease so need a gluten free meal. They do not have much to choose from in the way of gluten free. (Not compared to other places that I ate at on the same trip). Our meals were mediocre, nothing great, which would have made up for the terrible service. If you want to indulge in their banana french toast and don't mind less than par service, you will be fine here. If you are looking for healthier , friendlier service, with more variety , try somewhere else.

Worst experience ever! Sat at the bar and ordered the Korean skewers which were to come with Kimchi. Ultimately I received a sub par skewer of poorly seasoned, under cooked beef on a bed of of cabbage. I asked to speak to the kitchen manager. Ultimately they sent Paul to review my complaint. Paul is without a clue as to how to deal with a customer complaint. I said "Gawd damn, Paul, this is not even close to Kimchi.". That's all it took for Paul to call security as he shouted, "you can't cuss at me like that". Security quietly shuffled me to the side where they asked me a few questions and ultimately said I needed to go, to "keep the peace". I asked them to call the police if there was an issue . No call made. Pretty sure I ultimately got some food poisoning from the experience. By far the worst part of my week spent in the area.

Never got food poisoning in my life. Never have I been so sick in my life immediately after eating here! Put me out for the whole weekend. Have been here before and didn't have an issue but want to give the heads up. It was a pretty terrible experience. My friend had it as well and it was her birthday! The food tasted good. Especially the fried cheesecake.

Food is absolutely disgusting!!! Sushi is far from fresh and all their pasta and rice dishes have literally no dam flavor!!!!Bathrooms were atrocious with all types of stuff including vomit on the floor like are you people serious??! I'm so upset that I wasted my time and money!!!
Got food poisoning from this place yesterday. Anybody else?

So, tried this new place last week. I love a good sandwich so I was excited to check them out. Location is the old Quiznos spot in the Tarhet shopping center on South Virginia. Sadly, I was not impressed. I am so hoping it is just bugs that need to be worked out since they are fairly new but, it's my understanding that they've been open for awhile now. I ordered on line. The process was smooth but I was a little dismayed that although their website lists their special sauces, there is no description of what is in the sauces. Because I have no food allergy worries, I went with their Bomb Sauce. I chose The Dream Team sandwich. Their signature sandwiches all come with lettuce, tomato, pickle, blah, blah...and peppers. I assumed pepperincinis. Nope, bell peppers. So, if you don't like bell pepper on a sandwich, beware. Again, no clear description. Also, my sandwich was supposed to have cheddar cheese. It was american cheese. Maybe just an error but, over all, I did not enjoy my sandwich. When I picked up my order, I still did not see anything describing their sauces or type of veggies but, the staff is very nice. Seem friendly and excited to promote the place so I was willing to look the other way. I was also a bit disappointed that the website let me order Doritos but they don't carry them. I think it's just a little inconsistent due to those bugs that need to be worked out so not the biggest deal but I hope they get it together soon. I also wish they had a pick up area for online or called in orders. I had to wait in line behind people just ordering before I got my sandwich. Then...pricing. $16 for a so so sandwich, chips I didn't really want and a drink. I likely won't give them another try but, I wish them well. Update: I truly meant to give 3 stars, not two. Updated that! I didn't realize until I saw the reply. My intention is not to hurt a new business. I just was not a fan, not worth the price in my book. I think they can make some adjustments and it will be a great place. Just not my cup of tea. I encourage all Yelpers to give them a try and decide for yourself. Thank you to the management for the kind offer to retry on their dime. I will likely pass. Not out of any ill feelings. Simply because nothing was so wrong that it should cost the owner. I love trying new places but I'm always going to give my honest opinion. Best to you as your sandwich shop grows.

A very nice outing after our time at home with the shelter in place order. It was great to go to a restaurant and see people! That being said there were a couple things they need to address. Rubber gloves should not be worn by wait staff and hosts. This is a serious concern with cross contamination and not reassuring. As for the food it was a mix. My husbands ribeye was amazing. Cooked perfectly and so was his broccoli. My sirloin on the other hand ordered medium was firm and dry. A bit of a disappointment. Our check with two dinners and two glasses of wine was $94 before tip. Our waitress was great and very attentive so overall a 4 stars but room for improvement.

This is without a doubt one of the worst restaurant experiences I've ever had the mispleasure of having. The food is actually fairly decent, but the terrible service and awful way they treat their customers certainly dampens the experience. I had to remind my server multiple times to bring me my drink, 30+ minutes into being seated. There were two other tables in the whole restaurant, and she cited the reason as being "busy", when the server was sitting on her phone the entire duration of our visit. I had to reorder my ramen 3 times before they actually followed my instructions as per my dietary instructions. I'm deathly allergic to vegetables they add as a topping in their ramen, and made it very clear when I ordered that I couldn't consume any of the veggies or meat. They brought out my ramen twice with the veggies and meat, and when I explained for the third time *why* I couldn't have them in, they asked if I could just pick them out of the ramen with my hands. My server even grabbed the spoon from my hands and started picking out the veggies for me, trying to explain how easy it was. After remaking my ramen for a third time, finally without the veggies, they added in meat. I finally decided that they clearly weren't going to listen to me, and paid for the entire meal I didn't eat, and left the restaurant crying. TLDR, ramen was great, restaurant staff is incompetent.

I'm really digging the "Chipotle"-style eateries where you have a base and then put whatever you want with it. Now we have it pizza style! I'm not crazy about Chipotle actually - I enjoy finding more unique eats with quality ingredients that isn't really a chain. But Snap seemed to get Yelpers riled up and I wanted to see what it was all about It's tough, walking in and being presented with so many options. They have a few preset options for you to choose if you don't want to go full-on custom pizza. Presets are $7.49 while custom pizzas with unlimited toppings are $7.99 (gluten free crust is an extra $2 and they're good about making sure your pizza isn't contaminated if you're super sensitive or allergic). There's various proteins, fresh greens, cheeses, sauces... anything you really want you can get on a pizza! The crust is not something you can really change the thickness of but they have a nice, thin but perfect crust (not too dry, a bit chewy) and I can say the same about the gluten free crust. Some things they'll put in the oven but if you went for a Farmer's Market, they add fresh arugula and ricotta on top after going through the oven to keep it nice and fresh. I went for lunch on a Saturday and thought that I could finish a whole pizza but still had about 1/3 left because it was nice and filling. At least I had breakfast for the next morning ready to go. Will definitely come back and hopefully have a better plan for my next pizza.

I got food poisoning after eating here on the evening of Thursday February 2nd. I had the quarter dark chicken and spicy beans and salad. 3 hours later I became violently ill. I believe there could be a sanitation problem as I was very sick. Stay away.

I don't understand. Their service is fine, but the food comes out poorly. I usually come to Courtney's for breakfast, but my scrambled eggs come out yolky and not even good at all. The bathrooms aren't clean, because everything inside was old and not remodeled at all. Their food choices have so much bread that I'm gluten sensitive. I just wish that this place had some gluten free options available. The staff was doing a so so job. I just wish that they would hire new chefs in the kitchen that would know how to make their food nice and good like Gondola House. Please make this place better. That way I can come back sometimes.

I wanted to wait 24-48 hours before I posted this due to potential for food poison. I'm good so, here is my review. Ended up here because I didn't want to spend $17.00 for 1 roll of 5 pieces of Sushi. So I honestly didn't have super high expectations. First thing I notice upon entrance, how bright it was with yellow walls. Just couldn't get too comfortable in there...perhaps this was done by design. It's all you can eat Sushi and Hibachi, and it's pretty good. Not as bad as I expected. I got chicken and steak w/ veggies Hibachi, and a few of pieces of Sushi, everything was pretty good. Whatever you do, stay away from the 2-1 roll. My girl ordered it and I legit felt bad for her because she felt pressured to finish it (they charge .60 - .85 cent for each piece not eaten). I tried one and I instantly thought it was horrible. Bottom line if you're hungry, this place will satisfy.

Tried this with my two friends while I was in town... the veggie stir fry was okay tasting however, all three of us got sick from eating here. Not sure if it's the oil they use or the ingredients but the three of us got food poisoning. Staff was friendly but they were not very knowledgeable regarding the difference between vegan and vegetarian. Wouldn't go back though.

Our pizza was rank! When we got it in our house, it stunk up the place, not exaggerating, like sewage. After touching it, our hands smelled really bad, and it didn't come off after washing with soap. I called and talked to the manager. He said he'd look for the problem and send us another. I waited a bit and called back because I wanted to find out what the problem was. He said that everything was fine. That made me worry that the food was purposely contaminated by a disgruntled worker. So, he remade the pizza with the exact same ingredients and sent it over. I made sure to smell it and it was the same so I sent them both back. You should not have to do that with food! The thing that really pushed me to leave a review was that I was told that I'd be refunded. Then when I listened to my voice mail there was one from Reginelli's saying that our "refund" was a store credit. So I paid $30+ for poopy pizza that we neither ate nor kept. I definitely will not be using that credit.

Not happy. They added mayo to my pizza and it's not on the menu! I hate mayo and worse yet I hate false advertising. If you're going to put something on a pizza, say so. The waitress was nice and she took the pizza off the bill and the beer was good which is why I give it 3 stars. If you have a food allergy or want to know what is in each meal make sure you ask and they know up front.

I have very mixed feelings about this place. These are the same owners of Zahav which I adored and maybe my expectations were just a tad high.. The atmosphere (and our waitress) was adorable but the food was ....just ok. There were five of us and we all got the sabor which is 3 courses for each person. Aside from the dessert, everything is gluten free so i MADE SURE we all ordered different dishes so we could taste a good portion of the menu. My family is hard to please but their major complaint was "it's a Mexican place and the food isn't spicy!" I thought the guac (made table side) was good but again people complained no taste. I asked everyone what they thought collectively were their faves. For the appetizer, the soup and the main dish, the salmon. Agreed both dishes were excellent. but you don't go to a Mexican spot for salmon amirite?

Pretty good for a quick healthy salad. Some offerings for gluten free customers, but stir fry's are all made one after another in same wok; GF sauce or not. Cross-contamination likely. Service was nice. Ambience okay - way too loud, especially since there are only 7 people in here! Music is nice, attempts to drown out kitchen sounds.

I would like to give a great review because the food is received was amazing however, I ordered online. I asked to replace shrimp with chicken due to a shellfish allergy. They did not. The meal was already paid for, tip included. I called to let them know of their mistake and the man on the phone acted stunned and stammered. Now I have a $30 charge for food I cannot eat.

Me and a friend ordered from Samurai this past weekend and within 3 hours were both extremely ill--two days later and i am just getting over food poisoning from this restaurant. DO NOT ORDER FROM THERE!!! this was my first time and i will NEVER go back

I am very disappointed with this establishment. I got on their website for two reasons today, one because I'm gluten free, and two because I'm under 21 and wanted to make sure I could attend a friend's birthday party later in this evening. There was no mention of age restrictions of any kind on the website, and I checked every page on the site just to be sure. When I arrived, they had a chalkboard stating that the restaurant was 21+ after 5 PM. Also, keep in mind this is a restaurant with a full dinner menu, so it would not be obvious that an age restriction would be in effect like it would for an establishment that is advertised strictly as a bar or pub. I was very disappointed that I was not allowed to attend my friend's party because this establishment could not be bothered to put this restriction anywhere on their website. I will not be visiting this restaurant in the future.

A couple of weeks ago, I surprised my wife with a Spa weekend getaway which was much needed and let's say the Spa did it's job. Just what we needed! Safety Harbor Resort and Spa is in the perfect location as this is one my favorite walking and friendly, active towns that you feel safe to be in. I love the diversity of businesses that caters to pretty much all walks of life. Pet friendly as can be yet clean. The first night we dined at their restaurant and it was Pasta night (any way you want it & all you can eat) and fairly priced at $15.99. At first, you may say who wants to try Pasta all you can eat but I figure why not and it did not disappoint (I'm Italian). The red sauce was crazy good and the plate portion is Extra, plus it came w/Salad bar which tasted fresh. Also we tried room service and their response time was quicker even compared to Disney standards as well as super friendly. We also enjoyed the outdoor pool bar grill which is a lot of fun, a great place to socialize. Yes, the food was also very good and plenty big. Enjoyed their burger and the grouper sandwiches have my recommendation. Now for the accommodations, this is a Wyndham trademark resort, I will say I was expecting a little more upscale for the price points. Initially reserved a King deluxe w/water view which was delivered and it was quite a spacious room w/ a mini refrigerator, mini-microwave on top. Spacious bathroom and tub. A nice size flat screen, BUT a bit aged and we felt the room had humidity issues. The linens was not fresh and the pillows need replacing, like badly replacing- like years ago overdue replacing (stained).. you get the picture. Needless to say, we did not sleep good that night. Also, in the tower, there seems to be more of a maintenance decline and a bit of a spider problem. To be fair, you can tell that the owner is trying very hard to renovate and clean it up but probably not fast enough. Hopefully he has an adept maintenance team to handle this enormous project instead of cutting corners, especially for this gem of a place. The next day we went to front desk as we were planning to leave early because the room was that bad - terrible if you have allergy or sinus issues. I must give them credit because the hotel manager did not question especially when we showed her the pictures and quickly moved us into their $1000 a night suite right by the Spa also offering a complimentary breakfast. They made sure to re-send housekeeping to the room ensuring that all was fresh. Ironically, as she's wiping the patio door handle, it fell off but the maintenance guy came out to fix it quickly. That night was a much better night and you can tell the difference with the air quality in the suite. The Spa amenities was worth the trip, albeit, there's some room for improvements yet pretty clean. Overall, it's still worth the trip and I will do it again. The spa services & merchandise are reasonably priced plus quality service. One last thing, they really outta market their brand of water, put them in the rooms and let me tell you, as funny as it sounds, it tastes great. Compared Spring water, you can tell the difference. I wish they sold it in the local stores. A Refreshingly crisp taste. I'm glad they have it available free around the resort hallways.

My boyfriend and I went through the drive thru today . He ordered me a cheeseburger with no tomato he said no tomato twice the girl repeated it back no tomato. We get home I'm just about to take a bite of my bury there's a tomato. This is bad as I am highly allergic to tomatoes. Please have your employees listen and checks ppls orders properly as an allergic reaction could result in a lawsuit.

Absolutely NOT the place to go if you have any sort of food allergies. Had some great friends (without me asking) who had told our server about my food allergies while I was in the restroom. I proceeded to order what I deemed acceptable to have taking my allergies into consideration. Proceeded to order the salmon (after waiting over an hour for our food) and was given a very small portion of salmon on a bed of what looked like completely flavorless, unexciting cauliflower rice. It had no seasonings and didn't come with any of the other "extras" that were in the description on the menu. When the server came back over she proceeded to tell me that she elected to make sure my order was "allergen free" even though I, personally, never said anything to her about my allergies. She proceeded to tell me I "needed to stop being rude to her" and "that she would send her manager over". Her manager came up to the table and said "so, what's the issue?" And I proceed to tell her. She said that they "take allergies VERY seriously (even though they don't have an allergen menu) and asked if I wanted something else, the manager said she would come back after I looked at the menu again. By the time I had looked at the menu again and decided what I wanted to eat, the manager had never come back (like she had said she would), the server came back and said "so what else did you want to order?" and I proceeded to tell her I didn't want anything as the other two people in my party were completely done eating. TERRIBLE experience here and would never recommend this restaurant to anyone who has food allergies or otherwise for that matter. No one deserves to be treated this way.

Awful experience!!! My daughter (2 /2 yrs old) has a severe nut allergy. Upon arrival, told waitress and she said "no problem". In my past experiences, most restaurants will not bring anything to the table that has nuts. Everyone ordered their food. I ordered an entree with multiple crawfish dishes, one of which was a crawfish caesar salad...now I am from south Louisiana, about an hour from NOLA, so I know that a caesar salad does not have nuts in it. We receive our food and I find that there are pecans in my caesar salad!!!! Notified the waitress and the manager....the waitress proceeded to tell me it was MY fault bc I had ordered that food...NO WHERE on the menu does it describe that particular dish as having nuts. They just did not care...their lack of concern infuriated me!!! They could possibly kill someone...I tried to follow up on the Monday after our experience with a GM...no one answers the phone and the number that is on the neworleansrestaurants.com site is not functioning. I will never go back and will be reporting this restaurant to the BBB!

A friend and I who are Vegan and Celiac respectively decided to try this place out because it accommodated both of our restrictions and was a few blocks from his apartment. I think I've now found a new favorite takeout place. The food was really good, particularly for takeout and you could taste that their claims of using fresh natural ingredients are true. The interior was very clean and well designed for such a small space with a food bar. The selection was well curated, which I appreciated because I am overwhelmed by food bars that are too big. I loved the prominent Gluten Free and Vegan labeling of all of the dishes. And, when we paid at the register I was shocked by how cheap everything was. I definitely have a new detour from the Whole Foods Salad Bar a few blocks away on South St. Note: As someone slightly neurotic about cleanliness, I thought that everything here felt super clean. Another reviewer noted that they thought they got food poisoning here because they were sick the night they had dinner here. Generally food poisoning (particularly from meat) takes at least 12 hours to develop (but we all tend to blame the last thing we ate) so this place may not have been responsible, but something eaten earlier in the day . . . just a thought.

Fish was overcooked. Service was pretty bad too. I told them of a food allergy, but the food came out with said ingredient on the plate. They agreed to remake the food. By the time my food actually came out, everyone had to leave to get back to a work event (and we were there for 1.5 hours, so it's not like they didn't have enough time!). The servers and managers came over and apologized profusely, but they did not offer any compensation: e.g. dessert, drinks, a free meal. Talk is cheap. Luke is not cheap... and not cheap enough to warrant this kind of service and food.

Run. This place is dirty, digusting, and sad. If you order online your order is going to be wrong, if you call in your order will 100% be wrong, and if you order in the store...be prepared to have your next 4 birthdays while sitting in the dank restaurant. Walking into this place is like walking into a 1975 horror scene but worse. There are only ever 2 people working their who would rather be talking crap on other stores and employees then helping you, dont bother them. They constantly complain to customers about other employees and how crappy that place is. We tried this place twice because I wanted to give them the benefit of the doubt. For shame ....they did not get better with time. The first time the food was completely burnt which is odd considering its on a timed conveyor belt of heat. But these numbnuts some how screwed that up. The second time I ordered they gave us all gluten free dough which was like gnawing on a thick piece of cardboard that had been under someones car seat for 10-14 weeks. Do yourself a favor and go down the road to dominoes....its cheaper, cleaner, and better service.

This taco Bell is the worst you go in there is no one at the counter then when they come to the counter they helping in the bag the staff is all over the place the manager has her pants under her butt the place was dirty I went in with a co-worker I was going to order some but I took a double look and said nevermind no thank you. I used to go to this taco Bell but lately when I go is all discombobulated and I don't know what to order so I just leave and go to another food chain. The last time that I ordered from there was around December I believe. I wanted to order the party pack of tacos but we don't eat beef so I tried to order the chicken tacos and they was at least $16 for the b but if you add chicken 12 little tacos would have been $30 plus tax. Absolutely crazy. And when you order from the $1.00 menu they don't give a hoot they think because you order from the dollar menu that your food should be sloppy and thrown together. I was very unhappy with my two little tacos and my quesadilla and nachos and they all was from the dollar menu. The nachos look like someone went to the bathroom on them the chicken quesadilla just had melted cheese look like vomit and the chicken tacos was the only thing okay but us meat of chicken was on the tacos. They really need to come up with a price that will fit your budget at taco Bell for chicken if they can make the ground beef they can make the ground turkey or chicken and that would be fine. I live too far to be leaving and coming all the way back because my food is wrong. so my best bet is just to stay away from taco Bell and do it at home.

I want to give them higher stars because I have had some great dishes here but the problem is it's really inconsistent. Every time I go there I request no cucumbers, which I loathe and am allergic to and EVERY time there are cucumbers. Also, the meat is really fatty. They are super sweet and it's not a bad choice but just looking for better.
My sister got food poisoning from this place after eating the Prime Rib Sandwich, so we will definitely not be going back. I thought the food was overpriced as well. The staff was nice and friendly.

The staff was very friendly and helpful. The lobby was small but clean. The courtyard is very pretty. The breakfast that is served is very nice, the food is very good with a lot of choices. The only problems we did have is the room was very small for our family. The pictures of the lobby and rooms are misleading. The shower was missing a door causing water to leak out when we showered. There is tiling throughout making it dangerous to come out of the shower with water all over the floor even with tons of towels we laid out on the floor. The room had a horrible smell of mold. Both myself and my son have allergies and asthma. We had a hard time sleeping and breathing while in the room. It has been 10 days since we are back and both of us have been sick with upper respiratory infections and sinus infections since we landed. They definitely have mold issues and need to clean out their HVAC systems and filters. Absolutely terrible air quality in the rooms! Nice hotel but would never stay there again. This was not our first time in NOLA but our first time at this hotel and definitely our last.

A cute little family-owned diner-like restaurant that's perfect for post-church brunch. With only about 10 to 12 tables, this place is teeny tiny, so it's essential that you're in and out. Although I didn't feel rushed through my meal, I think it's courteous to eat quickly, as a line begins to form at the door just before noon. My breakfast was amazing. Sunny side up eggs, bacon, a pancake, and home fries really hit the spot! The prices are great (breakfast for 3 under $25!), and on Monday through Friday, they have really great breakfast specials until 11AM. Just a strange fluke, the ketchup had jelly mixed in with it, and it almost ruined our whole meals! But the waitress was very apologetic and offered us new food. Thankfully, we were able to clean the contaminated ketchup off of our plates and food and still enjoy the meal! My only true complaint is that the coffee is terrible. Kind of a let down, considering this is a breakfast joint! Also, they accept cash only, and the closest ATM is at the Blue Dog a few doors down the strip mall. The waitress was sweet as pie and my friends and I really enjoyed ourselves. I will be back!!

The food used to be better. Now its just yucky soggy gross calorie filled food. Gluten free menu is non existent for bfast. I could only have yogurt and egg whites. Used to have a better gf selection.

Our daughter has a dairy allergy. We informed the front desk ahead of time and informed the waitress twice. We ran each dish by them. We were assured that, after checking with the chef, the chicken did not have dairy in it. We checked again after a few bites when a buttery taste was noted. We were then informed that the kitchen made a mistake and that the allergen had been consumed. Will not trust them again with her safety. A real shame for a restaraunt that we previously enjoyed.
The food is bland and over priced. I have been here numerous times and always disappointed. Last time I was here I got food poisoning from their burger. I will never come back here.

Cute cute cute. Got the miso and literally had diarrhea alllll day. I think it was like tooo much jalapeño juice or something. Like I ate it, loved it. Had drinks. Didn't feel sick, so it wasnt like food poisoning or anything... but my butt was on fire alllll day long. Still gets five stars, but maybe watch out for the jalapeno miso BUT! The whitefish was soooo good and didn't give me any problems. Also love their coffee and fun drink menu.

After an hour's wait with being unable to reach them via phone, I received my extremely pungent and brown mango and pineapple smoothie. I nearly vomited whole dumping it because it was so foul. Then I opened up my bagel sandwich, with avocado and tomato, to find brown avocado and very mushy tomatoes. So whatever they were spending that hour doing, it clearly wasn't paying attention to the quality of their food. Grubhub has been trying now for almost 2 hours to get a hold of them for a refund, but they're refusing to answer the phone. I've ordered from them nearing a dozen times, and this experience has completely ruined all the rest. Late, rotten food, then ghosting on customers... I'll never order from them again. Update: After two days, Grubhub finally got a hold of them but they're refusing to do anything. So I called myself and the manager was so unbelievably rude and started yelling at me, not letting me speak. I was told that my brown smoothie ended up that way because the driver took too long to get there. Sorry, but fruit doesn't brown quite that quickly. I've waited an hour for their food before and all that happened was the smoothie separated. This was brown... But instead of trying to help, I was yelled at. They had a chance to redeem themselves and passed on it.

FOOD POISONING ALERT!!! I specifically had oysters, filet mignon and creme brulee. Any place that gives me food poisoning, automatically gets a 1-star rating. Additional details: - My steak was chewy - Service was slow and non-attentive

Well let me start by saying that I traveled all the way from Houston to come see Nashville. One friend recommended me Ole Red to eat and grab some drinks. When I got there, my family and i had to wait about an hour to get seated because they only have a couple of table for 5+ people. I ordered the redneck nachos and it honestly looked like crap and tasted like it had beer in them. My dad had ordered the burger and it was small for $16. He told our waitress to put the cheese on the side but instead they gave him the wrong burger with chesse... My dad is allergic to cheese so we made them take it back. This place is great to hang out and drink but not a great place to eat...

Looks are very deceiving. This place is going downhill. Every time we ate something at a restaurant it was awful and our last meal I got food poisoning SO bad that I had to go to the hospital for dehydration and it ruined our entire trip!!! They offered us free food, are you kidding me? A good hotel with good managament would have said all expenses paid and re-evaluate their food situation. Unbelieveable! THEN when they were trying to take care of us because I was so sick resting in the room for 2 days they screwed that up by sending someone to bring us towels 3 times when we JUST WANTED the bathroom cleaned. I was trying to rest but they woke me up late at night when someone FINALLY came to bring MORE TOWELS when we literally asked the front desk manager for someone to clean our bathroom and bring us toilet paper. NOT one sweet southerner working here but all foreign people they are probably underpaying who barely speak English. Only good thing about this place is clean bed but I would have MUCH RATHER STAYED AT A HOLIDAY INN EXPRESS!! RUN the other way and save your money!! Do not miss out on downtown Nashville and all the fun things to do by getting distracted by a touristy, 1 star indoor Atrium hotel.

Yes, this place has more toppings than any other froyo place that I've been to (e.g. mochi, etc.). I wasn't too happy that the chocolate flavor wasn't available. The machine just wouldn't give me my chocolate froyo! They do have 2 flavors of sorbet in rotation for the lactose intolerants. The flavor here had a slight yogurty taste initially (the sour taste), but that went away as I ate more of the froyo. Other than that, the variety is there. Very clean as Stephanie S. mentioned. Ambience was kitchy & cool. Now, if they could just open a froyo place in Arnold I would be a happy camper.
Stay away from this place, waited forever for my food and then got food poisoning. You'd be much better off going somewhere else.

Ate here one day looking for good fried chicken. Not only was the fried chicken burnt - the skin disintegrated upon touching it - but I also got food poisoning and spent the next 12 hours in the bathroom throwing up. This all happened during g the city-wide mandatory water boiling mandate so maybe that's why. Many restaurants were closed....and obviously this one should have closed down too. I don't think I'll ever eat fried chicken a

AVOID THIS LOCATION! I would give them negative stars if I could. Went through the drive through and it took over 30 mins and I was the only person there! It took about 20 mins for me to get two burgers and fries and when they gave them to me my fries were cold. So I kindly pointed it out to him and he said he gave us attitude but said he would remake the fries. This took about 10 mins. During the waiting we were starving so decided to eat our burgers. One of the burgers was supposed to be no cheese for someone who is allergic with added lettuce onions and pickles, they gave us a plan cheese burger. Normally I don't return things if there is a mistake but she could not eat cheese. So we tried to explain what we would like and he got very rude then slammed the window. 5 mins later he came back with a box full of lettuce and onions and was like HERE. Umm, that doesn't solve the fact that there was cheese all over the burger, but at this point we had been there for over 30 mins dealing with this rude guy and just decided to cut our losses. Then here is the kicker, I ate my burger since I don't have any allergies and got terrible food poisoning. Would not come back again. Would not go back to any Freddy's again ever.

I had the fish platter and the fish was wonderful. My side was the "buttered noodles " -they had pesto on them (it was good, but I would have liked to have known that when I placed my order). My husband ordered the half rack of ribs. Sadly, they were not done well. They were over-cooked and looked sad. He said the more he ate, the worse they got. The waitress was nice, but did not make any notes for the chef when I told her I had a soy allergy. Our service was nice though and she even refilled my water twice before being asked. We will try it again.

came here because of all the vegan options, both our entrees were great however we got the vegan cheesesteak fries and unfortunately they were made with real meat. i know the server did his part and it was probably just an unfortunate mistake but had i not been vegan by choice and actually allergic to meat it could be more serious. just a request to the kitchen to be a little more vigilant in the dishes they send out:) overall not a bad experience, really great vegan options when actually done vegan

Horrible!! Terrible service. Took 15 mins. to be seated and there was nobody else waiting. Took 15 mins. for the server to come and greet us. Another 10 mins. to get our drinks then our food arrived one minute later so no time to enjoy them before our meal. The food was slightly warm, very bland, gooey, and overall bad for the 16.95 price. Then to make matters worse I got food poisoning from the meal. I will never return and never recommend to anyone. Worst meal I have ever had. Doesn't even deserve 1 star but yelp is demanding it.

I came upon this place when I needed a quick gluten free meal while my husband indulged at Gluten filled Sonny's down the street. Yes, they have a gluten free menu. Whether they've ever trained their staff on it? Don't think so! I got the steakhouse burger. I was asked if I cheese would have gluten in it... um no. So, I explained to them what had gluten in it. Not the first or the last time, I've had to do it, and happy to oblige, but seriously, train your staff. The steakhouse burger was supposed to have caramelized onions, mine didn't come with any, I also had to sub the fries for broccolini. The whole meal was delicious. Burger was juicy and tender with great cheese that was just sharp enough, the broccolini was flavored well and tasted great. Then, I go the bill. $25.
