They charged me the dinner price for the burger, even though they didn't make it dinner style, and then up-charged me for the broccolini. Seriously? So, the food was good, the service OK, the price, NOT worth it!

I got very very sick after eating 3 pieces of their pizza. I ordered 2 medium double pepperoni double cheese and NO sauce. Spent $28 and was up all night with diarrhea. I don't know if it was the food poison or not. I have took laxatives before and that's what it was like excepting was like you took a whole bunch and if I could prove this these ppl would be in very big trouble.

This place is awful or should I say the whole building is awful, it's contaminated with black mold and the owners will not do anything to fix this deadly problem. Do your health a favor and don't eat from this place!

This restaurant is very hip and trendy but I was not crazy about the food. The service was good and they were very accommodating with my gluten allergy. For appetizers, we got the whipped feta dip which was fabulous. For dinner, I got the riced avocado and steak. The meal was extremely spicy and I only liked the steak (not the other food in the dish). My friend really enjoyed her cauliflower steak though. For dessert, I enjoyed the ice cream. Fun atmosphere but I would order different food if I went back.

This is not the Hong Kong Sunny of old. Quality and service have hit an all time low. Young male waiter doesn't understand menu. He was sitting most of the time when his tables didn't have beverages. When water was brought to the table, it had little or no ice in it and tasted horrible. Requested no carrots in a dish that showed up with carrots; good thing I'm not allergic. Requested spicy mustard; was brought something of the same color but the consistency of water. One small bowl of rice brought out for two entrees; didn't even put serving spoons in the food platters. It'll be the last time we eat here.

Avoid this place at all costs. Top price, sit down dinner, so so food and refuse to let you use bathroom. I overlooked everything till I got sick to my stomach and was about to vomit and they said go to Starbucks across the street our bathroom is for employees only. Avoid this dump.

We ordered from this company via Uber Eats- I love giving both good and marginal reviews on food. We just got home from Mexico- maybe this was our issue! Craving a good taco, we ordered 5 tacos. two of the five tasted like literal dog food. My husband almost literally threw up. Not sure what was off that night... Or if this is normal... Our first time at the restaurant or eating at the restaurant I should say definitely will not return... Taco should be simple and tasty and nothing more.

Your review helps others learn about great local businesses. Was in the house the last time the Eagles won the NFC championship and it was raucous. loved the crab fries, would only be better if they were house cute. Also had the crab and it was above average. Got there around 1pm and a drunken mob was still doing the Eagles chant, I was told they'd been doing since 5am. Loved the atmosphere and energy. Except the toilet vomit. But all in all will go back and do it again, but this time like the locals. Boozed up!

If you are looking for another main line restaurant with overpriced food (and weak drinks, untrained staff and management that doesnt care you have found your spot. I was so disappointed with our meal, and felt so ripped off I will never go back. Also if you have any food allergies, do not expect to be accommodated. With restaurants like Tredici where they bend over backwards to make you feel welcome I dont see how Avalon will survive.

Had heard wonderful things about this place. When we stopped by everything look fantastic. Our very first question when we walk in at every restaurant is related to allergen contamination in the kitchen. We were told that it wasn't a problem. Then we walked further in and looked through the glass wall of the kitchen. There is SO MUCH cross-contamination in the kitchen that had to leave.

Called to place nice size order on sushi spring rolls, the lady who took order was horrible! Really nasty and mean ! I was like Huh? Anyway being a responsible person I went to pick up thinking maybe she was just busy. When i got there (the door looked like it hadn't been cleaned in years) (filthy) That should have told me then there to get out now. I picked it up thinking i don't want them to get stuck with food. I received food from same Lady so nasty and mean again went home took it out. Ate one piece of sushi and knew something wasn't right 1 out of 18 pieces i ate woke up 8 hours later throwing up violently :( it was that sushi I knew it.. when I smelled it the next day I knew OMG i was sick all day. Do yourself a favor DON'T EAT THERE! you can die from food poisoning...and they are not cheap over 15$ for just one person. But even if cheap not worth even if free! the spring rolls just as nasty, but cooked so not as deadly. I am following up with dirty dining to try and save someone else from being poisoned. the springrolls were all breading and dripping with grease old grease. take care if i could give no star it would be appropriate, but they won't let you submit w/o a star!

Food was not good. We had it delivered and the delivery service was great. And that's about where the good experience ended. My hubby has an allergy and i asked for that specific food to be left out. It wasn't. So for $65.00 i would have expected all three of us to be able to eat. But because of his allergy he wasn't able to eat at all. Plus the food was pretty cold and not very good.

so this review is not about the food. I give it four stars so the juiciness and ingenuity of the burgers. I also will give 4 stars to the cooks, who work efficiently and smoothly despite the business of the place. However, I give this place ONE STAR for the cashiers (2 girls) who dip their fries with their hands in to the big jugs of BBQ sauce and ketchup behind the counter. GROSS!! I almost vomited my food!! My husband stopped eating his burger. Who does that?!! Does management know? Why didn't anyone say anything??? Never coming back if this is the norm.

Yeah, it's OK, but just, OK. Nothing special or noteworthy, unless spending $15 for lunch is special. I am not a fan of a hamburger that has more bread than meat. And, while I love that they have a gluten-free bread option, but I hate that the bread was 3 or 4 times thicker than the meat. Really, it's just Meh (2 stars), plus an extra star for G/F bread option. Edit: I wrote this hiaku this morning upon reflecting on my quick lunch choice yesterday... Skinny fries are GREAT More bun than meat no bueno Should have kept looking

The food is great. The beer selection is great. The service is usually great. Tonight we had a large party. Our waitress was rude and inattentive from the start. When my bf with celiac disease asked if they had a gluten free menu or options she responded with "you know what you can eat" not informing us of their gluten free pizza crust. The nice hostess did that. Then another waiter or a manager came over and yelled at us for taking chairs from tables that were waiting to be sat...because our party grew. We had to inform him that no we didn't take chairs from any tables...we asked for them and they were given to us by an employee from a stack of extra chairs. When it came time to split the check, instead of just splitting it evenly amongst us like normal adults do, the waitress had us write down on a piece of paper our name and what we ordered. Just not a pleasant experience. Everything could've been overlooked but the inappropriate comment to someone with a true disease that will get sick from eating specific foods is unacceptable. Especially when they are advertised as gluten free accommodat

I ordered a pan pizza. I trusted them. They are professionals. They do this all the time. Well, this isn't what I experienced. I ordered half green pepper, tomato and olive. What did I get? No olive. Onion substitute instead. I bit into it, in a darkened room, and immediately chewed and swallowed the onions... tried to pick the onions off, but there were too many. Soon after I was off to CVS for tums and benadryl. I know how I get. So I ended up eating a cold-cut sandwich instead. Why Pizza Hut? Why did this happen? Explain? I have English as a first language, as did the guy who took my order. So, how soon can you guys make me a free half of a pizza? I didn't appreciate my allergic reaction. So now I await a managerial reply. Experience date: October 27, 2019 Time: 7:00 P.M. E.S.T. Sincerely, Hungry in Clearwater

This restaurant DOES NOT have gluten free options!! When I called in advance, I was told they do not have a gluten-free menu but they did have gluten free alternatives the waiter/waitress could specify. Once my party was seated, the waiter told me the only thing I could have on the menu was raw sushi. That's it. Since I couldn't eat anything on the menu (I don't eat raw sushi), my entire party had to leave. I was incredibly disappointed.

I used to frequent this location with my girlfriend because of the location however we found that it's usually a hit or miss when it comes to the service and quality of food, and more often than not it's a miss. My girlfriend always orders their French Onion soup without cheese because she is lactose intolerant. For whatever reason they never get it right. The last time we were there the forgot her extra bread and when she went back up to ask for it the cook behind the counter literally threw it onto her plate. The staff including the management are either happy and energetic or sluggish and make it obvious that they do not want to be there. I've worked in the food industry as well and understand that it's overwhelming and tiring however, when your staff is constantly making the same mistakes and make your customers feel like they are an encumbrance then that is when I take issue. We'll spend our money elsewhere.

For $85 this was really a terrible experience. Out of the 4 dishes we ordered, 3 were wrong. And not just a little wrong, completely wrong. My mother in law is allergic to eggs. She ordered the burger and asked them to leave off the egg because she's extremely allergic. We said it 2x. Her burger came out with a fried egg on it. She said she wanted it well done, it was medium rare. I ordered the St. Bart's POACHED eggs. It came out with SCRAMBLED eggs on top. My daughter ordered the kids meal with pancakes and scrambled eggs. This meal came with a drink. She got French toast and NO egg. AND the server charged us an extra $3.50 for her orange juice!!! That's just the issues with the ordering. There was no manager apology, and the waitress said she normally works the night shift which is why she got everything wrong. Ok so let's talk about the food. The poached egg was barely cooked- the yellow is supposed to be soft and runny, but the whites are supposed to be cooked. Instead I was eating a cold runny egg, and I could even send it back because my husband was already done eating since his order was the only one they did right. The croissant was soaked completely through so it was a mess. The hash browns were cold, so clearly they just used my original plate. My biscuit was heavy and floury. Yuck. My daughter said IHOPs pancakes tasted better. And I have to agree. These pancakes were not fluffy at all. They tasted like they were made with wheat flour. And the scrambled egg looked like it was made with powdered egg. The dad's steak special tasted good but it was a total rip off at $24. The steak portion was tiny. For that price, we would rather go to Ruth Chris and get a real steak. Overall, it was a very disappointing Father's Day brunch.

I visited RAT last night, with 2 other couples. It was not a particularly good experience. The service was poor: we sat for 20 minutes before a drink order was taken and our glasses sat empty for another 20 without an offer of another round. For some reason, only 2 of us were offered dessert. The server took those 2 orders and walked away. We had to flag him down for the others to order. I can't remember the last time I tipped under 20%, but I did last night. Most troubling for me was the unhelpfulness and inflexibility when I tried to order gluten free. I have celiac's disease and get quite ill when I eat wheat. The server had no particular idea what I could eat. The entree I wanted came with a side dish I could not eat. They refused to simply swap out the side dish for another. I could eat the chicken or steak as is, but not the pork loin with a different side. Even though I did not really want chicken, I finally ordered it to stop holding up the entire table. The chicken dish seemed to be seasoned exclusively with salt. I've never been to a restaurant that bills itself as "fresh" and "local" give me so much trouble and flat out refuse to be flexible to accommodate my medical issue. I've had better service, better food, and more accommodating kitchen staff at Houlihan's, for a fraction of the price. I went in with high expectations and was very disappointed.

Absolutely horrible food! We got a pizza that I swear was store-bought for $1.99 - we each ate one piece and threw it away. Also ordered a Chicken Caesar salad to take on the plane and when I opened it up it was the strangest looking Chicken Caesar I had ever seen - tasted just as strange. My friend and I ate a couple of bites and threw that away as well. Several hours later, we were both in the bathroom - I'm certain it was borderline food poisoning from this place. NEVER will we eat there again! Be warned!!

If I can give this zero stars I would this place is disgusting I ordered general tso chicken it was pure dough and fried slimy greasey the ribs tasted like cleaning product ugh these good reviews must be people that are high because this was the worst Chinese food iv ever had and super exspensive fuck this place!!! Let me add I got food poisoning!

I've only had the pleasure of ingesting Rohypnol twice in my life. Brew Brothers popped my cherry here and let me say I'm eternally thankful that I am not a 120 pound girl because that stuff steals your memories like orphans in Russia snag wallets. I tell you this so you have a vibe for the aura of this establishment. I've not spent a ten minute period in this place free from the bro vibe that is a typical frat party. The bartenders can be nice, but only if you're slightly more good looking than me and female. The patrons are all various stages of completely blacked out. The floor is slick with beer, blood, or vomit on an interval so regular that you might mistake it for the alley behind that dive bar you like. All this being said, it's couldn't have a better location, which is why they are still open. The casino is one of the better spots in town and hosts more tourists on a Wednesday than any Rolling Stones concert could handle. There is never a dull moment, but be careful how dull you are in the moment you choose to party at Brew Brothers.

Well the food is great, but my wife is unfortunately highly allergic to dairy. They had no options whatsoever that did not have dairy, or dairy substitute. She is not the only person that has a dairy allergy, and being a well known it's very unfortunate that they can't accommodate everyone.

I'm not sure why this place has good reviews. I came in with my boyfriend and had high hopes -- it always looks full and I've wanted to go for a while. I've never had such horrible service. A former server myself, I know when someone isn't doing their job. I'm allergic to dairy and asked if I could have jam on my bagel instead of butter. The server corrected me "we have jelly" in a sarcastic tone. That's fine -- I just didn't want butter. We had to walk up to the counter to get refills on our sodas after waiting ten minutes. The server spilled a glass of water next to my boyfriend's seat and left the ice and water on the floor the entire time. His eggs were disgustingly undercooked. No one checked on us and the food took forever to come out. Never again. Perhaps we got off to a bad start -- maybe the server thought I was a jam snob. Regardless, there's no excuse for horrible service. 30 minutes and no offers for drink refills? No thank you.
I bought 4 hamburgers and fries from them. Once I got home and opened the bag the smell of rotting hamburger nearly made me vomit. Waste of money. So disgusting

Checked it out for gluten free! Okay I went with my wife to check this place out because well I'm gluten free. it's hard to find gluten free places so I bought one of each of their flourless cookies. Well the snickerdoodle and macaroon was good, but their chocolate chip tasted old. My wife didn't want to try a slice of pizza because it looked old. We tried a flourless peanut butter brownie mini torte and that wasn't bad. It wasn't overly sweet and had a good texture, but the brownie tasted gummy/stale. Wouldn't go out of my way to go back to this place. I do not work for or get anything for saying this from writing this, but I've been to sweet freedom on South Street and it is by far the best bakery I've been to for gluten free. To top it all off they gave me a free cupcake when I went in for my birthday.

I can't stand Yelp honestly, or folks who review constantly to be honest, but i feel as though this is a safety issue at this point: I came down with food poisoning after eating g take out from here a couple months ago. It cost me a shift at work! Thought it could have been a one time occurrence since this wasn't our first time eating from here. I switched to vegetarian dishes thinking I'd be safe-all was well a couple of times, and today we got lunch to go, and I have food poisoning again! Our order got here WAY too fast. They must be serving leftovers/old food, or the kitchen isn't clean/combo of both. We will NOT be ordering from here again, and I'll be reporting them to appropriate resources for sure.

We were really excited for this place than instantly disappointed. The restrooms and floors were disgusting I should have left then. Instead we went in. Waited a ridiculous amount of time for service, the food was just ok and I'm pretty sure I got food poisoning from here. The milkshakes were good though

Went here for dinner. Had a reservation and had requested to sit right next to the tank. Even though there were two tables empty, they wouldn't seat us closer. The tank is beautiful and the food was delicious but my dad got food poisoning from the shrimp. He was so sick that he missed all of Thanksgiving the next day which he had traveled all the way from Ohio for the first time in 10 years to spend the holiday with us. Now I will think twice about going there to eat. :(

Go to Noboru. I have never, in my life, written a completely negative review for a restaurant. But there's a first time for everything. Save yourself the food poisoning and eat elsewhere. The food was left out for so long that it was hardened. The business end of the tongs to serve yourself food with was left resting against a rusted pole that has probably never been cleaned. The sushi was out for so long the avocados were brown and they smelled fishy. Even the iced tea I ordered was gross, I couldn't drink it. Don't want to spend the extra dimes on Noboru? (which is well worth it for their sushi) Then head over to Wegmans. That's what I did after I couldn't finish my dinner at Jim's Buffet.

Sub-par service and not gluten free it's gluten friendly. I kindly asked if they could have put my pizza on a metal tray and cooked it on that to avoid cross contamination as I have celiacs and it was a hard no. They said this after i had already built the whole pizza. They didn't even cut my pizza and was not that good. Go to Pizza Rev downtown Santa Barbara, so much better.

For some reason, this place has a reputation as an awesome restaurant that serves great mexican food. I don't understand this. I've eaten here several times, and the food has never been good. It's like this tasteless blob of tex-mex on a plate, usually in a quantity that is repulsively large, and leaves you feeling like you just ate a plate of Taco Bell (i.e., vomitous). Superior Grill is not without merits. The margaritas are pretty tasty. Of course, they're also ball-achingly expensive. And when it comes down to it, I have a blender, and can make my own margaritas for a fraction of the price without suffering through the loud environment, bad food, and splendidly OK service that I get at Superior. Though the building looks cool and is in a great location, this should never have been a place to go for New Orleans tourists, and hopefully won't be so for long.

We ate here (party of 5) during a spring break visit with family a couple weeks ago. The restaurant has enough seating for about 15 guests and is mainly a take-out and catering restaurant. The owner was very friendly and patient with our indecisive (and quite young) gluten free guests. I was very impressed with the owner's knowledge of celiac disease and with her very careful business practices. I had a tasty pastrami sandwich on very delicious GF bread. My mother who is not gluten free was able to order a sandwich on regular bread. Our server explained that the wheat bread is prepackaged slices that are brought in and are prepared carefully in isolation. All equipment used to bake the homemade GF breads and bakery goods are free from cross contamination and made on dedicated equipment. The cupcakes are yummy and the butterscotch bar was fantastic. We bought goodies to take home with us too. Try the pasta salad. It is high in protein and very healthy! Portion sizes are large and we all had leftovers to go home with (which we all enjoyed). Loved this place and will make the trip again the next time we are in Nashville.

Took my 2 year old daughter here for a treat last night, to enjoy some brownies and ice cream. Anyways once we walked outside the building we BOTH immediately threw up. I know it's tmi but I think it's needs to be addressed. I called the store once we got home just to tell them and warn them. The guy who answered straight hung up on me. After I told him what happened.

I was really excited to check this place out but came away a bit disappointed (for reference, I got a dulce de leche tart, 2 chocolate raspberry cupcakes, 2 chocolate peanut butter cupcakes, and a pumpkin cupcake). First, the good: It's a beautifully decorated place, the staff was friendly, and it looked like they had a really varied selection including gluten free and vegan options. I also really liked that they had cake servers for sale at the counter. The dulce de leche tart is delicious. The bad: it's expensive. Probably not relative to the area, but in general, very pricey. Also, the cupcakes I got were pretty bland. The raspberry frosting tasted like nothing. Literally, no flavor, definitely not raspberry. The cake itself was dry, and also didn't have much flavor. The peanut butter frosting was better, but had sort of a burnt flavor. Would I go back? Maybe if I was already in the area. But I wouldn't go out of my way.

Food is good but nothing really stands out compared to an $ asian restaurant in south Philly. Just couldn't wrap my mind around their charging separately for rice that shoulda been included such that their customers can dilute down the salty food. $3/ small bowl of rice? Pretty sure wasn't GMO free or gluten-free. What is it? Rice grown on golden soil? Bottom line is: bring your own rice cooker and make yourself some nice affordable rice; unless you want to pay premium money on mediocre rice; or constantly chucking on water to dial down the salt!

We came here for valentine's day with my best friend and his girlfriend. I will say that the food was delicious and the atmosphere was very enjoyabke, but that's where the good news stops. My friends girlfriend is allergic to gluten. Not like fad gluten free, but very seriously gluten free because of a serious allergy. When we asked the waitress if any dishes had no gluten, she told us that she wasn't sure, but if we were unsure we should eat the pasta because that is gluten free.....Which is obviously ridiculous. She was rude the rest of the service, treating us like idiots even though she didn't even know the menu or apparently what gluten is. When it came time to pay the bill, each couple informed the waitress that we had a groupon, $24 for $40 worth of food. She told us that if we had been at different tables, both groupon would have worked, but since we were together, only one could be used on the total bill. We thought that didn't seem right so she brought a manager out. The manager explained it, but informed us that the waitress was correct. We were frustrated, but it was in the Groupon fine print, so he was admittedly right. The way he spoke to us was incredibly degrading though. The lower level dining room is fairly small and it was packed since it was valentine's day. It wasn't so much what he said, but the volume at which he said it. He did not seem willing to listen or help at all and he was speaking so loudly that people on the other side of the room were looking at us. All four of us are 23-26 and I'm guessing, maybe unfairly, that this is why he felt it was okay to embarrass us like this. I'm sure he wouldn't speak to an older better dressed group in the way he spoke to us. He, like the waitress, treated us as an annoyance and an inconvenience. You could hear it in his voice. Finally, when we got our check, the waitress refused to separate the checks, one for each couple. We told her we would like separate checks twice. After the second mistake, my wife had to break it down for her like you would a chikd, telling her that we were not a 4 way relationship and that we needed the check split in half. All in all, we paid about $60 apiece for a horrible experience. My wife and I spent the whole ride home wondering how we had heard such good things about this place, and I am certain my friend and his girlfriend did the same. I still have my groupon, but I'd rather let them have my money then drive 45inutes into the city to be treated like garbage. Do yourself a favor. Find another Mediterranean /Italian restaurant where you can pay half as much, get twice as much food and be treated like an actual paying customer and not an inconvenience. There's alot of places for that in st. Louis. Don't give this place business that could go to a deserving establishment elsewhere.

The food here is offensive to people who are not intoxicated. You will actually find yourself wishing that you were eating dinner on American Airlines overseas flight ingesting Lean Cuisine's take on chicken. One time I set a piece of salmon on fire. The fire department put it out. That char of salmon tasted better than Axis' grilled chicken platter. I was pulling an all-nighter and ordered Axis to make me feel better. Now, I'm not only tired, I'm also worried about contracting food poisoning. The grilled chicken platter is chicken bits from the salad bar that they warmed up in a microwave and dried out. On the side, I got a salad (which was tolerable, a high compliment for this horrible establishment). Macaroni is hard to fuck up. Yet, Axis did the impossible and fucked up mac and cheese. It is simultaneously oozing Tostito's-esque "cheese" and has no flavor. But the string beans, the string beans are anus of the anus meal. These strings taste like they've been sitting out for a million years. They're slightly white and totally overcooked. They cannot even be salvaged by the included ketchup packets (the highlight of the meal). Overall: If you're thinking about ordering Axis, you're better off eating spoonfuls of ketchup.

Great choice for food unless you have a food allergy. We've been here twice and both times my friend, who is allergic to peanuts, has had a pretty bad allergic reaction. She has specified both times that she has a nut allergy and the staff seemed to understand that. I wish they revealed more whether their foods used peanut oil in their sauces because twice in a row now is not a coincidence. Very upsetting.

We went for dinner on Saturday night. Not too long of a wait. At our table I told the waitress about a gluten allergy as I ordered off your gluten friendly menu. I ordered the steak and ribs with vegetables. Food took a long time to arrive, of course mine had onion straws under the steak. When the waitress came back she seemed annoyed that I wanted a new dish. She assured me they would recook it all, as if there was another option. Needless to say my family had cold food by the time mine arrived. A manager brought it, no apology, nothing! Well, I don't know what your kitchen staff did when they redid my meal but I have been sick all night. There is no doubt they did something to my food that has had me in pain all night. I am furious that after giving a heads up for an allergy that not only was the food made wrong but now I am sick.

Used to love Nadia but it's gone downhill over the years. The place is cute, what with the orange sponge-painted walls under a spray of gold glitter and the little bronze bells that ring at the door, and the service is great. Friendly people here. The Tom Yum has that satisfying balance of tang & spice, and the Coconut soup sooooothes the soul. Their curries, especially the mango, are good, though I'd recommend the noodle dishes. The lunch special's a great deal. You get soup, appetizer and entree in smaller portions for the regular price of one entree alone. It's both tasty and filling. I've been pleased again and again by the Drunken Noodle, so you can understand my dismay when the last time I went it gave me food poisoning. I tried really hard to convince myself that I was sick before going, but out of the group of people who went, only those who had eaten the Drunken Noodle fell ill.
Disappointed in the soggy flavorless gluten free bread. Cheese was good. Service friendly. For $11.75 I expected a good sandwich. Too bad.

The phrase for this place is, polished turd. So this place has been around since I was little, and so has the grime on the walls and floors, (several decades). Today's experience was absolutely horrendous. We walked in and were instantly hit with a stench that was comparable to that of old lady fecal mater mixed with baby vomit (don't ask how I know, just trust me). We mistakenly stayed to order, (should have left but we were on a time limit for lunch, we stayed). The "deal" of the day was one chicken strip, which is a standard deep fried-nothing fancy chicken strip. Oh, and it also came with some coleslaw. All for a whooping 8 bucks. Woo hoo... The cashier was all too ready to take our order with his fancy chef's hat and striped shirt attempting to appear as though he was educated in the fine art of deep fry from some sophisticated culinary school in the deep underground of a Russian Gulag. However, as much as I would like to not judge an individual based on first impressions, I get the idea from our cashier's vernacular that he had not attended any form of post secondary school, or even grammar school. The menu consists of fish, chicken, potatoes, and chowder, all of which at one point or other in the preparation process meets the authentic cooking style of the McDonald's deep fry. Opting to not go with the special, we decided for a two piece fish and chips, and a bowl of chowder. We also neglected to have one of the many beverages that were offered at this fine establishment, as they all appeared to be the same adult beverages that are sold at the bargain groceries store that occupies the same parking lot. This assumption was made based off of the off-brand beer, still in the store bought six pack carton resting ever so cleverly on the cash register for those daytime drinkers who simply cannot wonder over to the bargain grocery store on their own. To accompany this wonderful experience, we are subject to the tones of symphonic melody blissfully blasting from a 1980's style boom box strategically placed on the upper corner of the deep fryer. This is obviously done for maximum coverage across the entire establishment. Because this place is offensive to so many of our senses, at least those foolish enough to eat here can hear something nice. But really, this is in such stark contrast to the rest of the experience that it would actually be better if we were listening to something more fitting, like an constant backfire from the engine of a diesel truck. Moving to the actual food,... "food".... the sauces were watered down. Seriously, watered down. Fry sauce came out like water. Tarter Sauce was of equal consistency, and so was the chowder. I have been to both coasts, and from my experience chowder is not supposed to be watery. Maybe I am being overly judgmental, maybe this is supposed to be authentic southern Idaho High Desert cuisine, but watery and bland chowder is not something I am willing to pay 5 dollars a bowl for. All in all, this was a terrible place. I seriously cannot find a positive aspect about this. It was over priced, terribly greasy, limited choice, and incredibly disgusting. After eating here, the next big decision I had was to either poop, or vomit. ... still deciding....

First time visit. Had to wait to be greeted by a hostess. No other patrons in the restaurant. Nice looking restaurant, appears clean, bright colors. Ordered fried chicken, mashed potatoes and gravy, house salad and cornbread. Chicken leg was raw, very bloody and not the very light pink tinge that I consider dicey to begin with. Waitress assured me that she had them check it at 165 degrees and that blood is pushed out of the bone during cooking. My life experience is that the juices should run clear. Contaminated my whole dinner plate. They cooked another piece and it was cooked thoroughly. The mashed potatoes were thin, gravy not much flavor. The cornbread was cold, dry and over baked, cupcake size. Waitress grabbed it from a styrofoam box so who knows when it was actually baked. Salad was decent with romaine, tomatoes, onion slices. Came 30 seconds before the meal was served. She mentioned she had planned to get the salads out earlier. Not a big deal to us. Sweet tea was tasty. Older gal (?owner) walked around eating at least two bowls of potato salad during dinner service. Never greeted or checked on the patrons. Table next to us had a very attentive waitress. My husband had the chicken breast and rates it as "an expensive coffee shop meal." Unfortunately, we won't give this restaurant a second chance. KFC is better and that's saying something.

Here on a weekday...the menu was extensive however for a place that is famous for pancakes...it's RIDICULOUS that yhey dont have a single gluten free pancake. Come on. Get with the times. Very exclusive to the allergy community. I left flabberghasted and hungry.
Food and service both terrible, got food poisoning from their chicken burger. Would never recommend

Way too overhyped. My oatmeal accidentally had eggs in it. How does that happen? The coffee tasted watered down and bitter. Also the place had a bad odor that lingered near our table. And the cooks don't use gloves... a lot of cross contamination. Just gross

I got food poisoning here. Don't go here! My husband and I both ordered burritos Friday, June 22. The only difference was my husband got chicken and I got the carnitas. Thankfully, I couldn't eat much of my burrito because it was so big but within an hour I started having severe stomach pains and got very sick. My husband was completely fine since he didn't have the carnitas but this is the third day and I'm still sick! I've tried calling the restaurant for 3 days now to talk to a manager and they're never there. So the issue is still unresolved. It's so disappointing because I actually liked this place before but I'll NEVER go back now.

And this is being nice about it. I come here lots and always eat the chicken & wontons with rice & they hit it normally on the spot . Today was the worst experience I had they forgot to clean the deep fryer and there was stuff from pervious orders in it then they cooked my chicken in it. I found exactly 11 burn pieces in my dish. The manager was friendly and explained it was due to dirty oil and apologized for the mistake ! You would think they would do a bit more for a regular customers? Very disappointed this time round will rate it on my next visit.so I got home after they serve me the chicken and wonton for the second time had more burnt pieces and I took them out and I just ate it because I was tired of waiting for my food I woke up the next morning around 730am vomiting and diarrhea with a touch of food poisoning as I called 311 and talk to an Alberta health nurse she told me it looks like it's a sign of food poisoning because that's the only thing I ate that day she suggested drinking plenty of water to try to flush it out there's nothing much more they can do. We called Earls talk to a manager who said that there is another complaint last night besides mine so they've closed down the deep fryer are there cleaning and scrubbing it also inform me that they're going to call the health board and have them come in and check to make sure the kitchen passes the Canadian health and food standards because I'm not the only person that got sick. I hope they find a way to make this better or I will make sure I tell everyone in Sherwood Park and anywhere not to eat at that Earls location ever ! nobody should be served food that was burnt bad the first time and then given it again when it was burnt again this time it only had four pieces in it I put the pieces aside again to show the manager. I guess the point is the first time when I was that badly burnt and I had 11 pieces that were burnt chicken and made the food taste funny they should Of just closed down to deep-fried right away. For my experience at this Earl's location it is always been good this is the first time I've had something this serious happened to me where I'm sick and I was quite shocked they only took off one chicken and wonton after putting us through waiting for our food again which they told me would be 10 minutes which was almost 20 wake up earls Sherwood Park time for a reality check. We spent almost $300 there for Terrible service! I can't even explain how terrible it was. We will never go back. I wanted to get the salmon tostada but didn't because she wasn't able to tell me what was in it (I have food allergies) We didn't even get any salsa with out tacos, my boyfriend ordered a burger with fries. He got a burger with salad and when he told the waitress he had asked for fries she just stared at him and walked away. I'm not spending $13 for a taco there again. The service was so bad that it made the food gross. Just go to the taco truck on milpas.

Great fish tank loved it so did the kids!! Service was good - the kitchen made an error by cooking with mushrooms and my family has allergies that we made them aware of when ordering. They apologized and the dinner was on them - very unexpected - and we were flawed by their attention to safety and customer satisfaction - manager was very on point and involved !!

Nacho Mama's Mexican Grill. Humm how to put this in the nicest way possible... It was a place with a seat on a rainy morning. Yup that's about it. The nausea and borderline food poisoning I got after eating here was the nail in the coffin for this place so far as I was concerned.

I'm gluten intolerant so this was on my list of restaurants in Nola that provide a gluten free menu. Most of the regular dinner menu with a few tweaks here and there I was able to have. I chose the fresh oysters to start which were very good although a couple hard pretty big chunks of grit in them. My partner got them baked which smelled divide topped with their garlicky cheesy goodness. The beet salad was good too although the beets were cooked a little longer than I normally like. The dressing was the perfect tangy amount of top. I chose the ribeye with sautéed vegetables on the server's suggestion. This is the main reason I gave this place 3 stars instead of 4. My steak came out thin and ragged where one of my friends who ordered the same thing got a nice thick juicy cut. I understand the fat content can make the cut look like mine did but it's disappointing nonetheless when two steaks arrive at the same table with this extreme disparity. I also ordered mine rare but it came out more medium instead. This irritates me the most when ordering a steak. But I will say the sautéed vegetables were some of the best ever- perfectly cooked with great garlic seasoning. I did give Luke a second try at brunch the next day since it was right around the corner from our hotel and again the gluten free knowledge. I got the crab omelet which was impressive with it's fresh large chunks of crab meat inside. But I also wanted the grits and was informed they weren't gluten free. Why add wheat to a wonderful product of corn is beyond me. My partner did get to enjoy the jalapeño cheese grits which he found thick, rich, and very good.

This has long been the only place that my guy and I would dine at in Clearwater Beach. Usually they're awesome, but this time I'm leaving mortified. All I wanted was the Grouper sandwich without cheese or bread (due to allergies). I was told that they can't do a lettuce wrap. Okay, that's fine, the usual toppings can go to the side. Not sure why it became an issue. Food came up and the toppings were missing. I asked to have those added to my plate and I was lectured about how the toppings are extra. I don't want extra toppings, just the toppings that come with the sandwich. Apparently the other employee had put my order in wrong, yet again, not only was I informed of that like it was my fault, but the guy who took my order starts talking about how I was wrong, knowing that I could hear him. I don't embarrass easily, but I walked away with my food feeling mortified. $28 for two Grouper sandwich combos. We're talking fast food here. I paid for a piece of fish, pickles, lettuce, and tomatoes that apparently is too difficult to assemble correctly. Also, if a customer is omitting half of what constitutes the sandwich- why not add an extra piece of lettuce to hold the protein? Unbelievable. If anyone at UB is reading this, try asking what the issue is before snapping at customers; also, the employees should govern themselves a little more professionally than speaking unwarranted and inaccurate frustrations loud enough that the costumer can hear. We won't be back.

Completely got my order wrong. I am gluten free and ordered a Hickory burger lettuce wrap with an extra patty. Not only did they not lettuce wrap it but it was the completely wrong burger and didn't even have the second party. When I called to let them know they didn't pick up the phone and when I tried to go back to let them know the restaurant was closed. Very disappointed!

Sadly, this place as gone down hill. I have given it 3 chances after deciding that it was bad. I really wanted to like it since it's a neighborhood staple, but the food and drinks are just terrible. :( Update: 3 hours later, I have food poisoning.

My spicy chicken sandwich with cheese was not spicy and it tasted like the Patty was about 3 hours old, it was hard and had zero flavor. My Coke was Miss marked as diet so I took a big big swig of what I thought was my Coke and it was the diet the diet was marked as my Coke. I am allergic to aspartame which is what diet Dr pepper is sweetened with. Spent the rest of the night with a migraine.

Food allergies beware!! Let me first say that the food was pretty decent albeit a bit pricey for what you get. This place is hipster heaven. Enjoy fashionable extreme high waters? Ever want to eat in an urban outfitters? This is the spot for you. The two stars is because the restaurant is pretentious. I am lactose intolerant and was forced to eat a muffin (that was not bad actually) because they refused to make substitution or accommodate for food allergies. Not a made up gluten allergy but a legitimate allergy that would have had me locked in the airplane bathroom for the duration of my 3 hour flight.

I love that they have the exotic meats. They are cooked well and very tasty. I loved the milk shake and iced tea. I'm giving 3 stars because I had cross contamination and got very sick. I have celiac disease and being a known gluten free resturant I had gotten sick 2 times I went there. I had the sweet potato fries and gluten free bun with elk burger and a banana milk shake with unsweetened ice tea and was sick within minutes. I called the General Manager, Eric and told him. He was very apologetic & also explained how his mom had celiac; which was comforting, and explained they have completely separated all gluten free cook wear, grills, toasters, utensils and plates. He explained sometimes it has happened by wait staff or busers not having experience or mixing them up. The only two times I had ever gone of course I had the new server. Eric immediately refunded me on the 2nd trip.(I didn't know at that time of 1st visit I had celiac disease so I'm not going to take that into consideration although I still ordered the same I just asked for no bun. I will say that I absolutely did NOT care for the very young waitress, chewing gum and rolling her eyes, who was short & very annoyed that I was asking so many questions. She clearly was completely uneducated about celiac's disease and the true reason behind gluten free: Bu saying "Like a lot of people come in and like order gluten free and like everyone likes it and stuff". I was being me and always overly nice and never saying a word even though I had 100% doubts after that ignorant remark. Especially because it's NOT a "fad diet"; although a lot of people jumped on the band wagon, it's a life or death situation for true Celiac's. Well not even 5 mins after finishing my meal I was in the bathroom violently ill and was all day after. The 3 stars are only for the General Managers excellence in customer service and for being totally awesome sharing he understood, & even shared his personal experience. I know he can only train, remind, review and go over with the staff & servers so many times. Most should know if working with food the importance and true facts about allergies with food, gluten free, and if using gloves that means not leaving them on while checking on regular bread then putting a salad together. I too was a young & inexperienced server, but when it comes to severe food allergies. I never messed that up. I even called ahead and asked many questions; But should have just asked for the Manager or General Manager right away. Maybe It would have been different. I'm nervous to try 3rd time but I will if I'm back in the city.

Just ok. My hubs had the cinnamon roll, it's giant but he wasn't overly impressed. I'm gluten free and the hostess said they don't have gluten free and she needed to inform me that anything I order, "there will be cross contamination". Also, we wanted a mimosa but can't get till 8am... and .75 cent up charge for a coffee refill. Meh.

Whoa! What an underwhelming experience. The 'whoa' is for my shock over this shop's super high (at the time of this writing) 3.5 rating. How did this place manage to secure a respectable 3.5-star rating? I was not only underwhelmed, but also a bit irritated. It felt almost like theft to offer me such a mediocre cup of flavored water in exchange for over $5. I am not a boba snob (or maybe I am, I don't know), but this was the worst boba experience I have ever had in my life. I have been frequenting boba establishments since the dawn of American boba in Southern California in the early 2000s. I love boba so much that I even moved to Taiwan for a year (really) and learned to speak Mandarin just so that I can drink all the cheap boba I could ever want. (Well, I went to Taiwan for multiple reasons, but the orgy of boba shops was definitely a factor.) Of course, when I went to Chatime here, I was not expecting a life-changing experience. I was not expecting to throw my head back in milky euphoria. We're in Tucson. I was just excited to discover that boba even existed here. I was merely looking for something that was drinkable. Something drinkable is not what I got. I ordered milk tea boba, the quintessential boba drink. It is usually the first item on any boba menu and it is probably the simplest (and most important) thing to get right. As soon as I received the drink, my smile quickly turned upside down. All I could do was stare blankly into space. The milk tea was really weak. No character. No life. I'm not even sure if it had real tea in it. Or milk. The tapioca balls (boba) were also disappointing. Not gooey and chewy. Just sugar-flavored, like the milk tea. I quickly finished the drink. I finished it not just to relieve my suffering; I sort of felt like my drink was suffering too. The deed was partly humanitarian. Aside from the drink itself, the place was just so dull. It was not comfortable. It was not inviting. It was sterile. It was sad. The cashier was nice. But something just didn't seem right with the guy. He had a lot of trouble with the money exchange (among other things). Not his fault, of course. But someone should be there supervising and guiding. Signs everywhere draw attention to the "50% off drink refills!" Has anyone ever asked for a refill? If so, please explain to me why you decided to subject yourself to a second serving. Boba doesn't require much genius. So, what the heck.. I gave it two stars because (1) I did NOT get food poisoning (great job!), and (2) the cashier was friendly.

Do not go here during peak times or in between lunch and dinner. If you drive through they will forget items from your order, even when the manager checks it. I'm lactose intolerant and the line was busy so I ordered a hot dog to go along with the burger just in case they forgot no cheese. When we checked it there was no hot dog and the burger had a chunk with cheese on it I had to cut off. I went in to ask for the hot dog and they gave me attitude so I just forgot about it. The best time to go here is after 11pm they have never got our order wrong or missed items. That is why I am giving them 3 stars because this is the culmination of 10 times visiting and 3 times were bad but 7 were great. The 7 times everything was fresh and the guy working the counter once even caught that my burger had cheese so he sent it back and asked them to cook a fresh one with now cheese.

I have been going to this place for years. It's mostly about the location. I can deal with the sometimes surly service and overpricing, but I finally hit my limit when I got real, honest-to-god food poisoning because of their poorly handled, lukewarm potato salad. I'm just coming around two days later. My complaint was met with indifference. Also, I LOVE the fact that I wasn't even told that my food was ready and that it sat on the counter for God-knows-how-long before I noticed it. AWESOME!

Cute, trendy atmosphere. This place is the equivalent of a carrot under a box for hipsters. Extremely limited menu: sandwiches, salads, and pizza. Don't expect any pasta dishes. No tiramisu either. Gluten free options for most choices, but very bread-focused. Sorry to my low-carb friends. I got the chicken parm (no bread) and the waitress offered to put it on a salad. I asked for arugula, no dressing or other toppings, but the waitress said the salads were pre-made. Strange, my appetizer (grilled cheese) arrived on a bed of arugula. Great to try, but I don't think this is the best Nashville has to offer.
Nastiest food ever! My Stromboli was burnt and on top of that I got food poisoning! Never again!

Wanted to like this place, I've been here 3 times The first time the food was delicious but 30 min after eating I got an upset stomach, thought it might just be me so I tried them again months later well not only did I get an upset stomach but I threw up everything. I Thought again okay maybe it's me. Upon the third time trying and me throwing up AGAIN I realized it's not me it's the food. Sorry I cant risk my health or the health of others. It's mainly vegetables so the question now is how did I get sick from eating only vegetables? Cross contamination and poor food safety.

We found ourselves in Reno's newly titled "Little Portland" neighborhood and after enjoying a late afternoon coffee and tea at See-See we decided to check out Sizzle Pie. Having lived in Portland from 2001-2007, I had my hopes up for a pretty special dining experience, like what you might enjoy in Portland's Pearl District. But I left with a much lighter wallet and not much else. I should preface this review by noting that we ordered a gluten free crust since my wife is gluten free. So comments regarding the crust should be ignored unless you're ordering the GF. We waited nearly an hour for our pizza. Some heads up from the counter staff would have been appreciated since we would not have ordered had we known it would take that long. When the pizza finally arrived, my first impression was that the the crust wasn't fully cooked. It was a bit pasty. My wife noted that it was better than some of the other GF crusts she's tried. So maybe a shade better than "meh". I don't mind spending money for good food. But $35 for a 14" pizza is kind of ridiculous. What did we get in the way of toppings for that $35? Pesto Sauce - Honestly the pesto sauce at Blaze Pizza is better Sausage - OK, but not very flavorful Basil Red onions - tasty Mushrooms - nothing special Cheese (Yes they charge you $3 if you want cheese on your pizza) Couple of other things. First they didn't bother to slice it so I had to take it up to the counter and get that done. When I looked back in the kitchen area, I saw two young men working. I fully admit that I don't know what all the food handling rules are, but one of the kids had very long hair and a ponytail but wasn't wearing any sort of head covering. The other worker did though. We won't be back to Sizzle Pie based on this experience. And in Reno's competitive foodie scene, I don't think this place will last long. So if you really want to try it, you might want to visit sooner rather than later. You can find better pizza for less than half the price.

Like others who have reviewed, I heard this place was closing and everyone was so sad about it. I get that. We don't want to see a small local business fail. Unfortunately this was a terrible experience. First and clearly the last. The restaurant itself looks charming. But the carpet is disgusting. No restaurant should EVER have two seater tables with one side facing the wall. It's very uncomfortable for that person. It doesn't matter if your with a loved one or not. We went for breakfast. So after the two things above were a concern, I was hopeful it ended there. Nope, we ordered our coffee. Terrible , terrible coffee. The coffee in any restaurant for breakfast sets the tone for the rest of the experience. My husband didn't even drink his. I drank 3 sips. I ordered their special - the quiche and hash brown. Hubs ordered ala cart (he's allergic to eggs which limited him on what he could get, but he's good about working with it). He got toast, sausage, hash brown, avocado. We waited no less than 30 min for our food. Once we got it we both took a bite of the hash brown. It was odd. That's the only way I can explain it. I didn't trust it. He cut into his sausage. It was still pink. The avocado was brown. His toast was dry and no butter or jam offered. My quiche was good, but nothing to brag about. So, he didn't eat anything. AT ALL! I ate my quiche. That's it. So, we asked our waiter for our check. Mentioned the sausage and avocado and he did remove it from our bill. Since I couldn't see anything but a wall, my hubs did say the manager/owner looked very flustered and overwhelmed. One last thing, as I looked at other reviews, I noticed no one from the restaurant responded to any of them. Good or bad reviews. This owner is not connected to the community. It's time. Make today Your last day!

Frozen yogurt is hardly frozen...it starts melting as soon as it hits your bowl. Just not as good (and way more expensive) than if you go to a kick-butt ice cream parlor and order their best sundae.

Atmosphere: dim lighting, Spanish style, clean, slick floor tiles, east to slip in heels. Outdoor pavers are very slippery in rain. We had a fall. Service: attentive, friendly with a somewhat annoyed by questions vibe. Bus boy is way over the top with trying to take away dishes that are not even half finished. Felt rushed. Felt uncomfortable with how he stood over top and lingered waiting to swoop in to take plates away, yet somehow we also ended up with completely empty plates from appetizer to desert. Food: Was presented nicely. I particularly had a problem with my food. I have celiac and am Gluten free. They were very untrustworthy as far as knowledge of what was gluten free. You can tell the cooks in the back are not true Italian for an "Italian" restaurant. I was told a specific salad dressing was gluten free, then later told it had "corn starch" so they weren't sure?? My salad had a lot of old rotten pieces in the plate. So I picked most of it apart, and ate it without dressing. The salmon that they assured me would be cooked separate, WITHOUT the crusting or sauce, came out with both. So I had to send it back. After waiting while everyone else ate; they brought out another plate they assured was cooked to be Gluten free... (plain) was not. I ended up throwing up all night. Price for the size of my salmon and 5 smaller than grape tomatoes sized potatoes was over priced. Overall: To inconsistent, and unknowledgeable in the culinary arts. I would consider this place to be decent. If you do not have any dietary restrictions and don't mind spending a lot of money per dish, plus a lot of up charges then you might enjoy it.
After an extremely long wait Dinner came out cold & undercooked Not at all seasoned tasted like a frozen $.99 dinner Icing on the cake woke up in middle of the night w food poisoning

Customer service was horrible. My order was incorrect and their worker cursed at me and tried to convince me that the order was correct. After cursing at me when I called she told me she would never correct our order again. Never will order here again!

I had high hopes for this place since it is in walking distance from my house. Unfortunately I just wasn't a fan. I got just a simple cheese pizza and the dough was bland and there just wasn't great flavor. I do like that they offer gluten free options and are working to add vegan meats and cheese to the menu. Love that this casino has an entire floor that is non-smoking. Having a Non-Smoking area does not help and is usually still contaminated with a lot of smoke. There is only free soda and water.
