Placed an order for lunch today and got a stir-fry and a dessert. Unfortunately I ended up finding a dead fly in my dessert. I'm so disgusted by this, and almost threw up. This is unacceptable and even more so because I'm pregnant.

I was super excited to get some good seafood during my trip go SB, but unfortunately Bluewater was a huge disappointment. If you're going there for a drink and to just hang out, it seems to be okay. The restaurant itself is really pretty inside, great location, and has a beautiful view of the water! We came into Bluewater shortly after 9 PM on a Friday night. Being that the kitchen closed at 10, I didn't think we were cutting it too close. (I've been in the service industry for over 10 years so I know how it goes!) The host suggested/pushed quite a few times that we sit at the bar, which we declined being that my partner and I were on a date for DINNER. Our waiter seemed to be slightly overwhelmed with the number of guests he was serving, so I felt as though he was rushing through our ordering process and my questions regarding ingredients due to my list of food allergies (and yes, they're legit). He was also very inattentive and slow to take our entree order which could have been the cause of our OVERLY lengthy stay at this place, not to mention it most likely caused the shortage in time taken to properly prepare the snapper that I ordered. First of all, it came out lukewarm at best- no big deal. When I cut into it, the middle was borderline raw with the outside and ends being overlooked. I showed our server (who didn't come back to check on us for a long time) and he said it seemed "normal" to him for red snapper, however I was uncomfortable eating it like that. Another employee assisted in the process of placing my fish onto a separate plate to take back to the kitchen. 10 minutes go by before she returned with THE SAME piece of fish I had cut up, and relayed a message from a cook who said "tell her that it's cooked fine, it's almost too done..I should know because I'm the one who cooked it." At this point, my fish was ice cold. It seemed as though it was a hard "no" from the kitchen in terms of preparing me a fresh piece, as this SAME piece has been toted all around the restaurant and back to my table. I ended up having to eat that same piece of rubbery, tasteless red snapper. It seemed to me as though the fish was frozen, quickly thawed for me, then thrown on the grill at high heat in order to rush it to me. I can't imagine how else it would have turned out so rubbery and inconsistent in texture and temperature. Our server did try to remedy the situation towards the end and seemed to be a little more empathetic. My partner had a steak dish that was decent, but nothing extraordinary. She didn't finish about 80% of her meal, so they offered to box it up for her. In the midst of us trying to figure out the check, and just being frustrated, we got into our cab and realized that the staff never brought her leftover dinner back to the table after being taken away to be "boxed up". This place has potential, but it was NOT worth the $

Bland food and dim bathroom lighting are the highlights. Not only was I scoffed at for requesting the tortillas on the side, but my fiance was not informed that guacamole was in his burrito. He is allergic to avocado. He brought this to the attention of the waitress and she acted like it was our fault and we should've known. We mentioned that it wasn't stated in the menu and she told us that yes it was. (It wasn't, I checked). We weren't going to waste time arguing. Add in ridiculously long wait times for service with only 3 tables of customers to serve. We have no desire to return.

The product is good but this location is poorly run. There is an unacceptable level of cross contamination between the pizzas, so don't go here if you have any allergies or dietary restrictions. The pizza boards they use to make the pizzas were filthy from the previous customers, and the cutting boards were also dirty. My friend found a pepperoni on his pizza, and he didn't order any! Also we came in at around 7:30 and they were out of a lot of toppings. The staff seemed annoyed that we were making them work, as opposed to chatting in the back room. All of these problems would be easily fixed by better management!

I visited Sociale last night with my husband.I ordered the Italian salad and chicken Milanese. The chicken was tasteless and the meat on the Italian salad was rancid. I took two bites and was up for 12 hours vomiting. Followed by a daylong visit to the ER which confirmed food poisoning. My husband ordered the sliced sausage which made his stomach upset; terrible reflux all night long. This was our second visit. The first visit, we had rancid crab meat on our deviled eggs. We will never ever go back here again

This place is a total dump. The beat up seating and the flies buzzing were a nice touch, but the hamburger meat was the big winner. It tasted as if it was purchased as cheaply as possible, then frozen for a year, and then left out for a few days before cooking and serving. I can't imagine the condition of the kitchen. *Shudder. This place is the first stop on your way to hospitalization for food poisoning.
My daughter ate here last night and has been throwing up ever since. The first thing she vomited was uncooked burger. Check your burgers to be sure they are done before eating here.

Not only was the service slow and the food undercooked, our chef cross contaminated raw meat and dirty dish rags with everything he put on our plates. After all that, the manager was offensive, accusing our complaint of being racially charged -- when in reality, the chef was outright untrained. Worst dining experience I have ever had.

What a huge disappointment. First the good...really aesthetically pleasing space, good looking menu and a truly lovely and engaging server (Amanda). But the bad unfortunately outweighed the good to the point that this will be my first and last visit. We arrived around 2:45 on a Saturday and proceeded to order a couple of delicious cocktails, followed shortly but their meat and cheese board (also very good) as an appetizer. I'd explained to the server that I had a couple of allergies (including gluten) and she passed that on to the kitchen immediately with reassurances that there would be no issue with accommodating them. Fast forward 15 mins after receiving our app, and our server very apologetically informed us that the kitchen was closing for the transition to the dinner menu and would only be serving their pizzas (no gluten free option there)!!! Upon asking when they'd be returning, we were told it would be over an hour and 15 mins. Since I had planned on ordering their tuna tataki (all raw and requiring no cooking), we asked if she could check if they could please squeeze that in since we weren't given any advanced notice that this would be happening. She came back a few minutes later to let us know that the kitchen refused. I was left unable to order anything else and my birthday lunch was cut severely short. I'm assuming that since we were just a 2-top and the only ones in the dining room, the kitchen simply didn't concern themselves with our experience and whether we'd be returning. Having worked in both fine and casual dining, I can honestly say that I've never seen anything like this. A truly bizarre and disappointing experience.
2 out of 3 dishes were cold. One was ordered with a gluten free option, wasn't told the item was available until the dishes were brought out. Service was nice and food tasted decent

After reading reviews that Green Basil happily accommodates vegan and vegetarian diets, I ordered delivery specifying that everything must be vegan like this: (***** VEGAN PLEASE *****). Normally if a restaurant cannot accommodate this, they have the courtesy of contacting me to let me know. Green Basil did not contact me and delivered two curries. Satisfied with the meal, we attempted to dine in a few days later. When we asked about making our curry vegan again, we were informed that they do not make vegan curries because they use fish sauce in all their curries. That means that instead of contacting me to let me know they could not make my curry vegan, they just sent me a non-vegan dish. Luckily I am not allergic to fish, but had there been an allergy that would be a VERY DANGEROUS situation. I am extremely unhappy that I was not contacted before my food was delivered to let me know my request could not be completed. I was, however, informed that I needed to approve a +$1 update since i added tofu to my veggie dish. To me, this is inexcusable and I cannot dine here again. I feel obligated to warn others who may encounter the same issue.

Our server, she was very friendly and knowledgeable about gluten free foods and even double checked with the cooks. The food and drinks were good, it was a little pricey but we went for a nice dinner. The table we sat at was extremely small and uncomfortable. Took an hour for us to get seated, and about another 45min to get our food. They were just super busy.

The food wasn't bad, but from what we witnessed, a health inspection is definitely in order. We were seated by the window and saw a van pull up to the front entrance full of trash bags driven by what appeared to be a homeless woman in a bathrobe. We initially thought the restaurant staff was bringing her food they hadn't sold as an act of charity, but were horrified to witness her and the restaurant staff pawing through garbage bags filled with produce. They would place bananas and things on the street to organize them (my mind went to the possibility of dog feces, car chemical run off, general dirt and grime on city streets now being in our food in trace amounts.) There was also a box full of fruit that fell into the street gutter that the van driver placed back into their container. Please see photos of how I can only assume this restaurant gets all of their produce (The second photo, although blurry, is a restaurant employee taking the box of the street-contaminated produce to the kitchen.)

Wow-- looked forward to#1 rated Indy restaurant for Brunch. 45-minute wait in sweltering heat was tolerable, but moved into 75-minutes for seats at the bar. Tea and coffee ok and plenty of refills. Food allergies caused pause on some dishes (with disclaimer on menu of no moderations in dishes allowed)and some questions were answered, others got the response, "Not sure." The grilled cheese was soggy with oil and a runny egg on top, only 3 bites before stomach started reacting. Waffle was miniature, tasty and drenched in syrup. Blueberries and apricots on top were delightful. Sorghum bacon-- very thick and charred-overrated, just like entire experience for a $40 breakfast.
CLOSED. A new favorite. High Asian with a southwest twist. Excellent. Gluten free menu, knowledgeable staff.

What the hell happened to this place? When I was in high school, Arner's was one of our hangouts. Coffee, breakfast, mile-high pie. Did the food get that much worse or did I just get a better palate? At any rate, we went tonight. I said, "I'm going to order breakfast. It's really hard to f--- up breakfast." I shouldn't have tempted fate. My husband got a French toast combo. He loved the sausage and bacon that came with it, thought the French toast was decent, and said the eggs were weird. He made out okay. My 18 month old got the pancake that was supposed to have a chocolate chip smiley face. It looked like that face got melted with a hot iron. Oh, and his was the one that came with the sausage as wide as his forearm. (For a kid's meal? Really?) We ordered him a side of scrambled egg. They charged us $2.99 for it and it came out a pile of gray shreds. I'm not even exaggerating. My son, who LOVES eggs, who NEVER refuses eggs, wouldn't eat it. He hated it so much he pushed it off his plate. And then there was me. I ordered an omelet and tater tots with an English muffin. The tots were deep fried in grease that wasn't the right temperature - they were more oil than potato. But the omelet itself was the worst. It was raw inside. Yes, there was goopy, raw egg running into the cheese and making me want to vomit. Did I mention it took them 30 minutes to make this meal? Just long enough that my super well-behaved kid, who waited patiently for the first 25 minutes, started to lose his isht. And then I couldn't even find someone to give us the bill. Eventually, a woman who hadn't served our table came by. I told her the omelet was raw, I didn't want them to remake it, and I wasn't paying for it. I offered to pay for the English muffin, which I did eat. Then I took my son out to the car while my husband paid the bill. It came to $17, folks...and that's WITHOUT my meal added in. My child's melted-face pancake and gray egg was $7.98. What in the actual f---? We will NEVER step foot in Arner's again, not even for the pie. I should have known better when we pulled up on a Wednesday night and there were literally four other cars in the parking lot. Eat at your own risk. You've been warned.
Cute trendy spot with yummy food and gluten free options. The orange juice is an absolute must! The downside is that the wait was 2 hours long for a typical brunch.
The chicken fingers were ok. Crispy but a little pricey. DON'T ORDER the brisket and cabbage egg rolls!! They taste like vomit in a crispy wrap.

I'm so upset that I wasn't feeling my best on my recent voyage on the Steamboat Natchez, the experience was so much fun and so informative that I used every ounce of my strength to hold it together just long enough to make it to the end of the trip. As some others have pointed out, and the staff of the Natchez will remind you. This is the only and LAST real Steamboat on the Mississippi. The boat was so vintage and cool, and had I not been rife with the flu bug I may have taken more chances to explore. The decks were great as they provided ample shade and sun exposure depending on your pleasure. The dining hall was like that of a fancy restaurant from a time gone by long ago. I didn't partake in any eats but from what I saw it looked pretty tasty. The bar was well stocked and my Pimms Cup was just tops and totally refreshing - thanks for the bar staff for handling the crowds like real professionals. My favourite part of the trip was our captain/voiceover person who announced and described all that we were seeing along our trip and gave exceptional historical context to every part of our trip. I seriously think that guy has a career in voiceover work for commercials. That or I'd like to hire him full time to narrate my life day to day - basically almost a good as Morgan Freeman in my books! Now I can't be sure if this was caused by my flu, the heat, the boat - which seemed to move along smoothly, or a combination of all three, but sometime before we docked I got super woozy and barely made it to the little boys room before unleashing all hell. Yep I was the guy who threw up while on a boat - it's never happened before and for some reason it happened this time. As a warning, if you typically get motion sickness,take a gravol before boarding - it might just save you from the same embarrassment I suffered. I need a do-over on the SN when I'm not feeling under the weather, however what I was able to experience was just tops. Thanks to the staff for being so friendly, I'll definitely be back and recommend that all my NOLA bound friends check you out!

I drive past this place frequently and finally decided to stop in. They have La Segunda Bread. That's some damn fine Cuban bread! Feed the cows! For a small price, they will give you a helping of veggies they've cut up for the bovines out back and you and your littles can go feed them. They will thank you, your kids will thank you and you, might just enjoy the break from being on the computer. Get some local produce, fruits and veggies, some herbs and meat too. THey've got hives now, so Honey is there as well. This is a nice agribusiness!

As someone who is allergic to wheat I haven't had decent pasta in nearly a year since I was officially diagnosed with my allergy. They claim to make gluten friendly pasta since it has shared equipment with the other pasta. I went out on a limb and decided to see if it triggered an allergic reaction since I so desperately wanted pasta. Let me tell you, hands down best pasta I've had in so long! Even their gluten friendly pasta easily trumps many other standard wheat pastas I've had in the past. Best part is, is that the pasta is made from scratch so you can literally order anything from their menu to be made gluten free. It's a bonus that great quality food also comes in large portions. My 6'-7" 300 lb college football brother couldn't even finish his calzone! I'm in love and can't wait to come back!!

Came here to celebrate my son Joey's 5th birthday. He visited us for a week since he lives with my parents (my boyfriend says he's allergic to him) and I was dying to take him out to his first restaurant. He sat in between me and my boyfriend on the floor and was so well behaved that we decided to pour some beer on the ground for him to lick up - it was his 5th birthday after all. Yea so you can bring your dog here, and they'll even bring you a bowl of water for them to chill with. The menu is very English, and that made it really hard for me to choose something to eat...because I didn't really want anything on the menu. It was confusing to pair things together because they had all these delicious sounding sides and these yecky entrees - like calf's liver blech - that I wasn't sure how to game plan my meal. I ended up ordering three sides together while the boo had a burger and the duck egg rolls. The roasted brussel sprouts with bacon are delish, buttery enough that it ends up not being a healthy option. I also got the roasted cauliflower which was meh - tasted like roasted cauliflower, nothing special. I was really excited for the goat cheese polenta. It tasted more like fondue...and not like goat cheese. It was dark so I couldn't see if the color even resembled goat cheese. I used it to dip my cauliflower into, but I regretted ordering it. Should've gotten the bacon apple bread pudding. The duck confit egg rolls were pretty tasty with a dark brown sweet sauce - not sure what it was. The boo's burger was nice - he said it tasted like a burger on an english muffin, which is what it was. I'd rather just go here to drink and eat french fries.

Got bad food poisoning here from eating a turkey sandwich on Friday 12/22. Reporting this incident. Have ruled out all other sources. Really put a dent in christmas plans! Last time I was here, I found a long black hair in my sandwich. You guys need to check your cleanliness procedures. Will not ever be coming back.

I came by here in early summer during a weekend getaway with college friends. We wanted to grab a nice breakfast before the drive back home. Honestly, Fiona C has perfectly worded EVERYTHING I would want to say about this place. Everything on the menu looked amazing and it took forever for me to decide what to get. The food was prepared beautifully and the servings were enormous, I should have shared! My favorite part though was probably my salted caramel latte. Unlike snobby coffee shops that charge for syrup/soy, this place includes it! Super nice for those who are lactose intolerant because hey, having to pay extra to avoid being gassy sucks! My reasons for not giving 5 stars are more of personal preference, I'm just not a huge American breakfast lover! Definitely a great brunch spot though!

Beware..if you show up and sign in, but a larger party comes in AFTER you, they will seat the larger party first, even if you have been waiting 20 minutes. Also, if you get all you can eat and leave leftovers, they will charge you for the leftovers at their discretion. Subpar sushi at best and food poisoning at your own risk.
My son ate at this location and got a very severe case of food poisoning He was hospitalized for 2 days due to salmonella.

Admittedly, I am a "pizza snob"; I do love all three styles though, Chicago, New York, AND St. Louis...much to the chagrin of fans of the former two. I had very high expectations of Pi, great name, a few friends had been there with moderately good experiences, but pizza snobs...err "aficionados", they are not. So before a concert at a venue nearby we decided to finally try Pi. We had to stand and wait for a table(usually a mark that the food is good, mistake number one). Finally we were seated, next to a "gaggle" of self important twenty-somethings that were apparently having a contest to see who could be the loudest AND the most annoying. We left before a winner was declared, and we stayed for the entire meal....ahh, the real reason there were no seats, people just sit there and hang out and have "annoyance contests". Normally I would not complain about such patrons, but they were NOT the only table like that. So I do hold Pi responsible for not "encouraging" their customers to "eat it and beat it"...lol. The menu...ugh...I went to a California Pizza Kitchen(or whatever they were/are called) ONCE, and only ONCE, and it was not by choice(women can make you do the craziest of things....). Pi's menu was a very unpleasant flashback to that day of terror and pizza "abuse". I am not adamantly against trying new toppings on pizza, or even odd combinations of ingredients. But what they did was NOT offer what I consider to be "staples" of pizza toppings. Instead they had a plethora of pretentious preconcocted pizzas pacifying my poor palette...yep, thats Pi in a nutshell for ya.... Nutshell....I think that was a topping offered...SMH.... So I figure they have to have the standard pepperoni and sausage, right? The server actually had to go in the back to ask. We should of left then, we did not; mistake number two. Once I finally got approval for my "specialty" pizza it was nearly an hour of listening to the before mentioned gaggle contest next to us before my burnt, and I mean BURNT thin crust pizza arrived. I said something about the BLACK bits all over my tray and the sever said, without a flinch, "Oh that's how its supposed to be"...ugh. Since we were on a timetable for a show now, I didnt have the time or energy to argue. I then, against all common sense and fiber in my pizza loving body took, a bite of my "pizza". This wasnt pizza dough, this was filo dough...maybe two or three pieces. I like THIN pizza, and I mean THIN, but this was beyond ridiculous, however it did go a long way to explain why they didnt want my "greasy" toppings on it. So I put "disgusting piece number one" down and tried for a middle piece, thinking that it might not of suffered the same burnt wrath of its outer brethren. No dice....it was FUSED to the platter(too greasy?, or did it sit too long in the back AFTER being cut???). I have worked in award winning pizza shops, I know the do's and dont's; at least for "regular" pizza. And I know if you cut a pizza too soon, or cut it and let it sit and cool, it WILL fuse to the platter. So I basically scraped the toppings off, ate them(mediocre at best) and left what they called a crust behind, untouched except for that one lonely piece that I had managed to get off the platter, along with the fork/knife marks left behind from trying to liberate the rest of my "Pi" from its "platter prison". Not only should they not be making pizza, they should not even be allowed such a clever name as "Pi". However they do keep popping up all over the area, so who knows....I do know that between my pizza disaster, my wife's Gluten Free pizza, that SURPRISE....WASNT GLUTEN FREE(yeah we missed the show cause she got sick), that I spent nearly $75 RUINING our night and spent another night to the Emergency Room. "Pi"...infinite possibilities to ruin an evening out and almost killing my wife. Needless to say, we will NEVER go back...unless it is to celebrate a "closing".

The waitress was fair. The cook was HORRIBLE, ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE! My 12 year old son has a shellfish allergy and the cook did not take that very well when I told him that my son's food needed to be cooked separately or before everyone else's. The cook rolled his eyes and blew his breath when we explained to him how severe my son's allergy. The cook then proceeded to have an attitude as he explained to us how he would have to go all the way back in the kitchen to rearrange and to re-prepare all of the food. Not only did his attitude and rudeness upset me, but upset my family and especially my son as well. IT WAS MY SONS BIRTHDAY!!!!! The cook is EXTREMELY RUDE and needs to be fired for just his rudeness alone. He needs to be taught better etiquette and manners and they need to apologize for their rudeness. I am sure there are other people that have food allergies and they need to be able to handle it better. Also.., the floors were sticky, the place was dirty, there was grease covering the heater and the burner that looked like it had not been sanitized or cleaned. The bathrooms were unclean, there was bugs in the florescent lighting in the bathroom. This place was atrocious. Also the food was just awful and not cook the way you asked for it to be. I think that the BBB needs to come inspect this place and it needs to be condemned. RUDENESS is uncalled for, especially when you are paying almost 30 dollars a plate. Will NEVER come to this place again.

Wish I could give 0 stars. We had a reservation and weren't seated until 30 minutes past our reservation time. Then, almost no ones order was correct at the table. Forgot two sides of fries, gave one of us fried fish instead of chicken tenders. Luckily it wasn't given to one of the people at the table with a severe seafood allergy. Never got refills on our drinks. Overpriced & overhyped for how underwhelming the food and service was.

Went in to eat because it looked from the outside a nice, trending spot to eat. Went inside and got seated in the corner away from everyone in the restaurant except for the party room. The party room then opened up and out came a baby shower that took tons of pictures in front of our table and didn't even flinch to say sorry. Not only was the party rude, our server came by our table once to bring an extra cup of coffee which the coffee itself was served in an extremely small cup to begin with. The food was not good at all and it was way too expensive. One small pizza was $24.00. When asked about Gluten free options I was treated like I didn't know what was gluten free myself. Another server came over and explained that most of the menu was gluten free and the pizza could be made with cauliflower crust. I wanted to explain to him the difference between can be gluten and it has to be gluten free. So we ordered and the service turned from bad to horrible. We will not return and discourage others to not go as well. I really enjoy the modernism of SOHO restaurants and the availability to eat out sometimes. This experience was horrible!

If you have to self aggrandize yourself, then you really know you are in trouble. An example that comes to mind is when we were driving through South Carolina and stopped at a place that self titled themselves as having the best breakfast in the country. What we ended up getting was greenish steak and eggs and a crab omelet that sent the Girly into vomit mode. N'awlins Cafe & Spic is another example. This is a place that should NEVER, ever serve food to people...ever. If you want gumbo that would make a geriatric go, "Hey! Where's the flavor?" then this might actually be a place you might want. And as someone else mentioned, they don't clean their shrimp too well. All in all, you can pay less and get more and better all over the place. Keep walking.

Food is slightly above average. I had a weird waiter at the bar area that kept asking for me to pay in cash or tip him in cash even before the food has come. Is this the service standard in NoLa or did I get a waiter reject? He just said "I only got one dollar all night and scolded me how I needed to tip in cash." It takes a long time to build a loyal customer but just one has experience to lose them. I was also told that since I'm allergic to shellfish that he can ask the chef to fry the catfish in a different oil but I would need to pay for the meal in cash. What is going on here?

I am giving two stars because my dinner the pollo franchese was very delicious. Aside from that the service was poor and the atmosphere was not impressive. Before we walked in there was a sign that had early dinner specials from 3-5pm every day. We walked in at 3:45 pm and the waiter asked if it was our first visit which we said yes. He brought us regular dinner menus and proceeded to push the most expensive items. He said there was a full bar but when I asked for two different alcohols they did not have either. When I mentioned the early dinner he then brought us a special menu. My mother asked for gluten free pasta which he said they had and then came back and said they didn't. My mom ordered grilled chicken with sautéed spinach, he brought her lettuce with chicken on top. Again my plate was good but no one else enjoyed their meals and the service was not good. I would not go back nor recommend.

*The only reason that I am giving this another star besides one, is because the red fish fajita's are absolutely amazing. Other than that- the entire experience deserves a ONE star.* Or waitress did not introduce herself. She came up to us and greeted us by pushing alcohol on us. Telling us all about her drink and shot specials, neglecting giving us her name or telling us anything about the food. We were not interested in drinking. We ordered queso for an appetizer. We finally get it, and I take a bite.... and what ever the hell she gave us was SWEET! Tasted like chocolate! I almost threw up from the surprise!!! I was expecting cheese... NOT SOMETHING SWEET. We tried getting our waitresses attention for about 5 mins to tell her about the screw up. We finally just asked another waitress. Our waitress acted as if she had no idea what could've been served to us and she takes it back into the kitchen. She comes back, telling us how she's making us fresh queso and it is currently in the microwave. I'm a server, and we do heat up some foods in the microwave too... but that's just something you never say. Lol. Then she tells us that it probably tasted weird because the queso has been sitting out all day and has probably gotten old. YOU NEVER SAY THAT TO A TABLE!!!!! I couldn't help but laugh!!!! Wow! I ordered the Redfish Fajita's as my entree. They were amazing! I highly recommend this. But please, whoever the owner may be, get rid of your singer! He is not all that great, and why on earth is he a Hispanic man, in a Mexican restaurant, singing only Elvis songs? He came up to me and my mother who were enjoying conversation between each other, and interrupted us asking if we had any song requests. We simply said thank you, but no thanks. He then kept talking to us... almost disturbing us. He eventually asked us our names and then left our table. Then he got back to his guitar and microphone, and said our names, getting mine wrong... lol.... dedicating a song to us. Then came BACK TO OUR TABLE AGAIN... asking us how we liked it. I'm sorry but it was very obvious that he was begging us for tips... he went above and beyond... resulting in disturbing us. The fajita's are really good. But the service is terrible, and verrrrry inexperienced and unprofessional and it shows! I would have also really appreciated if they would have admitted to what they gave us to eat on accident instead of queso. I just want to know what I ate and what was mixed up... it would've been so much better to admit to the mix up than to tell us that "it was sitting out all day and old." Fresh queso or old queso... it's never SWEET!

I have Celiac disease (which requires me to eat strictly gluten free), which means going on vacation is difficult because I can't just pop in somewhere. I need to research, look at ingredients beforehand and then decide. I was staying at a nearby hotel and stopped by Salty's for breakfast, because I saw 2 options that I thought were GF. One was an omelet and the other was a scrambler with eggs and potatoes. I informed my waitress that I had a gluten allergy (the best way to explain I need to eat gluten free....celiac means nothing to waitstaff who have not heard of it..) and I asked about the ingredients in the scrambler, which the menu claimed to include roasted potatoes. I was told that there were no gluten ingredients. My dish arrived, I took a bite and the potatoes were fried. I know...you're thinking...soooo? Potatoes themselves are GF, but when they are fried in a fryer that all other food (battered fish, chicken, etc) is in, they are no longer gluten free. So therefore, I was not given a GF dish, even though I asked and informed my waitress. I called the manager over and explained. He took the dish away and I ordered an omelet. When the bill came, the scrambler and the omelet were on it...the staff was apologetic, but at that point, it didn't matter. I know not everyone knows what Celiac disease is, but if someone said they had a peanut allergy, you wouldn't serve them something fried in peanut oil. Restaurants should take the responsibility to educate their staff on basic food allergies. Gluten free is absolutely necessary for people with Celiac disease. I didn't want to spend my vacation sleeping and sick because of one roasted potato, and I took every step within my power to prevent it. EDUCATE STAFF AND MARK MENU FOR SAFE ALLERGEN CHOICES.

I wanted to like this place more than I did. First the atmosphere - I did like the clean, open and modern feel. I did not use the restrooms but I noticed a long vanity with two sinks along one wall in the dining area that was very unusual and a little uncomfortable feeling and must admit I don't like it. I tried several dishes to get a feel and satisfy my cravings that night. I started out with the fried calamari. In an Asian restaurant I pretty much expect this to be a tempura batter or at least panko. These looked like the typical pre-breaded frozen calamari rings you can buy in the grocery and they pretty much tasted as much. Not particularly fresh and just a hit of toughness that comes from not being fresh or slightly overcooked. Next was the shrimp tempura. This was just ok. The only thing that kept it from being good to great was was such a small thing but the whole difference. The tempura batter was not cooked enough or the oil temp was not hot enough when they were dropped.It was soft, but not soggy, instead of crispy. My biggest disappointment came in the Korean fried chicken wings. I wanted to try both sauces but on the side for several reasons. I wanted to taste them plain. I knew something would be going home with me and probably some of these and the calamari rather than the tempura so if they weren't sauced, they would reheat and crisp up better. And because I wasn't sure of which sauce I would prefer. I was told that they cannot send them out plain because they can't finish the dish that way. Well finish the dish out must have meant sprinkle the sesame seed on top of the sticky sauce coated wings and have it stick. I was not crazy about either sauce and particularly disappointed that they both had a good bit of sugar in them as I am diabetic and it's just something not needed to make the sauces good. And since I did take most of them home, they were soggy and did not crisp back up with reheating. I also asked them if their crust was gluten free and the waitress could not answer me nor the hostess but she said they could make it gluten free. That sort of made me uncomfortable with bringing my friend that truly has celiac here. We had another place that made all of their kfc and sauces gluten free. Overall it was an okay experience but not good enough that I really want to go back. There are several places that do these dishes well nearby though they don't all try to attempt so many different Asian styles under one roof.

DISCLAIMER: I'm probably spoiled coming from the DC area, where Ethiopian cuisine abounds. I came to Abyssinia on a weeknight, and the place was mostly empty, as expected. Service was fast and friendly. The food was fine. I tried a meat and veggie combo that had chicken, beef, and lamb. The spicy beef was the clear star of the show. I didn't really want more than one or two bites of the chicken, because it was a bit tough and not nearly as flavorful. The lamb tasted like it might have gone bad, so I didn't eat much of that either. My dining companion did eat quite a bit of the lamb and literally vomited later in the day. The veggies were fine. The more flavorful of the lentils had a fishy taste I wasn't a huge fan of, but they weren't bad. The other was bland. On the plus side, their enjera was great. I would consider trying this place again, but sticking with vegetarian options or beef.

I want to start this review by saying that we have been coming here since before the pandemic and loved it. Now we've moved to Largo, just down the street and became regulars. The gluten free offerings are freshly baked and taste like normal baked goods, and are delicious! The coffee is the best, and their oat milk lattes and mochas taste as creamy as the dairy we can't have any more. Service has always been top notch and friendly, and we happily swing in any time we drive by or our son yells out 'Bellair Coffee!' We REALLY appreciated their adherence to mask wearing and as such gave them all our coffee loving, GF eating business. Sadly, this appears to have stopped, even if the pandemic has not. As the parents of a child not old enough, or able, to be vaccinated, we'll be going to the Starbucks drive through I guess. I'd much rather give our large coffee drinking budget to a local place with delicious everything...but safety comes first and I'm disappointed to see where their priorities lie.

Sad. We really liked this place the first two visits. Tonight was just bad. The food wasn't terrible, just ok tho. The fiesta salad came with a honey mustard dressing...? Gross, but at least it was on the side. The service was the worst part of the night. The waitress seemed very friendly at first until I asked her if she could please check to see if the lemon vinegarrette was dairy free for the salad that I ordered. I have some food allergies but I was really trying to not be a pain. I simply said if you find out if it has dairy please just bring me oil and vinegar, no biggie. She seemed really put out when I asked this of her. I requested no cheese and no pita in the salad. It came with no cheese but with pita (which I just picked out because I could not get her attention... even though she walked past us at least 10 times she would stare straight ahead). I had also ordered a side of savory tots. They didn't come with the meal so halfway thru I had to say "excuse me" twice a little loud because she ran past us again. She swung around and when I asked if the tots were on the way still she looked bewildered but said "yes!" and ran away again. Over ten more minutes went by, no tots. We were both done eating. She had swung by and refilled the empty Arnold palmer glass with water. We didn't say anything still... then she brought the check. I said to her "when the tots come out please just box them up to go?" She looked bewildered again and said "ok!" and ran off. I looked at the bill and yep-no tots on there. She came by to get the card from me and I just said, "the tots aren't on there so please just don't bother". She said, "ok." Then came back a minute later to say "they're on their way anyway!" with a smile. So we smiled and tanked her and waited. And waited. Almost almost ten more minutes... the tots arrived in a to go box. We left quickly. Thank you for the free tots that we waited over 25 minutes for... she obviously forgot to include them not one but twice then just gave them to me. Which is nice but what a disaster... and waste of time. Just very disappointing overall because we did like this place but I can't see us going back, honestly.

My boyfriend and I went here a few days ago and we used a coupon for buy a meal $5.99 and up and get a Mexican pizza for free. First off, they forgot to make the pizza and then they rushed it and it's supposed to have beans and beef in it. The lady on a disgusting amount of beans on one side and then very little beef on the other side. My boyfriend could not eat it. He said it tasted gross and it looked like baby vomit. Also my burrito was hot on the outside and cold on the inside. Like they heated up the tortilla and used old ingredients for the inside.

I am giving this restaurant three stars because the first two times we ate there, we found the food to be delicious and the service to be extremely attentive and friendly. If not for tonight, I would have given it four stars for sure. I have been grateful to have it as an addition to our neighborhood. That is until tonight which was quite a different story. Any restaurant can have a bad night, and this may have been an isolated incident, but this was an all-around disappointing experience. Let's just say that if it was our first meal there, it would have been our last. The service was lackluster from beginning to end. Our server seemed to be put out from the moment he arrived at our table, never told us the specials, brought the cauliflower appetizer with the entrées (we did not request this), and seemed aloof and disinterested in serving us or anyone else (on his phone in the back room). When my husband asked if we could possibly get some bread before our meal arrived, another server pleasantly agreed while letting us know that they do not do bread service. The bread that we were brought was four very thin (1/4" thick), very small (1 1/2" round--seriously this small) slices of baguette. For a table of 4. We had to make an additional request in order to get olive oil because no butter or olive oil was offered. I am vegan and this restaurant is not meant for vegans which I understood before going. In the past, they have very graciously accommodated my dietary preferences. Our server did kindly check the ingredients on the gluten-free pasta before I ordered to assure I could eat it. This was definitely his shining moment and most appreciated. The pasta, itself, was prepared well with a delicious assortment of vegetables. However, the "marinara" was more watery tomato broth than sauce and the pasta and vegetables sat unappetizingly in an inch of this liquid. My son had the avocado toast which was so drenched in olive oil that it was practically inedible. The aforementioned cauliflower appetizer is flash-fried and, particularly compared to previous visits, was disappointingly soggy and flavorless. The salmon and the pescatore were okay, but not up to the quality/taste of previous visits. The manager was present and with only three tables occupied in the entire restaurant never once came to check to see how our meal was. Perhaps the regular chef was off or on vacation? Perhaps it was just an off night. We may try Avalon Bistro again, but we are definitely in no rush to return.

The food was mediocre, the rice in my burrito wasn't cooked all the way. My boyfriend and I got juices also. Mine was wayyyy too tart and his didn't even taste like what he ordered. The worst part was they were cutting so many onions that the air was contaminated and my boyfriend's and my eyes were on fire the entire time. It got so bad we had to leave and I couldn't open my eyes for a couple minutes outside. I won't be going back, ever.

im generally a fan of any restaurant that doesn't laugh or hang up the phone when i ask if they offer any gluten free options. the girl on the phone was super helpful and let me know which items were safe or could be modified to be safe. i should also mention that the food was VERY good and i assume they are also very careful of cross contamination after mention of a food allergy because i had no problems after eating their food any of the times i've ordered food from them.

Strawberry lemon eegee tasted chemical/plastic flavor thought it may be the spoon or straw nope tried it again when I got home spit it out threw it away! Other people have had this issue I almost threw up when my coworker had me try hers a month ago(from another location) quality control or how they store them hopefully it will change but I won't be getting an eegee for a very long time!

came into this restaurant for the 1st time with high expectations seeing that this is philly's 1st official pokè spot. i ordered a large bowl which was averagely priced compared to other pokè spots in the US. i ended up getting food poisoning only a few hours after eating here and am still throwing up and suffering effects from the food a couple of days later even after a doctors visit. my 1st and last time eating here. there goes the high expectations i had for this newly opened place!

As an avid lover of all things brunch I would say this place has neither been the best nor worst establishment I have ventured to. Living in the city I do appreciate reminding myself of the local flares that brought me here in the first place, but I would say Katie's is a bit too limiting in food options. I believe that a meal is only enhanced by the complementing variety of sides and was thoroughly disappointed when my crabmeat frittata was "riding solo" on the plate. I was intensely craving a side of greens or fresh fruit that came with so many other plates. Anyway, the vibe fit the small neighborhood feel but could really use some work in updating their menu items. I need some more flavor added and hit up some gluten free options for us who need a break from the egg.

This place doesn't even deserve a one star! Do not go here!!! Had crawfish etoufee and it was barely warm, but was so hungry I didn't send it back. Also had the oysters on half shell. Terrible as well. I woke up at night with food poisoning! Makes you wonder how long ago the health inspector hasn't been there. Stay away!!!

GLUTEN-FREE? THINK TWICE BEFORE GOING HERE. We visited Nashville last 4th of July and our first stop was Butcher & Bee after doing research on some of the best new restaurants in town and places where we could order a late dinner. You might wonder why I am writing a review 6 months after the fact, but I can't stop thinking about this terrible experience, which I have recounted to many friends both in Nashville and beyond, so I just finally had to do it. We hit traffic on our way in, so we were later than we expected, but we got to the restaurant around 10. We decided to sit at the bar, which ended up being a mistake, but the tables were relatively empty, and I thought the service might be quicker at the bar. Immediately I notice that the bartender (gentlemen with a beard and Hawaiian shirt -- could describe anyone in Nashville but that's what he looked like) was complaining quite loudly to the other bartender and bar back and servers (anyone who would listen) about how he was filling in for someone's shift and was very ticked off that he still had to be there (insert lots of profanity here). The environment felt tense because he was so upset, so we sat and waited quietly. Probably 10 minutes after we get seated, he asks if we want anything; we both order cocktails and sheepishly ask for waters. Another long wait and we finally get our cocktails, but he doesn't ask if we want food. Sit there awhile longer, finish our drinks, and finally he comes back over (still complaining loudly about hating his life and job). I tell him we would love to order some food (me trying to be super friendly), but I did have a question about the menu. I am gluten-free and wanted to know if there were any dishes that were safe to order. I understand that a lot of people claim to be gluten-free and have joined this trend in recent years, but I've been wheat-free my entire life and gluten-free for the past 11 years, so I'm not just a trendy-gluten-free person and know a lot about it. He immediately says, "that's going to be very difficult. Why don't you just order something with only vegetables?" -- not encouraging. I'm not vegetarian, and also a lot of vegetable dishes could contain gluten. Then he looks at the menu and he points to the lamb neck and couscous and says I can order that. I tell him that I didn't think I could order that because it has couscous. He looks very agitated and tells me that couscous is rice. I kindly tell him couscous is not rice. He looks at me and says, "Do you even know what gluten is? You don't seem to know what you're talking about." Couscous isn't gluten free, and I don't know anyone who thinks it is. Just because it looks like rice doesn't mean it is rice. His tone was pretty volatile and abrupt, and I thought, you know what, I don't need this. I'm hungry, I just got to town, Nashville has thousands of restaurants, and I'm not dealing with this. So, rather than getting into an argument with someone over what is and is not gluten (why not shuffle us off on a server or simply go ask the chef? the hostess? anyone else?), we asked for our check and left. Really unacceptable. I don't live in Nashville, so this review probably doesn't matter much to this restaurant, but I wouldn't go back, obviously.

Been twice. First time was not so great food or service wise. Second time was a huge mistake. I got food poisoning. Not sure what did it, but it sealed the deal for me about eating there. A lot of people love it. Maybe it was a fluke I got sick, but not trying a 3rd time.

Food is not a good as it has been in the best. Ordered lettuce wraps food came out way overly spicy, and I love spice! Asked for some rice to tame the taste and had to send back way too spicy, then dish came out bland with no flavor and was charged for rice... They do have a large menu with many options, including gluten free!

They had a gluten free menu! I don't have celiac so I didn't ask about dedicated grills & fryers. The wait staff was pleasant & responsive. I had the grilled chicken sandwich on gluten free bun. It wasn't very flavorful but it was decent. And I didn't get sick.

Underwhelming and overpriced. Pizza Fusion seems to have a lot of hype and a lot of potential but it is poorly executed. I would give them 2.5 stars... most people would round to 3, but I'm sticking to two because my experience wasn't really "A-OK." Even with a Creative Loafing deal AND a nightly special, I feel like we really overpaid... $27 for a large Do-It-Yourself Pizza alone. How is that possible? This is how: they don't tell you on the menu that the base pizza is $12 (I looked for pricing and there was none). They do tell you that each topping is between $2 and $4 (or more), but you would expect that to be the full cost of the pizza since only those prices are listed, leaving ours at $15 but alas it was actually almost twice that much. Dang! The final product was good, but for that price I can get three equally good take out pizzas. When you add my small white pizza to the mix, our bill was ridiculously high. I do not recommend this place unless you have a CL voucher. They are priced high assuming you will have one. Here is the link: http://www.cldeals.com/products/valid-at-pizza-fusion-downtown-tampa-25-value-2 Want to know something else they don't tell you? The soda is not normal coke product. It's their supposedly organic version, which tastes like a flat diet coke with a whole cup of Truvia added to it... like a previous reviewer said, it's basically cough syrup. They really should tell us this when we order. My "diet coke" was so gross I cringed when I took the first sip and literally could not force myself to get it down. I have never felt that way about any other soda or drink for that matter. Trust me, I know what Truvia tastes like as I use daily it in my shakes and cooking... and I know it's better than aspartame... but this was WAY TOO MUCH TRUVIA! I was so turned off by this product. Yuck. The service was pleasant but super slow/sparce and we watched as everyone was served before us. As for the food itself, it was alright but honestly not amazing. I wasn't blown away. Also, I ordered the wheat crust and got the regular one on my pizza... didn't make it an issue, but it added to the overall annoyances. I really wanted to like this place. I really did. But Pizza Fusion and I are not meant to be. I won't give them good reviews just because they offer gluten-free items. Summary: okay food, kinda bad service, really bad value, overall a super MEH experience.

First, I should clarify that I tried Whaley's BBQ from their mobile truck at c.1949, not in the actual restaurant. Second, I will admit that as I ate the food, I thought it was actually quite tasty. The reason I'm rating it 1 star is because of the devastating food poisoning that ensued just hours after consuming a plate of Whaley's food. Without getting into detail, I will simply say it was the absolute worst experience of my life. I was sick for days after that initial first night - I felt weak and physically couldn't bring myself to eat real food for what felt like forever. I'm not sure what kind of cross-contamination had to happen for me to get so incredibly sick, but this place should be shut down on those grounds alone. I haven't eaten bbq since then, and I 100% will never try their food again.

I love Elevation Burger, but a recent trip to this location was a let down. Clearly, I was not the only person frustrated with the service. Waited far to long for the cashier to get off their phone and decide to work. The burger was overcooked and dry- very untypical of Elevation. My vegetarian friend ordered a grilled cheese, which was only a hamburger bun with a slice of cheese cooked on the same grill with the burgers. It was unsatisfying and contaminated. Will continue to patron the Willow Grove location, but not this one.

Very good ice cream. Unfortunately for me I discovered my stomach is unable to handle ice cream any more...I have developed a little bit of lactose intolerance...darn. Still recommend a visit for some deliciousness.

Right off the bat, not a big fan of the flavors. The dishes looked amazing, smelled great as well right as we walked in. The place was a bit crowded (coz the reviews are so great). We took our son there and he seemed to do quite ok but too noisy for us. The portions were big and shareable quanity (not family style though) which was nice. The soup we ordered was pretty good. I wasn't very fond of the entrees. Its been a while that I've been there so I don't remember what we ordered. The servers were nice, helpful and knowledgeable to allergen requests.

Terrible choice for vegetarian/vegans or those with allergies. This is by far the least accommodating restaurant I've eaten at in the St. Louis area. For the price, location and atmosphere this restaurant should be much more customer friendly for people with particular dietary concerns. Instead, I was made to feel like a second class citizen. My simple request (to leave egg off the one thing I could eat- not joking) was ignored. Many other Thai restaurants in the metro area can make a Thai curry without fish sauce, the chef here couldn't be bothered. I will not be back. I'm incredibly disappointed. One positive, the wait staff was very friendly.

First time visit was @6pm Friday night. We got a table promptly. The atmosphere was very bright, loud, abundant, big tv's with every sport imaginable playing, and lots of families with small children. Our waiter came by and we inquired about the beer selection. He didn't know much about the beers so he got us a beer menu. We ordered pretzels for appetizer and 3 - 8" pizzas. One person in our party has allergies. We were very specific about what they were and and not to put them in the pizza. The pretzels came, long brown sticks with no salt at all on them. Quite bland. The cheese dip was quite tasty. Then we waited. 45 min later we waved down our not so attentive waiter and asked about the pizza. He informed us they were backed up and there were 2 orders ahead of us. 1 hour into our visit we finally got our pizzas delivered to our table by a food runner. The 'allergy' pizza had 2 items that we specifically said 'no'. We asked for the manager. She was very apologetic and said 'I will take care of it'. Did we want another? No - after an hour wait we didn't want to wait more. We asked for Togo boxes. We waited. They finally came as did our bill - we were charged for the beers, pretzels and 3 pizzas. The waiter ignored our attempts to inquire about our bill. We wanted to pay for our beers & pretzels but couldn't get help. So we got up and approached the waiter. He said 'it's not my fault', looked and the manager was no where to be found. Longer story short - we left our pizzas and our bill. I hope this restaurant makes it. But it's not for me.

I'm all for a good burger, in fact, I love a good burger. So, being that a new burger joint opened in the Park recently, I was excited to try it. I have to say, I was a little disappointed after the hype I'd heard about this chain. They're opening businesses all over the place, including Calgary, but I'm not totally satisfied with what we experienced here. I do have to give the business kudos for moving customers through efficiently. We arrived at around 6:00 PM on a Saturday evening and there was a substantial line-up. Even though the lineup was large, we still moved through ordering and getting our meal (take-out) in under 15 minutes. The restaurant was clean and bright, with tons of staff working on at least 12 different stations - all in plain view of the patrons. Everything looked nice and clean. On to the food. Both my girlfriend and I ordered double patty burgers with all the fixin's (lettuce, tomato, pickles, mayo, etc.). I had mushrooms, cheese and bacon on mine, my girlfriend had just cheese. The burgers tasted good, but I was frustrated from the start. The bun was WAY too small to contain all the burger inside. I ended up eating the last part of the burger with a fork as it had slopped all over my plate. The bun needs a serious re-design. The rest of the ingredients, including modest patties made from what looked like freshly ground beef were quite good. Now, this chain claims to have some of the "best fries in America." Sadly, I wouldn't know. They fry their potatoes in peanut oil and I'm allergic. I know I shouldn't find this frustrating, but I do. With all the people out there who enjoy fries and a good number of them who are allergic to peanuts, this seems like a problem to me. But I guess I shouldn't feel slighted... I am in the minority on this one. In summary, our experience was just OK. Service was friendly, burger was tasty, but really needed a better bun and not being able to have fries was a let-down. Time will tell if we give them another try.

My friend got food poisoning from here... that was my first red strike. I went and the fish did not taste fresh to me. It was all sort of bland. maybe it was an "off" day for the chefs but I just did not enjoy my meal here.

ESTO ES UNA ESTAFA!! No es autentica comida peruana. 1. Es muy probable que el cocinero no sea peruano, la sazón no es igual y la calidad de los productos menos. 2. Ayer por la tarde decidí ir a comer por primera vez a este restaurante y pedir un pollo a la brasa, el cual lo pedi con yucas. Uno, el peruano sabe que jamas un pollo a la brasa puede venir con frejoles, y es uno de los sides que te ofrecen junto con el pollo, en este caso yo lo pedi con yucas, para esto el restaurante estaba vacío, fui la primera en llegar, el pollo que pedi estaba seco y estaba caliente como si lo hubiesen calentado en un Microondas, las yucas estaban frías y la ensalada desabrida. Al comer me di cuenta que nada estaba fresco y que estaba comiendo algo guardado sabe Dios de cuantos días, pero no reclame en el momento porque pensé que nada me iba a pasar. Mi sorpresa fue al llegar a mi casa, tenia un dolor muy fuerte en la boca del estómago, decidí descansar para ver si me pasaba, pero no. Mi experiencia fue tan horrible que estuve a punto de ir por emergencia, no paraba el vomito y el dolor, sentía el sabor del condimento malogrado en mi boca, mi deshidratación fue tanta que llegue a desvanecer del dolor y el vomito, he pasado toda una noche sin dormir, lamentablemente por comer en este restaurante. Deberían hacer una inspección sanitaria a este restaurante y no engañar a la gente. En mi caso pudo haber sido peor, gracias a Dios hoy estoy mejor pero aun sigo con dolor leve, me da mucha pena escribir esto pero es la verdad sobre este disque restaurante peruano, tendrá muchos años y trayectoria pero no es lo que aparentan. NO ENGAÑEN A LA GENTE!!!! 3. La sazón no es peruana, la comida no es fresca, muy mala experiencia.

Been here a couple times, Im always happy to support small businesses especially ones with vegan options. However every time that I've either called in to order, attempted to order online or went in they are out of dough for pizza or don't have what they need to make the vegan Cuban. Once I checked google before calling to make sure they were open and they never answered. I tried the next day and was told they were out of dough because they had a doctors appointment the day before. I bought a vegan "steak" from here because the owner hyped it up so much. He said everything in the store he backs and he wont buy vegan alternatives unless they are good and very close to what they are supposed to be mimicking. So I paid a decent amount for one steak and it was disgusting. Smelled like dog food and no one in the house could stomach the taste or texture so we ended up tossing it. I work around the corner from this place and have been told by numerous coworkers that when they have gone here they had the same issue of not being able to order what they want because the restaurant is not prepared. Also a heads up to any ethical vegans and people with allergies to animal products, I was told that multiple people have seen them use the same knifes to cut the meats and the vegan food. Havent seen it myself but thats pretty serious so i figured i put it out there, so make sure they use different utensils to prepare your food. If they could get their stuff together be more organized with ensure they have have what they sell on stock as well as If i knew for sure that there was no cross contamination between the animal bodies and the vegan food i would consider giving them another chance. If you want old school food, and a non-up to date type 2018 Menu, then this is the place for you. Your Grandmother would possibly like this place, because the menu has probably not changed much in 30 years. It's ok, but as for Vegan, choices and any true healthy food options, this is not the place to look. Now, I get it, this is a Deli style place, and it's a corporate model, so all of them serve the same foods at different locations. But, come on, not much to even pick, from the salads to sides to call even tasteful or up to date. I guess if you like that old school type of iceburg lettuce and pale tomatoes you'll like that and the meat that comes with the dishes. Don't come here looking for amazing, but come here to be fed at a decent deli style price. On the upside, the help was delightful and cheery and they did their best to make me feel comfortable in their store, but as for me one visit here is good, no more. God bless their hearts for at least serving the general public since 1989. I think the menu is about the same. If you like meat, you are in the right place. If you are working towards a block artery, you can work on it here. All said and done, this place is not a place for Vegetarians, Vegans, people who are diabetic or on a serious, gluten free or health food life style. It's not bad, it's just not side stream America, it's definitely main stream America, with old school flavors and menu. It has it's place, but not in my belly.

I ate there today 12/21/16. My wife is allergic to MSG. Nowhere did the menu indicate they used it. When questioned, the waiter said they did in fact use MSG. My wife felt queasy and we asked for the check. I said I would not pay for her Pho, but they but both servings on the tab. When questioned they gave us a blank stare. MSG should be indicated on the menu as many people are allergic. They did not seem to care. I live in the neighborhood and will not return.

On 09/18/17 I went to Mad Crab with my sister. My stomach started bothering me while still eating so I went to the restroom. I ate, paid for my meal, then left. Within 15 minutes of leaving the restaurant, I ended up in the QT bathroom on Saint Charles Rock Rd for an hour in excruciating pain until a relative picked me up. Long story short, I ended up in the ER. I was diagnosed with FOOD POISONING!! I contacted the manager at the restaurant and provided him with all the information that the hospital had given to me along with the foodborne illness complaint form he provided me. Chris the manager at 8080 Olive Blvd. offered me a $100 gift card as if I would even consider eating food from this restaurant ever again. Completely ignored the fact that I have an ER visit bill, or missed work/pay for that day. I have eaten here a few times before and that did not happen. But, on 09/18/17 I literally felt like I was dying and they want to offer a gift card. SMH. PLEASE BE VERY CAREFUL EATING HERE! Sadly, If you do eat there, ask for Liam. He is an amazing waiter.

Went here tonight. The service was friendly but not great. The atmosphere was horrible I felt like I was in a cafeteria instead of a restaurant. The tables were sticky and the washroom was filthy. There's a couch by the wall I think someone sleeps there. We weren't given any menus. It was cold in there as well. I think they care more about skip the dishes more than a actual customer that comes in. The food is the only reason I have it two stars. It was salty and there is MSG in it. My wife is allergic and she sneezed and sneezed. I don't think I'll go there again. No fortune cookie either

I can only assume the founder majored in social media marketing with a culinary elective. The food is slightly better than Cracker Barrel, but not line around the corner good. The line was a half hour on a rainy Saturday morning. They don't offer and refused to make vegetarian/kosher biscuit gravy, which is always disappointing from a place specializing in biscuits charging premium prices. We went with the tomato gravy which lacked the southern heartiness of traditional gravy, but was good. It tasted like tomato soup thick with cherry tomatoes and was perfect with the rainy weather. Strangely, the biscuits had the texture of vegan (maybe gluten free) biscuits, which is not an ideal quality in what I assume are not vegan biscuits. You'd think of all the things to be subpar here it wouldn't be the biscuits. They were flat and lacked the flaky, fluffy texture you want from a biscuit. The potato casserole was incredible in that southern artery clogging kind of way, but we were surprised by the Lilliputian portions. At $4.00 it was nearly a dollar per bite. All in all the place was pretty good. I just hope they're still working to improve and not complacent just because the cash register is placed close enough to the door to force a line outside.

DO NOT EAT HERE. ! I am ServSafe certified and also a manager at a well known restaurant who follows important food safely procedures daily, and I witnessed many things done wrong at this establishment, they definitely do not follow food safety laws ! I was out with my significant other, trying to enjoy a nice lunch at a location we've never eaten before. We came across Animo and decided to try it out since they had lots of vegetarian options for myself, but our experience was repulsive. First of all the customer service was just not there at all, employees were not even close to welcoming or friendly. While waiting for our food is when we noticed how unsanitary this place was. One of the employees went over to refill a water jug, where anyone was aloud to grab a cup of complimentary water. While he began to refill the water jug he dropped the lid on the floor and it wasn't picked up until after a long period of time, when most of the employees were kicking it around and stepping on it. Eventually one of the employees picked it up and put it right back on top of the jug of water without washing it, wiping it, or trying to clean it at all. After that, I began to notice that none of the employees changed their gloves not once. A lot of them were touching their hair, rubbing their nose, touching phones, and money from the cash register, and then going back to chopping the fruit and the food that they were handling. Very unsanitary. They also had some bananas and some other fruit on the floor by the prep area. When an employee was refilling the spinach storage drawer, she careless dumped it into place, and half of the spinach fell on the floor and it was never picked up. The amount of food on the floor could attract pest. During food prep, NONE of the employees had hairnets on either. I also saw a lot of cross-contamination between the different food, which is very unsafe especially for anyone who has allergies towards certain foods. Overall it was a terrible experience, and I will never be coming here ever again. The employees definitely need to be monitored and need to be trained on the correct food safety procedures. Please be aware of these things wherever you go. Food safety is very important, no one should ever have to worry when trying to enjoy a nice meal out.

I was here on a weekend around 3 pm for some lunch and it was pretty quiet. Too bad there was no coat check but that's no big deal. I ordered a shrimp tempura bento and a beer to start off. The tempura was greasy, soggy and gross. Later on I was having greasy burps and felt like i was gonna vomit but it didn't happen. Perhaps I should have had the sushi. I might go back and try the all you can eat sushi but definitely nothing fried!

Having worked in a restaurant most of my life, I'm usually very understanding when it comes to poor service. That being said, the service I received here was particularly bad. We waited thirty minutes for our meals that were brought to us cold. My husband's glass sat empty for twenty minutes. The waiter didn't come back to check on us the whole time we waited for our food. My meal came out with a muffin on top of my food even after I had told him i had a gluten allergy and couldn't have it. Tables sat uncleaned the whole time we were there. And our waiter never took the time to apologize or explain the situation to us. I gave them two stars because had the food been warm it would have been great and the manager took the time to ask us about our experience and gave us a discount even though we didn't ask. If they had been better staffed I think it would have been a better experience.

Awkward experience and below average food at a very high price. We walked into the newly remodeled Maynard's Market and were greeted by staff that seemed to be as confused as why we were there as we were trying to eat there. It was 1pm and the place was nearly empty. We walked up to the counter cash register to order, only to be moved along to another section to order. At the location we were directed to, the employee seemed confused that we wanted to order and pay for food. We bought a salad, ordered a margherita pizza, a cheese sandwich, and their "morning calm" sandwich, then looked for a place to sit. There was only one table large enough for more than two people, and it was the only occupied table in the place (one person) so we decided to sit outside even though it was a bit chilly. Outside it was completely unclear if the tables were for the Market, or for the Kitchen, that was until the Kitchen staff served another table near us, giving us the stink eye for sitting there. Side note, they are owned by the same group... Our food arrived. It took some time, more than it would seem necessary for a pizza and a sandwich they were making with a panini press. The pizza was described as "Red sauce, fresh mozzarella, fresh basil", though it came with whole sliced tomatoes and spinach on it. Needless to say, my daughters wouldn't touch it. I tried a slice, it was also burnt. The "Morning Calm" is really just a pretentious corned beef, cabbage, and hot mustard sandwich. Intended to be served warm, the outside was cooked in the panini press, but the corned beef was cold. We ate what we could, though the food was so bad we didn't finish anything. Then were were confused, should be clean our own table, or leave it for the wait staff that were giving us the evil stare? Looking around and seeing no trash cans meant for more than cigarettes, we left our trash. Sorry. My daughters were quite upset that the pizza was not to the description on the menu, so I promised to buy them ice cream to make it up. We walked up to the ice cream counter, but all the ice cream was covered in freezer burn. Not a good look in an open display. I promised them I'd take them to the Hub instead (great place!) I then went to buy a coffee and cookie for my wife. Of course the staff was again confused that we were trying to buy something, we were sent to a different counter again (the counter is a big rectangle, so we just kept walking around and around it, with little room to walk.) I went to the coffee area, and asked for an Americano and a chocolate cookie. The person took our payment, then disappeared. The cookie was directly in front of me in the display counter, and the coffee machine was next to it. We stood there for several minutes waiting for someone to notice we had no cookie or coffee. I then left. My wife must have wanted that cookie quite badly, she stayed. She received her cookie and my coffee and walked over to the Hub (GREAT PLACE!) to join me. My coffee was pretty average. Her cookie on the other hand had a special treat not mentioned on the sign, Walnuts! My wife is allergic to walnuts. A little "heads up" would have been nice. So all in all, one pizza, one salad, two panini sandwiches, a cookie, and a few drinks. $50 later, most of the food uneaten, I don't think I'll be back.

Broke out in massive full body rash/hives right after eating at the Plymouth Meeting location. (I'll spare you the photos) Ordered chicken pad thai and it came with 4 tiny pieces of chicken and extra tofu and scallions. Disappointed once again in P.F. Chang's extremely salty, high priced and average food. There's much better options out there for Asian fare.

Ordered a vegan salad and a rigatoni pasta, the salad was fine, the pasta with the vegan meat was undercooked hard and tasted pretty bad also not to mention it came with pesto which it was not disclosed on the menu, I can't have pesto/ basil it gives me rashes... I took another shot, the restaurant took the plate back and I got a vegan chicken parm instead. That was OK not bad not good, I didn't finished the whole plate though, however as I was leaving the restaurant I started to feel SO bad that I had to run right after I paid for my food and threw up inside my car. I can't tell if it was the pesto or the vegan chicken parm or everything, 30 dollars later I'm still nauseous and with stomach ache. The worst.

I usually frequent the Carl's Jr down on Broadway, but wind up at the Overland location once in awhile. My biggest issue with this location is the drive thru. The lot is tight and it is sometimes a battle to get from the street to the order box if the restaurant is busy, or if you encounter insensitive louts. I've never experienced poor service, or less than the quality of food I expect at Carl's Jr. Oh and they have flowers planted by their order box, so if you're allergic to bees, be careful in the spring and summer months!
Was super excited to try this place, especially since they have gluten free crust. Alas, I instead sat on hold for over 30 minutes before giving up. Dang.

It was the 2nd or 3rd day of our (semi-business) trip to New Orleans, and the drunken frat life on Bourbon Street was starting to get to us. Where would we find good food and wine, instead of cheap beer in plastic cups and the smell of yesterday's vomit? This place!! Yes, Bourbon Street is hoppin and all, but holy crap this little gem was such a wonderful getaway. Hidden in the middle of nowhere by some traintracks, Bacchanal is really a unique concept. You basically enter this wine/cheese shop, buy what you want, then head out back to an outdoor patio space with live jazz, and where you can order such decadent food as lamb t-bone and clams, all while they plate up your stinky cheese on this massive plate with crisp bread and sweet spreads. The heart and soul of Nola lives in this very spot. If we're ever in town again we're coming straight here!

I'd give a 4.5 if I could but Yelp doesn't let me. My boyfriend's parents took us here for lunch while visiting town recently & overall it was a pretty great experience. They all love seafood, but I have a shellfish allergy so RumFish was a great option as it had grouper sandwiches & fish tacos along with the lobster ravioli & other shellfish based meals. I still got a simple Caesar salad just because I had a contamination reaction a while eating out few days ago & was a little on edge after that. My salad was huge, well dressed, & I could've added chicken, shrimp, or another meat if I was inclined, but it was lunch so I wanted to keep it light. The dressing does have anchovies in it but not to the point of overwhelming the dish & there weren't whole or chopped anchovies on the salad thankfully. My boyfriend got the grouper sandwich & he inhaled it so quickly that it must've been tasty. His mom got the fish tacos which she definitely enjoyed, but she was ready to pass on the Thai peanut slaw she got as a side. Go for the curly fries or sweet potato ones instead. His dad liked the bisque soup quite a bit & he enjoyed his burger almost as quickly as my boyfriend enjoyed his sandwich. They do have non-seafood options but it's incredibly limited - it's a seafood place so I understand, but only one entree was both shellfish & seafood free when we went there & it wasn't vegan or vegetarian friendly. It was a steak that certainly sounded good, but too heavy for lunch & there was next to no options for vegans & vegetarians. Lots of gluten free choices and/or substitutions though, so that was appealing. Our server was great & we were seated right near the massive tank, but there's a viewing area too where you can see the stingrays better & see the fish right above you. A very interesting dining experience for sure & overall a really good one!

Went to Edison's for dinner and games with my son. Ended up getting food poisoning and missing work the next day due to illness. I spoke to a the Food Service Director and was not satisfied with the way he responded. I requested to speak with someone else and after a little back and forth on Yelp, the owner called me. He apologized for the Director's response but also stated that he "wasn't convinced" that I got sick from eating at his establishment. Seeing that my illness cannot be proven nor disproved we will have to agree to disagree. I am updating my review because at least the owner responded and sent a gift card for the poor service.
