I feel better about returning but just for games and bowling.

If I could rate this a zero I would! Not only was there a hair in my food, but my husband got a severe case of food poisoning because of their pork belly. He has been sick all day!!! This is unacceptable. Please be careful ordering from this place!

Bad service and overproced sandwiches. Its sad because they are one of the few places that had gluten free bread. The biggest problem is the stick regular cookies (without asking or warning) with the gluten free sandwich. I'll spare the details of what happens to a person who is gluten intolerant and ingests gluten, but its not pretty. This kind of gross negligence can get someone really sick.

Came here for restaurant week. There were 4 tables when we got there; it still took 15 minutes to get our drinks (a beer, wine, and two cocktails). We ordered the baked Brie, which didn't have anything listed under it on the menu. Turns out it had almonds in it. My friend had an allergic reaction to it. The server didn't know about the almonds in it and when my friend said "I won't die or anything" about the severity of her allergy he was like oh ok! My friend's husband had to leave to get her Benadryl during dinner. We had to ask for new silverware for her. The steak was tough. We got another round of drinks. It took another 15 minutes and one of them was wrong. We got the bill and nothing was taken off and we weren't offered anything for the food my friend couldn't eat. Immediately after paying (we still had full drinks) the manager came over and asked us if we could get up so he could have the table. He did buy us another round of drinks for that. Overall terrible service and something that could've been disastrous if my friends allergy had been worse.

Let me preface: first time we went was on a Tuesday, it wasn't busy and had a table by the window. We had the rabbit and the burger. Food and drinks were decent. Service was okay. Unsanitary: Then, we went on a Friday and it was packed. Sat at the bar for drinks and charcuterie. This is where it goes south. One of the bartenders was extremely rude and not personable at all. Waited a very long time to grab her attention for a second drink and she acted bothered by it! The other bartender was bartending and slicing meat and cheese for the charcuterie. He would go from cleaning the bar with a towel and spray and switch to handling the meat without washing or using gloves. He also had a very noticeable open cut on his finger and served us contaminated food. We were appalled as he was sending everyone's plates out like this; it just wasn't ours. And the funny thing is, he immediately put gloves on when the Chef came out to assist and then never used them again when the Chef was no longer present. He knew what he was doing was wrong! It really is a shame that people take shortcuts, especially when it's right in front of us. Told the Manager and he comped but it doesn't fix the unsanitary conditions we experienced. Chef was friendly, but I will no longer be going back. Go to Good King Tavern, Southwark, or Ela.
Very disappointed. I ordered a salad and gluten free pizza to go. Should of checked before I got home. No pizza, some chicken thing instead and horrible looking/ tasting salad.

I ordered a takeout lunch from cheesecake factory yesterday. It was a turkey burger with sweet potato fries, something I've gotten often in the past. The fries were overcooked and cold, consequently they were not palatable at all. I asked for a different bun on my turkey burger since I am allergic to wheat bran. I was hoping for a sesame bun or just a plain old white flour bun of some type. The sourdough bun that they put on my burger was so tough I couldn't bite it and chew it, so I had to eat the turkey burger by itself. The burger was not warm, so again it wasn't very palatable. I only ate two or three small bites of the burger as this is all I could tolerate. Very disappointing because I've had a lot of good turkey burgers at cheesecake factory. Maybe they have a different cook staff since the coronavirus event. I don't know, but to spend $20 and not have any lunch to eat is pretty sad!

Note to self: Never eat/order here again. I ordered delivery for pad Thai. It was the saddest looking pad Thai I ever seen. Bland and tasteless. I also found a tiny hair. Gross. I asked for utensils and extra sauce and got none. No napkins. NADA! I nearly threw up eating it. The pad thai isn't even a pad Thai. Please avoid this place at all cost. Very disappointed.

Really wanted to like this place, but unfortunately falls short of expectations. Iced latte was unimpressive and tasted muted. Food took way too long to come out, and when it did, was bland. Eggs had no flavor aside from the cheese, sausage was dry and dull. Way too overpriced for what we received. Having a gluten allergy I ordered the gluten free pancake.. 1 pancake for $3.50.. a bit steep for an underwhelming pancake. The service wasn't great either. I explained to the waiter how I was unimpressed with the latte, and he seemed annoyed and rushed. The only one who seemed to enjoy his job was the younger guy with glasses, he was nice and seemed to care about customer service. He recommended if do come back to try the Huevos Rancheros. As much as I would've wanted to like this place, I can say I likely won't be coming back.

Affordable, healthy meals committed to supporting organic and local farmers and offer a wide selection of vegan, vegetarian and gluten free menu items. If you like to try new things, have a restrictive diet, or want to try the newest restaurant on the block, this is the place for you. They only do breakfast and lunch though so be sure to stop in before 2pm.

Tired Hands is a fairly large brewing facility, with everything under one roof. Unlike many breweries in my home state of NJ, they do in fact have food, and it's good, too. They have lots of seating, with waitress service. The focus is still on the beer. They have a counter with cans for sale, too. The location is in Downtown Ardmore, which I had never visited before. It's actually a really nice spot with a younger crowd. The only problem is that there isn't enough parking. I was able to park about a half mile away and walk in, but I can imagine that might be difficult for others. There are no flights available. While that may annoy some people, it didn't really bother me because I just got three 8 oz pours. The service was efficient with that, too. However, I do have to say that the beer is slightly overrated. The Hefeweizen I tried tasted nothing like a German Hefeweizen in Germany because it was light, not nearly as wheaty as a German Hefeweizen, and it had a stronger citrus flavor built into it. I would call it a "Light Summer Citrus Ale." I still enjoyed it, however, once I got used to it and got over the fact that the name was wrong. Their hazy IPA had no substance to it; it was just bitter on the edges with no middle. I finished by trying their Strawberry Milkshake IPA, which has lactose and a natural, mild strawberry flavor, and that was definitely the finest beer of the three by far. The way that the lactose balanced with the genuine strawberry flavor was delicious. So, I didn't leave totally disappointed. My recommendation is to be a little more discriminatory when choosing their beers because some are delicious, and others are not as advertised. The food looked pretty good actually, although I didn't order any. The crowd was standoffish. The bartender also wasn't the chattiest person. Nobody asked me whether I enjoyed the experience, and the people at the hostess stand didn't acknowledge me either. Overall, the place felt like a factory to me, but I imagine it's fine as long as you come with a big group.

The staff is very nice, drinks are amazing, and the food was decent. I don't usually review restaurants, but I thought it was important for those that have food allergies or food sensitivities. There is wheat in the "corn" chips/tortillas, making them not gluten free. They have blue tortilla chips that are "gluten free", but I was informed there is still a trace of gluten in them. The steak I ordered is marinated in soy sauce. I had to ask 3 different people about what was actually in my food after I ordered because when I ordered the server did not mention any of that (even after I had informed her of my allergies). The server was very sweet and kept coming over to check on us, I just think it's important for the manager and/or owner to inform the staff on food allergies and how to properly handle them. If you have life threatening food allergies or sensitivities I would avoid this restaurant until their entire staff is on board about every ingredient you may eat/come in contact with.

Wish I could give this place a zero. After a simple order of two dinner entrees we got the wrong order. Delivery took 2 hours and after getting the right order the food was cold. The following day we got food poisoning, and the manager gave us a refund for our meal after a week of reminders. I had to personally go in to get the refund because they didn't have an updated computer system. Awful place and avoid it.

We ate here 2 nights in a row. The first night we got the Sampler Plate (Jambalaya, Gumbo, Red Beans & Rice) and Shrimp n' Grits; everything was amazing, Shrimp n' Grits some of the best I've had. We decided to go back the following evening for full orders of everything, and all share what we got. The 2nd night though, the shrimp tasted like chlorine. If you're unfamiliar with the use of chlorine or trisodium phosphate, it can be used as a food additive in old fish and seafood to restore color and moisture. It's legal, but it's definitely NOT acceptable. I only half of the Shrimp n' Grits, and took the rest home, which I ate the next day, and was sick all night. While the majority of the food here is amazing, I don't return to a restaurant once I've gotten food poisoning there, especially from seafood. However, I don't recommend staying away, just don't order shrimp without asking how long they've had it thawed, and if you taste chlorine, send it back, as I should have done. I recommend the Jambalaya and Red Beans & Rice; Also, in NOLA, there is no reason for seafood to be anything other than absolutely fresh, ever. Remember that food poisoning with seafood can be dangerous. One other note, the Gumbo just didn't suit my taste, due to the use of File powder, which in cooking school, is referred to as a "slime agent".

I've tried to go to P&P three times and each time the wait was well over an hour, so I skipped it. Maybe it's the Tucsonan in me, but waiting an hour for breakfast is just silly...run down the street and get a tasty burrito and call it good. Finally, I visited on a week day and we managed to get a wait that was only about 25 minutes. ONLY! With this kind of popularity, I thought, the food has to be UNREAL! Well - it was good. I'd even say it was very good. But it was certainly not wait-in-line-1-hour and forego the burrito down the street good. I must place the caveat, as well, that we did not partake in the amazing selection of cocktails. Maybe I'd have given another star for that. I have an allergy to dairy and eggs, and there were almost no non-egg, non-dairy options. I ended up with the pancakes (a little egg won't kill me) and a side of bacon. The bacon was truly amazing - thick, crispy and flavorful. The pancake had lightly fried margins. My husband's eggs and toast were prepared exceptionally well and were obviously very fresh. The coffee was thick, black and tasty. However, our service was still slow and distracted, the room was noisy and I had to wonder whether the food was actually that good, or if the wait combined with the drive plus the anticipation we had before our order arrived must made us think it was that good. If you're a breakfast/brunch lover, can do eggs and dairy and don't mind a wait as long as you can sip a cocktail - this might be just the right match for you. For a "feed me before I turn into swamp thing" egg and cheese avoiding simpleton like myself, this place just didn't live up to the hype.

My husband and I visited Chef Bond and his hands on cooking class while we were on vacation in Louisiana. We were aware that the class was inside his home, but were told that he was a chef that would teach us the aesthetics of true southern cooking. I have mixed feelings about this class, so I will give you the good and bad and let you decide if you want to participate. The good points: * We learned the difference between Cajun and Creole cooking * We learned how to make a Roux * We learned how to make bread pudding * We learned how to suck up an egg yolk using a water bottle * Chef Bond sent us the recipes from the day to my e-mail * Stacey Chef Bond's helper was fun and made the experience more enjoyable * The wine was plentiful - (and lord it had to be in order for me to swallow some of the things that occurred during this event) The bad points: * Chef Bond is a smoker and my husband has a bad allergic reaction to smoke. The Chef was smoking on the porch when we arrived and we were encouraged on two more occasions to go out on the porch to participate in "quizzes" about food. Let's just call it what it was - a smoke break! * While we are attending a class inside someone's home, it IS a cooking class! I would expect that good hygiene habits would be upheld. On the occasions when the chef went outside to smoke, I had a hard time swallowing the fact that when he came back inside he did not wash his hands. * Also, I realize that we are in the south and there are some big and unavoidable bugs that can be in your house. However, when you are teaching a class, I would think that you would make efforts to make sure that everything is clean! There was a big dead cockroach right under the table where we were cooking. I picked it up and threw it in the trash, but it was nasty and led me to wonder what else might be crawling around. Not to mention the cobwebs in the lights above where we were cooking looked like they had not been dusted for fifteen years. * Sometimes it's the group that you are with that can make or break an experience. We were paired with one other lady, who was sweating profusely and talking like a crazy person, boasting of her job and herself. It drove me and my husband almost mad! At one point this woman picked a chocolate chip out of the bread pudding batter, put it in her mouth and then put her hands back in the batter. Also, she was a smoker who continually went outside and when she returned, she handled food without washing her hands. * On one occasion while we were outside for one of our "quizzes", our fellow class attendee said that she had some kind of infection on her foot, then she proceeded to point out the fact than our chef had foot fungus. When I looked down at his open toed flip flops I almost gagged! Not exactly appropriate talk for people taking a cooking class! * The cooking area is very small. It did accommodate the three of us, but just barely. * And lastly, I was going to give our helper Stacey a $40 tip. I really didn't think that it was appropriate to tip Chef Bond, since this is his business and he makes the majority of the profit from the class. Chef Bond even encouraged us to tip her, however when I told him that I was going to give her this tip he said that the money was his. I told him that I had already paid for the class. Which he replied that we could split the tip. The whole exchange left a bad taste in my mouth. Poor Girl. I have taken several cooking classes, this being the most informal and one of the most expensive. For $340 I would recommend finding another establishment to get skilled in cooking, or treat yourself to a really nice dinner. I could never in good conscious recommend this to one of my friends, nor would I ever return for another class should I visit New Orleans in the future.

Such high hopes... People at work were hankering for sushi at lunch, which is a tall order in Jenkintown. We decided to make the drive over to Queen Sushi in Glenside. They offer Chinese and Japanese. That should have been a tip off, but it wasn't for me. The place isn't a dump or anything. It's clean, well maintained and decently lit. I got a spicy tuna roll and a salmon crunch roll. They have lunch specials that are under $11. It just wasn't that good. The texture was weird and the rice rice wasn't sticky sushi rice. No one else in the group liked the rolls they got either. My more melodramatic friend is concerned he has food poisoning. Maybe they are just a better Chinese place. The egg roll I got was the best thing there.

My sister and I decided to finally visit Broad Ripple Brewpub because we wanted to try something different in our neighborhood. I have a gluten allergy and this popped up for being gluten-friendly which was surprising for the traditional "brewpub" restaurant. While many dishes have an English influence there is a variety! There were options for gluten free bread and buns. I ordered the Shepherd's Pie which was gluten free with the option to add bread for additional $$. I skipped the bread this time. I ordered the "lighter portion" which was still really large so the large portion could definitely feed two people. It doesn't come with any sides. My sister ordered the vegan sloppy joe which she was delicious (and she's not vegan!). I tried some sauce and it was. (It's not listed as gluten free.) The pub chips are a must have (cross-contamination could be a concern for gluten.) We sat on the patio and it was packed on a Friday night but service was great!

If you have a food allergy, DO NOT EAT AT INDY TACO! This used to be a 5 star rating. My family used to love Indy Taco, but after my last few visits, I'm not inclined to come back. Tonight's dinner was bad and bizarre. I have a gluten allergy. I was quite clear in telling my waiter of this allergy. He even went as far as to have a kitchen staff member come talk to me about it. This was a great start! Then it took a turn. The chori fries were amazing, but they now contain gluten. I was disappointed, but ordered a side of refried beans instead. The kitchen staffer then thought it appropriate to tell me how beans will make you fart and poop. (I'm guessing this staffer is 7?) I no longer wanted these beans as the mental image he gave me was pretty unsavory before one eats a meal. Then, my tacos all came back on wheat shells, despite me asking for the corn shells that I'm not allergic to. This was so maddening as I had now discussed my allergy with two Indy taco employees. Now my wife is eating while I wait for my food to be remade. The last time they ignored my allergy and gave me wheat shells, after I reminded them I was allergic to that, they just simply put the taco filling from the wheat tacos and placed them on corn shells and gave them back 30 seconds later. This is obviously unacceptable! This story is over right? Wrong! As we are eating, a young woman, who apparently worked there but was on a day off, came in with her yapping dog! I couldn't believe it. Not a service dog. Just a little barking purse size dog. In a restaurant. Needless to say, I'm not wanting to come back to Indy Taco. If you are lucky enough to not have a food allergy, eat there. Support local business. If you do have an allergy that's worse than mine, they may kill you!

1)They have a rotating menu based on what is in season, so do NOT use previous pictures of menus to help you decide. Hopefully you 3 star readers will see this. 2) The menu they have is very unique, but I'm not sure how they handle dietary restrictions and cross contamination. If you don't eat pork, just be aware while you have options, there are many pork dishes (including their bacon waffles). I'm not sure how they handle cross contamination due to the volume of pork items. It's def something I didn't ask but should have . 3) They have veggie options such as bowls and of course pancakes and waffles. Their potatoes are amazing!! I had the Nutella waffle and my partner had a duck entree. My partner usually orders eggs and toast no matter where we go, so I was surprised that he ordered and enjoyed the duck so much Overall: cute setting, good food with exciting rotating menu. Great place if you want to go out and do something different, but definitely not a "must visit"

Went recently. We all liked the appetizers better than the main dishes. My husband got the expensive $50 2 lb fish and it was worthless. Maybe 1 lb at the most and the flavor was just okay. A fish that expensive should at least taste amazing. Go to Vernik for a whole fish that is very flavorful and tasty. Don't bother with the fish here AT ALL. They have the menu labeled for vegans and also for people with allergies....very convenient. We went early in the evening but sat at the bar until our party arrived. It was a nice large bar and the drinks were nice.

Apparently I can't give 0 stars, so I'll give this place 1. Stopped in to get take out tonight since I'd heard so many good things... After explaining to the waitress that I was severely allergic to nuts, I asked her if the dish I was ordering contained nuts, and she said no... Fast forward to an hour later, halfway through eating, and my throat completely closed up. Turns out there were ground up cashews in the sauce. Thankfully, I popped a couple benedryl, jabbed myself with an epi pen, and didn't have to make a trip to the ER, but had I eaten the entire thing or been more allergic, it may have been fatal. It's very unprofessional AND dangerous that servers don't know what is in the food!!! Fellow nut allergens, be wary of this place!!!

Got to give this place 3 stars for now. As far as drinks go, the place has some unique concoctions such as the jalapeño margarita and some good crafts on tap. My issue was sanitation. The menu looked awesome and was ready to order but as soon as I walked in the restrooms and saw how disgustingly filthy they were I had to pass. I know a lot of people think this maybe an anal retentive reason not to eat some place but if a restaurant can't keep the bathrooms clean how do you think their other sanitation practices are? I have read too many bad reviews indicating food poisoning from eating at El Camino. For this reason and for my guts sake I think I will pass on the food until they clean up their Act a little.

This review is about trying to order a wedding cake. Since the shop opened I've wanted to have one of their beautiful, arguably overpriced cakes for my wedding. I've been calling for the last 2 months to ask an allergy related question and find out when we can do a tasting. A while back while in the shop I was told we only needed to give two days notice to do a tasting for a special diet. But when I called to schedule it seemed no one had heard of doing that. Every other time I've called, no one was there who could answer my questions, so the person would take my name and number and tell me I'd get a call back from the owner by the end of the following day. I've never gotten a call back or gotten any further than that. It's too bad but it makes it easy to want to look elsewhere.

Decided to splurge on dinner tonight (I'm a grad student, so $10 for 1 meal is a treat). The woman before me complained about the way the guy bagged her food. The guy apologized profusely, re-packed her food, gave her new fries, and even a free lemonade. While waiting 20 minutes for my golden nugs and fries, I saw the employee pull out the trash can, toss something in, and push it down. He did not change his gloves. Then, while wearing those same gloves, he went through my french fries as he was trying to get them to fit in the box! When he handed me my bag, I said something. He turned around and asked the kitchen to re-do my food. A minute or two later he tossed the exact same bag of food at me and walked away before I could say anything. No apology from him AND he gave me the same contaminated food. I tossed the food away wasting $10 and 25 minutes. Apparently this place doesn't believe in treating customers equally or health codes. Very disappointed as I'd had good experiences here in the past.

I like to go there because it's close to work. I like the view and the atmosphere. I usually eat like gumbo or chilli. Today I tried the special all you can eat boneless chicken wings for $9.99. I ordered grilled with BBQ sauce. I got friend chicken breast pieces with BBQ sauce. The waitress did apologize and reordered grilled. I got grilled chicken breast with BBQ sauce. I was hungry. It did not matter if boneless chicken wings or boneless chicken breast . What bothered me was the texture from this 10 pieces. Some where grilled through and some where kinda sushi seared chicken pieces. I could not detect after cutting blood but the texture where off. I mentioned that to my waitress and she admitted that my nighbor noticed the same that they where not cooked right. Now an hour later I am not uncomfortable and I feel all right . I just asking me what is worse - eating undercooked chicken or chicken that is prepared with probably chemicals so you don't get food poison if eaten raw? I guess I will still go there but I if I ever eat there I will stay with the gumbo...

Our bartender was delightful.... in the BEGINNING (we came in at 10pm on 2/6) . My friend had asked to remove some items from her nachos due to allergies and the bartender immediately got frustrated. I then asked for no relish on my chicken sandwich and more attitude came flying our way. She then forgets to take the remaining person of our parties order. I asked her how sweet the sweet tea was and she said "I don't know I don't drink it " she did then bring me a taster with a lovely eye roll to go along with it. The food tasted very good though. I will not EVER come back due to service.

The grounds and building are absolutely beautiful and elegant. We went here for Mother's Day lunch. Service was spot on but the food was mediocre at best. Perhaps, it is because we had the last seating. However, in general, I thought the food was bland. It did not meet my expectations for the price. They were great at accommodating my gluten allergy. I had the salmon with lentils. The lentils were very cold. Must have been left out from previous seatings and not re-heated. They even gave me a special dessert due to my allergy (very small scoop of melon sorbet). My husband and son liked their apple crumble. It is a place I really wanted to love but just couldn't get there.

OK..... Superior Grill may not be actual "mexican" food but who cares!!! It is good food with excellent margaritas and excellent chips and salsa (and queso!!!). I live in uptown new orleans and eat here often and it is always good AND myself nor my friends have ever gotten food poisoning. It may be that you drink too many margaritas and your eating mexican food..... guess what that will get your stomach upset! Again... who cares! The drinks are not $11 for a small... it's $11 for a double and if you go during happy hour (3pm - 6:30pm) the margaritas are 2 for 1. So you get the double for $5.50. Highly recommend for going out with friends for food and drinks!!!

One of the worst attempts at customer service I've ever seen at any restaurant including the several cheese factories that we've been to. There was three girls working at the front desk they seemed in complete chaos. We received notice on their device that our table was ready . When we walked back to the restaurant we were told to hold on as they needed to make sure the table was ready .After we were seated we proceeded to wait 20 minutes and did not receive any service whatsoever. Not even a glass of water. I saw at least eight servers walk by our table no one even said hi or smiled. If front desk is this chaotic you can't get served I'd really hate to think what's going on in this kitchen. Can we say food poisoning? I called the manager right after we walked out and informed her of the situation. if that was my business I would have immediately offered that customer to come back immediately and find me at the front desk. I don't even understand how they have three stars.

This could have been a really good experience, however, between the service and salt content, this restaurant gets a bad review. I should have known something was off when there was " plenty of availability" for open tables when I called at 6:30. But, I took a chance because the menu looked interesting. Ease up on the salt and educate the staff on the menu (gluten free options).

Great Chicken Parm but the Spaghetti I didn't like at all. It was overcooked and didn't have a good flavor. Wasn't a case of the sauce it was the pasta. Wasn't impressed with their Soup either. The value for the $ though is stunning. Very very inexpensive and portion was large. Unfortunately tonight I feel like I have food poison coming on and that's all I ate today. Not accusing them, but if any others from it then now you know it was them! Update: IT WAS FOOD POISONING FROM FRANK'S!! Probably the Spaghetti as it didn't taste quite right. I'm getting the Philadelphia Health Dept on this - my Family is involved in the Food Safety Dept.

I've used and been a loyal customer for years. Unfortunately things have gone way downhill and people with allergies need to know they are not safe for allergies anymore and refuse to label allergens. In addition, customer service is nonexistent since the company split and it's really sad. Their food was good but not good enough to tempt an allergy attack and certainly not for a business owner who doesn't care about the customers and only her bottom line instead of being appreciative for years of support.

If you are vegan and gluten free this isn't the place for you. About a week ago I tried blaze pizza for the first time after reading their website that said they provide both gluten free crust and vegan cheese. I loved it! Usually the gluten free crust most pizza places carry tastes the same but blaze pizza had a very thin amazing tasting one! A few days later I went back and they informed me they were completely sold out of there crust.. which wasn't a surprise because it was amazing but I was annoyed I had driven all that way just to leave with nothing. Today I went in to try it again and was informed that they no longer carry gluten free crust, instead cauliflower. I find it bizarre that you would sell out of something because it's so popular and then stop carrying it all together! I'm very annoyed that I left twice without pizza because of their changes. If you have celiac disease and you're vegan MOD Pizza is the place for you in Reno.

I decided to return to Blondie's last night to get one popover and more of that awesome strawberry butter that I enjoyed so much last time. Sean wanted a rootbeer float. We arrived at about 9pm or so, maybe a bit after. We were seated by a woman who told us it was her first day working there. It was pretty much a foreshadowing of what was to come, though... she didn't have a full grasp of their menu yet (which is understandable seeing as how big it is.) I ended up getting not quite what I ordered...some kind of popover with ice cream and strawberries on it. It looked pretty good but it was huge and I wasn't really in the mood for a gigantic dessert explosion right then and there. Sean's rootbeer float ended up having booze in it. He doesn't drink alcohol and he made sure to order it without alcohol...but when it arrived, it had the root liquor in it. He took one sip and nearly vomited because yeah... Sean + booze = disaster. It was like suddenly the U.S. was on the verge of pushing up to DEFCON 1. Yeah. But obviously it was all a misunderstanding and our new waitress was replaced with a veteran and the manager even came out to apologize and make sure those things weren't on the tab. I was brought out a popover with the much-coveted strawberry butter and Sean was brought a non-alcoholic rootbeer float. He was happy, I was happy. Yay. I felt a little bad for the first waitress though. I was worried she thought we were mad at her (and seeing how some patrons can blow up on a server, I guess if she was paranoid we'd get mad, I could see why lol.) But we weren't mad! So yeah. Even though there were mess-ups, I will give Blondie's a 4/5 stars because the popover and strawberry butter combo is now cravable status for me, and they really go above and beyond for customer service. I will definitely be back!

Our experience was pretty awful. First, the guy at the desk tells us that the deluxe king room we had reserved was not available. We asked why, since we had reserved that type of room, and he informed us that room reservations are just requests and the room type is not guaranteed. What? We were somewhat grumpy about this, so as revenge (we think) he put us in a suite with ONLY A SOFA BED. No real bed. Massively uncomfortable. Thankfully, after we complained the next day, the hotel comped our stay for that night and moved us to a real room. But we already had bad feelings for the hotel. The nasty clerk was quickly christened DB. The hotel was fine inside, but the towels always smelled like split pea soup - really gross. I recommend airing them out for a while before you use them. Not the hotel's fault, but next time we will not be staying on bourbon street. Fun to check it out, but not fun to emerge from the hotel the next morning onto a street that smells like vomit. But the beignet place across the street was great for breakfast. Would not stay here again, not worth the money.

Today we went to Semenza's because my mom remembers this as being awesome when she worked for the school around the corner. They seemed to have good deals and it is a cute pizzeria style business. But that is about where it ends sorry to say. We went inside and waited. And waited. And waited. Nobody in front of us and the hostess was waiting tables and helping in the kitchen and did not even acknowledge us for about 10 minutes. I was getting ready to change the venue when she arrived. She had longer dark hair skinny about 5 feet 4. She did help me with answers because I am allergic to pork and at this point seemed nice but not into the job. Sadly they have no chicken and only ground beef...Blah. No real options for me. I would have loved to see some meatballs or chicken or even, gods forbid, some turkey peperoni? So I got a veggie and my other half got a combo and 1lb wings...as well as some chicken fingers. The wait was supposed to be about 20 minutes and was closer to 40 as our food sat waiting to be brought up. During this time I watched the huge family who must have had a hundred dollar order of several pizzas and fries and wing go to the counter and wait...and wait...and wait. Then he went back to the table and a new customer walked in as did a new server. She took the new customers order and the guy from the big family table was finally able to slide in for the much needed soda order they forgot. I would have been pissed off. The dark haired gal never even checked the table to see if everything was alright at any time while bussing tables. We are also talking about 3 or 4 tables of people so not busy really. The pizza had a great crust. The sauce was very mild and lackluster and the toppings reminded me of Burger King throwbacks on my pizza. The wings were cooked before the bbq sauce was dumped on them. All and all I give a 1 for service, a 3 for crust and otherwise unmemorable pizza and wings. a 4 for atmosphere and cleanliness. Price would be awesome until you see how small a medium pizza is...about the size of a small. In a town of competitive pizza where Nu-Yalk is up the street a ways as it Pirates pizza and some other amazing pizzarias...Not to mention the prices of Pizza Hut being better and more memorable...I do not expect this business to survive unless the schools carry it. Years ago they were very good...Not so much today. Please guys, this could be a great place and it is right up the street from us...soup it up and iron out the kinks! Improve the sauce, toppings, sizes, service. We may be back if we do not decide to just go big!

Pros: great place to do work on the weekend; friendly staff; fairly accessible parking situation; the breakfast potatoes; the selection of hot and cold coffee and tea drinks Cons: menu is being revamped, so no more of the red velvet pancakes; portions are small for what you pay; food is decidedly average; pretty sure one of my friends got food poisoning from her breakfast hash Overall: go, if only because it's one of the better cafes to camp out for hours at a time

Really sad to post this review as last night was my husband and I first time eating here. A friend came with us and said it was pretty good. After checking the menu out online we decided to go! I ordered the French onion soup, and the margherita pizza. My husband ordered a burger as well as his friend as well as the lobster macaroni. Everything tasted fine but when I woke up this morning I felt so awful. I had to force myself to drive to work while not in the right mind set. I get to work and cannot stop getting sick. I'm at work for 2 hours and I had to leave my job because I couldn't stop getting sick. All day I've been getting sick. The only item not shared on the table was the burgers and my pizza. The guys didn't get sick but I did. I will never ever come back here. I lost a day of pay and had to be home sick all day and night. I am posting this at 8:30 PM. I got confirmation that I have food poisoning and this really ruined my trip here. I hope everyone in the kitchen is using the right measures so this does not happen again.

My wife and had identical breakfast here except that her omelet was vegetarian and made with egg whites while mine had whole eggs and meats, etc. About 20 minutes after leaving the restaurant I came down with the worse case of diarrhea I have ever experienced in my life, which is a sign of Food Poisoning when it happens this quickly after eating. Additionally, there was a news report that evening about salmonella found in eggs in Indiana recently. Although our server was professional during breakfast, I cannot say the same for the First Watch Regional Manager, whose primary interest during our phone conversation about probable kitchen challenges was to manage potential liability by trying to convince me that food poisoning doesn't occur this quickly. He did admit that salmonella can be transferred from egg shells to kitchen staff hands and then to other food. However, he accepted no blame for what happened to me in his restaurant.

I'm into this whole BYO, "pizza whatever the heck way you want it" concept. You get to build the pizza of your dreams and it costs $10 or less in almost all cases. Pretty good deal and experience overall. I had some really high expectations when it came to Blaze. I'd watched the company sweep across the country like wild fire (get it?) and after a few other BYO concepts opened, they finally opened a location here too. I'd seen about a million friends visit their local Blaze stores, cook up stellar looking pies, and brag endlessly about how good they were, so I really wanted my experience to stand up. I built my own pie on their traditional crust with red sauce, bacon, pepperoni, sauteed onion, fresh garlic, meatballs, ricotta, parm and mozz, and a drizzle of pesto to top it off. I asked for the pie well done, to make sure it crisped top to bottom, and moved down the line to wait for it to emerge from the oven. True to form, the pizza cooked quickly, and they left it in a few minutes longer per my request, resulting in a nice crisp with a little char. Unfortunately they also left my wife's gluten free pizza in there that long as well, which came out with some very dark edges that I wouldn't call charred. Overall the pizza was good, but I had higher hopes based on the experiences of my friends. The food at Blaze is just a good example of a personalized pizza. I'd hoped something might've set them apart, but alas, nothing jumped out. I'd say they're my second fave BYO pizza spot now though.
Blakes in NM is awesome. Here, it sucks! Can't get the order right and long wait times. Also the food is so salty and i also got food poisoning the first time I had it.

I placed an order from Postmates and specifically asked for sub bacon instead of sausage and ended up getting cold bacon AND two sausage patties. The rest of my food was super cold as well. It helps to pay attention to detail when customers order food. It would have been a problem if I was allergic to sausage and you still gave it to me. Do better!

I am NEVER coming back here. I came here knowing exactly what I wanted. My husband and I can rarely afford to eat out together so this was supposed to be a special time. I was really looking forward to us sitting down together and enjoying a meal. I asked for the Fisherman's combo. It was fish, clams, and shrimp. I tend to have an allergic reaction when I eat clams, oysters, and mussels, but no other shellfish. It's weird. So I just asked to substitute the clam for a little extra of either the fish or the shrimp. Sam, my server, told me no. I do not understand this. I have never been to a restaurant where you couldn't substitute something simple, especially to cater to an allergy. Like all I needed was for you to take the clam off the plate and add 5 extra baby shrimp and I'm happy. She would not do this. Then I felt like I didn't want to order the regular fish and chips because if I could get shrimp with it for only a couple dollars more I felt ripped off. So I was bummed and I really felt like I didn't want to order anything, but my husband already put his order in, so we were obligated to stay. To add insult to injury, Sam completely ignored me the rest of the night. I was clearly upset. She did not make another recommendation, did not send a manager over to fix the issue, just gave my husband and I the cold shoulder. She wordlessly threw his burger down on the table at him like it was somehow his fault. This is just confusing to me, as I have worked in customer service my entire life. I was not rude to her, just visibly disappointed. Her first move should have been to try to make it better or send over a manager. We ended up leaving, I ate nothing. What was supposed to be a very enjoyable date night turned very sour. Not even just because I was told I couldn't make the substitution, but because of the lack of customer service that followed. I am just very disappointed.

Burger Study exceeded all of my expectations and then some. We rolled into Indianapolis on Friday night and were hopeful for this burger joint. Our server named Gabby was very nice and helpful. I ordered the Double Major. It is two thin patties,American cheese, pickles, lettuce, and their signature "Study Sauce." My comrade ordered their Southwest Classic burger. He loved it! The only downside to this visit was the douchey man sitting across from us who was wearing Brutus Buckeye socks. This is not Burger Study's fault obviously. It's a shame that this wonderful city has to be contaminated with Ohio State fans for the weekend. Anyway, Burger Study is delicious and I would love to be back next time we come to Indy.

Come here for the wine and the interior design. Don't come for cocktails or the food... I made the mistake to order a French 75... It tasted like pure freshly squeezed lemon juice and I mean pure lemon juice. I mentioned this to the waitress, who just shrugged her shoulders and told me that their French 75 are always really sour. Uhmmm.... Maybe you should note on the menu not to expect an actual French 75. I did take advantage of the 'before 6:30 pm' specials: Loaded Baked Potato Tots: Nice presentation. However, do not expect actual tater tots with stuff on top... these are like mashed potato balls, with the 'loaded' ingredients rolled into them and then baked or fried. Not bad at all, love the dipping sauce. Brussels Sprout Salad: Nice presentation, lovely taste on the top. The sprouts towards the top of the dish were nicely flavored and I loved those. Unfortunately only the small top layer was wonderful. Since the salad was spread out over a large flat plate, the layer on the plate was swimming in grease,, I assume olive oil, or some sort of vegetable oil. I took half the salad home, which amounts to about a cup of veggies... managed to drain 3 tablespoons of oil from those... not teaspoons, but tablespoons... and the remaining salad still tasted greasy. The Small Charcuterie Board: I'm allergic to the mold in blue cheese, so I asked up front if there was any blue cheese on the the board and then asked if it could be left off due to my allergy, the waitress assured me it would be left off. It was... usually the restaurants substitute a little more of another cheese for the missing item, but not so here. Let's get to the good parts first: Candied walnuts with fried black-eyed peas are fabulous. The ham and spicy sopressata are both quite yummy. And you got enough of the sopressata to cover a slice of their bread. The not so good: Mortadella, about a quarter of a very thin slice of it. About a half slice of ham, which barely covered a small slice of bread. Two whispy thin skinny triangles of unidentified cheese. Three paper thin triangles of another unidentified and cardboard dry cheese. Bread served on an identical but separate wooden board... why? Bread itself was super crunchy and parts of it quite burned. Altogether a very dry affair, which could easily been helped by a dollop of jam, or some wholegrain mustard, or a little butter or a smidget of aioli or even a tiny pickle, a pepper, or some pickled onions... anything of the sort would have been great. Kudos to the interior decorator: Great job, the place looks spectacular. Unfortunately I don't think I'll be back any time soon.

Came here to this restaurant while in Reno for vacation, based on their online menu they seemed to have an idea about allergens that were present. They had gluten free and vegan items labeled throughout their menu and upon arrival I informed the server about my celiac disease (gluten free) and dairy allergy. He went back to the cook to make sure they could use new utensils and they were able too. I decided to order the deluxe scramble which was labeled gluten free and was easily able to be dairy free with no cheese or sour cream. It was a scramble of eggs; potatoes and my choice of three other ingredients. I chose spinach, broccoli, and red bell pepper; on top they put avocado and salsa. When the scramble came out I was surprised on the size, it was bigger than I expected. While it wasn't huge it was perfect for me. What I liked most was that the salsa was nice and spicy, but our biggest problem was they didn't salt anything. This became a particular problem for my dad who ordered a breakfast burrito and none of the eggs inside were salted. Overall the place was good and I think as long as they aren't too busy I feel they could accommodate allergies. Unfortunately since the kitchen is relatively small if they got any sort of crowd I don't think they would be able to do much for you. The employees were different, but very nice and were trying to do what they could. Wish they had a few more options and were open later so I could get breakfast anytime of day.

I haven't been to Toscana since they changed their approach, but I had heard good things. I think the decor is better and the menu is certainly much more extensive. I love the idea of being able to sample half portions of almost everything, allowing for customizable meal of one's choosing. We were there on Tuesday night and the service was very slow. Our server was fabulous and very nice and continued apologizing for how slow everything was, so at least it was acknowledged. They were out of a lot of menu items as well, which was pretty disappointing. That said, I was sitting with my Mom and my sister and I wasn't ravenously hungry, so I did not mind it taking a long time. I started with grilled octopus, which was good. Nothing out of the ordinary. For dinner, I had the kitchen salad, which never disappoints. My Mom started with the veal meatballs, which were amazing and had the butternut squash ravioli for her meal. They tasted more like dessert than an entree, but were delicious. My sister had the polenta for her appetizer and capellini with seafood for her entree. She was pleased. For dessert, the two things we wanted were not available. The third could not be made without nuts (my sister has a nut allergy), bu our server returned and said they had one remaining of one of the unavailable desserts, the pear tart. It wasn't that great, but the ice cream it came with was awesome. I would try it again on another night because the food was solid.

This cafe is "line up and order" style. I met 3 people there after an afternoon film at the Garneau. They have several types of chai on the menu but I chose a pomegranate juice. Once you order they give you an electronic buzzer to let you know when your order is ready- I like this and can name a number of restaurants who could benefit from this system.The butter chicken wrap comes with mayo unless you specify- I asked for hummus instead. I ordered mine "gluten free" for an extra dollar, and got two small wraps instead of a large one. I found my gluten free wrap to be heavy with yellow coloured rice.- so the proportion of curry to starch was rather thin, given that I paid over $20 for a wrap and a drink. I traded one of my small wraps for a palak paneer wrap- cheese and spinach. I found there was too much potato mixed in with the spinach Also, the tamarind dipping sauce that came with 3 out of four wraps was turned into a thin, pancake-syrup-like substance by too much water, sweetening (sugar) and cinnamon-way to ruin tamarind sauce. I much preferred the hot mint sauce that one of my friends got- green and spicy- sorry don't have the name. It was all quite filling, and I still had a stomach ache the next morning so I'm a bit wary of their "GF" claim. I had a taste of a friend's tandoori chicken and I thought it was quite good- I like spicy so I might try that next time-or just stay away from wraps altogether. Sorry left my camera at home so no pictures.

I've been to Applebee's many times, it has always a pleasant experience. But due my recent order on grub hub from Applebee's, the way I feel about the restaurant has shifted. My daughter is allergic to bacon, although her reaction after ingesting bacon it is mild she does get hives. On grub hub I ordered two baked potato soups. While processing said order I specifically listed "no bacon in one cup". When I received my grub hub order there was one soup with visible bacon on the top, that was mine, the one with bacon. I then gave my daughter her soup and she proceeded to eat it. I was appalled when she pointed out the fact that she found bacon hidden in the bottom of her soup. This kind of behavior from a multimillion dollar company is totally uncalled for and irresponsible . If my daughter would have happened to eat the entire soup I don't know what would have happened to her tonight. Due to this horrific experience, I will never be ordering from Applebee's again.

Bummed to find out today that they replaced their gluten free vegan crust option with cauliflower crust. The cauliflower bound with milk and eggs meaning the only vegan option has gluten. Not to mention I don't love having cauliflower crust forced on me. I asked the guy making the pizza twice if the cauliflower crust was vegan. He said yes twice. I asked the manager who informed me of the dairy and eggs. I walked out. I won't eat gluten just to have vegan crust. My Pie still has a gluten free vegan option so I'll go there.

Wish I could give zero stars every time I order from here it's always a problem. I'm pretty sure Burger King puts their burgers together better, it was so slapped together ... The first time that I ordered A lettuce wrap burger it was folded in properly wrapped in the lettuce this time was not. Glad I paid extra for a bacon burger and got no bacon specifically put in no mushrooms allergy and got a shit ton of mushrooms on my burger.

I gave it a 3 because of very good gluten free pizza and great service! Unfortunately the other food that was ordered needs a lot of improvement. Spaghetti sauce tasted bland with too much pepper and the meatballs and chicken parm were obviously from frozen and seemed like school cafeteria food. The Greek salad was pretty good. We will not be back.

Me and my family were visiting my Grandma, and she said that this place was famous for my favorite ice cream type, vanilla. I tried it...OMG I was blown away! Grandma tried it, liked it and said it had a creamy taste to it! But my brother threw up although! That day I was happy and sad!

Remedy Cafe is nice for a hot meal. And by hot I mean spicy. Portions are generous, food is inexpensive, and there are a number of alternatives for people with dietary restrictions. Customer service has been consistently friendly, and I'd like to stop by more often. It does have a few downsides - the layout is very crowded, it's not terribly clean, and the music is definitely too loud for conversation or studying. Anyone allergic to nuts or diary will need to watch out - a number of the curries contain almond milk, which may limit your choices. All in all, it's a conveniently placed hang-out with good pricing, good food, and a few flaws. Worth it if you're nearby and want curry!

They have really nice choices in terms or sandwiches and salads. They have some gluten free options which I was very happy about. However it's a little pricey for vegan compared to what I'm used to. Wasn't too happy with how the tofu was cooked, however nice choices & excellent juices !

We had a pretty straight forward experience. We dined in we got our food quickly and were in and out within an hour. Staff was very friendly and helpful with recommending gluten free options for me.The red beans and rice was gluten free and very very good. My husband loved the fried creole wings. I would highly recommend this spot and return again. It was within walking distance of our hotel on Canal street and we spent about 75.00$ total. The decor was not great, but we were in and out and service and food was good. Staff was very very friendly!

Poor service really brought down our rating. Appetizers were brought out without plates. Drinks arrived after apps. When ordering our entrees server could not answer basic questions about a burger, "Is it spicy?" My daughter ordered a gluten free roll. When the food came out they weren't sure which burger had the gluten free bun, "That looks like it." Finally my husband asked for a different bun on his burger when he ordered it. It came out with the wrong bun. It took 10 minutes for a new bun to arrive. There was no sense of urgency to get a new bun. Our server was standing around. "Someone will bring it". Disappointing

Le Peep was great, but since ownership has changed hands the service has taken a plunge. Before I would drive all the way from Kuna for the GF waffles, but since the new owner has changed product manufacturers they are HORRIBLE. Nothing worse than spending 30% more for gluten free products and then have them arrive tasting terrible! I won't be travelling 25 minutes for those waffles and slow service anymore. :(

We bought a Groupon for the entrance to the boat (for a party of 8) and scheduled it about a month in advance. They called not once, but twice the day of to confirm, once in the morning and one 40 minutes before asking when we would come (we were on the way, and we're confused as to why they kept calling us when we confirmed in the morning?) Anyways, got onto the ship and we're seated and our waitress took our drink orders. My mom has a latex allergy so we asked the waitress then if she could check the box in the kitchen to see if they used latex gloves. She comes back to our table for dinner orders, and when she gets to my mom, we politely say she can't order until we know about the gloves. She just says "so you're not eating?" Safe to say our waitress was not helpful the whole time, and acted as we were a burden to her whenever we asked a question about accommodation. Overall, the experience of the boat is great but the service and food lacked. Each course I kept thinking, oh the next course will be better...and then we got to dessert and everything was underwhelming. My "stuffed shrimp" was over cooked shrimp on top of a lump of crab cake. Safe to say come for the experience of a sunset cruise, but maybe skip eating.

Khyber pass is known among the vegan and vegetarian community to be super accommodating and everything is labeled but I have a wheat allergy and asked the server about options other than salad and they didn't have any idea. It was frustrating because they never offered to ask the chef and without that knowledge my options were very limited since I didn't know what was in the sauces. The menu looked great, I just wish it was more accessible to those with allergies or the staff was.

I honestly think this was the weirdest dinner of my life. Pro: Beautiful view Easy parking Great waitress Apologetic manager who came around twice Con: Horrible food. So so so so so bad I ordered the fresh catch of the day, salmon, flown in from NZ and splurged on a date night with my husband which is rare for us. I love salmon and eat sushi all the time and was stoked for Brussels sprouts because they're my fave. My first plate, the salmon was cold. It tasted like it came from the fridge. Not luke warm, cold. Didn't have a lick of seasoning on it, no salt, nothing. It was so strange. Like they forgot to cook it. The Brussels sprouts were awful! Tastes and looked like they'd been boiled and had bac'n bits sprinkled on them. Soggy and really bad. I really really wanted to have a good night and was so stoked to be there, I downplayed it and told the waitress who was nice about it and they brought me another one, made by a different cook. Also, the mango salsa side was the worst salsa I'd ever had. Tasted like someone cut some onions and just dumped tequila on them. So it was fine, chalked it up to honest mistake. They brought me another and it was seasoned and the outside tasted great. Then I cut into it and it was completely raw inside. My fork couldn't even cut into it. The inside was completely chilled still and not cooked. It had been seared on the sides and that was all. I've never had that happen at any restaurant before. The waitress saw it and agreed and was very nice. The manager came out and looked embarrassed and also said, I'm so sorry we served you raw fish. I saw it and it was completely uncooked. They gave us free dessert but what a weird experience. I think quite possibly the worst food I've ever had. I am so sad, I wanted to love this place because it's so beautiful looking and the employees all seemed so nice. It's ripe and ready for Gordon Ramsey to come work his magic on. Fingers crossed I don't get food poisoning.

This review is strictly about the food: it pains me to do this but it needs to be known. I'll start with the positives; The french fries were perfect as well as the cheese and charcuterie plate. The Mac and cheese was bland even with sausage and tasted of only cream (I tried someone's with the sausage and then another one that came out later without it). The jalapeno poppers had no cheese inside and the peppers were raw. The batter on the chicken fingers fell off as soon as they were touched and tasted strictly of smoked paprika (the chicken itself was cooked perfectly and tasted fine). The bratwurst with potato salad is why I'm writing this review. My first brat came with a 2" hair curled between the sausage and potatoes so I quietly sent it back and requested another. The replacement came and appeared fine so I cut a piece just to find another (shorter) hair sticking out of the sausage (looked like it came from inside). I didn't want to annoy anyone so I put it aside and cut another piece in hopes to move on. There was another hair on the paper under the newly cut piece. At this point I felt like a total bitch but had to bring it to the attention of the kitchen. I took it to the window and showed them the two hairs I left on the paper and expressed that I thought one came from inside the sausage. As I looked up I finally noticed that everyone in that little kitchen has full heads of hair and beards with no nets to protect the food. It became pretty obvious where all the hair had been coming from and confirmed that the hair had indeed not come from inside the sausage and must have been under it along with the other. That's three hairs on two plates. Hair leads to contamination, is a physical hazard and proves lack of hygiene.
This place is gross! Steaming beef in shrimp water? My Husband is allergic to shellfish and had the beef pad thai and had a reaction! Not edible and very expensive.

Despite having lived just up the road (not now but years ago), I'd never been to the Pancake Pantry before recently. I know. It's crazy. But it's not often I find myself in Hillsboro Village in the morning with hours to spare. Life just doesn't work that way for me. So, when I found myself in Hillsboro Village at 1 pm on a Friday (no lines), I thought I should carpe that diem and head on in to a Nashville legend. It might sound weird to say but I am proud that PP has so many reviews. Yelp had an... odd start in Nashville. After 6.5 years there are only a couple of handful of businesses with over 1000 reviews (which is MUCH more than it had, even, 2.5 years ago). PP is one of those businesses. That says a lot. So, with as many reviews and as much good will as PP has, I'm a bit saddened to only have had an 'okay' experience. Much of my experience has to do with me. I'll take ownership of the fault. 1.) I should have come here while the original owners were still running things. 2.) I should have come here when I was younger (especially when I was a student) and gorging on stacks of pancakes would have been just another day and not a recipe for antacids and laying on the couch. 3.) I should have come here before gluten became my enemy. So, yeah. There are some things I did wrong. I own that. BUT I was hopeful that I could experience a variation of the pancake magic. Y'see, PP has both cornmeal pancakes and buckwheat pancakes. Both are gluten free! Yes. Done. Well... not done. Despite thoughts to the contrary, all the pancakes are made with wheat flour. All of them. I asked. So, cornmeal? Made with wheat. Buckwheat? Made with wheat. It was a major bummer. With pancakes out of the equation (and my reason for coming), I opted for the grill cook's medley and bottomless cup of coffee. The medley was fine. It was what you might fine in any reputable diner: a mass of eggs, hash browns, onions, peppers, ham (cubed), tomatoes, American cheese, swiss cheese, and picante. It's a mound of food. I struggled to take it all down but I did it. It was fine. It was as good as any Dennys, etc. as you might have had before. But I doubt anyone comes to the Pancake Pantry for eggs, hash browns, etc. They come here for pancakes. Despite thinking they were in my future, they were not. I'm pretty sure that had I had pancakes, my star rating would be higher. But... y'know. I'm glad I didn't wait for a table. One final note: my waitress was very patient and attentive. I appreciated her.

A decent ice cream shop in Bellmawr. Whole list of flavors to choose from, along with shakes, fried oreos and funnel cakes. Still on my list to try the fried oreos. I'm lactose intolerant and yes, I crave ice cream once in awhile. And oddly enough they have lactose free vanilla or chocolate, which makes me very happy. A small cup did seem semi high in price..but seriously how many times are you eating ice cream that you've got a list to compare it? Cute seating on the deck and a bench or two over on the lawn to get out of the sun. Throw some rainbow sprinkles (jimmies) on there and you have yourself a fun treat.

Waitress was pretty rude once she found out we were splitting an entree. She asked us over and over again, almost demanding, to order more. Waited over an hour for that food, she only came over 1 time to tell us she couldn't read her own handwriting (it was the note that I have a severe shellfish allergy). After that she ignored us completely. We finally got a hold of her by flagging down another waiter. When we mentioned how long it had been, she was very defensive and said, "it's because you only ordered 1 thing. If you'd gotten an appetizer it would've been faster." She essentially said it was our fault and had a very rude attitude about it. We shouldn't have to apologize for not being that hungry (we came at 8pm). The food itself was good. We got the rigatoni with vodka aurora sauce. Very flavorful. We had the chocolate mousse cake for dessert (they were out of souffle). It was phenomenal. It was rich and creamy - more of a dark chocolate than milk. Also once we ordered the other item (dessert), the waiter was much nicer.

Genuinely the worst food I've ever had. Ordered the tuna melt as well as my other 2 buddies getting an egg sandwich and another tuna melt. The girl comes out carrying the food with possibly the worst attitude. Practically throws the plates on the table and leaves. Heres the best part, the food is insanely disgusting. Tuna straight from the can. Cold. WTF? The employees hate their job, the food is horrendous. Place is a scam. Avoid at all costs. PS We all have food poisoning from this shit show.

I was just discriminated against because of my therapy/service animal at the 7-11 on Second street & Wells avenue. It was totally illegal for the lady to ask me anything other than A) "Is she a service animal, & B) "what does she do for me?"... I almost just sat on the floor and refused to leave as a form of peaceful protest to being discriminated against. I've never had something like that this happen to me, it was f*****g embarrassing to be called out, made to stand and answer questions I didn't have to, and then be talked to like a dumb ass. I have Ptsd and severe anxiety, my dog does wonders for my ability to tolerate being out around people. I am not sure how to go forward from here but I am so f****** mad right now... This disrespectful dirty blonde haired, broad named Jamie Rush has the worst customer service skills in the world... she completely violated my Civil rights as a disabled American. I'm going to contact a couple lawyers offices on Monday and see if they want to pick up a civil rights violation suit... The pertinent part of the ADA act that has to with my dog, myself and how we are to be treated is as follows; Inquiries, Exclusions, Charges, and Other Specific Rules Related to Service Animals When it is not obvious what service an animal provides, only limited inquiries are allowed. Staff may ask two questions: (1) is the dog a service animal required because of a disability, and (2) what work or task has the dog been trained to perform. Staff cannot ask about the person's disability, require medical documentation, require a special identification card or training documentation for the dog, or ask that the dog demonstrate its ability to perform the work or task. Allergies and fear of dogs are not valid reasons for denying access or refusing service to people using service animals. When a person who is allergic to dog dander and a person who uses a service animal must spend time in the same room or facility, for example, in a school classroom or at a homeless shelter, they both should be accommodated by assigning them, if possible, to different locations within the room or different rooms in the facility. A person with a disability cannot be asked to remove his service animal from the premises unless: (1) the dog is out of control and the handler does not take effective action to control it or (2) the dog is not housebroken. When there is a legitimate reason to ask that a service animal be removed, staff must offer the person with the disability the opportunity to obtain goods or services without the animal's presence. Establishments that sell or prepare food must allow service animals in public areas even if state or local health codes prohibit animals on the premises. People with disabilities who use service animals cannot be isolated from other patrons, treated less favorably than other patrons, or charged fees that are not charged to other patrons without animals. In addition, if a business requires a deposit or fee to be paid by patrons with pets, it must waive the charge for service animals. If a business such as a hotel normally charges guests for damage that they cause, a customer with a disability may also be charged for damage caused by himself or his service animal. Staff are not required to provide care or food for a service animal.

I used to love this place. Being born and raised in Germany I grew up eating Dönners all the time. Last time I went (and trust me this will be my last time) I ordered my regular dönner Berlin and within an hour felt horrible, like food poison onset. Fortunately I threw it all up and just felt whacked out the rest of the day. This place used to be my go to lunch place but I'm not risking getting food poisoning. What a pity bc I really enjoyed this place....

When Gluten Free is Not Gluten Free My wife has Celiac which means she needs to eat gluten free. Puckett's advertises itself as having a GF menu. Waitstaff had no idea what GF was and the menu listed biscuits (made with regular flour) as a GF choice. We left without ordering as there was no way for her to have a safe meal.

We visited this place because they advertise they offer gluten free food and my wife in coeliac so it is very important for her not to eat gluten as it causes her to be extremely sick. We clearly told her she was coeliac and needed a gluten free dinner. We sat at the Hibachi table and they informed us that her meal was going to be prepared (correctly) in a separate area. They brought her meal but 5 minutes after she started eating, the waiter rushed to our table, took her plate away and disappeared leaving all of us (including the hibachi chef) really puzzled for what happened. About 2 min later he came with another plate saying that the previous one was wrong as it contained soy sauce (which has gluten). We were shocked! We called for the manager who didn't quite care, blamed the waiter and left. Of course my wife did not eat anything anymore and when we left we told the manager this was not a proper behavior. He laughed in our faces saying he did not charge for her meal so we could not expect anything else. I was really shocked! Of course they should not have charged for her meal as she did not eat anything and she is going to be sick for what she ate! Their behavior was honestly disgusting and we would advice avoiding this place for how they treat people!

We snagged a coveted outdoor reservation during happy hour and were seated promptly. While we were waiting for our drinks, a party of three walked in and seated themselves at a large table behind us. The hostess came over and explained that the table was already reserved and they could be seated inside. One of the men was awful - so condescending and entitled - barking that he knew the manager and to just tell her he'd be sitting down. The poor hostess went to get her manager, Lydia, who came out and greeted the customers warmly. Lydia didn't waste a moment before throwing her hostess under the bus -- she apologized to the rude patrons on her hostess' behalf, and said she had moved around other reservations so they could have the table. Now, a party who had actually made a reservation and requested an outdoor table, would be bumped inside because the manager refused to stand up to this patron -- not a great way to run a business. Now for the food -- Copper Vine has their menu coded with "gluten free." Nowhere does it say that the items are only GF when specified or modified -- it just labels them GF. I ordered the pork belly, which purports to just be gluten free, but mentioned that I have celiac, and our waitress responded "oh, let me actually go ask the kitchen. I don't think the menu key is right." She went and checked, and much to my shock, was right. At this point, I was rattled and wanted to talk to someone who truly knew what was gluten free. Our waitress sent over the manager, Lydia again, who had literally no information. She started off with "well I try to eat gluten free too," which is never something that someone with celiac wants to hear. I could tell she was making it up as she went, as she couldn't answer any follow up questions. If I'd been with my boyfriend, we would have just left. Since I was in NOLA visiting friends, I stuck it out, opting for a seafood dish that I was confident was naturally GF. The food was good, but management makes or breaks a restaurant, and Copper Vine needs to spend some serious time retraining their staff.

Doesn't CVS have any rules about dogs in their store?! Thousands if not millions of children are bitten in the face every year because dogs are at their level. So you can't even go into a CVS and turn a corner without worrying about your child being bitten the face! If I ever see this again I will never ever shop in any CVS anywhere in the country. The Ridiculousness needs to stop. If people can't go outside their homes without some animal to comfort them and hold their hand, then maybe they should just stay home. What about the people who are allergic to dogs and their hair? Since when in any common-sense Arena do you put animals before human beings?

Spent $50 for pizza and I got the most pathetic pizzas I've ever seen. Crust was Udis GF crust not even hand made. They said 20 mins and the pizza was cold when I picked it up. They didn't even put all the toppings I asked for and got the order wrong after charging $1.50per toppings. This is not a place that takes pride in the food they are serving but just in it to charge premium prices for less than mediocre pizza. Also got to-go drinks and more than half the cup was filled with ice. I will never go back and if you are looking for gluten free pizza or a place that values customers and the food they serve do NOT go here. This is by far the worst pizza I've gotten in the area. Very disappointed and appalled that someone would even serve such dry and tasteless "pizza."

We made the mistake of stopping at this restaurant. We ordered a #1 and a 8 pc. grilled chicken nugget with a power side salad. After waiting for 10 minutes (there was no one else in line) the cashier looked up and saw us not looking so happy. He walked over to the counter where our order had been sitting bagged and ready to go for awhile. He didn't apologize, but simply said, "Here's your order!" And that's not the worst of it! We got our food and left. Within a couple of hours of eating my husband's stomach started churning along with burping. We realized his order came with more than he bargained for--food poisoning. I have never been to such a slow, uncaring, unmotivated Chick-First-A in my life! After reading the other reviews, we wish we had read them before we ate here! I'm posting to hopefully encourage this franchise to live up to the standard the Chick-Fil-A company has established. Whether it be the management, the employees or the franchise owner, this is a clarion call to fix your restaurant--for the health of all who will eat here unaware! We will not be back!

We were very disappointed in our experience here which was unfortunate because we are in the neighborhood and had very high hopes. We went for breakfast this morning and they seemed to be out of a lot of items. I could look past that however when the breakfast that I ordered came out there was an item that was substituted without notifying me. I have a food allergy and could not eat the substituted item. When I notified the server there was no apology. He kind of brushed it off like it wasn't a big deal. Not to mention the item that was supposed to be in the dish that was substituted was corn bread. I'm not sure how you are a southern restaurant that serves breakfast all day and you are out of corn bread before 10am. My coffee was lukewarm and the other dishes that came out also seemed to be lukewarm. Overall not a pleasant experience and will not return.

Very poor customer service. I called the toll free line after their gluten free bread made my mom very ill. The representative was very rude, very cold and hung up on me. I would never purchase their product again.

Chase appears nice on the outside, but the food was mediocre at best, certainly not worth the price. My mom got terrible food poisoning from the ravioli that kept her up all night. The vodka pappardelle and eggplant parm were good, but swimming in sauce. If you are considering Italian in SB, skip this place.

Bocconcini is more casual than I expected -- more like a pizza parlor with mood lighting than a fancy Italian restaurant, but it was clean, with the added benefit of being BYOB. For appetizers, our table split rice balls and a personal gluten free pizza. They were good, not great. For entrees, I got a gluten free bolognese ($19), and my friends got two salmon pasta specials in vodka sauce ($24/pp), and a vodka sauce penne ($15). Two of my friends commented that the vodka sauce was overly rich / heavy. My bolognese was fine--underwhelming flavors in the gravy. Our server was nice, but careless. When he dropped the rice balls off, they were on our table for two minutes before he came back and said they were actually not ours, then gave them to another table (weird?)... Once our entrees came out, he asked if we wanted cheese -- we said yes, then he forgot to bring it. We waited about 5 minutes before flagging him down. When he did come back, he started to put cheese on my pasta, then panicked... he'd noticed that the pasta they'd given me wasn't gluten free! Luckily, I'd been waiting for cheese so I'd only had one bite. As a celiac though, it was pretty upsetting that a restaurant purporting to be so GF friendly could actually be so careless. When he returned my dish to the kitchen, I overheard that he had forgotten to enter my dish as gluten free (as opposed to a mistake in the kitchen). Infuriating because he took our order from memory instead of writing it down. I was a server for many years... if you can't get every order 100% right from memory, you should be writing it down! To apologize, he brought out two desserts on the house. I appreciated the gesture, but certainly won't be running back here. Giorgio is still the best place for gluten free Italian in Philly.

In & Out is a great place to eat, but my wife and father both got sick (food poisoning) after we ate there yesterday. They had onions on their burgers & I didn't. Unfortunate! Ruined the last day of our Christmas vacation in CA.

I give this two stars because it wasn't exactly horrible. The atmosphere is ok, but gets a little loud. The App we ordered never came, and the gyro was only Ok. Please note. The traditional Greek food a Gyro Only comes with French fires, a Belgium/French side. And substitutions (even for food allergies) are Strictly prohibited. So if you are looking for good Greek food, there are certainly better places to go.
