We came to this restaurant and explained our Celiac disease and the cashier checked with the chef about if the Maiz (elote-corn) was GF. I could already sense they were not taking it seriously. They brought it out and my wife had a few bites and noticed a fried pork rind. We asked them about it and they said its fried in the fryer with flour. I spoke to the manager and they then changed their mind about the corn quesadilla that we ordered and said they cannot ensure its gluten free. I would not come to this restaurant if you have any allergy.

This place is a neat little stop! Rustic and unique it's definitely pleasing to the eye! I attended a wedding there this past weekend , the venue was quaint and the food was delicious..... Until that night and the next day, and the day after that! Come to find out myself and my husband weren't the only people suffering from this event! The entire wedding had come down with food poisoning! I am embarrassed for the bride as she had to apologize to the people she chose to share this life event with, that they had fallen ill from attending! Addition to this review: the entire wedding was struck with NOROVIRUS !!!! Such a bummer, now my husband wont eat there, and it totally would have been a place I would have gone to again....

I was here about a year ago and though I don't remember what I ordered I definitely enjoyed my experience. I went yesterday though and it was a whole different story. My party of three's deviled egg appetizer was overly salty. I ordered the cheeseburger as did one of my other friends (only because the entree she'd originally wanted was sold out). She found hers way too salty. When she told the waiter he was very nice and apologetic about it and offered to get her something else. My burger on the other hand was very good but the fries were some of the greasiest I've ever encountered in my life-yuck. The three of us split a small chocolate pudding dessert and it was delicious but incredibly rich, more than one small ramekin split three ways would have been too much to handle. On top of this sub-par experience I began to feel ill about and hour after the meal and was stricken with food poisoning that lasted a few hours [TMI but it was coming out of both ends]. I'm not someone with a sensitive stomach and this has only happened to me one other time in my life. I was especially disappointed because I know that the people who run Pub & Kitchen also run The Diving Horse in Avalon, one of my favorite restaurants where I've never had anything but a fantastic meal. Bottom Line: If you want heavy, salty, greasy food that might get you sick, save your money and go to Mcdonalds.

Love the decor, gets super busy and parking lot is kind of difficult to navigate. First visit was a Sunday afternoon, great service, great food. Portions a little small on the tacos for the price, but that visit deserved 5 stars for sure. Second visit on a Thursday evening was not as great. Server was kind of rude, but as a New Yorker, I don't usually let that bother me. Just odd because service the first visit was spectacular. Guac was amazing. Tacos seemed kind of haphazardly thrown together, and portions were even smaller than last time. I think they just need to work out all the kinks and will be an outstanding experience every time. As a clean eater, and a gluten free eater, they have SO MANY options. So happy to have them in my neighborhood and can't wait to go back and watch them improve!

Worst Chinese food I ever had everything was hard like it's was sitting in a buffet and I know they don't have one I live 5 blocks away and it took an hour and a half everything was cold the wonton soup was sitting so long they were in a million pieces and the order was wrong this place use to be good , don't waste you time woke up with food poisoning

We are new to Santa Barbara and wanted to try the local sushi on State street. We actually attempted to call before walking 25 minutes to this location to which they didn't answer their phones on the two attempts of calling. This was for my wife's and best friend's birthday; and we had a party of ten. When we arrived, they told us they would have to seat us at two tables of five, possibly separated, and that there would be a 15 minute wait. After waiting well past 20 minutes, a seated customer they over served alcohol to vomited on the floor under her table. After 5 minutes of scrambling their workers to address that mess, they walked up to us and tell us they won't be able to seat us Because, "It will overwhelm their servers." We were ready to indulge, pay good money for drinks and food, they made us excessively wait and turned our business down. Absolutely haphazard of the staff and a terrible experience for us.

Everything here is gluten free which is amazing! They also have some dairy free items as well for people who are dairy free or have lactose intolerance. In my experience, being someone who is dairy free and gluten free, it is almost impossible to find a place that serves dairy free and gluten free French toast! I always order it when I come here and I love it! My mother and sister like their flat breads as well. Their df/gf cupcakes are great too! My favorites are the Bahama Mama cupcake and the Lemon cupcake. If you are looking for a place with no chance of gluten cross contamination--look no further! This is a great, tasty and safe place to eat!

After seeing my previous review, management reached out to me and offered to re-do my latest order that I wasn't pleased with. This time was a total success! To be fair, I had written my last review while frustrated with food poisoning and might have been harsh in my rating, because as I stated before - my previous visits were always pleasant. So, they have regained me as a customer and I hope that my future experiences mimic this re-do. Thanks for the good customer service, and the yummy rolls, Tomo!

*** HEALTH WARNING *** After reading all the great reviews I had to give this place a try this past Wednesday 10/9/19... I even decided to bring my brother who was in town. My reward? 48 hours of the worst food poisoning - violent, uncontrolled vomiting and diarrhea I have ever experienced or even heard of. My wife called my brother the next day to tell him I was deathly sick and HE had the exact same thing only starting two hours after me! It gets worse... my brother brought home half of his Chicken Quesadilla which his son ate Friday - when I called to check on my brother today he told me that his son was in the bathroom floor having started vomiting uncontrollably overnight. We are literally taking stool samples to Vanderbilt tomorrow to have checked for Listeria, Salmonella etc. This place needs to be shut down immediately. Hoping that this warning saves some others the pain my family has been through. It was a living hell.

We got into the restaurant without a reservation which was great, but we were seated in the hottest spot of the entire restaurant which was behind the oven. Our server was nice and took our order and explained some options on the menu. Our appetizer came out fairly quickly- we shared a plate of escargot on french bread. The bread in the middle was soggy, but it was okay. We waited 40 minutes for our food to come out. My mom took one bite of the food and about ten minutes later got very sick & vomitting, passing out. She has no known allergies to any food. Our server was polite about it and admitted it was pretty hot back there (she didn't seat us there, it was someone else). My mom's friend refused the rest of her food, I stopped eating mine because I was helping my mom, & my mom got a free replacement of the food she ordered but likely will not eat it. I bought my mom an extra plain tomato sauce spaghetti because she hadn't eaten all day and I felt terrible for her. She never gets sick. The bill was around $60 for her (I believe she paid only for my food and her friends, as well as the appetizer), & $17 for me (the spare spaghetti I got my mom). We got home and now I am sick (also pregnant), & my mom's friend is sick. The staff did nothing wrong, but I do feel like we deserve to have our money back. At least my mom's bill. She works very hard for her money and never goes out.

Do you like dodging bird droppings while you shop for groceries? Do you enjoy the eye, I mean mouth watering aroma of hot garbage whenever you cook up your freshly purchased meats? Have you ever wanted to buy milk and then throw it out as soon as you open it because it's curdled before you even got it home? If you answered "yes" to these questions, then your store of choice should be Cousins Supermarket where the aisles are filled with flying (pooping) birds, the meat is always rotten, and the dairy products are already pre-curdled for your enjoyment. I've been going to Cousins off and on for about 7 years. I didn't go for about 3 years straight because I got fed up with wasting money on rotten food and dodging bird sh!t. But then I had some lapses in judgement and decided to go again because it was close to me. Big mistake. Even bigger waste of money. I've had to throw out milk, cheese, beef, chicken, freezer burnt(yellowed smelly) fish, and wilted pre-packaged lettuce for salad. There may be more, but please forgive me if I forgot something. I'm completely disgusted and not wasting money there anymore. Oh, wait. 1 star for their deals on bread - you can often get 2 loaves for the price of one. But that's about it. Stay away unless you like bird sh!t or spending lots of time at the hospital with food poisoning.

We used to frequent this chain restaurants on an almost weekly basis but haven't been in a while because life has changed. We decided since we were running errands and in the are that it would be a good place to grab some lunch and we stepped in to the Charlotte Avenue restaurant. We realized the menu changed which was disappointing because my favorite thing on the menu were the buffalo fries, however knowing that I still love french fries I got the loaded fries. The portion came to the table it was extremely small and disappointing compared to what they had been, and what we used to get on a regular basis. The fries were especially lacking as the cheese and bacon were very sparse and did. Ot compare to the buffalo fries that were previously on the menu. The ranch that accompanied the dish was also very disappointing, as it seemed more like a side of sour cream and less like a dipping sauce. My husband's burger was decent but again the side size was significantly less than it had been previously. Another serious issue was the service. As i was not at the table when the waiter arrived, and unable to order, the waiter took 15 min to return to take our drink order, and had to be prompted to bring water to the table. The waiter was constantly at the table behind us, but was aloof and distant toward our party as we had a child and did not appear to be a party that would drink copious amounts. As we only had three beers total and had to flag him down for a second round for my husband, or anything else for that matter, we feel as if we were profiled and discriminated against just because we had a child. The overall experience was disappointing and we felt like we were singled out in our section because we're the only one with kids and we were not drinking as heavily as the tables around us. Not even an hour after leaving the restaurant I felt sick to my stomach and as the only thing that i had eaten in the past 8 hrs was from this establishment it is obvious that it was the food that I had just eaten. This chain of events is really sad as we will not be back for a very long time due to the disappointing service, poor quality of food, and potential food poisoning, which is very sad as this used to be a favorite of my husband and I.

Ervice could have been better.. Our waitress brought water for one of us but didn't fill the rest of the glasses that needed it. Paper towels were not brought to the table, we had to go take them from an empty table. Didn't come back to ask how everything was, plus side we didn't get charged for "glass" of wine we didn't drink. Crawfish boil seasoning was heavy on the crawfish not mixed on to the boil water and had a bonus stick in with them. Chicken wing breading was too salty had to peel off to eat. Siitting outside when your allergic to Marijuana is not a good idea as the neighbors and pedestrians partake.

On 2/20/16, I encountered this place that my friends raved about. Once we were seated the waitress brought water to the table OMG the PLASTIC cup was cloudy, Grease was floating on top of my water made me want to VOMIT. I asked for a to go cup of water she said those cups are not allowed on The tables in the dining room but she did give me a straw to drink my GREASY CLOUDY WATER. I have no idea how the food taste. All 8 of us left went around the corner to Jerry Bobs, the food was great got my water with my meal in a to go cup. Everyone does not drink from plastic ware. For me the impression I got from Brawleys made me VOMIT

The place is disgusting and dirty. I don't understand how this place is rated so high. I went in looking for something to eat and the place was a giant mess! I would not grab anything here for fear of food poisoning. I would not recommend this place!!!!!!!!

St Pete beach has great views and a fairly high density of tourists. The Rumfish grill caters to the family crowd who doesn't want a diner or chain experience. The giant fish tank is a draw for all and a great visual at one end of the dining room. The menu is as focused on seafood as you would expect. Portions are small and our group of 5 ordered the crab/artichoke dip and a mussels to start. The dip was good if light on crab. The mussel order left 4 per person which for $10 is OK, but the server could have let us know it was small. Entrees were just so so, the swordfish was over cooked and under seasoned, the shrimp and grits was heavy on grits and had the same amount of shrimp as the cocktail, 5. The gluten free options are fine but underwhelming.

I wanted to love this place, but it was just a "like". I ordered off the gluten free menu, and selected the BBQ Chicken. The manager came to the table to ask about my allergy severity, which was nice. The sauce arrived on the side, and the fries were excellent. The disappointment is really the fact that no salad comes with dinner, nor is there bread for the table. I wouldn't have been able to eat any, but my companions would have enjoyed it. For the price, I would like a bit of extras. Our waiter was attentive, and efficient. Atmosphere was great for a Saturday afternoon. Cocktails were pretty good as well. I had the Indianapolis.

"Church basement" is spot-on, but not in a kitchy way - rather, just in need of disinfectant. $14 bucks for a tough burrito and an imported Coke. Luckily, the storm knocked the power out so I had an excuse to stop eating without feeling rude. It's been 24 hours and no food poisoning! Hip-hip, 2-stars!

I've gotten food poisoning from here twice. Both times from the hummus! The first time I wasn't sure that it was Phat Bites that had made me sick, as I'd eaten somewhere else as well that day. But when I went back this past weekend and got sick again, that sealed the deal. Very questionable food safety standards. Don't recommend- at all. EDIT; Forgot to mention the length of our wait! 30 minutes for my husbands sandwich? And it was cold when it came out.

I had a horrible experience with this restaurant. I ordered delivery the other night ( pork shoulder ramen) and within 1-2 hours of eating it I was violently sick - don't want to go into detail- but very sick all night. I called the restaurant the next day and a manager rushed me off the phone and said they were "trying to get me a refund". I didn't really care about the lousy 15 dollar refund. I was letting them know that I basically got food poisoning at their restaurant and that is the response I got. Fast forward, it is 2 days later and I STILL don't feel right. I would normally never write this kind of review, but was extremely upset by this and disappointed in how it was handled. I have ordered from this restaurant before and always thought it was very good. I will not be ordering or frequenting this place again.

Alright. So I said I'd update my review (way back when) if I ever ate at CBQ. Those pictures I posted from August of 2015 were the first and only time I will eat here. CBQ must use the same sort of spice that Gilley's uses. Because less than an hour after eating my pizza and some of my boyfriend's fries, I was breaking out on the dance floor, and I don't mean the newest line dancing moves. I broke out in hives, MUCH worse than when I was at Gilley's. In case you haven't read my Gilley's review: when I broke out in hives it was on my face and neck there. Here, it was face neck, back and chest. I must have missed the possible allergen note on the pizza and/or chili dog and/or fries. I refuse to eat there because I have no idea what made me break out again, and considering the fact that it was worse the second time, I don't want to know what the third break out will be like. Another note on the food, the service was horrible. I'm pretty sure we had to flag down a server to bring us a menu. Luckily the wait wasn't long between ordering the food being ready. But the longest part, was waiting for the bill. 6 months later and we're still waiting! I think my boyfriend and I have bought enough booze though from the place that it more than adds up. So that dropped my star count for this place. Also, the on again off again Saturday night dancing. It's disappointing when I hear that CBQ has dropped the Saturday night dancing. It's a place to come and dance early, so if I don't feel like staying out super late to go dance at GSR, I can come here. Luckily, for the moment as of 2/24/2016, there is Saturday dancing. Another star drop, would be what happened this past Saturday (2/20/2016). I do believe O'Clearys and CBQ are owned by the same person, hence the connector hallway between the two (one I've heard of and haven't seen). Apparently there is a band that plays every Saturday at O'Clearys, well this last Saturday it was fully rented out and there was no place for the band to go, except next door to CBQ. I was wondering how we were going to line dance to rock or something, but their set list was country. Cool. When they began playing, I was nearly thrown to the back of the place like a bug squished on a wall. Their sound was far too loud. I felt like I was at a concert and could barely carry on a conversation with my friends. I feel the manager should have stepped in and asked the band to adjust their sound, the DJ's music has NEVER been that loud. Secondly, the band was off. No one was harmonious. But, I still danced to their music as best I could, because I came to dance. If I wanted to listen to a live band I would go to Gilley's (nothing wrong with a live band, just not my style). What I love about CBQ is the DJ, who plays the songs the dancers request. A band has a setlist (I've never been to gilleys for the band, but I'm guessing that's how it is) they've planned and rehearsed and I'm sure requests are frowned upon, and not played upon. The final reason why I've dropped my review from 5 to 1 star is management. I wrote a note to the manager, expressing my displeasure (I'm better writing my thoughts than speaking on the fly). And rather than taking into account the displeasure of a regular customer (who spoke for pretty much all the regulars) and perhaps taking this into consideration and speak with the displeased patron, he became enraged that I should dare disagree with his choice. (At least that's the projection I got from the situation. I'm not sure how much longer I will come here and give this place my business, but for the moment, I'll still go and dance the night away. I'd give the place 0 stars, but there are two good bartenders, Tara and Jeremy and they're a redeeming factor for the business. They are prompt, and make your drink perfect, definitely worth the price you pay.

Worst FOOD POISONING EVER! I dined at Milk and Honey this past Thursday for lunch with my husband. All was fine, until it wasn't. I had the chicken sandwich, sans bun, with the kale salad as the side...everything else the same as the menu called for. Within the hour I felt extremely nauseas, followed by 12 straight hours of vomiting. It's now Sunday, I'm on a work trip, still feeling like sh#t and imagine my surprise when one of my closest friends had breakfast there on Monday of this past week and experienced THE EXACT SAME PROBLEM! She had to leave work and went home and was sick and dehydrated. What's scary is that this nearly put me in the hospital and I'm still f#cked up. To make matters more exciting, I woke up to the top story in my google news alert being about the lawsuits filed against them from last fall! WTF is going on at this place? How do two people get disturbingly ill from two different meals the same week? What's going on in the kitchen?!!! Nashville- please, for the sake of someone not ending up hospitalized-or worse- please please please send someone to investigate this restaurant. This is grotesque! I am BEYOND livid. This is unacceptable to have two people get such serious cases of food poisoning in one week- disgusting. NEVER EVER will I step foot in this restaurant again! Fingers crossed I don't end up at the doctor as I'm still struggling to get rehydrated and keep food down.

I will admit that I have only been to Brew Brothers after 9:30 PM on Friday and Saturdays, so this review is definitely a small sample size of the time that Brew Brothers is open. That being said, the experiences I have had are mixed. I have had times when the whole experience was awesome, the bartenders were nice, the bouncers were cordial, the music (DJ) was awesome, and the crowd was jovial. However.... at the same time there have been times I was hassled by the bouncers as "my ID didn't look like me" even though it looked exactly like me and I quoted all the information on it, the bartenders flat out ignored me to focus on ALL the girls at the bar who possessed two large "items" that I do not possess that happened to be flowing out of their tops, and the music has been strictly country music covers. Blahhhhh In addition, there have been several times when the smell of vomit hung pungently in the air throughout the dance floor with no one attempting to clean it up. My advice to Brew Brothers is be consistent. Either be an awesome time, or accept that you are going for the "Slimy" feel and look. Don't waffle back in forth there. For all the bad times I have had here, I will definitely keep giving it a shot as a party spot in Reno.

Superior is....good. I wouldn't go so far as to say great. I've been going there since I was in high school and have always enjoyed the ambiance and aesthetic more than the food. As I've gotten older...I've mostly enjoyed the margaritas! I have to admit that their margaritas pack a punch and you never leave disappointed - unless its Cinco de Mayo! This review isn't about Cinco de Mayo BUT i couldn't not mention how out of control the crowd is during this event and to top it off...when you finally get a margarita it tastes like "mix" without tequila. Not hot!! The brisket quesadillas are yum and the queso is typically delish although the other night, I'm convinced my boyfriend and I had a touch of food poisoning from it! Needless to say we won't be back for awhile! If I could choose...I'd choose Chipotle all day!

I'm really unhappy with the service I received. They forgot my appetizer and my dessert. It took them TWO HOURS to bring it out. It was awful. They brought my entree, then my dessert then my appetizer. In that order. And they made my entree with gluten when I'm gluten intolerant and specifically asked for gluten free. Then they told me that I would also have to pay for my gluten pizza as well as my gluten free pizza. I would rate 0 stars if I could.

Only reason am leaving this review is because Yelp keeps sending me notifications. Local to the Sponge Docks... My wife ordered the Lamb Shank with Pasta and came down with Food Poisoning. From 7pm till we hrs in the morning she was Throwing up and major knife stabbing pains in her Stomach!!! She had a Hella of a night! Other than that it was great!!

Food poisoning for the last time! Tried to give them one more chance as they are so close to home, but after three bouts of food poisoning, no more! They comp'd our future meals in an attempt to get us to return, which we did. And this is what we get . . . the last and FINAL incident happened the night before my husbands birthday. We had eaten at Bully's the night before and we were both so sick the next day (we shared a medium rare cheeseburger and had chicken wings for an appetizer.) I had to cancel all of his birthday plans the next day. And no, it's not the flu that's going around. It has happened two other times eating there and it's horrible. Never again.

I had high hopes for this place. My boyfriend and I ate here getting pork tacos and beef empanadas, both with green herb rice and then churros. We got a margarita and sangria. My margarita was oddly salty, as if someone accidentally got salt in the drink in addition to putting it on the rim of the glass. The food tasted good, save for the rice which was a tad weird. Maybe a half hour after leaving both my boyfriend and I had horrible stomach pains. We definitely each had a mild case of food poisoning. Lasted a couple days. To top it off I couldn't hear anything the waiter was saying, it was way too noisy. It was weird to see people exiting from the back of the building, and parking was tight.

I am giving a 3 star rating not because the Donuts are not good. These Donuts are amazing, great flavor, fresh, soft, my mom even liked them and she is very hard to please with food! I am happy that we had a chance to buy Donuts from District Donuts while we stayed in New Orleans. So why a 3 star rating? Well as me and mom sat and ate donuts and drank coffee, I noticed the cooks handling the food not wearing gloves while fixing food. This became really gross because as one guy carved ham with no gloves, he proceeded to eat a piece of the ham, put his hands back on the ham and continue carving. He then went outside to get something, it looked like a piece for the carving machine, he came back in, and just continued to carve ham. NOT ONCE DID HE WASH HIS HANDS. He touched door knobs, went outside in the rain, possibly going to his car, came back in, and put his hands right back on the ham. SO I had thought about eating a slider because they looked good, but I couldn't risk the food poisoning. It is way too easy to get sick from contaminated food, I need them to implement a glove wearing policy ASAP. I know the donut makers probably don't wear gloves either, and yes I could have probably gotten sick, but by the time I noticed that no one was wearing gloves it was too late, I had already enjoyed the donut. Thankfully I did not get sick. But notice to employees please wash your hands, and wear gloves or the health department may end up closing down District Donuts.

I'll keep it short. I got food poisoning. Wife ordered Lenten special shrimp nachos which consisted of 4, count them four tortilla chips each topped with it's very own shrimp for $15. One guy at our table got his food precisely 15 minutes after the first entrée was brought out. Watery, worst salsa you can get. Oh, did I mention that I got food poisoning? I lived in Dallas for a short while which has excellent Mexican food. This place would not even make it through the weekend over there. God awful!

I ordered the taco tacu a el macho and advised no shrimp as I'm allergic. However I received my dish with shrimps and I had to share my daughters dish not to wait another 10mins. They provided a to go plate but that defeats the purpose of going out to eat! I told the girl at the front it's my daughters bday and wanted to surprise her. We receive the check and no surprise cake slice so I go to the front to ask her and she said she forgot but walked by us like 6 times. We had a better experience the first time we went.

This quite possibly could be the worst "fast" food restaurant I have ever experienced in my life. And that in itself is saying A LOT. I really didn't think that this place could suck as bad as my previous experience(s), but I was proven wrong. I'm a baseball fan and this place...solid 3 strikes in a row. First time I thought, well it's lunch time and it's busy, places run out of ice, it happens, $5.00 burrito looked like a $2.00 burrito...I let it slide. 2nd time, after 15 minutes in the drive thru...when my turn was up to pay, I kept driving. Now the 3rd, you are probably thinking I am glutten for punishment. I am. I was hungry and from some cheap mex, Taco Bell was too far. Should have driven the extra 5 minutes since I waited in the drive thru for 13 minutes, only 4 cars in front of me!! It gets better. Dude gives me food after me sitting at the window there for a solid minute. A minute later I get my drink. I was speechless. As I am driving away, I realize there is no ice in my drink. It gets better, I do not dairy, I am allergic so I order everything with no cheese. So after all of this, when I finally get the chance to bite into my burrito, I unwrap it really quick just to check...Mofo'ers filled it with cheese!?! The only thing good were the fries. Only come here if you are playing the game "how bad can they F up my order" with your friends. Instead of taking my burrito back, I am giving it to my dog and writing this review. Worst EVER! Go check it out for yourself. #turndownthesuck #ithinkihearbanjos

Love the atmosphere in here! But you could use some more !!vegan!! /gluten-free items. Also, I excitedly ordered a banana sorbietto gelato smoothie with chocolate pumps and espresso! And it was amazing! But the girl Linda could have been a little nicer! I asked if I could have the rest of my smoothie in an extra cup and she said "no, you already had sixteen ounces." And avoided eye contact with me while began serving the next customer. I don't see why pouring good gelato smoothie down the drain is better than me drinking it! I paid $5.65. But she was pretty rude and choppy at taking my order! She was back and forth between making me pay and making the smoothie. It made me feel slightly uncomfortable. She could have just made the smoothie and had me pay after. Overall it wasn't a nice experience though my food tasted good, her service and interaction totally ruined it. Perhaps I should drop a line with management. Anywhere else I go, associates are happy to give me a little extra of whatever is left, whether at Starbucks or Jamba Juice. I've not run into such a rude encounter in the past. Especially because Whole Foods is usually super kind and warm and big on customer service. I love you guys!!! I've had all very positive experiences with Whole Foods in the past!!! But somehow Linda was stuck up and rude about a little extra smoothie at the bottom of a blender. You deserve better employees than this. Disappointed.

Gave it several chances. This is now the 2nd time i have gotten food poisoning from the tuna melt, so we will not be returning. Way too expensive for a "diner" and they got rid of their yummy steak fries and changed to a different type.

My God stay away. Stay away for your children, stay away for yourselves. Stay away from the Friday night fish fry. FOOD POISONING. My wife and I joined some friends here for their Friday grouper special....it has become apparent these special fish fries are to push fish that is turning so they don't waste product. What a mistake we made. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the poisoning was right on time...6 hours later we were taking turns for the toilet. Hmmmm...exactly six hours prior my wife and I ate "fresh" fish at Jimmy Guanas. Coincidence...? There is no excuse in 2011 for restaurants to be sickening people - there are way too many regs to follow. Of note, the grouper was horrible. If what I ate was grouper....my name is Sam Q.

Could vomit. I got the hummus and veggie sandwich since I am a vegetarian. Everything was going great until I got to the middle of my sandwich and I FOUND A RANDOM PIECE OF CHICKEN. C-H-I-C-K-E-N!!!!!!!!! I was already having a horrible day then to bite into a piece of chicken. GAG GAG GAG!!!!! I had to throw out my entire $13 sandwich then I HAD TO ENDURE FOUR HOURS OF CROWDED TRAINS WITHOUT ANY FOOD IN ME. I AM NOT HAPPY.

I used to go to Chill on the Hill frequently, and it was such a great neighborhood space... it seems like it is going downhill. Tonight, after calling first, then asking AGAIN when we got there, I was told by the clearly unsure employee that a certain flavor did not contain egg. I started to serve it to my stepson, who is incredibly allergic to egg, only to have the employee come out with the ingredient list (which he obviously hadn't checked BEFORE) and note that there was indeed egg in that flavor. THANK GOD my stepson hadn't taken a bite. To top it all off - ugh! - a bunch of the toppings were clearly stale. If that's your business - frozen yogurt and toppings - be good at it. Keep things fresh. It's not going to kill you to open a new bag of Oreos. And if you're going to hire employees - make sure they know the LAW about food safety and allergies.
Just ok to me. Overpriced, under serviced. They forgot the birthday, forgot my kids nut allergy, and forgot the food to go. Highly overrated :(

We've passed by this cute storefront for years but finally went in for a late lunch, and I'm so glad we did! The service was awesome, the food was delicious and the restaurant was meticulously clean. That's so important in this Covid-19 upsurge. These guys have all the bases covered. Food runners don't touch dirty dishes, only bus boys handle those items insuring no cross contamination. I started with the Saganaki(flaming cheese) and Skordalia(garlic and potatoes) then had the Grouper alla Hellas for my meal. Everything was delicious. First time in awhile that I had no leftovers. I just couldn't stop eating. We will definitely be back again real soon.

Do not eat here, I repeat do not eat here. My wife and I both got violently ill after eating here. Food was good however not worth the painful vomiting that ensured. Stay away! Please do yourself a favor and stay far far away

CALLING ALL CELIACS!! This place is absolutely incredible!! After talking on the phone with Rachel, she ensured me i'd be safe eating there. When we were seated, she remembered talking to me and made me feel right at home! She explained everything on the menu and all of the incredible gluten free options in great detail. I ordered the garlic bread, the mac and cheese, and the cannoli! All 3 were absolutely amazing! I never felt so safe at a restaurant before! I was able to dive in without any worries of cross contamination. If you have any type of gluten allergy, this is the place for you! Ask for Rachel and she'll take the best care of you!
Pretty tasty, but you have to go early on in the day or they are pretty wiped out. Like that they have Paleo and Gluten Free options as well.

The bones are there. Franklin Burger Company is still relatively new so expect that they're working out some kinks. During my visit, there were quite a few kinks but the fundamentals were sound. I think as time goes on and they get better oiled, the machine will work quite well. In this interim period, however, you might want to take a few things into consideration. Let's start off with the good: the food. Like I mentioned, the fundamentals are sound and for a restaurant to have good food... that's the biggest hurdle. Everything else can be fixed (hopefully quickly). I was excited to check this place out because it offered gluten-free buns. In 2019 (well, 2018 when I visited) -- especially in Middle Tennessee -- I am confounded that more burger places don't offer this simple fix. The demographic wants/needs it and it opens you up to a larger market share. In any event, FBC has 'em so I made my way from Nashville for a fancy burger. I ordered the green chile cheeseburger because I will usually eat anything with hatch chiles. I found the burger to taste great: chiles, American cheese, onion, tomato, (romaine) lettuce, and a creamy jalapeno sauce made every bite one that I enjoyed. The bun wasn't the best. I appreciated the effort but it was very crumbly -- which is a hazard wrt gluten-free bread. I liked my fries and was happy with the portion size. There were enough of them to accompany the burger and not act as a garnish. See? Sound fundamentals. The problem: most everything else. We came for an early dinner on a Tuesday night and were pretty surprised to see the place so full. The dining room isn't very large so if you come in behind a few parties you're going to find yourself waiting. After a brief wait, we were seated at a high top. I don't enjoy eating dinner at high tops but there wasn't much of a choice. People were lingering at their four-tops. The restaurant can't control people being inconsiderate. After sitting we waited a noticeable chunk of time for our server. Once he arrived, he didn't introduce himself, ask if we've been here before, explain the menu, etc. He jumped right in to asking for our order. This is a training issue. We explained that were newbies and had questions. He didn't have answers so he walked away and said he'd come back. Upon his return, we ordered drinks but he didn't know much about them. He claimed it was because he didn't drink. Okay. Fair. But a server should know the menu. We ordered blind and noticed it took a while to get our drinks. Thanks to our proximity to the bar, we noticed the bartender and a server discussing how to make the drinks. Not a good sign. My Fuzzy Fozzy told that tale. I would avoid the bar program for a while. Thinking better of mixed drinks, we opted for beers next. With my gluten-free issue, I ordered a cider (the only one on the menu). I was told that they were out. Okay. Begrudgingly, I ordered a glass of wine. I knew I was in trouble when it took the bartender a while to find a glass. Anyone who's been behind a bar knows standard pour sizes for wine vary by the type you order. I did not receive a 'red' pour but that didn't matter much considering that my glass had a lipstick stain on it. Repulsive. Rather than wait for my server to return, I went to the bar to exchange the glass. This time I received a wet glass (water inside and outside) and a worse pour. I returned to my table annoyed. My friend noticed the wine situation had gone from bad to worse. As if on cue, our server let me know that there were, indeed, cider bottles and asked if I wanted one. Yes, I did. I returned the wine. At the end of our meal, the bartender asked my table if we wanted the extra glass of poured wine (that I'd returned) because 'someone' didn't want it. No. No, we don't. And, yes: I was charged for the (more expensive) wine rather than the cider I ordered. Based on my experience, FBC isn't quite yet ready for prime time. I'd give it a few months to get its sea legs and see how things are by then. The 'problem' with living in an area with such a vibrant food scene is that competition is fierce and first impressions go a long way. The good news is, FBC has solid food. The rest can be trained away... and, hopefully, that can be done quickly.

The first time we wen to Izzos it was ok, pricey for a fast food place. The second time we went was awful. The girl who made our burritos was rude telling my husband to "relax" when he said he didn't need a cup for his bottled drink. She thought she was funny, she wasn't. She also didn't use the scooper for the toppings just her gloved hand. Isn't the point of having the scoopers so everything doesn't get contaminated and mixed with everything else? We overpaid and then took our food to the table and the second bite my husband takes reveals a hair in the burrito. GROSS! When he complained He was told that they wouldn't give him his money back but next time he came in he could get a free burrito. What?! You should give your customer his money back AND give him another burrito to eat at that moment! Staff apparently are not required to wear hair nets or hats and the manager is like 20 years old, it's a Mickey Mouse run operation over there. We won't be returning to Izzos. I'd rather drive to mid city and eat at Juan's Flying Burrito. Better service and food.
Cold food, even when they send you to wait, when they brought out our food 5 minutes later all was cold. Also, I've gotten food poisoning a few times here. Just...don't.

(Tempted to give two stars, due to how expensive it is. Being disappointed here means you've just dropped a significant amount for dinner.) My husband and I dined here for our combined birthdays, knowing its overwhelmingly fantastic reputation in Philadelphia. However, admittedly, because of its top-notch reputation and due to just being busy, I had not looked at the menu online beforehand. My mistake. It turned out to be not my style at all. I don't desire to go back. Way over-the-top-expensive, too "foo-foo" for me, and not worth it at all, in my opinion. -Small portions of 5 courses, one of them turned out to be fois gras, which I tasted for the first time and didn't like at all, and some of what they brought me was incredibly ordinary (a VERY tiny slice of chicken with a kind of a relish on it). And some of the food, to me, actually had a weird, mysterious CHEMICAL taste to it! Like Chloraseptic (numbing agent)! Definitely do your homework (which you're clearly doing here on yelp!) and find out about the kind of food and prices (esp wine/wine pairing) before you decide to make a reservation months/weeks in advance and drop $500 on dinner. (I believe our meal included 1 or 2 glasses of wine that my husband had.) We were aware of the pricey-ness, but it just isn't what I want or like in a nice dinner. Service-great, atmosphere-nice. If you go with the 5 course tasting, they can surprise you with what you're eating, each course--or I think(?) you can make your own choices, but it seems to be their thing to have the chef pick (after you've looked at the menu and just discussed any allergies or items you might want to stay away from on the menu).

Not returning to this restaurant. My first time here and it was not a pleasant experience. A Bug was found in my pho broth. Uncooked, bloody chicken wing that was reheated and brought back to us in the same plate (my chunk of the chicken that I bit off was still there and some chicken bones preciously eaten, a contamination issue). We ended up not eating it after it was brought back to us. Even my friends table had uncooked bloody wings as well. My friend waited for his pho order for a really long time after constantly asking and my second pho was even brought out before his . We informed the waitress the first time. The second time, the waitress was informed after I received my SECOND bowl of pho that was replaced due to the bug issue. It was not during busy hours, but the service was slow. Everything felt rushed. The taste of the food was not up to my expectations(which is okay), but the service did not make up for the lost of deliciousness.

Service was really good which is why i gave it three stars , but this restaurant is not allergy friendly at all. Barely anything on this menu states garlic and we picked this restaurant based on that info, yet everything i chose including the lobster mac n cheese had a ton of garlic in it . Never ever i had lobster mac n cheese with garlic in it . The only item in the menu that i could eat was the lobster roll which I ordered connecticut style (drawn butter) was tasty but it was disappointing . They also serve raw garlic fries and the table behind us ordered them so the horrible stench of raw garlic made it feel like i was at a dodgers game . Probably won't return to this restaurant as the menu was deceiving and as hard as the server tried the kitchen just didn't cooperate and left me no choice but the lobster roll . I wanted the steamed clams. this is the only restaurant that said they would not make me an order minus the garlic. It wasn't busy either so not like i asked for a lot. just don't throw the garlic in the sauce and wasn't willing to accommodate . Therefore I can't recommend this restaurant for persons with allergies no matter what it might be.
I got food poisoning from eating here this week. I was not happy when I staff tried to overcharge me but the food poisoning was just the icing on the cake. I plan on taking my business elsewhere

I work right across the street from Honey Grow, and I have tried this place numerous times. I can't comment on the salad options or the honey bar, because I'm not paying 10 dollars for lettuce or sliced strawberries. Anyway, I have tried the stir-fry twice, and both times it has been flavorless, absolutely flavorless. I ask for "light sauce" because I have no idea what the nutritional value on any of this is, and no one can tell you. When I think about asking for regular sauce, I might as well take myself to the Chinese Restaurant across the street and grab some Lo-Mein - i'm sure its just as fattening. If you have a food allergy and have questions, don't expect anyone to know what they're talking about when they give you advice - IF they give you advice. You'll just get a bunch of blank stares. Good luck people..

We chose to order Bocconcini while staying in Philly because it says on menu most things can be prepared gluten free. We ordered: GF Truffle Shuffle, GF Caesar, GF Penne Vodka and GF Truffle Mushroom Ravioli. There was no hint of truffle oil on the pizza, and came cold (maybe the biking Uber driver?). We requested croutons on side of Caesar, as me and daughter both have celiac, but others in my family would eat them... but no croutons were included at all. The worst part was when we opened our Truffle Mushroom Ravioli to see plain old GF PENNE, no Truffle flavor at all. If they substitute a completely different pasta for GF it should be on the menu!!! And to top it off no utensils AND I checked the box to please include. I never leave reviews, but we were so disappointed and are now out almost $80. Overpriced, tasteless Italian.

Last night, my boyfriend and I ate at the Fermentaria. We ate exactly everything the same during the day except last night at the restaurant, I had a veggie burger and he had a regular burger. Within a few hours, he had diarrhea, vomiting, and sick with food poisoning. We've been there lots of times and I'm a fan of their beer, but clearly their food preparation is an issue. We're not the first people on Yelp to bring this issue to light and I'm waiting for a call back from them...

We love visiting our local bakery! My oldest is anaphylactic to dairy and eggs and going to a bakery is a very special treat. We always find something safe and served with a smile. I can't recommend them more :)

So I am guessing if I wanted paleo or gluten free this might be my go to joint. But we ordered one of every flavor and I found them really dense - really really dense. I would have sworn the germ choc was gluten free based on the cake texture. Maybe it was. I'm not saying they were bad but they weren't my cup of tea. The service was great. They answered their phone promptly and it was the midst of coronamadness.

What is this? People really need to step of the games on these reviews. Tell the truth. It was a big disappointment from the start. My family and I went in and the server gave off this bad vibe. I told him nicely to change his gloves because I'm vegan and didn't want to contaminate my food, server gave me a bit of an attitude. Anyways, I didn't care about that. The pizza barely had vegan cheese, the taste was off, and the toppings tasted like they had been out for a while. It was super tasteless and nothing fixed it. I put garlic powder and other spices, pizza still tasted like cardboard. Although the manager seemed nice, the place lack in taste. Not sure how they could go wrong with pizza. Iced tea was alright too. Also, lacked i hygiene...Huge disappointment. Ps: Owner deleted the review they gave me and replaced it with just "I," when my cousin wrote about how she and I were together during the bad experience we had at Maddio's. They thought she was lying. Lets just say we got our money back. Pleased that they did not argue when we came in.

Placed an order on 4/27 for a medium Howies Special pizza, a small gluten free Works pizza minus black olives, Asian Howie wings and Buffalo Howie wings. Not a complicated order, was made online; estimated time was 40 minutes. As we approached the two hour mark I tried calling the store. Sat waiting for 15 minutes waiting for someone to pick up before I gave up. Tried calling again five minutes later, same thing. My son tried and got the same thing. No one was answering at the store. At two hours and twenty five minutes a delivery driver shows up with the food. I am not mean, I do not yell and I do not curse. I simply ask him why it took so long to get the food to us. He gives a sad excuse that really does not answer my question and says I need to call the store. I told him I would but no one is answering the phones at the store. He says something about this is why he isn't a manager anymore and beats a hasty retreat before I can ask or say anything else. The food was cold. Nothing is sadder than a pizza that has sat closed in a box and allowed to cool off except for chicken wings that have sat wrapped in foil in a box and allow to cool off. The pizza just sucked, the sauce was light on top of the fact that it was cold and the cheese was skimped on as well. The wings were inedible. When you get chicken wings and they are fried or baked you expect them to be crispy. That is part of the experience of the wing that makes them so good. The skin on these wings was like limp rubbery flesh. It was disgusting and there was no saving them at that point since the sauce was on them. All and all the experience left a bad taste in our mouths. While I understand that places are slammed with the pandemic this is the time for them to shine, not slack. You either put out your best work or you go down in flames. My business will go with someone else who can deliver a quality tasty (and edible) product next time.

Gluten free options a plus! Definitely need to ask for extra toppings, especially the cheese. Only disappointed about the staff tonight. Stood there waiting for someone to take my order or to even acknowledge I was standing there. Must of had a big rush or something! It was not very clean behind the counter and around all the toppings. The guy making my pizza was very sloppy and seemed annoyed when he would ask if I wanted anything else. The only person who looked like he liked his job was a young man named Dylan. He is the only employee who made eye contact and smiled.

My girlfriend is allergic to gluten and was served standard noodles after ordering gluten free. While this is an honest mistake, made occasionally by waiters, it is actually quite serious and the reaction by the owner was upsetting. My girlfriend was forced to miss her night shift at the hospital after she had confirmed with two waiters the gluten free status of her unusually good "gluten free" noodles. The waiter realized his mistake before we finished our meal, and apologized. The owner however offered an additional ramen instead of an apology and my girlfriend had to request to not pay for her meal. The owner still charged the rest of the table, saying she will take the gluten free option off the menu instead of offering compensation for the restaurant's mistake. While the ramen was decent, I left with a bad taste in my mouth, unimpressed with the owner and her handling of the situation. I will be one less person to clog the line outside an overrated resturant in a city full of amazing establishments run by people who care about their patrons.

Update: GM John called and agreed to refund my meal. He assured me that they will be more careful with substitutions in the future. I'm giving 2 stars because the staff is always extremely friendly. I've been going to this location for several years as it is down the street from my office. Today, however, I did not receive the service I am accustomed to. By way of a backstory, my 6mo old daughter is allergic to milk. Like, screaming in pain allergic. As such, I am very consciously dairy free while breast feeding. Today, I ordered a half sandwich & salad without cheese. I added the dairy-free garlic aioli sauce because that sounded yummy. About 3/4 of the way through the sandwich, I realized they either purposely substituted or accidentally added a cheese spread to the sandwich. Unfortunately the taste and texture was masked by the mayo and other flavors until I got to the end of the sandwich and got a bigger bite of the spread. The protein in milk that my daughter and many people are allergic to takes almost 2 weeks to clear out of your system. Breast feeding is exhausting and hard work without the added stress of knowing that my daughter is now going to be sick from it. She won't eat the hideously expensive hypoallergenic formula, before anyone suggests that as an option. I get that accidents happen, but when I called, the manager gave me a perfunctory "sorry" and offered to remake the sandwich. A little late for that, sadly. $17 for a half sandwich, half salad (with chicken added), a soda and a sick baby. Bummer.

We had high hopes for our lunch here at Spinners. Sadly, those hopes were dashed by the poor experience we had. We were told there was a 30-minute wait, and agreed to wait at a small table behind the hostess station. We were presented with menus, and ordered with the impression that once a table was available along the windows, we would be seated there. During our wait, we noticed that there were tables opening up, but were told by the hostess that once we had ordered, we could not be seated at a table. This wasn't the right answer. If I had been in that position, I would have made an accommodation for my guests, regardless of policy. The food was mediocre at best - bland and not nearly as flavorful as we would have liked. The fish was over-cooked and tough. The mustard on the Cuban was bland and had no snap to it. A member of our party has a severe Latex allergy, and when asked if the kitchen uses Latex gloves in the food prep, our server quickly asserted that no Latex gloves were used. Our experience from a previous visit was that the kitchen did, indeed, use Latex gloves. When we did look at the box, we were shown a box of gloves that had Latex on the side of the box. When we asked to change the one order, we were told it "was too late". Also, when you have staff sitting in the dining area on their phone texting away, that also leaves a poor impression. We are locals who have lived in the area for 35 years, and had a guest with us. This is the most disappointing visit we've had at Spinners, and won't return.

We stopped in here today while waiting for a table at Great Full next door. The chocolate gluten free cupcakes looked good so we bought two. Once we got home and took a bite, yuk, they were so dry and tasteless we threw them out. I am used to moist, delicious gluten free, dairy free cupcakes from Bless Your Heart Bakery in Paso Robles, so this was a big disappointment. I don't know how this bakery is going to make it with such awful cupcakes. The young man behind the counter was great. No complaints on the customer service, just the gluten free chocolate cupcakes. We will not be going back.

I can definitely agree more with the 2 star reviews, but I have never given a 2 star and I think it will have to be for a FAR worse offending place. **NOTE: I changed my mind by the end of this review, that the service sucked such a big one (read my experience below) that it doesn't even deserve 3 stars. I will say this - I am never going back. The search for Hot Dogs in Santa Barbara started here, and ENDED here. I will just have to make the commute to Goleta for the Costco Dogs (so delicious..) I came in with a girlfriend; she ordered a Bratwurst with Bacon; worker upgraded her to a combo and we decided just to add cheese to her fries, because! I ordered a regular Hebrew National, with a cup of water. Simple, right? It took surprisingly long, but we could care less because we were there to eat & chat anyways - but for fellow Yelpers who weren't so casual with their time; we were the ONLY ones there and got our Hotdogs & fries (1 order of fries..) 10 minutes later. Condition of the food: My dog was SO wrinkly, I have never seen anything like that before! A wrinkly, shriveled hot dog? It also, had a REALLY strong meaty smell to it that I have never smelled before. But, I am pregnant, and eating everything - so I closed my eyes and just prayed I would not get my first bout of food poisoning from this dog. I kid you not, I literally did that. -- My friend's dog, looked much jucier, tender and had no wrinkles. However, they forgot her BACON people! S'okay, not a huge deal, right? So we go up, and tell him we need the side of bacon. He looks at us perplexed, and annoyed. He then tells my friend that she did NOT order bacon, the only extra she ordered was cheese on her fries. She insists she did, he insists NO, but he exasperatingly says she could pay and he'll get her bacon. SHE ALREADY PAID! But forget it, she was so taken aback by her experience of trying to be convinced she did NOT order what she always gets from Hotdog places, that it killed it & she dropped it. She said @ least the dog was pretty tasty. No toasting on the buns. Just cold, whatever buns. Not steamed, or anything. Cheese fries - I really wish I took a picture to describe the 'cheese fries' - basically, you know when you put shredded cheese in the microwave on something & how it looks if you cooked it too long? (Hard, dark orange, and yuck) -- yupp those were the fries. Service -- I hate to admit it, but yeah the service worker was high off his butt, just like other reviews have said. When he turned around we couldn't help but cracking up at how in the clouds this guy was. It was, hilarious, sort of, but frustrating too because it made our food take long & the order was incorrect.. I am inches away from rating this place a 2, and you know what? For the places I have given 3 stars for I think I am now doing it. Decision made. This place is a 2!

We had very high expectations for our visit to the blue duck, unfortunately we were very disappointed (lunch 26th December 2019). Our less than experience starts with our waiter who kept us waiting for every aspect from the greeting, drink and meal order, followed by having to get up out of our seats to get our bill. If he would have checked-in on us more we would have ordered more libations from the bar. We were also equally disappointed with the burnt fries we received with our meal. My wife liked her turkey melt but ended up with food poisoning later that evening...likely from the Blue Duck. We recommend caution on your next visit to this place I doubt we will return....good luck!
Watch out if you have food allergies. Luckily I'd only taken one bite if my chicken dish when I spotted the shrimp on my plate. Unacceptable.

My family group of 8 went on a Friday afternoon (July 3rd). We went up to rooftop. The waitstaff are few and far between and very inexperienced. Our female waiter slammed utensils on the table & asked for our order. It took forever to get served. The online menu you accessed from the provided bar code showed tacos that came with corn tortillas (See photo of menu). When we received our order, the tacos came with flour tortillas. We told our waiter that it was wrong and unacceptable since the person who ordered it was gluten free. She got mad at us & said we should have stated the GF issue. Silly us, we believed the menu was accurate! The food we had was good (including the tacos) but the waitstaff seems inexperienced and not happy working there. We ordered 2 signature drinks that came in glasses which were souvenirs, but we were not told that we could keep the glasses. We discovered this fact later!

If you have celiac disease or a gluten sensitivity I HIGHLY recommend avoiding this place at all costs. My cousin and I both have celiac disease and went there last night. I ordered fish tacos and she ordered a chicken salad. I checked online about my meal and all ingredients listed were gluten free (I was mainly concerned with the sauce on the fish since I knew the tortillas were corn and the toppings were salad- all gluten free things). My cousin TOLD the waitress she was gluten free and couldn't eat gluten and the waitress said "I got you". She ordered chicken and salad. When my tacos came out they were fried in flour- does not say fried on the menu but that's fine. I sent them back and apologized for not asking further questions but explained I too have celiac disease and can't have flour and I asked if I could reorder what my cousin was eating since hers looked good and was gluten free. The waitress then says hers was not gluten free and says she didn't hear my cousin say that. My cousin had all but finished her plate by that time so it was only a matter of time before she was sick. She brought out my dinner which was chicken and salad and my chicken was made differently than my cousins was (without soy sauce). And it was really just okay. I understand this establishment doesn't claim to be gluten free. However when someone says they are, PAY ATTENTION. Especially since they do offer gluten free items upon request and she said "I got you" as if it wouldn't be an issue. It's a food allergy. Which can kill you over time so it's extremely important to listen. Drinks were good and service overall was decent. I hate that the waitress didn't pay attention though and then tried to say she wasn't told about the allergy when she was- we all heard. Won't be back due to this, which is unfortunate because it seemed like a cool place. If you don't have celiac disease it seems like a good place though!

I called this restaurant to make reservations. I had a question about an allergy. The man who answered the phone was very rude. He refused to answer my question. I don't care how good the food is..... rudeness is unacceptable!

This was so disappointing. :( Took my mom for a special treat and the food was subpar at best; I had bananas Foster and aside from the fact that it sat -- and sat -- and sat -- under the heat lamp so long the whipped cream was completely melted by the time I got it, the French toast was like leather and there was a teeny, miniscule amount of cream cheese. Worst $13 I ever spent, BY FAR. My mom got the entree with the egg, potatoes and sausage gravy - can't think of the name of it. I could have accepted the vomit-like appearance of the gravy, since sometimes sausage gravy doesn't look all that appealing; but the potatoes were so hard, she ended up taking most of them home to feed to her neighbor's chickens and the gravy was entirely flavorless. The waitress was very nice, however, and the interior was lovely. We will not be coming back and I will NOT be recommending this to anyone. So disappointing - I really hoped to like this place and make it a regular spot for my family and I. :(

Taste: mostly a miss on target, more below Service: very friendly and prompt Decor: very cute, smartly done, clean as a whistle Price per quality: as expected for a cozy microbrewery Beers: so... as with many microbreweries, they really don't quite know what they're doing and are extremely hop heavy, which masks most defects. Problem is, they are a one note hitter, wherein everything they offer tastes like an IPA. Their Pale Ale is definitely an IPA bitter-fest. The special Cherry Cheesecake tastes nothing like cherries and nothing like lactose was used, but just tastes like a smoother IPA. Their porter tasted like an IPA. Anyhow, luckily for them, their IPA tasted like an IPA, and most of these old fogies in a dry town like Haddonfield don't know the difference and don't much care! Just do not expect their menu notes, including IBUs, to have any relation to the taste of the brew in front of you.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! Dedicated Gluten and peanut free facility. My friend with a peanut allergy and I (very gluten intolerant) can actually eat at a restaurant together and choose anything on the menu! It's amazing to be able to eat literally anything they serve and never even having to worry about cross-contamination. Oh, and don't miss the bakery items!

The service from Stephanie was awesome she helped me pick out a pizza and was patient with me while I ordered my gluten free pizza, I got the pacific rim pizza which sounded delicious when she showed it to me everything looked good until I got home which is maybe if even 3min away I looked a little closer and the gluten free crust looks pre package and I've had those before but this one is so soggy I have to eat it with a fork and knife which loses the point of pizza. heese or topping have no color on them at all so I am upset about the quality of this pizza especially for the Price of $16 for a small definitely not worth it

I was frequenting this place a lot lately on account of my baby's many food intolerances. This restaurant has a great vegan and allergen menu which was awesome for me to be able to actually go out and eat without worrying. My review would initially have been five stars on account of good food and decent service. However during my last visit I was disgusted, when I saw one of the cooks exiting the bathroom while zipping up his fly. To me it looks like he did his business, didn't wash his hands, and proceeded to walk straight back into the kitchen (which is visible to the public) and continue cooking. So gross. We were on our way out when I saw this happen otherwise I wouldn't have eaten the food. Won't be going back to this location.

We got takeout from here and placed an online order. It was easy to make the order, but no where to specify instructions or allergens. We had a little trouble finding the restaurant. its kind of nestled in the back of a small plaza. its a cute space with an outdoor area. We were able to pop in and pick up the food pretty much contactless. As for the food the beef Dan burri was great and would recommend it. The seaweed salad and ginger salad were a hard pass for me. The seaweed salad had a strange taste and the dressing for the ginger salad was kind of odd. It did not have a strong flavor, it didn't coat the lettuce at all. We ordered 2 sashimi platters, online it says 5 items come in it, however there was way more than 5 types of fish/seafood in ours. Some of the items were unidentifiable and the Krab (imitation crab) usually contains gluten so it would have been nice to be able to add a note to omit that item. Anyway, both my husband and I got sick after eating that food and we weren't sure if it was the sashimi platter or the seaweed salad. asomething just was "fishy" and we had what I would describe as food poisoning. We probably won't return because of this and the fact that there are so many sushi joints in Tampa, ones with really fresh fish. I am really only giving them 3 stars because the beef Dan burri with the fried egg was great.

The worst restaurant experience ever! We went on Valentine's day & as soon as we walk in a couple tell us they waited for over an hour & couldn't get waited on. We should of taken this as a sign that nothing good was going to come from this. We waited 20 minutes for a table then when we were finally sat, it took us 45 minutes just to get drinks. Being in the restaurant industry, I could clearly tell the waiter wasn't properly trained as he had 9 tables he was waiting on, on top of that. I asked if they had a gluten free menu due to my allergy, I was told they will not stray from their set menu but on the phone they told me I would be accommodated. There were no prices on the menus which I thought was odd so I tried to look it up online & on the signs posted in the restaurant but couldn't find pricing. We finally get our food which is the driest filet I've ever had, the fishiest lobster bisque , the saltiest asparagus & the most generic desert possible. Just when I think the night can't get any worse I go to the bathroom & there was pee all over the toilet seat which I sat in. I tell my husband we must get the check & receive our bill that is $215. We apparently ordered 2 $75 filets from the menu that didn't have pricing. We paid our bill & we were waiting for our car that is valeted & I mentioned it to the assistant manager that the pricing is no where listed. He said "oops I guess it was an oversight". How do you forget to print pricing on menus?! The general manager asked how our meal was I asked her about pricing & I received the same response from her. We are then asked by the valet to come find our keys because he has no keys to a range rover. It took them about 15 minutes to track down our keys. Absolutely a terrible experience, beware of this place. UPDATE... Nathalie's has apologized profusely & sent us some coupons for our inconvienance on Valentines day. They were extremely embarrassed by what happened that night & explained one employees actions contributed to the domino effect of the night. I have changed my 1 star to a 3 star since they were sincerely sorry. Mistakes happen. We are all human.

Sorry We Went This cozy restaurant with a view of the bustling Elkins park train station recently changed names from Leila's Trattoria to Scillian Trattoria. We had been disappointed in its previous incarnation but decided to try again. The menu was limited and only modestly interesting. I chose spaghetti with fried eggplant, tomato sauce, shaved dried ricotta and mint--which promised a refreshing meal on a very chilly early spring evening. My fiancé decided on the grilled swordfish, and we started by splitting a hot vegetable salad, which turned out to be the star of the night. Served piping hot, the salad was a nice mélange of hot roasted root vegetables and green beans tossed just before serving with a crisp spring mix. It was presented with cold, nondescript, just-okay bread, but was so tasty we didn't miss the good freshly baked bread we always hope for in Italian restaurants. Things went downhill quickly. My fiance's fish arrived at the table flopped onto a too-large platter, with a sparse handful of lettuce dumped around it. The fish looked gray and fatty. It was. Even worse, it smelled the way only a no-longer-fresh piece of fish smells. As a side, he was given merely a salad that appeared straight from a bag of mixed greens. No potato, no pasta, no other component but fish and uninspired salad. My entree was also a disappointment, but not an inedible one. I had hoped for al dente pasta topped with crisp fried eggplant slices and sprigs of mint. Instead, the pasta was soggy, clearly heated-up rather than made to order, the eggplant bits were small and, if fried, it was impossible to tell as they had been tossed into the over-abundant sauce. The shaved dried ricotta was nice, and there was a hint of mint in the dish, but no visible mint to be seen. All things considered, it was passable. It was also $19.00. My fiancé--who loves fish, knows fish, eats lots of fish--sent his swordfish back and asked for a menu from which to re-order. Our waitress at first seemed stunned by this, then smiled and brought a menu. We heard distinct criticism of the decision coming from the door to the kitchen, in which the entire staff was clustered, glaring at us. Unacceptable! If there's ever a time for the chef to come out and ask what is the problem, saying a piece of fish has gone bad is that time. It used to be that restaurant staff were told to take these issues seriously because you never knew who might be a restaurant reviewer. Well, today we are *all* restaurant reviewers! The next entree out was gnocchi with a creamy mushroom sauce. "It's like canned Cream of Mushroom soup with gnocchi," my fiance whispered. I think that says it all, although I will add that the gnocchi themselves were excellent. The bland sauce simply needed some pizazz. One final question: Why don't restaurants try to offer at least one lactose-free dessert? Scillian Trattoria doesn't, so we didn't order dessert as we like to share, and I'm lactose-intolerant. This is not unusual, however, or specific to them. It's still a mystery. To sum up: The service was good at first, then ruined by what we overheard. The food was not good, and the prices were ridiculously high.

Terrible experience. Our first time there, and we will never go back. We come to Indy every year for a regional swim meet, and we will be coming for the next 8 years. We had a party of 10. Booked months in advance. We were seated at 7:15, and put in our entire order within 10 mins. The phrase of the day was "Amy, how long until our food gets here?" (Amy never communicated anything to us unless we flagged her down as she tried to race by our table unnoticed). We finally got our so-so calamari app (the sauce was good, the calamari were very overcooked) and 3 side salads after 40 minutes. No joke, 40 mins. We were told that the calamari app had to be "re-fired" because of a gluten allergy. Of course, no one asked for a gluten free app. The gluten free people weren't going to eat it. We didn't get the re-fired explanation until we flagged our waitress down 10-15 mins after ordering, and it took another 20+ mins to get it (they must have re-fired the bejesus out of it). After waiting nearly 1 1/2 hours for our entrees (again, no joke, it was 1 1/2 hours), we flagged Amy down again for the phrase of the day. We had 6 swimmers who needed to eat and go to bed for 5:30 am warm ups. Again, we were told that one of the 2 pizzas had to be re-fired because of the gluten allergy. I told her several times to bring out whatever was ready immediately. Instead of any food, the skinny manager guy came to say that Amy had communicated our instructions and the food would be out shortly. I asked him why he came to talk to us without any of the food (which was 5 kids meals, 3 salads with salmon, scallops, and a soggy signature prime rib pizza)? I had to tell him several times to go bring out whatever was ready before it sunk it that I really, really wanted him (and Amy) to bring out whatever was ready right now. 10 minutes later, again no joke, the food came out. (I've worked in a restaurant, and I was getting ready to go back to tray and serve it myself). The only thing which wasn't ready was my prime rib pizza - which was ordered by me with absolutely no changes to the menu description. When it came out it was soggy, and had clearly been under heat lamps for awhile so the cheese was leathery. No apologies, no offers to bring us anything while we waited, nothing. Nada. Zero. My pizza was garbage (I posted a pic of the sad limp mess), and the sausage pizza the kids ordered was likewise soggy. The salmon and scallops were good, most of the kids meals were ok, everything else was sub-par. To top it off, they had the b*lls to add in the tip to the check, and include an extra line so we could add in extra tip. The 10 of us had been to TGI Friday's at the hotel earlier for lunch that day. Friday's is Friday's. But Friday's smokes Harry & Izzy's in service, communication, and food. My advice, go to The Ram across the street (please see my review from when the 10 of us went there last year for dinner) - the food and service are far better.

Wish I could give them 0 stars because that's what they've earned. Never met such an immature and careless owner. Was greeted 30+ minutes after sitting, took 1+ hour for drinks. Served chips, salsa and water for the table myself. Allergen information incorrect and unclear. Server "forgot" to put order in. After waiting 2+ hours for food the majority of our party couldn't even eat their meal because of dietary restrictions that had been ignored. Luckily the end is probably near for this restaurant so few will have a similar experience.

They charge an additional $5 for gluten free crust-that is INSANE. $14.50 for a small salad and pizza is crazy enough and then to charge $5 more for gluten free is crazy. Unfortunately I don't see myself or my family returning-even though it is close. Whoa it's loud in there. Went for a business lunch and we could barely hear each other. Food is good. Gluten feee crust is good. It's a cute place and I will probably be back due to the location of my office.

ZERO STARS. It is because of this McDonalds that I will NEVER eat McDonalds again. I ordered a triple cheeseburger, witch is what I usually get, and it was the nastiest burger I have ever eaten. I literally threw up right after tasting it. DO NOT EAT HERE! They completely ruined McDonalds for me, and I have always loved their fries, but after that I will never eat anything from any McDonalds ever again or allow my children to eat that garbage. Just thinking about it makes me sick.

My first review of Bailey's Range was 3 stars and last night's experience was definitely worse so I'll go with 2 stars on this. When 1. we're seated by an emo hostess who ignored my first query about where to find the loo, when 2. it takes 45 min to be served dinner, when 3. the compensation for the wait is a plate of stale fries after we've already ordered onion rings, when 4. the bill includes an extra drink charge, and when 5. the manager has to apologize for a 15 min delay for paying the bill because their bank has a limit on the number of credit card transactions/day, I draw the conclusion that I don't want to visit again. Sure, I love the hipster decor and vibe but I wouldn't ever pay for that experience again. All that aside, if you still decide to go, here's a rundown of what we ate: 1. smoked onion rings -- good with a more tempura fry, not salty enough for my taste but a nice, new take on an old item 2. small salted caramel shake with choc sauce -- VERY good though the small was PRETTY small and, therefore imho, overpriced 3. PB&J on gluten-free bun ordered medium -- the bison burger was cooked nicely medium, the goat cheese and jam toppings were sparse, and the bun was decent but pretty bulky and difficult to fit in my mouth 4. Dave's Smoked Burger on gluten-free bun -- again, decent but the burger was too small for the bun 5. small peanut butter ice cream shake -- again, PRETTY small though tasty although I wish the peanut butter had been blended in better and wasn't left in chunks 6. comped fries -- I had these on my first visit and found them stale; they were stale this second time around, as well

The food was ok, but the service was terrible. With a serious food allergy the server didn't know how to accurately tell us about the ingredients, and then made snide comments about the allergy. He was rude and discourteous; and the manager wasn't much better.

Is it possible to give a zero star review? Do not go here. In fact, this place needs to be reported to the dept of health. The counters where the workers prepared the ice cream were filthy from previous ice cream making. Ice cream was dripping from the main machine onto the floor.
