The sink was filled with utensils and equipment. There was a 5 gallon sized tub of cherries on the counter and the workers would just grab a spoon and pour cherries over a sundae. Any extra cherries would fall back into the big vat. Over and over. When leaving we walked around to the back of the building and saw multiple trash bags lined up, not in a trash can or dumpster, just thrown on the floor. The door was propped open and there was no screen or anything to prevent bugs or rodents from walking right in. We witnessed a younger employee making a hot meal and were immediately disgusted by the preparation techniques: no gloves, cross contamination from using the same utensil, and the "prep counter" was filled with scraps of food and debris from previous meals. It was awful.

This review is only for gluten-free diners. I am Celiac, and I went with my husband to this restaurant because he had been hoping to give it a shot. I was happy to see they offered a gluten free pizza. I ordered, and told the server that I had celiac disease, and asked if the pizza would be safe. I was assured they would take extra precautions. When the pizza arrived, I used my Nima tester and confirmed that gluten was present in the pizza. I certainly understand if a busy restaurant cannot accommodate those of us with celiac disease. However, if you advertise gluten free and state it is safe, that is wrong. This restaurant is not safe for celiacs. As for the regular pizza, my husband did not like his pizza and we had to stop someplace else to pick up dinner. The crust was oily, the toppings were uncooked, and the cheese was not melted. Perhaps it was an off night all around, but at this time, we would not recognize this as a good place to go in King of Prussia

I'm almost positive Chao left, I haven't seen him in the last 5 or so visits. They are always busy, probably for the beer stuff, but the rolls are so crappily made now. Just slopped together, and too much siracha, I love it, but when the whole roll has it globbed on. Poop. Also, I know I got sick once from here, I never threw up, but I have anti-nausea pills, but I had a fever and felt like crapola all the next day. I'm finally breaking up with you as my only sushi choice. I have a couple on the side these days, and they love me more.

No chances taken: I know this going to sting a little but I'd say 3.5 stars. Sadly not an option. There's a certain trend occurring here that I participate in but feel I should put on the table. But first let's talk about the food. Just one anecdotal story first. A guy told me to watch the movie Sideways once said it was the best movie he's seen in a long long time. My expectations were peaked. The reality was: good movie but great not really. I mean I liked it. Who doesn't like Paul Giamanti. But.... The trend to which I refer is you have take an unfamiliar cuisine of a somewhat unfamiliar culture and make it safe. Beautiful space mostly beautiful staff....safe....no chances taken. The restaurant is beautiful. The service was efficient and they pleasantly monetize every inch of the space. Waiting for your table a hostess literally b-lined to us when it was apparent we wanted drink. I was thrilled to pay $8.50 for my IPA. Really I was. It's called service. The server knew every stitch of the menu. The food is where I think I'm not so sure it's worthy of the raves. This is Lebanese food. Do you not have Lebanese food in Philly? Growing up in NE Ohio we had a lot of Lebanese. So this familiar food for me. Suraya has good food but I feel like the reviewers of this restaurant feel like they invented Lebanese food at this restaurant. Very accommodating to food allergies. Our table wobbled. That was annoying. Anyway So when your walking your labradoodle past the dirty little middle eastern restaurant on your way to beard wax store resist the urge to pass it up. This middle eastern restaurant it's going to have 78 mostly attractive employees in their middle 20's. But its probably going to be good. Who are you to resist?
Worst food poisoning I've ever had in my entire life.. Their food passed through me like Katrina passed through New Orleans.

Worst service I've had in years. My girlfriend and I went to the Padaro Beach Grill for a casual meal tonight. She's pregnant, and wanted something both vegetarian and non-spicy. She asked the girl at the counter if the black bean burger was spicy. The reply was "no." I ordered the pretzel burger with no cheese (I am lactose intolerant). We also ordered fries and a side salad. Nothing about the order was good. The fries were cold. I'd be surprised if they were made less than half an hour prior to our order. My girlfriend's black bean burger was covered in a spicy sauce that made it difficult for her to eat. And of course my burger was covered in cheese. Now, mistakes happen. That's not a huge problem by itself. The real problem was how they handled their mistake. I asked them to re-make my burger without cheese. They told me they would do so. It came back out suspiciously quickly. Sure enough, they hadn't re-made anything, they just scraped (some of) the cheese off the burger. At this point I was getting angry. I went back inside to point out that they hadn't actually re-made the burger like I asked, and again told them to do just that. Again, the burger came out suspiciously quickly. They still hadn't re-made the burger. They'd just replaced the top bun. That, of course, does nothing to remove the melted cheese on the actual burger, or mixed into the onions, sauce, bottom bun, etc. Worst service in years. Inedible food.

My burger was delicious. Had a gluten free bun, not bad. Got cottage cheese as a side for the protein. All good. Unfortunately, the salad my partner got was less than fresh. There were some parts she picked out that could be described as rotten. The shrimp was good. She ate about a fourth of it. This was seriously off-season and maybe being busier would have prevented something like this, but a salad *has* to have fresh ingredients. It just does. Pretty pricey for rotten salad.

Went through the drive thru ordered 2 chalupas (we had to tell her twice it was two chalupas, not a single chalupa supreme). Once we received the bag of food and paid we got a block away and had to drive back to get the second chalupa we originally ordered. While waiting around 3 minutes for one chalupa we witnessed one of the employees on the food line eating off the line with his gloved hand and returning to work with the same CONTAMINATED glove. CALL THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT!!!! And the chalupa had spicy sauce on it!!! They don't come with PICO SAUCE. I think the Health Department would enjoy this place!

There is a tragedy regarding their turkey burgers. They used to be good, but now they have decided to make them with fillers like onions and mushrooms. So many fillers, in fact, that I began to wonder if they had run out of money and could no longer afford turkey. It was like eating ground mushrooms in dried onion soup mix. Worst burger I've had in a while. I couldn't even finish it, and that's saying something. I used to love this place, but we waited over 45 minutes, they got our order wrong, then we got the worst turkey patty I've ever had. Maybe the beef is better, but I don't eat beef. The loaded fries remain decent, if they actually come out warm. Ours tasted like someone had heated up leftovers halfway. We came in on a Sunday afternoon. The beer and cider list remains solid. The gluten-free buns are not bad. And they did comp one of our meals without us asking because they got it wrong, so that was nice. I hope ML Rose can get back to their former glory. Will try them one more time because it was an old standby we used to love. But I can't stomach another one of those vile turkey burgers. ML Rose, if you read this, PLEASE FIX IT.

I ordered some takeout online and received one of the worst Sushi orders I've ever picked up. So many things were wrong with my order: 1) They did not follow any of the special instructions. They weren't crazy instructions either, just "do not include this ingredient." Why bother to have a special instructions field if you don't read it? Don't order online if you have allergies, I guess. 2) They got one item completely wrong. This wasn't a close thing, either: I ordered Mackerel (Saba) and received Squid (Ika). Those aren't even vaguely similar. 3) Said Squid was BAD. I don't mean low quality, I mean it was spoiled, and if you've ever had the misfortune of eating spoiled squid you know how dangerous that can be. If you haven't... out both ends, for hours. 4) Their veggie "assortment" for tempura consists entirely of potato (not sweet potato, plain potato) and zucchini. The tempura batter itself was not good quality and had trouble sticking to the veggies, especially the zucchini. 5) The rice in their sushi was mushy and bland, exceptionally so. It brought the already mediocre quality of the sushi down even more. I really did not expect something this bad given all the other good reviews of this place. I don't know if they're having issues due to the pandemic or what, but I won't be ordering from this place again.

Well, I guess it's hard to give a fair review of a place after you've experienced the wrath of food poisoning after a meal there. The food and the experience were decent, until all that happened. I am thinking it was the clams... damn clams! The server was pretty terse and not all that friendly, but was able to help us pick out a good wine with certainty. The wine list had a nice selection and I was happy to find that it was well priced and not overly ridiculous as wine can usually be at restaurants. The "specials" rotate seasonally and are obviously the most expensive things on the menu. I did find them to be slightly overpriced compared to the rest of the menu which was surprising. The food was standard, classic Italian food, but honestly have had better or at least similar at other Italians in Philadelphia. I really do kinda want to go back, but I am probably too scared by my first experience there.

This is an interesting spot to visit for brunch. The menu is offers multiple spins on classic breakfast entrees, but the drink menu really shines. Don't waste your time with the spongy overcooked omelets and commit to the carbs if you want to enjoy your meal. Good for an indulgent brunch or quick bakery stop, but I'd like to see more dietary/allergen accomodations.
We have eaten at el Charro numerous times and it has been good, but yesterday at lunch I got a mild case of food poisoning. One miserable evening. I haven't decided if we will ever go back.
I love Five Guys but this place is consistently dirty and the staff is unfriendly. God forbid you tell them you have an allergy to something...que the eye roll.

Came here for dinner tonite...probably the worst meal and service we've ever had. We were seated right away at a booth at the bar area and my drink order was taken a few minutes later, just a sweet tea. My hubs was on the phone in the lobby, so I didn't order his. He came in, my drink was delivered, I kid you not, about 10 minutes after he sat down, so maybe 15 minutes after ordering AND she almost spilled it on me, and brought out rolls with it. Hubs also ordered a sweet tea, she brought that pretty quickly. Then we didn't see her again for another 15 minutes. We ordered an appetizer and our meals, the trio appetizer and I ordered the cheeseburger, no seasonings, medium with fries, hubs ordered the sirloin, medium with fries and potato soup. Appetizer came out, it was good, but no side plates. Meals were brought out about 55 minutes after we ordered. Server asked the hubs to cut into his steak, more of a medium well, than a medium, she asked if he wanted another one, he declined stating it would probably take too long). My burger also more of a medium well AND cold! The cheese wasn't even melted on it, and the top bum was hard, and even though the toothpick was in it marked no seasonings, it had seasonings. (I can tell because I have an allergy to something in one of the seasonings and my lips are starting to swell.) My tea sat empty for the majority of the time and the server finally took my cup to fill it when our meals were brought out and she finally brought it back filled to the top after I'd attempted to eat half the burger. Also, I think they gave us the bottom of the bag of fries as all we got were 1//4-1/2 inch pieces of fries, which were also cold. I'd think a manager would have been brought out after the hubs made the comment about his steak, but we never saw one, or at least a discount on hi meal, but no. (I didn't complain, not after waiting almost an hour for the entrees!) This is a shame that it seems that most of the restaurants in Mount Juliet are going downhill fast. I believe this is the last time we'll be eating at Logan's Mount Juliet.

I've gone to this location several times and they are nice and friendly and the service is fast--BUT I got the worst case of food poisoning EVER the other day. I ordered the lunch special of the individual deep dish and drink for five bucks. It tasted normal and I wasn't alarmed until later when my stomach erupted like Mount Vesuvius. I've never been in such agony before in my life...and I would have preferred going through natural labor with an ear infection and a toothache than to feel as if I were giving birth to a creature that was half satan and half porcupine. Just don't.
Horrible service... horribly rude. I'm gluten free and they asked me if I was "actually gluten free" and then made me wait 30 minutes for a tiny pizza

I was not impressed with this Stephen Starr restaurant. The waiter was not at all knowledgeable about food allergies. I wanted to order the posh breakfast (scrambled eggs, potatoes, spinach, toast), and he first told me he didn't think it could be made dairy free. Then he told me the kitchen said they can make it dairy and gluten free after checking, and just brought out eggs and greens (no gluten free potatoes or toast were available) so my $20 plate ended up consisting of just 2 items...The atmosphere and decor was nice though, but I would say this place is overpriced and nothing special

I should have listened to one of the other yelp reviewers - my boyfriend and I got the same sandwich here our first day in New Orleans, and rather than spending our first night out on the town, we spent it in the hotel with terrible stomach aches. I didn't eat real food again until two days later. Do I have forensic evidence that their sandwich gave me food poisoning? No. But I have a strong enough hunch to warn my fellow yelpers. And it wasn't even a very good sandwich.

Horrible service for a table of 1st time customers with a part of 9. Rude and unprofessional server, food was made even though food allergies were disclosed from the beginning. Never received 2nd round of drinks ordered, no refills were offered and they seemed bothered when ever we asked for anything. My food took over 1 1/2 hours to remake so the whole table was done eating and checks were being paid. When I tried to discuss how upset I was that the food took that long and I received a check for the entree the server was extremely rude. The server told me I was being charged because I was taking the food to go so I told him that he could have it back. He then snatched it off the table and mumbled under his breath to go adjust the check. I would never go back to this establishment after this treatment. Food allergies should be taken more seriously here. The staff should have a lot more friendly customer service skills.

I was honestly very disappointed after dining at R2L. I heard this place was an amazing view with great upscale dining. I decided to put down a $25 deposit for my birthday dinner here. It is very cool walking in and having your own personal elevator taking you to the restaurant. Once you get there, you are escorted to your table. However, once I was at the table, it took around 10 minutes to even be greeted by my server (and he wasn't very welcoming at all). Following this interaction, our server only came to our table once every hour I'd say. The food was amazing, but the service was just so awful I couldn't find myself rating R2L anything above 3 stars. As for the appetizers, I'd highly recommend ordering the flatbread and the nachos. The tuna tartare was also really good but the flatbread and nachos were honestly addicting they were so good. As for the main courses and side dishes, you can't go wrong with anything, but warning, it may be undercooked. I personally got the salmon and absolutely loved it. My friends got the scallops, shrimps, pork chops, lobster and short rib/filet mignon duo. The lobster was extremely raw as well as the rib/filet mignon duo, but I couldn't even get the server to come over to us in order to correct the order. My friend is also deathly allergic to nuts and it took around 10 minutes after the food was given to find anyone to confirm it was okay to eat. As for the dessert, the warm vanilla cake was fantastic. Overall, I was extremely upset because of the awful service (I believe our servers name was Timothy). That being said, the manager was very nice about the bad service, but the server was quite rude.

Highly recommend Firebirds. Server Cody, manager and chef were great and considerate with my food allergies. Made sure to avoid cross contamination. It is nice to go someplace and they really care. Food was delicious .

I can remember when this was the highlight of a trip to Reno. The Friday night seafood buffet. We went 11/16 and wow I was very disappointed on the quality. Specific items- The sushi rolls Spicy Crab were good. The King crabs lags were extremely watery and lacking flavor. Had what I imagine they think is Ahi Poke, it was more like dried Aku that wasn't completely dried, pleh. Had some seasoned salmon which almost made me vomit. It as if it was left over from the morning and un-refrigerated. The steamed mussel were better off being used as bait. Overcooked and chewy. What was always reliable as great quality were the Mushroom stuffed ravioli's, this time they were underdone. The clam chowder was good though. It's as if the chefs....correction- cooks don't know how the food should taste or they didn't care. Spent most of the night with the fear of food poisoning. Boy, what a let down.
Good chance I got food poisoning here and spent 30 min in the worst bathroom later that night because of it. Eat at your own risk...tasted good on the way in...you know the rest.

Food was somewhat ok. Atmosphere leaves a lot to be desired. Very cold inside for it being winter, too cold to take your coat off. When ordering a bean and cheese burrito there should be more cheese than a half dozen snips. The beans had a sour taste to them. Food was cold before you could finish it. The chips are very bland and the dip was way too hot for people that prefer mild. And why on God's earth would you roll fried ice cream in coconut?????????????? I have eaten it all across the United States and Mexico, NEVER has it had coconut on it. For people like me that hates coconut not to mention are allergic to it, it's quite a letdown after looking forward to it. Like others I know, we won't be back.

Regrub is one of those places you really, really want to love. It's new, it's been trendy somewhere else (Calgary), it's colorful, its menu is full of funny names, and it's convenient to the Whyte Ave walking stretch of pavement. I was excited to "drop a pin" into this nouveau burger experience, doubly so with a bit of the hangry. So the other half did the ordering while I soaked in the ambiançe: it's like the Teletubbies grew up to high school, got to plan a menu, decorate a space, pick a soundtrack and make social media accounts. Yeah, it's like that. That part is all good. It's a fun, colorful space with happy, shiny staff. The fail parts are the execution of the food and the value-for-money propositions. Those could use a lot of tweaking. She wanted the Lutter, a 4 oz Alberta Beef patty with bacon, egg, and cheddar surrounded by a bun of split glazed donuts. I liked the contrast of the sweet and savoury, whereas the 'bunny felt the donut didn't meet up to her Tim Horton'y expectations. (It tasted to me like a Krispy Kreme regular glazed donut, FYI.) The Cheesy Jr., a 4 oz patty topped with mac n' cheese with bacon bits, arrived looking (seriously) like those Halloween caricatures of a pumpkin vomiting out its insides. Yes, there's pale creamy pasta with bits covering most of the serving tray... in a competition, this contestant would have been sent home. It's a presentation that screams "I'm so drunk I can't even bother looking for flatware. I'm using my hands and lots of paper towels." Still, it's the taste that counts (mostly) but this explosion wasn't rescued: it was under-salted and nowhere as cheesy as it *needed* to be. My ultimate measure of a restaurant's worth to me comes down to whether it (1) delivers a food that I can't easily make at home along with (2) an experience that's memorable at (3) a rationalizable price. Regrub fails on the former; I can whip up dorm-quality meat patties & KD without any effort. The middle; okay, interesting location slash vibe slash space. The latter; meh. Everyone felt mugged. The worst thing of all? This is *so* close to executing well. Krikey, taste the damn food on the way out of the kitchen! Tighten up food design and assembly; try to be impressing someone... Oh, and your Instagram counter behind the till is broken. Even that narcissistic rush doesn't work. Meh.

FOOD POISONING!!! CRYING OVER TOILET!!! DONT DO IT!!! I ordered vegetable fajitas with tamarind juice and my husband ordered a veggie burrito with horchata. The food tasted ok but I left feeling like something was wrong. I figured it was because I'd eaten too much, my belly doesn't have much room these days. A few hours later I'm dry heaving, vomiting , and blasting diarrhea at the same time. I'm also 6 months pregnant and the pain from my stomach contracting in order to reject the food had me in tears sitting in front of the toilet for hours. I've never felt worse. My server was kind and attentive but the food was a no. I'll never go back and I plan to report them to every entity who has the power to shut them down.

I read the few reviews and decided I would give it a try... So on Wednesday that just past I decided to go and give it a try mind you I'm a very picky eater don't just eat from every where..was Food Poisoned from eating Spanish Food, so I watch where I eat!! So I ordered and decided to eat in, upon getting my food I just couldn't believe the portion... You could feed 3/4 ppl w the combination platter!!! I could say their food is to die for, I used to go to China 1 by 301 and wasn't crazy about how their food taste.. I'm so happy I found this place...as a matter of fact I'm about to go and get me some food from there......

I love Tijuana flats. My husband and I always ordered from the oldsmar location however he accidentally clicked on this Clearwater location instead. I ordered the floutas and atom bombs. When our food arrived the atom bombs were missing. The bag was sealed so I know the restaurant forgot or didn't check to put it in (sealed due to covid) they refunded me the money but needless to say I was disappointed because the reason I love Tijuana flats so much is for their atom bombs. I carried on with my night and noticed I started to feel severely ill. I got a low grade fever diarrhea and was throwing up from 8 pm to 4 am this morning. Needless to say I got food poisoning and this has never been an issue at the oldsmar location. I can only guess why (maybe due to cleanliness or bad food) however I rather not because I want to throw up again. Be cautious ordering from this location

I was a mother with a baby vomiting and having diarrhea. I wanted to make him chicken soup, my office is on 4th so the word "Market" caught my eye driving home to him. Went in and stopped one of the staff and asked where their poultry section was. He sarcastically took his time to tell me they did not have a poultry section, ( mean while my 15 month old is getting more dehydrated by the second)! What is with the rude sarcastic attitude! No where are there any large signs stating vegetarian! A simple no would have sufficed! Dear Staff person, Thank you for reminding me that kindness and consideration is a rarity in this city and that the next time someone is exceptionally kind and caring I will validate them and encourage them to keep spreading that love. I hope you all the best and hope that you gain meaning and peace in your life.

Modesto is as tasty as can be for tapas in St. Louis! I have been to Modesto several times throughout the past 10 years and dare I say, it's only gotten better with time. My husband and I visited Modesto after the USMNT game last week and we were pleasantly surprised to be seated right away. I ordered a glass of sangria and as soon as I had a sip, I remembered why I shouldn't order sangria anywhere else. Far and away the best sangria in the area. I am that person the fishes out the little bits of fruit with my fork. Manners be damned. With my gluten free hubby by my side, we stuck to all gf items but it wasn't difficult at all. A LOT of Modesto's menu is gluten free. If you have celiac, you may want to mention your level of sensitivity as a couple of fried potato items have possible contamination but our server made sure to ask and we selected something else. We had the Ensalada de Verduras (mmm manchego), Pimiento Rellenos, Pinchos Morunos, and the Paella Mixta. Every single little morsel was perfect and delicious. The service was quick, the tapas came out staggered perfectly, the drinks were flowing... such a fantastic dinner. We'll be back soon!

I have to start with the "not so obvious" things about this place, which contributed to my less than stellar score for Strange Donuts. From all the hype, I was expecting a normal donut shop with some flair, some pizazz..didn't happen. Matter of fact, this guy thought the first trip to Strange Donuts would be a great stop to take his wife and mother for breakfast. I was wrong. This location, by definition, is a hole in the wall. No wonder the lines are half way down the block. There is barely room for 3 people to stand and consider their options. There are no seats to sit and have a coffee and a donut, there is no ambiance, it is literally a door, a counter, and a guy (well two guys) dishing out donuts. Yipes! Once we realized this wasn't going to be the breakfast stop we were expecting, we flipped to option B which basically meant grabbing one of each donut we were interested in trying, and then heading off to a nearby pancake house to have a proper breakfast. Good thing we are versatile, because we were disappointed in the lack of even a bench to sit and scarf down one donut! As far as the selection and flavor goes, this was a mixed bag. From memory, there were about a dozen and a half different donuts to select from, ranging from a gluten free "puppy chow" donut, to more traditional looking choices. Our selections varied in taste and quality: Barts Revenge-Better than expected in terms of taste. The butterfinger topping didn't overpower the donut at all, and was almost lacking in all honesty. It tasted like a chocolate donut with chocolate icing, and not much else. Gooey Butter Cake-It was okay. The icing was buttery, but it didn't really capture the essence of a good gooey butter cake for me. The donut itself was also a bit dry. French Toast-again, tasted like a cake donut with powdered sugar on it, but not the "powdered sugar" style you buy at the grocery store, but a sprinkling of powdered sugar, more for effect than anything else. Banana Pudding-not a huge fan of pudding filled donuts, in all honesty, but this one wasn't bad. Definitely better than the previous donuts, but not something I would get again. Captain Chocolate (not sure that's the right name)-it was a chocolate donut, with chocolate icing, and chocolate sprinkles. Nothing strange about it, but it was a good donut. Puppy Chow-Gluten free and very dry. I'm not a fan of puppy chow, this was my mothers selection, but even she wasn't impressed with it. Pumpkin Spice-NOW we are talking. This was a damned tasty donut. I loved it. I want another. Strawberry Cheesecake-another wonderful tasting donut. I love jelly filled so this was a no brainer. Maybe I loved this one most because it was jelly filled, maybe, but still, damned good choice if you are going to go to Strange Donuts. In all there is a lot of potential with Strange Donuts, but there isn't enough appeal for me to make this a regular stop. This is, however, a great place to take an out of towner to show them something different! Just plan on making these treats a dessert selection unless you like eating sticky donuts in your car!

We chose Cafe Buenos Aires because of its location across from the Arlington Theatre and its beautiful patio. The restaurant indeed had a great atmosphere with arched doorways, a latin band, fountain and white lights mixed with vines. And, though it was cold outside, we were happy and warm on the patio next to a space heater. The waiter couldn't name more than two beers and had to refer to the list. My wine (which was a shiraz I chose from the list) was very good. But since the waiter seemed to have forgotten us through most of the meal, we weren't able to grab him to even get a second drink. I was excited to order because the menu had some tasty looking options. I requested the server check on an allergen in my dish, but he never came back to assure me the menu item was safe. Next thing, the dish was placed in front of me and I had to just hope it was safe to eat. I got a shrimp dish sauteed with applies and raisins and served in a coconut curry sauce with fried plantains. You'd think it would be impossble for a dish like that to lack flavor, but it was surprisingly bland. My companion's steak was also bland, even when he doused it in the herb sauce that accompanied it. I'm not a big believer in having to add salt at a restaurant, and when one salting doesn't improve it, that's pretty bad. The quality of the steak seemed fine though. The mango mousse was not smooth, but rather quite choppy, which seemed to explain the lingering bite on my tongue of unripe fruit. If prices were more reasonable ($25 plus per entree) I might be willing to try it again. But the cost of our mediocre meal did not warrant a second chance, which makes me sad because it was such a beautiful setting.
Hey thanks for the food poisoning last night from your mussels! At least the bottled beers were good. Stick with beer, don't eat the mussels, or use the bathroom!

Meh. That about sums up our experience. Took my sister in for a bday dinner with a couple friends and my order was about the only one that came correct. The waitress was funny and pleasant but not really focused on being there. It was not busy for a Saturday night, so I'm not sure what the issue was. 2 people requested no sour cream on their meals, one of which is deathly allergic...and both came with sour cream. My sister ordered no pico, and hers came with it. A ton if it. Like if she like pico, she would be the happiest person on earth. She was a good sport and picked it off for what seemed like forever. We did send the one plate back for the allergic person and I will say they were super fast in correcting it. You would think that with all these issues, you would at least pay attention to the fact that everyone was out of drinks...I mean, the waitress was at our table like a 100 times (she forgot several follow-up questions in the beginning of the order and kept coming back). But not once did she notice. I asked for a refill on water finally...she refilled mine...and left without refilling the other person's empty water. It was actually comical at this point since we are easy keepers for the most part. Will we be back...if we are in Sparks and hungry again. Will we make it a point to come back...meh...just like the overall experience...

I always pass by this pizzeria. This week I wanted to give it a try. I ordered a single serving of gluten free pizza and one medium pepperoni and onion pizza. It was obvious that both Pizza doughs were premade or frozen. The crust tasted like a cardboard. The onion was chopped very small, I didn't know they were onions. I give it one star.

This food is really just okay, I am not surprised that it was mediocre - the people of Yelp have informed be. But I was dining with a friend with several allergies and a vegan friend they knew that they could eat here as they had dined there before. As soon as we started talking to our server my friend disclosed all the allergies. One of them being a very serious dairy allergy. Couple that with the vegan friend (this is a no cheese zone). We ordered the guacamole (she had it before) and he insisted we do the tableside version instead. It was several dollars more but we thought heck - lets amuse him. So he made the guacamole "tableside" we kind of watched but not really, it was a lot higher than the table and we had soOooOOoooO much talking to do. Imagine our surprise when he presented the guacamole and there was obvious CHEESE in it!?? I know what you're thinking - cheese in guacamole?! GENIUS and while I agree, my poor friend with the dairy allergy does not. When we asked he said he would bring them some of the guacamole from the back (the cheeseless one we asked for from the beginning and should have stuck with), he asked me if I could eat it and I shrugged and said I guess. Sooooo he decided that me alone would be eating a family sized portion of $$$ guacamole?? I got stuck with the bill for a bowl of guac that nobody ate, and frankly it was super annoying. Even though the guac was good, my fish tacos were not. I can handle mediocre food but expensive mediocre food is a super no go in my life. One of my friends ordered a burrito that looked to be a good way to go for value at least. This whole review is a little TL;DR the table side guac has cheese, entrees are expensive, service is a little odd, I'd come here for drinks and salsa.

My son plays the & loves jazz & blues so the Sat evening band was a major bonus for him. Our waitress said she was a vegan (I'm an annoying vegetarian so I was asking about the menu). It's like we were both stuck in meat-ville. We chose this place because of location for a quick dinner & no one else in my family is a vegetarian so I'm in. Service-Oy! Wait, wait, wait, excuses ("someone was recently let go / fired from the kitchen staff"). Our nice waitress offered to bring our waiting table some "complimentary fries right away" since our food was delayed, deflated and delayed again...kids were super excited and salivating about that idea. Alas, they never came. Listen to the band...it'll take your mind off your food...well over an hour later, here it comes...hot & just OK at best. The menu has codes for items that are vegetarian or vegan and other things like gluten free. I ordered the 4 sides for & $10....a good deal & good vegetarian option. Many of the items are marked wrong I was told when I inquired. For instance, these are not marked vegetarian: collard greens, seasoned fries, hush puppies, mashed potatoes, sweet potatoes ...& more. Weird. The waitress said they were all vegetarian or vegan. Who's to believe, a vegan waitress & a bbq place or a franchise establishments printed menu? My kids liked the water glasses, which were mini individual pitchers. Husband and kids review on their two meat entrees & one chicken was just so so. This is a southern chain. This one seems to be their only non-southern franchise, well, if you consider Maryland "the south.")

$28 cake fee -- let's start with that. I arranged for a party of 7 to come and dine for a birthday (it's a small space so please let them know 6 vs 7 because it makes a difference). 4 bottles of wine for 7 people, great we love BYO, we love being able to eat cake and good food and dine with fine wine: but the mood slipped a bit when I see a $28 cake fee -- a price that is MORE than any of our slightly overpriced entrees. Why is this there? Maybe I should've clarified before we came but is this their way of deterring birthday parties from happening? Our total bill was nearly $300 for a party of 7 - we brought business and weren't that rowdy :( In the many restaurants I've been to during my lifetime, the highest cake fee I've ever had to pay was about $8. If they had cakes or desserts they wanted us to order instead, I would've done that - it's just that my friend has specific allergies and tastes so I don't want to risk his 26th birthday being his last (if you know what I'm saying) - even so, should he be punished with this? Unheard of. My bucatini portion was also smaller than the rest of my party's portions of tagliatelle, chicken parm, and crab pasta so I was a bit disappointed. Service was great though there was a big gap of time between appetizers and entrees. Love the burrata~ Bruschetta is not tomato, it's mushroom. Debating on whether I want to come back with a smaller group (and definitely non-birthday)..

Bar Louie protects customers from unprotected servers by ignoring older patrons Due to Covid, I chose mid-afternoon for a RARE and relished venture out. Arrival time, 3:11 ish. Outdoors, one other table occupied. Two servers. Awesome. A third server appeared after about eight minutes and said he would be all mine. Upon getting an IPA, I said I'd hang for a while, before ordering another drink and a burger. The while grew long enough to hang a herd of elephants, as my now-empty beer glass grew warm for about 19 minutes after I finished. Even the persistent gnats gave up. Then, I heard another server say, "Your friends are here." There he was! Finally! He burst through the inside/outside door, inches past my table, to engage in playful banter with his friends,...I knew he'd at long, last notice me, wide anxious eyes, drooling. Twenty-one additional minutes passed. TWENTY-ONE. That's a peace sign and one finger. I got up to retrieve napkins to soak up the sweat from my water in a ploy to get his attention. Wimpy, I know, but a "gentle reminder." It was better than apologizing for interrupting him. Yes? No? Still, no nod, no acknowledgement from three tables away, with no humans in between, much less 15 feet to the right and ten feet to the left. With all that time I had on my hands, I began to think--instead of eat and drink--and studied his mask. It hung just on top of his upper lip, leaving his protruding proboscis for all to see. Would he sneeze? Was he contaminating the food he wasn't taking orders for or wasn't serving? As my impatience grew, I slowly got grossed out. What if a drip from his nose contaminates my order? Maybe this was God's grace in keeping me from getting the Covid-19 virus by a server who saves people by ignoring them. Carmel, Indiana's Bar Louie, so convenient, so inviting for someone who had not left home much since March 23, 2020, such a thrill to be out...saved me today by treating me like "The Invisible Woman." GREY LIVES MATTER. Side Dish: My magical spell of invisibility dissolved when I ordered dinner at Bub's Burgers.

Grease, grease, and more grease. I was expecting greasy but honestly do not know how they fit that much grease into their food. Rolls = Delish, service is usually friendly. One of us gave this place 5 stars. Yeah. He also licks his fingers after touching raw beef. I gave it 1 star but grease literally makes me vomit and nothing but the rolls in this place are less than 50% grease. Even the roll is greasy but at least when you cut it open, a pool of oil doesn't slide out. But I come back and will come back because my dining partner loves this place and if I can drag him to a vegetarian restaurant, he can drag me to Joe Bobs.
The food gave my friend food poisoning and the food was NOT even that good. This place has gone down

This is the St. Elmo of cake shops. I am not much of a cake fan but my girlfriend drug me here and I was extremely impressed. Very fancy interior design. My girlfriend described it as, "It looks like Hobby Lobby threw up in here, in a good way."

How can you screw up a cucumber roll??? It's cucumber and rice with a seaweed wrap... period!!! For an extra treat, some places will sprinkle on a few toasted sesame seeds, but that's a bonus. So, back to my question... The answer: Ask Aloha Sushi!!! I was all excited for some sushi and I have many food allergies including seafood so I have to stick to vegetable rolls. Anyway, my husband brings home some of my beloved crisp, refreshing, tangy cucumber rolls (this time from Aloha) and THERE YOU HAVE IT... they put MAYONNAISE in my roll!!! It was a big ole sloppy mess of mayonnaise! I've been eating these rolls for longer than many Yelpers have been alive and NEVER have I seen such an atrocity! I called them to ask why this was done and they said plainly, "That's how they're made." ONLY at Aloha are they made this way! They then asked if we ordered the "Spicy Cucumber Roll" to which I told them, "NO! Just a plain cucumber roll." They offered nothing in reparation - not even an apology for the inconvenience. (We drove 40 miles round trip!!!) Needless to say, it was neither spicy nor plain - just a big ole nauseating mayonnaise mess. Now this was my 2nd experience there - and a definite deal-breaker. My first visit, I sat at the bar and the guy actually made my roll correctly (a real shocker in retrospect) and it wasn't THAT bad. Again, it's a cucumber roll - not a real culinary challenge. The bad part was the atmosphere and the lack of service. I couldn't get a drink to save my life! The waitress/hostess disappeared for over 30 minutes and the sushi chef was unable to take my drink order. The restaurant itself looks like a converted old casino. Or, the recipient of hand-me-down carpet and decor of a casino. After that visit, take-out seemed like a better option. Sure... only better if you want to go out of your way, pay money, come home, throw the crap away, and eat toast for dinner. Damn good toast though. P.S. I want my 1-star back. They don't even deserve that!

My Husband and I ate there last Friday. Food was alright, as always, but our server made this experience less than pleasant. Can't say what her name is, she wasn't wearing a name tag..... We ordered an appetizer to split and one of those combination plates for the entrees , also to split. Nothing for a good 20 minutes, then somebody from the kitchen brought out our entrée. Usually you each get a small plate when you split something. No such luck. And our waitress was nowhere to be seen. My husband went to cancel the appetizer (well, I guess it would have been called dessert by now) and round up a couple of plates. Halfway through eating our server showed up to ask if everything was okay. She didn't even apologize for the missing appetizer! I just gave her a look. We had just finished eating when she brought my husband a free refill on his half finished coke and we asked for the check. When we finally got it she said "be right back" and disappeared again. We were paying cash and had to wait for her. After about 15 minutes we saw here chatting and taking orders at a table on the way out and just dropped off the money with her. I could not restrain myself and thanked her for her service and told her the tip reflects her performance. We gave her the exact amount of x dollars and 13 cents. She probably had no idea that this was her lucky day. Had I not been feeling real bad because of allergies I would have had an extensive conversation with the manager about the complete lack of service.

Promoted themselves as just like Five Guys just a different name. Fries are frozen and coating tastes very weird. Burger was dry and I ended up throwing it up because it upset my stomach. Fries are no longer gluten free so my father cannot have them. Overall disappointing and I would rather drive out to Five Guys instead of eat this...

a nice little spot with really attentive staff. Prior to our trip to New Orleans I caught a horrible stomach flu or food poisoning. Still not sure what it was but it was ugly. During our stay it only got worse. Our first night in New Orleans we came to Muriel's for dinner. We started off with Seafood Gumbo and I had bbq shrimp as my entree. I was expecting more of a dry BBQ than a super saucy bbq. I don't remember what my boyfriend ordered but it was really good and he enjoyed it. We ordered desserts and I had a creme brule... Nothing super "new orleans" but it wasn't bad. Maybe the fact that I wasn't feeling well kind of dampened my experience here

I come here all the time and it has been my favorite cafe in the city for meeting friends and getting a bite. It has new owners. The drinks and food are wisely largely the same: my favorite is the hummus platter with grape leaves olives salad pita and I will ask for an omelette to be added. The tabletops are no longer a charming pattern under glass and I think a sofa was taken out of the back. No big deal: they have up paintings and that's amazing. My main beef is there also seems to be no gluten free bagels or pastries any more. I think it's possible that the owner doesn't have gluten free products because they think they can't guarantee they are wheat free from the kitchen but I think so many people eat those now that it would be lucrative and smart to keep them there. Every time in the last week (3 times) that I have asked if they have gluten free products the barista makes a face and says everybody's asking for them we just don't have them right now.

The restaurant staff or chefs are not adequately trained on food allergies/intolerances - after I was repeatedly told that there would be no dairy in the omelette dish and tater tot dish, I got severely ill the entire day of my vacation and the symptoms lingered for two weeks. I was concerned of the pool of oil in the tater tot dish and the mushiness of the potato tots so I even asked the waitress a third time after the food arrived whether or not there was cheese or butter. She blatantly responded that she had checked with the kitchen that there's only flour and potato in the tater tots. We contacted the restaurant whose owner later replied that the tater tots were made with ricotta cheese. Side note - the tater tots were essentially mashed potato balls that were extremely salty. The staff for our table was the tallest blonde woman during Saturday brunch time last month.

I like the setup of the restaurant. The band playing inside's mic was so low you couldn't hear the singer. Our waitress was fantastic and super helpful. However, I ordered the 8 piece chicken wing appetizer and after a couple pieces I noticed that it didn't taste cooked in the middle. The dark lights make me unable to actually see the color. Since the food is expensive, I kept biting into each piece and trying to eat the parts that seemed cooked. Out of the 8, I would say that 3/4 were fried properly. I ended up getting food poisoning because of it and threw up everything for the next 24 hours.

I can't tell you how disappointed I am in Mazzaro's. I recently bought some somewhat pricey cheese there and ended up with a severe case of food poisoning. Upon consuming the cheese I started violently vomiting for over 26 hours. I was in bed for 5 days recovering, weak and dealing with continued affects of the toxins for 3 weeks before I was back to health and get off bland foods. I missed work, canceled events and classes and felt lousy for the good part of a month. I understand that food can be bad and things like this can happen. But what I don't understand is that the proprietor of that food could not care less. I called the store to alert them of the issue so they could pull any of the cheese in hopes that no one else would get sick. No manager was available, so I reported it to the supervisor of the cheese area. She assured me that the information would be shared with Management. I never heard a word. I wrote a letter to the general manager with absolutely no response. No apology, no refund, no effort whatsoever to console a customer who was very very sick because of a product sold from your store. This is not a company who stands behind their products. They have plenty of customers so losing my business apparently is unimportant. But when we buy products, especially food, there should be a reasonable expectation of quality and a business practice of customer care. Current customers should be aware of my situation and think twice before shopping a Mazzaros's.

Just went to eat the buffet. 43 dollars later and we feel raped. Nothing, and I mean nothing was hot. It looked like leftovers from lunch. The whitefish was tepid. The lasagna was gross. The soup and gravy had at least a quarter inch of skin on them. Look, I like to eat. But the food was so gross that I ate lettuce with dressing on it. Even the little desert cakes were hard and nasty. The bathroom was pretty gross. The sanitary napkin disposal was overflowing and it was dim and dirty in there. The potatoes were instant, something that automatically triggers my gag reflex and makes me want to vomit. You know that a buffet is bad when your 17 year old son, who loves chicken and will eat chicken anything, pushes it away, and eats bananas instead. 10.99 a piece for a buffet plus 3 bucks each for crappy iced teas...no. Save your money. Go to the Circle K up the street instead.

I only go here for the blizzards which are good. First time I ordered a meal I had a chili dog and I got severe food poisoning. Never got sick from a blizzard though. I have also watched food being microwaved. Never will eat any hotdog or burger here again.

First time at Kobe's and I don't think I will be returning! I got the salmon add shrimp, the shrimp was juicy but my salmon was very dry and the rice was overly salty. A big problem I experienced was a lack of options for gluten allergies. The soup was not gluten free and neither was their ONLY option for salad dressing. They couldn't cook my food in front of me which I understand, but I ate much less then everyone else did for the same price Then, for dessert the manager refused to serve me anything besides oranges, even though I assured them that I know my allergy and as long as there's no wheat in the gelato I would be fine. The management needs to listen to customers and learn more about gluten allergies! Only good part of this experience was our server, Shawna, who was very attentive and kind for our large party of 14. And our chef Dat was hilarious, caring and very good at his job. Very upset with my experience for the money I paid. If you have any kind of allergy, don't go to Kobe's!

Got diarrhea & vomiting from here. Ordered 12 PC Mixed Chicken Meal & chicken was disgusting, old, dry, hard. Had upset stomach within 1-2 hours. Ended up with diarrhea, nausea, & vomiting. Avoid this place!
Totally disgusting smelled like sting chemicals when you walk in had lawn equipment in the front dining room.. people with allergies stay far away from this place!!

Whenever I'm in a random city I look up to see if they have any bakeries with gluten free options and I stumbled upon Batch. The gluten free pumpkin cupcake was really good although the Paleo chocolate cupcake was dry- not sure if it wasn't made that morning or what but it wasn't good. Overall this place was cute with friendly staff. Not sure what their regular cupcakes are like but give them a go- it's 50/50.

My family enjoys coming here for breakfast or for dinner to get breakfast! If you've been to one Cracker Barrel, you've been to them all. This one looks no different with a bunch of comfortable rocking chairs in the front, a store inside and then the restaurant. Food quality is decent and I find it to be consistent from restaurant to restaurant. My wife is gluten-free and she likes the fried catfish, which is coated with cornmeal. The boys and I always go for breakfast with my boys going for pancakes and I for French Toast. I also love their cinnamon apples as a side! We always get good service and while this location is a bit of a drive for us, we like to stop in from time to time and will be back.

Had their breakfast buffet yesterday for the first time. Terrible. I would venture to say it was the worst breakfast food I've ever had. The ham tasted like leather doused in salt. The biscuits were stale. The bacon was barely cooked. Everything just tasted old and salty. To top it all off, I believe my husband and I got a touch of food poisoning from it. We ate the same thing and we've been ill since yesterday. Steer clear of the breakfast buffet at least.

My wife and I met two friends for dinner at Granite City last evening (Friday). I had a 6 PM reservation and we were seated immediately. The first things we noticed were the table and the menus. The table had a foggy, haze on it and the menus weren't all that clean. Under the present Covid stuff, I almost did not want to touch the menu. The table cleaning should have been much better too. They were not busy so there was plenty of time for cleaning. Our server Anna was very sweet and she took very good care of us. She was friendly, attentive and saw to our every need. She was terrific but the food was a far cry from the excellent service. My buddy and I ordered the fish & chips. The fish was heavily breaded and the fish was totally overcome by the breading. It was maybe a 4 out of a ten for taste and quality. The fish came with fries but not very many. In short, if you go there do not order the fish & chips. I also had a cup of their clam chowder. On the menu it said "whole clam" clam chowder. Uhhhh....not. It was the typical potato chowder with a few (very few) small bits of clam meat. It was nothing special, just your typical canned chowder. Their menu made is sound much better than it was. My wife ordered a grilled chicken and asparagus linguini. It was void of any real flavor. It was flat as a board and had zero character. Jeezzzz...how could they screw up such a simple dish like that? But they did. My buddies wife had their prime rib sandwich (without the bun). It was the only gluten free thing the house had to offer. She ate it but it wasn't terrific. I noticed a lot of good Yelp reviews for this restaurant and many folks seemed to be pleased with their food. Good for them, but we had a much different experience. We won't be going back because there are way too many better bistros in the area.

I'm sorry to say that Batch has become hit or miss for me. I have been in quite a few times in the last year and more often than not I seem to be disappointed. Most recently was this past weekend. I had a Java Joe cupcake and my twin had a Keep Tahoe Blueberry. Mine was super dry and overly sweet, hers was quite tasty. That sums it up perfectly. This place isn't cheap, so it hurts my feelings when teh product isn't as expected. Luckily my twin was willing to share her tastiness. I'd also like to mention that all of their gluten free cupcakes taste the same. That was also an expensive lesson to learn! So save yourself the agony of deciding because it'll be the same regardless. If you are willing to gamble on a cupcake then hit place up.

I had the worst experience tonight, and I may not be going back (which is bad for them because I'm a multiple time a week patron). I went at 7:50pm tonight for a Peanut Power plye and had to state my order twice. They now charge extra for oat milk and vegan protein? A medium is now nearly $11..how is that? I'm sad because I'm allergic to the entire cow. I asked why the total was so high and the person who was waiting on me got super rude and laughed at me when I said I'd never been charged for vegan before. "Well you should have!" And when I said then I don't want it, thanks. She cackled. It was so off-putting because I wasn't at all a Karen and even said thank you after saying no. Guys, don't hire pieces of crap to wait on customers, you'll loose a lot more money than they are worth, I assure you. Also, don't nickle and dime those that have food allergies. That's seriously ignorant. Oat milk is cheaper than milk and most other vegan protein is cheaper than whey protein isolate.

I went here with my family. I was immediately disappointed once I saw the menu I looked up online was different from the in store menu. Far less vegan options than online and price difference. So I settled for the tofu scramble, fake bacon and gluten free waffle. The waffle was very hard and lacked any flavor. There exist alternatives to dairy instead of just water as an ingredient but I digress. I barely touched anything else. My dad had to send back his food to be reheated which they accommodated him very well. Overall food wise my family wasn't very happy with my recommendation of this place. The great part was the service however. Everyone foh and boh were very nice, including a cook who made sure my dad received hot food and manager I believe who visited the table. Our server, a young man was super personable and funny. I just wish the food matched the service. Three stars for service

Ok so i came to Reno to accompany my dear husband for a work conference. 2 1/2 hour drive and i was famished, he goes straight to the meeting and i walk around to look for fine dining. I stumbled upon The Buffet and i get in line to pay. I walked around to check out the food and finally selected chinese and mexican style food. The asian food was good i give it a 3 out of 5 i had the curry stuff, not memorable as it did not really pop in my pallet. Then, i was turned on by the street taco(al pastor) my fave, i grabbed 2, i gave that a 3out of 5. I grabbed some spanish rice, they didnt disappoint i had put some pork dish with sauce i forgot what its called. Then finally the menudo was what ive been wanting as well, i had a lot of it and it came with all the fixins, oregano, onions, chili, hot salsa etc. the taste was authentic but it still needed a bit of pizzazz but all over it was good. I also had their desert which was a 10/10. I started to feel queezy acterwards, i ate my food slowly while i finished watching episodes of Riverdale. By the way the service was ok although someone took my chair and water and sprite were often forgotten to be filled. I started to go to the restroom atleast 3x the whole time i was there. My hubby had a nice dinner prepared at the comference, i barely touched it as i was starting to have episodes of something felt like i was turning into a damn wareworlf. I kept going to the bathroom for a non stop diarrhea and i finally vomited everything i had eaten from The Buffet. The aftermath was horrible, upset stomach and continuos vomiting at the same time was not sexy at all, i was all dressed up to join my hubby for a night of fun with tequila and food but this was interrupted with often visit to the restroom to diarrhea and vomit. I went back to my hotel before midnight to sleep it off, i was in dire pain, still vomiting and diarrhea every 30 min. Food Poison is probably what i got from this place. The next day im still vomiting and i can taste the menudo i ate from yesterday everytime i burped, disgusting. This place gave me food poisoning.

Beautiful spot, classy host and great location. Unfortunately our server made it clear he knew all of these things and merely working there made him far superior. I've been in the industry in nice places for 12 years and it takes a lot to out-snob me. But holy mackerel was the distance from this man aggressive. We had a life threatening allergy and wanted to ensure from the out that we needed some information. This was greeted as though an outlandish request. When the lemon drop martini arrived clearly overly tart enough to need the traditional sugar rim and all we asked for was it a little sweeter without attitude, you'd have thought we asked for a coors lite over ice. The rest of the staff was lovely and sweet but we paid for our drinks and went elsewhere for a much better experience.

It's a cool, hipster breakfast joint. I get it. But that doesn't merit snobbery, which is all we got this morning when my husband and I decided to grab a late breakfast. We were told by the hostess it would take 20 minutes for a table and were directed to the bar for coffee and pastry options while we waited. Seemed reasonable enough. My husband ordered a Bloody Mary (which turned out to be below average at best) and for myself, a decaf coffee. The barista responded, "We don't have decaf." A little surprised to be told this breakfast restaurant doesn't offer decaf coffee, I asked if they had decaf americanos or latte options, and she replied, "We don't.. we haven't found a decaf coffee we like, but here's some juice options." I found it a little odd that they don't serve decaf, but the snobby comment was a little too much for me. A breakfast restaurant should offer decaf options, whether or not they've found an "acceptable" artisan Sumatran decaf blend. We waited another 15 minutes or so before we were seated, and browsed through the menu. While the whole staff gave off a "better than thou" vibe, something caught our eye on the menu that furthered engrained this negative vibe into the aesthetic: "We politely decline any modifications." So if I have an allergy to peanut butter, I can't have jam instead of peanut butter on my toast? Really? It was extremely off-putting. Furthermore, nothing on the menu seemed particularly appetizing, even though we are fairly adventurous eaters. After waiting over five minutes, not one person came to fill our water glasses, take our order, let us know it would be a moment, or even say hello. We decided to leave and go somewhere that valued and respected their customers over how high-waisted their 90s cut jeans are or how much mustache wax is holding their handlebar mustache upright, and we're glad we did.

On Saturday, Nov. 23, at about 6:15 or 6:30, I was driving with my three children and their neighbor/friend. The friend became car sick and threw up in the car. We stopped at the aforementioned Dollar General. The manager on duty, Cheyenne, went above and beyond in helping us find appropriate new clothes for the sick boy, and let him into the store restroom so he could clean up and change clothes. Her friendliness and helpfulness went a long way toward making an unfortunate (and gross) situation much more bearable, and helped us remediate the problems we were encountering. I can't thank her enough.

When you're on vacation, typically there's one night where you have "The Dinner". In my world it's typically planned to be a Friday or Saturday night, at a highly rated restaurant (the selection of which was agonized over many weeks ahead of time). There are always reservations involved, and expectations are high. Heaping all that pressure on Mr. B's Bistro seemed unfair as we were almost late to our own dinner (they won't seat you until the whole party is available, no matter how bad the parking is or if you accidentally turn down Bourbon street on Friday evening). And my hopes were swayed a bit as we approached the restaurant and were greeted by a vomiting man outside the front door. But in New Orleans, you don't know if that's food poisoning or just good old-fashioned alcohol excess. So in we went to join the others. Initial excitement behind us, we were seated in the 'low ceiling' area of the restaurant. Be mindful, individuals of above-average height, that you may want to request a table in the taller space... or just be careful when you stand up. Standing won't be a concern for several hours at least though, since the pace of dinner at Mr. B's is more on the formal side. As indicated by the old school menu, the name of the restaurant on the plates, and the fact that they will provide and tie a bib for you if you order something that requires hands-on eating. Though I'd describe the overall vibe as casual fine dining. The Menu Starters were the Duck Springrolls (duck confit, shiitake mushrooms, spinach and goat cheese; served with ginger-soy dipping sauce) and Garlic Truffle Fries (topped with pecorino romano cheese and porcini oil). And while fries aren't something I routinely order at every restaurant, one of my traveling compats is a fan, and these were probably the best iteration we had in town. And the duck springrolls... no chance those weren't going to be tasty. Next up, I moved on with the Soups 1-1-1, a sampling of the Gumbo Ya Ya, Seafood Gumbo, and Soup du Jour. The portions were a nice way to experience three more delicious menu items and even ended up being enough to share a bit also... I had a whole meal coming up after all. Duck Springrolls Garlic Truffle Fries That meal being... Bacon-Wrapped Shrimp & Grits. Not just any bacon, mind you, but pecan smoked bacon. And not just any shrimp was this bacon wrapping, but jumbo gulf shrimp. These savory meat bundles were presented on a bed of creamy stone-ground yellow grits with red-eye gravy (made from pan drippings of sausage, ham, bacon or other pork). Mmmmm, This was what I'd call a quintessential creole dish. Another must-try was Mr. B's signature Barbequed Shrimp entree. This is one they'll bring with a bib, so get ready to liberate those tasty shrimp from their shells and sop up the accompanying peppery butter sauce with plenty of French bread. Then you can die happy. Bacon-Wrapped Shrimp & Grits Mr. B's BBQ Shrimp Suddenly, an hour and a half later, it was time for dessert! Another very difficult decision, as every good dessert menu in this city had been so far. I decided on Bread Pudding... "A Brennan family recipe rich in eggs, cream, and butter, served warm with Irish whiskey sauce" and an espresso on the side. Both were a simply perfect end to an epic meal.

Wow, I used to really like coming here but the quality and availability of ingredients and the cleanliness of this location had made this visit my last. I have been a huge fan of pieology in the past, but starting with the removal of the build your own salad in the nice big bowls a few months back, it has all started to go downhill and fast. At this location there are also alot of specific problems. I can't say too much about lunch, but the last few times I have come for dinner it had been around 7. The store generally looks unkempt. Tables are always dirty. The lemonades are frequently low or out. At the pizza line, the pizza peels are dirty, not even lightly wiped between uses. Many key ingredients are often out (mushrooms and basil particularly). The ingredients are applied with little care, contaminating adjacent tubs. The store seems constantly understaffed as there are always just one or two people working. The staff appearance and and hygiene also leave something to be desired. I mean I know they are making pizza so I don't expect them to be sparkling but they could at least manage to button their shirts, maybe wear aprons that could be changed mid shift if they get particularly dirty. Lastly staff don't follow good food hygiene constantly touching their hair and faces and then not washing their hands. All of this has added up to this being the last time I will go until they address these issues :'(

I dont quite get the hype about texas roadhouse. Their rolls are okay, but their menu is quite sad in my opinion. For starters, I getthe culture of the place, but the amount of used peanut shells on the floor throughout the restaurant was repulsive! Wow. DO NOT COME HERE IF YOU HAVE A PEANUT ALLERGY On a Saturday night you are practically swimming in them.. Gross. Anyway, the food. I dont get it it was extremely underwhelming considering all the rave I hear about this place. I had a country fried steak that looked old and like a fried wing of a bat. I took one or two bites and was done with it. The sides were just that...sides. We also had a rib rack app that was okay, nothing to write home about . Their beer selection sucks... Idk, I don't get it. Do you people just have no taste? Or care about moderate cleanliness? Again, the rolls were soft, sweet with a cinnamon butter along with them, they were the best thing about our entire visit. The service wasnt great, our waitress didnt come until we had been seated for about 8-10 mins. After that she was very friendly and attentive, but I would just about never come back here.

Came on Taco Tuesday. Tried to order 2 tacos for my son with only beef and was given a huge issue. We were told no modifications, which this one, in food costs, makes it less. Made no sense. Told we would have to pay full price to have only meat and tortilla. He is a picky eater and I have dairy allergies. Totally ridiculous. It took forever to get seated and also for drinks. There is a ladder on the patio. Waited forever for drink refills. The outside fans don't work for some reason. I tried pulling one. The salsa was good and the margarita was decent for a Happy Hour drink. The food was good but the Taco Tuesday thing is off putting along with the ladder and no fans. Could be a good place if they work on customer service and exceptions for picky eaters and people with allergies.

BEWARE IF YOU HAVE ANY FOOD ALLERGIES!!!!! Cracker Barrel, Plymouth Meeting, PA has a common practice of cooking nuts & other highly allergic foods on the same grill with all other foods. They were not willing to make accommodations to avoid cross contamination of food for my family with nut allergies. Many other restaurants would use a dedicated grill, pan, fryer etc. to separate allergic foods, but not this Cracker Barrel. Needless to say we did not & will never eat at this site.

I cannot stress this enough. Stay away from this place. My wife and I have been here numerous times and it's always pretty good. Unfortunately, we will not be back. We arrived yesterday around 11:45 and the restaurant was dead. We started with the squash dumplings. They were good. Not much sauce but flavor wise they were good. My wife went with the chicken lettuce wraps and i has the Chang's shrimp. First the shrimp was breaded, that was a major bummer for me. The rice was good but covered in grease. The chicken wraps were good but then that's where the trouble started. Something had to be off. About 7-8 hours after eating there my wife became very ill. She was up all evening with food poisoning. Now my wife is in the medical field, I don't throw that term food poisoning around easily. I've never seen anyone that sick before. It was sad to watch. We eat out often and this is the first time this has happened. We will not be back nor would we recommend.

Dirty, and rude. They gave me mashed potatoes that someone half ate. Rude about not wanting to give a whole meal back. They did replace the meal after I called the regional manager. The next time l came back we got food poisoning need I say more.

they have some serious problems that need immediate attention. Shame on me for not actually reading the Yelp reviews beforehand, i was excited to find a cajun restaurant in my neighborhood but i got blindsided with one of the worst dining experiences I have had in 40 years of world travel. My first clue should have been an empty restaurant on a saturday night, in a neighborhood that usually has a waiting list for tables. The most egregeous problem they had was serving a guest raw hamburger meat. My wife ordered a 'well done' burger but received a burger that the middle was literily cold and raw, not pink, not rare....RAW. A food poisoning incident waiting to happen. The next problem, , waitress knew nothing about the menu (could be a training issue don't know), but definitly a communication problem. The chef had walked by and asked how our meal was and we had not even been served yet????? neither the manager on duty or the waitress knew the POS system and struggled to remove the offending burger from our bill. I love cajun food so I had the etouffe, which was edible but very lack luster, hardly any flavor or spices and so few crawfish that I thought I got a vegetarian dish, i found myself searching for the salt or pepper shaker, which did not exist on any of the tables. I understand this is a non-profit restaurant for some church group, and that is what it felt like, we were intruding in a private social club. The decor felt like a meeting room in the basement of a church. My suggestion make it members only and your church group can do their thing, but don't bother trying to serve the public. I don't mind spending a little more for a good cause/charity, but this was Premium prices for soup kitchen quality. Judging by the other Yelp reviews , I'd say they either don't care about public opinion or lack the computer skills to see what people are saying. The bad reviews have been going on for months and months, plenty of time to make changes and fix things.
Got food poisoning from here from the cheesy stuffed pizza. Guy was condescending when I asked for a refund.

Food Allergies Beware!!!! I wanted to share my experience yesterday at Brio Frontenac. I have been a long time customer since it opened up until yesterday. I ordered the Tomato Soup "to go" to take home and eat. I started to eat the soup and took one bite and it tasted different and then I remembered that they also have a Lobster Bisque on their menu. I packed up my soup and went back to Brio because I needed to make sure whether I had the Tomato Soup or was it the Lobster Bisque?? Sure enough it was the Lobster Bisque, I have a severe food allergy to shellfish, so much so that I could die from it. Here is what I am upset about, this experience happened more than 24 hours ago and the General Manager has not called me to follow up. What a serious mistake that could of had horrible consequences for me. "I'm sorry doesn't solve anything , tell me how you will make sure this won't happen again to another customer. The person on the phone rang up my order wrong, well you know what someone needs to explain the seriousness of Food Allergies to the restaurant staff and the Manager because "I'm sorry doesn't help" You lost a long time customer and it is obvious you don't care or take food allergies seriously because this whole situation was handled unprofessionally.

Week 1: Get Your Gat, We Are Going To Three Coins An excerpt from the Meatball Chronicles http://sundaymeatballchronicles.blogspot.com/ As I sit here excited to tell you about my first (and only) adventure to 3 Coins, there is also a feeling of disappointment. I've had so many culinary adventures and aside from a few uploads of corned beef hash, I haven't shared them with anyone. The Meatball Chronicles never reserve seats for the excessively meticulous. The engagements have included canned meat mountains, dirty tables, fraudulent Elvis booths, 6000+ calorie challenges, breakfast cocktails, sake bombs then falling for the love of my life (and not the other way around), raw food, cooked food, northern food, southern food, a meatloaf marathon, a few instances of food poisoning, some hand holding in public, and much more. I can only pray that some day I make it to Australia to eat those berries that grow in the digestive systems of emus and can only be found by picking through their crap. Three Coins Diner, Tampa: Last Sunday was like any other Sunday. We woke up on a mission for calories. In the mood for a hole in the wall, greasy southern breakfast joint, we settled on a Nebraska Ave location... we were on a mission. But Nebraska?!? Should I change my Burberry boots? Should I rent a gun? This was sure to be amazing. As we walked in, I was instantly bummed. Where's the big fat Southern Lady? Where are the cackling motel landlords? Why is everyone here a white elderly couple? Thankfully, there wasn't time to dwell on this because I was starving and knew what I wanted. We immediately ordered country fried steak and gravy, grits, corned beef hash, eggs over easy, a side of sausage links, two coffees, and two waters. The table next to us had two young guys and their food was served within minutes. What the F?!?! That grimy bastard ordered the same thing I ordered. Should I stand up to use the restroom and accidentally drop my face into it? I don't want to wait any longer. Thank goodness my better half has caught my attention with his outrageous Sunday morning thought. "I'd be interested in genetically engineering a child" I must have looked dumbfounded because he immediately got defensive and said "WHAT? We did it with cows all the time." I wasn't dumbfounded, I was lost in my own thoughts again... could i genetically engineer a child to have a fast metabolism so it could join me on my culinary adventures without being obese? Clearly these adventures are no place for children. "If you and I did this, it would definitely need my nose and my boobs." Really? You are a man, you don't have boobs. Oh shit neither do I. And what's this crap about my nose? You don't like my face? AHHH THE FOOD!!!! A GLORIOUS MOUNTAIN OF CORNED BEEF HASH. I DON'T CARE ABOUT ANYTHING ELSE I WANT THIS HASH NOW. To be honest, I was so starving that I would have enjoyed anything. But man, this hash... it was freakin' amazing. Crusted on the outside and everything. The grits were okay but anything is okay with a puddle of butter in it. Sausage- Good. Eggs- An egg's an egg. Country Fried Steak and Gravy- Well the gravy wasn't sausage gravy and although it wasn't my order, i'd say it was average. Major fail on the lack of sausage--they don't serve it after 11AM. I won't be back... the hash is worth doing illegal things for, but I'm positive there is more hash to be tasted someplace new.

The hostess and our server Maddie were both very sweet other than that it wasn't a pleasant experience. We came here because it popped up under gluten free options. There weren't many to choose from. I barely touched my food. My sweet potatoes were lukewarm. On the way out because I was still hungry I stopped at the bakery section. The gentleman working the counter barely took time to look up at me and after I asked about any gluten free desserts he rolled eyes his at my daughter and I. I had really high hopes coming in. Sadly, I'm disappointed over all.

Horrible service, the server Hannah told us we had to order one entree per person to have a drink there. So my date and I ordered guac and chips plus a grilled cheese. Grilled cheese was fine, however guac had a blackened layer over it which the restaurant tried to hide by sprinkling micro greens on it. Not a big deal but our server Hannah told us we are lying and the guac was not dark brown, she refused to take it off the tab even though we didn't touch it. She insisted on us ordering another entree since the law was one entree per person (which I have never heard of) after I said no thanks she brought over the manager that wanted to give us more guac that he said was fresher, I said no thanks. If a restaurant is willing to serve you old brown guac I do not trust them to remake it. All you have to do is stir it up to hide the old guac and boom you have food poisoning. I liked their craft beer but will never be coming back here.

Ordered through Uber Eats. They made the order 20 minutes faster than expected, but it was wrong. They put shrimp in my husband's Pad Thai. Thank goodness he's not allergic. But the most disappointing thing was the crab rangoons. They had less than 1/2 Tablespoon of filling and there was no crab anywhere to be found. You can see on the picture.
