They also appear to have been cooked previously and reheated. It's completely unacceptable.

Unfortunately, this one star is for the lack of response due to food poisoning. The pros - nice staff, beautiful interior, good prices, good beers. The negative - don't order milk. Our lovely waitress said she'd check to see if they had "good milk" as they have had issues in the past with questionable milk. She found some and not more than 3 hours later, our daughter was puking in her sleep and until 4 a.m. My husband called that night to tell them that they might not want to serve that anymore and I left a message the following day. No response. What a waste of money and terrible customer service. We will not return nor recommend.

What you should know about me: My favorite burger is an In-and-Out double double. I used to have an office across from The Habit. My favorite flavor is vanilla. I've never been to prison. Green is my favorite color, and I do love my mom. With that said... The Habit is good. Really good. The outdoor seating and the way you order and pick up food is endearing. Its a very beach-town setup, and I love that about it. The parking in back is usually not full, but the spots are tight. The minimal street parking is almost always taken. As for the burgers...well, its complicated. If I want a burger thats less cookie cutter and tastes like it came from a grill, I'll go to the habit. Add some bacon and you've got yourself a damn good burger thats very hard to beat. However, if I want a burger that I KNOW will taste exactly the same as it tasted last time, I'm going to In-and-Out still. A double-double is a guaranteed romance explosion in my mouth. A burger from the Habit is more like a dicing up a rainbow...its got a lot of flavor and makes you feel good inside, but ultimately its never as good as you hoped it would be. The vanilla and mocha shakes here are to die for! For the record, I must also state that I once contracted a nasty case of food poisoning from a burger here. I don't hold a grudge for it as I'm sure it was a fluke, but I wasn't able to eat a burger here for 6 months after that. -1 star for food poisoning. == Location: Good, if you're comfortable with Old Town Goleta. == The Goods: Excellent burgers that rival In-and-Out. Great shakes! == Ambiance: Total beach-town feel. No indoor seating, but lots outside. == Overall: If you live anywhere within spittin' distance of Goleta, you must try the Habit at least once.
I am so glad this place closed, it probably saved a lot of people from getting food poisoning like I did.

I used to come here a lot and quite liked it, but my recent visit was incredibly disappointing. On a really hot day (i.e. a regular day during the summer in NOLA), they had no air conditioning inside and the pastries/cakes were in a flimsy display case with no cooling system. This could potentially lead to food poisoning so I felt really uncomfortable. Additionally, I saw a maggot next to one of the cheesecakes in the display case. The service is also not the best.

The manager of this tropical smoothie in Ruskin was rude to my family and I after they made our smoothie wrong and I asked her to fix it . First she accused us of trying to steal half of a smoothie because I shared some with my toddler before realizing that the smoothie was made wrong. Instead of providing the customer service she could have she blamed her staff and tried to argue with me . Then ultimately she decided to ignore us .my daughter was crying and she didn't even apologize. . I have an allergy so I was really upset about them messing up my order . I don't recommended anyone go here.

My best friend and I thought this restuarant had great festive decorations for the holiday season and decided to dine there for dinner on our last night in santa barbara. The wait was extremely long, I don't think we were seated until an hour and a half after our arrival. While the food was quite delicious, shortly after dinner both me and my friend had food poisoning which resulted in a long miserable night over the toilet. Although we're not quite sure who's dish was at fault seeing as we both tried each other's dish, mine (the linguine with clams) and hers (chicken piccatta with spaghetti). So be warned!! You may get food poisoned if you go!

Instant food poisoning. 1 st meal in NOLA resulted in severe diarrhea. It dictated the rest of our first day in NOLA. We shared cheese fries compliments of our hotel Maison Dupuy. I had the Grilled Shrimp Remi with onion rings and my Friend (had more severe diarrhea) had the Hot Sausage Po-Boy with an extra hamburger patty, and the Fried Shrimp Platter. My friend was so affected with Diarrhea "I think I found the whistle I swallowed in 3rd grade." So much for any alcohol or food for the rest of the day in NOLA. I don't care if they're paying us to eat there it will never happen again. The empty restaurant should've been the first clue. Btw, Grilled Shrimp were not seasoned. Onion strings were actually very greasy onion bits. Deanie's was just across the street. Why didn't we go with our then healthy gut?

Really wish you could review the hotel and casino separately on here, as it's two completely different ratings for me. First off, the hotel. As you pull into the parking lot, the casino building is on your right. The building to the left is what they call the North Hotel; behind it, initially out of sight, is the South Hotel. I don't know if the South Hotel is any different, I stayed in the North. At first blush it looked like a good deal for $40 on a weeknight; like a motel 6 but a little nicer, and with a mini-fridge and free wifi. That impression only held up until nightfall, when other guests come in. Holy shit does this place have the worst sound insulation / privacy I've ever experienced! There might as well have not been walls at all. Loud-ass shower, bathroom farts and pissing, bed squeaks and even breathing from the wall the beds face. Loud-ass TV and drunkard conversations from the other wall. And apparently The Blob followed me from the last hotel to the room above. "Time to check out sir!" "NO ONE MOVES THE BLOB!!!" Oh, and it's one of those places where there's a good 1/2 inch gap under the door, so you get all the hallway noise as well. Also, the "non-smoking" room is meaningless as either they put them right next to smoking rooms, or people in them just don't give a fuck, and their chain-smoking seeps through the various cracks the sound apparently is going through to make your room smell all shit. So 1* for the hotel, just terrible construction. The one bright spot is literally being right next to Sparks Marina, which has a nice long walk around a manmade lake. The casino, on the other hand, was at least decent. It has that unfortunate Peppermill style of vomiting colors, wild patterns and video screens at you to apparently try to disorient you and get you to make bad money decisions, and the machines are grouped almost randomly with no indication of game types or denominations. Other than that, though, it's small but not bad. Mostly video machines, a few tables set up upon request. Small but adequate sports book with a decent bar and ten screens, sound on for the hockey playoffs (thank god). The high point is the eateries, which are inexpensive but serve pretty good food. This seems like a local casino where the patronage is mostly seniors, so don't expect wild party times. Could be a chill place to play video poker though, and worth checking out the restaurants. I'll default to 3* overall since the hotel isn't a mandatory part of the experience.

As a vegan, I was so excited to try Batch Cupcakery seeing as they have a few vegan options, and vegan desserts in Reno are few. The cupcakes look so delicious on their website and on Yelp. Sadly, I was so let down after my first visit. I thought they'd have more than 2 vegan options, so I was disappointed to find there were only 2. I bought one vegan cupcake (chai), one vegan gluten-free (strawberry shortcake) and one non-vegan (s'mores) for my husband. The chai cupcake was SO dry and stale-tasting. The gluten-free cupcake was the most moist cupcake out of the bunch, which really surprised me, but it did fall apart. My husband said the s'mores cupcake was very dense, and he didn't like it at all. I didn't finish either cupcake they were so bad. I make much better at home, so why would I spend my money here? Also, the interior layout is really odd. I don't like how there are cupcake cases everywhere. It looks cluttered. For the employee to have to come from behind the counter to retrieve the cupcakes for you is so strange to me. The 1 star is for the service and the cupcake aesthetics. The gentleman who helped me was very friendly, and the cupcakes look pretty. But due to terrible texture and taste, I will not be back, and I do not recommend Batch Cupcakery. Go next door to Great Full Gardens for wonderful vegan desserts.
Overpriced Gluten Free Pizza that tastes awful. 16 dollars for a super thin, burnt and smaller than 10 inch personal pizza is unacceptable.

While the food is decent, I got really horrible food poisoning from one dinner buffet. But I won't give The Buffet one star, because I have had some really decent food. The prime rib is tasty, the servers are friendly, the dessert selection is okay. The breakfast buffet is even okay. But I can't excuse food poisoning, especially when my meal from The Buffet was the only meal I ate that day. Minus stars.
I like Ron's but I had food poisoning after my dinner last Tuesday. I ordered the lasagna and a house salad. I think it was the salad. I plan to stick with the ovals in the future to be safe.

Place totally blows. Horrible food of every variety. The dopey kids behind the counter are inattentive and checked out. Asked for a plain cheese hoagie for my son and the morons made him a cheese hoagie packed (PACKED) full of meats that he is allergic to. Found out after I got home. Total garbage. Zero stars.

Made a Yelp just to write them a review. I'm not sure how this place has a 3.5-4.5 review on different mediums. Not sure if locals in Santa Barbara just don't have a very diverse palette, or just have actual bad taste. Carbonara was a great food poisoning experience and primavera tasted like dish soap. When describing this to management, apparently it was just an opinion and their food is the "best" in town. Also, service was garbage. Funny joke as a restaurant. Nice mirrors though.

The food I tried was alright but nothing to return for. The staff were friendly and the place seemed clean. There was a great selection of food but not a whole lot for vegetarian or vegan, and absolutely nothing for my gluten free lunch companion.

This is a very popular restaurant and therefore there's a very long wait time but the food portions are large and filling so it's worth the wait. Three of us girls got a variety of toast with eggs (pictured) that we truly enjoyed! We did have a few qualms overall - long wait time for food and we weren't informed of them being out of menu items until we tried to order them which is why I'm going with 4/5 stars. Their menu is extensive with a lot of items that draw your attention so it wasn't too hard to choose something new. Our server Charlie was really nice and friendly and the ambiance was great. Definitely worth the wait and there are cute photo ops in the area you can walk to while you're on the list! ** UPDATE TO 5 STARS: my sister unfortunately had an allergic reaction to something that was an undiagnosed allergy - not the restaurants fault!! We called to ask what ingredients were in the meal she ordered and the manager was very helpful. Even so that she called me back 2 hours after our initial call to provide me an update that she discovered. The thoughtfulness and caring nature of a staff that seats and feeds so many people in a day shows a lot about the quality of the restaurant.
Ordered using the app. The order was totally messed up. I ordered chicken but there was no chicken and some corn and nuts were there that I didn't order. Don't recommend if you have allergies

I have just barely survived this delivery. I am now writing this review in abject shock and disgust. I didn't know food could taste so horrific. The meal I ordered was Easily the worst thing I have ever eaten the only reason I've ingested any of this is because I was getting very ill from being too hungry. I can't figure out which sensation is worse: being sick from starvation or eating this food. I can't believe I paid money to eat this foul monstrosity they call "Chinese food." They insult an entire beautiful culture by being in business. Okay, now that I've gotten that out of my system. Let me break this down in great detail: 1) The chow fun rice noodles: at first glance they didn't look threatening... But when you bite into the noodles the texture of them is like they have been overcooked then saved for later to be overcooked again. The flavor is ineffably bland. I at times detect a rotting taste/odor. This flavor is present throughout the entire dish. (Vegetables too) as for the vegetables in the dish, I believe they have been pre cooked and then got freezer burn then reused. They have awful texture and taste. I could be wrong. I literally have no idea how you can screw up this badly. Even while being at the stage of hunger i was in, you would think i would be a more gentle critic. Next up, curry vegetable stir fry: nasty cesspool oil pit of freezer burned vegetables. I don't know if any of these dishes can be saved even with doctoring up from home. The egg rolls were a little strange, but i was able to overlook that because I was so hungry. The wontons were okay. Also strange, but out of the whole order, I struggled eating this less than what i actually ordered. I'm also furious that they charge just as much as other legitimate restaurants do. I was thinking about calling and requesting a refund, but after looking at these other reviews it doesn't look like I have a very good chance of that. The only way I can feel better about being the butt of this cruel food prank is complaining about it on Yelp, and hopefully others will take heed of this explicit warning. Ok, I'm going to stop writing now. I'm going to sit here in misery and try to digest this mess. I'll update later if I get food poisoning. Please listen to the majority of reviews. If you value your internal organs and have basic respect for your culinary palate, NEVER order food from this place.

Husband and I went there this past Sunday 6/30/19 to give the new hot place a try. I got the turkey sub and my husband got the Cuban. Both we thought were good, UNTIL we got home and my husband got sick to his stomach. Thought it was something else he ate, until we found out today 7/2/19 from 4 different neighbors, that they themselves all got sick off the Cuban sandwich from Jon Smith's within the past week. Of course, food poisoning is extremely hard to prove but, with 4 other people stating they also had the same symptoms as my husband from the Cuban sandwich basically points to food poisoning. I have already reached out to the establishment and spoken to the manager. Who is taking this very seriously.

I was unfamiliar with the menu and asked about details, and the response was it's like Taco Bell. Great customer service so far. The lettuce looked like it was just about to turn. I didn't get a real close look at the other food on the line, but I assumed everything else was similarly questionable based on the wretched state my stomach was in not long after I ate the food, which was a FAKE MEAT burrito and mostly edible. I don't know what health code inspections have turned up in the past, but it can't be great if fake meat crumbles can't make the chances of food poisoning go down. I won't be going back.

I asked for a roll without mayo, and the chef had a hissy fit. Not a "hey can you sub this for this and this for this" kind of thing, just a simple "hey, could you not Americanize my sushi to death by pouring mayonnaise all over it." He made our server come over to ask my if I would go over and tell the chef I had an allergy. It was incredibly awkward. But hey, the roll was delicious...because it wasn't covered in mayonnaise. It's pretty standard in terms of pricing. I would take the 5 extra minutes to go to Sakura or H20, where the chefs aren't as sensitive.
Why are there so many flies in this place? It's disgusting. They are all over the food. Combined with the filthy bathrooms don't be surprised if you get sick from food poisoning.

They were good until... If a person calls or complains about their food being raw. The 1st thing you don't do is get defensive with them. Following to be pretty offensive directly after. Especially if the complaining person is being super nice and sorry to even have to call and complain. The response after my letting the person whom answered the phones know that 2 we had tried already were not fully cooked. "Well we made a batch over 500 of those to order and you are the first one to complain, so I find this very hard to believe". Repeated this more than once in a slightly sarcastic tone also. THEN says, well I am so sorry if this actually happened to you. Can you come show me? In a tone as of such "come prove me wrong". So much of this was unnecessary. My jaw dropped at the way the guy handled this over the phone today in regards to a beautiful gift that was a delivery of 12 gluten free cupcakes for my mother/boss being her birthday yesterday. I was appalled as such towards this persons way of handling the situation so much that I handed the phone to her so she could advocate for her own gift (which she shouldn't have to). Only for the same type of treatment. Because of the way it was handled we don't even want the replacement. We don't ever even want to return. We didn't want to say anything but THANK YOU to the purchaser of the lovely gift idea. So simply called the shop feeling bad at first to even have to. Once more this is why I am bummed about the outcome. I have been going here for a couple years and never had such an issue, actually never an issue. Unfortunately all it takes is one seriously lousy situation to make a person never want to go back. Raw food and poor customer service. No thanks. Good luck to you Batch.

I'll admit first hand that I am a tough critic when it comes to restaurants, but in my opinion, If someone is gonna spend their time and energy somewhere it should be worthwhile. My first encounter with Mad Mex was this summer in Philly when I went on a fantastic date with my boyfriend. The setting was cool, the food was delicious, and we both left happy. So... When I found out that a new Mad Mex was opening in Wynnewood right near me I was really excited to go give it a try, despite it being a typical food chain with oversized menus and oversized meals. I cannot even begin to describe the sort of disaster that place is brewing, or should I say cooking up. I was with my family to start the meal we ordered guacamole. All was good and fine until it arrived at our table. At first I was unaware of how rotten the avocados were because of the restaurant's "pleasant" low lighting, but after consuming a bite or two I was appalled at the rancid flavor. After taking a second look I realized what I had just consumed. (See attached image) So very politely I asked the waiter if there was any chance he could bring "fresher" guacamole and his response was ohhh ok yes definitely" I'm sorry but shouldn't you always be bringing your fresh guacamole to your customers. When he came back to our table he told us the chef had received a bad shipment of "over ripe" avocados. Last time I checked if that happens a chef wouldn't then continue to make batch upon Batch of guacamole with them and who knows what else. Then, we order our main meal. I notice as I look at my newly obtained silverware that it is ridiculously filthy. At first I just see splotches of residue that may as well have been from the dish washer detergent but as I look closer I see an actual crusty attached to my fork. It made me nauseous. (See attached image) Instead of asking for a new fork, which would be useless because who knows what the other ones would be like I ordered steak tacos completely well done in fear of another fuck up in the kitchen and the result being food poisoning. My grandmother ordered the same thing and the waiter gave her a hard time about which types were considered proteins or not when she ordered a portobello mushroom and a chicken one stating "portobellos are a protein ma'm". Lastly, we receive our meals. I am shocked to see that the fajitas my parents ordered have side of the same god damn rotten guacamole that we ate as an appetizer. I mean really! The chef puts it back on our next dishes! As Im about a quarter way through my steak I am unable to swallow. I open my taco and the steak is completely raw and rubbery! (See attached image) After all of this the manager only took one of the taco dishes off the bill and we still ended up paying for a majority of the meal. I know this review may sound dramatic but I have to assure you that we were very polite about the whole thing. I just wanted to report what was going on so that Yelpers can be aware of this ridiculous excuse for a business

Good pizza and other items as well! Very flavorful and never disappointing! I love to be able to customize the pizza just the way I like it extra sauce, little sauce, no sauce, or normal, lightly cooked, normal cooked, extra cooked, etc. etc. And they don't charge extra for extra sauce on the pizzas. I love it, since I am pretty saucy myself, lol! Awesone sauce!! There's also tons of different crust options you can choose from like asago cheese, garlic herb, ranch, siracha, just to name a few, but there are more choices as well. I love that the menu items for anything other than pizza, are actually affordable and not over priced, just what Tucson needs. Sure, some people are only going to order pizza but with a name like Hungry Howie's, it's great that *good* items other than pizza are offered because people will be hungry for them, and we are blessed that Hungry Howie's applies to those options. The reward program could use some modifications, because basically you need to spend too much before a $10 reward is offered, but it's still not totally absurd like other places either. I prefer to spend less still get rewarded just because I'm giving the venue my business, but ya know, every place is different. Howie rolls are like strombolis and they are a pretty decent size. You get what you pay for. Those too, can be customized to your liking. They also now serve gluten free crust as well, but if you have celiac disease, I advise to ask about their practices on avoiding cross contamination. This is a great pizzeria.

OMG !! Major thanks to Amanda B (on 8/3/2016) for bringing this to my attention. I was not previously aware of the FDA - filed complaints, and the FDA's official review of Sami's Bakery starting in 2016. Notably, it wasn't until recently (Feb 2019) that the FDA closed out their records on Sami's. It took 2.5 years. Luckily I read Amanda B"s review when I was about to reorder. In addition to throwing out what I had left in my freezer of Sami's breads, I will NEVER order from them again. Based on the FDA's findings during their site visit to Sami's Bakery, I do not have confidence that Sami's keeps a clean shop, nor am I confident that they can be trusted to keep their products uncontaminated with other foods not listed on their ingredients label. For those who didn't look at the links provided previously by Amanda B, here are excerpts from the FDA on 10/26/2016: * From the FDA: "FDA has received four (4) complaints between 2007 and 2016 ... regarding the presence of gluten or wheat in products ... (and) ... are not listed as ingredients on the product labeling..." -- Per Gluten Free Watchdog, in July 2016, they had Sami's gluten-free products analyzed and found the samples contained 25-50% wheat flour! It is unlikely that such a high percentage be explained away due to just processing cross-contamination. "... ingredient storage bins ... which contained no identifying marks ... wheat gluten ... (do not have) a label ... stored directly (next) to a bin of rice flour." -- In other words, though Sami's kept their baking ingredients separated, their bins are placed side by side which are not adequately labeled. " ... filth and residue was observed on the raw pita dough conveyor belt; missing bristles and an accumulation of food debris on a brush being used to apply oil onto bagel dough; accumulation of filth and residue on the pita conveyor used to transport finished pita bread to the packaging room, scoops used in dry material bins, wooden trays used as food contact surfaces, and on screws within the seed grinder ..." -- Uh -- "FILTH AND RESIDUE" ? " ... the bread loaf pans were observed to be rusted with debris ..." -- Uh -- "RUSTED WITH DEBRIS" ? " ... floors within the grinding room were observed to be partially made of wood and were not constructed of a smooth surface that can be adequately cleaned and sanitized." -- Uh -- "FLOORS ... NOT ... ADEQUATELY CLEANED AND SANITIZED" ? " ... observed during the inspection ... two white buckets of ... old breads in the processing area, ... (observed) an employee taking a bite of a piece of pita bread and then throwing the piece into the white bucket. (Though, Sami's representative said) these buckets were designated for the trash) ... but (they are using this) old product as starter material for new product." -- So Sami's told the FDA rep that it was okay for the employee to throw a partially eaten pita bread into these buckets, but also they intend to use this old product in these buckets as a source for starting material ? This part's a little confusing, but this is how I read it.

Let me start by saying, my family has been coming to New Town Buffet for years, since they first opened their doors, and it has usually been decent food for a Chinese buffet. Today, however, was the worst. When we walked in the door, the hostess was chatting on her cellphone, and motioned us with her hand to follow her to a table, never once uttering a single word to us, but continued to talk to someone on her phone. Normally, within 30 seconds, our drink orders are taken, and we proceed to the buffet. Today we waited for nearly 10 minutes before someone took our drink order. When we went to get our food, several items were mislabeled. The chow fun noodles were labeled as "Steak", egg foo young was labeled as "Coconut Shrimp", and spicy chicken with red pepper flakes was labeled "Orange Chicken". Upon starting to eat our food we soon found many of the foods were cold that should have been fresh and piping hot, especially considering we got here at 11:30am. When we told the staff the food was cold, they told us they would talk to the manager and suggested we should pull the food from the bottom of the trays. And then about 30 minutes later, a staff member came to our table and told us we should go get more food now because it had just now been prepared hot and fresh. I do not know for sure why the food was cold, but I strongly suspect when they opened, the leftover trays of food from the night before were pulled from the refrigerator, and placed on the steam heating buffet tables to reheat. If we had come here an hour later, the food would have had time to heat up and we would never have known. The manager never came to speak with us. I sincerely hope none of us get food poisoning due to unsafe food handling. We will not be returning to this restaurant ever again.

Best fish tacos I've ever had, and I was born and raised in Southern Calfornia - where fish tacos are abundant in authentic and fast food form, from very fresh to food-poisoning-in-waiting. You get two good-sized tacos of Mahi Mahi (or tilapia) seasoned in a cajun influenced way, in a corn tortilla ... with large chunks of grilled fish inside, cabbage, and a white sauce drizzled over it all. In-freaking-credible! It comes with a side of black beans and an almost milky tasting rice. Amazing. Out of all the fantastic foods I tried and loved, these fish tacos are something I'd come back for and try to recreate at home. We also ordered the fried pickles. Just do it! Skipped the drinks because I was driving, but there's live music up front by the bar...open air windows to the outside - we were lucky to get to listen to Eric Von. He's awesome! He'll play almost anything you request (someone requested Lady Ga Ga's Pokerface as a joke... and he made a country version of it that blew her lame song out of the water and back again!) I had scheduled a visit to the Gaylord Opryland Resort as part of a Christmas trip to Nashville to enjoy the decorations and a performance of The Nutcracker at TPAC. We arrived to the usual traffic mess at the entrance to the hotel. Not unusual for this time of year. However, they were in no way equipped to differentiate between the cars there to check in to the hotel and those there to see the sights. 45 minutes in the car line got us to within sight of the drive through for registration. The employee at the street informed us that it would be another 25-30 minutes to get to the actual valet parking stand. So I turned around and made my way back to the self park lot and carried my bags to the lobby. Registration wasn't an issue and we headed to our room. No offer of bellhop assistance was made. At the room we opened the door to an incredibly heavy floral scent wafting out into the hallway. My wife, who is sensitive to odors and has allergies noted that the scent was extremely strong. I minimized it at first until I began to feel my nose starting to burn as well. I'm not sensitive to fragrance at all but it was causing me problems. She called down to the front desk and relayed our issue with the room smell. She was told that our room, in the Magnolia building, was an allergy free room! What?? Anyway, they offered to let us try a couple other rooms to see if they were better. We had to wait in the hallway for 25 minutes for a bellhop to come and get our bags and take us to the other rooms. We couldn't wait in the room due to the oppressive smell. The second room on the same floor and the 3rd in the Delta area both had the same smell that appeared to be an attempt to cover some other smell. We decided to go back to reception and cancel our reservation for the night. The front desk gave me a ticket to get my car out of the self park lot without charge and I began the hike back out to the car. When I presented the ticket at the exit gate to the lot I was told that the ticket was only for good for 1 hour from the time I parked in the lot. So I forked over $20 to get free and go to pick up my wife and our luggage. By this time, it had been 3 hours since we entered the property and were without a room an no remaining patience. The wait to get back into the valet area was another 20 minute just to pick up our luggage. I completely understand the high volume of visitor traffic but I do not understand how the hotel has not found a way to enable their guests to check in without excessive delays and frustration. I guess the hotel has become too big to provide quality customer service to its guests and is resting on its favorable reviews from the past. Very disappointing experience. Too many other excellent hotel options available to subject yourself to this experience.

First impression walking in was great, bathrooms are clean and lemony scented, atmosphere was laid back nothing to it you just do your own thing! Service was h o r r I b l e ! I had a two questions about the menu which had to be asked to another server than the cook in the back. Being a vegetarian and not having the veggie patties was pretty disappointing! After paying I was told they weren't able to accommodate and I would need a refund and repay the refund was given and than when I tried to pay the server said it went through I tried to argue that didn't happen. At my seat I was then approached and asked not to sit there and that the order wasn't paid for (no surprise I tried to tell them that the first time) overall a very simple question and order (gluten free bun for a celiac and no bacon) was over complicated unnecessarily. I would understand if there was a line up but we were the only new customers there! Once we receive our order it looked great but nothing past that sadly! The burger was okay (if you've tried burger priest patties this would not be up to par). They need to try the gluten free bun there's a lot of better choices and as for the mac n cheese it was MEH I could've made it better at home disappointedly I was hoping for a savoury, cheesy good time! High expectations and low delivery but as for the milkshakes I will give them a second chance as it could be the one thing worth it to go!

Yum yum yum! So I'll admit, the HD score posted on Ugly Crab's page made me hesitate. It's sooooo low! Is it a mistake? Will I get food poisoning? We were so hungry and couldn't shake the craving for seafood boil style food, so we took the risk. Totally worth it! And we did not get sick :) Ugly Crab is pretty much what you would expect of this type of restaurant except that they serve warm toasted croissants before your meal. That was a nice surprise. We ordered Raw Oysters and two of the combo meals with Cajun sauce. While I didn't try the oysters, I was told they were a little "off" compared to what is expected from a good quality oyster. Both of our combo meals were delicious! My combo consisted of shrimp, crab legs and sausage. The sausage was sliced super thin which I did not expect nor like. The potatoes and corn inside the bag were good and the sauce was superb. The pricing at Ugly Crab is good as well and made the visit worth the trip (and the risk!)

This review is for take-out only. I had been having cravings for Arby's when I realized that I haven't eaten there in over a decade. In my first year of college, I would eat their chicken fingers and curly fries every day. I don't know if this is location specific or not because that one was in Willingboro, NJ and was always on point. However, the Arby's on Aramingo ought to be brought on trial for war crimes for serving this putrid, disgusting food. The chicken fingers consisted of mostly batter and the fries tasted like vomit. I have a stomachache and will probably have to make myself throw up so I can eat something else.

I've had mixed results here. The first time, a few months after they opened, I ordered online from the Rock Hill location. My gluten free pizza was several inches smaller than advertised (smaller than my hand, and I am tall with above-average hand size) and missing several toppings. I called about this and was rudely told that the menu online wasn't accurate and the missing toppings aren't available anymore. They had no response to my question about the size. Offered to refund my $21 (before tip!) IF I brought the pizza back. I was so pissed off that I did return the pizza, because they were not keeping my money. Terrible customer service, and I have never returned to that location. Several years later (August 2019), I attended a family dinner at the T&C location, which was good. Food and service were closer to what I'd expect for the price. Since I had a good experience at that location, my SIL and I decided to go for lunch on a Saturday in January this year. There was a large party seated behind us. They were loud enough that it made normal conversation difficult for us but they were finishing food as we sat down so we figured they'd leave soon. This was incorrect. At least 30 minutes later, they were still there, still loud, and extremely drunk. One of the women tried to stand with a full drink in her hand but was so drunk she fell completely backward, throwing her drink all over me and several bar patrons. No restaurant employee came over. I finally got up and asked a server to do something about it. When I came back to my table, I was accosted by one of the drunkards at the table and yelled at for getting the manager. This entire table was completely over served. I worked in restaurants for a long time and would have never continued to serve drinks to these people. The woman who fell literally passed out at the table while the rest of them waited for their check, saying nasty things to us. We were moved to another table and our meal was comped, which I appreciated, but being harassed and flipped off by this other table for having the audacity to complain about someone dumping a drink on me ruined the entire meal. It was extremely poor judgement on the part of staff to continue to serve these people, when they were clearly wasted. I tipped the server well, as I could see she was super stressed out, but where was management? It will not be my first choice when choosing somewhere to dine out again.

UPDATED REVIEW: Angie the manager does not get it. When 3 in you party get FOOD POISONING and the customer call to let you know. Don't call back and tell them it's not possible. ASK THE QUESTION...is there anything I can for you. And although we use fresh chicken we know it's possible this happen. Not all of our employees had chicken fried rice and they didn't get sick!!!! The most disappointing point is she never offered to do anything!!!!

I ordered a take out order in person, and repeated several times that I was highly allergic to mushrooms. I asKed in everything I ordered if there were mushrooms and if so, no mushrooms. The woman spoke broken English, which is fine, but doesn't give an excuse to tell me there are no mushrooms in the rice or in any of the items I ordered. This was my first time and I asked a lot of questions and was VERY thorough. When I got there to pay, the woman that was o the phone helped me at the front desk. I asked again about the mushrooms and was reassured that there were no mushrooms. I got home, ecstatic to eat, and took one big bite of the rice. Suddenly, my throat got itchy. I mixed my rice around and sure as shit, a TON of buried mushrooms! I had an Intense allergic reaction and thank god I had something to helP it's my reaction because I've I could have DIED!!!!!! My girlfriend called and talked to them, and they played dumb. I kept the food for days to bring back but my allergic reaction kEpt me exhausted, drained and sick! I tried to call and explain and no one would talk to me or assist. I really should have cancelled the transaction but I was trying to work it out with them. I don't live in Carp and they are open in later hours and no one was there who could help. Every time I asked for a manager, "there wasn't one there". To date this has not been resolved. This was 3 months ago. Dont go there, and if you do, maKe sure they listen and you check your food, multiple tImes. They could have killed me and have not taken any responsibility!
horrible!!! customer service suck, lady was on her cell phone all time dealing with me as a paying customer... food was bad to the point i had food poison, i hope this place goes out of business

Simply put: the food here is good, nothing really special. there is no service per se : by which i mean there is no waitstaff though there are food order takers and food delivery people. We came here for my niece's 5th birthday celebration and yes we had a great time: a bunch of family, food wine, kids, the bd girl all a flutter and really happy and appreciative for all the attention, gifts and food that she actually will eat: pizza with black olives, chicken tenders with marinara dipping sauce and meat balls. We ordered quite a bit of food: Regular crust pizza with pepperoni, jalapenos, mushrooms Gluten-free pizza with black olives Cauliflower crust with pepperoni, jalapenos Chicken tenders Fried Mozzarella Sticks with Marinara Pasta Alfredo Side of meatballs with Italian gravy Pizzas The regular crust pizza was good. the crust was well baked, slightly crispy but did not have a particular flavor or point of view in order to make it special. Toppings were good: the Pepperoni was spicy and tasty. The Gluten free pizza was well baked, surprisingly (to me) tasty, toppings good. The bd girl dug it. I ordered the Cauliflower crust because i was curious. My only experience with a Cauliflower crust was a Trader Joe's one which turned out to be a debacle: flavorless, fell apart after baking. No. The cauliflower crust here was a little strange in that it had the consistency of graham crackers held together by butter and eggs which wasn't completely negative yet not completely successful. the toppings were good. The fried items: tenders, mozzarella sticks were ok, nothing special, well fried and not dried out which is a plus. The meatballs were obviously pre-frozen as the centers were cold when first served. i returned them for new that had been properly heated through. They were ok. my niece liked them, though. So the food here is fair to good and the order taker and delivery dude were pleasant. We all had a very fun time though. My niece was happy. I was happy. We were all happy. Now the very bad stuff . I went into Pizza Mizza about noon and made a reservation at 330pm with a woman named Janet, Jeanette (blondish, semi attitudinal). I asked for the back 2 tables. She said no problem "i will set it up for your party." I also asked for something special: i told her it would thrill my niece and her brother if they could actually make their own pizza. Could she set it up with dough, sauce, nothing fancy as these are young kids who will be jazzed. She said yes "i would set it up but it has to be outside." i said fine and thanked her. So we arrive at 330 and : No tables set up. 2 parties are sitting in the spot. Jeanette sees me and says nothing....at all. Not hello. Not i set up here instead of there. Nada, Niente, Nothing. There was no pizza making station for my niece set up and no explanation. I am glad i did not mention anything to my niece about my pizza making idea so no problem there. But: what the hell happened? That i was given no explanation is what frazzles me the most. I have spent a lot of time around food businesses: i know how things happen and how things can change even within one day. I would have understood. But i can't understand nor appreciate utter silence, utter disregard. I was really pissed but we proceeded with the celebration and as i state above: all went super well. We made our own party and the babies loved the attention and good times. Nothing was going to allow an inadequate, bad attitude manager ruin our fun. But shouldn't management work with their customers rather than against? I will never return here. Period. End of Story.

Easily the worst Italian food I've had in my entire life. I've had better pasta from dominos. There was absolutely nothing good on my plate so it's hard to even know where to start. Let's starts from the appetizer, I got the bruschetta and it was a bunch of croutons with a crapload of oil with some tomatoes in it. Main dish penne a la vodka with chicken, chicken had absolutely no flavor that it tasted like it was boiled, obviously not cooked in the sauce. Penne noodles were over cooked, the vodka sauce was among the worst I have ever tasted much like vomit in your mouth. The NY style cheesecake tasted like soggy lemons and had a terrible crust, much like a crappy Walmart cheesecake. Oh I forgot about the cream of mushroom soup, Campbell's out of a can would be a 100% improvement for them. Needless to say, anyone who gave this place 5 stars has clearly never had proper Italian food. I literally threw the entire meal in the garbage, I wouldn't even give it to my dog it was so bad. On the plus side I'll give them some credit for good bread, too bad they burnt it though.... update 3/17/18 see photo, nothing like getting threatened by one of the staff for leaving a bad review. Great job really proving you're a stand up restaurant.

The gluten free cupcakes are the best I have had in Reno. I had the gluten free chocolate cupcake with sprinkles. The only thing that I would recommend for people you have gluten sensitivities or celiacs like me is putting the gluten free bake goods into a separate container rather than combining them with gluten.

We went to Nashville for a weekend and we had to stop at Jason Aldean's because we heard so much about it. Atmosphere: Big Place. It was cool to see that downstairs there was room for a band and upstairs at the Rooftop Bar, another and different space for another band. The band that was playing the night I went was playing all different types of music so that was nice. We went near the stage on the rooftop and it smelt like vomit, which was disgusting. We decided to just listen to music far away. The drinks were good and it was beautifully decorated. Overall: I give this place 4 stars. I would give it 5 stars but I was a little put off with some of the crowd being overly drunk and the vomit smell but I loved the drinks and music and the venue is nice.

We were just passing through and looking for a decent Chinese buffet to eat at and instead we found this dump!!! Food was absolutely disgusting!!! Appeared to be there at least all day and possibly days old. Had a hard ti.e finding anything that remotely looked appetizing at all. Wish I could give it less than 1 star. Would not be surprised if I were to get food poisoning later!!!

The food is good, definitely the best exclusively gluten free cafe in the area. However, the staff that works the front register is super rude- if I'm spending $6 on a cupcake, you could at least be polite. You'd think at a specialty cafe like this they would have better people working customer service.

I have clicked one star cause that's the lowest I'm allowed to give. I just ordered from here and when the food got here is was lukewarm at best. I can overlook this cause I don't like super hot stuff you have to wait to eat but still. My real problem came from the fact that I found an Ant in my pizza. Not near it, not on the box, not from my apartment (as I don't have an ant problem) but IN the pizza. I ordered the personal cheese pizza and upon pulling the third slice apart from the last slice I see a black spot... look closer and yup, that's a pair on antennas and legs and now I want to vomit. Call the place and tell the person who answered the phone I needed to speak with someone, he asks if I would CALL BACK?!? What! No! I said I wanted to speak with someone right now. After a few minutes, someone picks back up the phone and I tell him what happened... the man then asks me to repeat myself, or rather "what is the problem". He wasn't surprised or in shock, he didn't hear me cause he was talking to someone else the whole time I was speaking. He asks if he can send me a new pizza, I refused and asked for a refund and I don't want to eat anything from here. Also, he never actually apologized. Never will I order from here again, and I have already told 8 of my friends to not order from here either.
Burgers were awesome, as were the waffle fries. Gluten-free options available with regular GF buns and Sweet Potato buns. Good place to watch the game, but LEAVE the kids at home!

Went here day before Thanksgiving bought a tiramisu cake $26 just had it for dessert the cake tasted like vomit sour and I brought this to someone's house for dessert six people and no one could eat it terrible terrible terrible day after Thanksgiving just went into complain about my order from the terrible terrible rotten tasting tiramisu cake that I bought on Wednesday and the manager says there is absolutely nothing that they can do unless I bring in the cake it was rotten it tasted rotten it was sour we threw the cake away now I'm supposed to go through the garbage and find it the cake tasted like garbage terrible place will never shop here again and is spent thousands of dollars in this place that's their customer service

I was really excited to see this come into Beaumont but have been disappointed for quite some time... I tried the delivery 6 times, each time I received wrong food or missing items, everything from missing sides or salads with no dressing. When we have called the customer service seems decent enough but the issues are never corrected. The customer service is terrible if you are looking to go in to dine. Their menu is apparently iron clad. No room to switch a side out on many of their items or use gluten free pasta instead of regular even if you're willing to pay extra. Things that other BP restaurants will do no problem. Your request is met with attitude. Today was my last attempt at liking this place, looking forward to some competition moving in...

This place was mediocre and they gave my son food poisoning. I would not recommend this mucho burrito. No love at all.Don't waste your money here. The one in capilano on the other hand is really good.

I want to love this place because it's local and they go beyond the normal pizza menu by offering alternatives (gluten free and vegan). But the three times I've visited have made me realize why it's never busy inside. Better than the chain pizza joints, certainly, but not nearly the standard that I expect for "gourmet" pizza. I ordered the Gambini this time, which had only a few onions and tomatoes, completely bland sausage, and a lot of ricotta. It was basically a cream pizza - yea, no one wants that. I'll keep trying every year or so, but please improve!

Usually This place is perfect, quick, and never super messy. I recently went and the food made me and my family sick with food poisoning. Please be better about you back of house staff and proper use of cleaning and safety when it comes towards the food.

This place is for you if you have no tastebuds and want to spend money on a plate full of boring. We ordered the veggie paleo pizza and the nook burger with the bun. The pizza crust was thin and crispy at first but got soft pretty immediately after it arrived. It was topped with raw cauliflower, zucchini, red onions, peppers and mushrooms. I'm serious, they were literally crunchy. Nothing was seasoned either. The burger was overcooked and small, topped with a few red onion slivers, lettuce and a tiny undetectable smear of aioli. It was so devastatingly bland that I begged our server (who was very kind) for the "house made ketchup" that I thought was supposed to already be on the burger. He promptly brought out a side of tomato paste. Bummer. Really wanted to like this place because I have Celiac disease and they have a wide selection of gluten free items. They are giving healthy food a bad name. I 100% could have whipped up something entirely more delicious and just as healthy at home.

I rarely give out one star. I don't like doing it. But I almost felt I had to save people from this horrific experience. I gave Nudy's two separate tries before realizing the food here is on the verge of inedible. The first time, I tried breakfast. I got eggs Benedict, it was terrible. Like another reviewer said, they give fried eggs instead of poached and the hollandaise tasted like cardboard and was so runny and thin, it looked like snot. The only edible thing was the pancake my son ordered. I think that's why there are so many photos of pancakes in the reviews. Pancakes with powdered sugar is the only thing Nudys can really make. The second time I went, I couldn't even eat the food. My mom ordered a blackened tuna salad and I ordered the buffalo chicken wrap. The tuna was not blackened, it was naked, unseasoned and tasted so fishy I thought I was going to get food poisoning from trying it. I spit it out. My mom just ate the lettuce. The buffalo chicken wrap tasted like SUGAR. It was so sweet and not at all spicy. I asked for a side of buffalo sauce to try to help the disgusting flavor and they brought me a cup of mayonnaise with maybe a drop of hot sauce in it for color. Eww. I never leave a full plate of food at a restaurant, I simply could not eat it. It was horrific. The waitress asked me if I wanted a box. I said no thank you. She didn't even ask if it was ok, or if she could bring me something else. She just handed us the check. Again, I hate complaining. I paid full price for food I thought might make me sick and didn't even say anything. I just figured I'd cut my losses and never come again. And hopefully this helps save another yelper 40 bucks or so because their food is honestly some of the worst food I've probably ever had in my entire life. I wanted to like you guys, but wow, until you step up your food game, I will not be returning.

First: I found a tiny bug on top of my Phoenix rolls (picture uploaded 5 months ago) Second try: everything was fine. They said 3rd time is the charm. Yes, I got FOOD POISONING! My 1st in my entire life and I'm not the type to complain about restaurants, but this is crazy. I felt nauseous, headache, muscle weakness, had diarrhea, vomit, stomach cramps that woke me up MANY times at night. I wouldn't waste my time & energy to call and complain to them. From what I read from other reviewers, they don't handle customer service properly. Even the driver doesn't have proper manner, he hit someone else's car next to him when he tried to get out of the car to give my food. This review is for you guys who read this. Be careful when ordering their sushi with shrimp tempura. Mine wasn't cooked all the way, maybe not even stored properly. Thanks a lot, Hibachi2Go. You just lost another customer.
Just your typical pizza place. Salad bar is only ok but my only choice as they don't even do a gluten free crust. Cauliflower would be so easy.

beware do not eat here!! i ate here with my girlfriend and we both got the worst food poisoning ever!!! we had to go to student health and thought we were going to die it was so bad! people on yik yak also asked if anyone else got food poisoning and they had to be hospitalized. i will be reporting romaines to the health inspector!! do not eat here!!!

My friend and I have eaten at BJ's in the past and loved the food. This time we went will be the last time we give this chain our money. We decided to order some appetizers- the brussels sprouts, fries, and the avocado egg rolls. I placed a to-go order of wings for my Dad, and our waitress left. Our food came out within ten minutes, which was a red flag. How can meat be properly prepared in ten minutes? We started eating the brussels sprouts, which had an interesting texture from crusted sauce on top, but I shrugged it off. The fries were okay, but how hard is it to mess up fries? Last we have the egg rolls. I took one bite and instantly knew something was wrong. I pulled them apart only to discover that they were raw! We immediately stopped eating and asked for the split check. The waitress then proceeded to ask my friend if it was okay to charge her twice for the food. We sped home and have been suffering from food poisoning a whole day after consuming barely any of the food. They clearly microwave their food to death. Sad!
I loved this place until last night. After eating went home to a night of toilet hugging and minor food poisoning...
My boyfriend got food poisoning from eating here last night. NEVER AGAIN! How about practicing some basic cleasniness to the people who entrust you to prepare their food.

BE AWARE if you have allergies! I ordered a salad and told them I had a serious shellfish allergy and they didn't alert me that they use clam sauce in their dressing. If you're this much of an idiot, don't work at a restaurant where you're preparing food for tons of people. I even complained to the manager and he was like "Oops sorry! Come back again." Disgusting. I even emailed the owner and called with zero response. I fear the meals they prepare here with people who are highly allergic to certain foods.

It can be challenging, like with all allergies, to eat out with a gluten intolerance. You are putting your trust in strangers to prepare your meal according to your needs. Fortunately, my personal issue isn't a life or death one, more like a moderate to severe discomfort, depending on food ingestion. All the same, when I can find a place that has a gluten free menu, I'm assuming that these foods are indeed, gluten free! This place is wildly popular and food smelled heavenly while we waited. On the plus side, they did have a GF menu. I ordered brisket off of it with French fries. Did not question anything bc both items were on GF menu. I got sick immediately after my meal, with painful cramps. I spoke with the manager and waiter telling him I was sick. They said French fries were not cooked in designated fryer, only sweet potatoes fries were. When I pointed out and showed them bc he didn't believe me (while holding my stomach) that regular fries were on GF menu, manager's response was "oh, sorry." They offered to comp meal but not so sure he took me seriously when I said I didn't care about that, that most importantly they need to edit menu. Brisket was fine but too salty. Entire experience tainted by incompetent, irresponsible advertising!
A large fly was cooked into my wings and covered in sauce. Threw away the rest and threw up what I ate. Won't be coming back.

It's a shame that I have to write this review. It's a new place and I expected more, but was very disappointed. I arrived and the place was empty...just my party of 4 at the bar and another party of 3 nearby. For a brand new place, you'd think the set up would be better and cleaner, but the chairs feel like they're about to fall apart already. I had no idea they were only open a couple weeks when we ate here because the furniture did not look or feel brand new. So either the furniture is cheap and got worn out quickly, or they bought used furniture. The women's bathroom already is falling apart. The walls near the sink look like somebody took a hammer to it and just left it. The food we got was not that great. It was pretty bland. And one of the dishes, a seafood burrito, arrived still frozen! (Please tell me how you mess up food when there is nobody in the restaurant ordering food but us 4...) Then, when it was remade, it was still horrible. As soon as the burrito was cut in half and the steam came out, it smelled like rotten fish. My dad still tried to finish it and ended up with food poisoning. There are plenty of margarita flavors from which to choose, but I'd much rather make mine at home to avoid the food poisoning. Side note....the bartender we had (we were eating at the bar) was very friendly and helpful. His manager, on the other hand, decided she was just going to sit in a booth and play on her phone, even after another customer (who was right next to her) asked for a manager. She rolled her eyes and whispered something to the bartender, who then told the upset customer. Not a good way to manage a restaurant. My 2019 prediction is that this place will be out of business by the start of 2019.

Ever since they changed owners the quality of the food is not the same. I stopped by today to get lentil soup and hummus. Simple right? Well not so much, the hummus was bitter and the soup tasted really bad. I took one spoon full and almost threw up. Maybe it went bad and they didn't notice. Anyways this place is crap now.

I have several, not 1 complaint about this place. First, I called ahead and asked if they can accommodate a gluten allergy and was told that the majority of things on the menu can me made gluten free. We came for brunch and my server advised me that in reality, only the omelet and hummus are gluten free, as they do not have a dedicated gluten free fryer so everything else is cross-contaminated. Also they do not have gluten free pita. I ordered the omelet, (which came out raw and oozing in the middle) and the lamb hummus, after which I later had a reaction so I believe the lamb in the hummus was also fried in the contaminated fryer even though I advised the server of my allergies. The manager did compensate us for the raw omelet...

Came here on a Saturday night with 4 tables seated . Ordered two small drinks and an appetizer order of spring rolls with only pork since I am allergic to shrimp . Stood there to wait 30 minutes while they got the spring roll order wrong twice. I come from a house where we can roll out 30+ spring rolls in 30 minutes. Especially with the ingredients already cut up and prepped. Asked the server if it was going to be any sooner since I have plans for the evening and this was supposed to be a quick stop and the response was "I'm sure it'll be out soon" ‍ if you really love the slushy's smoothies tea and Vietnamese food , I suggest you order in advance. But I can recommend a dozen other restaurants and cafés in the area with equal to better food and service.

My extended family and I went to Carrabba's last night. I really wanted to go to another restaurant that rhymes with polive marden. We started with the calamari that we all shared. (don't ask me why, sharing an appetizer between seven people, srsly?) My two pieces were good. Better than the other place I wanted to go but the marinara sauce wasn't as sweet- which is fine by me, it actually was nice like that. My family then took their time to order. I was ready halfway through the calamari but everyone kept, just, talking. Why couldn't we just order? What, so now, all of a sudden, everyone is allergic to talking after ordering? Should I carry an EpiPen? But anyway we ordered finally. I ordered the spaghetti and meatballs. Y'all, it was really good. I was ready to not like it because I like the S&MBs from the other place a lot but this was fanbloodytastic. I wasn't really engaging much in the conversation because I was enjoying my food and, I think, they were talking politics. Much liked, ty, would go again!

What is this? People really need to step up the games on these reviews. Tell the truth. It was a big disappointment from the start. My family and I went in and the server gave off this bad vibe. I told him nicely to change his gloves because I'm vegan and didn't want to contaminate my food, server gave me a bit of an attitude. Anyways, I didn't care about that. The pizza barely had vegan cheese, the taste was off, and the toppings tasted like they had been out for a while. It was super tasteless and nothing fixed it. I put garlic powder and other spices, pizza still tasted like cardboard. Although the manager seemed nice, the place lack in taste. Not sure how they could go wrong with pizza. Iced tea was alright too. Also, lacked in hygiene...Huge disappointment.

Went here for dinner for the first time because the menu has gluten free items. I explained to my server That my food had to be GF with no cross contamination. I ordered the Fabio with grilled chicken and it was delicious and it was gluten free. The service was great and so was the atmosphere. The rest of the people with me were not gluten free and their food looked delicious and I didn't hear any complaints.

If you enjoy food poisoning from a weekend "special", this the place to go. Husband and I popped in on our Anniversary dinner, a Friday evening. We both ordered the same seafood dish. Within 4 hours of leaving were in the same pain, excruciating stomach pain. Needless to say, our Anniversary dinner & weekend were both ruined.

Had an absolutely terrible experience at More Than Just Ice Cream. I have a very serious peanut allergy, and I ordered the gluten-free banana chocolate chip cookie. One bite in, and it was very obvious that I was going into anaphylactic shock. I had to use my epi pen in the middle of the establishment, meanwhile, the staff completely ignored what was going on. When I approached the woman behind the counter about labeling allergens, she looked at the label, said okay, and then continued with her normal activities. Meanwhile, I went to the emergency room. When I called the subsequent day to see if the issue had been addressed, I again was spoken to with the same attitude, where it seemed as though they didn't believe me. Terrible staff who clearly don't care about whether their customers have serious life-threatening allergies.

Went here for dinner while in Webster groves but didn't end getting anything but an appetizer and leaving. 1. Drinks are terrible, thursdays are 'margarita night' I'm pretty sure my margarita was Minute Maid Lemonade mixed with tequila, whatever it was tasted like sugar and nothing like a margarita. My fiancees Mojito was a sugarbomb, basically tasted like a glass full of simple syrip wiht mint leaves. 2. Menu has essentially nothing on it for someone who is lactose intolerant and doesn't eat meat, everything that wasn't meat was full of cheese or cream and when you pull those out of dishes that center around it they typically taste terrible. We ordered some Hummus because we felt bad and it was good although the tapenade that came with it was not. Its sad that places feel like they can't make good food without adding lots of fat to a recipe (heavy cream&cheese). I certainly wouldn't come here for drinks, I'm sure some of food is probably good if not run of the mill and uninspired.

My mom DRAGSSS me here every few months. I used to really enjoy Piccadilly until I grew up and realized it is just OK. The food is typically still warm and there are enough options to choose from. I usually stick with "safe" foods now, such as baked chicken, carrot soufflé, and broccoli. While we are on the subject, their carrot soufflé is the best in my opinion. I've tried a variety of carrot and sweet potato soufflés at other restaurants, but I must hand the crown to Piccadilly for that option. Other than that, their food tastes like basic school cafeteria food--I mean, it is a cafeteria though. It seems like they cater to our beloved elders more than anything, which is fine. Their food is never highly seasoned and, sometimes, not seasoned enough. I strongly dislike their cheese sauces, both for the broccoli and broccoli-cheddar rice. I used to love their broccoli-cheddar rice until it made me so sick to my stomach that I vowed to never return (but, my mom of course...). I narrowed it down to the cheese and I'm not lactose intolerance. The cheese sauce for the broccoli seems watered down. But that's enough about cheese. So maybe I'm biased because I prefer and appreciate nicely seasoned food, and I feel that only a few choices really hit that mark.

If you have a food allergy, DO NOT EAT AT INDY TACO! This used to be a 5 star rating. My family used to love Indy Taco, but after my last few visits, I'm not inclined to come back. Tonight's dinner was bad and bizarre. I have a gluten allergy. I was quite clear in telling my waiter of this allergy. He even went as far as to have a kitchen staff member come talk to me about it. This was a great start! Then it took a turn. The chori fries were amazing, but they now contain gluten. I was disappointed, but ordered a side of refried beans instead. The kitchen staffer then thought it appropriate to tell me how beans will make you fart and poop. (I'm guessing this staffer is 7?) I no longer wanted these beans as the mental image he gave me was pretty unsavory before one eats a meal. Then, my tacos all came back on wheat shells, despite me asking for the corn shells that I'm not allergic to. This was so maddening as I had now discussed my allergy with two Indy taco employees. Now my wife is eating while I wait for my food to be remade. The last time they ignored my allergy and gave me wheat shells, after I reminded them I was allergic to that, they just simply put the taco filling from the wheat tacos and placed them on corn shells and gave them back 30 seconds later. This is obviously unacceptable! This story is over right? Wrong! As we are eating, a young woman, who apparently worked there but was on a day off, came in with her yapping dog! I couldn't believe it. Not a service dog. Just a little barking purse size dog. In a restaurant. Needless to say, I'm not wanting to come back to Indy Taco. If you are lucky enough to not have a food allergy, eat there. Support local business. If you do have an allergy that's worse than mine, they may kill you!

After hearing recommendations for this place from seemingly everyone I know, we excitedly brought our out of town family to try it with us for dinner. SO disappointing. The menu looks amazing, but the food itself is subpar. The burgers were dry, thin, and not very warm. What looked like flavorful combinations in writing turned out to be bland and boring on the plate. Our order got messed up a couple times, despite being fairly simple and straight-forward, and it was loud and chaotic inside. The only thing positive I can say is that I appreciate very much the dairy-free milkshakes and gluten free buns, as I have a child who cannot have dairy/gluten. I was so hoping we'd found a spot where the whole family can truly be included on all the fun--even dessert--but no. Such a bummer. There are much better burgers in town.

I've enjoyed many great meals at The Love but was disappointed tonight that my selections were limited due to my shellfish allergy and a change in menu. Adding fried oysters to the menu knocked off my ability to have the ribs and the fried chicken, my first & second choice. Most higher end restaurants have the capability & willingness to be able to offer their non-shellfish options without cross-contamination, I was disappointed that The Love didnt. It's still a great restaurant, just not for me anymore, unfortunately.

I'm a physician staying at a hotel to protect my family while I take care of COVID patients. I called and placed an order and asked a lot of questions after telling him I am allergic to wheat. I went to pick it up and asked again to confirm it was wheat free. She said if it's on the receipt it is. I paid then looked at the receipt. It didn't say anything so I waiting and asked again letting them know it would make me really sick if there's wheat in it. She said the pasta in gluten free but not the sauce....really? Then I asked to speech to the manager. He was super condescending and said he was the one who took the order and I didn't need to talk to him like that! Really? You don't know what your doing and could have made me really sick! I told him I want my money back. He returned with only some of my money. Then he rolled his eyes and went back in and the real manager came out. Basically told Me off. These people are terrible human beings. NEVER EAT HERE! These people don't care about me, don't care about you, don't care about the food, the community or those working in the front line. They should go out of business!

Pros: Beautiful ambiance, impeccable service, interesting menu, charming views. Cons: Somewhat overpriced (even for a Chester County restaurant/B&B), contracted a mild case of food poisoning from dinner. Kind of ruined anniversary celebration.

I loved Bab Cafe and haven't had it in while, probably around a year. I was excited for today's lunch but I am extremely disappointed when I opened the box. The box hardly had any food in it. Before they would provide more than enough and now hardly enough yet the prices are still the same. Also, I am allergic to pork but they automatically include some egg roll type of food that has pork in it without letting anyone know. They automatically assume everyone can eat pork. That is extremely dissatisfying.

Ate here yesterday morning. A few things: the NICEST STAFF. (Or maybe New York has me forgetting the concept of common courtesy.) I used the bathroom there and never will I take for granted the New York food rating system (look- not everyone can buy off inspectors). I ordered a crawfish egg dish (the name escapes me). The dish tasted flat but the biscuit improved things tremendously. I got food poisoning.

I was definitely glutened by them, not doubt in my mind. It was either that or they're using chicken that's been laying around since before the panademic. I got horrible stomach pains and cramps and severe runs. I will never be eating from there again.

The misery I'm allergic to tomato I specifically asked if the breakfast pizza had I was told no I order all excited and get home red sauce everywhere... the best thing I guess was the plain bagel the person who worked was dingy looking it was a mess prices are great but you get what you pay for

First, the positive: It has a very pretty decor and a friendly hostess (who seems to be the manager also). The negative: SLOW, and wait staff that looks to dodge customers rather than break the news that the kitchen is understaffed and backed up. We ordered a simple dinner, though mine did have a slight special request with it. Things came out seemingly only when we inquired about them. We were not the only table with the issue too. Most tables had one person with food and the other person waiting. It was a mistake for most to wait for the others' food to come. After about 20-30 minutes our salads finally arrived. With the table cleared from that for another 10 minutes, our appetizer arrived. Finally the entrees came out after about 45 minutes after ordered and mine was not correct. I have a cheese allergy that I told them about and the kitchen messed up and it came out with cheese. It wouldn't have been so bad if it hadn't taken so long. I sent it back and they just scraped the cheese off at first. They at least owned up to it. After being exasperated and my waitress simply pointing out that it wasn't her fault, another waitress came over and was also just dumbfounded that there was a mistake. She reiterated that everyone has been waiting for their food. That moment was the most attention we'd gotten all night. The manager/hostess came over after a few minutes more and assured me that my food would be recooked promptly and they apologized. My wife ate her food as I watched. When the bill came there was an additional awkward apology and no offering to do anything, like comp my meal. I guess that is because they knew...my first time there...my last time there.
About two weeks ago I went to sushi Rose because my children wanted to take me there for my birthday well all six of us got food poisoning I'll never go back

Without question- this is one of the worst meals I've ever had out. Our service was horrendous. We had a person with a food allergy and they were extremely unaccomdating. I would never eat here again. When we mentioned the service to the manager, he was argumentative. I'd avoid this place like the plague. The burger was good. Most of the rest of the food was unappetizing. Our food came out in shifts so that one person finished her entree as another person's was coming out. We waited 24 minutes for drinks.

I had never had Moes before and can say that if I were a district manager here, or owner, I would have fired all but one person who was working today. Unfortunately I didnt see the two star reviews on here before entering and paying for a predominantly negative experience, because even two stars ...is overrated. This store was filthy, and I mean absolutely filthy. I saw cross contamination, and had to ask for someone to wash the tables so we could sit. (There were a few employees doing absolutely nothing so there was no excuse for the filth.) I watched an employee throw food on the floor when I told her I wanted fresh jalapeño and she had put jarred ones on. I also watched two employees argue. I watched another employee wear a mask but did not wash his hands after handling money or credit card transactions - but then he would reach in for tortilla chips with no gloves on and serve them to customers. (All of this occurred during non peak hours and with only four tables of people dining. I can only imagine how bad it would be had they been busy.) I saw an employee reach in her pocket to use her phone, with food prep gloves on, while in the middle of making food for one of our children, and did not change her gloves after, she just reached right back into the food prep station and finished the order. (Ya'll, lets be honest here... have you ever taken your phone to the bathroom? Apparently zero germophobes work at this store. ‍) I saw another gentleman with his phone out on the food line when the entire store was filfthy. I doubt these folks sanitize their phones if wiping a table is challenging for them. Someone should be teaching these employees that if you have time to lean, you have time to clean. The food was actually good aside from the oversalted stale chips, but the apparent health violations and poorly trained staff prevented me from finishing it. I get grossed out easily anyway, but this was over the top. I wont be returning. You dont get a second chance to make a first impression, and my first impression of Moe's is... "ya'll are nasty". Not your food, but your poor hygiene, poor cleaning skills, your negative energy, and for bringing the same phone you probably take to the crapper... onto a food prep line.

It's vegan fast food, but a little fresher, and I'm totally here for it! It's definitely a must-hit (any of their locations) while you're in Philly if you have a plant based eater in your party. I came here for one reason although I'm sure I'll come back for many more based on their menu. The vegan Philly "cheese steak"! While the rest of my party had been eating the real, original version all weekend, I was on the hunt for one I could safely eat without cross contamination. Finding this place made me ecstatic. The whole menu is vegan from drinks to entrees to desserts. It's less of a sit down place and more of a grab and go, so it's great for grabbing lunch while walking around the city. The Vegan Philly Steak itself was great, my boyfriend the meat eater even went back for a second bite of mine. I'm glad this place exists, so we can all get our tourism eating in!

I know I can get a bit star crazy with my reviews, but during the pre opening practice run they flat out impressed me. When we arrived to our reservation we were greatest by the manager outside and he proceeded to share some information and explained how our free meal would work. We were escorted to our seats by one of at least 30 staffers that were all there for training purposes, it's not very often the staff outnumbers the amount of guests! But this was understandable as they were all learning the routine and presentation process. Don't get me wrong, this was not a situation where they tossed them in with the sharks and said learn to swim. I had watched the previous days leading up to this where they were all huddled up inside for some 1 on 1 training. They pulled it all off beautifully. The food was even better than I remembered RedRobins being and I know I used to like them before I found out about my gluten intolerance. I still try and avoid places where I am tempted, burger joints are my weakness. I love me a good burger! I was absolutely ecstatic to find out that not only could I get the burger I wanted, but they have their own special gluten free buns. When it came I couldn't hardly wait, I don't get to eat many burgers with buns anymore, I think bread is one of the things I miss most. The bun was not like any other gluten free I had ever had before, this one was actually soft, and had flavour, talk about a reason to return. We asked to talk to the manager to inquire on the gluten free process we were told about. When you order something off the GF menu it is handled by a manager on duty to assure the chances of contamination are kept to a bare minimum. That on its own was impressive. You won't find that at many other restaurants.
