All I can say is if you are like me and want a good gluten free burger at a very reasonable price, I would highly recommend you give Red Robins a try, they won't let you down.

Stopped in with some family and friends last evening all the restaurants had over 130 minute wait so we decided to go to RISE cafe being it was the shortest. Waited about 20 minutes and was seated. Service was BLAH. We had two female waitress who completely ignored our table as far as refills, clearing plates and cups that cluttered. We felt like we were a bother while asking for things. Also noticed 2 other tables calling a manager over. So we were skeptical we get our food my sweet potatoes frys were cold, my husband threw up after eating the chicken finger dinner. Spicy mayo is delish along with the onion rings. We probably will never go back here after the service and food. It was OK better places to go to inside here! We went to The New Sugar Factory got in immediately had some drinks and dessert! Definitely wished we would of just ate there!

I would never shop here, the reputation they had was never good. You could smell sour meat as you walk in the market. People who do shop there obviously don't value their stomachs. Maybe they like having food poisoning. It's a Cousins on Baltimore Ave, I'll never shop there for food. I'll buy napkins, and paper towels!!!

The wife order over the phone and told me to pick it up since I was on the road. Got there and she the owner ignored me while standing there right in front of her said "picking up for Melanie" to find out the dumb old B*tch never took her name down and asked me what she ordered, I said idk then she told me to call her, I said f**k it and walked out. There was people food everywhere and unorganized without no names. I wonder how cold and nasty tasting it must be when the customer do come pick up the food. This place don't give a sh*t about you, your service, and the quality of the food that is being serve to you. The only thing they care about is how quick they can take your money. Help businesses like this one during the pandemic lmfao!!! I hope covid-19 closed the door on this place for good. Fyi never trust a small kitchen where your food is being made, I bet there is alot of cross contamination on the food people are eating there. Went home and told the wife to NEVER order from there again! Instead she ordered from la mint, further from the house but well worth it because she loves the ox tail pho.

This is a unique little restaurant that was once a laundry mat. I was really excited to try this place after looking at the menu. The menu had a variety of healthy vegetarian and gluten free options that all sounded really good. The food we got, however, really wasn't that good. Plus, my friend and I both got plates that did not match the menu's description. My friend ordered a salad but it ended up being a plate of tortilla chips with a small amount of greens on top. I think they may have given me a different bowl than I ordered. Since we weren't pleased with our lunch we voiced our concerns to an employee. He was really nice about the whole situation and apologized for the mishap. They ended up not charging us for our meals which was really nice of them considering the situation. I gave them three stars opposed to one star since they acknowledged they made a mistake and were kind enough to comp our lunch. I am considering going back to this place to give it another try - perhaps we caught them on an off day.

Filthy filthy filthy restaurant. Jammed my husband and two babies (in high chairs) at a table already full. We switched to a regular table only to be sat iin the filthy bar at a super tiny table. My infant even threw up after eating the food. Never again.

I've only had food poisoning 1 time in my life and it was from here (only took 1 visit). DONT EVER GO HERE. I rather stay hungry than go here ever again because it's not worth the risk. Even if the food doesn't give you food poisoning, it still tastes bad.

They gave me food poisoning! I never write reviews but I had to for this. After going there with my daughter we both had horrible food poisoning! DONT EAT HERE! Well unless u want to loose weight and feel horrible

Ok so as a celiac, Red Robin goes through appropriate measures to keep food safe and free of gluten and gluten-mingling contamination. For THIS I would give them 5 stars alone. However the issue I have is with their poor quality beef. I've eaten here several times and at least 2 of the times, I end up with hard nasty pieces in my mouth while eating the burger. Either bone, Or gristle or something. Unappetizing to say the least. When my husband and I had lunch there a few weeks ago, I let the server know and she was Very apologetic and had them remake the burger for me. Somehow I got another hard bit in one of the first bites I took again! I am wondering if the meat they used for their "Tavern burger" is different than their regular. The tavern burger is a little cleaner so maybe that's why? Maybe they're buying low quality beef for those patties to save cost and be able to offer it cheaper? Again it's a very nice option to be able To eat here as a celiac and to know that I'm not investing gluten but dang I wish their burgers didn't have hard bits in them

Man, I don't get it with them. Must have untrained staff at all their locations because they always mislabel foods in their cafeteria. Bought a premade salad, checked the ingredients for animal meat didn't include any, but when I went to eat it, there was a bunch of chicken in it. How do you forget to put that on the label? What about peanuts or gluten for people who actually severely allergic? It's happened with other menu items here. They did refund my money and gave me a big burrito, so they make up for it, but really I'd rather have them tighten up their labeling. Nice staff, good atmosphere, lots of healthy and overpriced vegan food, just double check the label.

My fortune cookie fortune foretold that I'd be released from past burdens. What it didn't tell me is that I was soon to suffer a horrendous case of food poisoning. I know it was Panda that poisoned me because the other food I had that day was stuff I eat all the time at home and well within expiration date. I generally avoid fast food but made an exception for Panda. That won't happen again. I was awake in a lot of pain the entire night.

We went for dinner Friday night around 5:30. Was ignored at first by hostesses. Nachos has all the jalapeño seeds on them still. I got the Gorgonzola salad which was ok. My husband got the crab cake sandwich, but later had food poisoning. The only reason why I'm giving it 2 stars it because of their good beer selection. Never again!

I hate leaving bad reviews but this place really let me down. The only reason I gave it 2 stars is that the service was decent. I was visiting St Louis for the weekend and since my daughter is gluten free I was on the hunt for a good place for us to eat dinner. I did see the recent reviews weren't great but decided to give it a chance anyways. It was a Saturday night and they had built up quite the wait and it was nice to be able to put my name on the waitlist through Yelp! It was about a 45 minute wait. It was super hot inside the restaraunt, and it was LOUD. The water they served wasn't cold. It came in those glass milk bottles and just sat on the table. We ordered the loaded fries which was a good choice. My daughter was looking forward to a burger with a gluten free bun so we got her that. Given that the burgers were around $11 we thought it would be large enough to split. We were mistaken. It was one of the smallest burgers I've ever seen short of a slider. My daughters burger came and the bun was TERRIBLE. It was almost a cornbread consistency so it kept falling apart, I tried it and it had 0 flavor. The pickles they served with the burgers had an odd plastic taste to them. I thought maybe their saving grace would be the ice cream. We all got a different dessert. I ordered a chocolate malt. When I recieved it, it still had chunks of malt mix in it every time I took a sip. I was really let down by this place and I won't be back.

Well- the cheese sauce (that comes with "crab fries") is scrumptious. HOWEVER- those " crab fries" have no crab - they are seasoned crinkle fries- not a shred of crab on them. Say wha?!! Head to the Delaware beaches if you want to see real lump crabmeat fries. I digress. Next, I tried the snow crabs which were, in my opinion, overly seasoned and served soaking in some kind of broth (?). For me, The liquid & seasoning masked the crab flavor completely - and not in a good way. Also, I found it annoying that all our food (3 people) arrived as is was ready. In fairness- the waitress did warn us this how they roll. But, by the time my snow crab arrived - the rest of our party was finished eating & sat there watching me. I found the experience disappointing-both in terms of waitstaff, food quantity & taste of our orders. The cheesesteak & buffalo chicken sandwiches looked small and the guys said they were just OK. ps- also bummed there were few gluten free choices.
Its currently 1:55 in the morning and my girlfriend can not stop throwing up from food poisoning after eating from here.

I met a friend here for a business lunch. Very nice place I ordered a salad that had grapefruit in it, due to a health allergy I could not have grapefruit I asked could that be substituted out.To my surprise the server said no she had to ask the chef. REALLY? How hard was that to do. It amazes me how owners forget little things can effect the customer experience in a negative way. The server came back and said the chief said ok. I felt like this was wasted energy for a few slices of grapefruit. The rear bar area looked like a place I would like to stop back in for Happy Hour.

PROS: The menu is huge and there are a ton of options depending on your eating restrictions-vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, etc. There are also a ton of different kinds of meat burgers available that you generally can't get at most restaurants (bison, goat, etc.). There is even an option to build your own burger and plenty of sides to choose from. CONS: I went here on a lunch break the other week. We were sat outside, ordered, and then no one came back out for a while (at least 30 minutes). Since my coworkers and I went during lunch, we didn't really have a ton of time to wait. I went in to speak to the host and asked for our food to go, because we had to get back to work. He said that they were running about 30-40 minutes behind because some of their kitchen staff had called out. The part that annoys me is that this should have been communicated upfront instead of leaving us out there waiting for our food for so long. Our lunch was good, but not very hot by the time we brought it back. They did take a little bit off the check which was nice for the inconvenience. The food is good, but I also find it to be a bit overpriced. I'd go back to try it again and hope for a better experience.
The boat was neat. My husband and I paid for the dinner to celebrate our anniversary and We were extremely disappointed. It was cold, tasteless and gave me food poisoning.
Started a new job in the area and wanted some Chinese. Picked up some lunch from here and Almost threw up afterwards. Will not return!

I had Mongolian BBQ at a restaurant in another city and absolutely loved it, so I decided to try C.I. Chu's. The selection of meats and vegetables is great. The bowls are very large and the price seems reasonable for what you get. The service was quick and everyone was friendly. However, there must be cross-contamination issues with the sauces or during the cooking process. I used soy, teriyaki, and garlic, the same a sauces I used at the other restaurant. None of those should be spicy, but my food was very spicy. Like lips burning 5 minutes after eating spicy. I don't love spicy food, so that kind of ruined it for me. I would definitely go back if they could fix that issue. Update: I asked an employee about the spiciness and she said next time I should tell the cook to make sure mine doesn't touch anyone else's because I'm sensitive to spiciness. I'm happy to come back and try that next time.

The food was good but if you are Celiac (have a medical allergy to gluten) this is not a safe restaurant in which to eat. I ordered the mushroom omelet and home fries and was told they are gluten free but turns out, it was not. I'm not sure if they there was gluten in the fish or it was a result of cross contamination but either way, I got glutened there. Beware.

I care about what I eat. I buy fresh foods, rarely items packaged in plastic or things to store my food, even if they say "BPA free" it just means that the manufacturer likely used some other hormone-mimicking compound. I mention my concern for what I eat because EVERYTHING here has GLITTER in it. If your food is good, it doesn't mean it needs bedazzling. And this isn't about price-I've paid 20€ for slice of cake and coffee in Vienna, I'm perfectly happy paying the money for food that is worth it. I asked what their glitter was once, and you'd think I'd asked for some trade secret. Someone said they were "natural", another said "I think they are made from fish scales. If that's the case, where is your allergen disclaimer for "contains fish"? Being the skeptic I am, I took some of the glitter buttercream put it in a coffee filter and poured boiling water over it. It was still there in the filter. I rubbed it between my fingers. Still there. If you buy edible glitter from a well known cake baking supply company at a craft store, or luster, it dissolves. At best, Cake Bake is probably taking the word of some product manufacturers who says the glitter they buy is edible. At best, Cake Bake is naive to what common sense would say. People make claims about products (like "flushable" wipes that are clogging our sewers) all the time that are too good to be true. At the worst, these glitter products with who knows what chemical or colorants, represent a health risk to customers, many of which are little children, who parents want up treat to the beauty and whimsy. Are these colon cancer cases in 30 years? Just for a sparkly piece of cake. Let's grow up and get the glitter out of your product Gwendolyn. For now, I'll be around the corner at a better bakery that doesn't need glitter or glam to sell their orod

We have been going to this restaurant for at least 15 years. And always loved it. Three weeks ago this has changed. We came in around 8 pm with reservation. Got seated and waited for at least 15 minutes for the waitress to show up. And she was outstandingly unfriendly. Took another 10 minutes to get my beer and it was room temperature. And she said it supposed to be that way. Really? And then came the food... Simply terrible. Our favorite escargot were swimming in sand, the meat was over cooked, and everything was just ruined. In all the years going there we never had a bad meal, ever. And late that night the food poisoning was in full display. What happened to our favorite restaurant?

Ate here with my wife a few nights ago. Though the food was good, it was expensive for the portion sizes. We paid $10 for literally two glazed carrots. We also got the dip trio which needed more chips with it. The chicken tacos were excellent. It is nice they have many gluten free options well labeled on the menu. The bar itself is nice, but the lights above the bar need to be dimmed as it was too bright in the bar area.

Had planned on going to another Manayunk restaurant but parking was so bad I had to park all the way on the other side of Main Street so my mom and I decided to just go to Cactus because it was close. It was not my first time at Cactus and I didn't remember loving it but wanted to give it another chance. We ordered from the very limited menu some nachos and some tacos to share. I felt prices were way too high for the volume of food we got. Our order took FOREVER and everyone around us seemed to get their food way ahead of us. We saw a waiter carry our food and then he was staring at it really closely. He showed another waiter and then headed back downstairs. This was concerning. When the nachos finally arrived they seemed much smaller than expected, as though someone had scraped off all the side nachos. We got vegetarian nachos and yet there was chicken sprinkled all throughout. Obviously they had realized that we didn't order the chicken and tried just scraping it off and hoping we wouldn't notice. Fortunately I eat meat so it was okay, but what if I had been really allergic to chicken or a vegetarian? The food was okay but not great and given the prices I really don't see any need to go back to Cactus again. It's just not that great.

We went about 8 pm on a Sunday. It closes at 10 but I felt like they were closing in 10 minutes the way the waitress came by every 2 minutes asking if we were ready to order . They should really train waitresses that if we're looking at the menu we're not ready . After the third time over I quickly said I wanted the gluten free Dr Dre. I assumed it came with sauce - its dry as bone. I've had better frozen pizza We also got two salads Cesar and the Greek . Both tasty but it's sad when the salad out shines the pizza at a pizza place. I'm giving them three for the salad and because I should've told my eager waitress to take a chill pill and I would let her know when we were ready.

I saw the commercial about the dinrr and made up my mind that I had to get there.The scallop dish looked so appetizing. Well I am writing this after a day of vomiting and sickness. The dish (which ) got as a take out was horrible!!! the scallop were like big knots of dough, mushy and gluey. The sauce that was poured over the linguine was like runny pus (scampi). No flavor and no taste. I tried to doctor it up but to no avail. There was no helping this dish. I am a devout scallop lover and have had them from almost every where. After not being able to stomach these scallop , I figured I would try the Jello which I chose for desert and OMG! ti was slimy and extremely sweet (how do u mess up Jello?) Before I got my order to go I sat there and had soup. The service left much to be desired and it's the first time that I watch construction workers working and drilling over top of the customers. The place was in renovations and it never stopped the whole time. They were laying a new floor and it was terrible., Yet the waitresses and host stood around laughing and talking like it was a free for all. I called in and spoke to the manager who first stated he would not return my money but give me credit. After telling him I was going to write this review he agreed to reimburse me me at anytime. I will be going back there today for one reason and that will be to get my $21.00 back . Sadly I must say, that I will never return.

If I could give this place half a star, I would. The service is SO SLOW and TERRIBLE. We ordered a couple burgers and were here for over an hour and a half, most of which was spent waiting to pay and then receive our change! Upon arriving, our server told us about their drink special- free specialty drink with entree so we got those, good deal right? Our hotel concierge had given us a coupon for a free appetizer with purchase of 2 entrees (which we had) which I presented at the end of our meal. Our server told us we could EITHER use our coupon OR have the free drinks. We were not advised of this upon ordering! One of us did NOT even receive her meal. I have a peanut allergy which I told our server about and she placed a meal MADE WITH PEANUTS in front of me! I could have died if I consumed it if my friend hadn't told me that wasn't my meal. The manager was sitting at the bar eating the entire time, NOBODY apologized, several people were standing up wondering where their change was, I was also not given all of my change! This place is such a joke.

Bought two 18" pizzas to celebrate an event with family. Used the online order process for the first time, which worked fine. However, the crust wasn't quite right. The person we were celebrating thought maybe we were given gluten free pizzas. It didn't taste bad, the crust just didn't have any flavor. Both crusts looked different also. They didn't have the rolled edge, and they were much lighter lacking any browning. They also had a lot of cornmeal on the bottom. This is used at most good pizza places simply to slide the pizza off the peel into the oven. However, there was a lot and did affect the taste. My wife called the restaurant to ask, but they said nothing has changed. She asked if we might have been accidentally given the gluten crust, but was told they only have them in 10" size. We visit all of their locations and they're all the same pizzas. So I guess we'll be getting pizza elsewhere. Too bad as this was one of our local favs.

They burnt my first pizza, put dairy on the second (I'm lactose intolerant) then when they made a new one it was completely trash and fell apart. All of this took atleast an hour and a half or more of waiting. Then wasted more of my time with very bad and inattentive service. Completely wasted most of my night out with my girlfriend. I don't usually review restaurants because I'm usually carefree but I downloaded yelp just to trash this mellow mushroom, place was simply run by people who were incapable of doing things correctly. I love mellow mushroom but do NOT go to this one. Terrible food and terrible service. UPDATE: I went back and kaitlyn, the same shitty waiter we had last time messed up my order most likely on purpose. The most unprofessional mellow mushroom, never go here. Literally terrible. The manager is very nice but this mellow mushroom needs new waiters.

This was not a good experience. First, they forgot we were waiting. Finally, seated us because as they told us, we had to wait outside. Second, the booth was wet but the table was dirty and dry. Third, I asked for fajitas without peppers which they said they could do and the dish had diced up green peppers of which I didn't discover until I was at home ....(and will continue to be throwing up until it's all out). Fourth, my friend had the ribs which were dried from overcooking and the cheesey chicken if which, there was no chicken. This was an abhorrent experience and I will never go back. We had two drinks and they took forever. It wasn't busy and I was horrified it was a $100 I will continue to throw up because they said there wasn't any green peppers! An expensive vomit. :( clearly, they need to get their restaurant together.

Tried for the first time and found to be way over priced! Was charged twice as much as Qdoba charges me for the same thing. Qdoba has a lot more options as well. Maybe Chipotle is over charging trying to recover from all the law suits and the hundreds of cases of food poisoning caused by them in the last two years. Even a local mexican restaurant charged me $6 less than Chipotle did and the mexican restaurant gave gave free chips and salsa. NEVER AGAIN WILL CHIPOTLE RIP ME OFF!!! I highly advise to go elsewhere.

Dropped in for lunch...ordered a grilled cheese sandwich with fries for both my wife and I. Then I thought I would like a cup of clam chowder. After 15 minutes, I signaled my server that I would like to have the clam chowder before the meal. She went over to ask the cook, but then brought our meals instead. She claimed the chowder was not "...ready" yet. A couple minutes later she brought the chowder. I took a spoonful into my mouth. Cold chowder. Then I noticed a funny taste and something red in my clam chowder. I took it up to the waitress and asked, "Is there bacon or ham in my clam chowder?" She answered with question "Why? Are you allergic?" I replied, "NO! I just don't want to eat red meat and there was nothing in the menu about it containing pork" I gave it back and did not get charged for it, but the service was lousy, (our waitress continually disappeared for long periods,...). I ALWAYS tip 20% and this was the first time in quite a while that I left a 10% amount. What is it that people have with this bacon fetish? It's CLAM CHOWDER!! WTF? Why ruin a perfectly good soup by sneaking bacon into it and NOT STATING THIS IN THE MENU?! I am not recommending because of the service and quality.

don't eat here. I threw up the whole night. I didn't even have the Sushi. The BBQ had no flavor. The selection was sparse. The Ice cream was not Ice cream but Ice Melt. I had to run to the rest room before I could leave. Never never never again!!!!!!

It was my first time here yesterday and I got food poisoning (I ordered the chimichanga). I was violently throwing up and miserable the rest of the night. The waitress we had wasn't that great either (she only came once to check up on my table and we had to flag her down after almost 20 minutes after getting to go boxes). The food was alright there was nothing special about our meal. Update: My friends also got food poisoning...

My family and I placed a to-go order this past Friday. We got two orders of wings (garlic parm and Buffalo), a grilled cheese with tomato and a side of the tomato soup, and the original Mac n cheese. The wings were okay, but had very little meat on them. I also requested two orders of ranch and was given two blue cheese dressings, which someone in my family has an allergy too. Luckily I noticed the difference before disaster could have struck but still was not a good start to the meal. The grilled cheese was good but it was cold and the tomato soup was not included in the order. The Mac n cheese was probably the worst part of the meal. The flavor was overwhelming and not in a good way. It made Kraft Mac N Cheese look like it should be served at a 5-star restaurant in comparison. When I went to get the food the inside seemed like a nice ambiance, but it's unlikely I'll be returning anytime soon.

I got food poisoning from this restaurant. I ordered a turkey burger with avocado, spinach. Two hours later I'm in the bathroom. I ended up in the hospital 5 hours after that from sickness and dehydration. I spoke to owner wanted to claim no responsibility but wanted to give me a gift card for my troubles. I said no I want you to pay my hospital bill! Don't go there unless you want to get sick!

Short of it: not worth $. Small, semi clean rooms. Paying for location. Nothing special. You certainly do not get what you paid for. Although when you first walk in this hotel is beautiful and ornate and historic, once you take the elevator to your room you will see what it really looks like. What was marketed as a classy 4-5 star hotel did not deliver any qualities of such. The linens on bed were ripped, pillowcases were stained, lightbulb in bathroom was out. No complementary anything including bottles of water ($6.50 for one little bottle, really?). Also you can hear almost everything that goes on on the street below even from our room on the 5th floor. The pool leaves much to be desired. The one bartender loves to close shop before the pool even closes. What you pay for here is location and even being on bourbon street is overrated because it truly smells like hot vomit right as you exit this building. You'd be better off to spend your money elsewhere and enjoy the tranquility of being away from the noise if you choose. And let me just mention that we understood what being on bourbon street was before stepping foot in this hotel but to market this place as a high class establishment and not be able to retreat into any semblance of tranquility is unacceptable.

Okay people. Did I miss the memo saying that 1 inch think hunks of grocery store ham is normal on 'authentic' Italian pizza? I suppose it's possible to get used to this, but 1 inch thick hunks of FAT off grocery store bought ham is just gross. Please stop this. Please for the love of pizza, make this stop. Their is more... I get it. Dessert management can be tough. Especially when it's tiramisu. You can't keep it in the fridge forever. Sometimes it needs to go in the freezer. I can accept this if it means not getting food poisoning. At the same time, if I wanted a frozen block of cream, I would have gone for ice cream. I ordered tiramisu because I wanted tiramisu. A didn't want a frozen block of cream and cookies. This needs to stop too. If a pizza box of fatty grossness and a block of frozen cream is the new norm at Famoso, the future of authentic pizza in St. Albert is bleak

This review is long over due, but worth the effort! If you're in the area, this joint is a must, but only for their food. My family and I came here on a Sunday about two weeks ago and the facility was only so-so busy. A few empty tables here and there so we were ushered fairly quickly to a table that fitted about 10 for our party. Right away, I was very disappointed in the service. Our waitress (who seemed experienced) was not the most pleasant. Her attitude was very snarky and known-it-all, but not helpful the least. Due to my allergies, I asked what kind of dip went with the chips and/what's in it and right away the waitress snapped saying they didn't give away anything. My mom and I looked at each astonished by the tone inflected in her voice before my mom told her I had bad allergies. The woman then answered very sarcastically saying, "yes, there's diary in it. It's ranch!" Needless to say, her ability to serve went down hill from here and fast. She wouldn't help me find something on the menu that Accommodated my allergies. Never in my life have I had such treatment to my allergies. I was pretty offended and almost called management but didn't want to cause a huge scene due to our large dinner party. If the food wasn't so stinking good, I would not want to return due to the poor service. I was and still am super disappointed in the service there. But to all those gluten free at there, they do have a gluten free bun. Don't get the fries, they're coated in breading. I would recommend the Mahi sandwich! It's out of this world! Once again, other than the poor service, the food is worth the try. (Might just want to get it to go to avoid such a scenario).
Cool place and cool decor. But I got food poisoning so that wasn't fun. Large space and good beer

This place is completely empty at dinner time, which may be explained by the unprofessional crew. We ordered Chicken Kabob without Pita, but the dish came with Pita on the Salad. They took it back and return after 20 seconds claiming it was a "fresh plate". If the place was busy, we might buy it. If you are Gluten Free, I would not trust this place.

Even though I only came here for the karaoke, I was hungry when I arrived. I looked at the menu to see what looked good and decided on a burger. Since I am allergic to black pepper, I asked if the burgers were cooked with it. The manager came out to tell me that while they are normally cooked with black pepper, they could make mine without. When my burger arrived, I was pleasantly surprised to find that not only was it cooked without the pepper, but it was cooked to a perfect medium as I had requested. I only had a few of the fries because the burger filled me up, but they were good, too. So to sum things up, the karaoke was good, the food was good, and I didn't end up covered in hives.

This place is in my neighborhood and I also really wanted to like it! Unfortunately, three of my friends have gotten sick from the food here on three separate occasions. Two of them have actually thrown up in the restaurant after eating, and one of them got food poisoning that lasted for two days from a chicken burrito they ate. The first time we thought maybe it was a fluke. The second time I was starting to be convinced that this place isn't serving good food. After the third time? Not going back.

The food has changed because this place has new owners. The food was very bland and old. My family only ate a little of the food and the entire house has food poisoning. When I walked in and didn't smell food...no curry, no onions, beans..nada.... That should have been my tell tell sign. Stay away....Trust me

First Watch is a breakfast place that closes in early afternoon. Staying at the Sheraton a block away we ate breakfast late at First Watch, then continue to the Circle Theater to pick up tickets for the evening performance. The food was ok, but the diarrhea from food poisoning 15 minutes later was the worse case I have ever encountered. Being nearby, I returned to the restaurant to use the bathroom only to find it was closed. Fortunately, the pizza restaurant next door was kind enough to allow me to use their toilette to wash myself and change into clean clothes that my wife brought from the hotel. Upon returning home the following day I called the restaurant, explained what happened, and suggested they check the kitchen and employees for unsanitary conditions and the eggs for salmonella. Instead of apologizing, the manager became defensive and tried to convince me that food poising take longer than 15-20 minutes after eating to occur. The worse part is that the company, which is headquartered in Dayton, Ohio, really didn't care.

I wanted to love this place, I did. And I'm hopeful I can improve this review in the future- but for now: the fish & a few other dishes I've tried had been excellent, but multiple desserts, drinks & their chartreuse tray are all just adequate. Given that service has been just adequate too- I'm just surprised as ambiance & ingredient quality seem high. I'm also very disappointed that there are no gluten-free nor non dairy options available. (It's not that hard to highlight foods not made or gluten or lactose amongst a standard menu. The location is fantastic, & I see the direction the want- she not quite there yet in my opinion.

Where do I start. I ordered food to go it was my first time here so I ordered the Blue Jawn burger no lie I vomited we had to hurry up and pull over. I ordered the general tso chicken tacos not good and the sauce was too sweet. They were using bare hands to prepare the food which was already a turn off. The place is small and tight everything is everywhere. My 3 year old daughter brung me spray bottles I guess they had in her sight. The Mac and cheese were like baby elbow and partially hard . Looks are very deceiving, everything looks good but I wasn't happy.My baby didn't even like her Mac and she love Mac and cheese and my son love General tso chicken but not this one. I will not be returning ever. The prices were very high too.The food was being prepared or put together after food was cooked at least when a pizza goes in the oven and bake it kills the germs.You'll do everything bare hand. No sarcasm needed. Thank you Nick

I was super excited to try this place after a friend raved about them. We called ahead and made a reservation for the same night, Saturday night. When we arrived, they sat us immediately and brought out beverages. Party of 4, 3 of us did AYCE and 1 got the shrimp bento box. They have a nice variety of rolls, very typical to what you see in the area. One in our party has a shrimp allergy. She really enjoyed the Pink Lady & the Geisha (this roll is a potsticker within a roll!) The miso soup was delicious. I really enjoyed the mushrooms in the broth. The other apps were fine. The stuffed jalapeño appetizer was strange in temperature, it is deep fried but its cold and the jalapeño is raw. It was a weird temperature experience, wouldn't order again. The 3 of us ordering AYCE ordered a total of 7 rolls to start. We typically eat about 3 rolls per person, but started w 7. The ordering is not similar to others in town, as they come to the table to order, instead of giving you paper to write down. Half of our rolls came on one plate, with appropriate portioned rice. The other half came with 2x the rice of the original plate. Wayyy too much rice. They also brought us out 8 rolls, not just the 7 that we ordered. 5 of our rolls included shrimp, which is what ultimately ruined our experience. The shrimp was not good, a very rubbery texture. The shrimp were huge, not easy to eat with the excess rice portions. Remember, they also brought us extra food that we didn't order. And their rolls are HUGE even without the extra rice.. the rolls were not edible, they were rubbery and ricey. Of the 7 rolls we ordered, they brought 8... and we ate as much as we could stomach... leaving less than 3 rolls to waste. As a business...seeing over 30% waste, this should have prompted the staff to ask why we weren't eating our rolls. But they didn't. They asked if we wanted a to-go box. We told them no, no to-go box, and advised that it didn't taste good and that they'd also brought us food more food than we ordered. Despite being honest with our dissatisfaction, we were charged an excess waste fee. Technically we ordered less food than cost effective for AYCE.... even with appetizers, we would have saved probably $10 if we had done ala carte. We honestly expected the rolls to be edible and expected to eat more. I was really blown away that they would charge the waste fee after we voiced out dissatisfaction, the small amount of food we actually ordered, and that I've never actually been charged that fee anywhere (but I have never had rubbery gross shrimp in all my rolls before either.) I was really bummed by the inconsistency w rolls & rice portion, and lack of interest in what we thought of the food quality. I wish we had started with some non-shrimp rolls so we may have had a more pleasant dining experience. Everything else seemed to taste very fresh. My rating would have been a 3/4 if it hadn't been for the waste charge.

I'm surprised this place has so many good reviews. I thought it was just a standard sports bar. Went here because they have a gluten-free menu which makes it so my acquaintance can eat. I do like that they have taps at some of the tables but overall was not impressed by this place. I went here on a weekday night and it was fairly busy but not packed. Parking is easy, huge lot. The server was really nice and knew the menu perfectly. The food arrived a good time after ordered, I ordered the OMG which consists of 5 patties and 5 slices of cheese. The burger itself was quite large but it was dry and had next to no flavor. Sadly, the fries were basically unseasoned also or at least tasted so. Unsure, if they use frozen food but I have tasted frozen food that packed more a punch than the food I had here. I would say that I had a decent time even though the food was disappointing, and there is even a chance I would go back just because this place has a gluten-free menu.

$26.30 for two bagel breakfast sandwiches and two 16 oz. smoothies. Yes, you read that right. I want to like this place. Really, I do. Because I live a block and a half away, and it would be so convenient to have a reliable cafe option this close. But this isn't it. I mean, the food and drinks are decent enough. But not worth the exorbitant prices you pay. And oftentimes, the bored hipster staff can't be bothered to get your order right in the first place. On several occasions they have "forgotten" to swap out the soy milk for almond milk in smoothies I've ordered. Not a big issue for me, but a HUGE one for my gf, who has a soy allergy and thus had more than one upset stomach thanks to their carelessness. I finally reached my tipping point this past weekend. It wasn't only paying through the nose for an order that, again, wasn't quite accurate. It was running to their house ATM mid-checkout, after realizing I was a few dollars short, and coming back and seeing a sign that says they now take credit cards--a fact the bored cashier didn't mention at any point in the transaction, even when I was frantically scrambling at the ATM. Any normal cashier should say, "hey, we take cards now if you want to pay that way." Sorry, Benna's. I don't care how much in a hurry I am, and how convenient you are. You're just not worth it.

Terrible. Waitress got mad because I didn't leave a tip, I didn't leave a tip because she was slow, ignorant, fake, snotty, and overall just the worst service I have EVER received. The food itself was shit. Cold, tasted terrible, took very long to come out. We were only getting dessert, and took over an hour. It's hard to screw up dessert but these found a way. The restaurant itself was hot, small, smelly, utensils were filthy, water was contaminated with specs of dirt. One star

Pizza out of the oven 7:57 Pizza out for delivery 8:14 Pizza showed up 9:14 Not hot not fresh. Called to complain Ratchet woman in a suit Won't order again. Chicken habenero sandwich no where near hot closer to food poisoning temp

Having eaten at the St. Pete location and finding it to be great, decided to try this location. Big mistake. There was a slight wait, so we sat across from the young man manning the cashier desk, only to find him wiping blood from his arm (from an open sore on his elbow) with a towel.....that appeared to be the type used in bussing tables. He was contaminating the entire area with his blood....so my friend suggested he go and get a bandaid or something. There were several waitresses who approached and they acted like it was no big deal, and finally a manager came up and my friend suggested to him also that the young man should tend to his wound appropriately in the back with a first aid kit. The manager told him to go get a bandaid.....at which point he placed the blood stained towel on the counter, then under the counter and went into the back. At no point did the manager or anyone else seem to find this a problem, and no one attempted to sanitize the area or remove the used towel so it would not be used to wipe tables or something. Nothing. The young man returned from the back, without bandaid, instead mopping his wound with a gauze pad, and this time entered into the kitchen area. At this point my friend and I decided to leave, as we had lost confidence that this place uses proper procedures for cleanliness and disease prevention. We phoned the manager after we left to tell him why we left, and he was just as unconcerned as before, and gave us a generic "sorry about that". Yeah, me too, especially with all the recent cases of disease spread by restaurant workers in Pinellas County, one would hope they'd take this matter more seriously. Maybe the health department would.

I really love Snap pizza but don't like this location. I recently came in to order a salad and saw that they adapted a touch screen ordering system. This is awesome! No more confusion or incorrect orders and no more miscommunication between the customer and the staff. I decided to go for the salad bowl but honestly I wish i got the gluten free and vegan pizza but the touch screen option didn't have the vegan pie? Not sure if I just missed it myself or it actually isn't available, so is it something you have to order with the staff? Kinda sad about that. Anyway I placed my salad bowl order and waited for it to come out. It turns out that another customer basically got a similar thing as me and there was a small dilemma. Now I don't mind confusion but the employee was down right rude and even said "I wasn't asking you this" I was a bit speechless and didn't know what to say but now looking back on it it was super rude. I was trying to say yes that condiment is not what I ordered so that's probably the other person's. Anyway I will probably avoid this location. However the food was great!

I have never had an omelette I have not liked until now. The omelette I ordered it was very tough and dry, and also very expensive. My order was over $19 for an omelette with spinach, feta, bacon, onions and a cup of coffee. I have celiac disease and communicated this with the waitress. I appreciated how at first she went in the back to double check with the kitchen on what omelettes I could have, but then my meal came out with biscuits touching my omelette. Instead of making my meal over again like they should of because it was them contaminated, they just took off the biscuits and brought back my plate with 2 corn tortillas where the biscuit touching my omelette had been. Needless to say I was in G.I. distress after that which unfortunately occurred on my 5 Hour drive back to Houston. Would not recommend this place to any Celiacs or anyone wanting an omelette. My other party's plates like chicken & waffles and the crawfish etoufee on hash browns looked delicious. I unfortunately couldn't have any of that.

So I'll premise this review by saying I have a food allergy. So my experience here was very much affected by how they dealt with that. But I'll start with the menu. They have a menu for the waiters that indicates what items are GF but that menu is not what guests receive. Which meant that when I ordered something that is almost always GF at other places (shrimp and grits), my waiter had to come back and say it wasn't GF. All of which could have been avoided, and was just a generally frustrating experience because my guesswork could have been avoided. And then, after I ordered a significantly more expensive entree to do something that WAS indicated as GF, and I ordered it as suggested on the menu, with full warning that I had a food allergy, I nevertheless experienced my usual awful reaction (details unimportant but read: lots of pain and need for medication to function normally). If I am paying close to $30 for an entree, and I say I have a food allergy that I alerted the kitchen staff to, I expect you to take it seriously. I'm "lucky" in that my reactions don't involve anaphylaxis. But that doesn't mean they don't affect my life in significant ways. If I could leave my hotel room, I'd come down and make you deal with me, but again, I'm currently not capable of doing normal things because your kitchen couldn't be bothered to cook something GF that you assured me you could.

Not a good place to go if you have allergies. They did not accommodate at all. They were also very rude about it. We ended up having to pay for their mistake. It was a very unwelcoming place. I would not recommend this place go anyone. Also the food that we did get taste very low quality.

Subdued atmosphere, yet eclectic. Envie is located in the French Quarter and despite being in such a heavily populated area, it manages to escape the boisterousness and tourism that pervades the area. Need a buzz, but you still need to stay awake for all the festivities going on? Envie's got it! They have a menu for caffeine & alcohol infused drinks. They also have a regular coffee menu. If you're vegan or have dairy allergies, they have dairy alternatives. I went to Envie on two occasions (3 check-ins & you get a free cookie). I ordered their Raspberry Schnapps Mocha, which was pretty decent, but I would've preferred more Schnapps. I also ordered an expresso, which was also decent. Their service wasn't horrible, but definitely lacking. Day one service was mediocre and not very helpful, but day two service was a lot better. Pros: + Coffee! + Good variety of alcohol & non-alcoholic drinks. + Location. + Atmosphere. + Dairy alternatives. + Free wi-fi Cons: - Coffee. - Staff isn't very helpful. Overall, I was expecting a bit more all around, but nevertheless, it was good enough for me to check-in twice. Would I recommend Envie, sure, especially if you would like to get away from all the noise, but you will definitely find better coffee & service elsewhere.

Not once has my order been made correctly. The most common issue is the kitchen keeps forgetting the pentagram on our pizzas - which is something extra you pay for. Recently our salad was prepared incorrectly and because of allergies we needed to toss it. When the pizza is made correctly it's hands-down the best East Coast style pizza in Reno. It's a bummer that I just don't trust them to make my order correctly - so now we don't order for delivery because it will get delivered incorrectly and then we have to drive it back to be fixed. We have to do pick up and check the order in front whoever gave it to us. Lastly, this is a specific gripe I fully respect will make me sound like a square - but the music is too loud. I'm a metal head, but when I can't hear the bartender to order a drink then that's a problem. Last time I was there an employee asked the bartender to turn the music down; she did and when the employee left the bartender turned it back up. I get it, you guys have a whole brand you're trying to adhere to. But if you have spiteful staff who don't care when someone complains it's too loud then why would I ever hang there?

What a TERRIBLE experience! Not only were they not busy, but they just had to sit us next to a booth with 3 kids who shook the back of my seat the entire time. And I'm not one of those who think kids should not be allowed at restaurants either. Our server was nice and did a great job keeping our drinks filled. The menu had barely any options. I ordered a combo platter which consisted of a piece of long john silvers fish, shit filled shrimp, disgusting hush puppies and some fries. My fiancé ordered a chicken sandwich. The chicken tasted as if it sat in the freezer for 6 years and will be lucky if she doesn't get food poisoning from her 3 bites. So glad we paid $43 for a side of fries for dinner and will be going home to eat cereal. Will never go back to that place!!! AWFUL FOOD!!!

Our first time. The decor is lovely and so inviting. You would never know how nice it is from the outside. We were very impressed with the extensive variety of their menu. Sushi was on our mind so we ordered the "Love Boat" which included 18 pieces of sashimi, 3 sushi rolls, miso soup and a salad for two. The fish was fresh but the boat did not include many of the greens we are accustomed to when eating sushi. The soup was very flavorful. The salad was a good size but the dressing was disappointing. I did not finish it. We passed on dessert. Dinner did not sit well with us---food poisoning. First and last time. Go at your own risk!

Can't vouch for the bar experience (I was there with my 77-year-old dad and 14-year-old son) but the food was terrible. Dad had a generic salad, son had a chicken-and-bacon sandwich that he really liked, and I had the Jerk Chicken, which was basically inedible. I couldn't tell if it was undercooked, overcooked, or just plain old, so half of it went in the trash. Beans, fries, rice, and fried plantains were all good but could'nt make up for the sketchy chicken. Update: Son vomited his chicken sandwich two hours later, so I had to drop another star.

Scout's is located in the Westhaven neighborhood, has plenty of free parking and easy walkable access. The interior at lunch is bright and inviting. We were seated right away, sadly, there were few people there. Our server was very helpful and attentive, giving us enough time with the menu but not so much that we got antsy. I eat gluten free and the menu is a dream come true for me. They offer gf bread and buns and pizza crust, how wonderful to have all those choices, as well as noting each item that is acceptable to eat if one is "gluten sensitive". I opted for the chop salad, others had curry coconut chicken and the truffle frites burger. My salad was delightful, fresh, lots of interesting add ons and delicious dressing. The curry coconut chicken was enjoyed very much. My friend who ordered the burger asked for medium well. When the food was delivered, hers looked medium rare, so they took it back and presumably cooked the meat more thoroughly, however, when it was returned, my friend said it seemed like they had reheated it with the lettuce and all in with the meat so what she ate had wilted heated lettuce. We will certainly return. It is refreshing to me to have some many gf choices.

I've come here a few times since my last review (which I still stand behind) and I have tried a variety of things on the menu that I really enjoyed. For me, this place is all about location (I can walk here from my house) and ambiance (I am 'outdoorsy' in that I like to drink on patios). I LOVE sitting on the patio and enjoying the margaritas by the carafe (the best deal in the house) on a nice day with the breeze blowing. On my last visit, my friends and I really enjoyed the empanadas & the mussels, and thought that the ceviche & the tamale were just O.K. (No melted cheese should be ON a tamale, it should be IN the tamale, right?) They serve Sunday brunch which has some gluten-free options and cheap mimosas (if you like your orange juice with just a splash of bubbly).

I really wanted to like this place but i am terribly disappointed in my experience at Brixx this evening. I have visited here more than once and as far as I'm concerned they only have one good employee. I ordered a drink tonight that said it had " mixed fruit " in it and at the bottom of all the fruit there was blue berries which i am very allergic to. It definitely cut our football Sunday short because i had to rush home to take Benadryl but to top it off when we spoke to the owner about this and suggested that maybe they could put on the menu that berries are in this drink he told us it was not his responsibility to care for other people's allergies and still charged us for that drink. Ordered a Siam Fried Rice with vegetables. It was typical, nothing special. I would eat it if I was hungry but probably would not order it again. We asked for spicy noodles with beef. It had shrimp and scallops. I'm allergic to seafood. We checked the description to ensure we didn't order the wrong thing. It turned out seafood charged an extra $2.00. We got food we can't eat. If I could give this 0 stars it would be more appropriate! Having Celiac is always a struggle to eat out, but I've always managed to find something to eat at every restaurant. Today I was told I could not eat anything in this restaurant!! Really??? Are you just lazy??? I should be able to eat ANYWHERE!!! Shame on you!!

I walked out and don't plan on returning. First of all, why label allergens with yellow icons on a light colored menu background? Difficult to read. I'm not sure why it's so hard to answer whether or not this establishment has a protocol in place to deal with guests who have a gluten allergy. Further, when asked if a certain bowl was gluten free, the young man behind the counter looked at me and said "well you can see what we put in it." That doesn't answer the question. Train your staff better.

Fiance and I just tried this place last night. He's still recovering from the subsequent peanut allergic reaction, but that is not really Wei Hong's fault and not the reason for my 1 star review - just a warning up front that you should not eat here if allergic to peanuts, even the dishes without peanuts are probably contaminated. The one star is for a couple of reasons. First, my straw was SALTY when I first put it in my mouth. My assumption is that someone with dirty hands touched it when they put it in my glass. I could not be more grossed out...then and now...shudder. Second, the food was really sub-par. We still haven't found a Chinese place we like here in STL, and this place did not deliver. I don't understand the reviews. St. Louisans, surely you've had Chinese food that isn't soggy, luke warm and greasy before? Help me out here, guys, cuz Wei Hong is not cutting it. Also, I have not tried the bakery, so this review only applies to the restaurant. I will say that the service was fast and pleasant, but that does not bump them up given the salty straw experience.

The absolute WORST Italian food I've ever eaten! To begin with the waiter, John, was indifferent from the beginning, complaining that he had allergies, so we needed to speak up. The veal parmigiana I had was the WORST Italian dish of my entire life! The veal was so paper thin I'm surprised Caruso's even bothered throwing it in. It was like "Where's Waldo?" or "Where's the beef?" It was so miniscule it was a joke. The manicotti with cheese my mother ordered, likewise, was sub par. When I expressed my dissatisfaction with the meal, the waiter basically said "This is the way we make it here." He never called over the manager or Maitre d', and just gave a lukewarm "I'm sorry the meal doesn't meet with your satisfaction." And, of course, I paid full price; there was no discount to compensate for my displeasure with the meal. The spaghetti, too, was utterly tasteless as was the iced tea. When it was time for dessert, John just laid the dessert menu on our table and talked away. I will never dine at Caruso's again because of the lousy food and poor service.

This TR is pretty decent. I went on a weeknight so the wait was under 5 minutes. I love how they give you warm bread with cinnamon butter as soon as you get to your table, Yay! My waitress was friendly and attentive during my entire visit which was nice. It took the food around 20 or so minutes to arrive, but someone in my party ordered a rib eye so I'm sure that was the hold up. The food was delicious and hot and we devoured it. I had the grilled salmon w/ loaded mashed potatoes and string beans! Heads up- the string beans have pork in them but they are oh so delicious! The loaded mashed potatoes come with a dollop of sour cream, cheese and bacon- DELISH! "If it's ya birthday, make some noise" because they will come around with a bull for you to sit on! No, it's not a mechanical bull, but it's fun and perfect for a few funny birthday photos! The restaurant was clean aside from the minimal amount of peanut shells lying around. *If you have a peanut allergy, stay away from this place!!* The bathroom was spotless which is always a plus in my book. This restaurant is apart of a very busy complex, but there's tons of parking all around. Overall, this place is a little above average when it comes to chain restaurants, but its definitely not a 5 star steakhouse. I honestly don't think you'll regret dining here though....

The ambiance of this place is great, I will give it that but the service and food is terrible. We waited 45 mins before we got our salads & bread. And the quality of the food itself was very bad. Our server rarely came around and we had to flag her down several times. The one great thing about this place is they have a gluten free menu and it has several options!

We arrived at the restaurant for lunch , we had family visiting from out of town . There was no one else dining and all open tables . They took a long time to seat 4 of us but it was ok, we were excited to eat. We ordered food and the waitress was HORRIBLE , we remained pleasant and polite. When we asked for containers to take the food home we waited 15 minutes --no one else in the dining room, still. We asked for the check and she took such a long time to bring it that my gf went to nicely ask for it, another staff member went to get her. We overheard the waitress say loudly I'm the kitchen, "they are a real pain !!" Enough said . We paid $150 for a large lunch and we will NEVER be back . I guess they don't need the business ..Don't waste your time with this place ....

If there's a negative rating; I'd rate the place that. Bought almost $300 worth of food. Young man taking orders was handling the money as well making the smoothie, cross contaminating, other young man was wearing his mask on his chin while the third came from the back eating definitely not trying to come back to this location

Coming back to Philly from LA, this is NOT "healthy" or clean eating of any kind. Don't be fooled by the name. The groothie tastes like bananas - I've had many delicious green smoothies and made my own and this one is pretty basic. They sweeten their juices with agave which is just as bad as pure sugar. Got food poisoning 6/27/21! Do not eat there ! Egg roll was cold the egg foo young was greasy and pork fried rice tasted weird! Got sick immediately after I ate it must be under new management! Does not deserve a star should be -5

Been living in Carpinteria for a few months now, but finally got to try out Siam Elephant. My girlfriend is allergic to gluten and dairy so Asian food is often difficult. With dietary preferences, the hard part is usually getting the wait staff to actually listen to you, and take the time to give you the right answer. Too often they want to re-assure you before you even get the question out of your mouth. Well Siam Elephant completely alleviated any concerns for us that our meal would be contaminated. Lea was polite to us when we stopped in days earlier to check out the menu, and also happened to take our order. She was extremely patient and took the time to address questions on multiple dishes and sauces and actually remembered when she brought the food to our table to re-confirm that the dipping sauces were gluten-free. I felt bad asking about the chicken in the sweet and sour chicken as it looked to have a slight breading, but she kindly described the preparation method that gave it a quasi-breaded look. The food was great, we had fresh springroll appetizer, spicy beef noodle and the thai sweet and sour chicken, with a Thai Tea to drink - which also was made with coconut milk instead of dairy at Leas' suggestion. It was really really delicious! Prices are good, food was hot, prompt, and above average in flavor, and the atmosphere was really nice. Overall the exceptional service made the experience and ensured we will return next time we have a Thai Craving. The look of sheer pleasure on my girlfriends face to bite into a special meal she knew was safe was worth the cost of the entire meal. Thank you Siam Elephant!!

Finally got an elusive Saturday evening reservation to Vetri, after about fifteen years of trying off an on, with little success. The service was outstanding; you'd be hard-pressed to find better anywhere. It's a VERY small place; the original location of Le Bec Fin, actually. Very cute room, maybe ten tables or so, and somewhat less formal than I anticipated based on the price. The room has a very romantic atmosphere, and despite the very loose dress code (the male diner next to us was wearing a t-shirt, and had his pants down so you could see his boxers) was very reminiscent of a small family-run italian restaurant you'd find in Italy. The chef welcomes guests with a complimentary flute of dry prosecco as well as a house cured meat amuse consisting of four offerings including house cured salami and foie gras. A very nice beginning. We found that included in the $155 pre fixe was soft drinks and coffee/tea afterwards, which was also a nice change from the traditional a la carte options. The menu is a pre-fixe, however the general theme is that the chef chooses from the options for the guests. My GF and I each received different courses, and we shared. You are able to select your options if you like, and can provide any preferences or allergy information as well. We felt no pressure at all to adhere to the chef's choice, but chose to do so and be surprised with the selections. I didn't take a detailed inventory of each dish, however there were a total of six courses, including dessert, plust two additional courses that were shared, the (rather large) amuse, and a pre-dessert. So, it ends up being more like nine courses if you count the two shared options as one per diner. Every dish was impeccably prepared and served, and we enjoyed everything. That being said, despite a good experience, we both felt the value for what is (unless you take into consideration the Morimoto omakase that can go north of $200 if you so desire) the most expensive restaurant/pre fixe in the city was somewhat a disappointment. Having sampled similar pre fixe menus in Philadelphia, New York, and abroad, I think this one falls down in the area of value, though certainly not in preparation nor execution. While we had a nice evening, the meal just didn't seem to rise to the same "special restaurant" level that you'd find at Le Bec Fin, The Fountain, Lacroix, etc., based on the cost. It's definitely worth the visit, but may not have the same "revisit" appeal for everyone.

I feel sick instantly! The chicken tastes like it expired and they chose to cook it anyway. The soups are so bland, no flavor! The noodles have a weird flavor like they were nuked in styrofoam. The fried zucchini started off good til you reach the middle and its old and soggy. Yuck I've had way better buffet before. Plus the booths are made for skinny people like ikea or something. Never going back. On my way home to vomit.....

Two stars for the weirdest order experience I've ever had. There were woefully few food options at BNA, and they all had crazy long lines. Pyramid had two lines- one long and one short. It took us a couple minutes to realize that the short line was where you ordered and the long line was where you picked up your food. The madness? They don't start your food order until you get to the front of the line and they take your order ticket. Everything is mostly pre prepped but still. Overly crispy fries and absolutely zero attempts to not cross contaminate- my steak sandwich and fries came with some chicken tender breading and my husband watched them dump falafel in with chicken and fries so good luck to anyone strictly vegetarian I guess. The bread was super soggy and soft, and overall the meal left much to be desired- especially since it took us 40 minutes to get it and we had to dash to the gate.

So this night started by ordering the vegan pizza with onions and peppers added from A Tutti from Uber Eats. I ordered this item as I have a dairy allergy and was excited to see a pizza that I didn't have to ask to be modified in order to be dairy free. Both on their menu and on Uber eats it explicitly states that this pizza does not contain cheese. So I get my pizza in a timely manner from Uber Eats, and when I open the box, what do I see? A pizza with ONLY cheese, peppers, and onions. There was not even sauce on the pizza and it did not contain any of the other toppings that were stated on the menu... I also received the actual A Tutti receipt and it stated the correct order, so I am very unsure how such a big mixup happened. I call the restaurant and they state that they will remake the pizza and have their delivery person deliver it to me as soon as possible. She stated that the driver will call me when he arrives at my apartment. So I wait for about 40 min and then TRY calling the restaurant back to ask what the ETA is. However, now their phone is not working. I had to call about 10 times for about 15 min before I can get through to the restaurant. When I finally get through, they state that they have been waiting for me to call back, because they were unable to get my address from Uber Eats. So I give it to them, and they state that it should be delivered soon. Another 30 min go by and I have still not received my pizza or heard from the restaurant so I call back again, but of course it takes another 10 min of calling to get through. When I finally do they state that the driver is out making other deliveries, and if he was not back in 5 min that they would call the driver and then call me when the driver was on the way to my apartment. So after ANOTHER 30 min I try calling the restaurant, and "surprisingly" cannot get through so I decide to get in my car and drive to the restaurant. As soon as I get there, I get a call from the delivery guy that he is at my apartment. I had not received a call from the restaurant stating he was on his way as promised. I go into the restaurant hoping to speak with the manager. I told the woman that had been answering the phone that I was expecting a refund seeing as it took all-in-all almost 3 hours to get the correct order delivered from the time I ordered it on Uber Eats until the time I got the pizza. She told me that when the manager was not busy, he would call Uber Eats to get my refund, so we will see if that happens. Also, I was obviously frustrated and upset with this whole situation, and this woman at the counter was giving ME attitude. So now I am sitting here eating the pizza, and it is soggy, tasteless, and obviously very cold. Save yourself the hassle and go find better pizza somewhere else.

I have eaten here several times over the last few months up to the week that the restaurant opened in the Winter. The first 2 or 3 times service was exceptional. The waiters/waitresses we had were friendly, checked in on us several times during dinner, and they communicated with the chef about my gluten allergy. It was easy to find what I could have on the menu that was gluten free. I was told all of the mole's are gluten free and most of the menu was gluten free with exception to some fried items and desert items. I was even told they had a dedicated fryer for the whole fish and it did not contain anything that had gluten. I was so happy and impressed with that. The food was great, there hasn't been one thing on the menu that I did not like, but the fried fish, elotes, and stuffed peppers remains my favorite items on the menu. Now, the last time I dined in it wasn't even busy because it was raining, our waitress had a major attitude with me in particular because I had a gluten allergy. She was rolling her eyes and talking under her breath and basically acting like she did not want to serve us at all. She never even returned to the table except to bring us our bill and she had charged us for food we didn't even order. We were so disappointed in service that night. There were questions about whether the once dedicated fryer was contaminated with gluten and if it was safe to order certain items. Then I was told nothing could be guaranteed to be contamination free wheres all the other times I dined in the staff and management was fairly confident that their kitchen could provide gluten free food. Of all the times I ate there this was the only time I was served food that tested positive for gluten and no one knew why. It was an extremely disappointing service and I left with having barely eaten anything. The situation was further exasperated by the rude waitress. We ended up paying the whole check (even the food we didn't order) and just left because we were tired of waiting for our waitress to come around to tell her about the extra items charged to us. With that being said, prior to these events I would have rated this restaurant five stars because parking is easy- they have valet and free street parking. The restaurant is nice and its got a nice design, decor, and nice rooftop bar. The food & drinks are great and fairly priced and the staff was exceptional and friendly- all except the one time. Now... I am not even sure if I can safely eat there which is obviously important if you have Celiacs. So, I can't say its even Celiac safe as I could before. That last experience may have been a one off, I am unsure, but 2 of the 4 times I ate there there were questions of if the dedicated fryer had been used to cook other items containing wheat.
