Service could have been better. When I was looking over the menu and I asked her questions. She was uncertain about a lot of things. Had a question about one of the dishes (protein), he told me she was a vegetarian. A few other questions I had she still was uncertain. I kept asking her can she go check with someone, to make sure. Eventually another waitress stepped in to answer 1 of my questions. She seem very knowledgeable and she was good. I'm aware someone may not have all of all the answers which is fine. She had a guide that was somewhat of a quick reference. It seem like she could have use a little more training or so. She brought out some chips and salsa. On the side there was some type of red sauce. I asked what type of sauce was it she just really a song and I want her to be certain. She didn't know if I was allergic or what. I asked her if she can check with the chef what it. It was like a house sauce with some lime juice (was not good). The street corn was not good at all. It was probably the worst streetcorner ever tried. On top they put a glob of parmesan cheese....waaaay too much. Next up my tacos came the presentation was really nice. However I had to pay extra for sour cream and the chef missed one taco all the hair was chicken no sour cream, cilantro or onions. When I decided I wanted a box. I ask if I can have some cilantro and onions to go. The waitress bought me cilantro and onions on an actual plate. I'm looking like what the heck I asked for it to go. The waitress told me this is what the chef gave me. I kind of was fed up at this point. I'm like it's common sense if he messed up why wasn't it corrected... Leslie when the bill came out I'm certain the total was $14, then eventually came to $11. I was just over the situation and wanted to leave..... but looking at the menu and also pictures on social media and the website some of the dishes look pretty good. I'm willing to give this restaurant another try but I will request for a another waitress. And for the record I saw the manager standing in the corner. I thought he would make his rounds and ask how was service...

Muriel's- you really let me down! After visiting a few years ago and enjoying the food, we decided to visit again after seeing pictures on social media of their COVID protocols. Unfortunately, it looks like they're mostly for show or were off their game the night we visited. When we arrived, a large group was ahead of us. None with masks and although they were turned away, they were never asked to put them on for the benefit of other patrons waiting in the entryway to be checked in. Our temperatures were taken, then we were escorted to our table on the balcony, passing countless guests wandering around maskless or with it around their chins. Somewhere I saw- maybe another review- the wait staff was gloved; they weren't when we were there. Our table was teeny tiny with teeny tiny chairs and a teeny tiny light that was completely pointless to even have on the table. We were greeted promptly and drink orders taken, drinks delivered and food orders taken, then pretty much forgotten. It took about 45 minutes for our appetizers to arrive and they were wrong when they did. The manager tried to force me to keep the shrimp and goat cheese crepes he originally brought and when I declined due to a slight allergy, he condescendingly explained the menu as if I had not already considered my options with an allergy in mind. My husband did enjoy the egg roll boudin and my house salad was skimpy, but good. I should have gone with my gut and ordered the pork chop like I did on our last visit, but my husband did and was very happy. I went with the half-roasted chicken and it was awful. It was only two wings with about 5 bites of completely dry and flavorless chicken. The mashed potatoes were watery, the serving of kale was the size of a quarter, and everything was drenched in the sickeningly Steen's syrup glaze. Our desserts- flourless chocolate cake and bread pudding- were good, but for me, the meal couldn't be saved. There was also a large party indoors and many attendees kept coming outside to smoke. That's fine- smoke doesn't bother me- but we were the only ones on our side of the balcony. They could have easily gone towards the other end to blow smoke in each other's faces instead of ours, take selfies, and be distasteful. Despite the manager seeing them out there as he was delivering food to patrons around the corner from us, they were never asked to move for social distancing/COVID purposes. Our drinks were never refilled, our waiter disappeared (but miraculously showed back up to get the bill and his tip!), and we were never asked if the food was to our liking. Out of our entire trip to New Orleans, this was the only place we didn't feel safe and COVID protocols weren't being followed. I expected more, not only from a fine dining restaurant, but also based on previous reviews. Maybe it was just an off night, but it was off in every way.

The manager was extremely insensitive. After finishing the apple spring roll dessert I noticed my throat start to close, we searched for the waitress to ask if it contained nuts (something I know I'm allergic to) and she said she would check with the kitchen. It contained two tree nuts, walnuts and another - I was too worked up with my reaction to remember the second. The manager approached our table shortly after I told the waitress I'm very allergic. I read menus very carefully and check all the ingredients listed but THEY DO NOT LIST NUTS ON THE MENU, one of the top 7 food allergens. The manager then tried to make it seem like it was my fault I ingested the tree nuts. I told her I already took benadryl to which she replied "oh then you should be fine, I have an allergy too" I was not fine and our allergies are not the same. Before I could explain to her the severity of the situation I was throwing up in the bathroom and racing home in time to use my epipen. The manager did not act professionally at all and was extremely disrespectful towards me and my medical emergency. I will not be returning and I will warn others with allergies of the dangers they may face at Dooney's Pub.

I was very excited to visit here, as I have been told that it is some of the best pizza in St. Louis. Well, just goes to show that St. Louisians just don't know what they're talking about when it comes to pizza. This pizza is NOT Chicago style, even though it claims to be. We had a mushroom and green pepper pizza, and the vegetables on the pizza tasted like dirt (like mold). The sauce is certainly interesting, but nothing exceptional. . . In fact, it reminded me a little bit of vomit. Harsh, I know, but I'm serious about my pizza. Okay, okay, so maybe my review is tainted by the fact that I lost my appetite while waiting for it. The place is a dump. The area we sat in (booths in the corner) smelled like pee...and to top things off (while we were waiting), a mouse came out into the middle of the room and sat for a while and stared at us. When we told the guy who brought us our pizza about it, he said "Yeah, we know about him." Health code violations galore, for sure. I was so excited to like this place, as some reviewers say the pizza is better than Pi or Dewey's. No. Not at all. We will never be back. I'm so glad we didn't get food poisoning.

We found this on YELP, and decided to give it a try, since it was an easy walk from where we had lunch. Nice to find a spot we can both enjoy the beverages!! The walk down the brick alley was pretty cool, and we were the only customers, so got the full attention and service of the folks at the bar. The bar itself was one of the coolest reclaimed wood bars we've seen. The decor was neat, as well, and the children's table with coloring books was a nice added touch. Not knowing what to expect fro. The mead (we have had horrible tasting mead and some pretty fantastic mead), we asked lots of questions. The staff were both VERY knowledgeable and helpful and patient. We decided on 4 of the meads ($21 for four 2 oz samples, but at 14%...that's all that's needed!). The first one i sampled, Black Forest... Oh, my god. It was like a chocolate port, but it didn't give me hives! Absolutely fantastic!! The others were very tasty, as well (Cab Ride 95 tasted like a slightly sweetened Cabernet...again without the side affects I have from red wine). My husband liked the Cilice the best..hints of bourbon! Definitely a MUST visit!!! They only sell locally online, bummer. We would love to enjoy these beverages on a regular basis!!

Chunky, sour, RANCID ranch dressing. They forgot to give us half our order and when we called they didn't seem to care. Can't believe someone would actually pour this into a container and sell it. They clearly don't care if people get food poisoning at this location. After many phone calls they offered us $4 in cash if we drove ALLLLL the way back to pick it up ourselves. I don't want to be a Karen, but really? Food was cold and soggy when we came home an hour later trying to fix THEIR mistake. Couldn't eat, too disgusted. :(

I came here one night after dinner and waited 10 minutes for a single cookie. The person in front of me asked if the spatula the cashier was using had peanuts on it since she is allergic and the cashier simply shrugged her shoulders, though she did end up getting a new spatula. There were 2 people in line, including myself, and the cashier just went into the back for 5 minutes and was yelling about something while we listened. When she returned, she didn't apologize for the wait and was very rude. She did not smile the whole time I was there. I had the macadamia nut cookie which was good but definitely overpriced. I would not recommend.

Not bad and not great. It's a neat place and the interior is fantastic. Love the tropical beach look to it. The check-in desk is a hammock hung between two palm trees. The CiP that was in Bloomington is now a HuHot and has been one for quite sometime. While here, we had a party of 14 people. I had the Cheeseburger in Paradise which is a burger on a housemade roll with pulled pork and onion straws with I think pepper jack cheese. I don't eat cheese, so I requested that to be left off. There was no mention of mushrooms on the menu, but I found a couple on the burger. I have a mushroom allergy, so this very much concerned me, but I think I caught them before I ate it. The fries were good. Nice hot and salty. I also ordered a side of the gumbo. Oh my gosh. That was incredible! I loved it! Our cups went dry a couple times, but I think our group was larger than the server anticipated. She did fine considering. Overall, it was good. I'd go back. Sadly, we boxed our leftovers and forgot them!! That was a lot of food we left behind. We will remember them next time!

A couple months ago I went thru the drive thru. Got a sandwich, fries and a drink. Ended up getting food poisoning. Contacted Chick Fil A Corporate and they responded that the store owner would contact me. The owner never contacted me... The Health Department gave this location an Unsatisfactory. I've been going to Chick Fil A since the early 1980's. I will never go back..,

My boyfriend and I came to this restaurant for our anniversary, I wish we really had the best experience but unfortunately we did not. It started out great, very friendly service and welcoming. Fast seating with no reservation, inside. When seated, took about 20 minutes to be greeted. Meanwhile looking over the touch less menu what drinks we wanted we also were ready to order appetizers and entrees. When server finally greeted, Jorge our server, asked if we had any problems with the touch less menu we said no and he continued to bring physical menus. When received menus, it took about 10 min to order our drinks, appetizers, and entrees. I had mentioned no mushrooms (allergic) and entree still arrived with mushrooms. My boyfriend and I had suspected our order would be off due to no notations of complete order. After the mistakes, we flagged down Ania, let her know our situation and our experience thus far. She immediately listened and took action to make sure our experience was turned around. Our experience was definitely turned around with the help of the wonderful Ania and the genius chef. The view is great and a beautiful setting.

Love the drinks, it's so tasty, but as this covid19 happening, people are allergic to cash, I was doing coffee run for my ladies at work, i was given cash by everyone, and i'm paying cash myself, for me i don't have a debit card to use, i have cash and my account doesn't have some mula on it, so i like to pay cash. I go through the drive through and says "We Do not accept cash." so i'm in the middle of a drive through, where there's cars behind me, so i can't back out and leave, at that point, too late, so they don't accept cash. is cash not a legal tender no more? so why not take cash? just wash your hands after you touch the cash, simple as that. So i have to leave and waste my time going to the line! very disappointed at dutch bro's! Cash is like a gold.

Worst service ever. After 20 minutes we finally got some attention. My glass had boogers on it. I posted a picture I'm not being dramatic; that's disgusting. I ordered a burger without a bun and said dairy allergy. I also asked for avocado but got charged and didn't get this. I got a bun but I'm not trying to eat that because butter on it. This was to go so my dinner just fries. So my guy isn't allergic to anything he tried it but it's WAY OVER DONE burger. Absolute not worth it. He said that's the worst hamburger. Staying at the hotel nearby and late night food after work was the only option. Just don't come here for food or expect good service. Avoid this place.

This is my first review in half a decade. I am writing this review as I lay on the bathroom floor. I just received a grub hub delivery and ordered seafood. The seafood is was so horribly spoiled that I am suffering from the worst case of food poisoning I've ever had. Tried to call and alert the owners but they couldn't care less. They already had my money. Do not go to this place. I am feeling as sick as I've ever been. So so sick right now.

Horrible food. Gave me food poisoning and when I called to let them know, they did absolutely nothing. It's been days now and upon originally calling the cashier told me "I will talk to my boss to see what we can do to compensate you". I still have the receipt till this day. I said that sounds good to me, mind you I told her I didn't want anymore food. At this point I don't trust it. Never got any type of response. You wanted a honest review, here you go! Such a shame, waste and disappointment. Don't eat here unless you want to get sick and then do nothing about it.

This is hands down the WORST food I've had in months. I only walked in there because it was late and I was starving .Everything was stale or overcooked, the tortilla though freshly made was soggy and had a weird mouth feel, the rice had probably been sitting there for days. One bite at the burrito and I knew had I eaten it all I would have been food poisoned.

Horrible experience! Blue Plate almost killed my daughter... Literally. I'll keep this short... I warned them of my daughters deadly all nut allergy in the beginning of service, even asking what oil was used for chips she had gotten. And then ordered chocolate ice cream for dessert. Well after my daughter ate a good portion of ice cream, her grandmother goes to taste some and we realize they have given her chocolate peanut butter ice cream. We ran out luckily down the street to her pediatrician, as she did have a severe reaction and could've died! It was the utmost scariest day of my life. And for Blue Plate to even try and tell me that they try to tailor their restaurant towards allergies is a joke!!!! Even if they have a child with an allergy, (so they told me) well their accident almost caused my child's life. And therefore I don't recommend anyone go there if the head chef/owner himself can't be responsible for not knowing what he is keeping in his kitchen.

Was there last night ask for no tomato on my sandwich. Sandwich came out with tomatoes. Ask for sandwich to be taken back . It was they pulled tomato's off the sandwich and gave it back to me . Not thinking ate a piece realized there was tomatoes still on it . Ended up in the hospital. I have a food allergy to raw tomatoes!

This is a great place to go if you want to throw up that is. I've ate at many Mexican places and this is by far the worst I do not recommend going here I would go to Bruegger's next-door to get something to eat . I now have food poisoning from this Nico's

I came here last year and went home feeling sick. The morning after I was hit with severe food poisoning. It was either the beef noodle soup or the pasta salad I bought from the arbor. I'm gonna go with the the noodle soup. Onto the food: expensive. However if it was tasty I would be more forgiving. The broth was greasy and I swear those noodles are spaghetti. Seriously now ? If I had to choose, I'd stick with panda. And this is coming from a chinese girl.

Went there to try something new and I got food poisoning so not so good. Customer service was just okay. Don't think I'll give that place another try or even the food it's self. I get a little grossed out thinking about Asian food now.

We ordered Papa John's for lunch one day. I am gluten intolerant so I tried their gluten free BBQ chicken pizza. It was just okay. The crust was very over-cooked and inedible at the top. The rest of the pizza was okay. Nothing spectacular here.
They have gluten-free pizzas (yay!); but they're small and coupons don't apply . . .

Last night wasn't my first time at La Mulita. In fact, I was really excited to go visit for Indy Taco Week because I've had their chicken tacos and shrimp tacos before and they were both good. This time was different, though. The (chicken) tacos were dry and just not that tasty. And now, I'm still (at 4PM the next day) fighting off what I think to be food poisoning (won't go into details, but google helped me self-diagnose). I really hate to leave a negative review, but I didn't eat anything else yesterday and as of right now, I'm not sure I'll be revisiting. On the bright side, the guacamole is really tasty and so is the Mezcal Mule. And the service isn't bad, either.

If you can avoid this place at all costs, please do unless you want bad service and food poisoning. My family and I came here for a wedding a couple weeks ago and we were excited to see this wonderful place that had a rustic vibe with great food. The area that they use for events was nice, definitely a little country, exactly what the bride wanted. We were given a drink ticket to use at the bar but I wish they would have brought that to the area where we were, because we basically had to wade through people at the outside/bar area and it definitely brought the experience down... because the bar area was disgusting and compared with the reception area, it was in disrepair. We were served a salad with a ligonberry dressing tableside, which I only took one bite of, and then it was a buffet of their tri-tip, chicken, vegetables and mashed potatoes. The food was just alright, nothing I would rave about (maybe the tri tip in a sandwich is better..?) but the service from the bar was terrible! The bartender was quite rude when we tried to use our drink ticket and told us we owed her 50 cents because I wanted a pineapple and rum and my husband said all he had was a credit card and she told him he had to buy $10 worth of drinks to use it, then took his card to "keep his tab". I went back five minutes later with a buck to get his card back, to which she told me he had bought a drink for someone and the total was now $8.50, giving me attitude the whole time. My husband and father-in-law went back to dispute this but she ignored them and kept saying he had bought someone a drink... I think she had charged his card on accident since her "method" of holding cards for tabs was throwing them on a small enclave with the bottles of alcohol. If that wasn't bad enough, two days later, 70% of the family was vomiting and feeling terribly ill and the bride calls to say that many of the other guests have been sick and that there was food poisoning at the venue... They contacted the health department and apparently this isn't the first time this has happened. So overall, I would have given this place three stars for ambiance and food taste, but minus those for lack of customer service from the staff and from becoming ill. If you want to hang out with bikers in a dirty bar and receive horrible service and possibly poisonous food, this is your place.

DO NOT EAT HERE!! I have lived in New Orleans for 25 years and tried this place out being its pretty new for us here, my boyfriend had the roast beef po Boy and ended up with food poisoning for 48 hours. Which didn't surprise it as we looked back at how our meal went, our server was dressed like it was Saturday morning and he was home watching cartoons, he would come out in between doing things and smoke cigarettes, of which I'm pretty sure he didn't have time to wash his hands between running back in to get something. The bartender chick is pregnant and also coming out to some cigarettes every 20 mins. Smoking is actually illegal inside restaurants and bars in New Orleans and outside the door to an establishment so having them come sit at the outside dining table next to us while we were eating was nasty and rude! I drink top shelf tequila and know the taste difference, I drink Don Julio and know the taste anywhere. I ordered a shot and it tasted like rubbing alcohol, it was NOT Don Julio, for sure! I said something to the guy to double check he had my order right and then the service got rude and went downhill from there. We asked for our check and when we paid we waited for change for 15 mins, with only 4 other tables of people at the place. I ask him for the 2nd time for my change back and he says it's close enough with the tip included and did he really have to get off his ass from smoking a cigarette and go get change for that. My bill was $32.14, I gave him $40. I surely wasn't leaving a 22% tip for this kind of shit show, and don't need my server telling me what they want me to tip them. I don't know where these clowns are from, or where the owners are from but you do not need this experience on your time spent in New Orleans. GO EAT REAL NAWLINS FOOD ELSEWHERE!!

The food is very good and the wait staff are nice. One time i was there and the one thing that almost made me vomit was when i was trying to eat, and the busboy was mopping right near me and the wafting smell of ammonia literally made me sick. Why in the world would choose that time to mop up ?? Cant you wait to clean after everyone leaves?? But ive been there many times and that doesnt happen too often. The Greek managers seem a lil angry, which i dont care for. But the food and waitresses do enough to carry a good review.

For me, ippolito's was a give or take. My girlfriend and I are always on the lookout for the freshest seafood we can get our hands on in the city. Typically I get our fish from the terminal and has never disappointed me but this weekend we decided to do some sushi and sashimi at home. We decided to try and find some amazing seafood place to ensure we got the absolute best. We ended up at ippolito's and i honestly was just not as impressed as i thought i would be. I inquired if they had any tuna or salmon that they considered "sushi grade" and the guy pointed to what they had in the case. (in my opinion, if you want to have "sushi-grade" fish to sell to people for raw consumption, you should have it stored in a separate case because cross-contamination is a thing to consider) The whole store had a fishy smell. I realize everyone reading is like "oh c'mon dude are you serious? It's a fish market" but in my opinion, if you are bringing in fresh fish and appropriately cleaning, segmenting, storing, and most importantly discarding waste properly, you shouldn't have too hard of a time keeping the fishiness to a minimum. All in all, the cuts were OK, my sushi was OK but honestly it wasn't as fresh as i had hoped. Maybe i hit it on an off day but for me, living in Old City, it isnt worth the trek down to ippolito's.

Okay I went twice on a Sunday for breakfast and has the best waitress both times (same one- she carries many multi-colored pens). The Apple Pie pancakes were just the best. Then today I suggested it for lunch for with a friend- touting the delicious food and good service- but that was NOT our experience. The waitress truly acted like we were inconveniencing her by being there- they weren't that busy. I asked a question about food that was allergy related and she literally didn't let me finish my sentence before walking away. I ordered tomato bisque and my friend ordered lobster bisque- same soup- but one had chunks of lobster on top. To top it off- they forgot to bring my 5yo son's pancakes- we had to wait an additional almost 10 minutes for those. The lunch food was kind of just so so- as was the service. Now I won't be rushing back or recommending them for a get together anytime soon.

Well to say I'm disappointed is the least I want to say about this restaurant! First things first is the dizzying mix of cones and post to prevent you from parking in their lot is confusing at best. Second is the outside order takers show a small menu that I could not read and had to ask for them to hold closer. The little girl holding it was very polite and did her job great. I order a grilled chicken sandwich wit mayo pickle and lettuce what I got was a cold breast patty with lettuce Pale tasteless hothouse tomato with nothing else this chicken patty had been cooked way earlier and was actually cold. I pulled back around to request some mayo or mustard only to be told I could not come in the dinning room. I made it obvious I was angry about the food I got. He went and got the the mustard and came back handed them to me and turned and closed the door. No we're sorry your food wasn't correct or anything. I only wrote this because with all of the crap about Covid 19. That was way more important than serving food that is the correct temp to prevent food poisoning. This sandwich is around $6.00 at those prices you would think it would be hot. Don't eat here!

Welcome to the worst service but nicest Wendy's in Pinellas County. It's a physically beautiful building updated interior Wendy's in a A1 location just over the IRB bridge where the average home is well over 1/2 a million. The ghetto this is not. It's Covid stupid here and you are suppose to read the silly signs before entering with your mask. Once inside you will stand and wait as if you were invisible by the entire crew including the dishelved manager dripping sweat from his forehead into the French fries (who hasn't washed his uniform in 3 days ) all ignore you. Don't expect a " hello " or "welcome to Wendy's" "Someone will be right with you" or a smile from any of the crew on this particular day. One dirty look suggested ugggh...another customer. My bill comes to $5.01 ..... no we don't give change.... didn't you read the sign idiot?Yes I need that penny¡!!! And I can't give you 99 cents change for the 5 bill plus 1 dollar bill ( Even though I rang up your order with a small drink $1.79 more then the senior drink I ordered. ( Usually free... I am only getting ice water) but I am not going to argue with this new clown kid on the register...so I walked out to my car to obtain the precious penny. I don't want to deny a multi million dollar corporation .01 cent. Wishing to sit at a clean table I had to ask for napkins....clean my table from the prior customer. Then I asked for pepper and chilli seasoning... Here is the photo. I get 12 chilli seasoning packs...about 15 pepper packs and 7 crackers in a .o5 cent paper bag. Came to Muriel's as part of a girl's weekend. The ambience is great but we were cold all through dinner. They sat us right by a window/door which was very drafty. I ordered the Fleur de Lis drink while a friend ordered the Chartres Street Fog, neither was all that great. The flavors didn't blend well and just overall not very good. We did 3-courses. My friends started with gumbo while I had the crepes. The gumbo was not as flavorful as they had hoped. The goat cheese crepe stuffing was more texture and flavor of sour cream than goat cheese. The sauce was good and the shrimp delicious. For dinner we did the crispy onion salmon - it was okay, no real onion flavor. The portions were definitely not consistent from one plate to the next. Disappointingly, there were only six mushrooms which honestly was the most flavorful part. Some of my asparagus was undercooked as well. For dessert we chose the vanilla bean creme brûlée. I also had the mint chocolate chip martini, it was actually quite good, not too sweet and tasted exactly as expected! The creme brûlée is traditionally garnished with raspberry but here was served with a strawberry - which I'm allergic to and this was not disclosed on the menu. Not a big deal but I did feel quite bad for our server when I had to send it back. He was very gracious about it however. The service was really good and our server was incredibly nice.

Disgusting food and disgusting people. Our entire family order was wrong and when we called to see what they can do the attitude and immaturity was unfathomable. They tried to lie and say it was right and wouldn't let us explain yet we were starring at our food that was all wrong. Chicken also tastes like rubber so looking forward to food poisoning tomorrow. Should also add this was my families 3rd time ordering and every single time it was wrong... it's not worth it for crappy food and horrible service. Don't eat here.

I ordered mozzarella cheese fries and pizza with tomatoes, mozzarella, and garlic for take-out and by the time I took the last bite, my stomach was already turning upside down. I ended up with the worst case of food poisoning I can remember (and I am not someone with sensitive stomach). I spent the net day between my bed and the bathroom, which effectively ruined my last day in Philly. Ugh. Do yourself a favor and find a different place to eat (there's plenty in the area). As for the food, the pizza was merely ok while the cheese fries were foul. Absolutely awful.

Cute place--well lit, some seating, easy parking, and ok prices. My biggest hang up is that it's not consistent. I've been about a dozen times over 10 years, because it close to me. The shaved ice is nice--but the flavors often taste off, or there's no cone shape snowball top (like it's half made), and the service is slow--whether you're the only one in line or 5 ahead. There's usually about 5 tiny boppers inside...goofing off. There was one time when I think the ice or something was contaminated--worse food poisoning if ever experience in my life after eating a bubble gum snow ball. That's all I have to say about this snowball stand.

I had been planning to come here since I booked my trip. The host was nice and helped us sit upstairs in the balcony area. After waiting for 20 minutes by the bar, we transferred outside to our table. Two other couples came after us, and the waitress went and attended them before us. After making the bar tender/manager aware she came and apologized. We placed our orders, I ordered the chicken platter (the only one on the menu) expecting mashed potatoes and grilled chicken. After about 45 minutes the waitress comes out with my meal, chicken tenders and fries. So I tell her that was not what I had ordered and show her on the menu and instead of apologizing she's like "oh you wanted the gluten free chicken platter", I quickly responded "yes the only chicken platter on the menu". I was very disappointed with the service, and very sad since it was my mom's birthday and I wanted to treat her to a nice lunch. Not recommending nor coming back.

I was looking for a place that had gluten-free options for me and just a regular pizza for the rest of the family. My husband did a regular google search and saw Pats offered gluten-free pizza crusts. We have had their food in the past and were not excited to try them again. I was hopeful and I really missed pizza since going gluten-free. We ordered online, which was quite easy and you rack up points towards coupons for future purchases. I couldn't find a coupon so we did have to pay full price for the items. It cost over $40 for a cheese pizza, gluten-free pizza with two toppings, and fries. This is more than we spend on pizza. TD Alfredo's down the street pizza cost us $10 a pie with toppings. My husband picked it up and it was ready on time. He came home and we opened it up and the pizzas look pretty burnt and not very appetizing. The fries were made perfectly. The family enjoyed them. My family loves pizza and they just picked at the one pie we got for them. Normally, they finish a pie in one meal. The gluten-free free crust was like cardboard and I know it's very difficult to make a gluten-free crust taste good or like a pie crust, but I'd be better off just eating the cheese,sauce, and toppings alone. I would not recommend the pie crust. I am going to attempt making my own pie crust. It certainly would be cheaper and taste better. I am not sure how this place stays in business when their pizzas are so expensive and subpar to the ones in the area? The pizzas have gourmet prices and taste like cardboard with burnt cheese on top. Please go elsewhere if considering ordering a pizza. We have tried this place time and time again and there is no love in their food. We have been to most of the pizza places in the area and the staff have such wonderful customer service and put their heart into their food.
I wish they had more gluten free options for people with dietary issues. I was only able to choose from a couple of salads or grits so it was pretty disappointing.

I never write reviews, but I feel like this time I owe it to others who are going to be disappointed. We had high hopes for this restaurant. We were sat promptly, so that was great. No wait, but now we know why. To begin, our waiter was afraid she was going to get in trouble by management the entire time. You could tell from the moment we asked to sample a few beers before deciding. For example, she let one person at the table sample, the rest not (because she "might get in trouble"). Our actual waitress was very sweet and trying to do her best, but I could already tell the management was a mess from that moment. The food was OK, but some of it was a bit cold. We did enjoy the salad. Unfortunately, all to be remembered was the terrible management and employee service. They handled an issue we had very poorly. The blond manager walked over to hostess stand to laugh and look back at our table after we asked a simple question. You would expect managers to be more professional. We even had napkins "accidentally thrown toward our table" by employees. We will not be back. I should have taken advice from others to stay clear of this place due to food poisoning. One person in our party had stomach issues the rest of the evening after leaving. Looks like the staff is just as bad. I can honestly say that I have never had this terrible of an experience at a restaurant. We won't make that mistake again.

I want to call the previous reviewers delusional and harass them for reviewing Ray's so positively, but I just can't. There used to be a time where I got so excited because the portions were great and the prices were great. This time was five years ago, unfortunately. I don't know if they just had a few too many poor experiences with college kids or rude customers that left a bad taste in my mouth, but you get pretty poor service from the moment you come in. Things used to not be like this. I can handle bad service, but the last few times I went I ordered my usual Italian or Turkey belly buster and it came with the same amount of meat as a regular sandwich. On top of this, it was on a large loaf of bread that was stale (one of the times I went was lunch time, so it's not even like it was the end of the night and I got bad bread). I talked to my woman about Ray's - all she had to add was that her friend got food poisoning from them 5 years ago. If you spent any time in this shop, that's no surprise to you. Because of TCNJ and Rider, the Ewing area is pretty flush with other sandwich places. The best one is Tastees in Lawrenceville, just go there and give me a 'Useful' vote when you do as thanks.

Sure this place is cute and hipster-like but their food and staff aren't all that great. Overpriced small portions at it's finest - which caused me food poisoning - definitely not worth it. Me and my fiancé visited Riva and the staff treated us very poorly, we quickly felt the racism in the air. So if you want to eat Italian dog food and get treated like less than by some punk millennials then is the place.

Do not eat here if you are gluten intolerant- it is not the right choice for you! As most of us who have celiac disease or severe gluten intolerances know, hibachi is usually not a safe bet because of the soy sauce. I have been to some hibachi restaurants that have understood gluten intolerance and have made me a great gluten free meal. Tsunami, however, is not one of them. I called ahead of time to see if they would be able to make anything gluten free or if I should just eat something beforehand (was going there for a birthday party). The girl who answered the phone said sure they could make me plain rice instead of fried (okay) and just cook everything without the butter and oil (hmmm....made me wonder if she just thought gluten free meant "healthy"). I told her the real issue would be the soy sauce and would it be possible to cook my food in the back without soy sauce and she said yes. At the restaurant, I ordered the food this way and the waitress seemed to understand. When the food came out, it seemed alright, but I was a little concerned they hadn't completely understood because the vegetables in particular tasted and looked like they had been cooked in soy sauce. I am not completely sure what happened in the kitchen but I know this- the meal was not even close to being gluten free. I became severely sick later that night and ended up in the emergency room because of the abdominal pain and burning skin (the abdominal pain was so severe I was worried I had appendicitis, stomach flu, or food poisoning- rapidflu ruled out flu, doctors said no appendicitis and once DH symptoms set in it was for sure gluten). If you are gluten free, just pass on Tsunami. If you're craving hibachi, take the hour drive to Disney and go to the hibachi place at Epcot where they understand gluten intolerance and take it very seriously. There you can have a delicious and safe gluten free hibachi experience.

If I had reviewed this place the first night I ordered delievery from here, I would have given them 5 stars. For being Chinese fast food, it was surprisingly really good. Better than anywhere else in this town. So good in fact that 3-4 days later I was craving it and ordered the exact same thing again. BIG mistake. Huge mistake! The plain white rice was not just cold, it was dry. You know, like leftover rice. I have made enough and eaten enough rice in my lifetime, that I can tell the difference. Okay, not a huge ordeal, I will just moisten it in the microwave. While I am waiting, I open the containers looking for my beloved pork buns. They were not the best I had ever had, but definitely the best I have had since moving to Tucson. I open everything up to discover that they hijacked my pork buns and put 4 cold, soggy, limp, dumplings in their place. Noooo! I hate dumplings!!! Ugh. My stomach starts to roll. I am not happy but I am still starving cause I haven't eaten all day, so I go to take a bite before putting them on my plate and immediately go to spit it out in the garbage. Beyond nasty! The rest go right into the trash. I then grab the rice out of the microwave and start to put the orange chicken on top. Weird, they are sticking together..... I go to put on the rice and see that the orange chicken is literally conjealing underneath. Like pectin or Jello. Ugh. My stomach rolls again. Crap. I am starving. I go ahead and heat it up so it is at least semi warn, and begin to eat. 3 bites in, and I am downright nauseas now and lose all appetite. In the trash goes the $25 dollars of Chinese food. It finally dawns on me..... The first night was good because it was obviously fresh having been made that day ...for the week. Tonight they just half warmed the leftovers from Saturday and threw in the dumplings because they were already out of the buns. Now Chinese leftovers are usually good if it was good the first night, HOWEVER, 3 or 4 days later? NO. Not even my Thai stepmother could make it so the leftovers still tasted good 4 days later. I am unhappy. And no longer even hungry. They just lost what would have been a loyal customer. Besides the fact, I do not order food delivered just to eat someone else's leftovers. I expect fresh food .... At least room temperature. I will not be ordering from here again, and my quest for CONSISTANTLY, decent Chinese food is over. I give up. It's just not to be had in Tucson....and I refuse to chance food poisoning again. The only reason I gave them more than one star, is because the potential was there. They just soundly blew it.

P.F. Chang's is one of those places that should be consistent, but it isn't. You would think since to-go orders are literally the only things they can do right now they would figure out a way to keep things fresh and hot, but everything was cold from our order. We picked the food up right when it was ready and only had a 10 minute drive home. We opened everything the second we got home and we TORE into it because we were so hungry and we were so disappointed. All of the hot foods were literally cold. Not even lukewarm...cold. The only reason I gave it 2 stars was because the salmon was cooked perfectly. It was cold, but it was yummy. The Mandarin Crunch salad was ok but they didn't have it all chopped up like they normally do and I tasted absolutely no mango in the whole thing which is disappointing because that's the best part of the salad. Honey crispy chicken was cold and soggy, the chicken lettuce wraps were ok but they didn't add any of those white crispies at the bottom which I look forward to every time I order the lettuce wraps. The pork dumplings were one of the most disgusting things I have ever eaten. I am so glad I tried it last because I took one small bite and almost threw up. It was cold, undercooked, and I think I bit my tooth off from some sort of rubber or maybe even a bone or something ground up in the meat. Spring rolls were good but kind of soggy but honestly the only truly edible part of the meal.

Nice staffs: host, busser and server This is not our first time eating at this place, but this time WE GOT FOOD POISON, NOT ONE, 'WE'. I wasted my time gently emailed them to warn about their possible contaminated foods. No one kindly enough to email me back; neither sorry nor thank you. So, take your risk. Enjoy your food

Went to Batch, Saturday, April 17th at 10:45am, during my Reno visit and was disappointed in the customer service. My experience was ruined by the lack of gluten free products and underwhelming service by the female at the register. Because of my food restrictions, I cannot have chocolate or gluten, I asked her if she could recommend gluten-free cookies and she said, "whatever is gluten-free will be labeled." I proceeded to ask about the pumpkin sandwich cookies, "is the filling chocolate or hazelnut?" She said, "chocolate!" Okay what about the cupcakes, she pointed to the small selection of chocolate gluten-free cupcakes. My friend was nice enough to take the drive from Spanish Springs to Midtown for me to try Batch, and this employee didn't even step out from the back of the counter to offer any advice or assistance. As we were leaving, I noticed the fridge had gluten-free strawberry macarons and pineapple cashew Paleo bars. We purchased cupcakes for my friend and the two items for me. My friend asked if she could have a bag and the employee said, "we don't have bags for the cupcake tray." Well how about for the two items?! No receipt was rendered or offered, no thank you for shopping with us, and no, "have a nice day!" It would have been better to have a machine, or robot at the register because this employee had zero interpersonal skills and wasn't pleasant what so ever.

Food good; service sucked. I just came back from breakfast at the stars from my initial visit. We were seated right away but the waitress had to be told to come to our table. Mind you the place was not that crowded at noon time. My wife ordered the BLT and I ordered the French toast with no almonds. The waitress never wrote our order down and my French toast was delivered with almonds on it. I'm not allergic to nuts so I just scraped them off, but that did piss me off. The waitress never checked on us and me and my wife were watching her yap it up at other tables. I'm not going to blame this on lack staff rather it was lack of effort on her part. Overall, I like the food but the service part needs leadership. Just one person's opinion...

My family and I had lunch at Rode's for the first time today ... and I do NOT recommend eating there if you have food allergies. Our server was fine, the decor was okay (sort of "country"), and my Waldorf salad was okay. However, I DO NOT recommend going to Rode's if you have food allergies or are on any kind of medical diet where you cannot eat specific foods. I have an anaphylactic food allergy and my mom is on a medical diet, which means that we cannot eat certain foods, period. We are super careful when ordering, and we aren't the type of people who ask for special allowances - we find things on the menu that we can eat and just verify that the foods we are allergic to won't come into contact with our food. I don't know if the service staff aren't knowledgeable about their menu items or if they are trained to essentially lie about what is in their food, but what my mom ordered from the menu was not what she received, and it was an issue per her diet. Instead of being gracious about the issue, the service staff doubled down that what was on her plate wasn't what it looked like. Here's the deal - if someone tells you that they cannot eat a specific food, don't serve it to them. If they are ordering something that contains that food, tell them. My parents and I aren't rude or difficult customers. My mom would have gladly had a different meal. What could have been easily fixed turned into a big issue. Never once did the manager come to our table or did the server offer to take her food back. Had that food come to me, I'd be in the hospital, possibly dead. I mean, honestly, if you own a restaurant, don't lie about what you are serving. I doubt we will do back. I cannot eat at restaurants that aren't forthcoming about what they serve their customers.
WOULD GIVE ZERO IF I COULD absolutely DISGUSTING I got the crawfish sampler and got food poisoning My boyfriend got a steak that looked and tasted like a TV dinner GROSS

Never have I felt so uncomfortable in an upscale restaurant. ALL the waiters were old, Italian men, most were rude and gave off a cold vibe. I feel as if they treated us differently due to my boyfriend and I being significantly younger patrons than their regular crowd. Anyways, I tried to substitute an item because of an allergy and was talked down on. I don't care what kind of business you run or what demographics you hit, but making your customers feel comfortable should be a top priority! The food was nothing spectacular, I could have gone to a pizzeria and gotten a pasta dish just as good. My boyfriend and I came here for a special five year anniversary and was left feeling uncomfortable and unsatisfied. The fact that the owner does not interact with google maps and care to apologize for bad reviews is truly telling of their customer service. Wouldn't ever return or recommend.

I asked for no veggies on my sandwich and the lady told me that it didn't come with any so I said thanks paid and when getting my order they asked if I want ketchup and I say yes please and when I got home they had put Mayo in my bag and purposely put veggies on my sandwich when I'm allergic..

Probably the worst restaurant experience I've had in a long time. We walked in it was pretty much empty (should have been my warning considering it was 5:30 on a Sunday) and order our food. We sit down and it took about 10 minutes for our server to even show up/in view so she wasn't busy with other tables. We get our drinks maybe 5 minutes after that. Our steaks arrive and off the gate they charged us for an extra shrimp skewer that we absolutely did not order but thankfully had got refunded on. Our steaks come, they are insanely tough, overcooked and WAY over salty. My potato was sitting on a pool of butter while a big ball of cold butter was placed inside it. She asked if wanted a refund and I said yes but asked if I could instead get salad bar. My boyfriend is now done eating and I still haven't received my refund or my okay to get salad bar so I tel them I'll just take the refund. We leave. I have an empty stomach and now my boyfriend has whats looking like some type of food poisoning. 0/10 recommended considering I've lived in Reno my whole life and this place use to be awesome. Oh yeah and we never even received a refill on our drinks. Won't be coming back.

This review is quite over due, but I'm in one of "those moods," so I felt it was necessary to speak my piece. After seeing the great reviews here, me and my partner thought we would give this place a try. The place just opened for the day and so we did not think much of it when there was no one inside. We both placed our orders (can't quite recall what we ordered; hence, not a very memorable experience) and waited a good 15-20 minutes. Someone else walked in after us and he got his order first (HUH?! We were there first..). Then, a little after that, my partner got his order. I finally got my order 5 or so minutes later...Not sure why it took so long to get my order, but realized when I got my sandwich, the female (I don't remember her name...which is probably a good thing) that made the sandwich, did not make it with "love." I ordered my sandwich with gluten free bread and I know the bread was frozen because the bread looked like it got attacked (the center of the bread was missing) in the toaster oven. I know this, because this happens to me at home IF you don't toast the bread evenly/long enough. I also forgot to mention, the restaurant was dirty! Mind you, this place just opened, so one would think it would be clean from people cleaning it the night before and/or the morning of; however, I had to wipe down our table as well as my seat before I felt comfortable enough to sit down. I could go on for days, but I have already spent too much energy on this place...not worth it and not worth trying again.

Every time I come to this location they're out of something. The past two times it has been chips. At 7pm on a Wednesday they're out of chips?? I don't understand why they never make more of whatever they're out of when they're still open another 3 hours. Most of the time they're out of fajita veggies. Two nights ago I had it delivered and received someone else's order. It had my name on it so it wasn't the delivery driver's fault, just whoever bagged it gave me someone else's order. Unfortunately, I'm lactose intolerant and the burrito bowl had cheese and sour cream all over. I love Chipotle, this just isn't a good location.

I recently ordered from this location around 840pm on a Tuesday. During my ordering I (in the notes section under my hoagie) I specifically stated "no mayo, oil and vinagar". The food arrived in the time they said it would and I sat down to eat. After a few bites I noticed something that tasted like mayo. I inspected my sandwich that I had clearly stated not to have mayo and it was covered. I am writing this from my hospital bed as I am allergic to mayo. As soon as I get out I will be bringing my lawyer and the hospital bill to this location. Be careful of this location!!! The lack of attention to detail could KILL!!!! I hope whoever put me in here learns from this.

Went for brunch. I was looking forward to it since I love the food in New Orleans and they offer a lot of gluten free options. The gluten free waffles were frozen waffles that you can get from the frozen food section in the supermarket! I'm suppose to pay $14 for that? The bacon was one step shy of burnt. The mimosas were very juice heavy, which is ok...I guess. We left and went to eat at the Reading Terminal. Never going back.

Years ago, I frequented this donut shop on my way home from work in the mornings. During this time, they began putting bacon on their maple bars and soon thereafter all their donuts tasted like bacon...this is because they fry the donuts in the SAME VAT OF GREASE in which they fry the bacon! This does not go over well when one's a vegetarian or perhaps has food allergies.
Very friendly service staff but the food was mediocre and the Decorations and vibe aren't very comfortable. Very few gluten free options.

Came here for a nice lunch, the hostess was to busy chatting up her BF to acknowledge anyone and after ordering from the gluten free menu the manger informs us they have nothing on the gluten free menu. What a nightmare this Applebee's is the only and I stress only good thing about this place was our server Brandy who tried so hard to make the experience a good one.....Hey Applebee's maybe you could employ managers who understand and enforce great customer service. Not ever coming back Chili's will be my go to place from now on!

Warning: food poisoning!!! My wife and I have done takeout here half a dozen times. Last Friday, we ordered 3 dishes: general tso chicken, vegetable tofu and garlic eggplant. I started feeling dizzy after finishing our meal, but my wife seemed fine so I thought I was just dehydrated. Not. That night, we both fell ill: nausea, stomach pain and muscle ache... I forced myself to vomit twice through the night. Clearly we both got food poisoning from here (we didn't eat anything else together the whole day). The ordeal continued on Saturday. I can't even look at this place now. Eat at your own risk. Food safety is nonexistent here.

I have to say I'm highly disappointed towards this Cheesecake Factory location. My family and I went here on a Friday evening. The service was extremely slow, waiter overall was good. The food took so long to get to our table, that when it finally got there we immediately asked for to go boxes. But, when I finally got home which was late, my hot wings were RAW! Yes, you read that correctly my hot wings were very undercooked (very pink). It's now 2:36am in the morning and my stomach is killing me, pretty sure I probably have food poisoning. What a waste of money, and no I didn't continue to eat the food. I immediately threw it out! Party of 4

I called Courtney's restaurant yesterday to confirm that they had chicken and dressing that evening. What they actually served on Tuesday evening was chicken in gravy so when I got there I could not have chicken and dressing because of my allergy to gravy. In my frustration I had to settle for meatloaf which was not bad. I also bought the meal for my wife my son and his wife my other son and his girlfriend and a step-granddaughter. The restaurant was cold I guess in retrospect our next meal will probably be at a different restaurant.

I used to love coming here but I've been here four times over the past month and every time my order is wrong. I do not know what happed within a month but they have gone down hill. I have food allergies so it is very important that my order is made correctly yet Karma has failed to do so on multiple occasions now. If you have any food allergies or dietary restrictions do not come here as they will very likely mess up your order and potentially endanger your health.

Very good food but the bad service and quirky rules keep me from becoming a regular. First of all service is always awful. At these prices service should be prompt. Their rules regarding substitutions for food allergies are also strange. The first time my server substituted cucumber for pita due to allergy at no extra charge. The second time I asked for cucumber I was charged an extra $3 and never given the pita. If I knew I was being charged I would have just taken the pita home for a family member! The most aggravating incident came this morning while my boyfriend was sitting outside at a table having a coffee. The plain Hummus is on the coffee menu so after he packed up to leave he asked the server for a hummus to go (I'll slice my cucumber at home thank you very much). The server looked embarrassed and reluctantly said "no takeout after 11am." Really!!?? it's hummus, just put it in a plastic container. But to make matters worse, he was actually sitting at a table being served but as a normal human would, thought he could order after he finished his coffee and take it home. Would they rather he take up their table for another 20 minutes to eat one bite of hummus and then have it wrapped? That's fine I guess they don't need customers or our $8 for tahini and chickpeas. Their loss.

My first experience with Batch started off great with super helpful staff, but ended in minor disappointment. After putting in an order for 18 cupcakes for a birthday party, when I arrived on the day of the party my order was nowhere to be found. After a few phone calls it seemed that the woman who took my order either lost it or never turned it in. Thankfully I kept the receipt from when I paid, so the woman who was there on the day of pickup was helpful in putting together an order close to what I had originally wanted. Unfortunatley only one of the three types of cupcakes I had ordered were available, and another was in a gluten-free variety. Not the end of the world, but also not what I wanted to begin with. The cupcakes I ended up with were pretty good, although I can't say gluten free red velvet is quite the same. All in all, not a terrible experience, but I'm not inclined to return here. If I do I'll be sure to review and document everything to make sure this doesn't happen to me again.

My wife met a friend for lunch at Piccadilly Cafeteria on Friday, July 26, 2019; she has eaten the same meal many times before, including with this friend. Both have been nurses (bachelor and master degreed) for decades; my wife finally retired after 45+ years. A few hours after she came home, she became violently ill with nausea, vomiting and diarrhea with a temperature of over 101; she lost 6 lbs. in two days. She has spent years in health care and recognized the symptoms of food poisoning. When she called the manager of Piccadilly Cafeteria this morning, the manager was dismissive and told her to get a physician's opinion, which she will in a few hours. The manager claimed that no one had ever become sick at that site. While that is highly unlikely since the outlet has been there for years, my wife chose not to argue with her that it (a) probably not true and she was lying, (b) might not reflect people who did not know what food poisoning is, and/or (c) might not capture those who did not know how to file a complaint. This lack of sensitivity is unacceptable; Piccadilly needs to know that this quality of product breach will not go away.
They had me worried about food contamination issues as I saw what the cook was doing and cancelled my order.

OMG! Never again! Took a huge bite outta my fish taco and threw up...it was one big piece of breaded gristle...both tacos were just big pieces of breaded gristle...threw them both away. I live close to this place and have had enough bad experiences here that I won't go back. Yes, when it's good it's very good but when it's bad it is so bad I can no longer give them my $$$$$...the worst part is...they don't care.

This place sucked from start to finish. When we walked in, no one greeted us to tell us how things worked. And when I asked, they were super standoffish about telling me. Same thing upstairs with the person who brought our food (telling us nothing about silverware or drinks) and then at the bar when I inquired about silverware. Last but certainly not least, the pork made my husband vomit for 12 hours. Go somewhere else.

I wish I could give this place less than one star. Lemmie set the scene for you: it's Wednesday evening and my girlfriend and I have a midterm the next day. We look at each other and figure fine we'll get Chinese food so you know more time to study. We pull up Golden Chopstick and peep the review. Well it's meh reviews but we've been procrastinating all week so decide ok. All of the sudden one of the pictures has a staple in the food; this is red flag number 1. But you know we're poor dental students so we give it a pass. So we order the food and not only does it take an hour and 20 minutes to get to us, but they forgot her rice too. Red flag number 2. We got general tso's chicken and a veggie lo mein, you know a casual order. So I hit em up like fam, where is my girl's rice? Who the hell eats just the chicken. (My apologies if you eat just the chicken). They credit us for the rice and I'm like fine. So we eat the food and we're like ok it's what we expected. Fast forward to 2 hours later.... my guy when I tell you that there is no pain like the wrenching of your stomach and fever that comes along with it you gotta believe me. My girl dips into the bathroom faster than OJ on a publicity opportunity and locks up in there for the next 1.5 hours. My homie our toilet hasn't smelled the same since. I can't even put my cheeks down knowing what kind of fire and fury has gone into it. I'm chilling consoling my girl then all of the sudden it hits me harder than my african Mom after seeing me sit on the couch with shoes on... we need a new toilet. I had the veggie lo mein only with no meat and somehow still managed to get food poisoning just not as sever as my girl. So we lost 4 hours dying in the bathroom and probably failed our midterm. I would avoid this place at all costs fam, they need to have a health inspector come through and re-evaluate their cleanliness. TLDR: eats Chinese food, bland and not flavorful, gets food poisoning, fails exam. Avoid this place.

Today I ordered on Uber eats an el jefe burrito for my fiancée with no onions because he is allergic, 2 beef empanadas and my torta as a meal. I received one empanada that was CHICKEN. And he got onions and pico on his burrito. So I called and the employee wanted to argue and say he didn't see it and he didn't know but didn't even want to offer to remake it. I took it all to the store and had my fiancée go in. The employee told him they won't remake it, offer credit or refund even though almost the whole order was incorrect and I didn't receive my full order. I am disgusted better yet he threw a phone towards my boyfriend and was disgustingly rude. We love taco bus and go to the one in 54 and down off Hillsborough with no issues. I am officially turned off from taco bus.

Used to be one of my favorite places to eat until I had food poisoning from their chicken lunch special. Even worse I later discovered that two- three of my friends had a similar experience. We now stay completely away! Would probably recommend taco bus or las vallettas over this place (at least their you won't get sick)

We left so upset. My mom and I waited 20 minutes for NOTHING! We were excited to eat tacos, came to this food truck, and yes when I saw that it wasn't the normal women that were working I should've just went with my gut and left. Instead there was two teenagers. The male working the register was not paying attention. It was as if he was nervous or something. I repeated my order twice and he read it back to me. I order 8 steak flour tacos. We waited, and waited..., when we finally were called, something told me check and sure enough....I was appalled to NOT only see the wrong food in my boxes, but food Im allergic to. SHRIMP TACOS!!! I got my money back and left. I AM CURRENTLY STARVING, driving to another place to get tacos. Didn't know it was this difficult. I see why they need a new cashier. To the owner: if you need real help, let me know. I'm bilingual and have food exp. This crap definitely won't happen while I'm taking orders. Im sorry for this review, but it the truth, and I'm so mad. I'll come back another day Bc I truly like the flavor and convenience.

When I ate here we had the traditional 7 course meal. Some of the cuisine was not to my taste, it was more traditional and perhaps more for the adventurous eater than I was used to. However, what really disappointed me was the severe case of food poisoning I got after eating here. I was sick starting in the night and it caused me to miss work the next day. I will not be coming back, and sadly would not recommend this restaurant. Regardless of the shortcomings of the meal, the service was really excellent.

Worst McDonald's experience I've ever had. I had ordered a chicken sandwich but got a burger instead. I was in a rush so I just accepted the mistake but half way through I noticed there was mold on the bun! Also ordered 10 nuggets but only received 7! These idiots can't even count. The staff are UNBELIEVABLY RUDE and slow, even by McDonald's in North Philly standards. Going to cut this review short because I'm pretty sure I have to go vomit now.

Can I leave zero stars? Discriminating prejudice staff. Fully vaxed and forced to wear a face mask had to pay $30 for a shitty meal and forced to pickup food and bring it to table after tipping. Food was very bland with no flavor. Just because it's vegan doesn't mean it has to be bland. I'm allergic to gluten and soy so all their meat substitute options didn't work for me, should have more options L. So again I ask can I leave zero stars?

You know...as "famous" of a place as this is....it only has 3 stars. I'm just going to throw that out there. I have grown up around Nashville and this was my Mom's FAVORITE place to come if we were in Nashville. On a random night, before a concert, etc. I'm not sure why it was her favorite because EVERY time I have ever eaten here I end up throwing the food up afterwards....just saying. (and i grew up with no food allergies) come again, maybe that's why it was her favorite...haha It seems like a promising place, but I have always gotten sick and there is always a very large wait time here. In my opinion it just isn't worth it.

I know I'm not in the majority but I was super disappointed here for a very specific reason. Em J's boasts to be gluten-friendly, advertising that they have gluten free pancakes, waffles, breads, rolls, wraps, desserts, etc. My daughter and I are both gluten free by necessity so we were excited to go. They had two soups that day both of which were gluten free. It was a rainy day so we said "great! soup and grilled cheese!" Well, the basic grilled cheese sandwich is $8.00. A little pricey for two pieces of bread and a few slices of cheese with a smear of pesto, but okay. The kicker came when we were told that it would be an additional $3.00 per sandwich for gluten free bread. Which means we would be eating $11.00 grilled cheese. Sorry, but that's ridiculous, and if you are going to toot your horn about being gluten friendly, then don't hold your gluten free customers to highway robbery surcharges. Even our server agreed it was unfair and said "I don't know why the owner charges so much." To top it off, my "Mexican lime chicken soup" was a $5.00 cup of broth with a few threads of chicken (not shreds -- they were more like threads) and a couple chunks of onion. No black beans, no corn, no rice. I asked for maybe some cheese or avocado, but that would be another added charge. So for $10 we had a cup of tomato soup and a cup of chicken broth and weren't offered even crackers. Won't be back.

I used ordered from this dump i ordered a double cheese burger some cookies & fries i threw up all theses items because they were cold & uncooked the cookies were raw & undone they weren't brown & golden they were light & disgusting.

Our experience here may not be the usual, but I wouldn't go back. I read a review saying they have gluten free crepes, but the girl working there said they sometimes do but not always (??). I made a point to ask about gluten free, so I assume she understood that I was gluten free. They don't have gluten free crepes, okay I can order something else. I ordered breakfast tacos, but they're out of avocado (it's 10 am?? How are you already out of a huge part of your menu). But it's fine I'll get over it. I order tacos and a (hot) coffee. She makes our drinks, and makes the drink iced. Hm okay, also whatever fine. Then she brings out our food and the tacos are in flour tortillas (not gluten free). Then I ask if I can just have some corn tortillas so I can transfer the meat to a corn tortilla. And they don't have corn tortillas either. Then we left without touching our food (not that I could eat it anyway) and didn't get what we ordered after a frustrating and somewhat rude ordering experience. I wouldn't recommend, but they probably have good coffee and it's a nice environment.

Tried this place out. They have lots of options, not just crepes but corn dogs and pretzels, which is nice. The atmosphere is weird, lighting is insufficient and it is very cramped with dusty shower curtains between booths and random stuff everywhere like papers and empty boxes of Nutella stacked, random dusty stuff. The service was quick if somewhat ambivalent. We ordered kids meals, and instead of offering the different options we had to ask for what options they came with as far as sides and drinks. It seemed haphazard. The plastic silverware they brought us for our savory crepes had chocolate smears on it so we grabbed new silverware. Our kids didn't care for the corn dogs but the pretzels were good. The drink selection was great though they didn't seem to know their own drink options. But the main event- the crepes- were a disappointment. All the crepes were undercooked. We left worried that we'd get food poisoning and not planning to return. Wanted to try this place for a while, was hoping to love it, but we left feeling let down.

This is a tough one. I want to love the place for its originality and sense of fun. And I have to say that the maple syrup and bacon glazed donut was the best donut I think I've had in my life. So major high marks for that!! But the other choices were eh....just okay. Puppy chow was creative but not amazing and the gluten free options while ambitions and accommodative to gluten-free life leaders came up short for me. The place itself, as has been noted in prior reviews, has absolutely zero ambiance and offers no place to sit outside. Even a little bench or some fading chairs would be nice. So I give it three stars. Great maple syrup and bacon donut and good coffee too. But the lack of a chair or bench along brings it down for me.

Sure this place is cute and hipster-like but their food and staff aren't all that great. Overpriced small portions at it's finest - which caused me food poisoning - definitely not worth it. Me and my fiancé visited Riva and the staff treated us very poorly, we quickly felt the racism in the air. So if you want to eat Italian dog food and get treated like less than by some punk millennials, In Riva is the place.

I have been wanting to try Denim since it was at its old location in Cherry Hill, but never got a chance. We finally got to try Denim at it's new location in Haddonfield. I had a good feeling walking in here and seeing a portrait of Anthony Bordain on the wall. I felt confident I was going to get a good meal if the owners/chef looked up to him! Oh and we were seated next to a picture of Britney and JT in their iconic matching denim outfit. Cute. I also really liked that you had the option of the $40 pre-fix menu. You were able to ~pretty much~ order whatever you wanted on the menu. Some things were an up charge of $1-$2. No big deal. Appetizer: I got the goat cheese croquettes and my husband got the pumpkin gnocchi. The croquettes were good.. fried but not too heavy. The goat cheese was mild. The lavender honey was delicious The only critique is the pieces of lavender in the honey were off putting in some bites. The lavender infused honey would have been best IMO. My husband said he really enjoyed the pumpkin gnocchi! Before ordering the appetizers/dinner I told the waitress I had a nut allergy so please do not include hazelnuts on the croquettes, peanuts on the short ribs or nuts in any of our dishes (as we like the share). The croquettes came out with no nuts and when the gnocchi came out I asked if the sprinkle on top was nuts to make sure but she said it was toasted Parmesan. She assured me she included on our ticket to not include any nuts on order. It was Parmesan and it was yummy! For dinner I ordered the Korean short rib. There was a sprinkle on top of the short ribs where I just assumed it was the same Parmesan as the pumpkin gnocchi and I figured if I asked this waitress one more time about nuts she was gunna lose it. So anyways a take a bite.... yep, sprinkled with peanuts. When I called the waitress over to tell her about the nuts she was apologetic and ran it back the the kitchen and they promptly brought me out another dish. The short rib was sweet and super tender. My husband had the south Philly steak frites. Oh my gosh. I wanted to trade plates with him. The steak was so tender. Topped with savory cheese and onion. Cooked perfectly. My only critique is the fries that came with it seemed like run of the mill frozen fries. The dish would have really been elevated with some gourmet pommes frites type taters. For dessert my husband had the bananas foster bread pudding. He pretty much ate it all before I got a bite so safe to say it was delicious. I had the Apple pie type dessert (I forget the name). It was HUGE! And put together beautifully. The dough was buttery and really held up with all the apple-cinnamony deliciousness stacked on top. My only critique is that it would have been perfect if the apples were peeled. Tough apple skin made some bites unappetizing. All in all, we would go back to Denim. Maybe in the spring to see a new seasonal menu. I was frustrated by the nuts debacle especially after being so upfront and after being assured by our waitress. I get that mistakes happen. Luckily my allergy to peanuts is not anaphylaxis. But others with but allergies wouldn't be so lucky.
Consider this a warning. I had food poisoning and was sick for 24 hours after eating a chicken sandwich from this place. They shouldn't even be in business.
Horrible service! My quesadilla looked like chIcken pot pie and the server did not want to take it back after I requested for it to be returned. My daughters got FOOD POISONING as well. Do not visit!

This used to be my go to place for Thai food. Hadn't been there in over a year so I stopped in. Ordered my usual favorite Paneng Curry. Was shocked when it looked like a pickle salad! The majority of it was large chopped up pickles or zucchini, hard to tell which. Looked unappealing but also didn't taste nearly as good as it used to, even after I sorted though all the zucchini/pickles. But much, much worse was the fact that I got food poisoning from eating it! I was sick vomiting and had the runs for two straight days! I had only eaten bland food the previous day so I know it was the chicken paneng curry that caused it. My son later told me he no longer goes there because of bug infestation. I won't be back. Ever.

We used to LOVE this place, but it's gone really down hill. To start, our waitress wouldn't let us get a word in edge wise to ask questions or even place our order. Every time she came to our table she wreaked of cigarette smoke and the perfume she used to cover it up with. One of the people at our table, has a sever corn allergy and the waitress brought a dish out that was covered in corn kernels. Lastly, she charged us for food that we didn't even receive; so we had to send the check back. The food over all was mediocre at best. Save your money and don't go here.

The food was average, but not out standing. It's quality is the only reason I can give a star at all. The service was the worst I've had in a decade. This applies only to our waiter Michael, however. The bus staff was friendly and helpful. Quite delightful in fact. I asked about a gluten free menu, Michael just named a couple of selections and said, in a very condescending way, if I was going to have the pasta he had to know in advance to get it started. His attitude the entire time was that we were a nuisance and he only waited on us because he had to. I asked about the grilled pork and whether or not there was any breading. His reply, "Well it's SAYS grilled." I replied that I have to ask these questions because I never know what a restaurant will do with their recipes. I settled on the pork and asked for the gf pasta on the side with olive oil and parmagiana. When the meal came and he asked if we wanted cheese I said yes. He proceeded to toss it to my plate scattering it all over the table and into my lap. He did the same with my mother and fiancee. I asked for more since he stopped without asking if I had enough. More cheese thrown at my plate. Oh, when he first came to the table with the wine menu he tossed it on top of our bread basket. There was so much I can't even remember it all. We will never go there again. He may be the bad apple of the bunch, but he's the apple we got. (And for other gluten free people...they have an upcharge of $3 for gf pasta. It's the only restaurant I've been to that's done that. Also keep in mind they have gf pasta, but ALL their red sauces have flour in them, according to Michael. Hence olive oil on my pasta.)

My wife and I went in last night with my daughter and her husband. We were seated by a very friendly young lady that was great at her job. After sitting for quite a while a young waiter came over to take our drink and appetizer order. I grew a moustache while waiting for him to return. After a long time he finally returned with our iced tea and soda. We were told he'd be right back. I don't believe that word means what he thought it meant. After a long time he returned to take our order -- minus the appetizers. Now, for another long wait. Drinks were long-since empty and no sign of waiter. We finally complained to one of the people. The young man finally returned, apologized and said it was because he was "in the middle of a Irish coffee situation" and our food would be right out. Again, I don't believe that phrase means what he thought it did. The mgr. came over and asked how we were doing. We told her and she said she couldn't find our waiter. He finally appeared and we told him we needed our drinks refilled. He apologized and said our food would be right out. I asked if it would be in our lifetime. Food finally arrived.
