Some of my favorite dishes include the calamari Sicilian, eggplant tower, grilled romaine salad, eggplant or chicken parm, penne vodka, pumpkin ravioli, sweet potato gnocchis. Their crab cake is my favorite -- served over sautéed spinach and vodka sauce. I'm getting hungry just naming the things I love at Scannichios. Some of these are specials and some are staples, but you can always ask the staff for recommendations as well! Save room for dessert (I suggest the italian iced cream sandwich with Nutella and hazelnut gelato.). I saw a negative review from a girl with celiac and honestly that's wild, I have a good friend w celiac and she wouldn't even consider eating at a restaurant unless they could guarantee no cross contamination of gluten (nearly impossible for an Italian restaurant that has been running since before celiac was a thing). Soooo I guess i would say I would not recommend for celiacs or for vegans.

I'm so done with this location. Upon entering the sandwich shop we ordered one vegetarian sandwich. We decided to order another but unfortunately I opened it and it had turkey on it so we returned it. When the waitress was making the sandwich we noticed that she was putting it through the oven with bacon. We informed her that it was not OK for us to be around or our food to be around bacon or any sort of pork and she just continuously asked was I allergic. We told her it did not matter whether I was allergic or not we just told her we could not have that pork around our food. So then the waitstaff got annoyed and decided that she would call the police. It's just this simple and cut and dry she decided to call the police because she was going to have to make the sandwich again. There was no cursing of any sort if anything at all the wait staff was being extremely rude and aggressive toward the customer that simply could not have a sandwich near pork products. This is always used as a scare tactic by white wait staff concerning but customers. This is done over and over again and it is absolutely ridiculous and less stop. That young lady needs to be fired promptly and I'm going to make sure that she is fired promptly. We will never eat at that restaurant again. This was at 7:20 PM on July 5th 2018

Under new and sleazy management. The food appears to be a good deal and it does taste fairly decent, but BE CAREFUL. The waitstaff may offer you a beverage, acting as though it is on the house, but it is actually going to show up on your bill. Worse: you may find yourself sick the next day with food poisoning. To those with allergies: eat carefully. Although there is a sign saying that you can inquire with the staff regarding the presence of allergens, don't expect the staff to actually know if there are any allergens in the the food! If you have a problem during your visit, don't expect to receive the appropriate level of hospitality you would expect from staff in the restaurant industry. Instead, you will be treated as though you are stupid. During our visit, the bathroom door was broken and did not lock properly. One of the girls went to the bathroom and had the unfortunate experience of being walked in on. When confronted with this problem, the manager insisted that this did not happen to her and did not even apologize for the embarrassing event. The meager difference in price between Tandoor's buffet and Sitar's buffet does not warrant my return visit to Tandoor.

From the website I had expected the restaurant to be fine dining. It has more of a brew pub atmosphere. Once seated, I was put off by being given a piece of paper and a pencil to write down my own order. They should rethink this approach. If you are "lavishing personal attention" on your customers as the website states, you shouldn't make your customers do the servers job. Our waitress was very friendly and accommodating. Most of the staff appeared to be well trained but still have their training wheels on since they have only been open a few weeks. We ordered the Charred Kale Salad which says it comes with a Sherry Vinaigrette and the waitress listed off all the different kind of salad dressing option (note to chef - I'm sure you didn't intend for this salad to have blue cheese dressing). We asked for the sherry vinaigrette on the side and it came soaked in it - we didn't finish it. The veggie burger was tasty but at $18 I expect perfection. The fries were fat, cold and limp and I didn't eat them. The bar is huge and they do have a very extensive collection of wine and spirits. Our cocktails were well mixed but inconsistently garnished i.e. I ordered the same drink twice and one had a garnish and the other didn't. Details. It's a great place for a large group as they have the space and the menu offers a variety of option for vegetarians, vegans and the gluten free. It was busy and loud so not ideal for a romantic evening out.

I'll never eat at one of these again, it was my first time trying yesterday me and my gf stayed up past 6 am with major stomach cramps bloating terrible gas built up all off of one burrito each I got steak she got chicken. WE BOTH GOT FOOD POISONING! The absolute worse feeling ever I knew something was gross about it but I gave it a shot she's actually from Reno so she's had it before. But never again will we eat at one of these places!

This by far has to be the dirtiest Qdoba I've been to. I'm surprised food contamination is a thing here. We arrived about 75 minutes prior to closing after a long trip. As you can tell by the photos, they were cleaning for closing time and the white cutting board panels on the prepping table are missing. In it's place was food sludge. They were wiping that watery sludge with a scouring pad on the stainless steel, with all the food still in their bins. Here's to hoping no food poisoning.

Tonight was my first and last visit to Glory Days, as I am left very seriously thinking that I may have just eaten dog food. There are certainly no other restaurants in first world countries serving food that shares any qualities with what we were just served. I ordered a bbq chicken salad. If I were blindfolded, I kid you not, I would have guessed that the chicken was pre-chewed McRib "meat." It sat atop a sad bed of iceberg lettuce similar to what you would expect to find in a salad from a dreary pizza shop that only uses sandwich and pizza toppings just so they can say they offer "salads." I know that GD is a sports bar, But I really thought they could pull this salad off... Boy was I wrong. Along with the sad sandwich shreds were spongy kernels of canned corn and some terrible, stale tortilla strips. We also had an order of chicken tenders that contained one special tender from an actual rubber chicken. Or it may have been some sort of fake food, meant only for photographing. It couldn't be cut with a fork, pulled apart or chewed. I should have brought it home to show my kids, it could have been a fun toy. We also had some cold sweet potato fries, pretty gross cole slaw, and a mac-n-cheese burger that was so lackluster it doesn't deserve a sentence of its own to describe it. Continuing to think about this food is literally turning my stomach. I have brushed my teeth and used mouthwash in an effort to remove the taste of all this from my mouth. If any remnant traces of these tastes continue to linger, I may induce vomiting.

Today was not my first visit to Monon Coffee Company, though I'll confess that Broad Ripple's atrocious parking situation tends to keep me away from the area with the exception of non-metered Sundays. I mean, c'mon. Broad Ripple's already pretentiously overpriced. I have to pay for parking now, too? While in most ways I've been fond of former Mayor Greg Ballard, I'll stand by my opinion that Ballard pretty much gutted the soul of Broad Ripple Village for the sake of a few bucks. Now, instead of a village you get hipster vendors and bored youth graffiti woven together into shops that are occasionally awesome, occasionally godawful and occasionally just the kind of shops that make you go "No, really. Who the heck actually buys this stuff?" Monon Coffee Company fits nicely within the "hipster" vibe, a solid purveyor of indie brews and Rene's Bakery baked goods (including health-conscious and gluten free options) all decked out in a grunge meets steampunk meets just plain ole' funky decor. There's affordable local artwork on the walls, another small section along the wall for packaged coffees and other items for sale, and a unisex bathroom so incredibly funky, and I'm not talking quality funk like George Clinton, that you'll swear you've taken an underground tunnel and landed in my own funky ole' commode. Boy, I wish I was kidding. They also serve up smoothies and they have some tea options, both hot and cold, so it's hard to picture anyone arriving at the order counter and not finding a way to leave happy. Located on Westfield Boulevard, Monon Coffee Company is, much like many businesses in the Broad Ripple area, not exactly stellar when it comes to wheelchair access. The good news is that there is an accessible metered spot one door down, a fairly decent but worn curb cut, and Monon itself doesn't have a step to get into it and is on one floor. The bad news? They have this old wooden door that opens inward and feels about as sticky as the aforementioned bathroom. Admit it, you visualized it. Here's the thing about hipsters, at least in my experience. They aren't exactly the most helpful bunch of folks. Oh sure, they'll fight like heck for your rights. They'll just look at you like "I'm reading a book and when I've finished my reading I MAY get out of my comfortable seat to help you with the door." Before you start getting all defensive, since we known darn well that Yelp is filled to the brim with opinionated hipsters, this is not an absolute statement. I know perfectly groovy, fine and hospitable hipsters. I've just never encountered them at Monon Coffee Company, though that could be because the tables/chairs where you can sit and enjoy your brew/baked goods are so tightly organized that you start to feel like you've stumbled into a filming of the next "Human Centipede" film. As a wheelchair user, I'd be hard-pressed to find a decent way to really relax in the funky yet claustrophobic setting. There are good things, of course, about Monon Coffee Company. They start with the employees, who've never been less than helpful and today were patient, funny and hospitable. I ordered a 20 oz. iced coffee with cream ($1.99) and I was impressed that the male employee immediately stopped paying attention to the attractive female he'd been talking to (she was cute) and gave me his full attention. In case you're wondering, I'm nowhere near as cute. As I was leaving, some metal part fell off the door - I think it may have been from the mail slot, though I never did quite figure it out. That's about par for the course in this ultra-casual but still quite good local coffeeshop. Monon Coffeeshop has its own reputation for supporting local artists and businesses, always a great thing, and has definitely more than held its own despite being only a block or two away from a Starbucks. Monon Coffee Company is never going to be one of my favorite coffee spots in Indy, though it's also not a spot I'll be hesitant to visit when I'm in the neighborhood.

My Husband and I visit PF Chang yesterday for dinner. My husband ordered the Kung Pao chicken with ice tea and I ordered the pepper steak, for appetizer we ordered the crispy green beans. The crispy green beans was amazing and the drinks (coconut cooler) was really good. My husband said there was too many peanuts in his dish. The flank from the Pepper steak was cooked perfectly, but the dish taste just like black pepper. It was so overbearing that I could not taste the flavor of green pepper/red pepper nor the steak. The waiter ask us how was the food, I told him that the pepper steak was too peppery. He said it is too hot for you, I said it taste just like black pepper. I was cooling my mouth down with the coconut cooler. I had soooo much heartburn from the pepper it made me vomit.

Don't get me wrong these poke bowls looks good but they're the worst I've ever had. The rice is so mushy that it feels like paste. The fish was warm and almost felt half cooked instead of raw. I didn't even eat most of my bowl and my boyfriend stopped after two bites due to being afraid of food poisoning. They need to keep their fish cold, sauces cold, and learn how to good rice. Also the mango was really mushy and that was gross.

Due to COVID-19, you can only order via online. They are allowing "dine in" currently but only two tables outside. None of the tables inside were available when I went. They are also not currently offering any of their lemonades or specialty drinks which is one of the main reasons I go. Also no refills currently if you "dine in" which I really don't get. I'm all for whatever each individual restaurant/chain feels they need to do to keep safe during this pandemic though so I'm not complaining. I probably wouldn't come back to this place until things are normal though. Some places are just better when there are NO restrictions and Blaze is one of them. The pizza itself was fine. I've had better though to be honest, given the price tag. My girlfriend claims they have one of the best gluten free options so I'd take that into effect for any one with dietary restrictions.
Food was okay, but two of the three of us got sick and vomited after eating here. Not fun

I ate here twice in two days and I give it 3 stars because the food was so inconsistent. The first day, I ordered an iced coffee, an omelette and turkey bacon. My omelette had pepper jack cheese, mushrooms, spinach and caramelized onions. It was great as were the home fries on the side. The turkey bacon was also a little crispy which was really nice. The iced coffee was nice and strong too. Day two was a completely different story! I ordered the Ultimate Mexi Scramble with the cheese grits, gluten free toast and a decaf coffee. The Mexi Scramble was cooked to death, the cheese grits were barely warm and the decaf coffee had no flavor. Also, I just moved up from the shore and it was very easy to find gluten free options such as pancakes and waffles. That's an easy win for a restaurant to add to a breakfast menu as it's just a separate batter. But here, gluten free toast was the only option. I do have to say, the wait staff was amazing on both days. But, I am going to need to find out who the chef is on Saturdays and stick to his work schedule.

So after a little over a year i decided to give it another chance. This time I get a delivery order of BUFFALO WINGS but the thing is the wings were dry and had no flavor they tasted plain! I also got curly fries and they were soggy and gross! The worst part is i end up getting food poisoning from it, the worst two hours of my life just sitting there throwing up! Save your money and eat somewhere else please! I've never been so disappointed.

Ordered a spicy salmon roll, California and two Cajun rolls through grub hub last night. Opened the box and all of the rice had fallen to bits and the rolls weren't even held together, and the raw fish was HOT! It felt like it had been microwaved! The entire box also stunk of ROTTEN fish. My boyfriend and I each ate 3 single pieces and instantly felt nauseous. It's now the next day and I still feel nauseous and have been stuck in and out of the bathroom since last night. Extremely disappointed considering we've dined in numerous times with no issues, and last night absolutely ruined the chances of us ever coming back. Good to know we wasted nearly $45 on food poisoning and now a doctors visit. We did not even bother with trying to contact the restaurant further, since I had called twice and had no answer. Not worth the prices for cheap old food and possible food poisoning.

Peruvian Apology! I'm peruvian and this place has nothing to do with Peruvian food, sorry Gringos but this place is an scam is more Texmex than Peruvian. I ordered lomo saltado because no peruvian will mess up that dish but surprise they f..up royally, meat burned and way too much soy sauce and vinagre, my sister asked for the Ají de Gallina (spicy chicken) the chicken was almost liquified it look and tasted like vomit. I will never go back to that place!! If you want peruvian food, please drive to Chicago and go to Tanta Chicago, Ay picante or Fina Estampa this last restaurant has rotisserie Chicken. The Incas are upset.

Sucha cute and quaint place. The workers there are extremely nice and helpful! The coffee and batteries there are delectable I had the maple spiced latte and chai-spiced pear tart and did not regret it one bit. The only reason why I gave this three stars and not five is that some people feel entitled to bring their dogs with them which are not service dogs. I have really bad allergies to dogs and there was a gentleman there who also had really bad allergies he was constant sneezing for over 10 minutes and the owner of the dog didn't care so the other guy left. It's unsanitary and not appetizing when you have animals in a place where they sell food and drinks.

This place has horrible disgusting food. I knew as soon as we walked in that we should have turned around and walked right out. The food was completely BLAND. The chicken and steak tasted like it was boiled and the accompaniments were not fresh at all. My husband got food poisoning from eating a steak burrito. Such a disgrace to Old City.

Took my daughter with Celiac(totally gluten free) here thinking there were many options based on the bio of their attention to all kinds of dietary restrictions on their website as well as the reviews. I was extremely disappointed. She did not like their gluten free offerings, so asked for a substitution of an item in one of their dishes. The waiter was clueless( scary for someone with celiac), so I asked for a manager. She was very nice and tried to help, but admitted that on this particular night, did not trust her own kitchen not to cross contaminate the dish. My daughter ended up with a bowl of zucchini noodles with a marinara sauce. My mahi tacos were good, however my husbands steak chimichuri was tough and flavorless. My daughters friends burger was just ok. So, I would say we may have just had a bad night, however if you are totally gluten free, proceed with extreme caution.

Stay away from this pathetic excuse for a pizza shop. We were staying at the Embassy Suites and came back from site seeing and found their menu under our door......1st thing to be aware of id NO REFUNDS ...........................that threw up a flag but we decided to try them....When someone generally post no refunds then that means they do not stand behind their product or service which in this case both SUCKED. We ordered a pizza and 2 philly steak subs 12 inch subs which only 6 inches of the sub had meat.......also we asked for them to add mayo which they threw a few packs in the bag. Both sub rolls were burnt..............My wife called back and kindly asked for them to send a few plates and napkins which they forgot to send....the driver was polite but didn't speak much English. We requested that one of the subs come without mushrooms because my son has allergic reactions to mushrooms........the subs arrived unmarked and it was impossible for us to decide which had the mushrooms so my son had to eat left overs....When I called to express my concerns it fell on DEAF ears..... Eat at your own risk Coach Jimmy

My stay at the Gaylord Opryland was the stay from HELL!! Not only did the front desk staff give me a very hard time checking in with a corporate reservation and not having a credit card present even though there was a credit card on file and 5 other rooms booked with the same credit card. The Valet parking was very rude and gave me a difficult time getting my car because I called from a different phone in the hotel not my specific room phone even though I had my room # etc. The overall feeling I got from the staff was Could Not Be Bothered!! If all of that wasn't bad enough...I never left the hotel for 2 days only ate at hotel restaurants for 2 days then on the 3rd day of my trip...I woke up at 1 am with the sharpest pains in my abdomen and horrible chills and a headache. I walked down to the gift shop in horrible pain to buy some stomach medicine. I did not have my ID with me since I stumbled out of bed and ID Was not on my mind. Here we go again, the lady at the gift shop gives me the hardest time for trying to charge PEPTO BISMOL to my room without an ID. I stagger back to my room. My stomach is so upset that (sorry for the details) I begin to projectile vomit in the bathroom the second I walk in the room. The horrible stomach pain, chills, fever and headache lasted for about a day and a half. At first I thought it was something that I ate (which would have been at one of the hotels restaurants) but then I googled and saw that the hotel had an outbreak just a month before of norovirus I must say that chills,fever and headache don't usually accompany food poisoning. I did not go to a doctor so I was not officially diagnosed with norovirus. But I know the symptoms that I experienced and they were very similar. I checked out of the hotel yesterday and I could not have been happier!! Never will I stay there again!
Trying. Had lunch there. They neither really know their stuff, nor are able to accommodate allergies other than those on the menu. Very in the box.

Underrated! Food was gross and unedible. I ordered orange chicken. It tasted old and spicy. I asked for a mild version of this dish. Someone else at the table had an allergy of a garnish of a soup dish, he asked the wait staff if they could make the dish without the garnish.they said yes, and the dish came out with the garnish on it. The restaurant itsself was small and dirty. I ate nothing, and went to mcdonalds across the street for my edible food. NEVER AGAIN!!

My husband and I were visiting from Seattle. We are big fans of açaí bowls and have tried countless bowls across multiple states. While the bowl itself was okay (I've had much fresher and flavorful bowls elsewhere), the service was terrible. The wait was 40 minutes and two of our four bowls were the wrong size. However, it was the lack of care and attention to my food allergies which precipitated this review. I cannot eat gluten and paid for the gluten-free granola. When retrieving my order, I asked multiple times which bowl was which to confirm I was getting the one that was gluten-free. It wasn't until I was halfway into my bowl I realized I was told the wrong bowl and ended up feeling terrible all day. I would caution about going here if you have any food allergies or sensitivities as I do not have confidence in their customer service.

First off my review would probably be different if I could eat almonds, regardless, they were good about accommodating to my nut allergy. As sort of a picky eater (not a fan of vinegary things), the first course was alright. Not a fan of the cucumbers or carrots but I LOVED the eggplant. The second course, I did not like it at all. Probably bc it didn't have the nuts and the chicken and eggs were so bland in my dish. I picked off the top of puff pastry and ate it. The chicken was tender, the bones came right off. It was the best thing they had. Unfortunately, since it is family style, if some people want spicy and others don't you have to settle for the non-spicy. They do give a side of the hot cumin sauce (it was good, but not spicy in my opinion). I had the beef kabobs, super chewy and okay seasoning. Didn't finish it. My friends who had the lamb really liked it. Everything after this was just subpar. The couscous, fruit salad, baklava (my friend said) were just blah. The highlights were the eggplant and the chicken but that being said I do not think I got my money's worth with the almond allergy. My friends said they would give this place 3 stars even with the nut dishes. I guess these reviews really hyped this place up and maybe my expectations were too high. The rose water was a nice touch but the mint tea was too sweet.

Came here for the first time and I'm pretty disappointed. I ordered one roll which had a hair in it. I told the waitress who took it back and i could see her talking to the chef about it. She then brought me a "new" roll which i ate until getting to the same piece that the hair was in, where i then found another piece of hair. Not to mention the tempura salmon was a strange pink and brown color which i thought maybe was from over cooking but honestly who knows. Definitely won't be coming back, I'll cut my loss and enjoy my food poisoning. But if you enjoy eating hair and brown fish maybe this place is for you.

The better half once got food poisoning here, so its forbidden that I suggest we return as a couple. I, fortunately, have never had any bad food here. Overall, considering its proximity to Vanderbilt, a pretty speedy place for Lunch fair. You'll be in and out in time to get back to work. The food is pretty much what you'd expect. Maybe I just haven't found the magic dish here, but I can't say that with the "Better Half Embargo" I miss coming here with her.

This was my kids choice for dinner as she was craving Italian and this was in the area we were in. Had never been before so thought we'd give it a try. The service was great. The food was hit or miss depending on what you ordered. My kid enjoyed her food the most (and I agree it was the best of the 3). She had the chicken Parmesan with Alfredo pasta. She also haspicy chicken noodle soup which was AMAZING. My husband enjoyed his shrimp Parmesan. I had wanted something I've never tried before. So I got the pollo Rosa Maria minus the mushrooms. The chicken was juicy and the sauce was tasty. I was just disappointed with the prosciutto filling. Very little in there at all. Overall the food was pretty good just a bit overpriced at on average $20 an entree. My only issue was in the bathroom. This may be a bit much detail but I'm gonna say it anyway. When In there it sound like someone was coughing up a storm, maybe even vomiting in one of the stalls and the occasional flush. It's a bathroom so I get that's what it's for. My issue was when I was finishing up washing my hands. I heard the stall unlock and I went to hurry and dry my hands to get out of the way of the sink and paper towel dispenser. An employee comes out. Doesn't even go NEAR the sink. I used my paper towel to open the door and then tossed it in the garbage can behind me. She follows me out and goes right behind the bar. I just kept walking and wanted to get out of there. I was stunned. She even looked dead at me and smiled as if not washing her hands was ok. So I don't think we'll be back.

I ordered the enchiladas suivas because they looked good on the menu. They turned out to be the worst tasting enchiladas I've ever had (they tasted like vomit), and looked and tasted like they'd been pulled out of the freezer. I ate half of one enchilada (there were 3) and am kicking myself for not sending it back. Everything was over-salted and over-processed. Most of us felt ill by the end of the meal from the sheer amounts of salt in the food, and only one out of the six of us enjoyed his meal. Top it off with an extremely long wait for the food. Our waiter was pleasant and did a great job, just wish the food was better. Won't be going back here ever again.

I've discovered the absolute worst "Japanese" restaurant in town. It was so bad my husband threw up before we left. There's an art to Japanese cuisine and it is absolutely lost here. Super expensive. Super greasy.

My husband and I had the following; Satay Tofu - Very nice, not oily even though it has been deep fried, nice amount of satay sauce Seafood Lo Mein - Quite bland, I had to ask for chili. I have to say I did ask to substitute the Lo Mein noodles to Singapore noodles just due to preference. I don't think it has anything to do with it being bland. Lots of noodles with not much seafood or vegetables. Sizzling Seafood Trio - My husband is allergic to prawns and the restaurant was nice enough to take it out. I am not sure if their put more of the other seafood in but I said to my husband, " where's your seafood?". I've noticed the seafood were overcooked that it shrinked and "disappeared" in the sauce Kangkong Belachan - Pretty good, quite oily. We only ate the vegetable on the top. Ice tea- can't comment, I didn't take a sip. My husband ordered it Rambutan drink- I was happy to find rambutans in it but the drink itself was like tap water with a bit of sugar. Not enjoyable at all ABC dessert - inedible to me. It was just ice with tasteless syrup and "minced up" green jelly at the bottom. I had a few mouthful but stopped. I think it's not worth the calories. I'm Singaporean and I feel the food here is below average. Super large portions, you kind of lose your appetite just looking at it. I live in Australia and traveled enough around the world to know there are good Malaysian restaurants around not just in Singapore/Malaysia. The service was efficient but too efficient that they make you feel that you need to eat fast and go. The brought in the bill before we can start our dessert. Food is reasonable priced and a nice touch with the welcome tea and fortune cookies at the end

I got food poisoning!!! I will never eat at any KFC location. I went there Thursday night 11/17. I ordered a famous bowl when ch is popcorn chicken on top of mashed potatoes, corn, cheese and gravy. As soon as I was almost finished I started feeling weird. I woke up through out the night going to the bathroom. I had it for a few days but my symptoms lasted 8 days. Which a nurse told me is normal. Another thing when I went to give the cashier my credit card she gave it to a boy and he started walking to the back. I asked where was he going she told me they have to charge it back there. I said no and paid with cash instead. Please beware of both of this situations.

Did not have the chicken (which I paid for extra for) on my salad, then when I asked for it, they brought out not even a half ounce of chicken (this salad was $11!) with a LONG hair attached. Chick-fil-a has better salads. So disappointing. Wish there were good gluten-free options for when my boyfriend wants calzones.

So disappointed. Went there with a good friend for the first time. Was expecting a fabulous breakfast. While our waitress was very nice she didn't tell us that Green Eggs does breakfast a bit differently than other breakfast places. We asked for RYE toast but we were served Marble rye toast, which is not rye toast but a mix of pumpernickel and rye. (I am allergic to pumpernickel). I asked for turkey bacon thinking it would be thin and crisp like ALL bacon but their "special" version of turkey bacon is a thick cut version so that the bacon becomes like chunky ham particles. Alas, I did not ask for chunky particles. My friend asked for cheese in her omelette and was served an omelette with melted cheese poured on top of the eggs. Whoever heard of melted cheese being poured on top of an omelette? Truly odd. Cheese should be INSIDE an omelette. Most of the customers were eating ice cream/whipped cream French toast and sickly sweet breakfasts. They were all overweight. Very slow service. Had to ask for more coffee. The corner diner is better.
They sold me uncooked rotten food! Save yourself the food poisoning and don't go there.

I want to give this place 3 stars. I really really do! I might be the only person who prefers this truck to the one right next to it. The sweet potato burrito is amazing. In fact, the only reason the review gets two stars instead of one is because of the sweet potato. Their service is efficient and if they don't have something, they'll swap an ingredient for no extra cost. But....and this is a HUGE HUGE but..... Apparently, every once in a while when you eat here, you get food poisoning. A guy I work with had this happen to him a while ago. I thought nothing of it. That is, until today. A girl I work with and I got a veggie tostada salad. Both of us are sick now. Ugh. This is probably a risk you take eating at any food cart. But since it hasn't happened to me until now, MexiPhilly Truck, I'm sorry, but I'm taking it out on you.

This was a very hard decision how to review this restaurant. I believe it's a solid four stars, here's why: the food by far hands-down was five star or very close to it. Everything we had was very excellent and they claimed the file gumbo, the salad dressings and such are all homemade. I believe they were and they were delicious but maybe just a little too salty. The only reason it's very close to five star cuisine was because of the salt level and it seemed a bit pricey for what it was. Still this could have been overlooked and very easy could've been a five star review except for the service. The service started off okay but rapidly declined. When we got there there was only two other tables in there and about three showed up when we were eating. When this happened the service went from slow to nonexistent. The service was at most three stars but probably more likely two stars. Because of this, this can never be a five-star restaurant no matter how good the cuisine is. One other thing that made me a bit iffy was I decided to try a sweet tea with lemon. After I squeezed the lemon and dropped it into the tea I realized, upon seeing the lemon because it was still floating, that the lemon was contaminated. I won't claim to know what it was contaminated with but I had my suspicions and because of this I could not drink the tea. However, we had no service so I couldn't request a new tea. It's hard to eat a complete salty meal without any drink. However this alone would not prevent me from returning to this restaurant. This is a four-star and not a three star because the food was that delicious. It's a four-star and not five star because everything but the food was horrible.
It's good. And gluten free buns. And local. But to drop over $40 on burgers and fries at lunch? Not that good. A Nashville classic though, so check it out if you're here.

Looking for a new local spot and this will not be it. To get a feel we ordered two lunch sushi roll specials that came with soup and salad. Alaska, salmon avocado, spicy salmon, yellowtail scallion, tuna and spicy tuna. Both tunas we tried one piece of and spit out because of the fishy taste. My husband swallowed his and threw up later. Hoping just the tuna was off we kept tasting. The yellowtail was tasteless so I guess that was a good thing. Lastly the salmon was also fishy and spit out. We also ordered a chicken hibachi lunch that we'd tried first and thought was tasty though the chicken was a little dry. We threw everything away and to be safe we tossed the salads and soups too. I assume this place was good before and maybe just the pandemic has them less busy. But regardless, you sold me $40 (with tip) in bad fish and fine hibachi.

I wrote a review about getting food poisoning and the owner, Florian, is basically calling me a liar because mine was the only complaint that day. Why would I lie about the food poisoning? I actually really liked you guys, but I'm seeing a pattern with the negative reviews I've read on here. Any time there is a negative comment Florian calls the review fake. Maybe they are maybe they aren't, but this unfortunately is not a fake review. I had food poisoning from Illegal Tacos last Friday and it lasted for 3 days. I know Florian said they are careful with food handling, but something obviously went wrong and my critique was meant to be helpful and to inform you not to attack. Learn to take criticism and make your business better.

Why did my short rib pappardelle smell like vomit? Perhaps the cheese had gone bad, perhaps it was something else, who knows, but whatever it was, there was no way something that smelled like that should have been allowed to leave the kitchen. We ordered takeout so unless I wanted to drive back there wasn't much to do about it. So we tossed it. Problem was, the smell was so bad that we had to then toss the garbage bag into the outdoor can. Oh, well. The tiramisu was okay, though.

I was ordering RamaPong online, and wanted the vegetarian ramen. I am allergic to garlic, and so before I ordered it, I checked the menu- which has ingredients for each dish- to see whether there was garlic in the ramen. There was a long list of ingredients, including sesame seeds and green onion, but no garlic. However, when I received my ramen, I immediately smelled the garlic in the broth. I then called the restaurant to ask whether there was garlic, and they said there was. When I said it wasn't listed on the menu ingredients, I was told it was my fault for not going out of my way to ask if there was garlic- even though I assumed that the ingredient list was sufficient. A restaurant should either list all ingredients, or very few to none so that the customers have to inquire in case of allergy. This was a poor experience. However, the edamame dumplings were solid and the packaging was cute.

I was steered towards Pizza Mizza for my Niece's BD party by SB family members who informed me that the space is large and super kid friendly: which it is. All good. We ordered a bunch of pizzas, drinks, salads and even a gluten free pizza for one of the babies (how do you know that a 3 year old is gluten sensitive is what i would like to know!). Pizzas arrived at the table lukewarm. but hey the kids could have cared less. and the parents were relieved that they did not have to worry about anyone burning their lips/mouth. As for me, I'm thinking to myself: just shut the hell up! this is about the kids, not you. And to be honest: we have all eaten cold pizza straight out of the refer. Also; the rules that i ascribe to a kid's party are a lot different than those i would to an adult party. In any event, I ordered several variations of Cheese and Pepperoni Pizzas: a few with mushrooms, a few with jalapenos (for the adults) though my 5 year old nephew scared the bejesus out of me by ONLY eating the Jalapeno/Pepperoni/Mushroom Pizza. And this from a kid, who sitting at my table eyeing the outrageous Christmas dinner spread I put out for my family, asked for a scrambled egg...just 30 days previous to this. I spent a week prepping for Xmas and he asks for a scrambled egg?? You gotta love kids though: the minute you think you have them pegged one way, they turn around and slug down Jalapenos without one peep or act in a manner that leads you to believe that there is not a thing unusual about it. Thank God they have wine here at the Mizza. BTW: the salads were crisp (a Chopped Salad and a Caesar) and the dressings tasty. good Job. Previous to this event I made sure that the Mizza dudes (all young, eager and nice) had enough Wine on ice, made sure they had the advertised Disney movies running and had plenty of toilet paper in the bathrooms.(though one of my sisters had the foresight or more to the point, the paranoia to bring rolls of tpaper and kleenex) The party though short (2 hours, whew!) was successful. No fights (and i am talking adults here), No crying. No food fights. No reminiscing about the "good times" which often leads to tears. Both the adults and the kids acted in a way of which i was proud. (i have hightailed out and away from several out in public family parties, believe me) Fun time and the Mizza guys were first rate and came through like champs. We will be back!

I was very disappointed. I was excited to support a local all vegan restaurant, resting assured that my food would not be contaminated with animal products or bi-products. The food was underwhelming to say the least. Order Pad Thai noodles and hot greens. The greens dish was decent. The noodles though.... just, no. Tasted like a giant squirt of siracha and ketchup comprised the sauce. The mung bean salad and crushed peanut toppings were almost non-existent. I couldn't eat more than a quarter of this dish. The greens were okay but were lacking key elements as advertised. When I am thinking I will get Bok Choy and Kale and other mixed greens and there is a scrawny portion... from a vegan restaurant... so disappointed. I am not sure there was any Bok Choy at all. The brownie was decent thought. That helped the bitterness of the meal. I am not sure if I will try here again, perhaps some of their other dishes are better, but with the steep prices, I don't want to risk another disappointment. If the food were awesome, I'd happily pay the top dollar prices they ask for a truly vegan meal. but ... nah.

Based off the reviews on Yelp, I was excited to try this place. However, I found my visit to be rather disappointing. The staff working here was very friendly and prompt, but the drinks and snacks were very subpar. I ordered a chai tea latte, and it was one of the worst I've ever had. It was extremely watery, bland, and had a strange aftertaste to it. I couldn't taste any chai in it whatsoever, but just a hint of sugar and milk. Very disappointing for a coffee shop. I also got a gluten-free maple donut. It was okay, but a tad too sweet. I also took a vegetarian burrito to-go, and I was very disappointed. There was a huge glob of cheese, some scattered mushrooms, and a scant of rice and beans. It was not a well-constructed burrito, and it left an unsettling feeling in my stomach. On the positive side of things, the people working here are extremely friendly and accommodating. The ambience is also very trendy and comforting. It's a great place to hang out and study or just relax.

Overall: Great lamb, but mediocre and overpriced as a whole. I was excited to try a new Greek food place in Nashville, especially one that claimed to be "street food." What I had in mind was a huge falafel gyro. Upon arriving, I was disappointed to find out that they did not have falafel, so I decided to give the lamb pita sandwich a try. The lamb was excellent! It was very tender and juicy. I would order that on its own next time. The fries were fantastic as well. However, the rest of the pita sandwich was a pretty big disappointment. The sandwich itself was very small, especially given its $12 price tag. The pita was also burnt, which ruined the flavor of the sandwich. I had to order without tzatziki yogurt due to lactose intolerance, but I should've added hummus to the sandwich, because it was pretty tough and needed a softer texture. This also wasn't very authentic compared to real Greek "street food." The highest priority of this place is blending in with East Nashville fashion, not food authenticity. I feel like any number of the Greek restaurants around town can offer a much more authentic product for a much better price. $15 for a pita sandwich, fries, and a soft drink is a pretty steep price tag for "street food," especially for the mediocre flavor and small portion sizes. I would not go again unless a group of friends wanted to go, and then I would just order lamb and fries.

Had the lunch buffet and the food was quite good. Reason for the 3 stars is that it is basically a vegetarian buffet with a a bit of seafood. If you are a meat eater you will probably be disappointed. The roasted vegetables were really delicious. Especially the eggplant and asparagus. Cannolis were disappointing in that the shells were soft. There were two types of pizza. I tried the one with no cheese, just tomato and garlic. Very good but the garlic was powerful. I was hoping there would be sausage or meatballs somewhere in the lineup but there wasn't. There was one pasta dish that was mushroom and spinach which was enjoyable. Apparently the type of pasta changes daily. The previous day it was a seafood pasta which would be bad news for anyone with a seafood allergy because there was no other pasta dish to choose from.

I have celiac disease. I'm deathly allergic to wheat. I'm also on my honeymoon in New Orleans and am having a hard time eating anywhere because of the Cajun seasoning and abundance of bread. I came into desire because I'm staying at the hotel and I tell my waiter I have an allergy please check to make sure the food I'm eating is gluten free. After he assured me that he asked and everything was ok I took a bite of my food and immediately knew he was wrong. I told the manager to check and sure enough I had just been poisoned. She apologized and didn't make me pay for my meal but that's not much considering I will be spending the next 3 days sicker than the exorcist.. while on my honeymoon.

It's hard to give a review at all and I'm going to be kind because of COVID; however, the name is no longer Denim, its Wanda. I went to place an order at Cluckwerx which was, I thought, a division of Denim. I called to ask a question and they were very confused and at no time explained the situation of the changeover. 2 minutes before I thought my order was to be ready, I get a text saying my order has been cancelled. I proceed to call the restaurant realizing now that there is a name change. When I questioned whoever answered the phone why no one said anything before when I called about my order, more confusion. We went in and tried to order and it was just chaos in there. No one knew what anyone was doing and we decided to just leave. I didn't want to take a chance eating any food (especially since I'm a celiac) at a place that was just so disorganized. I hope they get it together soon or else I see another name change and more confusion in the future.

This was a hard review to go between either a 2 or 3 star rating because the food at the price point is solid. Service was atrocious. We were in a corridor of 4 tables and witnessed our Tasmanian tornado waitress have egregious errors with each table. Everything from messing up food allergies, wrong orders, following up bad orders, and consistently flagging her down for every foundational need like asking for water, bread, and check. We had to ask for every minute thing--but we weren't the only ones. We got there at 7:10, were seated at 7:50, left at 9:20 because we were waiting the entire time. Our order consisted of two entrees and water. So that whole dining experience was nearly an two hours for two people. I can't imagine the patience of other patrons with larger parties. The only positive thing I can add was that the food was solid for the price. If you're willing to go through terrible wait times before being seated, even worse wait times in between ordering and getting your food, then yes--come here and order. Unfortunately for my husband and me, I don't have the patience to come back.

Major disappointment in price and taste! Have ordered gluten free margherita pizza for years at many many places and make my own. Website says gluten free pizzas are $9.95. Ordered a basic margherita pizza by phone because we couldn't get our order to go through on the site. The girl asked if I wanted white or red margherita. I'd never heard of white margherita so asked - sounded good but not anything like a margherita. Ordered 1 red and 1 white and 1 medium regular pizza with onions, olives and tomatoes. Total came to $48!! What?!? The gluten free pizzas were about 12" and they charged an up charge of $5 per pizza for margherita! Unbelievable!! $15/pizza for what?? And the red margherita pizza was thick tomato paste with no flavor with 3 circles of cheese and a few sprinkles of basil. I very rarely write a negative review but this was highway robbery! Total disappointment and although we were told 25 minutes to puck-up and arrived a few minutes earlier than that the pizzas were all lukewarm at best. So sad.

1st & last time ordering from them (delivery via Grub Hub). Ordered 5pc catfish, Pick3 combo w/whiting, perch, jumbo shrimp, 2pc fried chicken legs, 1 lb gizzards, fries, & fried okra. Fish (-5 stars): The fish on each plate was inedible. It was clearly old & past its prime to the point where the flesh/meat was no longer flaky & white but was a putrid nauseating grayish color. Had to throw away all the fish; we refused to eat it. Stars Balance: -5 Shrimp (5 stars): This was only meat that was good, fresh, & edible. They were truly jumbo & cooked perfectly. They were soft inside & not overcooked. Stars Balance: 0 Chicken (-3 stars): The 2pc fried chicken legs were seasoned well on outside but were undercooked & pink/raw inside. Had to put them in the oven to finish cooking them. Scary to be served raw chicken. Stars Balance: -3 Gizzards (-5 stars): They were inedible bc they were overcooked, dry, old, hard, & extremely salty. So disgusting & disappointing. Stars Balance: -8 Fries (5 stars): Best thing about order. They were perfect fries; fresh, seemed hand cut, crispy outside, soft inside & seasoned perfectly. Not overly salty. Seems like they do the double cook method. Stars Balance: -3 Fried Okra (5 stars): Was freshly prepared, not dry, not salty, fried well. Stars Balance: 2 It's really scary to think that restaurants in these times would have the audacity to serve such bad quality & health risk food. Food poisoning & salmonella are REAL people! If you want customers to come back & patronize your establishments, TAKE THE TIME TO PREPARE & SERVE them fresh, fully cooked, not overcooked, edible food! If you can't do that in these times, CLOSE YOUR DOORS!
Food line was not clean or wiped down. Food was cross contaminated with different foods in each bucket of food. If I want sour cream, I don't expect salsa to be in it. I understand busy but come on!

The people here are so sweet and they're so enthusiastic about helping you out and letting you try anything to make sure you like it. I'm excited to try this bowl! EDIT (5/15): They have great safety/cleanliness measures in place while they're still open during COVID-19!! You write your order on a paper (they provide gloves) and have the cash register at the door so you don't have to go in and potentially contaminate the inside since it's fresh food. Then you wait outside, and they gave a free lychee rose drink!!!

If i could go lower than a star i would . I never leave reviews but i downloaded yelp just to leave one after my experience here . Even after previously reading some bad reviews on Samis Bakery i gave them the benefit of the doubt & ordered a gluten free birthday cake for my mother who has celiac disease. The next day, after driving 40 minutes to get there, the Baker says my cake isn't ready, to come back in 30 minutes. Meanwhile they close in 2 hours. So i go eat & come back more than an hour later to find my cake will be done in 10 more minutes. (Good thing i didn't return in 30) I stand & wait . Finally he comes out with a cake on a card board plate & says sorry we have no box. Not only was he expecting me to carry this cake home on my lap with no box, the cake he made me was completely different from my order. I even texted the guy in detail EXACTLY what i needed. His response when confronted was ill understand if you don't want the cake. I ordered a gluten free strawberry cake & he gave me a sample something completely different. He said its almond mixed with gluten free . He understood nothing about gluten whatsoever. After that remark i left. Gluten can be a very serious thing & if cross contaminated in someones food who is diagnosed, make them extremely sick. I wasted so much time coming here & can gladly say i will never return . I do not recommend anyone to make cake orders ESPECIALLY if you have a food allergy, do NOT rely on them to be gluten free. Take this review with seriousness and continue to the next gluten free bakery on the list . I do have a recommendation who saved my moms birthday extremely last minute . Petite Madelyns Bakery on Bloomingdale Ave. She went above & beyond for me after hearing the circumstances i went through . Even coming in the next day on her day off to give me my cake . She can cater to anyone food allergy !

My family and I dined at Veekoo tonight. Recently my sister was diagnosed with a moderate allergy to gluten. When ordering her food she made sure to note that she had the allergy and asked that her food be made gluten free with gluten free soy sauce. When our food arrived we all dived right in and shortly she noticed that her sushi had a crunch like there was tempura mixed in. My mom tried it and sure enough there was. Within minutes my sister had bright red hives all over her neck. We called the waitress over and asked her if she had made sure that the sushi was made gluten free and she seemed confused. Turns out she didn't really understand what it meant and never relayed the allergy any of the chefs and or managers. After the food was returned the manager came out to apologize. We tried to explain the severity of the situation. That in this case my sister would be uncomfortable but she would live but someone else with an allergy might not have been so lucky. The manager although apologetic didn't seem too worried. I felt like the situation was treated the same way a manager would treat a customer that had been served an over cooked meal. I would not advise anyone who has an allergy to eat there. I'm really disappointed that they don't take things like this seriously because like I said to the manager someone could really get hurt.

I got Chick-Fil-A for breakfast before an appointment and that was a huge mistake! The chicken gave me food poisoning! I have not and will not be eating at this Chick-Fil-A location or any other Chick-Fil-A ever again.

My brother's and I ordered some from pasta from this place, and the quality absolutely awful. I got the stuffed shells and he got the baked ziti (not 100% sure) but they only gave me 4 SHELLS and the thing costed more than $12. It tasted like it went through the microwave. Plus the soup they gave us smelled HORRIBLE. I think it was black bean soup. My brother almost threw up as he poured it down the drain. Would not reccomend this place to anyone. Terrible food, terrible prices.
Been here about 6 times, always stop when we come down from Michigan... always loved it... sadly the three of us got food poisoning from here on Friday.

I've seen a store like it in Downers Grove, and am familiar with the concept of drawing oils or balsamic vinegars from silver metal casks into green glass bottles that are capped and sealed by staff. There are little tasting cups next to the casks, so you can sip to your heart's content. Balsamic Babe picked up a honey ginger vinegar, along with a herb de provencal, and a kalamata oil. She let me pick out a small bottle of basil-infused oil, which I'm thinking about drinking for breakfast with my toast. Aside from the oils and vinegars, there's a limited selection of pasta, sauces, spices, and flour (a few gluten-free) to help you in setting up bread or an entrée to use your oil and vinegar. The staffer on duty was very friendly and a Cards fan (a plus for me). He gave us a larger bottle than we deserved for a gift certificate we brought with us. The store is pleasantly neat and decorated, even a couch near the door, but a little bit on the boringly boxy side. Perhaps it was decorated by a Germanic type like me who needs a free spirit to "feng shui" the shop a bit more. The entrance approach is not helped by its position between the vacant shells of Countrywide Financial on one side, and Gaffney Sports and Bipod Running on the other. Those shells are reminders of how unforgiving the local market can feel when the economic forecast is not as bright as it was just three or four years ago. I hope Olive Oils and More does well, but suspect it will need to focus MORE on the "and More" part to make it so.

I legit had to get up and VOMIT like 4 times no exaggeration! I really don't know whats going on, my wife had to give me a massage cause of how bad it was! No exaggeration you guys made me never want to eat lil Caesars ! Im really over this cardboard pizza ! Health issues going on.

Service is good. I went there once for a banquet. I had gotten there early so I had The peel and eat shrimp. I was glad I had that at the bar before the lecture because the banquet fish dish was terrible - I didn't even eat it. I went there a second time (not my idea) and since I knew the shrimp was good I had that as my entree. my cousin had the fried shrimp which was pretty good for fried shrimp but my husband did not like his fish and chips, although he thought the french fries were OK. The fish dip is pretty good but it is not gluten-free even though they serve it with cucumber slices, they use flour in the mix. So peel and eat shrimp and fish dip a good option there

Stopped by at 1:15 on July 24 with a group of 5. It took 40 minutes to get our drinks, they were clearly overwhelmed and yet continued to seat people. We then waited another 45 minutes for our food, which was a complete joke. The two burgers ordered has lettuce that was brown and completely wilted. The turkey wrap was ok, but decided to show its true colors that evening at 10:30 with full blown food poisoning! I shared everything else all day with my husband, except this horrible wrap and clearly paid the price. I understand many places are short staffed, but if you can't handle more guests then don't seat them. Please know your limits!
So my grandson and I got lunch today. Burger and fries. We both got food poisoning. He has it coming out of both ends and I am on the toilet also. Stay away.

Everyone in my family has allergies. We were hopeful in Fuzzy tacos... sadly their was cheese in our rice!? My son has severe allergies.. has seizures.. we were very disappointed in the food.. it wasn't great.

I was traveling on business and I'm giving Tavern an extra star for going above and beyond on accommodating my Alpha-gal food allergy. Service was absolutely outstanding. Unfortunately, the food missed the mark. I had the salmon with which was crusted over and very hard with a very thick layer of salt. It was just too much. The bok choy - I don't even know what they were trying to do there. One end was burnt (not charbroiled-burnt) and the other as a soggy mess. The rice was the best part of the meal. Hubs had the nachos as his tradition when we try a new place. It was a very large portion, but that's where the good stops. Uhhh Alpha-gal syndrome and beef don't go together, and while I was not going to eat the nachos, they brought beef instead of the chicken he ordered and quality was sub-par. He said they were like average bar nachos. So while it was a good service experience and I want to give them 10 stars based on that, with the food price and quality, disappointing.

This was absolutely the WORST Italian food I have ever had! Server was attentive but the food was god awful. I only hope I don't get food poisoning tonight. Cannot believe this place is in business!! Do yourself a favor and avoid this place.

Does not accommodate diet restrictions. All pasta has egg, even gluten free. Almost everything has cheese. Came with a group of 7 people. I wasn't able to order anything and they wouldn't make anything special because it was a busy night. Sat here with no food watching everyone else eat. Never coming back if I have anything to say about it.

I told them that I was allergic to shrimp. They put my order in. Then manager came back later to tell me that the French onion soup that I consumed may have had shrimp in it. WHAT THE HELL? Then manager told me that I should've told him earlier! umm I told the waitress that I was allergic to shrimp and they decided to blame me? That makes no sense I then ordered the salad as main course and he charged me $6 to replace chicken with the shrimp that I'm allergic to. You just told me that the dish I just consumed will make me sick for the next 24 hours and now you want to charge me chicken? I do not understand your service and hope that other customers are aware of the way you treat people. This is unacceptable I'm sorry.

Three of us went in for lunch. They brought every item out individually, not all together. Done with my slice of pizza before they brought out my salad. Crazy!! Pizza is paper thin like a cracker,, no sauce or cheese and its way over priced. And if you want gluten free its $12 for a 10"" pizza, talk about Gouging. Won't go back there.

I went here about a year ago and had wonderful coconut ice cream. I have tried to go back several times but they haven't had the coconut ice cream back. It is the only place I can get a dairy, nut, gluten free treat. It would be okay except they always say that they are out and I wonder how can you always be out. :( Bring it back.

Went here for dinner tonight and was not pleased at all. I ordered the bang bang chicken and shrimp no shrimp because I'm allergic. I thought it was going to be spicy because it says bang bang... it had 0 spice at all. It honestly tasted like a peanut butter sauce. My boyfriend said it smelled like peanut butter as soon as they sat it down. My boyfriend ordered the chicken n biscuit. They should call that chicken n mashed potatoes served with a tiny biscuit. He got 2 little biscuits that were burned and hard as rocks. The waitress barely came to the table. But she did take my meal off since i didn't eat it which was nice. And of course the cheesecake was good too.

Be careful! I am not saying the food is not good. Quite the opposite. I am a huge fan of Korean BBQ, and I have to say the food was quite tasty. The reason I will never go back is because of potential cross contamination. The waitress used the same tongs to put the cooked food on our plate as she did to put the raw meat on the grill. Strike #1. With Korean BBQ, you always get lettuce to wrap the meat and/or sides in. She used one of the raw meat tongs to hand me a piece of lettuce. Strike #2. After that, we stopped eating and left. If they do that out in public, who knows what they do in the kitchen. That was enough of a warning for me. I recommend either asking to cook the food yourself, or be VERY observant as to what is going on.

Food great! I had the Quinoa black bean burrito twice in two goings. The popover with macademia nuts was perfect! Service is very friendly but spoty. This place is for those that enjoy a meal...and are not on a tight schedule. Expect a hug from mom. Great place especially if you are looking for gluten free and/or vegan! I gave it three stars because we had a very delayed smoothie (we had to ask for it multiple times...it ended up being on the house).

Probably the worst pizza I ever ate. I won't be back. The toppings were scarce. The crust was blan & overcooked. The selection was lacking. Note: Not everyone is a vegetarian/vegan/anti gluten/lactose free hippy.

Whole entire household developed food poisoning must of gave us some bad fish I called plenty of times to speak with the owner you would have thought they cared about their customers and would have called me back. NOPE! no call back so I will be contacting Dept of Health

We tried this place out tonight. OMG! First of all, my son opened our nachos and two flies walked out of the container. Talk about getting grossed out! I ordered the chicken fajitas. There was no option to order corn tortillas instead of flour tortillas so I just ate the chicken, peppers and onions as I'm gluten free. The beans were tasteless black beans. The rice was dry and flavorless. The cheese on the nachos reminded me of the stuff that comes in a can that you squirt on cheese fries. Disgusting. Honestly the rice and beans tasted like they came out of a bag. They were not fresh. California Tortilla trash bins should have hazardous material signs on them to keep poor unsuspecting dumpster divers away. I should have read the clues. For instance, desserts were chocolate chunk cookies or brownies. No flan, no tres leches, no sopapillas, etc. One of the tacos was Korean BBQ. Who puts BBQ sauce on tacos? What is spicey sunset sauce? Folks, do yourself a favor and go to El Burrito on Bridge Street or Los Mariachis on Gay Street. Both are wonderful family owned places. P.S. If you work at this place I suggest you find another place of employment. No way can this place stay in business with the quality of food they are slinging. Oh, I almost forgot: the delivery person was delightful.

Stay away from the Ginza Roll! You have been warned. I wanted to try a new sushi variation so I went with the Ginza Roll and the crab meat and apple roll. The Ginza roll is basically grilled salmon with onion, masago, and mayo. I love all the ingredients but once you put them together you are setting yourself up for failure. I almost threw up after tasting it. To my surprise, the crab meant and apple roll were actually pretty tasty and I recommend it. The service in this place was just border line ok. They get incredibly busy at lunch so obviously they service wont be as quick. Decent place if you go super early and avoif the ginza roll.

Food poisoning!!!! Beware, they served under cooked shrimp and "weird" tasting pork dumplings. When I contacted the corporate office they gave all of these excuses as to why they didn't give me food poisoning. I was in excruciating pain, nausea and vomiting for 48 hours, starting 1 hour after I consumed the food here. I will NEVER eat at another PF Chang's. My daughter also was sick. She ate the pork dumplings.

Copa is the Jekyll and Hyde of West Philly. By day, a humble outpost serving fine Mexican fare, and its sweet weekday deals beckon the wallet of the most frugal man, woman, and inexplicably mature child. The staff is Bueno (Spanish for good), and the flavors excellente (Spanish for excellent). But you're not here for the good doctor, are you? Of course not. You'd like to make the acquaintance of one Mr. Hyde. And so you shall. Any night Copa breathes a fire not unlike those you may have seen in a household fireplace. The bar is full, the tables overflowing. A collision of locals and university students, brought together by the allure of the famously mediocre margarita. The first sip greets your lips like an old friend. The second, like an old friend who you just remembered owes you money and has not paid you back in years. Enough money to be reasonably irked, but not quite enough to bring it up when you only see each other at weddings and birthdays, anyway. The rest goes not in sips, but gulps. Time slows, conversations slur, everything grows dark. Your friend stabs you with your epi pen and you come back to life. A novice mistake, you had a small helping of almonds before coming out with the boys. But your allergies don't stop you, no, Copa overcomes all. You pull yourself back onto the barstool and request a napkin from the bartender to apply pressure to your bloody skull while the bar tender shakes up your next marg. This one will be taken with nachos, because they keep the kitchen open late - - a class act. This is the good life. I have some beef with Copa, albeit only two very thin slices. Slice number one is that there is nowhere to dance, yet the bastards have the audacity to play a bumping set. Slice number two is that they charge a small cover when you're just trying to get in there to give them your money anyway. A good business practice or a slap in the face of bona fide American democracy? I leave this as an exercise to the reader.

Went to Olivers with a friend for an early Sunday night dinner. We split an appetizer and ordered separate main courses. My friend was extremely disappointed in her main course. We both ended-up with what appears to be mild food poisoning with body aches, tightness in the chest and headaches. We will not return.

Was really excited to try this place out but was not impressed at all. We had the garlic knots to start and they were so dry, it was like having thick slightly burnt toast with no butter. Then we had a Shipwreck Pizza and The bacon on it was still white! It was horrible and pretty sure I got a little food poisoning. The only thing that was good was the people. They were very kind and the service was great.

I'm frankly embarrassed to admit that I've never even heard of this place until about a week ago. My friend who knows literally everything and is good at literally everything mentioned this place at work and everyone in the room was completely losing their shit over how fantastic it is. I immediately made a reservation for the first viable time slot in my upcoming life which just so happened to be yesterday for brunch. Appointment was made for the only time on open table, 1:45. Also, this place is on open table which earns it a few extra brownie points in my book. I had to work on said morning and my departure time is usually capricious so I figured the extra wiggle room was prudent. I actually ended up getting out significantly earlier than planned and this place was amazing and accommodated us about an hour earlier than our reservation. When you first walk in, you'll notice that the space is INCREDIBLE. We were squeezed into the most adorable little table whose seats were a in a corner and thus adjacent to each other. This was EXTREMELY EXCITING because my fiance and I are obsessed with one another and I actually hate the standard across-the-table seating for two. Like, I'm expected to sit with an entire table-length between us? (I'm sure 99% of the population rn is like "BARF!!!"). Anyways, the service was great.........initially....... We both ordered a bloody mary which is our usual. If you read my reviews you'd probably be perplexed by the fact that I repeatedly order bloody marys as my brunch beverage and repeatedly hate them and complain. This was one of the first occasions that I actually ENJOYED a bloody mary at a restaurant. It's unconventional in that a sip doesn't lead to a mouthful of horseradish. The flavors are different than a classic, run-of-the-mill bloody mary and it was very enjoyable. We ordered the crispy chickpea hummus which comes with a giant, inflated pita bread. The texture was smooth, like genuine and authentic middle eastern hummus. Flavor was delicious. I ordered an omelette which I know was stupid in a place like this. There was like a christmas tree of herbs on top of it. It was more interesting than the characteristic omelette I'm accustomed to ordering at other places that gets boring, definitely a middle eastern twist that I appreciated, but overall the omelette was disappointing. Bae got the falafel pita and adored it. I had a few bites and I agree that it was wonderful. The fries are seasoned to perfection and perfectly crispy. The food here is good, but I finished my bloody mary probably before the food came out and our waitress never came back to our table to ask if we needed anything or wanted something else. I waited for the entire duration of our meal and then some. Finally, I had to flag down a busser to request to place an order for another drink. I felt like the dreaded restaurant hostage. Given my anxiety about being stuck at that table for another 45 min without the ability to request the check, I requested the check right then. There's nothing worse, I guess besides food poisoning, than feeling like I'm stuck at a table and I can't get another drink and I can't ask for the check and am therefore TRAPPED and I'm stuck at the mercy of any restaurant employee remembering we exist. I hate giving three stars because this restaurant is really special and this might be just an isolated incident but unfortunately this is something that might legitimately prevent me from going back.

THEY DO NOT DO CUSTOM! First, the quality it good. The ingredients and dough are awesome (Best gluten free for delivery), but every time, EVERY TIME, I try to customize one of their pizzas (add or remove ingredients) they mess it up. This is especially frustrating since there a food allergies in my home. Tonight, he even repeated the order back and messed it up! Their prices are also higher than most places. If Flying Pie had Gluten free crust, I would never order here again.

I honestly think this was the weirdest dinner of my life. Pro: Beautiful view Easy parking Great waitress Apologetic manager who came around twice Con: Horrible food. So so so so so bad I ordered the fresh catch of the day, salmon, flown in from NZ and splurged on a date night on a vacation with my husband which is rare for us. I love salmon and eat sushi all the time and was stoked for Brussels sprouts because they're my fave. My first plate, the salmon was cold. It tasted like it came from the fridge. Not luke warm, cold. Didn't have a lick of seasoning on it, no salt, nothing. It was so strange. Like they forgot to cook it. The Brussels sprouts were awful! Tasted and looked like they'd been boiled and had bac'n bits sprinkled on them. Soggy and really bad. I really really wanted to have a good night and was so stoked to be there, I downplayed it and told the waitress who was nice about it and they brought me another one, made by a different cook. Also, the mango salsa side was the worst salsa I'd ever had. Tasted like someone cut some onions and just dumped tequila on them. So it was fine, chalked it up to honest mistake. They brought me another and it was seasoned and the outside tasted great. Then I cut into it and it was completely raw inside. My fork couldn't even cut into it. The inside was completely chilled still and not cooked. It had been seared on the sides and that was all. I've never had that happen at any restaurant before. The waitress saw it and agreed and was very nice. The manager came out and looked embarrassed and also said, I'm so sorry we served you raw fish. I saw it and it was completely uncooked. They gave us free dessert but what a weird experience. I think quite possibly the worst food I've ever had at a restaurant. I can't think of a worse one anyways. I am so sad, I wanted to love this place because it's so beautiful looking. It's ripe and ready for Gordon Ramsey to come work his magic on. Fingers crossed I don't get food poisoning.

We visited Empress Garden on spring Saturday afternoon around 18.00 Hrs. The place was clean and had a moderate crowd. We were quickly seated and our server brought out tea and iced water almost immediately. Our server then disappeared for 15-20 minutes before taking our order. We then waited ten minutes for our soups to arrive. I found the hot and sour soup to only match its name in one adjective: the temperature was hot. The soup had a very thick consistency and very oily. The soup was rather bland with no flavor. My dining companions agreed that their wonton soup also was oily and bland and one remarked he thought the meat in his was "off" which he did report to the server. We only consumed about half of our soups before pushing them away. Our server removed the half consumed soup and listened to the report of bd meat in the wonton. Fifteen minutes later she brought out our main courses. I ordered the General Tso's chicken with a vegetable roll, our server said the substitution was no problem, as I have a seafood allergy. My companions also ordered a General Tso's and sweet and sour chicken, all with shrimp rolls. I found my General Tso's also to be rather bland: the sauce was sweet but no "kick" or orange flavor to it. My companions stated the sweet and sour chicken was okay but nothing rave about. They also agreed that the General Tso's was bland and uninteresting. The final straw was when one of the companions consumed their shrimp roll only to find out it was my vegetable roll. I'm glad I didn't immediately bite in to my egg roll as I did not have my Epipen with me and spending a Saturday night in the emergency room is not fun. We chose the Empress Garden based upon Yelp reviews so maybe we got an off night or the place is not consistent. Either way we won't be going back.

I got a Food Poisoning here by eating their Doner yesterday. It looked dry & old and thin, that should have been a warning sign for me. I even told the cashier at that time it looks dry. She said nothing. I have a diarrhea all night long and couldn't sleep and soon heading to emergency room. Their doner was probably at least a week old given the fact that it was a Thanksgiving week. Their fries was also terrible due to old Smokey oil. Rice was not cooked properly either. These guys don't know what a hell they are doing, hazard to publics health. They ruined my Friday night , and today and possibly my short vacation. What a mistake.

Server was clueless and came with a lot of attitude; our chef was a young kid who had no skills dropped knives and cut the food as slow as a school kid (not very fun at all actually was very boring). The food was lack luster and was cooked in WAY too much butter - suppose that's what you get with big chain places... OH and my daughter threw up once we got home I guess the food did not agree with her either.

WORST chinese food we've EVER eaten! My mother's been wanting to try Han Dynasty for the longest time due to it's being touted highly; so I thought I'd "treat" her and take her there...all I can say is if CNN thinks this is one of the top 50 chinese restaurants in the US then they must not have tried very many or they must equate smothering food in large quantities of chili oil to the exclusion of any other flavors with "good" food. We got their signature dan dan noodles - large quart sized quantity but huge disappointment! Noodles were overcooked and much too mushy, the sauce was mainly hotter than hell and unappetizing chili oil with tiny odd accent of what tasted like chinese five spice powder and topped with tiny amount of overly fried and overly minced ground pork that was inedible and hardly any overly minced scallions - ugh! felt like Clara Peller - where's the pork??!! Mom thought they were more like hard flavorless pieces of turd. I vomited up the dish and what I digested has been sending me to the toilet with the running shits for 24 hours! We also got the Scallion Beef - the few pieces of beef were OK and tender enough; didn't discern the hoisin or oyster sauce in the flavoring and the Scallions were all but absent; instead powerfully strong and bitter undercooked chunky onions and bell peppers dominated the dish - seriously PF Chang's Mongolian Beef was more impressive and flavorful and I've eaten much better than both for less money. I also made the mistake of ordering a third dish the Chicken with garlic sauce - very odd sour disappointing garlic sauce again overly dominated by chili oil making it almost unpalatable and again accompanied by chunky undercooked onions, carrots with maybe #3 wood ear mushrooms (the only chinese vegetable) in the whole dish with the chicken not tender and left in hard to manage large dried out pieces. My family enjoys szechuan and hunan chinese cuisine and have been eating it for over 40 years. We're not afraid of spicy food, but we prefer sauces to have some flavor to them other than just chili oil, as well as to not be made sick by our meal! We agreed that the food is much much better at Yangtze River and Mulan, and for the price we paid for the meal we'd be eating the food which would be twice as much for days! If eating chili oil straight out of the bottle is your idea of great chinese food then this is the restaurant for you...it's definitely NOT for us!

This is a touristy waste of calories, a rather average burger place. I had the 96 burger, which was just ok. I'm giving it two instead of three stars because there are so many great artisanal burger places everywhere now that the average bar is higher than this.
