The milkshakes were generic as well and my two kids were unimpressed. The waitstaff messed up two dishes. Also one of our party needed to be strictly gluten free due to Celiac and the waitstaff/kitchen was not knowledgeable regarding cross contamination. If you're Celiac, you are rolling the dice.

I walked in to see a "MANAGER" stock his station with handfuls of chicken, then handle ALL the veggies he was stocking WITHOUT a glove change, then go on to prepare several meals. I was watching intently as I have been a devout vegetarian for 4 years and I am extremely keen on noticing cross contamination. Then, when I asked for him to do a glove change, I was given attitude by both he and the other employee on shift. The girl replied "all the meat it pre-cooked"... instead of "ITS POLICY NOT TO CROSS CONTAMINATE"... ew! He did not wash his hands between glove changes, which is required by Eco-sure. THEN, I watched him talk crap about having to change his gloves, when I watched several nasty instances of cross contamination. I am not impressed by the customer service. Food was decent, not worth the attitudes though. High prices too, and we are not cheap people.

Ah Marathon, you never fail to disappoint. We've eaten a few times at the one by Macy's, and mostly had bad experiences, however had never tried this one before. We actually ended up here unintentionally. It was a Sunday and my fiancé and I wanted to get 500 degrees (some of the best burgers and veggie burgers in the city!), but sadly people in this city seem to have an allergy to working in Sundays as nothing is ever open. So, we saw Marathon next door, and being super hungry and since it was actually open, we figured what the hell...big mistake! The place is pretty small, but they have a lot of seating due to the fact that they cramp tables so close together you may as well be sitting on someone else's lap. The two of sat right next to a lady who was eating by herself (awkward to begin with), and our tables were literally a foot apart...I could have grabbed the salt off her table if I wanted to. It was busy in there, so understandable that our waiter was a little slow, but do they not employ more than 3 people?! It seemed like he was waiting at least 10 tables in our area. Took him roughly 10 minutes to come over the first time, and another 10 to bring our drinks (2 glasses of lemon water). Pretty ridiculous, and considerably worse since we were both really hungry...After bringing our water, he took our order, but didn't write anything down so that should have been a sign of trouble right there. Anyhow, I ordered the soup of the day, chicken tortilla, an iced tea, and the cheesesteak. I also requested mushrooms on the cheesesteak, meanwhile my fiancé just ordered the veggie burger. About 20 minutes went by, and nothing was coming out, not even my soup or iced tea. From my vantage point, I could see the kitchen and it was obvious that the soup was all ready to go in a big pot that they just had to scoop out. Finally, I flagged the waiter down and said, "you know, I wanted that soup as an appetizer, not with my entree". He muttered something, then went right over and scooped some out into a bowl for me...it was that simple! Pathetic. Not a minute had gone by when a different person came by with our sandwiches. At this point I was pretty pissed and said, "I told our waiter I wanted my soup as an appetizer. I literally just got the soup and now this is coming out." The girl seemed put off, but said she could leave it under the heat lamps until we're ready. I was feeling really bad for my fiancé, so I gobbled down the over-salted soup and told our waiter our food was sitting there ready for us. He brought it over, and my fiancé was of course happy, but I was still kind of pissed. To add to my anger, there were of course no mushrooms! The sandwich was crap with or without the shrooms, and it was at this point I decided we're leaving a crappy tip. For those not keeping track, I had also ordered an iced tea, but didn't mention it because it never actually came (of course it still showed up on the bill and we had to tell him to remove it..."oh sorry guys, it's been a long day". Yeah, well its about to get longer since your getting jipped on your tip!) I mean seriously, do they hire the biggest dumb@$$es off the streets to work here? None of these people could even put on so much as a smile... Just wrote a whole to say that I plan to NEVER again go to ANY Marathon Restaurant in this city. Can't believe these places exist, much less that its a chain of restaurants. How do people actually enjoy eating here?...

I was happy to find gluten free "Pad Thai Rice noodle bowl" as this weeks Aldi Find as I have a GF mate, till I made it. The instructions stated to, Drain Well after noodles become soft, but firm. Empty sauce & vegetables over noodles, microwave one min on high then enjoy. There was no joy, what you are then left with is a stuck together, gooey wad of sadness. I was lucky enough that about a 1/4 of the water I drained off landed in a clean bowl that was in the sink and was added back into the glop in hopes of freeing it up. Even with adding soy sauce and chopped green onion it was still just above gruel. I bought 2 so the second one, when I get the nerve to try it will get a cup of chicken stock/broth added back after the water draining.
Asked for my burger cooked Medium Well. This is what I got. It also had no flavor or taste. Waste of money I hope I don't get food poisoning!

CRAP SERVICE: Slow as molasses in the Antarctic. Though I'd give the food a 3.5 star. Sat. 10/22/18--not busy, two waitresses. 20+ min. to get water on the table-- 25min. to get an extra setting (three sat at a table with only two settings)...Asked TWICE for a third setting. Had to remind TWICE, "Salads please". Went there with friends with whom had been twice and liked the food. They told me the service would be SLOW (SO worse this time). Yet this time--it felt like reverse racism--as we were the only white people--and we were ignored completely much of our meal. My friends agreed that this service on Oct. 22, was so much worse than either of their two prior visits. One of the redeeming points was that the chef was out in the dining area, talking with another table--he overheard about my friend's celiac (gluten) issue-- and directed our waitress accordingly. The "chef/cook" seems to be on top of things re: food...but he does not train/nor teach the SLOW front staff--as he does not see their poor service--he is mostly behind the scene and does not see the crappy service...From entry through the door...and crap service to the table and crap service until departure. My order, 'Catfish Orleans", really tasted SO MUCH better as leftovers the next day. The option of it being served on shrimp-corn grit cakes was NOT available to me: "we are out"-- only other options: angel hair pasta or rice. I had the angel hair pasta...As I said--SO much better the next day. Food is tasty. Crap service. I'd maybe give the food a second try in the restaurant BUT the service was SO BAD and SO SLOW with such untrained servers...AND no front of service restaurant manager to guide the servers. I would NOT. I'd rather NOT.

We gamble there because the machines are great. We usually get inebriated, get a room and leave the next day broke. But we have a great time. I called to inform them that they had bedbugs in their bed. As verified by the doctor that I visited, because I thought I was just maybe allergic to something. Turns out it was bedbugs bites. They told me that they basically didn't care. Even though I was trying to tell them which room it was. I am a local and will gamble elsewhere. I am not a Karen, just don't like bed bugs.

Hands down THE best falafel in Philly! Quality food and ingredients masterfully arranged. He never disappoints and I always come back. Don't expect a menu. You only get one choice. You WILL enjoy it. Bring cash ($10). Expect a wait. Bring an epi pen if you have allergies...who knows what's in it. Today, I can identify a roasted peach, sprouts, chicken, spring mix, green falafel, GARLIC everywhere, limes, a tomato-ish gazpacho-like sauce, hummus, couscous or grits. Listen. He's the truth! Love the spicy, seasonal, fresh flavors!

Scattered service. First, I asked if I could get a smaller size beer (less than 12 oz) because I was trying to not drink that much. The server told me they could do that and proceeded to give me a 12 oz can! Yikes. I have a dairy allergy and wanted a burger. The server put my order in and 15 min later told me that all the buns had dairy. I asked if I could have it on any other bread. The server called someone who looked like a head chef. He very condescendingly told me my options were no bread or lettuce around the burger. They eventually figured that they could give me pita on the side. This seems like an ok place if you have no specific food needs, but for me, it was not worth the effort. Every single question I asked, the server had to check with the kitchen and the kitchen seemed pretty unaccommodating. Once my food came, my fries came with a sauce with diary! Um....

Recently they've gotten rid of yet another gluten free bread option, so there's only one (Italian GF) now. There's a beautiful covered patio, but no fans - so you're eating surrounded by flies from the local ranches and no fans to blow them away or deal with the heat. (There's no logic to having a covered patio in the Tucson area without fans, folks!)

Ordered from Grubhub. Entire order wrong they included an item I specifically asked to omit that I'm ALLERGIC TO. 5 separate things wrong. No accountability and no help from Grubhub. Good luck with this terrible establishment in fulfilling your order correctly.

Right next to Barnes and Jewish, this place is way more convenient for me than the Blk Market. But - this restaurant fails mainly in it's execution. First, if you say you are gluten free - have a list or train your employees. Some of the staff are great and others are meh. And please have your employees wear gloves. I saw them dump frozen crab raggon with their bare hands. And I've been here now multiple times and although the food is decent and it's getting better. I am not the biggest fan. Things to Note: 1) Three sizes: 2 - 4 tiny scoops. The large is equal to the standard at the Blk Market competitor. 2) Lots of seating and it is hot inside 3) Fish needs to be colder. This is the thing that bothers me the most 4) Quality of Tuna is much lower than Blk Market and not seasoned well 5) They have soba noodles 6) Wifi is coming. Oooo 7) Customize your own, but there isn't a opt in standard if you don't know how to mix/match Pros: 1) Lots of Seaweed Salad 2) Choose whatever toppings but avocado is extra Cons: 1) Seems like they always run out of stuff, and they didn't even have a simple spicy mayo sauce left by 1pm. Make more! 2) Not generous with their scoops or they just need bigger spoons! Or make sure u just get the large scoops bc of the ratio/rice/salad. 3) Warm rice was too mushy 4) Basic mix salads and they emptied the edamame right out of the frozen bag I love Poki but this place is the reason why you shouldn't have Poki in the midwest. Raw fish should be cold! If this is your first time with Poki, then it's decent. But - def. go to the Blk Market which is like down the street for better Poki and fresher ingredients. Pass.

6/9 - Ate lunch here about two hours ago with my significant other. Ordered the full pound of tri-tip. Order took about 30 minutes to get to us, while people around us seated later were getting their food already. Took ~25 minutes for the waitress to tell us she "just checked on it", and the kitchen would be another few minutes. Food comes out about 5 minutes later from a different waiter. He explains they delivered our food to a wrong table, and that the table "happily accepted it", so they didn't realize they were in err. The tri-tip was bland, extremely tough, questionably cooked - rarer on one side, more medium on the other. I'm starving, and it wasn't bloody red, so I eat the rarer side, leaving the more cooked side for my wife. If I hadn't have been starving, it would've been thumbs down after the first bite. Like chewing rubber. Now, it's about two hours later, and both my wife and I are facing "Oh, ****" kind of stomach distress. Wondering if it's gonna turn into a full blown episode of food poisoning - in the middle of a work-day. Great.

After trying the Tikka Masala at a catered party, we decided to try out the weekend buffet. I was shocked at the gluten free options, all clearly marked on their menu, and the staff there happily walked me through the buffet to confirm what was or was not safe for me to eat. Because so much of it was gluten free, I wasn't concerned about cross contamination from the buffet line. (Note that I am not celiac, but highly intolerant.) The buffet was kept fresh and well stocked and we truly loved it all. Will definitely be back again!

AWFUL. Place wasn't crowded. Fully disclosed that I had allergies to gluten and cheese. Cheese was on both my salad and my meal and even the reorder. Gave specific instructions for my salad. Came out with both croutons and cheese. Waited several minutes for it to be corrected. It was eventually corrected. Ordered my dinner it came out with cheese. Waited several minutes for the waiter to return. Informed him on the mix up. Waiter swears up and down that the meal has no cheese... when I could physically see it. Finally takes back the meal, apologizes and it comes back the exact same way. This time he says again theres no cheese. I ate the dish and I have been sick all day. Paid $21 for a meal that made me sick. RIDICULOUS. WILL NOT BE RETURNING!

Amazing gluten-free pizza! They take appropriate time and attention to make sure not to cross-contaminate by getting toppings straight from the fridge (not the bar) and using a separate oven for gf. My fiance and I have been there several times since I was diagnosed with celiac and it's always been great, I can even drink their "better for you" soda! We love the fresh toppings (plus truffle oil!), the ability to customize with gf crust for me and regular for him, and the casual yet refined environment. Great for a weeknight date (BYO) or a quick "real food" lunch. The staff is always friendly and patient while I'm debating among the many delicious choices. We enjoyed taking advantage of the half-off charcuterie board special last Monday night!

So I was not very pleased with this restaurant. We were seated at our table and forgotten about. When the waitress and manager came over they offered us free appetizers, which they forgot about and charged us anyway! My daughter's white sauce had hair in it, so I'm sure the whole container was contaminated! I just told her not to eat it. After the wait I was just ready for this experience to end. We went to the restroom and the floor was disgustingly sticky. Me and another customer dared not try to figure out why. Not sure if this place is always like this, off Night maybe? But I'm done!

The first time I ate there, I paid for my soup and waited 25 minutes while watching others who had arrived after me, recieve their food almost immediately. I then politely asked if my soup would be ready soon. The man yelled to me with an annoyed look in his face. "It'll BE ready in a few minutes!" Five minutes later he hands it to me, and it was 50% frozen. I politely sent it back, pointing out the problem, and he flipped out on me. He yelled at me in front of everyone, giving others the impression that I was the one at fault and eventually he refunded my money. Two months later I was walking by, didn't see the unfriendly man in the kitchen so i decided to order chicken soup, which I ate and even gave a piece to my small dog that was with me. 30 minutes later, at home, my dog and I both commenced a three day long food poisoning illness. I won't be returning to this place that doesn't even know how to correctly spell 'Boss' in Spanish. PATHETIC.

TL;DR: probably 4 to 4.5 stars on normal day because of the quality of food and location, but only gets a 3 today for slow and spotty service. Wife and I just moved to Germantown and figured we'd try to grab some grub from a local place we could walk to. The atmosphere was like most other bars you've ever been to, with a variety of clientele. It's seat yourself, so we grabbed a table outside and waited. And waited. And waited. Turns out someone called in sick, so our poor waitress was working the relatively busy place all by herself. Didn't catch her name, but she was super nice and apologetic the whole time, so it didn't affect her tip in least (but it does affect the rating). We started off with a Tennessee mule (made with grapefruit vodka; it was delicious and I don't like grapefruit) for my wife and an alt old fashioned for me (made with rum and ended up being way too sweet). Again, it took forever to get the drinks because of the single waitress but also because the bartender was apparently new as well. The food took a while to get to us and they had to remake my wife's burger because they put tomatoes on there and she's very allergic, but once it came out, boy was it good. I got the Nashville hot burger (special rub, pickles, Pico, pepper jack, and a big ol' jalapeño on top) and my wife got the GTP burger (fried egg, cheddar, and swiss). Both were mouthwatering delicious with great flavors that complemented each other well. I particularly liked the homemade pickles on mine; nice crunch with a great sour flavor. The house fries that come on the side were also truly fantastic. The side Caesar salad my wife got was okay, just drenched in dressing, as salads are wont to be when you don't order the dressing on the side. Overall, we'll probably come back and give them another chance because the burgers really were that good and it's so close to our apartment.

I first ordered from here last week and it was super delicious and I was very happy with my order. However, tonight I ordered a salad and I thought I tasted meat in a couple of bites but I didn't see any until I was almost finished eating. I saw what looked like little bits of bacon at the bottom. I don't eat bacon for personal reasons, this is not okay. Cross contamination is never okay.

Ordered through Door Dash. I am Japanese and this is not Japanse food!!! Yakiudon had some strange seasoning and spice and we were not able to even eat it, so we had to throw it away. Miso soup was not edible and my son almost threw up on the ​first sip. Side salad was hard and bitter. The only thing has was OK was Niku tofu, but this $18 dollar dish only had three tofu and few slices of meat​ and all others were just veg. We have​ not tried their sushi but these other entrees​ were terrible. Please don't think this is Japanese food.

I wish I could give this place no stars... MY HUSBAND GOT FOOD POISONING!!! When I called the next day to complain, they offered me a gift card, like I'd want to return after the VIOLENT THROWING UP FOR 24 HOURS that we had to endure. When I explained that I had no intention in returning and I would be agreeable to a refund of the offending dish (MUSSELS, BTW) I was told that "it isn't our policy to refund in this situation". The fact they HAVE a policy in this situation is enough explanation for me. I hope the Health Department shuts them down.

Well, this used to be one of my favorite Thai restaurants in Nashville until yesterday.I went there for lunch, & I order the great green curry! my son ordered cashew chicken. Service was great all of a sudden we noticed a steange strange odor. I thought it was gas from the kitchen, my son who's being a Restaurant manager told me "no that is sewage.I couldn't believe it. I noticed waiters covering their nose when walking down the hall from the restrooms. Sure enough plumbing services were outside, all of a sudden they walked in armed w/ huge hoses! The odor persisted. It was extremely intense I cannot believe the management did not close the place for 1 hour meantime they took care of the problem, and they actually exposed all customers to possible contamination with whatever was in the air. My son asked the guy to pack our lunch and we took it to go. It ended up in the compost we couldn't eat it. It was an awful experience. So they cared more about the money than the health for customers! you'd be the judge. It makes me wonder what type of decisions do they take when produce is half bad and half good? I don't think I'm willing to take a risk. On top of all they didn't tell anything to any customer, they didn't apologize whatsoever( not good business in my point of view)

La Casita wasn't exactly what I pictured when I think of a Mexican restaurant. It doesn't have the typical decor, it is a darker small bar that has two TVs over the main bar so that you can watch a game while you grab a meal and a drink. While there is no gluten free menu. Most of their menu items, i.e. tacos can be server on a corn tortilla or as a bowl as it is a safer option. The staff was very open in making this suggestion as they do store the corn and flour tortillas next to each other. I do have to commend them for understanding what cross contamination was without having to be the one to bring it up or having to explain it. The food itself was good and filling, plus it was on the cheaper side. Plus, if you happen to go during Happy Hour, which is from 3- 7 pm, you can grab a drink without breaking the bank after just one. Overall, the staff was friendly, to newcomers and regulars alike, and helpful. If I happen to be in the area again, I would come back to dine again.

Very disappointed in this restaurant. I would suggest that you just walk right past this one and enjoy good eats at another restaurant. We walked in for lunch the restaurant smelled like vomit, I couldn't even order food but since we was there we just ordered hoping for the best. I had the crab cakes they were overly spicy and not good. My friend got the gumbo and alligator he only enjoyed the alligator. I'll save everyone the time and disappointment just skip on this one.

I did love this place mostly because it was the closest chinese and sushi place in the neighborhood. Never again. Got food poisoning yesterday 2 hours after eating here. I thought I was going to die. You've been warned. Reporting to local agencies today when I recover. :(

Food is always good. However this place is filthy. There is nothing worse then after enjoying a good meal walking into a restroom that is filthy. In my last visit there was vomit in the sink, urine on the floor, filfthy sit down toilet and the room stunk. They have had broken exposed plumbing in the handicap toilet stall for months. One must ask if the bathroom are this filthy then how dirty is the kitchen?

I love the interior space, it's super cute. I love the idea & the menu layout BUT ...NO GLUTEN FREE?!?!?!??? So confused.... you don't need to have 100% gluten contamination free offerings to cater to many many people who have less severe allergies. I am a celiac but I can eat something made in the same space as gluten.. I can eat fries from a frier that has had gluten in it with 0 problems. Many MANY people are the same. I cannot however of course eat bread or a biscuit etc made from wheat flour. I wish they catered to help us gluten intolerant out a bit more... just more GF options on the menu would help

This is a great market, great selection and quality all the way. Super disappointed they are not enforcing mask wearing particularly given how crowded this market gets. So they are allowing some customers to potentially contaminate items for others, not sure why. On my recent visit most customers 95% wearing masks, 5% not super disrespectful at this time IMO.

Horrible customer service from the wait staff. Just like what everyone says who had a bad experience or not a great one, food was just ok, not great, had way better and would definitely not wait for a table. The place was way too crowded, the server was not prepared. No silverware on the tables, nor did she even tell us where to find the menu's then proceeds to ask what we want as our meals. Once the food comes, still no silverware, really? The alcoholic drinks all had orange juice in them, which I am highly allergic to. Why have EVERY drink have orange juice in them, there are other options for drinks out there or atleast offer to ask for something else for me, have a variety. The food is average and probably a bit lower because the meal was not prepared as asked. The meal felt heavy on the stomach and not healthy. Can't places serve vegetables without loading them up with butter or oil and adding seasonings and flavors, some people like vegetables without all that, much healthy too. We should be able to add things, or make it an option. The only positive was the rolls and cinnamon spread. Nasty! Never again!

I ordered the gluten free pizza crust and it's totally burned. The guy who made my pizza must be new because all of my toppings and sauce were in the middle of the crust and not spread out at all. The pizza is cut in many different sizes. The guy who made my pizza was kind of rude. Clearly there is some work place tension going on there because the employees were not happy with one another. If you cut my pizza and Botox ce it's burned wHy wouldn't you make me a new one or ask if I'd like a new one? Won't be back to this place. Blaze it is. I'd post a picture if this app would let me....technical issues

Terrible customer service! We ordered takeout & received the wrong food. I'm allergic to what they gave us, when I called & told them, the response was, what would you like us to do? Well... maybe give us what we ordered or give a refund. Will never go back.

I am Yelp trust kinda guy. But my god did this place suck. Went before the concert tonight and I can Honestly say I threw up this food at the parking lot in order to make it. After a lot of coconut water I recovered. This was the worst food I've had in a long time. I mean it was bad veal wow. The sauce was gross. I see why you get big portions to give to animals at home. Greek and Italian that's a bad combo in Tampa

Great atmosphere and great tasting food, but later this morning I regretfully learned the burgers weren't fresh. In the Nashville Scene, I read about how this has become one of the top bars to hangout in Nashville. The music was great and the crowd was good too. Service was even great too, and I was actually ready to give this place at least 4 stars. But experiencing food poisoning this morning and all day today is just a nightmare. I almost want to give this place 1 star but I think the atmosphere, music, and service is preventing me from doing so.

Two years ago (shortly after opening) the place gave me food poisoning, and opted not to go back. (possibly ever) Yesterday, I'd an auto service appointment across the street, and Redwood Rotisserie + Grill was the only Yelp-reputable place to grab a drink within walking distance. I figured it was unlikely I was gonna get poisoned by a Vodka Gimlet, so I meandered over to see if anything had changed. Sat at the bar, found out they comp (some) drinks for play, so I decided to tempt fate and got a burger to go with the drinks. The food/drinks were satisfactory, and the servers (and owners) were very friendly/attentive. The only complaints: - Sticky bar machines. - Food service is slow. (Seems the front of the house is doing better than the back) Maybe by the time I come back next - those issues won't be issues anymore.

A full celebration tea for 2 contains: 2 pots of tea, a fruit plate,salad and soup, 2 tier tea stand and cupcake with icecream as dessert. The environment is very well decorated , and apparently it's someone's home. When I made a reservation they told me there's only 12 and 1 o'clock available...so I had the earliest "afternoon tea" of my life,because I usually have it around 3-6pm, but when I leave the place at around 2, it's still empty like the picture shown below, and according the internet the place closes at 3pm. The tea was great with quite a big selection, how ever when I ask for milk the owner said my tea isn't usually pair with milk, and for the record I ordered earl grey with rose,lemon or milk I got none of it served until I asked. The food was okay nothing amazing but if you are lactose intolerant I don't recommend going there, everything savory was filled with cream cheese and the sweet was filled with cream and butter. I didn't like the scone as it's sprinkled with sugar crystal so it got the sandy texture while you were eating it. I expected some small pieces of cake but instead I filled myself up with sandwiches.

I came here with a group of friends who several are gluten free. We were very excited to have found such a place because not many exist that actually take the time and care about food allergies. We were very pleased upon receiving our order of French toast. It was delicious and amazing and our gluten free friends thought it was so good. But our troubles came from ordering the biscuits and gravy. The gravy tasted sour and awful. We questioned if it was even good anymore. Upon asking they told us it was like that and we were denied getting any different food without paying for it. We felt too sick to continue eating the biscuits so our friends shared their French toast graciously. Before leaving my GF friend decided to try one of their desserts, a small pastry. To which broke into several pieces outside when she bit into it and it fell to the ground. We appreciated the idea of a full gluten free restaurant. But they definitely need some work. I would steer clear of the biscuits and gravy. We felt sick the rest of the day. Not a good dish to be eating when it tastes just straight rotten.

Can't figure out what happened. I've been there several times over the last few years - last time being 18 months ago. The gaming area upstairs was cool for the kids. Pretzel was good, service was great. Beer was just bad. Very plain in general and it's VERY rare for me to leave glasses unfinished. I wonder if something/someone has changed. The lemon "lactose" beer was nothing like the name would suggest. From the IPAs to what was once a decent PB Stout - it was all so bad. I don't see how you can compete in such a crowded market with such bad product. Sorry to go negative but that was the worst beer I've had in an established brewery in a long time.

If I could give a 0 star score, I would. My husband and I came in for a Friday night date night, we live in the area and had never tried it. First of all, the service was extremely slow. I could see there was adequate staff but our server seemed to be helping everyone but us. My biggest issue was their unwillingness to accommodate my food allergy. The chef was essentially saying the food I'm allergic to was in everything. For a place that makes everything in house, I find it surprising that he was unable to locate what ingredients he uses. For patrons with allergies, this is a horrible place to go. We will not return. We left without ordering.

I was excited to try this place and I have to say the wait staff was great. The decor is trendy. The seats are really uncomfortable though. The chips were amazing, but the rest of our food not so much. The food items sound good, but we were not impressed. We were out food tasting and asked what there top items were and thats what we tried. The queso fundido: the cheese was not melty just a glob of cheese we had to cut to eat and so hard to chew. The chilaquiles: not much flavor and a weird after taste. The tacos: the raja taco was probably the best thing we tried the carne asada taco was nothing special. The rice was hard and flavorless and the calabacitas were just steamed squash. I did like their corn tortillas and they are made in house. A word of advice to the restaurant list ingredients! I have a food allergy and read all ingredients so when one of the tacos came out with avacado I was disappointed. I didn't see it at first and almost ate some of it.

This place was extremely busy (and so, so noisy) on a Wednesday evening around 7 pm. We ordered a small salad and a large deep dish pizza. It apparently takes about 25-30 minutes to cook a deep dish pizza, which we were not told when we ordered. We were starving, so we would never have stayed had the waitress informed us of this fact. By the time the pizza came out, we were more than ready to leave and took the food to go. The food ended up being good, but the poor communication and the noise (it literally sounded like every single person in the establishment was screaming) means I can only recommend this place for take-out. Unfortunately, that means I'll never try the gluten free skillet, since the waitress told us that can only be eaten in the restaurant.
So surprised this place hasn't been shut down yet. The amount of negative feedback- including food poisoning- should be more than enough to close this awful place down

Be wary of the grilled fish taco. My fiance ordered the grilled fish sandwich taco the evening of Nov. 18. He says he doubts it was snapper as noted on the menu board but rather cod. I noted a fishy smell when he got his order but I did not say anything because I didn't want him to think I was fussy. But, unfortunately, I sure wish I had. This morning, he is sick as a dog, vomiting all night through this morning. He had to cancel his appointments with clients because he can't function beyond vomiting in the toilet. I feel so bad for him. I'm sure it was the fish taco because he's had nothing else to eat since then. Otherwise, I've always enjoyed this establishment. I've been coming here with my grandchildren for more than four years. This is the first incident we've had with the food.

We used to come here a lot and always enjoyed it, but with recent menu change the Gluten Free options are limited so after that dinner of struggling to find something to eat, haven't been back. Great salads and love their white chili. Good wine selection. Have always had good service. Word to management-no need to contaminate every food option with gluten. French fries d
We have eaten at el Charro numerous times and it has been good, but yesterday at lunch I got a mild case of food poisoning. One miserable evening. I haven't decided if we will ever go back.

Bailey's range is a place I've visited a handful of times. Once a short while after it opened, a few years after that & then yesterday. Being a part of the Bailey's restaurant group, I tend to have an expectation of quality as I have had good experiences at a few of the other restaurants (bridge, small batch, rooster). The restaurant group typically does a decent job of putting a quality meal on the table served by quality staff. In the three times I've been to Bailey's Range, the experience went from "OK" to "Not good" to "I'm never coming back".. Reasoning for going back the 3rd time was out of convenience and desire to have a burger downtown with gluten free bun. Some good: The pickles on my classic double were tasty. Seemingly pickled in house. Crunchy, tasty, I'll take a jar if you have them. The beer selection is good. Lots of good local beers and some good non-locals too. I had a 4Hands Warped Perception Some ok: Our server was nice enough, and we sat at the bar, which was fairly empty, so we expected the service to be on point and quick. I think we waited like 5 mins for a greeting/waters and another 5 mins to take drink order, which were delivered another 5 after that. This seemed like a long time for how slow it was. The food taking a while wasn't her fault as far as I'm aware anyway. And the far too much bad: I got a classic double and asked for American cheese. I was told they didn't have American Cheese.... This is America. This is a cheeseburger. Get it together Bailey's.. Get some American cheese. Take a note from any other burger spot that I would've had to wait in a line to get the burger, not at an empty bar.. My bun was not fresh. Seemed to have a decent flavor, but it crumbling to pieces led me to think this had been hanging out for a little too long. The burger patties were far overcooked. They were dry, crumbly and hardly seasoned. Reminded me of a crappy backyard bbq burger you get at a friend's bbq that doesn't know how to cook but demands to man the grill. My girlfriend got a Chop House burger on a gluten free bun. This burger is what made me write this review. Im actually a fan of human size portions at restaurants. Portions that make sense for 1 person to eat and not hate themselves afterward, but this was far beyond a small portion. This burger was about the size of an average slider at other restaurants. I actually thought this was the kids burger and there was a mistake. I didn't say anything because my burger was also small and I looked at a couple burgers around me and they also seemed fairly small, so just seems to be the norm here. All in all, this specialty burger restaurant is not so special. It seems tired and in need of some major changes.

Worst gluten free pizza ever! Spent $17 on a 'specialty maguerita gluten free'. Horrible. Greasy. Come on. Help out those of us who can't eat gluten and maybe find a little enjoyment in a once favorite food. Does it really cost that much to add tomatoes? Next time I'll eat a few cherry tomatoes and a paper plate. Consistent experience with Pat's. This was the last straw. Done.

The atmosphere is super cute and trendy! It was very busy on a Monday afternoon when we went. A little too crowded not much place to wait. Plus the texting feature to find a table isn't helpful. The service was fine nothing fast or overly slow. Average. Waitress was friendly. Our table order the biscuit w/ chicken, chicken and waffles, and the protein grain bowl. The biscuit was good but nothing insane. Was too dry barely any gravy. The chicken and waffles were ok. Waffles tasted like box mix and the chicken was not great but It wasn't bad. The protein bowl was awful. The raw kale had no dressing on It so it was too hard to eat and It made me very sick. So much that I threw up later that day due to the kale not being massaged. Overall we were disappointed with the food although the coffee was amazing .

It's a shame such a charming restaurant has such poor issues with cleanliness. On three separate visits, I experienced an issue with food poisoning. Each time I ordered the lunch soup and salad. I changed up the type of soup on the third visit in hopes of a better experience. Their food is good and I didn't want to give up on them. However, the soup did not seem to be the problem; it was the salad. When I reported the issue to the manager, my report was not well received and I was criticized. Eat at your own risk!

The only reason I still go here is bc they offer gluten free bread. 3/4 times the bread is stale and mealy. The lettuce and onions taste day or 2 old. Only one measly slice of each piece of meat or cheese. Once in a while everything will be fresh and the sandwich will taste good, but overall this place sucks

I didn't know what to expect because I refused to read reviews first before going. I did although see the assembly line style toppings bar while walking past one day. My curiosity grew trying to guess which toppings they offered. I walked in and learned once it was my turn that not only do they offer gluten free crust,but they also offer a way for me to make my pizza gluten and not having to forgo the cheese. This in itself was a huge win for me. Not many can offer both. After I chose my crust I moved down the ling to the toppings. They have enough options to satisfy any palate. When it came to sauce I chose the classic red and I thought it was very good. I consider their meat and cheese selection impressive for a very inexpensive pizza place. I added mushrooms, spinach, artichoke hearts, black olives, bell peppers, and pineapples to my pie. I would've liked to see more veggie options so next time I could create a totally new pizza. Next time I'll do less toppings or plan ahead so I won't run out of options and get bored with it. My crust was cooked perfectly which is also something that is hard to accomplish. The toppings all had a chance to do their thing in the fire bricked oven. I think it only took about 4 or 5 minutes. Gluten free crusts take a little longer. I was worried about the beer selection since I hadn't had any of those they offered. I did appreciate them all being local brews. I chose "Southern Drawl" from a brewery in Shreveport named the Great Raft. I really enjoyed it. They offer wines also. I will return soon to make another creation of my own.

I called the night before and they were closing early because it was slow. Harsh for a business traveler trying to get a bite. I asked about gluten-free BBQand was assured that I could be accommodated, if I could comeback when they would be open. Stopped by tonight and was told they can't do gluten-free BBQ. What changed? I praise them for not serving me a meal that would of made me sick, but wish the person last night was honest about their capability.i fought a bunch of traffic just to be let down.

I got the WORST food poisoning here! It's too bad because the owners are so nice, the selection great and the prices reasonable. However, I would get a little sick each time I ate here, then the last and final time I really got dangerously sick. Wrenching stomach cramps, clutching the porcelain altar for a good 48 hours. I mentioned this to someone else and they said their daughter got really sick from eating here as well. Be careful!

We went on a day trip to River Horse to check it out. They are, in fact, one of the most established craft breweries in NJ. They got in on the craze before it was cool. The part we enjoyed the most was how informative the tour was. The guide really knew her stuff. Most of the time breweries don't get into that depth. They have a relatively small tasting room. It's not the type of tasting room that I'd come back to. I was also surprised that they served the beers in plastic, disposable cups. Any beer snob wouldn't appreciate it in anything except out of a glass. The beers themselves are actually pretty good and definitely better than your corporate brands. The brewery itself is no longer owned by the three guys who founded it. It has since been bought by investors. You can tell. It doesn't have that warm-and-fuzzy small business feel that so many other breweries in NJ have. It feels more like a smaller version of the Busch brewery. It also explains how River Horse got all the contracts throughout liquor stores in NJ to have their product sold there. They're great with the business / marketing side and not as much with the personal side. I have allergy-induced asthma, and I could feel that there is a lot of mildew in the brewery. It was hard for me to breathe in there. Makes sense with all the puddles everywhere that they don't clean up and all the cobwebs on the ceiling. Overall, we were all glad that we went so that we could get the background on River Horse. But we just didn't like the brewery itself very much.

Wow. Quite possibly the worst Starbucks experience. Came in with a couple friends, one of which lives down the road and usually avoids this terrible Starbucks. I asked the cashier if the "salted cream cold foam cold brew" could be made as nondairy. He said of course and gave me my milk options. I went with coconut milk. My friend then said she wanted the same thing but with soy milk. He then asked if she wanted it hot or cold. Idk how cold brew can be hot he then said he thought she wanted a salted caramel mocha. We clarified what we wanted. As we waited for our drinks, the barista sneezed in his hands and had a huge snot rocket. Gross. He then walked to the back, wiped his hands and came back out. Def wasn't back there long enough to wash them. He stood around behind the bar and a girl I assume was the shift lead motioned to him to wash his hands. So he rinsed them. Kept sniffling and touching his nose. Not who you want making your drinks, especially when you have a 7 week old, as my friend does. He should not have been working in food service. Point blank. If you are sick, do not work around food. My friend asked the supervisor if someone else could make our drinks because of what we witnessed. As she was asking this, I see him blending heavy cream for our drinks, which of course, does not fall into the nondairy category. He hands us one of them and we don't even want to touch it. The supervisor sends him on break and comes in to remake our drinks. She asks if our drinks are the "salted caramel mochas", which clearly homeboy rang in wrong so we let her know what we actually want. She then says it's made with heavy cream so I point out that the cashier told me it could be made nondairy. He says "oh I thought you wanted salted caramel mochas". I asked if I could get something else since i don't want dairy and they say they'll try to make it nondairy. Which btw, totally possible but might not be as foamy. After being in here 15-20 minutes for 3 drinks, to say i was frustrated was an understatement. There was no apology, no service recovery, nothing. Definitely need to retrain this staff, never seen such an incompetent bunch. The shift lead seemed to be the only one who knew what she was doing, understood food allergies, and cared about her job/customers.

What better way to ring in 2018 with your closest friends on a night topping out at 8 degrees than warming up with spicy food? This should have set the stage for our evening, yet management has yet to respond to my message to rectify the following situation: Our group of five sat down for a 7 pm reservation. We were presented with a pre fixe, three course menu set at $39/person. Each of us had the choice of an appetizer, entree, and dessert. That's a great deal for New Year's Eve! Our orders ranged from the fried avocado or ceviche for the appetizer, the brisket or paella for the main course, and the Très Leches cake or the grilled pound cake dressed with guava sauce. We all tried each other's and thoroughly enjoyed the food. My ceviche and paella were on-point! The portions were so generous that two friends -including myself- opted to take our mains home. Once the check arrived, one of my friends excused himself to the bathroom. He was gone for a good ten minutes, but upon his return he told us of the stomach pains he experienced. We should have taken heed, but the night was still young. From the time I left the restaurant, I couldn't shake the feeling of tiredness. I had not a drop of alcohol and the fatigue worsened. I drove home and went to sleep, only to wake up more than an hour later sicker than I've ever experienced. Sure enough, I came down with full blown food poisoning that laid me up for the rest of the week. The friends who ordered the brisket had the stomach pains and uncomfortable trips to the bathroom. It's worth mentioning that we felt rushed to finish our meal because our table was set up where the band was supposed to be playing. Wait. Whose brilliant idea was it to cram a five piece band in a corner, telling us we're in the way, yet not even offer us another seating arrangement before any food was set on the table? How about exercising some situational awareness? Seating was aplenty, so why another accommodation couldn't be made was just baffling. The customer(s) shouldn't have to be subjected to poor planning on management's end. I would have gladly passed on Mojito had I known that $39+tax and tip would have bought me food poisoning. It only seems logical that a place like this that has changed names/management so many times would want to know if patrons have gotten sick after dining there. An excellent owner and manager would want to amend the situation. If you can visit our table and check in with your guests' experiences, you can most certainly respond to an email with the words 'food' and 'poisoning' in the body of the message. Slow service, waiter being non-existent, and the like I can deal with and give another chance. But foodborne illness doesn't warrant a repeat visit.

Ordered a sandwich to go - baguette with prosciutto, cheese, tomatoes. The bread was stale, there were no tomatoes, and it was just awful. Soooo upset as I was in a hurry and this was my first meal of the day. I was already driving down the road so what recourse did I have. I had to throw it out Bc it was just disgusting. You'd think they would at least have edible food but no. I mean stale bread?? Who does that?!?!? Freaking cheap, stupid, pretentious fake hippies; that's who. I'm really really so angry about this. Plus how come this place doesn't have any gluten free items?? I guess I wont even bother asking about organic. Plus this place has very few electrical outlets as well. That whole middle table? No plugs anywhere. Ahhhhh so angry now. Thanks a lot for ruining the first meal of my day w your sorry excuse for a "baguette" sandwich.

Excited to find out they have gluten free products until coming into the store to not be greeted and once we asked a question about specialty items for gluten free products, the individual working said "you can call the owner!" We would like that, but she didn't give us any information.

OMG .... If you want to throw up for an hour enjoy your dinner.... I don't do the buffet, I ordered off the menu.... Shrimp Egg Foo Young....1st bite I New I was in trouble....took the second..... RANCID...... Threw up 4 times......DO NOT GO here unless your a Marine!! God help me I will get thru the night.... Beer was skunky as well.... Worst FOOD EVER, Staff was very pleasant....Beautiful restaurant....but...... Beware if you want to take a road trip across the street, I barely made it..... I love my toilet.....my best friend after going to this reusable, reservable, put it back out there eating facility. Texas Roadhouse or Cracker Barrel if you don't want to be ..... loving your hotel toilet!! -------0

Wish I could give them 0 stars! I was with my bf on our way home and we decided stop here. The workers are extremely rude and careless. We went inside and order and the food was cold. My bf's burger was soggy and weird looking of course he didn't eat it. My sandwich was ok and the fries too. My surprise was when I got home after a couple hours and I started throwing up and feeling sick. This food gave me food poisoning. I'm assuming they leave the food sitting out until someone goes and buys it. It was suspicious that no one was there when we went. No customers at all and I understand why. This location either has to close or change the workers.

I understand why people would like the prices here, but they sacrificed all other aspects of a decent restaurant. Including quality of food and especially service. I am allergic to many things and they did not really seem to care or listen when I told them, which made me concerned that there may have been things in the rolls that could have made me very sick. When we received our food it seemed as if the sushi chefs have perfected the art of making fresh sushi appear as if it had been made the day before and left to sit under fluorescent lights. When we noticed one roll had a topping on it that was not listed on the menu that I was allergic to, when we alerted the chef they seemed annoyed with us and refused to remake or replace the roll with something else. After this final slight, we asked for all of our uneaten food to be boxed and went to get Italian food up the road. The sushi was later consumed as high munchies, and it still tasted like fishy paste. Something's fishy is right, but not in the way you would like.

Well first off, our waitress was incredibly rude. She was very short and didn't say a word as she served our drinks. Second, DO NOT order the steak salad. My mom and I both ordered the steak salad for lunch just yesterday and in a few hours we were both doubled over with food poisoning. We lost a whole day of sight seeing in Nashville because we were getting sick for the rest of the day in the hotel room. This is by far the worst bout of food poisoning I've ever had and it is pretty worrisome that an established restaurant does not take proper care with their food. Definitely would not recommend.

Perhaps we were at Vetri on the worst night they ever had. I hope so. Vetri has been great for the city and we live nearby. But what we had was a first class price, not a first class experience. One fellow whom Vetri thought fit to welcome wore a t-shirt and cargo shorts, though he was a picture of refinement next to a four-top whose one member vomited on the table and floor, a kind of real-life reenactment of the Monty Python scene. We unfortunately had a front row seat for this. The staff grabbed the linens, and once the people were gone re-set the table -- without wiping any surfaces until I spoke up and insisted. The meal? Well...Some very nice moments for sure, but with two bad misfires. A badly prepared ribeye, raw and chewy, unseasoned -- a complaint the GM later responded to by saying they've had "great feedback" from others (presumably from such experts as the guy in the cargo shorts) and a cheese course with goat cheese so overripe it was separating, with ammonia smells that would have been appropriate and very welcome had they come from the floor and the table where the vomit had just landed. That staff thought it appropriate to keep rolling out the courses to us, was more bad judgment in a situation they hadn't of course created but handled ineptly. It was as if it was time to turn the tables over. All this for a mere $630 including tax and tip, with the GM later, having had time to, um, digest the whole thing, offering to make up for the disaster "next time," including helping with a reservation to get in. What do you say to an offer like that, thank you, master, and may I have another? Oh, and they gave us a cook book, a memento to remind us of the experience should we ever manage to forget it. We anticipated a once-in-a-lifetime experience, and I hope that's exactly what it was.

BURGER DOWN. 1) My son just drink curdled milk..... we did not discover it until getting home. Totally spoiled. 2)#1 on top of complete dietary insensitivity. You know, if you have any dietary restrictions, this is not a great place for you. After requesting no egg, meat, or dairy, My salad came out with a dressing that had egg in it (after being reassured that it did not-I kept asking that God ) and bacon directly on the salad...and the SECOND time it had egg on it. And all of this is after clarifying, I am vegan. It's either lack of attention to detail, lack of ability to understand the definition of vegan, or you just don't care. Anyway you slice it I won't be back and would encourage anyone with a food allergy or restriction to follow suit.

where to start... we selected this restaurant because my husband has Celiac disease and it said they offer gluten free pasta. Thinking this meant they would be educated on how to handle a gluten allergy, WRONG. The waiter had no idea what gluten free was or what menu items contained gluten, and was very annoyed at the questions we were asking him. If you are going to offer gluten free you need to specify if this is allergy friendly. The atmosphere was tacky and the lamps were dusty and had spider webs coming off of them. The other patrons were all elderly individuals, which they seem to cater to, and it was very clear that we were the youngest people in the place and it was very awkward. Personally, I am a very picky eater and simply requested a full size of the side of pasta marinara, the waiter had no clue what to do and charged us $20 for a bowl of penne that obviously came from a box with marinara sauce that was 90% olive oil and was awful. My husbands gluten free pasta was very overcooked, because they clearly have no training on how to properly prepare gluten free pasta. Finally, the dessert. They need to have an actual dessert menu available and not rely only on a cart, the cart is cute but not practical. We asked about dessert and our waiter made a huge deal about bringing over this giant cart to our table, even though we simply asked if any dessert options were gluten free (wishful thinking). When he showed us our options we said no thank you and the waiter got angry and pushed the cart away, making us feel very uncomfortable. All said and done we paid $50+ for terrible pasta and ended up going to Wendy's afterward because we were still hungry. Over priced and will eventually fall out of business if they don't change their ways and hopefully become more appealing to the younger generation who don't want to pay $20+ for a terrible dish and be forced to have your car parked by a valet, even though there is a huge parking lot. Its trying its hardest to be upscale but its just tacky.

I love Wawa. Beats the pants out of 7-11 and it has made-to-order breakfasts, rapid (not fast) food, innumerable types of coffees, and plenty of veggie snacks for the health conscious. This Wawa, located in the middle of downtown Media, is always busy with transient workers, school kids, housewives and everyday people looking for a bite to eat and convenience items. Store employees are always nice and eager to get you out of the store satisfied and quickly. This particular Wawa, however, has no gasoline. And as well, and chief reason why it doesn't rate four stars, is the fact that Wawa has made the express decision that they won't stock milk substitutes. For God's sake, almost 60% of the population is now lactose intolerant! Get with it, Wawa!

Probably one of the worst Carrabbas I've ever ate at and the chain is one of my favorite places to eat at! I ate there Wednesday 5/22 around 11:00 I ordered my usual chicken bryan, grill asparagus with lentil soup! About 4 hours later I began to feel very ill, vomiting, diarrhea, nauseated and had a really bad headache. The next day same symptoms but felt very weak, my joints hurt I was still vomiting and had diarrhea. Here it is day three and I was up vomiting again last night and woke up to an excruciating headache that I couldn't get out of bed as soon as I woke up. It's 11:26 on Friday been having diarrhea off and on but still feel weak and tired. I would hope that this restaurant follows the national standards for food and safety! But looking back my lentil soup was only Luke warm and my chicken didn't taste like it normally does, it usually has sun dried tomato's but these tomato's didn't have the same taste, my chicken had a weird color and I should've sent it back, but being in a hurry and hungry I disregarded these things. I was only able to eat half of the chicken bryan! I just wanted to share my experience here hoping this doesn't happen to anyone else and I hope Carraba's looks into this and test those foods I ate to avoid making anyone else sick!

People are nice enough, and so is the setup. It was nice enough to sit outside, so that was enjoyable enough. Parking was difficult to find during the day with it being on busy Virginia Ave. Definitely not worth charging $15 for a "patty melt". After stumbling upon spicy ketchup, bacon that was actually ham and being challenged on my fake egg allergy (a must in order to get my patty melt without an egg, otherwise it would have been "politely declined"), I won't be rushing back to Milktooth anytime soon. If pretentious atmospheres are your thing, go for it. Otherwise, you're not missing out.

The only reason I go here is if work people want to go. Today I got a caesar salad. it had parm and blue cheese. Um, blue cheese? What if I was allergic? They took it back. A man instead of my waitress brought it out and said "here you go. FRESHLY made." There was still blue cheese in my salad! They actually picked out the blue cheese. I expect a LOT more from a "nice" place that charges expensive prices for mediocre food. Really annoyed.

What a disappointment. It's so cool looking and I was ready for a great protein packed breakfast sandwich but I have an allergy to pork. If I see there is only one grill, I ask for an egg to be cooked separately - no way, not here. When I asked if I could just get an english muffin, the counter gal said, nope - they're on the grill too. Is there anything I can get except for baked goods - anything hot involving an egg? Nope. Wow. NO way? Won't be back.

Hi . Last night we drove to Han Dynasty in Exton to see if they were open. They were, however, for take out only, which was fine with us as we are social distancing! We tried to place an order with the one man who was there. He was totaled stressed and could not confirm modifications to our order with the kitchen staff as he said none of them spoke any English. I have a severe allergy to an ingredient and to be honest he could not help or cared to help us. I think he was overwhelmed. We have been customers of this location for years and wanted to share this story with other customers who may also have allergies and require modifications to entrees. We were also a bit surprised that he was the only one outside of the kitchen staff.

Food is great been there 20x pre covid but as a business they are a mess especially when ordering take out. Couple months ago wanted to order pickup, was told if I came in I could, came in and was told whoever I talked to on the phone was wrong and had no idea what they're talking about. Yesterday placed an order for pickup, an app, arribiatta and bolognese pastas. Someone I was splitting these with had a dairy allergy (which both pastas would be fine with) so I asked if you could put any cheese on top, on the side. The girl on the phone even asked if it was because of an allergy on the phone! I show up to pick it up, was told it wasn't ready and also given an FYI the kitchen would probably just put cheese on it anyway. Like are you kidding? An accident is an accident if they put cheese on, but to consciously say screw someone with an allergy we're going to do it anyway.. Walked out ordered something else. Why would I pay for something that you told me is a health concern to someone eating your food?? I get calls and nonsense texts from the chef francesco about it two hours later. How about you guys figure out how to tell customers our chefs are unable to make any changes whatsoever and just not take my order in the first place (or just not throw cheese on top which seems pretty simple to write on an order ticket for the kitchen to follow) instead of waste both of our times. Maybe make sure your kitchen and staff understand what each other can and can't do and communicate that to customers if there is going to be an issue?? The food is good, I'll give them that. But this ordeal is unacceptable...

Okay so I am no Chipotle feen and now I exactly know why. I just purchased a chicken burrito bowl and all it did was make me want to starve myself for a month. First of all, the chicken was ANYTHING but chicken. Like exactly what part of a chicken did I just eat, I have no idea. The grilled veggies were burned. The guacamole was disgusting. The rice was probably the best part of my meal. I swear the beans were raw. Everything was so tasteless and bland that thinking about it right now makes me wanna vomit already. I don't get the fascination with this place. You want some good food?..head over to Freebirds in Isla Vista. Must admit thought,the fact that they have brown rice was pretty cool. I am sorry this place deserves to get shut down. On a happier not, I probably won't eat for another day or so, yay to losing a couple of pounds -___- Oh and the workers are a little on the 'rude' side. The outside seating is nice. I've been sitting and staring at this foil plate of a failure for the past 30 minutes.

We sat for 15 min before we got our drink order then after waiting 12 min for our drinks it took another 40 min for food, table never pre bussed. The app came out before the beer then I asked for refills they never arrived. I had to ask another random employee for a refill 10 min later.Our server was mia through our whole dinner. Then 20 more min for check. Horrible service on my husband birthday. The guy was standing in back talking to all his buddies as I sat watching him thirsty as hell. The ambiance was cool but the server didn't care about us at all with that being said I still tipped $18 because I realize sometimes their busy but he ruined my husbands birthday . My husband was so irritated the whole meal. He didn't even eat hardly any of the food barely drank his beer what a waste of time in such a beautiful restaurant. Sloppy service , so disappointed. Then since we posted Birthday on the reservation the guy brought a dessert, he was so stressed he didn't eat it. Also we were in the restroom so we (me & my son) couldn't even sing. What an epic failure. As mothers we always have to put on a smiling face but this broke my heart for him. Then a few hours later I was throwing up, my hubby woke me at 6am with same issues. I called this morning and spoke with manager. I had the snapper curry. I eat snapper & curry often it tasted ok but my body did not like. I threw up to the vial. :( hoping today is a better day & my husband is all upset with the whole experience.

Long story short, I got food poisoning from their steak fajitas and I would never eat there ever again. I seriously thought I was going to die, worst week of recovery EVER. I had to fight with them and submit a complaint to the BBB to get a refund and reimbursement for my medical bills. I would never eat here again. I should have known better than to eat at an establishment that lets their customers throw peanuts on the floor...Dirty place.

The instructor was fabulous, but the studio's pit bull was present throughout the class. WTF. Typical Reno trash (pit bulls, tattoos and tobacco) don't belong in a yoga studio. And you probably wouldn't want to go there if you have a dog allergy.

Never going here again! I repeat, I will never give them another penny. The staff is slow and clearly overwhelmed. When my food finally came, it was cold and uncooked. 1/2 the mussels weren't open. I asked them to recook the food. When my food came back a 2nd time it was still cold and looked exactly the same like they did nothing to it. I sent it back again and asked for the manager. The manager took about 20 to 30 minutes to come to my table. In the meantime the rest of my friends were basically done eating. My request was to get my food to go and of course have it taken off the bill. The manager told me that they can not offer "free" food. He did however offer a bottle of wine or dessert. Wait what?!? I have never in my life been to a restaurant that would not go above and beyond to make up for serving uncooked food to a customer. And per another review, I do know that they in fact do offer some type of discount for their lack of service. I guess you have to be of a different hue for them to value you as a customer. 98% of the guests were black. 98% of the staff was non black. You get the picture. Moving forward, I will spend my money where I am valued. By the way, I actually had food poisoning and was projectile vomiting from the few mussels I ate that I thought were cooked. Never again!!

Old, dried out food. Over priced. Half the time there is nothing even appetizing. The service is surly and unfriendly at its best. Don't waste your money or make yourself suffer through some dried-out--who knows what this is--and pay $$$$$ for it. Just walk across the street and get something edible and reasonably priced....and probably much nicer service. Oh....and the place is filthy. It does not look clean. And if you go to sit down and eat your "meal" at one of their tables, don't expect to find one even remotely clean. They are all dirty, smeared with food, left over crumbs and who knows what....it's like eating in a pig pen. Gee....that's real nice with Covid-19. "Here's your dried-out, over-priced food stuff. Now go sit at any one of our filthy tables and catch Covid-19 or any other pathogen that THE HOSPITAL STAFF may have left to contaminate the table YOU'LL be eating. For a hospital, it's a filthy, inedible over-priced "dining" experience that you really DO want to miss. Walk across the street and get some fresh food in a clean environment. You and your loved ones deserve better than this. Oh...sometimes patients come down and eat at those tables. Who knows what germs they have or why they are there, but I don't want to eat off their dirty public table when they are done. They are in a hospital, you know.

I hate to give this place such a low rating as my experiences have varied. I'll be honest and say that I've only eaten here about 4 times, as I was a always a patron of the Lee Garden in Broomall. Unfortunately, the Lee Garden has closed. My first three experiences at Szechuan Hill were great! The food was excellent and I thought I had found a replacement for the Lee Garden.... On my fourth visit I ordered the same thing I always order, the General Tso Chicken platter which includes pork fried rice and an egg roll. My wife ordered the same and we split some Wonton Soup. I went to pick up our food, and as always the cashier was friendly. I brought the food home and my wife and I enjoyed a nice dinner together. About 15 mins later I began feeling very ill and faint. (I have no allergies or food related allergies.) Long story short, I became violently ill to the point of going to the E.R. as I was unable to walk or speak. I was essentially told that the food poisoning I had received was so severe that I had gone into a form of toxic shock. I write this review not as a rant, but to bring to light the inexcusable response we received from Szechuan Hill. When my wife called to explain what happened while I was in the E.R. the owners kept repeating "no refunds". We were not looking for a refund, we were simply trying to inquire if our food was prepared separate or together as we both had the exact same meal, yet only I was sick. Overall, had I not had that experience I would have given it a 4 star.

It doesn't look like much, but this local place was great for take out. Due to COVID-19, we haven't been going out much, but got real tired of cooking after a whole month. We wanted to support a local business, and were able to have a no contact pick up. Win win all around. I ordered the Thai shrimp wrap on a gluten free tortilla and a side house salad. The wrap was extremely filling and I ate my salad the next day for lunch. I always love when I can get two meals for the price of one! Would have saved half the wrap but it probably would have been soggy the next day anyway. Will definitely be back here to try something else.

Okay... I love this place because they will do ANYTHING gluten free and as someone with a gluten allergy you really start to miss Italian food. The service here is sadly always terrible. It takes forever to get your drinks and food. The pastas are average at best in all honesty. Not very saucy or big. The pizzas on the other hand are delicious. They are personal pizza sized and you can add/ take away anything you want. The desserts are all right but once again if you are GF then you take advantage

I tried this place for the first time over a year ago, but I got really bad case of food-poisoning from eating here. I had to call out of work for 2 days. I have a pretty tough stomach and don't get sick easily, so that means either the meat was bad or someone didn't wash their hands after going to the bathroom then prepared the food. The burrito tasted decent and I liked the chips and salsa but obviously I would be crazy to return to any place that lacks sanitation. I tell everyone to avoid Moe's like the plague. Chipotle has never let me down. Its more flavorful too. Stick to the burrito joint that earned a superb wide-spread reputation for a reason! Plus now its a few doors over.

I got cookies from here and got an allergic reaction, even though I was explicitly told there were no peanuts in the monster cookie. I tasted peanuts and I am having an allergic reaction right after eating the cookie. Fix this.

This place is so gross and dirty. I knew we should've left without eating, but we didn't and now I have food poisoning. The women's bathroom was disgusting. It stunk and the one sink didn't work. One of the kids menus we got had dried up food of some sort on the back. Good news is of the 4 of us I seem to be the only one that got sick. Sadly the food was good going down. Not so fun coming back out.

We chose this on our first night in Nashville. Pros: good atmosphere, lively upscale sports bar, friendly service. Tuscan tavern fries and salmon were really good. Good beer selection; I enjoyed the Bearded Iris IPA Cons: fish tacos were just okay, wish they were grilled and not fried. The taco shells were over cooked and hard to eat. Short rib tacos also just okay- really tasty sauce but meat was over cooked. Mahi sandwich was really over cooked and I wasn't a big fan of the homemade chips. The worst part was my mom got sick while we were still there. Her stomach did not do well with the fish sand and fries. Others ate some of both and didn't get sick, so maybe it was an allergic reaction (she has never had that happen before). Unfortunately, I just couldn't go back.

I'll start with- NUT ALLERGY SAFE!! Only nuts are on salads (they're great about no cross-contamination). YES the whole grill is safe for anyone with any kind of nut allergy. That means you can eat the pancakes/french toast for once!! (And do it- get the chocolate chip pancakes, they're insane). It's fair to say that I think about Ants Pants almost every day of my life... All the hype is true. The quality of the food has NEVER gone down, which is huge. And there's so much variety- meaning fabulous different options from every other basic cafe. The owners are also completely lovely people who deserve the great reputation that proceeds them. I also recommend the spinach/goat cheese omelette (caramelized onions- swoooon), the sweet and hot, or the hashes. And get the Tim Tam milkshake to go. You will have a hard time choosing anywhere else after you've been here!
This food does not taste correct. The sauce, veggies, meat. I can't pinpoint it, but it doesn't taste like other Korean food I've had. Also, everyone in my party got food poisoning from the chicken.

This is the worst Los Betos on planet earth I highly recommend no one ever eat here in their lifetime I would give this place a half star if I could I have literally been food poisoned by this place I am going to get the health department definitely involved it is a disgrace that this place is still open I have literally been throwing up all night long and I literally can not wait till this place opens to give these people a piece of my mind I paid over 35$ for three burritos two California burrito and a chorizo egg and cheese and I was very disappointed not only was there something wrong with the meat it smelled like it had been marinading outside in the middle of 110% weather DO NOT GO HERE PLEASE TRUST ME VERY BAD HEALTH DEPARTMENT WILL BE NOTIFIED...

Welcome to the Hotel Gaylord California -- you can check out any time you like, but you can never find the door to leave. Kidding. Kinda. I told someone while I was there that I felt trapped in a nine-acre mall slash botanical garden with hotel rooms (seriously, some of my colleagues had their allergies aggravated by all of the greenery. It was crazy. Pretty and green, but crazy.) It was also so big I felt slightly confused and overwhelmed, and it took forever to get to the places I invariably needed to go for the conference I was attending. Tips: *Get a map. Read it. Keep it with you. All of the hallways look the same and if you end up in the Jack Daniels restaurant drinking with the band you'll need help finding your way home. I did. (I didn't drink with the band, just near them. That's different.) *The meal I had at said Jack Daniels restaurant was the best. The fried chicken there was absolutely wonderful and a highlight of my Gaylord extravaganza -- not like I got to go anywhere else in Nashville, because I couldn't find my way out of the hotel. *Do not go into the sports bar if you are easily overwhelmed by lights and sound. They have eleventy billion televisions and you cannot escape any of them. I love sports and tv and I was blinking within minutes. *The Mexican place is pretty good, too. You can eat well here just sticking with the apps, especially the guacamole. Entrees were okay, but not awesome, and you can easily make a meal on starters and drinks here. *The lobby garden place that also serves sushi was my least favorite restaurant in the joint. Order there with care. *Room service is really limited and super expensive. I was disappointed because we kind of wanted to hang in the room the first night and would have had to venture out for full service in the place pretty late, which we didn't want to do. Also, no Bravo on the tv! No Top Chef! We were sad. ;) On the good side, the staff was friendly, the room was nice, and the restaurants were pretty good, although overpriced. It just wasn't my scene overall, and if I were going for vacation, I wouldn't find it relaxing at all. This would probably be good for the Jack Daniels' bottom line, however, as my friend's tea-marinated pork chop was so good I'd totally go back there again just to get my own.

I would have rated this a 4 star up until today (wide selection, but a tad over-priced). This is the only place I have found in Philly that carries Gluten-free beer. I live some distance away from the store, so I walked down, and after my 45 min to 1 hour walk, I was told that the employee couldn't provide me with a 6 pack of Red Bridge because "[he] was the only one in the store." Their refrigerator with the GF beer was broken so he would have had to go in back to get it. I was literally the only customer in the store and I even offered to stand outside while he got it.... He told me to "come back later." I will either go without gluten free beer from now on or go some place else. It's sad to see a local store with so much potential employ people who won't help customers with their products.

We were seated on time for our reservation. The wait staff when present was pretty good, I would say very accommodating due to the food allergies of my girls. My steak and shrimp came out tepid. My wife had salmon that was over done and her mashed potatoes were cold. I was disappointed with the kitchen service. This used to be my go to place to celebrate a special occasion but I think the reputation of firebirds is on the decline. We will be finding a new place to celebrate.

This review pains me to write, because I wanted to love it here so, so badly. Ivd been to Kanella twice now, and both times I have had the same issues: the male servers I have had have been terrible and I've gotten sick after my meals, which is a total shame because this is my favorite cuisine of all time. The first time I dined, was for my birthday and I informed the staff I was gluten free and couldn't eat onions. They seemed accommodating off the bat but I later learned in my meal, my dish had scallions and breadcrumbs nestled deep inside of it. The waiter was the least bit apologetic and I suffered for the next 2 days. More recently, I came here for brunch and was so excited to finally try their gorgeous looking menu.
