After 22 minutes of waiting for water, the waiter seemed to not really know anything about the menu or when I told him about my restrictions. We're started with the Greek plate which was unreal but when we moved to entrees, my meal had onions completely inside the eggs. Again, pissed. His nice gesture was to bring me the house made baklava as a dessert but I guess he didn't realize that was a puff pastry of gluten?

Nice restaurant with a good atmosphere. Accommodating for our large group. Everyone loved the biscuits and focaccia to start. Sure wish I could have shared in those! Being gluten free, I was appreciative of the servers knowledge of which food choices would be appropriate. Friends at the table who ordered the oysters were not impressed. All agreed that presentation was on point. The portions were all quite small for the price. The sea bass was very good, but the rest of the dish was lacking. My husband thought the short ribs were a little bland, and his asparagus was terrible. The lobster risotto that we shared was very good, but there was only one actual piece of lobster in the entire dish. We were charged for an additional bourbon cocktail & the check had to be corrected. Overall way too expensive for what we did have.

Went here with a couple of friends when in town for the Gem & Mineral show. We arrived at the restaurant at 11:30am, received the food at 1pm, left at 1:15pm. I ordered the cornbread waffle, one friend ordered 2 eggs scrambled with hash-browns, and the other ordered 2 eggs over medium with hash-browns. Simple orders, nothing special, very friendly with waiter. Several people who came in after we were seated were fed before us. My guess is they feed the locals first, can't blame them much for that, but way too long of a wait. Once the food arrived, it was HORRIBLE and INEDIBLE. My waffle was so dry it was a real challenge chocking it down. Both friends said the eggs were not done properly and the hash-browns were overcooked making them hard enough to be painful to bite into. Even worse, I got FOOD POISONING!!! Just thinking of that waffle gives me a strong urge to puke. I slept from the moment I got home from the gem show (about 7:30pm) until about midnight. At the time I woke all sweaty and nasty so I took a shower completely in the dark, then tried going back to sleep. At that point I was finally able to throw up, but not everything. I had to get a bucket so I could try throwing up from bed. I still couldn't go back to sleep because I was overheating, so I had to put a cold wet washcloth over my tummy to cool it down, then I was able to sleep until 9am. I woke up no longer feeling sick but with a bad headache. Took some Excedrin and a few hours later was finally able to function as a human.

Ever since this joint opened up i've been itching to try it, mainly because many nights i've had some drunk cravings for pho, but a lot, if not all, pho places in edmonton close before 11. Miss Saigon is open late on weekdays, and until 4am on weekends!!! CRAZY! I came here with my boyfriend, unfortunately he was recovering from food poisoning the night before, so he wasn't too hungry or ready to eat. Bless his soul though, he forced himself to eat regardless since he knew I wanted to try it. The parking isn't ON whyte ave, so it made it easy to park without having to worry about paying. They have their own parking lot shared with other stores The decor inside is light bulb themed with some booths and some half booth half tables. Smaller than I had anticipated but still nicely decorated! The sizes here are larger than other places. The regular size at Miss Saigon is a large any place else, and the regular is only $10 dollars! The broth was good, I could tell that they simmered the spices and bones for a long time. The broth itself is really hearty, but had a little too much cilantro for my liking, none the less, still good! They have a big wall painted with chalkboard paint that showed all the spices and things they put inside the broth (such a cute idea!) Another popular item I wanted to try was the bubble tea that came in the light-up light bulbs. I tried the original milk tea, which was a bit too sweet for my liking. The tapioca was soft and chewy though. The next time I have a hankering for late-night vietnamese food, I'm definitely coming back to Miss Saigon :)

I was very impressed with Kawa's customer service. I spoke to the man on the phone about peanut allergy concerns and he reassured me that they could be sure there was no cross contamination as long as I left a note about it on my online order. Once we picked it up too, he said that they were sure to not leave anything even remotely resembling something that could've come in contact with a nut on the plate. (I did miss having ginger with my sushi though lol.) Their system for COVID measures was great and interesting too -- with a mic that you speak into when you pick up your order so there's no contact whatsoever. They had the entire order ready perfectly on time for pickup and my favorite part was how the spicy mayo and eel sauce complimented the sushi (it's a little bit extra, but well worth it!). Cheers again for their awesome customer service and attention to detail.

Warning, this is a Devour Downtown review. I was so excited to try out Livery and I was so underwhelmed. Three friends and I decided to try Livery during Devour Downtown. We found they didn't accept reservations, but weren't worried. We were coming on a Wednesday night and had read that it typically took about an hour to get seated. We put our name in at 7:15 and were told that the wait would be about 40 minutes. We grabbed seats at the downstairs bar and were unable to get the attention of the bartender for about 30 minutes. Once we finally got their attention and got our first round of drinks, we were not able to get a second round. One of my friends never got her drink she ordered the first time. We tried to get the bartenders attention several times over and were unable to do so. By 8:15 we still hadn't been called to be seated. When we spoke to the host, she said that our table would be ready in 10 minutes. We weren't seated until 9 pm. Once seated, our server was unable to take our order for a few minutes, which was completely fine as they have so many options. I ordered off the Devour Downtown menu selecting the Polenta and the Chile Relleno. Our food arrived at our table at 10 pm and by then most of the restaurant had cleared out. The Polenta was absolutely to die for an definitely the best starter on the table, everyone loved it. The other starters my friends ordered (civiche, queso empanadas) were less exciting. The Chile Relleno was so disappointing; it lacked flavor. I had one bite and didn't finish it. Then our server brought out the flan and churro dessert. This was tasty and we all really enjoyed the sweet finish. We were all impressed with the space. As other reviews mention, it's much bigger than you expect with both an upstairs bar and downstairs. Also, our server was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu, including it's gluten free options for my friend. He did apologize for our wait time (from arrival to finish) and mentioned several times that they were very busy. However, It seemed silly to us to arrive at the restaurant at 7:15 on a Wednesday and not leave until 11 pm. I will absolutely go back to Livery and re-review them not during Devour Downtown and try their other food and drink options when they aren't so busy, but if I were you I would not go back while this special is running.

I hate giving negative criticism, but I feel like it is sometimes necessary. I wanted to like this ice cream shop because it's in my neighborhood, but it just doesn't compare to Brics in Broad Ripple (in my opinion THE best ice cream in Indy). It does have some good points though. Pros - Lots of flavors and options (kosher, gluten free, dairy free, soy, fat free, yogurts, low sugar, dye free, etc.) - Lots of parking - Friendly staff, willing to give you lots of samples Cons - The single scoop is literally only one scoop for $3.75. I guess I'm spoiled from getting 3 big scoops for the same price at Brics in Broad Ripple. - The sterile dining room doesn't make me want to sit down and eat ice cream. It feels like a chain frozen yogurt place. No character, like The Scoop or Brics. Hopefully, some/all of these concerns will be addressed at some point. Again, I really want to like this place, but sadly, I don't at this point.

I honestly do not like putting up bad reviews. I would like to think that over all my experiences will be good no matter where I go, but that's just not life. I live right down the street from this store, so it is one of the places I frequent about 4 times a week. That's very quickly changed. Today I went in and Had a terrible experience. All stores will have issues with one thing or another, But what I witnessed totally turned me off completely because it is something preventable. I was waiting in the deli And as I waited for my turn, I watched one of the employees blow their nose in the open, open this tissue and inspect the mucus, Toss the tissue in the trash can and proceed to go cut my meat. I was so angry that I didn't even have it in me to say anything because I knew whatever I said would be very volatile. I told the manager who quickly apologized and got me another order of meat and refunded my purchase. Regardless, the training here must be lacking because as a nurse, and human being, i know the importance of hand washing & cross contamination. I'm seriously just disgusted and appalled. Ugh. Never again

Just arrived here and the hotel room is disgusting. Hair on the bathroom walls. Bathroom floor is dirty. Went to the front desk she offered to down grade my room with no compensation. Called Wyndham Customer Service spoke with Account Supervisor German id number 73787 and he basically said there's nothing they can do. They weren't even willing to compensate my points or compensate me for the night. This is disappointing and I will be talking to Silvia the manager in the morning. This is ridiculous. I was given bleach though to clean my hotel room. So now I'm housekeeping. But I'm paying to be here. Free labor for them at my expense. To top it off I'm allergic to bleach and I asked the front desk for gloves and she said there were no gloves.

There are many better options for a Chinese buffet in the area. None of the cutlery looked clean and a large amount of the plates were dirty. I had to ask for a knife four times before we were actually given a knife that was only marginally cleaner than the first. The only reason I had to ask for a knife was that the cutlery was placed next to the deserts. The white rice was hidden in a corner by the soup so if you didn't want soup you weren't finding the white rice. There were no labels over the food only writing on the glass which was often incorrect. The only food that was marginally better was the food cooked on the hibachi grill in the back. Unfortunately it was very unhygienic in that he was handling raw food with the same utensils as he was the handling the cooked food with. There was the possibility of cross-contamination with between the food. Some of the placement of the dishes were strange such as having shrimp next to grapes. Their vegetables had no flavor only covered in a sodium-filled sauce, the exact type you would get at a bad type of Chinese restaurants. We get all of this for the price of $16.00 per person, $15.00 with student I.D.

Always a good treat! And they're celiac-friendly! I get the little burger in a lettuce wrap. You can get as many (or as few) toppings as you'd like for no extra charge! The only thing fried in the fryer is fries so they're safe to eat as well (no gluten cross contamination). Fries portion is huge! You can definitely split the smallest size or the medium size with another person. Treat yourself and enjoy!

Worst meal EVER!!! Don't do it, just don't. Went for Thanksgiving because they offered a three course meal with options. Where do I begin, had a reservation, was told there was other reservations ahead of us, what does that even mean? finally seated, holiday menu choices included turkey, ham, tri-tip, salmon, was told they were out of turkey, out of salmon. OK, ordered a main course off the regular menu, lobster, and tri-tip. The lobster, size of a large shrimp, was spoiled, smelled like old cheese, but what do you expect for 19.99, tri-tip was chewy, please note ALL food was served cold. Desert options were apple or pumkin pie, we order both. Pies were, I kid you not, directly from a frozen pie cook off gone bad, both were tasteless and thrown on different size plates, and when I say thrown I mean it, what a joke. Waiter was an idiot. Oh yea, ordered a drink from the bar, only received it after asking three times. I would have complained to a manager but could not find anyone responsible for this dinning nightmare. Last but not least, the place is a dump with disgusting dirty carpet and loud as hell old holiday music blasting. Went there years ago and it was nice, WILL NEVER GO BACK, will let you know if I am vomiting up my lobster in a few hours. What a way to spend Thanksgiving, live and learn, at least we will have a holiday story to tell and laugh over for years to come. But seriously, do not go there to eat. Again, WORST MEAL EVER!!!

I was really excited to try this place today, decided to skip the wait and place a take out order. Almost everything was right except I ordered onions on my sandwich, it came with none. The sandwich was terrible. Moving on. My son ordered fruit and granola. Couple hours later threw up all his fruit all over the Nashville Zoo. So not only was my order wrong but the food was terrible. I gave it 2 stars because my husband, and other sons food, was fine.

What a disgusting city! Tucson is one of the worst cities I've been to in America! As a world traveler and someone who has been all over the states, it is pretty bad if it made my top 5 worst cities list. Driving into Tucson, the whole area looked sketchy. It honestly looked like the run down sections of Blythe, California. There seemed to be one main highway running through the city and the main streets had dangerous intersections! Have you ever driven through a double left turn lane that did NOT have a green arrow light? Neither had I until Tucson! The trees and shrubs were all overgrown and hid street signs, parking signs, freeway exit signs, and even speed limit signs! The streets were filled with potholes, lumps, and bumps, making for a rough ride everywhere you went! The streets were not driver friendly at all. Tons of homeless living on the streets in tents; comparable to the streets of Los Angeles county! There was so much trash and litter all over the streets and on the highway, the city looked and smelled like a hot pile of stinky garbage! Where was the city clean up service? It didn't appear that they had cleaned up the highways and sidewalks in the past 20 years! The amount of police patrolling the streets and highways was unbelievable. I've never seen so many cops on the highway pulling people over. Restaurants consisted of major chains and a few local spots of mainly Mexican & Asian food. There were no healthy options for the health conscious traveler. I literally felt sick the entire time I was in Tucson from the lack of normal food! If you have pollen and seasonal allergies, good luck to you in Tucson! I have never experienced allergies like I did in Tucson. Mesquite trees in every parking lot and on every street corner. Not to mention the Palo Verde trees and all the rest of the desert plants emitting their pollens into the air! No amount of Claritin, Benadryl, or prescription allergy relief medication worked! I was miserable the entire time I was in Tucson and couldn't wait to leave! Will not willingly return to this city!

Great talented musician, a one man band....guitar voice harmonica all top notch entertaining on a quiet noontime in sunny Bywater. Wines seriously overpriced Roses. An otherwise eclectic selection of whites & reds.....$ some okay value. Staff appeared tired and disinterested... maybe was a big late night yesterday? We were here noon hour.... Food selection not too flash for a dairy free or gluten free .....rustic....parking fine for a bicycle but ruff on cars in this neighbourhood watch out for MANSIZE potholes in the By water!

I commented food had been served undercooked or burned so they could know. I did not even want my comment highlighted by me, however they did. Instead of saying, we are sorry, thanks for the feedback I recieved retaliation every time I came in. It got increasingly aggressive and finally when I complained a server refused to seat and serve me. Telling me I complained so I would not be served. The manager on staff refused to take a complaint saying this person was her friend. Then I had a drunk in a mumu telling me I was rude, quoting things a random stranger would not know if the staff was not slandering me. I tried to be polite, when I was interrupted 3-4 times in 30 minutes, not even giving me a chance to put my conversation on hold, to respond. In 6 years I only commented on the food quality 3x. Yet the staff treated me as though I was a problem, not serving fully cooked non burned food. Instead their response is they cook their own food now. Awesome. Then it should still be consistent, not dripping in oil, scooped out, burned, or chunks of raw or varying degrees of being undercooked. I made a comment trying to give feedback. But instead of that I am gaslit. And when I respond to be quite clear the food is not ok how it's been served and they do need to address it. I am mistreated every visit and treated as rude leading up to that. Extremely unprofessional. I have watched people sit there 6-7 hours and not made to feel uncomfortable or pushed out as they are still drinking eating, which is what I experienced. Save yourself being treated as I was, or risking food poisoning eating here, and eat your food somewhere that will treat you well. Wow, I'm not the kind of guy to make a yelp post, but after the "dining" experience I had today, it's safe to say I will never be returning to this McDonald's location. They messed up my order and put cheese on a relatives burger, who is lactose intolerant. I called the place, the manager apologized and said they would be happy to replace it, and I went back, and everything was fine. But TODAY, I went in and had the same error occur, and called the manager, she apologized and I went back to the window, only to be treated as if I was stupid. I'm the one who had to drive all the way back 5 miles to your location for an order that was triple emphasized no cheese. And the issue is that I'm not even mad about them messing up, it's the way I was treated by a brunette female in the first window. I'll never be returning here again, and by the way I was treated today, I can't even be generous enough to give 2 stars.

If the Devil vomited a miscarriage, it would be the Foodery. I cannot think of any other place in Philadelphia that exploits the b.s. alcohol laws in this state and the lack of product knowledge in its customers harder than the Foodery does.... That's right, spend 20 minutes putting together a six-pack you know nothing about, wait on a line, bitch about the other customers, sweat the fact that you should already be somewhere else, and finally get to cashier and have him tell you that you owe him $55. Honestly, try to put those beers back and get new ones... your allowed... but, it's not gonna happen.... you'll buy them out of guilt or because you already wasted too much time.... It's a joke. No one but a few bartenders, alcoholics, and the staff at the Foodery know how much these things cost. Yea, there's the extremely intimidating price guide to gaze through if you have an extra 40 minutes of being-cheap-time to shuffle beer back and forth....but if they wanted you to know the prices of their products, they would tack the price of the product on the shelf thats holding it... They want you to goto the counter blind.... Flat. This isn't a bar. Its a convenience store. The Foodery participates in price gauging, and another convenience store needs to come along and undercut them to even this garbage out. Absurd.

I ate there with my whole family since the owner gave me a gift card, we all got sick. I don't k ow if it was the eggs or bacon (we all had that), but my mother actually went to the hospital over it. 3/5 threw up and all 5 felt horrible. Never eating here again, worst free meal I've ever had. If I could redo it, I'd pay to have NOT eaten there. Horrible horrible experience. Ps- our server was great though and did have good/fast service.

More like 3.5 stars. There were several gluten free options and all the food was delicious, but the service was slow. This was particularly annoying since they gave us the table for only an hour and then it took us 15 minutes to get our drinks.

I was on the way to the US Rowing Masters National Championships in New Jersey last week, and one of my rowers and I decided to stop in West Chester most of the way way through our very long drive to have a sit-down dinner and avoid the Philadelphia rush hour. West Chester, unlike nearby King of Prussia, looked cute and promising on Trip Advisor and Yelp, so we decided to get off the highway and just walk around looking for a place to eat. Avalon had a pleasant-looking sidewalk dining area with available seating, so after a few minutes of deliberation we settled on it. The staff seemed friendly enough, and we immediately scored an outdoor table. It wobbled pretty significantly, and after two reminders our server eventually came back and fixed it for us. Since it was early on a Wednesday evening happy hour was in full swing, so we were able to take advantage of discounted food and beverages. There was a nice little wine and beer list, and the entire menu looked delicious and very inspired by dining in Europe. I ordered a burger and my friend got the unlimited mussels. She chose the red sauce with tomato and chorizo. Her food arrived within ten minutes and urged her to begin eating, since I naturally assumed mine would be out shortly. It took maybe fifteen to twenty minutes more for mine to arrive unfortunately. Our server was also MIA during this time, so I was unable to check in with him and get the status of my food. Once it did arrive, I found that the fries had cheese all over them and had to be sent back due to my allergies. It took an additional ten minutes to receive more fries, during which time I occupied myself with my burger. I was starving at this point and certainly enjoyed it for that reason, but the patty seemed cheap and the bacon on top was definitely of the microwavable variety. The best part would be the sautéed yellow onions it was topped with...they were sliced in medium pieces and lent a nice depth of flavor to an otherwise unmemorable burger. I was grateful I'd only paid the happy hour price for it! The fries were delicious once they arrived, but I do wish the menu had said something about them being topped with cheese. I felt terrible having to send them back! My friend enjoyed her mussels but had just eaten a far better serving of them at a different restaurant the previous week, and therefore was underwhelmed. That sort of sums up my experience at Avalon in a nutshell. The space was gorgeous, the outside dining option was great, (once the wobble in our table was fixed) and I really liked the Dogfish beers they offered, however the spotty service, bland food, and miscommunication about allergens left a little something to be desired. Improving some of those things would make it a wonderful little restaurant!

Ok Indian food at a good price. Had the chicken curry, basmati rice, onion naan, and the gulab jamun for desert, all for about $10 bucks. They pride themselves on cooking healthy Indian food, with vegan and gluten free options. Probably the reason the food seemed to be missing something. Hard to pinpoint, but the food just isn't quite on the mark (not spicy enough, missing spices, etc..) and the menu is very limited. For example, no lamb curry on the menu, in fact the only lamb dish they had was available at the buffet. Never been to an Indian restaurant that did not have an ample selection of lamb on the menu. The gulab jamun was also not right. The syrup seemed to be lite and the balls seemed to be missing the ghee. Overall the place is bright and clean, the service good and friendly.

I got food poisoning from this restaurant. I ordered a turkey burger with avocado, spinach. Two hours later I'm in the bathroom. I ended up in the hospital 5 hours after that from sickness and dehydration. I spoke to owner wanted to claim no responsibility but wanted to give me a gift card for my troubles. I said no I want you to pay my hospital bill! Don't go there unless you want to get eix You didn't give me a gift card I didn't want a gift card. I wanted my hospital bill paid. Why would you offer me a gift card if you feel like it wasn't your fault. Food was mishandled that day, I'm sure of it. Many servers were very busy. I am sure that the proper procedures weren't being used. I was sick from YOUR RESTAURANt no where else. I also wasn't the only one who got sick. I'm just the only one with guts to say something. Sorry is not enough! I missed two hockey games ( was there from out of town for my son's hockey tournament) spent over a day in bed and went to the hospital and got a large bill even with my insurance which is extremely good and expensive every month. And I'm sure I will get more bills. It's not fair!

So we came in for a slice of chocolate loaf and a latte .... instead of sitting down to a delicious piece of chocolate-loaf...we get a hard stale piece of cake .... as I return to the counter I see the display piece of chocolate cake is missing .. and I ask the employee "did you take this out of the display case... and she replies " yes but I touched it to make sure it was ok.... of course I flip out .... the sign clearly says inside the case that those things are for display purposes only. Those things can be in there for days at a time. And she says to me this one was not that old .... I respond well those sandwiches in there look like they have been in there for weeks so I'm sure they are bacteria ridden and could certainly cross contaminate ... I had my $3.16 returned but how absolutely GROSS And then, I see the other young lady eating in the coffee station ... literally hand to mouth... and then without washing her hands she starts making someone's coffee order. :(

Well, after eating here for over 7 years and this being one of my absolute favorites, multiple dinners, birthday parties, client lunches, business lunches and THOUSANDS of dollars spent here this place did a 180. For the first time ever I was treated as a pile of trash by the manager while trying to place a large pickup order. Now my wife is gluten intolerant and Jazmine's has always accommodated her. Y using Tamari sauce instead of soy sauce. When I asked foe Tamari in the rice noodle dish, I was told by the female manager that "they didnt have Tamari" I stated I've had tamari in the sushi bar and food. She responded with "we only use it in the sushi bar." So I cancelled the order, however, with Jazmine's being one of my all-time favorites I decided to drive there and order in person thinking it could get straightened out. When I got there the manager was indeed the one on the phone. I explained to her my wife being gluten intolerant and how we've always had tamari there. She shrugged indifferently went into an adolescent tone of indifference and disgust with me and proceeded to tell me they have "three new chefs, and they told me no." So it went from no tamari, to tamari is only used on the sushi side to the chefs being the real problem all while the attitude was reminiscent of one of the worst teenage attitude "get out of my room" looks and tone from the "manager." So, I left and drove down the street 1/2 mile and spent roughly $250 at La Mint where the service was amazing and the attention to gluten free meals and needs is well attended to. To Jazmine's and all of the people I have recommended to you and the thousands of dollars I have spent there were dashed in one evening by one manager who could care less about her job, her customers or your reputation.

Delivery order... the good and the bad Ordered through uber eats. The good: ordered a gelati and a cocorush. Arrived well packaged and in tact. Tasted good too. The bad: ordered the cheese pretzel... it was pretty much a wawa pretzel w a cup of cheese. The cheese is DISGUSTING! Its nasty processed cheese. Almost made me vomit. The pretzel is decent, but not worth $4 bucks. All in all good, just don't get the cheese

Love the food. But as a vegan you should not put meat and vegan tacos in the same container when getting takeout. It does say in the instructions that it's an allergy issue as well. Tried to call to get a replacement but the phone just rings. Food was wasted as well as time and money.

What a lovely thing when the Patriarch and the Queen Mother appear on my doorstep offering gifts of lunch. Of course, since they are Seniors, this means going to a restaurant they are comfortable in. No african-thai-russian fusion food for these folks. They like their food straightforward, no curves. Samurai is their go-to place for Japanese. The same things are always ordered: Chicken & Vegetable Tempura Bento Box, Chicken Teriyaki Bento Box, and Chicken Gyoza. The Patriarch and I get cucumber sushi because we're both allergic to seafood, and the Queen Mother got the California Roll that comes standard with the bento. Both dishes are consistently good. The tempura is nicely lightly fried, not soggy or burnt, and has good flavor. The chicken teriyaki is a nicely grilled tender sliced chicken breast with caramelized onions. The meal is the same every singe time, bonus points for consistency! The service is usually nicely attentive, and the place is clean and warm (also important to Seniors). Parking can be a bit of a challenge, though you can often park across the street in the mini-mall's parking lot. Samurai, you are a Senior's dream. Good food, consistently prepared in a clean environment. Good job.

If I could put 0 stars I would. I tried to order to-go and the whole experience was ridiculous. I NEVER write bad reviews and I realize that COVID has been difficult to navigate and there has been reason for changes, I completely understand that. However, they now charge you $3 each for soup and salad on to-orders, which is included in the teppanyaki meals at the restaurant, "because not everyone likes it so they removed it from to-go orders." On top of that I have allergies and tried to order a meal without egg or dairy only to be told they will not accommodate allergies on to-go orders???? So they can gouge you for soup and salad but cannot make sure I don't go into anaphylactic shock? Normally I love Kobe's and I really wanted to be able to enjoy it today, but I am so put off by their complete lack of customer service today it will be a LONG time before I even consider coming back to this nonsense.

ABC Pizza House is a great example of a 3 star restaurant. Food is OK. Service is OK. Atmosphere is...well, I'll get to that in a minute. A very casual Italian/pizza restaurant- this place was busy on a Saturday night. We were sat quickly and started gazing over the menu. We got a pepperoni pizza as an appetizer- and then we all got entrees- I had eggplant rollatini and my friends had: chicken parm, seafood alfredo, and lasagna. All of the entrees came out looking the exact same- COVERED with cheese. No complaints here!! We also ordered a carafe of wine- only $8- score! But, be forewarned it's more like a 1/2 carafe size. And they also give you the teeniest little wine glasses. Now onto the atmosphere-. I feel as though they gathered all their employees and said "hey- our walls are kind of bare- could you each bring in a poster you have from home?" ...And that's how they decorated. Also, I should note that there were "placemats" with bail bonds and pawn shop advertisements on them. So classy- and was of much amusement to our table. The eggplant rollatini I had was quite good- but it seemed to be the only Gluten Free thing on the menu. A place like this- with a menu full of pizza and pasta- is torturous for those of us who are GF. If I don't return- that's the only reason- I have little willpower. But, overall- an enjoyable, cheap night out.

I hate to write bad reviews. But -- Kids Mac & Cheese had 2 pieces of hair in it. A friend and I shared a Fajita plate last night, both of us ended up with what we believe to be some mild food poisoning. Thankfully neither of our kids ended up sick, but my little one didn't even end up eating much because of the hair. Service was mediocre, waitress was kind and had a good attitude, but only came by 2 times in the hour plus we were there. Food came out fast, which is always nice especially when you're dining out with kids. They did comp they Mac & Cheese, but overall, I definitely wouldn't return.

Who knew that you could find a sushi buffet in the downtown area?! Someone recommended and we check out Crafts and Hops .... but when we got there, we learned that the food options were few and far between. So... we headed out on foot for lunch with no particular place in mind. We literally stumbled into this place. When I walked in, I was overwhelmed by the fish smell, but we were hungry and it seemed like a pretty legit spot. There were so many choices of sushi, that I wonder how long that each sat out before being consumed. I can totally see food poisoning in the future of anyone who intakes too much of this stuff. Here was my way around it. I figured out the one kind of sushi that wasn't on the buffet and I asked when and if it would be available, and voila... a few minutes later, as I was partaking in my miso soup and ginger dressed salad, appeared the California roll sushi. The host mentioned that it was ready, but I was going to wait and finish my soup and salad, instead he brought me a plate of if directly to the table. Wow, that was nice gesture and that main reason that I'll push my 3.5 review into a 4 ;)

After the hike lunch again. Saw the mixed reviews and took a chance. This time my luck ran out. The buffet foods were lukewarm on steam tables. The best were the desserts and the cilantro condiment [very spicy and tasty]. Everything else indicated that the chef cannot find the spice cabinet, as it was all BLAND. Won't go again. Peace a Pizza is right next door and they have a gluten free pizza!

We ate at The Buffet prior to a concert. My husband didn't even have time to finish his plate before he started getting sick. I waited until I got to the concert for my night to be ruined. After spending an hour in the bathroom, missing a great show, I was able to drag myself back to my seat. I don't think I will ever be able to eat seafood again! FOOD POISONING....not highly enjoyable! Of course we will never go back. Practice safe food handling folks, or you might just kill someone!

In response to this business. I was asked to revise my post. I simply stated the FACTS. The fact of the matter is...... there are strict guidelines regarding food service during this Covid-19 pandemic that were not being followed. I am not discrediting the business by simply stating the facts. Whomever the person taking orders and handling payments on that day did not switch gloves, let alone wash their hands in the process of transitioning from food orders and payments to handling food. There were 4 other workers on the truck whom were handling food. There are no valid excuses to not adhere to proper protocol while handling food. It should not be used as an excuse that no food was actually being touched by hands or the gloves but instead by serving instruments, or that orders were behind. The simple fact that the serving instruments, containers, etc. were being touched after handling orders and payments, with no hand washing or glove changes during transition leads to cross contamination. I should not have to explain this. Obviously we have differing opinions of what is considered sanitary and unsanitary. When you know better, do better. I completely understand how hard it has been for everyone during this pandemic and that is one of the reasons I came out to support. This business has definitely got to do better going forward. Even if we were not in a a pandemic, as food service workers they should know better. They should know the importance of hand washing and what the guidelines are and be putting them into action. If I hadn't pointed these things out, these gross errors would have continued.

Located in the Salesforce tower, this breakfast/brunch restaurant is a nice place to sit down for a quick bite or carryout to take to your office/desk. There is nothing that stands out about the menu or the food aside from the strawberry orange juice which is very tasty. Water is served in a wine sized bottle that you have to pour yourself. You would need to ask for ice. I ordered "Protein and Eggs". Scrambled eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes and gluten free toast. All tasted good. Again, not much stood out or was better than any other breakfast restaurant. The food did come out pretty quick and the food was hot. The menu is pretty pricey for breakfast. My bill was $18. I paid an extra $1.50 for gluten free toast. Based on the price, I probably won't come back here.

I'm sorry but this place has gotten so many last chances from me. I gave up already on the downtown one as it's clear they have no concept of returning customer satisfaction. They are on the tourist route so they don't need locals coming back there. Since I live up north, we decided to try the Oro Valley one. The one major gripe I had about the downtown one -- one of many gripes I've already reviewed here -- is that they forgot to make the meal gluten-free on the takeout three times in a row. Meaning, they'd never gotten it right -- as I'd ordered take out there a total of three times. They didn't really think it was much of a bother to have me wait 20 more minutes with an "I'm sorry" and have the rest of my takeout order get cold. So yes, the same thing happened in the restaurant/dining area of the Oro Valley location. They brought the meal, which specifically is designated on the menu as having a gluten-free option, with a flour tortilla. And since my dining partner didn't doubt it was gluten-free, he ate some of it before realizing. I can't believe this restaurant has no kitchen staff equipped to make changes; they are obviously a fast-food type of kitchen in the back where any variant requests would disrupt their automaton routine. The waiter was apologetic, I believe he comp-ed the meal, but the meal was ruined so it was the least he could do. So the downtown location is touristy-ridden, and the Oro Valley location can't think outside the box. No more chances.

Wanted to have a great experience here when they reopened but it was pretty ok. We arrived and we're seated quickly which was great and they accommodated getting us in a spot where a baby car seat could easily fit next to our table outside. The menu seems to be a lot smaller and different than the previous menu at the project which we were bummed about. When our waiter first came over I let them know I had a few dietary restrictions, he seemed unsure about how to answer my questions so bc of his uncertainties he just said I shouldn't order basically anything. When I asked him to check with the kitchen he initially said no. After much pressing on this he finally went back and asked. I learned that the blue corn tortillas (which are gluten free at corazon) are not gluten free at the project. When he finally asked the kitchen they let him know they did have some pre made gluten free corn tortillas on hand that they could use to make a taco. It always is odd to me when restaurants make corn tortillas which are traditionally gluten free with gluten, this should be more clearly identified on a menu and staff should be more knowledgeable and willing to accommodate. Once we finally got through the pain of ordering with our waiter we got our appetizer. We ordered the "avocado" which we assumed would be chips and guac. It was a little different but was delicious! The avocado dip had some sort of different season in it which made it delightful, would definitely recommend this! As for the tacos, we all thought the old project menu had better options and decided we'd prefer to just get the tacos at corazon as we thought they are ultimately better. Love the fun vibe of the project, but we'll keep going to Corazon at public market where they have everything down to an art and customer service seems to be be more on par.

I dine out very frequently and this place is not safe to eat! Food poisoning from the fish that they served The kitchen didn't seem clean at all. I also noticed the manger was running the food with the cook which was a sign of it being a unsanitary kitchen. Heath department should definitely be called to check this restaurant. NOT safe. Bad food!

This gave my husband food poisoning. He said the steak tasted off and kind of fishy and made him sick when we got home from eating in at radish. I got a pretty bad stomach ache after their food too, and we both left unsatisfied from not being full whatsoever. It was a bummer because people rave about this place but there wasn't anything special about it.

ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!! Honestly, the rice tasted like soap, some of the food I ordered smelled sour and I refused to touch it, the main dishes were HORRIBLE and either completely bland or just tasted like salt. This is honestly the worst food I have ever had, it was so salty I actually threw up. I wish I would have seen the reviews before ordering so I could save myself the trouble of ordering, throwing up and wasting money. If I could give zero stars I would.

I ordered via GrubHub and my order was completely wrong. I ordered a double burger on a gluten free bun and I was delivered a single burger with a regular bun. I have celiacs disease and my food was completely Inedible. My lunch break was completely ruined. I tried to call the restaurant and the phone just rang endlessly with no answer. This is the second time this restaurant has ruined a courier order and I am so upset. There are very few restaurants in Reno that actually offer gluten free buns for burgers and the upgrade is expensive. Literally the worst service ever.

This was one of my favorite Chinese eateries in stl because of the price and authentic dishes. Unfortunately I came here while I was home for the holidays and got horrible food poisoning that lasted for a week. If it makes anyone feel better I don't think it was the cooked food. I actually thinking it was the rice. No one else in my group got sick it was just me but I got so violently sick that I threw up on my way home and had chills for 24 hours. I think after a week my stomach is finally back to normal. I've eaten here three times, it was my first time getting sick but it'll haunt me forever. Eat here with caution!

Easily the worst dining experience I've had in my life. We entered the establishment and noticed a sign saying please wait to be seated so we stood at the door and waited while the server was at a table down the dining hall we stood their for 5 minutes while she sat talking with a group of people the cook had to come out and bring us to a table but we finally ordered a .5liter of beer, a coke, and a water then ordered two döner bowls but was informed they couldn't make bowls because they were out of rice which was ok so we switched to döner box meals booth without feta as were allergic which we informed are server of we were then brought a single water and then waited 15 minutes only to be served food covered in feta after waiting 15 minutes for food we made clear we could not eat and no drinks other then the water we walked out. Avoid this place if you have any self respect at all the service is a absolute joke

You can the burnt oil in the lobby. The chicken has no flavor. When you bite a chicken tenders it doesn't rip like NORMAL chicken tenders, it feels rubbery like. And the cook is going to get ppl sick with cross contamination. So unsanitary.

Some restaurants have famous chefs creating classic masterpieces. Others have kitchens creating complex recipes with carefully balanced ingredients to make works of art that cannot be changed. Other have such a high volume business at a very low price point that they cannot take the time for special requests. Milktooth in the Fletcher Place neighborhood of Indianapolis is none of these. Yet, they seem to be of the opinion that their food is so special that no alternations whatsoever can be made, and while it is mentioned at the bottom of their menus (but not on their Web page menu), their waitstaff is very snooty and unapologetic about it. Anyone with food allergies, gluten sensitivities, or immune disorders should beware. This restaurant does not care if you merely don't like certain food items or it those food items could kill you, they won't alter their food for anybody. I saw the food coming out of the kitchen for nearby tables, and I don't see why they have such arrogance. They weren't busy. The food presentation didn't look special to me. One of our local friends had recommended Milktooth as a trendy, artsy place for us to try when we were in Indianapolis on a business trip. One of the items my companion wanted to order included a sunny-side up egg. She, on advice of her doctor, does not eat uncooked egg yolks. They refused to fully cook the egg. What do they do with people who have serious egg allergies? They also refused to leave off the egg. When I wanted a sandwich with no bun, they refused to leave off the bun in the kitchen. I have a wheat allergy. The waiter told me to order the sandwich as it comes out of the kitchen and take the bun off myself. Well, once hot meat and sauces have been in contact with the wheat, that is not an option for me. He didn't care. "It is clearly posted on our menus that we do not alter our food." So, we told him that if the kitchen couldn't handle our simple requests, we wouldn't eat at all. He seemed shocked. No apologies at all. Apparently, Indianapolis diners are easily bullied by waiters at pretentious restaurants. For the remainder of our stay as we finished our coffee and tea, the waiter came by several times with a condescending tone to see if we wanted refills. It's a shame that, with people in Indiana suffering from hunger and starvation, this pompous little cafe would rather throw perfectly good eggs and bread in the trash. The coffee and tea we had was okay. Can't tell you about the food, because we didn't eat anything. The service was unacceptable. The general attitude of the management clearly is not concerned about the needs and desires of their customers, as they'd rather sicken their patrons than make very simple little changes. We shan't be back. If you go, beware.

This is my 2nd visit this year & I will not be back. The 2 stars is for the food & the chef. We didn't even stay this time because the manager's attitude was totally unprofessional. His name is Marvin. Maybe because they were understaffed & running late on reservations was the reason. But it was enough for half of our party to leave. My review will continue on the visit 2 weeks prior. The food was hot & delicious. I have food allergies so my food was prepared in the kitchen. It arrived hot with no complaints. We had children in our party so they were completely excited with the chef's performance. The restaurant was clean & practiced sanitizing frequently. Hand sanitizer was provided as you walked in. Masks were worn by the staff as well. Social distancing was also in effect. As stated previously, we will not be returning to this location but will try another. Hopefully their staff will be more professional.

Came here because they had bacon on sale and I wanted some of the sliced apples and mango dried fruits. Typically prefer Publix and will continue to go to Publix or Target for my needs unless liking for something specific like for this trip. The store has a lot of your more healthy food options and does have a great variety of gluten free foods. The are pricey of some items however. I do like that I can come here and get the bulk dried fruits and nuts in bag selections that I choose. I sure do wish the mangoes were not sweetened with sugar though.
Disgusting food. Food late by 2 hours. Manager hung up on me. Unprofessional. First and definitely last time I'm ever eating at THIS location. Now my family and I have food poisoning. Happy new year

I'm giving it two stars just because their staff was awesome and the bloody mary's were good. Other than that, their bacon has literally made my husband and I, never want bacon again. Do NOT order the Bacon Sampler. Like, how do you mess up bacon? All of the flavors tasted like rotten feet or dog treats. I just threw up in my mouth thinking about it. Not to mention, I wish someone would take Berryhill down a notch, not exactly the nicest person. If you're a bacon lover, don't go here. You'll be throughly disappointed as we were. Barf.
Feel like the old location had better food. Pizza is still good but not great. I went gluten free last month so no more pizza for me

Ice tea was stale. Oysters made me vomit. Waitress said they didn't have cocktail sauce which I know they do , and didn't bring lemon or sugar caddy with the ice tea Don't think I'll bother coming back again

How on earth does this place stay open? Arguably the worst burrito I have *ever* eaten, old ingredients, small burritos, and a true shame that an old Boise institution that used to serve amazing, huge, fresh ingredients is now serving utter garbage. I supposed the bar must be what's keeping this place open because you'd have to be blackout drunk to consume this food. We threw half of it away and are just praying we don't get food poisoning. Avoid at all costs, this place is disgusting if not downright dangerous.

I have always enjoyed eating here. It is a super modern, delicious sushi/hibachi restaurant with extremely reasonable prices for a big city. After I learned I was gluten intolerant, I didn't eat out for months. I visited Tomo after a couple months of eating in, and not only did they remember me and my husband, but they went above and beyond to make sure I didn't get sick or "glutened." They checked every ingredient in all of the foods/sauces I ordered and sure enough, I felt great after eating there. What great service and amazing food! Their sushi truly is edible artwork! Additionally, most of the employees there are asian, however the typical language barrier issues didn't apply. So add knowledgeable and helpful to the list here. Will I be going back soon? Definitely!!! Thanks Tomo for a great experience! You have my business for life.

This is the worst place I have been to in my life. I've never had a chef come up to me and tell me that I was wrong about the order that I placed. I came for lunch today and ordered the lunch special sushi boat. I told the server that I was allergic to shrimp and in that case I cannot have the shrimp in the boat and to substitute it out with anything like tuna and salmon. But after making that comment I told her that I was also allergic to all shellfish so if you need any of other substitution it would have to be efficient with scales. I also ordered a rainbow roll and told her the same substitutions because of my allergies. They brought up both of the orders. The boat which contained shrimp was substituted for octopus. The octopus is also shellfish. In the rainbow roll there was regular shrimp even though we were told them otherwise. After informing our waitress she took back the food. But moments later the chef came from behind the bar and started yelling at us. I have never felt so offended. I left hungry. 10/10 do NOT recommend.

I guess coming from Vegas buffets are around every corner. It's a pretty standard place and you get what you pay for, which was food poisoning. All you can eat...okay, but hot lamps and dirty facilities is a fail, not to mention I watched some kid repeatedly grab food with his hand. My family and I left after that, we would've left sooner but we were stuck to the floor.

We ordered Condado Tacos Sunday evening and I woke up Monday AM with food poisoning. We suspect it had to be the meat bc my wife did not get sick (she ate the vegetables tacos.) I be been here before too. I don't think it's any good. It's kind of a fancy Taco Bell. I don't like that they load their tacos with crema.

severe allergic reaction suffered here!!! DO NOT COME HERE IF YOU HAVE ALLERGIES. i triple checked with the waitress about gluten allergies. she still said the spicy tuna was safe. i took one bite, and it was riddled with tempura flakes. now i'm suffering from an intense allergy attack. it's straight up negligence.

First time experience for me trying the particular Korean dishes. I ordered a bulgogi top-bab, upsized it, and ordered the spicy Mayo and Korean gochujang. Didn't receive the sauce and had it delivered so that really bummed me out. The vegetables were unseason and The sauce I feel could have made the dish a little more flavorful. The glass noodles (Japchae) was great and complimented the flavors and consistency of the bulgogi. I ended up using the miso to give the plate a little moisture and flavor. I try not to harp on missing sauces when everything else is good to go but It was really underwhelming without.. and I was so excited for this place!! The bulgogi bibimbap my friend ordered was a little better, she didn't get her sauce requested either. But the selection of veggies in the bibimbap lent themselves to the dish without sauce a little better. They were all tender and chopped. She is gluten free which was awesome because she can't always find options that work for both of us. Overall, there's potential and I will have to give them another chance because I have heard good things about bab cafe.. and they were beautiful dishes.

I never leave a Yelp review but I'm going to leave one here. We ordered the Dungeness Crab and asked them to leave the guts in, which we expected to be sweet, we're COMPLETELY bitter. Thinking it was the hand sanitizer we had just put on our hands, I went to wash it. came back and it was still very bitter. We then tried to the meat and it was also bitter! If we would've known that bitterness means that the crab had spoiled. 2 hours later after we ate, I felt very nauseous, dizzy, bloated, and ended up vomiting. Basically, it wasn't until my friend told me that bitter meat was spoiled. However the uni was really tasty and fresh. We heard good things from this place, and if it wasn't for the crab, I would have such a good experience. But because of that I'm traumatized.

I have mixed feelings about this place. I always sit down to eat and a server never comes to take my order. It has happened the last three times, I got up and walked to the counter to order yet they say to sit down and someone will be with me shortly. Don't come here with limited time on a lunch break unless you have a to-go order. The food is reasonable and yummy- I've had the pho and chicken pad thai and both did not disappoint.. The servings are huge! The menu is rather extensive and will accommodates all diets/allergies (GF/vegan). They do not accept American Express.

My problem isn't that the cake is expensive. My problem is that when you ask a cake specialist which desserts are safe for people with nut allergies, and he says "any of the desserts without nuts are safe." And I say, do you have a list you can double check and says he is sure. He's wrong. One cake without bits has heath bars in it and heath bars are not safe for people with nut allergies. Macarons are typically not safe for someone with a nut allergy because they typically use almond flour. If I didn't know that, My Wife might have been exposed to a potentially dangerous allergen. In the end, she didn't feel safe to try anything given how clueless the staff was about allergies.

Unfortunately they don't have negative stars otherwise that's what this establishment would have received. I felt the need to balance out the other two 5 star ratings which must have been written by the owners. The food is absolutely disgusting. The worst rice I've had but the general tso chicken took the cake for the nastiest food ever. Pieces of multiple fried chicken smothered in a horrible sauce. My wife threw up after eating only a few bites and i had a bad stomache for hours. The restaurant had 3 small children taking up 3 tables with their toys, books etc. The only positive is the young girl taking the orders. She must be about 12 years old and handles the phones and in person orders like a pro. I've seen many grown adults that wouldn't hold a candle to her efficiency in this area. Botton line is; save your money and eat anywhere else. Decent Chinese is tough to find in Tampa and this place should be at the bottom of that sad list.

Ok, maybe my 3 star review was due to the company I had during my meal (a narcissistic ex...gag!). But honestly, I wasn't enthralled with my Milktooth experience. For starters, the wait was redic. Don't expect to get a seat in less than an hour during prime time on weekends. There's also very few places to wait, so we awkwardly stood against the building during our 75 minute wait for brunch. When we finally got inside, we were seated at the bar overlooking the grill. I thought it was cool, but my date complained about the heat raising off the griddle. To be fair, it was a little warm. The menu clearly states that there are no substitutions, so every item comes exactly as described with no additions or subtractions. As someone with a food allergy, I found this a little off-putting, but found something that accommodated my dietary restrictions. My waffle was ridiculously overpriced for the portion size and flavor, but thankfully, I'm not a big eater. My date's burger was good but nothing to rave about. I'm not rushing to go back to Milktooth, to be brutally honest. It seems to me to be an over-hyped hipster joint that's just that...hype.

The peanut butter ice cream tastes like strawberry. No peanut taste whatsoever. Maybe they didn't do a good job washing the tubing or something. This could be an allergy concern. Also very expensive. Over $7 for the smallest size and they no longer weigh the cup.

I didn't like our server not masking and speaking bent over very close to me and my silverware, Made me feel anxious and like everything is contaminated with spittle. She had to repeat herself many times and couldn't take our order accurately. "I don't even want to eat here anymore." I said before my food even came. The executive chef felt it was acceptable to stand over the food at the station under the heating lamps while waiting on the other orders to arrive. He coughed! OK he turned his head but it still makes me feel uncomfortable that he has a cough and he is standing over food that he is bringing to tables. I find it disrespectful and unsanitary! Why did I eat alone and why did my husband eat alone? Because our food was not brought out at the same time. The Brussel sprouts tasted good but were cold, yuck. My husband's fish was hot but overcooked/double cooked and dry. The whole experience was beyond disappointing and I don't recommend it. Because of the respiratory coughing spells by unmasked service, we did not eat another meal here!

My father was just in there to get me a cheesesteak. He inquired what was being added to the cheesesteak because has deadly food allergies. The man preparing my steak was very rude and said it was the rest of the ingredients. Again my Dad inquired again. He was told to just leave and get his money back. I don't live in this state so getting a Larry's cheesesteak is a treat for me. We will not be patronizing your establishment anymore.

I gave two stars because my shake was amazing I got Cinnamon Toast Crunch, I came across this place on insta and was instantly excited to try after seeing the menu and seeing they offer a dairy free option for the shakes I arrived ordered my shake and told the lady to make it dairy free she asked me was it an allergy or intolerance and I let her know intolerance anyway get my shake and head home I drink about half of it because it was so good and hour lady my bottom is on fire I couldn't stop going to the bathroom and it was very uncomfortable I get really bad intolerance to milk and I'm very disappointed that it was not made dairy free like I asked lucky I will be okay but what If I actually had a dairy allergy it could be worse because I didn't get what I asked for which was dairy free.

I ordered a sandwich from the deli and I had to wait seven minutes for it to be made while others after me got theirs in under two minutes. I asked for an Italian sandwich with no tomatoes and I told them it was because of an allergy. They thought they could take a pre made sandwich and just take off the tomatoes as opposed to just making me a new one. When they finally made me a new one they put tomatoes on it when I got home and opened it when I made it explicitly clear that I cannot eat tomatoes. If I didn't check me sandwich before eating it I would have ended up with an allergic reaction. The customer service is horrendous they don't listen or take into consideration that some people simply don't have the time to wait 10 minutes for a simple sandwich.

Get an order correct and learn to speak English! First off, my straw smelled like curry. Nice right? I am lactose intolerant and ordered black coffee and got with cream. Not once twice. After you place your order the cashier says "come to window" because they cannot speak correct or complete English. Do yourself a favor and go to wawa or better yet Starbucks.

I have eaten at Food Connection 3 times. The first couple experiences were great. The food was tasty and left me craving more! But last night I ate the pastor nachos and my boyfriend had the pastor burrito, and unfortunately we are both trying to recover from food poisoning. We both had pleasant experiences the first couple times, but now I don't think I can look at this food truck the same way again.

I really wanted to like Milk & Honey, but I was overall not impressed by my experience! My major complaints are about the service and cleanliness. I went with a group of 10 and we divided ourselves between 3 tables. The server that we had was unfriendly and inattentive. Two of our tables placed our orders and the other table didn't have their order taken for an additional 20 minutes. Some of the cups were dirty and we struggled to get refills and when we did the water pitcher that we were served from was very dirty. The kitchen may have been backed up because we waited for about an hour to get our food. But the table that ordered 20 minutes after us had their food within 5 minutes of the rest of us getting it. The food itself was decent, but nothing that I feel we would return for. It wasn't overly flavorful or hot. One thing I will mention is that they do offer gluten free bread, it's not on the menu, but they do have it and didn't charge additional for it, which is great! I like that they have individual restrooms, but the restrooms were not maintained- dirty wet floors, tissue on the ground, etc.

Some restaurants have met the COVID-19 challenge and have done well with their take-out orders, while others, sadly, need to teach their kitchen staff how to read -- English! Ordered breakfast for take-out over the weekend because we both had appointments at the SJ Radiology up the street. Food was good, BUT not what we ordered. I placed the order over the phone and had the nice gal read it back to me. She got the order correct so we then drove over to pick up the food. She told us to just pop our heads inside to tell them we're here. Big mistake! They had outdoor dining tables and the waiter literally screamed at us when approaching the door to go inside and pickup our food. OK, sorry, we were told to do this! Another person brought out our food and we were off to our home to enjoy them as we were ravished by now. First, the omelette was EGGS when I twice stated that it HAS to be egg whites because of a yolk allergy. The nice gal confirmed this earlier so the kitchen screwed up. Second, the sausages were pork when I ordered turkey (again, confirmed by the gal who took our order). We called the restaurant to report this, thinking they'll credit our VISA for a major mistake. They said to bring the food back. We're 20 minutes away now so no thanks! Never again!!!

I've taken some time to think about what my thoughts were on this new restaurant. I am gluten free so I was extremely excited to try a restaurant where I could eat pretty much everything. We tried the short rib tacos, the bacon and guac, the angry shrimp, and the lamb pizza. Unfortunately I just didn't love anything. Every dish had a middle eastern spice to it that didn't go with the other spices added. It seemed like they just were trying way too hard! Too many spice combinations in each dish. Less can be more! I will go back and try something else that's maybe less heavily spiced. We also finished with the key lime cheesecake and I just couldn't do it. It didn't taste like key lime and it had a very off consistency. Honestly this restaurant doesn't have to have dessert! The baked apple looked wonderful. Maybe more of that?! Less of the fake desserts trying to taste like the non paleo desserts?

If you want to find the best brownies it's right here at Batch! Batch is definitely not what I expected when I first tried their desserts. I'm not huge on cupcakes or sweets in general when it comes down to them being gluten free, vegan, etc but they are actually really good. All their sweets are extremely soft and gooey. It takes a long time for them to go hard. The only dessert I have tried and didn't like was their lemon bar. It wasn't really a bar though. It was a mini loaf like their brownies are. It was terrible. Now, that isn't the reason why I gave them 3 stars. I gave them 3 stars because the staff isn't that friendly and every time I go in to grab a delicious brownie they ignore me until I'm ready to check out. The last time I was in there the boy working didn't acknowledge me and was on his phone which then proceeded to taking a personal phone call on the work phone. He didn't speak a word to me and got upset when I didn't tip him. I love their brownies but every time I go in there I feel really uncomfortable because the workers make you feel like you're bothering them or something. Anyways, keep up the good work on making those delicious brownies!

It's a diner. We go for a good yet inexpensive breakfast. The servers are all wearing masks. No gloves but I am glad of that because technically they would need to change them with every order inorder to stop cross contamination. We come about once a month for breakfast and enjoy it everytime.

I used to love this place. I have had almost every pizza on the menu and they are all pretty good. The sweet onion flatbread is the stand out item on the menu though. I always order it with a pizza, though it is big enough to enjoy on its own as it's the same size a large pizza. Tonight I decided to try the sweet onion flat bread made with a gluten free crust. When I picked up the pizza it was the size of a small pizza here but cost $1.00 more. Very frustrating!! It was not big enough for two people to share. Watch out for the cost and size of gluten free items.

I have long been a fan of VeeKoo in Royersford. Their food was really quite good - the preparation and the ingredients really showed. I ate there so often, I would by the gift cards at Costco. I brought business colleagues there for years. This is why it is so sad for me to report that a great has fallen. I have noticed a gradual change in the overall quality of the food these last years. Recently I got takeout and this will surely be the last time I ever go there. I got Chinese Ribs and fried rice. The ribs were almost tasteless and very, very tough. Ultimately I threw out two of the five ribs. The rice was as bland and tasteless as anything I have ever eaten. I disposed of half of that order. My wife had sesame chicken - this was an abomination. The breading was thick, wet, and poorly adhered. The preparation, sauce and taste were all a failure. Add to all of this the pricing is very, very high now. The last three times I got food here - twice dining in and once take out - were all the same. I only kept trying them again because I had been going there for years and had previously enjoyed the food so much. As far as tonight, I can honestly say this is one of the worst meals I have had in years, keep in mind I had food poisoning at a different restaurant three years ago. I am not trying to be malicious, my review is fair. One thing that has changed a little but is still good - the hot and sour soup. It has a smoky flavor that makes it a standout.

Waited 40 minutes for two simple bagel orders. I ordered a bacon, avocado & cheese on a bagel (a little weird I know, I'm allergic to eggs) and I received a bagel that was very clearly a bacon, egg and ketchup (zero cheese) in which the egg and ketchup was roughly scraped off. Leaving me with a soggy ketchupy bacon avocado sandwich. If I'm going to wait 40 minutes for a bagel I'd at least hope you would make me a new one when the order gets messed up. It was inedible!

Great place to get food poisoning. My husband and I have gotten their poke bowls in the past and enjoyed them very much - no issues. A few weeks ago we got poke bowls and it didn't sit too well, but I attributed it to something else. Last night we both had separate bowls and both ended up with the worst food poisoning. We will never be visiting this establishment again.

I am definitely a foodie, but one problem here would be that you can not delete an item from a dish. REALLY????? I love new exciting and different food, but I'm allergic to cilantro and I couldn't request for it not to be added. Sorry, I won't be back.

My friend and I and our 3 small children 3 years old, 3 years old and 2 years old just visited and tried the ice cream which was delicious but the way that we were approached at our table and told that it was not a playground was extremely rude and we will be sure to spread the word that Latteria is NOT kid friendly and we will be sure NOT to come back!! I think that it is just hysterical and hypocritical that Latteria website says that they have come a long way to enjoy ice cream with you!!...when they can't even appreciate young children being super excited to enjoy and have fun eating ice cream together!! The approach was the absolute worse and I would've even entertained and let go a polite could you quiet down please but to come over to our table with attitude and compare innocent young child excitement to playing at the playground was offensive, very exaggerated and NOT appreciated at all. Our children are very well behaved and get compliments all the time everywhere we go and even at a fancy restaurant so to be reprimanded in a suppose to be fun environment of going out and eating ice cream is outrageous and ridiculous!! Written on their chalkboard along with all of the homemade flavors should read: Please eat your ice cream in silence, stay seated at all times and no laughing or giggling allowed!! On a side note also NOT peanut allergy friendly!!

Rude & uncaring staff. Orders are ALWAYS wrong. I've ordered from here at least 15 times - majority delivery - and there has been at least one thing wrong with our order every. Single. Time. I order directly from them not from uber. Anytime I call to mention it, the staff seems annoyed and offer no apology or nothing to make up for it. The only reason we continue to order is because of the Gluten free pizza since I have celiacs. Ex's: pizzas missing extra protein & sauces (paid extra for), salads coming without dressing.

We have tried Fiamme twice: once dining in and once with carry out. Dining in was March 2021. If we had known how small the inside of Fiamme was we likely would have opted for carry out, but by the time we got there we were ready to eat. There are half a dozen tables inside and they are in extremely close quarters. My husband and I are not particularly concerned about COVID precautions, but if you are someone who is, the set up would likely be a turn-off for you. Part of the reason we had gone to Fiamme was because of their advertisements mentioning they have vegan and gluten-free options. When we asked our server about these options, he seemed stunned, like we had just asked what color he thought our auras were. He took our drink orders and left us to investigate on our own. Luckily, after reading more into the menu, we were able to navigate to Fiamme's gluten-free and vegan options without our server's assistance. Service was slow and our server seemed confused and/or possibly inebriated. We enjoyed the food when it finally arrived. Once our food came we never saw our server again. After about 30 minutes I went to the front counter and asked for the check. The second time we ordered pick up in April 2021. The pies were ready on time. The server who took my payment and gave me the pies spent most of the time I was interacting with him yelling at another server he was working with. It made me uncomfortable but I was in and out of there quickly. Again, food tasted good. After our first visit, I came down with some gnarly food poisoning (fever, stomach cramps, intestinal distress). I generally have an iron stomach and I think associating food poisoning with a business is generally a jerk move. BUT, after our second visit, my husband came down with the exact same symptoms, which leads me to believe this may be an actual risk of eating at Fiamme. (Given what some other reviewers have noted about the kitchen practices, this is less than surprising.) Between the sub-par service and our post-food-consumption experiences on both visits, we will not be returning to Fiamme. Which is a bummer, as it is a legit pizza experience.

A great spot in U City right on Penn's campus! If you go around 12/1pm while school is in session, be prepared to wait at least 15-20 minutes to order. My go-to is the falafel salad, just as it comes. The falafel is fresh and still warm, and the toppings (especially the beets!) are the perfect match. It is just the right amount of food. 3 stars are for this: I ordered a mint chocolate tehina shake after being told there was no nut contents in it... I drank the shake and was bothered by it a bit. When I went back the next time to verify there was no nut contents, I found out they all have a nut milk base. The first counter attendant did not know this and said there was no nut contents in it at all... Just be aware. I luckily don't have a detrimental nut allergy, but it could have been a bad situation if I did.

We were visiting Philly last weekend and arrive in time for a late lunch. It was a pretty day, so we decided to eat outside. It looks very casual on the inside. My brother has eaten there before and said that the food was good. It's conveniently located in Old City and the paddle-bars seem to use this location as a meeting place. They are very accomodating to gluten-free needs and some items are either gluten free as prepared, or are modified to be gluten free. I decided to go with gluten-free as prepared. I had the Filet Tip Salad (pepper crusted filet mignon tips, mushrooms, red pepper, blue cheese, spring mix, cranberry merlot vinaigrette). It is wonderful! Boyfriend had the Bacon Cheddar Burger (applewood smoked bacon, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomato, and onion). The bacon was a bit stingy, but he really liked it. Brother had a large Mac n' Cheese. You can add add crab or chicken to it to make it a meal. It looked really good. All of the food was great and the portions were plenty. Unfortunately, the service...was...slow. Painfully slow. There were staff members standing around while we waited between tasks that seem simple at other restaurants (like processing the payment). We were one of three occupied tables, so it could not have been caused by overwork. Fortunately, the food is good enough that I'll try it again.

This review is based on my most recent experience! I really want to continue to give this place a 5 star rating, but things have changed. This has been such a great go-to spot and the staff has always been awesome so I don't want to take that away from them. Before I dive in, I'd like to acknowledge Taylor, she is a stellar server! She was amazing! Sooo..... My favorite chips and queso were on my mind, so I decided to go for dinner and drinks with my husband. I was so excited to indulge in the queso fondo.... Our server Taylor brought a food & drink menu and said there's a new food menu, so you'll get to try our new food today. I looked over the menu and didn't see the Queso Fondo. I thought to myself, I really hope this new menu is in addition to the old one. When Taylor came back with our drinks, I asked if they still had the Queso Fondo and she responded with a sad No! I couldn't believe it, this was the very reason I came to Record Street Brewing today and why I often return. We initially came for dinner, but left after one drink. The new menu wasn't why we came, so sadly we went somewhere else for dinner and drinks. As a regular of this bar, a new executive chef changing the entire menu up, this wasn't the best news to receive. The menu offerings have some options that sound delicious and I like that there are more salad options. But no more queso fondo, also there aren't too many pizza options, the Alpine Classic Pepperoni pizza was no longer available. They now offer a Puccia Sandwich in 3 different flavors. At first, I didn't know what a Puccia sandwich was, but learned it was a sandwich with bread made out of pizza dough. The appetizer menu is sad, only two options; roasted cauliflower and garlic Parmesan bread. The new menu doesn't have much description, just ingredients of each item. I was not a big fan of the new menu! Record Street Brewing is a brewery and should have bar fare that you want while drinking beer. The Queso Fondo was exactly that. A perfect appetizer to share. The old menu has everything you would want at a brewery, solid options. The menu really needs to match your customer base, is having trendy high end food options now the goal, because that's what it feels like. Not every one wants to eat this type of food all the time. When adapting your business, stick with what works and don't reinvent the wheel. Provide innovative food options to your menu, but incorporate it with what you already have in place. The vibe of this restaurant has totally changed with the new menu and you can totally tell when stepping foot in the doors. Currently, I would only go here for the beer and that's disappointing since I considered this brewery a one stop shop - good vibes, bomb food, and tasty beers....and was one of my favorite breweries in town.
