My suggestion: Incorporate a menu that has all of the "local favorites". Paying homage to the regular customers that come here for their favorite menu items, would be awesome. You guys really need to bring back the Queso Fondo, Alpine Wings, The Troubadour and The Tower sandwiches. More pizza options are needed, bring back the Roxy, Waikiki, Pepperoni, Viper, & CBGB. Let people know you offer gluten-free pizza crust. It would also be fun to see which beers pair well with your menu items. Let me know when the queso is back and I'd be happy to resume my regular visits. Side note: I also found out that gluten-free crust is available for a $5 up charge, this wasn't listed anywhere, I just happened to ask the server if this was option. So that's a bonus for us gluten-free peeps.

I would rate no stars the staff / managers. also 3 of us got food poisoning from them and the manager will not do anything. She is very unprofessional. I am highly upset and I'm going to sue. I am a regular customer and this is not okay. By all means do not go there.

Never thought I'd be writing a bad review for this place since it's always been good. Don't get me wrong the food is excellent , however, I have a nut allergy and I understand places use nuts so on so forth. That's not the point, what I'm mad about and the reason for this review is that I made an online order last night through their website for 2 chicken Makahnis and 2 naam. I specifically made a special note stating no nuts no peanuts no cashews and no coconut. So I waited about 35 mins for my for to arrive(not bad). I served my boyfriend and I some (he's Indian btw so he knows his food) and we start eating. A few bites into it he tells me "hey I think it has nuts" and I said no that's not possible because I specified in the order and it was even on the receipt. So I start eating and about the 5th bite i felt I bit into a nut so I look and there it was a cashew. We have been there so many times and have asked if they use nuts or nut powders and they always say no. I have never found a nut in my food either so I kept going back because their food is great, however, they do need to be more careful! Luckily I have an epi pen so I had to shoot myself up with the epipen. What if I would've gotten into anaphylaxis? We called and asked them why our food had cashews but the manager did not have an answer for us. We got refunded which is good but if I would've died no refund would've been worth it. Also the waitresses who work there don't know the food, don't know what's in it and one of them told us she had never tasted a dish before!! Educate your staff on the foods and the importance of allergies in foods. Not to mention the girls serving chewing gum which is anti hygienic.

Cute little spot nestled away in Dunedin. I thought some of the decor was a little much... it looked like Hilo Hattie's threw up in there (too over the top for me). I was with a group of three, we were seated immediately. The entire time we were there (mind you we got there at six), we were the only people there the entire experience. It freaked me out too because there wasn't music playing. You would expect a restaurant to be near full or at least close to capacity between 6-7PM? Whatever. We started with the nachos and added pork. They were good- we finished the plate. It was Taco Tuesday so all of the tacos were half off! The tacos come in twos I believe and they are a la carte. I ordered the shrimp tacos! They were great! I feel like Florida kind of sucks at the whole Mexican taco game (which is weird because of where Florida is on the map) but these tacos hit different. The shrimp was cooked to perfection; seasoned and juicy and HOT. I LOVE when my food comes out hot but you'd be surprised how often it doesn't (LOL). They also warm the tortillas and I believe mine was finished on the grill because it hard that warm crunch to it. Not a crunch even... it just crisps up the shell enough to where it doesn't get too soggy! This place is a cute little gem. I'd like to go back one night where the atmosphere is more lively and possibly try some different menu items. I have no complaints about the food- it was lovely!

Update- now that I've lived near this Rally's for the past several months, I've gotten food poisoning from their wings and been turned away because they didn't have ingredients or their "systems were down" at least five times. If you can catch them at a time that they are actually a fully functioning location & can manage not to get food poisoning, you may have a semi-decent experience

For all of the look that they have right, so much was wrong. It seems a petty trifle, but I was first put off by how dim the restaurant was. The décor is nice, let me see it! The service was fine. Our server was kind, though he tried to tell me Chianti was a sweet wine. I haven't laughed so hard. When told of my fiance's allergies, the server was very helpful and the chef even delivered our meal personally! Now we get to the food: not worth the price. He ordered the ribs, and I ordered the strip steak. Neither of us was particularly impressed with the flavor, and he absolutely hated the barbeque sauce. When dinner for two is costing $90, I expect more. Go to Longhorn or one of the other steakhouses in the area, and save a bit of money.

I'll give you the short version to start with, but I think you should read the rest of this review to hear more about our excellent dining experience at Cayton's. The food was outstanding, the service was phenomenal (more on that later, but I'm not using that word lightly), and the ambiance was not only safe but warm and very comfortable. The phenomenal service started before we'd even arrived at the restaurant, when I'd contacted them by email to inquire about gluten-free options, and engaged in a very helpful, informative, accommodating, yet personal conversation with a few of the restaurant personnel, including the gracious chef Peller himself, who assured me we'd have plenty of gluten-free options (usually, we get one or two options but when chef let us know they have a dedicated fryer and other equipment, so the number of gluten-free options actually exceeded our expectations even at that! It's great to know you can trust your gluten-free dining experience including the management of the risk of cross-contamination. You just don't see that kind of accommodating approach that much from other restaurants. Cayton's really delivered on this aspect, as well as all the others. But for us, eating out is not just a matter of whether we can get gluten-free items, but the quality of the food and service. Our server, Joe, was on top of his game. I'd seen other reviewers mention him by name and I can see why now. And I'm sure the other servers are very good as well, but Joe just had a pleasant demeanor, a solid knowledge of the menu (both food and drink), great timing (checking on us to see if we need anything else), and an engaging personality. It was really pleasant having Joe as our server. We were very fortunate to have chef Peller stop by our table and to be able to converse with him. He's got a very engaging personality and he is putting out dishes that are not just solid but memorably excellent. I mean, the food quality at Cayton's Burger Bistro is absolutely top notch! Don't dismiss the tater tots as just another comfort food appetizer. These babies were amazing! First of all, the presentation was great, in that metal mesh basket, so you can see that delicious load of tater tots sitting there, waiting for you to dig in. Secondly, the texture was just perfect. The way you remember tater tots from your childhood, but I sincerely doubt the tots you had as a child tasted nearly as good as these. Crispy on the outside, tender and fluffy on this inside, with true potato flavor and a little spice. I don't even know how he does it. I mean, there's not only no oily residue on the tots, but you're not even gonna see it on your fingers. You just keep on grabbing another one and enjoying. Chicken drumettes were also great, very nice crispy outside and tender inside, but it's hard to compete with the tater tots. Next time we may even go for the mini pork shank "wings" (the dish is called "if pigs could fly"). Just a lot to choose from here. Burger itself was excellent, I really loved how I could taste that little char on the outside, but still have perfectly (medium well) cooked temperature, delicious beef flavor, and the right amount of cheese and lettuce. In fact, I think he might have actually placed the slice of cheese immediately next to the bun, which I thought was a nice touch (instead of placed atop the burger patty), because it changes the dynamic in a good way, I think you get a better balance of meat/cheese taste that way, it was almost as if the cheese slice was part OF the bun. Anyway, definitely a solid burger, with several preparation options. Happy hour is a great deal, too. Pretty nice quality $6 wine glasses, very pleased with both the white blend and the Pinot noir. And plenty of dishes to choose from. And in terms of our comfort level related to health and safety practices related to COVID, we couldn't have felt more comfortable. Staff were wearing both masks and gloves, tables were spaced more than adequately far apart (plus it's a nice big dining area, so it's easy to separate folks safely), patrons were required to wear masks (including to/from the restroom), it was just good to see them taking it seriously. It really was just a very pleasant and even special dining experience. For us, Cayton's Burger Bistro demonstrated not just the ability to make dining out during the COVID pandemic work, but that you can actually have a wonderful meal and a very enjoyable dining experience - just like before the COVID days.

My boyfriend and I left that establishment an hour ago had the ribs. They did not taste good going down and even worse coming up. The service was great. But I don't know if the food was spoiled or bad but neither me nor my boyfriend have ever had our stomachs turn so quickly after eating. I threw up 3 times about 20 minutes after leaving the resturant. My boyfriend is also having stomach issues, almost pooped himself. Truly it was just the worst dining experience we've ever had and sadly we will continue to suffer from Texas road house with how our night is going

AJ's is a very disappointing excuse for an "upscale" grocery store in Tucson. First of all, the layout of the store is horrific and whenever it's busy (which it usually is) it's extremely hard to move around. There is also way too much merchandise packed into such a small space. Second, one time I got an iced tea from here and ended up projectile vomiting into a bag in my car on the way home within minutes of drinking it. Third, every time you ask the service bar to heat anything up it always comes out cold - forcing me to just take the food home and heat it myself (if you ask them to reheat it's still not hot and they just give you attitude). The only reason I'm giving a 2 star is because the black bean burger at the outside grill is fire. Aside from this - save yourself the headache and your anxiety meds and just go to Whole Foods.

Ordered an $18 burger with a gluten free bun and fries. 1 1/2 later, I got an $18 burger, with no bun, that I paid an extra $2 for. The fries were stone cold. When I called, I got unapologetic arrogance masquerading as whit. If it was Baredog, Barecheesesteak, or Bareseafood, ok. But, when you're BAREBURGER, What's the excuse?

I've seen some negative Yelp reviews but I have to say, for us, it's been nothing but great at El Charro Cafe (and yes, the one on Oracle Rd in Oro Valley). Now, we do typically sit at the bar, so I don't know if that makes a difference, but we've been treated so kindly by the staff, the bartenders, by everyone. First of all, Ciara has been great, to mention one bartender. She remembers what we like after very few interactions, she's pleasant to talk to, she's efficient and personable and makes great drinks and checks on us at the appropriate times. Rachel, if I got her name correct, is also a great bartender. Very pleasant to talk to, knows the menu, knows her stuff as far as mixing drinks is concerned, she's great too. Margaritas are excellent here, not that overly sweet mix out of a machine but good tasty drinks. We've never had an issue with food not coming out fast enough or anything at all in the service department. And the food is great here. I particularly enjoy the tamale stuffed chicken but there are lots of winners on the menu here. Original enchiladas are great, the hola hemp tamales are also delicious, and the standard fare (tacos, etc) are also quite enjoyable. You absolutely cannot beat happy hour here either. Incredible value for the quality of food and service you receive. On top of all that, lots of gluten-free options - and truly careful gluten-free, not lazy "it's corn therefore it must be gluten-free" but real care in understanding cross-contamination (i.e., yes you can eat the chips without worrying about other fried items because it's a dedicated fryer). We will continue patronizing El Charro (we really like Charro Vida too and still have to try Charro Steak) because of excellent food, service, and value.

Do NOT order any of the açaí bowls. They are premade. I am allergic to coconut so couldn't get it without it. So ordered a different kind. I got it and half of it was rock solid and the other half was soup. The bananas were BROWN. it looked like it had been frozen for months and then they stuck it in the microwave and gave it to me. The granola was barely even granola anymore it was complete mush. The other food isn't bad. Just whatever you don't. Don't order the açaí bowls.
Very fresh and clean! Display case is organized, not like other Subways where the cheeses are in other containers, cross contaminations. This is the one I go to.

We've been long time lovers of Maynards, and used to enthusiastically attend their wine dinners, in addition to standard dining. So we were so excited they are open again. We arrived a little before 5 and sat at the bar for a bit. The beer list has been dramatically reduced and is draft only, so my dining partner struggled a little to find something decent (and ended up with decent, not great). A little disappointing since they used to have some great and unusual choices. But the bartender was lovely and offered a couple of different wines for me to taste - wine options were far better than beer. Service was also excellent when we were seated. Server was knowledgeable and friendly, and we were never without water or a fresh glass of wine or beer when we wanted it. We decided on the tasting menu, since there were many things we wanted to try and I'd heard good things. And every element was delicious, even the course they had to sub out (the pasta) so I could be gluten free. But...the portions were TINY. I'm a 40 year old woman on the small side and typically eat 1200-1500 calories a day and take home half or more of my entree when we eat out. So it wasn't like I was expecting Claim Jumper portions. But at the end of the meal, I was mostly satisfied but not actually full. Majority of the courses were 1-3 bites. Those bites tasted amazing, but were just so tiny. And there seemed to be opportunities to fill out the plates without a big increase in cost. For example, there was a parsnip dish that was delicious, but it was one parsnip the size of a baby carrot. 2-3 instead would have bulked up the meal quite a bit. Same with the tomato and watermelon salad. Doubling the portion from 1.5 cherry tomatoes to 3 doesn't seem like a crazy idea. We ordered an extra appetizer (fois gras) and desert (madelines) to round out the meal and the fois gras was also minuscule - $21 for about 4 bites. So at least for now we will limit ourselves to a drink and snack vs dinner.

The food was absolutely terrible, surprised I didn't get food poisoning. Had the "all you can eat" and they would forget to bring items out. Im not too sure when their last health inspection was but the establishment was very dirty (including glasses and bowls) and smelt of mildew. At the end of the meal we asked to speak to the manager and she was VERY defensive and cut me off as I was politely expressing my opinion. Would not recommend this to anyone.

Food: ROLLS 8/10, sashimi 2/10. Sashimi was NOT fresh. Both of my friends got food poisoning after eating here. Also, it is $60 for the sushi platter pictured below. However, I think the price we paid for were the decorations and not for the food. I would have liked better fresher sashimi rather than pretty decorations. However, rolls were great and I'd get takeout of the rolls. Service: 8/10 Atmosphere: 6/10

Ate at this location on Friday evening and our entire group has gotten violent food poisoning. I was the only one who did not eat dinner and I am the only one not sick. The service was great and our server was very pleasant but the food was awful. Very disappointed with the quality and obviously now knowing they may not take care of the food products correctly, we will not be back.

Been coming here since they opened, stop going for a while due to the poorly trained staff's and quality of the drinks. But recently I started coming back a couple times a week because of my uncontrollably craving of milk teas. Yesterday was probably the last day I'm going to come back. The staff was rude, messed up my order and blamed it on me because I was on the "telephone." Which I had put on speaker so I can order my milk tea properly. I usually get the Jasmine Green Milk Tea with half of the milk they put in and extra sugar. Literally that's it. Nothing complicated, just put less of whatever dairy you put on, and more sugar. No, they put EXTRA COW MILK (which I cannot digest) and LESS SUGAR. I realize the sugar part when I was in the car so I came back in, instead of making me a new one, they used the same one and just added more sugar. I had already left and realize that this tea taste awfully different and very milky so I had to throw it away before I vomit everywhere. Thought I give them a call and SHE was absolutely rude about it, even blamed it on me. Instead of agreeing to replace me with another drink, she critique my ordering and told me to order differently because it was too complicated for her to understand. Not only that but she had the audacity to ask me why I cannot drink milk and told me to try something different if I can't. Rather go back to Bing's because if you are not satisfied with their drinks, they are willing and pleased to make you another one, no questions asked.

I order the double cluster, crab cakes, Rasta Pasta and requested to cancel the order for carrot cake if it contained nuts due to an allergy. What came to my door was walnut laden carrot cake and somebody's soggy salmon fries I never ordered. They refused to honor doer dashes redelivery request for the $80 in food I didn't get. Nobody was trying to get over you really sent out the wrong order, very simple to do because the order was in a black plastic bag with no name on it. Do better. 4 hours no food.

I would have liked to give Padaro Beach Grill at least a three star review, but I have to go with one star due to the fact that I contracted food poisoning from the fish sandwich. To preface, I know that I contracted food poisoning from the restaurant as all the meals I had the day I went were shared with other people and they did not get sick. The only meal I had where I ate something different from my family members was here. I would advise the staff/owners to thoroughly inspect their fish preparation method as it is very concerning. Other than the food poisoning, I thought that the sandwich was pretty good! The bun was nicely toasted and it had a good amount of tartar sauce. The fish was the big issue as it was likely contaminated but I was unable to tell due to the fact that the tartar sauce and lemon juice probably masked any weird flavors. The view of the ocean is also quite fantastic and makes this restaurant really enjoyable to eat at during sunset or sunny days in general! I don't think I will be coming back here as I personally didn't find it worth the 40 minute drive from my house and because I contracted food poisoning. However, if you live nearby, then definitely give it a try, just don't get the fish!

I hate that this food is so gross and makes me sick because I work at the government center and it would be awesome if it was actually good food. The prices are high for what you're getting, which is a notch above prison food. And I know, because I worked at a prison. I'm pretty sure, the food is the same. And I don't want to open a door for human rights on what gets served at prison, but if it is the same as this place, they're doing okay, because they get it a gratis. Anyway, I ate here twice, both times, had food poisoning. A lot of people eat here everyday and don't get sick, so maybe I am just unlucky, or its what I picked. If you have other options, take them!

If you are looking for mediocre food with an amazing view of a fish tank, this is your place to go! I brought my friend here for lunch the other day as she was visiting from out of town. The vibe is definitely touristy (it's on Tradewinds property and is adjacent to the Guy Harvey store) but the ambiance is nice. A huge fish tank with all kinds of sea life takes up an entire wall. The menus light up which lets them keep the restaurant dark inside. Food was eh. The paella was good, but extremely salty and they use frozen vegetables. My fiancé liked his burger but nothing out of this world. Service was friendly but slow - waters were empty and not refilled for quite some time. I will mention that it is a good place to bring someone who is gluten free. My friend, who has celiac, was able to enjoy her burger on a gluten free bun and a side of baked sweet potato fries. The prices are high for lunch, but that's to be expected on the beach. I personally probably won't be back, but enjoyed my time there and it was something unique for my tourist friend.

Rough delivery night from Blaze. Our first time doing delivery from Blaze (they use Grub hub). Normally we pick it up ourselves. We ordered three pizzas online from their website directly. Nothing complicated..one cheese, one pepperoni and cheese and the other gluten free. The website stated 25-30 minutes for delivery. I received a text with the drivers phone number and when the pizza would arrive. I was able to follow the process on a live map they provided. Everything seemed normal when she left the store until she passed our house and then hung out at the summit mall parking lot for about 20mins. At least that's what it showed on the map. Was she picking up someone else's order from a different restaurant? Who Knows? After 45 minutes I tried to call the delivery driver and the phone just rang and rang, so I texted... nothing. I called the store and it went to a corporate line then they transferred me to the store. Then I was hung up on. I emailed Blaze from their website and still have not gotten a response. My husband was past hangry and it was all around not good. Finally our ring notified us someone was at the door. No knock or doorbell ring. Weird. The driver then gave the pizzas to my husband and left. The pizza was barely warm. Everyone took turns reheating their dinner.

My family and I went to Mangia and were all excited because 3 of us are gluten-free. The staff was nice but the restaurant was oddly empty for 7pm on a Friday. We all found the food to just be mediocre--nothing special, some odd textures, and not totally flavorful. Maybe we just all ordered the wrong thing, but we all left feeling a bit disappointed.
It was okay. This is a local chain. My friend got food poisoning after eating here.

My wife has a dairy allergy so ordered ahi tuna nachos without any cheese based sauce. Waitress delivered them only to come back after my wife had started eating them to state it was made with dairy so had to be remade. I ordered my steak medium rare and it came out completely brown and dry, not even a hint if pink left. They overloaded the steak and potatoes in a dark gravy sauce that was too sweet and even after scraping most of it off, it overpowered the other food items. With a bill close to $100 without any drinks, was not impressed.

I would give Burger Republic two stars if not for the fact that the staff is polite, friendly, and knows their menu well (even well enough to discuss allergens). The burgers were underwhelming: not terrible, but not great. The truffle fries were basically identical to the regular fries with a dash of truffle oil. The children's salad was a handful of half-wilted greens with a couple of pieces of diced tomatoes and cucumbers. With so many great places to eat in the area (and so many amazing burger joints around), we won't be back.

Just don't. It's like 6 flags threw up in here. Unsupervised teens run amok. They are not ready for guests post COVID. We had technical issues with the hotel checking us out a day early causing many calls and time wasted at the front desk. Most of the restaurants are closed and those that are open are way, way understaffed. We waited 3-4 hours to eat mediocre meals. Nowhere to even get a nice glass of wine. We left the hotel time and time again because everything here is closed and there are a million people trying to use the very limited resources. The Elf thing is awful just nothing compared to ice and the many past years of great shows. Overall, they need to lock down 1/2 the rooms just to have a normal staffing / guest ratio. We have stayed here many times over the years to get ready for the holidays. We won't be back. This "vacation" has been stressful and miserable walking only to find things closed and waiting in long lines for crappy food and crappy service. Spend your money elsewhere. Desperately wish we had stayed downtown.

Cupcakes are amazing. One of the favorite places to purchase gluten free items. Not super impressed with the workers. This is my 3rd time going in, and every time, workers are rude and not helpful. I walked in, not a " hi" not a "can i help you" they look at you like your bothering them. Didn't say a word. I asked where the gf pastries were, the kid just pointed... still not saying a word. If they didn't have some amazing gf food, I would definitely find a happier, friendlier place. Hoping I can find something else.

Mixed feelings about this one. Taco Bell usually serves me a good feeling in me tummy, that crunchy Mexican pizza with the fire sauce is well...fire. The Baja blast right off the fountain just does your taste buds some justice. But I did get food poisoning from this taco Bell once and that yummy in my tummy feeling changed to a not so yummy, ache feelin!

I just don't get the hype regarding this place. Came in 07/22/2021 around 230ish as a group of 5 adults. My mother-in-law arrived first and was seated quickly and drinks came quick too. Thursdays you get free warm sake with ayce. We had 5 waters 3 Sapporo's and 2 warm sakes. The BF & I were running a little late so the rest of our group started an order that was delivered once we arrived. Once the first order arrived, my BF gave me that look of "This does not look appetizing in any way." There were a few uncooked rolls I didn't know the name of and didn't care to try as the avocado on them was brown and not from the sauce they put on top of the rolls and a few cooked rolls also came out like a Godzilla which tasted very fishy, I did not care for it at all, and Godzilla's are my go to fried roll, there was a cooked one that had cream cheese and jalapeno in it which was outstanding in my opinion. We also ordered some nigiri like unagi (fresh water eel), hamachi (yellowtail), sake (salmon), and some Donald Ducks. These were all good except the rice was very dry. The maguro (tuna), was dry in both fish and rice, very unappealing. The pot stickers, miso soup, and yakiton were all good n hot, but those are kinda hard to mess up. The service here also leaves a lot to be desired. We weren't checked on regularly and even had to clear our own table of dishes, which I didn't understand as they weren't understaffed and there were only 2 other tables eating at the time. Also a little weird that this is the only sushi bar I know of where you can't see the fish in the bar case, they have it tiled off which makes me question how fresh everything really is. I don't know about you, but I enjoy seeing the sushi get made if I'm sitting at the bar. This is unfortunately one of the first times we've ever gone to sushi and not left with a belly ache from over eating. I did leave with a belly ache but not from over eating..I'm thinking it was because of the Godzilla roll, because as soon as I got home (which is 5 mins away) I started vomiting. My BF didn't feel good the rest of the night either. We will definitely not be returning!

Pretty pricey for the quality, but you can't beat the vibe and atmosphere. We've been here a few times and the staff kind of make you feel like a nuisance. We got AWFUL food poisoning the first time we came, but gave it another shot and haven't had an issue. The crab cakes are delish, and definitely a good sized portion. Oysters have been tasty each time we had them, and the tacos are just ok.

This is the worst meal I have ever had. I should preface this by saying that I've been to some disgusting dive bars. At least those place are cheap. I'm also in the service industry and rarely get upset over restaurants. We came here for brunch. At first glance, it looks cute. Their menu has a great selection. My espresso martini was served HOT and in a wine glass. This is usually my favorite drink, I've never been served a hot one. My meal came 10 mins before my husband's. My meal was okay. I ordered eggs over medium, they came over hard. He got eggs Benny that came with potatoes. One egg was completely over done. The English muffin was covered in black gristle from the kitchen not cleaning the grill. The potatoes were undercooked. The bottom of the bowl was covered in black grease from the kitchen not cleaning the fryer. After a few bites, we both wanted to vomit. The restaurant floor is dirty and the furniture is either broken or torn. This place is terrible. Do not go here.

VEGANS BEWARE! The food I ate was fresh. The place is friendly and clean. But vegans beware. I was told the flan from oopsy Daisy's was vegan and it's not. I found out from ms daisy after eating it unfortunately. Good thing I'm not allergic. Wish they'd be a little more mindful instead of serving food that there unsure of being vegan. It really makes me wonder now if I ate anything else that wasn't vegan. I was going to try the cold slaw but it smelt rancid.

This is a cute neighborhood eatery! The food is delicious. The service can be slow so don't come in a rush. I usually order to go, but if I dine in I will be waiting. I highly recommend the veggie black bean burger on gluten free bread and hummus. Edit: I didn't realize until AFTER I are my vegan "gluten free" burger that the bread was not gluten free. Thank goodness I don't have an extreme allergy to it. But I do have an intolerance and my throat has flared up. The server, Caitlin, was new and friendly. But we had to keep asking her double check because it was like she just made things up as she went along and we've eaten here enough to know when she wasn't giving us correct info.

I love wimpys. Their food is always great and the cowboy burger is the best. However my experience ordering wimpys for delivery was not so great. I placed an order #E7848 on Uber eats and specifically chose a plain steak (as my fiancé is allergic to dairy) and the steak came with cheese on it. I was very disappointed. I attempted to call the store but they were closed. I will be hesitant to order delivery from here again unless I am there at the store. My rating is 2 out of 5 as the food is good but they struggle to follow directions

The customer service I received last night was horrific. The cashier clearly was unhappy and unknowledgeable. I have a raisin allergy and asked if there were raisins in the carrot cake and she says "uhhh Idk" so I'm wondering isn't there a way to find out ??? Anyway so I went from delivery 55min wait to saying hey I'll just come pick it up would I be reimbursed for the delivery fee and tip and again she has an issue then tells me a signature is required yet I go in she tosses the food I've missing half of my order and says don't sign. It's a long story but needless to say never again

I don't know WHAT was going on in the restaurant on Tuesday evening. I ordered the Jesse's special without bread, escargot, and chicken fingers. I arrived to the restaurant and they had me go to the bar. The first thing I saw was the server picking up olives with his bare fingers, picking up the little swords, and putting it into a customer's drink. There were little fruit flies buzzing around the garnishes. I got my food and drove the 2.5 miles home. When I got home, my escargot needed to be reheated. I opened the box with the chicken tenders...the box was full of greasy, the tenders were burnt. The sauces were honey mustard and??cocktail sauce? OK. After that, I couldn't/wouldnt eat my chopped steak. If the open area of the bar was that gross, what did the kitchen look like. I won't be going back, I don't want food poisoning/bacteria from someone putting grubby fingers in the garnishes when he has touched trays, food plates, dirty plates, silverware, money, credit cards, meal tickets, and anything else in the restaurant that wasn't clean.

No. They were one of the better places in town, but no more. Not even close to average. We paid $24 (a complete waste of time and money) for a 12-inch pizza. It was supposed to be a customized Bianca (mozzarella, no marinara) with: EXTRA garlic, olive oil, basil, and mushrooms. Simple, right? W R O N G. What we got: mozzarella, a few mushrooms, and unnoticeable basil, visually and in taste. No olive oil, just cheese on top of pizza dough. One can taste both basil and garlic in a pizza, or not. This clearly was NOT for both. Someone who is deathly allergic to garlic could've eaten this pizza with absolutely no use of an epi-pen or a trip to a local ER. My hubby ordered at the counter to go. I'm unsure if the royal screw-up was thanks to the person at the register who was beyond clueless or the cook, but I'm thinking the buck stops with the cashier. She did not give him a receipt, wasn't wearing a mask, and when he noted the problems with the pizza, she proceeded to breathe on the pizza (REALLY???) and wave her ungloved finger way too close to point out that no, there's no red sauce. Bonus! Two containers of parmesan and a packet of Luigi's red peppers were thrown INTO the box with the pizza. I don't even want to fathom how many people touched those items which ended up pressed against our food. Here's a comparison on the price-point. A White 20" pizza with 8 slices at Manero's on Mulberry in Little Italy (Manhattan), made with fior di latte is the same price. A larger pie made in M A N H A T T A N. Fior di latte! Lastly, we only went here because (a) Fresco was previously fine and (b) our beloved Pizza Luna is temporarily shut down due to compliance with vaccination requirements. Also, they kindly regard both their staff and customers by masking up. I'd recommend that you pay Pizza Luna a visit once they're back as Fresco is just a Fiasco.
No attention to food allergies when addressed at the beginning of the meal. Items delivered were not correct. Service is very slow. No care for danger they caused. Will not be back.

I asked the server specifically how the kitchen was with altering the meal. She replied " no problem" I asked for nachos very light chips, extra lettuce, no onion. My order returned FULL of onion. (It's an allergy) It happens quite often but ok make it right the next time. Came out second time no onion but full nacho chip order (I'm low carb diet) with a tablespoon of lettuce. At this point I eat just the chicken on top and some chips because I'm starving. There should have been a manager to address the issue, but I never saw anyone who I thought may be the manager. I told the server, but still had the nachos on the check. I never "expect" anything for free, but I thought the whole experience was the most unprofessional we've ever had at a restaurant. Also, no outside entertainment like it states on Yelp. This is the VERY FIRST time I did not want to tip. My husband and I are always extremely generous with the tipping, especially since our daughter is a server. **If you are on any sort of a diet or have an allergy please do not eat here, they take it too lightly.

We ate here and service was just ok. Our waiter was neither friendly or rude he just did his job and seemed uninterested in being there. We ordered the special of the day which was the seafood boil for the holiday, it seemed like we were shorted on food by as much as 1 order because they claimed to have brought out both orders in 1 pot and it wasn't a lot (per the photos)...when my husband asked them about it they admitted it looked short and brought out another small pot. I really wanted to try the raw oysters, but online (their website and via Facebook Msgr) I was told they only had oysters on the rooftop after 4pm. When we were there however, I asked and was told the rooftop was open and was closing at 4pm then re-opening later for dinner. That's very disappointing since that was the whole reason for making the trip and I probably will not be back. Even living in Tampa proper its a drive like 35 to 40 minutes so...anyhow, the positives is that the seafood boil was great, it's was gluten free (including the sausage), it tasted great, it had good heat that built up in your mouth, it just severely lacked salt. As for desert, my husband loved the brownie and it was huge. Street parking in front of the restaurant and on that street is free (first come first serve). It's right across from the beach also so thats perfect. Although I did not get to experience the rooftop I know its probably great overlooking the beach and all. It was a good experience, I would visit again if the menu was compelling. Im an oyster lover so the fact that they didn't serve any one the 1st floor was unfortunate.

We went to this restaurant based on reviews and recommendations. It was great! We got the cabeza, lengua, and birria tacos. Our favorite was the cabeza as it was soft and juicy. Birria had amazing flavor as well. The corn tortillas were soft and had good texture. I got a tostilocos as well. I usually don't comment on other reviews. But I have to say, as a physician, that you can't get diarrhea from food poisoning in 10 minutes. The food hasn't even made it to the colon at that point. The prior reviewer either got food poisoning from something else or had some other sort of illness. Final remarks: food was good, would go there again. Probably try the pozole as all the locals were getting that.

I've been wanting to check this place out for for brunch for months now. I finally did and man am I disappointed. The dining experience got worse and worse with every passing moment. First-the $12 Bloody Mary "bar." For $12 I thought there would be more to the make your own bloody bar. It was so basic. I've had better bloody Mary's at a dive bar for way less money. Not to mention on the menu it says pick your vodka. Our waitress never even asked! She just walked over with what looked like half a shot of some random vodka over ice. Second- My friend and I told our waitress that we were going to be sharing our meals and asked if the food my friend ordered could have the gravy on the side because I have a pork allergy. Our waitress said, "yes not a problem." Then, when our food came out the gravy wasn't on the side and she proceeded to argue with me and tell me she didn't hear me say that! She did offer to take it back and bring one made correctly however, at this point we had already been waiting an ungodly amount of time for our food and we were both starving and had places we needed to be. Third- This is by far the most bland/tasteless, and disgusting meal I've had in a long time. The presentation was good. However, our food was cold and had absolutely no flavor. Fourth- After the accusatory mishap with the waitress, she stopped coming by our table. I had to get up and ask someone else for ketchup to try and drown out the flavor of the burnt green onions that were hiding on the bottom side of my hash-browns. I had to flag her down to refill my water glass and all the while she was making up one excuse after another why she screwed up our order. Fifth- when it was time to pay for our meal we waited and waited for her to come back and cash us out. My friend and I finally had to get up and flag her down yet again so we could pay and get out of there. She had one last opportunity to apologize for the mess up on our order and perhaps discount the meal but she didn't. So between the horrid service and the tasteless, cold food, I think coming here was a one time thing. The location is cool and I love the wine cellar in the back but, that's all I see that this place has going for it. My friend and I both ended up leaving there frustrated and with an upset stomach. There are better options elsewhere for brunch.

Not one vegan menu item or baked good. Even the Kale Salad comes with Cesar dressing. And if you don't want to drink cows milk in your coffee, they charge 75 cents extra for soy milk or almond milk. Come on Helena Bakery... jump into 2019. Check out all the great bakeries in Ventura that are offering vegan & gluten free options, like Caffroite or Sticky Fingers Baking Company. Please provide at least one ethical, planet-friendly, tasty and healthy menu item or baked good. Having some vegan options on the menu will only broaden your customer base and then you will be ready to cater to practically any customer who comes through the door. Please don't punish those of us who would like to save cows milk for baby calf by charging us extra for plant based milk. If you build it, we will come...

Since we are local we have frequented Carmine's often for a quick pizza. Since we are gluten free we have come to rely on Carmine's being an easy go-to for a gluten free option. We dined here for lunch and were incredibly disappointed that they switched their gluten free crust to the cracker-like, tasteless gf base that some other local pizza places use (like Spatola's). The crust is awful. I wish the nice woman at the register had told us they switched their gf crust because we would not have wasted the $15 on it. We took 3 bites--the dry, tasteless crust wasn't worth the calories. I gave this feedback to the kind server as a way to give feedback in a nice way so hopefully management will know and maybe change back to a tastier option.

Decided to try Florida Ave on NYE. Checked the wait list on line and added my name for party of 6. Said current wait time was 20-35 minutes around 5:30pm. Figured we'd go early as we had a party to attend later. Arrived 20 minutes later and the place only had a few inside tables occupied. Said they were getting ready to close the outside for private event so we sat inside, no wait. One of the reasons I picked this spot was numerous Gluten free options listed on the online menu, my wife eats GF. We were disappointed to find they were serving a limited menu due to New Year's Eve. Why? The regular menu didn't seem that extensive. Still were a few items she was able to order so we went with it. Small plates / appetizers we had: arancini, buffalo cauliflower, and naked buffalo wings. All were okay but not great, wings needed to be fried harder ,with less sauce, cauliflower needed more sauce and arancini was just bland. Entrees: I had Nashville "hot" chicken sandwich. It was not hot in taste or temperature. I felt like the chicken was reheated and not cooked to order. When I mentioned to the server it wasn't spicy he brought a side of buffalo sauce.(Nashville is not buffalo.) 2 in the party had shrimp and grits which tasted okay but again temperature was not hot, also leading us to believe not cooked to order. Burger was mediocre and blackened salmon caesar salad was okay. On the plus side, beer and cocktails were good, but I don't think I will eat here again.

The food quality was excellent, but the service wasn't the best. My girlfriend and I stopped at Cheddars for my birthday and we were extremely satisfied with the food. We have been here many times and enjoy going. However, it appears that most of the employees would rather much talk about their personal issues than take care of customers. We were sitting at the bar and we had a bartender continue to talk to employees more than her own customers. You would think that would be a good thing in a way because that would mean they can work more efficiently. Our visit was not the case. My girlfriend has a gluten allergy to where if she is exposed to any gluten, she can become extremely sick. She mentioned it to the bartender before ordering a steak and mashed potatoes. Since it was on the gluten free menu, it shouldn't have any. Once it was brought out, there was gravy, which has gluten, all over her food. She was able to salvage the food that didn't have any and at least the bartender was kind enough to bring new sides. We appreciate the hard work from this restaurant during the pandemic, but it has become unpleasant when we overhear how a few employees wish they weren't at work and don't seem to care about certain health situations. We believe in second chances, so please come if you enjoy great food, but use this review as a recommendation and forewarning.

Ok so this is a little disturbing but I went in to pick up our Pho and see the chef come out from the kitchen as I wait at the register. You can see the chef and kitchen clearly he had no gloves on came out rang me up, took my card and gave it back then without washing hands wiped his very runny nose then grabbed some noodles with his hands and threw them from the bowl to the pot . I nearly threw up. I looooove pho but why did I have to see this.

It's too bad that it's closing. While Sprinkles was an import, it was reflective of the change (for good and bad) that Nashville's experiencing.* I don't quite understand why it's closing, considering the hordes of people lined up for its product but I'm not in the books. I don't have the answers. That said, I'd hoped that Sprinkles would have gone out as it lived: strong, pleasant and on top of it's game. I get it. I'm sure the workers were over it and closed early. Stocking the kitchen and counters make little sense when going out of business but... standards are in place for a reason. California (the birthplace) was one of the first states in the country to recognize that gluten as we knew it no longer exists in the United States and we needed alternatives. Discovering Sprinkles' gluten-free cookies was a fat kid triumph. So, imagine my fat kid pain to discover that, for its last weekend in existence, Sprinkles was out of gluten-free cookies. It wasn't serving gluten-free red velvet cupcakes. And the flourless chocolate cupcakes weren't exactly gluten-free (they were cross-contaminated which makes one wonder why they were made at all). Yes, I hear it. These are first-world problems at their finest (worst?). But when paying $4 for a cupcake (again, I hear it), you're going to want the right thing. In previous trips, this wasn't an issue. As Sprinkles shuffled off this Nashville coil, nary a [redacted] was given and it showed. You were better than this, Sprinkles. Catch you in LA. *I still don't 'get' 12 South. Y'all remember what it was, right?

The girls at the registers are really unprofessional and rude. This was my first and last time coming to this establishment. Also the wings, i asked what the yellow sand wings were and i was told the sauce was a mix of lemon pepper and ranch. However, what i received was wings in a mix of mayonnaise and lemon pepper seasoning. Yes mayonnaise. I was completely disgusted and vomited my entire meal because i had a whole glob of mayo in my mouth. Never again. If i could give negative stars i would.

Upon my first visit to Brandon burgers my hopes were quite high based on many other reviews left here and on other sites. It would appear that from some of the early reviews compared to now this place may have gone downhill a little bit. The positives I noticed were strong teamwork, a desire to please their customers, an extremely delicious burger patty, as well as the staff on site doing the best they could to accommodate my food allergy. I noticed that the kitchen itself was somewhat clean on the surfaces, but also somewhat disorganized and I also saw some things on the storage shelf from behind the counter which concerned me. French fries all over the kitchen floor and garbage under the counter storage unit in the middle of the kitchen. This is completely unacceptable for any establishment! It would also appear that they do not know the Allergan listing for all of their components. For example they could not tell me what was in the buns that they use etc. They suggested a bowl or a lettuce wrap which I was happy to oblige. The lettuce they used to wrap my burger was fresh. However they didn't wilt it at all. As a result it was a lot of lettuce in a big mess around my burger and I had to peel the lettuce away to get to the burger so that I could eat it. Other burger chains or places which execute lettuce wraps are able to do so in a way that makes it like a bun so I think this staff need some additional training in that area. Now onto the fries! They are clearly the frozen variety of french fry which they then deep fry. Their fryer oil tasted old --- while they came out hot and crispy, these fries had an unpalatable taste to them. Typically this is a sign that the fryer oil is old and has not been changed in quite some time and that the fryer unit itself has also not been properly and thoroughly cleaned in sometime as well. I could not eat these french fries! So my meal consisted of an iced tea and a burger patty and a little bit of lettuce. Perhaps others will have better luck in this establishment I think they could be great if they solve the problems I have listed here. Also I want to say that the manager or the lead person on staff did go out of his way to make my burger and fries as allergen free as he could. I don't blame him or the staff for the issues that I encountered -- these are management or owner issues which should be resolved right away.

I'm honestly so upset by the service. The waiters were mean and I told them I was gluten free but they gave me rolls with soy sauce on them. The waitress was very rude and the hibachi man was not energetic. Sushi was bad tbh.

I really wanted to like this place because I am a fan of Amanda Fredericksen. I'm not sure if I was there on an off day, but the staff did not seem to know what they were doing. I was telling them what I wanted in my order and they struggled to put our orders together. The couple in front of us got frustrated mid order and left. It just seemed chaotic behind the counter and people were confused about menu items and what was available. On top of that, the employee was sweating and it was beading off his face into the ingredients. That was off putting. We have food allergies as well and they did not seem able/willing to remove gloves to avoid cross contamination. Maybe they will work these kinks out soon. Nashville could use a great healthy fresh restaurant and hope things improve.

Mediocre food, restaurant reminds me of New Jersey. Not a good thing. Something from here gave me food poisoning so I do not recommend eating at this restaurant unless you have access to a bathroom. 1/10.

Went to eat this Friday night by myself, and I sat at the bar. I proceeded to order my drink and meal - which came rather quickly. I was pleasantly surprised. However, when I started to ask the bartender who is waiting on me about gluten-free options, she became very kurt and kept telling me to just read the menu (which was partially marked with some gluten-free items). I told her that the selections marked were not for me, but rather my son, and she didn't seem interested in helping me find anything for him. Another bartender just happened to hear our conversation and interjected that they had gluten-free corn tortillas that were soft. I ordered four things for the rest of my family and friends and the bartender seemed very snobby. I waited fir my order and - after a very long wait this time, - they arrived. When I wanted to make sure the order was right, the bartender just counted to four and flung the receipt in my direction. Not cool. The food is really good, but the service here stinks. I won't return if they think this is how you operate a business.

Food here is horrible. I got food poisoning after I ate here and will never come back again. The noodles I got here was way too salty and the meat was old and looked like it was frozen prior to serving. The prices are not cheap as well for thai food

I visited Nook for the first time last night during an EatHereIndy Food Tour. While I don't have any dietary restrictions, I do enjoy health-conscious foods and try to cook that way at home. Lately I have been experimenting a lot with new ways to prepare traditional dishes using new oils, subbing certain items, etc., so I was definitely excited to try this place. Thank you to Nook for starting us off with a gluten-free margarita - delicious! We sampled the roasted brussel sprouts cooked with bacon and topped with a paprika aoli. While they were prepared really well, the coconut oil that they were cooked in was completely overpowering. I cook with coconut oil at home, but use the triple filtered kind, which is flavorless. The lasagna was probably my favorite item. Instead of traditional lasagna noodles, they used sliced eggplant and zucchini, layered with ground beef in marinara and mashed sweet potatoes. I thought that the flavors worked really well together. I will actually try to recreate this at home, so thanks for the inspo! So I will say this...I don't think this place is for everyone. I don't think that long-term it's realistic to have a restaurant be so niche-specific, at least in Indianapolis. If I had dietary needs that restricted me, this place would be great. But I would have a hard time rounding up 5 of my girlfriends to agree on this place for dinner on any given night.

I went in this morning and grabbed a McMuffin meal and a pie. First of all they gave me the wrong pie but it's what ever, then I went to pull my sandwich out is wasn't even in the wrapper which was a mess and so gross. So then I noticed something black by the straw hole of my tea. I took the lid off to get a better look and it was a SMASHED ANT. Then I noticed another dead ant on the inside of the lid along with a hair. After I dumped the cup there were two more ants under the ice. Can you imagine if someone who is allergic to ants had gotten that cup. When I called to tell the manager she just said okay thanks and was quick to get off the phone. No apology or anything. I will NEVER go back and I'll be contacting corporate and maybe the health department. This is disgusting.

Have never been so unimpressed and bothered with a brunch spot. It's like they came to Chicago went to handlebar and thought "this isn't hipster enough we must make a copy of this that's not as good, but ten times as hipster" Once we finally sat down it took 30 minutes for someone to take our order. Now mind you it wasn't even that busy. Took another 45 minutes to get our food which was absolutely not worth the price or wait, also the portions are so small a child couldn't fill up on them. The menu tells you you aren't allowed to make changes to their food. I am allergic to most fruits and 90% of their menu has a fruit jelly or garnish. When I ordered and said I have a deathly allergy to fruit and need the Dutch baby without the jam the waitress acted like I murdered her baby. Now maybe being from the Winnetka/Chicago area I'm used to a little better service/food/drink but this was ridiculous. The menu is overpriced, the Bloody Mary is $11 and doesn't even have a single garnish in it. It's a mix with pepper added. Mind you I had a few because I probably would have had a fit due to the wait, quality of service and quality of food. But each time I ordered it hurt my soul a little paying $11 for a bloody without even a lonely olive added. I would never ever recommend this place, absolutely pretentious, overrated and the literal bourgeois ideal of what a hip brunch place is. I'd give negative stars if possible.

This is certainly one of my new favorite restaurants in the city. From it's simple but lovely decor to the amazing food and service, I had no hesitation in giving Spice Finch a glowing five star review. I had a 7pm reservation on a Tuesday night for me and my friend who was visiting from Canada. She just recently moved out of Philly and when deciding where to go for dinner, her only request was for me to choose a place that was new for both of us. Spice Finch had been on my mind for a few months now so I figured this would be perfect for the occasion. Our sweet waitress gave us a rundown of the menu and told us that dishes are typically made for sharing. With that in mind, we both ordered fries to share but decided to choose our own entrees. I'm allergic to both chickpeas and lentils so unfortunately, I have quite a few food restrictions at Mediterranean restaurants. I shared this with the waitress when I ordered the peri-peri shrimp and she assured me that she would speak to the chef to make sure these ingredients were not used in this dish and there was no cross contamination. Thank you to the team at Spice Finch for making me feel so well taken care of! The peri-peri shrimp was incredible. So flavorful and rich with well-cooked, plump shrimp. I became a huge fan of peri peri during my trip to South Africa last year and am so happy I got to enjoy it here. The dish came with a side of buttery flatbread that I dipped into the sauce. The fries that my friend and I shared were also very good. They were well-seasoned and the portion was huge. I couldn't have the hummus aioli they come with but my friend said it was delicious. Although the sauce looked great, I was more than content just enjoying the fries sans dip! For dessert we enjoyed a slice of chocolate cake with tahini soufflé and blood orange sorbet. I was a little skeptical because I'm not usually a fan of fruity desserts but wow was this dish really something! The blood orange sorbet really balanced out the rich chocolate cake, but in my opinion, the tahini soufflé was the MVP. I could have eaten spoonfuls of that alone! The restaurant is beautiful. It is open and airy with the appropriate lighting. It isn't too bright but not too dark either. Lighting can make such a big difference - it really sets the mood and Spice Finch does it just right. This restaurant is great for get-togethers, celebrations or dates. I can't wait to return here. I'm tempted to make my next experience a brunch outing, but with such an incredible dinner, it'll be hard not to go back for that!

I rarley write reviews. But sorely disappointed with dinner here. Specifically chose this place because they claim to accommodate for allergies. I called ahead asked questions about cross contamination, talked to my server, and then to someone else as well because my server was very dismissive about my allergy. But even with all that and assuring me it was actually wheat free and not just the hipster version of wheat/gluten free got extremely sick. Everything is cooked on the same grill including the bread products which they failed to mention even though I asked specifically about it. On top of that I was still at the resteraunt when I discovered this and got sick and they did not take any opportunity for service recovery. The staff and chefs needs to be retrained about allergies because it is not taken seriously. So rude that made me feel safe eating there. If you can't accommodate just say it and people with allergies wouldn't go there.

When you ignore substitutions based on allergies you put people health at risk. The community trusts you to be reading delivery orders, especially when you ask for specified ingredients to be added/omitted, not being there to watch to make sure an allergy substitute is not accidentally added.

Just stopping by for some lunch during a fabric-shopping day trip with some girlfriends. They have a large patio for outside dining. There are plenty of umbrellas so you have little chance of being in the hot sun. You can also dine inside if you prefer. We chose the outside because we are still trying to be careful about Covid. I think there were limited options for anyone trying to do gluten-free or keto. The main items were pasta or pizza. I ended up getting the Argula and Mushroom salad. I did get a taste of the meatballs which were pretty good. I liked the dressing of my salad. There were four meatballs for $12. I think that was a bit pricey for $3 for a small meatball. Service was a bit slow. We waited a while for refills of our drinks and my meal came after my friends have already finished half a pizza. Not sure why a salad could have taken that long. Friendly service. Parking is limited. There is a small lot with very tight spaces. I just parked on the street and it was free parking.

I wish I could leave 0 stars! Ordered Moe's through Uber Eats a short time ago. My wife entre was ordered with queso on the side. She is lactose intolerant and can't have any, but she asked for some on the side to have it available to share with rest of the family. The order arrived with queso drizzled all over it. I called to complain and request a replacement, but was treated rudely by the staff. They refused to offer any type of replacement solution, and just kept stating my only option was to contact Uber for a refund. The employee raised his voice at me on the phone, and became combative. No help from Moe's was given, and I had to seek a refund from Uber which took 48 hours. Uber was apologetic and helpful, but it didn't change the fact that my wife's dinner was ruined. Contacted Moe's corporate and filed a complaint. Was contacted by a higher up who initially seemed concerned. I didn't ask for a refund since Uber provided one already, I just asked for an apology. I didn't hear back for nearly two weeks, and only got a response when I sent an angry follow up. I will be making a different restaurant choice the next time I use Uber Eats. TLDR: Staff ruined item by not following directions. Made no attempt to replace incorrect item. Rude staff, apathetic manager. Negative experience, stay away.

I may have gotten a bad batch but this is the worst pizza ever I am a foodie who travels a lot and will always try the local foods and I got the deluxe late last night and I swear it looks like someone threw up on a box! I ate some cause I was really hungry and couldn't get past the fact it almost tasted like trough up too

I ordered the gluten free pizza and was very disappointed. I picked up so I did not call and complain after I got it home but it was clearly over done and most of it was thrown out. I got a frozen gluten free pizza at Giant for half the price and was better (I cooked it correctly). I cannot say anything about their other pizza offerings only that they are pricier than locally available pizzas at other establishments.

We stopped near closing time tonight. The dinning room was closed 10 minutes prior to their closing but the gentlemen working said he could take our order through the drive through. I ordered a thick burger with no cheese no bun and no mayo. I got my order and it had cheese. We drove around again and told him about them mistake. He said he was sorry and took it back and said he would make another. The guy in he kitchen just scrapped the cheese off and flipped the burger over. I'm glad I checked. I have food allergies. This would have sent me to the emergency room. I will not eat here again and I will be calling on the morning to complain. This kind of behavior is so dangerous. I understand they wanted to go home but his could have really hurt me!

This place actually has a range of really good items, so the 2-stars really comes down to the abysmal cost/quality ratio. I'm all for good food, and paying for it, but the prices at this place border of arrogant and pompous. Let's start with the pizza, ok gluten free, I'm down with that. Yet at a baseline of 15-20$ by the time you add a topping or two you are pushing $25. My advice: go to Blackbird Pizzeria and get their pizza; it is better and not nearly the price. As I see it, a $30 pizza should have gold chips on it, not some burnt crust and scant toppings. The pizza left a bad taste in my mouth, literally, and it was not soothed over by the pastries. In the end my wife and I were the suckers. We were happy to see this new place in a spot that desperately needs revitalization. But we dropped $55 on just a few items and I can only find myself shaking my head every time we drive back by. High price + unrealized expectations + long wait = 1 star.

We came here for a happy hour to celebrate one of my friends accomplishments. They are one of the few places in this area with a good happy hour menu because we didn't want to go all the way downtown and get stuck in traffic. The margaritas are really good although they are strong. On the happy hour menu you can get the regular margaritas, and then you can order the flavored margaritas off of the regular menu. I also ordered the chicken quesadillas off of the happy hour menu which were a nice size and good taste considering the price. I would beware if you have a shellfish allergy, as before I ordered fries I was told that they are cooked in the same oil as the shrimp. I am always nervous when places cook revaluation foods in the same oil as the shrimp because it means there's not a lot of restrictions for cross contamination within the kitchen. Overall good happy hour and quick food place. The waitress was nice and accommodating.

I will never go to this subway again or maybe any of them. I ordered a bowl online and didn't realize it came with ranch. The person I ordered it for is allergic to one of the ingredients in the dressing. The worker was rude and was like that is how you ordered it. The worst customer service ever refused to remake or return the money, supposedly he is the manager. I was advised that I should leave a negative review.

Following the order of a blackened salmon burrito, I watched in horror as the line cook grabbed a raw salmon filet out of the refrigerated drawer with a gloved hand, and then continued to prepare the burrito - with the same glove and raw salmon juice - as the salmon cooked on the flat-top. The line cook grabbed lettuce, scooped rice out of the spoon, and spread sauce with contaminated gloves before I stopped my order. If you ate here on 11/16/17 and got sick, this might be why. Never coming back. My experience in kitchens is that raw protein should only be handled with color-coded tongs. Not so here...

DO NOT take group orders from here. We placed a group order from work and literally every single order was incorrect, plus there were some items missing. When we went into the restaurant to discuss our order, we were met with hostile staff who told us there was no way they would be making us new orders for free. They didn't give us refunds or anything else to make up for their plethora of mistakes. Everyone that placed the order was unhappy and some couldn't even eat their food because of being vegetarian or having food allergies. What a HORRIBLE experience. Restaurants should make it a responsibility to own up to their mistakes and fix them, because no one wants to pay good money for something they didn't even order.

We came here for a bridal shower. The food was good, however during the 3 hour shower (12-3) the main food did not come to the tables until about 2:30-2:40. They were accommodating as far as having allergies. However, they were VERY misleading towards the actual bride. The soon to be bride had to deal with the stress, confusion and aggravation on her special day, of who had to pay extra for a dessert the party itself brought. The bridal party was told that they were allowed to bring cake, cookies, extra dessert. However once is was time for dessert the staff made a big issue that it would cost an extra $2.50 per plate, for anyone who wanted a dessert (that the bridal party provided). So the only dessert that was allowed to be served with no extra charge was the main cake. Which would be fine however the bridal party spent $ for no reason on extra dessert. Another BIG issue was the bridal party was charged for 10 extra plates, for people who didn't show. But the restaurant did NOT allow the party to be served or take home the plates they were charged for. It was a huge pain in the ass, and a scam it seems from the restaurant itself. I would NEVER book or even visit this restaurant simply bc of the fact they have no empathy or understanding for the person booking the party. Also they were VERY unclear on their rules they are NOT willing to budge on. Very unsatisfied.

This place has good food.... the service is the worst I've ever seen. The girls are rude, they talk about the customers in Spanish, which we know because my husband speaks it fluently. They roll their eyes, say they don't like fruit, have no advice or information on ingredients... they aren't helpful if you have a food allergy like my oldest daughter. They talk while you are waiting to order and aren't attentive at all. We tried it 3 times. Every experience was the same. We will never go back.

I want to make this review in hopes for improvement. I have been to Kei Sushi about two times before and had good experiences. However this time It was the worst experience I have ever had at any sushi restaurant. On July 19th, 2020, My friends and I came for lunch. All the appetizers were good, and when the sushi came out it looked fancy. However we soon discovered the sushi tasted horrendous. The Godzilla roll is known for its crunchy texture on the outside and warm, fresh fish in the inside. In this case it was cold, soggy and tasted no better than a pair of dirty socks. The fish was probably older than my grandparents. The crystal shrimp roll was also dreadful. The shrimp inside was drier than the Sahara desert and every bite was like eating a bag of sand. Not to mention the GIGANTIC size of each individual piece. I would have better luck putting golf balls in my mouth. Of the 6 rolls I only found one good and one decent. The rest I wouldn't even feed my cat if I had one. The Server even charged us extra for the pieces we had left but it's a small price to pay to end our suffering. Lastly, I want to mention that out of the three of us, one did get food poisoning and legend says to this day he's still sitting on the toilet.

I am livid, and I will never patronize this establishment again 1. The portions and prices are not compatible. Secondly, I was charged for two large breast platters and the meat is all dark meat and to exasperated the matter my credit card was billed 12$ over! Thank God that I asked for a receipt! PLEASE BEWARE THEY'RE OVER CHARGING FOLKS AND THE FOOD WAS HORRIBLE DREANCHED IN SAUCE TO HIDE THE OVER COOKED DRY ASS CHICKEN! IF THE STORE WAS STILL OPEN I'd definitely return this trash! This place has to be under new management. I ate here years ago when visiting Philly and had a great experience. This has me ready to vomit I'm so dam mad

Not at all a great experience, me and my family went there for dinner one night and were greeted by the host. We were told to wait 30 minutes and said we can self tour so we got a drink and waited about an hour for our table. Once we were seated we felt very discomforted but continued to go about our business. Since it was the pandemic my family hasn't been outside in a while and we're excited to see the scenery anyway. The waiter took our order and we waited about an hour and fifteen for our food to come. We got our food and my cousins chicken was undercooked. We sent it back and then we're told that's why it was taking so long. I had the salmon and my two other family members had steak. By the time the food came she wasn't hungry anymore our bill was outrageous and then to top it off the manager had nothing to say about it. He was rude and disappointing. We then went home and had food poisoning. I could not stop VOMITING! The entire night!!!!! Horrible service from everyone on the team. I am also a rocky point resident which is even worse on them. I will not do business here nor have my events here. Very bad.

Most times I order HipCityVeg I end up regretting it. Their gluten free selection has expanded, but it adds several dollars to any meal, and it is already pretty expensive for what you get. Their sweet potato fries and aioli are usually decent, and I have also had okay experiences eating the green smoothie and the gf maitake burger. Overall, I would say it is unfortunately rarely worth the price.

Want to spend a Sunday afternoon sunk into an uncomfortable desk chair, pulled up to a community table, trying to decode Milktooth's menu with the "I'm Feeling Lucky" Google function, only to walk away still hungry? ...Eek! Methinks not. The menu was anything but appetizing. Trying to decipher the verbose and picture-less paper menu through a Pollock painting of previous diners' splatter marks was unnecessarily gross and very frustrating. I even asked the server for a picture menu: they did not have one. Trying to eat gluten-free? Our server suggested her favorite dish on the menu, minus the toast. She said a lot of interesting words... but more accurately it should be described as a single small egg in a bowl of stewed tomatoes. In an effort to salvage the meal, I asked for hot sauce. The server made me specify which kind I wanted, only to come back five minutes later saying they were out (Cholula). She kindly brought a few options, two of which had disgustingly crusty tops (Red Habanero Sauce and another I can't recall). Gross again. Also, no gluten-free sweet treats in their menagerie of baked goods. I visited with my vegetarian friend and you really get the feeling that if you require any specific dietary needs you are not welcome. Point taken. I will likely not return.

I came here for the first time last weekend. Service was a bit disappointing. I would've appreciated a check-back from our server after we got our food because I needed something for my dry a*s gluten-free toast (I regularly eat gluten-free, so I expected it to be crustier than my hands in a Midwest winter, which is why I always have to slather it in a spread of some sort). I instead ate it plain af because I was so hungry from what little portions my food offered. I got the smoked salmon frittata which was pretty good, but it wasn't a lot of food. Overall, the service could've been better for the lack of business at the time I dined. I also wish the dishes offered more quantity in addition to the quality (a b*tch is hungryy).

I recently moved to STL and everyone that knows I'm a Celiac instantly told me "PI now has gluten-free pizza!". And yes, it's true. I eagerly got a new acquaintance to meet me at the Delmar loop location to try out the place I'd been hearing so much about. Now let me say, I not only love pizza but it's one of my favorite things to make at home...gluten-free of course. So I'm a bit picky about pizza. When I first try out a pizza place I always get a basic/favorite of mine - either pepperoni or Hawaiian as a sort of litmus test. Reading over the menu from what I gather their fancy/unique combinations may be what they are more known for. However, I believe the crust is the starting point of a good pizza and if it is just "meh" you can't mask it with toppings...and I was not very impressed with the gluten-free crust. It was just OK. It held the yummy toppings but itself was a bit dry and flavorless. Talking to the waiter he confused they buy the crust from somewhere else and basically heat up the toppings before bringing it out...and it tasted that way. My pizza didn't have enough sauce to account for the somewhat dry crust. Toppings and cheese were however yummy. As a gluten-free person in the Midwest I know my options are few...and I really, really REALLY appreciate places that offer things I can eat and make a good attempt at it. That being said, I will make my pizza at home most of the time but when I'm not in the mood for the dishes I will come here. To end on a more positive note they carry gluten-free "Bard's Beer"!! Yay!! :-)

I love the idea of this place in theory and the food was good(not the best, but good). It probably would have been 4 stars for me. Service was quick and friendly and the portions were generous for the size, but the one thing I can't get over is the sauce bar. I love hot sauce and in theory the idea of a sauce bar with so many hot sauces is fantastic, but in practice the way they have it set up is really gross. The entire area was dirty and sticky when we went in, and it was mid-afternoon on a Sunday so it wasn't like it was being overlooked during a rush. A couple of employees were casually going around cleaning but just totally skipping it over. A lot of the bottles were old and crusty and it was just not a good experience. I really prefer the way other restaurants do this where they have pumps. It seems a lot more sanitary. I don't like to think the worst of people but with so many bottles just being out in the open like that it's easy for them to be contaminated some way, especially when the area isn't kept clean. I'll be back if I'm ever in the area but will sadly skip the sauce bar.
Used to be my favorite Mexican restaurant until they changed the menu recently. We ordered the "el chapo" quesadilla and it gave us food poisoning the same night after we left.

Since it opened, i've loved Milktooth. but no more. Yesterday, after a typical hour and a half wait, i was finally seated only to be treated rudely by the chef and wait staff. You see, I can't eat pork due to a religious dietary restriction. Normally this would be fine, I am usually able to avoid pork. Not at Milktooth. Their menu contains one chicken dish (which comes with pork sausage gravy), which they were out of, one lox dish, and one beef dish. the beef was a ribeye steak with egg foo young. this is what i wanted, in fact, this is what i came in for having seen a picture on the restaurant's instagram site. unfortunately for me, the egg foo young that came with the ribeye had pork in it. the restaurant has a strict "no modifications" policy. Even though they say that they like to accommodate for food allergies, they in fact, will not serve their food other than EXACTLY the way it is described. I knew this, so I didn't ask for them to try to make the egg foo young without the bacon. All i asked for was, "could i have the ribeye (at full price) without the egg foo young?" My server, who was a manager, absolutely refused to even ASK the chef if this could be done. she said he has a 'vision' and that it's the ONE THING he required when he came to Milktooth. wow. really?
