I asked to speak to someone else. another manager came. i explained to her that i have a religious dietary restriction against pork (isn't this a thing? don't people know that some people can't eat pork?) and that i'm really wanting to eat the ribeye without the egg foo young. could i have just the ribeye? she said she would ask the chef, but seemed very put out. At Milktooth you can see the chef working from your seat at the table. I watched her ask him, he vigorously shook his head and said "NO WAY". THE CHEF WAS NOT WILLING TO SERVE ME THE RIBEYE WITHOUT HIS PRECIOUS EGG FOO YOUNG. The manager came back and told me it would not be possible to eat the ribeye steak without also being served the egg foo young. At this point i was in shock i think. because i could see him making the egg foo young separately from the steak and then plating them together. so why could it not be served without the egg??? I told the manager that i'm finding it incredibly hard to believe that i can't just have the steak. she went back and talked to the chef some more. she came back and said that the only thing she could do is have the ribeye plated on one plate and the egg foo young plated on another plate. BUT I HAD TO BE SERVED THE EGG IF I WANTED THE STEAK. i can't believe the pretentiousness of this place. i ate that damn steak. it was good. and i refused the plate of egg foo young before it could land on my table. i told them to send it back, and when it did go back, there was ACTUAL commotion from the grill area. the chef was visibly upset. that's how crazy he is. he was upset that i could not eat his artfully created vision because of my religious restriction. it gets worse: when i VERY politely complained that the chef is too pretentious to let his customers eat steak without pork he recommended i go to denny's (see photos). he also tweeted to me that it makes no difference that it was a religious issue because "we don't base our policies on anyone's faith." He also tweeted that he believed that the "customer is always right" is a "myth" and completely wrong. wow. for a business who just hosted "Big Gay Day" in an effort to show inclusion, this is an extremely exclusive attitude. about 20 tweets back and forth, they still refuse to apologize or even just simply say "hey we're sorry you had a bad experience, please come back" and by not saying that, what they ARE saying is "WE DON'T CARE ABOUT YOU, DON'T COME BACK." I won't be going back. I loved Milktooth but they did not love me back. Rude wait staff (who were managers) and beyond arrogant and rude Chef. There are plenty of chefs in indy who have vision but also care about their customers. it's possible to do both and it's possible to be KIND. JUST BE KIND.

Stopped in for a second trip in a week . Again service was on point and friendly. But have too say they changed the Caesar salad I raved about last week from what I would say was a loaded Caesar to a regular Caesar. The egg, charred broccoli , bacon, and Avocado were now gone. It was still a good Caesar and a small with a sled of calamari made a great meal. Truly hope the loaded Caesar returns to the menu( server told us a lot of people were asking about it). My daughter was in for her first trip and had the small salad topped with grilled shrimp and was very impressed as she said shrimp were perfect. Wife got salad with a side of meatballs and had one and took other 2 home and was ecstatic as she said meatballs were closest she had had in a restraint to her Italian born aunts homemade . A side note that should be mentioned..,for anyone with tree nut/ peanut allergies.. was well documented by server and manger came out to assure us nothing on menu to worry about but dessert and that that is kept in totally different prep and storage area . So no chance of cross contamination and that she personally had staff change gloves and wash hands as extra precaution ... needless to say from someone who has been to the ER a couple of times with my child due to nut cross contamination that made the meal a lot more enjoyable and comfortable as in our family it is truly a life and death issue . These days it is a most welcome relief. Looking forward to many more great meals and happy times at this new much needed community establishment.

I had my very first Cuban coffee here and it was terrific. The perfect wake me up on a warm rainy day in Ybor. The cafe offers board games inside and small tables for outdoor coffee. It was really satisfying to sit and sip my coffee watching people walk around the area. This place offers a great piece of the culture of the city. This shop is located in the heart of Ybor and has a beautiful tiger mural inside. My only recommendations would be to add at least ONE plant based milk for the Cuban coffees as a tourist I wanted to try the coffee. There are plant based condensed milk options on the market - such as coconut. With the current trend of vegan diets, food allergies, and food sensitivities having a dairy alternative seems appropriate.

Absolutely disgusting. does not pass health reviews. serves raw questionable looking food. if i could give it 0 stars i would. horrible. DO NOT ORDER PINEAPPLE CHICKEN. i threw up. literally trauma i cannot eat any chicken now because of thiss.

So ecstatic that my friend just introduced me to Prep & Pastry. We went this morning for an early morning breakfast, and I could not be happier with my experience. This place is definitely a place I'll be visiting again! To begin, the restaurant is very cute with some rustic feels. The hostess looked really happy to see us and had us seated. Almost instantly, a young man brought us water and told us that our server would be with us in a moment. Our server was Ryan, and within five minutes he came and let us know what the daily specials were. He took our drink orders and told us he would be right back to get our breakfast choices. I ordered a cranberry tea which was delicious and for $2 I ended up getting 3 steeps from the same tea (yay!). My friend got the citrus tea and she loved hers as well. I ended up ordering the chef's choice pancakes. The chef makes new things each day (different pancake of the day, french toast of the day, etc.). The pancakes this morning were walnut and chocolate chip. I ended up getting three huge pancakes for $7, and they come with syrup (which was good, but I'm not a huge syrup fan) and creamy whip. I actually ended up taking half of my breakfast with me. I was not expecting such a huge helping, but was glad to have it. The pancakes were delicious! My friend ordered the basic breakfast, which comes with toast, eggs, and potatoes (hash). She's a vegetarian, and Ryan made sure to let her know that there was no meat in any of these products and no contamination. BUT! They do have several vegetarian friendly options if you or your friends are veggie lovers. Next time, I might actually try "The Mac is Back," which has vegetarian sausage. The service here is just as wonderful as the food. All of the servers seem to work in unison, and we saw several different servers refilling people's water, coffee, etc., when they were running low even if it wasn't their table. When Ryan brought us our checks, we had just finished putting our cards in, and a different server asked us if he could run them from us. Several different people asked us if we were enjoying our meal as we ate. Basically--they have great attention to detail. At one point, my friend asked for some honey for her tea, and they provided it. She also ordered a scone to go, and they brought her a HUGE scone in a box. I ended up paying $9.73 (before tip) for 3 pancakes, 3 cups of hot tea, and a glass of water (I had about 2 glasses). I'm definitely coming back here! I can't wait to try the lunch options. But the breakfast is great. There were several things on the menu I'd go back to try out!

Pretty sure I can't say one good thing about this place other than its in a good location. It's super dated, the servers couldn't be less interested and the food (what I could eat of it) was poor quality. I was really excited to try Sunset 44 as I've lived in Kirkwood for several years and never made it into this restaurant. I ordered the fish tacos and requested nothing with mayo be on the plate as I am allergic. It was a huge portion of fish - which was great. It was, however, covered in a mayo based sauce. I politely reminded the server that I asked for no mayo. He sighed and took it away. He then returned 30 seconds later with a soggy piece of breaded fish that had clearly been rinsed off and put back onto my plate. Two thumbs down.

I came in last week for the first time. I think the prices are a little high for the portion. I spent over $20 on a wrap and juice. The wrap didn't have much filling in it but was tasty and I was happy for the gluten free option. I chose the wake up one for my juice and it was delicious with an almost creamy quality and I was appreciative that they serve it over ice. The service was slow. They were busy when I walked in. I understand why I had to wait so long to place my order, but they did not even address me for a good 7-10 minutes. I stood there awkwardly, waiting to put in my order. I will definitely give them another try, but hope that they will fill my wrap a little bit more next time! Also it seems as if they have a decent kids menu. I will have to bring my little one next time so she can try it out as well.

What happened what happened too fast food that it Doesn't even have the slightest relationship to Food anymore I remember when McDonald's became big I remember being a kid and getting a big Mac and not even be able to get my mouth around it I remember getting a cheeseburger and not being able to finish it french fries were crisp customer service was paramount what happened to fast food it is not even edible anymore this is utterly ridiculous I can't say that I patronize fast food restaurants often but come on it was always an option when you were completely busy running errands Christmas time you didn't have time you went through a drive-through but at least you knew that the burger was good the french fries were good that you weren't going to be sick after you ate it with both food poisoning and regret. Running errands busy tired hungry let's grab McDonald's I have no idea what the hell I ate last night I took pictures of it because I'm completely gobsmacked by what was inside this roll. the big Mac was the size of a cheeseburger the cheeseburger was the size of a thimble none of it had any flavor it was thrown together so haphazardly that I almost believe that they found it laying under a car threw it in a bag and handed it to me. why where did it all go wrong where are you customer service where did pride in your job go where did pride in the symbols and places that we have known since we were children go. I tell people constantly that I wish I could've lived in the 50s but I wish I could go back to the 80s it's not because I'm nostalgic it's simply because things were real things were cared for things were done with pride things were worth it they were worth the money that you spent $13 for two big Macs two large fries and a chicken nugget and all I did was go to bed with a sick feeling in my stomach and less money. come on get it together or stop altogether

This location is DISGUSTING. I ordered a medium dunkacino. About mid way through the drink I felt something in my mouth and spat it out right away. I was completely disgusted. How could you serve this to someone? I talked to a manager that promised to call me back with my claim number and adjuster information. It's been weeks and I'm still waiting. I was sick for hours vomiting after this incident.

I recently visited here with a group of 6 and shortly after dinner, two members of our group who had eaten the taco salad we're sick to their stomach and spent a large portion of the rest of the night vomiting with food poisoning. Aside from that, we also had serving staff that was less than thrilled to serve us and seemed annoyed by the few minor requests that we had. I am not one to typically leave reviews but being that I often take other's reviews into consideration when choosing a restaurant, I wanted to inform others of our experience. We visited Margaritaville with high hopes but we were certainly let down. With all of the other great places to eat in Nashville, I definitely wouldn't recommend this one!

I had gone to their grand opening party and I left there thinking it was just okay. I was able to try different smoothies, but they all tasted the same to me. They didn't have much flavor and there was still huge chunks of fruits in mine. I figured maybe it's because they were swamped and still needed to work a couple of things out. I went for a second time after a couple of my friends who are frequenters here to give it another chance. I ended up getting their charcoal vanilla ice cream, which was almost $6 for one scoop and 3 (free) toppings. I thought it was cool that they had vegan chocolate chips and gluten free granola, since you don't see it often. Most places only stick with either being vegan or gluten. The ice cream itself was okay. Definitely not worth $6 though. I think the vegan chocolate chips were my favorite part. I might give this place another try, but I don't really have high hopes. Maybe their açaí bowl could change that?

Got the prime rib Medium cooked. Unfortunately was probably one of the worst steaks I have ever had in my life. Tough and not much flavor. In middle of night got violently ill and threw up. Will give restaurant benefit of doubt on another dish, but never would order the prime rib again.

So, ......I used to eat here alot. I mean ALOT. I don't go as much now, but it's still was one of my favorites. It was always clean, the staff friendly enough, and the food always hot and fresh despite how busy they always were. Well ladies and gents....hold on to your hats cause we've got a live one here!! Come on boys and girls....can you say FILTHY? Try it with me...Fiiiilllllthy! Oh....you better believe I took pictures, but they cant do it justice. They had a rude manager who got an attitude when i asked her for a towel to wipe off our dirty table. Their entire staff seemed to consist of a bunch of middle schoolers that didn't want to be there. The floors .....DIRTY. The kitchen.....DIRTY. The tables....DIRTY. The bathrooms....DIRTY. This place is a salmonella festival waiting to happen. I did contact the corporate office and send them my complaint and pictures. The response I got was "We're sorry you didn't like our restuarant ". I'm not telling you not to go there. However, I will say, Be careful.....food poisoning is just around the corner from this place.....always lurking....always watching.

The bougie sister to a typical Giant grocery store has more selection than a minit market, but too many pricey staples to make it worth anything more than the occasional stop, in a pinch. Giant Heirloom Market subsists off the "Student Loan Industrial Complex," getting students to buy overpriced organic and non-gmo (lol) alternatives to things like the usual college student fare. It has a place (which I don't think is on a college campus), but you're better off just going to a regular store. Pros: Many organic, non-gmo, gluten-free, vegan, etc options. Who's this marketed for at 34th and Chestnut? It's better than going to Wawa or a bodega, but not by much. Definitely quality-controlled though, which is nice. The selection isn't as good as, say Mom's Organic, but it's an oasis in the desert. Plenty of fresh-made options if you're looking for that (and you're not - just get a hoagie). Service was friendly and attentive. They sell wine and beer! Cons: Very overpriced. Bad selection of traditional items. They didn't have the Soy Sauce I needed for a recipe! Weirdly limited selection of non-organic or similar non-niche items. They had organic broth but not just regular chicken broth/stock or even bullion cubes. Incredibly cramped and uncomfortable. Employees were moving a cart around trying to stock shelves mid-day on a weekend making one of three pantry aisles impassable. It doesn't make sense. Conclusion: I mean, I guess it's fine and it's better than nothing, but I don't see how it advances the grocery-store dessert of U-City. You're better off just going to Fresh Grocer if you're actually looking for anything other than an item or two.

Ordered the ahi club sandwich. Looked over the menu closely to make sure I knew what was on it, because I have allergies, specifically to avocado. Menu says there's no avocado on this sandwich, but my sandwich had sizable slices of avocado on it. I'm allergic so I couldn't eat it at all. I wouldn't have ordered this if it was described accurately on the menu.

I gave it a two because my breakfast was delicious. My husband ordered "plain French toast". Received with almonds. He has a nut allergy. We told the waitress and she said no you didn't say plain. Ok. Took it back and we waited 20 minutes for a new one. Well we got it cold and without the bacon we ordered originally. The Manager brought it over and without a word. Not very pleasant. Then to add insult to injury we were billed for BOTH French Toast. We said this is ridiculous and it was cold. They did take both of these off and we walked out very disappointed in the Customer Service of that Manager. Very poor representation of the place.

okay... the food was great. i got a small mac and cheese, a medium fry, and a fruit punch to wash it all down. service was great too. have to knock off 2 stars due to the fact that about 2 hours after finishing my meal i proceeded to projectile vomit it up. would go back tho.

First, onion ring sauce tasted like fishy vomit. Onion rings were not seasoned at all. Cheese curds were falling apart the sauce was good though. Pizza was trash. They said it was hand tossed, doubtful. It tasted like they got it shipped in from Chuck E. Cheese. Twisted tavern? More like twisted tummy!! Will not be back. The server was sweet but the whole staff seemed not really with it. They dropped one of our pizzas, they gave us two orders of cheese curds when we only asked for one, and they forgot our salad.

Fake maple syrup that leaves a persistent funky aftertaste...seems like syrup should be real for the price ($51 for breakfast for three w/ tip) The single-use plastic straws in every glass of tap water were especially dissonant and off-message given the ocean theme. Breakfast burrito was good and the gluten free pancakes were fluffy and tasty ... bring your own syrup from home, though.

This place was horrible! We got there early -4pm with reservations. Waited 15 minutes to see a waitress. Ordered. Salad served but we had to ask for utensils. Salad eaten before wine was served. ten minutes later and 3 requests finally got us water! Lasagna was average and dry. Specialty grouper dish tasted so fishy we knew it was old. My husband is allergic to msg and after three bites he started getting sick. Bad food and bad service. We will never return!!!

Their now serving Pre-cooked chicken we just ordered four 4-wing combos all the chicken was dark (when their natural color of their wings is light) the wings were extremely dark & super crunchy because they re-cooked the chicken. I'm calling the health department this is what causes people to have food poisoning

Awful food! Daughter went to take a bite of her mashed potatoes and there was a dead fly - not on the potatoes, but IN the potatoes! We gave it to the manager and he swapped the potatoes out...not even an apology or a refund even though we asked. His response was we have people coming and going all day long and the flies come in when the doors open! You want to take a few days off work or not attend a function? Go to the Golden Corral and pick yourself up some food poisoning!

I see no sense in burying the lede here - we got food poisoning and had horrible service. Needless to say, it was a terrible experience. But here's how it all went down... We had a 9pm reservation for a party of 4. We sat outside and were one of only 3-4 tables at the whole restaurant. With it being slower, I expected that, if anything, we'd have an above average experience. Not the case. Our server was fine at first - explained the menu well and gave us a minute to look it over. He then came back to take our orders - we ordered a round of drinks and small plates to start. He explained how everything would come out and when to put in our order for the large plates based off that... then was a no show. We didn't see him for about 30 minutes after the time HE told US to put the order in. He eventually came back and we put in the large plate order, including the whole fish, which came with a glowing recommendation from him. After putting in this order, our server went completely off the map. Other servers were bringing food out our food - he never even came to check on us. We didn't see him for over an HOUR. It took so long that we eventually had to go inside to ask for the check. No one inside could find him either, but they said they'd send him out when they did. During this time, the only other table outside had their check transferred to the bar because they hadn't seen him in an eternity either. About 15 minutes later, our server returned to close us out. I asked where he'd been (lol) and he said he had to help the table outside move inside... lie - they moved inside BECAUSE no one knew where he was!! We left feeling dissatisfied with horrendous service but the feeling in our gut got worse from there. Literally. 3 out of 4 of us had the whole fish... 3 out of 4 of us got sick about 45 min-hour after eating it. I probably don't need to describe food poisoning to you - but we're talking vomiting, nausea, diarrhea, chills, sweats etc. We later looked up Spice Finch's latest health department report and things added up. For those reasons, I'm out. Spice Finch had some great reviews online and we were extremely excited to give it a try, but it was a major flop. Ugh

Pagoda Noodle Cafe is right near the Ritz East (smack dab in Old City). It's a medium-sized, multi-level venue that can handle a good lot of folks. A friend and I had dinner here one night, quite randomly. Our server (Sam) got us everything we needed, including our dishes. The food itself was okay: The crispy soft shell crabs ($15, for two) were deep-fried with a crispy (read: salty) coating, stir-fried with green peppers, dry garlic, and a five-spice powder. Not too spicy, but it did the trick. We shared a broiled Hawaiian fish (~$12) too, which wasn't bad. Wasn't floored by what we had, but at least I didn't get food poisoning! If you're in the area, feel free to stop in.

Ordered food at 5:25 and picked it up by 5:45. I had ordered an appetizer and bento box.The food was all cold and seemed like it was sitting out from an order before. The sushi could barely be called that and I felt like I was going to get food poisoning just by trying it. Do not waste your money :(

Food was meh. The chips are oddly seasoned (taste like they have Lawry's seasoning salt or something), but they're alright. Quesadilla was inconsistently filled. The rice was undercooked. The enchilada was pretty good. The California specialty taco wasn't good. The black beans aren't worth mentioning. House margs were alright, I was pleasantly surprised they weren't too sweet. Wait for the food was a bit longer than expected. All said, I would have given them 2-3 stars (price was ok, atmosphere was fine). But... The Big Problem: we saw an employee place ice buckets on the floor, dump the ice into the soda machine, and then USE THE BOTTOM OF THE ICE BUCKET TO PUSH THE ICE AROUND. So, she fully rubbed the part of the bucket that touched the floor all over the ice. I... I've always heard gross things about ice buckets/ice contamination and I just pretend I don't know about it, but this was way worse that I'd ever seen/heard. Also, she later rolled up the floor mats in from of the soda machine, brushed her hands on her jeans, then just started bagging to go orders. I'm a confrontation coward (like, I will cry, and it will be ugly) so I didn't say anything in the moment (also I was slightly buzzed and in shock), but hindsight I really wish I would have called her out in the moment ().

I have been coming to mike since I was a teenager, and it's still good! I miss him though he use to be out every week day. Now my kids go to him. The hot sausage is so good raw onions mustard and sauerkraut is my thing! The sweat that accumulates while eating his sausage is a workout I happen to love doing! Lol His changing of gloves him being mindful of cross contamination in the street cart world, kept me going to his stand. He's clean thoughtful, great small talk, he's a staple in south Philadelphia. You haven't experienced part of Philadelphia until you see his line to his stand it moves fast cause he's the best at it!!!

Breakfast with attitude. Would you like to order something and leave off one ingredient that you are allergic to? Nope, "we can't do modifications on the weekend." Ok, I will modify my dining choices and eat at one of the other many great breakfast places nearby. Recommend: Toast, Surrey's, Daily Beet and Ruby Slipper

I've always enjoyed firehouse, but my most recent experience was overall quite unpleasant. I asked for a sandwich with no cheese, no mayo, and extra mushrooms. After waiting almost 20 mins I finally got my sandwich, but there was mayo on it. I returned it to them and requested a new sandwich, when I got the sandwich back it looked as if they just changed the bread and scraped off the mayo contaminated mushrooms. When I got the sandwich back again there were barely any mushrooms on it. To fix this the crew member gave me a side cup of mushrooms that were cold! In addition to this there was still mayo on parts of my sandwich. Overall it was an unsatisfying experience.

My husband, daughter and I went in for pizza the other night. We usually order our pizza (1 regular and 1 gluten free) to be picked up. This particular night we decided to go and dine in. They were out of gluten free pizza; which was fine as this happens of course. My husband asked the manager if we would get a cheesesteak with no roll and french fries on the side. The manager said no an asked us to leave. I have never been so upset or offended. My daughter and I were sitting at the the table while my husband was at the counter speaking to the manager when this happened. I will never go back to this pizza shop again until the manager is not there. We are huge fans of their sister restaurant Giorgio on Pine and have gone there often over the past 7 years of living in the neighborhood; but their pizza shop is something to be desired. Great gluten free pizza... probably the best in the city... if they have it and if the manager will server it to you.

Our food was great and the service was wonderful but my mom has to eat gluten free. We were excited to try their gluten free pasta but was very surprised that they have no gluten free pasta even though it is on the menu and on their website. It was very disappointing.

Horrible. Disgusting. Over priced. One of the worst meals I have ever had. The poached eggs on the Eggs Michael were well cooked and the only thing good about this meal. The sherry sauce was pasty, the mushrooms in the sauce were rubbery, the English muffins were untoasted, and the sausages were greasy and spongy. The potato pancakes were so sour (yes sour) they were inedible. Hubby's diced ham and eggs looked like something off the line at a elementary school cafeteria. The scrambled eggs on my kid's plates looked like they came out of a container and had an artificially orangish hue. The pancakes my kids ordered were in the chewy side and didn't taste very good - particularly for a place featuring that product in their name. The butter (if it even was butter) was whipped and very salty. The syrup flowed like water. Even artificially colored and flavored corn syrup typically has at least a modicum of viscosity. The sour potato pancakes left my mouth burning. I learned from the manager that they mix in citric acid powder to keep the potatos from browning. Perhaps they didn't mix it in well enough and I got all of it. I hope nobody with a deadly citrus allergy orders them. The coffee was bitter (not good bitter) and the cost was outrageous. This one goes into the "oh, hell no, never EVER again"list of restaurants. Save yourself the agony and money. You will get a much better breakfast at McDonalds at a much better price.

Long time customer of Timpano Hyde Park. I have been here numerous times over the years and have had issues with gluten cross contamination with my food. I had a chance to dine in the newly renovated restaurant and its absolutely gorgeous now with chic floral interiors and instagrammable spots. I had 0 issues with gluten cross contamination, in fact like always I was greeted and told immediately they knew I was a Celiac and would take extra precautions preparing my food. We opted for outdoors seating which is really nice and enclosed by lush plant life. The new menu has maintained old favorites like the steamed mussels and it also has new items like the Berkshire porkchop with vinegar and peppers whi h was out of this world. ai recommend the smoked whipped potatoes also, they are so light and fluffy and fresh tasting you will want more. This was a 5 star dinner and I am so happy they re-opened with fabulous renovations. athe price point is still the same at about 150 to 200$ for a full meal for 2 from starters to entrees, sides, and desert (3 drinks also). Parking is free if you park in the garage also!

TLDR: Inexpensive coffee with expensive baked goods! We ordered the gluten free maple donut ($3.25) and espresso caramel bar ($3.75). It's a little expensive for snacks, but their coffee seemed to be a good price. My GF maple donut was very sweet, even though I love sweet and normally can tolerate quite high amount of sweetness. I bearly finished it, luckily the size wasn't too big. Plus, the texture was more like maple cake instead of a regular donut. The espresso caramel bar tasted very strong coffee flavor which my wife loves. The caramel wasn't too sweet and the bottom layer (looks like cheesecake crust) brought more texture to enhance the entire flavor. My wife enjoyed it a lot. The decor was modern and yuppie, lots of people were hanging out there with the computers or friends. Location wise was a little confusing, the entrance was at the corner but wasn't very clear from the parking lot. We went to the wrong entrance and ended up at a pizza place where it's right next to it. Service was nice and friendly.

Horrible experience twice in a row. Last time the rice tasted like windex And I should have learned my lesson. Today i stupidly went back and the white tuna tasted weird. Near the end of my meal, a guy switch the floor rugs and decided to lean one against the table where people eat. The rug TOUCHED the eating area (I took a pic). After informing the staff, one of the managers refunded my meal, but not before I vomited in the parking lot walking back to my car. I also puked near the entrance door a couple of times , so if you ignore my advice and want to go there anyway (especially today ) , you may want to step over the vomit I involuntarily left there as a warning to all those that dare to enter. Sorry to those who try to escape ...don't blame me ...blame the white tuna. Never again

So I'm weird about Chinese food in that I only like Cantonese/Shanghainese food, or mall teriyaki like Maki of Japan - basically a heart attack in styrofoam. I won't touch Panda Express either? Anyways, ordered lo mein and a simple California roll from this place. The lo mein was not flavorful and the noodles tasted almost floury and gritty. The California roll was not even room temperature, but warm?? I was starving so I ate half of both, threw out the rest of the sushi, and within 2 hours I definitely had food poisoning (I'm always a fast reactor). I ended up having such a bad experience that I threw out any leftover lo mein I had as well. Haven't gone back so unfortunately have no pictures, but I say that this satisfies neither my Americanized Chinese cravings or anything remotely authentic.

I used to really love this place, so I took my in-laws last night. Service was ok, most everyone's food was good, but within an hour or so of eating their shrimp fettuccine, I fell violently ill. This has been the worst food poisoning ever. I let the restaurant know, and their response is why I feel I must only give 2 stars. They told me there understand if I never returned and that they'd let their kitchen and management know. That was it. No concern for my well being at all. I am severely disappointed. Also, they had somehow run out of straws so brought my toddler a sippy cup with no way of actually drinking the water, which was weird

Let me start by saying that I once considered Ron's to be the premier family dining establishment in the area. We used to stop in there at least once a month or more. That is no longer true. I will not go into all the minutia of the meal, but the bottom line is after waiting an hour on a Saturday at 4:30 PM for two medium burgers and a basket of fries I should not receive: a rare cold burger, a somehow well done yet cold burger (clearly it sat waiting to get picked up), and no fries (when the table behind us received the same basket with their meal right away). When these errors were pointed out to our clearly junior and unseasoned server he took away the burgers, returning minutes later to ask "the kitchen wants to know what you want us to do, warm them up, make you new ones, or take them off the check." Um, I came for dinner right? So I want what I ordered to be made correctly, right? Then what I assume was the manager/owner came over begrudgingly to say the order would be fixed (without any apology), and when the burgers came back, my undercooked clearly hexagonal shaped meat paddy shows a clear lying on behalf of the restaurant that claims: "Featuring scratch-made dishes with the freshest ingredients possible, our extensive menu includes gluten-free, vegetarian, spicy, hormone & antibiotic free, and from house-made options." If you let me know how you can get a purely hexagonal shaped burger scratch made from the freshest ingredients instead of frozen, you let me know. You know as they say "Meats - We do not use pre-portioned packaged frozen meats for our dinners." Clearly due to rising costs that is not the truth any longer. The restaurant is quick to point out all their rising costs due to wages, covid, or whatever they want to claim this week when the truth of the matter is that Ron's no longer "consider(s) our customers and employees part of our family and the health of our family is important to me." Now their attitude seems to be "you decided to come into our restaurant, so you are just going to accept a lower standard/higher cost experience, and if that is not ok with you, then go to the chains we hate comparing ourselves to." You know, the chains that are quick to point out are cheaper than you, yet have lesser (controlled) quality and the ability to answer service and food complaints in a rational and pre-determined manner that does not make the customer feel they are being "difficult with the "just trying to make it in these unprecedented times/support locally owned" business." That is what you run, Ron's, a business, not a sympathy gathering establishment. You may have labor and supply problems but guess what, we all do. You already are transferring that cost to the customer, maybe you shouldn't pawn off the decreased quality as well. "Here at Ron's Original, it is our pleasure to serve you delicious, scratch-made wholesome meals at reasonable prices without sacrificing taste. The bottom line is, "If I Wouldn't Eat It, I Won't Serve It!" These are your words, yet your attitude at the potential loss at two frozen burgers to keep your customers happy says otherwise. Finally I want to point out that since it took us so long to get our food, the restaurant was packed by the time we left, with a wait. So any cries of lost business are out the window. The world is going back to eat, if you are not prepared to meet the challenge due to staff or costs, then keep the doors closed.

AVOID! I'd give it 0 stars if I could. Not only did I feel ripped off by paying 12 dollars for a "Greek platter" of 90% salad, one piece of lamb, and a old potato chunk, and four pieces of stale pita bread. I ended up throwing up everything I ate due to food poisoning. The thing is, the only thing I threw up and ate was this Greek platter dish I had the night before. Save your money, there's other Greek places that won't give you diarrhea, vomiting, and rip you off for your money. I'd attach picture proof of this but I'd rather not scar people like I've been scarred from eating this place

My first trip here was a mommy daughter date. Mind you my daughter is 4 and like many young kids can be a bit picky and unsure of new things. Regardless we both LOVED everything. To begin our dinner we were promptly greeted by the staff and allowed to choose our own seating. Our beverages were brought quickly as well as our soup and appetizers. Our server was even considerate enough to inform me that not only do the mussels take a tad longer so if I would like them to order them right away. He also let me know that is should order 2, which I most definitely did. Very glad for that choice as they were beyond tasty. As many people know the ordering of mussels can often be skimpy. Many places do not allow you to order too much. They were not one of those places. Made for my happy night as I'm a huge mussel fan. For my daughter they were above and beyond with accommodations. The really likes tobiko so they made sure she got her foll with the nigiri. Not too much rice but plenty of the "flavor savers" as our family refers to them. The seared tuna nigiri was put of this world good. I'm quite picky about my fish being spoiled with a retired sushi chef that is a Japanese immigrant for a grandmother. I'll tell you wow was that good. To end things my daughter and I accidentally over ordered, she decided she was done last minute after ordering more. I offered to pay the additional to just now and bring home the last nigiri piece and half of a roll. I could no longer try to accomplish finishing it all as it is highly rude to waste. Again our server was sweet as pie and refused to make me pay the additional costs and allowed for me to bring the rest home. Then desert happened and they made my daughter the most adorable tempura banana and vanilla ice cream sundae with the sprinkles to top. This establishment won me over in many ways just from my one visit. Also for anyone curious they are amazing at offering gluten free and are especially careful not to cross contaminate. Go check them out.

I will be crossing My fingers for days we don't get food poisoning. Our food (for 6 people) tonight was absolutely awful. Every single person commented on how bad it was. As a sushi fan and frequent eater, this was the worst rolls I've ever had. I threw half of it away. Simply disgusting. I have never had grosser sushi ever. The hibachi I was told had barely any meat and didn't taste good at all. Our take out was supposed to take 25 minutes. We arrived after 35 and still waited another 10. No One else was there, not sure why. Wow, what a horrible tasting dinner. Huge fingers crossed we don't all get sick. I regret eating any of it.

I am all for a great salad place in Maryland Farms, with the pandemic we lost Newks and Zoe's so I was pretty excited to discover Chopt especially since they offer curbside delivery. The Pros: Curbside delivery, text updates for carry out orders, options of warm bowls in addition to salads. A large variety. The Cons: Chopt is located in a large busy plaza; there is not a specific designated place for curbside pickup. The way the plaza is designed, you can't pull up in front of Chopt so you are unsure if you should park on the side street or on the main street. All 5 times our office has ordered something was either missing or wrong. Generally it has just been the side bread or the salad was not tossed when we asked for it to be so we have just let it go. The last time we went though was really the breaking point. We didn't get dressing (tolerable). I ordered a warm bowl without any bread items, intentionally because I have a gluten sensitivity. So I ordered a bowl that does not have any bread items that are supposed to come on it. That is the standard. After getting back to my office with our food. I sat down with my salad, took a big bite and got a big mouth of croutons :( There were so many, I couldn't pick them out. I called and brought it back. I did get a new one but I didn't even get an apology. Just an acknowledgement would have been appreciated. Like "sorry we made you an interpretive bowl, glad you didn't die". The manager just acted like I was being a major Karen but I don't think being like "hey, this had croutons when it doesn't even come with it and it is tossed so it is impossible to pick them out because the whole thing is contaminated, may I have another?" is being a big jerk. I even ran in and got it myself. I feel like 5 times without a great experience warrants 2 stars. Pretty bummed too.

Only good thing about this place was the hostess. Super friendly and outgoing. Set a good first impression. While waiting to be seated grabbed a coffee and juice. The person making the coffee had a Black Lives Matter mask on and make America end again hat. Both my gf (who's black) and I were taken back. Not a good representation of the business. What kind of message are you trying to send to your customers? We were seated on time - ok great. Ordered food - ham and cheese omelette and chicken and waffles. Chicken and waffles was pretty good but the ham and cheese omelette was TERRIBLE! When my gf smelled the omelette she said it smelled rotten. I didn't notice the smell so I ate half the omelette. BAD IDEA! Within 2hrs I was vomiting and have massive diarrhea. I was so sick the rest of the day. I do not recommend this place.

Had i written this review on my first visit here it would have been 5 stars. Ive been to two other Trident locations and have never had a problem. Yesterday my gf wasnt feeling well and needed to raise her blood sugar. We were shopping next door so i called in a Pick Up order for two Cod tacos. When i arrived i was in a hurry so i paid and rushed to get the food to her. The bag was given to me tied tightly so i didnt smell it but when she opened it the smell hit us like a sledge. It was bad. However, because she was in a pinch and we had eaten there before, she took a chance and ate it anyways. She got food poisoning and skin signs of elevated toxin levels. I was shaking with how upset i was. Will never return to this location. How can a chef knowingly serve that?

I used to love this place. I always got my food promptly and never had any issues. I have a severe shellfish allergy and all of the staff has been accommodating about my allergy until recently. My last few to-go orders have been problematic. I've had to wait 30+ minutes inside the restaurant (when I had called in the order 20 mins before). The first time this happened the manager gave me a 50% off coupon and told me it wouldn't happen again. Yesterday, I had to wait even longer for my to-go order AND my order contained shellfish. About 20 minutes into waiting for my order at the restaurant, I asked one of the employees about the status of my order. He said that the chef wanted to make sure it was right (since I indicated that I have a severe shellfish allergy), which I appreciated. However, I noticed that they put fake crab on my sushi (which has crab juice in it) and explained that I couldn't eat that with my allergy so they remade it. I assumed that the rest of the order was correct and walked out of the restaurant with my food. However, I came home and realized that my order contained shellfish (scallops). I called to let the owner know and she told me it was too difficult to accommodate a shellfish allergy and that she didn't want me as her customer anymore. I have never been discriminated against by a restaurant due to my allergy. I'd highly recommend going elsewhere for your sushi!
Terrible service; line was out the door, very rude, not allergy accommodating. 1/5 for sure

I went here almost a week ago on a Friday evening with two other people. The restaurant itself was relatively busy and has a nice atmosphere with the colored lights. The service was not great, however it was late in the evening and we had ordered many things so we let it pass when the waitress forgot two oyster shooters, an eel and avocado roll, and one other roll our table had ordered. The rolls themselves were okay, not my favorite, but then I tend to prefer traditional sushi myself. The crispy rice with spicy tuna was probably my favorite item I tried. Although I thought there was a bit too much cucumber in the seaweed salads, my girlfriend and I thought it was a cute touch that they were served in martini glasses. Overall the dining experience was pretty average. I'm giving one star for the fact that I the uni I ordered and ate alone at my table gave me FOOD POISONING for the first time in my life and I'm not sure I've ever puked so hard.

The absolute worst drinks we've ever had! We couldn't even drink them. I almost threw up trying! I got a hurricane and it tasted nothing like a hurricane and honestly tasted like ginger and poison somehow. I don't know what my husband got but I tasted his and it was even worse than mine! The gummies they have are awful too! Do not go here! It's bad!

Every Salad I get from here is warm and has a chemical like smell which I believe is from the warm dressing. This time, I pulled a PUBIC HAIR from off of a piece of chicken which was towards the bottom of my salad. So who knows how many public hairs I consumed before seeing that one. Needless to say, I am nauseous to the point of nearly vomiting. I can't promise I still won't. And just to be clear, this is most definitely a pubic hair. It is not to be confused at all with any other type of hair. Even a short head hair or arm hair. See photo.

Lines are very confusing. I stood in one line for twenty minutes only to find out it was the wrong one. So you order in one spot and then they don't even start your order until you get to the end of the line and give them your ticket. Everything frozen and cross contaminated. Also, the price on the menu board is not correct. They will ring you up for $2 more
Got food poisoning at Harpers in Clementine N.J. Should have known better. Kai looked out of it. If you want to Drugs like that. You should not be around children.

Well, I ordered Pizza Hut again this afternoon and went to pick it up. I didn't check it before I left much to my dismay. I get home and it's not even close to the pizza that I ordered. I'm allergic to pizza sauce and can't have it but I love pizza anyway. So I ordered it without sauce. I brought it back to the store and the young lady proceeded to tell me that it had sauce on top of it. I told her I knew that that's why I ordered it without sauce. Now I'm waiting an extra 25 minutes to get the same pizza that I ordered hoping that it Be right this time. My faith in Pizza Hut is slipping by the minute. Should've ordered from a local company instead. Check your pizza before you leave the store. I realize that this is a busy location and that times have changed. These poor people were running around frantically trying to get these orders out. What I thought was most shocking is the store manager and the district manager were both in the store at the same time I watch them while I waited and they did absolutely nothing to help their crew. So with management like that there's no wonder that that store has many problems. It's such a shame. Pizza Hut was pretty good at one time. Now it's just pure luck whether you get a good pizza or not. It's very sad.

Came here because El Rez was an hour wait and we were hungry, unfortunately I think we should have waited the hour. It really isn't something I enjoy doing but I have to leave a bad review simply because the fish tacos I got made me extremely sick. I ended up going to the bathroom multiple times to vomit and wound up with a pounding migraine. I probably wouldn't order the fish tacos again.

This place was was overpriced and the food was terrible! We got the prime rib (one standard and one bone-in)and they were both rare to the point of raw, fatty, tasteless and hard to cut. Mine was so rare that I was afraid I would get food poisoning if I ate it. I sent it back to me cooled more and it came back an odd grayish color :-( The only redeeming part of the meal was the overpriced side dishes which were yummy, but nothing that were particularly hard to make. Overall, a place that I would NOT recommend and would not return to.

I like their wings and suggested we (wife, daughter and friends) go there after I hadn't been in some time... Unfortunately All five of us got food poisoning. My daughter was hit quickly heading to the car, then the wife and then me overnight. I found out this morning our 2 friends also took sick overnight. Not happy and have no idea what it was, as well all different things.

This place sucks don't go here! I have a lactose intolerance continually ask for no cheese!! Beans!!! Or sour cream spend well over $35 bucks a pop and they always mess up! Always Then they laugh when you complain middle finger up guys Never have this problem at the Carson location

We decided to go to Carrabba's one night when our reservation at another local Italian restaurant was given away to the wrong people. The food was good, honestly the cannoli cake was the best thing we had all evening. I can only give it one star because we were both in bed the entire next day with an absolutely terrible case of food poisoning.

What an awful experience. Our server was incredibly nice but that's about it. My friend had a dairy allergy and her food came with dairy on it. My salmon arrived slightly undercooked, but the server insisted on bringing it back and when she did (which took forever) it was very over cooked. The sides were cold both times. I will not go back to any Bluewater location.

Ordered a burger meal on 11/8/2020 & only took a couple bites from my meal because it didn't taste well & now I am unfortunately dealing with bad food poisoning definitely won't be going to this location again

Food is over priced for what you get and server gave me the wrong sandwich! Good thing I'm not allergic to the turkey I didn't want The bread was toasted so much my nePhew cut his mouth! Wait in line and for food is too long! Not worth it at all!!!!!!

May 18, 2016 Found hair in the chicken. Manager got mad at us and said it was from customers. We found it at 11 am as we were the first in to eat. It came from the cook. Manager was rude and yelled at us after we waited 20 minutes for her to come see us. She walked away while we tried to show her the hair. Hot food was cold. A good place to get food poisoning. Do not go here to eat.

My friend and I stood there for 15 min while 6-7 tables were becoming available. We still were not seated. My friend asked for the manager who really didn't care to hear our concerns. We were finally sat, we ate and drank and both got horrible food poisoning. I told her my issues this morning and she said that is exactly what happened to her. I will never eat there again. Contaminated food and poor service. Gross!!

This place should be ashamed of themselves! 2 and a half hour long wait for 2 hoagies! First time it got here after an hour the order was completely wrong! I called them up they said oh we just had a $400 order and got caught up. I said okay fine. They offer to remake it I said fine and was promised it wouldn't take as long. Literally another hour just for my chicken salad with mayo to be WARM you cannot eat that warm or you get food poisoning! I called asked I wanted a refund they refused said they will not refund me DESPITE me not getting what I ordered! Then said they putting my number on the block list! I will be taking this up with the better business buru because I never got what I ordered twice and was refused a refund

For a city that excels in taco-dom, I am shocked to find people fawning over this place. To each their own but I won't be putting in an ownership claim on this one. Yup, the corn tortillas are made by hand but they are so thick that eating a taco feels and tastes more like eating a tamale. The meat (carne asada and pollo) were bland and pale in color with a subtle lingering smell that made me raise my eyebrows. That same smell tends to drift from the bathrooms and kitchen. Don't get me wrong, I am nowhere close to being a clean freak. But an olfactory feline I am and after some seriously crazy brushes with death due to food poisoning, my nose is my trusty protector. This place did not comfort me. I still ate most of my meal and after a short-lived, mild feeling of stomach-upsetness, nothing happened. So that's good. I just won't be coming back. Maybe the shrimp and fish, being deep-fried annihilations of anything living or subtle in taste, are the way to go here?

Hello! I have a severe egg allergy. I started this account to review restaurants' ability and level of concern when answering my questions about their food's allergens. I came into the restaurant with my husband and there were only three other customers in the restaurant-none in line. I asked the owner if the bread on the sandwiches had eggs. He said "it came in a clear bag without ingredients from a bakery." He said "I could call them, but I'm sure it has eggs." He completely brushed me off and did not take me seriously. It was as if he thought all bread has eggs...why would I be checking if all bread has eggs? Do you think I'm going to miraculously find the first bread of my life to eat at your restaurant? No, I just was hoping to find a another "safe" spot in St. Louis for me to feel comfortable eating without the fear of dying. If you have an egg allergy and are craving a deli in St. Louis, check out my 5 star allergy review for Blues City Deli.

This used to be one of my favorite restaurants in Reno but I recently went there for dinner and ordered the short ribs. During our meal my husband and I were commenting on how the food used to be quite a bit better and this was not great. We started not feeling very good and I threw up all night that night :( I told this to a few friends and heard from several other people that they had not gotten as sick as I had but that the food had definitely made them feel ill. The reason I still give The Depot three stars instead of one or two is because of the friendliness of the staff and their amazing cocktails. Drinks are great but I will not be going back here to eat.

By far the worst customer service! We have ordered from the South Tpa location numerous times and it always seems that something gets messed up with our pick up or delivery order. But we have continued to give them chance after chance. Order was sent on Door Dash and we called the store to correct the order since it wasn't correct online. We were very detailed with allergy restrictions and of course again the order was wrong. One of the rolls had eel sauce on it, which is a huge allergy for a staff member. Called and spoke with manager Amanda, and she was extremely rude and blamed the mistake on us. Never was it offered to be corrected or re-delivered. She continued to debate about what ingredients are in the eel sauce. Great customer service do not treat customers like that. I really don't know how they are still in business with the management they hire. We will NEVER order from this establishment again. I hope the owners see what is happening with their facility.

The thought of anything not Italian give me hives (usually quite literally due to my allergies). BUT, I have been trying to expand my palate so when visiting a friend, I decided to live on the dangerous side (Again, quite literally). Thankfully I like an adrenaline rush, and thankfully Zorbas was a great place to try Greek. I would say this is as authentic Greek as you can get... it's a small little resturaunt, with large paintings on the walls, decor, a bake shop in the front, and everyone working there speaking Greek. Again, a great place to try Greek. We ordered a sampler for appetizer with Pita and Taziki, Hummus, and a spicy one. I actually loved the Taziki (which is not that surprising), and am in the process of learning to like hummus, which is longer of a process than I anticipated or desired. I ordered a chicken dish with all the sides. In the past, looking at the dish, would have been my nightmare. But with an open mind, moral support, and a lot (a lot a lot) of wine, I was able to overcome my fear, and enjoy my meal. Thanks to Zorbas, I can now add "Greek" to a type of food that I enjoy. Delicious, tasty, inexpensive, and dangerous all in one.

I threw up in the restaurant after eating shrimp!! After talking to the manager she told me that I must have a stomach virus. I didn't come into Denny's sick. And then told me that a man threw up in there previously and had to be taken off by an ambulance because of the virus! WHY would she tell me this when I am trying to explain to her that the shrimp are no good? I paid and left. I hate this place!

I just wanted to drop a review in here to let you know that the shrimp here gave me a severe case of food poisoning. Left me stuck in bed with trips to the bathroom every 30 minutes and 48 sleepless hours. All because they were to cheap to throw out the bad shrimp.

If only I could give them zero stars, unfortunately, I can't. Food was okay but it's hard to enjoy a meal when the customer service was disastrous. I overheard the waitress/owner talking to the table behind me about their food allergies and her tone of voice was very disrespectful. I thought maybe it was just a bad table. Waiting for her to give me my bill to get the hell out was a nightmare. She never came. I had to walk up to the host area and hand her the bill because she was unwilling to come and get it. I was running late for an appointment so I didn't bother to argue with her(she kept going on). She can keep her extra $2.50 "tax" as tip.

Got takeout for date night! Beer & bacon burger was just okay (the bacon jam stuff was really sweet and took it a weird direction). The tacos were kinda dry, and sauce for the white dog fries had a weird mashed potato consistency. That said, the fry sauce and jalapeño popper egg rolls were SOOOO good. I'll be back for those egg rolls and more fry sauce for sure, and I want to try their pulled pork. Also glad they have gluten-free buns since we have some food sensitivities in the fam.

Ordered a half-batch of gender reveal cupcakes so my boyfriend and I could celebrate the news of our new baby with a little special moment together! I asked my doctor for the gender in a little envelope and dropped it off at Batch. The great thing about this bakery, aside from the fresh ingredients, is that you can order however many cupcakes you want, you don't have to get 12. I almost just ordered two because it's just the two of us, but decided to get six so we could surprise some relatives over facetime and share with our neighbors. I picked their gluten free pumpkin cupcakes with vanilla buttercream. SOOOOO AMAZING! They were moist, perfectly spiced and you could definitely taste the pumpkin. The frosting stayed very creamy too, even on day three the cakes were still fresh and moist. As someone who reacts to wheat, I was nervous about cross contamination in their kitchen where they also use flour. I didn't have a reaction, which leads me to believe they are very safe when it comes to keeping allergens separate from gluten free recipes. The baker was kind enough to fill the cupcake with frosting representing the sex of our baby! They even decorated them with little yellow pins, such a nice touch. We hiked them down to our favorite Tahoe spot and took the biggest bites we could to see what we were having. Since then we've been back to get more pumpkin cupcakes to remind us of our favorite memory. Can't wait to order some of the other flavors, like Tahoe Blueberry and Lavender!

Super cold. Sweet. Average customer service. Expensive ass drinks. Didn't finish mine, threw it away, but thankful I didn't get food poisoning like some of these other Yelpers are stating. If I had read reviews first I probably wouldn't have bought anything. Even without anyone else's input, I don't feel like this was a worthy buy.

I LOVE bao, and stock up when in Chicago. Now I can, and have them delivered! They were delish. I also added an order of potstickers that were fresh and tasty. Unfortunately not all of the family enjoy Bao, so we included an order of Orange chicken. It was a huge disappointment. The bowl, although large, was 98% sticky rice with a splash of something on top. My daughter likened it to vomit- that unappealing. I was the only one brave enough to taste it. It was bland bland bland. I hope we just got the wrong order because there was nothing orange about it. This was a delivery order. Go for the Bao - it's the bomb.

Our daughter moved to St. Louis from NYC two months ago and discovered Indo. She's a foodie and loved the small plates, ribs, hamachi, and other items. As she was leaving she asked if the restaurant could accommodate a person with a shellfish allergy and they assured her that they could easily. So she made a reservation two months in advance to buy her moms dinner with one of her first paychecks. We were excited. Shellfish allergies are certainly tricky especially for restaurants like Indo that serve Asian style cuisine. But our experience was an all out disaster. There were only two dishes on the menu that could have been safely eaten and one of them had to be returned because the chef included fried onions prepared in the same fryer with other shell fish items. Then there was the nigiri sushi which we were told was possible but then the server said it had a fish sauce on it. (Turns out he was mistaken but it certainly didn't instill confidence.) We left, disappointed and discouraged and hungry. Perhaps this article might help the team at Indo https://www.menutrinfo.com/blog/fish-shellfish-menu?cn-reloaded=1 As a trendy restaurant with good food, Indy should at least try to be better about shellfish allergies or just let people know they can't. We would have happily gone to a different restaurant to celebrate our birthday and have our daughter spend $300 on us.

I hope people with allergies take precautions when ordering there.

In town visiting with my girlfriend and she suggested this place for lunch. It's basically $12 for all you can eat sushi, hibachi, stir-fry, etc. It seems too good to be true, but it really is a great deal and you certainly will not leave hungry. Be sure to finish everything because they do charge for uneaten pieces of sushi, shashimi and other things. I see a lot of reviewers mad about this policy, but to be honest if I owned a restaurant I would have a similar policy. All too often people don't finish their food and it goes to waste, and at an all-you-can-eat and order-as-you-go place, the waste can definitely pile up. Bravo to this restaurant for having such a no-waste policy. We started with egg drop soup, a salad and crab rangoons. I didn't care for the egg drop soup but the girlfriend liked it. The salad was just iceberg lettuce with a tasty dressing. The rangoons were nice and crispy fried but out of all of the ones I ate I did not see or taste any crab in them. We then ordered one sushi roll each. I got the Fuji roll and she got a chicken roll. I thought mine was very good, and didn't much care for hers. We also split a chicken and steak hibachi. This was not very good at all. The steak was very chewy and low quality, chicken not bad, overall not that great. We also got green tea ice cream for dessert which we both have never seen before but really liked. Service was attentive and quick. I forget our server's name but she was nice. After our meal I would probably advise staying away from anything that isn't sushi. Our sushi was good, seemed to be of decent quality, and I didn't get food poisoning or anything afterwards. Saki gets 3 stars because our meal probably would have exceeded $50 at any other similar place. Granted I thought everything but the fish sushi and ice cream was meh or bad, $12 for all you can eat sushi is unheard of and a super good deal. We will be back for the cheap sushi.

No joke the best burger I've ever had! I had the Brewski Burger with a gluten free bun. Burgers cooked to order and the fries were perfect. Fries are cross-contaminated but are gf otherwise. I still went for it and no regrets! These were huge burgers and so filling! My friend and I were both hungry and thoroughly enjoyed our meals. The wait was about 15 minutes on a Saturday night and it took a while to get our food. Our waitress didn't come back more than once during our entire meal and never checked in on how we liked our food. Other than that we had a pleasant experience. If in town, would come back for another burger!

I paid 12$ for a sandwich with no cheese for my lactose intolerant girlfriend. They put cheese on it. When I returned back to the store for the correct sandwich, they didn't offer me a refund, and threw away the previous sandwich without bothering to ask if I'd like it, despite me waiting 20 minutes for my 30$ order of two sandwiches and an orange juice. I would have loved to eat that sandwich, but they just threw it away in front of me. I will not be getting food here again.

I used to love this place. However on May 23, we ordered 4 salads; all different. During the night I woke with diarrhea. In the AM I asked everyone else who had eaten with me how they felt. Everyone responded that they were sick. Symptoms ranged from diarrhea, vomiting, fever and chills. On May 24, my dogs started having diarrhea. To my horror, I recalled feeding them some of my salad. I reached out to my vet and MD at that point. We were all diagnosed with Salmonella. One of the dogs progressed to bloody diarrhea. Our symptoms continued until Tuesday. Needless to say, we will never step foot in this store again. I also noticed another review stating the same issues on the exact same date. You clearly have issue with food handling that needs to be addressed.

The gluten free red velvet cupcakes that I ordered tasted great, however, half of them were overflowing and very ugly for display. The dozen that were overflowing were placed in the bottom of the bag I was given. I should have looked them over, but I drove 40 minutes to get them. One of our guests also found an egg shell in their cupcake. After paying almost $100 for 2 dozen, I feel the cupcakes should have been close to perfect. I won't use them again.

Over-hyped. Disappointing. Overpriced. Not brunch food. After hearing positive reviews and being recommended to eat brunch here I finally went...and was disappointed. We only waited 20 minutes for a table and were able to have coffee while we waited. Basic latte. Nothing special. Our table outside was perfect to enjoy summer. Careful of sitting on the benches- one collapsed with three adults and a baby on it. No substitutions on the menu, even refused to remove the powdered sugar from the pancakes. I ordered the strawberry rhubarb pancakes- $12. Good flavor. Nothing like a pancake- had stalks of rhubarb with a strawberry sauce. Don't expect to find your typical breakfast food or a meal under $10. Only baked goods are under $10. The place was cute and unique. Family friendly environment but not a children friendly menu. If you have food allergies, don't bother. Water would be the safest option. Definitely overpriced for the quantity and quality of food. Would not recommend this as a brunch spot. Overall very disappointed and will not return. 2 stars for unique spot and friendly staff.

That was the toughest $18 fish sandwich I've ever had. So overcooked that anyone who has ever eaten fish before would be embarrassed to serve it. The fish was chewier than the roll it was served on. My girlfriend ordered a pizza - the crust was barely cooked, and the sauce was way too sweet. neither of us finished our food. Side salad was the typical pre-made stuff - no effort. This was not at a peak time, either - no excuse that the kitchen was overworked. I gave two stars because we didn't get food poisoning, and I don't want to seem to be overreacting. Seem to be relying on their location right across from the beach for business - enough people must wander in to keep them in business, I guess. Our waiter was nice though.

I ordered food to go, took a bit longer than I expected but it was ok for the price I payed for it. Who knows if she had an allergy so the wasn't ok to me.

We chose Square 1682 for the 6th night of Restaurant Week, and I was pleasantly surprised. They called ahead of time to confirm the reservation and ask about any food allergies, which has never happened before, and was much appreciated. There are so many mixed reviews- many with legitimate complaints, and not just people being difficult to please or unrealistic. We had an early reservation, and were seated right away. Although it was fine when we got there, once the restaurant filled up, we realized that the setup is a bit tight, as other diners had a hard time getting through the table to leave or go to the restroom. Our server was Adam, and he was great- attentive and friendly. He had quite a bit of tables that he was taking care of, so we had to wait awhile to get our leftovers boxed up and ask for the check. Also, although they took note of my food allergies, they did not tell our server, so that seemed a bit pointless... We had the cornbread that came with the Restaurant Week menu, and it was delicious. My boyfriend asked for more, and we were charged for it, which was interesting- I've never had a restaurant charge for extra bread, but oh well...We both started with the rigatoni, and I chose the everything salmon for dinner, and the peach cobbler for dessert. My boyfriend chose the jerk chicken and the chocolate cake for dessert. We both had Tito's with Sprite, and found the drinks to be nice and strong. The rigatoni was very nice- the pasta was perfectly cooked, and the pesto was tasty. The salmon was interesting. I don't think I would have ever thought to put everything bagel seasoning on salmon, and I'm not really sure that it works so well. My boyfriend really enjoyed the jerk chicken. Dessert was pretty tasty UNTIL I found a large, hard piece of plastic in my peach cobbler. I didn't eat anymore of it after that, and our server never returned since the bill was paid at that point. My boyfriend enjoyed his chocolate cake.

Got a burger with blue cheese dressing (was supposed to be crumbled blue cheese), got tomato (which I am very allergic to) and no fried onions. The restaurant was not very busy and it was a small to go order. The potato chips were good though Very disappointed and will not be patronizing the establishment again.

A big pet peeve of mine is hair. I ordered a basic Reese's blizzard, and good thing I looked before I dug in. Low and behold, a curly strand of hair was right on top. I was so disgusted. I went back, and they were kind enough to make a new one. After analyzing the top we'll, I started eating and even did a happy dance. Mid was through, another fricking hair! At this point I almost threw up. It's like someone dumped a ton of hair into the Reese's mix. I haven't been back since.
Alright! I downloaded Yelp for this. Nothing like getting hairy cockroach pad Thai! Threw up twice. Not cool.

We really enjoyed our visit to this place! We heard about them from all over and were stoked to try their famous coffee and beignets. The beignets are delectable! Cafe du mond is located in a perfect spot, city park! You can grab coffee and walk, or sit and eat! We did both! Sitting to eat, before strolling around. The coffee is strong, and super tasty! Our one complaint is that there are no dairy free options for coffee. So while the coffee tastes great and the scene is amazing, the coffee definitely upset my stomach afterwards. I would strongly suggest adding nondairy options for those with allergies or sensitivities!

To preface this review, I've been to Bar Louie once before and had a great experience. I went with my mother and sister this weekend. We waited an hour for our food, and I had an allergic reaction to my cocktail. That being said, Bmy the GM and Cole did everything in their power to make it up to us. They were both fantastic, and while we weren't thrilled to be there for as long as we were, they certainly made it up to us and we'll be giving them another try. The food was pretty good, too, and they have a great selection to choose from. All in all, I'd still recommend giving them a chance.

Got half of my refund from Tasha the manager on duty I received a pink quarter pounder wasn't even attempted to be cooked this is a very unsanitary place to eat my 8 year old is now vomiting the burris management team will hear from my attorney this is a pandemic and the manager on duty had no mask on they have no care for their customers health

My stomach hurts so bad, I'm ill Why is there so much Velveeta in the Étouffée Like I get that it's chili cheese Étouffée,,,, but why THAT cheese Bread smacks but it is not worth what it tastes and feels like upon the food's second visit to your mouth,,,, when you inevitably vomit I'm not the only one who can attest to their last Yat's experience due to a bad batch. Seriously, is someone sweating & ashing in to the cauldrons. Do yourself a favor and eat some Cajun food cooked elsewhere in the city ,,,,

My friend & I went to the Starr Diner for dinner. Food was absolutely terrible. Service wasn't much better. Waiter did not come back to check to see if we needed anything.the chicken croquettes, so they say that's what they were, had a seasoning that was definitely a mystery to us both. My friend is sitting at home with a bucket in front of her, and I am hanging close to the porcelain throne. NEVER AGAIN!!! The place wasn't exactly clean either. Praying we don't get food poisoning. Seriously. My advice, take Pepto Bismol prior to eating there if you still plan on going after a lot of these comments.

ambiance is great - just make sure you get an outside table. other than that, this restaurant FELL SHORT. I went there for the ambiance even though I have a seafood allergy. They have other items so I ordered the half chicken plate. What they brought me was reheated chicken. It had that old taste to it. You know that nasty taste chicken can get when it hasn't been seasoned that much and you attempt to reheat it? Well that's what they served me for $20. It was awful so I called it to the attention of the waiter. He said he had never been told that. And I care because?? He then went and reported this insight to the kitchen staff. They ADMITTED TO SERVING OLD CHICKEN. GROSS! For $20 you should know how to cook a bird. The waiter said he was so surprised that I could taste that difference and that no one had ever called this out before. Yes, it was gross old chicken! He then went on to explain that it would be too hard for the restaurant to make the chicken on demand. Hmmm.. well TONS of other restaurants somehow manage to do this. If you can't figure it out, then DON'T PUT IT ON THE MENU. What killed me is that after all of this NOTHING WAS COMPED. NOTHING. NOT MY CHICKEN, NOT MY BEER, NOT A DESSERT. NOTHING AWFUL COOKING AND AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE. TOTALLY LAZY TO JUST RELY OFF OF THE LOCATION TO GET CUSTOMERS AS OPPOSED TO PROVIDING GOOD SERVICE AND FOOD.

I'll start by saying I wanted to impress some out of state family with a good burger in the area of The St Pete Pier. I found Ford's Garage restaurant online and saw that this would be the perfect place. The renovated St Pete Pier was another place we'd been watching and waiting for many years. When I googled the pier I saw Doc Ford's, I incorrectly thought they were one and the same, so this was my fault. That's the only reason I gave 2 stars. Doc Ford's only had one or two burgers, so I zeroed in on their special which was two blackened fish tacos. I'm gluten free, so I was happy to hear they had corn tortillas. The fish was fried, not blackened and the pico/relish was flavorless. I asked for more of the sauce, because I knew I would have to doctor this meal up on my own. Extra sauce could not revive the little bit of fish (never mentioned what type of fish), so the French fries wound up being my lunch. One friend had a pulled pork sandwich and complained that he'd had better tasting pork elsewhere, in Tampa Bay and was disappointed because he'd heard of the Cuban heritage in this area. My other friend had a very small piece of blackened chicken with fries. Although, the fries were good, for the price we'd hoped to have a better meal. This restaurant has a very strong tourist trade, as it's right at the beginning of the pier complex. It was obvious that the waitress knew she would have many more tables, after us and didn't really care if we were happy or not. We will not be going back for another lunch. Too bad, because it's such a pretty area and the Discovery Center is something on bucket list.

I had a bad first experience. At first I was delighted when I thought I found an allergen conscious restaurant. And super friendly staff. Over the phone and in person I was told "everything" was soy free and gluten free". How exciting! I ate there and felt tired the next few days. I went back and It turns out that they are not a soy free restaurant. Soy is actually in everything! EVERYTHING ON THE MENU HAS SOY. Staff were very friendly and helpful, but unfortunately staff was not trained about allergens. Management confirmed everything has soy. I can't eat there again unless I want to just eat a few vegetables. Even then, there's such a strong potential for cross contamination in a restaurant that uses soy as its main oil. Staff had to go around reading all labels even for the vegetables. Many health conscious restaurants have stopped using soy oil. There are better oils for restaurants. Even "Smokey Bones" uses Canola Oil, including in their fryer. This cute little restaurant saves a little on the cost of oil but then they lose all customers with a soy allergy. Yet prices are a bit on the trendy high side. Disappointed! I'll come back if they change from using soy oil.

I am a huge baby with a weak stomach and am continually poisoning myself with gluten and lactose on my lunch breaks at Penn. NO MORE! I am completely obsessed with Goldie. Crispy falafel with a tender interior, a veggie-dense salad free from cross-contamination, and well-made fries with whatever the hell seasoning they offered me. I can't remember what it was called, but get it. Last, but not least, the tahini shake. Holy shit. How do they do it without dairy? How do they make it so addictive? Just, how. HOW.
