It solves the problem of halvah's horribly dry mouthfeel, delivering glorious globs of sweet sesame to my palate with every gulp. I am considering quitting water, as this is clearly the superior beverage. If I die, don't blame Goldie. Blame my stupid brain that loves candy and hates being hydrated.

Doesn't matter what time of day or if I order from door dash, this location always messes up my order. Every time, something is missing, made incorrectly, and just made like a pride of primates put it together. Oh and the food poisoning. If you're looking to get disappointed, eat here.

They were selling expired baby yogurt. I bought a pack of Stonyfield organic yogurt for my 11 month old twins on Dec. 30th. I gave my son some and he didn't seems to care for it, and my daughter gagged on it and threw up. Turns out it expired Dec. 13th! I returned to the store on January 4th to exchange it and went to the dairy case to get the same flavor. They were expired as well. One expired Dec. 17th, another Dec. 13th, and another Nov. 20th! This is food for babies and they're selling it far past its expiration date. I took the three to the front and spoke with a woman named Cassie, who said she was a manager. She refunded the money and apologized but kept making excuses like that it must have been shoved to the back. First off, no it wasn't, and second, THAT DOESN'T MATTER BECAUSE IT IS ON THE SHELF FOR SALE. Then, she told me that it was weird I found them because she personally checked all of them the night before and didn't see anything. Bull. I will never ever shop here again, and encourage other people to avoid it as well. Who knows what else is expired on their shelves?!

This place use to be great but now with their new menu, it has all changed. The chicken is horribly dry and I am pretty positive i got food poisoning. I ate the salmon tacos and that same night, I was extremely ill. I'm very upset they took off some of my favorite foods off the menu. Not only that, but the restrooms are messy with paper on the ground and the cups for water aren't always the cleanest. I wish they were the old cafe. I won't eat here again.

I am originally from San Diego California, we have one back home and I can say that as a Californian I feel offended with this place. I did not have the fries because I am allergic to mayo and when I asked the cashier what the sauce was she couldn't tell. She was extremely rude and responded with attitude with everything I asked her. I also confused the 55c wings for Wednesday instead of Tuesday and I asked nicely and I got a rude ass response. Like they've mentioned before if you can't be friendly and professional you shouldn't work in a food work place. Specially when you have allergies and want to make sure you can enjoy a meal without dying, the cashier made me feel stupid for asking by the way she was looking at me and responding to me. Also food is overpriced and their wings are skinny and tasteless. To each their own but it wasn't my cup of tea, service is huge for me.

I would never recommend this place. Although the cook was entertaining the food was just not it. Upon entering this place it had a very strange smell. Almost like being in a very old building with a moldy smell. It was like a cloud just following you with this smell that it made my stomach very uneasy. They sit me and my spouse down with another party of 4, cool. I order my food then decided I needed to use the bathroom. While using this semi dirty bathroom another walks into the stall next to me and start vomiting. Her friend is telling her "maybe it's just cause you haven't ate today and the food is heavy". In my mind I'm thinking dang I hope she's alright. I go sit down start having the soup, steamed dumplings and the plum wine. The plum wine was gross and asked the waiter he can take it back. He kind of hesitated like I should just drink but no it started making my stomach feel VERY Uneasy. I go to the bathroom cause my stomach is just hurting out of no where. Sure enough now I am vomiting. My spouse is like not feeling it either. The cook did not season none of the food. I couldn't eat the rest of the time because the food was just making me sick every bite I had. I couldn't even eat my leftovers smh.

Save yourself the time, money, and effort and DO NOT go here. Please know there is absolutely no hyperbole when I state the following: It is a TRUE MIRACLE that I didn't get food poising from eating here. The quality of the seafood was incredibly poor. I ordered shrimp and muscles with all of their sauces mixed together. Added corn and potatoes (WHY do you even have to add these? Corn, potatoes (and usually sausage) are staples of authentic seafood boils). Here are the main reasons for my 1 star review. Note, I'd make it 0 stars if that was an option. * Their quality of seafood is awful. At times my shrimp and muscles were SOUR. At first I thought I was picking the "bad ones"but realized that was 80% of the bag. After 10 minutes I nearly threw up and had to throw my $40+ meal away out of fear of getting sick. * The seafood was terribly overcooked. The muscles had the texture of hardened rubber and the shrimp could barely come off the shell and were insanely chewy. Perhaps they overcooked it to death because they knew they were serving days old/ poor quality seafood . * That sauce was AWFUL. Lacked flavor despise being so oddly chunky from the garlic/ginger/whatever else they use. Moral of the story, save yourself the money and possible gastrointestinal issues and don't go here. I'd highly recommend Krab Kingz off Delmar for better quality and slightly cheaper prices. Krab Kingnz still has work to do on their sauces but it's far and away much better than this mess of a hazard.

ABSOLUTE TRASH. I had maybe 6 bites of my lo mein and an hour later I was puking in a strangers front yard. Friends have also reported sanitary issues as well as food poisoning symptoms. I want to give this 0 stars

The woman I spoke to on the phone at Bocconcini was exceedingly helpful and polite when I called to ask if my boyfriend's severe peanut allergy would be an issue. She assured me there are no nuts used at all in the restaurant and we would be good to go. Loved that confident reassurance! We ordered through DoorDash, everything arrived on time, and it was so well-packaged. None of the sauce leaked at all, as they took the extra precaution of wrapping the takeout boxes in tinfoil. Our meals each came with a box of bread knots. However, we were a bit let down by the food itself. The sauce for my Penne Vodka (large portion) was very creamy and tasty enough but it stated on the website that it came with seasonal vegetables but the closest in there were long strips of basil. I also ordered the Meatballs and I really thought the main flavor was plain old beef, with little seasoning. I had one bite and couldn't eat the rest. As for my boyfriend's Chicken Parmesan, I wasn't crazy impressed with the marinara and it really is a thick chicken cutlet so it completely overpowers the breading and the mozzarella. One other note I'll make is that you should ask for a side of Parmesan with your pasta, as I neglected to do that and would've wanted some. Overall, I think this is a good place for protein lovers but not so much for those that are craving really well-seasoned Italian based on my experience.

I just bought some Greenfield smoked pork chops and thank God I read the ingredients before serving to my husband. We were so looking forward to having these for dinner. They have a host of really crappy additives including propylene glycol which my husband is severely allergic to. MSG is in it which I have an allergy to. Several other ingredients I can't even pronounce. I thought greenfield was supposed to be more natural meats? Just wasted $14 dollars and now no dinner. Never again.
I unfortunately got food poisoning from their food. I ordered the steam chicken and broccoli along with the beef on stick. Not sure which one of them caused it.

So we asked my daughter where she wanted to go for her birthday dinner and Hibachi was her first choice. First off, she likes her birthday on the down low, no mariachi bands and sombreros for this kid! We respect that so we weren't there with the intent on it being some over the top evening filled with embarrassing surprises. So I have no idea how Benihana is for birthdays. We love Hibachi but the service and the food were disappointing. We made a reservation and were seated at that time. The restaurant seemed to be laid out well and didn't feel overly crowded. The waitress came and took our order and that was pretty uneventful. Usually, at least when I've been, hibachi is a show, it's exciting and fun and sometimes u even get a little rice thrown at u. Not here. Some tables seemed to be having a better time than ours...I began to wonder I our chef had a terribly tragedy and still came into work. He was lackluster and not really into it I guess u could say. I was glad when it was over because it almost felt awkward to be watching someone just cook our food but at the same time it felt disrespectful to have a conversation during the "show". Anyway, on to the food!. One word...BLAND! No seasoning at all. The rice...fried rice...was bland. The veggies, bland. The steak, bland! And they don't put salt and pepper on the table so unless u wanna use the aggressive palate destroying sauces your just stuck with bland food. Also, if you have an allergy...be careful here, cross contamination is bad and due to it I wasn't feeling too great afterwards despite letting them know I had an allergy and explaining what I could and could not do. I understand that this is an easy place to cross contaminate but I've been to plenty of hibachi places before with ZERO issues. Overall, not a good experience at all. I'll stick to the little hole in the wall hibachi places from now on.

Went here this week Thursday night to meet a friend. We started with 2 borderita without salt. Drinks were good. We had the empanadas with beef which never disappoint. We ordered a chimichanga with sour cream and queso, carne asada and a pick three sampling. The food all looked nice when it came out but it came out cold. There is nothing worse than cold food. Especially when your hungry. The waitress did send manager to table he was very apologetic and did offer to remake food. We opted against it since it took a while to begin with. Customer service was good. The wait staff was spotty since two people were covering entire bar area. Which included maybe 10 tables. 88.00 all in with gratuity. The salsa and chips get a 5 star review but .... maybe they could give salsa to each guest in these uncertain times so no fear of cross contamination.
Recently ordered a shrimp burrito. It was early in the morning. Got bad food poisoning. Buyer beware!

We ordered a birthday cake from here last week for our son's birthday. My husband is seriously gluten intolerant so I was glad to see gluten free options on the menu. We had a dinosaur toy to put on the top and asked for the design to be very simple so there was a lot of room for the dinosaur- just brown land with a blue river going through. When we picked it up it looked very cute- the river ended in a little waterfall down one side, there were candy "rocks" along its edge, and something that appeared to be a sandy beach as well. But when we went to cut the cake, my husband looked more closely at the "sand," which was made from some kind of crumbs. "Do you think those are gluten free?" he asked. "Better cut around them just in case," I said. He was able to avoid them in one narrow slice, but they were scattered across most of the top of the cake. The next day he called the bakery to check before daring to eat more. Sure enough, they were standard graham cracker crumbs, and NOT gluten free. He spoke with a manager who apologized but didn't come across as terribly sympathetic. She offered to send us a credit for the store but couldn't refund us anything directly. We don't live in the area so we had the gift card sent to family. He suggested to her that they make the language on their site more clear that their bakery is gluten "friendly" rather than gluten "free" and to warn customers that cross-contamination is likely; also there clearly needs to be better communication between the bakers and the decorators. She agreed, but again, was rather brusque about it. Same story when we ordered the cake in the first place- the people we spoke to were never terribly friendly. I'm sure working during a pandemic is stressful, but if they're so busy that everyone must be blunt all the time, and are making potentially serious mistakes with things like gluten, perhaps they need to hire a few more employees. But the cake itself was pretty good (not amazing, but good), it was ready on time, and it looked great.

Ah...so much hope, so little delivery. I have waited MONTHS for them to reopen so I could try their "authentic cajun." Today, for Fathers Day, we finally tried them. I knew that my only choice would be crawfish, what's more Cajun than crawfish? I opted for the cajun season and wanted it as hot as possible, having lived in the Gulf Coast, I have really missed real authentic crawfish, heat intense enough to make you question if you're allergic, but flavor so wonderful to push through the heat. Sadly, the crawfish did NOT deliver on either front. Yes they were large, but were previously cooked, then frozen, so tough and with absolutely none of the incredible flavor fresh mudbugs have. Heat, seriously, they call this cajun hot? This was cajunish mild and that was being generous! I?d like to suggest someone from corporate to try my favorite place in the Houston are, Dickenson Seafood, that or any of the Crawdaddys locations in the gulf coast. THAT is what good mudbugs are supposed to taste like. I wonder how many people try craws here, don't care for this sad travesty, and never give them the chance to be the thing of beauty they can be. M wife, she ordered the chicken as she's not a seafood person, she was also disappointed. So the question is, will I return...probably, alone, but never again for frozen crawfish! Look, crawfish must be fresh, live, if they're out of season, don't offer them, simple as that.

Food is always amazing here. I've been here a lot when I lived in the area and not so much now that I've moved a bit more toward the city. The staff themselves is very good at wearing masks and servicing customers under new regulations. However, masks are not enforced for customers. I also work in the food industry not too far from this honeygrow location so I know how difficult it can be to enforce the new mask rules to all of your customers. The only thing aside from some folks entering without masks that I had a slight issue with was the way their takeout containers are stacked. They are stacked so high that they are above the glass panels and are also located directly in front of the ordering stations. Normally I wouldn't care about something like this- but when masks are not enforced and people are ordering in front of these takeout boxes, the only thing I can think about is the contamination. Again, please do not take me wrong I LOVE this honeygrow location. They have the sweetest staff, most fresh food I've had out of all the locations I've tried, as well as a very clean service floor. I won't be leaving them any time soon!! Love this location the mostest!

We stopped in at Tryst Gastropub for a quick dinner before our show. Dinner honestly left a lot to be desired. It was only 7pm and they had already run out of chicken and that was the one gluten free entree on the menu that I wanted. So, I just ended up having a salad because I did not want pasta or the fish of the day. The salad was so not all that great. The fried chickpeas had to be removed so it would be completely free of gluten. The chopped carrots were soft and not crisp. And it came with cucumbers (no cheese) and lettuce. It was supposed to have bacon on it and honestly it looked like less than half a slice of bacon which was a rip off. The salad was 12$. My salad basically cost as much as each of the two meat dishes my husband ordered and my salad didn't even contain a full slice of bacon... Everything else was my husbands food which contains gluten. He is a lot easier ro please since he has no dietary restrictions and was pleased with the wagyu steak kabobs and his fried chicken. I did not even order a drink because a lot of them contained flavored vodka (which is more likely to not be gluten free) or was made with stuff I don't drink (whiskey, Gin, Boubon etc). Qhile the restaurant was nice, they had nice decor, the location is good because it's right next to Flute and Dram and you can listen to their live jazz. We wont be returning just because the menu is kind of limited for me (gluten free options). But we did have a nice time and only spent around 50$ and parked eight out front so everything was super easy.
Although the food was good and the setting was nice. I got food poisoning after eating either the chili cheese fries or the Tavern burger.

No vegan options. Super disappointed because one of my friends just went there a few days ago and they told her that her food was vegan. Went today to check it out and turns out someone lied to her. Not only is it dangerous (people have food allergies) it is also unethical to lie about what you are serving people.

I called for a curb side pickup and the manager was INCREDIBLY rude. She acted like it was an inconvenience that I was calling. It's unfortunate because I enjoy their gluten free cupcakes and like to support local business. This transaction was so bad that I will not be returning.

I ordered a Gluten free cheese steak. I specifically asked if the roll was going to be grilled or warmed up bc I preferred it that way but it wasn't. They did do a good job of cleaning the grill and making sure to use a gluten free knife however, they layed the slices of cheese directly onto a contaminated surface. I don't frequent maybe Deli's so I don't have much to compare to , but prices seem to be high.

Food was ok. I had the Chicken Pad Thai and asked for no peanuts. Good thing I don't have peanut allergies because BAM, micro pieces of peanuts at the bottom hiding under the food. The fried rice was an extra 2.50 if you want it with the PT otherwise it is only $1 with the other lunch items. Not sure if I will be back but if I do i am going to avoid the fried rice since it is light skinned and does not remind me at all if Chinese food. Ok ok I know it's a Thai joint and it's not really fried rice, but they shouldn't call it fried rice lol. I will say the lunch amount you get is not bad for the price, so they have that going for them.

Got take out breakfast from this spot today. I ordered the gluten free breakfast sandwich. I took one bite of my sandwich and it was so dry I could barely swallow it. The eggs were overdone and there wasn't any sauce or condiments on the sandwich so it was like eating stale bread. I ended up just eating the one piece of bacon out of the sandwich and the potatoes instead. If you're ordering something other than the breakfast sandwich it may be worth stopping here but overall there are better breakfast spots in Boise!

Warm and welcoming, positive vibes, adorable health-conscious restaurant tucked away in Ozona. I ordered the Loco Moco - bowl of brown rice, buffalo patty, grilled onions, brown gluten free gravy, on a bed of spinach. Typically comes with a fried egg on top but I requested without. I found it to be very bland, absolutely no seasoning in anything (perhaps the egg would have given it some flavor?). The soup of the day was lime coconut which was a hearty bowl of carrots, zucchini, and chick peas with shredded coconut mixed in. I did not taste a hint of lime and I guess I was thinking it was going to be a thai coconut milk type soup (which would not have been healthy). The BF ordered the Vegan Falafel Wrap - a huge burrito shell filled with tons (maybe 3-4 cups?) of spinach, tomatoes, onion slices, and a thin patty of baked falafel, with a side of Lebanese sauce (a tahini lime mix). Not your typical falafel sandwich - the ratio of spinach to falafel was 10:1 and I missed the crispiness of a typical fried falafel ball vs. mushy healthy baked version. Accompanied by a wonderful coleslaw with sliced almonds and cranberries (delicious!) and Veggie Straws (like the processed kind of out of a bag - found these a super odd choice for such a 'clean' food restaurant). For dessert we tried the red velvet cupcake and popover with macadamia sauce - both were amazing, especially for vegan desserts. Want to love this place because it's amazing conceptually and the owner is so sweet. I love that they offer healthy organic vegan options. I think it's a little too healthy for my palate and perhaps I am addicted to sodium? ;)

I have order from here a few times and they were all great except this last time. On Friday the 20th I ordered a large cheese pizza to bring home with my wife and 1 year old baby. Once I got home we ate, my wife and I both noticed it tasted sort of like soapy or sour. Later in around 9 pm my daughter starts committing uncontrollably for about an hour. We though maybe she's still not use to pizza no big deal. Saturday morning my wife wakes up and she's not feeling good, so I went out and got her coffee and a pastry. She's not feeling good then starts vomiting like crazy. Around 2 pm I start feeling unwell. We both were vomiting and had the worse diarrhea for 4 days straight. Couldn't even go to work until Wednesday and after doctors checked for COVID. After work on Wednesday I talked to the manager a short heavy set women. While talking to this individual the entire time she a smirk on her face a she seem to be enjoying my story! Never in my life had I ever been this sick from any restaurant. STAY AWAY FROM HERE!!!!

Ok so let me start off by saying I've only been to a few of these and they've never let me down before food was always good. I prefer IHOP but sometimes IHOP is to far so I have to settle lol. Any who this morning I ordered a omelet with bacon ham and jalapeños in it. I received a omelet full of sliced pickles. I couldn't believe my eyes so I immediately asked the waitress to ask the cook was he high on meth? She apologized and said he was new he can remake it . Came back 30 minutes later after I'm sitting there dying of starvation and said he put pickles in it again ............... by now I'm fucking mad I told her screw the omelet make me a BLT who fucks up that ? Them! I threw up all over the bathroom the BLT was disgusting. Will not be returning to any Waffle House ever again ! Wish I could give them a negative star

I wanted this to be a good review. I really did. I ordered twice in the last week. I received everything, as ordered, and it was well packaged. It's a bit annoying when the plastic lid sticks to the top of the bigger sushi rolls. The delicious sauces and toppings stick to the lid and are removed when you lift the lid off. It's a world-wide sushi take out hazard. My first order was two rolls and a Tom Yum Soup. The rolls were average, but the one that touted "seared tuna," was not appetizing. The tuna on top of the roll was heated (not seared) and kind of grey-white. It didn't taste bad, but it looked awful. The soup was dreadful. It was bland and a weird color. The veggies and shrimp inside were fresh and delicious. The first run wasn't so bad that I didn't want to try again. My second order was three rolls and Tom Kai Soup. The rolls were not awesome. They were not rolled well and were falling apart. This might have been due to the number of pieces crammed into a small box and the sticky rice becoming one in transit. It tasted okay, but was a bit of a mess. The nori was dark and very flaky, which indicates good product. The Tom Kai soup was even more terrible than I could have expected. It wasn't white and creamy, like I expected. Also, it tasted like vomit. I know that's a really awful thing to say and I know it wasn't vomit, but it tasted and smelled reminiscent of vomit. I couldn't even. This joint is off the list.

Great music and a place for drinks and music. Will not eat here again. Ordered the nachos they threw a whole chicken filet on the top of the nachos. It was like dark brown/black in color. The waitress was appalled herself and did take it off our bill. Asked for a vegan patty on a regular burger bun. It came out with a gluten free bun, my side of pickles never came out. Have been at our table 2.5 hours still haven't gotten receipts. Waitress was very kind but not good with checking on our table or in a timely manner. Kept disappearing.

In our search for Korean food in the Tampa We Came here today for lunch after our beach day Arrived as they opened at noon We were the only ones here The server was nice but was talking to us from the other side of the bar a lot so had call out our orders to him For starters we got fries and fried pork belly The seasoning on the fries were a bit much for me but Hubz and baby loved it The pork belly was great just a tad bit greasy for my liking The sauce they give with it is awesome, kept dipping my fries into it Entree I got the bap bowl with beef bulgogi and asked to made spicy, loved it The K pop (fried boneless chicken) soy garlic were kind of similar to the pork belly both had the same flavors We couldn't get the spicy flavor because it has crushed peanuts and I have an allergy (which I didn't get because if it's fried fresh and tossed in the sauce then they should be able to opt the crushed peanuts right?!) Here is what made me give them 3 stars We had left overs Especially the fries and I asked the server if we can get the sauce that was served with the pork belly on the side to go He asked if I wanted one or two I said two would be great thanks He walks over with the sauce n swaps out our check! They CHARGED us for the sauce! Why didn't you mention that?! And why would you charge for it? If I took the pork belly home it came with the sauce, I was just upset by that! Inform your customer please Overall not bad but we weren't wowed! Will not be coming back

If you know me at all, you know I avoid chain restaurants like the plague. The risk for gluten cross-contamination is always way too high, and chain Italian restaurants? Forget about it. I was recently invited to attend a Yelp Elite Event at Carrabba's of Metairie. The staff was so wonderful and there were plenty of gluten free items on the menu for me to try. About two weeks later, I returned to Carrabba's of Metairie with my fiancé (who probably hasn't been able to eat in an Italian restaurant since we started dating). The wait staff remembered me (and my gluten allergy) and made sure that I was well taken care of. The menu had plenty of gluten free options and a wonderful deal called "That's Amore Monday." I had prosciutto wrapped asparagus (which was a switch made to accommodate my allergy), minestrone, and prosciutto wrapped pork for an amazing deal. Zach had a steak covered in butter sauce with some house wine and a side of asparagus. The portions were perfect and our waitress was so sweet. I look forward coming back with my future mother-in-law (also gluten free) so we can feast on some gluten free pasta and taste some other pieces of the menu.

FOOD ALLERGIC CUSTOMERS NOT SAFE HERE. Tonight we stopped in at this Olive Garden location because it was nearby when we had finished errands and we knew there was a gluten sensitive menu. Though I ordered from the gluten sensitive menu, I received a meal hat I realized a few bites in was absolutely a regular gluten-containing meal. I was sick before even leaving the restaurant but our ticket was only partially reduced, as our drinks were still billed at full price. Because we had to move quickly as I was getting sicker by the minute, we did not dispute this. However, I will now require a full course of prescription steroids to mitigate the effects of a kitchen SNAFU. Do not try to eat here if you have a food allergy or sensitivity- the risks are too high for a place that is ill informed as to the outcomes of food allergies in customers.

This is the most awful place I have been to in Reno! The pizza was so undercooked and the only staff member working was a complete a**hole she was so rude and had the nastiest attitude! Her attitude and that gross ass pizza went together perfectly! I 10/10 do not recommend you spent your money here, and to too it all of my husband got food poisoning! I never leave reviews it I need to warn people how awful this place is!!

I've visited many Pho places around town and outside of the state so I will just give the facts. Environment: There is no Vietnamese decor or music. Someone commented it looked like the inside of a cafeteria style restaurant. Also, musicwise I think I heard Whitney Houston 3 times while dining. Those multi bulb light fixtures are too bright making it hard to read the reflective laminated menu. Food: 1. Vietnamese coffee was brought pre mixed and did not have enough condensed milk was a hot chocolate color. It was good and strong but not what I'm accustomed to based on prior experience for the coffee. (My opinion) 2. I ordered Pho Ga (chicken) the menu clearly states is made with beef broth (as it should be) but when I inquire as to why mine was so clear.... I was told it was made with chicken broth not beef. I stared in disbelief that you would not have that on the menu or tell a client when ordering. 3. I asked for veggies and was advised the only options would broccoli and onions. No mushrooms, carrots, bok choy etc were available. Price: The small bowl is slightly smaller than the size at other locations and it's a little over $1.25 more.(compare with Pho Viet, Saigon Bay as examples) If you are new to Vietnamese cuisine you may differ in opinion but if you compare to other locations in the area they still have room to grow. I don't know that I'll be back soon as I'm very disappointed in the deviation from the menu as listed. It should be a big no no as changing the recipe of an item as listed changes both the authenticity of the food and not telling a client of the change which can affect flavor. Another big thing is that you changed something and didn't even consider I may have an allergy and many other things. (Yes....it was only the broth but I prefer how the beef broth salts up the bland chicken. So in my opinion the soup was just....OK and bland. But again I graded strictly that they changed what I ordered by changing the broth and not letting me know)

Update: on top of everything being short-dated or even expired, the "service" here is nearly non-existent and ALWAYS ALWAYS double check your receipt, as items do not ring up correctly! I picked up what seemed like a great deal on a gluten free Amy's organic pizza- $2 and change. However, when looking at the receipt, the store charged me $8.99, complete rip off. I walked back into the store, allowing $50 worth of other foods (many of them frozen) to sit inside the car on a roasting August afternoon. Inside I was "greeted" (if you count ignoring me and then telling me to hold on because you're "waiting on a phone call") by Danielle at the service counter. Already long story too short: they did fully refund my money and let me keep the item they overcharged me by over 200% for. It just took me showing where the item was (and being condescended to for not knowing the full layout of the store) and waiting again while Danielle finished her phone call, with some other manager type standing around giving no f's. I'll add that I've tried reaching out to the store in the past and have gotten no return calls or emails. So that shows you how much they care... go at your own risk. It's not like I'll stop going here, as it's a 2 minute drive from home. However, the store is pretty awful: -sky high prices on many goods ($6 for 20 ziplock bags or a jar of peanut butter) -the "customer service" is non-existent (you'll probably bag items yourself at check-out) -check your receipt, as items may be rung up incorrectly/prices on the shelf may be off (I got bagel bites marked at $7.99, came home and saw they charged me $9.99, wasn't gonna go back and waste an hour for $2) -check expiration dates, as I encountered several items I wanted that ended up being expired, one by several months -they were completely out of rotisserie chickens and we were unapologeticalquoted a 1.5 hour wait for one to be ready. Sure, I'll wait! -the place can be a zoo and the parking lot can be awful, but we are almost in central NJ, it happens. I wish the place were better, but for where I live, it's the most convenient by far. Extra star for the fact that a pet supply store and Starbucks is also in the plaza, as is a UPS store.

Holy Food Poisoning !! Last night around 8pm, my family and I ordered food to-go (Chicken Cobb salads and wraps) and by 1/2AM not one but ALL THREE of us were running to the bathroom vomiting and had explosive diarrhea (cute, right ??)... This was our second attempt eating here, the first was during bingo and that experience left much to be desired, but, we figured we would give these guys another shot... Well, lesson learned. Never. Again..

Let just start by saying that I started bar tending at 21 and have now been working in the hospitality industry for about 2 years now (10 years total in customer service) this place is seriously lacking service. As a bartender you should be bonding with your guests and laughing/smiling etc. I did not get that vibe here. I got the bourbon steak sandwich it was phenomenal but wouldn't go back for the life of me due to poor service. My boyfriend wanted the buffalo chicken sandwich with out onions and the bartender said and I quote " I'm sorry we don't alter our recipes, we've got Chef Ramsey back there" had he been allergic to onions I would have made a big deal but in this case he just didn't like the taste so I let it go. Thought the whole thing was just weird and unprofessional. I was expecting it to be more like Paddy's Pub.. Way too expensive and no service at all....

I had high hopes for this place because my family loves their sister restaurant. But the food and the service were terrible. I'm giving one star for the ambiance. We sat on the patio and it was lovely. The second star for the server offering us separate checks which was nice and made it easy to split. I ordered the kobe bacon burger medium on a gluten free bun, and asked for it to be toasted, with fries. The burger came out medium well at best, the bun was not toasted, it was completely dry, no house made ketchup, no crispy onions, the fries were soggy, and the burger was not seasoned well, kinda bland. I realize that either the server or the chef left off the crispy onions thinking I wouldn't want them because they are probably not gluten free but nobody asked me and I did want them. Our server checked on us 3 times while we waited for our food, which took a pretty long time. I don't know how long it was because I was engaged in conversation, but it was much longer than it should have been. I saw a table next to us come after we did and were served much quicker. My guess is our server forgot to put our order in. When our food finally arrived, I asked for a side of aioli right away, as did my friend, it never came, and our server didn't come check on us once after our food came out until we were done. So, bland, dry burger, soggy bun, soggy fries, terrible service. Oh and we had to ask for silverware, the server brought a handful of forks and just held them over the table waiting for one of us to grab them, no knives, no napkins, so we had to ask for those too. Lastly, the bathroom was dirty and smelly. It is obvious that it is not cleaned daily. I'm sure they have better menu items, better servers, and better cooks than I experienced based on several good reviews I've read, but it was too bad to ever return.

This place was a total bust. First off, I have celiac disease and require a gluten-free diet. I asked for a gluten-free menu and explained my allergy and was automatically concerned when the menu said "gluten-sensitive" instead of free. I opted to order a salad just to stay safe. They brought me a salad... WITH CROUTONS. I was so upset. I made it very clear what I needed to avoid and was completely ignored. I should also add that our food took TWO HOURS to arrive. I was with a party of people and we were missing items and waited forever for the meals. My other party members said that their fish was salty and the rice/potatoes weren't cooked all the way. My family and I make NOLA trips every few years, and Landry's will NOT be on our list to return.

I don't believe I am unique in saying I am one of a few looking for that great pizza in this area. I have been searching for that one pizzeria or restaurant that will satisfy my craving. A friend asked me have you tried Sizzle Pie on Center Street? That prompted me to find an excuse to go try it. It was a cold wet late afternoon. I noticed how cold the place was, with really dark walls. They serve New York-style pizza, the one with a thin crust. The place has a menu with a lot options on the menu including different sauces, pizza combos, or you can make your own. They have other goodies: garlic knots, salads, gluten-free pizzas, seasonal pizzas, a full bar, and just about everything and then some you would expect a pizzeria to have. My wife and I ordered a large salami, red onion, and mushroom pizza and 2 soft drinks. We made our way away from the doors looking for a warm spot, which did not exist but not as cold as by the front door. We had our pizza in about 15-18 min. A large 18" inch diameter pie. It was very hot when it was delivered to our table. The pizza consisted of 8 oversized slices and the aroma was intoxicating, to say the least. I served myself a slice and I saw the salami on my pizza, it was practically the same color as it was when it was placed on the pizza, not a good sign. The mushrooms look very undercooked to me as well (more like warm mushrooms). The first bite was very hot and I noticed that the sauce and the crust were teasing my senses. Both are excellent but do not make up for the undercooked ingredients. With all due respects to all places that make pizza in this area, the sauce at Sizzle Pie is hard to beat and let's not forget they have several types of red sauces to choose from. Likewise, my senses were telling me that the crust was also excellent and is one of the best in this area. It was somewhat disappointing that the red chili flakes at the table had no heat to them. So what is the point of having chili flakes that are not one bit hot? You have to bus your own dishes as you do in a lot of fast food places. I was disappointed that no one came by to see how we were doing or needed anything. There are no waiter or waitresses, just counter service. The place can be a little tidier and cleaner and can certainly use some heat. Our pizza was lukewarm by the time I served myself a second slice. A "thank you" as you leave or something similar would be nice as you leave. So much potential and improvement on minor details that will make a huge difference in the way the public perceives the establishment. $36.00 for a large 3 ingredient combination pizza and 2 soft drinks.

3.5/5 stars. I really want this place to do well. The man who owns this place is incredibly friendly and makes all the ice cream at the shop. We went during the summer where you would expect ice cream to be relatively higher in demand, but because business was slow, this shop was somewhat limited in flavors. I ordered mint chocolate chip and got... exactly that. As far as ice cream goes, it was decent, and nice knowing it was all handmade, but somewhat lacking compared to some of its competitors. Again, I'll emphasize that I really want this place to do well to support local businesses, but feel that it will need to take some additional steps to appeal to the passerby and obtain loyal customers. Price is fair, staff is friendly, food is fair. Please note that there are no dairy alternatives for the lactose intolerant, at least as of the time of my visit.

They need to seriously re-work their menu. The dishes are greasy and over fried. Little options for allergies or diet limitations. The food was a supreme let down. As well, they charge around $30 for some meals and you can buy 1.5kg of shrimp for that cost and yet their portions are very small for what you are paying for. Their fish was poorly cooked flat,blan, and greasy. Their fries where undercooked and floppy. Overall nothing like their counterpart in the south. If I was Forrest I would run

We ordered from this company via Uber Eats- I love giving both good and marginal reviews on food. We just got home from Mexico- maybe this was our issue! Craving a good taco, we ordered 5 tacos. two of the five tasted like literal dog food. My husband almost literally threw up. Not sure what was off that night... Or if this is normal... Our first time at the restaurant or eating at the restaurant I should say definitely will not return... Taco should be simple and tasty and nothing more

When you're on a time crunch, the last thing you need is a slow moving line in a fast food drive-through. As we inched through this particular Steak 'n Shake, we all immediately regretted our decision on choosing this place. Due to being squeezed between two other vehicles, we weren't going anywhere anytime soon. Finally we got to the speaker so we could order our food. We gave our order - twice - knowing that they'd probably end up getting it wrong. For my order, I distinctly told them "no cheese" for my sandwich. Simple request. No cheese. Said it twice. So we get to the window and grab our food and drive off. Because of our time crunch, we couldn't sit at the restaurant and go over our food to make sure it was correct. As we're driving down the road and opening up our sandwiches, none of it was right. What was on my hamburger? Cheese. Dear heavens, people. My friend's sandwich? It wasn't what she ordered? Napkins? Of course not. My other friend that happened to order a "steak frank" (ha - we laughed about this order for awhile) - well, it was covered in ketchup and mustard. I tell you what - I am usually a fan of Steak 'n Shake. What is up with this place? So disappointing. Get your stuff together. And when someone doesn't want cheese, don't friggin' give them cheese. I'm lactose intolerant darn it.

I make it a habit to visit gluten free bakeries and cafes when in different cities, and stopped by New Deal when driving through. I really wanted to like it because I appreciate fully gluten free restaurants. Here's what I tried: French toast - Good! Nothing spectacular, but it was fluffy. Sausages - average Biscuit - it was not very biscuit-y, more like a dinner roll in a biscuit shape. I would not order it again. (I've had gluten free biscuits at other places that are amazing - flaky and you would never know they were gluten free because they are so amazing.) Brookie - Good, but nothing spectacular. I wouldn't drive out of my way to eat here again, but it's a good option if you're local.

This place is disgusting. I received moldy bacon and when I returned it they gave me "fresh" bacon but the new bacon looks like it has mold on it too. Don't go here if you want to risk getting food poison. I had food poison before from a breakfast restaurant and it's not fun. Look at your food before you eat from here.

Myself and 8 others went here last night and had a horrible experience. 3 of our meals were grossly undercooked. After leaving, 3 people had food poisoning. We called to speak to management about this food safety issue which resulted in him accusing us of eating bad food after "his restaurant" because they could not possibly have this issue. Will not be going back there...

My family had dinner at Muriel's Jackson Square on Saturday, June 8, 2019. Both my wife and my daughter have celiacs disease (gluten intolerance) so it isn't easy to go out to dinner. My wife in particular is VERY sensitive and she will be out of commission for 24 hours if she gets contaminated. We made a reservation through OpenTable, and the morning of our reservation we received a call from Muriel's to confirm the time of our reservation. She also wanted to let us know that although Muriel's strives to provide gluten free food, they do not guarantee that there will be no cross contamination. We decided to go ahead and eat and we were very happy to do so! Both my wife and daughter ordered the gluten-free shrimp and grits. I ordered the scallops and my oldest daughter ordered the ala Carte chicken (Cajun Demi-Poulet). Everything was delicious. My wife and daughter had no problems with their gluten free food. We had a wonderful waitress and the servers were also very helpful. This is a very nice restaurant and the food was fantastic.

I really wanted to like this place, but I need to give a bad review because my brother and I got sick. We were on the way home from a 2 week road trip and found this place, ignored Yelp's health rating of 41/100 and went in. We ordered fish taco platter and carne asada platter. They were good portion and looked good. The chef had no gloves on and she grabbed red plastic cups and scopped ice right out of the chest. I was a bit weary of that but didnt think much of it. After we had the food, my brother started to have diahrrhea about 10 minutes after he had the food. My sromach wasnt ferling well but the womens bathroom was dirty with sink clogged smelling like someone threw up so we left. We pulled over in less than 30 min at the outletmall where I too had a diarrhea and threw up. We had an 8 hour drive home and we had to pull over 3 more times to deal with our sickness. Looking back, the food was served in room temperature which could have been sitting like that for hours.

Friday night,none of us felt like cooking. Wife suggested the Mexican place next to wawa she drove by. Walked in and saw 2 families only here. Should have ran away then but I'm pretty willing to try anything once. So it's three of us,wife orders beef and chicken fajitas..instead of pico,regular tomatoes. Daughter orders fajitas ..no sour cream. Me? I'm easy..nothing special.steak fajitas. Not going to even mention when wife simply asks..do you have unsweetened ice tea? Waitress rolls her eyes and waves towards the machines and says..what's there is all,wife didn't bring her glasses..so just says nothing to drink. Fast forward ten minutes.. Food arrives... Instead of steak and chicken...wife has steak and shrimp,she's allergic to seafood...wonderfull... Big pile of pico.. Daughters plate full o sour cream.. O for two... Wife's dinner finally comes out finally.. Five tortillas fir three people? Really? The food really was decent but I can honestly say the service was the worst I've had worldwide,which really is ashame. Won't return

I went to Bailey's Range last week for the first time. It is in a fun location in downtown Saint Louis and they do have a lot to park in (does cost) or off-street parking. The burgers were very dry and definitely could have been better for a place specializing in burgers. Two people in our group were gluten-free and I would like to thank Baileys' Range for having plenty of gluten-free options including buns and fries. Although it was one of the worst gluten-free buns I have ever seen, it fell apart immediately. The shakes and ice cream were by far the best part of the night. I would go back for dessert in a heartbeat. It was very smooth and you received a lot for the price. Although there were problems, I would go back again before taking this place off of my list.

If I can give 0 stars I would. Don't judge me because I couldn't find a way to add a review from the years before. I really don't know how management is now but in 2018 my wife and I ate here for a DATE and left with food poisoning reflecting towards their NOT FULLY COOKED meat and cold food. I spoke to the manager and all they did was offer a refund. I accepted the refund yes only because after they gave me my meal again (trying to make it "better") it was still cold, had hair in it and someone literally spit in my food. I'm glad I don't eat here no more.

This place was a huge disappointment. It was quite an unwelcoming atmosphere and I swear on my life I am keeping my Manayunk/Roxborough businesses to other places that are not only more welcoming, but also just as good, it not better. MF and I walk in with Checkers, a caged small mammal. We're by the door picking out a flavor for the three of us. So we've decided that Florida key lime was the only one that looked appealing. Well, the manager approaches us and the very first question she asks was, "Is that a cat in there?" So we're standing there thinking to ourselves, "Oh, is she severely allergic to cats?" Well, it wasn't a cat. I don't know if that's a good or bad thing. If it were a cat, would we have been able to get a bloody key lime cupcake to go without having to be booted out to their stoop? 1. She says it's the Philadelphia Health Department policy. Fair enough, BUT then why did it matter if it was a cat or not? It sure as hell was not a service animal. If the first thing she said was, "I apologize, but we don't allow animals," this place would be okay in my book. Nope, she wanted to know the species first. So what pissed me off was the way she framed it. She had a discriminatory tone. That was the deal breaker. 2. She says we can wait outside (in the rain) and she'll bring the stuff out to us. What is this, Lady and the Tramp? A caged small mammal at outside seating is more sanitary than a dog sitting there with a leash, who is still free to defecate and urinate on the restaurant sidewalk. 3. We went to two other food places prior and ordered stuff to go, and no one else had an issue. I understand that there are federal regulations one must be in compliance with. It's the way I was approached. I felt like my baby was bullied.
Came here for vegan pizza, the pizza was OK nothing special. Wasn't the BEST. I'd visit again if i have no other options. They have regular, vegan & gluten free options.

HORRIBLE! Whoever created this nauseating concoction must have been clinically insane, and lacking functioning taste buds. This garbage is like barf in a box. And speaking of barf, the next time I vomit this stuff up I don't even think the dog will want to lick it up off the floor. The runny, provel cheese is the worst part of the pizza. The sandwiches are pretty abyssmal as well. The square beyond despair takes disgusting to a whole new level. I'm truly outraged at the pizza situation in St. Louis. The fact that Imo's is terrible is clearly shown in the fact that everyone outside of St. Louis realizes that Imo's sucks.

Went here today for breakfast. My daughter and I had the cream chip beef. Not long after we left we started not to feel good! I had to stop somewhere down the road to use the bathroom ASAP! My daughter started not to feel good not long after we pulled away. We have been sick all day. My daughter is now throwing up and showing all signs of food poisoning! We will never eat here again! So thankful we each only ate half of our meal or we would be a lot worse! This is the only thing we both ate today!

Ordered curbside takeout. I called in the order to ensure items were gluten free and specifically said "no bread". Guess what was in my order? Bread! I ordered a Filet and it was the worst steak I've ever eaten. Very, very tough. On a positive note, the loaded potato was very good. Very disappointed!

WARNING: If you are expecting a Michelin Star restaurant experience, think again. This place is a complete gimmicky joke, which takes advantage of people who are not very knowledgeable about the food industry or fine dining. A few days ago I ordered a risotto with mushrooms (misleading title in the menu and just a plain butter-parmesan risotto with three almost raw mushrooms on top) which came out significantly undercooked and gave me the worst food poisoning of my life for several days. This dish was so bad, that it had me throwing up all night long. They could seriously kill somebody if they are not careful. At the same time, during our dining experience we observed how one of the line chefs in the kitchen dropped a towel in the floor, picked it up and started cleaning his station with the same dirty towel. The service was great, however the food and quality did not even come close to matching the service. We called this restaurant to notify them about our incident and they dismissed us without any follow up calls back. Pretentious, unsanitary and soul-less sad excuse of Italian cooking masquerading as a high end restaurant. Try this place at your own risk.

Underwhelming. Don't make this your first choice in the area. There are a lot of other places to enjoy breakfast. Didn't have black teas, gluten free or vegan food options. Service is slooooow. They were out of so many food and beverage options , we drove 45 mins to this cafe because we love an organic option , and we called twice to make sure they were open and had GF options first but they never picked up the phone We are local in Tampa and won't recommend this

The food here was a little average. There was one dish that was very good (honey chicken) but there were some problems with almost every other dish that I tried. The rice in the sushi was dry, as it had been sitting out for some time, making parts of pieces entirely inedible. Which is important--because this place has signs up saying they'll charge by the pound for uneaten food (even if it is dry rice that no one should be forced to choke down). The sesame chicken could have been okay but I got several tough, dry pieces. This seemed to be the case for most of the chicken dishes--a few good pieces within several bad pieces. I did appreciate that some of the dishes were heavy on the veggies. There was one pork dish that had lots of green peppers and onions. It was a little cold though, and should have been served warmer. I wasn't that concerned about the food temp, but others were. Here is what bothered me the most about the experience though: They have buffet monitors wearing all orange that watch every move you make. At one point I had put some hot and sour soup into one of their soup cups. No big deal. I walked over to the cheese wanton area and picked two up and placed them into the soup. It is something I like. One of the workers came right up behind me, stood up on her toes, and then looked over my shoulder to see what I was doing. Keep in mind--I had done nothing crazy here. Was not contaminating food. Was just making a rendition of a dish. I found it extremely rude to get into my space and look over my shoulder. I said, "Is everything ok?" when I turned around. She didn't say anything to me, just waved a hand and then walked off. So I'm not entirely sure what the exchange here was, but it made me uncomfortable. I suppose I could see them checking on dishes, but they're actually very carefully watching every move you make. I was not a fan of this encounter either so I may not come back here. U-Like and other buffets are not as obnoxious to guests. Service, poor. Had drinks refilled once but had to wait about 15 minutes and had to flag someone down to get the refills.

Not allergy friendly. Manager lacks basic knowledge of serving customer with an allergy. Since the restaurant was crowded, we dined in the bar area. Bartendress who waited on us was excellent. She, however, turned us over to a young man, who we found out later was the manager, to handle our food order. His service and response to my query/needs were extremely poor. Based on this experience, my friend and I decided that we would not be gathering for dinner with others at Brio's the following week. We will go to a more allergy friendly restaurant, like Maggiano's. Food, however, is very good and reasonably priced.

I needed a birthday cake for someone with celiac disease, the REAL disease, not some fad diet bullshit for closet-eaters justification to think they are eating properly. If he ate wheat or gluten or foods contaminated with such, he would definitely have serious gastro-pain along with getting sick. So, I had to be careful, do my due diligence with searches and reading reviews and came up with this total savior and gem in Chalfont. The layered custom cake, one layer chocolate and one layer yellow, with chocolate buttercream icing was to die for (no pun intended). It was fabulous, perfect, moist but firm. I left the decoration ideas to the baker's choice, and I was totally thrilled and excited when the box was opened. I also bought some other treats to try. Here's a quick summary: Crumb cake - 5 stars Fruit and chocolate filled Kiffles - 5 stars Pumpkin muffin - muffin itself 5 stars, icing too sweet 4 stars Lemon Pound cake - quite tart and lemony, but not crazy about the lemon glaze on top - 4 stars Cream cheese brownie - 3 stars, again the icing was too sweet for me but a solid, but dry brownie The custom layered cake was as good as, if not better than, any regular bakery cake I've had in the last 20 years. No lie!

I go here solely because I am gluten free and they sell gluten free pizza. I typically have a good experience, but it really depends on the server. If you get a friendly server, it will be a great experience, but some of their staff look miserable and like they'd rather be elsewhere. My chief complaint is the time I was given a regular pizza after I ordered a gluten free one. I ate half of it before the waiter realized his mistake. I am very sensitive with my Celiac's and it made me sick for weeks. The management was apologetic and gave me giftcards, but I still hope this never happens to anyone else. Always double check! Their gluten free crust is really good and the topping choices are endless. Their hot wings are also gluten free and they have great gluten free cookies. Overall, I like the restaurant chain but do not frequent this location as often as I once did.

After the devastating discovery that our favorite local bagel shop (Bagel Junction) had closed (we drove up and it was empty), we drove over to what we thought was still Manhattan Bagel, only to find Newtown Bagel Company in its place. Still bummed about the disappearance of Bagel Junction, we decided to try it out. We found a pretty decent selection of bagels, cream cheeses and sandwiches. The workers were friendly and service was quick. The flavored coffee that I have was pretty good. However, the bagels --- if you would call them that --- it may sound a little harsh, but they tasted like plain old BREAD, if that makes sense. They were not bagels by our standards. Small, round discs of dough with a small sprinkle of "everything" bagel seasoning. A good bagel will typically fill me up for breakfast and sometimes through lunch. We were still hungry when we left. Newtown needs a good bagel place again. I won't come back here unless I have to. If you want good bagels, try Bagel Train in Yardley or RJ's in Morrisville. It is worth the short drive. However, I have a family member who is gluten free, so I did encourage her to try out the GF bagels they sell here.

Scullys, was mediocre at best. The best thing about this place was the view. The food at a very hefty touristy price left you wanting and wishing you went to the pizza place along the way for a good slice and a cold beer. I am allergic to shellfish so I did not order any seafood. My friends and I all ordered from shellfish to pasta dishes and none of us were like, "This is so good!" We all ordered drinks and they did not come out as explained on the menu. I ordered a beer just a domestic and it was warm. Nothing bothers me more than when your in a warm climate and they serve you a warm beer. For dinner I ordered the chicken marsala and it was more like a beef gravy than a mushroom wine sauce that I was expecting. The salads were served warm too. They should be served with crisp lettuce on a chilled dish. GRRR! This just annoys me crappy salads. I think this place is just a tourist trap and is very pricy for the food you get. However, our service was good. I think the servers realize they have to be good because the food is lacking quality and flavor.

I GOT FOOD POISONING AFTER I ATE HERE TODAY. Please save your money and go somewhere else. Also they play music very loudly and when I asked the server to turn it down because I had a headache he either didn't do it or barely turned it down so I ended up having to get my food to go. I used to love coming here, but both the service and the quality of the food have gone downhill. Would not recommend unless you want food poisoning

Let's start off by saying the food wasn't bad. The experience I could have done without. Yes they smoke in this bar. Yes the chairs are comfortable -- kind of gives you the feel of plush patio furniture. The bartender was veryyy let's just say b/c of his personality I wouldn't ever recommend or visit here again. I don't even remember him washing his hands when he was preparing the food. Yes ... yes.. the bartender prepares the food. God I hope I don't get worms from contamination. He (the bartender) was very interactive and engaged - like too engaged. Like as we were eating he was sitting right in front of us talking to us and watching us eating .. I couldn't have felt more uncomfortable and then he decided to show my girlfriend a video of the other bartender running around with only shoes on.. I wish - I wish I could tell you I was lying but no.. The gentleman was entirely naked in this video and the bartender did ask can he show her something disturbing but "We" wouldn't have thought it will be a video of their coworker naked.. Were they Friendly in the bar ? Yes. Music and parking? Yes. But I would never ever return here. Ever.

Waited in the drive thru for 27 minutes. Got our coffee that did not have cold foam on top, when I asked why they said "Oh were out" ok but didnt tell us that when we ordered it... then they handed be my donut that was absolutely destroyed and looked like the bag had been stepped on or something then I bit into my egg and cheese sandwich and it was ICE COLD and I almost threw up. What a waist of time and money food was completely inedible

On my way into the bathroom I slipped in and fell into another diner's vomit. I just got my clothes back from dry cleaner and they are ruined. I can't comment on the food because once you've lain in another person's oyster vomit it rather kills your appetite. I went back to my hotel for obvious reasons, but my friends who remained felt that the grilled oysters were subpar.

update: I have been contacted by American social and they felt it appropriate to mention that no one else complained about the food making them Ill. That is good for them but the food made ME ill and incapacitated for several days, so this was a highly inappropriate response. I had not eaten anything prior to arriving at American social and was in good health prior to arriving. Luckily I was alone or my party may have fallen ill as well. The representative mentioned that they take health very seriously however I was brought dirty silverware and had to ask for a new set. I also witnessed an inappropriate level of cleansing of the tables and no cleansing of the chairs once other patrons left. I understand that no one likes to receive negative reviews on their business but they should always respond appropriately. I was it disrespectful, I merely spoke my experience and deserved a better response. I was sent a link saying it takes 6 hours for food poisoning to occur, well this establishment must be competitive because I experienced extreme nausea, dizziness and vomiting in record time. Do better. Previous: I visited American social recently and was promptly seated. I ordered the vegetarian chili and the turkey sandwich. I started to feel light headed and my vision went blurry. I was afraid to stand up to run to the bathroom I sat and increasingly felt worse. Increasing Nausea , extreme dizziness. I eventually made it to the restroom and vomited until there was blood. (Graphic I know... sorry). I felt better after I vomited so I paid and left. Once I got home I started to feel worse again and spent the following 5 days confined to my bed only able to drink water and eat chicken soup. I lost weight so I'm looking sexier than ever, but it was a very terrible experience. American social gave me very bad food poisoning. I couldn't even spend time with my children.

Looking for a vegan friendly brunch place to go to with my friends and this looked cute. I called and they are NOT vegan friendly AT ALL. Unless you want oatmeal and a fruit cup. I can make that at home. Dairy allergies are a big deal, and a vegan diet is a very popular thing. Disappointed that they don't even have ONE vegan breakfast choice on the menu. If you ever decide to become more accommodating, please let me know bc I'd love to try your place out and change my rating. And make sure you take down your "vegan friendly" tag because you are not and it's misleading.

Chicken tikki masala is rich and spicy, although the chicken was a little tough this time; lamp kashiri in a thick broth with onions and peppers was well-seasoned, but not a good sign when I use this much red sauce. The samosa were a little crisp - almost crumbly and overcooked, but the naan was perfect. The service was odd - a huge mob was spilling out the door, yet our server didn't seem inclined to tally up our check with any sense of urgency. We loved the slow pacing as it was Valentine's Day and we wanted to do some eye-staring, but I felt anxious about the swelling, hungry hoard. The strip mall couldn't be any uglier, but Shere Punjab is normally well worth its strong reputation, just not on a high turnover evening. Come on a slow night and let them spoil you.

I really appreciate their dedication to fresh organic ingredients however, the flavor is not there. Their meatballs were bland. The texture was perfect, the meat was good quality, the price for the portion was great but they had no flavor. I'm not someone who likes salt or adds it to my food but these meatballs needed garlic and salt or maybe some good grated cheese instead of salt. Their gravy tastes decent but there's huge chunks of tomato in it that I personally don't care for. I like a smoother textured gravy. I was excited that they offer cauliflower crust pizza. It was tasty but what's in it? I was expecting the usual ingredients of cauliflower, cheese, eggs and seasoning. This had some type of flour in it. I asked the girl at the counter what was in it. She didn't know and there was no ingredient info on it. She said it was gluten free. I don't have a gluten allergy, I'm more concerned with low carb. This wasn't low carb. So unfortunately it's not something I would order again because the carbs are probably similar to a regular pizza. But I don't know and no else knew so I'm guessing. I just feel if your offering special diet items you should have an ingredient list so people know what's in it. At least educate your counter employees on the ingredients. So a 3 star, not terrible but not a place I would put on my go to list.

I have a severe shellfish and fish allergy and ate here last night. I am also vegan so I like to make it easy when going out and I simply got the Insalata Mista, which is not dinner size but I realize my options are limited. I of course confirmed all of this could be made vegan and allergy free before ordering with the waitress. She went back to kitchen to check and came back saying "absolutely", they can do it. I asked what was in the dressing and she said its just balsamic vinegar and oil. I thought ok, how can you mess up a salad? I felt satisfied enough, ordered, and we waited for the food to come. About half way through the salad my neck felt a little itchy, I thought it was my scarf so I took that off. Getting more itchy, I stopped eating thinking 'what is in this salad??' I called the waitress over to explain the exact ingredients in the salad dressing. She didn't know so she went to get a person from the kitchen staff. Five minutes later, some pompous Italian guy came over and slammed his big fists on the table and started talking really loud about the salad. No mind that we were in full conversation that he very rudely and abruptly interrupted. His tone started getting elevated as he exclaimed "the salad is fine" "I know what is vegan" and "no meat in salad dressing, only fish"(because fish ISN'T meat???? Oh, and I'm not allergic to it or anything!!!!!) I told him I was ALLERGIC to fish and shellfish and the waitress told me they could make it vegan/allergy free-and that I made this as clear as humanely possible to the idiot waitress who either didn't bother to communicate this to the kitchen staff or didn't take the allergy seriously. His response to this "Don't come to my restaurant with allergy! You eat at home!" Yes, you read correctly... that is what this prick said to me. I told him to "stop yelling in our faces and get OFF of our table." WHAT A POS!!!!!!!!! He also had said the dressing had honey-mustard, which is NOT vegan. I wasn't very concerned about it at that point as I wasn't sure how much fish I had ingested and if my reaction would get worse. I did not end up having to use my Epi pen but did take 3 Benadryl when we got in the car (which is a lot for me!!!) :( This was HORRRRRIIIBBBBLLLLLEEEEEEE EXPERIENCE!!!!!!!!! If you have ANY severe allergies, are vegetarian, or vegan DON'T go here!! Oh, and this prick needs to go to BEHAVIORAL SCHOOL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

As our first covid dining experience, meeting (vaxed) family for a small lunch together felt safe on their outdoor patio. Food was very good, as on pre-covid visits so that aspect doesn't seem to have suffered under duress. Service was almost adequate. We never got side dishes (vegetables) ordered to flesh out entrees which came with no sides. Didn't see the server enough to have those brought or removed from bill. Wanted a pleasant outing so didn't make a scene or delay paying and leaving, but wanted to stay focused on our loving goodbyes to young family members moving from the area. We enjoyed greatly all the food that was delivered -- some had pizza, others gnocchi, and we had lunch-sized serving of Bronzino with perfectly crisped skin and an olive tapenade. Accommodating of food allergies, with no less delicious results. Low rating because they subsequently gave run-around about hosting moderately sized, vaxed gathering for a landmark birthday (for cancer survivor). Filled out their online form for events. No response. Called and was told manager would call back. No response. Finally called again after several days waiting and manager said they are no longer doing events at all -- now or in the future -- because of staff shortage. (Doing an event actually requires less staff, not more, because you have a more fixed menu for food and drinks, and people are happy to fill time with socializing and toasts.) There is no more risk in having 20 vaxed people on an open-air patio who know each other than having several unrelated, perhaps not-vaxed smaller groups of patrons on that same patio. They can have a no-event policy, but not updating their website with a disclaimer (so easily done with a very long time to have done it), and not getting back to people promptly for inqueries to GIVE YOU MONEY is unforgivable. Added heartbreak is they are the best location for people coming from center city and Main Line to meet at a convenient mid-point. The bloom is off the rose.

My first impression of Pei Wei - they're like the Chipotle of Asian cuisine. Chinese dishes seem to dominate their menu but they also offer a variety of Thai and Korean inspired dishes. Extra points to them for offering two portion sizes, a lighter menu, and also gluten free options! My friend and I ordered takeout on a Sunday afternoon that took only a matter of minutes for the friendly staff to prepare. As a first-timer, I was excited to try a little of everything! Here's how they rank in my book: 1. Kung Pao Chicken: Not spicy as it claims to be. Vegetables seem fresh and a good meat to vegetable ratio. Dish was dry but alright in my book. 2. Dan Dan Noodles w/ Chicken: First off, I wasn't a fan of the minced/ground chicken. The sauce was a bit bland but the cucumber added a fresh note to the dish. Pretty good IMO but I haven't had other dan dan noodles to make a comparison. 3. Sesame Chicken: Pretty darn dry. Scarce vegetables. A bit bland and meat was a little tough tbh. Probably wouldn't order again. My friend's bf ordered beef and broccoli and it turned out opposite of ours: - Smaller portion than what is usually served (he's a regular so he would def know this) - LOTS of sauce, too much in fact (maybe that's where all of our sauce went? lol) I'm not sure if I would order again from Pei Wei as I'd much rather order from my typical Chinese takeout spot. The portions are pretty good bang for your buck but I'd get the same portion from my typical Chinese spot for those prices. While the food was not outstanding, it's clear that the menu tries to cater to the mass population. Not a bad place to start if you're nervous about venturing into the world of Asian cuisine.

We ate there this past Sunday. Their pizza oven was broken so they had no pizza. There were cobwebs all over the wall next to our table and gnat like bugs flying around. My child's burger was cold and raw in the center. He took a big bite before realizing and got sick from it. My salad had rotten tomatoes and cucumbers and the lettuce tasted old and slimy. I immediately spit it out. I'd recommend not going here so you can avoid your family getting food poisoning. Very disappointed.

This Acme is open 24 hours which is good for me. They have a section for gluten free products & other products through out the store are labeled a such as well. The beat time to go to avoid the long lines is definitely late night. Their products are a bit higher than other markets I frequent. For the convenience, I will pay that for now. I have encountered several EXPIRED PRODUCTS & have brought this to the manager's attention in the past. MAKE SURE the dates are checked on EVERYTHING before you pay. They are good with accepting returns but SAVE THAT RECEIPT. It's a good place to "pick up a few things" but heavy duty shopping I'll reserve for elsewhere.

What can I say? This guy's an artist. The freshest and most eclectic ingredients, daily rotating plates, and items made to order make visiting this food truck a delight every time. Now, let me echo everyone else by saying this is like no other truck in the city. I have a special place in my heart for Philly's food truck scene. I revel in the joys of dancing with food poisoning over a greasy saucy $5 gyro platter. Octopus Falafel is nothing like that. Each plate is visually striking and a symphony of tastes. (Yes, seriously! I know this is a food truck we're talking about!) Here, lines stretch across the block thirty minutes before the truck even opens. The first time I arrived I stood in line, shivering in the rain amongst other customers. Everyone excitedly shared remarks about making time for this man, analyzing his reputation, and anticipating today's treat. It's almost like a pilgrimage, and the results are amazing every time.
I got the WORST case of food poisoning after eating their egg salad! Seriously thought I would die and had to be admitted to the hospital for fluids.
They have great gluten-free options including grouper nuggets which are outstanding. We stayed in a nearby hotel and ordered them every day for lunch.

I thought I'd try their chef salad ordered it around 330 got it around 430 and I have been in the bathroom the rest of the evening I have food poisoning I'll be calling the health department on Monday beware of eating at this place

I am writing this review as we are getting ready to leave the restaurant. DO NOT ORDER THE STEAK!!! We came to Ballyhoos because I was in the mood for good seafood. My husband was not, so he ordered the 14oz Ribeye. I ordered a delicious grilled grouper. When we got our entrees, he smelled a strong oder that he thought was my fish. It ended up being his steak! He had me try a bite and I spit it out and almost threw up. The server brought the manager over and he immediately took both our plates away. We were given a check for our drinks and appetizer. The manager NEVER came back to apologize. We paid the check but will not be back.

I have lived in Warminster since 2001. Unfortunately in the past I have visited this restaurant and noticed that the cashier is tending cash and then handling food. I visited today after visiting after 10 years to buy a roll. The cashier took my money which was cash and then went and got the roll I asked for. I called the restaurant to complain as I had before on and the manager on duty basically blew me off, saying I'm busy I have to go. I asked for the locations owner his name his name is Dave Christie. Dave I got news for you it is disgusting that your staff is so poorly trained but you can't have a cashier ringing up sales and other people handling food. For the last 15 years I have not visited your restaurant because of this reason. Everyone listing, if you want to why you come down with a stomach virus or flu or tuberculosis, the food you're eating is being shared by the currency it's being touched by these uncaring fools at this location. Customers, please order your food in person and you will see what I am talking about, if you order it online you'll never know what you're missing!!!!!till days later when you're vomiting from a virus. Mr. Christie, expect a call from the health department.

Our server Capri was awesome! She was very attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed. I wish I could give this review a higher rating, but due to lack of sanitation I can only give this review 2 stars. The food: I love a good order of potato skins, you cannot go wrong with their version of skins. They're pretty big and large enough to share as an appetizer. They're only $7 on their happy hour menu. They're served with a side of sour cream and ranch if you'd like. I also ordered the Cobb Salad, it was a pretty big bowl with plenty of toppings. Unfortunately after a few bites, I noticed a hair in my salad. I immediately lost my appetite and showed my server. I was pretty bummed because I was excited to eat my salad. After my findings, there was no way I was going to get another salad from this kitchen. Our server happily took the salad off of our bill. I hope this kitchen works a little harder to ensure that this doesn't happen again, because this tells me that there is a lack of sanitation in this kitchen. Hair in foods can lead to contamination of foods and that's just not sanitary or good business. Do better Bully's! The drinks: The Bloody Mary with jalapeño vodka was perfect. The vodka gave it a little extra kick, but it was so tasty. A perfect blend of what a Bloody Mary should be. A 25 oz. double shot big unit Bloody Mary for $4.50, you can't beat it. Also had a Michelada. I've had Micheladas at other Bully's locations and those have been consistently great. The ratio of beer to mix and spice have been pretty spot on.
