But this location lacks that consistency. The rim is not salted at all and the mix to beer ratio is completely off, it's almost more beer than mix and the spice was mild after we ordered it spicy. I noticed there was a little tajin added to the top, which didn't really help the flavor. This Michelada was a bit disappointing, not sure I'd order it again at this location.

Sad experience with friends after church. We waited 30 minutes to be seated which I expected, but not for what we got. Appetizers were great, but the burgers were not. One friend ordered burger with no mayo, yet it came with mayo. He asked for it done again and it was back at table almost immediately. That tells me they just scrapped it off. I orders bison burger and it came so well done I couldn't tell what it was. Worse yet, my last 2 bites had something very hot in it like jalapeño, so that tells me it was cross contaminated with something. Fries were soggy also so not very tasty. I got one refill on my drink ten never saw waiter again, yet our party of 6 was auto tipped 20% on our bills. I would have left a tip regardless but was annoyed to be charged when we barley saw our waiter.

Me and my boyfriend came here after the beach on Saturday May 9th, the next day I was in the bathroom in pain throwing everything up coming to the conclusion I had food poisoning, not long after my boyfriend also was having the same symptoms as me( nausea, headache, stomach pain and other things that are too gross share) we both ordered two different meats and tortillas and they usually come with the salsa Verde. This is my first time having food poisoning and I don't wish it on anyone. Just a warning before you decide to eat here. Sorry for being a Karen but the pain ain't worth it !

This used to be a really good Starbucks, but their service has gone way downhill. 2 weeks in a row I've put in the same order and something has been messed up both times. All I ordered was 2 bacon breakfast sandwiches and a coffee with 3 cream. 1st trip last week, coffee comes to me black. I can forgive this because the coffee is still edible when it's black. Today I go there and put in the exact same order - 2 bacon breakfast sandwiches and a coffee with 3 cream. I get my sandwiches home and it turns out one of them is a sausage sandwich. I hate breakfast sausage sandwiches, because they smell so nasty it's like anus wrapped in vomit, diarrhea, and period blood. I spend 20 mins on the phone with the Starbucks and they can't find my receipt. Fortunately, they put an approximation of my order on one of the breakfast sandwich wrappers so I still had that. They asked me if I could come back, I said not right now but later I could. I went to the gym to work out and then on my way home came back through the Starbucks. I gave them the wrapper and this time they stepped up and paid for their mistake, gave me a free bacon egg and gouda breakfast sandwich - they were all out of the bacon egg and cheese ones by that time. Still though, very frustrating to go there twice and have the order screwed up both times. There's a new Starbucks just down on the road in between Gateway Blvd and Calgary Trail and 51 Ave. I'll be going there from now on, give a new location a shot. If I had put in an order for 20 customized coffees than I could forgive them for screwing up something in the order. Even a 1 time screwup I could forgive. Consecutive screwups on a simple order, though? I cannot overlook that.

I really wanted to support this restaurant because it's in my neighborhood. The ambience and decor are immaculate but for some reason our food took over 1 hour. My one friend ordered the Grandma Carnie which never came. We were informed there was an issue with there POS by our server. We were told that they would be comp a shrimp appetizer. My friend has a seafood allergy and was unable to accept the shrimp. We asked for a manager and was told by our server that she was "busy". We felt that was unacceptable and and informed our server of this the owner came to our table and explained that the my friends meal wasnt prepared because of issues with the POS. Her response to our complaints was to take off 5 dollars from our bill. The side items are 4 dollars. The food and service was great but we were disappointed in how this issue was resolved. I won't be going back.

I got severe food poisoning from the food here, I believe it was the wonton soup because no one else I was with ordered the soup. The food was only okay going in, but it was terrible when it left my body. I was severely ill and because of that do not recommend eating here.

We were in the parking lot taking our dogs to be groomed. We decided to stop at Manila eats we've seen it many times but we're always in transit or not in need of a meal. I'm not familiar with Filipino food but my husband is so he explained the menu to me and I was excited to try a few dishes. I am a celiac which means I can't have wheat, wheat derived products or barley (Gluten). I needed to ask if there were any of my allergens in the food items. Our server seemed to understand and told me the dish I picked did NOT have gluten. This interaction was difficult and might be avoided in the future with a concise ingredient list or common allergy menu available upon request. The food was delicious!! And looked beautiful. I ate the cassava cake assuming it was gluten free per my interaction, I had a allergy rash, extreme stomach upset and diarrhea for two days. The cassava cake had gluten. I don't usually like to ding people on language barriers but this is avoidable and dangerous, her level of answer confidence gave me no pause, it could have been way worse with any allergy that causes anaphylactic response. In summery my husband REALLY likes the food, I thought it was tasty too. The portions are good the service is fast and polite. The restaurant is in a prime location and has outdoor seating. I cannot warn allergy sufferers enough. Communication is not safe enough for us.

I am extremely disappointed with the Turning Point in Cherry Hill I have been there several times and I honestly may not return at least at this location ever again. I have always had a great experience here with my boyfriend but I believe they tried to kill us with the food. When we first arrived they had told us it will be a 10 minute wait but we only waited about five minutes and we were seated so I thought that we were going to have a great time but they messed up at least 3 to 4 times. Let's start with strike one. Strike 1 - Our table was not as clean as I hoped it would be and it was in a tight space by the window between another table in front of us and then the cleaning station was right behind us so I could barely fit in my seat. every five seconds a waiter will sneak up behind me to do whatever they were doing at that station which was very bothersome. It looked as though they just did a quick wipe for the next party to arrive and didn't even bother to clean the floors under the table. That is a pet peeve for me. Strike 2 - when our food arrived I had the Basic skillet which was OK it wasn't the best and also it looks like whoever was in the kitchen does not wash their utensils before using it in another meal because I saw spots of avocado in my egg which you can see in the picture if you were to zoom in. Even the white dish itself does not look the cleanest. I still wanted to attempt to try the meal but I couldn't even finish it especially after what my boyfriend found in his plate... my boyfriend had a Key West shrimp omelette with a side of hash which is what he usually gets without any problems however as he was eating he tasted a hard crunch when he was eating his omelette and then he felt something hard. when he tried to eat some more come to find out there was a piece of metal or plastic in his hashbrowns. we had to Inform the manager and she took his plate back and stated that they will make him a new dish and we said OK. We were totally disgusted especially because God for bid my boyfriend were to actually eat that and choke on it it would've been a whole nother story. at this point I didn't even want to finish my breakfast especially because it wasn't that good anyway so I told our waiter to take the plate back as well and we just decided to eat his cinnamon roll pancakes which was pretty good and usually what my boyfriend also usually gets. Strike 3 - so after a while we were still waiting on my boyfriends "revamped" dish and halfway through eating his pancakes we noticed a long green and black skinny piece of string as he cut another piece of pancake. we couldn't tell what it was but it looked disgusting at first we thought it was apart of the cinnamon in the pancake but then we realize it wasn't! my boyfriend grabbed the skinny piece of string and pulled a Long piece of string like object. it looked like a piece of stem from a vegetable or something at this point I was furious and I wanted to flip the table because not only was the food not that great but also my boyfriend could've died the first time he found something in his food! We called our waiter over the table and asked if she could make out what was on the plate and she said it could possibly be a part of the cinnamon but then she looked closely and said she doesn't know so she took the plate to the back and the manager came back and apologized for the recent events that took place. She stated that she will take care of the bill. What I will say is that the day that we went could have been just a bad day for the people in the kitchen because as I have stated before, usually they are pretty good when it comes to their food but because of the experience that we have had, we will not be returning to this location because we are darn near traumatized and it seems as though they cross contaminate a lot in the kitchen. Sherri, the manager, handled the situation very well and she gave us a coupon to have two free entrées but I don't know if I would ever use it.

This is an update to my previous glowing review We ordered from here for my office birthday party. First - the hummus is consistently the best anywhere. We said no bell pepper - allergy. After eating the salad we saw a bell pepper from the salad I ate under the rice. So instead of enjoying the memory of delicious hummus baba ganoush tabouli etc I will be remembering how upset my tummy is for a week after eating here. DUNNO if bell pepper is in the delicious felafel or not But certainly it was simply picked out of the salad instead of being prepared fresh for us. It got me bad. Allergies are like that. Having - in this case the thing THAT HAD THE ALLERGEN IN IT BUT IT WAS REMOVED - makes the person sick. PLEASE - when someone says no bell pepper or the like ASK if it's an allergy and then TELL THEM IF THE FOOD THEY ORDER IS NORMALLY PREPARED WITH THAT ALLERGEN. I could have simply avoided the salad if I had known. Thanks

This is *the* place to go for breakfast in Indianapolis. It makes every list. I wish I knew why. They had an unreasonably long wait time; we sat under the heat lamps on a bench of an hour and a half in rain/snow. In hindsight, we shouldn't have stayed. As some of the other reviewers noted, the servers seemed overworked and irritated. They also didn't have an understanding of what ingredients were included in each dish, but were adamant that dishes be served precisely as listed on their very limited menu. (I have food allergies and have developed an extensive knowledge of what is typically used in dishes. If in doubt and there are no other options on a menu, I'll ask the server what is included in the dish. I ended up being very ill as a result of their lack of knowledge.) If you are looking for specialty brunch places, I suggest Cafe Patachou or one of the local public houses. I don't like to disparage restaurants that are trying something new or different, but there are other restaurants doing a far better job.

I love this place because I got food poisoning from here but it caused me to quit smoking. Food poisoning was from the filet and chipotle mashed potatoes. I was so sick that I didn't smoke for 4 days. Thank you cava for serving contaminated food.

Excuse the errors in the text above but I had to check with a real bartender to see how she would handle this situation that occurred. And as expected, she'd handle it with empathy and professionalism. The classless manager at Green Eggs on Gaul chose to argue instead immediately rectifying the issue. For someone who didn't "have the energy", you sure wasted a bunch of it finding a way to put the blame on the customer. It's simple!! Stop pouring cheap substitutes when you do not have what the customer asks for--that's deceptive practice. Brands matter!! If I specifically order a drink by it's brand name, that's what I expect--not your cheaper replacement. Someone could have an allergy to a different brand of liquor based on how it's made. It's deeper than matching the "type" of liquor, or a flavor. Example, someone orders cranberry and Tito's (corn vodka) specifically because they react horribly to Kettle One (potato vodka). Sucks because I usually tip 20-30%. Couldn't bring myself to tip a damn thing outside of the service charge after the ignorance from the person who is supposed to be in charge. Smh.

I was out with a friend the other day, trying to find a new place to eat at when the bears outside caught my eye. We ordered the House Special Smelly Pot with Chicken (Schechuan Spicy) and the Beef Stew & Dry Bean Curd Casserole. The chicken was cooked really well, and it was very flavorful. However, we were late to realize that the Smelly Pot had stinky tofu in it which contaminated the whole dish (both of us do not like stinky tofu). The Beef Stew & Dry Bean Curd Casserole was also pretty good and tasted exactly as I expected. Overall, I would come back to try other dishes (but will never order the Smelly Pot again). Also, it is good to note that this place is CASH ONLY (or Venmo).

The food and drinks here gave me food poisoning. As I was waiting for my order, I was just looking around and I saw they had milk (which looked old) sitting on the counter. Also, they need more staff. I saw only 2 people at this location. I will NEVER come here again. And if this is the closest Starbucks to you, drive a little farther to a different one, it'd be worth the drive.

Overall a fun place especially the rooftop. We tried to dance on the upper level but there was an overwhelming smell of vomit and poop. We went back the next night and it was the same. Everyone around us was dancing and holding their nose. It was disgusting. We had to leave. We wanted to stay because the music was great and the atmosphere was fun but the smell was sickening.

Delicious - but don't go if you're in a hurry or on a budget. For a sandwich spot, they sure take FOREVER! Busy or not, no sandwich should take 30 minutes. Also, I paid for chips then saw ALL are cooked in peanut oil. I'm allergic to peanuts. So that didn't go over well when I only ordered chips to have during my 30 minute wait because I was starving. That being said, theI sandwiches use fresh ingredients and creative combinations. Probably justifies the expense but it is a pricey fast(slow)-food lunch. I still go because there aren't many delis and I know to expect a long wait and high price tag.

The beer selection gives you options & the food can be a hit or miss depending upon if you have an iron stomach. I haven't had the good fortune to catch their Happy Hour. HAPPY HOUR Mon. -Fri. 4-7PM as of 9/11/17 Domestic & Crafts: $3.00 Import Draft: $4.00 Seasonal Cocktails & House Wine: $6/glass (SWEET POTATO TOTS 4/5): When you order it as an additional side, they present it in a large bowl with lots of crispy 2'' rectangular shaped sweet potato tots and since that's a nickname my mom gave me, whenever I see anything sweet potato related, I have to get it and try it! The exterior of the sweet potato was fried to perfection and crispy when you bite down into it, but it lacked the natural sweetness I am used to and for this reason, I'd skip this for my own personal reason. FRENCH ONION SOUP 3/5): This is your standard French Onion Soup with nothing special or extraordinary that stood out. The soup was sort of warm and not hot like I expected. It was alright and I really can't think of anything special about it... FILET MIGNON SALAD 5/5): Four out of eight of us at the table got this and it turned out to be a great choice! The seared filet was cooked medium and every bite was soft, not chewy or overcooked and on a bed of baby lettuce. I loove arugula intensely and I guess you could say I'm obsessed with it. The menu said arugula was a component of the dish, but I didn't taste any at all, so I was a little disappointed. However, the roasted tomatoes were a really nice touch and a nice change from your standard fresh tomatoes, so I really enjoyed that! The candied bacon was sprinkled on top of the filet and was one of my favorite parts of the salad and made it a complete meal combined with the green peppercorn dressing. I don't know if they made the dressing it in house; it was pretty darn gooood and not an icky, thick dressing. The dressing was light, refreshingly good and different from your normal Ranch, Blue Cheese, Caesar, etc. BEER (5/5): They have a nice selection of craft, domestic, imports, speciality cocktails and wine. I love that they support local breweries and had to get the Beach Blonde Ale made by 3 Daughters Brewery in St. Pete. There are so many wonderful local breweries, making it an easy choice to choose what I wanted to drink. Kudos to them for supporting our local community! Unfortunately, the customer service is not up to par. If you come during your 1 hr. lunch, good luck getting your food in under 45 minutes! Also, you should set aside at least 15 minutes or more to get your check...this isn't the first time where they fell on customer service and a reason I prefer not coming here during the weekday when it's so busy during lunch. Also, my manager and coworker did experience food poisoning and I felt so bad for them. Luckily, I have not gotten sick. I think the beer and food is decent if you can get it in a timely fashion. I would not come back to this place on my own unless food is served much faster!

If I could give zero stars I would. I used to be a loyal customer. This is the worst place on Earth so don't waste your time going there. I stayed a loyal customer even when I had got maggots in rice bags and even food poisoning from buying meat from this place and staff is rude and especially the owner and the cashiers, they don't give you any importance if you are loyal customer. I have never reported this place to health sanitation department but now I will. If you complain they will simply humiliate you and turn the back to you. Never going back there anymore nor will recommend to my friends this place. All the md oriental is owned by the same person who doesn't care about the customers.
There is no social distaning here i am getting tested as I write this had a fever of 101 diarrhea and vomiting food was horrible so I praying it's negative because the definitely a lot of.

My family and I have been long time lovers of Maynard's so when they announced they were reopening, we were thrilled! To say I was disappointed was an understatement. They took away so many of our classic favorites (the steak tar tar, pomme frits, muscles), but we were still excited to try their new items. The new menu is confusing, only listing tasting notes, so we were unsure as to what was going arrive. We ordered the potato starter (which was only about 2 bites of cold, under flavored potatoes for the 3 of us and was wholly underwhelming.), the fois gras (which while the best thing we ordered (a generous statement), it was literally the size of 3 quarters next to one another, and came with 2 tortilla chips for $18.), and the mushroom starter. The mushroom starter came covered in sesame seeds which the description had no note of and I am severely allergic. When I told the waiter this and asked for it to be remade, he was very unfriendly and annoyed. I had to ask for it to be remade a few times just while he said "oh." Until he said "I mean, I guess. I'll see." Later on someone different brought out the mushrooms without sesame, which was again, underwhelming ‍. Once we finished our last plate, our waiter (without saying anything or making eye contact) tossed down our check and left. Overall a very disappointing experience. In the past Maynard's was a wonderful place with friendly staff, delicious food, and while still pricey, you got the quality food that you paid for. That was definitely not our experience this time around.

Even if this was the only place open for food ever again, I would NEVER return here. I waited a day to post my review so I could mull over the meal and service and still can't find anything to brag about here. They charged $4 for my friend's tea and it was Lipton brand. Such a rip off on pricing. I ended up going to the Starbucks next door for a coffee instead. I have to say, I was surprised at how small the brunch menu was and how pricey these items were. I ordered the hangover tots because I wanted to try the SPAM in it. A few of us ordered drinks, and enjoyed conversing outside at our table. The food finally came and almost all of the meals were incorrect. One person in our party can't have gluten, and asked for her meal without ketchup or avocado and had to send hers back because it came with both on it. I asked for mine without ketchup and saw it was served on top. My scrambled egg on the hangover tots was like rubber. The ketchup, aioli and other toppings didn't mix well at all. I was expecting a ground sausage, but was surprised it was sliced. On top of that, no SPAM. I was going to ask for a replacement, but didn't want to wait for it as the original meals took some time to arrive and I had to be somewhere soon. Honestly glad I didn't wait, because the replacement meal we ordered for our gluten free friend didn't arrive until after the checks were paid. The hangover tots meal really was nothing to rave about for $15. Our appetizers never came. The waitress for our table barely checked on us. We had to kindly ask another waitress for the check because we hadn't seen ours in about 10-15 minutes and she said she would just be taking over our table for the rest of our meal. It just seemed like they weren't on top of their game. When we got the check, we were charged for a bottomless mimosa (which someone did order) AND a bottle of champagne. We asked to have that fixed, and she removed the bottomless mimosa order, but kept the champagne bottle on (which was more expensive, mind you). She had already charged my card for this, and I was so frustrated, so I didn't ask for a refund. The ONLY redeeming thing was that our friend said her gluten free meal, that came out as we were getting up to leave, was delicious. So, brownie points I guess? It's also kind of terrible that a 20% tip was automatically added. Had the service been top notch, this would have been deserved...but it's like they could have cared less about us because they knew it was going to be added anyhow. Looking forward to never coming back and making sure none of my friends do if they're in Philly.

I have been patronizing SMK for several years and never had a problem, but I will not go there again. I ordered a fish platter with cabbage and potato salad. The fish tasted odd, perhaps it had been frozen and not fresh fish. I wouldn't eat it for fear of food poisoning. The sides were so BLAND! That was a waste of money.

Not good at all. Horribly cooked. I asked for turkey bacon received pork sausage patty. Allergic to pork. The steak in my omelet over cooked the eggs tasteless bland over cooked. My kids meal food came with wrong meat. My French toast meal came with the meat I asked for. Can't eat none of it. Horrible food ever.

One extra star for being one of the very few ( or probably just one) Taiwanese restaurant in Reno. And that extra one star is included in the total 2 stars which was deducted from the other wise 2 total stars due to the waitress' pushy attitude promoting the non-oyster fried oyster omelette. She was at the edge of an outburst when we did not want to succumb to her pressure of trying that dish which does not live up to its name and I had to resort to a white lie of a case of allergy just so we can move on. Stinky tofu which is totally not stinky and almost tasteless. Can hardly remember any other dish because they are so bland. All in all, any domestic attempt to make Taiwanese food with star anis and goji berry should provide you with better food than this place does.

Portions are pretty small so don't expect to get full off this meal unless you order a lot. Overall, I wasn't impressed enough to justify the cost...but the things I did like I'd be willing to eat again. Note to self: do not sit under the vent again, it was too chilly. What I liked: * Sausage & Peppers Pizza - Ahh I really liked this, probably my fave thing from the meal, but quite oily * Gnocchi - Pretty unique with the pomodoro, pesto, and pistachio flavors and textures! Wish there was more of it, I used the extra bread we got to dip in this sauce. * The Mix: Ordered 2 Salumi (Soppressata Piccante, Coppa Piccante) & 2 Formaggi (don't remember the names of the exact ones we got) - I liked that the meats were spicy, but didn't care for the cheeses at all. They also refilled our bread and gave us two sauces but I never used them. What I didn't like: * Prosciutto and Arugula Pizza - to be honest I don't like arugula all that much and it overpowered the prosciutto...my fave thing was the cheese? Haha * Tagliatelle - This was the only dairy-free pasta we got for the lactose intolerant folks and I think I had higher hopes of the flavor with this pork ragu, white bean, kale mix...it felt like within a few bites it was gone. * Ravioli - I think I locked onto "lobster butter" in the description and ignored the peas and carrots after it...not sure why I thought it was a good idea, but I wasn't a fan and this was the most expensive pasta yet had nothing special about it.

I tried the chicken pho here and it tasted like there was fish sauce in it- I asked them and they said there wasn't which had me believe they may not have washed the dish very well or perhaps some cross contamination because it was definitely fishy. Anyway I hate fish sauce so I couldn't enjoy the soup. The second time I went I tried a vegan pho so that there would be no chance of fish sauce and it was alright. Perhaps they shouldn't have named the place pho bistro because I hear that there sandwiches are really good. It's hard to find good soup in Isla Vista and state street in my opinion. Maybe I'm just use to Irvine/ Westminster/ and Korea town quality so my standards are higher.

Been here twice, Average sushi, food is pricey. Needs to be more aware of consumer allergies. bartender (female) provided excellent service. The rest, service is lacking. The atmosphere is lacking. I really wanted to like this place.

So after seeing so many posts about this place I finally decided to give it a try. Initially walking in it was pretty clean (which is a rarity in west philly might I add). Now, Im not a vegan but Ill eat anything that wont get up and crawl off my plate so I was down to try whatever off the menu. I got the jerk chick'n caesar salad and a chocolate milkshake (made with soy icecream). There was these weird water cress type cubes in the salad (I have no idea what they were). The fake chicken I just couldnt get passed. It tasted like grilled rubber. And I wanna just say that those of you reading this that think eating vegan is healthier, youre wrong. There are so many vegan products out there that are so over processed and gross. I.e the "chicken" on this salad. The soy milkshake had me excited since I am allergic to dairy. But for some odd reason I did get a stomachache after this shake. Perhaps I have a soy allergy too? Who knows. It was also a bit expensive here. I paid about $16 for a salad and a shake. Hate to say it, but I probably wont be going back here.

When I heard that a Vietnamese fried chicken place was opening, I was all over their social media accounts waiting in anticipation. Owned by the same crew as Jack's Burger Shack and Cerdo Tacos, we're going back to Vietnamese street food here at Ong. The place itself is small with very few chairs, and a tiny menu. Pretty murals on the walls. Everything is gluten/celiac friendly except for the spring rolls, which are fried in their own separate fryer, so there's no cross contamination. You order at the counter and the food is brought to you/called out by your name. Spring rolls are reminiscent of home style cooking. Lots of onion, noodles and black mushroom. Comes 5 to an order with a dipping sauce. Wings are full wings - not broken apart. So each piece is the tip, drummy and two bone piece. Deep fried and then tossed in a sticky sweet and fish sauce based glaze, then garnished with cilantro. Loved these! Chicken is a big thigh/drum and a breast piece, both coated in rice flour and fried. Tossed in the same sauce as the wings and served with rice and pickled cucumber. Since the chicken is so much thicker, the flavour of the sauce isn't as pronounced. I like the crispiness and it was very juicy. Pro tip: if eating in, there are bottles of sauce on the table that is a lime-y, salty, garlic sauce. Dip your chicken in that and it'll be amazeballs! Very excited that this is open and will very happily recommend as an authentic Vietnamese flavour profile. My go-to order would probably be the wings with a side of rice!

CASH ONLY! A 4 star if you're out for a place to study as this place is often occupied by student from nearby universities. However, the somewhat muggy air inside and the slim selection of vegan and gluten free snacks takes a star away. And the second for the air and the uncosy layout of tables. BUT don't miss the oUTDOOR seating in the back yard! That lifts the whole place!

Before mothers daythis would've been a five star rating.we've been going there for years and having phenomenal lunches and breakfast. I was informed there is a new chef and that they cook everything in butter including the eggs, the vegetable they put in the eggs Etc. i'm very disappointed the whole point of going there was to get a healthy meal and having options to modify the menu. Myself along with a couple of my clients will no longer be going there. I myself cannot eat cow dairy I have a cow dairy allergy. A couple of my clients are intolerant so they won't be going back either. Hopefully management will make some changes and give people the option of using butter or oil. Makes no sense why the change was made.
Definitely got food poisoning after eating here and there was a hair in my food. My fiancé rice was also burnt. And over priced! Very disappointed
Got food poisoning within 30 minutes of finishing dinner after spending over 100$ on a bill won't ever be back

It pains me to give a business 2 stars but I have to. We walked in and they were not busy and told us it would be a 10 min wait. There were about 6 tables cleaned and empty. The hostess was very rude to the couple behind us. We order chips and salsa(that is not free) and they tasted as if they were sitting out for a week. I asked for no guacamole and they put it in my burrito anyway. Then when I told them I couldn't eat it, she said well you should of told me you were allergic to it and we wouldn't put it in there!? I think it'd the staff was more friendly our experience would of been way different. Other than the horrible chips the food was amazing. I would never go back to eat there but I would definitely order food to go.

Hi, thanks for making sure your tables are clean. And by making sure they're clean, I mean....well....Oh, wait. They weren't clean. Every table that wasn't occupied (so all but 3) were covered in crumbs and dishes. The staff stood and stared, gape-mouthed at us for about two minutes before doing anything. They seemed to be rather busy discussing to complexities of how to clean tables. Like, should we move the plates first or the silverware? And then, like, how do we wipe up the crumbs??? Oh nooooo, ugh. So you know, after a few minutes we confirmed that, yes. We are a party of two. The party of two that entered the restaurant after us also confirmed that they were a party of two. And then the waitress said "So....six of you?" COME ON. COME ON. How do you have a job if you can't add? Furthermore, how do you have a job if you fail to notice that my party of two has been in the restaurant for longer and is not associating or even standing near the OTHER party of two? COME ON. The menu is beyond boring and uninspiring. Whoa, cheese pizza? Whoaaaaa pepperoni. OMG NO WAY a Greek pizza? With olives? How cray-cray! And let me just say that ONE freaking vegan pizza does not a vegan restaurant make. If you're vegan and good at being a vegan, you know there are so many other options in Tampa that can do it better and cheaper. The dough on the pepperoni pizza tasted frozen and the pepperoni was actually really gross. And I looooove me some sliced tubular meat. The cheese blend was pretty decent, and I was a fan of the tomato sauce. And to those who are OHHHH MI GAWD GLUTEN FREE...I hope your delusional hipster asses noticed that the sausage isn't gluten free. Know why? Cuz it's made with fillers. So please just go live on a remote island somewhere and take your idiotic fad chain restaurants. Yeah, Pizza Fusion is an effing franchise. How trend setting. What concerns me most is the false belief that a chain restaurant that overcharges for mediocrity is somehow better than an independently owned busines. It's time people riding on the back of the "organic" movement get their heads out of their asses because it's become so suburban and mainstream that I might as well be eating at a damn Applebees, except the people sitting next to me at a place like Pizza Fusion are more annoying because they are so self-righteous and believing that they are treating mother earth right by eating this pizza. Come ON. The only reason to come here, really, is to drink. Their beer selection is good and affordable. And the service, though awkward, isn't inherently bad like some places.

I must of came here on a bad night, every thing was off. Super crowded and loud and just felt very unprepared. The restaurant advertises itself as a Chef owned and operated establishment and sometimes this can be a sign of caution. Our Hostess was very helpful in customizing a dish that my wife requested because of a allergy she has yet it arrived with extra sauce. She was able to deal with it, but should of had to. I might try this again in the future but not for a while.

The service was great but the freshness of the ingredients on the pizza was questionable. The gluten free crust tasted slightly doughy. The salad, however, was fresh and the shaved parmesan was a nice touch. The atmosphere is somewhere between an upscale pizza shop and a sportsbar with huge TVs.

ummm.... what did i eat and what did the rest of you yelpers eat?? I am NOT understanding how this place's rating is so high. maybe I cam on an off night, but I doubt it. UGH! In town for business, normally avoid anything that has a touristy spin to it, but since first time in Nashville and a quick trip from the hotel, I decided to check Opry backstage out. BIG Mistake! The food was GROSS! I have never had such awful mac n cheese in my life. very odd taste, flavors not well blended, tasted more butter than cheese, etc. The green beans were so overcooked, they pretty much were a clumped ball, the fried chicken was so-so, and the mashed potatoes were the only thing I could finish on my plate. Also, I literally put my order in with the server, and I swear, it was less than 1 minute when the server came out with my food. I said "whoa that was fast!" he didn't blink and walked away. Long story short... I'm not very good at telling my waiters that my food isn't good, so I just left my plate full - it looked pretty much the same as when It came out minus the mashed potatoes and one piece of chicken - and said "oh, I'm full." And now I feel a little ill as I type this. Hope it's psychological and I didn't get food poisoning to top it off...

Great Chicken Parm but the Spaghetti I didn't like at all. It was overcooked and didn't have a good flavor. Wasn't a case of the sauce it was the pasta. Wasn't impressed with their Soup either. The value for the $ though is stunning. Very very inexpensive and portion was large. Unfortunately tonight I feel like I have food poison coming on and that's all I ate today. Not accusing them, but if any others from it then now you know.

It was okay. There's lots of breakfast choices around that beat this place. The decor feels forced, likely trying to emulate the original. The whole place has a powerful smoked meat aroma, which was a bit overwhelming- was it purposeful or so they just need a better hood?! I got a custom omelette with some horrible commercial shipped tomatoes - I should have known better. No gluten free substitutes for the typical toast so I paid extra for the cheese grits which had a heavy smoky taste that became bothersome. Our server did well but wasn't very engaged with us. Overall it was overpriced and overhyped. Meh.

I've chosen this place many of times since the day it opened. I believe that the owner needs to be reminded that she is in the SERVICE "serve us" industry. Without patrons, your restaurant will fail. I have hardly been greeted with a smile, or even a "hello" for that matter. Having dined here enough, I know now that seating myself is the only way to be seated, even though there is no signage of how to be seated (which holds true from most reviews). After sitting down, it usually takes a good 3-5 minutes to be acknowledged and asked what I would like. I guess only 1 person is in charge of that since most of the time I see about 3 different servers walk right by without saying a word. The disorganization of this restaurant is clearly evident the more times you choose to come. I come here for one reason, the smoothies. I would say 30% of the time the blender is broken as they only have 1 blender.. One instance took 2-3 days to get the blender fixed! Go buy a new blender! The environment of this place is gloomy. No one smiles, including the owner who has a permanent frown. If there isn't music playing, you can hear the ceiling fans turning. The fans are also a problem because the lukewarm food turns to cool before you can take your first bite. Lastly, all portions are small and are becoming overpriced. I just paid $3.50 for a cupcake! The water (if they serve you it) is in a glass that could be considered a triple shot glass and most of the time I have had to pour my own. Any restaurant could opt to serve vegan, gluten free, dairy free, or hair free food. This place is most consistent at serving smile free and friendly free food. Get it together. I do sometimes feel like if I had more of a "hipster"ish look or vibe about me that I'd be better served. I know I tip well so other than the lack of dressing to fit the Cafe's style, I do not know why their service is so terrible.

The signs for "Top 100 Chinese restaurants in America" should probably include the fine print of "...as voted by white people." Quiet location in a strip plaza with a full bar, family-friendly booth/table layout, and clean bathrooms. I was in the mood for mapotofu, double cooked pork, and duck. Instead, our friendly Malaysian server with great English insisted we wouldn't want to try any of those, but that the General Tso's chicken was "their signature dish" and perhaps the Hunan pork would be a suitable alternate protein dish. I stared at him in disbelief before caving, thinking it would be better to be underwhelmed than have food poisoning on the way back. Complimentary fried wonton noodles served with sweet and sour sauce. I somewhat regretted going for the roast Hunan pork, since the cuts were a bit dry. Vegetables used were fresh, where applicable. Chicken was garnished with steamed broccoli. Pork included snow peas, sliced carrot, baby corn, halved broccoli florets, chopped green bell pepper, button mushrooms, chopped onion, and garlic. Other than that, most things tasted of the generic brown sauce on both dishes. Fresh rice, good pot of hot tea readily refilled upon request. Enough leftovers for lunch the next day. Would be reluctant to go back if they can't be confident in their more legit menu items.

I don't get it this place has a lot of good reviews, but our meal, and service was terrible. Then we ended the night by finding a huge cockroach. If we don't all wake up with food poisoning I'll be amazed!
I've been to the Green Hills Mall before. There's better preppy BBQ in Kansas City. ps: Gluten free dude, just order meat and don't use the sauce.

Typical Trader Joes, from what I've experienced. I have always had a good experience here and the staff is usually in a good mood and very friendly, as well as funny. I usually use Trader Joes to supplement my usually grocery trips to Giant, I would not shop exclusively at Trader Joes. They have a tasty selection of soy yogurt and non-dairy ice creams, great for lactose-intolerant types like myself!

The pizza is pretty decent and I like that they have a gluten free crust! The downside is that the gluten free crust is only prepared in a medium size, so if you are ordering for a large group, the combo deals are out. Oh well. And I would not say that this is "thin crust" pizza - it's more like medium thickness, but the toppings are fresh and the sauce is good. They also serve chicken, which I haven't tried, but it smells good while they are frying it!
Super greasy and burgers fall apart and don't even fit on the damn bun. Yeah they have gluten free buns a plus but sub standard and flavorless greasy food. Charcoals is far superior go there.

Ever since this joint opened up i've been itching to try it, mainly because many nights i've had some drunk cravings for pho, but a lot, if not all, pho places in edmonton close before 11. Miss Saigon is open late on weekdays, and until 4am on weekends!!! CRAZY! I came here with my boyfriend, unfortunately he was recovering from food poisoning the night before, so he wasn't too hungry or ready to eat. Bless his soul though, he forced himself to eat regardless since he knew I wanted to try it. The parking isn't ON whyte ave, so it made it easy to park without having to worry about paying. They have their own parking lot shared with other stores! The decor inside is light bulb themed with some booths and some half booth half tables. Smaller than I had anticipated but still nicely decorated! The sizes here are larger than other places. The regular size at Miss Saigon is a large any place else, and the regular is only $10 dollars! The broth was good, I could tell that they simmered the spices and bones for a long time. The broth itself is really hearty, but had a little too much cilantro for my liking, none the less, still good! They have a big wall painted with chalkboard paint that showed all the spices and things they put inside the broth (such a cute idea!) Another popular item I wanted to try was the bubble tea that came in the light-up light bulbs. I tried the original milk tea, which was a bit too sweet for my liking. The tapioca was soft and chewy though. The next time I have a hankering for late-night vietnamese food, I'm definitely coming back to Miss Saigon :)

We've been regular customers for the past 6 years. Since the new management some 2 years back the place has deteriorated. While the menu is the same, the physical state of the restaurant has become unbearable. Our last visit was on December 29 for lunch and when I went to the washroom to wash my hands I nearly vomited! The toilets were so filthy literally with poop. Toilet paper all over the floors and honestly how safe does one feel eating in such an evironment where cleanliness is no important? I just hope their staff properly scrub their hands after washroom breaks. Another issue was the slow service. Only 2 people to serve all the tables. And at the time the place was packed to overflow capacity. A few times our orders were missed. We marked them on the "eat all you can" menu and they didn't come. We had to flag down the server to check whether our food was coming. Be careful also as they would make mistakes of giving you items which were for other tables. Overall a disappointment. I hope they get their act together and improve on these things. And please clean up the place.

My parents got deathly ill after eating mussels here Tuesday night and had to cancel their 4th of July celebration at my house with the children . One had mussels red one had mussels white with a Coors Lite each. For some strange reason both ended up in the emergency room after one day and a half of vomiting and diarrhea . They were given IV fluids , blood work , X-rays , ultrasounds and medication for nausea. I emailed this establishment on Facebook but they were unresponsive . I followed up with a phone call to the restaurant and got through to a manager who most graciously telephoned my Dad to discuss what happened . There is no explanation as to why the mussels at Chickies and Pete's Packer Avenue landed my parents in the emergency room . How can this be? Will be a very long long time, probably never before anyone eats mussels ever again . Thanks to whomever poisoned my parents .

Went to celebrate a friends birthday and have wings and beer on a Saturday evening. The wings are very spendy at $1 each so we hoped they would be good. Absolutely the worst wings I have ever had in my life. They were more like jerky than wings. Dry beyond belief and not very large for the price. The service was sub par considering that there were only about 10 people total in the place and it took 15 minutes to get our beers. The worst part was the next morning when my wife and I felt like we had mild food poisoning and had to stay near the bathroom all day. I will not be going back to this place, EVER!

I really wanted to like Raz'z. I really did. But they didn't make it easy. My husband and I stopped here before a movie about 6:30 on a Tuesday night, and the atmosphere was great--business casual, with several tables filled with what looked like after-work dinners or business meetings. The room was lit dimly and each table had a candle. I felt a little underdressed in my jeans, but soon noticed a few other patrons wearing similar attire so I relaxed. As a vegetarian I was happy to see several options available to me, including a vegetarian pasta, a veggie burger and, sadly on Fridays only, a vegetarian lasagna. I opted for the vegetarian pasta al fresca and my husband ordered the beef lasagna. But then, trouble started. As he was eating his house salad, my husband discovered he was chewing on a shrimp tail--and he's very allergic to shrimp. Then, as he was eating his lasagna, he not only pulled out several pieces of gristle but an inch-long piece of what appeared to be plastic. My pasta al fresca, which was described as including a "medley of vegetables," only had broccoli and carrots, which were undercooked and almost impossible to bite through. The chef and our server apologized for the shrimp incident, although they were conflicted as to how it could have happened (our server told us seafood and lettuce are chopped in separate areas of the kitchen and never come in contact; the chef told us they are both chopped side-by-side next to the sink). We weren't upset, just a little surprised and wanted to bring it to the server's attention, but they both were very apologetic. As an apology, our server offered us a complimentary walnut-brownie dessert, but unfortunately my husband doesn't eat walnuts. She didn't offer up any of their other desserts instead, so I accepted the brownie. I'd like to say it ended happily, but the brownie was so hard I would have had to use my knife if I wanted to eat most of it. I ate as much as I could, and we decided to cut our losses and leave. It's unfortunate that we had a bad experience at a restaurant with such a great menu, cool atmosphere and friendly wait staff, because I would have loved to have been able to leave them a great review. At this point, I'm not sure if we're going to return. One problem with the food is enough, but finding shrimp tails, gristle and plastic all in the same meal seems like a symptom of a larger issue.

We've been here quite a few times and have always loved our pizza! I always order take out, so I can't speak for their service, but their staff is always friendly, both over the phone and when I pick up my pie, I know I can always get a bunch of red pepper flake and parmesan packets! Their specialty pizzas are both creative and delicious! We've gotten their Muffuletta, Philly Cheesesteak, Sgt Pepper, Italian Club, The Krewe (formerly called Sweep the Floor, I personally am glad for the name change, the old name gave me unplesant mental images!), Bacon Cheeseburger, and Angry Pig pizzas, as well as the Deluxe Combination as a calzone, and have built our own pizzas, usually pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, and jalapeño. They have all been amazing! They also offer a gluten free crust for their medium (12 inch) pizza for only $1 more (Bringing the cost of a specialty to $15.99, and $10.49 for the starting price of the build your own 12 inch), which is great since I am super gluten sensitive, as is my son (I don't have celiac, so have never asked if they are prepared on seperate pans from the other doughs, although I've never had the pain I tend to get from cross contamination). You can also get a whole wheat dough for no extra charge. They offer a 20% military discount, and if you sign up for their emails, you will get a coupon for a free pizza for your birthday, good for a week before the date until the week after! I do wish they had some gluten free appetizers, maybe an option to get sliced veggies with the hummus and spinach artichoke dip, or making the meatball app gluten free. I'm not certain about the sauces for the wings (which are baked and not breaded), but would like to try them some time if they're gluten free!

Red Mesa used to be one of my favorite restaurants; the food is amazing. My problem is with the way the restaurant handles mistakes they make in the kitchen. If you ask for the kitchen to leave something off of your food, and they put it on by mistake, they just wipe it off and send it back without regard for food allergies. I'm really disgusted and I will NEVER return.

If you can swat enough flies out of your face to see clearly, you'll spot that the majority (greater than 50%) of what they have is covered in mold. Save yourself some time, trouble & food poison and walk a few blocks to Sue's.

I came in two days ago, on Thursday night. The man behind the counter seemed like he couldn't wait to go home even though they weren't closing for two more hours. He said very little to me, and once I was done ordering, slapped my cut of tuna on the counter in front of me, gave me my total, took my money and then turned around as if he was done with me (only one other customer was in the store, being served by a different cashier). When I asked for ice for the way home, he seemed irritated. But I can ignore the lack of proper customer service... what I can't ignore though, is the food poisoning my significant other got from the fish. When I placed my order I asked for sushi grade ahi tuna. When I saw him grab the fish, I specifically asked if it was good for sushi, to eat raw. He assured me that it was, and when he gave it to me, said nothing regarding suggestions for proper handling of raw fish. I got home and immediately rinsed the fish and made the intended dish with the fish (ahi poke). My boyfriend ate it the next day for lunch, and has been in the bathroom ever since. It has been over 24 hours and his stomach is still upset. We will not be back.

I've been here a few times. The food is good, but my recent experience last weekend was very unpleasant. I had dinner with my friend who introduced me to the restaurant and has dined there at least 5 times; in fact she was greeted by the manager when she arrived. Our visit was marred and unpleasant because of our very rude server Amber. My friend asked for her daughter's burger to be cooked in a separate frying pan because she has celiac disease (the restaurant had done this before for both a burger and I believe eggs). Our server, proceeded to argue with us that they don't do this. My friend asked the server to ask the chef, indicating that the chef had done it in the past. When the server returned she told us that the chef would do it this time, but proceeded to tell us that the chef said he never recalled doing it and that he couldn't do it again. She also added that he was very busy and it was hard for him to do it. Really, did the server have to argue with us? Make us feel bad? Even our 12 year old daughters recognized how rude she was. When it came time for dessert -- 12 year old girls love dessert - our server argued with us again about the ice cream and blueberries (that we had ordered before) so we gave up and went somewhere else. My friend, determined to make this right so she could feel better about dining here again, asked to speak with the manager but was told he was too busy to speak with us. I live in Queen Village, like this location and frankly, I like the Whetstone salad a lot. Not sure I can bring myself to go back right now.

We've been coming to Josef's for years - like many locals (and travelers) have done. This trip was different - hence, the review. Our daughter was recently married and our new son-in-law has a severe allergy to nuts - we've never had to consider baking standards or ingredient lists before him. He went to their website and was very happy to see a section specifically for food allergies. It allowed him to easily browse the amazing baked goods without concern for a trip to the ER or an epi pen to the chest a la Pulp Fiction (yes, I know that's not how they're given). I'll forgo drafting the obvious posts about how amazing their coffee and baked good were because from this establishment, it's a given.

My son is very sick currently (possible food poisoning) after we dined there. Make sure your burgers are WELL DONE before your child consumes any meats there. You'll hate to have your child vomit 5 times in 6 hours because he can't hold anything down after you've ate there. Our Waitress was decent, but the cooks don't know the difference between medium & Medium well, let alone to refresh the order completely after we made the complaint. Went from Garlic butter to plain-as-Day Steak. We will not be returning to this location, period.

So me and some friends went to Liberty Bar after work and it's fairly small but a nice atmosphere. The bartenders were great especially Chris and the staff was welcoming. My biggest complaint is the food was tainted. My friends and I had food poisoning. I would be happy if it was a hung over but no an upset stomach and illness was not a good sign.A practice of hand washing and making sure the food is properly handled would be great. Ugh

First visit to this little spot. Was excited to see a burger spot with local sourced food, coffee, and beverage. However they missed the mark. We purchased the build your own burger, which came back with lettuce and mayo on the bun which was not ordered.....this would not be a issue.... except it was my picky child.... I ordered the steak sandwich with a gluten free bun and sweet potato fries. Which came back with a regular bun and regular fries. They did correct these issues and the food came out in a timely manner. As for the service, our server seemed to have tooo many tables. He seemed rushed with every stop. Our drinks sat empty for quite a while. The manager walked by several times, looked at our empty cups and did nothing.... not the best first visit. However I believe in second chances. Atmosphere was great and the Patio cant be beat.

There's no way not to love buying only what you need when you need it! Who needs to store 20lbs of flour?! Not me! And gluten free. The selection is really good and kept away (mostly) from accidental cross contamination. Did you know the scoops w/yellow zip ties are usually reserved for gluten free? They are cleaned daily too. They work hard to keep it as safe as they can. Sales! Oh yes, coupons on the website or promos where you get $5 gift card for spending $15! I can say a few prices aren't cheaper than the store (instant powdered skim milk) but I don't have to make an extra trip. Spices, bird seed, candy, popcorn, chips, ever single last thing you could ever need for cake decorating, did you know they rent cake pans?! Sure you can buy them, but you don't have to. Piñatas, Xmas cookie boxes, ready to decorate ginger bread houses and cookies... this is your party headquarters. Wedding supplies? Cake toppers... the list is endless!d

When we moved here we were amazed by the amount of business this place got. We finally decided to try it when family visited. The wait is usually pretty long, but that does not warrant low reviews. In fact, that usually means it's a great place! They seated us at a sticky table, never came to refill coffee cups and served up cold food. Thinking it was just a fluke we went back months later only to be seated in a room that smelled like vomit. The server was rude when we asked to be moved - we even offered to wait until a table in another part opened. The third (and) final visit had a very nice server but cold food again.

Probably the worst seafood house I've ever been to. I've never waited so long to get my food. Literally there for 2 1/2 hours. Then absolutely the worst fish tacos over had. To top it all off I somehow got food poisoning.

Finding a good restaurant with vegan options in a new town can be difficult. Siam Elephant was intriguing and within walking distance from our hotel, so we decided to give it a try. Siam Elephant is a Thai restaurant, which raised some concerns for me as someone with severe peanut allergies. In addition, I'm vegan, so the customer service would be put to a test. We alerted the waiter that I had a peanut allergy in addition to my vegan diet, and asked if any dishes could be altered to suit me. The waiter told us that they could practically do anything, and we went on with our order. He was very helpful while we ordered, as he listed each non-vegan ingredient in each dish and asked us if we wanted to substitute or take it out. The overall ordering experience was pleasant, as he was very thorough in making sure we knew what each dish contained. When the food arrived, the true test began. I had seen reviews about the restaurant being insensitive to allergies, which worried me. Whenever I consume any food I am allergic to, I immediately get a reaction. Ready to grab my epi-pen, I took my first bite of the Spicy Noodle dish... And I let out a huge sigh of relief. The foods were exactly as we had ordered. Everything was vegan, meat subbed with tofu, with no trace of a peanut in sight. Confident in the food, I dug in and devoured most of the meal. The actual flavors of the food were delicious. Everything was well-balanced and seasoned nicely. The Spicy Noodle dish was delicious with the mix of hot rice noodles and bell peppers. The special at the time, Tempura Avocado, was also delicious and I'd recommend to anyone that likes avocados to snatch it if available. The Coconut soup was also extremely good, not to mention the overall presentation. Pro Tip for vegans/lactose intolerants: the Thai Tea Boba comes with half-and-half. However, just alert the waiter about your veganism/intolerance and ask to sub for coconut milk. Tastes just as good! Overall, the experience here was gosh-darn amazing and it would be my first choice if I ever returned. I recommend it to anybody, as there are so many versatile options that the waiters are willing to tweak.

So... My family and I have been here multiple times over the years and the food is very basic, but good and reliable. Which is actually hard to find. Until Chuys Tex came in down the road. My husband lived in Dallas and it's a great go to. That being said we decided to give these guys one last shot to handle it, and they completely fell on their face. We walked in and seated, got our complimentary chips and salsa, order the special jumbo margarita, also some queso with beef. Which came out completely cold. So we sent back... which they proceeded to I am going to assume "microwave" it and bring it back, but this time with a friend... I am going to assume a nose hair or something comparable ( it was extremely coarse)... So we have now decided to leave. Because that's gross, and I can only imagine what our food is now going to come out like. As we are trying to get the servers attention (who was actually very nice) the manager try's to serve us again with the same queso Really?!?! To be quite honest they've pushed the 3 star rating, and quite frankly after this visit they don't deserve 1. We will never be back, let's all pray we don't get food poisoning

Stopped at this location (River/La Canada) the last Saturday Am, ordered myself a cheese and "scrambled egg" wrapped in a four tortilla for breakfast, ordered a pico de Gallo burger and asked to have the lime cilantro sauce to be put on the side through the drive through. Understandably the wait was a little longer since the location is basically only the drive-through, what I got was evidently egg carton egg food mix eggs on a tortilla some kind, no cheese. The pico de Gallo Burger was not made as as pictured in the ad ad run on TV by Whataburger,it only had one burger Patty( TV ad shows 2) the Pico de Gallo was extremely dry and old looking, and my husband didn't feel well after he ate the damn thing. I totally did not put the cilantro lime juice sauce on the side as I ask. They had it listed as dry. It seems like the girl that was taking the order through the drive-through speaker was not paying attention to what I was saying to her. 30 to 45 minutes after I ate my breakfast thing, my stomach cramped up violently and I and I vomited and "number 2 d " whatever that breakfast thing was out of my system. Food poisoning ( I think the eggs were bad) , but I was so hungry after doing my morning nursing visits that I just ate it. Moral of the story: find another Whataburger, the sad thing is this location is less than 1/4 mile from My house. Never again. I will go the the Whataburger on Speedway. They listen.

I came here to eat with my children. They were served undercooked chicken tenders! Sadly I had noticed AFTER my 3 year old had almost finished the two tenders! I got ahold of the manager and he offered me a 25% discount...WTF?! Then he came to our table a second time telling us we don't have to pay for our meal tonight. Needless to say I lost my appetite and could not eat my dinner. I'm still waiting to see if my sons have any symptoms of food poisoning...I SHOULD HAVE NEVER EVER GONE THERE. I knew we should have gone to The Cheesecake Factory instead.

I didn't care for the place and it didn't live up to the current 4 star review on yelp. We took my sister here for a thank you dinner because of the reviews and it was new since I moved away from Edmonton. Nice decor and central location. Service needs a ton of work. There was no hostess at the door and I waited for several minutes before anyone came around to seat me. Our server at the table was terrible. She had a hard time handling special requests such as a nut allergy and vegetarian diet, and the timing of the courses was terrible... who brings appetizers when we're still eating the bread course, and then my sister gets her entree while she's still working on her salad! Drinks ran empty several times during the meal. The food is average at best. Maybe I came on an off night, but honestly, the best part of the meal was the bread service, which was a popover style bread served in a large measuring cup. Really cute presentation. However, the items ordered were 'meh'. We had a variety of dishes including salads, ravioli, fish, mushroom risotto, and bison. The risotto was too saucy and the fish was quite bland. Ravioli was decent and the bison was average... Given the price point ($30-$35 an entree), the issues noted should not occur. My sister had a tart for dessert but the rest of us passed given the mediocre food to that point. I left my e-mail for them to follow-up regarding my comments, and to date, there has been no contact from the restaurant. Skip this if you need to impress or say thanks. There are much better places in town.

i feel like i am literally going to choke on my own vomit every time i see a dominos box after my experience here!!!!!! so so so gross and disgusting and greasy and it made my stomach hurt. i think they don't wash their hands. i got food poisoning. there were rats.

Checked out Delicia last night with some girlfriends celebrating a late birthday dinner with me. Very nice atmosphere and ambience and the food was good as well. Our server was ok, not too attentive, but he was friendly. Menu was pretty limited we had some food allergies at the table and they didn't have any options to accommodate those. We worked it out and still had a good time. I will visit again.

A HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT! I took my girlfriend and her brother here for my girlfriend's birthday. We have been wanting to come here for several years now, given the ghost history of this place. I made reservations over a month in advanced, and made sure to ask for the best table possible not in the middle of the room. When we get there, we are greeted and then taken to a table in the middle of the room, in very close proximity to another table. The host didn't even mention where the table was or ask if it was okay. While we were looking at our menus, the waiter from the close table next to us kept pushing his butt into my girlfriend! I then got up to speak to a manager, who of course, didn't care to accommodate us at all. I asked if he did anything for birthdays and he said he would try. What does that even mean? Honestly, worst customer service and idiot staff. When we ordered, our waitress Liz didn't care about my girlfriend's gluten allergy. When we asked about which bottle of wine to get, she was snarky and impatient. We asked if we could try a sip and she laughed in a rude way and gave us attitude. That was her the entire night. We ordered the shrimp and grits and the duck jambalaya. Both very mediocre. I spent over $200 and would have been better off at McDonald's. Regardless of the money, worst customer service and staff. DO NOT GO HERE! They rip you off and use their location and ghost history to their advantage!

Creamy, yummy, goodness! After a hot day at the beach and relaxing in the pool, we stopped in for a cool treat at Uncle Andy's Ice Cream Parlor. The ice cream was delightful, portion sizes were generous and overall delicious with a capital D! We ordered a total of 6 different flavors in ice cream cones & in cups with additional candy toppings to sweeten our treats. We needed a little extra help and appreciated the extra care given to our order because of peanut allergies... a fresh batch of cookie dough was brought out with a clean scoop to ensure no cross contamination occurred. The 2 young men servers were 100% awesome no only taking our "to go food" orders and dished up our ice cream, they also talked with our kids and made the night memorable.

This is the worst gluten free pizza EVER - you should just say you don't have it instead of serving a pre-made shell with some canned tomatoes and cheese thrown on it. I complained to the girl at the counter and she didn't seem to care - wouldn't do anything except give me her boss's number. The pizza even comes in the aluminum pan the pre-made crust comes in - way too much money for something that just doesn't taste right. Never again!

Dudes, this was so bad I'm writing a review to help you out. Because you have a good idea, great location, cheap prices and big portions. But oy, the food. Do any of your chefs taste what's going out to customers? My guess is No. Let's start with the seasoning. There's none! Look, I knew I wasn't getting authentic Mexican when I saw the playful Queso Americana on the menu. (American cheese in 2018? Really?). But no salt or pepper? Let me backtrack. The carnivore in the family ordered the chicken cheese bacon burrito. The pescatarian ordered a whitefish burrito with aioli. We got them to go. We get them home. They're not labeled. Okay, should be no problem, right? I mean, all we had to do was unwrap them. Should be easy to ascertain chicken bacon cheese from fish aioli, right? Err, wrong. They looked exactly the same! We tentatively sniffed. Absolutely no aroma. Finally, we dug into one with a fork and after digging and digging, we extracted a limp piece of fish. "Are you sure?" I asked nervously, not having eaten meat in 9 years. "Hope so!" said my husband, who is allergic to fish. We took a bite. "Ew," we said simultaneously. "This has absolutely no taste. It's rice and beans without even salt stuffed in a doughy cold burrito," I said. "No flavor at all," my husband agreed. Unfortunately, not the same could be said for the twice fried potatoes, or rocks covered in a container of dollar store garlic powder. I can't even. Suffice it to say that one fell on the floor with a thud and for the first time ever, the dog spit something out. Dudes dudes dudes. There is no reason for food this bad in 2018 and it's almost impossible to screw up a burrito. Get your act together!
Two words. Food poisoning. Had the Chicken. Service was great, enjoyed the atmosphere however defecating while simultaneously vomiting on the side of the road to make it home was life changing.

Checked out this store for the 1st time over the weekend. I generslly shop at Aldi and I'm not exactly into healthier foods so I am probablt not the target audience for this store...but I get the ad every week and it always has good deals and cool stuff. So I stopped in to grab a couple produce items and shop around a bit. The meat counter employee was proactive and helpful- he offered tips on how to cook a few items I hadn't seen before and asked about. I liked the bulk shopping area and enjoyed checking out different food varieties. The produce section looked amazing- i purchased some bell peppers and lemons and they tasted great. Also- if you have a gluten free dietary restriction this is a great place to shop- lots of options including cool baked treats like brownies and cookies. I gave it a 3 because i wasn't impressed overall with the staff. I was looking for a few things I can't get from Aldi but was hoping to get here. I asked a couple of employees where general foods were and they didnt know (ex. Cooking sauces/oils). One employee told me its not her section so she wouldn't know. I did find an employee thay helped me but didn't seem too familiar with the options on the shelf. Overall if the employees are "on the floor" I expect them to be able to point me in the right direction or say they need to find out and ask a colleague for help.

I went in to try and get a fruit bowl. I didn't want cucumber cause I'm allergic to it and I wanted chamoy, lime, and tajin added on but since there was only one worker she said she can't make a customized bowl because it's only her. I would understand if other people were in the store but it was just me and her and she wasnt doing other things.. I just feel like it would of been easy to pull out the cucumber in the prepackaged fruit bowls and throw some lime and stuff on top real quickly but idk I guess not. Disappointed but I'm getting my fruit bowl so off to another spot I go lmaoo

It makes me kinda sad to have to update my review after a string of really bad experiences at Red Habanero. This used to be our weekly "go to" and have found that since a few key staff members have left the taste and quality of the food, the service, and the attention to detail went downhill quickly. It seems that our food has not come out right for at least the past 5 visits -- if not more. This wouldn't be a huge deal if my hubs didn't have a true allergy, but I would like to keep him around for a bit longer. Tonight we have seen our waiter 3 times -- when we sat down, when the food came (wrong), and I am hoping the third will be eventually when he brings the check as it's been a while -- I have been finished with my meal and had the time to re-write this review ... Sorry Red Habanero -- we tried to give you the benefit of the doubt ... 5 times in a row is just too much. (And no, we still don't have our check)

My wife and I haven't been out together, without the kids for a while so on a whim we were able to get a sitter, and arrange some adult time we tried a couple of places and saw you had availability on opentable - great! Were in So I'll start by saying that the blue crab dip is phenomenal. I would almost go back just for that, but to be honest thats where you hit your crescendo. It was a fast downhill from there. Next course was your seafood gumbo. I've never in my life described soup as tepid before but it was tepid (gumbo is not soup) not hot, not cold but like someone turned off the burner an hour ago and just said "go with it". Had the waiter been at all attentive I would have honestly sent it back. Finally we come to your veal parm. I love pasta, cheese and veal, this is almost the perfect dish for me. The problems started with the waiters thumb on the plate top. I had to make a mental note not to eat anything that touched there.... The veal was overcooked, not burned just a little over done for my liking. Honestly it would have been fine if not for the fact that you managed to undercook the pasta, and somehow now use any salt at all? I mean I was looking forward to my angel hair after I ordered it an could maybe stomach five bites..... If your going to do fried seafood just do that, the other stuff on the menu was obviously put there either to appease someone, or because you thought what else can we fry and not screw up.....I would just call it. If I was desperate for food and in your neighborhood, and allergic to greek, there's a burger king down the road with higher standards.

Only giving it 1 star because I can't give zero. I have been here a few times before and always order the exact same thing. This afternoon I got lunch and got extremely sick about 3 hours after eating. Our plating looked different from usual (assuming it could be a different chef or something) and the cooked fish did not seem fresh at all. I recall three friends of mine all getting sick from here about a year and never took it seriously until now. This isn't just a simple nausea from eating a lot, I am genuinely extremely ill and am positive it is food poisoning. Never eating here again and may be turned away from sushi for a long time. Recommend just going to the real deal on magazine or just getting something else if you're in Elmwood.

On 2/20/16, I encountered this place that my friends raved about. Once we were seated the waitress brought water to the table OMG the PLASTIC cup was cloudy, Grease was floating on top of my water made me want to VOMIT. I asked for a to go cup of water she said those cups are not allowed on The tables in the dining room but she did give me a straw to drink my GREASY CLOUDY WATER. I have no idea how the food taste. All 8 of us left went around the corner to Jerry Bobs, the food was great got my water with my meal in a to go cup. Everyone does not drink from plastic ware. For me the impression I got from Brawleys made me VOMIT

Very disappointed. Walked in with an outside vendor's food only because I have an allergy. My entire family of 8 was getting food and I was asked to leave and wait in the car by someone working at your coffee station. She was very rude even after I informed her that I had an allergy and would like to stay with my family who was all ordering there. She even said I can't move the stools I was standing by? And I hadn't moved them. Not sure what her issue was. So disappointing as I wait in the car for my family to get their food.

The food here is great as always - if you can get it! Service terrible. After the standard wait time of 45 min, we were told it's going to take another 30 minutes. 25 minutes later, we are told gluten free pizza is not available. Thanks for all the great management and service.

This is a different review bc it addresses high staff turnover in fast food industry with minimal if any ability or investment by owner and management to assure a certain quality of staff and food with no real oversight of either. At customer level, which is me (but could be you!) the take home message is you eat and interact with staff at your risk and I do NOT use "risk" in light manner. This HIGHLY upsetting began one week ago today when I ordered their "2 for $6" special and Upon arriving home discovered a third item not in the usual carton but wrapped in aluminum foil which upon opening revealed it was NOT MY ORDER but a pepperoni (or lookalike) sandwich with few bites eaten! My daughter warned me to throw everything out (which I did) and to contact the store which I did and spoke with a woman manager who seemed attentive and apologetic. She promised a full refund. Most customers would never return no matter how much of an inducement provided. I did expect a follow up call by management on this matter bc this was definitely not a typical situation of customer dissatisfaction with THEIR ORDER but represented a case of essentially a foreign object "contaminating" your food if not physically but then psychologically. Yes some review was reasonable and yes I REASONABLY expected some follow up to me. NOPE NOT HERE. I took pictures of the offending item and shared them with the manager and do so again here. Consider me too naive for my own good but I went back for the promised refund and willing to give THIS Arby a second change because of a long fond attachments to the brand and its iconic Jamocha shake dating back to 1967 (!!!) as a HS senior. I proceeded to order and apply my refund. Instead I was forced to interact with a staff person who behaved in a challenging manned to a SENIOR customer!! He asserted the extra item could not come from Arby's and looked like a pizza shop product implying it was a situation I created. At one point he challenged me to show my receipt! Again we're talking a total bill of $6 and change and I was treated as the accused party. This front line worker was not a manatee and I'm not sure if he had any authority to even get involved. The expected mature response would have been to call the manager who was aware of this situation and conclude it UNEVENTFULLY. That was the lowest level of acceptable resolution and even this was a total failure in the way this worker OUTRAGEOUSLY behaved. Of course more could've and should've been done. Even at a fast food tier of business serious mature management exist to conduct a credible in house review and report back to the customer often with refunds COMMENSURATE TO THE NATURE AND SERIOUSNESS OF THE INCIDENT.
