They are protective of their reputation as high end fine dining destinations. ACCORDINGLY, THEY RESPOND PROACTIVELY AND CREDIBLY TO ANY CUSTOMER. THIS RESTAURANT DID NEITHER WHICH TELLS YOU EVERYTHING ABOUT THEIR LACK OF PROFESSIONALISM. Instead they seem to hire certain staff who behave confrontationally from the outset. YES we all know fast food staff turnover had broken records before the pandemic and it was common knowledge as well that any warm body was hired on the spot out of desperation and without background checks or drug testing. But the better places don't have situations end like this where a senior is reduced to yelling to protect his good name. BETTER RESTAURANTS EVEN FAST FOOD REFLECT BETTER OWNERS WHO ENFORCE BETTER POLICIES PERIOD. To date I never received any semblance of a credible in house review and doubt I ever will. Instead I was forced into a belligerent exchange at age 72. My advice at the very beginning of this detailed review stands: eat, and engage with staff of CERTAIN fast food restaurants AT YOUR RISK. I won't henceforth be anywhere around this one much less order from it. I'm even uncomfortable walking on its long block. That's how shaken I remain hours after this interaction and I'm a genuine understanding and forgiving people. NOT THIS TIME WITH THIS BUSINESS. GOOD LUCK IF YOU GO HERE. You have been forewarned.

Food poison alert!!! Food tasted awful. Eggs were cold, and tasted like it has gone bad. I am getting ready to submit a formal complaint to the health department. When asked about items on the menu, Waitress/owner's daughter was rude, made snarky comments, and had lots of attitude during service. The Apple does not fall far from the tree.

This is still my favorite location. Just recently the orders have been wrong alot, most recently in the last 2 days. Yesterday wasn't a big deal because it was just lemonade missing. Today is an issue because I've only had 1/4 of my drink and feel sick because the wrong milk was used. Mistakes happen but 2 days in a row and people have severe allergies, luckily I didn't drink it all and it will pass but please starbucks pay attention a little closer. (Plus we pay extra for these things) 1 Star- Total failure of an experience based on this experience would not return. Would not recommend. 2 Star- Below average on several levels, not a total failure. Wouldn't seek out to return or recommend. 3 Star- Average experience, minimum expectations met. Nothing that says wow or that stands out. Would return if someone else wanted to come, not a regular go to. 4 Star- Above average experience, will come here again and recommend to friends and family. 5 Star- This will be a regular go to and will be highly recommended to people I know. Exceeds expectations on a consistent basis.
These people do not handle food with proper care! I immediately threw up after eating a sandwich I ordered. Like WTF????? The meat must've been old.. NEVER AGAIN!!
Was there 10/30/21, got food poisoning and was wiped out for 5 days. Had wine, clams and raw oysters. Should have know better - oysters tasted odd. Won't be going back.

Went here and had catfish and sides... violently sick the day after horrible stomach pains. Food poisoning fo sure. Please check out the Department of Health's website and look at Piccadilly's inspection: http://inspections.eatsafe.la.gov/ Thank God my two year old didnt get sick like I did. My family will NOT be returning here. http://inspections.eatsafe.la.gov/Summary.aspx?accountID=26-0044763&pageIndex=0&pageSize=20&All=Piccadilly

The positives: I didn't get norovirus or e-coli after eating here. That's always a plus, right? Giving your customers possibly life threatening illnesses HAS to be really bad for business... Build your burrito/taco/bowl your way with choice of meat, fillings and sauces.Their business model is successful and has been copied by everything from sandwiches to pizza. The food tastes OK. It's good, not great. As long as you stay away from flour tortillas, most of their menu is gluten free. That's a plus for my wife when we're looking for something fast and easy that could potentially be eaten on the go. The negatives: Portions - I don't like filler in my burritos so I ask for no rice, beans or anything besides meat in my burrito. At least one attentive person recognized that I was gonna get a twig-skinny carnitas burrito and offered to just charge me for a side of carnitas. I give that guy four stars. Add-ons - two bucks for a side of chips and salsa. Mexican food is supposed to come with chips and salsa and you're not supposed to be charged for it. I think it's a law in some states. I can understand charging extra for guac, but that same two bucks is still a little steep for a tiny cup of the stuff. Chipotle will do in a pinch and, if we're in a hurry, we'll hit it up, but there are a couple of other really good Mexican places close to me where I'd rather get my taco, burrito or chips and salsa fix.

This restaurant took about 2 hours to get our food out. Even the drinks took 30 minutes to come out and nothing was above average. Nothing on the menu was worth the wait except for the mac and cheese bites. I ordered a cobb salad and the dressing tasted expired and gross. I would not recommend this place for anyone with a gluten allergy as the options were limited. The shirley temple and fries were the only things I enjoyed during my dining.

I would give this place zero stars if I could. This establishment has the worst customer service. My mother has severe celiac disease and she made the waitress very aware of her allergy before ordering a meal she has ordered a ton of times prior and has had no reaction. Tonight they put relish on her burger which is not gluten free and she did not order this relish and when she asked for the ingredients so she could prepare herself for the type of reaction she'd have and the manager said she was to busy to help her and that it wasn't her problem. So my mother was so beside herself because she has eaten a food she is allergic too and has now been told that her concern is not important. She orders the same gluten free burger everytime and they had the audacity to tell her she should have read the menu. Their website says they take allergies very serious. clearly they do not. The customer service is beyond awful. The waitress never came to our table and messed up multiple of our orders. If you have any type of food allergy do not go here. You're health is not a concern of Red Robin establishments.

Verdict: A good brunch spot to try new things Atmosphere / decor - 4 Service - 3 Food - 4 Location - 3.5 Value - 3 Overall 3.5 We got here an hour before close on Sunday and still had a half hour wait which surprised me. The front deck was open but the heaters were broken so it was cold in the shade. You can order drinks and pastries while waiting so we got tea and coffee. I was immediately disappointed with the fact that they only have orange juice for the mimosas. It was a good mimosa but I thought they would have at least one other juice to mix. The drinks took a little bit of time to come out but it gave us time to decide on food. I am lactose intolerant which usually isn't a problem anywhere but it was difficult here. We got the grits with the works and I asked if it had milk in it. Our waiter said yes so I figured it was mixed in. Then he mentioned that it was ricotta on top that had the dairy but that couldn't be removed or placed in a side bowl. I did try the part without ricotta and it was really flavorful and savory. We also got the ancient grain porridge and asked for dairy free milk (have to ask!). I also enjoyed this, it had unique flavors and was savory and warm. Finally, we got the steak and egg with creamed spinach. I asked about any dairy and the spinach did which was no surprise. He then said the steak and egg were fine but the steak was placed on top of the spinach. When asked if they could put the steak next to the spinach instead of on top of it I was politely declined. I get wanting to have presentation and taste be a certain way but restaurants should be accommodating (the menu says no modifications but usually allergies/intolerances are an acceptable reason to modify in my experience). The steak itself was okay. I thought it was average and not worth $30. My bf said the creamed spinach was really good though. Although the grits and porridge were good, I won't be back considering that only a few things on the menu don't have dairy and no modifications can be made.

We ordered to go at this restaurant bc it was just across the street from the hotel our family was staying. The host that took our order over the phone was very cordial and nice. We walk over about ten minutes after our order. We then waited about 20 min for our order to come. The brought our order and we checked to see if they got our fathers order correct because he has certain allergies. It was. All of our food was cold or Luke warm and we only walked a cross the street not even 5 minute walk. My burger was not cooked medium it was cooked rare. My husbands burger was fine. But the spaetzle was cold and over cooked mushy. Very underwhelming. My husband brought my burger back and for the garlic fries they forgot to include with our order that was a free Yelp deal. When he went back the restaurant the manager was apologetic. She took the burger off then a 25% off the total order and gave him a free Coke while he waited.

I was there around lunchtime on Thursday (4/7) and had one of the worst food experiences of my life. I ordered chicken fingers with tater tots, very basic order. After the first chicken finger I noticed it tasted a little different than most but I convinced myself it was just a different kind that I hadn't had before. After I swallowed my first bite into the second chicken finger I realized it wasn't cooked all the way through. After about an hour of golfing and uneasiness in my stomach, it hit my like a freight train. I had to rush to the bathroom and projectile vomitted. I apologize to whoever had to clean that up in the bathroom but I hope it was the cook who couldn't even handle making arguably the simplest dish one can find on a menu. Even writing this review I'm getting nauseous thinking about that half cooked piece of fake meat. I will never eat at Top Golf again nor will the 5 other people that were with me.

The staff was wonderful from the hostess to the wait staff. However the menu is far from "American ". Not even the hamburger was normal. Also it is a problem for someone like me who has allergies. It was not a case where they could omit it. It is the first place I left without a doggie bag. I am a light eater but the portions were small and extremely expensive!
Worst meal of my life. Had Tile fish which I had never had before. Within 3 hours had food poisoning. Spent the next 24 hours in Abington Hospital. Had to give it one star so it would print this.

The husband and I have been devotees of a certain Indian restaurant since we moved to Edmonton, but we decided we needed to branch out this afternoon and give a new establishment a try. Of course, we'd heard New Asian Village was THE place in town, and selected the Manning Road location based on its proximity to our home. We made a beeline to the buffet. The offerings were numerous and fresh. Among the ones I tried were mixed daal, vegetable korma, an eggplant and potato dish whose name escapes me, tandoori chicken, butter chicken, and a chickpea and mixed veggie salad (which I topped with raita and mint sauce). On the dessert side, I tried a moong daal and fruit paste, the mango pudding (amazing), and the rice pudding. Everything was really good, and the lunch buffet came out to ~$15 each. For people watching their diets, helpful signs by each dish identified whether they were low-fat, gluten-free, and so on (FYI: not much but the rice is low-fat :)). For some reason, I was enchanted by the copper water cups--I've heard copper supplements drinking water and positively charges the ions in it, but this vessel kept my water extremely cold and fresh without any ice. It's definitely closer than our favourite place, and there were some dishes at NAV that I preferred. Now that we've been, it's a contender for our regular Indian spot.

I dislike writing mediocre reviews. But..... I was looking forward to eating here since a few of my clients love it. Im always up for a new breakfast place. Positives: service was excellent Coffee fresh English muffins were to die for! Im about 80%gluten free. For these I made an exception to eat half . But they only the little package jams on the table. Wawawaaaa. The other Negatives: everything was extremely salty and tasted like it came from a bag or frozen. The eggs were greasy with that butter oil stuff. It was just to generic for me. The restaurant is so cute. I expected homemade jams, fresh sausage,farm fresh eggs, freshly prepared potatoes. My husband had bisquits and gravy and the gravy was the powder glue ,just add water kind. If I am going to spend those kind of calories it should be worth it. Sadly it was not.

I'm allergic to cheese and I ordered some pasta, stating that I didn't want any cheese on it, which isn't super complicated. They smothered it and not in grated mozerralla or Parmesan but in slices of what looked like kraft singles. They did fix it no problem, though. The sauce was basically ketchup and the pasta was smothered in it. Also the sausage I got with it was over cooked, dry and pretty flavorless. I have no idea about their pizza (again dairy allergy) but from what my family has told me its pretty sub par. There are tons of other cheap pizza/italian restaurants a stones throw from this place go to one of them.

Avoid at all costs. Four coworkers and I went here to avoid the fast food chains we're normally relegated to - it turned out to be a worse decision. After waiting nearly 30 minutes for the waitress to take an order, it took another 15-20 minutes to get our drinks (which were spilled - literally - all over us), it took another 60 minutes for our food to arrive. The food was so-so - nothing great, but not extremely revolting. Unfortunately, I ended up getting food poisoning and spending the entire next 36 hours within 3 feet of a toilet at all times. All in all, a terrible experience - bad service, bad food, and no redeeming qualities.

Hate to say it, but the place is not the same. It is still clean, but the service has gone down hill as has the food. They now have a gluten free menu, but it is very limited instead of having the server customize what you can eat like before (the best server, Lai, is no longer there!). We had four different servers wait on us which was annoying. The food was still okay and fresh, but not up to previous visits in terms of flavor.

Nonetheless disappointed-no gluten free bread but only deserts from the local gfree bakery they proudly disclaim in one of the 3 bulky menus seriously 3? Gee I wonder if it took the same effort to order g free bread from the same gfree local bakery...? Decorations-overboard! Less is more...don't take it for granted. The place is quaint and sells "the home experience" the coffee machine that looks like an iMac - sore in the eyes-prices? Are you for real? Overpriced for a place that advertises an experience in the ad and delivers subpar. On a good note the taste of the food - phenom - fix the rest will ya?

As a non-celiac/non-vegan, these baked goods just tasted super dry. Though I will say, for vegans and celiacs, this is probably the best they can do with regards to baked goods. For now, I'll stick to my milk, eggs and glutenous foods. Bottomline, if you're vegan/celiac go here, everyone else just find a good regular bakery.

The worst restaurant I have ever been to ever...... the catfish fingers came with some shrimp which I didn't order and am very very allergic to. The manager is definitely not able to handle a bad situation. If she had any idea she would have realized how bad it was. I am grateful that I caught it before I put it in my mouth. She just said sorry I will tell the kitchen. So my husband had to go get benadryl and she said I took off the app. Really we didn't even eat the rest of our dinner becuase we had to leave . Maybe you should have thought that out.

The Palms is a Carpenteria original that provides good food at very reasonable prices. They have a menu which offers a cook your own meat entree and another list where they will cook your meal. The cook your own meat option was great for our gluten free friend who often has issues in finding good gluten free dining options on menus. This is an old style, say funky, steak and potatoes kind of place. It's comfortable and unfancy. They don't take reservations. It wasn't busy when we went there mid-week, but the weekends are packed. This is a good group/family place that provides good food without breaking your wallet.
I had the blue corn tacos which were good but had diarrhoea or food poisoning shortly after ...

Came for lunch with the kids. One star for atmosphere (clean, open, loud enough for comfortable conversation) and polite employees. One star for options of hot dogs, chicken, vegetarian, grilled cheese. My burger was fine, but underseasoned and pretty expensive. My husband's burger was undercooked (still traces of pink inside), but within acceptable margins from a food poisoning perspective. However, he really, really did not like his burger. Described it as one toned, and not a good one, and flavorless (even the jalapeño). The employees were very attentive and came to ask how we were doing several times, but we didn't say anything since it's not really something they can help. I was disappointed with the grilled cheese sandwich, the cheese was barely melted and there was no gooeyness when I sliced the sandwich in half. Will not be coming back, (hence the 2 stars), but I appreciate the kids stool in the bathroom!

I am incredibly torn over writing this review. I'll start off by saying that I will plan to give Flyte another try and re-review at that time. In the meantime I would like to start with positives! The servers were incredibly sweet and we had no issues with them per se. They tried their best I am certain...however the overall experience was not what we were expecting. Myself and 11 other girlfriends decided to treat ourselves to some wine and unwind time and restaurant week could not have been a better time. .. right? Well we made reservations and were quite surprised to have gotten them so easily. They had our table ready and we were seated immediately. Which was fantastic. Now here comes the trouble. When you start spending in the $50+ range per person for a meal.. you really start to expect a certain experience. We all ordered wine and cocktails and appetizers. Like I said.. we came to wine, dine, unwind. There was no wine in any of our hands by the 20 mins mark from sitting down. At one point, someone stopped by and put the bottle of wine we ordered on the table....uncorked... and walked away. That was an incredibly awkward moment for all of us. I think my friend said it best when she described our night as just plain "bizarre." I understand it is restaurant week and that they can be busy.. but I was disheartened that they did not even acknowledge the delays. (And honestly, the restaurant had a number of open tables). Now strike 2. Most of us ordered from the prix fixe menu. We sat down right before 8pm, had wine right before 830. Dinner came close to 10. Unfortunately everyone's meal came but mine. That was truly my own fault as they had to adjust my meal for allergies..but I thought they would wait to bring it out all together...as I sat as everyone else ate (never make your Hangry girlfriends wait). That time though they immediately acknowledged what happened which I truly appreciated. In regards to the food, we all thought it was good. The carrot soup was far better then the roasted beets. 10/12 people had the steak and they said it was okay. I had the trout and was quite pleased. However, I can't believe I'm saying this.. but the best part of the whole meal was the bread. AND i was not the only person that said that. We all collectively agreed that the sour dough at Flyte was the best thing they served all night. It was truly fantastic. Presentation was spot on and the butter was apparently to die for. Overall, I would say that I expected a finer experience then what I got. Our table easily spent $700 and we did not feel that the price was equivocal to the experience. However, I am certainly open to giving it another try in the future... just not during restaurant week. And I would like to reinforce that the staff was very courteous and kind. I am sure they did their best in that situation. On a last positive note... at least they had valet!

Been there only twice in the last 5 years and do not care to return. Unfortunely my boss took us there for lunch. The food was mediocre. I ordered from the gluten free menu and had the onion soup and mediteranean salad for lunch. My coworkers all ordered crepes. The only good part about the soup was the bountiful cheese. Otherwise, not really good. The salad- overdressed and really small. As for the crepes, my coworkers said they were ok. However they did not appreciate the manager/wait staff litterally picking at the food on the table to determine if it was indeed the wrong crepe. My coworker was not pleased what so ever. Personally I would not like someone opening up my crepe with is hands and a fork so see what's inside. The sauce alone should have screamed "wrong order/table". The man also had his zipper open as he leaned over the table. And yes he litterally leaned right over the table to pick at the food. Price wise- a little pricey for the quantity and quality of food. The gluten free menu crepes were outrageously priced and had nothing but vegetarian and seafood crepes. I don't eat seafood and like other meats such as beef or poultry- which they somehow do not offer gluten free. I would not go back, the services was not great, the food mediocre, cleanliness for a restaurant not great, prices overpriced. I rate this place 1/5.

Really bland food. Said everything was gluten free, but lied. My friend has Celiac's disease and did not feel well after eating here. Very disappointed with the food, especially for the price we paid.

My roommate and I were visiting a friend in Philly and super excited that there were vegan options here. We called ahead of time because my roommate has a severe nut allergy that requires 0 cross contamination and complete confidence from the kitchen that her food will be safe. We asked the staff member about this and clearly stated these things and they assured us this would be a safe place for her to eat. When we arrived, our server communicated the exact opposite and said she couldn't make any promises that food would be safe for her. I got up to let her know that we wouldn't be able to stay seated and dine then and instead of listening, she backed up defensively and waved us away. I am incredibly frustrated that we were given inconsistent answers and treated disrespectfully when we tried to explain why we were leaving.

Really, really wanted to like this place but just couldn't. The service was great but the baguette made me keenly aware that I'm gluten intolerant which I was hoping to avoid at a gluten free restaurant. Maybe it just wasn't my thing, but I think they can do better.

went for lunch with my gluten free daughter since she said they had a gf menu. well - they did - and what we ate was crappy. the pizza was doughy and undercooked. we mentioned it to one of the managers there. he confirmed that he knew the gluten free crust was a problem. their pizza belts run at 6 and 10 minutes - 6 makes it undercooked and 10 burns it. but he did nothing to rectify the problem, only point out that he knew it was a problem. it was a big disappointment. he didnt offer to refund or offer to get us another meal. i was shocked. we also ordered steamed broccoli to be on the healthy side - but it was steamed in a vat of butter. wish we would've known. we also got a surf n turf. the shrimp tasted like lunch meat: bologna to be exact. overcooked and nasty. i ordered a soup i cant even remember anymore. the server was green and overly friendly to try to make up for it - but he wasnt bad. he was polite and that was our saving grace. no thank you

Ohhhhh Sweet Freedom indeed! I actually found Sweet Freedom online during my big lactose free wedding cake fiasco. (for financial reasons I couldn't use sweet freedom and will have a home baked little cake for myself to cut). I met with one of the owners, Megan, who was FANTASTIC. She was very laid back and friendly as well as knowledgeable and helpful. She offered a ton of different options to us as far as size flavor and decoration. She had some great insight to even offer me should I not choose her and go with a regular bakery, regarding cross contamination etc that you have to deal with for food allergies. I also found it inpressive that she actually said hello to each and every customer that walked in on that busy saturday afternoon. I love that. I even got a chance to talk with the cake decorator, who was seriouslyjust as sweet as the cupcakes she decorates!! I only had a chance to buy the caramel toffee cupcake, a chocolate cupcake, a cookie, a vanilla cupcake and a slice of tomato pie. All fantastic, although I'm partial to the chocolate. I'll be back soon...after the wedding so i don't have to worry about not fitting into my dress!!!! :) Hands down a great place for people with food allergies!!!!

4 of Chef's tasting menu, which was pretty good, but 3 of the 4 received food poisoning and had GI issues the rest of the weekend, not woth the 60$+ a person, i felt terrible because I am the one who suggested it from the article in Sauce magazine August 2011, also there was a short in the light bulb above our table and we felt we were eating under a strob light

Never had a problem ordering from them until today. I ordered a grilled chicken Caesar salad for lunch and ended up getting food poisoning. What little bit of chicken I did eat was chewy and tasted horrible. Bah! Will never be ordering from here again, that's for sure. Thanks for the unpleasant Friday night I'm currently enduring.

Sorry to hear of the passing of your founder. Respect your decision and commitment tomboy being open on Sundays. Please stop using peanut oil! Can't visit your restaurant due to your use of peanut oil and allergies.

BRÜ-more like BOOO. I had high expectation for this place, just fell short. Very dark, very crowded, tight space & even tighter seating. I am a fan of sour beers, many to choose from and our waitress had sick knowledge of all the beers, well that's the positive. Food was average to Blahhhh. Started with the BRÜfries, looked like a cat threw up on them, but very good..Girlfriend started with the apple and potato pancakes, ahhh it was OK. Time for another beer to take my mind of the disappointment if the apps. Dinner, I had the Doner Kabob- (lamb shoulder, pickles, iceburg, yogurt sauce, flatbread) it was OK, and a side of Spätzel- fried, no taste, needed salt or even a gravy. Time for another beer to add some flavor to this food. Girlfriend got typical Wurst sammy, she said it was good, she didn't finish it....I guess we'll have more more beer before we roll out since the beers were on point.

I will say the food is delicious..service a little odd, like sort of inattentive but nice. Servings are a bit small, like way smaller than a regular Mexican place. This isn't necessarily bad tho, I ate everything and didn't want to vomit from being stuffed. Back to the food....in my opinion absolutely delicious. Despite the aforementioned shortcomings, we will be back over and over.

We've been going to this place since it's one of the few places in Voorhees to get healthy vegan and gluten free food. Anyways last time we went my friend got a falafel wrap, thinking it was vegan and GF. We just came back and it turns out it's not gluten free which no one said. The person at the counter was very terse with us when we were trying to ask some questions about the menu. He then explained that cous cous is gluten free (it's not it's made from wheat- https://en.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/couscous) and that cous cous is just like quinoa (quinoa is its own grain. it is not made from wheat plant at all- https://www.thespruce.com/what-is-quinoa-3376836). We also asked about the veggie burger, which he said had bulgar in it, but explained that bulgar is gluten free (bulgar is made from wheat- https://en.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/bulgar). This is super messed up because there are people out there who actually can't have wheat- this is called Celiac disease- https://celiac.org/celiac-disease/understanding-celiac-disease-2/what-is-celiac-disease/. It's not just about Voorhees moms wanting to be Gluten Free and trendy. All in all, the food was fine. I got myself the southwest wrap, probably won't get it again since the chicken was bland but the rest was fine. It wasn't very spicy at all, and a good nutritious item from the menu. Unfortunately the person at the counter did not treat us with respect and was very short with us. It was very easy to tell he was annoyed with our questions, even though this is supposed to be an accommodating place. I'm not sure if he's like this with everyone, or just people who look like brown women. A man came in while we were thinking and he treated him very respectfully and was talkative with him and answered his questions. Honestly that doesn't come off great to me, and considering Voorhees is my home town, very disappointing.

My boyfriend and I went to try their Chowdown Midtown menu. We had never been, so we made a reservation, but when we showed up there was no record of one anywhere. it was ok though because there were not a lot of people in there so we still got seated quickly. We knew right away what we wanted but the waitress sort of forgot about us after we were sat. Normally I am pretty patient, but we were both hungry and grouchy! The menu was fun to read with lots of little jokes. I really wanted to like the place, because it seems like the owner is a fun person, but it just was a very subpar experience. For me, the most disappointing thing was I did not get to really eat very much of the food. I told our waitress I had a spice allergy, and said I had my inhaler just in case, but to ask the chef to avoid peppercorn please. She just started bringing food out so I assumed it was ok, but... The salad had peppercorn ranch dressing on it. the steak tips had pepper for sure, and I would be quite surprised if the risotto did not also. I only got to have a bite or two of pretty much everything, and my boyfriend ended up eating for two basically. I know that it can be really inconvenient to cook for me, and it was a special menu, and I normally call ahead to mention it and ask the kitchen if it was ok but did not since it was sort of on a whim that we went (which is why i didnt make a big deal about it) but... I feel like they could have at least but some other dressing on the salad, surely? I dont know. It was frustrating though. I do think the alcohol menu is well picked with a lot of great variety, first of all. It is not often my boyfriend and I can both find something we like. I had a pineapple cider and he had some kind of dark coffee ale. We got a salad and a bowl of clam chowder. My boyfriend ate both. We tried the shrimp cigars, which were unevenly warm, the middles were cool and the outside very hot like a microwaved hot pocket. They tasted decently good, though the sauce that came with them did not. I had the mushroom risotto with steak tips and my boyfriend had Chicken Zidane. Both of our meals were partly room temp when they got to us. His food was decent, even at room temp. I liked my risotto alright, what I ate of it. We got both desserts. I was not feeling very well so I only had a bite of the coffee cake, but it tasted decent as well. My boyfriend loved the bread pudding, and took the coffee cake home and ate it for breakfast.
If you want food poisoning and A poopy butt this is the place go!

We've come here in the past for car shows but this was our first time eating here. The manager and our server Angelena were both helpful and knowledgable about gluten free menu items which is always a plus. Our service was prompt and our food came out fast. With that being said the food was just ok. They advertise the best wings in town but they were only a 5 out of 10. The food portions are small. We also order the loaded magna fries and were disappointed when they came out with barely any toppings.

Wow, this place is a VERY locals-only kind of place. You walk in and are greeted with a the smell of fried foods and the sight of a thousand Phillies shirts. None of this is a bad thing, but a bit jarring when your previous stop that night was Franklin. I had the massive long island (obviously) which was drinkable and --did I mention?-- massive. No regrets there. I could see myself coming back here when I'm in the mood for a no-frills night of cheap booze and sports on the TVs. The bathrooms did, however, make me want to vomit.

Came here to catch up with an old friend, and overall we had a pretty good experience. I got a chimichanga and it was super tasty, and I was surprised by how quickly it came out. I do have to say that I was a little disappointed when we inquired about the ingredients of a couple different dishes (my friend has allergies) and the staff were unable to answer our questions. Overall though, it was a good experience.

2 words: Food Poisoning. I was in Reno for the weekend, just staying for one night. On my first day there, the only place I ate was at Toucan Charlie's and I ate a whole mess of seafood. Around 3 am, I woke up in horrible pain. Without getting too graphic, let's just say I spent the remainder of my weekend locked in the bathroom, praying for a quick death.

ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTED. 1) I ordered the Seafood Rice Noodles and found a half eaten crab. 2) Got food poisoned from their shrimp fried rice. 3) Their fried rice portion size keeps shrinking. I used to get a full plate of it, but now i only get a small lump. Stingy much? They have lost my business. They are so unhygienic with their food. SO GROSS. DO NOT EAT HERE. Save your money and eat elsewhere.

I'm not sure what I expected before walking in which left me open to what was in store. I expect 25% experience/environment, 25% service, 25% Food Quality and 25% cost/value. It's located downtown, and has a full bar in the front, with room to have appetizers and loiter until getting seated. The bar was playing "ubiquitous" house music over the speakers to create a kind of 'din" to the place. For a Saturday at 6 pm it was pretty full, and were seated within 10 minutes. It seat between 80 and 100 is my guess. There is a large low slung black "negative edge" fountain running down the middle of the restaurant, This stands before a 4' tall Buddha that overlooks the guests. If "colorful almost kitchy" were a stereotype of Asian culture, this restaurant would fit that. There was a projected Buddha on the wall overhead, as well as 5 colored screens over lights. I couldn't get over the flatware, which has square handles, and is extremely heavy. The 'bamboo' place mat looked a little dirty, but I didn't scrutinize too much. The wall sconces had different colored lights. I think the decorators wanted "modern simple" and ended up with an inability to "refrain" from another little "touch." I've been told many guests put their elbows into the fountain because it is almost a mirror like surface, and the tables are pushed up very very close to it, and at table height. So you may accidentally think it's something you could rest your arm on. Ordered a Liberty School Cabernet ($9.50) which seemed very $$ for the restaurant. Obviously the bar is a significant contributor to it's financial success. The glass was a very nice Cabernet glass when served. Kudos to their glassware choices, boo for their cutlery choices. Our group wasn't certain what we wanted, but decided on some appetizers then we'd work up our appetite to determine our course of action. Ordered the "Summer Rolls" and the were a bit dry, cold (supposed to be, but more "right out of the refrigerator cold) and tasted like they were pre-made and while edible, they seemed... boring. Spicy side dipping sauces seemed pre-made from an Asian market and poured on the plate like ketchup. We asked for pot stickers and they served spring rolls instead. Not sure how those wires were crossed (my host did ask if summer rolls were still in season to which the waiter shrugged, Dry joke.) We ate these none-the-less.. A note, the plateware for all the dishes is all extra large, and extra heavy. Not sure if they did it on purpose but the appetizers were brought out one by one and the plates were huge. Took up a significant portion of the table. Again, O.K. deep fried stuff. My host ordered Pad Thai with the nuts and sprouts on a bowl seperately (allergies). When the waiter delivered the sprouts he tried to hold the plate by the corner to place on the opposite end of the table. He spilled it terribly across the table. The wrist strength would have been phenomenal to do this and not sure what he was thinking. We let the server off the hook about it, BUT he never came back to clean it up. I guess he expected us to pick the bean sprouts off the table to put in our Pad Thai later? He apologized for the mess and said the Pad Thai would be stricken from our bill. The Pad Thai was with chicken. My hosts spouse discovered that the chicken was soft, and upon further inspection, raw and uncooked. It was the last straw. The waiter brought over the manager who approached us quickly and said he'd take the Pad Thai off the bill. By this time, we were disappointed in the meal enough to decide there was no salvaging this meal experience. I can only say the one bit of the Pad Thai I had was mediocre, bland and seemed... uninspired. At this point were were ready to walk out. Getting poisoned at a discount isn't a good deal. We offered to pay our drink ticket, and be done. He did the right thing, excepted our offer, we walked out disappointed and and we went to Bitter something for a burger. Although by this time my hosts wife had lost her appetite. Due to the lack of a lot of Thai food options in Boise, i'd suggest P.F. Changs down the street. Say what you want about it being a chain restaurant, but they've never come close to poisoning their guests.

This bar is anything but cozy, with its industrial feel, but they're serving some nice beers. They have a Simcoe Simcoe IPA that's crazy aromatic and tasty. But their alpha storter is mediocre. The RyePA they have on is beautiful and complex. Their staff is friendly, helpful, and talkative. They have a gluten-removed Ale with only 48ppm for those with gluten sensitivities. (Gluten-free labeling is only available when it's 20ppm or less.) There's no food. Check this place out before it becomes a douchebag bar thanks to its Washington Avenue proximity.

This place gives the WORST FOOD POISONING!!! Avoid at all cost!!! I love Korean food and dining out. I eat out a lot and rarely had any problems. I went to the restaurant traveling on business not too long ago and ordered two entrees, the seafood tofu stew and the beef bibimbap. The seafood tofu stew was probably amongst the worst I had had. It also tasted different from the ones that I had at dozens of other Korean restaurant. The beef bibimbap was worse than average but edible. The restaurant was almost empty and it was also very smokey from people cooking bbq. Problem began the same night a few hours later. I had the worst food poisoning symptoms of my life for the rest of the night! I stayed at a hotel so I called up the front desk for medicine. Although meds weren't available in the hotel, the hotel staff eventually went to a pharmacy to get it for me. I continued suffering from the food poisoning symptoms throughout the night, but the meds helped. The next morning I woke up, I was concerned to see that my tongue was all black! After multiple attempts, I finally was able to speak with the restaurant manager, Yang or Young, who is also the son of the restaurant owner. He was cold and did not want to help at all and asked me to wait until more people report food poisoning so that he can report the incident. After an hour of conversation, he agreed to give a very small compensation if I can get the hotel to write a letter describing the incident. In retrospect, he's experienced enough to bank on the fact that hotels would not generate such letter to potentially get them involved in legal troubles. I went through quite a few hurdles to get the hotel to write a letter. After numerous attempts to finally get in touch with him again, he said that during our last conversation, he was thinking about going through insurance to compensate me the whole time. What's ridiculous is that he never mentioned a word of insurance! He must have been surprised that the hotel actually had the corporate office write a letter for me and offered contact information! The call ended with him telling me that I will be contacted by the insurance company in the next day or two. Two weeks passed and I did not hear from the insurance. I messaged him about it and guess what? He never responded! Please do yourself a favor and not visit this restaurant. The food was way below average, not to mention poisonous! Even the restaurant name il (ill) suggested that it gets people sick. The restaurant manager Yang (Young) is the most irresponsible and difficult human being I have encountered. Run the other way!

The dining experience was not very good. I think this restaurant needs to retrain the staff. I don't like to go negative, but I family came at a not so busy hour, and saw a lot of the staff just standing around laughing and not doing much. We were seated by an unfriendly host. Our order was taken, food arrived in a good amount of time. Our food was brought out by a different person than the one that took our order, she asked if we needed anything else, we told her what else we needed, and she didn't ever come back. Our original server came back and got us what we needed, but very late in the game. Food was over salty, and I Queen may have some food poisoning. Definitely not coming back. Step up your game.

So the last few time we have been here I haven't felt so hot afterwards. If you have read any of my previous reviews or my profile you will see I am a Celiac so my dining choices are slim. I was ordering the Margarita Shrimp Bowl from their Gluten Free Friendly menu but I found my tummy hurt afterwards. Now when I consume enough gluten I become VIOLENTLY ILL but all I had was pain. On our last visit on June 18th I decided to try the Chipotle Chicken Fresh Mex Bowl. It was yummy. However by the time we got home I was in mega pain and it got worse as time passed. Again I didn't get sick but there was enough gluten in that dish to cause issues. I know very well they can NOT guarantee there food is gluten free etc and I take my chances when I eat out. So I am not blaming them but I think there is something in their bowls that have hidden gluten b/c I don't think cross contamination would give me such a reaction. Hell even my home isn't 100% gluten free as I am the only Celiac in the home and I'm sure I have cross contamination here. But 4 bowls in a row causing issues again isn't a coincidence or cross contamination. So if you are a Celiac I have to say you might wanna give Chilis a pass. If you are avoiding Gluten to be trendy and cool go ahead an indulge in their Gluten Free options.

I would give this place 5 stars but the order I just had delivered is wrong. I asked for brown sauce instead of sweet n sour because of my allergy to pineapple and I got sweet n sour sauce. I normally love this place, but I love not going into anaphylactic shock more. I hope this doesn't become a common thing because I really do enjoy the food from here

Went with my wife, Asked if the items where gluten free , the gentleman told her "you are all good this salad dressing is gluten free". After she was done eating he mentioned they might have put bread crumbs in ( which contain gluten) but we already suspected since she started to get an allergic reaction. He hen proceeds to say to her" darling it's 99% gluten free I think but I don't know, the chef is gone so nothing I can do". You all need to understand to much gluten means a night in hospital. Wake up!! It's no joke. Learn or don't work
Primo is the exact opposite of its name. The staff was primo but the food was Vomito. There is nothing else to say.
Got food poisoning from here yesterday. Usually a good experience. Not yesterday however.

Minus the Beans came here on our road tour back in April of 2013. That was earlier this current calendar year that I am living in, for the people of the future who are reading this on their futuristic reading devices. We had some dinner and some drinks while we had dinner. I think there were some sports games on TV, maybe. And there was definitely a guy playing a guitar and singing songs. He seemed like he played there many nights. He was talking to people in the crowd, but not in a way that a musician normally would. It was like, "Hey, what are you doing later? Yeah? I'll hit you up." I had some Ace cider that wasn't that good. When I tried to switch it up with the waitress, she suggested Redd's Ale. I told her I was allergic to gluten and she said yeah, this is a cider. Nope. It's a beer with apple flavoring. 1. Glad I checked myself. 2. Why, Redd's? Why? That sounds terrible. Beer, or not beer. Not quasi-beer. That makes no sense. PS the bathrooms are 500 feet away from wherever you can sit in this place.

HORRIBLE! People with food allergies - BEWARE! My son has two life threatening food allergies (tree nuts and sesame) and got extremely sick after eating a cheese pizza from here. He was a guest of friends, so I only heard about it after the fact. When I called the restaurant to find out the ingredients in the pizza I was faced with a rude and uncaring person on the line. He was dismissive and unknowledgeable about the food prep and ingredients. I wouldn't eat here even if I didn't have a food allergy. Terrible service. Shouldn't be allowed to serve food.

Uh oh.... This has been one of the places that I consistently recommend for an evening out with food, vino, music and friends. Last night makes me sad. The music was lighthearted and fun, with some solid jazz players. The vino was outstanding (their selection is VERY reliable). The friends were fun as always. The place was crowded, sold out night likely with the valentine's weekend peeps. Not enough staff to cover the floor well and it showed. I really liked our server, but but the time we were offered a second bottle for the table we were long tired of waiting. Similar wait time for dessert menu and then dessert order and then the dessert. The biggest problem was my order. After discussing vegetarian options, I went with the pad thai recommendation. The first bite of shrimp was a surprise (perhaps a stray?) the piece of chicken in the next made it clear the dish in front of me was not what I ordered. I consider myself a flexitarian - I eat meat, but usually prefer vegetarian meals. Service was so slow I ate around the meat and enjoyed the peanuty sauce, but this is a major faux pas for a vegetarian and vegan friendly spot. My hubby thought the goat curry was not as good as it has been in the past and the vegetarian lasagna also ordered at our table didn't get finished. The pavlova had the consistency of a sponge toffee (brittle and crispy) - pavlova is supposed to have a crispy shell and soft and marshmallowy on the inside. The fruit was on the side (usually in the centre or on top in a bed of cream) and was served with rinds on the melon & pineapple without a knife. The whipped cream clearly came from a can, skimpy lines with nozzle marks - at least they could have tried to disguise it! I sincerely hope this was just an off night, the owners are fantastic supporters of original music and have great taste in wine. Including vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options shows a dedication to keeping customers happy. If only the execution met the expectations.

Great vegan, allergen free bakery, with both traditional and edgy goods. They have a wide variety of treats -- doughnuts, cupcakes, cookies, and bars. I had the chocolate cayenne lime cookie -- the cookies are thin and slightly crisp, which I guess is to be expected from an allergen free cookie. It was tasty and had a nice spicey bite. Not bad for $1.65. Also tried a sample of the chocolate chip cookie, which is not noteworthy (skip it) and the magic bar which was just okay. They list out all their ingredients for those avoiding certain foods. I will probably be back for a cupcake -- I feel like icing is the real test for an allergen-free spot. Don't expect "normal" treats, because that's not what they're about.

This review is solely based on the fact that they put sour cream and cheese in the guacamole and call it "authentic". That is NOT authentic, that is a restaurant scamming you out of your money but putting fillers that are less expensive than avocados into perfectly good guacamole, and then charging you an outrageous amount of money for it. Even though it's partially my fault, I ordered the guacamole without looking at the menu to eat on the way home from work. Being extremely allergic to dairy, you can imagine that this did not have good implications for my stomach. Avoid if you want actual authentic Mexican food that doesn't cost an arm and leg.

I'm not that familiar with pubs and such, but this is really no different than a bar-and-grill restaurant. No, I'm not comparing it to all the cookie-cutter chains like Cheddars, Applebees and Chili's. This is one that does their own thing, but with a better vibe. I've been here a few times, nothing really special. The service was great, and the food is okay. (Note: Usually when I do reviews of places that mostly make money and turn their marketing focus towards on alcohol, I mostly judge on the food and atmosphere.) I've had their pretzel sticks, their spicy jalapeno burger, and on my most recent visit, The Pogue Mahone. I don't know where they got the name from, but its sure a heart-attack waiting to happen! (laughs) They did get minus points from me for putting mushrooms on there, even though I specifically said no mushrooms, because I'm allergic to them. Otherwise, the burger was alright. Fries portion was small. They serve multiple local and independent brews, and I'm surprised they serve Coke products (unlike most independent places these days that sell local soda...). But the atmosphere and vibe were great, and the bartenders are super-friendly. Plus they're always playing great tunes! One time it was 2000s Indie Rock, one day it was the Beatles' White Album. Again, its your average bar-and-grill place, which is good to some. It can be a great hangout, especially at night.

Worst experience at Azie. Have a very serious gluten allergy (Celiac) and thought with "gfree" written everywhere on this menu that we would be able to eat great sushi here. In good sushi restaurants, you just have to avoid items with soy sauce since soy sauce is derived from wheat. You also have to accept that there is always a risk of cross contamination when you eat out in any restaurant -this is a fact of life when you have a gluten intolerance or Celiac. That said, sushi rolls come down to rice and fish so they should be safe since both ingredients are inherently gluten free. Massive disappointment at Azie. Their version of gfree sushi is to make sushi with nasty brown rice. Apparently, the rice vinegar they use to bind the white rice together in the regular sushi contains wheat. Using these lower quality rice vinegars that contain gluten is cheaper and easier for restaurants like Azie. Azie management, I applaud your effort to offer gluten free menu items so thank you for that. I also appreciate that you are up front that the regular sushi is unsafe for those with gluten issues. But put your money where your mouth is - use higher quality ingredients so everyone can eat your sushi. What you don't understand about folks with food allergies is that they just want what everyone else is eating- they just want to eat safely. This is an EASY fix on your part but, yes, it may cost you a little extra. Then you really can say you have gluten free sushi instead of the poor substitute you currently offer.

I recently contacted Roberto's about some concerns I had with sanitation at Roberto's by sending a message through Contact Us on the website. Rey, the owner, who's father was the original, "Roberto" contacted me within 1 hour (Impressive!) He told me he's instructed the staff in Reno to change out containers that hold salsa, jalapeños and carrots, etc. rather than refilling. I feel 100% confident this is the right thing to do. The reason is if anything in the containers gets contaminated, which is highly likely at some point starting after a few hours up to 2 days maximum, contamination will not get fixed if you don't change out and sanitize the containers. I thought deep about this, you don't cook over and over with pots and pans, so why would you not clean out and sanitize a container? It's really the same thing! If you think about this our hands should be washed, and washed often, which I personally do, but I think I am the exception. Before you start customizing your order w/ salsa, jalapeños, etc. EVERYONE was just touching something VERY GERM LADEN examples: cell phones, keys, credit cards, cash, door handles, steering wheels. etc. At some point between a few hours up to 2 days there is going to be a transference of germs, hopefully unintentionally. Once that happens the container will start breeding and growing stuff that can make you ill. I won't go into specifics, but cell phones have tested dirtier than toilet seats, and you can imagine everything else you touch often, what's lingering there. I really appreciate the professionalism and concern, and as always, this place again proves it is 5 stars! I am excited to get my red salsa, jalapeños, carrots, and asada fries or burrito 1-3x again per week as I was doing!

Dang, this place was great. A whole hell of a lot better than Steve's. I typically hate omelets, but I got one here because I'm doing the low carb thing. And It was the first omelet that didn't make me want to vomit. That sounds bad, it's not. It was awesome. The salad that came with it was fresh and gave a nice contrast to the cheesy eggs. The lady got the huevos benedictos which was also amazing, some crazy flavors going on. If I had to say something negative it'd be that it got a little noisy for a few moments, but there was booze. So all good. Definitely worth checking out.
Super lackluster food. No flavor at all. Pretty unfriendly service. Not worth the $12 and definitely not worth the food poisoning it gave me.

GAVE ME FOOD POISONING! Do not eat here! I ate the chicken and rice combo and it destroyed me. I was flying to Europe and after about 2-3 hours in the air it hit me. Throwing up in a tiny airplane bathroom for 6 hours with turbulence in the middle of the night was one of the worst experiences in my life. Landed in Europe and was still throwing up. This place is disgusting, can't belie the Philadelphia airport would allow this junk to be in their terminals.

A nice place for a sweet treat while on Mass Ave. There are a billion flavor combos to choose from and options like soy milk. A nice selection of toppings too! The line may seem daunting, but if you've got some time to kill, wait your turn and chat with your friends. If this is your first time to the place and you're a little indecisive, I'd suggest going with at least one other person so you can step out of line and really get a good look at the menu. Part of the allure of the place is the actual making of the frozen treat, but it does seem to hold up the line a bit. If you have some severe food allergies, I would definitely bring it to their attention to avoid some cross contamination during super busy times.

This place should just stick with Korean food rather than Sushi and Korean fusion. The only good thing about the restaurant is that every thing was COLD. My sister and mother were visiting from New York City. I brought them to this restaurant because the first time I was there, the sushi was good (perhaps I got lucky that first time). My mother ordered Bulgogi which was decent. My sister and I started off with a tuna nacho to share, which again was decent. Then every thing went down hill. Let's start with the scallop sashimi: mushy, bland with no taste of fresh scallop, was like eating an over chewed melted piece of gum. The sweet shrimp sashimi was the same: mushy and lacked the sweetness of fresh shrimp, (like the scallop- over chewed,melted piece of gum). Finally came the yellowtail sashimi that turned me away from this restaurant forever. Four pieces of yellowtail sashimi came out with the Wasabi roll. The jalapenos over powered the entire wasabi roll. My sister and I had to wash down the spice with the Bulgogi. The yellowtail sashimi was served with a frozen center. We had to ask our waiter, David, to return it back to the sushi bar. We over heard the sushi chef telling the waiter to bring it back to us. The waiter brought it back to our table and said, "Just let in sit for a bit, so it can defrost and you'll be able to eat it". My sister and I was in shocked that he stated that. We're not clear whether it was the sushi chef that had asked the waiter to state that or was it David's own justification. But that was UNACCEPTABLE. We did not go to the restaurant to order frozen centered sashimi, let it thoroughly thaw at our table, and then eat it. This was like ordering water and the waiter giving us a cup of ice, having to wait for it to melt to drink (which WAS the case because the waiter NEVER once refilled our cups). By the end of this dissatisfying meal, the waiter came over to remove our plates. He DARED to state, "Oh just to let you guys know, and for next time. All sushi restaurants served frozen fish. Our fish comes in frozen. OUR SUSHI CHEFS MELT THE FISH BY SQUEEZING AND HOLDING IT IN THEIR HANDS. The yellowtails went really fast tonight. Therefore we served what we had since you ordered it". First off, my sister and I are sushi connoisseurs. We know the quality and the elegance of Japanese cuisine. NOT all sushi restaurants receive their fish frozen, ESPECIALLY not restaurants of NYC and Las Vegas where they fly in fresh fish from Japan; or where the sushi chefs hand pick their fish from live fish markets every business morning. Second, if the sushi chefs were professionally trained, they would not served sashimi that was not fully thaw through to their customers. That would be a disgrace in Japan. Third, to tell customers that their "SUSHI CHEFS MELT THE FISH BY SQUEEZING AND HOLDING IT IN THEIR HANDS"..... to us that was a BIG RED FLAG FOR FOOD CONTAMINATION. Sushi needs to remain at 40 degrees or cooler to prevent bacterial growth. The human body temperature is around 98 degrees. If the frozen sashimi is "melted" (thaw) by squeezing and holding in the chef's hand, bacterial will begin to grow on the outside before the center is completed thawed. There will definitely NOT be a next, don't worry David.
I just have lunch and I get food poisoning from there. I guess I have been poisoned from green musels. It's so terrible experience.

OK when I first moved to Reno 4 1/2 years ago everyone said "oh you have to try Jimboy's Taco's".......... so I did - I had an enchilada platter, it was not good at all - which being from Texas I'm a die hard true Tex Mex fan and also being close to the boarder know the difference between Tex-Mex and traditional style Mexican food......... Jimboys was neither..... Ok but being I'm a sucker, I made a 2ed trip to Jimboys and had tacos - I wanted to get a feel for the place so I ordered a regular crunchy taco, a soft taco, a fish taco, and one of those nifty hamburger style tacos - thinking surly out of all of these there had to be one that I'd just love and figure out what was so great........ sadly I ended up sick with food poison! I can't say for 100% sure it was Jimboys but I'm like 99% sure! The regular crunchy taco was so greasy that it wasnt crunchy at all - but very soggy.... same with the soft one it fell apart from being too greasy.... The fish taco was too weird after one or two bites I threw it in the trash sack...... The hamburger taco is the only taco that I was able to eat all of - and really its just a bun-less hamburger with the veggies stuffed in the meat pattie folded in the shape of a taco..... but it was pretty good.... unless of course that was what made me sick? Who knows....... I have never been back, and I still dont know what people were raving about...... some things need not be known right? I say if your really wanting a cheap quick taco fix just go to Taco Bell thats always a sure thing!!

Food poisoning! I went last night, ate the boneless wings, teriyaki sauce, Blue Moon to drink. I have never been so sick in my life! Seriously, I cannot get out of bed but to use the bathroom every 20 minutes, my 8 year old is taking care of me, and I missed work! I will never go back and plan on reporting this more!

We came here on a double date with some friends. I thought the interior was comfortable, but girlfriend wasn't a big fan of the green everywhere. We were seated quickly and we all enjoyed some wine while we looked over the menu. There was a great looking tasting menu, but like many restaurants they require the whole table to do it. Not great when one person has a limiting allergy. I know you want to keep everyone in sync, but I've been to plenty of places that have made it work just fine. The menu rigidity came back when the waitress was oddly unhelpful in any substitutions for the intolerance and instead just insisted to skip the item. Overall the meal was good. A couple of the pairings on a dish were odd. Fire toasted chocolate marshmallow sounded really nice, but was poorly executed with the foie gras. The main courses were better than the appetizers, but nothing really stood out. The service was about the same. It was good, but nothing exceptional. Overall everything at Bistro 7 was good. I wouldn't say no to coming back, but I also wouldn't go out of my way to make it back.

I was excited to check out Amerigo because they offered gluten-free pasta, and I never get to eat pasta out, but the meal was just ok. My pasta sauce was bland and I honestly felt that going home, boiling pasta, and pouring some canned pasta sauce over it would have been comparable. I'm sure they had more interesting things on their menu but I wasn't impressed.

I love BWW and was excited to take my family for the first time. When we arrived we, total of 6 people including a 3 yo, were sat a large circular table. Since my family had never been before they wanted to take their time to look over the menu, especially my mother who is on a relatively strict diet, and the waitress took our drink order and it came out promptly. This was the calm before the storm.. The drinks came out and our order was taken. Then we sat looking at each other for what felt like 40+ minutes with most of having empty glasses. This would not have been a problem and understandable if it had been busy but there was 5-6 tables of guest with us being the largest group and as we continued to wait we noticed the wait staff, including a lady who seemed to be the manager on duty, gathering in a booth, of about 7-8 people, talking, laying down, on their phones, and etc. Our waitress was not to be found until 5 minutes before our food came out to let us know that it would be a few minutes longer and brought us more drinks. Our food then came out and as usual I was happy with my food, small boneless wings half honey mustard half Parmesan garlic, but my family wasn't so impressed. Let it be known that we did not order much food either for it being 6 people 2 sets of snack sized boneless wings, one small order of boneless, a plain grilled chicken salad, grilled buffalo chicken sandwich, one order of potato wedges and one of fries, chicken strips and 2 apps. of fried pickles. Most of the food ended up being over cooked/dry or sloppily put together. Now, 6 hours later I feel like I have acute food poisoning. I have worked in restaurants and know that unless we were slammed that amount of food should not have taken that long. All in all, I was extremely disappointed in this particular wild wings and believe they need a surprise inspection from corporate and maybe the health department. Very unprofessional, too long of a wait, and food was mediocre at best. I would have been better off going to McDonalds and at least saved a little money and would understand why I feel sick. Like my dad said, it reminded him of an episode of bar rescue that is in need of some serious help !

I got food poisoning from this location as well in December. Along with a very NASTY ATTITUDE from the woman who does the cooking. Ranch dressing left on the counter and not in the refrigerator. I was sick for two days. They offered me a family 50 pc meal as an apology, yeah, I don't think so! This experience has convinced me to #NEVEREAT @WINGSTOP AGAIN!
STAY AWAY! Gave my friend's husband food poisoning within an hour of eating it. Had him down and out for the whole day.

Nothing really special going on here. Franchise with basic cupcakes trying to capitalize on a trend . Wedding cake is vanilla and vanilla. Chocolate indulgence whatever the fuck the name was, is chocolate and chocolate. However, it was yummy. The Salted Caramel was good too. The gluten free broke apart in a million pieces. Cookie dough was vanilla and vanilla with cookie dough pieces on the top. Boring. It has all the makings for a Shark Tank Go Found Me. But, they do make a good cupcake when you need one or two.

THIS IS THE by far, THE WORST FOOD I HAVE EVER HAD. I will start my saying that I received the wrong order and when I called, the manager told ME to come and bring it to them because she did not believe me! I did not have a car so the man cam, e and brought my order back TO THE STORE TO be inspected by the woman. When they came back, I had received the SAME order I returned!!!! The few bites I had eaten I actually threw up in was SO DISGUSTING. The sauce tastes like sugar and the mushrooms were not even fried - barely breaded and absolutely DIRTY. I would never give this food to my dog - PLEASE DO NOT EVER get this food. You will regret it.

COCKAROCHES COCKAROCHES COCKAROCHES Worst experience of my life!!!! Some friends and I went there after a day at the river.. I can't believe I recommended this place. I was so embarrassed!! I talked it up and then looked like an idiot. The food was good. I was a habitual customer since I can remember, My family and I were regulars. I actually liked it. Until I seen a COCKAROCH on my plate!!! Just crawling all over it leaving its trails of disease I still feel like vomiting when I think of it. I will never return!!! I'm working on reporting it to the health district but they aren't open until Monday Steer clear.!!! I am just updating my review cause I can't fathom why this place is open!!! It's now 9/1/16 there has been two reviews stating they had cockroaches in this sh*t hole I will attach a photo of the other reviewers picture. Unfortunately I did not get a photo however the roach on my plate was double the size. I almost burnt the place down in disgust!!! If that was on my plate and the roach Raul found was in the dining room imagine the kitchen.... Cockroach central!!!!!! Idk if I would eat food coming from that kitchen after I reading a review like this.... your welcome. I'm sad that a place where I had so many child memories is a dump. I will never return.

i love this place! 17 dollar meal for two (before tip but including iced teas) and i cannot get enough of their cheese crisps and mole...and enchiladas and....everything. seriously love the food and the atmosphere. it has a unique style and flavor that is hard to find in amongst the sea of mexican food of the southwest. also, extra star for attention to vegetarian items i.e., what is vegetarian and what can be made vegetarian. (EDIT: i got food poisoning at this place the week of thanksgiving, don't want to turn anyone away from it since it's locally owned and we all know that's rare, but i won't be heading back anytime soon...)

Oh, Hellas! We went there on a Friday night in hopes that I could tuck a belly dancer. When we got there, we were seated quickly and near the live band of two gentlemen - one playing a bouzouki, I think, and the other a guitar! It was a great surprise and in no way disappointing that there was a band instead of dancer. I love live entertainment. Our waitress was attentive and although they didn't have a gluten free menu, they were able to offer anything grilled and a salad. Since I didn't want to risk any of the side items having gluten, I asked for a slightly larger salad, which they quickly brought out. The salad was enormous and could have been a meal itself! My love had the saganaki (it is a compulsion now to get it when we can) and he said it was good. He also had the pasticcio which he said was different from others that he had, but was itself very good. I had the lamb souvlaki and it had great flavor. The only thing that was really strange was that my food was wet. Usually, when things are grilled (this had the grill marks), it is fairly dry and crisp, but this souvlaki had a bit of liquid on the bottom of the plate. Salads often have liquid if the lettuce isn't spun, but the entree was a bit strange. The flavor was good though and when I go back, it will be on a Fri or Sat for the entertainment. OPA!

The last two pizzas I have had at Noble pie have been Terrible!!! I live a couple blocks away and had really hoped for better so I could make it a staple. Last nights Gluten Free pizza was a under cooked nasty doughy terrible pizza.. Ask for gluten free and it is this restaurants chance to rip you off. Come on $19 for a small .. Not going again and will never recommend..

I recently went to this BJs with my boyfriend and roommate and had some issues. I have some very severe and life threatening food allergies and am very careful about telling servers about them so I don't, you know, die. This was the first time in years that I forgot to do so, but as I've eaten at this restaurant before, I knew what to avoid so I wasn't too worried (I made sure nothing I ordered had any nuts listed in the ingredients I didn't participate in the appetizers because I was unsure about the ingredients). Out comes our food and I notice something strange--almonds, or what looked like them, on my pasta. I have my boyfriend take a bite and he unfortunately confirms my suspicions. We immediately alert the server who apologized profusely and takes the pasta, bringing it back to the kitchen to be replaced. Luckily everything turned out fine, the wait staff was amazing, and I didn't end up needing to use my EpiPen. Here's the issue, though--if I had taken a bite, it is very possible that something serious may have happened to me, and I definitely would have gone to the hospital. It's not too much to ask, right? That a chef doesn't add ingredients to a dish without listing it? Because if it happened to me then it probably has happened to other people. All in all I probably won't go back, not because the food wasn't delicious or that the wait staff had any issues, but because I shouldn't have to risk serious health problems when I eat pasta.

So my girlfriend and I decided to give this place another chance and it didn't turn out any better than the first time. We both ended up with mild food poisoning. Both times I had a burger and both times I got it cold. My girlfriend got the native stripper platter and that was also cold. We waited about 25 minutes for the food so I didn't want to have to wait again just for them to remake my order. Also I'm not sure if it's the way they make their wings but the wings looked as if they got dipped in the sauce then had the sauce wiped off and placed on the side. I Will never eat at any native grill again

There's a surprising amount of good, authentic Mexican is this area, so I was surprised when I saw this chain place open, but we decided to give it a try anyway because it was so close by. First up was the guacamole, as I saw the cart for made-at-the-table guac being pushed around and got excited for fresh avocado. Our order was NOT made at the table, for which no explanation was given. It was also TINY and badly in need of salt. I suspect a premade and refrigerated vat of the stuff, scooped out with an small ice-cream scoop. The chips were bland and stale (think rubbery.) For the entree, I got the tacos barbacoa, and my companions got the enchiladas with mole sauce and the chimichangas. The tacos were soaked in some kind of oil or grease, so much so that they could not be picked up. The tortillas underneath were literally dissolving. Super gross. The meat - and there was only meat on the tacos, no onions or anything else - wasn't impressive. There were a couple big pieces of gristle I had to discreetly remove. The spicing was not a usual barbacoa, either - I love barbacoa (preferably with goat, which this place notably does not serve), and this tasted like no barbacoa I've ever had. It turns out that that is probably a good thing, as I had an allergic reaction to something in it later that night. My only allergy is cardamom, not usually a barbacoa spice, so who knows what that was. The server (who was the one good part of the whole experience) asked my fiancé if he'd had mole sauce before, as they "make it different here." They certainly do, but not in a good way! Fiancé's first reaction was that it was "bland." Enchiladas in mole sauce is one of the ways he judges a good Mexican place, and this place disappointed. The mole tasted like it was ketchup-based. The chimichangas were large but also bland and boring, and not crispy on the outside at all. The rice was yellow, but tasted like plain rice to which tiny bits of frozen carrots and peas had been added. For all this, also, it wasn't cheap. The far better, far more authentic restaurants in the area are cheaper, too! Even without the allergic reaction, between the terrible taste and the price, I'd give this place one star. Our waitress is the ONLY reason this place gets two stars. We will not be back.

Famoso salad is good, but the menu lacks gluten free options. Pizza according to my friends is good. I don't like that you order at the cashier and they just bring you your food. no waiter service for food, just drinks.

We were downtown to book a staycation for next week and decided to grab a late lunch here. The staff was nice (blonde woman bartender and a tall bearded guy) and I was THRILLED to get a draft beer that wasn't competeing in the "Our IPA tastes more like sweatsocks than yours!" Competiton. Firestone Pils for the win! He got a plain slice and about 8 minutes later I got my meatball Stromboli. If you put 7 (I counted when I was removing them) whole cloves of garlic in a thing that is only six inches long, maybe include them in the menu description. That's more garlic than cheese. I accidentally bit into one and it almost burned. I couldn't eat anything else for a while. And I got it with chips. Which were some kind of vegan/gluten free vegetable based pseudo chip. In addition to being unsalted, a major ingredient in them is mushrooms. My mother would have needed an epi pen, my sister would have broken out in hives, and I didn't eat more than 2 because I'm trying not to exacerbate a sensitivity into a full blown allergy. Chips implies potato chips. Not compressed powdered veggies. I'm sure it's fantastic when you are drunk.

I came here after searching on Yelp for "Gluten Free bakeries" but they had only one type of crusty muffin available. She forgot about my son's ice cream and when I went up to ask about it she stopped mopping, didn't wash her hands and put it In a to-go cup because I guess she wanted to leave right at closing. I was too stunned to say anything. The furniture is also really threadbare and gross.

The original store in Jackson, MS is one of my family's favorites so it's really disappointing to go to this location & be so let down. The food was eh okay, but i was up all night, really sick with stomach issues. I still feel a bit queasy. I know it wasn't likely food poisoning, but I felt so gross & icky and like i said... up all night sick. the coleslaw was strangely dry too & we realized we were never served pickled onions, supposedly a part of the meal. our waitress was very nice & attentive, the only redeeming things abt the experience

Cut to the chase-I may have just had the best meal so far in over a year in Nashville. Now back to the beginning. The Old School Farm is so much more than a restaurant, make it a destination and plan on relaxing, unwinding and sitting a spell. After all, you didn't take the drive out in the country to hurry things, now did you? We arrived early on a Friday, and made our way into the bar for a flight of ciders. They have several local beers on tap as well as Guinness, along with the above mentioned ciders. The wine list looked extensive and they're crafting some very inventive house made cocktails. We sampled the Bloody Mary with house made tomato juice bursting with the flavor of the garden. They have a beautiful large bar room with stage for live music and tables to dine here besides the main dining room. Since they weren't yet busy we could engage with the staff and learn more about the wonderful program the Old School Farm supports as well as their bee keeping endeavors. The menu changes weekly depending on what's fresh from the garden and the local farms. We decided on three plates to share. A roasted eggplant dip with grilled flatbread, roasted baby beets over yogurt drizzled with their local honey, and the shining star- sweet corn ricotta tortellini with pea shoots and soft boiled quail egg with chili oil. One bite of the tortellini and we both declared it the best pasta we can remember having. We finished our meal with a dessert of deconstructed grasshopper pie. Every plate was a winner. While we were dining the jazz quartet added to the ambience. We took time to walk the property, admiring their gardens, chicken coops and bee hives. It looks like they have an open air building that would be perfect for weddings or events. A visit here is so much more than just a meal, it's an experience worth taking your time to explore.

Really delicious, unique food and I greatly appreciated that they had some gluten-free options. I had the salmon tacos and they were phenomenal. Also had guacamole with veggies (sliced cucumber, jicama, radish) and that was delicious too. Excellent service from the waitress and the food presentation is gorgeous.
