The reason I gave them 3 instead of 4 stars is because the manager forgot about me when I asked a question. He left to ask the chef and he never came back to our table. The manager needs to have the best customer service out of everyone.

Food is very good. We get it to go usually. We continue to go there because they have gluten free food that has never made my husband sick. However, they make errors in our order almost every time and give incorrect wait times- had to wait over a half hour after the specified time. Not happy with service.

I really wanted to like this place since there's a scarcity of decent Asian food in the area. We finally tried Souzou last week and I could've easily passed off the experience as unmemorable, but the service unfortunately had me remembering for all the wrong reasons. For an upscale Japanese restaurant, the sushi selection was basic. Our first indicator was that our waiter didn't know what "ebi" was (it was on the menu). Then my bf asked how the fried rice is prepared, and the waiter replied, "In a wok." I think we could gather that much, but he was asking for allergy reasons. Meaning: ingredients. Finally, my friend almost had her wine spilled on her multiple times. Pardon your reach? Definitely not worth the price of the entrées, we won't be coming back.

Stopped in here with a few friends on the way back to Edmonton from an event in St. Albert. Cozy little place, with lots of gluten-free items on the menu. I had a cappuccino and I thought it tasted great, albeit reading a bit more like a latte with extra foam, but I don't necessarily think that is a bad thing. The others at my table said the soup was really good, as was the sandwich that was ordered. There was only one person working the front counter, so it did take a while to get acknowledged as he was busy getting other people's orders together. However, I would come here again if I am ever in St. Albert and need coffee.

If you like very well done thin pizza this place is for you. Unfortunately, that is not my taste in pizza. I did email the store and let them know I was not happy with my food. The reason I did not give this place one star was because they promptly emailed me back answering all of my concerns- even offering me a free pizza. Also, they do offer a gluten free pizza which is rare for pizza shops and my mom was happy she could get something from a pizza shop like the rest of us.

If I was rating the food alone - I would give it 3-4 stars. It is reasonably priced, the sushi is fresh and the delivery is quick, however my negative review is due to the fact that they almost killed me. I am highly allergic to shellfish but have been eating Chinese food for 25 years no issues. I ordered a combo platter that comes with an eggroll and either they make their eggrolls with shrimp or they mixed up and gave me a shrimp springroll. Either way I am lucky for my Epi-pen. I understand its common for Asian dishes to have shellfish but I have never heard of an eggroll with shrimp in it, so I am inclined to think they got my order wrong. I also tried to call and let them know what happened and just got put on hold. So if you have no food allergies, this place is great, but beware otherwise. =(

Ok... so how can I put this. I went with two other people because one of them really wanted to go and I told them it probably wasn't a good idea and the one who really wanted to go got diarrhea and the other one who was foolish enough to go threw up all night. As for me, I had a sub-par meal but didn't get sick because I chose something that I knew would be burned to a crisp therefore could not get me sick even if it didn't taste good. I am not a fan of the whole Applebees/Chili's/TGIFriday's chain only because they put in way too much salt, burn most of the dishes, are greasy, and have flavors in all the wrong places. Service was good but that couldn't save their menu. The only thing I remotely enjoyed was their sweet potato fries. If you must go, just order this and you should survive alright. Parking: Shared lot Price: $10-$15 per person Wait: 10 mins after ordering

To anyone with food allergies, this place is probably amazing. Coming from someone who doesn't have food allergies and is vegan, I have had MUCH better desserts. Nothing is outstanding and most items are just okay. My suggestion if you have food allergies: Enjoy, because you probably don't get these desserts often. My Suggestion if you're vegan with no allergies: Walk a street over to Govinda's who get's some AMAZING desserts from Vegan Treats. Now those treats will really make you happy!

Extremely poor customer service from the manager, Brandon. We had an incident where there was a misunderstanding about the contents of a brown ale that we picked up from the store. We had initially ordered a Civil Life Brown, which we were old after the order was placed that it was out of stock. We agreed to get a different Brown instead, at a cost of $90. However, upon reading the label of the keg returning home, we noticed that there were pecans in the ale. As we have a relative that is highly allergic to nuts (anaphylactic shock allergic), we did not want to install the keg in the kegerator due to contamination concerns. We immediately called the store and explained the situation and that we would like to return the keg. The store was completely unwilling to accept the keg back into their store to obtain a refund due to "Company policy". We spoke to multiple contacts at the store, all of which pointed to Company policy for their decision, without any attempt to understand the situation and acknowledge that we had been reliable customers and were willing to work with them to resolve the misunderstanding. We returned the keg 2 hours after it was initially purchased, receiving the $50 deposit fee back but not receiving any of the $90 cost of the beer that we were unable to tap at the house in order to keep our family safe. Due to their complete unwillingness to listen to our situation, and the fact that they took our $90 without refunding us any of the difference, Friar Tucks has lost the business of our entire family. We are extremely disappointed in the management of the Crestwood location.

I don't understand anyone who says this restaurant is good. I will say that the chips and salsa were good, but that was the one redeeming part of our meal. I ordered the chilaquiles, mainly because I thought it would be hard to mess up, and it was one of the few items on the menu that did not have cheese dip on it. I am lactose intolerant, so I can't eat anything with cheese dip (made of real cheese). I don't eat artificial cheese at all. Chilaquiles is supposed to consist of tortillas and salsa fried with egg. The menu said that this specific version had chicken on it, which is also normal. However, El Stuffed Pepper apparently does not use eggs but instead uses cheese dip... All of the tortillas were mixed with cheese dip. So basically, I was unable to eat my dinner due to a dietary restriction... which I had no way of knowing would play a role in my meal. I also can't imagine that this would have been edible even if I had been able to eat the cheese dip. It looked like a huge mushy mess, and my fiance said it was inedible. I thought I might have just ordered the wrong thing here... but after splitting my fiance's meal and us both having upset stomachs for several hours after, we will not be back.

Visited El Sitio on a random Thursday night and was happy with it, though I don't know that I ordered quite right. First of all - this place is definitely gluten free friendly. There was quite a bunch of things to choose from, and the waitress was very helpful and knowledgable about good choices for me. My friend Linda and I started with a mushroom appetizer that was yummy - I think they were marinated in a chimichurri-type sauce. Yum. Then we had these flattened plantains with a dollop of guac and a salsa on it - YUMMY. Very good! Entrees were good, but I think I should have gone with a grilled meat here. I chose the Peruvian Picante, which I thought was a seafood stew of sorts. My friend went with the chicken stew, which also had the same yellow-ish sauce on it. The two dishes we got were described so differently on the menu, and yet they looked quite similar in this bright colored sauce! Either way, the portions were nice-sized, and my dish was decent, but I think another dish here would have been better. I will definitely be back. Places like this give Collingswood a great variety of spots to try!
GOT FOOD POISONING HERE! DO NOT EAT!... The wings weren't that great either, regardless of whatever nasty bacteria they had crawling on them.

I finally had the chance to stop by The Jam due to a rumbling stomach and a crazy work schedule. As I was driving in the Wedgewood area, I kept thinking, "I am starving, I am starving", but I did not want to fight parking in the 21st/Belmont/12 South area due to lunch time. So as I came up and saw The Jam's cute retro sign, angels started to sing as I thought MUFFINS AND COFFEE! When you walk in, it has a cute retro feel. I love the vintage furniture. There was a small menu of hot breakfast items, but I was in a rush. The muffins are homemade, so while they may not be the prettiest things on the planet, they are really good. The gluten free pumpkin muffin was moist. It was a little difficult to eat in the car due to just how moist it was, so I feel like a fork would be in order for next time. The ice coffee is very yummy. Once again, I love that another coffee shop can make and appreciate a good cup of iced coffee. I will for sure check this place out again on the fly due to it's friendly customer service and ample working space. Also, great parking!

My friend picked to go here for her birthday after getting a living social / Groupon deal. We have gone before and it is a good time if you're into Karokoe. She made a reservation for a room on a Saturday night and there were no problems with that. So we got in the room and looked over the menus and go to order sushi only to find out that they no longer serve sushi. Bummer but not the end of the world. My vegetarian friend who is gets very sick with shellfish ordered the vegetarian soup. It comes out and she instantly suspected that there was shrimp in the soup. It had a fishy smell and she thought she could see chunks. So she tried a small sip and felt that she was confident with knowing there was shrimp. So I tried some and agreed that yes, she's right. Keep in mind that it's dark in the room so it's really hard to see your food. So she tells our server about it and the server disagreed with her, assuring my friend that she received the vegetarian soup and that she's just not used to the taste possibly because it's asian. Now my friend not wanting to cause a scene just said ok. She knew she was right and the server was wrong and so when the server came back she told her again, only this time insisted. So the server pulled the other server that happened to be in our room and they both leaned over the soup and inspected it before agreeing that it's possible my friend is correct, then our server took the soup back to the kitchen. Later she comes back with a new bowl that IS vegetarian and explain that the two soup are next to each other in the kitchen and it was the kitchen's mistake and they are so sorry. I get that there are mistaken in restaurants all the time BUT IMO with the amount of people that are allergic to shellfish, why would you have the two soup next to each other. Plus I thought it was not appropriate on how the server told my friend the first time that she was wrong. Since I didn't see the bill in the end (just handed over my portion) I'm not sure if they compted the soup or not. Other than that, I'm not sure what goes into getting the rights for songs but the song selection is mediocre and some of the videos for the songs feel like they were filmed in another decade in other countries. One video for a current song had a family swimming in the ocean with a naked baby and the camera just stayed on the baby for an uncomfortable amount of time.

Disappointing, un-imaginative, bland food. Especially from a chef with another well-loved restaurant in town. From the blog upon opening in 2014, Owner Woolsey writes "To me, Bistrot La Minette and La Peg are members of my family. They're babies that require nurturing and guidance." It seems as if Peter Woolsey has lost his way with La Peg, as clearly there is no guidance in the kitchen. Oysters had bits of shell and were not properly released in their shells, making them difficult and unpleasant to eat. The Salmon arrived overcooked on a bed of bland rice blend that took over the plate, think diner portion here. No thought or creativity went into seasoning or plating. There was barely a hint of the promised hollandaise. Birthday celebrant pined for crème brulee, and after ordering, 10 minutes later discovered they are out of it. The proverbial icing on the cake was the ladies room with vomit gracing one of the commodes. Who is overseeing this Woolsey family member? The ambiance is super hip in an historic pumping station on the river, and the service was excellent. Mr. Woolsey needs to spend some time in this kitchen and whip it into shape before he has to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

Ever been to a place that tries to be something more than it really is? Well this is that place. Take a location in an upscale neighborhood, describe menu items like no one else has ever cooked them and tell your servers there can be no requests or changes.....no matter what the customer wants or asks! Then you have the Fat Hen Deli! Menu items are over priced and the staff have a sarcastic tone when you ask for anything to be cooked or served the way you like it. Their main item, the Shane Burger. You don't like onions, you want onions on the side, you are allergic to onions....too bad! They WILL NOT serve the burger without cooked onions! I'm not kidding! And if they say the portions are "hearty," well no there not. Great food and impeccable service make any restaurant. Let's just say they are trying, but not trying hard.

Cannot believe this hype monster breathes fire with five star reviews. Maybe if you love salty feces slithering down your throat and surly employees who have to "make nice" when the management is present. Christ. Typical cafeteria routine. Think Lubys on a smaller scale. They're doing construction inside. Maybe cleaning the salty vomit off the booth backs. I dunno. Reached for a Hot Chocolate Pie, a brownie pie with cayenne pepper added to it, the old woman didn't like how I moved one of the plates to reveal a much bigger piece behind it. "Can't touch the plates" she yapped. How about cutting them even then? Black eyed peas and turnip greens with roast beef for the meat. Holy Man. This shit was pure salt. Like licking Usain Bolts Balls after one of his Olympic runs. OMG It was so over salted that I didn't know if I was in an Old age home of just in a shithole. Inedible. Those who give good reviews have no taste buds left.
Thumbs down. :( No gluten free options. The establishment is very clean and staff is very nice through.

Amazes me that people are lining up for overpriced pizza on a tasteless crust. Ingredients are top notch, toppings on most pies are good, people are friendly. Crust is terrible. Gluten free crust is worse. Bleh.

Our Valentine's Day dinner turned out to be a preparation for a colonoscopy (x100). The restaurant took our order over the phone and within 20 minutes I picked up our food. The people there were very friendly. The food tasted fine, but halfway through the meal, I started feeling sick to my stomach and excused myself to use the bathroom. I ended vomitting portions of my meal that evening. At first, I didn't think it was the sushi because my wife felt fine after her dinner (so we thought). Fast forward to 1am, I was in the bathroom vomitting again. Around 2am, my wife ended up doing the same thing and she hasn't stopped since. It is now Monday and my wife is still suffering from food poisoning. It's more than a coincidence that we both got sick from the sushi on the same night. I have seen my parents prep for a colonoscopy many times and our experience is quite similar with body aches and pain.

Doesn't care or consider allergies or dietary restrictions. They won't make eggs to order and they put milk in the eggs. I would give 0 stars if yelp would allow. Dairy is a common allergy an lifestyle choice. They don't even tell anyone. I only found out because she asked if I wanted a sandwich an I told her no dairy no gluten. It should be posted on their menu since there is no alternative/substitute. It would've saved me the walk . Your a customer service based business you should be catering to more than just what you want and like.

Really good, big burgers! I can't give it 4 or 5 stars though because of the fries. Although they are good, they're just not crunchy. Sure they're fresh, I mean they slice 'em on site, but they're limp. They taste okay, but I prefer a fry with some crisp and a little more flavor. You pay a good amount to eat here so I expect the fries to live up to the burger. When I brought my wife and son here there were several minutes that passed between each of our orders being ready. We put it on one order but the food wasn't ready at the same time. I didn't want my wife's food to get cold so we told her to go ahead and start eating. A couple of minutes later my son's food was ready and then another minute or so mine was ready. One more thing to make note of, they use peanut oil so my wife, who has a nut allergy, can't eat the fries. For people who have a severe nut allergy you probably should stay away all together.

We ordered a buffalo chicken pizza - cost us $20, including the extra $1 they charged us for a side of ranch. It was drowned in oregano, it looked like the cap fell off while they were making the pizza. The waitress was not friendly. Immediately after while walking back to our hotel next door, we both got hit with a wave of nausea and both threw up once back at our hotel. Not ok, don't go here.

I have never had food poisoning before eating here! Not only was I poisoned, so was the person I went out to eat with. I called the Camden County food safety board and they said I was not the only person to call in the same week. We ate completely different meals with no similar items so they said it was most definitely a cleanliness issue. I left after eating here and it wasn't an hour later before I was violently sick. I have never been so sick in my entire life! I threw up and down no less than 30-40 times over that night. I had to carry a bucket through the house with me for two days. I called my friend the next day and she had the same debilitating experience. I had to cancel work for the rest of the week costing me about $1,200 making this the most expensive meal I have even eaten. I have eaten many questionable things in my life (I remember a tuna hoagie that had been left out in the sun) and have never gotten sick. I can't imagine what could be going on there for something like this to happen but I know for sure I won't be going back to find out.

I'm torn between 3-4 stars for Blue Tortilla. The food was good, but not out of this world, and it's so strange that it would be BYOB. A little awkward even, in my opinion. The margaritas they serve are very weak, so it's really like you're just drinking margarita mix, but again, in my opinion. I will say the gluten free chips and red and green salsa were really good. I had the chicken tinga, which was tasty, but I wasn't a fan of my friend's chicken pumpkin spiced dish. It's in a nice area though, so on a beautiful day I would return for a Mexican fix.

Best gluten free breakfast in Reno! Safe for people with gluten allergies and sensitivities. The staff is very careful to avoid cross contamination. GF pancakes and waffles are so good. Great GF lunch options as well.
Food was good. Have great happy hour specials. Server was kind. Our lacked "crunch". Egg rolls were delicious. Willing to work with allergies!

We almost left this place as soon as we got their because of the bar tender. I asked if they had any drink specials and he said "everything is special" and walked off. Then he told the other bar tender who was getting ready to ask for our order that we don't know what we want. She came back a few minutes later and we took our best guess on what might be a good beverage. Since our group wanted to stay and eat, we did. The waiter was much better than the staff at the bar. He actually helped out with the menu, recommendations and even checked with the chef to confirm menu items my daughter wanted could be prepared gluten free based on her dietary requirements with celiac disease. Maybe they can have the bar tender shadow him one night to learn about customer service. The food was good so no complaints there and this is a great place to eat at sunset overlooking the beach.

Terrible! I thought I was very satisfied and write you guys a great review but I've been sitting here calculating how many thousands or tens of thousands of dollars I've spent in 20 years of drinking one almost every day at three to now 5+ dollars a pop and you cannot seem to get my banana allergy correct. I'm having a huge allergic reaction because of you and it's not OK. It's very dangerous and I'm furious. I've been a customer as I said I literally ask since I moved to town and 97 and to get sick from your products constantly and have to ask them to make me another one and watch the wrong one get tossed down the floor drain is just too much. This one I had driven home put it in the freezer and went to drink it for my morning and only meal and now my entire mouth is on fire and I don't have an EpiPen. It's not acceptable AT ALL!!!

This is a 3 star place. Service 2 stars Food 4 stars Our waiter, a younger clone of Jeff Foxworthy, and I could not get along. He is going to school as a welder. Perhaps, hidden under a mask, so he doesn't have to speak with any one, he will do better. We ordered a carafe of red wine. There were five of us, and he automatically said the carafe only is four servings, perhaps two? 22 ounce carafe to start is good enough since I don't know how the HOUSE wine tastes. Also, one of us does not drink. Also the rest of the party has not arrived yet. Now we order the cheese tray. And he reminds us that it is a SMALL portion of cheese. Should we order two? Do we mention that 1/2 of us is lactose intolerant? The tray came and it was a pitiful portion of regular very day cheese. Every one, save me liked their food. I got the duck burger. Meh. The trout, the gnocchi, the roast chicken he salmon, were all reported and looked good. I was the only one who ordered wrong. Time for dessert and once again the "too small for you portion wise" comes up. We finish and I ask for a to go box. Twenty (20) minutes later it comes back. The waiter was AWOL. If a guy looking like Foxworthy shows up at your welding job, make sure he has his tools.

Worst boba I've ever had. Came here on a Saturday afternoon and ordered the rose. It looked and tasted like vomit. The syrup was way too strong and had no sweetness at all. Not only that but they served the drink to me warm with little bits of ice in it that melted straight away and had no effect on the temperature of the rest of the drink. Drinks were also over priced. This is what you get when you try boba in a non Asian dominant community.

Very difficult to find a good burger in W. Philadelphia--swear sometimes that it's much more difficult not to be a vegan or vegetarian in my neighborhood! That being said, Local 44 has a pretty decent burger and it's very easy to find a good beer to wash it down with. Also, perhaps one of the only places I've patronized that has a palatable gluten-free beer. Props.

Lucky you to have stumbled upon this life saving review. I can't believe what I was served. For $20, a side salad with stale shredded cheese and cheap croutons over mixed greens, and the unforgivable, crawfish etouffe. A brown curd like substance that carried 3 tiny crawfish over rice that may have broke my teeth. I keep it real, I rarely give such a review but this is purpose of yelp. You want real, NOLA food, then get out of the quarter and go to Jacques-imos cafe. Or anywhere in the garden distric, midcity, or uptown. Otherwise plan on being constipated and nauseous as a result of the food poison in the quarter.

Horrible food. Ordered the baked Alfredo Chicken...sounds good, right? Not at all! The chicken was obviously frozen for a long time before they cooked it, you could taste the freezer burn on it. There was absolutely no "Alfredo" sauce, just a bunch of noodles and cheese. You can't call it an Alfredo dish if there is no sauce. Their "garlic" bread isn't garlic...its some weird pesto garbage. Save yourself from going here! These people should be ashamed of themselves to let food leave their kitchen. I'm probably going to get food poisoning from this.

Desperate for a place to sit on memorial day weekend, We went up to the second floor, the smell of fresh vomit greeted us. Sat down, a rush and haggered waiter took our drink order. Sat around for a few, ate some wings and onion rings, it was just not a good night to be there, bailed quickly.

I told the server I had a Gluten allergy prior to ordering. I spoke with 3 people about my allergy, the manager said he could accommodate. After I spoke to everyone the server brought me out chips and told me these are GF. After I ate a couple the chips the manager came out with a separate plate of chips and informed me the ones I have been eating were cross contaminated. He did nothing to make up for his employees mistake and I was so sick that night. It's a shame because the food is actually really good but the worst services and staff is very careless and poorly trained
The food was tasty, but I believe i got food poisoning from here after ordering on UberEats. This is really disappointing because I originally enjoyed what I got. :(
The inappropriate and rude hostess overshadowed the par Italian cuisine. Fortunately they have a knowledge of gluten free cooking and offer rice pasta.

Stopped in because my original restaurant choice had a 30 minute wait and El Sitio was empty. Cue the "after-the-fact realization". I'm not coming back. Not because I was wronged or food poisoned, I just don't see the point. I started with the surprisingly bland grilled provolone appetizer. I guess if you add enough oil to something, it will eventually lose any semblance to the original object...(maybe that means I had a homeopathic appetizer?). The entrees are not memorable, and service is slow. Why bother?

The lines are always long, and there's never enough cashiers open in the 20 or less lanes. Samples are only out about once a day, if you show up after work, expect everything to be gone. They have almost nothing for you if you're diabetic, but you can get vegan/gluten-free everything.

I really am disappointed in this location. I am on a restricted caffeine diet due to high miscarriage rate. Two times now I have gone through drive-thru and ordered a decaf latte. It shows up on the board as a regular café latte. When I get to the window both times they have been very confused on whether or not it was a decaf latte they handed me or a regular. But instead of checking with whoever made it they just assumed it was decaf and sent me on my way. I didn't trust that it was a regular decaffeinated coffee since the servers were so unsure, so neither times did I drink the coffee I ordered after I specifically made it clear to them I could not drink a regular coffee. I don't think the staff care they just want to get you away from their window. They obviously do not care about people's allergies or restrictions as to why they need foods made a certain way. I'll drive the extra two minutes down the road to go to the Abbey from now on.

I was really excited to come here because I had heard good things about it, but it definitely fell short of expectation. The dining experience started with the worker cutting her had and just rinsing it off and putting on new gloves which I feel like is probably against some code if not just social code. When she took our order she was friendly and was helpful. However, she definitely skimped on the cheese as if it was a precious commodity and cross contaminated ingredients like no other. DO NOT COME HERE IF YOU HAVE STRICT DIETARY RESTRICTIONS because like I said the sauce ladles were contaminated when I asked about mixed sauces, she was grabbing veggies with the same hand she grabbed meat with, she dropped olives in the spinach, garlic in the peppers, you get the point. Next, my mom ordered a beer. They have a local brewery on tap so my mom asked what it was like, the girl said kind of like a citrus-wheat. When she brought out the beer it was way closer to an IPA and she asked my mom how it was and we confirmed that it was what she ordered. The girl then informed us that she doesn't really drink beer but that's what she was told it tasted like. We told her that don't say that because it's totally inaccurate. She didn't offer to switch out the beer or anything which was kind of disappointing. Our pizzas were good and it's a great concept, I'm hoping that I just caught them on an off day.

What is all the fuss about? After hearing an obnoxious amount of people say that New Delhi is, "by far," the best Indian food in Philly, I had to give it a try. What did I find? Meh. Being a huge advocate for Indian food and a regular diner and buffet patron, I have been to my share of Indian restaurants in the area: Ekta, Tiffin, Himalayan, Delhi, Sitar, and the list goes on. The New Delhi dinner buffet is perhaps one-up from the bottom of my list. Options-wise, they simply didn't have that much to offer; two chicken dishes, one of which featured "white meat" which was in fact dark, and tandoori chicken which wasn't horrible, but definitely on the dryer side. Their saag took on a shade that resembled an olive brown, rather than green--was the spinach fresh? Their vegetable pakoras consisted of pieces of puny, slightly burnt cauliflower pieces covered in gobs of batter; the pakora chicken wings were not burnt, but simply had almost no meat to them. The vegetable malai kofta were decent, but also not the best I've ever had. All in all, the buffet was a bit too americanized for my liking, (there was macaroni salad in the salad bar!), and not spicy in the slightest bit. Maybe that's why people like it? All-in-all, the food was mediocre, some dishes even being cold (not intentionally), and not too many options to choose from on top of this. New Delhi is very attentive service-wise, however, with servers constantly coming around, asking how you are and attempting conversation. Not always what one wants when eating their meal; yet, at least dirty plates were taken away speedily. They also serve you your choice of dessert to your table, which is a nice touch. The pistachio ice cream itself was just average, but I liked that aspect of their service nevertheless. In the University City district, skip New Delhi and head on over to the tastier, albeit shabbier looking, Sitar a few blocks away. I'm giving New Delhi three stars because they also labeled the buffet item's if they were gluten-free or containing potential allergens, which pleased my gluten-sensitive self. I knew what I was getting, even if it didn't take the greatest.

Only giving 2 stars because of the meat in my vegan meal. At a teacher training right down the street. Went here for lunch 2 times in a week. Friendly and quick staff. However, I am a strict vegan and found a chunk of beef not once but both times in my sofrita salad!!!!!! Cross contamination? I noticed the sofritas are located at the far end of the service bar/station so not as if the meat was dripped from a passing spoon. Not sure how this happened but twice in one week? I wont order the sofritas again too much of a risk.

HORRIBLE FOOD !!! Horrible service!!! I ordered a turkey bacon egg and cheese because I am allergic to pork! And sure enough they gave me a sandwich with one egg & pork bacon!! When i reported that it was the wrong order, they said it was the correct order! IN WHAT WORLD IS TURKEY BACON AND PORK BACON THE SAME! The sandwich looked like a child made it. Disgusting! I immediately threw it in the trash n would NEVER order from there again!! Stay awayy!!

This was an extremely disappointing experience. Stopped by around 3pm on a Sunday. No one was dining in, but their takeout and delivery business was keeping them extremely busy. We ordered the Tuscan pizza with gluten free crust. Even setting aside the possibility they have a really poor GF crust, the pizza was awful. They forgot the grilled onions and thyme (2 items on the description) and somehow managed to both overcook the pizza and serve it lukewarm! How is serving lukewarm pizza even possible when there is only one patron is in the restaurant? It was probably the worst pizza experience I've had. To their credit they were very apologetic and baked a replacement pizza at no charge. But it was only slightly better. They also didn't charge for the beer I ordered while waiting for the re-do. I appreciated that. Even if GF crust is lacking you can still make a topping that holds its own; however, Zpizza failed spectacularly even at that. Food: 1 star. Service 3 (for trying). Average: 2.

Nice space and decent enough neighborhood bar. The food I got...the Kathy Romano wrap....was terrible. I had a big chunk of chicken skin in the middle of it and had to ask for more ranch dressing that tookTEN MINUTES to get from the bartender. That was after I asked for a second beer from a different bartender but she threw up her hands and said, "I'm done" and wouldn't take my order. At 8pm at night? Weird. My husband's burger looked great and the fries were good but I was seriously disappointed by the food. Funny enough, the lollygagging bartender had a shirt on that said, "the food doesn't SUCK". How wrong that was!

Had lunch here a few weeks ago and got great customer service. I had the Umami burger in my hands within about 2 minutes of my ordering (when was the last time that ever happened to you at a *good* food truck?? exactly...). My only issue and why I don't go here all the time is that the bun is not great and seemed to give me an almost immediate allergic reaction (lot of dairy in the bread?). Just thought I would mention in case anyone is lactose-intolerant, as I am 98% sure that was the issue.

Must've picked the wrong night to try this joint. They were out of nearly everything I wanted to try. They don't serve chicken The sides all looked dry & old. Needing replenishment. The customer service was terribly sour & rushed (namely Jess at the register) Explained it was my first visit and the protein guy didn't give a damn...kept it moving like an assembly line. First experience was a busy and totally not what I expected since everyone compares it to Pappy's which is my fav (not just today, check my review) I love Pappy's because all things are properly aligned: food, service, freshness. My sister liked the brisket and I thought the turkey was pretty good. Both were well smoked in our opinion. I have issues with Sugar Fire's sanitation. The tables needed to be busted, the sauce containers wiped, floor swept and food wells cleaned. Jess dumped the container of pickles sitting at the register for customers into the a larger batch of refrigerated pickles that stored the bulk of pickles for replenishing. Can you say contamination hazard! A random young man (maybe the friend of a coworker strolled through the kitchen area with FroYo) And 1 last thing, the gentlemen I assumed to be a manager began counting cash on the pie counter surrounded by food. I threw my hands up! C'mon guy, you've got to have an office around this place for business such as tallying profits and completing paperwork. Can you say unprofessional and tacky simultaneously! No thanks I'll pass...FOREVER!

Here right now having a bad experience. They do not cater to gluten free diets. My mom tried to get the grouper sandwich without the bun and asked if she could get lettuce leaves instead and the waitress gave her attitude and said she needed to order the dinner on the back instead and just pay the up charge to get something in substitution for the rice. My mom went for something completely different because of the fee. The waitress never came back to the table to refill our drinks and a man came put and tried to give our appetizer to two other tables before a different waitress said it must be ours. My dad was now upset and asked to talk to the manager, he apologized and said he would comp her meal but the check came and he did not do it. The waitress must have refused to come back she served other tables while giving us dirty looks. I just wanted my parents to have a nice beach experience on their vacation but it didn't work out that way. The food was typical.

Seemed like a good choice until we got home. Food Poisoning for over 24 hrs. Called the owner to make them aware. He thanked me but assured me that no one else was sick. Seemed fairly indifferent. If you wanna roll the dice be my guest. Too many other good places to eat.

I have tried so many times to like this place. I go over and over again because I really would like to support a local organic and healthy grocery store, but I just can't. 1. Customer Service is REAL spotty. There are literally 3 good employees that work there. The rest are just waiting until they can go home, are rude, don't care, or are super slow. 2. The hot bar is kind of disgusting. Imagine food sitting out for hours drying up to nothing. 3. I actually got pretty terrible food poisoning eating off their salad bar. 4. The prices can be over the top expensive on certain items. An item that is normally 2.99 everywhere else will be 5.99 at Earth Fare. I'm okay with a little mark-up, but that is crazy. 5. They are so concerned with leaving on time that they close everything down super early. I actually walked in and slipped because they had wet mopped the floor an hour before closing. An employee saw me slip and said nothing... of course. 6. I was trying to get ground beef out of their meat department. I asked the meat employee what the fat content was of the meat. He said 7%, I got the meat and clearly on the label when he handed it to me it said 14%. To me the fat in meat is very important to know. I try to eat lean. Every other grocery store, including Fresh Thyme and Kroger has meat that I can clearly see the fat content of. I've really gone a lot to try and give them many chances, but I'm done. To Kroger and Fresh Thyme I will go now.

This place was recommended to me but it was subpar to every hibachi restaurant I've ever been to, and I've been to a lot. The food was all under seasoned and flavorless, however, the portions were HUGE. The chef didn't do anything even remotely good either. The chef was terrible. He cooked the food so fast and even though there was a shellfish allergy he didn't clean anything or use different utensils so my boyfriend either had an allergic reaction or didn't eat :-/ even after voicing our concern he wouldn't do anything. We won't be back. Kinda ruined my birthday.

My fiancé brought me for a day getaway to Opryland. It was a beautiful, but I got food poisoning:( When I called to speak to the manager of the Cascade restaurant, the next day she was less than kind. I told her I wasn't looking for a refund, just to make them aware to double check things, so that no one else would get sick. No apology, no I'm sorry you were horribly sick. Just a reply of, I've received no other reports. No kindness what so ever. Very poor customer service. We will not be back.

I thought we had found the perfect sandwich shop and had found nora s thru a friend. Had been in a couple times and had good food and gluten free options. Twice now we have gone in and gotten rude service. One time a couple months ago the cashier was so angry about something that happened prior to us entering he was horribly rude to at least 6 customers including us. We didn't go back for a couple months because of this and went back last night and got less than friendly service. Guess I will look for somewhere else that will appreciate their customers. Too bad.
after getting food poisoning twice, I think I will just steer clear of this joint.

A good friend brought me a slice of cheesecake as a nice treat at work from here in June. She made sure to tell them I have a nut allergy, and was told that the cheesecake was nut free. The first thing she says as she sees me, handing me the cheesecake is "It's vegan and nut free!" After taking a tiny bite, I realized it most defiantly wasn't. I'm thankful I didn't have a larger bite that would have resulted in me going into anaphylactic shock, but it did result in getting sick enough to have to leave work early. I won't be spending money at a place that doesn't value my safety. I hope this establishment learns how unacceptable this is- and hopefully others with allergies can be warned to avoid Remedy.

I just called in to make a reservation and the host who took my call was just so unbelievably rude! I had one simple and important question which is life or death for me about my soy allergy! Not only did she not care calling it a "gluten" allergy and that i probably won't have much of an option (which is so dismissive) but made a very simple thing extremely complicated and told me to ask my server once I arrived when i asked her if she could find out! She was eagerly trying to get off the phone with me as i tired to explain to her that I checked online to find out if they have an allergy menu and that it did not specify if you cook with soy oil (I am anaphylactic which means I can die) if she could just please find out for me. She told me flat out NO! That the chefs were busy! I'm just so appalled by how out right rude and uncaring this lady is and how much of a disservice she is for your establishment! Clearly if you did cook in soy i wouldnt waste my time to drive there to then wait on my server to find out! I think its pitiful that your host can't answer basic questions about the food and that she clearly doesn't care enough to make time to find out! Needless to say i canceled my reservation. You should really be kinder to customers with questions especially if they are clear to inform its about an allergy. As for your host she definitely doesn't belong answering phone calls or handling customers at all!

Not fresh. Flavorless. My husband has a severe food allergy & the supervisor asked, "how allergic are you?" Not appropriate. Come to find out during this experience, nothing is fresh. They were able to check the boxes for ingredients (I guess we were lucky this was the case because none of the employees knew the ingredients in the dishes). Even the chicken was from a box & she said it was seasoned but not sure with what because she didn't still have the box. He had to eat awfully prepared, and quite boring, Mac & Cheese. My "spicy" dish lacked spice and flavor. I've been to this same brand in CO and it was so much better - and fresh... There's a lot of great restaurants in that area, but this wasn't one.

I am gluten free, and on the website the orange chicken stated it was GF. My mouth was watering all day long for my GF Orange Chicken! When we get to the restaurant, the menu said they are now using a 'new sauce' for the orange chicken and that it was no longer GF, and couldn't be made GF. I ended up ordering the chicken thai lettuce wraps ($10), which were okay but very salty. I also ordered the Miso Soup ($6), and it was the best part of the meal in my opinion- delish!! I ordered a side of Jasmine rice as well, and they charged me $4 for a tiny bowl of rice! The pros of this place are that they have an awesome wine and cocktail list, and the atmosphere was super hip and trendy. I think the food was sub par and overpriced for what I got, but I think I'd go back and give their sushi a try.

In regards to the food, most of the time I have had a four or five star experience here; however the customer service has been lacking. The kitchen staff is usually fighting with each other when I go in to pick up my breakfast order. I love their fresh clean menu, breakfast soufflés & frozen lemonade. However, I pay because I don't want to know who's dating who or who doesn't like each other behind the counter. I also was not impressed with their 'gluten conscious' cookies that are not gluten free & seem like a disaster waiting to happen.

This place is getting a three for great food and good prices. My onion allergy has always made it tough for me to eat anywhere. But after informing the cashier that I had an onion allergy and ordering my meal I found out that their dome fries are smothered in them. So a quick trip to the counter later A rude cashier simply told me my options where grits or more grits. Looked at me like I was doing something wrong , before the manger/owner? Came By And I let him know I Only Wanted A Pancake. He was very charming and gracious completely understanding. Delivered my pancake to the table with a smile

Cute, small space. It was pretty empty with one other table of two. The server was abrupt and intense and had weird timing. He told us what the brunch desserts were either right before we got our plates or before we even picked up our forks after we got our plates. The food: The biscuits and gravy were tiny and looked unappetizing, like gravy looks like literal barf and killed the presentation but it tasted good. Every component of the benedict that my husband got was totally disgusting. The english muffin tasted like I bit into fake, plastic groceries at the Please Touch Museum. We did not order gluten free and it wasn't indicated that this was the default bread in the menu. The veggie patty-like thing could have been replaced by a trader joes veggie burger and at least I would have eaten it instead of pushing it back over to my husband. Basically I left hungry after seeing the "dessert" that was delivered to the other table and hearing how hard it was for them to cut through this blueberry scone with a butter knife. Rocks with powdered sugar on them. We asked for the check and the server yoinked it up within a minute, not because he was a jerk but because it was just another off thing with regards to timing and overall feeling of a 2-bit operation. $31 total. I'm starting to think diners (as limited as they are with vegan selections) are the way to go. Plain home fries with salt 'n pepper would have won over the food taste and presentation at Flora and would have been 1/20th of the cost.

It has been a while since we have eaten at this location and now I remember why. They like to say they 'team serve' you, but what they really mean is no one serves you. Every time we have been to this location there is a problem. Always poor service. The manager is unfamiliar with how Foursquare check in specials work and basically accused me of checking in twice (how?) to earn my 3rd visit free dessert. In addition, this visit my burger was overcooked (I asked for medium, it was medium well) and found a hair in my fries. Lastly, I planned to order the chocolate peanut butter molten lava cake, then the waitress informed me she was allergic to peanuts so I would have to pay BEFORE I ate dessert! This is not how I would expect this to be handled. Please save yourself time and money and drive on by this location. Go the Hendersonville location instead!

My husband chose this restaurant after searching through many options for Mother's Day. The person he spoke to said they had lots of gluten free options that included bread items. Well...not so much. For someone who is gluten free and doesn't eat meat, eggs is your only choice. The manager cleared that up for us in a mostly nice manor and we thought we were fine, eggs and potatoes well done. First my husbands eggs came with the chicken he requested be left out, and both our potatoes came mostly raw. The waiter was very polite and apologized multiple times. The manager brought one plate of potatoes recooked and then when she found out we were still waiting on another plate she yelled "you're welcome!" From across the room. Rude to say the least. Considering it is Mother's Day Kitchen Bar was less than prepared and disorganized at the best. We will not be returning here ever!

Two stars because I really wanted to like this place and the food was not bad. Now that that's said... I really should give them one star. Ordered pho again last night. Meat comes raw and then it cooks quickly in the hot broth. But if the meat is not fresh... You get food poisoning! And, boy, the kitchen and/or preparation must have been unsanitary or really not up to par because Omg I thought I've experienced food poisoning before but this was bad. Semi Liquid coming out of every orifice. I literally passed out and woke back up drenched in sweat screaming in pain. Never have I experienced poisoning to this severity and never will I put myself in this situation again by ordering from here.

My husband and I dined here recently. Loved that parking was convenient and plentiful and the restaurant is nicely decorated and has a beautiful ambiance. Our waiter was very attentive and friendly. Fair pricing and I loved that the menu was small but had a little something for everyone. I ordered the tortilla burger and he ordered the breakfast sandwich. We selected cauliflower bites and brussel sprouts as our sides. My main complaint is that the brussel sprouts were cooked with pork. There was no mention of this on the menu. I was unable to eat my side item because of this and it was frustrating. In todays world with food allergies and diet restrictions, I believe that menu's should do a better job of informing the customer about what they are ordering. Our main dishes were described well and were tasty. A hair on the oily side but I do think that there were menu items we could have selected that would have been less greasy.

Passing by this restaurant for the last few months waiting for the place to open. Having been to there location in France I was excited to try out the new Santa Barbara location. Full bar with great martinis. Escargot on puff pastry over a dozen very tender however they still had that earthy canned taste. French onion soup. I asked for double extra cheese. I could not find any cheese. I asked our server who stated that she had asked the kitchen for extra cheese...and I showed her the cheeseless soup???? The onions were perfectly caramelized. The soup was cut short by using a Swiss Knorr style soup base. French onion soup is a signature Café de Paris soup so it better be the best scratch stock you can make. I judge a French restaurant by the French onion soup, the steak frits, and the duck confit. "Entrecote is the part of the meat between the bones and the ribs of beef. A slice from the contre-filet or from the rump is often served under this same name. A steak taken between the two ribs of beef. The real entrecote is usually grilled or fried in butter." " A cut of meet located above the loin and chine." (Larousse Gastronomique pg. 106, 361) In France the entrecote was a New York or Ribeye cut usually served with a grilled anchovy garnish or the classic green secret sauce. Montparnasse became famous at the beginning of the 20th century, referred to as les Années Folles (the Crazy Years), when it was the heart of intellectual and artistic life in Paris. From 1910 to the start of World War II, Paris' artistic circles migrated to Montparnasse, an alternative to the Montmartre district which had been the intellectual breeding ground for the previous generation of artists. The Paris of Zola, Manet, France, Degas, Fauré, a group that had assembled more on the basis of status affinity than actual artistic tastes, indulging in the refinements of Dandyism, was at the opposite end of the economic, social, and political spectrum from the gritty, tough-talking, die-hard, emigrant artists that peopled Montparnasse. I could not find any garnish from this region. Entrecote Monteparnasse was served as a sirloin perfectly cooked garnished with a "Famous sauce"???? Didn't we just vote on truth in labeling??? What if I was allergic??? I want to know exactly what I am eating. A sauce Verte which is a green herb sauce consisting of parsley, watercress, chervil, tarragon, & spinach. That's my description. The server could not tell me what I was eating. That scares me. The server said it was secret. I don't like secrets. The vegis were perfect and no complaints from the pomme frits. I found the menu limiting and lacked pizzaz. However in France all they serve is a vinaigrette salad and pomme frits with about 15 desserts. I found the wine list to be challenging and very exciting with French wines that you don't normally find, at good prices. Good value...Great service...I would stop at this restaurant for a pre dinner cocktail and appetizer before venturing on to a more formal dining establishment.

Went in for lunch and had a pepperoni pizza and a coffee.The pictures looked good on other reviews. It's a clean,well designed place with loud newfie and classic rock playing on the music system. Staff was friendly and the coffee was decent. Waitress kept my cup full. Pizza was a little disappointing .It was fairly dry and the cheese quality wasn't there. The pepperoni was hard to spot as they had cut it up pretty finely but i had ordered the spicy pepperoni so i could taste it good enough. The last couple places i've been to all seemed to be allergic to pizza sauce as they just brushed it on like paint hence the dryness. It tasted ok after i put salt and pepper on it. Can't comment on any other dishes. Next time.

WARNING: Don't let the adds fool you...this place is AWFUL!!! The food isn't even kept at a healthy temperature. My chicken was cold and had small bones in it. The watermelon looked like it was bad. I literally had to get up and go the restroom because I started gagging uncontrollably at the table. I just hope I don't have food poisoning. Ugh!! STAY AWAY!!!!

Service is hit and miss ...accuracy is hit and miss... food is usually hot and fresh tasting...I think they nay just pick a fryer to use because I have had fishy tastung chicken and fries before.. not necessarily a good thing as I know people with severe fish/seafood allergies.

Food was decent, about what you would expect from a chain restaurant. However, about 1 hour after I left, I was struck with nausea and some horrifying secretory diarrhea that was almost certainly caused by some sort of food poisoning... my guess is that it was Bacillus cereus or staph aureus based on the timing till the onset of my symptoms. My advice, don't order anything that could act as a culture medium for any sort of bacteria... My guess is that the hand hygiene around these parts may be a bit lacking. So, please enjoy your food, but be ready for the fireworks afterwards.
Good gluten-free pizza. The place was hard to find in the dark; they need to keep up the Christmas lights year around.

Came here about an hour before closing a few months ago and very specifically asked the staff if they were trying to go home (which I would completely understand) or if eating food at this time would be ok. After being informed it wasn't a problem, and taking a seat, not only was my waiter completely miffed about serving me, but I continually heard both the waiter and the kitchen staff complaining about how terrible it was they had to cook my meal. (There were only about 5 tables total but other people were certainly eating as well) After a night of rude customer service, I could barely make it home before having the worst food poisoning I have possibly ever had. Instead of leaving a yelp review, I immediately contacted the owner with exact details as I felt this was somewhat deliberate - either my food was made purposefully bad or something was put in it. Although the owner originally seemed interested in getting to the bottom of this issue via email, once he saw that I might not press the issue further he went immediately back against his word, stopped emailing me and continued to run a poorly managed (possibly unhealthy) restaurant. There are very few restaurants in SB that I am completely scared of and this is certainly one of them.

My girlfriend and I come here often seeing as it is very close to The College of New Jersey, each time the food has been decent and service good. My review is one star because I believe my fish was undercooked, I took one bite and it was rather funky so I didn't take another bite. Flash forward to now, food poisoning! I would have rated this place 3 or 4 stars but after this I will not be returning. Stay away from the fish!

I will start by saying this: the ONLY reason I gave two stars instead of one is the buttermilk fried chicken. It may have been the best fried chicken I've ever had. HOWEVER, the entire experience left so much to be desired that I can't understand how they're even still open for business. We had a party of 14, for a friend (with celiac) who was in town for the weekend. Our reservation was at 7:30 on a Friday night. We arrived on time, our table was ready, and there were only two or three other tables seated. Our server was a very sweet girl. It took too long to get our drink orders, and even longer to get our drinks out. She didn't even get mine on her first trip to the table. I had to call her back out. I'm not a drinker, so I ordered a tea, and was one of the last to get it on the table. When she FINALLY took our appetizer order nearly an hour into our sitting, she brought out one or two plates at a time, sometimes ten to fifteen minutes apart. I waited a half hour from the time I ordered the butternut squash and ginger cream bisque to the time she brought it out. The taste was lovely, but it should have been a dip with bread as it was more suited to be eaten with a fork. Upon ordering our fried chicken topped with pesto with sautéed kale and garlic mashed potatoes, she told us that they were out of the mashed potatoes And offered mushroom risotto instead. A friend asked for mac and cheese instead of risotto, and was informed there would be an upcharge. Once again, everyone's food came out at different times, and my entree came with the mashed potatoes, while the others' fried chicken came with mushroom risotto... I'm so thankful for that, because a bite of the mushroom risotto was nearly impossible for me to stomach. It was disgusting. I'll say it again: the fried chicken was incredible. The mashed potatoes were divine. The sautéed kale? Was one skinny lonely wilted piece of kale hiding under my chicken. And the pesto it should have been covered in? The tiniest little dollop of pesto, ever. Not an entree worth $20. My food came out an hour and 45 minutes into our dinner. At two hours, I asked for a to-go box. At two hours, the last plate of food was delivered to our table, in a to-go box at the request of the girl sitting next to me. The server brought it out and said quietly, "the kitchen apologizes for your wait." The kitchen should have apologized for all of our waits. It was completely unacceptable. She waited two hours for her dinner. We were all finished eating, and the server had to ask her twice what she ordered before she brought it out. As I am not affected by celiac, I would never have eaten at this restaurant had my friend not made the reservation to accommodate her eating restrictions. After this experience, even though the chicken must have been fried in some nectar from the gods, I will absolutely not be returning. I was so disappointed. I wanted to love it so much. It's wonderful that Nashville has a gluten-free restaurant. But with so many places now offering several gluten free items, I think AMOT needs to seriously step up their game, and their pace.

The only thing that allowed 1 star was the hibachi grill. At least I knew my food was cooked which is much more than I could say about anything on the buffet. Crab legs were so undercooked they were like rubber and very difficult to break open. The other buffet items were cold and the salmon was so undercooked I only took one bite for fear of food poisoning. This buffet is like so many other Chinese buffets - the owners don't care about quality, they just know Americans are suckers if you advertise All You Can Eat and just want to make money. I would avoid this place like the plague and get carry out somewhere instead.

I love that Taffets gluten free bakery exists and just wish it were better, or that there were some competition. They have a few products we like quite a bit but most everything would benefit greatly, in IMHO, with half the salt salt if not less, leading me to wonder if the baker owner is a smoker or just has a heavy hand. As a result I buy far less than I otherwise would and tend to stick to just a couple of items at most to have something in my freezer besides Udi's Whole Grain sandwich bread, which is good but rather ordinary. Most disappointing is the saltiness of their challah, which would be so good if it weren't so salt laden. I also think they would benefit from better customer service to make you feel like (a) there is awareness of your presence and (b) that they have interest in your business--customer service 101.

I made a reservation for Father's Day brunch today. I was so highly impressed. Service was outstanding. (Server was Kenneth- well educated on the menu-thank you!) great atmosphere, and food was delicious! I was most impressed that our server asked when we were sat if we had any dietary restrictions or allergies. I have an avocado allergy, which of course makes dining at a Mexican restaurant sometimes difficult! He alerted the chef and they made sure that my food was made to avoid any cross contamination. This doesn't happen just anywhere, folks. I made sure to thank the server and the general manager, Korie. We will definitely be back for dinner. And the nadaritas!

I want to give this place 5 stars because it should deserve it. I came back the next night to get my meal right- no meat! And, they did a spectacular job! It was delicious, meat free and obviously a lot of effort was put in to getting it right. I was so happy! But I got violently the next day. I woke up at 4:26 with the most intense migraine and my body was swelling. I was vomiting water to try and get the food out of my body, because I hadn't eaten anything since the night before, and my body was in total reaction of being 'poisoned'. It lasted the entire day and night. I can only believe it was preservatives that were in the ingredients. Only preservatives and chemicals in the food will warrant such a reaction in my body. I would love to eat at this place every single day, but I don't think I can come back. :( also, though they said the beans are vegetarian, they tasted strongly like pork, so vegetarians be forewarned!

We live so close and it is super convenient to order from here. Their pineapple curry rice is delicious, sadly it's inconsistently made. We love it in our house however, we have an allergy and when it is made different every other time it forces us to not order it. We tend to cave and order it on occasion, we now have to request certain vegetables be left out of it since the ingredients change. We repeat the request three times minimum and ask that the order gets repeated, our request is never repeated back. Our order is large and to dig to the bottom of our bag to double check is not ideal so I asked the gentleman what the usual ingredients are and he says all the Ingredients we are used to having in the rice so I trusted that everything is good. Get home and nope the order is wrong, I call back to let them know, they did replace it and I checked at the restaurant this time. However when we went to eat it they decided to add some other random vegetables that aren't usually included and the flavor was off completely. We love ordering from here but be aware that special requests are not followed and the recipes change, if you have allergies and dietary restrictions I wouldn't order/eat from here.

Big- Old- Marriott hotel in a great location right on Canal Street. Easy in and out due to the large covered drop area on the side. Large lobby and plenty of staff for check in. Even with all of this, check in was slow. That's ok. The Bad- The room. We are Elite Gold members and were upgraded to a corner room in the River Tower. I'm not sure if "upgrade" is the correct term for the room. On the surface it looked ok. Partially renovated. But, after spending a little time in there, it obviously needed a deep cleaning. The bathroom situation is awful. Fake drop ceiling that is dusty and dirty around the edges. You can see the dust hanging. Only one person can fit into the tiny space at a time. Really uncomfortable/impossible for 2 people trying to get ready. Our fridge was dirty. It had not been wiped out between guests. The inside of the windows were dusty. A previous occupant had drawn hearts on the windows in the dust that became obvious in the morning light. Yes, really. Nevertheless, if you have allergies, as I do, do not stay here. Old popcorn ceilings need upgrading also. The 1970's are over. Time to fully renovate these rooms. The Good- Breakfast in the M club room. Probably the best breakfast I've had at a Marriott property. Nicely put together, anything you could imagine. The only low quality items were the breakfast pastries. They were even frying beignets. The breakfast was far superior to the afternoon happy hour. The other "good" was the elevator system as others have mentioned. Extremely efficient. Also, the view from our room was great. If this is the location that you need to be, it's fine. If you have a choice, I would look further. For the price, you can do better.

We just got to Florida and we were starving. So we went to Miller's ale house. The service was ok, not to ambitious. We order the apple walnut Salad and the grapes on the salad still have the stems on them. They could of taken the stems off. Come on. We also order chicken and steak fajitas with no onions. They brought them out and we remind the waitress we didn't want onions. She came back with the meat on the plate and the skillet with onion in her other hand. Since my mom is allergic to onion she still couldn't eat them. That's why we asked for no onions when we order. Most restaurant make a new order without the onions, not just taking the meat of of them and putting them on a plate. We just switch our meals. Maybe next time they will make the meal we asked for.

The menu is not so groundbreaking. However, the atmosphere and the flexibility of the kitchen with respect to dietary restrictions is a welcomed thing. I chose the veg pho, others at my table were happy about the falafel (which is on special on Fridays). Overall, a nice choice when visiting a city with very few options for the vegan gluten-free diet.

We stopped in for dinner around 8pm. We missed a happy hour and flights of wine but that's ok. We ordered a pretty fairly priced bottle of merlot and sat in the courtyard. Our waiter, Jason, took our order for a cheese plate as the appetizer. The food runner brought it out without an explanation of the cheeses... the plate looked nice but it was lacking cheese labels. Both of these would've been very helpful for me since I have a tree nut allergy. I tried a dark brown cheese which could've passed for pate(?). LUCKILY, I didn't experience anaphylaxis as I have before with the most minute tree nut ingredients. So I asked Jason about the cheeses, told him about my allergy and he said he couldn't believe the food runner neglected to explain the plate and he asked what he should expect with my potential reaction. I explained that I seemed ok. And I was which was a relief! I stayed away from that cheese... We continued to enjoy ourselves in the courtyard minus the nut incident until I saw what another table confirmed, was a rat. Yep, it ran like Ratatouille across the courtyard under our table towards the kitchen. Umm, is that normal for your business? I put my feet up on the empty chair next to me. We ordered dinner and it was good! I had steak medallions and goat cheese salad. Hubs had a crab cakes and liked them too! Dinner progressed and I saw several roaches. Ok, now I'm pretty grossed out. I've been to a lot of places but I've yet to see a live rat and cockroaches in a restaurant. So I asked Jason about the dining environment in the French Quarter. He played it off like it was an expected and normal occurrence for the whole FQ to have rats and roaches... I'm only visiting so I don't know if he was pulling our leg or telling us the truth. We are close to the river and the area is old so maybe these rodents are common? Jason felt badly about our experience and offered to buy us dessert and coffee. We thanked him and said no thanks since we were ready to leave the courtyard and rodents. I told him I'd be Yelping the experience. He said ok, others would understand about the rodents. Do they? The food was good. The ambience was nice. Well, if you read this far, I'm sure you can make an educated decision about whether or not to eat here and in the courtyard.

First off if you are looking for a good pizza and are not worried about it being gluten free this place is great. However, if you are looking for a truly gluten free pizza this is not the place to go. While they do try by having a special tray to put the crust on and the worker changed out her gloves they then took the sauce from the same containers as the rest which are then smeared with the ladle on the pizza. This causes a cross contamination unfortunately.

FOOD POISONING. From the traditional burger. Obviously they don't give enough attention to their kitchen hygiene. The taste of the burger wasn't bad, but the subsequent GI infection was. Would avoid this place entirely.

The food was good, once we got it. They brought our beer out and weren't sure if they gave us the correct one's. It also took forever to get any of the beers we ordered. Then brought us our pizza with something we asked for not to be on it because I have an allergy. They left the pizza on the table sitting there until we asked them to take it away. We did end up getting our food after waiting about an hour and a half. That's fine, but they acted like it wasn't really that big of a deal to put something on the table that shouldn't have been there. Overall, the food was pretty good, but the service isn't great and was pretty disappointing.

I went in for "birthday" brunch with two other girl friends on a Sunday around 12:30. There was no wait which was nice, but I think is a red flag. I expect to wait for a table for amazing brunch. The experience was average. For starters the waiter may have been drugged. He was so slow, not just in service, but all of his reactions seemed delayed it was odd. He never checked back to offer coffee refills. When our food arrived we did not even have place settings, we stared at our food for a good five minutes before we even saw another server to flag down. Worse our server placed one of our orders wrong! My lactose intolerant food received food smothered with cheese! So we had to eat with out her while her dish was prepared again. That whole ordeal was handled by the waitress we flagged down for silverware, she did not apologize, and neither did our actual waiter when he finally came over a good while later and noticed she did not have food. The food was blah, nothing memorable. I also can't say that there was anything else on the menu that made me feel intrigued to come back to try somthing else. I had the Tortilla Espanola. It is a frittata with potato and onion, piled with fresh arugula and spanish cured ham, also some where in there is suppose to be a pesto aioli. I don't think mine got the pesto aioli at all or it was the blandest pesto I did not even notice it. The frittata was boring, no seasoning to it at all. We were interested in dessert but our waiter never even offered, and since were all underwhelmed we did not push it. We had told him it was my friends birthday, but still no dessert pitch! The atmosphere is great, it's right off of the park along front street. Maybe brunch is not their forte, but after my experience I am not sure it's worth giving dinner a shot!

Went to have dinner and ordered a turkey burger with avocado and mushrooms only. The burger showed up with provolone cheese and no avocado. I looked at the waitress ( Chelsea) and explained I am lactose intolerant. No Dairy. She looked put out but took my burger back to the kitchen. It came back a few minutes later. Cheese scraped off the burger and returned to me. This is the only time I will ever eat at this place. Horrible customer service.

Everything was good here except for the one thing that really, really matters to me: cleanliness. If it weren't for that I would have given this place five stars. My friend and I stopped here on our first day in New Orleans. It had been a long day and we decided to eat here since the menu sounded delicious. We ordered crawfish cakes as an appetizer, the corn and crab bisque soup, and split the southern pecan pie with ice cream. I don't know if it was because we were tired and hungry, but the food tasted like heaven. Here's where it kind of gets gross. My water glass looked a little dirty, but I decided to not make a big deal out of it. I've worked in a restaurant before and I know that sometimes hard water stains can make a glass look dirty even if it's perfectly clean. Then, I unwrapped my silverware. There was food still crusted on my fork. My knife looked like it had water stains or it was just plain dirty. I grabbed the silverware from the table next to mine. The fork was clean, but the knife was dirty. I also noticed that our server saw me doing this and saw the extra dirty silverware on our table, but never mentioned it or asked about it. I have a feeling this has happened before. The only reason I didn't get up and leave was because we had already ordered all our food and the appetizer had been brought out to us. Actually, mostly it was because we were just extremely tired. Like, so tired you feel drunk and not willing to walk around looking for another restaurant tired. You better believe I inspected every single bite of food. Luckily, it seemed like the plates were clean and the food looked ok. Finally, the bathrooms looked like the ones straight out of a club around 2am on a Friday night. Dark, dingy, and dirty. Now, I'm kind of grossed out that I ate here since who knows how clean the kitchen is, but at least the food tasted good. Also, I was fully expecting to get food poisoning but I was perfectly fine.

I am a fan of Parc, more so in the summer time than any other time. I love to eat next to the big windows and watch the people walk around in Rittenhouse Square lol it gives me good energy. Although I haven't been here for lunch or dinner yet, I've been to breakfast about 5-6 times and everytime I go I get the same thing......PANCAKES. Forget IHOP because Parc has the best pancakes I ever had. They're so simple yet so delish! I have no clue what they put in them and I dont even care lol. And lets not forget the added powedered sugar on top. TO. DIE. FOR! My boyfriend gets their eggs bennedict. He loves it however I think its best that I don't give my opinion of it due to the fact that i HATE raw egg yoke (yuck!). He forced me to take a bite and I literally almost vomitted all over the place. Good hot chocolate and mimosas.

This is a nice cozy cafe that my Mom and sister and Grandma's and I came to specifically because of the gluten free menu as my Mom is Celiac. We had soups, sandwiches and salads. They have really good cornbread (gluten free) and a nice caramel macchiato. It's priced accordingly to what you get, maybe a little pricey but I think it pays for the ambience you get. The staff is pretty welcoming, though a few of the girls seemed snooty. Overall a good experience!

Went on a Friday and there was no one in the restaurant. This did not change the service which was terrible. Salad was brown and waiter brought dessert with nuts on top after we told him we had a nut allergy at the table. Won't be back.

GREAT Cold sandwiches and hoagies!! They should stick with that. I have not had one (1) item of food from Rock's cooked that I would ever order again! Simply Awfulle. One time I had to take back my hot sausage (grilled) and onion sandwich. As soon as I bit into it, I threw up (sorry if too graphic). Do not order the cooked foods or prepared salads! Stick with cold sandwiches, ONLY!!!

What a disappointment! After all these amazing reviews, I feel bad writing this, but it's my honest opinion: so the food tasted just okay, but the portions were small! The food came out in about 5 minutes - but it's raw so there's no cook time... Anyway, I got the meal version of their burger which comes with a small salad and a side dish. I got the jicama potato salad as the side. For dressing. I got the avocado cilantro orange dressing. All of which sounded amazing. The jicama potato salad was the only thing that tasted close to the real thing. It was pretty good. The veggie burger only came with one piece of "bread" so it wasn't even a sandwich. I forgot this place was gluten free when I ordered the veggie bread. It should be called the veggie cracker because that's what it looks like and, again, it was only one piece so it didn't even make a sandwich for the patty. The salad was just okay. Nothing special. And the dressing was super disappointing. All I could taste was fresh squeezed OJ. No avocado. No cilantro. Very disappointing. Mainly I'm complaining about the portion sizes. For $13, I shouldn't still feel hungry at the end! I just didn't think the burger had much flavor and everything was so small. I don't think I'd come back here again. Sorry! I love that it's raw vegan and gluten free! That's awesome! Make your food portions slightly larger and I might come back.

This place is horribly over priced for the worst food I've had in my life. I got food poisoning that night. Read below for my boyfriends review. Great location but yuck. You're seriously better off going to Taco Bell and drinking sewer water.

The food is ok and service too. The place is not clean and the atmosphere is boring. Just another so so place for breakfast and the place needs to be maintained better (all the condiments shakers had sticky fingerprints and does not appear to ever been cleaned. No complaints about the service. The portions were smaller than expected and the place/environment just is so drab and depressing and appears to be something out of the 50's or 60's. The place is ok, but I am going back to Bob Evans for great service and food next time. If management was doing their job, this place could seriously use an upgrade with a fresh look and feel and the place needs to be be much cleaner. Something about sticky tables and menu that turn me off instantly. I doubt if they clean menus from the looks of speared finger prints and greasy too. Menus should be washed with soap and hot water after each use, I doubt if they ever heard about cross contamination. !
