I have celiac disease and other food alleriges. Trying a new restaurants can be extremely stressful for me. I usually always have an anxiety attack some where that I've never been to before. When I saw this place I walked in to see if they had GF crust. When I saw they did I went and had them make sure it didn't have 5 of my other food allergies in the ingredients. When she came back to let me know she also pointed out on the menu about their cross contamination concerning food allergies :-( Cross contamination is obviously one of my big concerns. I watched a few people go through the line and saw how they made each pizza. I decided to chance it!!! As soon as the young man asked me what type of crust I would like was the beginning of the best food service I've had in a LONG time! He asked if I'd like a glove change? Of course I said yes. Everyone from the line came over and changed their gloves and cleaned up the line. He had a separate pan for my crust. Asked me what type of sauce, I will admit that is when I started to get nervous bc all of the sauces were next to each other. I asked for red sauce and he opens something below, pulls out a separate bottle with red sauce :-D Each employee was very aware and careful about how they handled my pizza. This pizza was so GOOD too I ate the whole thing! I want to thank the staff of Pieology in St. Charles Missouri for giving me an awesome restaurant experience! I will be making a stop their this weekend on my way to the Cardinals game for sure ;-)

Went to Tegry Bistro last night for dinner, and was disappointed at several things... When we sat at the sushi bar, the placemat and plate were dirty with left over soy sauce. It was set up like it was ready, but nobody paid attention to cleanliness. While watching the sushi chef prepare the meal, he used his gloved hands to touch the door frame going back into the kitchen. I wondered how many times that transfer of bacteria happened. The rolls tasted good, but within an hour my wife started symptoms of food poisoning. The only difference was that she had cream cheese on her rolls. Made for a long night at home! Maybe the health inspector needs to make a surprise visit. Not sure we will be back.

This place has good Thai Food. Not fantastic, not over the top amazing, but solid. I have had dinner and lunch here, both times the dining room was fairly empty, but the service was amazing! My dining partner has major food allergies, and they are really attentive and careful. The decor is fun and not something you would think of finding in Idaho. Eat here, and to quote my favorite MN Thai, "Thai it, you'll like it".

This is one of my favorite sushi restaurants in St. Louis. The service is excellent and the sushi makers are so friendly, especially if u sit up at the bar itself, they will even give you something for free sometimes! I always leave there satisfied - just don't eat the super white tuna - my mom got food poisoning from it.. it was the only thing i did not eat! It is also a little pricey

I go here all the time, it's one of my late night faves. But tonight I went there, ordered my usual with one of my friends. Pulled up to the window and asked for 2 water cups. We got our water cups and took a sip. They were basically carbonated sink water or sprite with zero flavoring, my friend immediately spit it out. We asked why our water was carbonated and got told that's the only water available right now. I understood and drank the stale, bubbly water but my friend couldn't stomach it. It burned our throats and was slightly concerning. Also, the veggie power bowl i ordered had a curly ass thick hair in it and I almost threw up. Thoroughly upset. Wawa it is next time.

So, I guess I lied when I wrote in my last review that I wouldn't gorge myself - because I definitely did just that last night. As a matter of fact, I was asleep by 8 p.m., that's how liquored up and full I was. I'll keep this short - last night we got a pitcher of blood orange margaritas since I didn't get to sample that kind last time. They were good, but I think my favorite is definitely the passion fruit. In terms of food - the goat chimichanga with cheese was OUT OF THIS WORLD GOOD. I'm considering docking a star because they serve such large portions and it makes me want to die. On the way home my husband said, "I thought I was going to have to pull over to vomit for a second there." It's pretty much impossible to leave and not feel gigantic. This would be a great place to break a fast...

Super disappointed, The fries are no longer gluten free:( They recently just switched over to a beer battered version. Heads up! I couldn't eat them, but the feed back was more oily and the original version was much better. Worst news all day! Please bring back the original fries you are known and loved for!

For many years this Applebee's has been our 'go to' If I didn't want to cook. "Let's just grab something quick." sort of deal. It wasn't great but it was acceptable and reliable and fun but in the last few months it has slid downhill badly resulting in an experience I can only call disgusting, disappointing and downright bad. The chain recently went over to a wood fire grill motif to try and be upmarket but this seems to have limited their fare and my wife says she's found it harder to find something she wants on the menu. On this visit I see they've added new sides, all flavored with garlic-garlicky green beans, garlicky fries and garlicky mashed potatoes. Great if you love garlic. Limiting if you don't and if you have a garlic based food allergy-hint hint-it makes a person very worried about cross contamination. Also the flogging of such a single spice implies they are trying to cut costs by having a more uniform flavor mix they just toss on anything. Now we get to our latest experience. We get there and there's a long row of empty tables but they want to sit us right at the corner-the heavy traffic area. I asked "could we have one of these?" pointing to the row of 4-5 better shelters tables. "Let me check" We got one but this already had me leery of the place. You need to check? We put in our drinks order and it was a long time coming, 10 minutes. A basic beer? For a place like Applebee's getting out those drinks fast is as priority. They are high priced and people will often order several. We'd put in our order and considered leaving before just the beer arrived. It went downhill from there. We put in our order and waited. and waited. A waiter made two trips to bring things to our table. Neither of which were ours. "That's not mine." by the 2nd trip he looked like he wanted to argue the point. We finally got our appetizers more than 20 minutes after putting in the order: Boneless, Buffalo wings, pretty basic food. It had aspirations of being warm. By no stretch of the imagination could it be called "hot" food. The server had to be reminded to get plates and flat ware meaning more of a delay to eat and when mine came, the fork was beyond dirty, one of the tines had so much dried lettuce on it I actually thought, for a moment, it was a design. "Could I have a fork that doesn't come with its own salad please?" further delay. My wife and I were halfway through the wings when the entrees arrived. Now at this point we're feeling rushed. I tried the wonton fried shrimp. I'd had it before and remembered it fondly. Never again. The shrimp, unlike the ones in the picture were small, grey and anemic looking. The wontons instead of spread over were dumped in one corner as if someone remember just as the plate was going out the door and threw a handful after the retreating platter. Even worse, the stir fried vegetables were burned, blackened even. I started to make a mound of the inedible, charred bits on the side of the plate but it was just too many, the rice was dotted with tiny charred bits of pepper and broccoli and trying them, hoping the sauce would smoother the flavor, was a mistake. It was just foul. I left almost all of it on the plate. At NO point did the server ask how was the meal, even when done and I asked for the check, there seemed no interest in what experience their customer had. As I said this Applebee's had been a favorite just to go out casually. It has been degrading with increasingly poor service over the last few months but it's hit rock bottom now. with inattentive and slow servers and food that is just flat out bad.

Love this venue. I'm seen numerous shows here over the years ranging from B.B. King, Steely Dan, CSN, to Earth, Wind, & Fire. The parking situation is a mess and walking around the area after dark will likely get you stabbed but I usually take Septa and that is by far the most convenient way to get to and from the Tower. My favorite Tower story was years ago seeing Frampton and Robin Trower and the guy sitting two seats to my right threw up all over his seat and the seat next to me. The section usher was great and let the whole row that didn't vomit sit in any open seat we could find down in the orchestra section.

Food was good, service was good. They will bring you lots of chicken, just don't fill up on that. The lamb is always my favorite. But.... woke up with food poisoning the next morning which makes me not want to come back. They were not busy so I'm sure the meat had been sitting for awhile. If I wouldn't have had food poisoning probably would give it a 5 They did not reach out to me to determine the cause

It saddens me to give this restaurant 2 stars. This was one of our favorite restaurant to go to. I have celiac disease and this restaurant was always over the top accommodating which is why we kept going back. Last night I found out they no longer offer gluten free pasta and the waiter told me the chef would not do any special orders to accommodate. The majority of restaurants are moving forward to help their diners with dietary restrictions while this place seems to be the complete opposite.

I had to give this a star but it should have zero. This is the worst restaurant in the area. Over priced, the staff thinks they are doing a favor by serving you and the food is mediocre at best. The drinks are watered down, I watched it the waiter with my own eyes at the bars add more soda and ice and change the glass to appear like they are giving you more. I order the shrimp and lobster risotto, I could only find 2 shrimp and a trace of lobster, I sent it back and then never saw the waiter again. To make the meal even worse they had a sardine appetizer special that was served to the table behind us, the smell was so bad that one of our guest who is a,Lerwick to all fish items had to leave the restaurant because of the smell, she could have had an allergic reaction, i too left holding my scarf over my nose and I felt and still feel ill from the smell. Oh and the busser who cleared the table did so in such an obnoxious way, almost spilled the p,ate of olive oil all over my shoulder, but didn't acknowledge me when I said something to her about it. I had been to this place 2 times because it was a work function, I'll NEVER go back again.

TL:DR; Ordered one Bourbon and two Scotch. All were watered down extensively, one with what tasted to be dish water/soap. I really hate giving one star reviews and it really takes a lot for me to do so....but holy hell Let me start out by saying the bartender was really nice and I rate the customer service a solid A+ However, I went in midday to "take the edge off" of a long few weeks of working 60-70 hours/wk. I ordered a bourbon and coke. It tasted a bit odd and watery while drinking it, but figured it was because I was sleep deprived/out of it. I decided to opt for my typical drink of a Chivas Regal neat. I took a sip, gagged, was able to hold it down for a minute to ask the bartender what the hell was in the bottle before I threw up in my mouth and went to the bathroom. After cleaning myself up, the bartender poured a sip to test and was also disgusted by the taste of which I can only approximate to being 20% Scotch, 70% Used Dish Water, and 10% Soap. She then nicely apologized and offered me another drink on the house. I opted for another scotch they had. She poured it and handed it to me and it was extremely clear/light colored for a scotch. I take a sip and it's not disgusting, but tastes like a mixture of half scotch and half water.

I went to Denny's Saturday night, and I highly recommend you don't get what I got....food poisoning. The service was great and everything tasted fine, but I was in bad shape the next day. I am still recovering, but I probably won't eat at a Denny's ever again.

Peace.....LOVE........and Curry Chicken??? Wait that's not how it goes at all or does it?? I love Caribbean food and I remember seeing this place at the old locale and saying to myself "That must be a food truck that serves Jamaican dishes....that sounds delicious" Well I said that to myself for months never stopping in and never venturing to try food from a truck...then it was gone POOF I was sad and swore that if that Truck was still in Tucson I would find it and dine there and enjoy or get food poisoning from whatever was contained within. Well low and behold right up the street from my church in a dirt lot it stood before me calling upon me to try...then to sweeten the deal a yelp check in deal for half off my second entree??? It was like destiny or just great luck or maybe the fact I searched for it on yelp and realized it was up the street from church and had a check in offer...either way I DINED HERE!!! I loved it...love love love loved it!! Great flavor, a personable owner who you can tell loves his craft and serving his delicious Jamaican treats from the back of his Wagon. I dined on Curry Chicken my wife had the Oxtails she was always upset by the Oxtails at the other Jamaican restaurant in town because they didn't have enough meat on them. The moment she opened her box a YESSS came out her mouth as she said "babe they have meat on them" .... "thats what she said?????" The rice is perfectly seasoned and the slaw has a sweet tang the meat rests upon your rice seeping all your flavor into it and creating a foam box of heaven for you to enjoy. Served with a deep fried donut thing that I lack the proper culinary term to describe this place is amazing. My curry was amazing a slight mustard meets citrus and spice flavor that really brightened my day. The chicken was fall off the bone tender and if you are the type to eat the bone they are stewed enough that you could do so easily. Food like this not only fills your belly but lifts your spirits and changes your mood. I will be back regularly whenever that itch for some Island flavor hits me...you should too.

My lovely wife and beautiful two daughters decided to surprise me with a 50th Birthday party with all of my family and dear friends. I was so surprised and it was going to be the best night I have had in a long time, I was extremely sick for over 1 1/2 prior so it was kind of a celebration. I was getting well & together with all of my family and dear friends. As usual my wife was extremely clear and cautious about my daughter's food allergies prior to that evening so they could be prepared but that night she took her 1st bite of her appetizer she started having a severe reaction to the food. She is allergic to milk and eggs and shellfish, so we have been helping her deal with this allergy for 18 years now and understand clearly those types of accidents are going to happen from time to time. Just own it and say you're sorry and we go home and move on. For some reason this manager insisted that there was nothing wrong with her food and was insulted in a weird way she implied as if we were making this up or something because nothing could ever be wrong with her food when in fact my daughter needed Benadryl immediately than went home with my niece and was vomiting for an hour or so with hives. Normally we would have gone home with her but we had a lot of guests and that was not an option. The shocking part was that night the management team continued throughout the evening as if nothing was wrong or nothing ever happened besides our waiter, He was clearly concerned. But Management acted as if nothing ever happened or it was no big deal. We all felt awful for her, We had spent a lot of money for a nice night and a careless chef did not do his or her job than they still charged me for my daughters meal this was the end I was crazy mad she only had one bite. My wife asked me to hold it in we had guests but a few days later I called back after I cooled off and they did a little research and told me they are sorry there was egg on my daughter's appetizer. I was outraged, that manager and chef should have both been fired for implying she was lying. To not stop by my table at any point to see how she was doing at home was just unbelievable. Not once did anyone of his or her kitchen staff asks if she was OK neither did the manager. In a measure of good faith after I called them back and explained that this was unacceptable they decided to send me a $50 gift card that I though away. I was not going to review them but I can't let this one go. They need to understand that the customer is always correct and they can make them or break them and if I was that owner I would have bought desert and apologized to no end. My god how embarrassing is that. I also would have sent the child something possible a card to say we are sorry, No call no card no concerns, All the way to the end that night they denied it as if we made it up. To this day no one has apologized to my daughter and we are certainly not looking for one now. Look accidents happen just man up and deal with it never insult your customer because you will lose them and their 40 guests. Sad part is the food is good just awful management team.

I know this will be an unpopular review, but I just have to go there. Charlie Brown's is terrible! The last time there, over a year ago, was the last straw after vomiting for hours after being served undercooked pork (biscuits & gravy). The coffee is terrible, the cheese in the omelets, etc. tastes like Velveeta, and it is all the things bad about a greasy spoon diner with none of the good. Generally the wait staff is very kind, but the food they are forced to serve doesn't live up to the standard they put forth.

Meh. This is a little belated, as I went to their soft opening when they first came to Goleta. Poke is a part of Hawaiian cuisine that's slowly swam its way into hip, trendy Southern Californian joints, and people are obsessed. Although not much of a raw fish aficionado, I love anything that's new and gives me a reason to reassure my mom that I've eaten something that wasn't bread or deep-fried in the last week. For a soft opening, all the elements were there: harried workers, limited menu, line going out the door. Those are all things I don't believe influenced my review, but definitely something to note. They have a cool boba shop called Sno-Crave in there that I wasn't able to try, but I certainly will when I return for the cool glasses they serve them in. As for PokeMee, I'm not sure I can say the same. The ingredients were all fairly good quality -- the fish didn't smell of anything other than the sauces they were marinated in. I definitely noticed that the crab meat that I paid an extra amount for was imitation crab meat. It just didn't have that same texture or taste that ordinary crab meat does. That's definitely a skip if I choose to return for the poke. I got a large bowl with salmon, yellowtail, albacore, shrimp and tuna. The shrimp was legitimately difficult to find after mixing my bowl together. I know that out of five proteins, finding one would be difficult, but I genuinely felt like I was chewing and everything was the same fishy texture. The edamame offered as a protein might be an interesting option to shake up the feeling of what I'm chewing if I return. Aside from that, while it was a functional meal and I didn't get food poisoning, it was one of those cases where I hear someone going, "I eat to live, not live to eat." It's sustenance, but it didn't quite dazzle me the way it did others. For roughly $12 for a full price large bowl, I think I'd rather make my own poke bowls at home.

Saw the Groupon and decided to check it out. First impression from the outside was not so great. The first thing I thought of was am I going to get food poisoning from the raw fish? Still decided to give it a try. Waitress was nice and we ordered water. Water came with a fly floating on top. Now this can happen. One of those gnats can drop in at anytime. I let waitress know and she apologized and said she will get me a new glass. Got a new glass of water about to drink it and I see lipstick marks on the cup. Sigh....I just couldn't get myself to eat there so I politely notified the waitress and she was mortified. I told her that we will just go. So I have not tried their food unfortunately but two times is too much for me.

Food was good. Unfortunately despite a long discussion with waiter about nut allergy, somehow nuts were in food, probable cross contamination. Spent the night vomiting. Spoke with management who said he would follow up and call back. Have heard nothing. No recompense not even a complimentary dessert or cocktail. I spent $100 to be poisoned. This is not how you run an upscale restaurant. If they aren't professional about food allergies then what else is wrong?
Awesome happy hour drink specials and inexpensive every day food prices. Good food and quick service. Were able to accommodate my gluten allergy

The reason for the one star has nothing to do with the food or service. I have been a big fan of Arpeggio. My husband and I have gone there frequently and have always had an enjoyable experience. And we have often picked up takeout from Arpeggio. I will say that I liked the previous location better but understand the need for expansion. Two weeks ago on Sunday afternoon after attending a workshop with my daughter, we went to Arpeggio for a light meal. She and her husband have never been there and I knew she would enjoy it and want to go again. We got there at the in between lunch and dinner time so the place was empty. We were seated pretty quickly and attended to immediately. But I realized that I was sitting near a flower arrangement consisting of stargazer lilies. I am highly allergic to these flowers. If we had not already ordered our food and received our beverages, I may have suggested we leave immediately. But we were moved to table away from any flower arrangements and our waitress couldn't have been more gracious. She was suffering from a "lost voice" that I'm sure was a result of the flower arrangements in the dining room because it is one of the minor symptoms I experience when in contact with them. We got pretty much through our meal with little annoyance due to the flowers. But suddenly the scent permeated through the room and with every bite of food taken I was inhaling the scent of stargazer lily, making it difficult for me to breathe and I was coughing horribly. Apparently the air conditioning had either been turned on or turned up because the scent was everywhere! It was awful and I had to get out of the place in a hurry, leaving my daughter to find our waitress and settle up with her. It could have been a lovely experience but it turned into an absolute nightmare for me. My extreme disappointment is not in the food or the service but in the fact that I left a voicemail message for the owner, my voice was shot and I thought the message might not be understandable so I followed up with an email to mary@arpeggiobyob.com about my experience and have never received a call back or an answer to the email. I wanted to bring to someone's attention that stargazer lily is a flower that many people have allergic reactions to and they obviously had other complaints because the woman who seated us brought someone to the table where we were seated originally and we could hear them having a conversation about the flowers. I am extremely disappointed in the lack of response and because of it, I doubt that my family will be returning to dine in or to take out. Very disappointing!

This location sucks!!!! They steal your change and can't get an order right to save their lives!! Just gave me hazelnut instead of Carmel and my daughter had a huge allergic reaction. The DD at City Hall is by far the best location they have; this was a good spot a year ago. They lost all their good people! Save yourself the trip

What makes it good: Great lunch specials Great "late" night app/drink specials Good tasting food Fairly prompt service- sometimes What makes it poor: Unengaging "chefs" Price How they handle allergies Managment's unvinvolved attitude My ultimate bottom line: Lunch is great, dinner is terrible I went for a birthday part just last weekend and this was my...fifth or sixth time there. FORTUNATELY this time we'd made a reservation because the lobby was packed. We couldn't move through it. Everyone was irritated and the staff didn't seem to know what to do. Furthermore, once we sat down our order was taken incorrectly for at least 3 of the guests in our party. The habachi chef looked like he was ready to leave, I had to wait for 15 minutes for the chopsticks I asked three different people for, and when we did finish our meals they sort of hovered over us waiting for us to leave. Now, I understand wanting to turn tables, I was in the restaurant business for a lot of years and most of adult working life, BUT! We had a birthday shindig going down and we wanted a few minutes to finish our food/conversation without management breathing down our necks. Literally, I could feel the hot breath. On my neck. CREEPY! I'll go back for lunch when it's less crowded, loud and overall a terrible experience.

I wanted to like this place so badly -- Double Knot exceeded all expectations, and Sampan is consistently delicious. Harp and Crown had so much potential... But. Around 7pm on a Sunday night, the place was basically empty. Despite this, service took forever. The menu wasn't particularly enticing (especially with my annoying gluten allergy) but we placed our orders (eventually) and hoped for the best. Drinks? Good, but took forever to come out. Food? Overpriced and meh. Two people ordered the scallops, and said they were so salty they were inedible. (One said that the salt actually burned her tongue and gave her a little ulcer.) The margarita pizza was reported to have tasted like soggy cardboard. The cheese platter was good, and my fish dish was good -- but for the amount of time we waited, and the price, I wanted everyone to be blown away by everything. By the time dessert rolled around, everyone was fed up with waiting for not-amazing-food, and we kind of just wanted to be done. The atmosphere IS beautiful though -- the place is lovely. Intrigued about the bowling alley in the basement (fancy bowling with fancy drinks could be an interesting grown-up adventure?) we asked the host if we could go check it out. Keep in mind the place was basically empty -- and we (a group of thirty-something yuppies) would be the ideal prospective candidates to rent $200 bowling alley lanes in the future -- and yet, we were denied. Apparently you are ONLY ALLOWED to go into the basement if you order at least one drink, per person. We wanted to go home, but were curious about what the bowling scene was like there, and we left unsatisfied on numerous fronts. Hopefully these are just growing pains and this place will tweak and edit itself to live up to it's potential.

The food is delicious. I like that they have a gluten free menu and an under 500 calorie menu as well. The food quality for a place like this is impressive in my mind. However, the reason I'm not giving it more than 3 stars is because of the service. We went last night close to 8 and it took us 30 minutes for our food to come out! We ordered steak kabobs, hummus, and a turkey sandwich which should've taken 10-15 mins max. For a "fast food" place I find this absolutely unacceptable. The restaurant only had 4 tables in use, all of which were waiting for food when we arrived. From this particular Zoe's Kitchen I will stick with ordering online and picking up.

I'm not judging this Boston Market as much as I'm judging Boston Market as a company (aka I'm totally judging their menu items). This Boston Market was cool - nothing extraordinary and nothing terrible about it. Parking was easy to find. I placed my order online, so I was just picking up. Although they have a separate line for pick-ups, I waited for a couple of minutes (even though there were cashiers that could've helped me out). Anyway, I'm patient, so I waited! When the cashier at the normal line was done checking out a couple, she called me over and got my food! The food preparer read out my order and that was an added bonus. She printed my receipt (which has a coupon on it!) and wished me a happy day! The inside looked pretty clean and was pretty empty. Now, onto my actual order. I ordered an individual meal: half (all-white meat) rotisserie chicken, with steamed veggies, mac and cheese, a side of squash casserole (I wanted to try it), and some cornbread to bring back to the fam. I also had the Sweet Thai Chili Garlic sauce. I would like to say that my order was ready and warm when I got there (which is a plus). It was still warm when I got home (another plus). The chicken was bomb dot com. The sauce? As delicious as I remember. The perfect amount of spice. The mac and cheese is as good as I remember it to be. Not too cheesy but enough to make me want more! And the cornbread. Good lord, the cornbread! My mom makes the best cornbread, and while BM's cornbread definitely isn't the best, something about it is addicting. I'm not sure how I limited myself to one piece. Two MAJOR disappoints? The steamed veggies and that damn squash casserole (aka vomit). The steamed veggies tasted like they were steamed in garbage water. They had this odd taste to them and were definitely not seasoned with anything. I managed to get most of the broccoli and zucchini/green beans down (by dipping them in the cheese sauce) but those carrots were so hard I didn't even bother! I would definitely recommend just getting a freaking SteamFresh bag of veggies at Publix instead of getting this as a side. I have had several types of casseroles in the past, and they've all been pretty good. This one? It was bad. Not only did it look SO unappetizing, it didn't taste like anything! It looked like I was eating vomit, the consistency was horrible, and it just had no freaking flavor. I don't even know how else to explain it, but seriously, please opt out, unless of course you like eating barf. Then, by all means, go ahead! Also, there's a $1.50 off of $10 coupon online! You can apply it to your online order.

Attention all Ponzio's diners, if you want to experience food poisoning then this is the place to dine. We were 100% healthy before eating dinner and a few of us hadn't eaten earlier. We ordered the infamous 7 fishes for New Year's Day, and after we ate the food, we experienced projectile vomiting and diarrhea. We told the owner about the food poisoning and he just brushed it off stating it was probably something else we ate - no refund or credit! You are responsible for making your customers ill due to a dirty kitchen, improper food storage/temperature, cross contamination, dirty food handlers or rodents/bugs. Stay away, the owner totally disrespects his customers and has zero interest in your well being. Go across the street to Famous Daves, Whole Foods, Or to nearby Cheesecake Factory, Lamberti, Brio, etc., anywhere but Ponzio's!! Happy New Year!! Diners unite!!

Sigh. After allowing my sister into the show for hours with her draw-string backpack (which just had her epi-pen in it), a security guard noticed she had an "illicit" bag RIGHT before the headliner came on and literally dragged her out of the theater to the security area. She showed him the epi-pen and this guard said she could keep the pen but not the bag that held it...after explaining to him several times she had no pockets, she just walked away. And he grabbed her by her shoulders and pushed her out into the street. I told him he should take a moment to evaluate what he'd just done and stormed out myself. Not okay.

Beware of food poisoning at this restaurant! My husband and I came for dinner on March 4 and ate at a high-top in the bar. The food was very good but within a few hours we both got identical, horrible food poisoning that kept us up all night, and we were both dehydrated and exhausted the next 24 hours. Two days later, when I was feeling well enough, I wrote Amada a respectful message telling them what happened and listing what we ate, in case they were trying to track down other instances. That message was ignored for two weeks. I sent the message again (using the Garces Group website, as before), and that's been ignored for more than a week also. I understand that this can occasionally happen in a kitchen, but the complete lack of response or concern from Amada suggests they aren't especially interested in taking any steps to reduce further occurrences. Enjoy the food but eat at your own risk.

Dirty, empty, and disappointed. I went here with a small party at 6:30pm. We were the only patrons in the restaurant...Not a good sign. The menus, plates, grill, even the check folder was caked in old food. We watched the chef cross contaminate all our food with raw chicken. He wiped the spatula off on a dirty old rag on his cart and continued contaminating further. Save your money.

Tango, you are getting 2 stars because you have a separate gluten-free menu (thank you!) and because the other diners at my table seemed to like their food. However, the service was poor and the duck was tough and rubbery. Need I say more?

I came in today (Sunday) for the first time. There was quite a long line, but it moved very quickly. The girl who placed my order was very friendly. However (I hate howevers), I ordered a very simple bagel (plain with peanut butter on the side) and it came out wrong. I didn't know until I got home, boo! I asked for the PB on the side because have some recently developed food sensitivities, and I can tolerate a little peanut butter but not much. So I scraped off as much of the peanut butter as I could, added some sliced bananas, and ate it anyway. It was really good!!! Nice and chewy and FRESH. The coffee was really good as well, and I truly appreciate the option of using almond milk (dairy allergy here, as well). Another minor snafu, the very friendly girl took my name wrong (it's pretty loud in there), so I sat there like an idiot while they called another name for my bagel. No worries, I'll just say and spell next time :)

I came here for a birthday gathering for a friend of mine. The decor is absolutely stunning! I love all the pictures everywhere and the comfortable seating! You certainly could come here to meet friends and be very comfortable. I also like the somewhat Punk theme they have going on as well. I absolutely adore how the emphasis is on Nevada and how they literally showcase Nevada's history! There even was a baby shower going on! That really has to give a sense of the people they draw in and that it is not just about "drinking" at a bar. I had two drinks at the bar. One was a Moscow Mule: vodka, ginger beer, lime and a ginger candy came in the famous copper cup! It was good, but a little too much ginger for my liking. They sort of have to be just the right mixture for me. I felt like there may have been just a little too much ginger. I could definitely drink it though and would give it another shot. I also ordered a beer for my second drink and honestly I can't remember what I ordered. I always have to order beer and ask what they have that has little hops as I have a slight allergic reaction to it. The bartender was quick to answer with several of their beers and a friend recommended what she was having. It was delicious, if I could only remember the name, I would highly recommend it! =o) The staff were very friendly and upfront. What I mean by upfront is that when we ordered the bartender was quick to inform us that their delivery for that week had been messed up and they did not have a lot of the things on their drink list. Thank you for letting us know, I can't tell you how frustrating it is when you order and they tell you they don't have it and you order something else and again tell you they don't have...well then tell me what you do have then! Don't set me up for failure! Thanks to 1864 Tavern for helping us be successful! =o) Any way enough of my little rant. Overall, I would definitely come back!

The food is amazing! I love the different flavored crusts, BUT management is incompetent. The GM Dave DOES NOT know how to work the computer to take your order; he can't seem to understand proper American English spoken directly to his face, AND he does not seem to care about his customers. My husband and I specifically told him numerous times during our order, that my husband's food CANNOT have cheese! He said, "I got it. I know what you want. Emily you put the order in, I'll make it." My husband is DEATHLY ALLERGIC to cheese. The pizzas looked good, so we expected the pizza rolls Dave made to have been alright. My husband calls me from work saying there was cheese on his Hungry Howie Pizza Roll. He was between throwing it up when he called. We go into the store after picking him up from work. Emily profusely apologized and give us our next meal free, to make amends for her boss trying to kill my husband. We go in today, Feb 24, to take up that generous offer. The GM Dave is there. He says he will not honor what Emily gave us. Says he doesn't remember making my husband's pizza rolls. Blamed Emily for doing it. This incompetent man has cost his place of business money. I give out word of mouth about how great this place is, but no more. NOR will we spend our money there. I implore you to order from Emily or Josh. Even Cody. They care. They listen. And they are good at their jobs.

If i could give this no stars, i would. Despite a big selection, all of the food appeared to have been sitting out for hours and was absolutely disgusting. I was trying to eat it to be polite, and with one bite i knew i was going to get food poisoning. Very greasy, bland and full of MSG. I have been in bed all day vomiting. Do not eat here, it is not safe. I am so glad i did not give my 2 year old food here. You could hear the staff members screaming angrily at the tops of their lungs at each other on the kitchen. The service was slow, but since its a buffet you really just need drinks. We went here 4 or 5 years ago, however, and for a buffet it was good. They have definitely gone downhill and i plan on reporting them to the board of health and getting our money back. It was $33 for 2 adults and a 2.year old. Way overpriced for the quality of food and service and lack of cleanliness.

Just do yourself a favor and don't go here. Go a few more miles down the road to city restaurant. I asked for a burger no bun with cheese and chips. I am a celiac. They brought me out a burger on a bun with French fries. I sent it back and they came out 3 more times asking me what I meant I wanted because I apparently me explaining 2 times before that wasn't enough. The burger came back out with just a burger and a bag of chips. No lettuce, onion, pickle and when I told them that I just didn't want it anymore the (what I'm assuming to be) manager said that his "wife acted the same way" I was furious. Great customer service ahole. You'll be closed by the end of the year and thousands in debt. You deserve that.

* important note: if you are a sushi connoisseur and crave things such as Uni,eel, or sashimi then this is not the place for you. The sushi is very Americanized and covered with wasabi mayo and Panko crumbs. * it was only after our waiter noticed our annoyance that he became very attentive which should not be the case or the need in order to get good service. After seeing all the great reviews of this place we thought we'd check it out. The first sign of discontent came when we waited nearly 20 minutes for our waiter to take our order. Once the waiter knew of our annoyance he was very attentive. The table next to us had patrons that had a gluten allergy. It was sad to watch someone who is new to the gluten-free diet having to shift through the menu to find something only to be brought the wrong thing repeatedly. Even though she made it very clear to the waiter and the person who I assume was the manager that she had a gluten allergy. No one offered her options on the menu to help her navigate for a gluten-free diet. Overall service is slow and unresponsive. While the manager person talks loudly with patrons at the sushi bar she ignores all others except those who spoke Japanese. We will not be returning.

It'd be a while since I'd been here and though it had never stuck out as a favorite to me, it always seemed decent enough. My most recent visit the food was quite good, but there was something more than a little off with the Bloody Mary's. We had already had a previous round of drinks when we ordered three of these guys. They came with a dark liquid floating on top which we later identified as Yard's Love Stout. I'm down with whatever weird stuff restaurants want to do as long as it works, but in this case it didn't. All three of us, who either are currently, or have been bartenders in respected restaurants, tasted what seemed like balsamic vinegar as the dominant flavor. Every sip was accompanied by a cringe. We got the attention of our server who had already been a little cool with us, but we nicely explained the situation. She said she would check what she could do and so began a chain of three different people explaining to us that as "there were no other complaints" they couldn't do anything and that we could "order it differently next time." One server told me that "beer is always in Bloody Mary's" as another justification....false. The manager explained that she didn't have comping powers, so we should just grin and bear it. I don't understand how that's possible, but if it's not another beer-is-always-in-Bloody-Mary's type lie, that is an egregious restaurant policy. Either way, they could have offered to simply remix the drinks and try to cut the vinegar taste in some way. Any gesture of good faith would have been appreciated. Side note - wonder what their solution would have been if one of us was gluten free. Anyway, if you don't mind eye rolls with your service and you like a little masochism with your Bloody Mary's this is the place for you. You just better be prepared to pay for any of their mistakes, as this restaurant does not seem to be concerned with customer service.

My wife has wheat allergy and she wanted to have a nice filling meal before the half marathon which took place earlier today. The reviews were overwhelmly positive with gluten free pasta option. So we decided to go. Man it was not to my expectation. First off, the wait was terribly long. Even after putting myself on wait list In advance. She got the one gluten free pasta with clams. She complained the pasta Was too salty. My son got their famous fried risotto balls. That was pretty good I have to admit. I myself was very dull from earlier so just for a simple 12in pepperoni pizza. It was decent. Nothing I would boast about or say this was one of the better pizzas I had. For the long wait and positive reviews, I am really expected more. They do have a decent ice cream selection where I got the guava coconut flavor. All in all, not very good pasta joint. Look elsewhere guys. Oh yeah, no free wifi and no free parking on site.

Easy breezy blenders...no fuss and if no line it's heavenly! Love it. Easy parking usually and can sit too... You guys MUST get allergy orders Correct!!! I just had a huge reaction to a mango I specifically ordered no banana and bc of asking for soy it's common that the maker misses it and follows the recipe off the wall, I'm super sick now and it's your fault!!! I've had one almost daily since 98 so I am appalled that you can't get this right ever. Ttys -k
PLEASE Share your experiences with this location with chipotle corprate before someone dies from food poisoning.

I love Mexican food, so I was very excited to try Vida. Unfortunately I was very disappointed. My boyfriend and I started with the Vida guacamole, it came out promptly but was loaded with crumbled cheese on top. The menu did not state it had cheese and my boyfriend has a dairy allergy. When I finally tasted it I was disappointed to find that it had no tomatoes, onions, cilantro, or any other ingredient found in guacamole besides avocado. And there seemed to be very little avocado as well. The guacamole tasted like sour cream at best. I know you can cut guacamole with sour cream to make it smoother, but this was all sour cream. For dinner we ordered the habbenaro chicken wings, chicken taquitos, shredded pork tacos, and mahi mahi tacos. Habbenaro chicken wings: came out with the same crumbled cheese on top (no mention of this on the menu) and they looked great! In reality they did not taste like much of anything. They had no heat, but were oddly sweet. Every other bite I got a hint of black pepper, but over all they were gooey and devoid of flavor. Chicken taquitos: the tortilla was very thick. It may have been home made, which I give them credit for attempting, but it was much too thick and doughy. The only thing i could discern inside was the chicken. No texture, no depth of flavor, just smoked chicken. Over all the dish was mushy and one note. Mahi tacos: the fish was fried, which again was not stated on the menu. Despite being covered in what looked like ranch chipotle sauce this too had no flavor. Shredded pork tacos: my boyfriend asked for no cheese, these came out with a puddle of white cheese wiz on them. They had pickled onions which was a nice touch and I was happy to find some texture in at least one dish, but overall the only thing we could taste was pork and onions. Overall the food was overwhelmingly bland. There was no citrus or tomatoes in any over the dishes that I tasted and the presentation was poor. Finally when it came time to pay i was told their computer wasn't working and was instructed to write my credit card number, expiration date, and signature on a piece of paper so they could run it later. There was no sign on the door saying that they did not accept cards, and no one told us when we sat down or made the reservation that their machine was not working. That was unacceptable. And their method to take my card info was unacceptable as well. I had to leave to go to an ATM and come back to pay cash. Overall, it was a poor show of Mexican food, and management.

The food was delicious. I had a gluten-free portobello burger and it was the best gluten-free burger I've ever had. The only thing that made it not great was the service. My co-workers and I went there for lunch and we told them we were in a bit of a time crunch and the hostess assured us that the kitchen is super fast and we would have our food in like 10 minutes. We ended up waiting about 20 minutes for our food and had to scarf down our food. I did appreciate that we were given a free appetizer or dessert.

This is the second time in 2 weeks that I have gone and my order is completely wrong. I only have a few minutes to eat I expect what I order to be correct. I'm allergic to ham so I can eat it so I paid $8.00 for something I can't have. Thanks!!!

This being my first time in New Orleans, I wanted to try the boiled new orleans crawfish that everyone talks about. I had been warned beforehand that crawfish is not in season in November, but still wanted to have some regardless since - when will I get another chance? My order consisted of boiled crawfish, turkey neck and an order of corn. Turkey neck - 5/5. Tender, juicy, well seasoned. Can't go wrong with this. Corn - 2/5. After sitting for a long time in the boiling liquid, the kernels of corn were saggy and way too salty for my taste. It was like 40% boiling juice and 60% corn. Couldn't finish Crawfish - 1/5. Now this is where there restaurant really disappointed me. I knew in the back of my mind that these crawfish were probably previosly frozen since crawfish season is many months away, but even with these lowered expectations I was disappointed. The size of each crawfish was great, but the taste was just not good. There was not a lot of flavor in the meat (maybe because my tongue is recoiling from the saltiness of the corn?) and I could definitely taste that the little guys were not fresh. The meat was not bouncy and clung a lot to the shell, and definitely develops the taste of frozen-then-thawed seafood taste that you can find in frozen snow crab legs from supermarkets. I should preface this with the fact that I have had crawfish before and knew what to expect. Just on its own, the taste of the crawfish was probably closer to 2.5. However, after I started eating it, I felt sick to my stomach and threw up in the bathroom. Did not finish my bag. Today is now day 2 and I have thrown up 3 more times since eating this meal. I usually have a really strong stomach and have never had food poisoning before, but this seems to do the trick. TLDR: Had low expectations going in, was disappointed, got food poisoning(?). The price was good (4.99/lb of crawfish) but I would definitely think twice before getting the crawfish during off season. The only reason I didn't rate this 1/5 was because the turkey neck was so darn good. However I couldn't finish that either because my stomach had started to turn.

My family was looking for spaghetti and meatballs and found that and more. The atmosphere was very casual pizza parlor type. The food was good, although not extraordinary. Unfortunately our waitress was not familiar with the soup of the day and gave us incorrect information that led to an allergic reaction. I would recommend this restaurant if you don't want fancy but are looking for a solid dish of pasta or chicken for the family.

Par for Reno, okay food served at prices that are too high for what you are getting. The ambiance is hip but LOUD, outdoor seating is minimal, and you have to be a fan of Mark Estee's food esthetic to enjoy the food and cocktails since it is another one of his endevours. The wait staff was friendly and the business is locally focused. The thing is, it's just not memorable. it's another hip place with subway tile and steampunk photos with a big bar in a prime downtown location but the food won't wow you. Ironically I've gotten food poisoning nearly every time I've eaten at one of Estee's restaurants (didn't know this was his until we were there) but this time I didn't, however, despite ordering many options and sharing the same food my friend did get food poisoning. It's fine for Reno, but it a big city it would pale in comparison to good places.

**GLUTEN FREE REVIEW** I'm not only avoiding gluten, I'm also avoiding gluten free bread. I thought I wasn't going back to a burger place but Red Robin has a funny new way to having any of their burgers... the name is pretty funny... it's called a "wedgie burger" which basically turns any burger/sandwich into a lettuce wrap. I ordered the chicken... DELICIOUS!!! ***garlic fries are fries with garlic oil poured on them... not great... I gave them them 3 stars because the place had a strong odor... yet the food was good.

I wish I would have reviewed Virago after my first purchase so I could have given them the four or five stars my heart desired, but unfortunately I have made a few trips since then and each time, I'm a little more disappointed. A review for their Joy Cupcake Tray of gluten-free cupcakes alone would be five stars without question. The tiny cupcakes are just the right size for a treat, and are delicious with creamy, puffy icing on top. I ordered them to take out to my brother's house to give my sister-in-law a treat and everyone was floored with how great they were. I would have given up every other treat to eat the coconut chai cupcakes for the rest of my life. Sadly, each trip since then, I've gotten regular sized cupcakes, and I just don't love them as much. The flavor combinations are fantastic and delicious, but the texture of the cupcakes makes them crumble and very difficult and messy to eat, and I just don't enjoy the icing at all. While the mini cupcakes had a light icing (not sure if it was because they were mini, or because of the gluten-free), the full sized cupcakes I have gotten each time had a hard shell of icing that made the cupcake even harder to eat and came across as far too sweet because of the texture. I'll have to go back and try their other products and hopefully raise my rating because I really REALLY want this place to be as great as I thought it was after my first trip, but for now, my 3.5 star rating feels more appropriate to be rounded down than up.

First time here and was told it was a great place to eat.....waited 40 mins on a Sunday morning to be seated. I understand it is a Sunday morning and everyone and their mother wants to eat out but several empty tables were seen within the restaurant and outside patio. Must be short staff in the front of the house and back. I ordered avocado toast with a side of sausage, side of potatoes and a fruit cup. The toast was gluten free which was hardly toasted, good amount of avocado was a plus but they put the sausage on my toast. By the time it got to me it was cold on the toast. Also the toast came with potatoes so I had a whole another order of potatoes. My fruit cup grapes, pineapple and cantaloupe which was $2.99. Kinda cheap that strawberries, blueberries and blackberries were on the special but you I received grocery store quality fruit. After eating the fruit I noticed the bowl had cheese on it still from a prior meal in my bowl. We notified the waiter who went to tell the manager. The manager sent the waiter back over with no service recovery. My husband spoke up and said that is not acceptable. The waiter once again went back and the manager still didn't come to the table. The server David came back and had taken my breakfast off the bill. This was disappointing meal to say the least. We will think twice about going here again. Update review- I received a gift card from First Watch following this review on Yelp so my husband and I can try them again. We finally went yesterday to a First Watch and enjoyed our food/service better this time. I had the quinoa lemon blueberry pancakes that were delicious. My husband had the traditional breakfast and some coffee. He raved about the coffee. We were informed by the server that it is from a small women owned business in South America. Which is only served at First Watch. This visit was definitely better than the previous one.

A new pizza place in Providence Town Center that occupies the same place as a prior pizza joint. If you've been to Mod's Pizza, the concept is basically identical. You go to the counter, select your crust, toppings, etc. and then they quickly cook it in a wood fired pizza and bring it out to you within a few minutes. They do offer several crust options, including a gluten-free crust, which my wife said was one of the better ones she's had. Lots of toppings to pick from. I went with their Pure Fire Hawaiian pizza and I should have noted that it came with a spicy red sauce. For me, it had a little too much kick, but to be fair, I'm not a big fan of spicy food. The pizza was pretty good, but the spicy red sauce for me sort of kept me from being able to finish it. These are personal size pizzas but they are of decent size. I do wish they were cut into eight slices rather than just four. The place only opened a few weeks ago and you could tell that the employees were still in training as they were pretty slow in putting our pizzas together. The place was pretty empty, so not a big deal, but during a lunch or dinner rush, it would not have been good. For my kids, they were disappointed that there was not chocolate milk offered to drink. The owner came by several times and cleaned up our napkins and even refilled a few of our drinks. We will definitely be back again, but will likely wait a month or so and by then, service should be humming along.

They make very convincing chocolate desserts here. The magic bar had a lovely chocolately taste to it. Not my favorite, but it was tasty and resembled a dense chocolate toffee bar. I think I expected too much of this one when I came in. The vanilla cupcake was delicious and had more of a muffin-like texture to it. Just the right amount of sweetness, moist, soft. The chocolate frosting was surprisingly tasty! I'd come back for a cupcake. This was probably my favorite. The crumb cake is ... meh. It tastes GF and vegan, if you know what I mean. I was least impressed with this one. The cookies are tasty. Doesn't have the same caramelized texture and crispness as a real cookie (i still prefer the real thing), but they are darn good! The pumpkin cookie sandwich had a great flavor to it. The spices were nicely balanced. The blueberry oat bar was very good! The blueberry filling is super intense though and jam-like. The place IS expensive. For a sampling of 5 things, it cost me $20. However, the fact that it's GF, vegan, everything-allergy-free makes it special and worth the price if you have special dietary needs. The goods were pretty greasy (the box that I took everything home in had a super greasy bottom by the time I got home...), but I expected this of vegan desserts. All in all, definitely the best vegan desserts I've ever had. Overall warning: don't refrigerate. Not sure if they go badly more quickly if you don't.. but after refrigerating, they all got flavorless and chewy?

Unimpressed by the service and underwhelmed by the food!!!! For starters our waitress Dominique all though we had her for about 10 mins was extremely unpleasant and just plain ignorant. We asked if they used latex glove because our friend has an extreme latex allergy and you could tell she never checked with the kitchen about it. She brought the waters and said nothing about if the used latex gloves or not then came back with drinks and asked for the food order. At this point we all looked and said what about the latex and you know what her response was we can work around any allergy. Uhhhhhh latex allergy is pretty hard to "work around" . About 20 Minutes later she comes back and was like I'm cut but Seth will be over to help you out. We get our food and a eat about an half and hour and still never see or meet Seth. At this point extremely aggravated since we never had anyone check on us and keep seeing Dominique floating around the restaurant to the point where I had to ask the host where the hell our server was because we need to check out and don't want to ordeal this horrific service any longer. The only saving grace to this trip was the brisket prime dip! So yummy and would recommend but it's not worth the service we endured. The deviled eggs though had really gross after taste and would not recommend. Please post a photo of the too cool to greet server Seth, Im dying to actually meet him! I don't think I will ever be persuaded to come back if either server are there. Don't worry I will be happy to tell everyone that will listen about my worst costumer service experience I have ever had and that's tough to do because I understand everyone has bad days !!!!!!! If you do venture in there dispute the review request someone other then Dominique or Seth as your server so you can at least have a pleasant experience.

I have seen this place many times and decided to give it a try with my husband. He had been going on and on about wanting to have dinner here for a while. We had tried previously to go to the Sparks N.V. location for some soup and hamburger and it was very good. We thought we'd try dinner. Normally we go to Texas Roadhouse or Tamarack Junction. This was a bad choice. The service spot on, our waiter Nate was excellent. Attentive, engaging, funny and my husband with no filter usually banters and Nate was laughing and just as funny. He made suggestions everything sounded like it would awesome. This however was not the case. I ordered chicken parm, my husband Joe ordered balsamic chicken. He also ordered salad and I had stuffed mushrooms Joe is allergic to them. The salad looked really good, look being the key word it was a bit wilted and it was to sweet and the lettuce tasted odd. He thought it was his imagination he asked me to taste it. It was not is imagination. I then had the mushrooms with spinach. They were very good, I am picky because my favorite place to any kind of stuffed mushrooms another chain. Carino's in south Reno N.V. Nate came back he was very nice and fast service. He then brought out dinner. I took one bit of the chicken parm it was ok, sauce was way to bitter.Joe's was way to sweet for him we switched. It was tolerable, but still tasted funky. We then tried desert. I will say the pazookie as the hot cookie deserts with ice cream on top very good. I had red velvet and Joe had Oreo cookie. Dinner pricing was a little high just shy of $60.00. For what we had food wise not worth it. I am usually very hesitant to review like this, but I was so bummed. Again could have been an off night, but I doubt it.

WORST RESTAURANT EVER!!! I've had some pretty rough meals in a Pakistani airport, a rural spot in Brazil, a highway food stand in Egypt, and a dump in Detroit. But NEVER have I had a meal as unappetizing as what I ate here! I tried something that I think resembled potatoes, but I nearly threw up in the bathroom. Keep in mind I haven't thrown up in 25 years, so that's one heck of a streak! I ate a hamburger that I'm pretty sure was raw. When I sent it back, it was returned to me still undercooked. Yuck! I even tried their namesake, waffles! Disgusting! They can't even get that right! Toward the end of the meal I noticed the cook was smoking a cigarette, which made me wonder what may have fallen into my meal. You can't write this stuff!!! And the cardinal sin... all I want the server to do is keep the water glass full, especially when I'm eating disgusting food and need to wash it down. A waiter doesn't have to be my best friend, correctly remember the specials of the day, or bring the food out in a timely manner (that's the cook's job). All I ask is one simple thing to earn my 20% tip. Do not let the water glass sit empty for 10-15 minutes and disappear from view while I'm practically choking on my food.

I was really excited about the atmosphere. That was quickly erased by the service. The salsa was pretty good. We ordered queso which came pretty quick along with some yummy margaritas. The service went downhill from there. Our order was taken and the food came very slow. My husband is allergic to shellfish and asked for all meat entree. We made it clear that he was allergic since part of his entree usually comes with shrimp. We were assured it was not a problem. The 1st bite was shrimp. We didn't get an appology or visit fromthe manager. A simple apology would have Bern greatly appreciated. Food was just OK, service was horrible. I'll try one more time, but I hope it's better!

I'd give this place another shot if I was from around here, but I'm not. The chicken itself was good, moist, cooked well, but the seasoning was over the top hot... and I ordered "medium". The sides were lackluster, and because of being stuffed into the same Styrofoam container as the chicken, got contaminated with the super hot chicken rub. Did I enjoy my meal here? Not really. But some of that may have been my fault for not knowing what to order. I can enjoy spicy hot food, but this "medium" chicken was almost off my chart, and certainly hotter then I could enjoy. Heed the warnings you've read here. Order mild and stress the "mild" when ordering and hope for the best, I guess.

The food was good BUT, the service was not. Plenty of options for toppings and all diet restrictions including vegan and gluten free. The ingredients are fresh and high quality, the reason we went there. The problem: They messed up our order and ended up charging us for both the wrong pizza and the corrected one. No one offered to bring an appetizer or salad while we waited 35 minutes. The bill for two people was over $58.

Thoroughly disappointed in Ellendales! Went for brunch today with a reservation. Stood in the entryway for 15 minutes (10min past our reservation time) without even being greeted by the hostess, who was apparently in the back clearing tables. When we were finally greeted, there was no apology. In fact she barely acknowledged that we had been waiting. Brunch buffet was sub-par at best and overpriced for food that obviously came from cans and boxes. My date had "orange juice." We had to wait for them to "make a fresh batch," so he was expecting fresh squeezed; instead, he ended up with Tang or some other orange koolaid equivalent. Biscuits were hard as a rock and the bacon in the buffet line was nearly raw - can you say food poisoning waiting to happen? Definitely wouldn't go back.

Worst "Mexican food" in the city of Philadelphia. Overpriced tacos, soggy undercooked quesadillas. While I was waiting for my dismal food, the prep cook was making a batch of guacamole. During this time I watched him stick his finger in to test it multiple times without washing it, as well as rubbing the sweat and snot off his face with the sleeves and front of his t shirt. Disgusting place, no sanitation. Threw my food out, didn't want food poisoning.

Today we went to daughters cafe expecting the same amazing service and food we have had the last two times. Sadly, the service today was awful. My pregnant wife has an allergy to gluten and they would not allow us to modify the menu (which I understood), but when she wouldn't allow us to order just a side of fruit or bacon in lieu of the gutenus menu options we were appalled, especially as these items were already being served as sides for the main dishes. My wife was so upset she ended in tears. Needless to say the service has gone downhill and we will not be back. NEEDLESS TO SAY WE WONT BE BACK!!

I don't often write a review. I only write them when warranted. This was warranted. Went to the bonefish grill for dinner on a Thursday night in the beginning of march. It wasn't busy. I ordered a simple haddock with browned butter. I was served the special which was haddock with artichoke hearts and feta cheese. I wanted to vomit. The combination of cheese and fish turns my stomach. I didn't send it back because I already waited a while for that meal on a quiet Thursday. I scrapped off the artichoke hearts and feta cheese. I didnt want to waste the fish so I took the fish home and fed it to my dog. The side dishes weren't that great either. The spinach was cold, mushy, and tasteless. The fish was also cold when served. I was very disappointed. I will not return to or recommend bonefish grill.

I did not have a good experience here. I've had multiple good experiences here and no complaints previously. However today we ordered some quesadilla appetizers and one was supposed to be chicken and one was supposed to be cheese. After eating half of the quesadilla that was supposedly cheese, my sister realized there was shrimp in there! I don't eat seafood and luckily I don't have an allergy to seafood, but this could have been a problem for someone that has a seafood allergy. They really need to be more careful! I don't eat seafood at all and this completely grossed me out, ruined my appetite, and made me nauseous. Other than today, I've had good experiences here so I am still willing to come back, but I just need to be careful about checking my food when I get my order here.

The tall, large, older man with glasses basically blocked me from entering because they closed at 2:00...it was only 1:50. I mean, I get it, he wants to go on break and I would've left but my friend that I was meeting had just been seated by a different employee. Let's just say, this dude was NOT happy about having to serve us. Before I literally touched the menu, let alone glanced at it, he coldly said, "Do you know what you want?" I was pretty scared of him and didn't want to piss him off anymore than I already had (sorry for existing, bud) so I ordered the first thing I saw which was the chicken quesadilla. I nervously asked for light cheese, bracing myself for a possible punch in the face by this clearly disgruntled and very intimidating man. No punch in the face. Relieved. Then my food came. Sadness. I ended up getting a cheese Only quesadilla with extra cheese. Was this Opposite Day? And When I say extra cheese, I mean this bad boy would send a lactose intolerant person to their death bed. I just ripped it apart, and pretended to eat it because I was just over the entire situation. So yea, it sucked. We all have bad days, but that dude needs to take a Xanax and crank up his hearing aid. On the plus side, the woman who seated my friend and told us goodbye was extremely polite and courteous. ...but yea...that dude... :'(

Extraordinarily rude service. The products are good but overpriced. I had a standing weekly order as we have a family member has a gluten allergy. I was spending on average $50/week for many months. Last week, the donuts we got were tasteless. I have never uttered a complaint before. I called and left a message about the situation and received no return call. So I decided to stop in. The manager, Laura, acknowledged she received the message and told me know else had a complained so that is just the way it is. I had asked for replacements she said that they would not do that. She clearly never planned to return my call. How much could it really cost to replace 5 donuts? Now they have lost my business and they clearly don't care.

My boyfriend is from Minnesota and didn't know any good sushi places. I'm from Arizona, and had gone to Sushi Garden several times a couple years ago and had liked it so we decided to try it out. The first time we went, we went at lunch time. There was hardly anyone in the restaurant so we thought the service would be decent. We were sat in the bartenders section. It took her several minutes to approach us and when she did she didn't seem to pleased to see us. It took her 10 minutes to bring us drinks and to come back and take our order. Considering, we were 1 of 2 tables in her section. We both ordered two rolls. After half an hour, I got curious as to how sushi could take that long and I looked over to see our sushi plates sitting on top of the sushi bar and our waitress was no where to be seen. I have no idea how long it was in the window, but it took her 15 minutes from when I noticed it for her to reappear, without our sushi. When she did, I had to flag her down and point it out to her. When she finally brought it, she dropped the plate in front of me and stormed off and then continued to glare at us from behind the bar. We were dissatisfied, finished our meal, and left asap. We decided to give it another chance tonight as our date night. We ordered the all you can eat and a glass of wine and a beer. The waitress was very nice and prompt, and we were having a decent time until about halfway during the meal. I began to feel unwell. Our bill was around 60 with tip. By the time we got in the car, both of us were not feeling well. By the time we were home, we were horribly sick. As much as I like food poisoning, I'd rather not get it on date night. We will not be returning.

Disclaimer: I grew up eating real Mexican food in Los Angeles. I have not found any place in Indy that comes close to the quality and flavor of Mexican food found in southern California. I actually had to look up the company info to see whether Taco Bell owned this restaurant (I was surprised to find out it doesn't). The food quality was abysmal. Started with guacamole, chips and salsa. Flour tortilla chips which I am not a fan of, not crunchy like corn tortilla chips. The guacamole was worse than wholly guacamole. The salsa tasted like it was from a can or jar. Got the chicken Al carbon tacos for lunch with a side of rice and beans. Salt was the main flavor in all food. The chicken was rubbery , and the taco was primarily cheese and a thicker than usual tortilla. The rice and black beans were seriously not good - more Tex Mex flavored, very unappealing as far as appearance, texture and that the beans (more like bean sauce) were served over rice. The rice was not detectably Mexican/Spanish. So disappointed considering the good reviews. If you are downtown and want tacos, go to Bakersfield or La Parada. Skip Nada... One star on food alone, but will give one more because it was hip looking and I am not showing signs of food poisoning so far (only been 1 hours since leaving though...so there is time).

I haven't tried the food here. I was about to get in line until I saw a woman prepping raw chicken next to open salad display. Then watched as she finished using tongs to move the raw chicken from the cutting board to a container, proceeded to "rinse" the tongs and place in the salad container. Can anyone saw food poisoning?

Been here a few times. The service is always lousy and slow. Despite having nobody else in the restaurant, they wouldn't allow my party to sit in a particular booth because we weren't big enough. The last time I went there, I got severe food poisoning. That was the last straw. Don't go here!

So my pregnant friend wanted to go here because her baby is craving red meat and fried pickles. I am not a food snob, I knew what to expect. I know this place is a chain and I'm not bashing it because of that. The fried pickles were pretty tasty and the blooming onion or whatever it was called was also as good as a fried onion usually is. My steak would have been pretty good too if it was actually cooked the way I wanted it -medium rare...it was more like raw/rare. But I know better than to complain about an undercooked steak...you will get it back and it will be grossly overcooked. I'd rather just chance it and eat the rare meat and pray I don't get food poisoning and/or crap myself. I was in luck, I didnt end up crapping myself! My complaint is on the level of cleanliness. I know the throw your peanut shells on the floor thing is part of the appeal of this place and part of the fun. But what it does is it lets the people that work there ignore OTHER trash on the floor. Accidentally dropped dirty napkins and food products on floor are just left there. Forever. Because its supposedly part of the fun! Just throw shit on the floor! Its fun! Maybe I'm being a stick in the mud, but I felt like I was eating in a friggin dumpster. At least the bathrooms were clean.

I ordered takeout for the 1st time a few months ago. I can't even remember what I ordered, but it was the nastiest food I've ever tasted and that's not an exaggeration. I think I had a BBQ Pork dish with some gross, red sauce that looked like vomit. There was no seasoning at all added to the dish. I didn't even eat it, so that was a $13 waste.

Probably one of my "ok" places to eat when I'm visiting my close friends in Tucson. It's as comparable as it gets to chain type Chinese food I've had in the Bay Area in California. Overall, food is cheap, won't give you food poisoning, and fills you up.

I ate at Sahara Grill over the weekend, and it was decent enough. Not the best Middle Eastern food I've had, but it was good. Our waiter catered well to my gluten-free needs. He confirmed that there was no wheat or flour in the sauces and marinades in my dish, and because the rice was mixed with wheat vermicelli, he instead substituted fries, which he also confirmed to be gluten-free. The chicken schawarma I ordered was tasty enough, but nothing spectacular. The chicken was well cooked, though I couldn't really taste many of the spices that were supposed to be on it. The sesame yogurt sauce for the chicken was really nice, though (I'm not exactly sure what it was called, but it tasted similar to tzatziki, albeit warm instead of cold). The grilled vegetables--peppers and zucchini--were actually my favorite part of the meal. The fries were standard. I doubt they were handmade on premises--they looked pre-packaged. They tasted good when dipped in the sesame yogurt sauce, though. While I would go back here again to try something else (maybe a beef or lamb dish), I'm not in any particular rush to do so. It's worth mentioning that their dessert "menu" consists of nothing but a small piece of baklava (which I couldn't try, of course, since it's made with wheat flour), so this isn't the place to go to if you're looking for a variety of sweets after your meal.

There's a certain nostalgia that goes with Einstein for me since we used to have one on my first college campus. I was more than happy that their lunch menu now includes a "Vegetarian Southwest Veggie with Quinoa" which also just happens to be vegan (though not gluten free, so be careful my gluten-intolerant friends). I thrilled that I was not "forced" to have a doughy, starchy, carby bagel with no topping (no shmear or butter for me, please!) as I normally do at bagel shops. Soup was great, coffee was great and as anti-corp take over as I am, I really do continue to love this one.

Grazie - Grazie - Grazie!! Hands down THE BEST and MOST REASONABLE option for Gluten Free Pizza in and around Nashville!! Don't get me wrong, there are other wonderful options for a good GF pizza in Nashville, however at said spot I am talking about, you only get 4 small slices and it is pretty darn pricey! But at Italia you get a FULL medium (8 small slice) one topping pizza for only 11.99!!! My bank account felt like it was buying non-gluten again, ha! I ordered a pepperoni GF pizza for myself (they only have one size and that is medium) and a large thin crust pepperoni for my boy. He is able to eat pizza anywhere and says that hands down this was one of the BEST pizza's he has had in Nashville. The best part both pizzas - including a tip (because they were so darn nice) and a two liter soda - was less than $26 bucks!!! We didn't do delivery b/c we didn't live close enough .. but that is an option for East Nashville folks! For those wondering, I asked about the gluten free pizza dough and they said it's made special for them out of house (great news for those worried about cross contamination). I have no clue who makes it - but it was fabulous and fresh! I read one review elsewhere that it was too "doughy". I agree it was a tad bit on the soft side only in the middle - but I thought it was delicious!!!! If you prefer it more done - just pop it in the oven for 10 more min! Thank you Italia for not only caring about your customers enough to take a risk and offer a Gluten Free Pizza - but for having such reasonable prices!! I don't eat pizza often but when I do this will be the only place that I go!

We shared a small, low-fat ice cream with cheesecake flavor added and cookie dough mixer. It was tasty and delicious. The process is a little slower, but it's neat to watch and there are plenty of taste combinations to discuss while you wait.
