It's basically Cold Stone...with several key differences: instead of JUST having ice cream, they have regular and low-fat ice cream, soy milk, almond milk, custard, and yogurt...and the almond, soy, and yogurt are available sweetened or un-sweetened. instead of pre-made ice cream that's mixed on a cold stone, the ice cream is still liquid and it's frozen right in front of your eyes with liquid nitrogen and mixed in a steel bowl. no cross-contamination! Every bowl is NEW so only your flavors will be in there. I think some of the people complaining about flavor got something unsweetened and didn't tell the person to add sugar to it. Someone even said the problem was "not enough sugar" but they had ordered almond milk. The stuff isn't naturally sweet. Next time I go, I'm going to get pumpkin and cinnamon flavors with graham cracker mixer...frozen pumpkin pie!! I had 2 other combinations all planned out by the time I ordered, but when I go someplace for the first time I usually go with the standard cookie dough/cheesecake combo to establish a baseline. Another complaint is that the motion detectors in the bathroom are useless. I walked in and it stayed dark. I walked out and walked back in, stomped around and waved, and the lights came on. I started washing my hands. They went out again. I waved my hands in the darkness but to no avail. I finished washing my hands and dried them in total darkness. Fine for a grown-up but that would've been terrifying for a little kid! The lights stayed off as I groped my way back to the door. So yeah...lost star for stupid bathroom lights.

I went the other day for happy hour and appetizers with my partner. When I called to make a reservation, I was hung up on after being put on a brief hold. They were extremely busy when we arrived, and we had a waitress that was training another waitress. While I understand the added burden of training someone new, the service could have been much better. They gave our calamari to another table and we had to remind them, to which the waitress exclaimed "Oh!" And she ran off and added another order to the kitchen. At the end of our dining experience they pitched the rewards program that their dining chain/group offers and it was extremely classless and unprofessional; I just wanted to have a fun evening and Chart House really let me down this time (not my first time at this location, I typically enjoy the food/atmosphere here). While the food I had was delicious, I got food poisoning from either the shrimp or the mahi fish tacos. I felt fine after consumption and everything seemed thoroughly cooked, but after returning home about three hours after, I began to feel sick. I felt warm and I began to perspire some and then it came...after vomiting three times, I returned to my normal color and vowed that I would not eat here again. Reasonably priced, great wine list, but honestly...after getting sick from seafood at a restaurant, that is the only and final straw for me. I will not eat at Chart House again. Severely disappointed.

First off, let me say that I'm neither vegan nor gluten-free. I like to try vegan foods, though, because when there's a reasonable vegan option, I'll generally go for that. Unfortunately, places like Sweet Freedom are the reason people think vegan baking can't be good. I've baked and purchased some amazing vegan treats over the last few years - even vegan frosting. The cupcakes I got here were pretty terrible, though. The cake was dry, dense, and oddly gummy (perhaps because they were gluten-free). The frosting was grainy and had a weird sugar-alternative sort of taste. Agave, maybe? It wasn't good. As far as price is concerned, Sweet Freedom was pretty average. The employees were about average in terms of friendliness, and I did see some people leave because they couldn't buy bottled water on a credit card. I can't recall if it was a minimum purchase kind of thing, or a no credit cards at all thing, though. Either way, it's probably easier to bring cash or ask in advance. I won't be back to Sweet Freedom. If you're gluten-free or vegan, you might be okay with the cupcakes here. Or...you might be inspired to take up baking. It really depends on how high your baked good standards are.

I'll start my review with an American proverb from the mid-1970's: "The knuckle dragging dingus may look upon his plate, scanning the small bits of torn up scrap, and scoff while thinking to himself, 'I will never find my fill on portions fit for finches.' This man is blind to the one steadfast truth of fondu. Take not pity on this fool, for it is only the oldest and wisest of fondu druids who understand the truth: when it comes to fondu, less is more." The Melting Pot is pretty next level. The last time I was there I witnessed a couple end their relationship in the middle of dinner. It wasn't a quick affair either, in fact it was the kind of slow burning break up that can only be likened to an evening at the symphony--in short, there were movements. I watched the man spring the break up on the woman. I watched her denial. The sink in. The brick hit. The wide eyes. I watched the bitter crocodile tears and whisper yelling. I watched the man, sensing the collective eyes of the restaurant on him, trying to keep his cool while pressing the waiter to try running his card again. Finally, I watched both of them take a lot of to-go boxes, while simultaneously telling the waiter that one of them would take him on up on his offer of a 'desert course raincheck' ticket. In no way did any of this ruin my meal. I reveled in their darkness. The more their night unraveled the better my food tasted. I wanted to kiss both of them on the forehead and place two small squares of cheese covered pumpernickel bread on their eager tongues. I will never know how to thank them. They tainted nothing. In fact, the combination of the break-up with the disposition of the waiter, who had this strangely refreshing no B.S., no handholding, 'I'm in my junior year of intensive acting classes at Juilliard and this black turtleneck is the only thing that can contain my inner decay' vibe, I felt like I had died and gone to heaven. This is definitely my kind of fondu place. Viva la whatever word is Spanish for Fondu. In closing I'd like to briefly touch upon the opening proverb. Some people may think that the food isn't enough for the price point. That's understandable, you're the kind of pure bred, diesel pissin' American who thrives on the Hardee's Five Dollar Bowel Breaker Burgers™ and when you see these puny pieces of meat with names you can't pronounce, being dipped in boiling vats of sauces that you can't pronounce, you start thinking that someone is pulling your leg. As a fellow American Bad-Ass I'm here to tell you that your leg is not being pulled and that the portions are actually more than enough. I don't care how much of a renegade you are, by the time you get to the forth course, you're going to be crawling to that finish line. So ante up, Hoss, and get ready to pound down some serious fondu fun. It's going to be a wild ride and as long as you don't cross contaminate your meat or break up with your significant other in the middle of your third course, you're going to be fine. 3/5 will return.

Nope. This place seemed so promising from yelp reviews, so I decided to stop by for lunch. I ordered the chef selected 7 piece nigiri with spicy tuna roll, as well as a quail egg nigiri and super white tuna sashimi. I could smell the fishiness of the nigiri as it arrived to my table, which raised red flags. I tentatively took a bite of the tuna nigiri and immediately tasted a warm, unfresh fish. The salmon and snapper were just as bad. The spicy tuna roll was also warm, rotting, and disgustingly chewy. The white tuna sashimi was obviously frozen, but that at least kept it somewhat fresh. The best was the quail egg nigiri. As I gulp down several shots of sake to kill whatever bacteria that has now entered my system, I pray for no food poisoning and wonder if I should have stuck with cooked food. Overall, this visit has left a very bad taste in my mouth. The service, however, is phenomenal. I may be back to try their ramen.

Rouses Market has almost everything. (almost) because they have to! There are no health food stores in the French Quarter. At least not that we could find or that our hotel knew about. For the most part I do not go out for breakfast. We did a lot of calorie loading like most tourists in Nola so for breakfast most days we had Greek yogurt that we got at Rouses. There was something that they did not have and every store I called in the area not only did not have it never heard of it. It is called Liquid Acidophilus. If you have an upset tummy it fixes it immediately. Every island we went to in Hawaii has it near the hotels. The Hawaiian islands are said to be the most remote islands in the world but they all have it! I would think Nola would have it. It is good for drunks it fixes hangovers for real. (that is good free advice for tourists going to Nola to drink) I do not drink and just needed it for my tummy. Most people know about acidophilus pearls. But they take time to digest and are more for maintenance. Liquid acidophilus helps stop vomiting or any other tummy upset. Take as much as you want it is just natural fruit juice and acidophilus from yogurt. Anyway Rouses has Greek yogurt and many other things tourists and employees of the hotels might need. It is right in the French Quarter. You can also get New Orleans cooking spices and sauces at a better price than at the tourist stores. It is kind of like a local Fairway (for New Yorkers who might want to go and check out what the locals eat). Plus it is open later than most stores or mostly anything else in the area except bars. So for us night owls it is nice to have a place to shop for things to bring home!

HORRIBLE HORRIBLE SERVICE AND MANAGEMENT-The customer is NEVER right here and constantly argued with. This review is based on the way we were treated last night. Let me just say that I have NEVER been treated so badly in a restaurant before. Me and my friends decided to go here for dinner last night because a few of them have kids and we all agreed that it would be a great place to take the kids (there were 5 kids total). We sat at a Tepanaki table where we were greeted by a waiter who seemed to be really friendly. We put in our drink orders, which took him a while to get since he also had another table he was waiting on. When he came back, we began telling him what we wanted (Some of us wanted all you can eat Sushi while others only wanted a few rolls) The waiter told us that we couldn't get all you can eat sushi at the Tepanaki table and that you had to sit in the sushi bar area to have it, so we asked to speak to the manager (since we were already settled in and didn't want to move all the kids to another section). The manager came to speak to us and I asked him if all four adults could have the all you can eat sushi (in order to not have to move to the other section) and the kids, Hibachi and he said that it was fine. The waiter came back and handed us two sheets of paper between four girls because he wanted to "save paper". This turned out to be a huge mistake that caused confusion between the sushi chef, the waiter and our table. My friend and I picked what we wanted and she then specified on the paper that the crab sushi (which I ordered) couldn't be on the same plate as the shrimp sushi (which we both ordered) since she has an allergy to crabs. The waiter said that wasn't a problem and he took our papers back. He then came back while we were waiting and after the hibachi chef made the kids dinner and stated "anything you don't eat we will charge you for because you ordered 17 rolls total" huh?? My first thought was WHAT?? isn't this all you can eat? but I didn't say anything because I thought he was just joking and that anything that went unfinished I could have a box for. Had i known this, I would have been more careful in my selection and probably wouldn't have gone with an "all you can eat" . The first two plates of sushi were for the other two women who had shared the paper and me and the girl I shared the paper with waited for ours to come out. About 10 minutes later a plate of shrimp and crab sushi arrived and my friend couldn't touch it and I didn't order what they put on the plate. She told the manager and they made her her own plate about 15 minutes later. Because they made a mistake they didn't let me wrap the sushi in a box and take it home, they THREW IT AWAY. What kind of immoral idiots do this? There are people who don't have anything to eat and to just dump it in the trash because of their own mistake makes me lose all respect for an establishment like this. The manager told me that we "wouldn't be charged for the extras" We were also told that the paper we wrote on stated the charge for the leftovers. We asked to see our papers and as we thought, it WAS'NT written on there. We went back and forth arguing with the waiter (who was screaming at us) and manager who sat and argued with me about what to charge since the other two girls at my table didn't finish some of their rolls. I will make sure I tell everyone about this experience until the restaurant does something to make up for my ruined night. I will be writing a letter to corporate in addition to telling blogs and various media outlets about their practices.

I never thought I'd stoop to writing a review of an Olive Garden, but these guys irked me. It's the only restaurant in the North Wilmington area that refused to put some food that we brought on a plate in a microwave for my son with the food allergies. Insurance issues? Huh? Screw 'em. We only checked because one of my daughters, whose palate needs refining, wanted to go there. Even she's annoyed at them for her little brother's sake. Check out any of my other reviews of Wilmington restaurants, fellow parents of allergic children. They'll all nuke something for your kid if you ask.
Actually got food poisoning from the Philadelphia location: my hamburger was ice cold. Stay away!
So we went to this little place while on vacation... STAY AWAY!! I got a salad and chicken fried rice. I got EXTREME food poisoning! Do NOT eat here!

I woke up hungry on a Sunday morning and wanted a yummy brunch. Brunch is one of my favorite meals of the weekend! A friend told me that she loved the brunch at Warehouse Grille, so I headed on over. I really like the atmosphere of Warehouse Grille. It's open and spacious, and there are plenty of TVs for sports viewing. There's a big outdoor area that is also perfect for watching some sports when the weather is warmer. My friend and I seated ourselves and then proceeded to wait...and wait...and wait. After 15 minutes of not even being acknowledged, I went to the bar and asked the bartender to please send someone to our table. We waited another 5 minutes and our waitress finally arrived. Waiting 20 minutes to be acknowledged and get something to drink is unacceptable. Our waitress was really nice, but when taking our order, she sat at our table with us. I found that to be kind of odd. We both decided to go simple and just ordered the classic breakfast of 3 eggs, grits, bacon and toast for $7. Not a bad deal at all. The only change I made was to request cheese on my grits. Our order arrived and my grits didn't have any cheese. Our waitress said she'd bring me some more. When the new grits arrived, they didn't have any cheese on them...but they had corn in them. Weird. I am thankful that I don't have a corn allergy. The food, while not bad, just wasn't very good. NOTHING had ANY seasoning on it...not even salt. Any self respecting southerner knows grits need salt. I do have to say though...the bacon was to die for. But then again, bacon is pretty hard to screw up if you're working with a great product, which this was. I trust my friend (that highly recommended it) when it comes to her taste in food. Maybe this was just an off day? Maybe they do their specialty dishes like the chicken and waffles, or cajun benedict better than they do the classic breakfast. With the combination of the 20 minute wait to be acknowledged, the waitress sitting at our table while taking our order, never getting the right order of grits, and the food just being mediocre, I have to give it one star. While I can't recommend it to anyone now, I will give it another try to see if this was just an off day. NOTE: For brunch, they offer $8 bottomless mimosas. This is a great deal...and they allow you to sit there and drink them until 3 pm. This is especially wonderful when the Saints play at noon.

I grew up and spent the majority of my life in very culturally diverse places and have tried cuisines from myriad countries. I love Indian food and really did want to like this place, but: 1. FOOD: A. Chicken Pakora - Asked for them be made extra crispy, but they were NOT. They were slighty soggy and one piece of chicken was undercooked (pink and bordering on raw) B. Chili Chicken - Good spice level C. Fish Curry - Good sauce but would have appreciated more fish! D. Baingan Bharta - OMG - so many onions! Baingan Bharta is one of my favorite Indian dishes (to eat and cook!), but this was a major disappointment. I tasted mostly onions and very little of the eggplant E. Gobi Mattar - Was decent. May have been better if the cauliflower pieces were bigger (i.e. bite size) F. Saag - Was good 2. SERVICE: A. Was not very friendly. In fact, no one smiled or said anything when I came in the door. Even after I smiled and said hello, I barely received a smile from anyone except for the one male server. B. I have Celiac Disease so eating out is always a hassle for me because I have to call ahead and make sure that it will be okay. When I spoke to the owner/manager the day before I came for lunch - he ASSURED ME that he would be present at the restaurant at 11:30AM. When I got there at our agreed-upon time, he was not there and he never showed up for the entire duration of my meal. His wife ended up having to take my order and give "explanations" for not being at the restaurant. C. I did not feel welcome and to some extent I felt that they may have taken advantage of the fact that it was my first visit to their restaurant. First of all - I ordered off the menu and did not opt for the buffet. The lunch buffet costs $9. I, on the other hand, spent the equivalent of 7 or 8 people eating from the buffet, BUT: 1. I was charged $2 for the hot sauce - which is included in unlimited quantities with the $9 buffet! No other Indian restaurant that I have ever been to has done this! 2. I was charged $2 for the lemon wedges - which I think were also included in unlimited quantities with the $9 buffet! No other Indian restaurant that I have ever been to has done this! 3. I also did not have any Naan (b/c of Celiac Disease), so I do not think that it was unreasonable for me to expect the sauce and lemons to be included as accompaniments for my meal Overall - this was my first exposure to Indian food in St. Louis, and my first experience at a India Palace. I really wanted to like it, but I walked away underwhelmed by the food and disappointed in the service.

I am currently recovering from the worst food poisoning episode of my life. On Friday I picked up Pizza and wings from Papa John's in Feasterville. We all ate the pizza but I was the only who ate the wings thank God and wow did I pay for it. Went through the most violent vommitting episode I ever had, accompanied with a high fever and the runs. The 1st night was the worst, goes down as one of the worst nights of my life. This place has been hit or miss for me for a long time but always liked their pizza. Not anymore, just the site of the logo makes my stomach turn.

Why do I keep visiting this location? Because I keep hoping they'll get it right, and I can enjoy this delicious chain restaurant once more! It's so hard to find real food, that is fast and inexpensive, but every single time I visit this specific location, my order is very wrong. Sometimes even to the point where I get sick. Yes, sick. I am a vegetarian, and close to every time I order the Sofritas (YUM), I get chicken mixed in. VERY DISAPPOINTING. I haven't eaten meat in over a decade, and if my food so much as touches meat, I get very very ill for 24-48 hours. Thank you Willow Grove Chipotle for countless nights of what feels like food poisoning. Food is fantastic, this location is terrible.

My sister and I decided to come here after my birthday dinner. We've been wanting to try it since it opened but hadn't had a chance. We were able to taste all the flavors (well she was) unfortunately I was allergic to half the flavors so I stuck to double chocolate and sugar cookie to taste. Both were delicious, I got a small cup of sugar of cookie dough with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It's EXTREMELY filling. I believe even if you go here on an empty stomach it'll fill you up. The dough was sweet and soft but some parts were extremely hard. Ice cream was good. The only thing that kinda bothered me was the cross contamination between the different flavors. Given I'm allergic to some things I had to be extra careful. I recommend trying it if you're in Tampa!

Good food and you can't beat the price for all you can eat. I hate smelling like it til I take a shower tho and burping up Indian food for a good 5 hours isn't too fun but I would do it again! The Bollywood shows on their TV will hypnotize you 2/1/2013 Ok so the last time we went we got food poisoning...

I went in to Red Robin with a friend for lunch the other day. We went to the bar to have lunch. The bartender was in a very cranky mood and I got attitude the whole time. I'm allergic to tomato, so I asked for my burger without. When it came out it had tomato on it and I had to send it back. So I waited while my friend ate his lunch. As soon as the replacement was brought out I was given the check. Being a former business owner and restaurant tour I don't like this practice and giving a customer the check when they barely started eating and after a major mistake. Still attitude from the bartender. I came home and filled out the survey and was contacted by corporate by email, saying that the store G and would be contacting me by the next day. So unprofessional, that they could not even do that. I have been going to this Red Robin since the very day they open their doors. No more, they have been going downhill, especially with service. When you tell a customer you were going to contact them then you better do it

I have eaten at Lucky Fins many times before and had good luck, but this last time I had the mojo roll and got horrible food poisoning. I called the manager to have him check into it and he did everything he could to deny that it was their sushi that made me sick. All I can say is eat at your own risk. If the manager is turning a blind eye to food poisoning I can't imagine what else is being swept under the rug.

I took my family to Native Gill & Wings and I have to admit I was not impressed. It was a Wednesday night and maybe 6 other tables of 3/4 top. It took our waitress about 10 mins after we sat down to even come take our drink order, then only brought out 2 of the 5 drinks (water & soda) and it took another 5 mins to get the other 3 drinks. She said she would be right back to take our order, but she felt talking with another employee about her phone was more important. When she finally returned 10 mins later, she continued to rush us on taking the order by after each person that ordered stating is that all, never waiting for the entire table to order. By this time there was only us and one other table of two left in the restaurant, and after 40mins of waiting for our food it finally came out. My 2 yr old sons chicken fingers plate had been under the warmer so long it burnt my hand. The chicken wings and the salad plates were also very hot from being under the warmer so long, but not nearly as hot as my sons. Our waitress assumed we all liked ranch dressing which we all dislike and when I asked for blu cheese she went back to talking to her friend about her phone and getting a phone charger for her phone. 5 mins later we finally got our blu cheese and we were also the only ones left in the restaurant. After eating maybe a quarter of our food, do to it being flavorless and overlooked tasting food, nothing that would warrant a long cook time, we all sat patiently for our waitress to come back so we could get boxes and a check, but what shocked me when I asked for the checked she asked us if we wanted water. Now isn't that a question you would ask at the start of service, not at the end? Needless to say my family and I will never be returning to this establishment and I highly recommend they train their staff, especially the waitstaff. As I am writing this review on my drive home from Native Grill my husband has had to pull over and throw up and I can tell you I'm not feeling very well either. If this results in food poisoning I will be contacting the health department.

I went to Sweet Freedom because I've heard it was a delicious GF bakery near by, which is hard to come by! I walked in with high expectations, but was disappointed. Maybe it's because I don't need all the extra precautions (dairy free, soy free, transfat free, etc... all I'm looking for is gluten free). Anyway, the Turtle Cupcake left a lot to be desired. Tasted very bland, even for such a fancy and loaded cupcake. Makes me wonder what kind of ingredients they're using if almost everything needed to make chocolate, caramel, cakes, etc is off limits. The chocolate chip cookies....meh. Taffett's is 10x's better, in my opinion. And right down the street. The brownie... don't get me started. Needless to say, I won't be back. Again, I am not looking for soy free, dairy free, or anything else. Just gluten free. So that could be a big factor. Maybe those who need all those restrictions think it prevails in comparison to other bakeries/products offering the same restrictions, but for this GF gal, it's a no-go. The staff, however, was super nice. The bakery was very clean looking, also. And prices weren't too bad. Higher than a regular bakery, but not awful.

First time eating here for breakfast. The place is very chaotic and didn't feel organized. We were seated and took over 10 minutes for a waitress to come to our table to talk to us. We almost walked out. We finally were acknowledged. The waitress was nice, but they all seemed very stressed. My family liked their food - omelette, pancakes, and prime Donna. I didn't enjoy mine. I love mushrooms and these mushrooms were canned and tasted very fake. There were a lot of them, too. Afterwards, I was the only one that got really sick. Was told it was food poisoning and that was the only thing I've eaten all day, so. . . For that price, there are so many better options around with better service and food.

They were out of almost everything. Also my friends are gluten free and although they did have gluten free biscuits, the neglected to tell us they were not included in the price of the meal we ordered--they were $10 each! When we asked why we weren't notified of this, the waiter said it was on the menu; however, when he went to look, he couldn't find it written anywhere. Then the owner came over and we tried to reason with her and instead of having a conversation with us, she rudely said, "excuse me" and stormed off never to return. I understand we are college students, but just because we're young customers doesn't mean we aren't worth speaking to. It was just a mediocre plate of eggs with a biscuit. Save yourself the stress, go elsewhere.
Very clean Typical cute waterfront beach bar Lots of gluten free options I enjoyed the chicken wings and a rum drink We enjoyed outdoor seating Plan to return again soon

Stay away from this awful place! We live in the doylestown area and really enjoy sushi, fresh sushi not frozen soft shell crab that has been thawed out and cooked for a spider roll and taste like freezer burn. The decor is decaying, cracked tiles, dust and christmas lights hung year round that only light half the string. We went here four years ago and hated it. The prices are way too high for the total lack of quality. We decided to give the place a second try last December and the sushi, miso soup and plain white rice was even worse than what we remembered. We were lucky we didn't come down with food poisoning!

Went out to grab Pho and the place was closed on Mondays. So Guppies seemed logical since it was next door. We ordered guac as an app and we were not impressed. First the chips were stale and the guac had 0 flavor. I ordered a burger without the bun and got a burger without anything on it... AND maybe the smallest portion of fries I'd ever seen. My plate went back to the kitchen 2 times before they got it right. But since it had to keep getting reheated, the lettuce and tomato were soggy and gross. Considering burgers are 1/3 of their menu, it shouldn't be that hard to make a burger without bread or any accommodations for food allergy. I'd been there before and had a decent experience. However the staff looked miserable and despite the ridiculousness of the issues with my food they offered 0 apologies.

Like the other veg-heads, I wanted to love this place, but it fell short for me. I'm a gluten free vegetarian so this place should be a shoo-in for me. I got the taco and was pretty disappointed. It is a gluten free shell (pretty good), sunflower meat (could've been seasoned better), iceberg lettuce (lots of lettuce), mushrooms (could've used some seasoning), salsa (so tasteless), hummus (I've never tasted such bad hummus), and raw zucchini slices (why?). I would recommend that they hire an independent chef to come in and give them some feedback. It has so much potential, but vegetarian/vegan food needs seasoning and flavor to be good.

Very nice guy owns/runs this place, but frankly the bagels & bread I've tried here are just not very good. These days to be gluten free, doesn't necessarily mean you must give up flavor and texture in bread. Certainly edible, but I think they need to update their recipes.

Meh - the staff were also super nice, so I feel bad writing this... but to be honest the food was just "meh"... the watermelon splash I'll give em - that was very refreshing - but the jerk burger wasn't fully cooked, and neither were the fries... I left hoping I won't end up with food poisoning... Maybe I'm missing something here, or I ordered the wrong thing or caught them at a bad time, but I just don't understand the appeal... having lived in the Caribbean for a number of years I was really craving something to remind me of my time there... :(

I attened this place for a company luncheon. The ambiance and the atmosphere were very nice, and it wasn't at all drafty (which suprised me since it is an older building). However, I ordered the fish-and-chips and it gave me food poisoning. So I will not be coming back to the restaurant.

My boyfriend and I went here after moving in nearby, it had the potential to be our neighborhood sushi restaurant. Unfortunately, they were very busy and only had one server. We had a long wait to order. When we did order we mentioned that I have a shellfish allergy, which is never a problem at other sushi restaurants When we finally got our sushi, it was full of shrimp and crab. When we finally were able to flag down the waitress we were given attitude and told to just pick it out. Considering we requested they use a clean knife to make my sushi, we didn't trust the rest of it. She took the sushi away and did not offer to fix it, or bring something else. When she brought the check, the sushi she took away was still on there. When we asked to remove it, she said no, that they had made it already. We insisted and they finally agreed. She had to go in the back to talk to the manager and we watched the manager berate her for her errors in front of the whole restaurant. We will never return. When someone has an allergy you take that seriously, and don't make the customer pay for your mistake.

My "go to" Chinese delivery place. I'll start by saying, Chinese is really my least favorite of all ethnic foods. I'm really more of a pizza/taco/sushi kinda gal. But, every now and then, I want Chinese food. And this is who I call. Is it the best? Not to me, but like I said, not my fav. It is insanely fast delivery, always hot, always fresh. My boyfriend is severly allergic to shell fish. Other Chinese places we have eaten at have a REALLY hard time understanding how crucial not slipping him a few shrimp really is, so I really do appreciate that about them. No surprises. The portions are freakin huge. We can both get very full off of one order, and bf is a BIG eater.

I had seen the glowing reviews for this place here on Yelp, and decided to give it a try. I quickly regretted this decision. Our waitress if you can call her that (she only came to our table once the whole meal) seemed friendly enough. The restaurant was entirely empty save for me and a friend, yet still our service came at a snails pace. That's fine, I can deal with that. But when it comes to the food, I was disgusted. The egg drop soup was nauseating. It looks and tastes like a scalding hot bowl of phlegm. Bland and way too thick and I couldn't shake the feeling that texture-wise it was way too similar to vomit. I couldn't eat it. Our drinks came and despite me picking up a bottle of Dr Pepper at the counter (mistakenly thinking you just pay for a soda and grab the one you want) I was told they were out of Dr Pepper. While I was holding the Dr Pepper. Our food came on paper plates with plastic utensils. My fork was missing both center prongs. The staff were arguing in the kitchen so we decided to just cut our losses and leave instead of asking for another set of plastic cutlery. After coming home and opening Yelp to revisit the other reviews for this restaurant, I can't help but notice the positive reviews come from accounts with profile pictures that look strikingly similar to the restaurant staff members. Wouldn't recommend to anyone

Meh, it's decent. I enjoyed seeing that their meat was sourced from local farmers. They use peanut oil to fry, FYI as not many people knew the answer to my question since I have an allergy. It's extra-condiments burgers...

Have wanted to try this place out for awhile, so finally made it today. I imagine that upon opening, it was much brighter and cleaner, but as other Yelpers have commented, this appears to be a one-man show, and the appearance of the premises are what suffer in this equation. I got the vegan plate and asked about the falafel or the alternative wrap filling of cauliflower or eggplant and found that ALL were deep fried to avoid cross contamination with the meat. I appreciate the non-vegan separation of items, but wasn't expecting them all to be deep fried. Roasting or baking these items prior to opening for the day would be much more tasty and healthy. The meal was okay, seemed fresh enough, and the falafels weren't overly spicy. Hummus itself was okay - nothing special. Seating is also sparse and pushed to the walls on either side, with the eclectic feel that is common today in dining - mismatched everything. The facility, both indoors and out, however could really use a little work. Maybe enlist a friend or family member to do the daily cleaning and repairs if owner cannot afford more than one employee (or if employee is the owner!).

We have been here several times in the past year, just for happy hour. Mostly our experience has been ok. Drinks are fine (can't say no to 2-fers!!!), food is fine (nachos with steak is pretty good, chicken tenders are not good), and we have had some lovely bartenders and servers. Tonight was pretty blegh though. There seemed to be about 15-20 people working on the floor but there was little service being offered. When the place is maybe half full, this is a worry. Everyone seemed to be more interested talking between themselves. Bartender in the Houston shirt was a dick. Tried to pour me a more expensive drink than what I had asked for, multiple times. He also swore up and down that the margarita mix was gluten free to my friend, when in the past we have been told by other bartenders to avoid it. Our food took forever, and was lukewarm when arrived. We had to find our own cutlery, because the server we grabbed to get some for us seemed confused as to what cutlery was! Lastly, the receipt we got was not itemized, just a total, which makes me think that the bartender screwed us over on the happy hour pricing. The only good thing was that it wasn't that noisy in there. I realize that it is hard to hire people in this town that actually care about their job, but clearly, Sandbar goes for quantity over quality in who they have represent them. We aren't going to be back for a while. Two stars for cheap drinks.

I really like this place! The homemade tortillas are definitely good, and I absolutely loved the Taco de Hongo (Mushroom taco). I had no idea what it was when I ordered it, was super skeptical when I received it (it looked like a cat threw up food), but it was SO FREAKING DELICIOUS. The creaminess, the mushrooms, the flavor... oh god it's SO good. If that special is ever up, you MUST try it out! Can be pricy if you come really hungry, and the "medium and large" drinks are more like "very small and small," but nevertheless, the flavors are all there. The guy taking our orders was extremely nice as well.

This particular restaurant was absolutely disgusting in appearance and food. The counters were all a mess and the tables looked as if they've been cleaned only once that day. The trash area was filthy. The food was delivered cold. It also was dry, and stale. I got the Mediterranean pita and the lamb meatballs and they were absolutely disgusting. My girlfriend got the Mediterranean chicken and it tasted as if parts of it had gone rancid. I'm normally easy and let places go but this was a new low for the level the establishment it's built to be. On the good however they're very thorough with their allergy control. So they got an extra star for that. I would not recommend this establishment to any friends.

Sauntered into this cute but pricey gourmet + organic store in Downtown SB but did not purchase anything. They sell items like gluten-free brownie mix, miniature BBQ sauce, and maple syrup sealed with wax - you name it.

this place is garbage. i had written a lengthy review but it looks like it got taken down. anyway, i got food poisoning from the shrimp and threw up 14 times in less than two hours. nothing i ate here was impressive at all. slow service, bad salsa, terrible sauce on my burrito. this restaurant is among many of the things in reno you are better off staying away from.

Food good, service horrible. Have been here with a group a few times, got barely acceptable service; came alone twice and was ignored--both times I couldn't get my bill and wound up going up to the cashier to try to get her to issue me a check, both times service was so bad I left $0 tip, and I'm an unusually generous tipper. Server never came back to refill drinks, on any of the times I've been here, and wasn't even in sight to be flagged down. Last time I was there, they had gluten-free bagels available. I was excited, as I have celiac disease and have to be gluten free; with a GF bagel, I had a chance of lunch, not just eggs. I asked if I could have the chicken salad sandwich on the GF bagel, they said it was no problem. When the bill came, they had charged me full price for the sandwich plus $3-4 for the GF bagel. I questioned the charge and was told it's their policy to charge full price for both, even though I didn't get both. So I paid about $10 for a chicken salad sandwich and a single cup of tea, in a diner-ish setting. Rip off!!! I will never go back, there's too many other places to eat that have better service. I would give them one star because the service is so bad, but the food is decent so I raised it to 2 stars. But barely.

Spicey Shrimp cocktail wasn't spicy,although shrimp were fresh. Cannelloni dish was salty and bland. Table cloth have stains from prior service. Informed Waitress and she blew it off. Waitress instructed of Wife citrus allergies , but food was lemon garnish I wont comment on the overcooked salmon Otherwise i would've canceled but was a birthday dinner for a friend so didn't want to make a scene. I wouldn't visit again.

My company recently got King Edwards for a special event and I'd heard everyone in my office raving about the food. I have to wonder if maybe everyone in my office likes eating cardboard because this food was so bad I ended up tossing my food and going out to get lunch. Salt, people. Salt is fine to flavor food. Potatoes were bland. Mac n Cheese was bland. I'm not even sure how they did it, but even the rolls were bland! The one piece of chicken I had wasn't even cooked all the way through, which disturbed me a lot. I'm sorry, but I've had food poisoning before, not going to risk it again. So I'm going to say no thanks the next time they suggest going to this place for any sort of special event.

Ended up going here for a work lunch. This menu seemed to have healthier options than most places around. e.g. kale salad, quinoa dishes, and I wouldn't be surprised if they had some gluten free stuff. Ended up getting the crab cake sandwhich with side salad. The waiter told me the side salad comes with the house vinaigrette which really didn't add much flavor to the raw bed of greens but was a good low cal option. The crab cake sandwhich was solid. Had a few larger pieces of crab and wasn't just claw meat and filler. Also had an imperial pumpkin on tap which I was pleased to see. Sandwhiches run about $12. The real treat is their bread which is home made. The crab cake came on brioche which was excellent. They supply their bread to many local places including for all the sandwhich made for take out at Sonoco. Nothing really drawing me back with the array of options on Main Street but a solid pick to mix it up.

Highly recommend this place. We all enjoyed are meals My family come here often. They are celiac friendly. Reservations recommended. The waiter was knowledgeable and said there's a dedicated kitchen area to avoid cross contamination. There's Gluten free pasta and many other options to choose. The food was utterly fantastic! I had the risotto with grilled chicken which they made separately and especially for me and it wasn't even on the menu! They ask up front if it's an allergy or preference so they know whether to use the dedicated kitchen area. Which I really appreciate as some family members that went just eat GF occasionally because of me so they got the GF pasta but didn't need the whole precautions, but I do. Also the owner and his wife were just lovely and most accommodating. I'd go back here every time I'm in Tampa. And my family who live here go often but you really should make reservations.

I never write reviews, but felt compelled to write this one. I was diagnosed with a wheat/gluten allergy 2 months ago, and have wanted a treat to satisfy my cravings for sweets I can no longer have. The photos for this bakery looked SO good, I ordered a variety of items to have shipped for the holidays. I ordered apple cider donuts, cake pops, and cinnamon rolls. I have not yet tried the cinnamon rolls, but don't have high hopes based on the other items. The donuts were inedible. They seemed stale, with a terrible aftertaste. I sadly had to throw them away. Next up - cake pops. Much better consistency, same horrible aftertaste. I had to toss those too.... a whole bunch of money down the drain and a huge bummer. I don't know if something was wrong with the products I received, but I couldn't eat them. The cinnamon rolls LOOK good, but I'm fairly certain they won't be based on everything else. Very disappointed... wish everything tasted as good as it looks.

LIke another reviewer below, I also was not impressed with the taste of the cheesesteak and did not finish it and had stomach discomfort immediately. I then woke up in the middle of the night throwing up for hours and hours, unable to hold down any liquids or stomach meds (not even water or tums) unable to sleep or feel any relief with terrible stomach pains and severe diarrhea. The strain on my stomach and back from throwing up so much and using the bathroom is unbearable and I had to call out of work because I was so sick and not feeling any relief. This sounds exactly like food poisoning symptoms. I will NEVER eat here again and will suggest you avoid it too.

How do you write a review recovering from food poisoning from their Chicken Tempura salad. It tasted fine when eating but I should have been suspicious when I noticed that some pieces of chicken were not white in the center. I had nothing else and not even a drink except water. Other than everything else being mediocre we will not be going back.

Just a heads up, don't go to Ella's expect gluten free service! Outside of a salad or bunless burger, your options are limited. Sidenote...thank you to the rude waitress that acted like I was a mad woman for suggesting gluten free pizza dough.... you did have it a while back! And you were kinda rude to our party. Unfortunately, no one at our table was impressed and wants to go back. :(

My husband and I ate here for brunch one Sunday morning. And I will not be going back. The started losing points with me because they offer Pepsi products, not Coke products. Then they lost more points when I asked the server to check with the chef about gluten free items. The server came back and told me I could eat the fruit. I asked if they added gluten to their eggs, and he replied he didn't really ask the chef and didn't know what I was talking about. Okay.... I ended up going through the buffet and picking up fruit and some cheese smothered pork. The fruit was good but I cannot say the same for the pork. I then ordered an egg white omelet (included in the buffet price). The server delivered it and the egg whites hadn't been cooked all the way through. Yuck. So I was ready to get the F out of this place. Enter at your own risk (and definitely with low expectations).

Much fanfare had been given on the Internet about the burgers at Good Dog, a bar located on 15th street between Walnut and Locust, especially in regards to their Good Dog burger which comes stuffed with Roquefort cheese. I opted for their traditional burger, prepared medium - which is how I ask for all my burgers. Medium gives you just the right amount of pink for it to be juicy, but not still mooing. I came during the lunch hour on a Friday, so it was full but not packed and I sat at the bar. And waited. And waited. When I was at the point of gnawing my arm off I was so hungry, my burger finally arrived on - SURPRISE! - a brioche bun! (But that was on the menu so I guess I already expected that. Plus, I could tell by everyone else getting served their food before me.) Their fries came with a side of their housemade aioli for dipping. It was kind of like a watery version of the onion ring sauce at Burger King. I prepared to dive into this delicious burger, my palate poised to receive the succulent, juicy meat. But, lo and behold after first bite, I realized not only was my burger not even the slightest bit of pink in the middle (it was hard to tell at first in the dim lighting of the bar), but it was dry, overcooked and charred - lettuce, tomato and ketchup used as an attempt to cover up the grill marks. I was starving so there was no way I was sending it back at this point and so, I trudged on and chewed through the meat like a dog chewing on rawhide. I was extremely disappointed. No flavor, just the taste of burnt beef in my mouth. And let's not even get into the brioche bun being used yet again in a completely unoriginal attempt to fancy-ify this overpriced bar burger. ($11?? Seriously??) Regardless of how busy your kitchen is, the least you can do is try to prepare food to your customer's request. I can only imagine what would have happened if I ordered a steak there (if they even serve steak; I have no clue.) Or if I had some kind of food allergy. (I actually think I did have some allergic reaction to whatever was in their aioli after I left. I've never known myself to have food allergies before, but my throat felt like it was closing up and made it hard to swallow.) I guess they just figured it was better to overcook my burger then undercook it, and that does not a good burger make. Bad dog, very bad dog.

Would give zero if was option went for lunch today ordered the lunch buffet everything was cold nothing upto temp for hot food can we say food poisoning waiting to happen told the waitress here response well 1it is got when brought out.

We ordered take out a couple of weeks ago and they got the order wrong. One burger was missing the toppings that it was advertised with. We called the place and a rude manager lady takes the call. She apparently couldn't pull up the order. We gave her all the information she asked for and she still couldn't pull it up. After dealing with her attitude and incompetence we gave up. She toon our number down and said she would call us back. Yeah never called us back. Now, we ordered our meal. The person said 13 minutes it will be ready. We pull up 25 minutes later and shocker, it wasn't ready! Why you ask? "It never went through in the system". We proceeded to wait about 25 minutes and we walk in and guess what? It's still not done!! The manager completely avoided me and didn't even bother to come over and make sure I wasn't satisfied. And to make matters worse, one the staff members tried insinuating that I was dumb because apparently "several people call the wrong red robin". There's no other red robins around here. Rather go to Buffalo Wild Wings and get food poisoning (happened to me once) than go to this place and get horrible service.

We came before Garth Brooks and left with food poisoning! Good news first: there was a wide variety of options on the drink menu. The Blueberry Smash was delicious! Sadly, there's a lot of bad news: there was a lot of food on the floor under our table. The place just didn't look clean. My husband and I split several appetizers with friends and he and I split the Meats pizza. We didn't finish it as it didn't taste very good and was possibly undercooked. I ordered the Chop Chop salad which came out with looking like a bagged salad - very few ingredients and brown lettuce. Six hours later (after the concert, thankfully) my husband and I were violently ill and up all night gettIng sick. Our friends did not get sick and what was the one thing we had that they didn't eat? The Meats pizza. My advice? Skip this spot! It's just gross.

Help Wanted The food and ambiance were good, but the service was bad, glacially slow and the management sorely lacking. We were told we would have a 20 minute wait because we didn't have a reservation - even with plenty of open tables in sight. A while later, after noticing that they were seating guests who had arrived after us, I checked back with the host and was told we had been forgotten. It took 20 more minutes to get water and drinks and over an hour to get served. The waitress got our order wrong - I had asked for gluten free bread on a sandwich and was brought the sandwich with regular bread plus a side of gluten free bread (?) and my date ordered a side salad with his meal and was brought a whole salad, plus the hot items were cold when they arrived. It took 20 minutes to get the check once we had asked our server for it - and only then after chasing her down. There were dirty plates strewn on the bar on many of the tables. We were told that one of the servers couldn't make it in so they were a bit stretched, which could understandably throw a lunch shift off, but which didn't explain being forgotten by the host and the poor service we received from our server. I hope it was a fluke bad day. It was my first time in Santa Barbara and as a vegan I was excited to find such an interesting looking restaurant. Not sure I'll go back.

I have had good service here before today. This was the worst. One took our order, another brought the food and after a very long wait a different one brought the check. I had to hunt down my own silverware and napkin from a table three booths down. No one asked how we were doing or about the food until we paid for it and all I got was "I'm sorry". By the way, the spicy chicken sandwich tasted like vomit. My daughter did enjoy her smiley faced pancake though.

This place has promise, but the wait staff needs some lessons in customer service. We were not allowed to order anything with ingredients left out...ie, if you're lactose intolerant...you can't order Chicken Parmesan without cheese...you must have the food prepared the way the waitress thinks you should have it. Most of the people seem very friendly, but if you get the wrong waitress, you are going to dine the way she wants you to dine...no ifs and or buts about it...sort of like the soup nazi on Seinfeld.

Stopped in at Taste today, our first visit, for brunch with my husband, daughter and her friend. The food was delicious, however the service was horrendous to say the least. We went through the line and place our orders 3 sandwiches, 1 Pom frites, 1 salad and 1 oatmeal. Pretty simple items if you ask me right? The Pom frites came out very quickly however it took 45 minutes for us to receive the rest of our orders. Here's where the horrendous part comes in, my husband goes up to the counter after waiting 30 mins and asks how much longer it will be and he is told by the order taker that since we had such a "large order" that they had to put other people ahead of us!!! SERIOUSLY! Then my husband had ordered the B.E.L.T sandwich which came with fruit. He explained to the man that took our order that he was highly allergic to all types of melon and the man assured him that none of the fruit was premixed and that they would make his fruit with just strawberries and bananas. When the sandwich comes out there are 2 huge chunks of watermelon laying against the sandwich. We told the server again that he was allergic to melon and she apologized and said they would remake his order. They bring out the 2nd sandwich with a cup of fruit on the plate and guess what it has cantaloupe and watermelon in it. Correct me if I am wrong but doesn't that come from the melon family!! We send the bowl back and again specifically ask for JUST strawberries and bananas. They finally get it right the 3rd time around. While all of this fruit issue is going on I am still awaiting my Salmon salad to no avail. I finally ask the server show her my receipt and she says "hmmm well you did order that, can I take your receipt back and show the kitchen"!! Finally they bring my salad out. While the food and coffee are delicious def 4-5 stars, you may want to rethink visiting here if you have more than 2 people in your party and definitely make sure NO ONE has any food allergies!!

The food we ordered came extremely late and out of order. The main courses didn't come for two hours. They forgot our drink order, until we asked a second and third time. We specified we had a celiac at our table, and they still proceeded to serve her two dishes that contained gluten after making very clear that that dish needed to be gluten free. The first we caught, as it had bread on the side. The second was grilled octopus, but after we ate it, the waitress came to inform us there'd been a mistake and the sauce on her dish contained gluten. The celiac girl at our table ended up in serious distress for two days.

We've walked past Posh Pop many times and each time my husband makes like he's in a trance and has to go towards the amazing chocolate sugary smell oozing from their doorway. Each time I drag him back convincing him that we don't need all those treats. That is until one day I saw they give you a free cupcake with a Yelp check-in. Done deal and I didn't need anymore convincing from him to get our free cupcake and at least take a gander. The shop beautifully displays their baked good and treats. Since the display area is quite small, I did feel rushed to pick something. Next time I'm going to take my grand ol' time, I don't care who is behind me! As per the suggestion of the server behind the counter we tried the S'more cupcake as our free Yelp check in choice and then in an act of weakness I could have seen coming a mile away, we ordered 2 more cupcakes and a cakepop. The total was $16. After picking up my jaw off the floor and taking our desserts to go, I told my family we'd all be savoring and splitting the treats. I also wanted them to savor every last bite of that $16 dessert. The cupcakes were phenomenal and after reading that Posh Pop is all gluten free, it makes them taste that much better. I do wish either the cupcakes were bigger or the price was more reasonable. Next time we're in the area and I'm feeling weak I may pop in (no pun intended) to try some of their other goodies or even a coffee/espresso.

Delivered wrong item. Refused to replace wrong item for senior with food allergies. Ugh. Claimed the woman said the wrong item when she repeated the order (um what?!) and since my dad took a bite (um he thought it was going to be what he ordered), they wouldnt replace it. Wow. So many other places out there worth your business.

Dine here in confidence! You and your party will be sure to get food poisoning that lasts for 3 days! If you LIKE getting food poisoning this is THE place for you!! The manager is guaranteed to patronize you and insult your intelligence! The owners, ever eager to be their best will deny that anyone can ever get bad Sushi at their 3 star mediocre worse than a sushi buffet place!

I ate here last Friday night for my husbands birthday during our stay in Nashville. It was convenient since it was right next door to our hotel. I ordered the pasta with ragu sauce and thought it tasted a little strange and sour. I ate about a third of it. 3 hours later it hit me and I spent all night and the next day with the worst food poisoning ever! Ruined my last 2 days of my trip. I called and tried to talk to the manager as soon as I got home and had to leave a message but explained to the girl that answered what I was calling about. Never got a call back. DO NOT EAT HERE!

It could be said it is true you get what you pay for. But I've experienced the polar opposite elsewhere in this price range. The store is rather small, dated, and mirrored like a fun house. It does make it seem larger. There are 4 buffet banquets. and a rather large drink station the size of a mansion kitchen island. The offerings were bland or greasy. Minimal spice or choice of anything that seemed to be made in-house. Dumplings were frozen steamed prior to putting out. General Tso and other chicken dishes appeared incredibly similar. The scary part for those with allergies would be the pork and scallions. It was actually shrimp....... There was sushi, but after seeing other options I wouldn't recommend that. Nearly positive it was prepackaged. Overall I would not recommend this place. Was hoping for a hole in the wall experience and lacked any real true positive experience.

After a co-worker raved about the all-you-can-eat crab, I decided that I had to check this place out. I went ahead and got the Comps+ card so I could get the deal for $7.77 and headed out on a Friday night. (Without the member's card, the buffet is about $16.) The boyfriend and I got into line about 6:15 PM, and despite the number of people ahead of us, still managed to get into the buffet fairly quickly. The cashier who greeted us was a fun and vibrant lady, but the girl who seated us was dour and tired-looking. She barely said two words to us. While the BF waited on our server (I asked for a glass of water), I went ahead and checked out the food. To say that it was disappointing would be a bit of an understatement. Each "station" only has one or two offerings, and none of them looked particularly appealing. I decided to start with the crab and shrimp, which was the reason why I came in the first place. Unlike the Atlantis, the snow crab was sort of piled haphazardly next to the shrimp under a strange plastic dome. There was a scary, fishy smell coming from under there which almost made me turn away. Still, I didn't want to leave empty handed, so I grabbed a little of both, some cocktail sauce, and returned to the table. While I'd been gone, the waiter brought me iced tea instead of water, which was okay, I guess. The shrimp was warm and rubbery, but didn't taste too bad. The crab legs were thin and wimpy, not the large, robust legs I've seen at other buffets. The meat was also rather dry and salty, so I get the impression that they were overcooked. The boyfriend tried the chicken madeira, which looked appetizing enough. To hear him describe the flavor, however, "It's bland and salty at the same time." After trying a bite, I had to agree. There were no exceptional tastes jumping out at me, and it seemed like the chef thought dumping a whole lot of salt would make up for that. The Mexican station was a near bust; the only decent thing was the Spanish rice, and it still would have been better with the addition of some fresh salsas. The Chinese station was pathetic; undercooked egg rolls, bland fried rice, and I didn't bother with the steamed rice or the chicken stir-fry. There were a couple of cold noodle dishes at the salad station that were okay, and the boyfriend said the pizza slices were edible, if doughy. The linguine with clam sauce tasted like watered down alfredo sauce, the clam chowder was extremely thin but surprisingly tasty, and the seafood dish with penne pasta was all right, but I found a bone in one of the fish chunks. (Though, I guess that's bound to happen, sometimes.) The supposed "steamed" veggies were drowning in butter, and the roasted red potatoes were too salty. By the time we were finished wading through that nonsense, neither of us really felt like dessert. (In fact, I got an upset stomach a little after eating the crab and shrimp. It wasn't bad enough for me to think of it as food poisoning, or anything, but it does make me a little leery to go back.) For $7.77, I guess it's not so bad, but I wouldn't pay a dollar more for this fare. Charging $16 for it normally is a rip-off! For shame, Grand Sierra.

Quick vegan review here, to help fellow vegans coming through. They have a few veganizable options here, and for that I am very grateful. For starters, you can get the hummus dish or the Middle Eastern (minus the tzatziki sauce). As a main dish, there is a veggie burger made with Match-Meat (an STL company), a Portobello Wrap (omit the aioli sauce), and a Hummus Veggie Wrap (sans the feta). I always get the Veggie Burger because I'm a fan of Match-Meat. In order to veganize the veggie burger, you must request the gluten-free bun. It's pretty thick and dry, so I'm not a fan of that bun. You'll also need to omit the chipotle mayo, which is unfortunate because you can get a 4-pack of Just Mayo vegan chipotle and garlic mayo from Sam's or Costco for under $5. With that gluten-free bun and no toppings (ketchup didn't cut it), it's underwhelming. If I lived in STL, I'd bring my own bottle of vegan mayo to help a burger out. But again, I do appreciate that they're thinking of veg*ns and offering veg-friendly options. As meat-free diets continue to become mainstream, I'm sure they'll continue to improve in this area.
We ate here last night. I had the chicken tenders. DO NOT EAT THE CHICKEN! I was sick all night and still today. Food poisoning. Very disappointed and sick.

This place is cheap. If you are on tight on cash and need a good amount of food, then you are in luck. The food is average. I've been here twice. The first time I had the "Obama" sandwich, which I was talked into by a few friends. It is a Cuban sandwich with honey glazed on the bread. I'd rather have the butter, it just goes better with the flavor profile of a Cuban sandwich. The sweetness of the honey was kind of odd. That is just a personal preference and is not why I gave this place one star. This place gets one star for my second visit (otherwise could have gotten 2 or 3 stars). I had eaten about 60% of my sandwich when I took a bite and noticed that I could not bite cleanly through the sandwich as I pulled away. Something was still connecting the piece of the sandwich in my mouth with the rest of the sandwich in my hand. I opened the sandwich to find a very long piece of hair on it and the rest of the hair was in my mouth. Needless to say I didn't finish that sandwich and questioned what I already had eaten. I really wish that didn't happen, but it did. I can never return to this place now as I do not trust the sanitary measures taken. That is probably one of the biggest single turn offs one can experience from a restaurant, outside of food poisoning of course.

The grasshopper was invented at Tujagues so we had to stop by and grab an original. The bartender was nice, but he did mess up the drink he was making for the lady next to us. We reminded him that a Gin Fizz has gin in it and then he made our grasshoppers. It was the day after French Quarter Fest, so the incredibly strong vomit odor made sense...but still, have they heard of 409 with bleach? The grasshopper was tasty and then we left. Didn't try any food so can't help you there.

I work nearby and we ordered out from here and i got sick and was vomiting about an hour later. Had to leave work early and was confined to my bathroom all night. I will NEVER risk coming here again and i will report them to the health department. Be careful of anything you get with seafood there.

Went here to meet friends as it is relatively close to all of us and, it being here for a while, I've never been there, so it was nice to check it out. Boy did I make a mistake. We had a rather large party for a Friday night, 8 people, but a server said she could seat us. She sat us at a 6 top, with 6 chairs and told us we could grab other chairs if we saw them, so we did just that. We ordered drinks, which our server (not trying to be mean, but she was THAT BAD) took in waves, because apparently taking 8 drink orders at once was too lage a feat. We received our drinks about 20 minutes later, our beers were cold and cocktails properly mixed, so there's a plus. The beer list was better than an Applebee's, not quite underwhelming, and not overwhelming. They had a few choice beers on tap and by bottle. The food was okay. Tasty basic bar food but somewhat bland and unoriginal. It seems they attempt to make something good but to keep prices down they use cheap ingredients, resulting in a shoddy product. I could tell my fries were once in a freezer, accompanied by our french fries, tortilla wrap, and crab cake. The prices were on the mark for what the establishment was trying to be, no complaints here. After eating my friends and I decide to venture out to their patio/tent as we were getting tired of the service and wanted to stand. The patio smelled like vomit. We ordered drinks waitiing for it to pass. The bartender was a guy who seemed to have been a big shot in his high school days and thought being a bartender at a mediocre establishment would restore some of that feeling. He seemed like he was doing me a favor by me paying him for services rendered. After a tasty Dogfish Head I noticed they had Summer Ale on tap, which I always enjoy but upon tasting it noticed it tasted like Sam Adams Summer Ale and some other beer; they don't clean their lines properly, or else a beer that's just rolling out now is already turning. I give this place 2 stars instead of one because the decor was entertaining, the place seemed clean (besides that smell), and it's in a decent location, though I won't be returning any time soon.

I've come here for years. As a rule I'd have to give four stars. Today was the worst experience I have had. Arrived at 9:04am, ten people in the place. Specified ham scramble no peppers and no avocado I am allergic. At 9:57 yes 53 minutes. We got our food and coffee. My first scramble came out, and as I was walking to the truck, I opened it and of course there's avocado. Turn around go back in, they make me a new one, and next time you come back your order is 50%off- wow thanks, a wrong order that could have killed me and an hour to get it. I get home open my new ham scramble, thanks for forgetting the Damn HAM!

Spunky atmosphere, lots of seating, mostly friendly staff, decent variety. Baristas are hit or miss: some are outstanding, some have their heads on backward. Food is eh. I'm happy they have gluten free muffins, though, like the baristas, they are hit or miss; they are sometimes of poor consistency or taste and other times downright scrumptious.

Went here to watch the football game, MNF means BWW and beers right? Wrong. We arrive and see that they are pretty busy, makes sense because it's Monday night. We wait by the hostess stand to be seated...and wait...and wait...until about 10 minutes go by I walk over to the "to-go" waitress and ask her if we seat ourselves. She says "oh, we have a private event so seating is only available at the bar". Sounds good, we make our way through a crowd that looks like they're having a private event and go to find a table. Every table, high top, etc. at the bar either has people at it or has trash all over it, waiting to be cleaned. So we end up picking a table that has least amount of garbage still on it and clean the table of ourselves. Fast forward to the meals. We had to remind our waitress about our appetizer, had to go retrieve our own silverware, and still had to wait for our food to come out.l way too long. My grilled chicken sandwich comes out and you think it's going to be, I don't know, edible..right? Nope. The chicken breast was still raw. It takes is a solid 10 minutes to get the waitresses attention and she apologizes, I'm calm about it and not the screaming guy in the restaurant, not her fault-she didn't cook it. Everyone else I was with ends up finishing their meal as they go back to "fix this issue" which consists of seeing the manager taking the sandwich from her and going into the kitchen. 20 mins later our waitress comes back with the sandwich after she already came up and goes "is your sandwich out yet?". No sign of the manager. The sandwich came out done this time, with the wrong sides on it, and a hand written "SORRY!" on the wax paper that lines the plate. Only the waitress had the decency to apologize for a raw chicken sandwich face to face. They did take the meal off of the total bill but what would it take to get the manager to talk to a concerned customer that already ate a bite of raw chicken? Me lose my mind and shout at people who's fault it was? Or was it the fact that they were so understaffed and poorly managed that they were doomed to have a bad night? (I heard another lady requesting the manager while I was waiting for my meal, looks like that person was spending all their time cleaning up the incompetency of other staff). I even had another staff member come over offering free samples with a name tag talking about a "customer services expert" or something. I don't want free samples, I just want to eat my sandwich I without the fear of getting salmonella. This review would have more stars if the manager would have came over and talked but I think that this place looks like inmates running the asylum. Needless to say, I don't think we will be back. I'll try to remember to update this if I get food poisoning.

I was really looking forward to trying this place. I was so excited when it opened, but it was a bit of a letdown. I've been here a few times. Every time, I waited for my food forever. When it got to the table, it looked great, but their food just isn't fantastic. I get that it's gluten free - I'm celiac, so believe me, I know the taste difference. But these guys really dropped the ball. I've been to so many other restaurants that can modify their dishes and have them taste amazing. These guys can't even get it right, and they're supposed to specialize in it! The french bread was absolutely terrible. Too salty, hard as a rock on the outside, and far too airy on the inside. I've had better gluten free rolls at other restaurants! If you can't make edible gluten free french bread, find something else to put on the menu! I can't remember what I've had for actual meals, I just know nothing was too exciting. I've tried both their chocolate brownie, as well as their strawberry shortcake, as well as another desert. All were letdowns. Such a bummer, because I really feel like they could be great. A lot of potential here, but they need to find someone that knows how to cook gluten free, and just get some new recipes together. It really seems like someone is just experimenting with food, which is great, but do it on your own time. I spent years perfecting certain recipes, and even my worst efforts were better than some of their dishes. I'll probably keep going back every few months, just to see if they get any better. Hope springs eternal - I really want them to be great!

If I could give it less than 1 star I would. This place was no question the worst place I've ever eaten at from both a culinary and customer service perspective. It took 50 min to get our food from the time we placed our orders on a night where there were maybe 2 tables occupied in the surrounding tables. Our appetizers came out after the main courses, our dishes came out at various times to the point where everyone had their food except for one person for upwards of 5-10 minutes, one of my friends didn't even get half of his order. After 5 minutes passed after asking side of ginger dressing, I asked a different waitress only to wait another 5 minutes to have to ask another waitress who finally brought me the dressing. After finishing the first round of food, the people who ordered from the all you can eat menu placed another order thinking it couldn't possibly take as long. Wrong. The whole dinner ended up being roughly two hours- 2 and a half for a party of 6. Just to put the cherry on top of the impeccable dinning experience, The bus boy spilled soy sauce on me. If my 2 year old niece prepared and served dinner for me it would have been a better experience. I will never go back considering 2 of our party got severe food poisoning the same night. Please choose any other restaurant, thank you.

As other reviewers have touched upon, the staff here are incredibly friendly and sweet, and it's difficult not to wish the best for them. I have only ordered takeout from this establishment, so keep this in mind when reading my review. The food is pretty good, with a noticeable exception (which I'll touch on later). While well flavored, there are dishes like orange chicken where the chicken should be crispier. Now, it takes me about 10 minutes to drive before arriving back home and eating the food, but the texture shouldn't have homogenized to soft breadiness in such a short time period. Aside from minor texture issues, I did have a very strange experience with their House fried rice. It smelled very strange. It tasted fine (nothing memorable) but the smell was off-putting. Nothing rancid, but it smelled like it got cross-contaminated with another entree. Aside from that one adverse experience, this seems like a pretty solid place to get food.

I would have never gave this place a chance based on looks and location but my husband is from the area and insisted I would not get food poisoning! Now it is my go-to for seafood. The clams are always fresh and we love getting a tray of the garlic crab pieces for parties. I definitely recommend stopping in and giving this place a try, you won't be disappointed.

Shank's is good. Not great, but good. Don't get me wrong, it's worlds better than anything Pat's or Geno's (vomit!) have to offer. I just remember the old location being better. $9 for a steak and a soda is pretty decent too. Pros: Great location for stopping while on the road in/out of the city. Great bread--those who are complaining about the hard, seeded rolls do not understand the magic of a Sarcone's roll. However, I do concede that the Sarcone's rolls should have more meat on the sandwich. Another great pro is the variety: cutlet sandwiches, eggplant/veggie sandwiches/steaks/pork/roast beef. Friendly and fast service too. Cons: Quality has declined slightly over time, but it's still decent. The pork sandwiches are a bit too sloppy for me. No indoor seating, so if you're there on a rainy or incredibly hot day, you may want to take your order to go.

My second one star review. We went here as a fairly large group around 10-12, and 4-5 of us got the same thing. Strangely enough, 4-5 of us also ended up throwing up(both ends) because of what we think was food poisoning. The staff wasn't the best either. Was seated promptly, to then be waiting for about 15 mins while the waitresses finished their conversations with each other.

My family and I found this restaurant on Yelp, mostly leaning because of the gluten free crust. If you're a celiac, then you know how hard it is to eat out AND have no cross contamination! We've gone here about 3 times, even brought our relative from Cali to test out the waters. We usually order the large gluten free crust with 5 toppings, and today we ordered two of them. The crust is crispy, flavorful and they offer gluten free options including ravioli, breadsticks, chocolate cake along with their sausage. It's a definite mom and pops store which we prefer, environment is relaxing, customer service is phenomenal. We even got the chance to meet the owner :)

Made an account just to review this place. Ordered a plain pie and an order of wings. There's a reason the large plain pie is only $10, it's the worst in town. At that price, we knew what we were getting and didn't expect much more. My main problem was with the wings. Although the sauce tasted great, we all took about one bite before we noticed the texture was completely wrong. They were completely undercooked to the point where the chicken was still raw near the bone in the center of the "drummettes". They even smelt like raw chicken. Raw poultry is a great way to get food poisoning, and that is more than enough to permanently lose the business of my friends and myself. I cant speak for their pasta or specialty slices; I never bothered to try them after trying their regular fare. Bottom line, stay away from this place. Although there is a large convenience factor of being in walking distance of Rowan's campus, it is not worth it. There are MUCH better pizza places in Glassboro and surrounding towns.

Unique dining experience to say the least. Salad bar left much to be desired. Excellent onion rings and the coconut shrimp was pretty good. Don't think I would come here again though. Not sure why one would pay to cook one's own food? Why not just eat at home? Also there was cross contamination with the steak and chicken.

My awful dining experience happened back in February but I didn't have a Yelp account then but I swore that if I ever signed up that this would be my first review. I had the duck salad after a show at HOB which I remember being ok... That night I had the worst food poisoning I had ever had in my life.
