My friend had a bite of my salad and got food poisoning as well. The next day I called and spoke with a day waitress and told her what had happened and asked her to have a manager or owner call me back. Two days later I had still not received a call back so I called and got the owner on the phone. I cannot remember what this jerk's name was but he identified himself as the owner. I told him what had happened and he told me that he had eaten the same duck salad and he hadn't gotten sick so I was wrong. As someone who works with service industry and bars/restaurants, this is the craziest thing I have ever been told. Food poisoning could come from unwashed lettuce, a contaminated utensil, cooks (or servers) not washing their hands, refrigerated meats or dozens of other sources. I have never been spoken to so rudely as from this owner. He continually asked me what i wanted him to do about it. How about refunding the amount charged to my credit card for starters?!? He refused to do this, even for the contaminated dish. I should have called and had my bank refuse the charge but I have decided that telling everyone I know in New Orleans never to eat there will be better. My friends who took me there were regulars until this incident. They too are in the restaurant industry and were floored by this owners response. I won't be surprised when this restaurant closes just like the many businesses that have occupied this space before them. The restaurant business is a hard one but it is only made harder by treating customers poorly.

Boy, where do I begin! When we arrived, it didn't look busy but were told it would be a 15 minute wait. As I scanned the restaurant, I noticed no less than 10 empty tables and thought to myself, why the wait? Over the next 10 minutes, I saw a few occupied tables clear out and bussed and yet we were still not seated. I finally said something to the hostess and was told they were understaffed and had to give the cooks time to catch-up. Pretty disappointing answer and you would think they would have told us that when we arrived. Minimally, maybe we would have been OK to have been seated and simply had a few drinks before we got our food, but they lost out on that opportunity. We were finally seated and our waiter came over pretty quick to take our drink order. I did order a drink from the bar, but sadly, that didn't arrive until AFTER I finished my meal. I even looked over at the bar a few times and they were by no means busy. Once I finally got my drink, our waiter apologized and said things got a little crazy and said it was on the house. Appreciate the free drink, but it was not crazy over there and I would have preferred to have my drink while I was eating. And while we are on the drink topic, none of us every got refills. That's likely because once our order was taken, we didn't see our waiter again until we had completed our meals. Unacceptable! As for the food itself, it was good. We started with chips and queso. The queso was good and had a little bite to it, but sadly you aren't given enough chips. We still had half a cup of queso left by the time we ran out of chips. I was going to ask our waiter if we could get more chips, but if you recall, we didn't see him again until our entire meal was done. My blue burger was tasty and my wife liked her hamburger (no bun as she is gluten-free) and my kids enjoyed their kids meals, which consisted of a cheese pizza and hamburger. My son wanted the peanut butter toffee cheesecake for dessert, which we originally said no to as we were just ready to leave, but since our waiter brought out my drink at the end of meal, I told him he could have it while I had my drink. That dessert was rich but delicious! Oh, and my wife ordered a side of ranch with her meal as she likes to dip her fries in ranch dressing. Guess what never came out? By the time we saw our waiter again, her fries were cold, but she did eventually get her ranch dressing. So overall, a very disappointing experience. While the food was OK, so many other things left such a bad taste in our mouth that it is unlikely we would return any time soon, if at all. Fortunately, there is another location at King of Prussia and I've been to that one several times for lunch, so maybe next time we'll make the trek there instead.
BAD experience with management. Not going again. Non-responsive to allergy issues. Poor customer service.

We went there for brunch today and even though it was a bit chilly in the shade the heaters provided over the outdoor seating did the trick for keeping us comfortable. The food was good, between the two of us we ordered the quiche and the pancakes with a breakfast pastries basket appetizer and turkey sausage and breakfast potatoes on the side. Both main dishes were delicious as was the breakfast pastries basket except that my brunch date is allergic to chocolate and one of the pastries had chocolate in it, perhaps it would've been helpful to ask if there were any food allergies before bringing any of the food out. The side dishes were ok, although I was a bit disappointed with the breakfast potatoes as they looked like they were at the bottom of the fryer (although everyone else's looked this way so I think this is just how they serve them) it wasn't quite what I was expecting when I thought breakfast potatoes so I just picked at them because they were a bit too greasy for me. Overall, not a bad place for brunch, the outdoor seating, or the seating near the windows, offers a nice variety of people watching.

I'm glad that this place is in our neighborhood--the owners are generous with donations for the area neighborhood associations, schools, etc. The food is delicious--as close as I'll get to Turkey anytime soon. It's a great change from the T-Ravs and such that are ubiquitous in St.Louis. My most recent visit; however, was odd and drove me to post a review. Upon arrival of our party of three (women, celebrating a birthday) the hostess asked if we had a reservation. We did not; having arrived at 7:45 or so the restaurant had about four parties seated on the patio and an equal amount seated inside (ie: relatively empty). The hostess seemed angry that we didn't have a reservation and said "it'll be ten minutes and you may wait in our bar area." As soon as we had ordered our drinks, the hostess asked that we settle our bill and we could be seated. It's all fine, but it seemed so obvious that they were trying to wheedle us for an extra drink and it was irritating. If the owner reads this, I hope you understand that these actions don't encourage me to buy more drinks or more anything. I left with the same bad taste as if I had gotten food poisoning there.

All I have to say is wow. I should have known with how bad the phone call went that this place was going to be awful. First I call and this is how the conversation goes "Pick up or delivery" "Pick up please" "Whats your name" "Amanda" "Hold on" * wait a few seconds "Ok, whats your name" "Amanda" "Hold on again" * waiting again "Sorry about that, okay whats your name" "Amanda..." "Pick up or delivery" "....pick up" "Ok what do you want" * place my order which comes with a salad so I ask "What kind of dressings do you have?" "Uh all kinds" So at this point I'm becoming very irritated with the way he's answering my questions "Ummmmm ok" "Oh... did you want me to read all of them to you?" (obviously being condescending) "Yeah actually I would" Seriously? I have to tell you my name 3 times then you get snippy with me for asking what kind of dressing you have? Didn't think I was asking you to move the earth or anything. So after he did that he tells me 25 minutes I show up about 40 minutes later and my order still isn't ready so I have to wait another ten minutes in the store where I barely got a hello because the girl and guy behind the counter are too busy watching seinfield. Once I get my order I get home and was disgusted. I got mozzarella stick and the sauce smelled and tasted like vomit. I order the manicotti which I always get from the location in Delaware and I couldn't even see the 3 manicotti in the dish. There was SO much sauce that the manicotti were literally swimming at the bottom. Not to mention the sauce was the consistency of water, so all of the filling inside the manicotti was mixed into the sauce because they were submerged in it. My order was 25 dollars and as soon as I took my first bite I threw absolutely everything in the trash. This meal was horrible. The pasta was extremely tough, the filling had spilled out, and there was so much sauce I could even see my pasta! I will absolutely never go back here. The service was awful and so was the food.

This is far from the tastiest, most creative, or most interesting place in West Philly. Don't bother going here for an intimate dinner with that epicurean vegan cutie you've been wooing. HOWEVER, sometimes you have a giant family event, like a rehearsal dinner or a graduation party, and all your raucous cousins from Cherry Hill are coming. And Aunt Lena is allergic to Ethiopian, and Uncle Steve doesn't trust the Japanese. Sometimes you just need a large restaurant with patience for big parties and a menu that pretty much everyone can find something on. Abbraccio is West Philly's iteration of that type of restaurant. Just go get your thai iced tea and sweet-potato fries *after* dinner, you crazy hipster.

Just went this past Friday. Our table ordered 3 agaves burritos , one was vegetarian. The waiter came with an agaves burrito, says "agaves burrito" and i said, is it vegetarian? and he said..."i think so??". So then he puts it down and tells us its vegetarian with the most uncertain tone. 5 minutes later after my friend took a bite, another waiter comes and says, "vegetarian agaves burrito?" Utterly dumbfounded.They take that burrito away and we are confused if the first one was even vege. Don't they know some people are highly allergic to shrimp/seafood? You think thats irresponsible? We finally get one non vegetarian agaves burrito after another 5 minutes. Then while I'm waiting for our last, another waiter came out with receipts trying to argue with me that our table only had 2 burritos. Really testing my patience there. I'm pretty sure I didn't come out to eat so I can have an argument about what I ordered and how they can't even keep track. Lo and behold as she is trying to prove her point repeatedly interrupting my table for 5 minutes telling us we didn't order another burrito, another waiter comes and says, "agaves burrito number 20?" ... which was for my table. So all in all, I can pretty much say it was the worst service I ever experienced. They couldn't even tell which burrito was vegetarian. Terrible Service, I didn't mind the line, or waiting for 30 minutes, but to wait 30 minutes and have them be so sloppy then accuse me of things. Not cool.

Always delicious!!! Vegan and gluten free options for those who have food restrictions and or preferences. They never disappoint. Dedicated fryer for those who love French fries but need to avoid the gluten cross contamination. Extra points for supporting 100% renewables!

I really hope that this was just a bad night. The night we went, our waiter had some type of an allergic reaction and had to be taken off in an ambulance. Because of this, all of her customers had to be taken over by another waitress. Since there was so much chaos due to the waitress being taken to the hospital (the waiters literally had a meeting in the middle of the floor) it took 30 minutes more to order our food after we had already been there an hour and a half. After we ordered our food it took about thirty minutes more to receive it and when we got it, it was cold and we had to send it back. It just left a bad taste in my mouth but I do believe that if I did try it again (which I'm hesitant to do) I probably would have a better experience because it could not get any worse. We did get 15% off of our meal but the almost 5 hour ordeal should have gotten us a free meal.

Mold. I had a migrane headache and bloodshot eyes for the entirety of my 5 night stay at the Marriott. Whenever I went out to lunch or left for a couple of hours, the symptoms would disapate, but then return immediately after coming back in. I had to explain that I had mold sensitivites (and was not on heavy drugs) to every professional contact I made at the conference. On the last night, I ended up going to the hospital because I was pretty sure something was really wrong since my vision was blurring and the room was spinning. NOPE- just a really unhygenic hotel. Everyone I knew from the conference was having some sort of allergic or cold-related symptoms, except for the few people staying in the newer of the two towers. Please don't let anyone elderly or imuno-compromised stay here. I'm young and generally healthy... and survived (though, still not back to 100%). I really wish I would have jumped ship and stayed at at another hotel right away.

So I'm a Buffett regular. I'm not naive as to their practices. Nor do I expect more than the $8-$10 experience I payed for. So I was completely ok to give this one a try regardless of multiple food poisoning complaints both online and in person from acquaintances. The hot selection was pretty lackluster and and even the Hibachi which I always love at every buffett was lacking. The Coconut Shrimp and Salt and Pepper crab legs were good enough along with the jello and bread pudding for dessert, until I used the bathroom. Everything went downhill from there. I watched one of the cooks take a piss and walk out without washing his hands. I was already throughly disgusted by that point. Somehow things got even worse then when we simply asked for change since we were splitting the bill and each only had large bills. Well they decided to pay the whole bill with our twenty. So after their desk staff being pretty rude we had to redo the transaction to finally get the correct task accomplished. There a few places that I will never ever visit again but this is one of them. Plus what is up with that cheap for sale jewelry display at the front? Just go across the street to Peking. They're a million times better.

For starters I have been here a total of 3 times so far.... I will go back for sure. My first visit was with a rambunctious group ready for some hibachi shenanigans and it was blast. The chef we were paired with was funny and entertaining. What I liked best was his ability to not contaminate my veggie style dinner with the rest of my friends meals. I was worried I would have to order off the menu and miss out on all the fun, but alas I did not. So on my next visit I wanted to try the sushi and made reservations for a Saturday, knowing from some others that it gets really busy on the weekends. I was seated in the side dining room, which I thought was more romantic and cozy. The sushi was very good and inventive too. My largest complaint of bad sushi most of the time is the temperature at which it is served. Mt. Fuji has it going on in the sushi department. Wonderful, fresh, and just the right temp. Too cold and the fish is not as tasty. So good I went back a third time for sushi and was satisfied all over again. They also had on Saturday a jazz ensemble (upright bass, piano, and singer) which I just loved. Jazz rules. So for a cozy date with some live music or a sake loving crowd ready for hibachi, Mt. Fuji will not disappoint.

Sometimes you end up getting dragged to douchebag central (apparently it's called channelside) and you decide a drink might help ease the pain. But not when the drink is disappointingly weak and icy (frozen water rather than alcohol or flavor). I almost threw up, not because of having too much to drink (very hard to do with drinks this weak), but from watching womanizing frat boy and fat slobs oogle and harass the female bartenders. And that the bartenders encouraged this as a way to drum up tips. I wonder how many drunk guys a night leave totally thinking they will return and get laid by one of the bartenders later that night, while she's already flirting it up with the next guy to sit down?

Food poisoning. The food is good but not worth the after effect. Sad day. I will no longer be eating at firebirds. It's a shame, I work at a near by business and unfortunately this experience has me steering others away from this place.

While visiting Nashville we decided to try The Wild Horse Saloon. Needless to say I was and still very disappointed with my experience. We went for dinner and had to pay a $6.00 cover charge because to was 7:00 pm. Then we had to wait for a table so we decided to have a drink that was way overpriced! When we finally got a table it took 20 minutes for the waitress to show up and she explained she was not aware that they had seated anyone else in her section since she was full. Once we got our menus we found they had a very limited menu and the prices again were extremely high. We went ahead and ordered because we were hungry and when the food arrived it was terrible. My daughter's got a meal for two which had fried cauliflower on it and it was so terrible that my one daughter almost threw up from the smell alone. Come to find out that it comes with some kind of Curry sauce, it was just horrible. I got a salad with chicken and the chicken was in huge hunks and it looked like it had been through a processor and then smashed back together. Needless to say I barely ate any and avoided the chicken. It was just a bad experience all the way around. Just another high priced tourist trap!

I have to say , first, the pizza my wife brought home wasn't bad, the quality of the sausage, very good, along with the gluten free crust. All that said, we went back today to try their Chicago beefs, and Italian sausage sandwich. We ordered ours the way Chicago makes them, or so we thought.... It's supposed to come with sweet peppers, and if you wish, hot jardinara.. The beef, Anjou , and the sausage, sweet peppers and hot. When my wife got her beef, it had cheese, bad sign, and no ajous.. Mine, they forgot the sweet peppers, and only gave me hot, not good. When I told the waitress that they had forgotten the sweet peppers, she went and got some, problem was, they were cold, there supposed to be warm..., totally ruined my experience, and my wives... We let the waitress know that a Chicago beef doesn't have cheese, she agreed, but hadn't realized that they had put cheese on the beef, bad again... Restaurants need to pay attention to detail, especially if they are advertising a food item a certain way, and the customer expects it that way, and no other way. If you can't make a dish, sandwich, or anything else the way it's supposed to be, then I personally won't be back. The bottom line is, you need to pay attention to quality, presentation, and not forget ingredients on the food ordered, else we go somewhere where they make it right.

The appetizer Sampler Plate is huge and everything on it tasted delicious. It fed four hungry people. My familyhad gyros and said they were good but not memorable. I'm a grape leaves aficionado and their's pass with flying colors. The hispanic woman who delivers the food to the table is super sweet, however the woman running the kitchen and take-out orders is a real b!&@&. She was yelling at the poor kitchen staff and was even curt with a customer who had food allergy questions. nothing is worst than witnessing poor treatment of restaurant workers who are trying to make an honest living. I would have given more stars if it weren't for that lady...hope she isn't The Greek Lady!!

I have mixed feelings about the Wildhorse Saloon. Very mixed feelings. On the one hand, it is a part of Nashville history--it's an enormous venue/bar/restaurant that is often host to some pretty decent musical acts. On the other hand, it's a goofy, line-dancing tourist trap packed to the brim with dorky white guys in cowboy hats, and that just ain't my style. As I mentioned, the Wildhorse actually hosts some pretty great shows from time to time. I mean, the Hives and Ringo Starr are booked to play there in the coming weeks, and, while neither of those acts exactly get me going (anymore), they're certainly a far cry from country and Western. However, more often than not, super country-fried bands play there. Anyhow, as is often the case with tourist spots, the food and drinks aren't exactly cheap, but most items taste good and the variety is pretty endless. It's actually a somewhat family-oriented place during the early evenings. If you're from out of town and really want the honky tonk experience, you can probably find a more authentic one within blocks of this establishment. If you want to go big, however, and you've always secretly dreamed of line-dancing in your souvenir spurs with dozens of Western-clad tourists, there's no better place in the city for you.

So I love this place I've been here twice but I have to say I came in got the beef and cheddar brisket it was amazing but 2 hours later I got food poisoning I was out for about 3 days so please just cook it better or wash your hands honestly idk what my food contained but it was a terrible experience

I want to give 4 stars because the food is great but the customer service is lacking. Some of the employees act like they honestly can't stand being there. I'd also suggest adding a Vegan boba option; maybe coconut milk or almond milk boba? I agree with the other Vegan comment, today the employee didn't make mention about the contamination of chicken and vegan meat until I was halfway through my bowl and I felt disgusted. Not cool

Never judge a book by its cover... I drive by this place daily, and it looks kind of hip, cozy with the outdoor fire pit and community tables. So, yesterday we decided to stop by for lunch around 3:30. The place was almost empty, the waitress was very nice, but the food... The wings, we ordered dry rubbed, could be called dry rubber, the sliders were so-so, but here is the part that upset us the most: the slider is $4.75, and they charge $3 extra to have it on gluten-free bun. The bun adds more than 60% to the cost! And the bun is tiny; I have shirts with bigger buttons than that bun. We can call it a smart business model, because they are tapping the trend, but it is simply a rip-off. As an afterthought, there are only two kinds of beer on tap, and it was almost room temperature. We will not be coming back... PS. Just noticed that other reviews mention their sticky floors... We noticed that too? What's up with that?

We will be relocating to the northeast Philly/Bucks County area in a few months - long story. Anyway being a foodie I have been searching for a good breakfast place in my soon to be new neighborhood - this is not the place. Went for breakfast Saturday morning. My omelet was overcooked and the filling tasteless. My husband had the roast pork sandwich - also tasteless. It also came on a sesame roll, and that might be good to note on the menu as some people have food allergies. Our waitress seemed to want to be there less than we did and disappeared for prolong periods. They have a wonderful outside dining area, but unfortunately they have no dining to accompany it. Maybe a good place for some wings and a beer and being as that is not our thing doubt we will be back. Think we will definitely be making at least monthly trips to the old hood for breakfast, etc

I'm a little disappointed to say that, although I appreciate supporting local businesses, I had such negative experience with the owner today. I brought my coffee to-go mug in the restaurant and when I sat down, she came up to me, pointed at my mug and said, "You have to put that away." She didn't greet me. She didn't welcome me. It was off-putting. I asked where I was supposed to put it away and she responded, "You should put it in your car." I didn't have a problem adhering to her request, I was just disappointed in how my brunch began. Then, when I stated I had a food allergy, I was informed that no exceptions would be made as the owner/cook misses them sometimes so I should just pick another dish. Again, I've had better experiences prior, but this day was not a positive experience. Some friends and I were meeting to share journaling we had began during the last time we were at Daughter's. I was looking forward to the brunch, but It was a disappointing experience, overall. We'll be meeting at a different locally-owned restaurant in the future.

Today I stopped in on my way to a doctor appointment at 9:30 am to grab a breakfast sandwich and medium ice tea. It was $5.50 for runny egg whites with cheese that made me vomit in my mouth. I couldn't stomach it! I think the eggs had gone bad. They charged me for an iced coffee. When I ordered a medium iced tea $3.50 for 10oz of unsweetened ice tea. That's a lot of some flavored water!! All in it was over $10 for food I couldn't eat. Next time I'll just wait for WaWa and save $7. The owner and her daughter were very pleasant but I don't feel that my stomach can take this!

I walked in and sat towards the back near the kitchen. 4 employees in the back cooking. Not 1 glove. Even watched one employee plate food with his bare hands. All 4 of them handling raw and cooked food cross contaminating with bare hands and no one washed hands. For obvious reasons I didn't stick around to try the food.

After being unable to find parking for 25 minutes we finally found a spot a few blocks away. So if you can walk or Uber here, definitely do so. The atmosphere was really cute and rustic, it looks like an old factory that they revamped with some kitschy decor. I liked the restaurant itself a lot. No one who I encountered in the staff was particularly nice though. Everyone seemed like they didn't have time for us. The food was okay. Nothing outstanding. We went for the brunch buffet and if you want eggs or an omelette good luck with that!! The line didn't go down the whole time we were there. You spend half of your time waiting in line for it to be cooked. Lastly it's pretty pricey...and then me and my friend both got food poisoning. So the whole experience, other than the atmosphere, was really disappointing. Most likely will not be back.

The watermelon water ice was awesome but the cookies and cream frozen yogurt was icey and lacked flavor. It also contained peanut butter and when I let them know, they just said it was next to the peanut flavor and did nothing to apologize or get us another frozen yogurt, even though I told them the child I was sharing with was allergic.

First, I have loved this place for a long time. But had lunch last week and did NOT have a good experience. Hostess was great, our waitress was excellent, the clam chowder was great, as usual, but my food gave me FOOD POISONING !! Ordered appetizer Steamed Clams, which came in a really large bowl. Only about 20% of the clams were fully open, 30% clamped firmly shut and the balance only open about 1/4 inch. I should have sent them back. Any idiot, or decent chef, should know if they don't open they are not in good shape. But being hungry (and they smelled fresh and tasted delicious) I persevered and pried many open with my large fork, not the dainty clam fork for easy retrieval. At least half of the serving was unfinished after wrestling them little guys out. Again, I know better. About 24 hours later, I started with headache, chills, made a dive under 2 blankets (was about 95 outside), experienced teeth chattering uncontrollably, then sweats, more sweats, and finally - you guessed it - diarrhea. A lot of diarrhea. I politely emailed their manager requesting a response but 3 days later I still have none. Sad.

Went in with a friend to take-out. We had a small dog with us and it took like 3 waiters to tell us the dog couldn't stay because the chef was allergic to dogs. (I would have been satisfied with them saying that dogs weren't allowed for health concerns or something... but whatever). The food we took out was really good, but the complete absence of people skills or knowledge on the part of the staff (one guy even used the "it's my first day" excuse), made the experience really frustrating and anticlimactic.

Went here late last year with a friend for an all-day-hangout type of thing and we decided to have breakfast here! I love the Berry Hill area; how can you not fall in love with it? We found the place easily enough and we went in on a day and time when it wasn't amazingly busy so we sat down right away. The people here were nice, the girl who was our waiter was super friendly and was from New Jersey (so we had to ask if she watched 'the Jersey Shore', which she didn't). I got some green tea, a glass of water, and their 5 grain wheat gluten free (?) pancake batter (or whatever it is) with a side of M&M's instead of the processed pancake batter that they had (I know there is a proper name for it but it escapes me at the moment). So, I don't really know what I was expecting, but I wasn't really that impressed with the way the pancakes tasted. I make pancakes all the time at home, so going out and paying someone about $5 for one bowl of pancake batter that would have cost me maybe $.50 from a box of pancakes was a bit of a stretch for me, but I wanted to give the place a try because my friend liked the place. I just didn't like the pancake batter. Granted, I haven't had that kind of pancake batter before, but it was so bland and tasteless besides the M&M's that even seemed to suffer because of the batter. The tea was tea, nothing special or spectacular about it, but it was a huge cup. I also got a side of their sausage; it was good. Overall, I left the restaurant full, but I was a little grumbly that spent $11 on a breakfast I could have made for a 1/4 of the price at home. I'd go back if someone asked me to go, but I wouldn't go for the pancakes; I'll stay at home and make my own pancakes thank you very much.

I wish I could give this restaurant a higher rating because the food is absolutely AMAZING, but my rating is tainted by my experience there today. My coworker and I ordered lunch for pickup. I ordered the beef pho and she got the vegetarian pho. I specifically asked the restaurant to label the containers of broth so that we would know which one is which--I don't want my coworker getting ill because she accidentally consumed meat products. I listed this request in the 'Special Instructions' section of the online ordering system, so the restaurant should've been notified of my request Unfortunately, the restaurant didn't follow my instructions and neglected to label the containers. Not a big deal, I figured I'd call. We have two containers of broth--one light, one dark--so it should've been easy for them to tell us which was which. When my coworker called the restaurant and asked "Which one is the vegetarian broth, light or dark?" their response was "Uuuhhh, light I guess?" Unfortunately, their answer didn't instill any confidence and she chose not to eat her pho, wasting her money. I'm really disappointed. I had built up Pho Barclay to be the best of the best (which it is, food-wise), but their customer service is VERY lacking. In a world full of food allergies and dietary restrictions, a customer shouldn't have to worry that their simple requests regarding food labeling won't be followed and their questions regarding their food could be answered with confidence. I will be returning to Pho Barclay because I love their food, but I will be very wary of bringing/ordering takeout for my vegetarian friends in the future.

So, I'm really badly allergic to dairy, not lactose intolerant, and I specified this when I ordered a burger there, and asked for no cheese. It was their last of this such burger in stock for the day. They put cheese on it and justified it saying "This order was too complicated." My partner and I ordered burgers that were supposed to have bacon on them, with a price tag to match the added ingredient, and there was no bacon. They did not offer me anything for my experience except my burger fixed- they didn't cover the cost of my meal. If this had been a peanut case, someone could've died.

As stated in other reviews delivery took forevor! I waited 1.5 hours then called to check on my order, they said they somehow missed the order and would get it out right away, I waited another hour. Gluten free crust was super soggy and toppings were very minimal. Stuffed grape leaves were not good either. The grape leaves weren't soft enough and the flavor was sub par. Waste of my money. I give them 2 stars for even having gluten free crust and the driver and whoever answered the phone were pleasant.

No one ever enjoys writing a bad review but I have to under these circumstances. On August 15th my girlfriend and I surprised her best Friend on the end of our vacation and spent time with her walking around Ybor. Toward the end of the night we got kind of hungry and decided to walk into Mama Rosa's. Worst decision of our lives. We purchased 5 slices and we split each of them. Today August 16th we have not left the bathrooms. All 3 of us have gotten food poisoning. My girlfriend and I have to catch a flight back home to NYC and we don't even know if we're going to be able to fly in the state that we are in right now. None of us cannot even function like human beings. We are sick to our stomachs. Now I unfortunately have had slight food poising before and ya you run to the bathroom and are usually back to normal after a few hours. Not this time! We have not stopped going to the bathroom each taking turns! Now I know this isn't pleasant to read and I am sorry. But I am only writing this review so no one else has to endure what we are going through. Honestly I don't know how this place is still open. We only got basic slices. One pepperoni, one veggie, one sausage and two ricotta and spinach. I've worked in the food/hospitality industry all my life and none of those items should cause any pain such as this. Unless they have come in contact with cross contamination. Again I hate writing these types of reviews. But please be cautious when eating here. I don't recommend it to my worst enemy. I hope this place gets there SHIT together because we certainly have. (Pun intended)

I definitely give high stars for the kindness of staffs here. I accidently vomit in the restaurant while having car sickness and hypoglycemia. The staffs are nice and patient to me，they also make me a hot honey lemon tea to take away and it helps a lot. Food looks nice but I didn't try much due to my situation.( ･･ )

We thought it would be real fun and real simple: pizza. On a tuesday night. And why not? Here's why not. Our pizza experience got marred by a pizzaman that made our outing absurd, frustrating, laughable, disastrously crappy. I'd give it 2.5 stars if I could. We weren't greeted for about ten minutes because our man was on the telephone taking orders with fervor. Once addressed (read: a cocaine induced confrontation) we were again abandoned for a phone. We were headed for the door to leave when from across the room he begged at us to stay & awkward it got (promises and reassurances of our good fortune, for tonight was our quote golden ticket unquote opportunity). Now, dear readers, imagine a dining experience dense with guilt, and unbridled, forbidden ambivalence. We mumbled something about having other (fake) plans elsewhere. He proceeded to pitch his specials with a cattle auction enthusiasm. We sat, defeated, found out the gluten free pie only came in medium (no good for our 3 person party), ordered 3 waters, then whispered in the barren silence. We went outside to openly consider what was happening to our pizza party hopes. Upon return, no waters, and a crowding dining room of phone orderers, all fiercely smirking. Pizza arrives! We ask for waters, we ask for parmesan (which is brought in little transient packets), and take the pie down. The pie was good but didn't warrant the preceding debacle. When we went to pay it was another ten minutes before the poor soul could calm down enough to ring us up. All in all one of the more awkward dining experiences we've had. Definitely a take out not dine in destination.

I can't help but cringe whenever someone suggests hibachi from Mt. Fuji. Not too long ago, I went with some friends. It was your average, run of the mill hibachi show (fun tricks, of course) and quite average hibachi food. The chicken and shrimp were pretty overcooked but still delicious dipped in the different sauces. I don't think it was worth the price at all. After a quite blah meal, I ended up having food poisoning all night! Definitely not the way I wanted to end my evening.

If your starving then you can order from here. But unless you starve don't eat here. I like the inside and it looks nice which is why there is a 2 stars but I got food poison 2 times so I am done with this place. It sucks so much
this place gives the worst food poisoning! avoid at all cost!

I was very excited to eat at a completely gluten free restaurant. It meant I could order almost anything and not have to worry if it was gluten free! But I also have a tapioca starch/flour allergy which often derails any excitement I have with eating at a new GF place Luckily they quickly went into the back and found out the only item they have on the menu that uses tapioca is their cheese rolls, everything else is safe! Most of their breads and rolls are rice based. I had the vegetarian hollandaise, which was on a GF biscuit. It had tomato and spinach with a poached egg on top. My only complaint was the egg wasn't really very warm when I got it. But the flavor was great. The biscuit itself was very gluten free, as in it was crumbly. Together with everything else it was very tasty. But if you ate a lot of it on it's own, it dried out mouth a bit. I also got the potatoes, which were roasted in the oven and very tasty. My husband got a vegetarian omelet and grits, but he was still hungry. He said it was tasty just wasn't enough to fill him up. From my personal experience, I liked it. I'll be sure to come and visit again next time I'm in the area.

If I could give this particular location a 0 out of 5 stars, I would. My Father and myself are on a 18-wheeler almost 24/7/365, minus when we are at either our home or a friend/family's home. I would say it's months between when we have what most would see as a 'home cooked meal', due to how expensive truck stop restaurants are, and a lot of actual restaurants don't allow, or have room, for semi (18-wheeler) parking, so obviously, we are fairly often shoppers at Walmart and Sam's Club. As I said, it's rare we eat in a sit down restaurant, so today, my Father decided, he wanted Denny's, and wanted it to go. I even called this particular Denny's before we pulled into the parking lot, to see if it was possible to use our own to go dishes we had gotten extra from another Denny's. At first the lady I spoke to said yes, so I came inside to make the order. Once at the counter, after waiting roughly 10 minutes to even see a employee in there, someone finally asked what I needed. I told her, and she seemed hesitant about putting the food in the containers, but agreed. About a hour later, another woman came out and said her boss said the containers were 'dirty' and could not be used due to 'cross contamination'. I would've understood if they had said that because they were outside containers, technically, they couldn't use them, but saying the containers were dirty was uncalled for. The way the inside of Denny's was, now that was dirty. I'm overlooking the snow, but their attitudes need a very good cleaning. So for anyone thinking of coming here? Avoid this place like the plague. Only thing going good for them is their wifi, and Flying J has plenty of that to use.
Me and several friends got food poisoning after eating here. I do not recommend eating here. I'm currently laying in bed experiencing a lot of pain.

I ended up here on St Patrick's Day. I got a steak bowl with all the fixings and a beer. Next morning I get food poisoning. I would also like to clarify I had only one beer and that's all I ate that day. I thought this place might be better than Chipotle but now I will never eat here again. I wish I could sew them for how much pain their food caused me.

They serve burnt black fajitas. Some staff have rude and have bad attitude. I did not liked the service. When complaint about the burnt fajitas the staffs says it is instructions received by their corporate. Cannot believe who will like burnt fajitas. It has no nutritional value and it absolutely unhealthy. May even cause food poisoning eating these burnt-charcoal fajitas.
This place is gross! The one time I did go I got food poisoning! Don't think I will ever try the food there again. I'll stick to other places

horrible horrible customer service- we had used sweet eats a few time and even though the last time we ordered a chocolate chip cake that came without chocolate chips i decided to order my nephews birthday cake from them and give them another shot- so last august i order a sheet cake with a dinasour theme-when i picked it up the cake looked like someone threw up on it- so i said to the girl working there "this doesn't look nice - does it?" so she said she would get someone to talk to- this person comes out of the back and decides to tell me that my not liking the cake is my personal opinion---to which i responded "too bad my personal opinion is paying for the cake-i winded up being throw out of their dirty bakery which i will boycott forever- i actually just booked a party at a restuarnat which told me they get their cakes from sweet eats- i said nevermind i'll bring my own cake---lol

We frequent their biz quite often for work. The toppings are fresh, but the specialty options are al too similar. I also think the size could be a little larger for the price. Pluses: gluten-free, prompt delivery. Minuses: the taste is pretty blah.

My boyfriend and I have always been huge fans of this place. The food is incredible! Just make sure you get the right waitress.... We are both gluten/dairy free, and live that they have options to pick and choose so that it best fits our dietary restrictions. Yesterday, my boyfriend became very, very sick because the waitress did not listen to his specific order. I love this place, and I understand that not everyone understands every food allergy or restriction...just warning future patrons to be VERY CLEAR WHEN ORDERING. I don't think we will be back for a long time...

Service: mediocre at best. Our waitress kept rushing us to order food even though we told her several times we were still waiting for a friend. She was terrible at taking extra plates away and fluctuated between not filling our drinks at all and suddenly giving 2 full drinks per person. Towards the latter half of our meal, we had way too many empty plates and unfinished drinks cluttering our table. I know cheap asian places are never known for their service but it would've been awesome to see her crack a smile so it didn't seem as if our very presence was a burden upon her soul. Quality and taste: The Arizona roll was my favorite and the yellow tail roll seemed fairly fresh. It's nothing compared to the nice sushi restaurants in California or Japan but it's okay for Tucson. Don't expect anything too authentic and you can most likely make tastier rolls yourself by getting some nice cuts of fish at AJ's. Portion size: Quite small in my opinion and I'm a ~90lbs Asian girl. I had to order so many rolls to fill up that it would've been cheaper to go with the all-you-can-eat option. However, the buffet option is far more limited in terms of choice so choose wisely if you're going to eat here. Over all, I would've given it 2-3 stars had it not been for the terrible food poisoning I received afterwards. In fact, the whole party got diarrhea within a few hours of eating there. I was especially luck to receive nausea and vomiting alongside the diarrhea. This is the my first time getting food poisoning from a sushi restaurant and my first time giving a business 1 star. I will not be coming here again and I am going to report this. If anyone else got sick from here, I hope you will report it as well. If you care for your health, go eat elsewhere especially if you like raw fish. Eating sushi that isn't prepared correctly is absolutely dangerous and ill-advised. tl;dr: if you're accustomed to eating good sushi, you won't like this place very much. If your favorite roll is the California roll and you're willing to risk food poisoning, this place is decent. If you must eat here as you are absolutely starving, make sure you order fully cooked rolls to help prevent food poisoning. The Mt. Fuji roll is bland so I would advise getting a different cooked roll.

I'm not really into all the raving reviews here. For as fancy and classy as this place is supposed to be the bar was average and lacking a variety of choice. As we were seated I kindof had the feeling i was sitting on a terrace outside, but to me it was just a few tables thrown in a brick room with some table clothes to make it try to appear fancy, the chairs are uncomfortable. The only reason I am giving them three stars is because of this: The four course appetizer sampler is just simply to die for. The lobster turnover was fantastic, the crab cake the least of the favorites. The salad kindof tasted like they went outside and picked the spinach, it was very earthy tasting. I ordered the lamb, ($32) while the chop was fantastic, i was not a fan of the shoulder and other part, i seriously almost threw up in my mouth, i gagged twice, it tasted like a garbage can, i wouldn't necessarily call it gamey, but OMG it was horrible. The beets were good, but I was not a fan of the beet risotto either. I did not stay for dessert, for the prices were just not worth it. I would come again for the appetizer but not anything else. My hubby had the duck which was just okay, it did come on a nice green plating and looked good, tasted okay. This place is good for a date night if you want to show her your made of dough, but it is not intimate whatsoever, they do not have booths, just tables and the fruit flies were annoying. I really wouldn't recommend this place for much.

This is the second worst restaurant I have been to in Tucson. The minute I walked in the door I could smell a combo of old fish and dirty grease, disgusting. If i would have been on my own I would of walked out but instead I stayed to endure the worst sushi I have ever had in my life. The tempura roll was fried in old grease, that stuff needs to be changed every now and again. Even the edemame was bad, totally over cooked. The sashimi almost made me vomit, it was mushy and not fresh, ewww, I am grossed out just thinking about that place!

I work in Clayton, and it was our Intern's last day on the job and we wanted to take her out to lunch.. (We only get one hour for our lunch break). It honestly looked like we were bothering the wait staff to acknowledge us. We were seated nearly immediately during the Clayton lunch rush on a Thursday, but once seated, it was like all of the servers wouldn't even make eye contact. After waiting 15 minutes or more, my coworker flagged down someone who looked like a manager and we were served quickly. The problem seemed to be 3 servers not knowing who is covering our particular table. My coworker requires Gluten Free, so this place has limited options for her. And the pizza was blah....over hyped and over priced. But you can get away with this in Clayton, right?! I will not be returning if I can help it.

Maggiano's is great for food allergies! We have multiple food allergies in the family and recently took a trip to Indy. My husband and I took the kids to lunch at Maggiano's, because let's face it. Mom can't cook every single meal all the freakin' time. Well, I can. But it sure is nice to take a break. The chef here is so awesome - he'll come out to discuss the menu with you if you mention you have food allergies, and they are aware of shared facilities and shared lines and cross contamination. Kudos to Mike - you made a tired mama happy.

We had an hard time getting seated together since we were a party of 14. Eventually we were seated scattered in different booths but that was okay. Buffet are not usually good however this time I gorged on crab legs and some oysters. I stopped eating the oysters after two tries. Good thing I don't have any seafood allergies! I finished up with 2 slices of prime rib and ice cream for dessert. The first slice of prime rib was edible, medium rare slightly slathered in horseradish. however the second slice was an inch thick. The butcher gave me the whole end of the prime rib. It was difficult to eat such a thick slab. I tried their cheese cake but couldn't finish it because it tasted old. Buffets are not my thing but this one was pretty good compared to the ones I eaten before.

pretty much the only place I can eat in Trolley. make your own decisions about cross-contamination issues, but if you get a salad or a burrito bowl, you can eat almost everything here sans gluten. the employees here are just spectacularly nice and are happy to change gloves without making you feel like a jerk - definitely allergy friendly, willing to explain what's in everything. I am especially a fan of the steak and short ribs, black beans, corn salsa (omg), marinated onions, salsa verde... holy crap, it's all really good. portions are huge and everything is fresh; some stuff is locally sourced (mushrooms for example). restaurant quality taste with takeout velocity. el diablo is mi amigo for sure.

We called earlier in the day to advise my girlfriend was gluten intolerant and could Kemoll's provide gluten-free dinner choices. The response was "Yes, we have many gluten-free menu items to choose from." Upon arrival were led to a back room with six tables and seated at a table that was directly next to a arge dehumidifier blowing noisily at full speed. We asked the waitress about the gluten-free menu choices and she responded "We really don't have that many gluten-free items on the menu." The waitress then dashed off saying she would be right back to take our drink order. She returned to seat people at other tables next to us and walked right by us as she left the dining area. No drink order. She then returned to serve a dish to folks at another table and once again walked right by us leaving, again no drink order. Then the third time she arrived back at our table where my date ordered a Hendricks and tonic with a cucumber. The waitress advised there were not any cucumbers in the restaurant, at all. As we enjoyed our cocktails I hailed the waitress over and ordered an appetizer. When the waitress returned with the appetizer the only plate I had in front of me was the charger plate, no dinner plate. I dished out a portion of the appetizer onto the charger plate. Classy I know, but it gets better. My date ordered the salmon with a side dish of asparagus and I ordered a house salad and a strip steak, medium rare. When the waitress returned with my salad she places it right on top of the appetizer mess left on my charger plate. Never have I seen this done in any restaurant, ever. I then cut into my steak and, well, it was rare, not medium rare but very rare. Plus is was cold and full of gristle. I had but a couple of bites and took the rest back home to the dogs. While the salmon was fine it was very obvious the asparagus came from a can. No doubt, at all. Now for the good one. For dessert I ordered their allegedly famous, made table side Banana's Foster. She takes my order and returns minutes later with, are you ready for this? "We don't have any bananas." I kid you not. No cucumbers, no fresh asparagus and no bananas. Give me a break. Thus was my dining experience at Kemoll's Fine Dining Restaurant. I will never, ever return to this place. Ever!

The staff was decent. Friendly but they are terrible wait staff. They talk about their customers and will have you waiting FOREVER to get anything. Many people will visit the table but nobody remembers what you just asked them for. You will be waiting forever to have someone refill water. Then the owner and staff will suck up to all the big tables because they think they will get a bigger tip. But trust and believe they won't even come to your table to see if you are enjoying your time. Food was alright but never again. Oo plus I got food poisoning.

I ate here last night and am currently experiencing what I think is food poisoning. I ate the salad around 7:00, woke up at 1:00am vomiting and having bowel movements. Today I felt nauseous, vomited, diarrhea again, and general dry mouth and not feeling well. I thought the grilled chicken I asked for maybe tasted a little off. It had to be from Saladworks because I felt fine when I went to bed and woke up feeling horrendous. I don't know what to do

Taffets is amazing and I was so lucky to have it so close to me! As a celiac, it's so wonderful to have a dedicated gluten free bakery where I don't have to worry about cross contamination. The everything bagels are legit and the carrot cake is scrumptious!

I've heard so many great things about this place! The food tasted so rich- so yummy! However; we ended up with food poisoning and the service was not that great. Everyone was really nice each time we had to leave the table to catch someone's attention. I would give it another try as a tag-a-long, but definitely wouldn't go out of my way.

We met some friends from out of town and had dinner together on an early Friday evening. The reason this restaurant was chosen is because someone in our dining party is sensitive to gluten and they frequent Pei Wei back home because of their gluten-free menu items. My husband and I had never been here before, so we were excited to try it. They have a couple of soups to choose from, a selection of standard Asian style appetizers (crab rangoon, spring rolls, edamame) and a nice variety of entrees that you can have made to your liking by adding the protein of your choice, including tofu. You can also choose brown or white rice. Because this is a standard, Americanised menu, everything is pretty much middle of the road and predictable. This is totally awesome if you are with a large group with many varied tastes, not so much if you are an adventurous eater like I am. The place was clean, restrooms were clean, service was friendly, the staff seemed to be very accomodating. We arrived early and by the time our guests finally made it to join us, the place was filling up quickly, which speaks to their mass appeal. I would certainly go back if someone wanted to dine here, but it would never be my first choice of places to go - there are too many wonderful independent eateries around town.

I went here with great expectations as I had heard great things about it from friends and family. We went for lunch on a Friday and we felt that the service was average at best. The entire staff seemed preoccupied with being too cool to work. Our meals came out wrong, mine being a gluten free burger served on lettuce. The server delivered it incorrect and when I told her that it was not Ina lettuce wrap she said that she could just pull the bun off and use the lettuce in the sandwich to wrap it. That is apparently what she did because when it was brought back there was little specs of bread on the lettuce. I won't die from gluten exposure but it seemed more like an inconvenience than a concern for her. The shrimp was really good but a bit pricy as was all of the menu. Not sure if we will be back....

I've gotten take-out here twice, and while the tacos are cheap and the meat has decent flavor, I found a pretty large bone in my carne asada tacos this time around. More importantly they forgot 50% of the taco ingredients... it came with only corn tortillas and steak, but they forgot the onions and cilantro! For a taco with only 4 ingredients, having two of them forgotten was a real bummer. I would suggest taking a peak at the individually wrapped tacos before leaving just to make sure. Also, the horchata recipe they use does have milk in it. It is delicious, but since a lot of horchata does not have milk in it, it's a good thing to note for all the lactose intolerant folks out there!

First of the service was horrible. Our waitress was very rude to us. The bread basket was rotten and disgusting. We all ordered soup prior to our main course and they were all luke warm. My son ordered the Cajun chicken, in turn he got food poisoning that night. Never go here. It is probably the worst place I've ever been to.

I was much more a fan of this restraunt before I found I was a Celiac, their alphredo sauce was amazing and breadsticks to die for, pasta alphredo with a grilled chicken breast was my absolute favorite. Now there is a gluten free menu, just ask for it before you are seated, they have a couple alergy exclusive dishes available. I do enjoy this restraunt, not just for the food, but the atmosphere and Italian cream sodas, which are wonderful. The gluten free menu has about 5-6 items on it, only one is made specially with a rice pasta, which was alright, but not my favorite, I suppose I just miss the food I enjoyed from there, the steak and chicken ka-bob(s) were pretty good, the steak was the best part, a savory taste of rosemary and a light pinch of garlic salt, I believe, mouth just started to water. So I would recommend this place for a nice evening out and for some somewhat Americanized-Italian food but still not an easy place for Celiacs and those of gluten-intolerance who would like more choices. Still, clean, great service and the servers assist you in any way possible.

I was far away from home in New Orleans, pulling license plates off my totaled car after having dealt with a food-poisoned boyfriend from 4-10 AM when I left for work, so generally having a crap day, figured I'd get us some pho while I was in New Orleans East. There are no vegetarian or pescatarian soups, my only option as a non-meat eater was a grilled shrimp bun. Kind of bummed me out, but whatever, as long as there's something I can eat. Ordered that and a brisket pho for Sir Pukes-a-Lot. Minimal atmosphere and all that in the actual restaurant, but you're getting Vietnamese in the East for the food itself, not for the decor. The manager ran my food over to me when it was ready, as I had taken a seat at a table, I said thanks and left, drove 30 minutes back to NOLA, and goddammit, my food wasn't in the bag. I hadn't eaten since the day prior, as I left my own job early and without shift meal to pull my plates off my car before the lot closed. I was somewhat irate, so I called the business in hopes that they would rectify it in some way, as it's frustrating to hand someone $10 to NOT give me the food I ordered. The only thing they offered in response to their error was that they would "remember me" when I came in next. I explained that I lived 30 minutes away and have NO REASON to be in New Orleans East, not to mention that I'm car-less for the moment being. I'm not going to drive an HOUR within the next week or so to get stupid bun. I asked them to send me something in the mail that I could present the next time I was over there, as I anticipated it being within like, six months, but not soon enough where they would "remember" me. I have a dumb facial piercing, but I don't have a tattoo of an orca whale on my forehead or anything. I certainly wouldn't remember me. I asked to speak to a manager and was denied that? Really shoddy customer service after having acknowledged that "the manager forgot to run [me] the rest of the food." In retrospect, I should have asked them to write down my name and I could present an ID upon my next visit, but I doubt they would have cooperated with this idea either. Boyfriend said pho was "okay."

Loved the vegetable of the day (heirloom tomatoes and shaved fennel), the fried asparagus, and the Vault and BCS salads. The BOG cocktail was perfect. The flank steak was not good. It was tough. I had been told good things about Idaho beef, so this was disappointing. What was worse though was the food poisoning. The night after our meal at fork, I woke up in the middle of the night urgently heaving. Unfortunately for me I'm not a puker, so nothing came out. It didn't take long for my body to decide that everything should come out the other end. I've spent the last day and a half visiting the toilet every hour, in a daze, shaking. I took a massive dose of Pepto and Advil so that I could make it to the airport and check in. Apparently this is not unusual. Of the two people I've mentioned this to, one of them had a friend who got sick from Fork's burger. I wish I had known.

One word: disappointing Traveled to Fish&co for Restaurant Week. Let's start with a positive: they have complimentary valet service. Let's start with the only other positive: the hostess was friendly and, while this has no bearing on anything else, she was attractive. Ok, done with the positives. The ambience and the building itself are stuffy, bland, and I cannot really describe the feeling that the restaurant was trying to portray because I simply did not enjoy the atmosphere in the least. Our server was kind enough to go and get the chef to address wife's Celiac disease (which is always a nice extra step); however, our server had a certain air of pomp and condescension that was unnecessary. Look, I get it. You think this place is some sophisticated 5-star hubbub. Quite simply put, it isn't. So, please remove that stick up your rear-end. We all ordered from the Restaurant Week 3-course pre-selected menu. I ordered the Flounder with Winter Succotash, started with the Baked Oyster Sampler, and finished with the apple tart. The Flounder was extremely bland alone. It had no taste. As Chef Ramsey always says on that TV show, "did you taste that... you, donkey?!?!?" The succotash made the meal edible when combined with the flaky unseasoned boring flounder. My sampler oyster platter to start was ok. The oyster rockafella were the best, but the oysters with garlic and hot sauce were completely unappealing - I could see the tabasco but couldn't taste it. How does one fail at tabasco? The apple tart was cold and the tart was not terribly flaky. All and all, I don't think that this restaurant is worth the Restaurant Week $30.11 (what gives, why not $20.11?) nor would it be worth the regular menu price average of $27+ per entree. My advice is to steer clear.

Food was subpar. I wasn't blown away by the black bean burger, fries or shake. The real problem is, I'm pretty sure that I got food poisoning after eating the food. Can't guarantee it, but I felt sick soon after eating it. I definitely won't be going back, because I'm not sure if I will get sick or not.

If you have any food allergies run away from this place! I went in with my two kids that are six and seven years old and the lady didn't not want to look up ingredient listing when requested. She kept pushing sorbet saying "it should be fine." However, when you have a food allergy you need to know the ingredients to ensure that your children are not going to have a problem. Then she squatted down behind the register looking into a book and said "I'm sorry you cannot eat anything. Everything has soy and dairy." When we were at the ice cream store we never said that Dairy was an allergy. She obviously was not interested in getting a sale and a potential new customer. We are leaving and heading to Culver's down the street. THEY actually care about customers and go out of their way to make sure you avoid your allergies when you're eating.

We are new to Dunedin from the west coast. We really enjoy sushi. I have a wicked garlic allergy & informed the waitress of this. At first, she appeared attentive, took our order, checked in with the chef & came back to us to "tweak" the dishes slightly, Surf & Turf and The Volcano. We ordered them both garlic-free & with brown rice. After eating our seaweed salads, we waited quite a long time for our meals....at least 30 minutes!! When they came, they were made with white rice. When I told the waitress that we waited quite some time & both dishes were not made with brown rice, she nonchalantly said, "sorry, that's my fault." She didn't appear sincere at all. We said we did not want them & asked for the check to pay for the salads. She simply said, "ok!" I have NEVER been treated with such an attitude, nor would I treat my customers in such a way. I waitressed while in college & I would have been sincerely apologetic & brought out the manager to discuss how Pisces could make the wrong right.....perhaps, comp a meal or offer a gift card for a second chance to get it right. We certainly did not want to wait another 30 minutes for them to be remade. We eat sushi every week to 10 days. You just lost 2 loyal customers.

Tonight was their "coffee after dark" special. Every second weekend of the month, they along with other restaurants, do something out of the ordinary for the community. They want to lure more people back in the area to generate more revenue for their town. The first time they tried "coffee cocktails and desserts," it was a disaster through no fault of theirs. We had a blizzard so they had very few people. This is their second time and we'll, they still need to work out some issues. Our seats were on the side of the counter by the coffee beans' grinder. A lovely young lady took out order and shortly thereafter have us our choices beverages. I chose Nastrino Latte. It is a latte where I choose hazelnut, espresso, blue ribbon laced into their foam art Hubby preferred his dessert Affagato. That consists of a scoop of vanilla ice cream with Costa Rica and Ethiopian espresso. They took the espresso and poured it over the ice cream. Finally The Kid ordered El Diablo. It gives you Satan's blood, double Dutch cocoa, espresso of course, cinnamon, heavy cream and whole milk. If you're lactose intolerant, I don't recommend this drink. The Kid Knew it was going to have hot sauce in their beverage. While most did not care for this drink , the kid loved it. I ordered the Nastrino Latte. Mine contains Hazelnut, espresso and their foam looked exactly was mine. The beverage also had a got pepper to help stir your coffee. Everything was fine but we waited over 15 minutes to be acknowledged for the check. We flagged sudden our waitress who promised another waitress will give us out tab. We waited and that still didn't happen so we went up to the counter again. After she have us the check, we waited another five minutes wondering if she forgot about us. That's there only fault I would say they have. Because it's their "open for after dark hands crafted coffee cocktails", they have to continue working out the links. I would also recommend for the waitresses to make mention of the coffee ingredients, expressly the Satan's blood. Their coffee and ambiance is good so yes, I would like to try them again.

Eating sushi can help you lose weight, ESPECIALLY when you eat at Sushi Garden!! If you're interested in weight loss, order the spicy tuna! I did, and the the next three days I threw up and had diarrhea which caused me to lose significant poundage!! The only thing I ate that was different than my date was the spicy tuna, and I was the only one who got sick. I also ran into a friend of mine on the way out. I told him about the food poisoning after I'd recovered and he said he had gotten sick too! And he also had the spicy tuna!! Apparently they get their spicy tuna from a package and don't make it fresh, like they do with the spicy salmon, which is the reason the consistency between the two is different. And though the Sushi Garden Diet is painful and makes you miserable, it's definitely cheaper than most other diet products and services. Though next time I may just go ahead and lick raw chicken...that's even cheaper, and not quite as gross.

Complicated review here. Just the two of us this go around. Philly was sweltering, much more humid than the west coast. We had reservations and were seated quickly. Place was empty, maybe 5 tables taken. Upon our seating, our very nice server sold us on the 6 course Pre Fix. Neither of us had much of an idea of what to order or expect. We have had poor experiences with Indian Food in the past, however we wanted to try at a higher level of eatery before we closed the doors forever to eating this type of food. I think the quality of the ingredients, the staff, the portions, the ambiance was top notch. The other person joining me loved the meal. But for a few exceptions, Please understand, I realize there is a difference between a quality meal which this was, and me just hating the tastes. I'll list the courses. And my ending of this challenging meal. Started with some sort of cold soup. - to me it was ok. The other person said it tasted like vomit. Fried Spinach Salad - Fantastic texture and taste! Simply marvelous, Both of us loved it. Seared Scallops,- Over cooked by a hair, not seared properly. Very sweet Sauce inedible. The other person liked it. Here take mine. Lolly POP of a Lamb Rib with a Small Chicken Breast. - To me inedible, tangy and very spicy. Chicken was in a spicy Coconut Chutney. The other person loved it, I hated it. The Naan Bread which came with it sucked. Pork Shank with a roasted Potato. To me inedible. Other person enjoyed it. Dessert was Fig Ice Cream Drizzled with Honey. I hated it, Inedible, Too sweet. The other person enjoyed it. I think this type of food is not for everyone. I gave it an honest shot.Never again will I eat Indian Food I did not enjoy it from start to finish. I didn't eat anything but for the one fantastic salad course. I think evaluating the experience honestly is to say, if you like Indian Food, you probably will very much enjoy this place. However I won't be joining you. I rather eat my own throw up

Total bummer. My gluten free Pomodoro pasta had an un-firm, over cooked texture (which sometimes can happen with GF noodles) but the worst part was the sauce was WAY TOO SALTY. I ate about 1/3 and brought the rest home to toss with additional noodles and fresh tomato for lunch tomorrow to try to salvage some of it. My oldest son got the clam sauce which was way too garlicky -- that's all you could taste/smell. My other son got the salmon which he said was okay. My husband got the summer zucchini lasagne which was rich and overpowered by the pesto on top, which would be fine if they advertised it as a pesto dish. It was not at all light, fresh and summery. The side of potatoes and side of brussel sprouts were the highlight. For a $150 weeknight family meal, I was very disappointed. It would be hard for me to go back again. I hate posting such a negative review!

Food poisoning during a weekend trip to the Santa Barbara area. We got in just before closing and ordered a calzone, salad, tortilla soup, and a halibut burger. Worst decision of the weekend ever. Yes, that did ruin our little getaway and yes I am still a wee bit bitter. P.S. If you do decide to go here, please be aware that there is a menu off to the side of the ordering stand on a side table that has more mundane (read: hopefully safer) options than those available on the short list chalked up.

Welp, I discovered the secret ingredient to the secret sauce everyone keeps talking about. It's FOOD POISONING!!!!!! ***ding ding ding! bells! whistles! alarms!*** What do I win for figuring it out?? One full miserable day of heaving and hoeing while being curled up on the bathroom floor for hours, complimentary of the chef! Aw shucks guys, you shouldn't have. Really, I shouldn't have and I never will again - eat here that is. I should have known after eating a meal where __everything__ tasted like fishy mustard that consequences would be had. At least aside from feeling explodingly crappy, I've never looked better from the waist down!

If you want food poisoning, this taco truck is the place, what a disgrace,there mexican and they don't know how to make a burrito, unless they did it on purpose. Knowing that I need to grab a quick bite and be on my way, without checking what is inside the burrito. I got to my destination and decided to eat it, what was inside the burrito was, nothing but beans and three bite of meat, I know a burrito comes with your choice of meat, bean rice, onion, cilantro, cheese and sour cream. How can you be Mexican that own a taco truck and don't know how to make it right? Well they did that on purpose, I believe they are racist against certain nationality. I WILL NOT GO BACK EVER!! plus they don't have jalapeno WOW! RIDICULOUS!!! AVOID THIS PLACE AT ALL COST

i don't think i could live without their breakfast burrito (the barking dog) It is so good. I'm not a big fan of sweet stuff in the morning but their french toast with bananas or pancakes with fruit stuff OR even whatever they are having as a special is always good. I have also loved their salmon burger and pistachio encrusted salmon entree, very very delicious. I love the the decor in the south Philly one but the one in fairmount is also very charming. I always feel like I'm sitting at someones home in the south Philly spot. Good coffee good food. I've never had a bad time or meal at either location. There was the one time on new years day that a girl threw up as she was walking by my booth on her way to the bathroom but i can't really fault Sabrina's for that. LOVE IT LOVE IT! I haven't found a place I'd rather eat brunch. The wait is tough (up to 1hr) and sometimes the people working the crowd gets grumpy but i still go back all the time!

I went here after a shower at the fox theater with a friend to get a quick dinner. I will say the chefs and saff are efficient and the food tastes halfway decent. The food is cheap, however I don't think they really put much work into making the food. I don't think I will ever come back though. They used WAY to much butter, not enough seasoning, and not to mention their food gave me horrible food poisoning the next day. My firends and I might have gone on an off day, but ALL OF US got horrible food poisoning. No restaurant should call themselves the best if their food makes people sick, to the point of vomiting. I will not come back until they clean their act along with the actual restaurant. It feels more like a school cafeteria than anything. I would never recommend this place until they fix their problems.

Really fun atmosphere for brunch and great service They had a Bloody Mary bar and good music playing. The veggie omelette was ok and was huge. It easily could be shared by 2 people. The eggs were a little burnt but the potatoes were really good. My cousin loved her side salad with the eggs. We also got a side of bacon, which was pretty good. Overall, there weren't many gluten free options here - so I got an omelette.
Can't believe you would discontinue gluten free!! Pizza is always great but... So many ppl that have gluten issues.

NOT FOR PEOPLE WITH SEVERE ALLERGIES. Management confirmed that "the kitchen is small and we can't be sure there will not be cross contamination." 1 of our party was unwilling to eat and settled for a coffee. She was charged full price for a refill. They didn't have my first selection. I was happy with my second selection. Potatoes, toast and sausages were very good and the eggs were marginally overcooked. Wait staff was not very friendly and gave the allergic member of our party the feeling that she 'could eat or not but it was her problem if she ended up with a reaction'. The food was good but the wait staff was barely adequate. Because of the allergy problem, we will not be back. There are a lot of restaurants in this city that will ensure that your meal will not be contaminated as well as provide good food and service.

I have celiac disease and I asked the waiter if they had a special menu, he said they didn't but he could alternate and take things out for me.. the menu was so small and if he alternated things there would be nothing on the plate. So we left . They honestly have 5 items on the dinner menu .

Chose this restaurant for a Sunday family lunch . Menu was varied enough for all members of our party. Service was fine even though we learned this was only our server's second day. The food was mediocre at best. I ordered the grilled chicken over salad greens from the gluten free menu. The chicken was fine but the greens were anything but fresh. My nephew's burger had an off taste which he described as game-y. My sister was told that the quesadillas could be made with corn tortillas but they came out in flour ones. The place is fairly noisy. We won't be returning.

Food was great. Not much explanation of options - pictures of food. Staff was disengaged-playing on phone, watching video, taking to others and THE BATHROOM smelled like hell - utmost threw up! But the food was so good and I want to try breakfast- I'd go back.

A Restaurant Week Review: First thing I thought when I walked into Supper... "Cool." The decor was very unique and suave. I don't think anyone would disagree on that. I couldn't stop looking around the place at all the awesome decor. Make sure to take a good look at the way cool "recycled" chandelier near the front door. Unfortunately the atmosphere was the more memorable part of the evening. Though rich in flavor, the food left a bit to be desired... I started off with the Black Truffle Deviled Eggs. I was so disappointed! The flavor was just blah and boring; too much mustard. They also tasted like they were made yesterday. Had that sitting-out-for-a-while texture. I really think this was due to the "high demands" of restaurant week and the eggs were made in bulk at some point and refrigerated. But still. Then I tried my dinner mates Housemade Soft Pretzels with green chile-and-beer fondue. The pretzels were yummy. But the sauce just tasted like plain ol' nacho cheese. Guess I just expected too much... For the "small plate" I ordered the Smoked Butternut Squash Soup with cinnamon marshmallow, apples and sage. YUM. After the 1st course I was kind of nervous for this one. But I certainly was pleasantly pleased with what came to me! Not only was the presentation awesome, the flavors and textures all worked so well together. Make sure to get the cinnamon marshmallow goodness off the side of the bowl and into each delightful spoonful! As for my "large plate", I went with the Vinegar Braised Chicken with figs, smoked bacon, anson mills grits and brussels sprouts. When in doubt, go with the chicken. That's what my father always told me and I'm glad I followed his advice. The chicken was super moist and the braise was phenomenal. However it was a major bummer getting bites of cartilage in there... But attention grits fans! I'm sure these would be some of the best grits you've ever tried. Normally I hate grits; bland, gritty, nasty... Supper's grits were so creamy and flavorful. Definitely lots of butter :) The brussel sprouts weren't half bad either! (On a side note... I thought my dinner mates Pork Loin was WAY too salty) Then came dessert and I got the Warm Apple Cobbler with biscuit topping and spiced whipped cream. I thought it was too bitter for my standards... And the whipped cream just tasted like fluffy milk. The best part was the biscuit. Monty Python would of been pleased... Dessert menu changes: It might of only been tonight, but the Olive Oil Sponge Cake wasn't on the menu. Instead they offered a "cookie plate" served with a chocolate egg cream.
