However they don't note anywhere that one of the cookies is peanut butter. So if you're allergic be careful! Cocktails... B-/C+ My Mandarin cocktail was supper refreshing. But my friends London Lou tasted like pure alcohol. As for service... A+ Our waiter was very friendly and efficient. Tried to crack a joke every now and then too. Overall I don't think Supper is the best choice, food wise, for restaurant week. But if you're one of those people who love a way cool atmosphere and being able to enjoy a rather somewhat pricey restaurant for a "good deal" during restaurant week... then be my guest!

We've been going to Palermo's in Blue Bell for quite a while. The food is good. My wife loves the gluten free pizza and she's there 4-5 times a week. But I just returned from there and I think it may be my last time. I came out to the parking lot and found my car blocked in by a pickup truck parked behind it. After waiting about 5 minutes I went back inside and found it belonged to "the boss", I guess the owner? He came out to move it but was in no hurry and kept telling me in a patronizing tone of voice not to worry, don't get excited, I'd be fine, etc. When I pointed to the 4 empty parking spaces across the lot and asked why he couldn't have parked there, he said that was too far away because he was delivering some pizzas and had to keep them hot. When I pointed out that I had 2 takeout pizzas getting cold in my car that i had just bought in his shop, he told me "Don't worry about it, the sun will keep them warm". In my experience, this is not how a business owner or employee talks to a customer who spends a couple of thousand dollars a year in their store.

Sunday afternoon my two daughters and I went for lunch. We ordered 1 kids meal pizza, and 2 Gluten free pizzas. It took 30 minutes to get served, then after returning home realized the pizzas were NOT gluten free. Have been sick since eating there & know what eating Gluten feels like! Will never trust B J's food again...oh yeah, the bill was $40!

Update - The district manager of this store contacted me to apologize for my experience and offered us 4 free pizzas for our next order. I appreciate him making it right. I had sent a facebook message to Papa John's and they contacted the district manager who got back to me in one day. I'll give this location another chance. We order from this Papa John's because my family is crazy and no one but me likes STL style pizza. Fine, order from Papa John's you weirdos. (it's cheaper than Dominoes and PJ's delivers.) So, every Friday night Papa John's on Grand gets a lot of our money because our boys eat like ravenous teenagers, like they do, and we don't want to cook. It doesn't taste as good as Dominoes and it's at least lukewarm when it arrives. Tonight was the last straw, though. We always order four pizzas. Tonight, the one gluten free pizza we ordered was wrong. So I called to get them to make me a new one and (fingers crossed) maybe even give me a credit for a free pizza bc of the inconvenience. (I'm HANGRY) That was an hour and 19 minutes ago. I've been on HOLD for over an HOUR & I still haven't talked to the manager even though I've requested that. This is just enormously disrespectful of me as a frequent customer and enormously disrespectful of my time. You lost a customer tonight, Papa John's on Grand. We'll take the $2000+ we spend a year on pizzas (holy crap!) to someone else. Leaving one star because the drivers are always very friendly. PS: Papa Johns on Facebook Messenger says they're going to resolve it. We shall see.

DISCLAIMER: This review is actually for the BAR ONLY. I had not been to Bar Napoli in awhile, so when a friend suggested their patio for enjoying the "cold front" we were experiencing, I was all in. However, the excellent company of friends was the highlight of the night. Nothing in particular was horrible; but nothing was great, or even good. Ordered two plain pies 30 minutes prior to them closing yesterday for a group of friends and I. Once the pizza was brought back we were all so hungry and immediately had a slice. As soon as I took a bite I noticed that the dough was not cooked fully. When you lifted up the pizza it would hang straight down due to the fact is wasn't cooked all the way. Thanks Milano for serving improperly cooked pizza and rushing before close. Thanks for making us sick, too! Won't ever return.

Had been to the Chili's in Downingtown about two months ago. Food was only so, so but the ladies room was filthy. Returned with six other people yesterday. Food was so slow in coming out that they actually gave a credit without asking. BUT, the restaurant was filthy. The ladies room was strewn end to end with towels and toilet paper and obviously had not been cleaned from the previous evening and someone had vomited in the men's room and they had not cleaned that either. There will be no third time at Chili's

I had one of the worst dining experiences here that I have ever had. The service was TERRIBLE and they were not accommodating at all. I came on a weekday for lunch with some friends. Their lunch menu was pretty limited and for someone with a gluten allergy, there were only two options prepared as is that would be safe to eat. I was surprised because usually Mexican restaurants have lots of options for those who are gluten free. My friend tried to order one of the quesadillas without onions, and they told her they wouldn't do that, that everything on the menu comes as is unless someone has an allergy. When it came time for me to order, I informed the waitress of my gluten allergy and asked if they could just make me cheese quesadillas on corn tortillas instead of the flour ones on the menu as I couldn't eat those. I've done this at several other restaurants and never had a problem with this before. She said she wasn't sure if they could do that or not but she would check. A few minutes later, either the chef or the manager (not sure who he was) came out and starting lecturing me about how that "is not a quesadilla!!!" and how it wouldn't work. I'm well aware it's not how normal ones usually are, and trust me I'd much rather eat a flour one if I could, but I do know it's possible to do. I ended up just ordering the enchiladas instead since this was becoming a big ordeal. A few minutes later, the man came back with a plate of one cheese quesadilla that was probably 4 inches in diameter and said "see I told you it was small" in the rudest tone of voice. My friends and I were absolutely flabbergasted by the way he treated us over something I cannot control. Just in case you were wondering, the definition of quesadilla is "a tortilla filled with a savory mixture, folded and usually fried."

The ambience here is definitely upscale. They did a total remodel of the old place, and the new fixtures and furnishings are high class. The men's room was clean. When I first got there, based on the ambience and presentation of the buffet food, I was initially planning on rating them 4 stars, but it seemed like too much of the food had been sitting out since lunch. I got there around 5:45 pm. There does seem to be a wide assortment of food though. (I've never been to Journey, so I can't compare to that.) Maybe if you get there around 7 or 7:30pm, after the dinner rush has started, you'll get fresher food after the first dinner turnover. With buffets, freshness and turnover time really count. And few buffets these days seem willing to throw out old food that has sat around for a few hours. Salads and fruit were very fresh. But the steam tray food was a little tired. I didn't try the high end stuff like seafood (duh on me, it's a seafood restaurant) because I filled up on other stuff before I got around to it. I didn't get around to the carved meats either. I tried most of the sushi and nigiri, and was disappointed in it. But then I'm a sushi snob. You need to keep sushi/sashimi/nigiri under wraps, like food-service film or in a closed plastic container like they do at Kroger/Marsh. You can't let it sit in the open, or it will dry out. _ALL_ the nigiri and most of the sushi rolls were dry to the point of degraded quality. Still edible, but the sushi-lover in me kept thinking "meh, I've had better." So if you're a sushi-lover, don't go here just for the sushi. Marsh's sushi, down the street at W 86th & Zionsville Road was better than this. The Japanese seaweed salad was decent, but was sitting uncovered too. The Japanese veg tempura was not warm enough, and too limp. For dessert, the fruit was good. A pudding/fruit salad was unique and delicious. But they committed a cardinal jello sin: the jello squares had a thick skin or rind, due to either being dried out, or else they didn't dissolve and stir the jello properly when they made it. How can you mess up jello? Service was good. The waitress brings your drink and refills. Used plates were removed quickly. Supper buffet, with only tap water for a beverage, and no coupon was $13.05 with tax (before tip). I'll try it again, but if the crab legs and other seafood don't measure up, it just aint worth it without a coupon. Bottom line, the food just didn't live up to the upscale ambience. But, I'll try supper again and also go back for a lunch. And BEWARE the ESCOLAR FISH! It looks like a filet, but IT HAS HARD BONES. The escolar fish I had here tasted very good. When I got home I wondered "That was good fish. I wonder what kind of fish 'escolar' is, I've never heard of it before." Googled and Wiki'd. Yikes! Escolar has been banned in Japan and Italy. Hong Kong government, and the United States FDA "advise" against it's consumption. Wiki says don't eat more than 6 ounces, squeeze out as much fat as you can, and do not eat the skin, or the meat near the skin. Wiki says: "Symptoms may include stomach cramps, bright orange oil in stool, diarrhea, headaches, nausea, vomiting, and anal leakage." I only had about 4 ounces of it, and did NOT get any of the symptoms. So I guess a little is okay. Escolar has actually been discussed before on Yelp: http://www.yelp.com/topic/los-angeles-escolar---the-ex-lax-fish-warning A couple more references. http://www.thekitchn.com/thekitchn/ingredients-seafood/use-caution-when-eating-escolar-066602 http://www.health.qld.gov.au/ph/Documents/ehu/23004.pdf

Food was ok, but we expected better. The service was so-so. We were able to take our dog on the patio and they brought him water. 3 1/2 stars might be a better rating, but compared to other restaurants in the area Brixx missed the mark. Hope the review helps them improve. Please make sure the wait staff understands food allergies!

About time this place closed. Hope they put something better in it's location. Had been there a few times because I work in the area and it consistently got worse each time. The last was the final straw when my quesadilla was cold with unmelted cheese, couldn't even pick it up because shredded cheese kept falling out. My co-worker's gluten free burger roll was moldy which the manager did replace and didn't charge her for, but still. Who let's a moldy roll even make it past the kitchen door?? Never had a problem at other Ruby Tuesday's, just this location consistently.

The food here tasted great and the service was good. Unfortunately, both my coworker and I got food poisoning. We shared appetizers of pork belly sliders and egg rolls, so I would maybe recommend avoiding those. I haven't called the restaurant about it yet but have been awake sick since 4am. We didn't eat any of the same food otherwise that day and other coworkers did not get sick, so I have no doubt it was something we ate at Kwok's.

This place has gone downhill! The quality is grade "Z". I ordered a chicken pot pie which had a few overcooked veges with salty gravy and something that resembled Spam over chicken. Our entire party shared the sampler appetizer and it must've had cross-contamination because we all got sick for the next 24 hours... Never again. There's nothing I can't stand more than paying $100+ to get nausea!

Terrible, and possibly harmful to your health. We came here one rainy day to try it out. Food tasted average to poor in quality. The service was shoddy. The servers are nice, but extremely inexperienced. So much, that I was concerned they might not be taking proper safety protocols. For example, server took our plate away with the wasabi on it. My husband asked for more wasabi and instead of bringing fresh, she brought back the plate she removed. Totally unsanitary. After eating, I immediately felt nauseous, but I thought it was my imagination. That lasted for about 5 hours. My daughter was not immediately sick, but was throwing up all night. Recently, my son came here for dinner. The next day he had diarrhea, severe stomach pain and nausea and vomiting all day. I don't think this is a coincidence. The food here is not fresh. If you pay for cheap sushi, you will get cheap raw fish. Eat at your own risk.

GLUTEN FREE CELIACS or PEOPLE WITH FOOD ALLERGIES DO NOT GO HERE!!!! I could see how this place has good reviews- the food was cheap and ok and the service was not bad. HOWEVER- they will not accommodate any variations from the menu. More importantly, the owner/cook is VOLATILE. I am very sensitive to gluten and am also soy and dairy free. We wanted to go to Rambla for breakfast since they cook gluten free but it was closed. Red Gravy was down the street. We sat down and I asked the waitress if they could accommodate my allergies. I told her that I didn't expect to be able to eat here. She said they could cook for me but you could tell she didn't know what gluten was. She kept focusing on the dairy allergy when my friend said "its not the dairy as much as it is the gluten she is worried about." I kept asking about the potatoes which she said were fine because they were just grilled in grease. I asked if she could make sure no flour was added to them. She said there wasn't as she has seen the cook make them. I now realize that the waitress was probably scared of the cook and didn't want to ask her. I ordered the omelet and potatoes. The meal came out with a big piece of garlic bread on top. I told the waitress that I can't even touch it or eat a crumb. She told me that the cook wouldn't make another one since she was closing the kitchen. SERIOUSLY???? How long does it take to make an omelet. I ate 1/3 of it (the part that the bread hadn't touched) because I was so hungry and didn't have an emergency granola bar on me. Usually I wouldn't even eat a bite of it. They charged me for the whole omelet. I was very surprised by this and agreed to pay for the 1/2 that I was able to eat. The waitress went to ask the cook who came out screaming at me and disrupting the whole restaurant. She blamed me and told me that I could see on the menu that it came with garlic bread and I should have asked for it off. She also said that she had no idea that I was allergic to gluten or wheat and I should have told me waitress. THEY HAVE NO IDEA WHEN IT COMES TO FOOD ALLERGIES!!!!! They comped my omelet but still charged me for the coffee :/ I am sure it is no surprised but I was glutened.

Found out the GM is making this location an Allergy Friendly Store!!! For those of us allergic to nuts (some drink flavorings contain nuts), cross-contamination can be deadly. This Allergy Friendly news is wonderful to hear! I wish all Starbucks did this! We got a drink for my Mother, who is allergic to coffee (I know, so sad). They made her a wonderful Raspberry & Carmel Hot Chocolate! No cross-contamination at all! Very happy! Also got a few other drinks also. They forgot one ingredient in one drink. They remade it correctly! Did have a small problem with an employee who tried to tell us we didn't know what we were talking about regarding ristretto. We gave up and decided to contact the company so they can be retrained them in that area.

A friend ask me if I wanted AYCE Sushi? I said HECK YEAH! Too bad the service sucked and the food was mediocre.... A party of 12 or more came here for dinner while staying at Grand Sierra. Our party took up three tables and each table received their own sheet of paper to make their order. The server got all of our table numbers mixed up and we ended up eating stuff we didn't pick. I like to eat mainly raw items and the next thing I know I was getting rolls that were fully cooked. I was disappointed at the fact that after telling the server that the table is reversed and we are supposed to get these items (told him the list), he still gave us the wrong items. All of the rolls you order gets placed on one big plate, so it is difficult to tell what was what. If you are allergic to certain things, it is best to tell them to separate the rolls for you (hope they listen). Food: it wasn't bad, but it wasn't ok either. I was in between. Some of the fish seemed fresh, others seemed thawed out, but I did like the quail shooters. Dessert: pretty bad (fresh fruit was SOUR), I wouldn't order anything they listed for the AYCE dessert list.

The food is very good and they have lots of gluten free options. I've bee here a few times and it is always pretty good. Had HORRIBLE service tonight though.. Melissa is soooooo slow omg. My life for a water...and I JUST WANT TO PAY MY BILL!

Honestly, I've tried so hard to love Noble Pie. The atmosphere is relaxed, the decor is unique, and the location is convenient and historical. The place is often the site for local music and events, and the clientele is interesting and polite. The food is generally pretty quality when done right, and the names are creative in that independent-and-quirky-restaurant sort of way. However, the service leaves much to be desired. I have only ever been greeted enthusiastically (read: politely) a couple of times, and those were usually times that I or someone I was with knew the person behind the counter. There is a clear view into the kitchen in the back, where it's almost painfully easy to see the ever-changing cook crew lounging about, fucking around, or being a little too friendly with the food (not the most sanitary bunch). The wait is long. I'm a patient person. I have no problem waiting for my food when it's quality stuff. If you're willing to brave a wait, it might be worth it to you, but I'm just saying: be warned. An order of wings and a pizza will set you back about thirty to forty minutes. It's not excessive, but it is a while to wait in a restaurant. Now for my own experience. Nobly Pie advertises themselves as vegan friendly, which lends a great opportunity to Renoites and visitors who have alternative food tastes or food allergies. I happen to be one of those people. Unfortunately, on no less than three occasions, I have placed very specific orders for totally vegan pizzas (which are NOT cheap even regularly, mind you), only to be disappointed by genuine non-vegan cheeses, milk-based sauces, or full blown meats topping my pie. Now, with the extra prices garnered from toppings, it's generally easier to order a specialty pizza and simply modify it to be vegan. That being the case, I can see where a cook might make the wrong assumptions based on the name of the order and mess it up somehow. Or, you know, any number things. Maybe it was an off day, maybe they just forgot. But three times? You know way they say: three strikes, and you're out, Noble Pie. This pizza parlor isn't a bad place, and its clientele is generally a loyal, dedicated bunch, and I know many people that love this place. If you are willing to try it out, you probably won't be disappointed. But in my own experience, it just seems like this place is attempting to emulate the great vegan-friendly, new age pizza parlors of Portland, OR and other such cities--only they have not, in my opinion, succeeded.

HORRIBLE!! Over priced and just awful! HORRIBLE!! The crepes are ok but I wish that the chocolate crepes didn't have vanilla yogurt in them. It is not my favorite I wish that they used strawberry yogurt instead . Going to the bathroom after the crepes is a disaster and my family isn't even lactose intolerant. The crepes are very filling so you probably shouldn't order 2 even if you are hungry. Had some bad chili here and got a bad case of food poisoning. Also had a bad experience with one of the staff. Not sure it was related but most the staff is pretty nice. But I won't be back. I'd be afraid to eat here.

I have a dairy allergy - so I told the woman that and she said the soy or almond would work but it wouldn't be as creamy. I said fine. Then when I get it, it doesn't taste like white chocolate and it is not sweet at all. *Don't take your choices back - they will give you an attitude about it and make you feel bad. Ps. Pieology is your typical fast casual pizza joint, allowing you to customize your pizza to your hearts desire. First you select your type of crust, then the sauce, cheese and toppings before your pie takes a short 5-10 trip into their wood burning oven. I ordered a Whole Wheat, Spicy Chicken & Bacon Pizza, with a Herb butter & Olive Olive sauce, only because they seemed to be out of the 3-Cheese Alfredo sauce. To call the chicken spicy was a mistake, there was zero spice to it. The crust selection here is limited to thin crust, house made, wheat, or gluten free. Overall the pizza was good, the crust was flaky and had a and the sauce really had a good taste. One problem I had was that initally they were very stingy on the toppings, however they did ask if it was good enough and added a bit more. Another issue was that their credit card processing was down, and I wasnt told this until after I placed my order and customized my pizza and presented my card. I am sorry but if you cannot accept credit cards put a sign up before the customer goes though the ordering process, luckily I had cash. Oh how I wish there could be a half star, because this location just opened last week and the staff is still struggling. However the food is good and reasonably priced. Overall the experience was good and I am sure they will work out some of the problems after being open for a few weeks. Solid option for the area, however the selection is rather limited when compared to places like PieFive Pizza.

Let's start with the good! The staff are really friendly, their bakery items (I had a browny) were really good, I didn't have to wait too long considering how busy it was, and got the correct order (although with way too much cinnamon). On the down side I have a few issues that will result in me never returning to this location. I get the logic of being busy and cutting little corners to get customers through the door, but throwing dirty used steamed milk jugs and whatever else that needs cleaning across your clean work space into the sink is gross. Re-steaming milk can get people sick. Not cleaning down the steamed milk spout and pushing through your lines can cause some bad cross contamination and get people sick. When pouring milk into a steamer jug and managing to pour it through your hands somehow you need to learn how to properly pour milk. If your work station is more milk then stainless steel, take the second and wipe it down. When lifting your steamer jug all the different milks are dropping into whatever is sitting there. If for whatever reason I couldn't have lactose I would be one sick person. All this being said, I didn't mention anything to the staff because the barista looked a bit overwhelmed. So I won't go back knowing that if the visible corners are cut who knows what else there is that I didn't notice. But again, the staff were super nice. :)

For my brothers Wedding Shower, we wanted to get a really nice, gluten free cake. We researched bakeries that made gluten free desserts and ended up finding "Cupcake Heaven". When talking to the presumed baker, she seemed confident and even recommended colors for the design in mind. Everything seemed to be going great, up until the day of pick-up. When we went to get the cake, they didn't even have a round box to transport it in which seemed odd since they specialize in cakes and cupcakes. But it wasn't until we opened the box and peered inside that we realized the horror our eyes had to endure. This was, by far, the sloppiest cake I have ever seen. The words were un-centered and squished together... the top of the cake looked like it had a layer taken off due to mistakes... and even the trim around the cake was uneven and looked completely unprofessional. At this point, there was nothing we could do about it but bring it to the Shower and have it cut immediately. I have never seen a "professional" cake look more like a child's art project. The only reason this review is getting 2 stars instead of 1 is because it actually did taste good, besides being overly sweet. But that doesn't excuse the fact that the appearance was absolutely horrid. (I will be posting pictures for you to see.)

I'm a reluctant, ambivalent Epic regular. A recent move places Epic as the closest cafe, and rapidly approaching finals coupled with an uncanny caffeine addiction drag me into this oddly eclectic and contradictory place. Hours: Open until midnight every night. Awesome. WIFI: The internet is more consistent and faster than at either Bentley's or Caffe Luce. It's less reliable but faster than Starbucks. It's less reliable and slower than Crave, UMC cafeteria, Raging Sage, Cartel, etc. Staff: I've interacted with nearly every staff member at this point. I haven't been the overly-friendly, open person I typically am - but even with that, all of the staff have been quite friendly. I'm a fairly observant individual and occasionally I'm here for 10 hours at a time - I've never observed them treat anyone poorly. I have observed them go out of their way to help people though. I like them. Coffee: The price is about the same as most other coffee shops, as is the quality. In my biased opinion, nothing has come close to matching Ike's in quality or price, and I lament daily over this tragic loss. Food: Over-priced, but tasty. It's on par with Bentley's ridiculous prices. They have a wide variety of freshly baked goods that vary by the day. As another reviewer has attested, the breakfast burrito is phenomenal - but again, paying $6.00 for a tortilla, potatoes and eggs is absurd - but hey, I'm an absurd person, so bring on some more egregiously priced burritos. Cleanliness: Many have commented on unsanitary conditions. There are flies buzzing about on occasion, sure; and the bathrooms - although I wouldn't call them a disaster - are vile in an aesthetic sense. I wouldn't consider them any less sanitary than any other coffee shop bathroom - it's just the aesthetics. Personally, I derive some grotesque sort of solace from the witty, inappropriate commentary scribbled over the bathroom walls. The furniture...it does seem a bit dingy, but that's what gives this place character. You want sterile? Go to Starbucks, you drone. Patrons: Diverse. College students, professors, graduate students, hipsters, yuppies, retired folk, indigents, etc. Unlike my vast experiences at Coffee Xchange, I've never witnessed an "event" here where shit gets cray cray. No bums throwing chairs and screaming about murdering everyone. No methed out college kids trying to guzzle down 6 red-eyes in one go while loudly shouting about how dark it is outside when it's 2am in the morning. No heavy drug use in the bathrooms (that I'm aware of, although it's likely, because people are awesome like that). Overall, it's safe here. If you're afraid of being exposed to peculiar individuals, crawl back into your hole or stick to Starbucks drive-thrus. On a personal note, I find it exceptionally odd that they so heavily push "gluten-free" foods, are a certified "green business," etc., yet they sell cigarettes here. This hipster element fills me with contempt. Further, the little spiritual / meditation / new age / snake oil pamphlet/books they have for sale near the window makes me shudder in disdain. Overall, I love and hate this place. It's comfortable in an uncomfortable way. The staff is great, the food is good, and the coffee is average. The prices can go jump off a bridge and die. Ultimately, I mourn the loss of Ike's. Epic is a necessary supplement. If Ike's or its functional equivalent were to open anywhere in Tucson, I'd instantly abandon ship and find residence elsewhere, regardless of the bicycling mileage involved.

Very disappointed. We hoped that after food network came in it would've been better. "Short" buffet only. Dried out pork, chicken smothered in barbecue sauce, and beef with mushroom gravy. Pasta with salmon. Very fishy tasting. No descriptions on buffet. Waiter described items but left off saying anything about the beef having mushrooms and I'm allergic. Beef was actually good but husband found a mushroom. Hopefully didn't eat enough to hurt me. Most of the food was cold, or dry. Waffles looked like mush. Chicken soup had no chicken, but a ton of Italian seasoning, inedible. $14.95 plus $3 for sodas and tea Online 12/7 menu shows price of 13.95 for Sat. Short buffet mini brunch, so it looks like they overcharged us too. If you are going to charge for a hi end buffet it should be one.
Hope you like food poisoning. Had it twice here. Don't bother walking in.

If you're like me and a Floridian who has never golfed in their life, this is the perfect place to start. You start understanding why people enjoy it so much. It's an awesome way to hang out with a group of people and enjoy the outdoors. Since the location is new, you'll have a good wait on the weekend so make sure to reserve a bay as soon as you get there. When we arrived on a beautiful Saturday, we were advised it would be a two-hour wait, granted it was only an hour. We sat at the bar and enjoyed a quick bite while enjoying the beautiful weather, watching others play, and kids enjoy Dance Revolution. The facility is clean, the staff friendly, and the food great. It's a little pricey on the weekends but no more than say...The Florida State Fair but with better food. The best surprise was towards the end of our day, we were walking to our cars and a Topgolf golf cart swung by and asked us if we needed a lift to our cars. Very cool considering you can also bring your own clubs, if you want. All around fun. We'll be going again and hopefully for a corporate event. UPDATED since we are now experiencing food poisoning of the worst kind. :P

I have to be honest... I don't know a thing about jazz music. I'm an LA girl now living in Chicago who just likes drinks and good music-- so that brought us here. Also, no cover. We will tip the band but hate paying covers. I'll be honest... we entered because we saw a cool band that sounded nice, a place full of about 25 people, the lighting was right, and the sign was very urban and cool. I love good signage. Anyone who says packaging doesn't matter is so wrong. We sat at a nice hightop and ordered a couple drinks. It was $10 total for a beer and glass of wine. Not bad. We asked for change from our $20 and the cocktail waitress simply said she had no change and could get it from the bar "I guess"-- so since she didn't have a huge desire to be tipped, we dropped her tip money into the tip container for the band instead. Her loss. Overall, nice experience. Didn't eat but it did look like they had quite a few sandwiches on the menu and something about a maison sauce. I asked the bartender what the sauce consisted of and she said... "Oh, a mix of mayo, ketchup, mustard...." VOMIT. Sorry, but that sounds pretty freaking disgusting! I'll stick to the music and booze. Thanks.

Their Nigiri is GROSS!!! I ordered the snapper - it was actually dry on the edges. The hamachi was sub-par. My favorite - Tobiko (flying fish roe) was off-colored, the rice ball was giant and overall it was probably the worse I have ever eaten! My boyfriend ended up with food poisoning and threw up ALL night! Go to Francis' Asian Bistro or Hiroba for good nigiri. That being said - they have decent rolls- but just decent - too much mayo! This sushi restaurant is VERY AMERICANIZED!!!!

Gosh I really wanted to love this place! I was so excited about the non-dairy options and came here after recently discovering I am lactose intolerant. We waited for an hour in a VERY slow moving line and what I got was...terrible. I can't speak to the dairy ice cream, but mine tasted like ice chunks. It didn't seem mixed well enough and truthfully just tasted like frozen almond milk with a slight marshmallow flavor. It wasn't sweet or creamy in any way. I was so disappointed and I am rarely disappointed like that. I've had a lot of lactose free ice cream and this was by far the worst. The experience is unique and fun, but not worth the hefty price tag. Obviously their regular ice cream is ok since they stay pretty busy.

Stopped by here on Saturday night after leaving the meeting of families festival (Pope Francis) they were on our long walk home that awaited us. They were open late & busy! We ordered 1 slice of cheese pizza, pork tacos, & an ice tea. We were charged for 2 slices of pizza, as there were 3 cashier girls talking & laughing amongst themselves & half listening to customer's orders. No biggie but my hubby is Lactose intolerant & I wasn't going to eat 2 slices, we gave the extra slice to a cop getting off her shift. *Staff friendly but distracted, but that may have been a one time thing. *Pizza tasted good. *Tacos really good. *Location was great & they had decorated it nicely with white & yellow balloon arches for Papal visit for their outdoor seating area. *Hours great open late. *Vibe great crowd. Yes, we'd eat here again but we'd double check the order before paying next time.

Pretty much consistently terrible service. Like the worst ever. I'd call to place an order for pick-up, show up at the suggested time, find out that they never actually put in my order, and then wait another 20 min for my food to be prepared. And once I got food poisoning there. If the place improved their service it'd be SUCH an upgrade as their gyro platters are actually very good. Just can't get past the rudeness and inefficiency (and food poisoning).

We brought in 8 people and 4/8 vomitted during the next and day after along with diarrhea. So do the math, you have 50% chance of getting sick but hey you get what you pay for. Steaks were burnt and extremely chewy too.

The ice cream is okay if you imagine you're eating one big dippin dot. The line takes a while to get through, and it's a little pricey. You can pick however many flavors you want though, which is cool. Lots of options if you're lactose and tolerant too.

I'm bordering on 3.5 stars. For some reason I thought this would be a little less fratty than it was. I really enjoyed the booze milkshake (I got the rice crispy one). It's made with graeters ice cream so throw sheets to the wind and abandon any dairy allergy you may have. It was VERY filling. It would be impossible to have more than one. However, alcohol wise you would probably need at least two to get a decent buzz going. In theory the pour your own beer thing is nice. You get a card and place it on a sensor with the tap you want to pour beer from. They charge per fluid ounce, with beers varying price wise. However, groups of people would just stand in front of it blocking, so it's hard to have a decent traffic flow. I heard others having issues with beer not dispensing and getting charged. The bar tenders would correct the issue though. The service was hit or miss at certain parts of the night. When we arrived we got our drinks quickly but then a huge gap in time before our server came to take our order. In the middle of ordering the server advised the kitchen may or not be closed and then took time to figure out. We then had to order apps for our meal. Overall, the apps were good we got cheese curds, buffalo wings (very spicy), and sliders. However, we were given a "basket" option of fries and coleslaw with the sliders but we didn't order that and it came with a $4 charge. We didn't figure out getting the fries and coleslaw wasn't part of the appetizer until the end. I'd probably go back and just get the fries and try another adult milkshake.

This is a beautiful, clean, and rustic establishment. The staff is very nice and friendly. Now onto my service. Basically put, it needs work. The coffee had grounds in two separate cups. I was not given silverware upon sitting. My server seemed a bit stressed and possibly overwhelmed (weeded). She did not come back to check on me or ask if I needed anything. I had to ask others to assist me. The food needs work. It looks beautiful, but it was cold when it arrived. Cold poached eggs is not exactly appetizing. The best thing, so far, is everything is gluten-free. I'm willing to give them another chance. It might have just been an off day. It has a lot of potential.

If you have food allergies, don't go here.. I was told they were out of the regular coffee (plain vanilla flavored coffee) that I usually get and they promptly gave me other options. When I ordered my food, I expressed that I have a dairy allergy. This wasn't an issue, no cheese was placed on my English Muffin. The issue was that the options they gave me, after telling them that I had a dairy allergy, contained dairy. I heard the lady in the back saying to the lady at the window that the alternative they recommended contained dairy. She tried to hand it to me and so I promptly asked what the lady in the back was saying about my drink, in fact, containing milk. Had I not heard the lady in the back, I could have had a serious reaction. She said yes it does but they put almond milk in it also.... seriously? You could kill someone this way. This is a serious health hazard!! I know it is super annoying to have specific orders, but come on people! The lady then took my order back and dumped it out and used the same cup.. do you not understand how allergies work? I just left and didn't argue with her and threw my drink away. I get it that allergies are not your issue, but you can hurt someone this way. Please, for the love, when someone tells you they have an allergy, take it seriously.

We happened to be on the west side and genius struck when I said "Let's go to the Peruvian restaurant over here!" The 3 of us were SO glad we chose this over having pizza delivered. We had good service and our questions were answered sufficiently. The interior is really nicely decorated, and our food was AWESOME! In fact, I am completely confident that if this restaurant were located in Broad Ripple (instead of in a strip mall on W. 38th St.), we wouldn't have been able to get a seat at 8pm on a Saturday night. This is a really top-notch establishment. Also, apologies ahead of time for not remembering the Spanish names for the items we ordered. Instead of the chips and salsa that Mexican restaurants bring you, a basket of soft, fresh bread is brought to your table (kind of like challah) along with a little bowl of pale green, lightly spiced dipping sauce (aji). It is so addictive! Seriously, we could've easily filled up on this and not had room for our meals. Our appetizer was a deep-fried ball of mashed potatoes stuffed with spiced beef, olives, and chopped boiled egg, and served alongside a salad. The salad consists of thinly sliced sweet onions, tomato, lettuce, and plenty of cilantro lightly dressed. I think the dressing was mainly vinegar and lime juice? The boys raved about the salad and we all loved the hot appetizer (reminded me of a cross between an Indian samosa and a potato pakora). It's not the best choice to share with 3 people as someone is going to complain about getting an uneven amount of some filling ingredient. I had the vegetarian green pasta which is served alongside potatoes in cheese (huancaina) sauce. The only thing that threw me about this dish is that the potatoes and cheese sauce were cold. Evidently this is the traditional way to serve this dish. So...you didn't get cold food...that's the way it's supposed to be! The green pesto-style sauce was SO tasty. It was just a little bit spicy and coated every single noodle. The portion was so huge I'll probably be able to eat it for 2 more meals! One of my companions ordered the green pasta with a pan-fried chicken breast (reminded me of schnitzel-delish) and a potato. He also had to make an effort not to over-stuff himself because he loved his entree. My partner ordered the half rotisserie chicken, which is served with salad and french fries, although you have the option to sub other sides if you wish. That bird was awesome! Total perfection. Moist, flavorful, tender. He couldn't stop raving about the flavor and said, "We're not in Boston anymore." There aren't a ton of vegetarian choices, but between the appetizer menu, the desserts, and the couple entrees, I don't think anyone will leave hungry. I think better than half of the menu items are or can easily be prepared gluten-free. However, if you tend to get very sick with even the slightest contamination, be cautious. There is a (very) slight language barrier and communicating "no wheat anywhere" might be tricky? Regretfully, we didn't budget any belly space for dessert. There are 2-3 available. There are a couple "exotic" Peruvian soda choices but no alcohol is available. Our pre-tip total for 3 entrees and 1 appetizer was about $43 with tax. Prices aren't cheap, but the portions are humongous and the food is delicious. I highly recommend making a trip to this restaurant, and I will even be encouraging friends in the northern suburbs to head down to 38th St.

Based on previous reviews, it appears that this is the one in Terminal F, which is the location I'm reviewing. Let me state first off, I've never been to Au Bon Pain before, they don't have any locations where I'm from. While I looked at the menu to try to figure out what I wanted, I tried not to be *that guy* and stayed out of everyone's way. The staff behind the counter were friendly, I'm pretty sure I ordered my sandwich in the most convoluted way possible but it wasn't an issue for them. It came out fast and was accurate and delicious. No complaints in terms of the food. The drinks? Ugh. I'm 105% sure the teas were mislabelled. I went to the carafe labelled "Iced Black Tea" (the unsweetened one, can't remember if they had sweetened but it's irrelevant) and got that, added lemon and sweetener. I'll come back to the beverage in a second. I went to pay and asked where the straws were because I looked all around and saw plasticware, napkins, coffee stirrers, lids, everything but straws. The cashier seemed baffled by the notion that I'd want a straw. I'm American and don't have a heavy accent of any type, surely I'm not the first person to ask for one. She directed me to...the plasticware. What. Ugh fine, I'll just drink out of the cup. Unhelpful. The tea was umm...not plain black tea. Given how it tasted, I'm pretty sure it was their peach iced tea. Given that that's sweetened already, being doubly sweetened and having lemon, it tasted horrible. So I basically had no drink because I could only tolerate tiny little sips of that crap. Disappointment. It might seem like overkill to give them two stars as a result, but basically getting the wrong drink (I look at it like, what if someone were diabetic? What if they're allergic to peaches?) and having an unhelpful cashier made it "meh" which according to Yelp is two stars.

Oh my gluten-free goodness! Piccione Pastry has gluten-free cannoli and they are FREAKING FANTASTIC!!! The hubby and I swung in here last night on our date night. I had heard there might be some sweet things a Celiac could eat here and boy were there. They can fill the gluten-free cannoli (they keep them separated behind the counter to avoid cross-contamination - ask for them) with most of their special flavors, just not their "signature" ones. I figured I'd start with the basic traditional vanilla bean. It was, umm ya... FREAKING FANTASTIC!! I can't wait to come back again and try the other flavors. They also had coconut macaroons and meringues. I grabbed a meringue to go but only made it down the block before diving in. Cooked to perfection - crispy on the outside, chewing on the inside and dusted with cane sugar. O.M.G. Gluten-free folks, this is the real deal. Go. Support this place and get your sugar fix!

The food and drinks are reasonably priced. However if you eat the food be prepared for food poisoning. We should have known something was wrong because the chicken was watery, not juicy in the chicken and cheese quesadilla. It was like they poorly thawed an old chicken breast. Will not go back and recommend others that value their health refrain from going as well.

Really amazing salmon fish and chips. Unfortunately, they cook the fish and chips in the same oil, pan, whatever with their shellfish, and I'm allergic to shellfish. I didn't think it was a problem, as I'm new with the allergy, but I started to have a reaction. Unfortunately this place is another added to a growing list of restaurants I can't eat at or return to because of their practices in serving their food.
Disappointing. The gluten free pizza was burnt crisp and cheese pizza just made us nauseated. We tried to eat half of it and all of it came back up. So sad. I really liked their pizza.

THEY DO NOT TAKE RESERVATIONS FOR SMALL PARTIES...FYI. They give you chips and salsa, and the salsa actually had great flavor. We got the dip sampler, and the chili con queso was DELISH, but kind of cold. The Grilled Baja Tacos (Mahi Mahi) were amazing. They had such great flavor. I will definitely be getting these again! The Pollo Burrito was also quite good, but it is a heavier dish for sure. I have also had the Blue Corn Chicken Tacos. To be honest, they were a little bland. To end the meal, the Sopapilla's are pretty good (and free), but honestly, I've had better. Just make sure they're steaming hot, and pour the honey inside the Sopapilla. Also, they offer a gluten free menu, for those that prefer that. The drink menu looks amazing, but honestly is kind of expensive for what you get. Just be aware. :) Last time I went, my husband and I split the Tempranillo Red Wine, which was $33, and worth it. The service has never been stellar, so we'll see how it goes next time we go back. We'll give it another try! ;)

I'm not going to take away a star because of a broken air conditioner, or a gluten free hamburger bun that crumbled into a zillion pieces when I tried to eat it. That's because the gluten free pancakes are so freakin amazing at breakfast!!! Seriously, even my favorite other breakfast place doesn't come close. That being said, I won't be back for a gluten free lunch. Had to order potato salad with the aforementioned burger. It was like eating cold potato salad flavored mashed potatoes. There was not a single solid potato piece in the whole serving. I wish that restaurants that make an effort for those who are gluten free by necessity would dedicate one small teeny fryer for fries that are not contaminated by other items. Is that too much too ask for? Service was good the 3 times that we've been and my coffee cup never got a chance to get empty.

Great wine list, well-made cocktails, and their ability to accommodate our food allergies/requests were the high points of out visit. There was only one vegetarian entree, which was okay, I have a few food allergies so the chef easily whipped up a vegetable plate for me which was tasty, but for an establishment that prides itself on local, high quality ingredients, they could've done a hell of a lot more than a plate of steamed vegetables in broth. I love the concept but the execution fell short for me the three times I've been there.
Good place to eat, good food. However I got food poisoning one time, and I haven't been back since. I got the Chicken Parmesan btw.

The best thing about this place is the great service! Not only do they check on you a good amount of the time, if you order coffee, they'll offer you a cup to take out with you when you're done with your meal. The menu has most of the common breakfast items with some Mexican inspired dishes. There are egg and omelette options, as well as French toast and pancakes. If you want a healthier option or gluten-free, they have that as well. They are very accommodating! I am allergic to melon, watermelon, cantaloupe and honey dew and they were able to separate it for me for my side of fruit. The chorizo omelette I ordered was a bit underwhelming. Nothing very special or outstanding about its taste. The chorizo was lackluster and it came with green chiles and onions. The majority of the filling tasted like the onions and green chili rather than the chorizo. The toast was delicious, including the jam they add to the plate. That is what saved the breakfast for me. I would come back because of the options and service, probably ordering something besides the chorizo omelette.

Long lines, sometimes rude and incompetent workers. More than once I was shorted on my change. The first time, the line was long and I handed the guy a $20 bill and a quarter to pay for a 24oz drink - which is $5.25. When I asked for my change the guy argued and said I only gave him a $5. I didn't want to make a scene so I let it go. Since then I decided that I would never go there without having a $5 bill. The second time I was overcharged, a girl was at the register. I gave her $6 for a $5.25 drink. I received no change and no receipt. At first I thought, weird the prices went up. But then the person behind me ordered the same thing, also handed the cashier $6 and received change!! I stepped back and asked the cashier, why that person received change while I didn't. Her response, "oh sorry about that"! Really!!?? You really have to pay attention. And $ isn't the only problem. A few times, I've opened a smoothie cup to use a spoon, an found large chunks of mangos or other fruit bits that were not supposed to be part of my smoothie.. sometimes there are even large chunks of white - possibly yogurt ??. Which means they aren't blending smoothies well or are not changing out the blender prior to making the next smoothie. Good thing I didn't have a food allergy to whatever was made in that blender cup prior to mine.

Ugh. I don't know what to say that has not been said, so I'll bullet point my distaste for this shithole: - Overpriced drinks - Overpriced (though NORMAL) cover charge - Bad service with attitude - Nothing special DJ - Trashy girls and disgusting guys - Long long long lines to the bathroom and I honestly can say I will never understand the "bathroom people" who sit on a stool expecting a tip for handing me a piece of paper towel. What I would tip for? If the floor was not splattered with vomit and piss. That would be nice. All in all, I am no longer 21 and I'm glad that I don't find myself venturing in here anymore. It is one of the worst bars in downtown Indy and I would not recommend this place for any self-respecting human being.

With a gluten free kid, good and safe pizza is darn had to find. Pure fire has the very best gluten free crust we have tried. The staff went above and beyond, without even being asked, to keep her food from cross contamination. Most of all, the pizza is just plain delicious. The crust is perfectly crispy, the toppings crisp and fresh and the cheese plentiful. We will certainly be back for more.
The food was fantastic. I made my own burger, but I ended up getting food poisoning. However, I will go back again and make sure to get a more thoroughly cooked burger.

Siam Square is one of the few Thai places that I can consider in my 'safe' zone. I have a very severe allergy to shellfish- and generally a cuisine that cooks 90% of their dishes with fish and oyster sauce would be a cuisine I would avoid at all times. Unfortunately, due to having exchange students from Thailand before I developed the allergy has made it a very to give up a food cuisine that I love. However, after many, many times- I have still not had a reaction at Siam Square. (I still carry my Epi pen just in case!) The food there is good- the main issue that I have had (and the reason I am giving them a 4 star rating over 5) is with consistency. Flavors are usually decently consistent, but the cook of the noodles and the heat profile can vary tremendously from visit to visit. Sometimes medium will be nothing but sweet and other times your mouth will be on fire. I am a pretty consistent orderer. I ALWAYS start out with the vegetarian spring rolls, followed by medium chicken pad Thai, and we always finish off with the Roti Rolls. The spring rolls are very good. Glass noodles, carrot, a little bit of cabbage, pepper and seasoning fried in a rice wrapper. The rolls are served with a vinegar and sugar chili sauce (think sweet chili sauce without the thickener). Honestly, I could eat a whole order but I usually have to share with my Fiancé. My fiancé always offers Pad Se Ewe as his entree (this was my favorite Thai dish before developing my allergy). It's served with thick rice noodles, protein of choice, Thai vegetables (similar to spinach) in a sweet soy and oyster sauce. I go with the typical pad Thai. Thin rice noodles, chicken, Thai chili sauce, peanuts, egg. Can't go wrong. Oh- and with NO FISH SAUCE ;). I have never had Roti rolls except at Siam Square. My fiancé is addicted to hem so much that he requests Siam Square just to order dessert. For someone who doesn't generally order dessert, this is a huge compliment. Think flaky pastry pancakes rolled in sweetened condensed milk and honey. I really don't know how to explain it any better. Just trust me- they are good. I would recommend calling ahead for reservations on weekends- or go for takeout. Siam square is definitely a gem in the fountain square neighborhood. Great for individuals with allergies- just make sure to tell them before you order :)

Let me preface this by saying that I love the food at Sidney Street. The scallops, the beignets, the pastries, the veal dumplings-- all absolutely wonderful, and though SS is expensive, it's a good deal for the money. Here's the problem. The last two times I've gone to Sidney Street-- nine months apart-- at least one person in our party has gotten food poisoning. The first time we narrowed it down to the steak soup, and last week (and without soup) it was the fish. You don't like to think that the best restaurant in STL has poor food handling, but we'd never go back to a less expensive restaurant with such a record, so I don't think we will return, as much as those of us who haven't been ill love the food. Hopefully they'll make some changes.

Why does Albertsons always smell funky? I am a frequent shopper at Albertsons mainly because they are just down the street from my house. They are your basic grocery store with the standard food options and for that they get a an average review. The one thing I wish they had was more gluten free options. I feel that most other grocery stores have come privy to recent food/diet trends and adjusted there offerings to accommodate such but don't see that much here. The other thing I wish they would address is the smell!!! For some reason it always smells funky in there, which is not the best atmosphere when you are shoping for food.

Good/great: tasty salmon, rainbow roll, tobiko. The rest of this review is what didn't go well on a busy night. They seated people ahead of us repeatedly. They were only parties of two - but they were sat at tables that would have accommodated our four, and they were 10 minutes later seating us than the estimated 25 minutes. Their ponzu (sp?) sauce tasted too vinegar. The shrimp were overly sweet. The octopus didn't taste as good as our favorite spot (Sushi 7). The mussels we ordered without mayo weren't good. The wrong food was delivered to our table, and the server told us it was our food - see look, you ordered this. Just because she had properly labeled paperwork didn't make it ours! Much of the nigiri surprisingly came with sauce, which wasn't appealing and in fact we're allergic to wheat - a little help would have been nice, to order without sauce, as we specifically ordered some of the food without sauce/wheat. Slow service. The server didn't offer to get us non-sauced plates, which would have been nice. We ended up semi-washing the dishes at the table.

I figured I should write an updated review for Nora's since my last was over a year and half ago and I've since tallied over 45 check-in's at this place. Yep, you read that right. Forty. Five. And I don't check in every time I'm there either. Needless to say, I am addicted to this place. This is the best place in town I have found to get a gluten-free sandwich. Hands down. And, come to think of it, in my 45+ times I've been here I have never gotten accidentally cross-contaminated. Not once. They know what they are doing back there in that kitchen. While I was pregnant the only thing I had a craving for was their Veggie Melt. I had it at least once a week for my entire pregnancy. And when I was in labor? Yep, The Hubby drove down the road from Barnes and got me my Veggie Melt and brought it back (baby wing wasn't equipped to feed me gluten free). I've since moved their Ruben to my "favorite pedestal" but I get that Veggie on occasion for old times sake. The food is fantastic. They have gluten free bread and cookies. I find the staff and owner very nice and helpful. They have indoor and outdoor seating. I get free refills on my fresh brewed ice tea. They have bendy straws. What more does one need? I'll say it again, if you are gluten-free/Celiac, this is the best place in town to get a sandwich. Go.

Yikes. I hesitated to write this review because I'm not a fan of kicking someone when they are CLEARLY down, but I never would have eaten here on 7-27-18 before the Manchester Orchestra show at Jannus Live had I known what I know now. I checked the DBPR website at myfloridalicense.com and it's all there about their forced closure just two days before. Outrageous and numerous health code violations too extensive and repellent to list here, but please, do your research. Started to place our order and there were red flags right away; kid behind the counter was super unsure about replacing a new vat of black beans.....does he line it with plastic or not? We hear him mumble something about "it" being "different" a few days before when manager comes over and has him just dump them in and finish our order already. Entire staff seems dazed and confused. Then I hit the unisex bathroom to wash my hands before we eat, (you know, because that's what civilized people do....) and this is what I find : 1/8th of an inch of standing water all over the floor, a completely dismantled soap dispenser falling off the wall, and broken handles on the faucet. I hesitatingly approach the manager to see if they have soap anywhere, he's on the phone with "someone who is coming to fix the soap dispenser, hopefully today...." and tosses me a small bottle of hand sanitizer. The rest of the joint is covered in grime, and the floors especially were disgusting. I will say the food was worth 2-3 stars, particularly the queso, but I'm absolutely stunned none of us contracted food poisoning or worse after seeing the condition of this place. Former reviews from 2016 show that this spot used to be beloved by many; no idea how it's going to get back on track again.

I had such high hopes for this place. Vietnamese is probably our #1 fav food to eat out and this is fairly close to our house. Even more exciting, they seem to offer a more varied menu than other places in town with new things to try. One of the new things we tried was the spring rolls with pork paste- a seemingly more "authentic" offering. Our server even seemed impressed that we were ordering this instead of the usual pork/shrimp version. Big mistake! It was so sweet and salty that it completely overwhelmed any of the subtle herb/peanut sauce flavors that I enjoy so much about spring rolls. After one bite, my husband said "is there Spam in this?" Totally ruined it for me. The egg rolls were crispy and flavorful. Even though the restaurant wasn't half full it took over 20 minutes to get our appetizers at which point they told us they were out of the Banh Mi we ordered. To make it worse, the server kept trying to offer us a substitute that we didn't want. To say that the owners/staff? "barely spoke English" is an overstatement and it made trying to order a replacement an awkward process. We decided to get a bowl of chicken pho and beef pho with rare steak to compare the broth. The chicken pho looked so promising with a deeply colored broth and pieces of shredded chicken breast. The chicken was flavorless and half of it was too tough to eat. The broth was deeply flavored, but oddly tasted nothing like chicken- did we get veggie both instead? The beef pho was the highlight of the meal with a rich flavorful broth and a generous portion of tender meat. We were pleasantly surprised by a full garnish plate with an entire sprig of fresh Thai basil! This makes the soup for me and most places in town either only offer cilantro or a few bruised/wilted basil leaves. Unfortunately, I don't even think we were out of the parking lot before my stomach started grumbling and was upset for the next 36 hours. I can't say I had food poisoning, but something certainly did not agree with me. At some point I would like to return for a bowl of the beef pho, but it may take some time to get over that negative association.

Waitress/Bartender - Whatever she was, was a complete "you know what." I had to leave, ended up going somewhere else in the Airport, which I think gave me food poisoning. So basically I blame management here for hiring a terrible waitress and through butterfly effect giving me food poisoning.

When I first moved to Philadelphia, I was told I HAD to go to Sabrina's to try their French toast. And being a person who is CRAZY about French toast, I did! I was soooo excited. The building was lovely, the service was great, but the actual French toast? Meh, it was okay; not bad, but just okay. I thought to myself, "Maybe it's just an off morning for the cook, or maybe that particular French toast special isn't what the hype is all about". So I went back again several week later, and ordered something completely different! Again, the environment was pleasant, the service was very good, but my food? Meh. Again, just meh. But, being a person who likes to give the benefit of the doubt, I thought, "Well, I didn't order the French toast this time, so maybe (again) it just wasn't the right representation of what they have to offer". So I went back AGAIN yesterday for my friend's birthday. AGAIN, the atmosphere was perfect, our server was prompt and attentive, and I was SOOO excited to order a French toast special that was right up my alley: challah bread, shredded coconut, mixed berries... HEAVEN. But when I took my first bite of this AMAZING looking feast... "Oh my God... This bread is STALE. Like, unbelievably and completely STALE. This is not fluffy, moist, warm, delicious Challah bread French toast, this is a ridiculously thick chunk of dry, crusty, undeniably STALE bread". But AGAAAAIN, I gave them benefit of the doubt and decided to take the rest of it home. Maybe I wasn't in the right mindset to enjoy it, being stressed about making my friend's birthday perfect. Maybe it was just that one piece that was less then perfect - mistakes happen - and when I got home and heated it up in the oven I would FINALLY experience the AMAZINGNESS THAT IS SABRINA'S FRENCH TOAST! Well, I'll tell you what I experienced. After a day of eating aaaall the same things as the birthday boy, EXCEPT for our orders at Sabrina's, I spent the night doubled over in pain, throwing up/generally purging my body from debilitating FOOD POISONING. NEVER. AGAIN.

First things first. The folks at Patrick's were very accommodating about my husband's garlic allergy (he gets sick for days after "too much" garlic. It's a real PITA because "too much" is a fine line. Also, he likes the stuff and pushes the limit.) So my husband's wife had a momentary lapse of judgment and ordered the BBQ Shrimp appetizer and didn't even mention the garlic thing until it was at the table. What a selfish little tart SHE is! Turns out, it's full of garlic but WONDERFUL. Hubby ate some bread. After that our server said they could prepare him something without garlic, or with less garlic. Very nice and always endears us to a place. They made him an oyster po boy and 12 hours later, hubby is still feeling fine. Whew! That po boy was HUGE and it came with some very tasty chips. I had jambalaya. It was the only "meh" part of the meal. I picked out the sausage and chicken and those were tasty but the rest was pretty tomato-y....had kind of a spanish rice flavor. I added some hot sauce and that kicked it up but on it's own, not very spicy. We both had a couple of good, cold beers and there was no room for dessert. Will have to give that a go next time.

I came here with my boyfriend during a conference as it was recommended to us by our prior uber driver. This place has been compared to Acme oyster house in terms of "best place to get oysters." I got a dozen chargrilled. They were smaller than the ones I had at acme the night before, and comparable in taste and preparation. Also got the Dragos seafood mixed grill which was lobster, shrimp, and a small Foley with corn maque choux and side of rice. The entree took way longer than expected because the chef had overlooked our filet. Because of the wait, the waiter let us know we would get comped desserts. Once we finally got our food, the rice had an eccentric taste I did not enjoy, and the filet was more rare than medium which I'd ordered. I let my waiter know and he agreed and said he'd let the chef know... The desserts were a a hot brownie a la mode and apple cobbler (we didn't get to pick the waiter just brought them over).The apple cobbler wasn't for me, and the hot brownie a la mode was pretty good, but oddly the entire plate it came on was adorned with a mountain of whipped cream, spiraled around up to a point like a Christmas tree with some chocolate syrup squeezed around. Being lactose intolerant, yet a lover of desserts and ice cream, I didn't find this worth suffering over... The waiter was super nice and personable and honest about southern oysters in terms of taste and size. Other than the wait and less than desired quality of the filet, I enjoyed the experience and would try it again in hopes for a better meal.

Last week my we thought we'd try Toyo after years of Ooka. We made a reservation since it was Saturday night. I should have been warned by the surprised voice that said, oh okay and never took a phone number. When we arrived they stared at us. A party of three came in behind and they were seated. We were sent upstairs to wait on that landing. Then our "reserved" table became the deuce by the steps. Immediately we could hear the waitress complaining about lack of communication with her coworkers. I asked a waiter if there was egg in the tempura batter since some have it and some don't. He said he was pretty sure it didn't. Pretty sure doesn't cut it with food allergies. He disappeared after a while. We watched and listened to the waitress stomp by us for 90 minutes before a guy from a hoagie shop who said they asked him to work that night, brought ONE bowl of miso soup. We asked for the second which he brought casually as if asked for another napkin. He brought more wine too. My husband never received his salad. When our sushi arrived it was perfect but but my shoes might have tasted good after two hours. The waitress said in an accusing voice, well YOU ordered sushi first-- the kitchen is fine and your food will be out in a second. Apparently the sushi chefs were overwhelmed which was hard to imagine since at one point not ONE table in the room had food on it. I really didn't need a lecture about foolishly ordering sushi in a Japanese restaurant. When the food came, my plate was loaded with Udon-/ eventually I realized there was some seafood at the bottom. Everything was loaded in salt with no other discernible flavors. And to the end the waitress stomped and careened like a diner waitress in a bad movie. THEY HAD NO TROUBLE TAKING MY MONEY. The only thing they did well that night.

After eating an appetizer of boneless buffalo wings, my husband and I had the worst food poisoning of our lives on Christmas day. The service was so terrible that when the waitress brought our food I stated out-loud "they probably poisoned our food." I should have trusted my instincts and gotten up and walked out. Do NOT eat here!

Seeing that this place is a not-for-profit AND they bring in excellent jazz acts I hate to give this place a 3-star. I was in a few weeks ago to see Kurt Elling. He was fantastic as usual. My dining experience was less so. I bought my tickets on the late side so our seats ended up back in the bar area. My bad. We expected to not be able to see very well but were surprised to find we had to strain to hear around the kitchen noises and bartender/waitstaff talking. It was quite distracting. My second dislike was the food. The waiter knew nothing about "gluten-free" but kindly offered to go talk to the chef. He came back and said I could only have the salad. Hum, thanks. It was fine but was incorrect and I had to send it back twice before they got my original order right. My date was already done eating by the time it arrived. So to recap, go for the music and get a drink...but make sure your seat is in the front room. Skip the dinner.

My gf stopped to get us 2 sandwiches yesterday. She said the girl that took her order was rude. She ordered a pork Italian seeded for her and a pork combo unseeded for me. It came to just under $20. When she got home her sandwich had no pork and mine was on a seeded roll. I called back, the girl answering the phone said there was no manager there. I described the problem and asked for 2 more sandwiches to be delivered. She said it would take 45 minutes. The sandwiches were at our house in Fishtown in 25. My sandwich still had seeds. I am not allergic, but I don't like them. It was the second time they made the same mistake. If they hadn't made the mistake again, I would have bought from there again. My gf's experience was completely ruined and will not eat from there again.

I left very unimpressed, especially considering it still felt overpriced even when we had a Restaurant.com gift certificate that gave a discount. Since neither one of us was super hungry we just skipped to entrees. His seared sea scallops were really delicious and cooked to perfection. But no side? I would rather the entrees were a few dollars more but included a side. It just felt really cheapo to ask if you want to order a side. I ordered the shellfish soffrito. Which was pretty lackluster overall, the shellfish was cooked nice, and the risotto cake was tasty. The broth was didn't really have much flavor and was super salty. That salt really killed the whole dish. It becomes almost like a stew but they don't give you a spoon. So I kept trying to eat and not spill food all over my ivory shirt...I could have asked our waiter, if he ever came back any time before we were almost done eating. I was also really suprised (not ina good way) by the menu. We are heading into fall and nothing was featured that was seasonal or local. And I thought that was part of their uniqueness? Having a gluten sensitivity I do really like they mention what is gluten free on the menu. But no gluten free salads or soups? That was disappointing. I wouldn't go back. There are better options for seafood in STL.

Wonderful meal and almost perfect service. The only issue we had was my wife bit into what we believed to be a fish scale, we had no fish in our meal. When I brought it to the waiters attention I got the impression he didn't believe us, despite the fact I was trying to show him the scale in question. We had already finished our meal when they came to check on us and they did offer to recook it, but we were done. Long story short they would have got 5 stars if there was better problem resolution and less cross contamination.
Pizza tasted kind of bland and i got food poisoning from the place. Made me sick for the night :(

One word: Horrible! I am pretty sure my boyfriend and I got food poisoning here!! We were sick all through the night. The service is bad, and the food somehow manages to be worse. Our waitress came and sat at our table to talk for half an hour about how bad the Tilted Kilt was across the street. The chicken wings are especially awful, dont even bother.

I created a Yelp account just to give this place the review it deserves. If I could give this restaurant negative stars, I would. Worst experience of my life. I completely regret buying the groupon and had I known what would come from this experience, I would have let it expire and gladly considered it wasted money. For starters, the service was absolutely horrible and slow. The food was bland and cold. And to top it off when I gave my card to pay the difference, she insisted on me paying the 9 dollar difference in cash. Luckily for her I had cash on hand and gave her a 20. After what felt like hours, she brought me back my change....I was expecting singles and a 5 with change as that would have helped with her tip, but instead she brings me back a 10 dollar bill and change. I did not feel like waiting another hour for her to break it in order for her to receive an undeserved tip. I have never left a place without tipping and I've been to some pretty bad places with unpleasant experiences, but this one takes the cake. Oh and to top it off, I ended up getting food poisoning from the crap they fed me. Also, bathrooms don't have any soap and the restaurant was completely empty (and they still took forever for everything!), I guess that should have given me a hint to run for the hills. Crappy food. Crappy service. Stay away!

Wed 10/21/15 at 11:20am. HORRIBLE upon entering, girl with long hair asked if I wanted booster seats, before I could answer she says "I hope not." I question why, she tells me she's deathly sick and "doesn't want to carry them." I said "oh that's nice." Sickly girl brings my toddler children crayons, as well as our plates, utensils and then states, "don't worry I'm not Ure waitress." Okay, well u basically just contaminated everything. My whole meal was completely ruined, I couldn't even block her comments out because her laying her head down on the wall staring at patrons. I wanted to walk out but my friend was meeting us there and we sanitized as much as possible and didn't use utensils, thank god for chicken fingers and fries. After completion we asked to speak to mgmt, he didn't even react to what she said to is, showing me that's the total norm there. I was disgusted!!!!!! Paid my bill and left. Our waitress was amazing though! Not enough to bring my star review up though. She pointed us in the direction of the $20 for two meals and appetizers and was very very apologetic to us about her behavior. The newtown applebees location was my fav go to place with kids, but after this horrendous experience, I vow to never enter anywhere ever again. Especially after reading consumer complaints on the applebees corporate office. They will be put of business soon enough.

By far the worst sonic I've been to in NJ . I came by for a sonic m&ms blast , when I got home there was peanut butter cups in my ice cream . If I had a peanut allergy I would have had an allergic reaction, waited a while and I came back again for the same thing. Asked for no whip cream , I receive a blast with whip cream I kindly asked the young man to make another one , all he did was scoop it out . Lol again what if I had an allergy to whip cream you don't just scoop something out you make another one because at the END OF THE DAY I AM A CUSTOMER AND I AM ALWAYS RIGHT

Horrible. Absolutely horrible. My family used to frequent this place long ago and it was always delicious food at a reasonable price but over the last couple years they have hit rock bottom. I truly don't know how they are still open. I work within walking distance and have tried it for lunch and have got food poisoning TWICE from this establishment... absolutely pathetic. Not to mention I had an 11 year old girl take my to go order for my business because apparently she is in charge of running the register..... seriously?!

Highly over-rated steak on a stick. I had high hopes for Fogo after experiencing Estancia Churrascaria in Austin, Tx & hearing Fogo was the best Brazilian steakhouse in Philly. Sadly Fogo doesn't hold a candle and is not good enough to even warrant a return visit. The lay-out of the restaurant is designed for maximum turn-over with tightly packed tables. It felt too crowded even on an off time on Sunday with reservations. The chicken and sausage gauchos visit your table every 3 times to every one gaucho wielding steak. Not long into the meats I noticed a weird unpleasant itching sensation on my gums. I don't have any known allergies but I'm assuming it was an adverse reaction to the spices. The only meat I really enjoyed was the Alacatra (top sirloin) and filet. Everything else was tough and fatty. The salad bar was limited to Bibb, spring mix, and pre-made Caesar salad & vinaigrette dressings. I was hoping to make a blue cheese wedge with the bacon but no iceburg or dressing. The watermelon feta salad was mushy and gross and the asparagus too large to be tender. The only upside to the salad bar for me was the manchego cheese and the aged barrel cheddar. The sides and rolls were standard for a Brazilian steakhouse. I was hopeful the menu would have after dinner drink Licor 43 with the option to be toasted but not so. Finally I'd say valet is chancey and slow. While waiting for our car we witnessed a gentleman with a gorgeous Escalade being told his car was hit & what he would need to do. He seemed calm but I'm guessing he hadn't peeked at the damage in the back like we did. No plans or desire to return.

Best French fries I've ever had!!! We chose this place based on reviews and it was pretty good. I didn't give more stars because both mine and my hubby's orders weren't exactly correct and there was no offer to make right. We were Really hungry and waited a while for our food so didn't want to wait again. I asked for my salad without croutons because I'm gluten free and they were in there - had to pick out. Burger came with an egg on it and I don't eat eggs so I know i didn't get what i ordered but i slid it off and ate the burger any way. The Mac n cheese was to die for. The vibe of this place is pretty cool but I'm not sure I'd say it's all that. It's in the trendy touristy area. The portions are large so some dishes are probably ample for sharing. But the fries......gotta have your own because you won't want to share

The food can be good & is inexpensive but they are not careful with their food. I have had food poisoning 2x and then a month ago (yes i was going to risk it again) got the chicken wrap & the chicken was raw. They need to change their salsa (it's sometimes fizzy from fermentation). I know they are putting out a lot of food but there's no excuse for raw chicken.

This used to be our go-to spot for burgers and beers. Needless to say NEVER again.
