Burgers were not cooked at all, chili just might be the worst any of us ever had, and one person in our party had an allergic reaction that broke out on their face. The whole meal was highlighted with a dude puking in the parking lot. Do yourself a favor and pick another place. Dadz is just Badz!!
Ate here then spent the next three days dealing with food poisoning. Feels like someone punched me in the stomach. I guess the quality has gone down since everyone eats there now.

The Hubby and I did a Delmar Loop date night last night - dinner, movie and desserts. We started the evening at Nico for dinner. I was very curious about this place after reading the reviews on Yelp...and I gotta say, I just don't get it. From a location/ atmosphere/ people watching perspective it is great. But from a food perspective (and that is really why we are there, non?) it left both of us very unimpressed. I immediately let our server know I was allergic to gluten and she pulled out prepared handwritten notes of what I could have, as is and with modifications. For this, I was impressed. Since we were planning to head down the road for a hefty dessert after dinner we skipped appetizers and went straight to dinner. I decided on the Seafood Saffron Risotto. It was like no risotto I'd ever had before. Not creamy - it really was more of a rice pilaf. The textures of the scallops seemed damaged by the defrosting process and the clams were just, well, gross. The Hubby got the Mushroom Ravioli and thought it was just OK. He thought a 2.5 rating was more in order for his dish. I think The Hubby said it best. As we were walking away we both agreed it wasn't worth going back. He described the food as "upscale presentation of poorly executed food".

The sushi was delicious! My favorite one was the spanish roll. It had a thin slice of lemon atop that added a delicious zesty pop! All of our sushi was outstanding. It's the only place that I trust to feed me raw fish. While we were having our dinner a girl in the table next to us vomited on the floor. The staff just walked around! No one was prompt to clean it up. It took about five minutes for someone to come sweep it up. Bear with me this gets better; the stomach fluids remained on the floors because no one bothered to mop it up. It became impossible to not acknowledge the stench of fresh vomit 10 feet away while chewing on uncooked fish. The staff joked and complained of how bad it smelled with no regard whatsover about the customers finishing their dinner one table over. Thank you for the 2x1 deal...see and smell vomit during one night out for dinner. Warmest regards

The atmosphere and live music was great, the staff was friendly and the food was hot and fresh. The next morning however anyone who had the fresh grouper (tacos and market meal) is now sick with some serious food poisoning. The waitress mentioned they recently changed chefs. Very disappointing for my family who are regulars there. We won't be going back.

My friend and I came in for brunch on Sunday and we both got sick that night, with what I am guessing was food poisoning. We both had ordered eggs benedict. The food came out rather quickly but the eggs were overcooked (basically hard-boiled eggs). When the waitress asked how everything was, my friend pointed out that the eggs were overcooked. They then took our plates right away without even asking if we wanted to order something else from the menu or have it taken off altogether. They just assumed we wanted them to remake it, which was not the case. Anyway, they brought our food back out with the eggs (which I suspect were) now under-cooked. They had put hot eggs over-top of our original food which was cold as ice underneath. Even the hollandaise sauce was cold and coagulated. I could barely finish my meal. We both ended up having to take off work the next day from being so sick. We will never be returning and recommend anyone looking for a place to eat to go elsewhere. I am still dealing with the aftermath of it all.

Honestly, the food is good, but, in my opinion, overrated. Although different, Commander's Palace and Bayona are much better, and so is the service. We ordered the paneed rabbit and smothered chicken. As noted, both were good, but not great. We waited over an hour to be seated. I also felt the staff was somewhat lackadaisical as to my nut allergy. I enjoyed my meal, and so did my date, but I wouldn't rush back.

Eat their oysters but be wary: Yes, the food's extraordinary, But the prices are quite scary. Do not eat the shrimp pasta: it's quite bland, and could make you ill. Food poisoning is very unpleasant. It is even more unpleasant when it ruins your evening and derails your vacation plans. As for the rest: The restaurant atmosphere is posh, but not unbearably so. The waitstaff at Drago's are pleasant and polite, but weekends are busy enough that the wait for service becomes annoyingly long. (Go during the week if you choose to go at all.) Eat at your own risk! UPDATE: (12/2016) My dinner partners insisted on Dragos... I can honestly say I gave it my level best, but even though it's been a year, I felt vaguely nauseous sitting in the place. (Eating anything with shrimp or oysters was completely out of the question.) A shame; they said the food was good..

FOOD POISONING: Do not eat here. I purchased their general tso's chicken and brown rice lunch special. Though it was cheap, the chicken was undercooked and the rice was old. Their wonton soup was nasty as well. I'm not sure if it was one thing I ate, or a combination, but I am 100% sure that New Imperial Chinese Resturant gave me food poisoning. The pain was not worth the price.

This place was a bizarre experience. When my family and I arrived I was surprised to see that the menu called for people cooking their own meals. I had a problem with this for several reasons. First the grill was not clean. Do I want to dine out and cook my own meal? No I want to take a break from that. I am not talking about cooking it by handing it to the chef, I am talking about actually walking across the room and cooking it on a tiny grill. There was not an adjustment button to control the flames. How can I cook a good steak on a one temp low temp grill? On top of cooking my own meal the idea of cleaning a restaurant grill first before cooking the meal doesn't sound appealing. . Second, why on earth would there be the option of chicken, seafood, or steak to cook on one grill next to each other. That is a recipe for food poisoning. third - the salad bad that we decided to go with -out of safety- turned out to be comical. Iceberg lettuce mix with the choices of cucumbers, black peppercorns ( that looked like seeds) chickpeas, beets, carrots, and several dressings. There were no tomatoes. I do have to say the croutons were delicious. Then the other station was the backed potato and red beans. I ended up trying to fill up on the potatoes. I went back for a second and they were out, but after a good laugh with my sister the potato tray we refilled. The staff is very friendly but the inside of the restaurant needs some updates. My sister actually shut off the lights to our dinner table when she accidentally tripped over the power cord and unplugged it. This really wasn't my scene.

Went into the Cracker Barrel on Long Hollow Pike today for lunch for my boss any myself. I placed an order with a waitress at about 11:15am. Was told by the cheerful waitress it should be about 15 minutes. I ordered a fried chicken salad (No tomato or onion, with extra cheese and ranch dressing) and a low carb double meat breakfast (three eggs, and bacon with sliced tomatoes and toast). At 11:45 I was asked by a manager the name on my to-go order and she then promptly sent a waitress to check on my order. There was relatively no wait to be seated in the dining area so I wouldn't say they were slammed but steady busy. The waitress comes to me and says "They are putting it together now." I said "It's been 30 minutes." Her response was "Oh, really?" Ten more minutes go by...still no food. So I went back and got the manager. The manager comes back out and tells me she's sorry and hands me a bag of food. The salad came out with tomatoes and no extra cheese, and I didn't notice until I got to work that my meal was the standard double breakfast so there was no tomatoes and extra items I did not want. But I didn't check it before I left, so that's on me. I really hate complaining but it was a very simple order that should have only taken 15 minutes per the waitress that took my order. How do you take 40 minutes to do the order and still get it wrong? I caught the salad and they fixed it, only for me to get to work and there were still tomatoes in it (glad my boss isn't allergic to tomatoes), and my food be cold as if it had been sitting for a while.

As a former restaurant manager myself the cross contamination alone on the slicer is something to be alarmed about. cutting different meats without cleaning and sanitizing the slicer in between is a big no-no. Needless to say I got sick off of the food I got from there last time and I won't be back. Not overly impressed with the selections either.

My criteria for a good restaurant may be slightly different than the norm. Lots of restaurants nowadays have gluten free menus, but they're often very limited and there is a serious lack of knowledge of cross contamination issues. When I looked into whether Maggianos had a gf menu, I ran across some blurbs about how they didn't have one but they could have the chef come out and talk to you. Oy. I was having flashbacks of my trip to Orlando. "We don't have a gf menu, but the chef will come talk to you" is the standard down there and led to endless frustrations. You have no knowledge of what gluten free dishes will be available prior to committing and a couple of chefs offered no help at all. They would ask "What food do you like?" How on earth am I supposed to answer that? I like lots of foods! After no suggestions, I'd finally say "Can you do nachos?" No. "Can you do this salad?" No. I'd ask what they've made for gluten free customers in the past and they'd offer something generic like "Steak is gluten free". They'd start looking annoyed and I'd give up and order plain grilled chicken--a meal I could've eaten for a tenth of the price at McDonalds. So naturally, I'm hesitant to eat here. Boy was I surprised! The chef comes out to talk to me and informed me that about 95% of the menu could be made gluten free. Now I understand why they don't have a gluten free menu--the gluten free menu is essentially the whole menu! It was awesome. The chef explained that pretty much the only things that weren't gluten free were the things that are obviously not gluten free like the breaded chicken or lasagna. Most of the pasta dishes could be made with the gluten free pasta they carry and they can custom make dishes as well. The rest of my family was thrilled with their meals as well. My picky daughter had lasagna and raved about it. My husband loved his meal as well. Highly recommended for gluten free dining.

Pei Wei is an asian-fusion diner quick service restaurant chain. The reason why I want to write this review is because I wanted to call attention to their gluten free menu. I've eaten there on several occasions, and they have a few GF dishes including hot entrees and salads that are yummy and readily available every time I'm there. It's great. It is becoming a big lunchtime favorite of mine. Try to the Pei Wei spicy chicken - comes with sugar snap peas and carrots with nice big chunks of chicken. A yummy alternative to the usual lunch salad indeed!

We come to this dennys often. Probably 2+ times a month. This past visit was horrid, and I'll never return. We arrived at 9pm. We were sat, our server came, took our drink order, and I ordered an appetizer at that time. Our drinks come 5 minutes later. 20 minutes go by, after him being to the table next to ours multiple times, and still no appetizer, or an offer of refills. Another 10 minutes go by, he brings us our appetizer. Luke warm, and stale chips. Whatever. So we place our dinner order. By this time, it's pushing 9:40pm. Simple food. Chicken strip dinner for me, with fries and mashed potatoes, and a slam burger for my husband. Finally, at 10:30, we get our food. ICE COLD FOOD. We waited another 15 MINUTES until out waiter finally came back over. We asked for our FIRST refills of the night, 10 mins go by. He comes to the table and says "can I get you guys a refill??".... I told he we already asked for them, and we now wanted to see a manager. All the manager did was DISCOUNT my meal. We didn't get out of this plus until 11:10pm. Worst part, my husband woke up the next morning with food poisoning. Needless to say, this man got NO tip, and lost loyal customers. Never ever again.

Ordered from here a few times in the last 6 months and thought it was decent for Chinese delivery. 2 nights ago, I ordered beef chow mein & chicken lo mein. Seemed OK, nothing out of the ordinary. I awoke at 6am the next day vomiting with extreme diarrhea. This reoccurred every few hours until I had nothing left inside of me to purge out of my system. I haven't been able to eat since and have been stuck in bed with cold sweats. No doubt where the food poisoning came from since that was the only thing I'd eaten all day. Funny thing is, another place nearby had a bad inspection recently, so I decided to stick with this one. Don't make the same mistake as me. You're better off starving than ordering from this place. 1 star because it wouldn't let me do zero.

Had the chicken jadore and it was HORRIBLE! I almost threw up in my mouth because it smelled horrible. The worst part of it all is when the waitress knows you are not enjoying your meal (full plate with knife and fork across the meal) and you know she knows it's horrible but she doesn't have the decency to ask if there was anything wrong with my meal.... I know French food quite well because I travel to Ex en Provence quite a bit and this is an insult to even remotely call it French food. On the good side the "French" fries were well prepared, but I hope they know it never originated from France .

Yeah folks....you know the heading on your Yelp search that says "CVS Pharmacy 24"? Well, this pharmacy is listed under that heading, which is why I picked it. Now I'm not sure if the hours of operation listed their actual hours over six months ago when I switched to this pharmacy over Walgreens. Sure enough, though, it's there now: 8am-8pm.....NOT 24/7. So why are they under this heading? Because the store, not the pharmacy, is open 24/7. Now, is this a CVS goof, or did Yelp trip up? I don't know....I do know that my face looks like a cabbage, due to an allergic reaction. I also know that when a doctor from my office called in a prescription for prednisone, I couldn't pick it up because my pharmacy was CLOSED. So, I call at 8:05am & tell them my situation....they said to call back in 1/2 an hour. I told them my eyes were almost swollen shut...that didn't get anyone to check the answering machine for the doctor's call while I was on the phone with them....that would've been considerate, I think. Well, I just called them back & my rx is ready, thankfully....that gives them 2 stars instead of 1. The moral of this tale, my friends: when looking for a 24-hr. pharmacy, call them & actually speak with a human. It's sad to say, but even Yelp can't be trusted completely.

We have never had a problem here until Sunday, I ordered the salmon in an effort to be healthy, later that evening I was very sick and basically had food poisoning, I think the fish was undercooked because my husband ordered a steak medium well and his steak was medium almost rare in the middle, I talked with the managers and they made it right, thank you so much for your help !

Had a strange visit. The food was great and the service was good. The issue is that we consistently had to remind them to get us the extra things that came with the entree. Brunch ends at 2, we came at 1:30, and then learned we could only order off of EITHER the brunch OR lunch menu. Our server said there was a special event and that was why we couldn't order off both menus...not sure why since other people ordered off of it so everything was already prepped. I ordered a banana french toast, and then got a date cinnamon roll with no notice. It was sugary and delicious, but (see picture), was indisputably NOT french toast, nor contained banana. I don't have a problem with subs, but just let me know in case I'm allergic or just don't feel like what you have left in the kitchen. The bf and I both ordered entrees, and he ordered a side of batata. We received our entrees, but nothing else. Halfway through our meal, we asked about the batata. My guess is that the kitchen staff forgot what goes with what, because our server seemed to remember, but they then had to start it from scratch and we were done eating before it came out. We also had to ask in order to get the side of fruit that comes with the meal, but it was brought out quickly once we mentioned it. But at least this gave us a chance to order a shake. I see why they emphasize burgers, shakes and shawarma. We ordered the chocolate tahini shake. SO GOOD! It was nice to enjoy a shake that wasn't sweet to the point of inducing sugar coma. It was really allowed you to taste the subtlety of the tahini flavor, a slightly bitter greek yogurt taste, and the balance of the chocolate, nuts and vanilla ice cream. All delicious just like last time, we'll be back.

I'm sure this would be "a hit" for any vegetarian or vegan who had no food-related, health concerns. It's just not a staff that's trained in answering questions about content or allergies. What I expected to be safest and closest to whole food, may be the reason for today's migraine.

A colleague and I jumped in here real quick on a short break from work. The menu is impressive in options and service was friendly. Unfortunately, some ignorance of our food allergies meant orders came out incorrect. My bun was definitely not gluten free but thankfully my allergy is not severe and a bite of the bun I got would only cause minimal distress. We would have said something but didn't see our server for quite some time so I just dug in and ate around the items I knew I couldn't have. The food was decent but we were wholly unimpressed by the absence of our server and the lack of attention to detail of our order.

Well, where to begin?? I am a minimum once a week customer at Mai Thai and generally the service is fantastic and so is the good (with the occasional mistake) but today has made it so I will never be returning to Mai Thai again. I called in a to go order around 7 pm, I could tell the hostess was new so I made sure to specify everything extremely clear, I ordered a taro boba tea not blended, panaeng curry with no bell peppers due to allergy, green curry fried rice with no eggplant and add potatoes, and a green goddess roll. I get to Mai Thai in the 30-45 min time span I was told to arrive in. The hostess goes to grab my food and the owner comes out and hands it to me and says "I will be right back with your smoothie" I replied with "oh no, not a smoothie just taro boba tea not blended please." And he says "ok" when the owner comes back and hands it to me it is blended! I said "oh sorry I asked for it not blended," then he turns to the hostess and asks her about it and she tells him that I did not specify that and I proceed to say that I did, he offers to have it corrected.When the owner comes back there is no boba in my BOBA tea so I asks if he could add the boba to it...this is where it got ugly, the owner looked at me as if I were asking something outlandish to have boba in my boba tea. So I say "can you please just add boba to it," he continues to look at me like I am crazy and tells me to calm down (I was completely calm, just asking for my boba) so I tell him that I am calm and then he tries to grab the food out of my hand and says "I will give you a refund" and I said "no, this is what I ordered I just want to correct thing." So finally after arguing with him he brings back my boba tea with boba. Unfortunately when we got home our order was incorrect the fried rice had eggplant in it and sweet potatoes not the regular potatoes we ordered, my green goddess roll was completely mangled and my curry had bell peppers in it which I did not notice until I had been eating it which caused my throat to swell and entire face to puff up. I guess I should have just let him take the food and give me a refund, it would have saved me an epi-pen and a whole bunch of discomfort. I'm sorry Mai Thai but I guess this is the end of a very long relationship we have had together.

I was excited to try this place. Never Again. We go in, there us one empty table and NO sign saying wait to be seated. After we sit down at a 6 person table, other people at a nearby 4 person table leave. The waitress comes and informs us that after she cleans a smaller table we will need to move. We left. It was so rude. Two or three months later, we wanted to give this place one more try, so we went back. The restaurant was basically empty, but we were seated at a cramped table right near the door, where we would be blasted by cold air every time the door opened. I went to the restroom and there was dried vomit on the bathroom floor. Now, I realize that this restroom could be shared by multiple businesses, but I personally thought that if I knew my customers were using a restroom for a restaurant, I would want it to be clean. I went back to join my family at the table, and I opened the menu left on my service plate, and saw that it was splattered with debris from various meals. I asked my husband if his menu was dirty, it was, and my daughters' were as well. On the back of the menu that was TOUCHING MY PLATE, there was crap that was about to flake off. I said lets go, and we left. If you choose to eat here, then good luck; I wish you well. I will NEVER go back.

No No No! Never Ever again. WARNING:: extremely high % chance of food poisoning. Un-fresh fish, un-fresh rice, and un-fresh lettuce. On top of that they're rude as Heck!. Will never give them anymore of my business. They're simply trying to get over on people, serving the lowest quality of food that they can find. I should have known, as soon as we walked in my 8 year old daughter complained of the smell. Disappointed that I have to give them even 1 star.

So here's the thing, I really want to LOVE Iron Hill, but I just can't. I used to love their french fries with that awesome rosemary garlic mayo dip. Hell, everyone I know wanted to go for beers there because that meant splitting an order of those amazing fries. And then, bam, they stopped making them. Maybe because it was the cheapest item on the menu? But after they were gone, we stopped going there as a happy hour option. I've had the chicken pot pie (Boston Market is better, sadly). I've ordered burgers, I always think they will be amazeballs coming from a steakhouse style restaurant like this and they just suck. They are always cooked wrong and cold when they come out, with cold cheese. It's just pathetic. So I kept going back for dinner and ordering random things because I like the location and the vibe and they have some nice beers on tap...and I stopped when my sister and I both ended up with wickedly horrific food poisoning from a pasta dish (no longer on the menu) last year. With so many other awesome food choices in the area, I just can't continue subjecting myself and my culinary companions to this place in the hopes of finding something worthwhile.

So far the service is terrible. We are thinking of leaving. Actually we are leaving. After waiting for 20 minutes for someone to confirm that there are gluten free items on the menu we sat down and waited another 10 for a server. And then the server asked if we wanted bread. Did she listen to any part of the conversation?

I hate BBQ. HATE. (Don't you judge me) So when the BF insisted that we get some "authentic St. Louis BBQ" for dinner, I threw up in my mouth a little. Then panicked at the thought of not finding anything on the menu that I would enjoy eating. However, at Bogarts, I treated myself to a "sausage fatty" which is even more delish than it sounds, my friends. It is essentially a long, thick slab of sausage meat (minds out of the gutter, kids) that has been smoked and sliced for my culinary pleasure. It was SO tender that it just melted in my mouth. I did try a few bites in each of Bogarts' signature sauces (ranging from thick/sweet to bitter/tangy)... didn't much care for any of them since I'm not a fan of BBQ, but I can appreciate that they offered a variety of options for BBQ connoisseurs of varying palatial preferences. My BF got potato chips as a side item (which were akin to crack), and we learned that Bogarts gets them from a local potato chip manufacturer. I dig that they're leveraging and supporting local resources. Prices are quite reasonable (about $10/person). Seating in the restaurant is quite limited, but there are picnic tables just outside.

Sitting here with FOOD POISONING after eating ponzio's takeout (violent vomiting). I would give no stars if it were possible. I called the restaurant and the manager told me that it could not have been their food. Unfortunately this was all I had to eat today so it had to have been the food. He said sorry and disconnected. No offer for a refund. Really disappointing.

oh Pizzalchick. Have to admit that we drove passed a few times when we first came to town laughing at such an awful name. Then visited with some friends after a day of hot springing. I was impressed with the salad and that they had gluten free pizza, but not the price. Wife's gluten free is much better, but she's not always willing to make it. We were once brought out an extra salad and the owner came out looking for where the salad was dropped off at. He informed us that they were just going to give us a $9 salad b/c they messed up, but made us feel guilty about it. Fred Meyer's rotisserie chicken's taste better and are cooked fresh every day for 1/2 the price. For a hippy, peace and love kind of a place, where is the love? Listen to what most are saying... drop the price a couple bucks and it's all good.

Let me be clear. If i were to review this place on their coffee and dessert crepes alone, they would probably get 4 stars. Based on my last visit, I wish they had a zero star rating. I ordered the Turkey Avocado crepe. After one bite I spit it out and put the plate on the edge of the table to signal the waitress (which after waiting 10 minutes still didn't come over- despite the fact that we were 1 or 2 tables in the entire place). The bacon in my crepe was completely raw! It was literally as if the bacon was taken out of the package and put on the crepe before it was served to me. My husband had the buffalo chicken crepe. He is a pretty fast eater and hungry. He scarfed down half the portion while telling me it didn't taste very good. He vomited about 15 minutes later... I have no idea what ingredients were used or how the sandwich was prepared. But based on the uncooked bacon in my sandwich, I could only assume the buffalo chicken or it's ingredients were prepared improperly. Besides the fact that there's a good chance we both could of got sick from this place, the service is awful. The waitress seemed overwhelmed with just 2 tables and the crepes are made 1 at a time. That blows my mind considering this is a place specializing in crepes!!! I;d love to know who invested in this poor excuse of a business plan. Oh and btw if you plan on checking this place out, it's closed Sunday's....genius. I personally know of several people that made attempts to go here on Sunday's to find that it was closed. Clearly this business owner is clueless. Otherwise, the interior is adorable and has lots of potential. My advice would be, nix the savory crepes, stick to desserts and coffees and stay open all weekend, and maybe invest in another $15 crepe maker so you can actually make more then 1 at a time.

If I I could give this place no stars, I would. Service chaotic and terrible. I ordered egg drop soup. How hard is that? After 20 minutes I still was standing at the counter while people screamed at each other in the kitchen. I finally walked out after I watched the chef use his ungloved hands to cross contaminate vegetables and uncooked meat. It may be cheap but I certainly won't go back.

Came here for brunch, and it's a really great place, the service was great and the food was very good. We were a large party, and they accommodated us wonderfully. However, it's important to inform anybody with celiac disease: While they do have "gluten free" options on the menu, everything is cooked on the same grill, using the same utensils, so a gluten free crepe will be cross contaminated. My partner was limited to ordering the soup, which was delivered with gluten free toast that was also toasted on the same grill as everything else, so we had to return the toast. The staff was effusive in their apologies, and I believe they actually comped us the soup. Everything else about the experience was good. This is just a warning for people who may have celiac, or have friends with celiac. This will not be a good option for you.

Had a choice between this Restuarant and R2L for my wife's birthday. I saw the high reviews and figured this would be a great experience. I also thought since it was more expensive than Chima the service and food would be better. My wife loves Chima and I was told this is a step up. Wrong! First, the restaurant is beautiful with nice wood trim and pretty wine racks. We made reservations and was seated promptly. We decided to put the salad bar on pause as we wanted to get right into the meats. I was not impressed with the beef or chicken. The guys with food was giving us big pieces which didn't allow us to taste other varieties. I felt like I was wasting food. The lamb chop was terrible. I love lamb chops. We ate a piece of beef that had a weird taste. The chicken also had a weird taste. My wife got sick and she didn't eat much. While in the bathroom she their was another lady who had an issue (vomiting) with the food. I didn't have some issues right away. It wasn't a great experience. The service was okay. We noticed that the staff (everyone) don't smile at all. Didn't feel level of attention was up to our expectations for a meal over $50. Our waitress was effiecie to but showed no concern that my wife was ill. She did present her with complimentary dessert for her birthday. It was a nice touch. My wife's experience was horrible. My experience was that the food was cold, not tasty, and not that much variety of meats. The seafood was a la carte. For $53 pp it should be included. Chima provides salmon. This restaurant is highly overrated. I enjoyed rodizio and Chima much more. I would not recommend this place to anyone. There are better options for Brazilian steakhouse and high end Restuarants.

If there was a 0 star option i would consider it, as soon as i walked in the decor was rustic and could appeal to be nice if it didn't look like it had been untouched for 100 years. Although hesitant to walk out i decided to sit down and order. Me and friend order water and there is a dead bug in water and it tasted like it was that water that you shouldn't drink in Mexico. Finally i order turkey and my friend orders chicken, no problem with service at all. Food comes promptly. I take two bites and decide to just eat the fries, he proceeds to tell me it tasted like "dog food". Long story short me and my friend may or may not have food poisoning and if not that then my stomach is seriously messed up. I have a strong stomach so this surprises me. I wonder how long the meat had sat due to lack of business. As a person who eats out normally twice a day i think this tops the worst restaurant list in my book. I would not recommend this restaurant.

This place is very accommodating for gluten free allergies. TJ came out to personally discuss our gluten free options. He explained thoroughly specific items that need to be avoided like anything fried due to cross contamination. Even the children's menu can be made gf! The kids had the pancakes and grilled cheese which were delicious. Both said its the best they ever had! I had the monte cristo modified with gluten free bread and it was amazing! Tj said it would be an experiment and it turned out so yummy! We will be definitely visiting every time we come to Reno!

First of all, men don't bother. I mean maybe gluten intolerance is only a "woman thing" in the South. I'm admittedly from the west coast where men can be openly gluten free without discrimination. This place, though, is very much oriented for the females. My husband wasn't sure if he was supposed to be there. Second, the atmosphere, besides being confusingly girly was also very cheap. The plastic white chairs were covered in dirt, the white curtain string things were turning brown and the place looked thrown together with less attention than a quick LA pop up. I mean if you're going to play off woman stereotypes, make the place look like a woman has actually been there and clean it up and make it look like you wouldn't be embarrassed when Mom visits, for heaven's sake. And yet the food was trying so hard to look classy. I mean leafy greens in my sweet potatoe fries? Who the **** ever looked at fries and thought, "I wish this was a salad"? No one. No one ever. Plus leafy greens + hot fries = wilted gross crap that's hard to pick out of my fries because I did not want it there in the first place. And their fries are not meant to be dipped in anything. You have to request any kind of sauce, which is only ketchup, mayonnaise or plain yellow mustard. And the fries are so thin and spindly that I finally gave up and ate those ****ers with a fork like a ****ing salad. I was so sad... And let's talk condiments. I ordered a burger as did my husband and we asked for "all the condiments" since their offerings were so few and basic. I was extra disappointed when they brought out 2 tiny tin cups with maybe a 1/2 tbsp of mustard and maybe a 1/2 tbsp of mayonnaise. There wasn't enough for both of us and it was obviously the cheap basics so we didn't even bother. The service was okay at best. She barely mumbled 5 words to us and didn't write down our orders. So when my husband asked for a fried egg added to his burger, he did not get it. Lost upsell for them. As my husband pointed , no one is ever impressed by your ability to remember their orders. They're only nervous that you'll miss something. And she did. So now we're just pissed. For drinks, we requested sparkling water and were unceremoniously handed two unopened bottles. I've worked in the industry and in restaurants, you give them an opened bottle and a glass to drink it from. I felt like I was at a dive bar drinking from the bottle. The only reason this place gets any stars is because the GF bun was decent and the burger was perfectly cooked. And since I was out to get a good burger that night, at least I got that.

I ordered a plain burger with bacon only. When it was brought to the table it had peanut butter on it. I told them that I ordered a plain burger and was allergic to peanuts. After being told "well this is what she put in the system, are you sure you didn't order this?" he finally took it back. When a new one was brought out I had my wife take a look at it because I suspected there was still peanut butter on it...and I was right. They pretty much just scrapped off what they could and tried to serve it to me. We called the chef back and again explained to them that I was allergic to peanut butter and if I hadn't checked I would have wound up in the hospital. He apologized and said he would cook me a fresh one himself. By this time my entire party was pretty much finished with their meals. We explained the issue with the waitress, and they still charged us for the burger. Everyone else in my party loved their burgers but I couldn't take the risk of coming back here again and neither would they.

If I could rate this solely on atmosphere, it would receive a 5 star for sure. The view of Channelside was gorgeous and the dining inside was beautiful as well. However, the aesthetic could not save us from the long waits between courses and the food poisoning that would ensue afterwards for two of the three members of my party. (Still, I am suffering as I type this review.) The server was nice enough but still there was an extended wait even between being greeted and receiving our drinks. Would not recommend.

First, let me start by saying that I am neither gluten free or vegan. However , I don't mind trying gf/df baked goods bc my friend is gf/df and we try places all the time when we're together. As a matter of fact she is the one that wanted me to stop and try this while visiting Philly. Needless to say I had to text her a bad report. I must say out of all the gf/df bakeries I have tried Sweet Freedom was the worse and I have had some good gf/df baked goods before. To me gf/df is just a healthier version of the regular sugary goods we all love. Yes the texture and taste differ some but it shouldn't be completely altered. I got the chocolate cupcake and chocolate chip cookie. Both were awful and gritty tasting. The chocolate cupcake had a very awkward taste and the frosting was a little stiff not very smooth and creamy.

I can prepare better Indian fare in my sleep. Not only that, but it took them two hours to deliver our food, even though I only live a few blocks away, and they even brought some wrong items. It took them another 90 minutes to pick up the wrong food and bring back the correct ones that were missing, and they tasted like vomit. To be fair, I have spent a considerable amount of time in the U.K., where a good curry can be found in any town or city there, so I am spoiled when it comes to Indian.

This last visit to Five Guys burger, the music was so loud, the employees couldn't, hear any customers, so it was hard to order. I am gluten free so I ordered one without the bun supposedly lettuce wrapped. When we got home my burger was dry and had no lettuce or anything on it, the bacon was so burnt I couldn't eat it. I spent $7 for one tiny dry patty. Too noisy. Too expensive. I'm not going to be back.

This is my fav! I go the their sushi boats next door. Until yesterday... When I arrived there was no one there and they had just opened yet there was sushi going around in the boats. The first piece I took tasted sea salty and just plain gross. Ended up w food poisoning throwing up until 4am with chills and a high fever. That day I saw a steal bowl of raw fish on the counter but thought nothing of it.... Not to mention had to wait 20 min for the check because the waitresses were too busy chatting w each other and giving each other back messages right across the table from us turning a blind eye. Super unprofessional! Not going back.

I love that Chef Ron offers a gluten free gumbo! So thumbs up for the option. The gumbos are solid and well-prepared, but wasn't wow'd. Had to order a whole separate side of potato salad for my gumbo instead of having an option of rice or a scoop of potato salad. Great little solid spot for gumbo though.
The place is nice, the staff is friendly, and the food tastes good. But I got food poisoning from the beef, so.... 1 star. I'll try the chicken next time.

My girlfriend and I went here tonight on a Groupon deal. Having never been here before, we were excited to be getting a chance to have some Greek food on the cheap. And actually, the meal started out really well. We ordered the Salata Caprese appetizer -- alternating layers of baked feta cheese and tomatoes on top of a bit of pesto with a dusting of dried oregano. The pesto was a bit on the tame side and the tomatoes reminded us that it is winter after all, but overall we really liked it. The trouble started when the waitress asked us for our entree order. My girlfriend has a gluten intolerance and can't have anything with wheat, so we asked our waitress what we should look at. She ruled out the pita bread and the pasta, as well as anything that came on a bun or had filo dough in it. I added, "And anything with bechamel, right?" She looked perplexed, and said that bechamel is a cheese sauce so we shouldn't worry. Now, having made bechamel before myself, I can tell you that a basic bechamel sauce is made from three ingredients: butter, flour, and cream. Accordingly, I expressed some hesitation, but she insisted. I told her that if she could make absolutely sure that the bechamel sauce did not have any flour in it, then we would have an order of the bechamel-topped moussaka, as well as the braised lamb shank in red sauce. Upon consulting the kitchen, she returned to tell us that indeed, the bechamel did have flour in it. One of the kitchen staff got her attention, however, and apparently told her that they had made a mistake: the bechamel would be safe -- they had looked at the list of ingredients. Perhaps needless to say, when the moussaka came out, it was immediately clear to me that it had flour in it, just like normal bechamel does (or perhaps I am wrong, in which case I have no idea what they're serving people under the guise of bechamel sauce). It was okay -- I just gave my girlfriend the lamb and we were on our way. Unfortunately, neither dish was that great. The moussaka was a pretty standard example of its kind, but it wasn't particularly well-seasoned and didn't impress me with its flavor. It came with some decent potatoes, some veggies that didn't really have much to distinguish them, and some straightforward rice pilaf. The lamb came with the same sides, but it wasn't the highest-quality meat and the red sauce was unrefined -- too acidic and not well-suited to the lamb. When we were finished, we asked about dessert and found out that we couldn't get the only gluten free one on the menu because they had run of yogurt (at a Greek restaurant!). Ultimately, this wasn't a nightmare experience or anything like that. Our waitress was actually really friendly, and although the food wasn't great, it's not like we found a severed toe in it (actually, my girlfriend pulled a hair out of her mouth at one point, but it could definitely have been mine). The restaurant itself was attractive and well-kept, the portion sizes were good, and the menu hit on all the standards. It's just that the food wasn't very good, and the staff clearly had no idea what they were actually serving people -- a pretty gravely bad sign in my book. Given the other perfectly-good Greek options in Tucson (particularly Opa! for this level of dining), I just would advise looking elsewhere.

We dined at Bob Evans on Wednesday evening, June 20, 2018, party of 4. My 12 year old daughter ordered the chicken tender meal - 3 tenders and fries. She ate one and a half of the tenders, I finished off the rest after I had already eaten my meal. As soon as we arrived home from dinner, less than one hour after eating, I was on the toilet. She was up all night vomiting and with diarrhea. I was spared of the vomiting, but have been in and out of the bathroom over night and appears to be continuing this morning. We both woke up with lingering stomach pain. She'll miss a day of pre-paid summer camp (non-refundable) and I'll have to struggle through a day at work. The worst thing a restaurant can do to a customer is mishandle food and make them sick. I have had cold food, mediocre quality dishes, and poor customer service, but making a customer ill due to food mishandling is simply unacceptable. I am extremely disappointed with Bob Evans as we were long time customers and unsure we can trust their food handling and preparation to consider ever returning. I do not think we are permitted to state the names of the persons at the restaurant, but our male waiter's name is shared by one of the 3 Musketeers.

The icing tasted great, the cake however was a little too dry - this day, the cupcakes were either over baked or too old or not stored properly? I bought a dozen for my office for around $32. We all had the same complaint on the cake being too dry in this batch. I tried this place a time ago before my Yelping days and don't remember anything bad about the cupcakes back then. This time, I felt it could have been better. There was a fruit fly buzzing around and it landed on one of my cupcakes while the staff was assembling my box, I pretended not to notice and watched to see if Lil Cakes would replace it, nope! SOLD!!!! To me to bring to my office mates with fruit fly footprints all over the icing, yum! I mean, it's hard to keep out fruit flies but I don't like to pay for food that's been contaminated with the legs of a fly. Lil Cakes just waved a hand to get the fly away. Im no cake expert but I know what I like - Lil Cakes has potential & can certainly make improvements.

I visited this bakery a few weeks ago as my husband and I were walking through downtown Haddonfield. It's an adorable shop (teeny tiny!) and has bright colored walls and decor. They offer all sorts of baked goods, including cinnamon rolls, breads, cake pops, cheesecakes, cupcakes, etc. and it's all 100% gluten free. Having been GF for over two years now, I have never come across an eating establishment that is as serious about cross contamination as they are. I don't have to worry at all about the products being okay for me to eat. The only downside is the price - everything is super, super expensive. Cake pops are $3 each, cupcakes are $4 and the cinnamon roll that I had (amazing as it was) is $7.50. I probably wouldn't have tried it if my husband hadn't insisted!! All in all, this is definitely a place to splurge :)
Got food poisoning from a gyro I ordered from here on Uber eats. Currently miserably sick, drinking Pedialyte and praying for a swift death. Never go here!

Response to owner: I have an app called "find me Gluten Free" which is where I originally was suggested to try your restaurant. Considering I have celiac, I always immediately ask the server (before ordering anything) if the place I am at has a gluten free menu. Since YOUR (obviously unknowledgeable) staff said YES. And brought me out an adjustment menu , stating the gluten free menu looks "ghetto"( her words) is only because the gluten free menu was being re-done, but wasn't printed yet. I posted a picture of the menu she brought me... that alone should show you need to re-educate your staff. I will NEVER be back to this establishment, not only because of the service, but especially because of the way you have responded to this issue. It's almost embarrassing for you, and your entire establishment. Very inconsistent, very unreliable, very untrustworthy. You should advise your staff to stop greeting new customers with the saying "this is a fast pace kitchen, so as soon as any food you order is ready it will be out." Everything we ordered came out at the same time... 30 MINUTES after we ordered. Disgrace.

I really want to like this PJ's, I really do - but they fail me every single time and every single time it gets worse and worse so I refuse to go there anymore. The hostess's can't be found, the waitresses are chomping their gum, twirling their hair and can't remember what you've ordered, the bartenders can't seem to wait on anyone other than their friends, the food is thrown together and stale/sits on a warmer too long, the crowd is super young and obnoxious, people bang on the bathroom door because they think it's a multiple person bathroom, it smells like vomit in the whole bar and to top it off the beer they make tastes like pennies. - If you're 21 I'm sure you can dig PJ's for sure but the older you get the less tolerable this place is.

Sorry but the second time going here after about 30 min of finishing my meal I got the most horrendous food poisoning. I could taste some of the fish did not taste fresh at all. Vomiting and diarrhoea for two days. Never going back. Just thinking about it makes me wanna yak

Started this review in Jan 2015 - and it was Freezing! Even in the back after moving away from the doors. Brrr. We've been here a few times now, both with and without a groupon and found it doesn't seem to affect food or service - will discuss the service a little further on. On this occasion we ordered the Fish bites, phyllo chicken, coconut mussels. All were delicious and mostly gluten free. As we dine with "regular" consumers of gluten, their dishes are theirs to eat, and they can review them since we can't render an opinion. Onion blossom gluten free? Yes please! It is a delicious treat to share with the table. I agree with Hans' review - myself and my table companions noticed that sometimes the cooks "over cook" and char the spices - maybe it adds a little "something" to the dish, but it wasn't an overly pleasant aroma for the guests. Maybe the fume hood doesn't have enough draw to take care of it all. Service has been inconsistent over the times we've visited, sometimes quick and prompt, and other times, we got our water and waited 30 minutes to order. And this last visit we wore our puffy parka coats for the entire meal. Yes it was cold out, but we don't think it shouldn't have been that cold at the back of the restaurant especially with an open working kitchen and tandoor. We also noticed that there were papers and "stuff" all over the tables at the back of the restaurant... I understand that the back table has been replaced with a Chai bar now, so we'll have to go visit and try that out. Don't forget to ask if there are Specials for the evening.

Really delicious food in an area that desperately needs more interesting restaurant options, so I am definitely a fan. Ordered a cheeseburger - chose the 4 oz. option, which is an absolutely perfect portion size for lunch. Asked to add Benton's bacon to it - because I am of the opinion that everything needs to be covered in Benton's bacon - and it turned out to be one of the most delicious burgers I've had in a long time. And at only $5, it was an absolute steal. My dining companions all went with the BLT, which they all agreed exceeded their expectations. It looked amazing too - really fresh & creative ingredients. Again, a delicious sandwich at a great price. We ordered a side of the potatoes... I think they were seasoned with rosemary? I can't remember exactly... and they were tasty too. I'm looking forward to returning and trying the other sides because we scoped out all of the other diners' food as it passed out the kitchen and it all looked delish. My only gripe is that the service was quite slow - an hour for an early lunch in a nearly empty restaurant when all we ordered was sandwiches is a bit much. And our server REEKED of cigarettes, as in everything she touched smelled like them (I'm guessing because after we waited about 4 minutes for someone to come to our table, we saw her come in a side door where I'm assuming she was outside smoking). I'm sorry, but when the dirty ashtray smell of the person who is serving your food actually overpowers the smell of the food itself, that's a little vomit-inducing and something I would expect from a greasy spoon diner, but not from a place like this.

I actually really like this place. The staff is super friendly. You can taste the soups before picking one without feeling like you're being incredibly inconvenient. The soups themselves are pretty darn delicious (exception being tomato basil, I found that one to be less flavorful than the others) and made with great ingredients. But they have never failed to make me sick when ordering gluten free. Every. Single. Time. When I mentioned it, I was told something about the bread looking different. I'm supposed to magically know when bread is gluten free or not? I can only have gluten when I'm prepared--I have a sensitivity and it will make me physically ill without a specially formulated enzyme to help my body digest it. If it's not a special occasion, I choose not to have to take a pill and pick food I can have without issues. Or try to, anyway. The 'eh, oh well' response I got when I finally raised this concern--after eating there 3-4 times and trying different things to make sure it wasn't just me...glutton for punishment, I know--has put me off ever returning again. It's decent food that I liked grabbing on my too-short lunch break, but nothing I want to have to pop a pill for. Every time I see a post it makes me want to stop by, but the total lack of concern over the fact their mistakes have made me sick (and in the middle of my work day, generally!) has completely ruined this place for me. It's just not worth it. Which is such a shame because I could crawl into a pot of their potato leek and live there. So if gluten isn't an issue for you, you're all set, but I'd advise lots of caution otherwise. Their new hours make it even easier to stop by. I should note it has been a while, and maybe their processes have changed to help avoid this so one can eat a tasty sandwich without living in fear of the aftermath, but based on the above, I rather doubt it.

Food tastes great, until 8 hours later when the food poisoning sets in, your gut is in knots, you are puking, and miss your sister in laws wedding rehearsal dinner. Both myself and another in our party ordered the brisket taco and we've been sick since. Try at your own peril.

I am a regular at sabrina's and I really like the food,But every time I order delivery,I am disappointed! Last time when I ordered a grilled veggies sandwich,it was messed up with the veggies that I wanted and the ones I dint want.(I have allergies to asparagus,so yeah not a good thing to forget!) This time i ordered french toast and veggie burger with sweet potato fries,they just added the regular potatoes,you know don't care about what the order says. And french toast came without the syrup,what is the point of the french toast then?! It's like ordering a burger and you don't get the bun! Kinda ruined my mood for french toast! Disappointing delivery orders.It's like they don't listen,or don't care to pay attention to an order. I know you are busy,but that is no excuse to mess up orders,that's your business. But if you walk in,it might be possible to have all the attention of your servers I am open to new breakfast/brunch places now.

Went here and I got the chicken parm. First of all, who in their right mind would garnish a dish like that with oranges? Not even my Nonna. And second this was the worst food poisoning i got in my life. The chicken tasted like it was fried in old oil and the orange garnish on top made it worse. Would not recommend

Ok...I have lived in SB since 1971. Back in the day, Rose was a go to spot for Mexican. The food is basically the same tired old canned sauces, only one choice of salsa in an DMV environment. There are so many better choices in SB. I ordered chili rellenos and they were crap coated with, what looked like cat vomit, sauce that tasted the way it looked. Good luck if you go there.

I often find myself paying a lot of money for food in New Orleans, and have yet to feel ripped off. Until this place. What should be a tapas restaurant, saveur is an over priced attempt at casual fine dining. The prosciutto flat bread would have been good but had waaayyyy too much truffle oil, the baked goat cheese was good, but don't bother ordering the 9$ arugula salad which is offensively overpriced. The arugula garnishing the baked goat cheese is bigger than the salad appetizer. Their version of steak & pomme frites had well seasoned steak but 4 thin strips weren't enough to justify a 23$ price tag. Especially with soggy, nothing to write home about fries. And everything I had came garnished with green onions. (Hack. Be more creative.) On another note: My date is allergic to shellfish, but not mollusks, which she likes. Asking about shellfish in a dish was like pulling teeth because having a staff that knows the difference between a mollusk and a shellfish can be difficult at times. After trying a friend's mussel (mollusk) my date began feeling strange, so I promptly asked for the check. Paid over 100$ and tipped over 35%. Fortunately my date remembered she had Benedryl in her car, so, crisis averted. After a quick trip to the car I came back for an espresso (asked for a double, got a single) and dark chocolate creme brûlée (which was good). When the waitress gave me my 2nd check for the coffee and dessert, she charged me for a glass of wine that she apparently forgot to charge me for from the previous check. That's just bad form.

The food is disgusting and the place itself smells. The waffle fries are okay, nothing special but the meat is way to thin and tastes like vomit. I couldn't get the taste out of my mouth and was tempted to make myself vomit because my sandwich was so gross. I will give it to them, the Dr. Pepper was good. It was normal tasting and the I've is nothing special. I will never ever go back.

Well this location had not been hit up yet for reviews even though it has been there forever. I have been quite a few times. Nothing special. Their desserts seem to be their strong suit. Wait staff are a little dim. We have someone with a seafood allergy. We inform our waiter of this. This person orders chicken alfredo. He is receives his plate and begins eating. Yup you guessed it. For some reason there is shrimp mixed in. We left immediately hoping to get some benedryl & avoid having to go to the emergency room. Stupid servers aside the food is not good enough to go back for. The dishes are mostly over-cooked pasta with a high price tag. I am not all impressed by their "brick oven pizza" it was bland and dry.

I've been here a few times since living in manayunk and have always had a mediocre experience. Pros: One thing I really like about Winnie's is that they have a variety of healthier menu options (gluten-free, wheat buns, etc) and are very accommodating with substitutions. I choose to come here for dinner when I am dieting or with someone who has food restrictions for this reason. I also like their outdoor seating area for the warmer months, it's situated in a prime people-watching location on main street. Lastly, their bread basket served before dinner is delicious and includes a variety if breads including corn bread(my fave). Cons: Their menu doesn't have a big selection and is not so good for people who do not tend to eat healthy. They have a good happy hour every day but only offer it at the very small inside bar. Their breakfast/brunch is not the best, there are many other places to go in manayunk. Finally, I think everything n their menu is a little overpriced. Neither the quality of food or ambiance of the restaurant are upscale, yet all their entrees are priced this way and their beers are too pricey for the size glass they are served in.

Horrible. The service was terrible, on all levels. The waitress didn't seem to understand that a dairy allergy meant that cheese was a no-no. (My wrap came with cheese on it, had to send it back) This was a disaster on all levels. No apology either for the mistake; nothing off the bill, no care about the fact I could have been spending the rest of my day in the ER. If you have any desire for good service DO NOT EAT HERE!! The food itself was just ok. Nothing to rave about. Really, I wish I had just gone to Jules right next door.

The food in this place is amazing. Everything in the lunch buffet looks like vomit, but it tastes like awesome. You will walk in there and they will give you a choice between garlic or regular naan, and either one is good, but garlic blows regular out of the park. All the curry dishes are good, but the chicken bone-in is a real pain in the butt. The only thing I would say that needs to change about this place is the service. That's the only reason I took off a star. Sometimes it can be super bomb, and other times you will be completely ignored, waiting to get a water refill or to get your naan, which you are supposed to have before you launch into the buffet. Spotty service aside, this place is so worth going to.

I do not like malls. In fact I am pretty much allergic to anything around them as well, which makes me wonder why I stopped here to begin with other than traveling and starving. Maybe I've been in East Nashville too long... It's weird how the same restaurant can taste different depending on the location. I was driving so I had the grilled chicken pita, chips, and bean and corn salad. I realize that this is a "healthy" establishment, but healthy should not equate with bland - and I've had better at the Elliston Place location and also the one on Gallatin Road. The chicken was too dry and there was some lettuce just thrown on top. Just wasn't really... anything. Also, the bean to corn to onion ratio was way off, it was more like onion salad with a little bit of bean and corn. I don't like giving reviews under 3 stars but sometimes you have to. Usually I always feel better for making a healthy choice (I must confess I went to Chik Fil A initially but turned around) but this just set me back $10 and gave my dog a nice lunch.

I have seen the billboard for this place many times and have always wanted to try it. My son had a soccer game in the area so we had our chance. They accommodated our large group with no problem. I am non celiac gluten intolerant. The manager kindly took me on a tour of the buffet to go over what did not contain gluten. She did mention that they can not guarantee cross contamination. I had no problems and everything was delicious!

So I stopped in for a hoagie and a soda to go. The staff is yelling at each other over the counters about orders and who took what pickups messed up people are rude as a lot of customers trying to get their food no type of order as to who goes next or call them people know thank you know hello there's a layer of dirt around the counters on the glass and it's around the counters on the glass and it's not from kids touching the glass either the lady threw my sandwich at me to the counter I get up to the front I'm going okay it does he even know what this says he misses me up for something I didn't even have that was less than what it was supposed to be if I wasn't honest and telling them I would have been under charged it seems like it's a bunch of kids running the place and no type of organization there's no adults there's no adult there doing anything then nasty hand washing not happening people touching through their hair their calves their clothes some people wearing gloves over behind the counter some people without gloves I really pray that I did not get food poisoning I really stop eating I didn't eat all my food, and it didnt have all the topping on it. IM REALLY UPSET NOW money down the drain.

our family are big fans of thai food + so we thought we'd try out this place that was not too far from our flat. we ordered pretty standard dishes for takeout. a bit disappointed: the pad thai (which i typically order from any new thai place i check out) tasted great. until, i was spending too much time in the bathroom --sick, sick, sick-- 30 minutes after eating my dinner from there. alas, i wish i could rate this food experience better, but i (physically + mentally) cannot give it more than 2 stars. food poisoning is not fun.

My father and I wound up at this restaurant on our first night in New Orleans. The food was great--until about 1-1/2 hour later. Yup. Food poisoning. My first case ever-- I thought I had an iron stomach after going to Mexico for over 30 years without a problem. Needless to say, no more seafood for the rest of the trip. Upon leaving NOLA today, we were reading in the Picayune about health hazards in the restaurant industry, and guess who was named as being among the worst transgressors in the area? DING DING DING! The French Market Restaurant. Enter at your own risk.

Did a supper club with some friends one hot summer night at Bistro 7 and I enjoyed the food, and the company. Save room for dessert! I'm not sure but I think they make it themselves, as the rice pudding was redonkulous...and by that I mean GOOD! It was coconut and had caramel on the plate...it was thicker than your normal run-of-the-mill rice pudding. So good. My girlfriends had pot de creme, which also looked and tasted great. My entree was good...though there was something not-GF on the menu but it looked so good I wish I could have had it. My friends had this crab-stuffed squash blossom thing on top of a pesto risotto - mmmm. I had a duck breast with lentils and there were some grilled peaches on the plate. It was good...well-done plate of food, and a decent portion. I recall eating butter lettuce salad with a buttermilk dressing (which is better for you or so I hear), but this wasn't anything to write home about. It was good, but I would have eaten two desserts instead! :) What I did not enjoy was a major lack of AC that night. I'm sure they were aware of the problem...so I didn't want to be that guy complaining about how hot it was in there. So I'd like to go back when this is not an issue, as I'm sure this affected my comfort level while trying to eat warm food, too. Pre-fixe menu seems like a great way to go here, as they give you many courses and a great value for the $s. The only thing is that we could not order it unless the whole table wanted it (WTF) and I could not do substitutions (which does not work for me given the gluten-free thing).

I have been to the Ship Inn a few times and my meals have been great. The only issue I have with this place is the staff. For the price, you would expect pretty good service, but don't depend on that. The first time I went there we were waiting to be seated and were completely ignored by all who passed by for 15 minutes and the restaurant wasn't very busy. Another time I went with my boyfriend who has a severe food allergy. We immediately told our waiter so that she could check with the chef about our meal dishes. He asked about a dish and she said that it was fine to order...well it wasn't! We had to leave our dinner early because he had a reaction to the food. I was so upset by this that I contacted the manager to tell him that his staff needs to be more careful with such a serious health issue. He apologized and gave us a voucher for a meal. I used it, had a delicious meal and moved on.

This was the first time I visited this restaurant. I was really disappointed. They accommodate gluten free only with lettuce wraps. No gluten free breads for sandwiches. The taste of the meal was very bland. While I was in the restaurant I observed a sandwich delivered to a table a chip and salsa eaten from that plate and the sandwich picked up and inspected. The waitress came back to the table and after a discussion I didn't hear she took the sandwich away and proceeded to deliver that same sandwich to the next table and left it for them. They ended up sending it back also for another reason. I was appalled by the waitresses actions. It should have been thrown away! I would not return to this restaurant to eat again.

The atmosphere was a little bizarre. A Japanese restaurant with some traditional decor (paper screens, Japanese dolls) some non-traditional modern abstract paintings on the walls, and 70s rock on the sound system (Rolling Stones, Aerosmith...) The service was great, friendly, knowledgable, esp for allergy-related requests. The food was nice. Very nice. The fried chicken balls (sorry, do not know the Japanese name) were dark meat instead of the usual white meat, so they were a little chewy, but not greasy, and tasted nice. Noodle dishes good. Sushi wraps good. The fried ice cream was okay. The men's room smelled like vomit. Don't know why, but it was horrible. We really liked the food so we may go back, but the thought of that bathroom is still a little off-putting. The rest of the restaurant was very clean and had no noxious aromas.

The only redeeming factor was that the service was very good, and the mixed drink I had was delectable. The food itself was horrible. As someone who loves escargot, I would not recommend it here. The moldy old taste of the snails made me gag and almost vomit. I had the salmon for dinner, and while it was cooked nicely, the sauce that accompanied it didn't go well, and the leeks that were served under it did not either. On the bright side, they do make pretty good French fries.
Ate the mussels and fries here, an hour and a half later I had the worst food poisoning of my life. Fries were fine, but steer clear of their seafood.

Got food poisoning on my last visit. Sushi is sometimes served on clean but hot plates. Also, lots of germs floating around that buffet even though they work hard to keep it clean. Disappointed as I like the atmosphere here and they have good tasting reasonably priced sushi.

This was one of the worst dining experiences. We spent over $100 on two buffets and the food was ok, not great. But the worst part was that the crab served to me was water logged and tasted very strongly of rotten fish. I told the server my concern, and she apologized, which was fine until as I finished my meal I began feeling nauseous. We left and barely made it back to out hotel before I began violently vomiting. I spent the evening hugging the comode. Today, I called and asked to speak to the manager, I was given "Casey" who was less than appropriate nor kind in his response, explaining that I needed to call "where I had eaten earlier" because it was too soon for me to have gotten ill from their food. I explained to "Casey" that I am a nurse and this was definitely not the case and that all I was asking for was a refund for losing a night on my vacation, I was declined. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY OR A NIGHT OF YOUR VACATION! It's not worth it.

Ordered food from here yesterday on news years and 2 of the 3 people got food poisoning. We ordered the broken rice and grilled chicken and the rice vermicelli with vegetables egg rolls and is still currently suffering it. It will be my first and last time ordering here.

I came here last night with my boyfriend for my birthday weekend...and an hour later I suffered from food poisoning. Or maybe my body just didn't get along with clams! The food was pretty good; I got the steamed clams, egg and bacon spinach salad and Brazilian seabass. He got something with crab, and I shared my clams with him. But when I got home, I vomited for 2 1/2 hours with severe stomachs pains and a high fever...I had to go to the ER to seek treatment but the waiting list was too long. But after 2 1/2 hours of hell, I was able to just go home and rest. The fish ***seemed to be cooked well, however, I suspect the eggs and bacon in my salad had given me the poisoning. If you plan to give it a shot here, I would keep an eye out for what you order. Cut open your food and check it out before you eat it, and identify weird tastes/flavors. I was really disappointed about this. Plus, servers barely checked up on us. So is it worth a shot? Maybe. My boyfriend has been going to Rapscallions for years and he was fine last night. So I guess it's a damned if you do, damned if you don't situation (especially if you're a big seafood lover). Maybe just don't order the salads?

This is a cute idea to name the sandwiches after dog breeds and grilled muffins. However, I did not enjoy the grilled red velvet muffin and I probably won't be ordering from their bakery section again. I have yet to try a sandwich because I am allergic to yeast...it would be nice to have more selections made in the form of wraps! I overall a nice place to stop for lunch if you are stuck downtown in a pinch but not one of my favorite places so far.

We were having a bad day in Nashville. The sky had opened up and and attacked us with water. Drenched, we hurried to meet up with the comedy tour bus we had picked as our day's prime activity. The bus did not show at the appointed hour. We waited and waited only to eventually learn that the tour bus we were waiting for had collided with a motorcycle parade [true story] and that our tour was cancelled. Distraught, we wandered around, wondering what we could do with our day. We ended up taking a short and uninteresting horse drawn carriage ride with a driver who immediately copped an attitude with us as soon as we said we were from California and who, as an added bonus, did manage to convince us that we were about to spend the rest of our vacation with food poisoning due to the hot dog we bought off the street while we were hurrying to meet the tour we didn't get to take. Disappointed and dejected (and waiting to become powerfully ill) we set out to see the Parthenon. In the vicinity of Parthenon, we stumbled on a gathering of food trucks. Having lived in LA in the not too distant past, where the food truck scene is prime, we pulled over and went to investigate. We sampled a couple of food trucks, most of which were forgettable and forgotten, and then we tried the chicken and waffles from The Waffle Boss. We were instantly tickled by the variety of waffles and the guy taking our order was so friendly. We became cautiously optimistic. My boyfriend ordered the chicken and regular waffle while I ordered the chicken and red velvet waffle. We had to wait 20 minutes or so, but man, it was so worth it. The chicken (which came in strip form) was perfectly cooked and juicy with a crunchy delicious coating seasoned in such a way as to give a little flavor punch and perfectly offset the flavor of the waffle. The red velvet waffle was a beautiful crimson color, so enticing to the eye that even if I was not a fan of chicken and waffles I would have been thrilled to eat it. [I confess to snapping a couple of pictures so I could elicit the proper amount of envy when I returned to Cali]. It was fluffy, dense (but not overly so) and flavorful. Sweet, but not too sweet. Combined, the chicken and red velvet waffle were genius. Not since Roscoe's in LA had we enjoyed chicken and waffles this much (and that is saying something). Our day was instantly saved. For a moment we kind of wished we lived in Nashville. Amazing work Waffle Boss! Cook on!

Our evening at Catch 23 was great. My girlfriend and I both got calamari to start and the sea bass as the main course. Tasted great. Presented great. Overall experience AT the restaurant was great. Once we got home it was a different story. Food poisoning. All night. Not sure whether it was the calamari or the sea bass but we will not be returning. You could say it left a bad taste in our mouths
Good staff sushi is awesome totally disappointed by the katsudon chicken looked like a bowl of unions and vomit other than that all the other food looks great def won't be ordering the chicken again

I don't like writing bad reviews but I feel very mislead by the reviews here. My husband and I went here for breakfast today and we're scared upon entering the establishment. First of all, the owner was nice but OMG he needs to cover his hair and wear clean clothes because one of those hairs ended up in my potatoes. Needless to say I was absolutely repulsed and almost vomited. It was so gross. The food was super grease and nasty. Who likes this stuff!?!? Why all the good reviews? Whyyy!!? I am still ill at the thought of that nasty hair in my food. I hope I don't catch something from the bit I did put in my mouth before discovering the hair. One of the worst dining experiences ever!

Jules pizza offers extremely thin crust pizza with extremely interesting specialty toppings. You won't find a lot of sauce on these pizzas but you can find lots of other interesting things like aloo-gobi indian pie; edamame and ricotta cheese; brie and sliced pears. I don't have the science to back this up but it seems to me that the relatively thin size of the pizza makes it cool down a little faster (heat transfer to surface area issue?). We took a couple of pies home and it was already pretty cool by the time we dug in. Might be better to eat it here right out of the oven to get the true experience. It is nice that they offer gluten-free crust (in addition to standard and whole wheat) and it's probably healthier for one to go thin crust but it also takes away from the pizza experience. Good pizza deserves good sauce (not here) and shouldn't need to be covered by all kinds of fancy stuff. Jules Thin Crust is more of a place to see some experiments in toppings than good execution. Nice idea but it's giving you something very different than your typical pizza so make sure you know what you're getting into.

Waste of money there are much better places in town that charge must less, I went in for a private party with some friends and family expecting quite an experience considering the reputation. As soon as we were seated I noticed water spots on the glasses, wine stains on the table from the party before tsk tsk. It was a 3 course meal providing 3 options for each course. After explaining that I have a dairy allergy the server looking very worried said they would make a quick dressing of oil and vinegar and the risotto will have no dairy. Thus began amateur hour, food runners coming out completely lost asking multiple guests at the table who ordered what ( which was the trend of the evening)...really. By the time I tracked my plate down after being offered 3 others , plain with out a single grain of salt or dressing with a few sad attempts of dyhydrated tomatoes again without seasoning some pickled onions...sad attempt for a salad. The time between courses was long much too long. We had to speak with a manager about it which didn't help. The main course I went with was risotto knowing I had called ahead days prior informing the kitchen of my allergy because you never make risotto to order. After the first very underwhelming bite I asked the server if he was sure it was dairy free and he said yes, I found out the hard way he was wrong. The dessert was a sugar bomb of no particular flavor... For a place of this caliber to be sending out dishes lacking of the price point is completely unacceptable. Don't make the mistake we did go somewhere else deserving of your money.

It's cool to have a new bar in this neighborhood. SouthHouse does most of it right. Service is good, and super friendly--but not in that condescending way like they're talking to a child. The space is pretty big and can accommodate a pretty large group. The food has a lot of options for people, so everyone you go with will have something to eat. There are vegan options and GF. In fact, there's a TON of gluten free options, so if that's your jam you should really check this place out. THe only criticism here: the food. The menu is great conceptually, but poorly executed. I ordered a steak med-rare, and it was overcooked and cut for me. Whenever I see a steak cut for me, I immediately know the chef has no confidence in his/her ability to cook a proper temp steak. I guess it's really just a kitchen issue, not so much as ingredients. Everything I had tasted good, but could've/should've tasted better. This place isn't even a year old, so some hiccups in the kitchen may be lingering. I suggest the owners go in and try the food one night, then get a new chef.

If you are gluten free be weary of certain locations! The Franklin TN location is wonderful for gluten allergies!!!! I have eaten at it several times and never gotten sick!!!
