BUT the Green Hills TN location is absolutely awful! I've never seen a more disrespectful group of people in my life! I asked several times about gluten free while ordering... when I asked if the rice and potatoes were gluten free the girl says "should be".... I said "well like I said before it is an allergy". So she said "well yeah I think it is". I asked her to ask someone else. So she started shouting around and no one knew. Then the rude manager, who looked like he didn't want to be there came up and said "yeah they both have no gluten". At this point I had a bad feeling. But I ordered anyways because I was hungry. My meal came out. And of course... my salad had a big pita sitting right on top of it. And the dang manager is the one who brought it out to me. At this point everyone is aware that I had an allergy, especially the manager. But I still had to say "I have an allergy... I can't eat that pita" He reluctantly brought me a new plate. I had a bad feeling about it. So I didn't eat it and left!! Avoid the Green Hills TN location if you can! Even the bathroom was disgusting!!!!! Which says a lot about the restaurant itself!

I've had my eye on this place for awhile now, before it even opened, and finally got a chance to grab a snack with a friend a few weeks ago. The woman working behind the counter was super friendly and helpful. We ordered smoothies and I got the banana bread. Smoothies too a bit longer than I would have liked, but they were tasty and definitely healthy! Banana bread was also delicious - gluten free, too! They are most definitely still in the process of opening. The second half of their store was basically empty and their fridges were pretty bare. Would like to see more lunch options in the future, but they have a lot of smoothie and juice options for now, as well as pastry options. It is definitely expensive, though. ~$15 for a smoothie and banana bread with tip. Just be prepared. Looking forward to see how they do and going back in a few months!

Casey makes this place one of my favorite restaurants. Despite me having an allergic reaction to the truffle fries (seriously?) the first time I dined here, Casey was super awesome, off the wall, and friendly. This second visit was no different, Casey was witty, and had us chuckling along to her antics throughout the night. This place rocks.

Eh! Not going again. Firstly, they are a 100% gluten free establishment which is why they got 2 stars. Me H. and I visited them for brunch and we were immediately seated inside. The weather was good outside so we asked if we can be seated outside. Our sever mentioned she needed to check with other server as outside was not her area. We were kept waiting but finally were seated outside. We could actually feel the tension between the servers and due to lack of communication no one came to take our order for quite some time. After a long while, our original server came and took our order. We were starving by then but we were like okay, things happen, let's just wait for food and not judge. We understand that each server has a fixed number of tables etc. but then the food came, it was BAD! Didn't taste good at all and was salty. We were completely neglected all the time as that servers couldn't decide who should serve us. It was utter chaos. I have eaten at other 100% gluten free places too. And wohoo to AMOT but please don't overlook taste and service, ultimately experience is what matters.

I have been to this restaurant twice now. The first time was about as perfect as you can imagine. The food was perfect the prime rib perfectly cooked and seasoned, the waitstaff helpful and polite. Literally everything was perfect. It was probably the best prime rib I have ever had. So this brings me to my second trip. I asked a waiter to alert my waitress that we had two birthdays. He pouted and insisted I take my "lazy ass" and go find her. I was put out. We ordered a shrimp appetizer that is apparently pre made and microwaved. It was frozen in the middle. Then we ordered three medium rare prime ribs - 18$/ea. Each and every steak came out raw and cold in the middle. They took them back and warmed them up. Now they came back out well done. Mine came back tasting watery, seasoning gone. I think they may have boiled it. My mashed potatoes had some sort of contamination from some other food as they tasted like cinnamon stick. Our waitress was great. We tipped her well. The manager "had a chat" with the cooks, and took 2$ off our steaks. If we had wanted cold raw ribeye we could have bought three from sav a lot for much less than what a single steak cost us here - and we would have known for a fact it was cooked the way we wanted it the first time. Who boils a prime rib?

Clean place.. If you go after lunch hour, better seating, better service, attentive waitstaff. I got the bleu cheese burger with bacon and they charged me (penalized me) for the GF bun. That's not right.. It's not my fault our food is tainted and allergies happen.. A burger, bacon, french fries, and a beer came to $25.00... The burger alone, with added charge of bacon and GF bun was over $16.. most expensive burger in town? IPA 16oz beer was $5.49.. Most expensive burger in town. Charged extra to change the bun out... Enjoyed it, but doubt I'll go back.

This location is pretty clean and generally have enough checkouts open so the lines don't get very long (YAY!) and when you use their rewards app and coupons decent prices along with fuel points for discounts at the pump in the area. I don't do all my shopping here because of limited options working around food allergies, along with higher regular pricing on a lot of items.

Unfortunately I cannot recommend this place. My partner and I had dinner here. Both of us had noodle dishes--mine with pork, shrimp, and sausage and his with seafood. We shared the pineapple salad app. The food tasted fine. Not the best I've had, but fine. A few hours later I was violently vomiting. I had food poisoning so bad I couldn't eat, or really do much of anything, for a week. My husband, who tasted my food, had some mild stomach issues and was sick for about three days. The manager I spoke with, Bruce, refunded my bill. But one thing he said I found odd: oh well, that happens sometimes. He didn't seem overly concerned. Does this happen often there? I dont know. He also offered me a gift certificate, which was nice but I won't be returning so I declined.

Decided to give this place another chance now that they have been open for a month or so. We sat upstairs on the deck overlooking the swelling Mississippi river. It was about 4 pm and we decided on wine and small plates. Hannah was our server and she was friendly, prompt and attentive. She was knowledgeable about the food, and a great spokesman for the venue by telling us about the upcoming events such as Ladies night and how to rent the VIP sections of the venue. This is a great concept for the FQ because it's an upscale nightclub type of place completely different from the Bourbon St. style clubs. Yet, it's also a chill place for afternoon drinks with an awesome view. Hannah was done with her shift but stayed behind to finish waiting on us. Another table was seated by the host on the deck and the table belonged to another server, unfortunately like my first experience, no one ever came out to wait on them and they left after waiting for about 15 minutes. Hannah did an excellent job but I guess some of the other servers still aren't quite up to par. If you get a bad waitress and are willing to tough it out, the food is actually quite good and the venue is a nice change from typical FQ.

My boyfriend and I ordered delivery. I ordered Fettuccine Alfredo from their "pasta specialties" menu and my boyfriend ordered Rolli Massamino w/ chicken. The delivery guy came 20 minutes late (over an hour) and made the excuse that he had the wrong address (I ordered from grubhub and have the correct address in my account). Small portions for the price ($16.00 each), but the worst of it was that my Fettuccine Alfredo which was described to have prosciutto and broccoli was literally ONLY linguini w/ sauce. No prosciutto, no broccoli. This meal was clearly worth about $3.00 and I would have been upset with it even if I ordered it at a low budget diner at 2am and paid $7.00 for it. My boyfriend's had chicken and broccoli in it at least.. however his broccoli was not fresh, definitely from a bag and honestly tasted like vomit. Neither of us ate our food and we will never, ever visit this restaurant again. Awful service, awful food, high prices.

Delicious!!!!!! We went here the other night with a small group for an anniversary dinner. All of the staff was great! No one acted irritated that we had a larger group. And they were all very attentive. Everything was delicious too! The bread you get prior to your meal was awesome and it has this oil dip that has this slight spicy bite to it and it's just ridiculously good. I ordered a burger and fries and the fries were awesome. And the burger was unique which was nice! It had a flavor I've never had on a burger. Loved every bite of my meal. The bathrooms were also very very clean. This is probably too much information but I ended up vomiting during my time here (happens a lot to me...don't worry it WASN'T food poisoning lol) but anyways I HAATEE throwing up in public cuz it's so gross as it is and nothing makes it worse than a super dirty toilet or floor. But it was soooo clean so it made it much easier and less terrible lol. Anyways overall it was great. Loved it all. I told my husband I want to eat there on our anniversary.

Hooray for healthy quick options on the North Side of Indy! Perfect location, close to the Monon. I can already picture myself in the need of nourishment after a robust jog, stopping in for a Acai bowl for a post workout snack. Last week I quickly stopped in for lunch and ordered a small Detox Bowl to-go. What I liked about the Detox Bowl was it contained Kale and Spirulina. For those unfamilar with Spirulina it's a super food high in protein (vegan/gluten free), it contains beta carotene, vitamins, good things that make you big and strong. The sweetness from the fruit in this bowl masks the kale flavor so you don't even taste the kale. Great way to hide your veggies. What I didn't like about the bowl was it was more of a frozen dessert consistancy due to the usage of frozen fruit verses fresh fruit. I had also planned on this bowl being my meal for lunch and it didn't fill me up. I ended up having to go out and buy more food to fill me. I can see myself coming back and pairing it with one of their paninis as a lunch option maybe or making this a breakfast/post work-out option only. As the bowl is more of a frozen dessert consistancy it seems better suited as a snack/treat option rather then a meal.

Really interesting concept in that you choose your own base of ice cream: Premium Cream 14%, Custard 10%, Lowfat 5%, Almond Milk, Yogurt, Soy/Rice. Great for lactose intolerant people or for those on specific diets! Then it's just like Coldstone Creamery in that you pick your toppings and they freeze it with liquid nitrogen and voila! Your dessert is ready :-) I had the cinnamon custard with dark chocolate flakes and graham cracker crust. Didn't expect it to be pink-and the flavor wasn't that strong-but I liked it overall.

My husband and I were part of a party of six for dinner at Marzano, and my rating would be much higher were I only rating the food. But ambiance is also part of what makes a meal wonderful or awful or something in between. In this case I want to be specific and clear: The food was very, very good! But this was one of the noisiest restaurants I've experienced. Now, loud is, for some, a good thing. It can be interpreted as exciting, energetic, fun. Or--as in my case--it can be annoying, painful, disorienting. All six of us expressed some degree of concern about the deafening decibel level at Marzano, and four of us agreed we would not return because of it. If you like loud restaurants, then please try this one--and I mean that seriously, because the food was very good. I had a split avocado filled with a very elegant crab ceviche as an appetizer--just delightful! My companions enjoyed mussels in a very good, light tomato sauce, calamari (I'm not a fan, but my friend is and said it was great), a nice minestone and some big, fresh salads. all good! Our entrees included a special of orecchiette with shrimp, garden-fresh cherry tomatoes and broccoli rabe in a light olive oil/white wine sauce; risotta with an abundant mixture of seafood, rigatoni with Fra Daivolo and lasagna. No one at our table had anything to say but positives about their meals...or, possibly, I simply *could not hear* any negatives. It was that loud, what I think of "smile and nod" loud, where, after the meal, when you finally escape and walk outside, your ears still ringing, you wonder what you just agreed to while smiling and nodding. One final negative--if, like me, you are lactose intolerant, there will be no dessert for you...but how often is there? All the desserts here are cream-based. Now, why a restaurant cannot put some luscious cake under fresh fruit with the option of refusing whipped cream I do not understand. Perhaps this is a cultural thing and most Americans just want dairy-rich desserts, I do not know. Nor will I fault Mazano on this score because--as a majorly lactose intolerant girl--there rarely *is* dessert for me unless I am at home. So, in summary: very good food that could cross that fine line into *great* food, if you could enjoy your meal without the headache of loud, deafening, relentless, my-ears-still-ring-an-hour-later noise. If that will not bother you, go! If it will bother you, also go, but go on a warm summer evening and insist on a table outside. Yeah, it will overlook a parking lot. And yet, you will be able to hear what your friends say, and not be reduced to smiling and nodding aimlessly...and agreeing to, who knows what.

I have food allergies. Sorry I'm allergic to milk. That's how I felt leaving this place. The waiter called me 'milk girl' 5 separate times while the cook made fun of me when the waiter asked if he could accommodate for the allergy. All they had to do was cook in a pan with oil instead of butter, which usually isn't an issue but I was made to feel like I was like a nameless animal while trying to eat. I asked him to stop the distasteful treatment twice and he didn't. The next time, I ended up leaving without eating or paying. I can't believe I was treated like this. Don't go here and if you and you do have a food allergy, expect to be treated like a second class citizen. This goes without saying, but 'milk girl' won't be back.

Cup Cafe.... About a month ago, my husband and I along with two other couples went there for dinner. I am highly allergic to gluten and eggs and made sure to order the tacos in corn tortillas as well as checking about mayo (egg based) since I can't eat eggs. All the meals were served including my tacos which came on flour tortillas and had to be sent back. I waited and waited so long to get the correct order that everyone else was almost finished eating. When the tacos finally arrived, they were swimming in mayo based sauce, and I couldn't eat them. This was about 1 1/2 hours into our arrival. Everyone else had eaten the bread which came first and their full meals, and I had a glass of water for my meal.The waitress said she wouldn't charge for my food...but I never got any...so that was not much of an offer. I finally asked the waitress if there was anything in the kitchen that was prepared that I could eat, and she brought out a basket of chips and some salsa. I went home and fixed myself dinner. At no time did the manager come to see what was going on nor did the server offer to bring something else-a salad perhaps. Had I not asked, I would have had nothing offered at all. Because of my food issues, I am always polite about finding out about the food so that I can have something to eat and also avoid being the center of attention or a complaining person...but this was the worst. To not be offered anything else after serving the incorrect order twice was really upsetting-it's challenging enough to deal with food issues, but to end up with a glass of water while everyone else was eating is very depressing. I did phone and speak to one of the managers the next evening, and he was very sorry for what happened and said that he would speak to the manager from the previous night. With so many restaurants including the cheaper chains being sensitive and nice about food issues, this was a real low point.

Love you guys and all, and as a person with Celiacs Disease I was pumped when I saw the gluten free cookies!! But then I got super super sick from the cross contamination, you have them unwrapped next to all the other baked goods and you use the SAME TONGS!! This is actually dangerous, you wrap the other stuff, just wrap those too so everyone stays alive. I've never made a yelp review before but this was so scary I had to say something
Great food! Way over priced on gluten-free up charge. Staff has been told many many times throughout the years and still no change. Get with the program.

Vomitted all night! Don't go. Save yourself. Gave us food poisoning prior to our son's graduation. We ordered a pizza with spinach and pepperoni. The spinach was shredded and black not fresh and tasted like it came out of a can. Spent all night vomiting both my wife and I despite eating only a couple small slices. Don't go here. Glad we did not feed it to our 2 year old!
Not good food. Table service was fine. Burger burnt, sausage shriveled, daughter threw up pancakes on way home, egg benedict had crusty sauce. Find elsewhere.

WOW, how the mighty has fallen! At least at this place! This was our go to place locally for fresh, great BBQ. NOT ANYMORE!!!! We arrived and the place was hopping, as usual. I liked that, Squealers is always busy, so we expected to wait, and to wait for good food we are fine with, if we only knew... The half hour wait came and went and we we were seated. It took a while for our waitress to get to us, we put in our App order and drinks. She came back in about 5 minutes and answered our questions and took our order. We had ordered the fried pickles, and it was taking forever, F-O-R-E-V-E-R, to get done, so I said, "watch, everything is going to come out at the same time! This runner comes over with the pickles and kind of throws them on our table, we just looked at each other, like, REALLY?!!! They were hot, so they had just come out of the fryer, but to do that, was just odd. Again, I go back to the "if we only knew" I was out of my Root Beer at this point and had not seen our waitress in a very long time, we waited another 10-15 minutes and I see her and our food is coming to us. She places them down and says she will be right back with my drink. Now the aroma that hits me is this stench of ROTTEN food. I mean really bad food. I looked at my GF who was just getting into her Chicken and she spit it out right away, she then asked me to smell it, to which I did and almost retched all over the table. I cut into my half slab of ribs, and again they were not any better. To top it all off they were cold, not stone cold but COLD. Our waitress comes back and we tell her, we gave her the chance to smell our items, and she declined, she went and got the manager, who came and proudly told us that they have things on a line (which I knew) and that they "temp everything every 2 to 3 hours" we stay on top of the temps! (If you are temping things 2-3 hours, you are well behind hon!!!) This food was rotten, the chicken was just rot gut disgusting! Pulled pork, was green, hence, ROTTEN, I just could not believe what I was seeing!!! Our waitress was MIA most of the night, and when we showed her this, almost acted like it was our fault for coming in!!! The manager asked if we wanted anything else, but we had basically between the 2 of us the whole BBQ menu with the pic 2-3 options, there wasn't anything left to pick, and she was not going to admit that the stuff was bad, she was saying in a round-about way that we were wrong! I know food, more then her, been working around food since I was 5 years old, and have 23 years experience as a Chef, 20 as a Executive Chef I AM NOT WRONG HERE. We just asked for our check which we were given, we had a coupon, which was not honored, lol, so we paid, and tipped VERY WELL (as we ALWAYS do) and left, DISGUSTED of the place that we used to be proud to come to. How they can do this is unreal. We then went to another restaurant, sat with around 15 people who are all from the local area. EVERY SINGLE ONE OF THESE PEOPLE had been to the restaurant in the last 6 months to year, and had suffered some sort of food poisoning!!! ALL said they would NEVER go there again because of it. SQUEALERS, you need to correct this problem before you don't have a restaurant to run. This was a unpleasant experience top to bottom!

Giving a two-star rating because I went out to eat with my cousin and, although the food was good, the service was mediocre. I had the fish and shrimp and chips meal which was good and filling. She had a burrito filled with beans, served with rice and refried beans on the side. She enjoyed her plate. We both shared their Spinach dip as an appetizer, it was served with pita, which tasted good. The server looked like her life was a streamline of perpetual shit. She didn't smile, introduce herself, I had to ask her for her name. The host wasn't as terrible,but she didn't seem too happy to be there either. The overall reason I gave this place a two, was because my cousin got food poisoning. She was sick for two days and it pretty much ruined our little stay in Philly. Aside from the bad experience, we went on a Saturday evening, and the place was popping. The decor is super comfortable and homey-like.

I have been to friendlys several times and different locations, but this is by far the biggest disgrace to a restaurant. From where we were seated we could see the area they put the food. I watched 2 guys eating fries off of the orders, one actually licked a fry and put it on a plate. I grabbed a manager and was told I must have seen something unclear their employees would never do such things. We decided ice cream would be better, I asked for no nuts on mine since I'm allergic. My first spoonful, if not for my girlfriend, would have sent me to the hospital because they put nuts under the whipped cream. The manager tried to convince us it was an accident, promised to take it off our check, and to send a gift card for a future visit. We got our check and guess what, nothing was taken off and the manager was "on the phone with corporate". I don't know how stupid they I think I was, but corporate isn't open on the weekend or 9pm.

Great place! We went here for restaurant week and the food, service, and atmosphere were terrific. Very fresh ingredients make great tapas! Their drink menu was also very good. We tried two different sangrias and the matador--- all were excellent. The best part was the effort they made regarding food allergies. They made all of my food on a separate pan to avoid cross contamination and all of the servers who ran food to our table knew that I had an allergy.

Jannie is located In the back of a huge parking lot (near the movie theater)-the decor is really "fancy" but old. The lunch specials are crazy cheap- $7 for tea, fried wontons, soup, rice and a main dish. The egg drop soup has little corn nuggets in it, but is otherwise kind of bland, the wonton soup a little watery, the miso is fair. Now that being said, the main dishes are REALLY tasty-- I had the hot and spicy chicken, which was fresh thin sliced chicken with carrots and green beans. Very good--and they made it without Soy sauce for my Gluten-free lifestyle. The time before I tried the house noodles which were also very good. With so few places to eat in this area, I will going back to Jannie.

We arrived at Metro diner at 830pm on a Saturday night to get some quick dessert; it was dead. Strawberry and chocolate cheesecake, hot chocolate and a strawberry milkshake. Took 15+ minutes to get the cheesecake (dessert display 10 ft. away). Didnt get milkshake until 9:30pm. Waitress was nowhere to be found in between that time. Service was horrible, got chocolate cake instead of chocolate cheesecake, and after an hour of waiting for milkshake, it was made with chocolate syrup in it (which my boyfriend is allergic to) and had to get it sent back. Took 20 more minutes to get correct milkshake. Because of horrible service, we wont be returning.

I had a very unpleasant experience on 12/10/15. I was there with a group for a party. There were several in the group with special dietary needs. Several of the dishes were pasta with hard-to-identify ingredients. I asked "which of these are vegetarian" and was told the gnocci and ravioli were vegetarian. I bit into a ravioli to discover that it was filled with lobster. Someone who works in a restaurant should realize that a majority of American vegetarians don't eat fish-- and should have either clarified that the ravioli included shellfish or should have asked a follow up question before assuring the patron that a dish was vegetarian when it was not. Even worse, a fellow diner with celiac's disease was given food covered with a sauce containing flour because the waitstaff did not understand that flour was not "gluten free." I was very unhappy and won't be back for this reason. I will also add that the food was disappointing even setting aside the miscommunications. Most of the dishes I tried were bland/unexciting (no salt/pepper provided on the table). The tiramisu was quite bitter-- almost as if the chef had accidentally omitted sugar when making the dish.

I took a party of 5 to this restaurant, the first sushi chef we had was a bit rude. I asked him for 5 orders of salmon nigir and he said "give me a minute." But in a tone that made you want to not talk. He made sushi farily quick, but he over filled the rolls with ingredients. I asked more a mountain long roll, the sushi roll was very all. As soon as i got half way of my roll I bit into one piece and I almost gagged and threw up. I dont know if he accidently added an extra ingridient by accident. A gooey ball bursted in my mouth, i dont know if it was a gian fish egg or what? But I had to swallow it; I did not want to barf over the table. Everyone else was creeped out by him. After an hour he left and we received a new chef. His name was Tony. Everyone liked Tone. He talked with us, he laughed and he even made my girlfriend a special roll! I ordered 2 orders of muscle without mayo. Wow! is all I can really say about those muscles. He added extra ingredients to them and made them outstanding! W all tipped Tony personally. Just him and we all tipped him very very high! I cant give a higher rating due to the fact that I almost barghed my sushi and how creepy the first chef was.

Let me start out with the good. The decor of the restaurant is nice. The food ingredients are fresh and organic. They offer gluten free options for pizza. The service was average. That is all that I can say good about it. Although the food ingredients are fresh, the food is tasteless. We order mozzarella fritti, cibo salad, rosemary carmelized onion wings, carni pizza, fioruccio(gluten free), and cheese pizza. The pizza taste like a cardboard box. The wings taste burnt with no seasoning. The salad was very bitter; I'm guessing from the lemon olive oil dressing. I admit I am a critical person when it comes to food, but even my family did not like anything that we order. Even the lemonade was water down. In a nutshell this restaurant has great ingredients, but poor execution of them.

My dad and I both got food poisoning from this buffet. I even tried to stick with bland food because I didn't trust the freshness of the food. It was terrible quality and worse than my university cafeteria. DO NOT RECOMMEND eating here under any circumstances. The service was also horrible; it took us forever to get drinks and for our plates to be taken away. Do not eat here.

I went here for lunch on Saturday with a Groupon I bought this week. They have a few "platters" that are gluten free. I had the falafel "platter" and my friend had the sea bass "platter". Platter my ass. It was a plate with the main order, a few veggies on the side and some spinach. The fish was dry inside and oily outside, the falafel was greasy, and the place was incredibly overpriced. The decor wasn't fit for much more than a fast food joint, yet the prices were about $13 a plate. This was way too greasy and cheap tasting for me. I feel like a cow.

Been there a few times and enjoyed the atmosphere, sitting outside. Really liked the chicken nachos. Fast and friendly service. Unfortunately, a dealbreaker was my recent experience when I found several pieces of steak in my "chicken" nachos. Since it was dark outside, it was impossible to see what was exactly on the plate and I ate most of it before noticing the steak contamination. I do not eat beef! This tells me that their cooks do not pay attention and do not care (or are too busy) to keep their ingredients separate. Eat at your own risk.

I was excited to have this open near our house so I took my two kids there for dinner during their soft opening. The first thing my kids said was, "There's no kids menu." So I was surprised that someone below got the "kiddie" sliders. I guess that got past us. I was excited at the menu online as it said they had gluten free buns since I have to eat GF. After we ordered our slider platters (mine with GF buns), my kids remarked "wow, this is taking a long time to get our food." Sure, they've said this at other places, but yes, it was slow to come out. When it did, my kids declared it their new favorite restaurant. The insides of my sliders were great - I had the basic burger and then a chicken one with arugula. The beef was overcooked but the chicken delish. The gluten free "bun" however was inedible. It was a dense corn-cake type of thing. One was definitely older and more freezer-burnt than the other. And they were cold. Not even an effort to warm them up was taken. It was like eating gluten free food from 10 years ago when they hadn't figured out how to make it good. The first thing I thought when we left was, "they need to call Bailey's Range and Five Star Burger to figure out what vendor they use for GF buns." If they can nail that, I'd go back once a week since it's walking distance from our house.

Food was good, but not great. Be careful if you have gluten allergy, all the food is cooked together and they cannot guarantee no cross contamination. However, the server kept changing their mind on whether things on the menu were or were not gluten free. The service was below average and we felt like our server lacked hygiene which made us generally concerned about our food. The server brought our food and then didn't come back again until they picked up our plates and brought our check. If the food was not good, we would have given this a one star review, but the inventiveness of the food made us give three stars. If you are in the area, stop in but don't go out of your way to check this place out.

Recently diagnosed with celiac, so I have to eat gluten free. Still getting the hang of asking for what I need. Husband (not gluten free) REALLY wanted to go to Perkins. I knew my choices would be limited. I asked the waitress if anything was GF, and she said no. I said, "If I order eggs, could they clean off the grill for me?" She ran off to ask, came back and said, "Sure can!" Had a nice breakfast. They're food is Good. Not excellent, but Good. However, they apparently have no concept of GF, because now I have the mother of all bellyaches. IF YOU'RE GLUTEN SENSITIVE, STEER CLEAR OF PERKINS! If my husband wants to go there again, I guess I'll just have coffee and tap my foot until he's done eating.
I ordered the chicken shawarma tonight and had it delivered. Major food poisoning. I will never return.

There has been a lot of hype around Turning Point for a while now and they just opened a new location in Cherry Hill, so I decided to finally check it out. I'd heard that they have a gluten free menu and seems like a chill brunch spot. What I discovered is that while yes, it's a chill brunch spot, it is not very gluten free friendly and it's PACKED. I think all of Cherry Hill, Marlton and Voorhees was waiting for a table for brunch and there is really not enough space to wait. The place is really cute and has a very relaxed, almost Jersey shore vibe but it's not that big. During the summer they open up tables outside but for the winter there was not enough room for everyone waiting. I unfortunately was very unsatisfied with their ability to provide safe gluten free options, as they would not attempt to provide options without cross contamination but at least they were very upfront about that fact. The coffee was great and everyone that I came with enjoyed their meals! So if you're not like me and plagued by tons of dietary restrictions, I would most definitely check out Turning Point!

Food is gross, Service is worse. Ordered Carside To Go, specifically asking for no mushrooms in my meal. Get back to my hotel, and it's littered with mushrooms. I call them and let them know that I'm allergic and the dish needs to be remade. Manager is nice enough to comp my meal, which is really the least they can do after wasting a half hour of my time driving back this late at night. The food is obviously reheated, as the spinach has completely wilted and the chicken is covered in condensation. The first to-go container was room temp, and this one is super hot. I call back to make sure they didnt just reheat a dish I was allergic to, and they assure me it's fresh. It is actually worse if this is a freshly made dish, considering how unappetizing it is. So I dig in, and it's gross. I'm starving, but this is borderline inedible. And all it took was an hour of drivetime and waiting. Applebees isn't that great to begin with, but this one is particularly bad. Oh yeah, and my hot dessert was given to me cold. I'm in a hotel and don't have a microwave.

It used to be so good. Now it's loud, uncomfortable and the sushi tastes fishy every time. They messed up my order once and when I told them they asked if I had allergies and actually tried to make me eat it anyway. So disappointing.

Our daughter Bronwyn is allergic to dairy ,beef,and pork. Unfortunately, she is unable to eat at many restaurants due to cross contamination issues. Bodega is different!!!! Every time we order every employee listens to her describe her allergies . She has never had a reaction to any item she has eaten. Bodega is her favorite restaurant !!! ( pollo sandwich with oil press) It's not just the food that's great, it's the people that work there. They make our family feel at home there. Thank you to everyone at Bodega!!!!

I went to Highlevel for a Sunday brunch with my friends and was not surprised to see a long line pouring out of the front door. I had hear good reviews and most restaurants that have survived off of Whyte for that long are there for a reason. We waited for about 15 minutes which in the land of brunch is barely worth calling a wait and were seating at a four top in the middle of the restaurant. We were greeted right away by our server who let us know their special as well as took our drink order. I was the only one that requested something other than water (a coffee) and started to peruse the menu. They had a good selection for a brunch and I also found out that they offer a full Celiac menu for their Sunday brunch which I was impressed by. Most offer celiac options not a whole menu! We ordered our food, I got the eggs benny with fresh fruit and toast and my two friends ordered the veggie omelet one with just egg whites. I received my coffee after the server took our order and much to my chagrin the sugar on the table was almost empty and what was left in the bottom was hard as a rock. The server apologized that it was not filled and immediately got me a new one. I did not see him set the small pitcher of cream for my coffee unfortunately which lead me to believe that it was sitting there during the previous guests visit. Don't get me wrong I am not usually anal about this kind of thing except for the sheer amount of children that I saw scampering around made me wonder how safe a un-lidded pitcher of cream was sitting unsupervised on the table. I have seen children lick the salt shakers at other establishments unsupervised which kind of takes away my carefree nature. I gave it a thorough inspection and once I deemed that it did not look contaminated I proceeded to doctor up my coffee. Our food took a reasonable time to arrive given how busy the place was and the portions were decent for the price. The omelets looked well made with a hearty serving of vegetables and a tonne of tangy Parmesan melted on top. My friends thoroughly enjoyed their meal and were quite happy to find a vegetarian omelet that was an actual omelet not a salad with eggs on it. My eggs benny was also very good; the eggs were cooked to perfection, the muffin was crisp and back bacon was nicely smoked. I would have liked more hollandaise as I feel that it is part of the dish not just a garnish, but I am sure my waist line agrees with them not me. The server was quite attentive throughout and refilled my coffee a few times which I appreciate given most brunch service. I did have a hard time with the giant wall of window catchers behind our table though as they were reflecting sun from the patio directly into my friends and my eyes but it was to dark other wise to put on sunglasses. I also found the noise level on par with a nightclub unfortunately. I am sure that it was because we were sitting right in the middle of the throng but it is the first time I have left a brunch with a hoarse voice. All things aside I know that I probably visited them during their busiest day of the week and as such I am excited to visit again and see if I can bump my review up from a three star.

GOT FOOD POISONING HERE. Violently ill for 2 days from eating the tacos. The tacos also weren't even good or authentic. If you want real tacos go to someplace on 9th street. If you want food poisoning, go to Rosy's Taco Bar. It's too bad because I wanted a taco spot close to my house but this place is terrible.
Pulled pork is fatty and tasteless, the cole slaw has to much vinegar and looks like vomit.

I would strongly advise against this place if you wish to be gluten free, as then are not sure what all is contained in their menu items, and do not have a gluten free menu. My food was not bad except I ordered a medium rare steak and did not get that temp. The food was still good, but the service was sub par and they just didn't seem to want to be there or even pay attention anytime we ordered or had questions.

I review places based on how they stack up to my expectations. In this case, my expectations are admittedly low. This location is pretty solid though. I'm vegetarian, so I'm always on the lookout for contamination issues, especially at quick service spots. This particular location (which I've frequented for years) is consistently better than most Chipotle (or Baja or Qdoba) locations. Keep an eye out though, once or twice I've had to politely call them on stuff like touching the salsa spoon to the meat on the dish ahead of me etc. In those cases, they've uncomplainingly started my dish from scratch. Cross contamination is a broader issue amongst this category of food establishments though. Super busy at peak times though... Definitely avoid Friday and Saturday nights!!

I ordered delivery from here 2 or 3 times with no problems and figured it was safe to continue doing so. Apparently not. I got pretty intense food poisoning from the sushi and was so sick I could barely move for several days. It's sushi, and I'm sure that happens (this was my first bout of food poisoning after about a decade of sushi eating, however), but I'm not sure this place would ever be my first choice again.

If you read the good reviews about this place, you'll realize that these people were drunk when they ate here... TIP: Get drunk before you eat here They have this entree called the "Customer Special" which is just Meat, rice, and queso mixed together and spread across a plate... What a "Special" customer indeed. It was probably inspired by the street vomit between this restaurant and the "Exit/In" club. Anyway, the point is that it's bad food, ok service, not too sanitary

Where do I start. I was looking SO forward to going here after reading the reviews. Made reservations based on ubanspooon.com comment turned away. I left VERY disappointed. Had 6 in our party - outside the door everyone rated the place a 4. I believe that they felt they needed to push up the number because my husband I had picked up the tab ($240 + tip, that's with have 2 bottle of wine opened we brought - $24 to uncork, should have be $20 based on previous call made to verify corking charge). Price fair going towards high side - ingredients we had on table for main course / soup we realize are not cheap. Service was good, Lowered to a 3 since I THREW UP during the night from my meal! I believe it was due to the pink amaretto sauce that was put on my pasta. Only one that got sick. AND NO, I haven't threw up from something I ate for many years! I should have ordered the veal! Started out with artichoke they everyone shared - those that are use to this, stated it was done very nicely. Then followed by lobster bisque that I offered to pass around the table - BEST I believe I have eaten, had good size pieces of lobster. Then everyone shared a large bowl of salad which consist of head lettuce, thin sliced tomatoes, I believe eggplant that was very thin and LOTS of olive oil. The bread that was offered on the table didn't seem as it was just baked that day - seemed a day old. Note we were the first customers in the door at 5:15 pm. States they will fix the ingredients how you want - WRONG. I ask to have lobster, shrimp and sea scallops made into a lasagna with a white sauce. TOLD they do not have lasagna. REALLY, you are making pasta for other dishes. One makes the flat noodles first that is used to make lasagna (based on thickness) then cut into other pasta. I know this because I also make my own pasta. Stated never heard such a think - told him I had it made by a 5 star chef and figured that they could make a nice dish as well. NO. So I choose to have pasta with lobster, shrimp and scallops with the pink sauce - which came with also clams, oysters and squid which I did not ask for. Another person had seafood paste with garlic & olive oil (he stated the olive oil was of good quality) without the lobster - guess what, he didn't have any clams, oysters or squid on his????? My husband had a steak along with sea scallops which he stated was good. Two had grouper - one ask for it to be lightly breaded and then pan fried, I felt as he was pushed into having it baked with lemon & butter. While the other one had it baked with a sauce without the spinach he suggested (which is their grouper picante) The last person had Chilean sea bass - she stated it was good. Two had American coffee and one cappuccino - coffee was good. No one had dessert. Except for the steak & scallops - you can see pictures of soup and main dishes on urbanspoon.com - http://www.urbanspoon.com/cities/30-tampa-bay/restaurants/342994-la-trattoria/menu Since they seem to push you to how they want to fix things WHY don't they just list their menu with everything as of market price. I believe this is why they don't offer a menu because of the cost of ingredients that vary especially on the seafood. No different than a restaurant that you request to have a item slightly changed to your liking. On the cart of raw ingredients - huge porterhouse, thick beef filet, strip steak, chicken breast, thin veal cutlets, sea scallops, shrimp, lobster, grouper, & bass. They do offer ravioli of different types as well as having parm of chicken or veal. Would go back for the soup....meal, I don't think so.

So a friend and I drove from Huntsville for a girl's night. The cheese balls appetizer were great, the calamari was mediocre. My main dish was the tortellini with crab meat, which I was skeptical of because I am generally skeptical of inland seafood. Definitely got food poisoning... so I'm gonna skip seafood anywhere that isn't the coast for a while. All in all was a nice dining experience but the food poisoning for a decently expensive pasta is not acceptable.

I love the tea, that's all I go for when I come to this place. Clean environment and good service and didn't try anything else because I am not a crawfish lover or any other food that cross contaminates crawfish or pork; however I really love the tea and that you can purchase it in bulk. Good job.

A family favorite. Something on the menu for anyone. Salads, steaks, burgers, vegetarian, and gluten free. Fabulous service, all orders were accurate and hot from the kitchen. Restaurant is clean and has plenty of parking. Food was wonderful from fish n chips to Cobb salads. Only complaint was my to-go chocolate chip cookie. It was stale and dry. When I took it up to the cashier to see if they had a fresher one, I was advised it had been baked on Sunday. Yes, that's good information, however, I replied that it really didn't matter if it were baked this morning, it was horrible! They traded it out instead of refunding my money. The second one was just as bad. I left totally disgusted.

A Solid 1 star. I convinced my husband that we should go here tonight for happy hour and some food before we go and see a movie at the Flicks. We get to the bar at the end of happy hour. It's pretty empty, the dining side is deserted. We sit at the bar and I order a beer, 1/2 price due to happy hour. The husband has allergies and can't do beer or wine. He clearly asks for a margarita, and is inquiring about the price of 100% agave tequila, for his margarita. She quotes $4.50 for the drink. She then proceeds to pour the tequila on the rocks in a salted glass. Things are looking good. The price is good, the tequila is decent and the service is prompt. She sets the glass in front of the hubby, but it's only naked tequila. He says, "I ordered a margarita". She says "Ok, I'll fix it". She makes the margarita, no problem, all smiles, sets it down and says ok. Problem solved, things are looking good, again, for Solid. We drink our drinks, I get a menu because we weren't offered one. We think about food, and then the bartender comes back. She doesn't ask us if we want something to eat, she has come to tell us that if my husband wants to continue to drink his drink, he now has to pay $7.50 because she had to shake it with some mix. She can take it back if he no longer wants to pay the additional $3.00. WTF? We were going to order food, I thought she may be coming back to ask if I had any menu questions or wanted to order! It was her fault, not ours, that there was a miss quote/ understanding. The drink has already been served and is being consumed! I have worked in the service industry for a really long time. She should have owned her mistake and told us next time the price would be $7.50. We would have tipped her the difference. I also would have ordered food. I really wanted to return my beer and just leave. I also wanted to tell the 2 managers hanging out about our experience. I didn't do either. I drank my beer, paid, and left. I didn't leave a tip, I haven't done that more than twice in my 30 years, but tonight it felt good. That girl clearly should not be in the service industry.

This was the first and last time I go. The Meat was rare even dripping with blood . The plate was red.The silverware was dirty and the Salad bar was not stocked. Very unsafe for people with allergies they were mixing silverware that had been in Shrimp with non seafood items. Too expensive and the food not that good at all. I can't believe they didn't even ask how we wanted our meat.

We have been to this place maybe 6 times. We just kept coming back hoping it would get better. Our first time we went it was opening weekend. They had no idea what they were doing. The food came out in completely random order and they didn't know what food belonged to what table. This they have improved on. Overall the staff is very rude. They don't speak English well and will get frustrated with you quickly when they don't understand you. They are very unaccommodating to allergies and dietary restrictions. They do not say on the menu how much food is in each order. For example, dumplings are two small dumplings, but chicken teriyaki is a full serving size of chicken. It would be fine, but they warn that they will charge you if you do no finish all of the food. They only allow you to have one paper all you can eat menu per table so it can be confusing to order for several people this way. They actually got angry because I made a mistake and accidently checked the wrong salad for another person since they weren't allowed their own paper. The fish is not the freshest. It is really hit or miss depending on the day. Overall, whole Foods next door probably has better quality fish.

My first visit to Philadelphia came along with a craving for some good sushi. After a long day of doing typical center-city Philly touring, I finally got my boyfriend to agree to try sushi for the first time. He is the pickiest of picky eaters (both by personal preference and because of allergies), so I knew I needed to pick a really good place. Trusting my always faithful Yelp! app, I found Bleu. Granted, it wasn't my first choice (the place I wanted to go to had a gap between lunch and dinner), but it was held in high regards. Fellow Yelpers seemed to rave about this place, so I thought it was worth a try considering the circumstances. We walked here from the Independence Hall Center, and it took us about 15 minutes. The outside of the building isn't too much to rave about, considering we almost missed it. It is, however a blue door, with blue-framed windows and small sign that reads Bleu. Go figure. We walked in to a completely empty restaurant. Its a really small place, pretty much just a strip of booths and a center walkway with the actual sushi making station at the back. We were asked if we had a reservation, which seemed odd because the place was completely empty with the exception of the staff. We informed the server wearing Nike sweatpants and a blue t-shirt that we did not, but we were seated immediately anyway. I was quite confused throughout the entire meal service. You have a very trendy, upscale looking restaurant that lives up to the name of Bleu (because literally everything inside is a blue color), yet you have servers and employees that are half dressed in sweatpants and a t-shirt yet the other half wearing slacks and a black button down shirt? I didn't know if we were underdressed or just fitting in? Ok.. Anyhow, we took a look at the menu, and their prices are typical of sushi joints of the same caliber. Please keep in mind that sodas are served by the can! Prices are around $5-$6 for regular rolls, $4-$5 for nigiri, and $10-$15 for specialty rolls. Being the picky eater he is, my boyfriend ordered the teriyaki chicken ($13) as a fallback and I decided for us to share the Rittenhouse roll, the traditional Philly roll (when in Rome), and the Ten Street roll. The Philly roll was the most unedible of them all. It was mainly just mealy and mushy cucumber wrapped into a roll with a teeny bit of salmon and cream cheese. The cucumber was unpleasantly overbearing and left a funny taste in your mouth. Unfortunately, it was the first item my boyfriend tasted, and it made him weary to try anything else. I convinced him to try the rest. The Rittenhouse Square roll was okay at best. It would have been much better if the sprinkling of herbs/seasoning on top was omitted from the recipe. It was honestly a clash of flavors and made the roll taste awkward and out of place. The Town roll was the one that we both enjoyed the most out of the three. Don't be fooled. Just because we liked it the most out of the three doesn't mean it was actually good. It was the most edible. It seemed just like Albacore tuna from a can was dried out, put into a roll and deep fried. Slap some spicy mayo on top and you've just made yourself the Town roll. It was very crunchy, even for a deep-fried roll (almost like the consistency of a Dorito), and was difficult to chew. Service was nearly nonexistent. The only time they really came to check on us was once when my water glass was refilled. At the end of the meal service they brought us two complimentary ice cream samples. They were about the size of a tablespoon each and were a vanilla/peanut butter mixture- very odd for a sushi place to be offering peanut butter ice cream after a meal service? Anyhow, the bill came out to around $51 dollars, and after tip it it was close to around $65. In my personal opinion, this is a very hefty price to pay for sub-par sushi and non existent service. Lesson learned I guess. I'm almost embarrassed that I brought my boyfriend there for his first sushi experience, because it was that un-enjoyable. I'm from the Phoenix, AZ area where sushi is known to be less than favorable, and I have had better from some places in my neighborhood.

I LOVE LOVE LOVE açaí bowls so this place to me was sure to be a hit. I popped in after doing some zip lining at eagle creek state park and it appeared everyone had the same idea. I had two friends with me as well. Since the breakfast bowl is typically a favorite that's what I ordered. First it took about 30 minutes for our bowls to come that was a BIG turn off. Second my friends ordered paninis as well. They never told them they were out of salami instead they had to ask about it. The final thing that really irritated me was we asked for our bowls to dine in and when our name was called it was given to us in to go bowls in a bag. EXTREMELY annoying. But I love the breakfast bowl. They made a delicious error and put peanut butter in mine. Though I thought it was delicious I can only imagine how it could've went south if someone had a nut allergy and expected a nut free bowl. BUT the peanut butter addition was delicious with the strawberries and banana as well as granola. I will give them another chance. Hopefully I'll have better service the next time.

Overpriced for what you get. I order gluten free and the gluten free was so thin and on the soggy side in the middle and almost too hard on the outside. Watch your grill butung into the crust. I dished out around 30 dollars just for a gf pizza. Good flavor but the consistency was way off. They need to improve the gf stuff.

This is advertised as gluten-free. I ordered a gluten free spinach salad, it came with breaded goat cheese and a slice of garlic bread. It was sent back, I began eating it and halfway through bit into a hidden crouton! When I complained the manager told me the chef was making four salads at once, and she was sorry for the error. Not sympathetic at all! Not sure they understand that gluten free means a little more than buying special pasta!

I'm amused at some of the other reviewers using words like,"old-fashioned" and "blue-collar food" and "no-frills." Well, guess what I want from a night out at a steakhouse -- FRILLS! As someone who has worked in over ten restaurants, I don't even know where to start with what is wrong with this place. There were nine people in our party, but they were able to seat us immediately on a Saturday night. (That was a HUGE red flag for me, but we were hungry and I was outvoted by my fellow diners.) The "menu" is printed on cheap paper placemats, a la the kiddie menu at Denny's. And at first, we were confused by the "You cook it" and "We'll cook it for you" sections, but it really is just that. If you want a steak, they bring a raw slab of meat to your table on a cracked, plain, ungarnished plate, and you have to stand over a small, filthy, crowded grill and cook it yourself. (And then, I suppose, put it back on the same plate. Pay no attention to cross-contamination issues...) When I foolishly asked the server (Maude) if I could have a steak cooked for me, she snapped that there was only one cook in the kitchen and he was very busy. Shame on me. Since I'm one of those crazy people who likes to have her food cooked for her when she goes out to a restaurant, I decided to order the salad bar, which came with bread, beans and potato. The salad bar had iceberg lettuce, cucumbers. onion, beets and carrots. Oh, and croutons. That's it. The bread was packaged, white "Texas toast" style, that you took out of the plastic bag yourself. Classy. The beans were tasteless and obviously from a can. The baked potato was wrapped very tightly with cheap, thin aluminum foil that shredded when removed. I'm embarrassed to say that it took me five minutes to get it off the spud and I still got pieces of foil stuck in my teeth. Some of my fellow diners did order rib-eyes, and said that they tasted okay, but when I went by the grill, I overheard other people asking each other how to cook their steaks and where the grill was hottest, cooler, etc. (You weren't expecting there to be anyone supervising the grill or helping out, did you?) The grill itself was covered with thick grime and charred bits of beef, and the metal shakers holding the seasonings were so old and filthy that I wouldn't have touched them if my life depended on it. Normally, I would complain if a waitress grabbed my plate from me before I was done eating, but here I let her do it. I had to ask three different people to refill our water glasses, and I left with a feeling in my gut like I'd just eaten a throw pillow. For all of the people who gave this place good reviews, do yourselves a favor and investigate other steak houses. You might find that they are cleaner and friendlier, the food isn't from a can and it is actually cooked FOR you. My 12 year-old summed it up nicely when referring to the placemat menus,cook-your-own food and lack of service: "Mom, this is the LAZIEST restaurant we've ever been to!" Yup.
I've been here twice.. The place smelled funny the 2nd time and I woke up with food poisoning after

Okay so here's the deal. My husband and I went here on our date night. Everything was great. Our waitress was so sweet and gave us amazing service. The food was excellent, I had the spicy kung pao and my husband had the coconut curry chicken. Very reasonably priced and we left happy and saying that we would definitely come back. Fast forward to 6 hours later, my husband and I are violently ill. I was so sick I ended up in the emergency room for a severe case of food poisoning and dehydration. I missed two days of work. The crazy thing is that I have a very strong stomach. I traveled through Asia and have eaten at the most "questionable" establishments and for me to get this sick must really say something about their kitchen. I wouldn't risk it.

So every Sunday, my mom and I goto brunch after church. Usually we goto the Cheesecake Factory because their omelet portion is HUGE and we just share it. We don't like chain restaurants but that's probably our only exception! Last Sunday we stopped by Half & Half to switch it up after my cousin said it's a must go. She did warn us there would be a wait if we went between 10am-1pm on the weekend - we showed up around 11:15 or so, and yes, we waited. And waited. AND waited. We were told 35 minutes, that turned into 1 1/2 hours. This place is SMALL. And the crowd is BIG. The wait is LONG. And you can't sit at the bar, or anywhere if you're waiting. You basically stand. It's like being at a college bar, it's crowded! While waiting, my mom had coffee and really enjoyed it - the coffee is rather inexpensive too. I had some green tea, pretty good. We were finally seated - at the high top table, which is wobbly. So are the chairs. I was scared mine was going to break, it was that wobbly. There was a group of 5 people standing next to our table CONSTANTLY bumping our table making it shake, it was beyond annoying. Especially for my mom who was sitting at the end of the table, and the table was nailing her in her chest and stomach. We ordered the cali omelet and asked for brussels sprouts to be added & light on the cheese (I'm lactose intolerant) - it came with house potatoes and toast, we had whole wheat. While waiting, we started with some mixed fruit, which was really fresh. Comes with homemade whip cream - yum. Our omelet comes out - Looked good, lots of avocado, etc. Well, I had to send it back because it was LOADED with cheese. So we send it back.... It comes back, a little light on the cheese, but then while eating it - We notice: 1. NO black beans 2. NO brussels sprouts 3. Didn't get our toast back 4. MUCH less avocado So basically this omelet was a plain omelet with nothing in it that it is supposed to acquire. So we sent it back (embarrassingly) - 3 times a charm right? This time, the chef brings it out, and it was done how it was supposed to be done. I usually don't complain about food because I'm not picky, but when it concerns my health, I got to... And the fact it came out TWICE not correct - that's not good. This place as a lot of hype. Other dishes looked pretty good though, I will admit. But having to wait THAT long and having to return our food TWICE, wasn't a pleasant first time visit here. If you do come here, come early, or come during the week. Or else you'll be standing and waiting for a very very long time. The building is entirely too small for the big crowd that it seems to attract. I suggest expanding, something, and adding a small area of chairs or couches where people can wait, because everyone standing around and BUMPING our table consistently is quite annoying.

Catfish, come on! Hot links, damn! Ribs, stop it! THIS is real BBQ!!! Getchu some! Best food in the area bar none. I wish it was open later but that's my only complaint. My new favorite is the chicken strips tossed in a garlic parmesan sauce w/ mac and cheese and a fried pickle. They serve it with ranch but, since I'm of the opinion that ranch dressing tastes like baby vomit I request blue cheese.

DO NOT GO HERE! I went here for the first time last week with a date. I really wanted to like this place. The vibe of this place was like a more-modernized, lower grade version of my favorite cocktail bar, the ranstead room. Our waitress was not very friendly and super-rushed. The food was ok, but certainly not good enough to warrant a return. The cocktails were overpriced for the quality that we got. All of this would have been ok except that I suddenly got really dizzy and nauseous about 30 minutes into my visit after trying a few of their dishes and a cocktail. By the time I left, I was sweating and feeling absolutely horrible. I managed to make it home, where I spent the next 3 painful hours in the bathroom. I must have gotten food poisoning from the food or drink. I'll never go back, and with so many other great options for food in center city, I wouldn't recommend going here.
Food is okay, and the place smells very bad. When we were eating outside by the door every time the door would open I wanted to vomit, it smelled like sewer water.

1st visit today. I had the asparagus Eggs Benedict and my wife had plain flapjacks. First was the "plain" flapjacks. 3 Light, fluffy pancakes and a real good size. Problem was the strawberry on top of the stack, so much for the plain. It should have Bergen noted for allergy reasons but was not. So at least I got to try one of then. As for my Eggs Benedict it fell real flat for me. While the hollandaise was perfect the eggs were cooked through and not soft at all. The asparagus was just cut stems and no tips all all. And the stems were so tough they could not be eaten. Plus the menu said it came with hot cinnamon apples but I did not get those. I'm wondering if this is new ownership since it looks different from the photos, everything is not in Greek style blue and white. Not really seeing why people I spoke with rave about the food.

The Colonial Diner in Woodbury, NJ is not only the best diner in South Jersey, but quite possibly the greatest diner in the entire country. One of my favorite dishes is the "Bronco Burger". A husky, meaty, and scrumptious mouthful of onion rings, beef, and bacon from the largest pigs in the tri-state area. Make sure if you DO decide to conquer the "Bronco Burger" you remove one of the three massive onion rings so you avoid cracking your jaw open while taking that first bite. Not to mention- this dish is only $7.99. An absolute STEAL! Fun Fact : the "Bronco Burger" comes with a side of cheese and BBQ sauce! But really, it's not BBQ sauce but some other type of sauce that nearly made me projectile vomit across the table at my girlfriend. YUCK! :p Complementing the "Bronco Burger" is a girthy dill, and a small cup of milky coleslaw. Now if that isn't enough to make your mouth water, I don't know what will! The water...well simply the water is TO DIE FOR. However, the lemon was quite thin cut compared to other restaurants such as The Melting Pot. As a man with a unique eye for lemon cut sizes, I was sadly disappointed. As well as my feelings toward the lemons, the Colonial Diner's selection of toothpicks were scarce. And if I were asked to comment on the quality of the toothpicks, I would have to answer with "poor". Colonial Diner will forever be a 5/5 in my book. As good as it gets!

I have been here quit a few times longed the nice line hanging out the door and all that because this place had a very very nice home atmosphere. Today was not the case the people that work behind the counters are usually quit awesome and very helpful on making your final choice. Today the workers were just simply rude between the snarls the lade was giving me and the confusion the first guy had when trying to make my ice cream and the just rudeness of all 4 workers over all. Not to mention my ice cream tasted like crap this time the guy mixing it all up took the lemon syrup and just poured it all on there so when i wanted a different one because it was pure lemon flavored and i wanted the critic fruit ice cream, that just told me i would have to pay for a new one. So i payed for my ice cream and just threw it away and sat there while my girlfriend ate hers. I will never go back there after my experience today and that really sucks because with being lactose intolerant theres really no where else to go.

Oh Oscar's. Two of my friends really like Oscar's so I was happy to give it a try. By text I invited another friend to join us and she said, "I was once projectile vomited on at Oscars so no thanks." This should have been a red flag. Firstly I loved the bouncer. Unlike the douchey body-builder jerks that are bouncers at most Center City bars, this was a friendly older guy in a tie dye shirt. The decor is something out of another era--probably literally, it looks like they have not updated anything since 1974, but that is part of what I really liked about this bar. The patrons were mostly too-drunk and in their mid 30s and above. This is probably the least pretentious place I've been to in Center City. Drinks are cheap, things are a little dingy, and you expect to find a bowling alley somewhere inside. It is not flashy and stylish but I love that. It's also not like a lot of places in the Fishtown area that try to recreate the vintage feel of Oscar's. Oscar's is the real deal. On the downside, the waitress was incredibly rude. We waited at a booth for quite some time and no one came to serve us so my friends went to buy drinks at the bar. The waitress finally appeared out of nowhere and said that the booth was "waitress service only." Me and our other friend had not yet gotten a drink so I walked over to her to ask if she would be coming to our table or if I should go to the bar. She rudely kept walking away from me as I tried to politely ask her. She acted as if I was not even there. After a long wait she did come and serve us but I was not at all happy with the way she treated me.

This is hands down the worst Japanese restaurant I have ever been to! The hot tea tasted salty, the salad was terrible. I had a tempura shrimp sushi roll which was OK. My husband had teriyaki chicken which was a hot mess. Everything we ate was cooked, nothing raw. But on top of that, I got food poisoning. Never again! If I could give it minus 3 stars, I would.
Used to love Bru for its gluten free options, but since they added a flour coating to their fries it's really cut down the menu choices.

Really disappointed tonight at the Slider House. Was told there were vegetarian and gluten free sliders only to be told the vegetarian options weren't gluten free and then when trying to ordering being told they are out of gluten free buns so I just needed up getting fries.

Ignorant and inconsiderate!!! Do not even attempt to eat here if you have any type of food allergy or dietary restriction. They are completely inconsiderate of making any accommodations. my friend took her daughter here who is lactose intolerant. She brought her own almond milk for her and they refused to allow her daughter to drink it. She offered to pay for a regular glass of chocolate milk and they said no, no outside food is allowed and she would have to drink something else. you mean to tell me if someone came to this restaurant with a baby they would not allow the baby to be bottle fed? This is absolutely unacceptable and they will NEVER get my business.

First of all we don't frequent chain Italian restaurants. We like the authentic mom and pop experience and I did research here on yelp to help pick this place. Worst experience and meal especially at an Italian restaurant ever. We had reservations and the owner was rude from the minute we walked in the door. We had made reservations an hour earlier and it was as though he wanted us not to have reservations. It said kid friendly but wasn't sure if it was our 4 year old twins that are and were extremely well behaved that set him off. I would NOT rate this as a kid friendly establishment. We were seated and a server whom was hard to understand showed us a choice of appetizers. None had interested us but we had the house salad and that was iceberg lettuce, a few mushrooms and tomatoes with oil and maybe vinegar. Okay but nothing special. Then we waited 45 minutes and the owner told the server to take our order and delegated another few tables to the servers. We had no menu and the waitress just asked what we wanted. Never explained sauces- nothing. Felt very fast food-like. The other tables the owner brought his cart and did a nice speel and showed them all his "proteins". He listened to what the people wanted and took their orders. My hubby got pork chops and they were huge, tasteless and covered with mushrooms and a brown sauce. It was stuffed with prosciutto and cheese. It was thick, touch and dry yet still pink in it and the worst pork chop it ever had. I definitely make better myself. I had eggplant parmesean and it was soggy and the 2nd to worst I've ever had. I didn't like the sauce at all. Very bland. The worst I've had would have been better had it been cooked through, it would have been better. We were really hoping for a nice experience and some great food as we have many mom and pop Italian restaurants across the west coast we've feel in love with. Absolutely not this one. The owner came over trying to get my hubby to encourage the table next to our give a good review to entice them and my husband was honest and was even nice and said it was "good" not wanting to insult him. He really tried pushing him to up his opinion. He wasn't concerned he didn't like his plate rather more About how could you not like it. I'd give zero stars but my kids liked their fettuccine a lot and are the spaghetti that cake with my eggplant parmesean. I'm 5 months pregnant and had an appetite and leaving hungry because I just couldn't stomach the food. The owner never greeted us. The pork chops were $25, fettuccine was $15 and eggplant parmesean was $15 and $4 for salad and my hubby had a glass of wine and the bill came to $70. I cringed having that experience and paying that much. I've never had such a bad experience so had no clue what to do!! We ate at Broadway deli for lunch and had an awesome meal though! Serendipity cafe was awesome too! You want mom & pop go to serendipty as the mom cooked, dad visited with us and their daughter was our server! This is my first review ever to warn people of the experience they may have:-( Hopefully yours is better! Update- I think both my husband and I got food poisoning from this place:-( both are sick as I had tried his pork chop. Luckily the kids never tried any. I should have showed them how pink it was inside:-(

This place is awesome! It is not the BEST sushi i have ever had but it is above average and SUPER convenient to the convention center. I am the meeting manager for the conference in town which means i have been working 14+ hour days. When I get back to my hotel room at the Marriott the last thing I wanted to do was go back out to grab dinner at 9pm so two nights in a row I ordered here. I used Foodler to place my order and I love the $10 minimum (vs the $15 that other places had since i am only ordering for one person). Maybe it is b/c I am from the DC suburbs but these prices are not high at all to me. PLUS, who wants to buy "cheap/discounted" sushi... ummm food poisoning anyone? Just kidding, kind of. Any way, the food was good, I preferred the california rolls I got the first night which had the mayo in them b/c without the mayo the flavor was lacking a bit, however, overall it was still good and a healthy option over BurgerFi (who has gotten my order wrong not TWO, like I said in my reviews, but THREE times now)... they meet me in my hotel lobby and it is super easy to order using foodler.com. The smoked salmon and avocado roll is good too (philadelphia roll with no cream cheese). The rice to filling ratio IS great... not too much rice... i hate places that give me too much rice bc/ that is the part i dont want. I was going to try the pork Gyoza but did not b/c the two rolls filled me up the first night so I didnt want to add anything the second time. I would definitely dine there again... I may have to order from there one more time before i head back home!

Meh. This was actually my very first IHOP experience of my life, which is kind of amazing. I'd always heard such amazing things and was kind of disappointed. I should preface this by saying that I'm not big on breakfast foods so that's probably where the problem comes in for me. I am also gluten free and there weren't many options for me. Prices were high IMHO and service was so-so. Meh meh meh

We tried the peanut butter bacon burger, blue cheese burger, baked potato, and gumbo. I like peanut butter in general so I liked the burger but some of the other people still thought it was too weird. The burgers are all pretty big. The baked potato was drenched in butter. This was the first time I had gumbo so I don't have anything to compare it to but I didn't like it very much. It was very watery with a little bit of rice and sausage. It was a bit salty and had a strange taste to it. All of the burgers tasted fine but it wasn't anything spectacular. I think the most interesting thing about this place are the unique types of burgers. Each burger is about $11. The main problem I have with the food here was the fact that I and two other people in my party ended up with a mild case of food poisoning after eating here. We couldn't figure out what caused it because we all had ordered different things and another girl that ordered the same thing I got was fine. We suspect that the food poisoning is from the way that the food was prepared. Food poisoning is not fun when you are on vacation!!! As for environment, it was a strange place. It is very small with limited seating. They had dark red lighting and the place just felt dingy and dirty. Overall, I think there are many better places you can go to.

My experience with this restaurant was the worst! Here are the reasons you should consider to avoid this place. TOO MUCH MSG - I am allergy to MSG, after diner I felt sour and bitter from my mouth. My mouth was very dry after diner, which was the sign of too much MSG! WORST SERVICE - My water was never refilled till I ask. There were only 9 tables, we waited for one hour. The OWNER was not patience; but the hired waiter and waitress were much better.....avoid the owner!! FOOD -- The food was nothing special, we order SCALLION style pork....ended we got ONION style pork which is not much different from the take out restaurant. I WILL NEVER GO BACK TO THIS RESTAURANT! Again, you can't trust the marketing!

I went there with my family a little while ago for the first time since I had heard great reviews. I have to say I left disappointed. My sister ordered the borch soup and gluten free club sandwich. The sandwich was delicious and I was fortunate that she shared since I sent back my food. I had the gluten free turkey burger- Disgusting doesn't start to describe how awful is was. The burger had too much thyme (and I love thyme) and the meat tasted bad and for some odd reason tasted moldy. The bun was also horrible, big and dry. I was completely turned off. Being celiac I have had terrible gluten free items, however there are really great buns out there. At a restaurant I would expect them to serve only the best to their customers. My mom had the gluten free curry chicken. It was really spicy, made with yellow curry... too much curry. It was pretty much inedible. The veggies were the only good part of the dish. Personally I would recommend maybe using a red curry with coconut milk- that would be delicious. The dish was simply one tone- yellow curry. The decor is eclectic... a mix match of everything. Service was ok. I may go back to on a thursday to try their Ukrainian night. Perhaps the regular menu is better than the gf menu... I don't know. The only item I would recommend is the gf club house sandwich.

I usually enjoy going to Texas Roadhouse with my family. Their food is usually delicious. Not last night however. The service was fairly quick and we were seated in a short amount of time. We ordered, ate some peanuts, and dived in to the rolls. We also ordered a Blooming Onion. Our food came and we began to eat. Both of my parent's steaks were undercooked. I got an All American cheeseburger with lettuce and tomato. I devoured it and ate my fries. I thought everything was fine. It wasn't though. When I woke up the next day I had a terrible headache along with stomach cramps. Turns out I had food poisoning. In conclusion, stay away from the burgers unless you want to spend your day by the toilet.

After stopping here yesterday for a late lunch, my fiancé has food poisoning. The only place we ate yesterday and thankfully we didn't eat the same thing. He had a savory beef soup and the salad bar and about an hour later became violently ill. Looks like a trip to the ER will be in our future.

I think the A-OK rating captures Down the Hatch perfectly.
