I've literally passed by the place multiple times, and it hadn't registered on my radar until being informed of their amazing game day special. I don't want to activate any hipster alerts, but I love me some $1 PBR. Although you would never expect it, Down the Hatch has a rather large back patio. I asked if they were dog friendly, and we have a winner! It's a little awkward to access the back patio with pupster because you have to walk through the front bar. I was peaking my head around multiple times to see if there was some sort of back entrance. None found, so I just moseyed on through. Although dog shenanigans don't bother me, if you know anyone with some sort of dog aversion/allergies this set up may bother them. Otherwise the back patio was great and not at all crowded for the game. They even had cool patio cushioned chairs to sit in, which were very cozy. So, we have beer, check! Game, check! What's next? Wings!!! I really love the wings here.... big, crispy and spicy (although I'm sure the sauce is a standard buffalo, franks maybe?). I would love to see more flavors on the menu since they do them so perfectly. That being said some of the other appetizers I had were not as amazing. I unfortunately was not a huge fan of the chicken nachos, as they were made with the movie theater style nacho cheese, and for the $11 price tag I was expecting some more shredded cheddar. Also, the cheese fries are made in a similar manner with the same nacho cheese, but these at least had the shredded variety as well. Anyways not to berate their cheese selection or to appear like a cheese snob with my $1 PBR, I would suggest sticking with the wings..... another round bar keep! Some other cool details about the place is they do have a back bar, which is very convenient for PBR refills, however, they make some of their mixed drinks at the front. For example, my Bloody Mary starters was made at the front, and then brought to the table. Their bloodies are good, and upon ordering a second round I learned they had vegetable infused vodka, cool let's give that a shot! I liked it, but I'm still on the fence on the $1.50 upcharge (that's a PBR and a 1/2!). Another funny/silly detail about the game day special is if you order a coke it's $2. Beer is cheaper than soda!?! Either way having said $1 and PBR enough times to sound like a cheapo, I admit that sometimes I am, but that doesn't mean you can't be too! Down the Hatch I will be back, with friends.

Props to Jules for vegan and gluten free options. It is fabulous that they use local organic ingredients and an impressive array of toppings. However, my praise ends there. Everytime I have visited I have been underwhelmed. Most recently I placed an order for a kids pie online. I stood at the counter unacknowledged for quite a bit while several workers waited on counter orders. I don't mind waiting but acknowledge me please. Plus, it wasn't overwhelmingly busy. It wasn't even 5 pm yet! After paying for my $15 pizza, I continued to wait another 10 minutes for my order. This brought my total wait time to almost 40 minutes! The pizza crust was chewy and kind of stale, not crisp and fresh. It was almost room temperature (had to sneak a bite bc I was starving) which leads me to believe it was siting there for awhile while I waited. The sauce was good but the cheese was super salty. In addition, I bought a treat for my kids- a grain exchange brownie for a whopping 4 dollars! This was one of many bad experiences here. Once I ordered a vegan pizza excited because they use Daiya cheese. They actually made me a pizza with moldy cheese! They made me another pizza without cheese, and gave me a credit, but how gross is that! There is one male manager who is very nice and friendly, however the rest of the workers seem to act as if they are doing you a favor. In summary, if you want to make yourself feel better by patronizing a place that advertises as being local and organic, great but don't accept freshness or timely service with a smile either. Visit a local farmer's market, google a recipe and make your own. Your pocket and tastebuds will thank you.

Food poisoning and bad margaritas! The food was ok, not bad but not spectacular. The margarita was unimpressive. We might have considered coming back but about 5 hours later the food poisoning set in.... And we were miserable for about 24-36 hours afterwards.... On what turned out to be the first night spent together, which of course was ruined.

Ok Mexican food... for Louisiana. If I stacked it against California Mexican food it would sadly come up much shorter on the flavor scale. Service was ok but seriously dont nod your head when I ask about gluten free options and you have no clue what gluten free means. Thats cool if you dont know, just dont fake it and get someone sick. Fajitas were decent. Prices weren't terrible. Service was ok. Told them I had to catch a flight up front and they accomodated.

So I have been dying to try this place out and finally made it in today. They have a credit card limit of $10 and I didn't have cash...fine...no biggy I'll get a lil sample of things. I got the tomato pie: totally soggy crust...not so great, I've def had better. A Banana cupcake with Maple Frosting: I agree with everyone else's reviews, it tasted like cardboard and was really dry. The sandwich cookie was good and the filling was nice because it wasn't too dense and didn't overpower the cookie. These things came to a total of $9 and they would not let me charge it! Really guys?? I was one dollar off! (So I got a cookie and it was ok.) For a vegan, I've had better, for it being gluten free, it was ok, but not convincing. And they really need to relax on their credit card policy or just not use credit cards at all.

Came here for breakfast after a night of drinking with my friends following a wedding. Walked in and it seemed everyone knew each other by first name. The customers and workers seemed to all be on a first name basis which was cool. It has that crappy diner feel which I love. If dirty spoons and plates gross you out, or you can't take rude service, just stop reading and go somewhere else. Seemed to be located on the verge of downtown Nashville and the ghetto. Everything is old and worn out and the service has a southern hospitality feel with a little attitude served on the side. Being inside this restaurant is entertaining. Mainly the locals that come here and how they interact with the workers. At one point I heard some yelling coming from behind the sink. One of the workers was washing the dishes and stopped ...looked up and yelled at a customer saying "What? Is me washing the dishes bothering you? Too loud? Well I'll tell you what...why don't you take those napkins on your table...ball em up..and stick em in your ears so you don't have to hear it, because I don't give a damn, I've got a job to do." The waitress also came by our table with more coffee, we all told her we didn't want anymore. She proceeded to fill up our cups anyway and said, "well I'm filling them up anyway because I'm not coming back with this coffee pot." The food itself was pretty good. I got the scrambled eggs, sausage, and biscuits and gravy. Holy shit there was so much gravy I couldn't see the biscuits underneath. My girlfriend who was with me is from California, not used to southern diners at all. When we got our food there was a big old hair on her plate in her eggs. She took one look at it.. went to the bathroom, threw up, and then came back and ate all her food. Haha so many good memories from just one visit to the place. I would def recommend going if you havn't been. You have been warned tho! And one last thing, they only take cash. They do have an ATM inside, but it charges $3.00 to use it so I recommend coming with cash. I would have given this place 5 stars if I didn't have to waste money pulling cash out of that ATM.

The food is great and the service was pretty decent......however a few policies need to be changed. First of all the no substitution clause causes issues for those who are diabetic like my husband and I are or someone may have food allergies. For example most of of the sandwiches are served with French Fries and we may not want fries( or any kind of potato or any thing deep fried) with our sandwich or even a side dish or possibly we may want applesauce or fruit but that seems to be available ONLY for kids menus......we have to watch our carb intake.The next big gripe is that the meals are very big and the three dollar plate sharing charge is just too much...... I could see one dollar. Both my husband and I can't eat a big portion at one sitting and no, salad nor soup nor even an appetizer cut it and truth to be told we have to avoid most of the appetizer choices.

One of the worst experiences I've ever had at a Panera. My Mac n cheese was barely full compared to the SAME SIZE my cousin and friend got ~ I asked them to please add a little more and they refused because it is prepackaged. I also asked for NO TOMATOES in my salad and yet , I still found one. This is extremely dangerous for people with food allergies: the manager was compliant and understanding and in turn gave me my money back ~ but it is still a danger.
Ate bad fish or something from this place. Woke up sick as a dog in the middle of the night on Christmas Eve. Oh what a wonderful way to spend my Christmas Day, with food poisoning!

Have been going here for years, therefore, let me lay some knowledge on Ya'll...s The good: *Hot and Sour soup *Seafood soup with or without the noodles *Lemongrass seafood soup (make sure you tell them to make it 1/3 the spice otherwise your toilet god will be pleased but your lower intestines wouldn't) *Vegie/Pork dumplings *General Tso's chicken *Singapore mai fun The bland: *Eggroll - the dough is too thick and over saturated with oil *Chicken with garlic sauce - somehow the chicken is always bland, like a piece of gum that was chewed for 10 hours straight and then left on the sun for a week (no, I didn't try such a gum but I do have a vivid imagination) *Beef with onions - I got a food poisoning once from their beef (like somebody mentioned below) so I just avoid it. *My regular server, Wendi is not there anymore. So sad!
Love that there is another breakfast place in Brentwood. Food is good but a little pricey. For a biscuit house, they should offer a gluten free biscuit.

Update: This visit we tried brunch, and sat in the main dining room instead of our usual spot in the bar. The dining room is a lovely light filled space. I ordered a Bloody Mary, made with their in-house fresh tomato juice. The drink had a perfect flavor balance, but was devoid of any garnishment, not even a celery stick. It would have been taken up to five star status by having some sort of garnish; pickled vegetables would be a nice touch. We shared an order of the goat cheese beignets which arrived warm sitting atop a caramel dipping sauce and dusted with powdered sugar. A definite hit. All four of us had the roasted root vegetable hash topped with two eggs and all four of us thoroughly enjoyed the dish. So overall another great meal. Cut to the chase-I may have just had the best meal so far in over a year in Nashville. Now back to the beginning. The Old School Farm is so much more than a restaurant, make it a destination and plan on relaxing, unwinding and sitting a spell. After all, you didn't take the drive out in the country to hurry things, now did you? We arrived early on a Friday, and made our way into the bar for a flight of ciders. They have several local beers on tap as well as Guinness, along with the above mentioned ciders. The wine list looked extensive and they're crafting some very inventive house made cocktails. We sampled the Bloody Mary with house made tomato juice bursting with the flavor of the garden. They have a beautiful large bar room with stage for live music and tables to dine here besides the main dining room. Since they weren't yet busy we could engage with the staff and learn more about the wonderful program the Old School Farm supports as well as their bee keeping endeavors. The menu changes weekly depending on what's fresh from the garden and the local farms. We decided on three plates to share. A roasted eggplant dip with grilled flatbread, roasted baby beets over yogurt drizzled with their local honey, and the shining star- sweet corn ricotta tortellini with pea shoots and soft boiled quail egg with chili oil. One bite of the tortellini and we both declared it the best pasta we can remember having. We finished our meal with a dessert of deconstructed grasshopper pie. Every plate was a winner. While we were dining the jazz quartet added to the ambience. We took time to walk the property, admiring their gardens, chicken coops and bee hives. It looks like they have an open air building that would be perfect for weddings or events. A visit here is so much more than just a meal, it's an experience worth taking your time to explore.

Possibly the worst restaurant experience I've ever had. The service was super slow, starting with a 20 minute wait with a reservation. After a hour, the place filled with smoke that burned my eyes. To top it all off, something in my girlfriend's food gave her a violent allergic reaction that she's never had before. Given the other yelp reviews, maybe I was just there on their worst night. But I can't recommend this place to anyone based on my experience.

Went for the first time for lunch, paid $8 for the buffet. Clean large and open environment. Better than alot of the cramped dark Chinese buffets that are much more common and usually end in food poisoning. The food quality was above average for a buffet and everything I saw at the time was clean. The food was hot and seemed to be rotated in between my trips to the spread. Sushi was decent as well. Our server was on top of the drinks making sure our cups never ran empty. All in all for the price and quality of food I'd say its the best bang for your buck if you are looking for a Chinese buffet to pig out at.

After reading all the negative reviews about the slow service and bad food I was hesitant about trying this place. Fortunately this time YELP was wrong. We went on a Thursday night and there wasn't any parking on the street so we parked in the CVS lot. As you enter the front door there is a small waiting area with a hostess stand and stairs to the upper dining area. We had reservations for 8pm and we chose to sit at the bar. As you walk in the bar lines the right side wall and there is a wood burning fireplace in the center of the dining area. Several tables with bright red chairs are scattered throughout the interior. They have draperies hung so it seems they can close off some of the dining area if needed. The bar has about 22 taps two of them are hand pumped. The draft list is written on the wall to the right of the bar. They had a very good selection to choose from. I had a Edmund Fitzgerald and a Dog Fish Festina. I wanted to try their dipping sauce for the fires so I got the Emlen Burger ( bacon / chedder) and my girlfriend had the Chicken Salad Croissant Sandwich. Our food came over quickly. The burger was juicy and cooked medium rare as I requested. The bun was fresh and doughy. The burgers are gluten free. I had a bite of my girlfriends Croissant and it was also very well put together. The chicken was chopped and not diced and they added the perfect amount of mayo. The only reason I gave Goat Hollow 3 stars vs 4 is because the bartender wasn't that great. I waited a good amount of time before he asked me if I wanted another beer. It seemed he was more concerned with cleaning glasses and saying hello to everyone walking in. The other thing I didn't like was the bar stools. They were metal with no cushion and I thought they were very uncomfortable. The total for our meal was $39. I thought this was a good valve for what we had and I will come back again.

FOOD POISONING!! Okay I really didn't want to write a bad review but here I am ...... I love Yummy house and was sooo excited to have one come to South Tampa .. I took my mom about a week ago, it was close to closing time (for lunch) and we just got a few things. The staff was extremely rude and rushed us as they were still seating other tables .. food was whatever chalked it up to I won't come back but don't need to write a bad review. Well my boyfriend took his daughters last night, they ordered orange chicken, a beef dish and vegetable bistro rice. Everyone was literally fighting for the bathroom by the time they made it home.. my boyfriend is a doctor and has legit food poisoning, basically didn't leave the restroom last night vomiting and diarrhea for hours and hours. Had to call out from work today. I won't be back ......

I was a little iffy about grabbing breakfast here while visiting town with a couple friends. (We were randomly wandering the city Sunday morning and had trouble finding a reasonable priced place for breakfast. Where are all the diners in this area?) .This and the deli across the street kind of look out of place (a bit run down) in this nicer, older neighborhood, but we stopped in anyway. It pretty much looks like a ghetto mini mart, but they have a nice sized breakfast menu and they make other sandwiches as well. The platters come with two eggs (your choice of style), a side (sausage, etc.), and pancakes or french toast. Nothing impressive, but it was quick and cheap, and I didn't get food poisoning from eating it! While waiting for the order, the phone was ringing off the hook of people ordering breakfast sandwiches, which reassured me. They also have a decent selection of convenience-store type items. Not too sure if the cat wandering the aisles is really up to health code, but he/she was very friendly, as were the workers. It would have been better if there was a table outside, but we just walked to a nearby park.

Pros - Very cute exterior and interior. - Delicious pineapple upside down cake - my friend enjoyed her sticky bun without raisins and was thankful they made both options - Took a chocolate donut to go and it was still soft and delicious the next day Cons - My bagel was very soft and one of the best GF bagels I have had in terms of texture but had zero flavor, ever the onion on top didn't come through at all which was such a disappointment, and it took about 10 minutes so I wouldn't order a bagel if you are in a rush. I wouldn't have minded as much if they told me when I ordered that it was going to be a while. - As with most dedicated GF places the prices here are significantly higher than other bakeries/deli's which I understand and am used to however, what was bothersome was that none of the baked goods were labeled with what they were (or showed ingredients) and nothing had prices on them, literally nothing except the bagels and coffee on the chalk board that hung above the counter. Thankfully someone in front of me had asked for some explanations and prices on a few things so that I didn't have to stand there and ask over & over with each product I was thinking of getting, especially b/c the young girl working at the counter had to look each thing up in the register, I have to assume she was new b/c she had no idea what was going on. They had samples out but they weren't labeled so I wasn't completely sure what I was trying & had to ask. The whole experience just took a lot of effort, way more than it should have when I'm trying to spend my money. I would strongly suggest labels with prices and what the products are, it's not that I'm cheap but buying GF can add up really quickly and someone shouldn't have to stand there and ask 10 times, "how much is this"? Lastly, please add an ingredients list somewhere, even if it's just a laminated card on the counter as many of us have other food allergies in addition to the standard dairy and nut.

DO NOT EAT HERE. Got severe and violent food poisoning from the chicken in my stir fry. Also when talking to my friend about it she said her sister used to work at natural cafe and that employees don't always wash their hands and that it was pretty unhygienic in general. Save yourself from a long night of retching.

Went here for the first time and was extremely disappointed!! ALL the food on the buffet we tried was cold. Hardly warm at all. Was also very stale tasting. We will NEVER be going back. This place also gave me food poisoning because they do not properly care for their food.

Visiting Philly and craving Miga, we had to quickly find a good Korean substitute. My friend's co-worker's Korean wife directed us to Sammy Chon's. Note: THIS IS A CHAIN, so with all due respect for momma Chon and her recipes, this is not the place I thought it would be. The best part of the visit was the service - our server, an additional server and the manager/owner were great. The ambiance was ok (made me think it was not a chain - tricky, tricky!). The food was hit or miss. I could not eat most of the banchan due to a seafood allergy (this is the 1st time I have had this issue at a Korean restaurant. They mix shrimp sauce/paste in everything) I ordered the kimchee pancakes and the chicken bulgogi dolsot bibimbap style. The kimchee pancakes had a great kimchee taste and a krispy crust that was heaven! It was also soggy in places and the onions were mushy. The chicken bulgogi dolsot bibimbap was MISSING THE EGG and when I pointed this out I was told it was included - just not on top. It was not! My friend had some soup, which she enjoyed. They gave everyone complimentary mini-yogurt drink, which I could have used without. All in all, I would say that in the absence of Miga, this would suffice. It would not be my 1st choice or recommendation to a friend.

Booked a table for my boyfriend's birthday. While the host and waiter were lovely, the chef was less than pleasant or accommodating when asked about options that were allergy-friendly. Don't get me wrong, I understand that it is difficult for a chef to work around allergens, but the fact that upon reading the provided allergy card (which says "COW MILK - including butter and cheese"), he said "Well there's nothing on here about no butter" made me wonder where his culinary degree was acquired. Thanks, but no thanks, we had a lovely dinner elsewhere.

I made a yelp account just to write a review on this dump. My first experience here I walked in and ordered General toss chicken. They brought me my drink and then I look back and see the cook open the fridge and put a plate in the microwave. I wasn't even there 2 minutes and the lady brings out my plate and told me that someone ordered the same order and didn't pick it up so that's why it was so quick, she lied right to my face. They literally served me a meal that was sitting in the fridge for god knows how long. The chicken was deplorable and rubbery and obviously old microwaved crap. I took one bite than walked out. My brother decides to order from here the next week I didn't tell him my bad experience, he ordered fried wonton, he ate two of them and complained it tasted funny, I open it up to find the pork was RAW!!!!!. He then calls back to complain and they was very disrespectful and said the he probobly won't get sick and "we have insurance so it's okay". He got food poisoning and was terribly sick from this place. Save yourself the trouble and avoid this place!!!!!!!!

Our waitress was sweet but got a few things wrong and that I can overlook. I had one espresso martini and the short rib burger. This was the only thing I had eaten today as it was for brunch with family from out of state. My drink tasted like the vodka was cheap and I understand that it probably would be since the martini was really inexpensive. The short rib burger tasted pretty good and I thought the curly fries were good as well. My issue is the severe stomach pains and vomiting I experienced a few hours later. It was so bad I was actually happy to vomit to stop the pain. I really believe I got food poisoning from this place.

Um NO! This is the worst Sushi I have ever eaten! SAVE YOUR MONEY.. Go to hiroba or tha joint instead! OK, So I was craving sushi, like always, and i happened to receive a coupon in the mail for Oceano inside the peppermill. My husband and I went that night, excited to sink our teeth in to some fresh Fish! To my surprise, Everything sucked! We ordered about 12 rolls and a bunch of nigiri. First of all the squid, way way fishy. Yuck! My biggest gripe though, is the fact that almost every single roll is filled with a long huge chunk of fake crab. no creativity or anything. Their signature roll, the Oceano, may have been the worst. It was 2 long pieces of imitation crab wrapped in rice and topped with more shredded crab with tons of mayo. No joke. I am not sure if this particular sushi chef made the roll wrong but this def was not the description that i read. The only things I liked was the Octopus, the quail egg shooters, and the miso soup! I told the waiter that I was not particularly happy with the quality of the food and he apologized. He came back a few minutes later and told me he was not going to charge me for my ayce. I was pleased with this seeing that this gross food would have cost $23.99 each (most expensive in town) He then asked if i wanted to try anything else. I chose to try a bowl of the lobster bisque soup. I had one bite and wanted to vomit. It was terrible. I will never eat here again. I gave this place 2 stars only because i appreciate how the waiter handled my problem. I was not looking for a free meal, and I wasn't really complaining to him. Just wanted him to know that I was surprised at the quality of the food. Anyways.. Save your time and Money!

Inconsistency drives the star mark between a 2 and a 3 star rating for me. Between the vibe of the place being a little fruity and the gluten-free fact, my first go around I just wasn't sure. When I realized the mimosas were $3 at happy hour and they had a loaded nacho fries dish, I got past it and went to town. It was pretty good. The fries were really good and the topics were fair. $3 mimosas, yeah... The next three times I have been have gotten slightly worse, where in one outing my wife's meal was really good. During my last visit, I got 4 shrimp and soupy grits for $16 and a hot beer (although she did warn me the fridge was a bit warm). I think I will stick to the mimosas to match the star rating.
Likely got food poisoning on Friday the 10th of November. Had blackened fish tacos and exactly 24 hots later, boom. Sick as a dog. Service was crappy on top of it.

I really did want to like this place...bowling, pool, beer, food! How can you go wrong right? The service! I came here for a late lunch on a Saturday with some friends. It was an off time so the restaurant was not crowded. First, our drink order was messed up, not a huge deal, it happens. But then for our entrees we Ordered fish tacos and a chicken quesadilla that my husband asked to be, "plain...just meat and cheese inside." The waitress said no problem and then asked about the pico de gallo that comes on the top, if that was ok served on the side or if he didn't want that either. He said that would be fine on the side. When we finally get our food instead of fish tacos I received fish and chips. I tell the waitress that I was served the wrong entree and she looks at me like it was my mistake when I clearly said fish tacos and then looks at her notepad to see what she wrote down. She takes the fish and chips back and Eventually I get the correct fish tacos. Meanwhile, my husbands quesadilla that was supposed to just be meat and cheese inside had onions and tomatoes Mixed in. He ended up picking them out and eating the quesadilla anyways but showed the waitress that the quesadilla was not plain like originally ordered and the waitress goes, "oh well that's how it comes." Okay, If that's how it comes then why didn't she say that when he originally asked it to be plain, with just meat and cheese inside? Instead of saying no problem! The icing on the cake was when we received the bill and we were still incorrectly charged for the fish and chips! No apology or anything! Thank goodness none of us had food allergies because I fear our waitresses lack of attention to detail could have been dangerous! And I would hate to see all that could get messed up if it was really busy! Needless to say, I won't be back.
Horrible!!! So far my sister got food poisoning from the shrimp! My moms dinner was cold! And I had mold on my bread! Never would I eat there again!!!! Yuk!

The place looks cute from outside with cupcakes, muffins and pastries on the counter and in the fridge. Nutella mini cheesecake is fluffy but not as moist. Chocolate cupcake with chocolate filling was so bland and doesn't taste like cupcake. May be it was gluten free?? Apple strudel muffin was also too bland for my taste. Prices are a bit high in there. The cashier was nice though.

Ordered a salad with seared tuna to go and bread pudding. Tuna was uncooked and coated in sesame seeds. I'm not allergic but the menu made no mention of it. Salad came coated in a revolting amount of dressing with huge gnarly chunks of blue cheese in a few spots. The lettuce was low grade pre-chopped romaine, mainly white rinds, no leaves whatsoever. The nuts were hard like rocks and coated in crunchy sugar. You couldn't even tell it was candied nuts they tried to put on the salad. It tasted like candy. The bread pudding was actually a cold refrigerated hard muffin with sauce on the side. I took it back. They remade it. The lettuce I actually ate was frozen, like, transparent clear lettuce. There were rotten clumps in the lettuce and the tuna they cooked came floating in a box of grease. If it'll let me post the pictures I will. The waitress was nice though. She tried despite the nasty food. Price tag for this? $36.

This is probably the worst Subway I've ever been to. I came here with my best friend to have a veggie delite. We were concerned when we noticed they do not change their gloves after making other sandwiches as my friend is allergic to all dairy products. Also, the food inventory was very messy and mixed together. For example; there was cheese mixed up with the lettuce. She was not able to eat here because of these factors. The woman who made my sandwich was very rude and lackadaisical while making my sandwich, she OVERFILLED It completely with spinach and the sauce wasn't evenly distributed on my sandwich. About 2 inches of my sandwich was nothing but mustard and nothing else.

This place is fantastic, as long as you have a dog's stomach. They're not affected by drinking from toilet or eating from trashcan I purchased a couple of Groupons after reading the reviews and the menu looked appealing. First visit was disappointing. The food was so-so. It was a little while ago so don;t remember everything. I do know I was not coming back. I do remember my wife's coffee mug having fresh lipstick on it, the silver being gross, and the service so-so Also the chicken sandwich was just bad. A few 1/2 golf ball sized chunks of chicken on each half and a couple other things thrown on and that was it. I know neither of us finished our food, it was that bad Yes, the melon ball scoop of potato salad is good, but how often do you come across bad potato salad? It's obviously something they buy in bulk from BJ's, as what appears to be the case for most of what's served Additionally, the whole place had a cheap, basement/college dorm/yard sale feel to it. It was put together on a shoe-string budget. Everything in this place looks like it was either purchased for 9 dollars or less or picked from the trash. You soon learn that theme carries through with everything, particularly the food and the lack of cleanliness. "Washing things takes time and money, and time is money" I told my wife to give the second Groupon away. She refused, and it was about to expire, so we gave it another chance. Big mistake. Funny thing is, the place was crowded, but I find many people either just don't care or don't make the connection between eating out and not feeling so well afterwards We sat a table they had set up with place mats and silver. There was ketchup on the edge of the vinyl table cloth. There were crumbs on the table, and again the silver wasn't so clean Grilled cheese sandwich. They can't even melt the cheese in a grilled cheese sandwich. How hard is that??? Cold folded cheese just partially melted in some spots between the Panini bread The rest of the food was so-so. But again, EVERYTHING can be made to taste better grilling in a panini. My 9 dollar turkey was not fresh roasted and carved, but bad bulk processed lunch meat. On the plus side, the lettuce and tomato were fresh.The final nail in the coffin was that my stomach was turning and rumbling as soon as I got up from my chair and I felt like vomiting. So instead of doing some other chores, I had to rush home to use the bathroom and lay down. So if you have no problem eating and being served like Fido, with a smile and a pat on the head, you'll probably enjoy this place. Just be ready to go for a walk. To the owners, clean your place up. It;s just a matter of time before someone's e-coli or salmonella poisoning is tied in with your irresponsible and reckless operation. I noticed you're still regularly relying on 1/2 off Groupon to bring in business. That says a lot.

Tried this place and it is expensive the ice cream melts quickly, better to eat it inside, this franchise has been closed twice due to contamination issues it has made the news I don't think I'll return anytime soon...I do like the half sizes served

Their food is really good.... BUT....... if you order to go, don't. I asked for truffle fries and asked for truffle bacon aioli, asked for chipotle ketchup for the build your own burger. I also told them no pickles because im allergic. I even had the server repeat the order back to me and she repeated it back correctly. When I received my Togo order, they gave me regular fries, regular garlic aioli, no ketchup at all, oh.. And pickles!! For the truffle fries and trufflie aioli and chipotle ketchup, there's an upcharge. And i didnt get any of those. I was really disappointed. I understand its insanely busy, but the food allergy for the pickles? Cmon. The two hour wait to dine in is not worth it. Did it once, took a server 20 mins just to ask us if we wanted something to drink. Told the server I'm allergic to pickles, and the kitchen STILL gave me pickles with my burger. Servers are friendly. I'm sure people in the kitchen are over whelmed, but i don't think its excusable to ignore customers food allergies when the server clearly rights it down. Its insanely busy. Once this place dies down and hopefully has more organization and decides to take reservations, I'll come back. It iust feels like the kitchen jips ur orders cause they dont think the customer will know the difference between truffle fries/aioli and the norm.

The Gluten free bake goods are delicious but the customer service is awful. Every time I go I feel like they are pressuring me to spend more money there. I asked for 3 cinnamon buns and the girl said "do you just want to do 4 for $20". They are $5 each, so the 4 for $20 was no deal. When you order they constantly ask if you want to add more. This place is also outrageously priced, be prepared.

So we ordered delivery just to test out their fare. Man, that was a seriously bad idea. We ordered wings, a Tex burger, and jalapeno poppers, and should have just stuck with the poppers. They were actually decent, however, my wings were still flapping for escape they were so uncooked. My friend said her burger was a giant grease ball, but I'll take indigestion over total food poisoning any day. Maybe we caught them on a bad day (or chef), but I've definitely seen better fare.

The rice is very dry and they only would give me 2 little pieces of each type of fish..however thinking about this the next morning as I write this hovered over the toilet, I am very grateful for just receiving these 2 pieces. I just paid 12$ for old rice, rotten fish, and food poisoning!!!

Ok...I won't eat here. Unless it's chips lol The food is not good and food poisoning has happened to more then one visitor. However...the water views...dolphin sightings. .outside seating...live music and decently priced drinks keep drawing me back. The brit amongst us really enjoyed it and of course the tourists bond with him and locals are fascinated by the accent. Silly Americans sometimes. Anyway..it's a good place to drink and chill. Inside or out. Eat at your own risk

I've come here many times over the years, but this is my first official review. I ate here today for breakfast and ordered the poached eggs and asparagus. It was very flavorful and the eggs were poached perfectly. We had outside seating facing the Park and the last table at the end. I felt like this gave is ample space because the tables are extremely close here. The only drawback is this is where the waitress and busboys are constantly going in out to get inside to the kitchen. I have found this restaurant to be extremely helpful and knowledgable (as most Stephen Starr) with food allergies and cross contamination. I will keep this as one of my favorite Philly restaurants that is a last consistent and delicious.
Staff was disrespectful, food was marginal, they advertise gluten free with a huge sign outside and then after all orders are taken they tell us they don't have gluten free. Don't bother

Worst AYCE buffet I have been to in my life. Clearly lots of selections but probably all reheated before heading for pig farm. Both my adult daughter and I got food poisoning on a Sunday night. Never again, STAY AWAY unless you are a Nevada food inspector.

two words... FOOD POISONING. My parents use to take me to marras as a kid and we use to get pizza and i remembered it being great. So my mother-in-law and I havn't been in years so we decide to go. We ordered four appetizers to share and a small personal pizza. Two hours later we were both violently sick throwing up EVERYTHING.. NEVER AGAIN!

After hearing about this place from a friend (who has never tried banh mi before eating here) and reading the reviews, I knew I had to try it out. After reading that the owners just came from France, I thought to myself, these people must know bread. Boy was I wrong and thoroughly disappointed. What makes banh mi good is the roll. It has to be crusty and flakey with that unmistakable crunch. The rolls here have none of that. Instead, the rolls were soft and chewey. I was also sad that they did not have a traditional Special (dac biet) with the liver pate, head cheese, etc. Instead, they had the "ham" which only had 2 types of Vietnamese lunch meats (cha lua and thit nguoi). Now I didn't have the pork, chicken, or beef so I can't comment on those, but they put lettuce in the sandwiches. That right there threw up a red flag. The only thing this place had going for it was the $3 price. Well...it was clean too. If you're in Center City, don't want to go to South Philly, and want a good banh mi, skip this place and head a block over to QT. It's a few dollars more but you get what you pay for.

My wife and I had a dinner there on 12/22. The food was delicious but both my wife and I got food poisoning... we shared all dishes (had several vegetarian dishes) and left happy and full but then at night/next morning started feeling sick. Next day was pretty bad. I know it's from there since we only ate out there that weekend.

Pros: BBQ MEAT Cons: Not many side choices for a person with dairy allergies like myself and that created a reduced value overall. 8 bucks for a portion of meat and no sides is just lame. REALLY SLOW SERVICE! MERCY! The food is already cooked no? WTF? Too pricey considering all I get to eat there is meat. The bread has fairy in it too. Suggestion: 1. Have more non dairy sides. a. Baked Potato, Potato Wedges, potato chips b. Corn on the freaking cob (un buttered) c. Simple Salad bar d. Simple rustic french baguette rolls instead of the milky butter rolls or in addition , simple non dairy buns (use a local bakery like beyond bread or a French one that is popular. e. Steamed veggies (asparagus, broccoli, brussels sprouts, carrots, zucchini etc. f. Roasted veggies (zucchini, asparagus, onions, eggplant, tomatoes) g. Fresh fruit salad 2. FIGURE OUT WHY IT TAKES SO LONG TO GET FOOD THATS ALREADY PREPARED ON A PLATE AND FIX THAT. Chipotles can do it so can you.

the hubby and i got some take out pho and brought it home. the hubby's pho came with some beef which the first piece of meat was raw and in a sandwich bag that sat on top of the onions and other toppings and other piece of meat. I WILL NEVER GO BACK HERE AGAIN! YOU DO NOT PACK RAW FOOD WITH FOOD THAT IS GOING TO BE CONSUMED! ITS CROSS CONTAMINATION !

As someone who is gluten free due to Celiac, I've tried lots of gluten free desserts. So when I stumbled upon Sweet Freedom, I was so excited to try everything! Big mistake! I've never had such bad gluten free products: the cupcakes are dry and crumble in your hand, even when you get them at 8am, the cake balls don't taste like real food. Whenever I eat here, I;m sick for the rest of the day in the bathroom. There are plenty more gluten free desserts available in the Philly area. Their two redeeming factors are their donuts and their icing (as long as you scrape it off the cupcake).

Gluten Free Cookie Price Gouging. I used to love stopping at Hope's Cookies for gluten free chocolate chip cookies and a gluten free pizza. (The shop isn't gluten free so you need to weigh your ROI personally). I stopped by yesterday and ordered three bags of the gluten free cookies and did a double take at the charge - $7.50 a bag. I typically would enjoy a few cookies and throw them in the freezer. A quick toast and the chocolate chips literally melted in my mouth. I asked the attendant about the cost. They used to be $4.50 ish a bag for six cookies. At $7.50 a bag, I feel taken advantage of - because I have celiac disease, the owner thinks it is ok to arbitrarily raise the cost. I bake and buy gluten free. I am not aware of any food shortages that would arguably support this astronomical increase in cost. I used to go out of my way for cookies and pizza. Now - the scenario is less appealing. I can buy frozen pizza and make cookies cheaper and more accessible than Hope's.

Because a few people in my family have Celiac disease, we are always on the look out for good gluten free finds. Unfortunately, this bakery left us disappointed. We got a variety of things to try: Samoa-style cookie was ok but shortbread was dry, chocolate cake with peanut butter cups was INCREDIBLY dry (to the point of being inedible), mini carrot cake... meh (but at least palatable). Granted, we did not try cinnamon buns or macarons that other reviews have mentioned as being tasty - but given the quality of goods we did taste, I'm unlikely to return to give it another try.
Ravioli was good. But when the main dish came out they served me spoiled chicken on my salad. I will not return. I could have gotten food poisoning.

Much more spacious than the previous location, to the point where I contemplated bumping my previous review up from 3 stars to 4... but I ordered the Garden calzone with spicy red sauce and ended up getting food poisoning. Sooo...

This was a decent breakfast stop. No frills. I had the ham and cheese (no egg) breakfast sandwich on a plain bagel. It was pretty tasty. They where accommodating for my order since I have an egg allergy and going to get breakfast can be a nightmare. My husband ordered the pepperoni pizza bagel. He said it was very good. We will more than likely return for a quick breakfast again, and I would recommend it. However the servers could stand to be a little more friendly. I don't like feeling like my mere pressence is an annoyance to them.

I ate here on 10/27/17 and me and my girlfriend got terrible food poisoning and it was the only think We had ate all night and we both had the chicken enchiladas I have never been so sick In my entire life.

Admittedly I feel a bit guilty about this two star review. Let me preface by saying that I am not a vegan and thankfully not gluten intolerant, dairy intolerant, soy intolerant, peanut allergic, refined sugar intolerant, intolerant of my neighbors, etc. etc. I stopped by to get some baked goods for a couple of friends who have some of these issues (I think one of them is OK with their neighbors, though). While they were boxing up my orders at Sweet Freedom I noticed they had some samples out on the counter. First I tried what I thought was a piece of an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie. Wrong! It was a piece of a chocolate chip cookie. To me, it was kind of grainy tasting, but I supposed if this was the only baked good I could eat or if I was stranded on a desert island this would suffice. I also tried a small piece of what looked like a peanut butter chocolate bar. I was honestly afraid to ask what it really was. Oddly enough, it tasted identical to the chocolate chip/oatmeal cookie thing I just ate. Maybe this is to P.C. for me and I need the real deal? That being said, my gluten intolerant friends seem to like the stuff we bring them from Sweet Freedom and I am sure I will be coming back in the future.

This is my go-to location when getting treats for my friends who are either gluten-free or vegans. The baked goods are tasty although the do taste different because of the lack of dairy or eggs. It's products are also pricy so I get them only for friends' special occasion.

All I can say is I had high expectations reading the chefs bio and I will say that the Mac cheese and bacon was the bomb, however the my salad was awful. I sent is back after one bite and I never do that as I am in the business. The place is clean and space is awesome, but that one thing was really disappointing. First and last unfortunately. I may give it one more shot as the wife is gluten free and I love her...

If you have allergies, for I tomatoes, its not the best place. The past three times I've went or ordered out they've put tomatoes and although it does get resolved, i find it lacking that I have to reorder every single time.

I must admit, since I'm allergic to seafood I was reluctant to try this place out. But it turns out that their martinis were perfect and the blackened chicken penne was delicious. I went with a group of 5 and through 'open table' was able to get a reservation for the same night. I would suggest it for either a date or a small group.

We were at Grounds for Sculpture. We called Rat's to ask about their gluten-free options, due to one person in our family having Celiac's. They say they would get back to us in a few minutes. It took them 3 days and 4 hours to get back to us. The 7 of us ate in Bordentown, instead. So we have no idea how good the food is, and we are not likely to be there again any time soon.
Gluten free options? The sign says so, but no. No gluten free pizza. Front desk, "i don't think well ever have a table for 7". What the heck? Elizabeth, our waitress was sweet, tho.

For me, this place was so-so....BUT, that's because I'm a mutant who is allergic to shell fish. Yeah, it was great of me to go to a place famous for grilled oysters. The grilled Oysters smelled great and were gigantic, and most of the people I was sitting with who had them, loved them. If you are like me, allergic to the bugs of the sea, there isn't much for us. There are a few mediocre chicken and sausage dishes. I wanted the seared tuna, and I ordered it, but after a 20 min wait, the waitress came back to inform me they were out of tuna....so I got a breaded chicken over pasta and ate it 20 minutes later as everyone was done eating. Bummer. Point is, the shellfish is great but this is not a place for a nerd like me, allergic to shellfish with an epi pen in my purse asking if they clean the grill after they cook shrimp on it. This is apparently the place to go besides Acme. The drive from the Quarter was short but parking was a bitch and the neighborhood seemed a bit rough. We were told we could park in the lot of a bicycle store( at night only) and that worked out fine.... Metairie is supposed to be a safe suburb and according to some townies we were with, is. The restaurant happens to be in a small few blocks section of Metairie that is not very safe. There was a police officer parked out front the entire night. I asked why she was there and no one would tell me. I assumed maybe there had been a bar fight there recently but upon leaving, the large group of kids hanging out front, cursing at everyone, made me feel like I was in an old "Juvenile" rap video filmed in the 9th ward.....though not much different from what I'm used to in D.C. so I felt right at home. Overall, I'm sure the grilled oysters are to rave about, but if you don't have a car, stay in the Quarter and go to the Drago's there.

3.75 A special birthday celebration for an older friend turned out ok - just ok....perhaps with a small "plus." We were able to make reservations easily (and changed by one fewer seat at the last minute due to an illness in the family). :-( Right on time we were led by a congenial host as we wove our way through a busy, filled restaurant and then seated in a "side" room filled with lots of tables and lots of other guests. (And after much peeking about and overhearing bits of conversations, it appears this was the unofficial (?) birthday room because at least 3 other tables looked to be hosting celebrants. Hints like a hand-signed card for our birthday guest Jack (very nice touch, Connors!), vestiges of other cards, and flowers, and the occasional singing of happy birthday identified these revelers. Our server came by immediately and took drink orders and in a virtual flash (no camera pun intended) came back with our appetizers. The apps were excellent: 1) Deviled eggs with Italian truffle oil, fresh cilantro, and a small slice of tender-crisp brown sugar bacon - were soft and creamy. The textures and flavors provided a nice contrast - sweet and savor and very nicely balanced 2) Grilled Pork Belly braised with sweet tea and served with a small dish of creole mustard, along with pillowy Asian buns; the pork was deliciously decadent - but, hey we're here in the south, it ought to be! The buns were fluffy and served as a palate cleanser of sorts. Yes, we'd order both of these again in a heartbeat. Our starters were mix and match. I would have liked to try the "homemade" lobster-crab bisque but was foresightful enough to ask about the stock. Unfortunately our server returned from the kitchen to inform me that it was made with a shrimp base (a shellfish to which I have a severe allergy) so I opted for the chili. Others in our group ordered salads of varying composition - all decently dressed and served promptly. Uh, but wait....what about my chili? It should have been served with the salads; after all isn't it just simmering in a pot, ready to be served? I waited, people finished their salads, and then my chili was served. I was only about half way through this run-of-the-mill, chili-cayenne-cumin laden, nicely dotted with chopped (not ground) meat when all the entrees arrived. ("Stars begin to fall.") The table was already filled to near capacity for our group of 6, so we moved and crammed dishes together to make it all fit. The entrees - all steaks save for one of the children at the table - were fired exactly as ordered - anywhere from well to medium-well to medium to rare. The chef & crew cooked these Filets, Sirloins, and Expresso Rib Eyes to perfection. They all were tender and flavorful through and through. I like Boursin, so I recklessly order the Boursin Filet, expecting a light schmear...but was a bit surprised to find my beautiful steak smothered in an avalanche of cheese (and topped with thin, crispy onion rings.) Too too much....so I scraped off the cheese and enjoyed a perfect steak. Sides and a child-ordered plate of mac and cheese and a small pizza (we'll train him as he grows)...were acceptable but not memorable. The baked potatoes, predictable and steamed tender; the creamed spinach delightfully rich. The child-ordered fries - tender but not overly crisp; and when dipped in ketchup our young guest was ok with them. We sipped on a smooth, palate-pleasing 2015 Coppola Claret, a great accompaniment to our steaks throughout dinner. Finally, we shared three desserts: Chocolate Mousse Cake - moist and creamy and chocolaty-good; Strawberry Shortcake - meh, wrong season for strawberries and the house-made ice cream was a bit crystallized; Key Lime Tart - a show stopper! But wait...our birthday guest insisted on ordering Bananas Foster...(big mistake - but it was his birthday). The dessert di not appear to be flambéed, was devoid of banana flavor, and had puff pastry cubes floating on it that were simply awful and tasted stale at best. Overall service was fair to good but inconsistent at times. Food fair to excellent. Ambiance - upbeat and rather loud. And when the birthday partiers to the side of us began to sing (all 20 or so of them) we were simply unable to do anything but join in.

I've heard about this place a lot, and seen the green little hybrid parked on the curb, and have actively avoided coming in since I don't really care how sustainable, gluten-free or whole grain pizza ingredients are. I only care that the pizza is good. It's gotta be a great deal, a new flavor, or perhaps service that inspires you to question all previous service. This place is just plain different. I ordered a whole grain crust personal. It was an absolutely hideous, sad looking pizza compared to puffy doughed places that slather on the sauce, but it tasted alright. I stuck to the organic wine. Again, I care not at all that it's organic. No matter, didn't seem like I was paying more for this organic thing I didn't care about. Wine and pizza are supposed to be a treat, something you only get once in a while, so that it's not luxurious, huge, calorie busting pizza concerns me a bit. If I'm not eating pizza every night, why would I turn it into a device that delivers me fiber? In any case, the service was great and I'll be back for the great deals, but with a bit of skepticism. I believe that you if for whatever reason you try to take a self-indulgent thing like pizza and give it a healthy, eco-conscious edge, it had better taste damn good. The odd shaped, small wafer that is their personal isn't going to do it for me, but I'm hopeful. The deals offered might make this a cool neighborhood bar, but I'll have to try something else and see.

Honestly it's a little flavorless. I suppose if you are vegan, gluten free, and trying to avoid sugar it's the only option but the flavor was really lacking without sugar. I bought a few cupcakes because I can't eat gluten, and didn't finish one of them. I would say just make your own and leave out the ingredients that you don't want.

The first time we dined at the Barrel back in March was phenomenal. Visited again last night and our experience was lack luster... there was a faint smell of vomit wafting throughout the dinning room. We ordered the Chilean Seabass. It was incredibly over cooked, tough and chewy. The pappardelle pasta with creamy vodka sauce lacked flavor. Luckily our server was very friendly and knowledgeable.

Ive never been so disappointed at an establishment as I am with this place. They have no knowledge of cross contamination between meat products and cheese. Right in front of my eyes the girl cut cheese, ham and turkey in the deli slicer. Right after that she cut a different cheese. So now the turkey has ham on it, the cheese has turkey on it and so on and so forth. When I brought this to their attention the other girl made a huge fit on how they only have to clean the slicer if it's a veggie sandwich. Well hello idiot you already contaminated the products previously... cleaning the slicer won't do shit!

Ice cream sucks. Food sucks. I got food poisoning. #yelpdisaster I saw half eaten food in the buffet and quite frankly that is gross. The staff was negligent and seemed very uninterested in my business at their establishment. I will not be returning to China Buffet.
Got food poisoning on my wedding day after eating their baked ziti with sausage the previous night. Avoid this place!!! Health hazard!!

This place is AWESOME!!! It's your typical, serve yourself, fro-yo by the ounce place with a nice variety of flavors and toppings set to please just about anyone who walks through the door. You want a chocolate overload with tons of peanut butter cups and butterfinger bits? You got it. Prefer that nonfat tart yogurt flavor laced with fresh fruit and granola? No problem. Prefer to add a little bit of yogurt to your toppings? You can do that, too. Nice high counters at the topping bar keep little kiddie fingers and sneezes from contaminating those yummy add-ons so you can eat your dessert germ free -- a big time bonus in my book! :] The place is pretty clean with a decent amount of seating space and a generalized happy feeling (mainly created by the bright green walls and constant smell of freshly baked waffle bowls -- Mmmmm....). They were running this promo for a while where they had a buy one get one free deal on Wednesday nights, too -- made it totally worth your time and money to go here! I'm holding off on giving them that last star mainly b/c of some inconsistency in their flavor quality. Most are pretty good (albeit a bit too sweet in many cases), but there are always a few that taste mostly like a flavored syrup, which is *not* how quality yogurt should taste! If you're smart and get yourself a taste-tester cup to begin with, though, you can avoid these lemons and stick with the rainbow of sweet goodness at your disposal from the other dispensers. :]

Overpriced, but wait, that's not all! I ordered a steak and cheese, thinking it was a steak and cheese. I watched as the counter person took sandwich roast beef and put it in the deep fryer. After I calmed down and kept the vomit down I realized she was just cooking it in au jus. Then it was put on a roll with cheese under a toaster. Just call it a roast beef and cheese, boiled and toasted folks. The ham was salty on the Italian? too. Just find a jimmy johns and ignore this place.

This bakery store is vegan, dairy-free, soy-free, gluten-free, corn-free, peanut-free, refined sugar-free and all this is stated on their window and website. I was extremely curious about this, since all the vegan desserts I've had had soy in them. I do like what this business is all about and I do respect them for that. But unfortunately I didn't like the cupcakes here. I had the Chocolate Cupcake ($3.50 each) which according to them it's made with the following; Cocoa powder, coconut sugar, coconut oil, agave, sorghum flour, potato starch, brown rice flour, coconut milk, arrowroot, vanilla extract, apple cider vinegar, baking soda, cream of tartar, sea salt, xanthan gum. I just took two bites of it and did not finish it. That's how much I disliked it. One thing that was okay; heart shaped chocolate doughnut. Maybe I'll come back to try something else.

I have a mixed review which lowers the would be score of 4 stars to 2.5 stars. Pros : the produce ( especially when one young man who is hearing impaired) is outstanding ! This young man always has a smile on his face and is quick to go back into the warehouse portion of the store to bring out the freshest of fruits and veggies. He also breaks his neck to make sure nothing and I mean nothing is sitting rotting or attracting fruit flies. The meat department under "Mannie" is also very good and he always does his best to try and accommodate your needs although his hands are tied with the company bringing in more and more crap which Is precut and prepackaged. Seafood also is good especially when Kellie is present she always makes sure that nothing is not fresh or in my case with food allergies has been accidentally cross contaminated. Cons: to start the deli department simply is atrocious .. people sitting around talking to each other while usually only one person is waiting on customers while there are three people working and there are more than ten or fifteen customers !! Cheese is horrible idiots cut it too damn thick and deliberately stack it so you can not pull it apart ! Total waste of money ! Meat department is as I said very rarely cutting meat with most of it coming in precut and already packaged so you cannot get steaks or roasts cut to your desired needs!!! Seafood if Kellie is not there well you run the risk of being sold something not fresh or cross contaminated! In addition I have found the prices are very high to make up for spoilage ! I think prices should be lower and you'll sell more hence less spoilage!! Also too much of the seafood has been previously frozen and it does make a huge difference between fresh and frozen ask any chef especially Gordon Ramsey!! Cashiers ... sadly many of the older non high school age cashiers are horribly rude especially two older women at the self checkout! They also never tell you your gas points. The belt is always dirty! Lastly I get frustrated when people move things from one aisle to another or simply just stop carrying something that you've purchased for years. Recommendations: NEVER EVER BUY CHEESE FROM DELI DEPARTMENT!i. Never use self checkout when the checkout NAZIS are working !!k

Went in expecting to get some Florida lobster, but to our disappointment the menu changed sometime this year and was completely overhauled and was no longer available. We stopped by while visiting friends and family in the area. Still ate in despite the lack of lobster. Food was decent, and good portions. There were a few creative looking items on the menu, and one that actually surprised me was the Cuban egg rolls. They were good, not mind blowing, but good. Sauce they came with left a little to be desired. My girlfriend tried the grouper sandwich which was also pretty decent. Can't say that this is a place we'd go out of our way to go back to, just due to the prices and the menu. Also, as a note to those with shellfish allergies (personally have them), a majority of the seafood dishes have some form of crustacean in them or mixed in. So sans requesting for a substitution or removal (risky in my opinion) your choices will be more limited to a smaller amount of seafood or non-seafood courses.

Three words - Listeria food poisoning. The server ran out of food by the time he got to our end of the table. First alarm. He then rushed in an order of chicken to complete my husband's meal. From there everything went down hill. The next day he began to get severely sick. After hospital, urgent care and seeing the primary care physician it was finally determined he had listeria bacteria in his system. He missed work and was violently ill for almost a week. It was horrible to watch. We were out of pocket nearly a $1000.00 before all was done. I have NEVER done this before - but I called to let corporate know what happened and submitted a claim. They agreed and sent us the out of pocket reimbursement. We will never go back - the thought of eating here makes us both sick to think of it. But I am thankful they reimbursed us for the expenses and lost work days.

This was by far the worst bbq I have ever had. The meat was mush, with no smoke flavor. The pork shoulder tasted like re-hydrated dried meat. It seems like it was either boiled or smoked, frozen then thrown in a steamer pan for hours. The brisket was very dry and seemed to be treated in a similar fashion. Something was off about the meat as I got a visit from the food poisoning fairy later that night. Who knows how long this meat was just sitting in a pan. The collard greens were horrendous, cooked in some sort of artificial sweet and fake smoke slop. The only good thing were the hush puppies, so unless you are a vegetarian, avoid this place. It is time for this place to go back to basics and work on food quality and not just chain appeal and food show appearances.

Food poisoning!!! Had happy hour chips, quac, salsa and a beer. We instantly recognized that the salsa tasted weird. I said hmm... I can't pinpoint what it is - maybe it's seasoning/style. Hubby said no way, I'm not eating that. I stopped too, we mainly wanted the quac anyways. Well as soon as we get back to the hotel all horrendous and unpleasant things related to food poisoning happened to me!!! Hubby has a stomach made of steal, I guess, because we ate all the same things!! I might have had a few more bites of salsa than he did. Definitely gross!!! They used tons of gross seasonings to hide the fact that they are either using old and leftover salsa or they are using old rotten unwashed tomatoes. Maybe it's been sitting out, who knows!!! Should have told the waiter that the salsa tasted funny at the restaurant..now I've learned my lesson the most unpleasant and hard way!

We decided to order from here last night for Delivery. Ordered the big pie pizza that is like a "loaded" pizza with veggies and sausage. Not only is the delivery service horrible but both my husband and I woke up ver very sick to our stomach! Our bodies are in sooo much pain & we have been stuck in the hotel all day because of how sick we feel. Definetly a case of food poisoning. Our vacay has been shot.

It's CB people, a tradition in itself. This is a great location that I have had the pleasure of frequenting and they have yet to fail me! Pleasant workers and always great food and portions. If it's a friday or a weekend and prime time for dining, you may have a bit of a wait, but that shouldn't come as a surprise. I noticed a review stating they had food poisoning all night and day after eating chicken here and NOT to eat their chicken! I will not be bossed by a mediocre review, especially when they aren't an avid yelper. #1- I ALWAYS eat chicken at CB #2- Only one or two forms of food poisoning have a fast onset of 1-4 hours, all the rest, most common, onset after 6+ hours after ingestion. #3- Could you write more than a sentence maybe provide a time frame and some facts to back up your poorly diagnosed sickness. And lastly #4- I do hope you called CB to let them know just what you ingested and when so they can take note if any other patrons become ill. Otherwise don't bother leaving a negative review via one measly sentence. NOW- I had the chicken fried chicken plate with okra, mashed potatoes and hashbrown casserole and it was amazing. It was my cheat night and I God forgive my gluttony. I do intend to continue eating lots of poultry from the wonderful country grown establishment. :)

This was probably the worst burrito I have ever ordered. I ordered the California burrito on doordash. First, it was late, which isn't a big deal but i received notification that it was being made after the expected delivery time. Second, it was undercooked. The fries inside were soft and oily and definitely not as warm as the rest of the burrito. Something tells me point 1 led into point 2. The carne asada was also rubbery and tasteless. The cheese was in the same boat. Long story short, I would have returned this burrito if I were eating at the restuarant. Only bright spot is that I'm on work travel so I didn't throw money down the drain on this. Here's to hoping I don't get food poisoning tonight.

Sandwiches are definitely big and tasty with lots and lots of variety of meats and cheeses! Just be prepared to wait 30 minutes to an hour or more if you go in person (what's really annoying is they will always, ALWAYS say it's only 5-10 minutes, and 0% of the time have they ever been right) or two hours for delivery, making it a difficult choice for those on their lunch breaks. One of the servers also will have an attitude when you try to customize "traditional" sandwiches...some people might have allergies.

heads up, i'm a gluten-eater, so this skews my review a bit, since i have way more options than a non-gluten eater. i went here back in february because i had a groupon so i figured why not? so here's a breakdown of each item i tried and how i felt about them. -chocolate cupcake with chocolate frosting: a combination of beany, chemically, and fruity all combined together. the fruity reminded me of taza chocolate, so that was good... except for the chemical bean flavor. :-/ mr. carrot took a bite and immediately drank water straight from the pitcher, he couldn't wait to pour a glass. i will definitely not get that again. it was wrong, very wrong. (but it wasn't gagworthy for me. i finished it up, if that means anything.) -chocolate chip cookie sandwich with vanilla frosting: the cookie hardly tasted gluten free at all! it was crispy and full of delicious chips. the frosting by itself had that faint chemically/fruity flavor, but the cookie did a good job of covering that up. -mint chocolate cookie sandwich with vanilla (i think) frosting: this too was really good. the cookie was vaguely beany, but the mint did a good job of covering that up. it was not as crispy as the chocolate chip cookie. -magic bar: this was also really good. it's a coconutty bar with a layer of solid chocolate on top. simple ingredients, flavors were great. the place itself smelled overpoweringly of chemicals. i could not place my finger on it. it was a breath of fresh air to step outside. (literally) next time i go in (since i still have an old expired groupon which is redeemable for the purchase price that i've already shelled out) i'm going to try the brownie (against my better judgement i think, when i look at the ingredients list. i think it's the sorghum flour that might be poking me in the wrong tastebuds), and i'll stick to the cookies which are non-sandwichified.

Putrid pizza.. could taste NOTHING but salt!!! Had to throw that whole large pizza out! GF's gluten-free pizza (with "extra cheese,) needed way more "extra cheese" when it was delivered, fortunately we had some mozzarella at home... Will never order from this est. again. Can't fathom why they have positive ratings!!!

I have come here multiple times. I always order a milk alternative in my drink and pay the extra money (I am severely lactose intolerant) this is my 5th time at this Starbucks that I have received whole milk and ended up extremely sick. All day long. So if you have any dietary restrictions I'd keep a close eye on your barista here.

I hate to give this place such a low review because I used to really like it. The view is great and I like the area. I came here for brunch and seriously doubt I will be back. First off, we were escorted to a booth not near the window when brunch was winding down and there were clearly window seats available. Then after getting our waters, the hostess came over and said she was sorry but that she shouldn't have sat us there, and needed to move us. Why? Apparently there was VOMIT on the floor under the table near my feet. The manager and hostess KNEW it was there and all they did was move us. No comped meals, not even one. No attempt to even comp even one meal. You charge so much for brunch, sit me in a booth with vomit on the floor and think that's ok?? That is disgusting. Ruined my experience. The Management should be ashamed. I can't believe I paid for that experience.

I was really looking forward to checking this place out after looking at their menu online. Went with my family Friday night for my wife's birthday (she's GF). We were seated at a table immediately behind a couple. There was very little space between these two tables, and I could barely squeeze in without hitting the guy. (There were other tables that were open and well-spaced). Started with the hummus appetizer, knowing the four-year old would eat it. I guess it was a black bean hummus, though the menu just said "hummus". Not what any of us were expecting. And it was grainy. Not particularly good. They did bring some extra chips for it, though. My wife had ordered a salad with green goddess dressing. She took a bite with the dressing, and went wide-eyed. She asked me to taste it, because she thought it was dominated by raw garlic. So I put a bit to my tongue, and my entire mouth buzzed and burned. It was the exact sensation of holding a 9-volt battery to one's tongue. Raw garlic? Horseradish? Bad yogurt? No idea. Waitress said she'd bring a different dressing. No other acknowledgement when she came back. My wife had to ask if she or the kitchen tasted it, and she said she did, agreed something was wrong, and said the chef was working to fix it (whatever that meant). No apology, no explanation, nothing from the kitchen. For entrees, my wife ordered the buttermilk fried chicken and mashed potatoes. This was by far the best - and only good thing - any of us ordered. It was delicious, though the pesto (?) on it was unnecessary. The chicken was cooked perfectly, and the breading was very light. It would be wonderful for fried catfish. I ordered the special, prime rib (medium) with marscapone mashed potatoes and roasted vegetables. I don't know what was set before me, but it sure as hell wasn't prime rib, and it was gray throughout. No pink or red anywhere. Seriously, I have no idea what kind of steak that was. My mashed potatoes, and my wife's, were cold. We ordered the pizza for the four-year old, who loves pizza. She didn't care for it. None of us did. It was completely soggy except for the very edge of the crust. Hell, I make gluten-free pizza at home, Dominos can make a non-soggy gluten-free pizza, I don't know why this place can't. They should probably throw a plain pizza skin in the oven for a few minutes to set it and make it firm and crispy, then remove it and dress it out, then return it to the oven. I think the pizza would support the marinara much better if they did this. Very disappointing meal and service. Not quite sure what they're going for here. Casual? Dressy or semi-dressy? Hip? Well, there is a large tv over the bar that was on the entire time, with some HGTV-type show on the whole time. So, let that be an indicator.

My band stopped here after finishing an outdoor concert. We all had sushi in one form or another. I had the chef's assortment - basic, but really pretty good. Some of the others had more exotic rolls, which they also really liked. Prices were a bit high, but not exorbitant. We didn't try any Korean fare ... only sushi. Our only issue was communication with the staff. One member of the band has celiac's disease, so he can't eat any gluten. Turns out some soy sauces actually have gluten in them. So he tried to ask a bunch of staff about various rolls, to see if they had any soy sauce or other gluten-suspects .... and he couldn't get anyone to actually understand or answer his question. No one was outright rude ... we just couldn't get past language barriers for some pretty simple questions .... But as long as you can point to what you want, and don't have any special needs ... the sushi really was pretty good.

Server brought cocktails and there was paper towel pieces in them... We told the server... He took them away and came back with the same drinks. Bartender said it was the oil from the olives. NO there is Positively PAPER in my cocktail. Finally got them to make them over but waited another 20 minutes. Server said we had to wait in the cue! We were being punished for wanting our $15 cocktails to not be contaminated! Always disappointed here. View of park is lovely however.

This place is in need of a cleaning bad. If you ever go there I highly recommend not looking in the crack between cushions. It will make you vomit. The food is frozen and tastes rubbery. I recommend you eat somewhere else. This place is horrible

We visited this establishment for the first time, the food was pretty good, but as I looked around in the middle of meal I notice none of the cooks had on gloves. One of them nails were very dirty, the owner or manager or whoever he was singing along with the rap music he had playing. The only problem with that is that the music had a lot of cursing. They were very unorganized and joking around too much. As I was getting my drink I noticed the area where they cook wasn't clean, food and oil or whatever was on the floor as well as the tables haven't been wiped off. Not many things have been wiped off for that manner, the guy at the register was very professional. The tacos and the queso were good, but after I looked around and after I saw the one guys nails I wanted to vomit. This could be a good place if they get their sh*t together, the place seems to be unsanitary and the workers need to clean themselves up. I won't be back in fear of getting sick, but what I did eat was cool.

My boyfriend and I stop in here for breakfast fairly often as its close to home and offers gluten free bread. The menu is extensive, prices are reasonable enough, and the food is consistent. For breakfast, I typically get something simple like GF toast, fried eggs, bacon and home fries. For lunch/dinner, I like the Tuscan panini (I add chicken). I once tried the Greek coffee and hated it, but that's just personal preference. My main qualm with the Bistro is that the service is really hit or miss -- I've had lovely servers, and I've had god-awful ones. Generally, the Bistro seems over-seated and under-staffed. It's a fine place to grab a quick bite, but not somewhere I'd go out of my way to visit.

Ok, they have decent sushi yes...and they serve the sushi late. I like both these things. I think the decor is nice, even if it is a little urban trendy and sort of looks like it's trying too hard. I mean, that's just my opinion....but I just don't like it when I'm drinking in a place that looks like it could have been in a Matthew McConaughey movie. It bugs me. Also, they have some decent vodka drinks, and yes, probably the largest assortment in the city. I love vodka...it's one of my favorite liquors. Somehow though, I just don't love this bar. I never have a good time here, the bartenders always ALWAYS give me attitude, it's always packed, and I always feel like there are so many popped collars in this place I want to vomit. No offense to anyone on here that's a regular, but this is just NOT my scene. I have enough friends that love it to know this is a very personal choice, and I am easily in the minority. I am being fair and giving it three stars because I know so many people that love it and yes, their drinks are good. But there are any number of bars I would rather go to on any given night. This is one I will probably keep avoiding until I am dragged back in by my friends...

I ordered the one item on the menu the waitress was positive was gluten free. Even after going back to ask the kitchen. So I got the fish which was incredibly small and still got sick. Not safe for celiacs. My BF however really enjoyed the wings(not gf).

Our first visit to Adama was quite a disappointment! The restaurant was quite empty today for a late lunch. We came in with our children excited about a gluten free and vegan meal we could all enjoy. Unfortunately the owner is rude. When our children chose 4 items from the bakery case, our server packed them up. To my surprise, the owner reprimanded the server, took out the fresh baked goods that we had ordered and replaced them with day olds!!!! Incredible, rude, and not acceptable.
