As a long time gluten free family, we know that gluten free baked good are always best fresh. I asked the server how old they were and she said they were yesterday's goods. Could have been older. Since my kids were already in the car I paid our very overpriced check -- spending over $120 for lunch. I'm still kicking myself for not complaining and insisting on replacements for fresh items. I paid full price for stale baked cupcakes. Never going back.

They randomly used ice cream with peanut butter which I did not ask for in my sundae instead of plain vanilla. That is very irresponsible considering there are so many people with peanut allergies. I guess they assumed I wanted peanut butter ice cream because I asked for walnut topping....wrong! Our server was fine but whoever made the sundae needs to be retrained.

I used to eat here frequently a couple years ago until I got the worst food poisoning I've ever experienced. I had explosive diarrhoea and had to run to the bathroom all day. I lost 13 lbs of water weight. It took 7 days of me missing work and a second round of hard antibiotics to clear it up. I have never eaten here again.
- good-fresh sushi and delicious - good size portions - fast at bringing out food - does not have Gluten Free soy sauce - small seating area inside - clean and great service

This is an OK place to spend time with young ones. It is costly, like other indoor playgrounds, but it offers the same entertainment and the grandkids had fun. My big complaint is the quality of food and service at the cafe. I am celiac. The menu says there are options, so I asked. I was told by the lackadaisical employee that there isn't any. Just salads and veggies and dip. When I pointed out the fact that the menu says there are options, she said, "well, we have dough...pizza dough". No offers of what they could do with it for me. I asked for water and was told it was in a vending machine. I was not happy that I couldn't get a water, and the employee stated that if I wanted a glass of water, she could do that and proceeded to tell me that they used to have pop machines but parents let their kids ruin them. I love it when employees bash their guests...who are paying their wages. The chips that they are proud of were greasy and tasted like stale oil. The pizza my granddaughter had was dripping in grease...literally. We will come back, but we will be fed ahead of time and will ask (carefully and very specifically) for water in a cup.

Ordered pizza and some fettuccine Alfredo and everyone who ate it is now throwing up. Stay away from this restaurant. I just read a review finding out that 4 days ago a rat was smashed in the dough machine and workers were vomiting and people were screaming. This place is awful. The food wasn't even mediocre. It was just bad.

Great...if you want to s(hang)your head(hai) over your toilet. Food poisoning for 2 days after eating here. Chicken was grey and as told by owner "it came from different restaurant, may have been cooked Sunday( it was Thursday ), and may NOT have been chicken" . Tell that to my sphincter which had been working 2 days straight voiding this garbage "food" out of my system. AVOID AT ANY&ALL costs You're safer eating out of the 711 dumpster down the street.

Cheap fast and average quality Not gourmet, but better than you would expect based on reviews I ordered General Tso chk platter with a spring roll and white rice $8.65 I received pork fried rice instead of white rice but it was no big deal bc I like both, but if you're allergic/vegan or have diet restrictions make sure you double check. Also the spring roll had a piece of shrimp in it, so it's not vegetarian. Probably the veggie roll is safer bet I ordered at 10:20 pm and picked up my food at 10:30 I would definetly go here again to get my greasy Chinese late-night fix

We went there with my cousin yesterday afternoon. The first burger that was brought out to me was still cold in the middle when I bit into it. They made me another burger and it was still extremely rare when they brought it out. I sent it back again and just asked them to cook the same burger longer and it came out pretty good. Now today I'm sitting in the emergency room because my pregnant wife got food poisoning while we were there

Terrific food. Lousy service more often than not. Really, I need two different ratings for this. The food is fantastic. Chicken korma is just perfection, and the mango lassi is fantastic. If you're gluten-free, the vast majority of the food is okay for you here, and there's even a tasty gluten-free naan made with chickpea flour (very earthy). But the service is pretty dreadful. We first went on a weekend and the service was good, but the place is always understaffed on weeknights and it takes forever even to get naan. We'd had a couple of iffy experiences but since the food was so good we decided to give it another shot. That was a mistake. They forgot about us for a good 10+ minutes after seating us, for one thing, and then it once again took a further 20+ minutes for the naan to arrive. Since they forgot about us, our waitress said she would take $10 off our bill. That was fine until the food arrived and it was so spicy I couldn't eat it. The waitress blamed it on a kitchen error and the manager said "they'd take care of us," but since we didn't want dessert, that turned out to be nothing more than a single free lassi, since we already had $10 off the bill from their first error. Anyway, my food came mild the second time and was tasty, but when the bill came we had a further surprise. It clearly stated that the waitress had put our orders in "medium" instead of "mild." And because the place is small they've crowded too many tables in on the left wall, which means that you're eating with a waiter's elbow in your face while your neighbors' orders are being taken, which isn't the most enjoyable. It's too bad, though, because the food is so delicious.

I GOT FOOD POISONING!! Last Thursday I ate a turkey sandwich with pepperjack cheese at this whichwich & less than 12 hours later became violently ill. I was supposed to go to New York City on Sunday! That DID NOT HAPPEN! I had to complete cancel my trip. Went to the emergency room & dr & confirmed it was food poisoning & this is the only new item that was introduced to my diet n the time frame (I was eating the same food for breakfast & lunch that I had been previously with no ailment.)

Cross contamination and egg shells. I ordered a late night breakfast burrito with potatoes egg and cheese. Inside was a piece of sausage, brown mushy fries, and egg shells. I don't eat meat, nor egg shells, so I went back in the morning to ask for a refund. The cashier was very helpful but she couldn't give me back my money and told me to come back later that day. I came back later that day and the man helping me was rude and wouldn't give me a refund, insinuated that I was lying because I didn't bring the receipt, and told me to come back in four days.... never coming back here again

I like Piper R, started the cleanse too (yesterday was my first day). I would highly recommend not drinking the juice! After drinking five juices, I felt sick. I ended up throwing up all night. The juices must have been spoiled. I also don't know if it was the acidity, the beet juice (because I heard beets don't settle we'll for some people) , or I just drank too fast, but I had a terrible experience. I threw up four times from drinking the juice, and will not continue with the cleanse. I will be calling the company to complain. Do not drink the juice!!!!

Unique sit in or take out spot for this type of cuisine. As far as the veggie options go they got em! And they label them vegan and gluten free as well! I got the veggie kabob entree vegan and gluten free. Altho it was light and healthy I didn't feel quite impressed. It came with 2 kabobs with almost burnt veggies. A side salad, and some bowl of white beans cooked. Also ordered the potato salad as a side which is apparently all vegan. Nice place overall if you want to eat light.
The food was good. Generous portions. The potato chips tasted good, but different. It turned out that they were gluten free. The wedding soup was OK, but a little salty. The service was good too.

Great neighborhood spot. Limited gluten free options both (both beer and food), but that is expected. Nice bar with plenty of TVs to watch your favorite game. Service at the bar Monday evening was good. With that being said this place need a better gluten free menu and some more gluten free options at the bar. It's not that difficult to do.

Is "disappointment" a factor in the rating? If so, I need to give Amadas 1 less star. Like I've mentioned in other reviews, it is my goal to hit at least one restaurant by each of the Iron Chefs. To be honest, I've been disappointed by all of them so far (Flay and Morimoto) but Amadas has been the biggest let down yet. First, the good: the ambiance of the place is really nice; dimly lit, rustic chairs and barrels, hanging meats, etc. The hostess and waitstaff were excellent. My GF was having a hard time deciding on wines since all the wines are Spanish wines you've never heard of, and our waitress brought over like 4 samples for her to try. We both settled on the sangria, (hers white, mine rose' with fresh cranberries....very nice). At $7 a glass, it wasn't too bad. The food was good. But thats where the problem comes in; Olive Garden has "good" food. This is an Iron Chef we're talking about. I just didn't feel wowed by ANYTHING that came out. We ordered the crab stuffed peppers, lamb meatballs, pernil asado (roast pork) and braised short rib flat bread. We were also given a complimentary tortilla and tuna fish appetizer that was tasty, but only got devoured because I was like Somalian hungry. Hands down the best thing was the short rib flat bread which tasted like a cheesesteak pizza. For the pernil, the pork was PERFECTLY crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, but it was LITERALLY about 60% fat. The loin was cut into like 6 pieces and 2 were nothing BUT fat, and the 2 of the others were more fat than meat. Although tasty, I totally felt gyped out of my money. The lamb balls were again, tasty, but there was just something off about them. The stuffed peppers were underwhelming to say the least, plus they came covered in almonds (which the menu didn't state) which my girlfriend is allergic to so.... The bill came out to about $80 before tip. I want to go back, but ONLY to try the suckling pig that you have to order in advance. Other than that, I don't see myself coming back here. I'll probably try one of Jose Garces' other spots but Amada is supposed to be his flagship so I don't really have high hopes. As usual, my vote of "good, not great" applies. I'd say its SLIGHTLY too pricey for "good" food, but if you like tapas and know nothing of its Iron Chef pedigree (thus lowering your expectations), I don't see a problem with Amada.

Only visited for ice cream during the summer. Ice cream is good, staff is more interested in their cell phones. One time the ice cream was freezer burned. But to my gluten free friends... they have gluten free ice cream cones!

We went to the Claim Jumper in Reno Nevada on Friday, 8-18. The service was good as was the food. I ordered a veggie wrap which was good but loaded with cream cheese. When I woke up the following morning I had a bad case of food poisoning. It is very irritating to be sick for two days as a result of someone being careless with the food preparation. I will never go back and would not recommend this establishment.

GLUTEN FREE AND VEGANS REJOICE! I have visited the restaurant 6 times for breakfast in the last year. We were originally drawn to the place because my wife is gluten and dairy free. Our meals have always been very good, closer to fantastic actually, and the service polite. We took out of town guests there today and were served by the owner herself. The food was great as always. One of the comments was "your body says thank you to you every time you take a bite", and these were not vegans! The true pleasure of the day was talking to the owner! To listen to her speak about the care and passion she puts into her restaurant was quite honestly the best interaction I have ever had with someone in the business. Gluten free, let alone vegan items are for the most part average at best, and cross contamination is always a concern when eating out. She has figured out how to make good food that is healthy and safe for those with special dietary needs taste hands down fantastic! Be sure and don't miss the carrot cake cupcakes!

"Chicken dum biryani? Can I get some smart biryani?" Vomit-inducing, cringe-inducing, jokes aside, that was one of the highlights of my visit to the lunch buffet at Hyderabad House. Today they had several kinds of Biryani (I wish I could remember the names of the others). The king fish, potato 65, and some spicy cauliflower were some of my favorite dishes. I thoroughly enjoyed the spiciness level of the food here, but after eating 1000s of calories worth, my spice tolerance broke down and I had to slow down because I began overheating like an engine with a coolant leak. Nevertheless, I ate until I entered into a soporific state of stupor, transcending this plane of reality as I closed my eyes. In other words, I had a food coma. It's 11 PM now and I'm still not hungry. #NoRegrets Desserts are meh, but the main courses are so good I couldn't possibly care less. I'll have potato 65 for dessert next time. The font chosen by the owner for the sign of this place is baffling because it is so bland, reminding me of using the default boring font for presentations I put together 10 minutes before a meeting. Inside, the seating capacity is surprisingly small, maybe accommodating 40 people at one time. The tables are a bit small, enough that I feared that I was sending flirtatious signals to my friend's friend when unintentionally stroking her arm with my elbow/arm every time I took a bite. Please don't get the wrong idea, Miss, the food made me sweat and turn red in the face. Okay, enough petty nitpicking. My friends and I drove over an hour from Purdue to Indianapolis just to eat here, so if you live in this area, consider yourself lucky. TLDR chicken dum biryani is not dumb and is one of their best dishes. Lots of good biryani and curries! Desserts meh. Place is crowded and seating limited; call ahead if you come with a party larger than 4.
Decent. I wasn't impressed by their gluten free crust. My bf loved the regular pizza.

I was honestly rather underwhelmed here. I came in for dinner with three other people on a weeknight. There was only one woman working the floor, but there was only one other table and they already had food. I was surprised when it took so long to make our meal and even more surprised at the quality. The word "Meh" really sums up my chicken dish. My friend had beef with rice, which again was meh, but unlike me he got horrid food poisoning 5 hours later. There must be better quality Korean food in Reno, I'm not coming here again. The best dish by far was a stone pot veggie beef dish my husband bought. That aside, we left rather unimpressed.

In all fairness the place was short staffed; however if the waiter has time to chit chat with his buddies then the service can still be determined shi^^$. Specifically, I am irritated when I tell the waiter I have a severe food allergy and somehow it still appears in my salad. Get your customer service and team together.

I wanted to try Mi Lah because it was rated highly as a vegan restaurant in the city. Many of their menu items were fried and when I asked what oil they used, they said vegetable. I have an allergy to gluten - many of the dishes were not gluten-free friendly. I also asked about their soy and corn - both were not organic and contained GMO's. I ordered mostly veggies - the avocado was brown and clearly not fresh. I went with a friend and we were rushed out - handing us our bill as soon as we finished eating. I ended up getting very sick that night. I can't be certain it's from Mi Lah but all I could think about was that the food didn't seem fresh...

Just ordered delivery through foodler. Food arrived 20 minutes late, tempura rolls were cold (not room-temp, but actually cold), there was no wasabi, and they put all 5 rolls in the same container, instead of splitting it into two like I specifically noted in my order. The person I ordered with is allergic to shrimp and couldn't eat because they put it all together. $30 each wasted for lunch.

My boyfriend and I went to Sabor for our anniversary dinner. We are both young looking (in our early 20s) and felt that from the moment we came into the restaurant we were not treated as well as other guests. I told the server that I had a peanut and mustard allergy. He said he would check about the mustard in the dish and never came back to reassure me that the food did not contain mustard. Although I assumed that the dish did not have mustard, it would have been nice if the server took the time to let me know, since I do have an anaphylactic allergy to mustard. On the bright side, the food was delicious. My boyfriend ordered the pork trio and I ordered the octopus. For dessert we shared a chocolate slab with white and dark chocolate. However, when we were ordering our dessert we had asked the server to give us more information about the chocolate slab (we weren't sure if it was more of a cake texture or simply chocolate). His response was pretty much "it's exactly what it sounds like." I was taken aback by his answer. I had worked in a restaurant previously, and am used to service where they explain the food to you, and maybe even try to sell it to you. I saw our server being quite warm and talkative to other tables; however, to us he gave us minimal service. Even though the food was delicious, my boyfriend and I both said we would not return to this restaurant. We both were looking forward to having a nice meal. I am in graduate school and do not get to go out to such nice restaurants very often. We decided to splurge a bit but I would have preferred going to a restaurant with more mediocre food but friendlier service. http://www.tripadvisor.ca/ShowUserReviews-g154914-d1342991-r325916570-SABOR_Restaurant-Edmonton_Alberta.html#

Features sort of in order of awesomeness 1. Cheap! You pay 30 cents an ounce so you only pay for what you want to eat. 2. Relating to point 1, no more compromising with your friends on flavors and topping to save money 3. Buffet style purchasing -- allows you to create a near infinite combination of flavors and toppings each time 4. Selection is huge! In addition to traditional toppings like strawberries and mochi and flavors like mango and plain tart, they also have fun and tasty toppings like blueberries and frosted animal crackers (no skimping here) and yogurt choices like taro and pistachio. (Stay away from tiramisu and cheesecake though. they taste like vomit.) 5. Decor is a nice middle ground between the hole in the wall feel of Rockin' Yogurt (across the street) and the upscale club/spa feel of Pinkberry 6. They have a bathroom! 7. They give you free self-serve water! With strawberries floating in it! 8. Seemingly unlimited samples! (without the awkwardness of having to ask. just reuse the little cups they give you) 9. Cool biodegradable neon-colored spoons (I'm using them in my packed lunches from now on) 10. Ethical -- they deduct the weight of the cups when calculating the price, something that they clearly don't have to do but which is totally awesome for cheapskates like me. Why? Because you don't have to buy more in order to absorb the a flat rate. 11. Cleverness -- they make you use big cups so you are fooled into getting more frozen yogurt and spending more. While this would be a point against them, it weeds out the weak and so I approve. 12. It's called Yogurtland which is descriptive of what the product is. (what the hell is a pinkberry??) It truly is a wonderous land.

This place has absolutely disappointed me twice. I have food allergies so I once ordered a steak and tonight I ordered the shrimp platter off of their gluten free menu. I'm actually surprised that they sent out such horrific food! Both times the food was completely unseasoned. Not even salt and pepper... and tonight I had to get some cocktail sauce to even choke down my shrimp. Also, the rosemary potatoes were actually covered in parsley. The only thing saving this restaurant is their charbroiled oysters. If you have food allergies, don't go here!!! I ate my unseasoned shrimp and now I'm sicker than a dog.

Some where between 3 and 4 stars Pie Five hovers for me. This is a fun concept that is perfect for families. It is set up like a Subway, where you pick out your own crust and toppings and they throw it in the oven. Every pizza is personalized and individual. For being a newly opened restaurant the wait was fairly minimal. The selection of vegetarian and gluten free option were very appealing. Side salads come in a small bread bowl that is more flashy than functional or appetizing. All of the employee were super nice and went above and beyond. When it come down to it though the pizza wasn't amazing and there is a ton of competition with multiple new pizza places nearby. Fun to try one and great for kids, but not for a great slice of pie.

Well, yes, Panera is a cruel place to be for someone who can't eat gluten. But it's a nice space to hang out, study, whatever. Gluten-free options include tomato soup (w/o croutons) and many of the salads, so it is actually possible to eat here. As soon as they hear the magic word "allergy," they are very understanding about having the food prep people change gloves and use separate utensils for the salad. Pretty awesome! Comfy and plentiful seating, the faux fireplaces are always a nice cozy touch, but the muzak is awwwwwfullllllll. Maybe that's the secret weapon to make sure you don't stay there for 5 hours.

My boyfriend and I came here recently when vacationing in Nashville from New Jersey. In general I had just an OKAY experience here. Definitely a tourist trap but worth going to at least once. The decor is pretty awsome! Tons of different funny horses are spread throughout the entire place. Great for taking tons of funny pictures. I wanted to order the Comfortly Jack to drink and wanted it without the souiveniere glass. However, to my dissappntment the waitress told me I cold not purchase just the drink without getting the glass as well, refills are less money if you do decide to get it. I caved because I really wanted the drink itself. It cost me $13.75 for it. Grantit the glass was nice but I didn't want it and the "signature drink" was to very good. There is a problem when the drink is huge and you barley have a buzz by the time it's done. My boyfriend just ordered a beer and that too was its a purchase of a souiveniere glass. I get the whole up selling customer thing but to make a costumer get one of those glasses is just stupid if they don't want it. We split two different things, one was the sampler. It came with quesadillas, chicken fingers, fried green tomatoes and fried pickles. My bf hates is allergic to pickles and told the waitress so she added extra chicken fingers with o extra price that was very nice of her. The green tomatoes were soooooooo good! Absolutely loved ! And the chicken fingers were prob the best chicken fingers I have ever had! The quesadilla was just okayyy. We then decided to split the Tennessee BBQ duo . The waitress tried to change our mind and up sell us to the priciest item on their menu the "Stampede Platter" ($23.00) after we already made up our mind and kept asking if we were sure. Yes lady we are sure! Especially due to the fact that both menu items were the exact same thing but the Platter was slightly bigger. The Duo (17.00) came with hickory smoked pork chops and shaved beef brisket. Baked beans co slaw and Texas toast. The baked beans were amazing but the rest of the meal was pretty bland. They had containers of BBQ on the table to add to the meal. I must say while being in Tennesee I had better dinners during my stay here. After dinner we decided to go upstairs and check out the pool tales and air hockey tales. The pool tales were very cheap and not good if your a pool player. The hockey tables were also cheap but fun. Both were free which was great and they had a lot of them. Overall my experience here was just okay like I said. Go there for the appetizers and beer and to take cool pictures.

I used to frequent this location almost on a daily basis until an incident happened where the employee had the gall to say that she made a beverage correctly and that I was wrong. In the customer service and hospitality industry, the first mistake one can make as an employee is to exacerbate the issue by trying to make it a point to prove the customer was wrong. But in this case, no way was I wrong: it was a clear as day mobile order for the same beverage I get every day: medium iced coffee, 2 splenda, 2 coconut shots, and skim milk. It's a mobile order! There is no chance for a mistake in translation. When I received the beverage, the color of the beverage was very light (as if cream or a swirl was used). The employee proceeded to say that she used skim milk and that's the color of the coffee. She went as far as grabbing a second cup, filling it with some iced coffee, and adding skim milk just to prove to me that's the color. I left saying ok, this isn't worth my time. As I am stepping into my vehicle, I take a sip and the beverage is WAY too sweet. At this point, I head back in to figure out what is going on. I speak with another employee asking her to remake my drink since she knows exactly what I get every day and I explained to her that it isn't the color that I normally get and it was way too sweet for splenda with coconut shots. She goes and looks for the coconut shot flavor and it's empty. When she asks the other employee what she used, she said coconut swirl. Um, coconut swirl isn't coconut shots. My thought is that the employee actually knew that it was supposed to be coconut shots but was too lazy to replenish the pump that was empty and thought hey let's just give him this. I then made it a point to show the employee the difference in color between what she originally prepared for me vs what was newly reprepped. I got an apology. Ok great thanks. I get home and noticed that I had minor swelling on my tongue probably from the original drink. I am still unsure of the ingredients of the coconut swirl, but if it has condensed milk, then this is likely the culprit. The repercussions could have been much worse if I went into anaphylaxis. I submitted feedback to Dunkin' corporate who relayed my message to Mr Charleston (regional manager?) and Mr Patel (franchisee). To add insult to injury, they send a gift card to make up for the issue experienced. Guess how much? A whopping $5! That's insulting especially considering that I spent more than that on antihistamines to reduce the swelling experienced. I would have preferred for them to have sent nothing and rather invited me back to the restaurant for a verbal apology and maybe offer me a beverage on the spot. Or maybe tell me how they plan on educating employees on consequences of certain mistakes i.e. food safety and food allergies in order to ensure this doesn't happen again to someone else. But nope, all I get is a $5 gift card. I even sent a follow up email which seems to be ignored by Mr Charleston and Mr Patel. Great job guys. Great job.

My husband and I went there for some appies early one evening. We ordered chicken wings (allegedly with their own homemade bbq sauce), spanakopita, sliders and their type of pizza bread with marinara sauce. First the spanakopita was deep fried in oil that was not hot enough so the filo dough was soggy and not crisp, next while the pizza bread was good, the marinara sauce was ice cold. We both thought it should have been at least been warm and both of us prefer it that way. The sliders were very good and the only things that escaped criticism. Lastly the chicken wings-i am sorry to say but they were terrible. The bbq sauce was non existent and there was some flavor or spice on them that was very off putting. I only managed to eat a couple and believe me that was enough. Within the hour we both had very bad stomach pains and felt not so good for the rest of the night and into the next day. I am pretty sure we both got food poisoning from the wings. They did not seem to have been freshly cooked, but rather precooked then heated up as they were a bit rubbery. I don't think a return visit is in the cards.

Pay $$ to get food poisoning. We ordered the non-veg dinner package for 2 (jodu). Food was bland. Both me & my wife had diarrhea the next day, just short of going to the ER. The restaurant had only 3 tables occupied for dinner. If the restaurant is not crowded, food sits in their kitchen longer, and is bad by the time customers are served. Avoid this place. A new restaurant Godavari has opened nearby. More crowded and food is fresh & tastier.
Never eating from here again. Food gave me food poisoning. Sick for days. Please learn to cook your food. Tried giving them a second try, same results. No Thank you!

We've been making a weekly visit to Slice as a family for quite some time. The pizza, salads, and other menu items are creative, fresh, and delicious. If you like thin, crispy crust this place is for you. They also have a fantastic gluten free pizza. My son loves that he can make his own pizza; it's BYO which is also great. We always had the same waiter who was quite attentive and good, but he recently left. Our experiences since have us seriously contemplating quitting Slice, which is heartbreaking. The wait staff is absolutely terrible. Horrendous. They are disorganized, inattentive, and slow. They forget items, order the wrong items, and it literally takes forever to have a meal and forget about getting your check without searching for your server. Looking at the feedback here it seems like a consistent theme, so I'm not sure why management isn't listening - the manager (who is possibly the owner) is always on-site when we are there. This review could easily be 5 stars if they improved their service; the food is quality and delicious. But, literally, our experience was so bad last time that my husband and I are questioning whether it's worth going back only to be highly annoyed. I really hope the owner reads this and addresses the staffing issues. If our experience changes I will update this review.

I am rating it one star due to the food poisoning that followed eating here. The worst I've ever had in my life. We arrived 6.45pm on a Saturday evening. It was rather quiet, but that was nice for a change. Serving staff was excellent. We were a party of 9 and he did a great job. The problem appears to be in the kitchen. One of us has onion allergies (odd I know) and on both requests they brought his food with onions. Having to have us send the food back. First time no problem. Second time they just removed the onions. Burger now cold. He for both allergy reasons and temp sent the burger back. I figured I'd do typical pub food and try their fish and chips. I just love a good fish and chips. It was good, about 3/5 on the way down. This am around 2am in the morning I woke up with the worst food poisoning I've ever had in my life. For the next 12 hours I was on unable to leave the bathroom. I'll spare you all the details but it was horrible. Just horrible. Needless to say I cannot go back to a place that does this to my body. It screwed up my fathers day, and I may have to take time off work. What's surprising is my stomach is normally an iron pot. I suspect the oil used to deep fry has gone bad - but maybe it was something else. Another one of our group commented later on in the evening the food wasn't settling well with them. Sorry Firkin & Wolf. I otherwise really liked what you guys are doing. We even discussed on the drive home that night visiting you guys more often. *runs to the toilet* Update 6.19.12 - Now Tuesday still feeling poor, doctor tells me to take it easy for the next week. So I would highly suggest avoiding the fish and chips. No one got sick from the burgers.

Stopped in recently on a late Saturday afternoon to try carry-out. It started out as promising because they said it would be about 20 minutes, which means cooking fresh, made to order. Ordered 2 differen pho dishes and some other items. Get home and within a few minutes of eating, my wife had a serious allergic reaction to the excessive amount of MSG! I didn't think anyone used that poison anymore. 1 of the pho dishes was with meatballs, of which there were few. They totally skimped on that dish. The other was with shrimp. My 18-year old said the shrimp were of really poor quality. I don't recommend this place and won't be going back.

Out of shrimp cakes app. Spring rolls were burned. Green curry was weak. And to top it off, when I finished off my iced tea, I noticed a fly, frozen in to one of the ice cubes. I about threw up. I mean really that made me nauseous. I'm not in Nashville that often, but I'm never going back here. Ever. I should have known when the place was empty on a Thursday night.

Really hard to review and rate this because it was so mixed. I had not been to a White Dog in decades, but my GF son had been here and wanted a celebration dinner here. There were 6 of us. On entering, I was delighted with the decor. So different than the Du Jour that used to be in this space [and where my daughter was a server briefly years ago]. We were seated when our party was complete. The round table for 6 was in a slightly awkward placement just next to an archway, so staff and other diners had to sidle around us. The service, like the decor, was excellent [5 stars for service]! And our server was very knowledgeable about GF needs. She brought GF rolls for the 2 of us, reviewed the GF offerings [unfortunately not extensive on the new summer menu]. She returned to tell us that the GF dedicated fryer which she had told us about was not dedicated that evening and offered us other sides to avoid cross-contamination. So all that was great, including that all wines were half price that night! Three of us got the burger with cheese, recommended by another in our party. It looked good on its GF bun [?Taffett's bakery], but mine had NO TASTE. I never put ketchup on a burger, but I had to in order to make it palatable. This burger was $19, cooked medium [pink in the center] as I had ordered, but had no beef taste at all. The others were okay with theirs. I also had oysters which were correctly shucked and slid off their shells nicely. I really don't think I would return

$$$ dining prices for $ dining taste. Not a fine dining experience. I could have eaten at Natural Cafe or Sojourner and felt I got a better value. But I'm glad we tried it, and now I don't have to go back. Let me preface that I am not vegan or gluten intolerant. Things were tasty here but not fantastic. I can only conclude that items used to make completely vegan and gluten-free menu is very expensive. Service friendly and welcoming. Strange but beautiful ambiance. And I also thought the bathroom situation was cool. Confusing at first, but a refreshing change from the norm. Warning on the full bar; they are phasing it out. They had a lot of gin and only things that have never touched wheat. We searched some recipes for the bar tender to prepare. Happy hour is only at the bar. Bummer.

Just a note that my family can not have any diary and bring regular milk instead almond milk is a bad mistake..... Specially with allergies.... We just know about this " regular" mistake because my Lo got really sick

Their gluten free pizzas are sooooo delicious!! I also adore their juice bar - yum!! They have a decent organic/natural section but I think I still prefer Whole Foods or the Co-Op as I feel they have a bigger selection. Their linguisa is pretty fab!!

Honestly I've written very few yelp reviews but feel compelled to. Just ordered the edamame and the impossible burger on gluten free bun (the whole reason I wanted to go). The edamame was undercooked and unseasoned. I had to use a utensil to cut several of them open. My guy got a kale salad that was 'marinated' but probably had been marinating for about 2 minutes. Our impossible burgers seemed overcooked. The gluten free bun (which we were charged $3 for) was just gluten free bread. My meal was $21 and honestly I left hungry. The staff was wonderful but there's no way I'd ever go back.

Unbelievable! This place amazed me from the second I looked at the menu...matter of fact, even before! We heard this place was a can't miss from a few sources who's trustworthiness is now seriously in question (good thing it wasn't my proctologist)! When we arrived at this little delight early on a Saturday morning I was surprised by how old everyone was, like I has just stepped into the mess hall of a senior citizen community. Thankfully I brought my grumpy face and knitting needles, I fit right in. To make it more "kid friendly" the staff places giant paper blankets under the highchairs of grand kids so they don't have to actually work and sweep up...genius really. Don't bother getting a kids menu because no substitutions are allowed. As if kids aren't picky about food. And here's where it gets unbelievable. You can get the exact same meals at almost every other breakfast place in United States for nearly half the price. I don't know how this place stays in business being literally 30% more expensive than every other breakfast restaurant! After my wallet vomited in its mouth a little and I gave it some antacid we decided to share the breakfast burrito for $11. What was unbelievable to me was our otherwise bubbly waitress, Shawna, choked and huffed when we decided to share breakfast and only ordered one meal. We also ordered some pancakes eggs and bacon for the kids. When my food came I could finally relax because the table next to us had just left and I was no longer getting an uncomfortable "I'm going to kick your ass and steal your girlfriend" stare down from these two old creepers who both looked like they were packing nunchucks. Oh yeah, the food! It's good I might even say very good. But it's your run-of-the-mill, nothing special breakfast for way more money. I'm never going back. Thus, 2 stars for being way below expectations, and making me further question the trustworthiness of people I hardly know.

I have a love/hate relationship with the Planet Organic, especially with the downtown location. This used to be the Big Fresh, until the Planet took over, so I am sad about that. The Planet sells mostly organic food items, but they also have a vitamin and supplement section, along with many personal care items. They are all about sustainability, health, and the environment. This location is smaller than the South location, so ready-made foods and baked items are transferred over, but there is still a fairly good selection. The ready-made foods are a favourite of mine. The vegan chocolate cake is so very moist. The samosas are awesome, but they have increased in price considerably. They used to be about $7 for six, but now they are $10 for the same amount! The hummus is quite good as well, and there are many different varieties, like sun-dried tomato and spinach. I like that they have a fairly good selection of gluten-free items, like waffles, flours, cereals, and sauces, but this location does not have any good gluten-free crackers, which should be a staple item. The prices are really expensive--so expensive that it pisses me off. Since the Planet is the only organic market left in the city, they can charge whatever they want, so I am somewhat resentful towards them. I will admit though that the Planet's sales have improved, and when something is on sale, it's a good price. The only problem is the good stuff sells out within the first few days or first week, and that is frustrating. The produce doesn't always look the best, but sometimes they have some nice stuff, but it's also very pricey. There's some really good organic cheeses and yogurts here, and if you're lactose intolerant, I recommend the rice cheese they sell. Be aware, the Planet sells some items that are not organic, so if this really matters to you, read the label carefully. It will usually be an item that is suspiciously cheaper, like the chocolate covered cranberries--still great tasting though!

Waited in line with only 2 people in front of me for over 20 mins only to find out that the girl is new and moved at a glacial pace. When I went to order I found out what I was ordering is no longer gluten free. Awesome. The service has been at a steep decline this took the cake. I'm done.

I stumbled across this bakery completely by chance while heading out for brunch on a visit. As a celiac who was travelling with a non-dairy friend, it called to us immediately. While we did grab brunch first, we immediately headed back to browse the offerings. They had a fauxtess cupcake which drew my eye immediately. Lots of cakes, cupcakes, donuts, other baked goods. I bought a couple as well as a mix for chocolate chip cookies and a loaf of challah with raisins. As a celiac, I have no complaints about the quality of the food. I'm used to some of the chalkier, drier textures due to baking alternatives. Considering these were not only gluten free (in a dedicated GF prep space!!) but soy, dairy, etc.I was not at all disappointed. Quality was impressive to me. I will say that payment can be a bit annoying if you're not prepared. Debit has a minimum of $10. While there is an atm literally right behind you as you stand at the register, you'll probably get a small surcharge to use it. Come prepared with cash!

my waiter was the best part of this meal. he navigated my gluten free challenge with dexterity. the maitre de saw that i was alone and wearing a sweatshirt so he tucked me in the corner facing the waiter's coffee station. i liked the food. they let me use my laptop. the manager came over and complimented my camera. way too stuffy for me though. again, i loved the waiter. too bad i'm shy.

We started off with a few appetizers, the guacamole, and two different empanadas, the beef picadillo and the sweet potato and pumpkin. The guacamole was spot on and the empanadas where perfectly fried with a nice balance of sweet and savory. We washed these down with some margaritas...I had the classic rocks with salt and my wife and friend both had the watermelon...all delicious with a generous pour. For my main I had a couple of tacos al pastor with the traditional toppings (onion, cilantro, and pineapple)...very tasty. I forgot what my wife and our friend had because our friend started to have a mild allergic reaction. He had failed to mention to us (and the server) that he was allergic to jalapenos. Several glasses of water and some medication took care of him (I guess he should have mentioned this to us since we were going to a Mexican restaurant). I am looking forward to going back and try some of the breakfast items....sans allergic friend.

The absolute worse food I've ever had. Notice I didn't say BBQ because it wasn't. The ribs were boiled or broiled. I guarantee they don't even own a smoker. The items that had mayonnaise were bad. Sour. If I swallowed I might have ended up in the hospital. The greens had no flavor. None what so ever. The baked beans were horrible. The only thing out of a the 54.00 we spent and enjoyed was the Mac n cheese. I would not give this meal to my enemies.

Last night I went to Nada for dinner. This is the second time I had been there, so I knew the food was amazing and I was really excited to be eating there. I will start by saying that the food was just as amazing this time as I had remembered. However, the service we received was extremely disappointing and really ruined the experience for us. There was some sort of corporate event going on that night so things were kind of backed up, which I totally understand. However, our waitress seldom came to check on us and we had to ask other people who worked there to find out waitress so we could get more water, chips, etc during our HOUR AND A HALF wait for our food. She only checked on us once during that whole time. My friend has celiac disease and is extremely allergic to gluten, and so she ordered gluten free tacos which were brought out to her touching the non gluten free tacos. If she hadn't been paying attention, she would have gotten really sick! I asked to have one of our appetizers comped because of our wait, and it was which I appreciated, but I wish that the appetizer had been taken off without having to ask. The food at Nada is unbelievable, but I will not be rushing back there for dinner any time soon!

We were delighted to find a new pizza place in the neighborhood! We walked in at 5:30 and were greeted by a waiter who appeared pale, sweaty and obviously sick since he sniffled (literally) EVERY OTHER WORD - it was very noticeable that he should not have been working. We passed it for allergies and sat down. He was very nice and accommodating to us and told us they had been open 8 days and that they had another branch across the street from Some Guys Pizza in Fishers. Hubby and his bestie ordered a 9 inch, I ordered a calzone and my toddler the spaghetti. Here is the rundown: 1. The 9 inch had an incredibly thick crust - the crust starts at about 6-7 inch in diameter of the pizza and radiates out toward the 9 inch mark. The toppings inside were meager but flavorful and what tasted like fresh mozzarella cheese. Because of this thick crust, the pizza appeared very small and slices looked awkward as we placed them on our plates. 2. My calzone came out in two pieces, open faced, just how Penn Station does it. I'm from the east coast and know calzones are to look like huge closed dumplings with hot cheese and goodness oozing with the first cut. It was also very small about 5 inches in length and 3 incges in width - maybe im just too spoiled by other places but it was about the size of a small sandwich. For over $8, penn station would've seemed like an all-you-can-eat buffet. The bread of he calzone was very white and thick. It was delicious and flavorful. My husband, his bestie and I all agree the calzone tasted way better than the pizza. 3. My daughter's spaghetti was floating in oil. I was incredibly disappointed. The meat sauce had very hard ground meat and there was no signs of tomato. Any person who knows how to cook, could tell this meat sauce was made purely of ground meat, oil and tomato paste. Because of this, the sauce looked dark brown and not red at all. I tasted it and it had a lot of flavor - the kind of flavor you find in tomato paste. Every time our server visited, he stood his distance from us because he knew, that we knew, he was sick. I really wanted to like this place since there isn't a good pizza place around the area and we usually go to Jimmy Stix Pizzeria in Carmel (owner of the old Wise Guys pizza which is now under new ownership). We followed Jimmy Stix because we loveee their breadsticks and pizza dough! We will still give the place another try in a couple of months in hopes we had picked a bad day. I plan to update this review at our second visit.

Question .. why does Rich City come up when you search Gluten Free Chinese but when you call them no one knows what has flour in it and what doesn't If there was one Chinese food place that used gluten free soy sauce (corn starch instead of flour) in their meals they would MAKE A KILLING. Such a simple switch with absolutely no taste change. Anyone want to make some money?

I really don't like giving poor reviews but this was a particularly rough experience: First the good: Nice atmosphere. Some really good dishes. Namely the Greek sausage, the cheese saganaki, the salad and the chicken kabob were all very good. The bad: - We arrived and there was no host to greet us for several minutes. People were standing around in the front wondering what to do. Ok I can get over that. - they guided us to our table and then turned us back to the front because the table wasn't ready. Ok. We can let that one go. - it became clear pretty early on that we were not remotely a priority table for our server. Not sure if it was because we were a two top or because we were under 40 but I've never been more neglected by a server. - the octopus appetizer was a bit too wet at and soggy. Decent taste but texture did not feel very cooked. Also left my wife barfing for hours on end through the night from food poisoning. Poor thing. She feels pretty certain it was the octopus and was definitely from the meal as it fully hit 2-4 hrs after the meal. - Our drinks weren't refilled until we were almost done with the meal. And the empty glasses were left at the table. - Our new plates always came late so we just used our dirty ones which we didn't mind but if we had actually waited, our food would have been cold every time. - the gyro meet was warm to luke warm. Definitely not hot. - our grill combo dish came out in three sections all with at least 5 to ten mins between. First the meat. 5-10 minutes later the rice. Which was practically floating in a soup of water. Then the 3 sauces which, again if we had waited until they arrived before eating, would have meant that the meat was all cold. - the end was probably the most frustrating because we were already on edge from the experience (and my wife and was feeling a little bit nauseas from what later turned out to be a night of vomiting). We asked for the bill. Watched the server attend to other tables for ten minutes before remembering to bring the check. Then after another 10 minutes of waiting we had to flag her down so that she could finally run the card. All the while our heaps of dirty dishes had been left at the table. We decided to stack them to help the staff and also clue them in to the fact that they had been sitting there for a long time. They still weren't taken by the time we left. We had a sense of humor about it at the time but felt like we had to say something. This was a romantic night out for us on a trip and what we envisioned and hoped would be a really nice restaurant with fine dining service. Though some of the food was very good the overall experience was very underwhelming and left my wife sick through the night.

We came here on a quiet afternoon because of the rave reviews on Yelp, but meh. The wild boar tacos are worth trying; they are very yummy and spicy. We also ordered the cheeseburger-very underwhelming, smothered in their house sauce that looked, smelled, and tasted mostly like plain mustard. Not sure what the fuss was about there. Also, I asked for the burger to be cooked medium well, and I was told they only cook burgers rare, medium, or well. Nothing in between. I asked for the meatloaf with pasta salad, instead of mac and cheese (dairy allergy). Nothing doing. They make absolutely no substitutions. Which would be fine if it in some way compromised the vision of the food, but this is not high-brow fare. Its at best so-so pub food. But if you like spicy, come here. They don't seem to flavor with anything else but cracked pepper and red chili.

Went to Salt Rock with high hopes based on the praise for it from some friends. And it was ok...average I would say. Not what I was hoping for. Service was good... very attentive and helpful waitstaff. Building layout, seating and all is nice. Every booth has a small TV... which I consider a negative since you can't turn it off.. and if you want to talk, it is a distraction. But I guess the emphasis on on Sports Bar, rather than restaurant. The food confirms that also. Pretty noisy... with the TV on, Music playing, and the surrounding diners chatting... not an intimate dining experience. We chose not to sit outside, since there is not an outdoor no-smoking area. Ordered water to drink, since I was driving... girlfriend ordered water also since she is deathly allergic to alcohol (literally)! Placed food orders... ME, Caesar Salad with anchovies, and medium rare prime rib, minus garlic mashed... so got more stir fried veggie mix (mostly squash). HER ... a Tuna Poke, and a house salad. We also ordered a Buffalo Cauliflower app to share.. Buffalo Cauliflower was ok... a little on the sweet side IMO, but many people like that. My Caesar (dressing) was very mild, not much flavor... so I was glad I ordered it with Anchovies... that made it much better. The romaine was fresh and crispy. Prime Rib? I suspect it was roasted much, much earlier, and then put in a sous-vide bath to keep it at the right temp until served. But I think it was sous-vided for way too long. It was lacking texture, almost mushy. Flavor was minimal as it had apparently been prepared with no spices or salt. Oddly enough.. even though nicely medium rare... no blood or juices. Au Jus was just mild broth... not salty at all, so dipping the meat into did little to add flavor (traditional use of Au Jus)... additional salt needed. The Horseradish sauce was good, although again very mild. Veggies were the best part of the meal... nicely done, with excellent flavor. My girlfriend reported her salad as good, and her tuna poke as over marinated (Teriyaki ginger) which is usually done to hide the fact that it is not super fresh. Pickled ginger was good, as was the avocado half that was served. Maybe the drinks make up the difference for those that indulge... I don't know. Happy Hour special seems to be very popular, and I would go back to try more of the apps. I will pass on the prime rib in the future though....

I walked into Sue's kitchen on a Sunday afternoon. I almost walked out because I thought the place was abandoned. Little did i know, it was in my best interest to do so. The place was run down, had old sketchy furniture, and a scary looking black woman staring me down as I approached the counter. I ordered the oxtail and was told that most of the sides were unavailable so i was basically forced to pick either cabbage, candy yams or mac & cheese. I chose all three since i could not get rice and beans, which is a staple/must have with this type of dish! The mac & cheese was the sole highlight of the dish and it wasnt even the main component! Don't even get me started on the main component (the oxtail). The pieces that i was given were greasy, hard, unappetizing and had more fat on them than 'precious'. It was the worse Caribbean food ive ever had and ive eaten at numerous Caribbean restaurants. It was an overall horrible experience as i believe it gave me food poisoning. I fell ill later that night and do not plan on ever giving it another chance again. Take this warning seriously. Its not worth it. This place needs to be shut down.

New menu items are bland. Sushi tastes pre-made and refrigerated (not fresh). Kids meal has no vegetables. Cashiers don't have access to an in store allergy menu and are not equipped by management to handle inquiries about food allergies. Overall not a Pei Wei experience that will have me returning.

We were utterly delighted with tonight's dinner at Amerigos. We told the waitress Tara that we were gluten intolerant and she graciously guided us through all the choices from soups to salads and mains. It's often a battle to find a restaurant and waiting staff that is knowledgeable enough to keep us from getting accidentally "glutened." This was by far our best experience in the Nashville area. We shared the generous and delicious chicken with Asiago mashed potatoes and sautéed spinach and had the yummy squash soup and Caesar salad- truly the best Caesar I've had in years. We will be returning to Amerigos soon and bringing our friends with us.

Really impressed at El Sur today. Inconspicuous, colorful building - definitely one of those Don't judge a book by its cover scenarios. Very friendly staff and always smiling. I ordered the fish tacos and my husband ordered the shredded beef tacos. The waitress warned me about the seasonings in the rice that might contain msg, so they brought me double of the beans. They brought a nice plate of shredded cabbage and pico de Gallo, and another plate of key limes to go with my tacos. The whole beans were a great flavor and if I wasnt full, I would have eaten every legume!!! My meal was delicious and I loved it. The waitress had told me the pan fried tacos are fried in contaminated oil because they do chimichangas in the same oil too. I really really like when the staff is trained and knows how to look after its patrons. We will definitely be back! The prices are extremely reasonable too. Happy Hour drinks are great prices. ..a Patron Margarita for $4! How can you go wrong?

I'm so disappointed. I've been coming here ever since this place opened and I order the Brielle with no pine nuts due to an allergy. Today I was told that all the sandwiches are pre-assembled because they were busy and they would not make my sandwich, even though i informed them of my allergy. I've never been to a place that wouldn't accommodate due to food allergies. Very poor customer service in my opinion, especially for a regular. I will not be returning or recommending to friends, who often contact me about places to eat in the Reading Terminal because they know I'm there every day.

Greasy greasy food and the only saving grace was the beer. It was sweltering hot in the place as well. Not at all turned on and won't be returning. I can't blame you for your patrons (or can I?), but if I have to see one more disgusting person flossing their teeth at the dinner table I'm going to vomit directly on them, the table, and the 3/4 of the burger they didn't eat and of course aren't taking home just having it thrown in the trash because they are wasteful douchebags. Arggh I can't stand restaurant patrons who throw away more food than they eat. Take it to go and give it to a homeless person in the park!

I always order a gluten-free pizza. It is consistently inconsistent. Sometimes the crust is very dry and sometimes it is palatable and even delicious. It is always a little bit on the salty side but I don't mind. The ratio of sauce to cheese to basil always changes as well. I just wish I could expect a more consistent pie. Additionally, the delivery is usually lightning fast, but yesterday I had to wait an hour and a half. Again, some consistency would be appreciated.

Delicious gluten free pizza. We order topped with broccoli. We have been ordering gf for over a year and have never gotten sick from cross contamination. We visit at least 2 times a month. You will not be disappointed. All of their food items are delicious. Our kids must eat gluten free for their health. Great staff. Clean restaurant.

I've been to this location twice now. First time service wasn't great she took forever to get us refills. Second time service was a little better but I ended up getting food poisoning. Don't think I'll be back to this location.

I wish I could give 0 star. I was looking for a good restaurant while I was driving thru Nashville. I saw that Bolton's spicy chicken and fish was rated really high. We ordered fish and chicken wings and plain chicken tenders for my son. My husband specifically ask how the spiciness come from? Hot sauce or batter? They sain it is IN THE BATTER!!!!so I agree with hot. But it came out with at least half a pound of blackened seasoning on top of plain chicken and fish. That is not cooking. Anybody can dumped a whole container of blackened seasoning on food and called it hot. It was redicurously salty and hot. The blackened seasoning was contaminated everywhere EVEN IN MY 2 YEARS OLD' FOOD. what made me made the most was the blackened seasoning got to my son' eyes. We did not even take second bite. Absolutely awful! !!!!! Missed represent Hot and Spicy. And I'm Thai by the way and I can handle hot like nobody.

My girlfriend and I went here on a Friday night. She ordered a chocolate mint cupcake, I ordered a dirty blondie, both from their gluten-free case. Neither one was particularly tasty. There was only one person behind the counter and she was busy; they could have used some more help, especially on a Friday night. And for a coffee shop-type place, the atmosphere was kinda drab. I like the concept and I applaud any place that specializes in Vegan and gluten-free food. Their selection is pretty decent and if I'm in the area again, I'll definitely stop back.

There are a very few number of times that I have frequented a restaurant and could not find any merit in it's service. Having worked my way up from the bottom-most positions in the hospitality industry, I usually feel for the hardships and annoyances that these employees have to endure. This was not one of those times. We visited this location tonight for a anniversary celebration for my mother. We brought our 11-month-old and fully expected a small degree of trepidation from the Sushi Garden team in serving as it is par for the course these days. What we did not expect was that start to finish we would be made to feel out of place, unwelcome and as a nuisance. We were greeted by a ho-hum hostess, seated in a cramped booth, and provided with a filthy high chair full of food from previous guests. Thank goodness for disinfectant wipes! Our server repeatedly ignored a request from my mother for gluten-free soy sauce until we had almost completed our meal and received an, "Oh, I'm sorry this is a little late." From that point on there was eye roll after eye roll from the young female staff at everything from the floor beneath the high chair, our request for more water and my sweet little baby leaving on my husbands shoulders. I'm still not quite sure why that last action annoyed the young lady so much. It was just so incredibly insulting. The food was forgettable at best and we were treated like we weren't worth the effort of the crew, even though we spent $100 for dinner for four. We will never return and as I still work in the hospitality industry, often answering requests for great places to dine I will be sure to forget this one in my responses.

10 years ago when I was 20, I walked in with another female companion with a group of 6 or 8 guys (I don't remember) . It was a Bachelor Party and they prettty much dragged us innocent girls in. I'm pretty sure we weren't served although I don't remember (this is becoming the theme of this evening)... Next thing I know we made it to her apartment and I had thrown up as I opened the door of her 325 ti... who drives a 325 ti... baby hatchback BMW?!? (No that is not nice Shiho!) It was a very cute car and a lovely birthday present she got when she was 16. I rarely threw up back then so something must have gone done during the night. I do not recall all the details but thank Sandbar for getting an eventful (unfortunately not very memorable for me) evening started.
